Don't you see that I've got two movie tickets in my hand? Let's get going! We weren't able to hang out yesterday, so we're going for double today!
You can take this as me blackmailing you to keep your mouth shut, or as a display of gratitude. Of course, you can just consider this hanging out as well... Regardless of the reason, let's get going!
Hurry, hurry! The movie's going to start! Oh, can't forget about the 3D glasses!
I thought Hornet would get all worked up at the climax scene, but...
She was fully absorbed in movie.
If anything, I was the one getting worked up, unable to ignore the feeling of her hand in mine...
The best parts of Westerns are the riding scenes and the shootouts~
Heehee~ Are you turning red just from holding hands?
Well then, let's head to the next place on our list~!
And just like that, Hornet dragged me along to all the other stores in the mall.
Whew... that was so fun! I feel like I had all the fun in the world~ The cowboy experience corner was especially good...
Commander, are you tired? Let's take a break then!
Taking my hand, Hornet and I sat down at a bench.
Ehem, is this one of those... special confiding events where my affection points go up?
Hmm... Is there anything I haven't confided in you about... Northampton and Enty have taught me a lot, and thanks to yesterday's practice, my head's a lot clearer and I'm feeling a lot better.

Speaking of which. Did you see Northampton cheering for me with a loud voice? I was really surprised, though I wasn't really able to make out what she was saying because of how far away she was, ahaha...
And, about my sister...
"Copying your sister isn't bad, but don't just copy her. Use her power as a basis for your own skills and show off your own strength."
That was nicely said, but I wanted to add one thing. ...There are times when I don't want to rely on my sisters' powers, don't want to copy their tricks, and just want to fight with what I have.
For example... Like, I'm not as much of a trouble to deal with as my sisters are. I speak the truth about what I like and what I don't like.
So, this is my fighting style. I'll say it loud and clear. Commander, I love you!
...Commander, how do you feel?

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids!

<size=45>Begin the Operation!</size>

scripts.say: Do I make myself clear, Bel? I won't tolerate failure on this mission!
We may have allowed the Eagle Union to hog the spotlight with their Christmas party, but the most effective way to prove that the Royal Navy is the mightiest faction here is through a show of force!
At the upcoming joint exercises, make sure that everyone trembles before our might!
In any case, that is what Her Majesty said...
So I must cross swords with my honourable Master's fleet once more...
So that's why you called for all of us?
I have no objections to facing off against Master's fleet, but... controlling the amount of force will take some finesse...
Well, we've already done this once before, so let's not take this too seriously~
That may be the case, but as these are the Queen's orders, I can't afford to hold back.
Indeed. Regarding that matter, I've consulted with Belfast and made some adjustments to the personnel who will be handling this important mission.
I'm a bit concerned... I just arrived at the base, and I already have to fight against my Master's fleet...
Will Dido also be cast aside like this child here...
Don't worry. Those are the actual orders that Her Majesty gave.
*fidgets*
In other words, I'll be supporting the Royal Maids and... fighting against my Master's fleet?
Demonstrate the glory of the Royal Navy, help improve everyone's skills, and improve communication between members of the fleet...
...and most importantly, prove to my Master that I can fulfill any request, no matter the situation...?
Understood! For the sake of Her Majesty and my Master, I will give it my all!
What a monster...
She's the right person for the job. If Belfast or I were to handle this job, we'd end up subconsciously holding back against the Master.
In contrast, Dido should be able to perfectly balance her obligations to the Queen, to the Maid Team, as well as to the Master, and therefore perform to her utmost.
Indeed. I suppose we'll be taking a back seat this time.
...The Master's fleet will be arriving soon. Everyone, prepare for battle.

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids!

<size=45>Secret Stratagem</size>

scripts.say: Let's take this from the top. As one would expect of my Master's fleet... launching such a fierce attack right away...!
Hehe, they really managed to catch us off guard last time. That's why Her Majesty decided to bolster our ranks.
Are we going to be all right? Our first defense line has already been broken...

I hope they aren't thinking, "look how weak the Maid Team is..." Look, there are so many ships from various factions sailing under the same banner. Wouldn't it be better for us to go all out as well...?
I do believe you're overthinking things.

From what I can tell, they're not attacking us with their full strength. If we were to counterattack with our full strength, my Master would respond in kind, and this would quickly devolve into a brawl.
While that may be enough to "put on a show of strength," from the perspective of a training exercise, we should approach this situation as if it was an actual battle.
I see your point. In this current era of aircraft carriers, it would seem a bit anachronistic to engage in a decisive gun battle.
Ugh...
In any case, instead of playing all our cards right away, it would be best to gradually ramp up the challenge we pose to my Master's fleet...
If I stick close to Master, I won't be thrown away... That way, I'll be able to stay with Master until the very end... Haah...
Ah, Master, my beloved Master...
(Is she really going to be all right...)
(She'll be just fine. After all, this is the best way to produce results that will satisfy both Master and Her Majesty.)
(W-well... If you say so...)
(Indeed, it'll be just fine. Despite her appearances, she's perfectly capable of thinking for herself.)
Ahem. It doesn't make sense for us to tarry longer here. Let's move to the next defensive line.

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids!

<size=45>Sororal Defensive Line</size>

scripts.say: Curacao, we're still hanging in there! Let's show them the power of the Royal...
All right, enough of that~♪ Dido and the others aren't fighting to the death, so why don't we conserve our strength?
Speaking of Dido, she certainly has a striking way of fighting.
Indeed. At first, it seems like she's just brazenly charging forward, but she has a good grasp of when to back off.
As a Royal maid, however, she still is a bit rough around the edges.
I do apologize for suddenly pushing such an important role upon you.
Think nothing of it. Rather, I'm actually grateful, Miss Belfast.
Despite the fact that I'm still a novice here, I am honoured that you gave me the opportunity to serve my Master and the fleet.
Hehe, you show a lot of promise. I look forward to your performance as a member of the Royal Maids.
And the same goes for your performance as a member of this fleet. After all, you are the nameship of the Dido-class, right?
Yes ma'am...!
She's even... placed her trust in me...!
...But still, I'm not...

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids!

<size=45>The Instructor's Tactics</size>

scripts.say: Kent, Suffolk, take advantage of your heavier armor to secure our supply routes.
In addition, those who are equipped with anti-air equipment and radars should take care of the enemy's aircraft. Stick to the formations that Belfast instructed you on.
Make sure to resupply now, as this will be our last opportunity. Double-check to make sure you won't run out of ammo.
The preparations for our final line of defense are complete.
...So this is going to be the last battle...
Just fight with everything you have. We've already come this far, so don't regret anything.
That's right. Keep fighting... until Master and I are the only ones standing...
And then Master will have no choice but to accept me...
Don't overdo it.
I'm not sure you'll listen to any of this, but I'm going to say it anyway.
When you're standing in front of the Master, know that all the maids have been supporting you so that you could fight without reservations.
You simply need to do your part, and give it your all. If you do that, Master will look upon you favorably.
Even if you aren't able to produce the results that you want, neither Master, nor any of us, will cast you aside.
......Understood!
They're coming. Master's fleet...
Dido, nameship of the Dido-class light cruisers...
Will fight with everything she has, for Master's sake!

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids!

<size=45>Her Reward</size>

scripts.say: The joint exercise with the Maid Team drew to a close.
More important than winning or losing was the ability for the members of each fleet to work with each other and communicate properly.
Or, as Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth said, for the Maid Team to "display the glory of the Royal Navy."
Even though the exercise was not perfect, both sides achieved the results that they had hoped for.
And now, we arrive at the present...
Master, I've finished passing out the results of the joint exercise. I've already archived the data within the intelligence room, as well as with the registries of the individual factions.
While my secretary was gone, this maid somehow made herself comfortable sitting in my office.
Thinking back about that training exercise, everyone did an outstanding job, but the way she fought all-out until she was the last one standing left a deep impression within me...
For going above and beyond the line of duty, perhaps she deserves a little bonus...
Hawawawa...
Haah... Ahh... Um...
Dido quickly became flustered.
High... five...? Oh right, wasn't this some kind of Eagle Union exercise?
This lowly maid has no right to touch the Master's hand! At least...
Um, let this one...
Dido lifted the hand of a stuffed doll and pressed it against my hand.
Master...? Are you busy right now...?
Umm, is there something that I can do to help...?
Aww... I knew it... Master intended to cast me aside after all...
Waaah... Master! Please don't throw me away... Please let me stay by your side...! ！ ！ ！
I can't live without you, Master! I'll seriously die! Please! Master! Please! ！
Oh... you didn't notice I was here...? I'm so relieved, Master...
I calmed Dido down and consoled her.
As such, we welcomed some new friends to the port...
Is there any work that I can help you with? Just ask, and I'll do it for you! I'll handle anything for you, no matter the request!
That's because I... I'm your maid after all, Master!

sequence:
Denver's Quest!

<size=45>1.Quest Accepted!</size>

scripts.say: So, I was in the harbor the other day, and someone brought up how they had this job they could use a hand with, but they didn't know who to turn to.
There are plenty of busy bees around the port, but not all bees are as busy as others, so I'm thinking we could set up some sorta system for people to help out if they've got the time!
And this is what I came up with. What do you think, Commander?
As per Denver's suggestion, we established a sort of quest board for people to request others' assistance with whatever they need doing.
Within hours of its creation, the board was already covered in written requests for various tasks and projects, held up by thumbtacks.
Hmm, this is neat...
Oh, hey, Commander! Thanks for implementing my quest board idea. You're a champ.
I stood beside Denver and inspected the quest board. A handful of jobs had been marked "Quest Complete" with a bright red stamp.
I was amazed. Only a few hours have passed, and already someone had taken it upon themselves to help people. The question was, who is it?
Upon closer inspection, I could make out the name of the girl who accepted the quest. To my surprise, it was Denver's oldest sister, Cleveland.
That's Cleveland for ya. I gotta take a leaf out of her book and do the same, as a fellow Knight of the Sea!
Look, she's even done the jobs involving moving stuff to that newly-built club building!
What a legend... We just created this quest board, and she's been knocking these jobs out one by one...
It was just like Denver said. I inspected some more quests on the board, and they had all been marked as completed by Cleveland.
Now I'm feeling motivated! New goal: aim for the top of the leaderboard, like Cleveland!
Denver always strives to do the best she can, but on this day she sounded especially fired up.

sequence:
Denver's Quest!

<size=45>2.First Quest, First Party</size>

scripts.say: Could you help me look for some quests, Commander? I want ones that'll score me as much rep as Cleveland.
Attaining Cleveland's level of prestige is a lofty ambition indeed.
In any case, solving practical problems around the port is part of my job. With that in mind, I agreed to help her. Denver started scouring the quest board, while I went asking around.
Around ten minutes later, Denver came to me with printed copies of some promising tasks from the quest board.
First off, here's one from the Royal Maids, who want help with decorating a huge cake... Not bad, but I dunno if it's the one for me.
This one's from Long Island. "LF partner to practice fighting mains with"... Uhh, Commander, what kind of jobs are these even?
"They might sound like odd jobs, but I think your best strategy is to be open to all kinds of quests, regardless of what they involve."
Yeah, I guess... I'm just a bit confused because this isn't what I was expecting.
I was hoping for something a little grander. "I really need your help!" sorta deal, you know?
She had a point. These quests seemed closer to busywork than calls for urgent assistance.
I presented what quests I had found on my own, hoping one of them might live up to her expectations.
Wow, you found a couple too, huh? Let's see what we have here...
Ooh! Storehouse pest control! You won't find a more perfect quest for me than this!
I'll be one step closer to Clevelandhood if I can get this done!
Denver's hardworking ethic and desire to help others are two of her greatest qualities.
Hmm. Judging by the handwriting, I'm 95% sure it's Spence who posted this quest.
You know, from the Little Beavers? I hang out with 'em all the time, so I know how they write.
Anyway, sorry for asking on such short notice, but could you come along and help me with this quest, Commander?
For better or worse, I had no other plans in particular on that day, so I thought "why not" and agreed to help her.
I knew I could count on you!
Every journey starts with one step, and today will be my first one towards Clevelandy greatness!
She balled her hand into a fist and extended her arm towards me. She held it like that, waiting for my response.
I realized what she was going for, and did a fist bump with her.
Hell yeah! That's how we do it!
All right then, let's go!

sequence:
Denver's Quest!

<size=45>3.Knights Need Advice</size>

scripts.say: We did as the quest said and headed to just outside the storehouse, where Spence and Charles Ausburne greeted us.
Salutations, Commander! And Denver, too!
A-are you here to take care of the pests? I see you've got the q-quest papers...
Sure are, sure do!
Answering the call of those who need help, now that's what real heroes do!
Clue me in on the deets. Where are the pests? There in the storehouse?
Y-yes. J-just have a look...
Charles produced a key and opened the door to the storehouse. The interior was lined with tons of rations and food.
I spotted a few bags which had holes chewed through the bottom. The infestation hadn't yet grown out of control, but it had to be dealt with posthaste.
I did what a hero would and searched every nook and cranny for those pesky pests, but I couldn't find them anywhere.
We're up against sneaky little buggers, eh? I doubt it'll be easy luring them out of... Hey! There!
Denver interrupted herself. She armed herself with a machine gun barrel lying around in the storage and went on the offensive.
I saw one right there! Get back here, you little bug!
Denver swung her improvised weapon with unbelievable speed and took out a lone cockroach.
Whew! That's one, but we should expect to find dozens more, based on the look of things.
D-d-d-dozens more?!
"We'll never get them all with this approach," I thought. A change of strategy was necessary.
I walked out of the storehouse and inspected the flower bed by the entrance.
Yeah? What's up?
I called her attention to the white flowers growing on the ground.
What about 'em? ...Wait, I see now! Columbia told me about these flowers, they work as a natural insecticide!
If we use these, we can take out the all bugs in one fell swoop!
Good thinking, Commander! Just goes to show that every knight could use the advice of a commander!
She looked at me with gleaming eyes and thanked me, then promptly picked the flowers and got to work on concocting a simple pesticide.
I didn't know it yet, but our knightly adventure had only just begun.

sequence:
Denver's Quest!

<size=45>4.The Knight's Sisters</size>

scripts.say: After Denver turned in the pest control quest, she came back with a new addition to our little party.
It was none other than her disciplined, self-reliant younger sister and fellow Knight of the Sea, Birmingham.
There you are, Commander!
Let me introduce you to my little sister here! Her name is Birmingham.
...Denver, this is silly. I already introduced myself to the commander when I took up my post here.
Fair enough. Anyway, you know what the commander and I did earlier? We came to face with a swarm of wretched bugs, and we wiped 'em all out!
Which is to say... what? That you have the potential to rival Cleveland? Don't take this the wrong way, but I'm skeptical.
Birmingham gazed intently at us, looking like she was going to throw down the gauntlet. Perhaps she would've, if someone hadn't interjected.
Oh! Commander! And two of my little sisters as well.
Cleveland! Hey!
Heh, guess I've got competition now.
Cleveland chuckled as she put the red stamp on a quest she had just completed.
What kinda quest did you take on today, Cleve?
Hm? Oh, nothing to write home about. Just did a sweep not too far from here.
You did a sweep by yourself?! Wow! You really are a legend!
I agree. That's incredible.
Uh... What? Literally all I did was sweep the floor of this place the R&D guys wanted to convert into a storeroom.
Then you made their job easier, so they'll be able to work faster and come up with a series of amazing inventions!
You made a contribution to science! Man, I wanna be as awesome as you someday!
Denver got fired up again, inspired by her sister's allegedly great contribution.
Psst, Commander. Is she always like this?
She must be a real handful... Thanks for always looking after her.
Denver sang Cleveland's praises, while Cleveland herself was left speechless. Birmingham, meanwhile, gave me her thanks.
Through Denver's enthusiasm, I got Birmingham to open up, if only a bit.

sequence:
Denver's Quest!

<size=45>5.A Rival's Quest</size>

scripts.say: A rival to my knightly companion approached the quest board.
Oh, if it ain't you, Denver. That explains that shoutin' just a minute ago.
It was Sendai from the Sakura Empire. She held a sheet of paper in her hand.
Was just thinking about whether or not to put this quest on the board.
What kinda quest are we talking? The commander and I could give you a hand.
You'd do that? It's nothin' important anyway, but if you wanna.
See, I got into basketball a while back. Been playin' with Ashigara and Nachi a lot. Too much, even, so I've been gathering up an away team to play against.
Away team? Ah, you mean like, people you've never played against before?
Basically. I've got some people already, but if I called 'em now it'd take all day for them to show. So what I'm askin' for is a one-on-one.
Sendai smiled and unfolded her handwritten quest paper.
So, what do you say? Heard your sisters are into basketball. They could spectate if they want.
Ah, so you're challenging me to a round of basketball, huh?
Sure am. You're the worthiest opponent I can think of. And how could I pass up a chance to find out who between us is the best?
Well, I'm sure as heck not one to back down when my rep's at stake!
They glared intently at each other. Not as enemies, but as friendly rivals, each looking to prove themselves the better basketball player.
Challenge accepted! This will be one more step on my journey to become a full-fledged Knight of the Sea!
All right, then we'll play in two hours. Get yourself warmed up and bring your A-game.
Oh, and Commander? I want you to be the referee. You're usually pretty impartial, compared to most girls with biases to their faction.
Yeah! Be our referee, Commander!
Sendai and Denver alike had fiery hot looks of determination in their eyes. One thing was for sure: an intense game of basketball was imminent.

sequence:
Denver's Quest!

<size=45>6.Leveling Up!</size>

scripts.say: It was time for the match, and I'd arrived at the basketball court. Word of the game must have gotten around, as the spectator seats were starting to fill up.
G-give it your all, D-Denver!
I normally wouldn't spectate a game. But it's a different story when Sendai and Denver are playing.
Hmm. Between the two though, wouldn't it be fair to argue that Sendai has the most potential?
I wouldn't be so sure! You've never seen Denver play before, so you can't gauge her ability!
The spectators were clamoring as Sendai walked from across the court. She looked at Denver while spinning the ball with her bandage-covered index finger.
The rules are simple. Scored shots from the three-point line are worth 2 points. Any other shot's worth 1 point. First to 10 points wins.
Simple is just the way I like it. Well? I'm ready when you are!
Sendai won the coin flip to determine who starts off with the ball. The whistle blew, and the match officially started.
Let's see what you've got!
Sendai swiftly dribbled her way towards the goal. Denver intended to intercept, and had to gauge whether she was coming in left or right.
It's gotta be the left!
Nice try! It's the right!
Sendai gracefully swirled past Denver's defense and threw a well-aimed shot into her basket. Sendai gained the lead with 1 point.
Now it's my turn! Watch this!
Go on. I'm ready to intercept where– What the hell?!
Denver threw the ball right from where she stood at the three-point line. Incredibly, the ball went right into Sendai's basket, scoring Denver 2 points.
Gotcha! By the way, I play my best in the position of shooting guard!
Hmph, not bad... Then I'll just have to double down on my defense!
The lead switched back and forth repeatedly, until the game reached a decisive point. The board stood at 9 to 8 for Sendai.
*pant*... S-Sendai's dribbling is so deceptive... I can't predict where she's going!
Denver's strategy had become almost impossible to pull off as Sendai gradually improved her defense game.
Heh, it's over, Denver... I can read your movements like an open book. You're not gettin' the ball from me again!
Don't count your chickens until they've hatched! I'm gonna win this, whatever it takes!
You sure sound cocksure. Hope that means you're finally gonna bust out your A-game!
Sendai undid the bandages covering her hands, while Denver gazed up into the vast blue sky.
Commander, Cleveland... I hope you're watching me. I'm gonna make you proud!
The tense match had reached its final stage, and victory seemed within grasp of either player's hands.

sequence:
Denver's Quest!

<size=45>7.Chivalric Oath</size>

scripts.say: We're still alive, y'know! Don't look at the sky, look at us!
Cleveland brought Denver back to reality from her little melodramatic moment.
Huh?! When'd you show up to spectate, Cleve?!
Don't waste time thinking about that! Focus! It all comes down to whoever scores now!
...Yeah! You're right!
Denver abandoned the strategy she'd used up to now, as it wasn't working anymore, and instead came charging at Sendai.
Watch this!
The hell?!
Denver dribbled the ball in a manner just short of a foul, going on the hyper-offensive.
This is it! Eyes on me, Commander, Cleve!
She completely broke through Sendai's defense, throwing the ball at the basket from the three-point line on Denver's own side.
Sendai stared dumbfounded as the ball flew through the air and went cleanly through the hoop, scoring Denver the win.
Damn... Feels like I just got topped in determination as well as skill.
The crowd burst into cheers. This triumph was significant for Denver in more ways than one.
Cleveland went and gave Denver her congratulations and a fist bump, then Denver jogged over to me.
Whew... C-Commander, did you see that? I'm amazed, myself!
When I heard Cleveland and saw you both spectating the game, I just felt this surge of energy and willpower!
Without you, I don't know if I could've clutched the win like that! Thank you, Commander!
Denver expressed her gratitude with a dazzling smile.
I know I'm still lacking experience, but one day I'm gonna be a gallant Knight of the Sea, just like Cleve.
And when I am, I vow to be your sword. The sword that cuts aside everything barring you from your future, Commander!
She made a chivalric oath that actually brought a blush to my face. I responded the best way I could think of: by holding her hand firmly.
O-oh gosh!
Err... Ahem! It's my honor and duty to serve as your knight, Commander!
She declared her feelings candidly. At the end of the day, her quest to attaining knighthood – or Clevelandhood, as she'd put it – continues.
And my job was to help her on the journey in any way I could.

sequence:
Full Steam Ahead!

<size=45>1 First on the Scene</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Today was the day I would welcome Shimakaze as my secretary.
I'd heard much about her quirky personality through her friend, Suruga. She said something to the tune of...
You're making HER your secretary? Don't get me wrong, she isn't a bad person by any means.
How should I put it... She's just as clever as she is dumb. She's proactive and quick to act, yet she's astonishingly slow-witted.
What I'm trying to say is, please temper your expectations. You'll be dealing with someone who's essentially an overgrown child.
Shimakaze has a good reputation as a shipgirl with outstanding abilities. Despite this, Suruga was quite critical of her.
The word of the many against the word of her closest friend.
As I watched the minutes tick away while waiting for her to arrive, I wondered whether there was some truth to what Suruga said...

options.content: Stay sharp, ready to greet her

scripts.say: ...30 minutes had passed since Shimakaze was meant to show up. I feared for the worst—that she had a case of Akatsuki syndrome.
All of a sudden, the raid siren began blaring. It was the signal that enemy mass-produced ships had appeared in the surrounding waters.

options.content: Get ready to sortie at once

scripts.say: I felt guilty about leaving Shimakaze hanging, but I had no choice but to deal with this pressing threat.
Great you could come, Commander. We'll need all the help we can to find them in this thick fog.
Before we could neutralize the enemy, we had to locate them first. What's more, we had to do it quick, before they could cause any significant damage.
Huh? What's this? I'm picking something up...
Abukuma had her eyes fixated on her radar. The look of focus on her face turned into one of surprise. What had she picked up?
Oh... It's a friendly signal. Looks like there wasn't any need for us to show up after all. Look!
I turned to look southwest at what she was pointing at. What I saw caught me by surprise.
Stupid, stupid mass-produced ships! Get back here! I have a very important meeting today, and I don't wanna miss it because of you!
Owwie! You... You can't target my ears! That's cheating! Hmph... Fine, if that's how you want it, then I won't pull my punches either!
A sweet, yet courageous voice rang out amid the thundering roars of battle. Was it really her...?
An eye for an eye, a torpedo for a shell! Watch out, because here I come!

sequence:
Full Steam Ahead!

<size=45>2 Cool that Hot Head</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Shimakaze came into my office the next morning and wholly devoted herself to her secretarial duties.
Right... I'll take out the trash while going to check on the laundry, and then return this folder to its storage cabinet in the archives!
"All at once? I've never seen this level of multitasking before. It's incredible."
Heheh! Please, this is all child's play to me! I'd know, because I played with a few destroyers on the way here!
It pleased me to see her working hard and enjoying herself. There was one thing that was bothering me, though...
Hmm? You look as if you want to ask me something, Commander.
"In fact, I do. Did you do the task I gave to you first thing in the morning today?"
Erp...
"I was concerned because I had wanted you to prioritize finishing that task."
Right, uhh... Err... The formal report, I presume...?
That's the one, right? For the incident with the mass-produced ships yesterday...
"Not quite. Thanks to your valiant efforts, we successfully defeated the enemies before they could cause any damage..."
Then what is there to explain? It was standard proce– Wait... Is this about how I was late to the meeting yesterday?

options.content: "That's part of it, but not all."

scripts.say: Figures...
"You could have reached me by radio or sent me a message. How come I didn't hear a single word from you yesterday before you went straight into battle?"
You are absolutely right, Commander... I should've communicated that I'd found the enemies right away! Forgive me...
"I hear the sincerity in your voice. Rest assured, you're pardoned. But listen, there's one thing I want to stress here..."
Huh...? And what... would that be...?
"Please, try not to get into any more dangerous situations without notifying me ahead of time."
Commander...! I'm honored that you're so concerned with my safety! I'll begin writing my report at once!
And she did just that, picking up a pen and paper without a moment's delay.
Aahh! Nooo! I pressed too hard and punctured the paper!
It was starting to seem like Suruga was more or less right on the money with her appraisal...

sequence:
Full Steam Ahead!

<size=45>3 Ride the Island Breeze</size>

scripts.say: Port - Daytime
Shimakaze finished her last task for the day, sat down, and yawned.
Gosh, writing that report was easily the most taxing thing I did today... That said, I really did pour my heart into it!
After thanking her for her hard work, I decided to give her a break which she could spend however she wanted.
That wasn't to say I was done with her for today. I just wanted to see Shimakaze in her "natural habitat," so to speak.
And so, I went to look around in order to see what she was up to.
Wow. It's finished already...
Mhm! Making a kite is easy, you know! All you need is a plastic bag and a bit of string!
I see, I see! The dev notes did mention that your hobby is collecting kites, no wonder you're an expert!
I didn't think you'd know that! Though, I'm not sure what those "dev notes" are... In any case, it started with me collecting them, but then I got really into making them myself!
Now, before we fly it, I think we should paint something pretty on it.
Good idea! Lemme go get some brushes and paint!
Shimakaze was hanging out with Inazuma and Ikazuchi, and the three of them were making a kite together. I observed them from a distance.
All done! I drew a cute little picture of you and stuck it to the kite.
That's me? Oh my god! I really do have a face only a mother could love, don't I...
Don't put yourself down like that. It's a caricature. It's supposed to be exaggerated.
Yeah. At least it looks a lot better than the one I drew on your rigging.
Hahaha! You know, I'm still quite fond of that one even now!
Art aside, come on! Let's fly this thing already!
Of course, in just a bit. This place isn't ideal for flying a kite, though. Hmm... Actually, wait here for a moment, I'll be right back.
Suddenly, my comms device started ringing. Shimakaze was calling me.
Commander, I'm, uh, with Inazuma and Ikazuchi, and we want to fly a kite. We're going down to the coast, just letting you know. I promise I'll be back on time, though!
It made me happy to hear she had taken my words to heart. I acknowledged her report and let her be on her way.

sequence:
Full Steam Ahead!

<size=45>4 Day at the Museum</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Sorry, Commander. I wound up spending nearly the entire day flying that kite...
"Don't be sorry. I gave you permission to do so, after all."
...Oh, I see now!
"There isn't much work to do today either, so you're free to spend the day however you'd like again."
Are you sure? In that case, there's this place I'd really like to visit...
Shimakaze and I arrived at a newly built museum just on the outskirts of the city.
Wooow! This weapons museum is incredible! Look at all the stuff they have!
She looked around the museum while hopping around like an excited dog. Or rather, an excited rabbit.
Oh! Commander, come take a look at this!
A plaque caught her attention. I walked over and took a look.
Apparently, all the weapons on display here aren't replicas, they're the real deal!
"That's unusual, but interesting. I just hope none of them are still loaded..."
Whoa! Look over there! They've even got quintuple torpedo tubes!
She was about to make a beeline for the torpedo tubes, but I put a hand on her shoulder and stopped her.
Huh? Excuse me, but I want to go take a closer look! Why are you–
I brought the two signs next to the museum piece to her attention.
One said to refrain from touching the weapons. The other asked visitors to be quiet inside the museum.
Oh, whoops... I'm sorry. My carelessness is showing again...
She slumped over in an exaggerated show of dejection. It was endearing in a way.
Since she apologized, I let her off the hook and cheered her up. Then we continued our tour of the museum, hand in hand.

sequence:
Full Steam Ahead!

<size=45>5 Double Bunny Trouble</size>

scripts.say: City - Amusement Park
After how successful our museum trip was, I decided to take Shimakaze out to see another one of the city's attractions.
Holy smoke! I see we're visiting an amusement park this time! This is going to be awesome!
We'd only just arrived, and she was already bubbling with excitement. Things were off to a good start.
All right then, time to conduct our "inspection tour"! I'll catch up with you later!
Gotta go fast!
And just like that, she ran off on her own.
La-de-dum~♪
Ooh, so this place is a house of mirrors! Everywhere I look there's a funny-looking clone of me!
Whoa! Now this is a truly wacky take on my appearance!
Am I... a wacky clone to you...?
Whuah?! Did... Did the mirror just speak?! I must've entered a haunted house instead...
I'm not a mirror. I'm Laffey...
...Oh! It's you! Laffey from the Eagle Union!
Finally, with the guidance of a Manjuu park employee, I managed to catch up with Shimakaze.
Mhm... The Eagle Union's scariest destroyer... And I'm here to haunt yooouu...
Aaahhh! Noooo! My heart can't handle hauntings, or scary stuff in generaaaaal!
And what a strange situation I found her in...
Thanks for treating me to lunch. I guess it's lucky I happened to come here today...
No, thank you for gracing me with your presence! I'm simply honored to meet one of the Eagle Union's most renowned destroyers!
Well, sure... Who's paying, by the way...?
In the end, I hardly got to try any of the park's rides. Instead, I had a pleasant lunch with two rabbits.

sequence:
Full Steam Ahead!

<size=45>6 One for All</size>

scripts.say: Port - Exercise Area
Everyone who can fight, please get into combat position! Suruga will lead the evacuation!
What she said! I'll keep the civilians safe... And Shimakaze, don't do anything stupid, all right?
I know what I'm doing, don't worry! Right, Commander?
All right, it's up to you then!
We got word of a fleet of mass-produced ships appearing in a sector close to the exercise area.
I mobilized all of the shipgirls in the area, ordered a reload from training ammo to live ammo, and called for reinforcements to aid with the evacuation.
I've fulfilled all my friends' expectations of me as the secretary! Now it's time foooor... Full steam ahead!
Shimakaze relayed my orders and swapped ammunition, then prepared to charge at the mass-produced ships. I yelled for her to halt.
What? Oh, right! M-my bad!
Luckily, she got the message right away.
We're here too, remember? Don't go running off without us.
Having plot armor doesn't make you invincible, you know!
Though I'm not quite sure what "plot armor" is, Ikazuchi is right.
The same for me! Do not forget I'm ready to fight as well!
Everyone was counting on Shimakaze and me. It was time for us to show them our teamwork.
Hmm... Okay! We'll capture this area first and hold it until everyone's been evacuated!
Abukuma! Akatsuki! Smokescreens, please!
On it. They won't know what hit them.
Acknowledged! Deploying smokescreen!
Shimakaze issued clear orders to all the shipgirls while they got into combat positions.
Inazuma! Ikazuchi! Follow me! We're going to hit them where it hurts!
Will do! I'm ready!
Gotcha! Let's dunk on these scrubs!
It was a blissful sight, seeing all the girls move toward the objective in such perfect formation.

sequence:
Full Steam Ahead!

<size=45>7 All for One</size>

scripts.say: ...And that concludes my mission report!
Shimakaze gave me a debriefing on yesterday's battle with the mass-produced ships.
"This is quite the detailed report. One should expect no less from a first-rate secretary."
Oh, please, it's nothing special! I'm just happy to make myself useful to you!
She flashed a proud smile. It made me realize how much more mature she seemed now compared to just a few days ago.
On a scale from 1 to 10, how would you rate my report?
Aww, dang it! I'll just have to do better next time, I suppose...
Frankly, I could have given her a perfect 10, but I just thought it'd be wiser to have her strive to become even better.
You know, being the secretary is honestly pretty great!
Initially, I agreed to do it just as a means to push my own limits. And while it did have that effect...
It also became an opportunity to inspire others to work hard because I myself am working hard! ...Wait, doesn't that make me sound like a slave-driver?!
Hearing her stumble over what she just said brought a smile to my face.
"I have to say, I feel like I've grown after working with you these days."
She fell silent. I worried that my joke didn't land, or worse yet, that she took it at face value...
This... This is why being the secretary's so great!
"What? Elaborate."
Oh, for goodness' sake! Do I have to say it out loud?! All right, fine!
It's great because I get to work with a strong, kind, smart, wisecracking person like you...
I mean, who wouldn't want to work with the person they love? I've loved you since– Whuah?! Oh no!
Before she could finish pouring her heart out, a cup of coffee slipped out of her hand and hit the floor.
And that was Shimakaze in a nutshell. Sometimes clumsy, sometimes reckless, but always lovable. And our time together had only just begun.

sequence:
Submarine Subterfuge!

<size=45>Chapter 1: Morning Surprise</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
I had gone through my morning routine and was right outside the door to my office. It seemed like it was going to be a normal morning.
Opening the door and stepping into the office, I heard all manner of different clinks, clanks, and ticks radiating from somewhere.
Listening closely, I assessed that they were coming from the back.
I scanned the place to get an idea of what might be making the noises, but I couldn't spot anything unusual.
Okay, let's stop and think for a moment. Remember yesterday...
Hey, by the way, I've left a little surprise somewhere in your office~!
Hehehe! Believe me when I say it'll be a bucket of laughs when you find it!
A surprise? What kind of "surprise"?
All of a sudden, something on one of the shelves made a clicking sound.
It came from a stuffed animal that had fallen on its back. That wasn't there yesterday.
Squatting to pick up and inspect the toy, I quickly realized its purpose...
This was no ordinary stuffed animal... it was the trigger for a trap!
Whiiish! Plonk! Splasssh!
A bucket of water that had been left on the topmost shelf was knocked forwards, splashing its contents over my head and shoulders.
Good morning, Commander!
Albacore appeared out of the blue with a towel in one hand and a mop in the other.
I've named this device the "Morning Dew Wake-Up Call"! Based on your reaction, it did its job! Hehehe~!
A lot of thought went into the delivery method and the trigger mechanism to make sure only your head gets drenched! Everything went according to my plan!
That little brat! I should've known!
I swear I'll find one of her weaknesses and get my payback, one way or another!

sequence:
Submarine Subterfuge!

<size=45>Chapter 2: Gato Do Your Stretches!</size>

scripts.say: Port - Exercise Area
I went to the exercise area to observe the submarines as they were practicing.
One, two! Arms, legs, shoulders, too!
One, two! Arms, legs, shoulders, too!
Three, four! Hips, back, stretch some more!
Three, four! Hips, back, stretch some more!
Five, six! Fingers, toes, that does the trick!
Five... six! Fingers, toes, that does the trick!
It seemed that they were doing warmup stretches before going underwater.
And let's not forget to stretch our backs!
Repeat! Lean back, lean forward! Back, forward...
That should do it for warmups! Everyone ready?
Sure am! I'm warmed up and ready to go!
Let's start already...
Hey, wait a minute... Where's U-47?
Not here, she's a lone wolf! She's basically all on her own both on and off duty, y'know?
Huh. Well then...
I'll just have to convince her to come with us next time!
I doubt... that's going to work...
I can make anything work! If I can't convince her to come, then my name isn't Albacore!
Albacore was brimming with confidence. She really did seem like she could do anything.
I suppose self-confidence would also explain why she was teaching everyone her strange stretches just earlier.
She only came to port a while ago, yet she had made friends with almost all the submarines here already.

sequence:
Submarine Subterfuge!

<size=45>Chapter 3: Dorm Gaming Session</size>

scripts.say: Port - Dormitory
I'll wale on it...
No, Laffey! It's enraged!
... Huh?
Bah, carted again! I'm getting tired of this stupid monster!
Albacore was in the Dormitory, sitting around a console with a few others. Apparently, they were playing a video game.
You can't dodge those swipes! It's so unfair!
I guess we've met our match if we can't beat it even with my next-level skills... gg, Monster Puncher!
It's not over yet.
I think I've figured out most of its moveset! If we stick together and work as a team, we can beat it!
Let's give it another try! I'll give orders, so everyone just do what I say!
Hey, yeah! With Albacore giving orders, we might stand a chance! She's got that charismatic leader thing going on!
Yeah...
She SOUNDS confident, that's for sure...
All right, let's do this. Begin quest!
30 minutes later...
It's down and nearly dead! Everyone, wale on it with all you've got!
Okay! HYAAAAAH!!
We defeated it... finally...
YEEEEEEESSSS!! WE FRICKING DID IT!!
We beat it... And we didn't even have to look up how to cheese it!
Hahah, it was easy peasy! No boss stands a chance to Hardcore Albacore!
Albacore seemed to be having a lot of fun.
It was good to know that she's on friendly terms with everyone... but my search for a weakness to exploit was going nowhere!

sequence:
Submarine Subterfuge!

<size=45>Chapter 4: A Deal With The Devil</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
I had been observing Albacore for a few days and learned that she hadn't been pranking anyone. On the contrary: she had made friends with everyone she'd met.
At least it was relieving to know that this wasn't an HR problem.
Commander!
Hey, umm, I was wondering something! Can I ask you a question?
She spoke to me in a strange, childish tone.
I have a bad feeling about this. What is this cheeky little prankster planning?
Well, what I was wondering is... have you been stalking me lately, Commander?
Well, well, I thought as much!
C'mon, Commander~ I know a liar when I hear one!
Though I tried to deny it, Albacore knew that I had been spying on her.
Gee~ Imagine if I were to tell everyone about this~

"Hmph! I knew the Commander was a pervert all along!" – "H-how could a student of mine turn out this way?! Why would the Commander go after someone so y-young..." – "Oh, Commander, you leave me no choice but to cut you up into tiny little pieces..."
Albacore was mimicking the voices of some of her friends.
Well, Commander? Aren't you going to say the magic words?
I see, I see... So, stalking stuff aside, you were just worried about HR, eh?
All right, let's make a deal: you do me two favors, and I'll forget this ever happened!
For the first favor... I'm feeling kinda tired, and I wanna sleep on your lap for the whole afternoon. That should charge my batteries back to full!
The second favor I'll save for later! Once I come up with something, I'll let you know! Hehehe~
... Hm? You've got work this evening? Well, that's... too bad for you, then! I'm getting my beauty sleep!
Once it was all said and done and I'd finished my work, my legs had gone numb and I couldn't move for some time...

sequence:
Submarine Subterfuge!

<size=45>Chapter 5: Sea for Two Pt. 1</size>

scripts.say: Port - Beach
Hey, I've got an idea for the second favor!
I'm gonna go to the beach tomorrow, and I thought it'd be nice if you'd play with me then!
Although I had little say in the matter, Albacore and I went to the beach in the afternoon.
Guess we have the beach all to ourselves! Hehehe~ So, what "stimulating" activity should we do first, Com-man-der♡
Really? Just a dip in the ocean? Not what I had in mind, but okay.

options.content: Suggest making it a race to that uninhabited island

scripts.say: That's better!
I'm putting my spotless record on the line for this! You're on, Commander!
"Say a snazzy line before a race" – scratch that one from the bucket list!
Splasssh!
"Secure a flashy head start" – scratch that one as well! See ya at the finish line!
Without waiting for my response, Albacore jumped straight into the ocean and swam off.
Believe it or not, but I managed to swim all the way to the island. However, I couldn't find any traces of Albacore.
Which means I win. Haha! Who's the sucker now?
Surpriiiiiiiise!
Ahahahah! Scared you, didn't I?
Well, you tried, but I got here way ahead of you. I win!
... The first lap, anyway. It's time for the second! Go!
Albacore dove into the water and swam off again.
I can't let her beat me twice! This time, I need to win...!

sequence:
Submarine Subterfuge!

<size=45>Chapter 6: Sea for Two Pt. 2</size>

scripts.say: Before we knew it, the sun had begun to set and the skies had turned an orangish-red.
Final score's 10 to me, 0 to you~ You'd need a lifetime of training or blind luck to beat me~
Gotta say though, I'm dead tired now... *Pant*...
I was resting in the soft sand where the beach and the water meet. Albacore did the same and sat down next to me.
Boy, it's been long since I exerted myself this much.
When was the last time, even?
... Can't remember. Whatever.
You know, Commander, I had a ton of fun today! Consider the second favor all done!
You did...?
H-haha, hahaha! I-I mean, obviously! Everyone has fun when I'm around!
Hah, what did I just say? I mean really, that was dumb.
I blame it on you blurting that out of nowhere, Commander! You made the mood turn weird!
Albacore suddenly stood up and went into the sea, then she started splashing seawater at me.
Take THAT! And THIS!
Ahaha! Now, THIS is what I call making waves!
Albacore and I stuck around until sunset, playing by the beach.

sequence:
Submarine Subterfuge!

<size=45>Good Night! Good Morning!</size>

scripts.say: Port - Private Quarters
Tired after having spent half the day at the beach, I swiftly went to bed once I'd returned to the port.
My rest was disturbed by somebody poking my face.
(Whispering) Commander, are you asleep?
That voice... It must be Albacore.
Are you really? Or are you just faking your z's?
... Welp, guess you really are asleep. Makes sense, given today.
Listen... there's a lot I want to say.
First of all: thank you. I know I basically forced you into doing those favors for me, but still. And hearing you say you had a lot of fun made me really, really happy.
I'm also grateful to be part of this fleet. Everyone's so nice and easy to make friends with. We practice together, chat, play games... Every day is just so much fun.
One day, maybe... just maybe, I'll be diving and firing my torpedoes not to sink an enemy into the abyss, but to startle my friends for a laugh...
I believe that day will come. Maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, but someday it will.
... What I'm trying to say is: I love my friends and all the memories I've made here.
And, although I tease and mess with you all the time, the truth is...
Albacore leaned in closer to whisper into my ear.
... I love you.
Also, I might have a surprise for you tomorrow♪ Here I am, going through the effort of telling you these nice things, and you just pretend to be asleep. So I'm gonna have a little payback, hehehe♪
The next day...
I-is it true, Commander?! Did you really spend the night sleeping in the same room as Albacore?!
What does "sleeping in the same room" mean exactly, Commander?
Commander, I can tolerate many things, but even I draw a line somewhere!
The Commander might be into little girls...
Albacore sure knows how to twist a story...
In the end, I had to spend half the day clearing up this misunderstanding.
It was stressful, but it was fun, too. I'm sure I have many days like this ahead of me with Albacore by my side.

sequence:
The Big Shot's Proclamation

<size=45>A Remarkable Calling Card</size>

scripts.say: It was a sweltering summer afternoon. The temperature outside was rising, but at least a cool breeze circulated through the office.
*yaaawn*... Perfect day for paperwork, if nothing else.
But just as I'm about to put my nose to the grindstone and start going through documents, I hear a loud crashing sound, followed by the tapping of swift footsteps approaching from the hallway.
Commander! Commander! It's a disaster!

The doors to my office are thrown open with a loud bang, and a frantic-looking Amatsukaze rushes right up to my desk and slams an envelope decorated with gold glitter and a red ribbon down in front of me.
Look at what I found on Shimakaze's desk!
It's a calling card, no doubt!
A calling card?
Yes! I went to Shimakaze's room, but she wasn't there!
Instead I found this, which means she must have been kidnapped! And this letter proves it!
Wait, what?
Erm, maybe she just stepped out to do something?
Unthinkable! I would know if she was out doing an errand! Err, I mean, umm... ahem!
Anyway! Commander! We need to do something! She's clearly been kidnapped!
Look at the glitter and the intricate design of this wax seal, not to mention the ribbon... This is not something Shimakaze would be able to put together on her own!
......You do have a point.
(It's fancy and ostentatious, almost to the point of gaudiness... The design is also unmistakably Sakuran, which can only mean...)
This is definitely a calling card left behind by the villain that kidnapped Shimakaze!
And this villain must be a big shot with an exquisite sense of aesthetics!
Amatsukaze. People usually send calling cards BEFORE the crime happens.
O-oh, I see...
Ahem! I was simply so preoccupied with Shimakaze's safety that I must have chosen my wording poorly!
Commander, we need to open this envelope and see what it's hiding!
Without even waiting for my answer, she produces a small knife from seemingly thin air and carefully peels off the wax seal making sure not to break it.
Heheh. This seal is truly a work of art~
See?! Shimakaze has indeed been kidnapped!
The letter, sprinkled with gold glitter and smelling of incense, contains a simple message.

sequence: I have taken Shimakaze. If you want to see her again safe and sound come to the back of the old warehouse! And come alone, or else!!!

scripts.say: That's three exclamation marks... They must be really serious about me going alone.
They're clearly no ordinary kidnapper. This must be a truly remarkable big shot with impeccable taste!
...Right, I'm sure they are. In any case, this looks pretty serious. I need you to wait in the office while I go take care of this.
Wait! It's too dangerous for you to do it alone! I'll accompany you!
But the letter said to go alone. We'd be putting Shimakaze in danger.
It's fine! I'm a shipgirl, after all!
Somehow, I don't think that's enough... If we're going to do this, we should call for some more backup...
Ahh, that's no good! I need to be the only one involved!
Otherwise, uh... Erm! This big shot with impeccable taste will take offence, and Shimakaze will be in dire danger! Oh, boo hoo!
(Are those crocodile tears?)
(Oh, well. She's putting in a lot of work acting this out. I might as well see what she's trying to do here.)
Okay, you're right. If Shimakaze's really at the mercy of the big shot with impeccable taste, we need to follow their commands for now.
Yes, exactly!
Oh, well. It'll have to be just the two of us on a rescue mission, then.
And there's not much that can stand in our way with the great Amatsukaze on our side, I'd say.
Naturally! I'll do my utmost to help Shimakaze!
Let us go, Commander! We have work to do!

sequence:
The Big Shot's Proclamation

<size=45>The First Gatekeeper</size>

scripts.say: Thanks to Amatsukaze's guidance, we made it to the old port warehouse the letter referred to.
The place should have been deserted, but for some reason we find the entrance decorated with a few wind chimes clinking lazily in the sea breeze.
From the looks of it... this big shot has set up many traps and trials to confound us inside of this warehouse.
Keep close to me at all times. We are not to separate once inside.
She takes a deep breath and slowly opens the heavy iron door.
Ahem! Amatsukaze and the Commander steel themselves and open the first door! The refreshing sound of wind chimes heralds their encounter with the first gatekeeper in spectacular fashion!

options.content: This feels a bit too on-the-nose...

scripts.say: Heh! Hahah! So you've finally come! I was about to assume you had left your comrade to fend for herself!
Shimakaze, who was supposed to have been kidnapped, stands before us on an elevated platform, doing her best impression of a baddie.
You... You must be one of the cronies of that mysterious, remarkable big shot of impeccable taste!
Where did you take Shimakaze, oh accursed gatekeeper barring our way?!
Y-you may rest easy! She is quite safe! Yes, verily!
All I want to do with you two is play a simple game.
Listen now! Behind me are three sets of doors and statues! And...
Amatsukaze, blow those doors away so we can proceed to the next area. We'll break through with overwhelming firepower.
- Huh?! - Excuse me?
I get it now. You want to play a puzzle game, don't you?
Y-yes, actually.
And inside the statues there must be hidden keys for each of the doors.
We need to solve whatever puzzles or riddles you set up to get the keys and open the doors and reach the place where Shimakaze is being held, right?
Impressive! You're quick on the uptake, Commander!
But if the goal is to just open the doors, we don't need to solve any puzzles, do we? We can just blow them away, can't we?
I didn't spend all night thinking up puzzles for you to... Err, no!
If we do that, our mysterious and remarkably tasteful big shot will be upset and Shimakaze's life will be in danger!
She glances at the first gatekeeper.
E-exactly! If you don't follow the rules and play along, Shimakaze won't live to tell the tale!
Okay, First Gatekeeper! Loath am I to acquiesce to your whims, but give us your first question!
Question?! Err, I...
It's very clear she's reading from a list of "backup quiz questions" if my lip reading is right.
Amatsukaze remains silent, but she also seems to mouth "They're expensive! Don't break them!"
*sigh*... Okay, give us the question.
Ahem! Here's your first question!
"Though autumn has not yet made itself known, the..." Now, complete the verse.
That's actually not as bad as I was expecting.
(Maybe it's a Sakuran poem?)
If you find the question too hard, there's a backup question too!
And what's that one?
Allow me... What is the cutest aspect of the great Amatsukaze?
Huh?
Go on, answer~

options.content: I'd rather answer the first question.

scripts.say: I'd rather answer the first question, actually...
"Though autumn has not yet made itself known, the northerly winds herald its arrival."
- Huh?! - Oh...
Th-that's right! You're absolutely right! You truly understand me!
I'll answer the second question, then.
The first thing that comes to mind is how cute your assertive and electrifying personality is. Also...
Five minutes later...
- C-Commander... - Woah...
Aww... Commander, you really do understand me!
The imposing door before us opens, revealing our next objective.
Rejoice, for you have overcome the first trial!

sequence:
The Big Shot's Proclamation

<size=45>The Second Gatekeeper</size>

scripts.say: We go down a barely lit path and reach the back of the old warehouse. Unsurprisingly, there's another statue waiting for us there.
U-unbelievable! To think my comrade would be laid low, and you'd manage to penetrate our lair this far?!
First of all, I will warn you to not use brute force on this statue!
Now, let the mystery solving begin!
Is it just me, or do you sound exactly like the first gatekeeper?
Ugh... Well, I...
Th-that only means their organization has a strict code of conduct and style guides that all members must follow!
But never mind the trivial detail! Ah, you accursed gatekeeper! How you confound us!
What do we do, Commander?! Force is out of the question!
Because the statues are too expensive to break, right?
Indeed! You catch on quick, Commander. Amatsukaze spent a fortune to get Akashi to...
AHEM!!
What's wrong, Amatsukaze? Is your throat bothering you? The air quality in this warehouse might be getting to you!
I'm quite fine! Well, the air is pretty bad, but never mind that!
Commander, do you have any idea what the colored buttons on this statue might mean?
(Are we seriously doing this puzzle...?)
On closer inspection, the statue seems to be outfitted with dozens of buttons and levers of all sizes and shapes.
Apparently you're supposed to use them to change the statue's pose until it finally drops a key.
(This looks really complex and delicate. I guess it makes sense that they don't want this to get damaged.)
(But it'd probably take us a few hours to solve this thing.)
(Are they really gonna just sit for hours and watch me do this?)

options.content: Can I get a quiz instead?

scripts.say: Huh? How did you know we prepared a backup quiz for this too?
So you do, huh?
Heheh! I have it on good authority that our devilishly well dressed villain figured the statue's mechanisms were simply too baffling, so they're being considerate of you.
Very well, Commander. Here's your question.
This time you'll have to answer two questions!
Huh?
Every. Single. Question!
R-right, I almost forgot! You need to answer both questions correctly this time around.
Okay, here goes the first. "When the autumn wind blows, the grasses and trees wither. Now..." Now, you must complete the final verse.
And your second question is this... What do you like the most about the great Amatsukaze's style?
You must answer quickly, Commander!
(Amatsukaze's eyes are literally sparkling. She's just stealing the gatekeeper's job at this point.)
After doing some thinking, the answer finally comes to me.
Okay, for the first question. When the autumn wind blows, the grasses and trees wither. Now I understand why a wind from the mountains is called a storm.
Marvelous! Heheh, I chose two poems about wind for this occasion. Pretty clever, isn't it?
...You chose the questions?
Ahem! No, actually! It was clearly that remarkably stylish big shot of mystery! They're truly something, aren't they? Ahahah!
Next question! Let's go!
As for the second... If I must point out something about your style, then I probably would start with the gorgeous embroidery on your dress. And then...
Five minutes later...
With an audible click, the door opens.
Out of the corner of my eye, I see Amatsukaze pulling a golden lever on the statue.
(Oh, so it wasn't as complicated as it looked? Now I feel kind of stupid.)
You truly understand everything about me!
Aah, I'm so happy! Our mysterious villain with great aesthetic sense must be incredibly happy too!
Shimakaze should be safe with this stellar performance!
R-right! I actually just got a message from the remarkable kidnapper with incredible taste!
They're very pleased with your answering skills, and Shimakaze will be temporarily safe after your stellar performance!
...Right.
H-however, you're not out of the woods just yet!
When you encounter "them," you'll realize that the only thing in your future is bitter defeat!
And so, the second gatekeeper vanishes into the darkness beyond the second door at super high speed.
Wonder if there'll be a third gatekeeper.
...Is it that transparent?
Ermm! Well, who knows! We might be about to come face-to-face with this stylish and dashing big shot of mystery!
Commander, let's press on!

sequence:
The Big Shot's Proclamation

<size=45>The Big Shot's True Identity</size>

scripts.say: And so, we arrive at the very end of the old warehouse.
Inside, we find Shimakaze sitting in a chair, loosely wrapped in a glittery red ribbon.
Commander, you've finally made it...
Erm, Shimakaze?
Yes! It's me, Shimakaze!

options.content: We're here to save you. Sit tight.

scripts.say: We're here to save you. Sit tight.
I'm so grateful, Commander...
Where's the third gatekeeper?
There was a change of plans, and...
Err, no, I don't know a thing!
After I remove the ribbon wrapped around Shimakaze, a lock clicks behind us.
Not so fast, Commander!

I turn around to face the (not) mysterious voice, and see Amatsukaze standing menacingly on top of a stack of wooden boxes, with her hands planted confidently on her hips and looking down at me with a smug smile on her face.
I think it's high time for me to reveal the truth. There was no mysterious big shot to begin with. And no one kidnapped Shimakaze to begin with!
The letter and all these devious puzzles and machinations were all carefully designed traps to lure you here!
...So that means you were behind all of this the whole time?
Ahahah! Surprised, are you? The mysterious big shot with impeccably exquisite taste was none other than me all along!
And now you're my prisoner!
After preparing things so thoroughly, it'd be a huge failure on my part if I wasn't able to catch you!
Amatsukaze leaps from the precarious stack of boxes and gracefully ties the ribbon that was wrapped around Shimakaze around my wrist.
And then she ties the other end of it to her wrist.
Heheh, what do you think? How's that for a grand entrance?
Much cooler than a mere "hello," if I must say so myself. Wouldn't you agree?
Anyway! You're a prisoner now! MY prisoner!
So from now on, you're not allowed to go anywhere! All you need to do is stay by my side! Forever and ever!
...Oh, okay.
After hearing that, my initial guess is proven correct.
But then, I feel someone give my sleeve a gentle tug.
I'm so sorry, Commander...
Amatsukaze said she would teach me the secret to running faster if I helped her.
Hey! We promised, remember? We're both sharing Commander!
And you're my gatekeeper! Don't start flaking out on me now!
Ah... Yes... You did mention something like that, heheh...
Very well. Now that you're my prisoner forever, do you have something to say?
If not! I'll just take that as your tacit agreement to do whatever we say for eternity♪
Seeing the satisfied grin on her face and Shimakaze fidgeting nervously, I can't help but smile and shake my head.
Evidence forgery, perjury, unauthorized modifications to a port facility, and kidnapping the Commander.
Hey, what are you muttering about now? That sounds a little like an accusation, so could you please stop?
I ignore her and simply raise my hand. Then I snap my fingers.
A cavalcade of footsteps can be heard approaching the dim warehouse.

sequence:
The Big Shot's Proclamation

<size=45>Ever at Your Side</size>

scripts.say: Listen very well! You are surrounded right now!
Heheh, to think someone would be bold enough to kidnap the Commander. I'll commend your bravery, at least.
Drop your weapons and surrender right now!
Commander, I swear I didn't know anything about this, nya!
We're enveloped in smoke, and then, the locked door bursts open just as a huge hole is blown in the warehouse wall.
The team I had standing by outside rushes in all at once, untying the ribbon around my wrist in a matter of seconds.
Sorry to keep you waiting, Commander!
No worries. That was amazing work. Thanks, everyone.
Once the smoke clears, the outcome of the short skirmish is immediately apparent.
B-but why?
How did you all know we were here?!
Amatsukaze is clearly perplexed by the turn of events.
My communicator was on this whole time, actually.
I was careless... That lone oversight did me in!
My perfect and flawless plan, ruined and marred by the smallest, most foolish mistake...
Why are you all looking at me like that?
Amatsukaze. I was suspicious the moment you brought me that calling card.
The glitter on it was the same kind you use on your room's walls, and the red ribbon and the wind chimes at the entrance of the warehouse are all stuff I've seen in your room before.
Y-you... You realized and you let me make a fool out of myself?! You huge dummy!
Well, uh, I just saw how much effort you put into all this. I would have felt bad if I didn't go along with it.
But you do need to take responsibility for remodeling the warehouse without permission and causing trouble.
We could have you prepare a tea party. Everyone here is invited.
Hmph! Is that all? You'll hear no complaints from me, of course!
May I assume you'll be attending this tea party as well, Commander?
Of course. I'm looking forward to it already.
W-well, seeing such enthusiasm, I'll have to make it a most remarkable tea party!
It doesn't take long for her to get her composure back.
Well, uh, if we're all done here, I should really get going...
Shimakaze, you're gonna help Amatsukaze with the tea party. You're an accomplice, and you're not getting away with just looking sorry.
Understood!
Heheh. Shimakaze, take notes. We'll procure the best ingredients from the best shop in the port!
This is my proclamation – everyone shall know of Amatsukaze's impeccable taste!

sequence: The Big Shot's Proclamation - The End

scripts.say: Port - Commander's Office
*knock knock*
Commander, we've received an urgent message from a Virtual Tower monitoring site.
They said active signals were detected again from the Tower about 30 minutes ago, and the surrounding 150 nautical miles all became enveloped in a space-time anomaly.
We'd adjusted the position of our monitoring station in advance based on what happened last time. Unfortunately, the area affected this time is pretty massive...
As a result, many monitoring sites and patrol fleets were caught inside the anomaly.
Furthermore, we believe that visitors from another world will appear again, based on our previous experiences.
Owing to the unprecedented scale of this occurrence, TB's assessment is that there is extreme danger involved, with a risk of significant damage to third parties.
So the Virtual Tower's acting up again, and it's bigger than ever this time...
Those monitoring sites constitute a part of our periphery defenses, so we need to treat this incident as an attack on the port.
I'll issue a grade III– Actually, a grade II alert.
Get the strategy department to come up with a response immediately, and commence reconnaissance over sector one. Tell all our fleets to be ready for combat within an hour.
Also, tell Enterprise to come see me. I'll personally command this battle.
Roger!
Ugh... My communicator isn't broken, but it's just not working.
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Three - Somewhere Else

scripts.say: What a surprise. No one could have seen this coming.
More pertinently, someone has been following us for a while now. Did you notice that?
Huh? You serious? Come on, now's not the time for ghost stories!
That is correct.
Eeeeek! Someone's there!
You referred to those machine life-forms you encountered as "Sirens."
As for you, you are "shipgirls." The equipment you wear is called a "rigging."
You caught on to me quite early, yet you still fed me information.
Why is that?
Because it would take too long if I explained it to you directly.
So, Miss Otherworldly Visitor, what should we call you?
I am Origami Tobiichi, former AST Master Sergeant.
Are you with the military? What is your rank and division?
We serve the port of the Azur Lane. Our rank, well... That would be difficult to explain indeed.
I see. Okay.
You just referred to me as an "otherworldly visitor." Should I take that to mean I'm in a world that's not my own?
I'd like to organize and share information with you.
Although this area isn't especially dangerous, we should preferably move to a shelter in a safer place.
Then we've got a common goal, Origami!
Whaddya say we work together, huh? I'm Z13, and this is Z2.
Z2 and Z13... Interesting names. They sound almost like codenames.
We're... Well, it's a long story.
I understand. I won't pry further.
I know close to nothing about this world, so your guidance would be appreciated. By all means, let us work together.
I know a nearby place that's safe. Come with me.
Hang on a sec. You say you know "close to nothing," but you SOUND like you know quite a hecking lot!
This place may be a warped imitation, but it's strangely familiar to me.
Take this building, for instance. It's where I lived before my world was rewritten.
Before it was REWRITTEN? Sounds like a huge deal, and you said it like it's nothing.
This visitor is certainly not just anyone, it seems. Show us the way, Miss Origami.
Origami, Z2, and Z13 went together around the fake Tengu City for a while.
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Three - Somewhere Else

scripts.say: They stopped at a shelter and made preparations, exchanged intel, and rehearsed rigging usage. As they were practicing, they eventually came across what appeared to be an enemy stronghold.
The moment they decided to investigate further, an airship came into their view.
What the– An airship?!
Well, I should've expected as much from a world you said got "rewritten."
Fraxinus...
It seems Kotori has already joined forces with your port.
Possibly thanks to Fraxinus AL's relaying, the adventure squad's long-unresponsive communicators finally came back online.
Seems like Origami went with a patrol fleet of yours and not only obtained tons of intel, but even figured out where the enemy's stronghold is.
Then it's obvious what we need to do next: Focus our forces and destroy the stronghold!
After a joint attack from Fraxinus AL, the Eagle Union, Iron Blood, and Sardegna, all the enemies in sector three were wiped out.
Kotori, when did you renovate Fraxinus?
It's not really a renovation... More like another thing entirely.
Call it "Fraxinus AL," if you would. Welcome, Origami. Glad to see you again safely.
Thanks, Kotori. You came just when we needed it
And thank you, Commander of the port.
My name is Origami Tobiichi. Former AST Master Sergeant, presently a high schooler – and also what they call a Spirit.
My skills should have some use here. I'd be happy to cooperate with you.
I look forward to fighting by your side.
Your Majesty, all our forces have led their fleets into combat positions.
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Four - Fleet Rendezvous Point

scripts.say: The Royal Maids' main force has also set off with its respective fleets.
Excellent. George, since my servant places high importance on this battle, I shall head to the front and command directly. I entrust you with our base and reserve forces.
As you wish.
Lion, while you won't be fighting on the front lines this time, your task of search and rescue is equally important.
You'll be looking for Jervis, Janus, and a blue-haired girl who controls a puppet. If my memory serves me right, her name is Yoshino, and her nickname is "Hermit."
She sounds like a powerful one. Quite unlike what I heard about her – that she loathes fighting because she doesn't want to cause harm.
Well, perhaps this is but a preconception.
At any rate, they are in your hands. Bring them back in one piece.
Understood. I promise that I will find them.
Now, ladies of the Northern Parliament, I believe it'd be most efficient if we split up and worked separately.
The Royal Navy shall concentrate on sweeping the whole area. You, meanwhile, can focus on capturing strongholds. How does that sound?
I have no objections.
This entire incident was clearly instigated by the Sirens.
I thought they'd finally learned after our years of beating them down, but it seems they're still scheming in the shadows.
Whatever it is they're planning, they won't get away with it!
That's the spirit! Bel, Vanguard, time to get going.
Let us reconvene once victory is ours.
KABOOOM!
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Four - Somewhere Else

scripts.say: "Ugghh! These guys are more annoying than the AST! We've beaten sooo many, but they just keep coming!"
I need... to hide somewhere...
"Whoa! There's a shopping mall right over there that'd be perfect! Let's go there and hide, Yoshino!"
...Okay.
Under the cover of several shells going off, the girl and her puppet snuck into the mall.
"Geesh! These guys just attack you for no reason whatsoever! Yoshino, you hurt?"
The girl faced the trembling hand puppet and shook her head, but then frowned slightly.
Excuse me... Are you injured?
Whuah?!
"Oh nooo! This place was packed after all, huh?"
Th-that's not strictly... Um, well...
*sigh*... Janus, let me do the talking.
I'm Jervis, and this is Janus. I'm guessing you ended up here through some happenstance, just as we did.
Janus noticed you were hurt, so she came up to treat you.
"Well, well! Seems silly Yoshinon mistook you two cuties for enemies! Sorry!"
I'm... sorry.
"Yoshinon is Yoshinon, and this is Yoshino."
"Alright, little Janus, think you could tend to Yoshino?"
Um, of course! I can do that! Yoshino, let me see your wounds.
O-okay... Please be gentle.
"Okaaay, where to begin... Ah, right! Jervis, do you know where we are?"
I can't say for certain, but considering everything that's happened so far, we're probably in a Mirror Sea – one of the Sirens' test sites.
Oh, and to be brief, "Sirens" essentially refers to those things outside who attack anyone they see.
That reminds me... Based on what I've heard from people before, what's happening here sounds a bit like another case of visitors from another world.
"Ahh! So basically, we're those visitors that little Janus just mentioned!"
So... we're in another world...
"This place does look a lot like Tengu City, but when you look really closely, some things are a little different."
It's like someone made the city from an assortment of buildings...
Supposing you are from another world, then there's a high probability that this city is a recreation of Tengu City that the Sirens made with data from your world.
Okay, I've disinfected your wounds and put bandages on them.
"Whoooa! Thanks a bunch, little Janus! Yoshino, what's the magic word?"
Th-thank you...
"That's a good girl! Okay, so what are you two cuties going to do now?"
Um, Yoshinon, if this place does resemble Tengu City, do you happen to know your way around?
"Hmm... It just feels familiar. I might know the general way around."
That's more than enough. At least we won't waste time getting lost.
Based on our previous experiences, the Sirens always have a central unit in command. We should try to find it before the reinforcements from the port get here.
That way, we'll be able to neutralise the Sirens at the same time as they arrive, and we'll be able to leave the Mirror Sea.
"Hooray! Alrighty, then I'll show ya around as best as I can! You better, too, Yoshino!"
I-I'll... try!
Yoshino, Jervis, and Janus went and waited in a safe area in the fake Tengu City for a while.
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Four - Somewhere Else

scripts.say: To be precise, Yoshinon discovered the enemy's stronghold while the group was on the way to the safe area.
Having accomplished their most important mission, they then waited in safety for reinforcements to arrive.
Eventually, an airship came into view outside the window.
"Well, I'll be! Ain't that Kotori's airship?"
...Fraxinus!
Possibly thanks to Fraxinus AL's relaying, the patrol squad's long-unresponsive communicators finally came back online.
At any rate, learning that Yoshino and the two patrollers are safe and sound is the best we could ask for.
You can even say luck is on our side, seeing as they managed to find the enemy's key base in this area.
Yeah. Their safety is the most important of all.
As for the Sirens' base, we'll take our time dealing with it next.
After a joint attack from Fraxinus AL, the Eagle Union, the Royal Navy, and the Northern Parliament, all the enemies in sector four were wiped out.
"I'm baaack! Aaand...?"
Oh... Um...
I... I'm... also back...
Alright, Yoshinon, that's enough teasing her. Welcome back, both of you.
"I'm sooo glad to see you in one piece, Kotori!"
"And who might this be, hmm? The Commander? You've got a heckin' unique vibe, that's for sure!"
"Pleasure to meet ya!"
I'm, um... M-my name is Yoshino... And this is Yoshinon.
I-it's... a pleasure to meet you.
Ladies, the Commander has finally issued the order for an all-out attack. Are all your respective tasks proceeding as planned?
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Five - Fleet Rendezvous Point

scripts.say: But of course. My fleet will shoulder the eastern flank.
Hakuhou and I shall handle the matter in the east-southeast.
The southeast is mine. Shinano, can I entrust you with the south?
Verily.
Then that leaves the south-southeast. May Kaga and I take that?
Amagi dearest, you ought to stay with Lady Nagato in the back. You need only sit and wait for good news from us.
We know scarcely anything about our foes. You mustn't let your guard down.
You needn't worry, Lady Nagato. I've sent out recon planes to scout ahead.
Speaking of which, have you caught wind of Ikazuchi and Inazuma?
Not yet. I'm still looking for them and the last two Spirits.
Our intel says that they fight by commanding the wind. I thought this would've made it a cinch to find them...
Sadly, as there is abnormal weather affecting this area, I've failed to do so.
That's no cause for concern, though, is it? Ikazuchi and Inazuma are clever. They know how to stay out of trouble.
Indeed. I believe it is implausible that they'd put themselves in danger.
I worry not about them, but something else.
In any event, we must rescue them from this anomalous space-time environ as soon as possible.
Of course. Everyone, please make it your top priority to look for the missing persons during the mission.
Should you find them, report it at once. I shall personally handle things.
As you say, dear sister.
Miss Gouden Leeuw, I'd be delighted to have your fleet's cooperation when the time comes.
