You shall have it. Given our limited forces, it only makes sense that you Sakurans take the spotlight in this case.
Be aware that communications are unreliable within the area. I implore you all to act reasonably and put safety above all else.
That should be all. Sakurans, set forth!
"Bind."
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Five - Somewhere Else

scripts.say: Penetrate!
WHOOOSH!
The ferocious winds whipped up intense waves that swallowed several mass-produced Sirens unable to get out of the way.
Good heavens, they just keep coming! There's no end to them!
"Confirmation. The enemy seems to be growing in numbers. It must be because you're being too flashy."
So it's MY fault? You're enjoying yourself too, you know!
"Affirmative. It was you who proposed a challenge to see who could defeat the most enemies, Kaguya."
Err... Okay, but seriously – there are too damn many of them!
So that's "Berserk"... They really fight like they're telepathic.
Even so, they won't get anywhere if they keep fighting aimlessly like this.
True. Cut one enemy down, two take its place.
We should back them up.
KABOOOM!
The two mysterious girls suddenly burst onto the fierce battlefield.
Hey, Yamai twins, over here!
The situation is dire. You should retreat.
Huh?! You know who we are?!
"Question. I do not recognize you. Are you acquaintances of Kaguya's?"
Uh, pretty sure I don't know 'em...
Strangers, are you Ratatoskr's reinforcements? Or do you serve the AST?
I went and got dressed and even covered up my gear, and they still think I'm somebody else...
That's to be expected. They can't have imagined they'd encounter someone from another world.
...Another world? So... You, unfamiliar ones, come from a world beyond our own?!
"Shock. I can't believe my ears."
No, it's the other way around... You're visitors from beyond OUR world.
Here, in our world, we call those such as you "otherworldly visitors."
Anyway, I'm Ikazuchi, type III Akatsuki-class destroyer number three. This is my sister, Inazuma, fourth in our class.
Welcome, Spirits Kaguya Yamai and Yuzuru Yamai, to the world of Azur Lane.
KABOOOM!
Oh crap! The Type IV Sirens' chain-hunting system has been triggered! They're closing in on us!
There's no time to stand around and chat. Just trust us.
We'll show you to someplace safe!
...You think we should trust them, Yuzuru?
"Considering. I conclude that we should prioritize escaping from this encirclement."
Yeah, figures! Could be a trap, but we'll think about that after we've broken out of here!
The Yamai sisters, Ikazuchi, and Inazuma went together around the fake Tengu City for a while.
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Five - Somewhere Else

scripts.say: They found a safe zone and came up with a plan to secretly disrupt the enemy, and then raided a number of Siren supply points.
With Ikazuchi's and Inazuma's help, the Yamai sisters were able to upgrade their riggings using the supplies they captured.
With this newfound strength, they were keen to destroy the Sirens' central base, which held even more supplies.
It was at that moment that an airship came into their view.
Behold! A giant ship that sails amongst the heavens! Its name, why, it's Fraxinus!
Get ready!
We're going to get extracted.
Possibly thanks to Fraxinus AL's relaying, the adventure squad's long-unresponsive communicators finally came back online.
Commander, Kaguya and Yuzuru provided some intel on multiple crucial enemy areas. We can take them out in order.
Also, those other girls – Ikazuchi and Inazuma, right? They sure are... quirky.
Yeah. They have a habit of saying things that make no sense.
More pertinently, we're nursing a theory that this may be a space-time anomaly, or maybe a large-scale dimensional anomaly. Have you seen anything like it in your world?
I'm no expert on the subject, so I can't say I have. Kurumi, on the other hand, might have a unique take on it.
However, it doesn't seem like she got dragged into this, so we can't ask her. Next time I get the chance, I'll speak to her about it.
Thank you. I'll leave it to you.
KABOOOM!
Another Siren fleet is reduced to wreckage following an intense explosion.
Commander, this is now the third Type IV Siren fleet that's engaged us in a mere 30 minutes.
That's making me think the situation might be far worse than our recon suggested at first.
Indeed. Owing to the space-time anomaly's effects, this area isn't actually 100 nautical miles in size either.
We're not only up against their strongest Type IVs, but they're also densely packed together.
Whoever the visitors are this time, they're no ordinary bunch.
Commander, I just spotted something strange in the sky.
Judging by the footage... I think it's an airship.
An... airship?
Positional data verified. I've locked on to the target's signal.
Please hold off on the attack order, Commander. I have a feeling that the target isn't hostile.
I'm basing this off of the fact that they've already engaged quite a lot of Siren fleets.
Then it seems our new allies this time are aboard that airship, and moreover, it confirms my hunch that they're no ordinary bunch.
TB, try to get in touch with them.
And Enterprise, give them some backup at once.
Meanwhile...
KABOOOM!
Tsk... There's no end to these dang things!
I thought this Fraxinus dead ringer of a ship was all form over function, but these defenses and power systems are better than I expected.
Its firepower is nothing to scoff at, either.
But, having said that...
KABOOOM!
Why do I still have to fight with my own weapons?
*sigh*... These enemies remind me of the AST quite a bit, but they don't seem human. They're more like some sort of intelligent life-form.
Can only hope everyone else is okay...
BEEP BEEP!
Huh? Someone's calling me?
After a joint attack from Fraxinus AL, the Eagle Union, the Sakura Empire, and the Kingdom of Tulipa, all the enemies in sector five were wiped out.
It is an honor that we should meet, O one by the name of "Commander."
Mwahaha! We are the Children of Typhoon who raze everything! Kaguya Yamai, and...
"Concur. Yuzuru Yamai."
I thank you for aiding us. Let us henceforth stand side by side in battle!
"Concur. We'll teach our rude enemies a lesson."
The port's many fleets displayed an eye-opening performance in this battle, as of course did the Spirits.
This was despite their inability to flex their full power, possibly due to some negative effects of having crossed worlds.
Even so, perhaps partly owing to the power of their riggings, there was not a foe who could stop them. They had free rein over the battlefield.
And so, by their powers combined, they were able to clear out all the enemies in this stretch of the sea.
Whew... Our search and destroy was successful, and we managed to link back up with everyone. Glad everything worked out.
Now all that's left is finding a way to get home.
Hmm... Well, yeah, but I also wanna stick around and talk to some of the new friends I've made.
"Concur. Our shipgirl friends are very pleasant."
"Hey, it's aaall good. If we can return to our original world, it prooobably means we can return here, too! Right, Yoshino?"
...Yeah. That's true.
Well, I suppose that's– Hm? Tohka? Commander? What's the matter? You've got expressions like you're at a funeral.
Hrmh... I am getting a bad premonition.
Same here. Something just doesn't sit right with me.
Up to this point, any abnormal phenomena would start vanishing after we'd destroyed all the crucial Siren infrastructure.
This time, though, the readings on our measuring devices aren't going down one bit. In fact, they're unnaturally stable.
Exactly. It's as though it's building up to something dangerous.
Warning: High energy readings detected at the center of the area. Prepare for impact.
Wait, what?! Quick, everyone grab on to something!
BOOOM!
From the previously empty center of the area, a muddy-green shockwave suddenly burst out.
While Fraxinus AL's shields barely managed to withstand it, a chilling impact sound echoed throughout it.
Immediately after, the shockwave spread further and further, dyeing everything in its path a dark green.
What the hell... is that?
A new area appeared amidst all the ominous green.
Everything about this area seemed to defy the laws of physics and nature itself.
It was where the Virtual Tower was supposed to be – except now it had taken on a nightmarish appearance.
Memphis, I'm going to call this new place "sector six." Tell all fleets to start scouting it immediately.
Also, tell them not to go into it until further orders are given.
Roger!
Commander, since Fraxinus AL was able to defend against that shockwave, I think it may be able to enter the area.
I suggest we gather intel around the periphery before you send in your main fleets.
Good idea. We need to go see for ourselves what's out there.
Then we have a plan! Fraxinus AL, go forth!
At the edge of the labyrinth was a spatial distortion visible to the naked eye. A clear warning to not approach recklessly.
Kotori slowed her airship down to the absolute minimum limit, carefully proceeding while testing the shield's limits, scanning the outer peripheries of the labyrinth.
Hold on–– Kotori, zoom in on the top-left monitor.
Huh? Is that... Kurumi? Doesn't look like she's moving, either. Is she... dead?
Since she wasn't with us since the beginning, I thought for sure that she wouldn't get pulled into this...
I can't believe it... In a place like this...
The monitor undeniably showed the corpse of a young lady dressed in Gothic attire.
Is she... one of your friends?!
Damn it... We were too late... But still, we need to hurry up and take her back to the hospital at port!
Oh... I should've explained this earlier.
Memphis, and of course Commander. Don't worry, this is simply the corpse of one of Kurumi Tokisaki's clones. But of course, that doesn't mean not to worry at all.
The corpse... of a clone? I'll need you to fill me in on the specifics later, but for now, I'll assume it's just one of her abilities.
––But, the takeaway from this is that another one of your companions is caught up in this mess, and there's a high likelihood she's somewhere in sector six.
Mhm. Judging from the state of that body, she likely ran into something nasty.
"Hrmmm... I can't name many people who can push Kurumi to this extent."
I wonder... if she's okay...
Commander, we've received the strategy department's conclusion.

According to the recon report, the interior space is a maze even larger and more complex than it appears. However, all the recon planes and mass-produced ships sent inside were able to withdraw safely.
Therefore, we've been cleared to head inside for combat operations.
It should also be noted, however, that all the equipment placed within was subjected to some unknown interference.
According to the report, this interference only grows stronger the deeper inside you go.
Looks like our best bet is to split up again and make our way in?
I agree. Let's decide how to split up our forces and allocate roles before commencing.

On paper, we have the advantage when it comes to raw firepower. We'll have the main fleet sweep the enemy from the outer perimeter working inward, while the airship heads in with a small number of elite troops to rescue our allies.
Sounds good. Let's go with that.
Memphis, assemble a carrier fleet each from the Royal and Union forces, and a main fleet each from the Sakuran and Iron Blood forces.
Meanwhile, have the other fleets on standby and await the order to launch a full-scale offensive.
Roger!
While the main fleet launched its simultaneous offensive, the Fraxinus AL was struggling to navigate through the labyrinth.
Ugh... Didn't we already pass through here?
"Concur. This place looks familiar."
Hmm... I suppose blowing a hole through the wall and forcing our way through won't work either.
Commander, we're trying to map out the area, but after our recon planes fly out a certain distance in one direction, they simply return from the opposite direction.
Also... the terrain here seems to constantly be shifting... I'm still trying to assess how long our maps are good for.
Is the space-time anomaly getting worse?
Space-time anomaly... a distortion of time and space...
Could Kurumi be at the heart of this strange phenomenon...?
That's an interesting hypothesis. What makes you think that?
It is not a good idea to venture blindly into an unknown space.
In our case, we first discovered the body of Kurumi Tokisaki's clone before entering the labyrinth.
A corpse showing up in a random area we happened to scan over, immediately after the labyrinth appeared? It's way too convenient to be a coincidence.
Now that you mention it... So, you're saying she was trying to tell us something?
It's a possibility. The answer might become clearer if we can find more of her clones.
"Wooowee! You're such a quick thinker, Origami! Even during a toootally chaotic time like this!"
In that case... let's go look for Kurumi's other clones...
Once we decided on what exactly we were looking for, sure enough, Kurumi's clones started showing up with each turn of the labyrinth.
Each of her clones had been slain in battle, but their old-fashioned flintlocks were always pointed in the same direction – at where the next clone would be waiting.
While the gruesome path they showed us seemed to be the correct one, the space-time anomalies only grew more turbulent as we pushed deeper into the labyrinth.
The space before me split, splitting into multiple paths like the branches of a tree, making it difficult to see which way we were even going.
The labyrinth... is getting more and more convoluted.
Everyone, look over there! There seems to be some sort of video playing at each branch of the road!
Could those be...
The videos that played at each intersection seemed to represent different possibilities.
In one branch, everyone who came from the other world, Kurumi included, gathered in a large area without splitting up––
Only to be attacked by an entity that had been lying in wait the whole time.
Their powers depleted by the effects of crossing worlds and their riggings unusable, they were no match for the enemy, and were almost completely wiped out.
Is that... the DOS named Ordainer El?
Do you know the identity of that enemy?
Yeah. She's a special type of Siren, an extremely powerful one at that... I suspect she's the mastermind behind this incident.
Don't tell me... she's also gathering energy from nature to create Spirit-like powers...
And trying to grow even stronger by defeating us?!
We don't know what her intentions or motivations are. In the long history of our fight against the Sirens, she and her DOS units are a new threat that has only emerged recently.
...If she has that kind of power, it's no wonder that even Kurumi would be struggling.
We must rush to her aid immediately!
"Question. Which path do we take to do that?"
First of all, we should start by checking the videos at each branch.
At the second branch, Kotori did not attempt to break through, missing her opportunity to rendezvous with our port.
Afterwards, she rescues the Spirits that were stranded at sea herself, leading them into the labyrinth––
Only to never return again.
At the third branch, Kotori and I met up, but the situation was so turbulent that we could not decide on what to do, so we carefully investigated to see how the situation would develop.

However, as soon as we finished our investigation and decided to set out, the space-time anomaly erupted, vanishing in a violent explosion that took everything and everyone within it – including our patrol fleet.
At the fourth branch, we were able to reach the labyrinth just as we currently have, but weren't able to find the clues left behind by Kurumi.
We would continue to wander the labyrinth, ever more agitated, until we were engulfed in an explosion that seemed to collapse the very spatial fabric.
At the fifth branch, we were able to find Kurumi's clues, quickly moving forward by following their lead.
And then...
The video ends abruptly. The last thing I see is Kurumi's face on the screen, smiling as if she had seen the Fraxinus AL––
Her right hand curled into the gesture of holding a gun.
This is the way. We've got to hurry and back her up!
The Fraxinus AL breaks through the labyrinth and leaps forth into a vast space.
Unlike the complex, confined labyrinth that had surrounded us earlier, this place looked more like the theater of a large-scale conventional battle.
Heehee~ How nice of you to finally join me.
The girl clad in crimson and black runs freely through the Siren forces, creating one explosion after another, her hand waving gently through the air... as if greeting us.
Phew.... Looks like we made it in time.
Kotori, let's deploy our forces and prepare for surface combat.
We'll join in as well!
Let's show those Sirens what we're made of!
"Concur. Let's go wild."
"CHAAAAARGE! Let's wipe 'em all out!"
Y-yes...! Let's go!
Our furious offensive was starting to cause the massive Siren fleet to crumble.
After crossing through the smoke and haze, I finally came face-to-face with the final visitor from another world.
Now then, I suppose I should introduce myself. A pleasure to meet you – my name is Kurumi Tokisaki. And who might you be, brave Commander?
Nice meeting you, Kurumi. I'm {playername}, the leader of Azur Lane's port.
Kurumi, we made our way here following the clues you left us.
Mind explaining the situation to us? Seems like you still have ample breathing room to be your usual self.
Heehee... Is that how it looks to you? I'm actually in quite the rough spot here, you know?
Dear friends, what you see in front of you is only a small sliver of this endless battlefield.
Now, please allow me to reveal to you the true nature of this space––
*snap*
As soon as Kurumi snaps her fingers, the entire scenery around us changes.
We now find ourselves in the middle of a battlefield where two armies are clashing violently.
On one side is a countless number of Kurumi clones. On the other, an endless stream of Siren machines.
Severed limbs and shattered wreckages floated in a sea of flame, an imposing shadow looming on the distant horizon.
Now, you see this space for what it truly is.
Here... I have already been fighting for a long, long time. Had you arrived even a little later, we would have lost our chance to stop this terrifying monstrosity.
Heehee... But now that everyone's here at last, we can finally take down this accursed thing.
As you can see, it's been there this whole time... but for some reason, I am unable to touch it.
But, as you whittle down the enemy's forces, it seems to become more and more corporeal.
A pretty straightforward rule, wouldn't you say? Heehee.
Well, that's everything on my end. Now, if you'd please, I have an endless battle to attend to.
Now then, everyone, please make due haste.
KABOOOM!
Honey~♪ The Eagle Union Main Fleet is coming to your rescue~!
Hahah! The battle's heating up! We came at the perfect time!
Combat power sufficient. Commencing enemy annihilation!
KABOOOM!
*gasp*... Finally made it out of that bloody labyrinth...
The battle hangs on the precipice. We must join in immediately.
Your Queen orders you–– all hands, set sail!
KABOOOM!
Commander, the Kingdom of Tulipa has come to your aid!
It's not just a new Type IV fleet. They even have new DOS units... To think that the Sirens have amassed such power from fighting in the Virtual Tower...
Iron Blood, in formation. We charge forth!!
It's... over!
KABOOOM!
The surrounding Siren fleets could do nothing but disintegrate in the face of the overwhelming firepower of the Eagle Union's fleet. After that, we finally got to speak with the airship's owner.
You're packing a pretty solid punch yourselves.
I'm Kotori Itsuka, a commander of Ratatoskr. Thanks again for backing me up.
You must be the commander of this fleet. What do you want me to call you?
Since otherworldly visitors are frequent visitors to the port, we've created a manual for first-time encounters with them.
This, combined with the fact that she is a commander, allowed us to swiftly exchange information.
It's believed that the rigging you have equipped is something that the Virtual Tower created specifically for you when it "summoned" you.
This is probably some kind of auto-transfiguration. The gear itself is harmless, so don't be afraid to use it.
As for your airship, I suspect the reason it differs from the original is that it's a replica the Virtual Tower made.
Given its complicated structure, we should probably take it back to the port and give it a closer look.
I figured it was a replica. I suppose I'll call it Pseudo-Fraxinus, then.
Speaking of ships, surely this isn't your entire fleet. You did say you were going to sweep through this whole area.
And as it so happens, Commander, I've gotten separated from five of my friends. If it's not too much to ask, can you help me look for them?
You've gotten separated? Alright, we'll help.
Memphis, inform all the fleets about our search.
Understood.
Miss Kotori, you can breathe easy. Your friends aren't the only ones stranded here – many of ours are, too.
Several of our main fleets already have the area on full lockdown. They'll commence an attack as soon as they get news from their scouts.
Until then, your airship would be a huge asset to have if you can get it running properly.
"Several main fleets"... Sounds like you have more power than I imagined.
So then, what makes you so interested in my Pseudo-Fraxinus?
Honestly, it's because I've only seen airships like that in science fiction movies.
I see... And what do you know about Spirits?
Can't say I know what that means.
Interesting... Heh. Then you're in for a sight you'll never forget.
Because when you saw me fight earlier, I wasn't using my full power.
Well, glad we're on the same side, Commander!
KABOOOM!
*yaaawn*... I heard the rumors and all, but seeing things up close in person is somethin' else.
Meals must be eaten one bite at a time, enemies must be defeated one ship at a time... We have to find a way to break through into the battlefield.
Comrades, let us stand together and fight!
KABOOOM!
Ohohoho! Did you see that? Such is the might of Marco Polo!
Indeed! You're so very impressive! (*claps*)
Mwaha! I'll have you know, I've mastered far more impressive techniques! Allow me to display them against those enemies over there!
Of course! I shall gladly follow you!
Ack... Wait for me, Zuihouuu!
At last, the time has come to tip the scales of this endless war of attrition.
With most of the Siren forces decimated, the illusory DOS Ordainer gradually became more corporeal.
Turn to ashes and disappear!
"We're coming for you too! Reaaady?"
Y-yeah... take this!
Locked on–– Fire!
Raph–– ––"ael!"
SANDALPHON!!
It's over... It's finally over.
Well then, as much as I enjoyed my time here... I hope we never meet again.
*BANG*
Under the withering onslaught of the Spirits as well as the shipgirls, the gigantic figure slowly fizzles into the aether and disappears.
Commander, the spatial anomaly index is decreasing.
Conjecture: This space is about to collapse. Recommendation: Escape immediately.
Commander, did we do it? Did we win?
Yeah... But, I have a feeling this isn't the end.
From beginning to end, Ordainer El did nothing to intervene...
An enemy that solely relies on mass-produced ships, with no combat capabilities herself... I can't believe there would be a high-ranking Siren like this...
No... This time, it's truly over.
...So you weren't defeated after all.
Where exactly am I? And what are you planning?
Some things are simply preordained to happen.
We have no say in the matter; neither you, nor I.
All we can do is seek the most advantageous solution.
Your response this time was simply superior, and I look forward to the next time.
...What do you mean by "next time"?
Of course–– {playername}, do you know what it means to "ordain"?
As the space-time anomaly fades, the blue sea and sky regain their former appearance.
After confirming that the Virtual Tower was calm once more, I heightened its surveillance, then began to withdraw the fleets one by one.
The Spirits aboard the Fraxinus AL also stopped by the port, waiting for Akashi to find a way to send them back home.
The battle left much to think about, but that seems to always be the case when it comes to confrontations with high-level Sirens.
But at the end of the day, if she ever shows up again, I'll just beat her back to wherever she came from.
At least, this battle... is finally over.

sequence: ––DATE A LANE: THE END

scripts.say: A while passed. The Eagle Union's fleet fully cleared out sector one, securing the beachhead.
With the information Kotori provided us, we divided the remaining space into four sectors.
Apparently, a Spirit is trapped in each of these sections. This follows the Virtual Tower's usual way of doing things.
The Iris Orthodoxy's and Dragon Empery's fleet got assigned sector two, where a Spirit by the name of Tohka Yatogami is believed to be.
The Sardegna Empire's and Iron Blood's fleet was given sector three, which should be where the Spirit Origami Tobiichi is.
Sector four went to the Royal Navy's and Northern Parliament's fleet, which will be looking for the Spirit named Yoshino.
Lastly, the Sakura Empire's and Kingdom of Tulipa's fleet was tasked with finding a duo of Spirits in sector five – Kaguya Yamai and Yuzuru Yamai.
I couldn't help but wonder why there were two of them in sector five, a unique situation.
Kotori explained that I should "think of them as one and the same Spirit." That's most likely the reason why.
Once the attack begins on the remaining four sectors, Kotori and I will lead the Eagle Union's fleet and Pseudo-Fraxinus into...
Ah, right, she rechristened it as Fraxinus AL... We'll take the fleet and Fraxinus AL, and we'll provide support to whichever sector needs it the most.
Thanks to a team of the port's experts – including Yuubari – the airship was repaired and ready. They not only restored much of its functionality, but also installed new and experimental weaponry.
Most impressive of all was the person recovery system that the airship had. It opened my eyes to new possibilities.
All these impressive technologies are sure to aid us in battles to come.
Commander, Miss Kotori, all fleets are standing by.
Fraxinus AL's systems are all green and ready to go.
Memphis, give the order to commence the attack.
Let's take it slow and steady. Leave no enemy in the area unscathed!
Roger!
We've got the superior force in this battle. I think we oughta apply pressure from the front while flanking 'em with our fleets from the sides.
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Two - Fleet Rendezvous Point

scripts.say: It should let us seize control of this area quicker. The extra time we'll get can be spent on looking for those trapped girls.
I concur. Incidentally, I've heard that a Dragon Empery patrol fleet has also become trapped here.
Yes. Fu Shun, Fei Yuen, and Fu Po. They're a clever trio, so I believe they'll be fine.
I'm more concerned about our guests. We need to find them as quickly as possible.
She's got hair as dark as night, purple clothes, and carries a huge sword. Nickname's "Princess," also known as Tohka Yatogami.
Saw the intel about her. Reckon we'll recognize her immediately.
I'm quite curious to see what this guest looks like.
Seeing as all the fleets have set off now, shall we do the same?
Let us hope we can resolve this incident quickly and bring everyone home safely.
Set sail!
Still no word back from the port, as I feared...
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Two - Somewhere Else

scripts.say: So what you're saying is...
- We're in a load of trouble!  - And nobody's gonna try to stop us!
Huh?
You weren't around for the last adventure, Fei Yuen, but now the gang's all here! That, to me, sounds like destiny's doing!
But how will we go on an adventure? There's nobody here but enemies.
Heheh... There's not JUST enemies here.
The Virtual Tower acted up, so you know what that means? That we've got visitors from another world again!
GRRSSHH... KABOOOM!
Right on cue. Sounds to me like someone's fighting!
That didn't sound like cannon fire, though, did it?
Which means our visitors aren't any average Janes! Come on, let's be quick!
Our adventure's officially begun!
Our adventure's officially begun!
But– Hey! Wait up!
Hiyaaahhh!
A girl standing atop some ruins brandished her sword against the approaching Sirens.
Hngh!
A moment later, a fierce shockwave blew across the surroundings, dispatching all her witless foes in one fell swoop.
Hmph. Any more who–
She prepared to swing her sword again, but she stopped herself once had a good look at who they were.
Holy smokes! I can't believe you just took out all those Sirens by yourself!
You must be from another world, right? What's your name?
Oh, sorry, I should go first! I'm Fu Shun! I'm the captain of our adventure squad!
This is Fei Yuen, and that's Fu Po – my skilled assistant and tactician!
Well met. My name is Tohka Yatogami.
You look quite different to those I just fought. Who exactly are you?
Hah! I knew we'd need a proper introduction! Telling Fu Po to get one ready was the right call!
Here you go. It's an overview of information concerning the Azur Lane!
Tohka received a book from Fu Shun, and began reading it carefully.
I understand. This place is a whole other world. That explains this strange equipment of mine.
Yes. I've got the broad picture now.
You sure adapted fast...
Oh please. This happens all the time.
Are we now in the place you call "the port"?
Nah, not here. There are loads of enemies here.
Where are we, then?
Your guess is as good as ours!
We were just patrolling and suddenly wound up here. We were just about to start gathering intel!
It'll be an adventure! Wanna come with us, Tohka?
An adventure, you say? While that does sound amusing, what exactly does it entail?
Come along and you'll see for yourself!
And so went the encounter between Tohka Yatogami and the energetic adventure squad.
Tohka Yatogami and the three adventurers spent a while searching through the imitation of Tengu City.
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Two - Somewhere Else

scripts.say: They mapped out its entire structure, finding not just spots to rest and a location Fu Shun dubbed "the Demon Castle," but also even learned of the wonder of something called kinako bread in the process.
Then, just as they were about to clear out the Demon Castle, a spaceship entered everyone's view.
Look! What is that? Some kind of new Siren superweapon?!
Isn't that... Fraxinus?
That's Kotori's airship!
Possibly thanks to Fraxinus AL's relaying, the adventure squad's long-unresponsive communicators finally came back online.
Tohka and that patrol fleet look ready for a fight. Seems they've found the enemy's stronghold!
There's no time to waste. We must press on!
After a joint attack from Fraxinus AL, the Eagle Union, the Orthodoxy, and the Empery, all the enemies in sector two were wiped out.
Hm? This doesn't feel quite like the Fraxinus I'm used to.
Let's just say some things happened. Do call it "Fraxinus AL." Oh, and welcome back, Tohka.
It's good to be back, Kotori.
You – I presume you're {playername}, the port's Commander.
My name is Tohka Yatogami. It's quite an important name, so do try to remember it.
I will need your assistance for the foreseeable future. On that topic... I'm hungry. Do you have anything to eat?
My compatriots, the anomaly in this area is a threat to the port's safety. We must resolve this situation with haste.
location: Anomalous Area - Sector Three - Fleet Rendezvous Point

scripts.say: Yeah. If we're lucky, this may even serve as an opportunity to destroy the Virtual Tower.
Things get worse every time it does something. It poses too large a risk to be left alone.
That may be wishing for too much. We searched that place's interior a while back, and... Well, it was like a natural Singularity in there.
By which I mean, it stands there as a force of nature, in essence. It won't be destroyed so easily.
That's why I said "if we're lucky." No need to overthink it. Our priority remains to clear this area of enemies.
With our firepower, that should be a walk in the park. What's with the excessive caution?
Let me head in, and I'll show these insects just far below me they are!
There is never a good reason to let your guard down. We are dealing with Type IV Sirens here, and nobody knows what awaits us at the center of the area of operations.
In addition, we are tasked with rescuing an otherworldly visitor.
Yes – a white-haired, borderline expressionless girl nicknamed "Angel."
I'm quite eager to see this Origami Tobiichi for myself.
Z2 and Z13 should be fine out there, but if any of you come across them, do bring them with you.
Naturally.
Now, then, it is time that we compose a new symphony.
Yorktown introduced Hammann and Sims to Ratatoskr's commander, Kotori Itsuka, and explained the details of the mission they needed to help with.
It's an honor to have the two of you helping out. Here's the situation: we recently upgraded our monitoring equipment, letting us measure emotional data with greater precision.
So, in order to verify this, we're going to need live data. Now then, let's get Operation Affinity Point underway. Any questions?
W-wait, time out... What the heck is "Operation Affinity Point" anyway?
I... don't think that's something we have any business knowing.
That's not what I want to hear right now. Didn't I already explain the process of gathering and testing affinity points to the two of you?
Hammann and Sims say nothing back, only shiftily glancing at one another.
The gesture doesn't escape Kotori's notice. Lollipop still in mouth, she gives an expression that seems to say, "I get it."
Hmm... So that's the issue. If you'd like, I can provide some one-on-one dating advice...
Th-then, let's get started!
After arriving at the shopping district, Hammann and Sims begin their operation. Yorktown and Kotori are not far away, gathering and monitoring data in the meanwhile.
If I'm understanding this correctly... You just want them to walk around town together and have dinner?
Of course. Because, these things are surprisingly important. After all, emotional connections are nurtured by the accumulation of small, everyday happenings.
In fact, it's often the little things that grant big opportunities to deepen your friendships.
See, their affinity points are definitely increasing, are they not?
And, the biggest boost... came from choosing their outfits together, enjoying snacks together, and watching a movie together... Heehee. How nice.
Yorktown breathes a sigh of relief after checking the graph on the monitor.
Oh, they just came out of the movie theater. So, there's just one last task on the list?
That's right. The last thing to do– is picking out a gift for each other!
Now then, let's see how high those affinity points will go!
Seems like they're starting with the accessories shop? ...Hm?
All of a sudden, Kotori's device starts beeping. The two lines on the graph begin to crash one after the other.
...Their affinity points are plummeting?
Hmm, that's odd... Maybe my handheld device is bugged?
One moment! I'll go check what's going on!
With an anxious look on her face, Yorktown heads down to see what the situation is.
Huh... Looks like there aren't any bugs on my end...
I saw it first!
Hmph... Doesn't count until you actually grab it.
Just as Kotori finishes checking out her device, Hammann and Sims come back while continuing to argue. Yorktown can only look at them with a confused expression.
I'm sorry, Kotori. There was only one thing left at the store, and they both had their eye on it... Which led to them getting in this argument...
This means... that their affinity points will go way down, right?
Kotori responds with only a shrug, smiling wryly while still holding the candy in her mouth.
Ah... I see. That makes perfect sense.
Don't worry. You know that they say – the more you argue, the closer you are. This sort of bickering is only possible if you've opened up to the other person.
Just then, her device gives off a little beep. The lines that had previously taken a nosedive return to normal... and then suddenly start to climb even higher.
Huh? Wow, you were right... it's going higher and higher. Heehee.
Heh. Now that we've come this far, I don't think it would be an exaggeration to call the two of them best friends.
Us? Best friends? Yeah, right. Are you sure your device isn't broken?
Yeah, that's right! A little kid who tries to grab the same thing as me is no best friend of mine! Dum-dum!
Hehe. Well, we were still able to gather some good data either way. Now then... who wants that one-on-one dating advice first?

The sound of glass shattering suddenly echoed out across the quiet back alleys of the shopping district. It doesn't take long for a woman to appear in front of Kurumi Tokisaki, trying to assess the situation.
My, my. Is something the matter? I get so very nervous when you stare at me with such a serious expression. Here I am trying to behave and follow the rules, but...
Miss Tokisaki, according to eyewitness accounts, you are responsible for breaking the window of a store in the shopping district. You will be expected to pay compensation.
Really, is that so? I do not remember doing anything of the sort.
Hmm... Perhaps it might've been one of my clones?
You... have clones?
Yes, indeed. My Angel, Zafkiel, can create clones of my self. At times... they can even act of their own will.
Perhaps what people saw... was a slightly rowdier version of "me".
Nya?! Does that mean multiple Kurumis can exist at the same time, nya?!
...Who might you be?
The witn– I mean, uhh, the owner of this store, nya! In any case, don't worry about the compensation, nya.
The more important thing here is your ability, nya! So, I hereby propose a partnership, nya!
...A partnership?
That's right! Using the cloning powers, we'll be able to create the greatest one-woman entrepreneurial service team in history!
If every job, from manager to staff, is just another one of you, then all the customers will get to have the authentic Kurumi treatment, nya!
My, my. How interesting...
But before that, I first want to know exactly what it is that my clone did. Would you mind showing me the scene of the incident?
Though somewhat deflated-looking, Akashi shows Kurumi to the scene.
Standing before the shattered glass, Kurumi finds herself deep in thought.
While the security footage undoubtedly shows you in it, nya... It doesn't actually show how the glass broke, nya.
Kurumi...? Thanks for saving the kitten earlier...
A kitten, you say? ...Heehee, I see. I think I'm starting to understand what this clone of mine was trying to do.
...Clone?
It seems this is no coincidence, then. Miss Laffey, could you please detail what happened earlier?
Kurumi showed up out of nowhere... and fired her gun at a kitten that was standing in front of a window...
She was aiming at the kitten? Not the window?
...Yes. But before I realized what just happened, the kitten was safely in Kurumi's arms...
Laffey's account finally begins to shine a light on what happened.
I see. My clone must've used the bullet that rewinds time – Dalet.
Rewinds... time?
Yes, indeed. It is one of the bullets in the arsenal of my Angel, Zafkiel. It is a power that only I can use, though I have stored a number of these bullets with my clones, just in case.
I set a condition that they would only be allowed to be used during emergencies, but I suppose if it's for the kitten's sake, there's nothing to be said.
...Mhm. In any case, thanks to Kurumi, the kitten was saved.
As for the window itself, it likely shattered for some other reason. But, let us see this through to the end. With this bullet, allow me to prove my innocence.
Zafkiel–– Dalet!
The moment Kurumi fires her gun, the window itself begins to return to its original state, like a tape played in reverse.
She's turning back time, nya?! If only I could use that for my businesses...!
So, not only can you create clones, but you can also turn back time... Quite impressive. Might I ask what other abilities you have?
Stopping time? Time travel? Teleportation? Projecting your consciousness?
Heehee. Who knows? You have quite the active imagination, Miss Akashi.
Even though her answer is completely ambiguous, Akashi's eyes start to shimmer.
This is the request of a lifetime, nya! Please partner with me, nya! We'll be able to embark on a business venture like no other, nya!
Should we be able to apply this power to tactical exercises and logistics... Miss Tokisaki, should you be willing, I would like to discuss this again with you in a... calmer environment.
I put in my request first, nya! I should be first in line for a partnership, nya! We can sign the contract right here and now, nya!
Heehee. Let's save these conversations for a later date– Aleph!
Kurumi raises her gun to her own temple, her lips curling into an elegant but mysterious smile. She then pulls the trigger without any hesitation.
Her figure is enveloped by a torrent of distorted time, and then vanishes completely.
...Where did Miss Tokisaki go?
Sh-she disappeared, nya?! What a shame... I had the best business idea ever, nya!
Ehh... I wanted to ask her to make time stop... after I went to sleep...
...Anyway, back to sleep. I'll ask... Kurumi again when I see her... zzz...
Since the botanical garden's watering system was upgraded, the plants have been watered more evenly than before, and the flowers even seem to be blooming more vibrantly.
Really? It appears Oleg has finally found a nice helper, and I'm sure the plants will be happy too♪
Heehee. You'd have to ask the plants themselves about that.
Curiosity piqued, De Zeven Provinciën and Hanazuki head towards the botanical garden, only to find the flowers there on the verge of withering, a chilly aura hanging over them.
H-how did this happen?! The flowers are freezing to death... Was there some malfunction with the watering system?
Where's Oleg? I need someone to tell me what's going on here first...
Urgh...
Is someone there?
In the corner of the garden is Yoshino, crouching and curled up into a little ball, a faint chill radiating from her entire body.
...Are you okay?
*sniffle*... Yoshinon...went missing... I can't...control my Spiritual Power...
Yoshinon... That's the name of the rabbit friend you always keep with you, right?
Calm down first. When did you notice that your friend went missing? Take as much time as you need.
Miss Oleg called me over...to use my Spiritual Power to help with the watering system...
But suddenly, the equipment broke down... Oleg...went to fetch some parts...and that's about when Yoshinon went missing...
Without Yoshinon, I... *sniffle*...
Don't you worry. Zeven and I will help you find her! Umm... why don't we check the surveillance footage first?
Hold on. Did you see that? ...The moment when Oleg left.
Yeah. It's a bit hard to tell with all the smoke and dust, but... There, tucked in Oleg's clothes...
...Yoshinon...
Well, that's a relief. Looks like Oleg took your friend by mistake.
Let's go look for Oleg together, Yoshino. By the way, you also mentioned she was looking for parts, right?
Y-yes...
That means she must've gone to the parts warehouse. Let's make our way over as well.
Indeed. Let's go pick Yoshinon up.
When they open the door to the warehouse, the three of them find Oleg engrossed in her work, Yoshinon quietly resting in her arms.
Yes, this model number should make perfect sense...
Yoshinon!
Huh? You're here too, Yoshino? ...Oh, I'm so sorry! I was in such a rush that I accidentally grabbed your buddy here!
Seriously, I feel really bad! You must've been worried sick, right?
It's okay...as long as Yoshinon is safe and sound...
Yoshino hugs Yoshinon tightly, finally letting out a sigh of relief.
Yoshinon has returned! Phew, what a thrilling adventure that was! But, I must say, resting in Oleg's arms was superbly comfortable...
I wonder though... Yoshino, did ya keep yourself together while I was away?
...*sniffle*... Sorry...
Now, now. Enough of that. More importantly, it looks like you've made some good friends.
Yoshino looks up at Zeven and Hanazuki, then bows her head in embarrassment.
Umm... Thank you for looking for Yoshinon, and also...for looking after me.
That's the ticket! Helping each other out – that's what friends are for!
Mhm... You're right...
Thank you so much, everyone. I want to do something useful for you as well! I'll do my best to complete the watering system!
Already picked up the replacement parts. Let's hurry on back, then!
Hehe. Our friends at the botanical garden must be eagerly waiting for our return as well.
Yoshino calmly releases her Spiritual Power, a pale green light dissolving into the sprinkler system.
A mist imbued with Spiritual Power falls evenly on the flowers, melting through the frost in an instant. The flowers not only regain their vitality, but even seem to bloom more vividly.
What amazing technology... Is everything back to normal now? Rather, the plants look even better than they did before...
Almost all of them have started blossoming... Yoshino, you're truly amazing!
N-no way... Miss Oleg deserves the credit, if anything. Besides...
Besides?
Helping each other out... That's what friends are for...
Woahhh–– So this is what paradise is like!
Affirmative. The signboard here says "cat petting area".
Hmm, looks like we can walk right in? In that case, I'll be heading on in first!
Disapproval. Sneaking ahead is not allowed.
W-wooow... What a fragile yet fluffy creature––
M-more of them are approaching...?! D-do you all wish to become my familiars so badly?
In exchange for your loyalty, I shall reward you with a "headpat"...
Meow, meow~
Nice kitties, nice kitties~ ...Wait, huh? Why does Yuzuru have more familiars than me?!
*gasp*... No way! Don't tell me it's those dried fish you took from the cafeteria earlier...
Affirmative. Planning in advance is a must.
H-how despicable, to resort to such tactics...!
Ahh! Do you lot intend to betray me as well?!
Seeing the kittens rush over to Yuzuru one after another, Kaguya is unable to contain her frustration.
Now is the perfect time for an Akashi intervention, nya!
Every cat's favorite treat stick, available now for 30% off, nya!
That's it! Gimme three, no, five!
Request. I would like some too. Dried food supplies are almost depleted.
Such generous customers, nya! You've purchased even more than the mysterious Client K who often frequents this place, nya!
The mysterious Client K...?
Suspicion. K for Kaguya... Were you coming here secretly without informing me?
No, I swear, it's not me! There must be some other cat-lover whose name starts with K! Not that I have any clue who it might be!
Thank you guys! If you ever need anything else, feel free to contact me, nya!
Akashi hands the twins a bag of cat snack sticks, then casually leaves the scene.
Heh heh... We haven't had a contest for a while. How about it, Yuzuru?
Agreement. A contest based on the number of kittens tamed?
That would be way too boring. So, let's go with this – whoever tames that jet-black beast first wins!
It is the only entity that showed no reaction to either the fish or the snacks... a truly solitary and noble being!
Meow. (Glances towards Kaguya)
Identified. Kaguya is being looked at with contempt.
What?! You have some nerve, looking down on me like that!
I'll make you bow down to me one way or another– Ah! Don't run away!
Mrreow... (Slightly grumpy)
Assertion. Attempting to be aggressive is the wrong approach. You should try to coax it with food first.
Meow. (Ignores Yuzuru).
Hellooo, you two~ You know, that kind of stuff isn't going to make anyone happy~
Question. Who are you?
A very suspicious person has appeared...
What if I told you I can get that kitten to fall right into your lap?
Oh? How interesting. So, how do you do it?
If you want a cat to like you, the most important thing is empathy~
In other words, you've gotta become a cat yourself! Here, I brought cat-eared headbands for the two of you. Why don't you try it on?
Question. Will this really work?
It's an important part of learning how cats behave! Now then, try saying "meow"!
L-like this? Meeeow~
Good, good! Now make a loose fist and shake it around in front of your chest♪
Imitation. Meow.
Yes, just like that! You look so cuuute... I mean, you look just like a cat♪
Now then. Cats also have a habit of rubbing up against each other...
Wow, yeah! Yuzuru's already got it even though I only showed you once! Amazing! Okay, how about this sound next? Purrrrrr...
Meeoww!!
Meoweow?! Why are you getting mad all of a sudden?!
Well, that's all for today! I'll be heading out first––!
I have a feeling... that this "secret ritual" accomplished nothing at all...
Meow...
The cat almost seems to let out an exasperated sigh, then trudges over and plops down between their feet.
Ah! It's getting attached to me! But, this outcome kind of feels...
Agreement. Let's call it a draw.
Truly, a genius invention that will revolutionize our times... so why is nobody interested?!
Ah, Yukikaze! What fortuitous timing! Come take a look at my latest invention!
Behold, a costume that lets you change anywhere, anytime! I call it the Everchanger Mk. I!
...It sounds a bit suspicious. Not the kind of stuff I'm interested in.
No way! I thought that you, as a fellow genius, would be able to understand the greatness of my work!
Genius, you say...?
I'm in full agreement. This is an undeniable breakthrough. A marvelous invention.
Hwuh?! That was freaky... Just where did you come from anyway?!
I was simply passing by.
I would like to learn more about your "Everchanger Mk. I", Soobrazitelny.
Wah hah hah! You have quite the discerning eye, Origami!
I am simply providing the objective viewpoint from an "adult" perspective.
(A-adult? What's that supposed to mean?)
Ahem! In any case, let's continue this conversation in my workshop!
Hmm... I must say, the mature and grown-up Yukikaze the Great's curiosity has been piqued!
Ehehe, I knew it! As a fellow genius, I just knew you'd understand! Follow me!
...Wait, hold on! Why are you making Yukikaze the Great change her clothes all of a sudden?!
If you're going to show off your invention, shouldn't you be the one doing the demonstration?
Unfortunately, it's a matter of size. It's difficult to adjust these things on the fly, so you're the only one who can be the demonstration model.
I see, I see... Wait, how is that supposed to make sense?!
Just button it up, and– tada! Take a look! A timeless invention from the genius mechanic, yours truly!
But... isn't this... a bit heavy? I can't even lift my arms...
There's a hefty amount of metal inside, and yet the texture still feels like silk. Marvelous.
Just as expected, Origami! You can tell with just a glance!
The internal mechanisms are what allow the colors and patterns of this costume to be freely changed.
Now then, Yukikaze. Please press the black button.
This one? It just made a click.
Woooah! It's suddenly getting longer!
This one's a formal look, a favorite among spy movie enthusiasts. Pairs perfectly with sunglasses!
What do you think, Origami?
Transformation took 3.47 seconds. Highly efficient, and well-suited for handling unexpected situations.
(Handling unexpected situations? ...Wait, is she thinking of having it change forms to deal with enemies on the battlefield?)
But this outfit is way too heavy. How are you supposed to move around in this...
It's still a prototype. Functionality has to come first. I'll work on the comfort aspect later.
I have a question. Is it water-resistant?
Perfectly so! It's completely waterproof and designed to withstand the elements. You can even wear it while swimming in the ocean!
Rating: Perfect. A truly ingenious design.
(Waterproofing... Is this really about combat performance, though? Besides, we already have riggings. How would this be superior...?)
So... how about the defensive capabilities? Especially compared to our shipgirl riggings.
Who said anything about wearing this to a battlefield?
Huh? What was all that talk about unexpected situations and waterproofing, then?
Of course it's about regular work stuff, like around the workshop––
Of course it's about going on a date––
Well, umm... I was more thinking, even if you get tired at work, you could just instantly change clothes and go to sleep...
While on a date, you would be able to change your outfit without disrupting the flow, keeping the mood right and moving onto the next phase.
Yukikaze the Great never should've listened to you in the first place!
And so, Yukikaze runs off, red in the face and pouty.
One more, please!!
Woah... the plates are stacked up so high, they're taller than a person! Umm, Tohka, are you sure you're not overeating?
Hrmm? Oh... is that so? I'm sorry. I seem to have inconvenienced you once again...
No, no, it's nothing that serious. I was just worried you might give yourself a tummyache. But, from the looks of it... maybe I'm overthinking things a bit?
I'm just glad that you enjoy the menu here at our canteen!
Mmhm! There are so many dishes I've never seen before, and they're all so delicious!
I've baked my own cookies before, but they never came out anywhere as good as these!
Things would be so much more fun if I could cook this well.
So... Tohka, would you like to learn how to cook?
...In other words, you're here on Saratoga's recommendation?
Yes ma'am! I'm looking forward to receiving your instruction, Master Lung Wu!
M-master? ...Ahem. I see that you certainly have the right attitude.
I can teach you to cook, but... You know the old adage: one step at a time.
First, I'd like you to start with prepping the vegetables. Please cut them into the correct shapes.
Understood! Cutting things is my specialty!
Y-yeah... I'm... glad you're motivated...
Master! I've done it!
However... I used too much force, and the cutting board broke in two!
That's okay... Beginners are bound to make mistakes, so just be careful with how much force you use next time.
Next, I'll be showing you how to cook, so watch closely.
By the way, what will we be making?
Steamed sea bass. It seems to be a dish that nobody can say no to.
The prep work can be a bit tedious, but the actual steaming process is quite simple.
I see... So in order to become a good chef, both patience and carefulness are needed.
If you already know that much, you're already at the threshold...
Alright, feast your senses upon tonight's meal.
...Everything smells amazing!
Mmh... Aah...!
If you want it that badly, why not go ahead and give it a taste?
C-can I really?
Part of a chef's duty is taste-testing the food before serving it.
I see! In that case, don't mind if I do!
*nom*... Mmh... Mmmm! This one got a little kick to it, but it's so good! And, so aromatic as well! Master, what kind of dish is this?
Chili chicken. Try the one next to it as well. It's one of my minor specialties.
This is... Woah! It's mapo tofu! I often see it served at supermarket counters!
Mmh... But it's so much tastier than the stuff you buy outside!
That is the charm of Empery cuisine.
And, you said this was only a "minor" specialty? Now I'm dying to find out what a "major" specialty tastes like...
Well, if you put it that way... I suppose I can give you a special technical demonstration!
...How's that?
Amazing! The taste bursts forth like bombshells! But, these are all everyday ingredients! Master, are you some sort of magician?!
Heheh... I'm not done yet~
S-seriously?
As your master, allow me to reveal to you some of my secret techniques...
In the evening, Saratoga quietly drops by the kitchen to check on Tohka.
Tohka, I came to see how you're doing~
Ahh... I'm totally stuffed... I don't remember the last time I felt like this. This immense feeling of satisfaction... You're truly amazing, Master...
Heheh... Keep up your efforts, Tohka, and I'm sure you'll reach my levels– No, maybe you'll even surpass me.
Umm... I guess... you could call this a successful cooking lesson?

sequence:
The Facts and Fictions of Devonshire

<size=45>1 A Sudden Invitation</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Afternoon sunlight shines softly through the window, casting a golden glow on my office.
As I pick up the next document awaiting my approval, there's a light knock at my door.
Come in.
Greetings, Commander. May I have a moment of your time?
Devonshire enters with a silver tray in hand. I can smell the donuts from here already.
You've been working without a break for some time now. As your personal maid, I must urge you to get proper nourishment and rest.
I've refined this donut recipe seven times now. Would you taste-test it for me, please?
Gladly. Thank you.
A stack of donuts is placed on the tray, with amber syrup drizzled atop them.
Also, I'd like you to review this document: the Commander's Rest & Relaxation Project.
She reaches into the pocket of her maid dress and hands me more papers.
What is this?
One might call it an invitation to a date. You've worked without a day off for over a month now.
It is my philosophy that an exceptional maid must not only care for you, but also provide for your personal happiness.
To that end, I've prepared a special itinerary with a variety of experiences.
Her tone is polite, but persuasive. There's an unusual gleam in her eyes, too.
Of course, if you do have other plans at the moment, I will not insist.
It sounds like fun. I can't wait.
It is an honour that you'd place your trust in me.
Other plans can wait until later. What do you have in mind?
A wise decision. I promise, I will not disappoint you.
I will be taking charge of your schedule tomorrow. Rest assured that all arrangements will be made with care.
After a quick curtsy, Devonshire smiles in that meaningful way of hers.
I hope you'll forget about work for a while... and enjoy a performance just for you.
Today's the day...
My office is empty, save for the golden envelope left on my desk.
Did Devonshire leave this here?
I open the envelope and find a map of the port inside. Three locations are marked on it.
The sweets shop, amusement park, and fortune teller... I guess these must be our destinations.
As I turn to head to the first location on the map, a card falls out of the envelope.

sequence: Commander, if you're reading this, then our date has begun.
Our route is simple: follow the clues you're given to deduce the true location of our date.
But don't worry. Your faithful maid will always be at your side.
Yours truly, Devonshire.

The Facts and Fictions of Devonshire

<size=45>2 The Call of Icing</size>

scripts.say: Port - Commercial District
An hour later, I go to the sweets shop per her plans. The sign out front has been replaced with one that advertises a one-day exclusive taste-testing event.
It's quiet inside. The only person I see is someone with a white chef's hat, whispering something to a plate of donuts.
Keep the margin of error of caramel thickness within 0.3 millimeters. It'll be bitter if there's too much, and too sparse if there's too little.
This confection features a three-layer gradient of icing. The base is lemon white chocolate, topped by orange liqueur, and finally a misting of gold dust and honey...
Noticing my presence, Devonshire turns to face me.
Sweets chef mode engaged. Why, hello there! Are you interested in my donuts, dear customer?
She adopts a whole new persona. I have to stop myself from bursting out laughing.
Sure, whichever one you recommend.
The chef places a donut with red icing onto a saucer and offers it to me.
Might I suggest my Velvet Veil donut?
I take a bite. The crisp icing breaks in my mouth, and the smooth sweetness of caramel spreads throughout.
Comm... I mean, dear customer, do you like it?
This is good. It's sweet, but it has layers.
She grins, apparently satisfied by my response.
You've captured the true essence of it. The rich flavor of caramel, wrapped in crimson icing...
They're like the passion and anticipation of a performance waiting just behind the curtains.
Oh? Is that why you call it Velvet Veil?
That's right. Flavor is only half the joy of sweets – the other half is how they stimulate the imagination.
However, few guests can interpret my vision so well. Are you a donut expert, perhaps?

options.content: I happen to know someone who is...

scripts.say: I happen to know someone who is an expert, so maybe.
I see.
I have a friend who loves donuts, so I've done my research.
How thoughtful of you.
True appreciation of a work of art comes not from inspecting the contents, but from one's heart resonating with the creator's intent.
You seem to have done just that.
I'm sure this person you know must be delighted to hear such an accurate interpretation from you.
With her wish fulfilled, she smiles happily.
Thank you for trying my donuts. Next...
We will meet again in a place where the curtain has risen.
Devonshire makes for the kitchen, leaving behind a card with a simple sketch of a stage on it.

sequence:
The Facts and Fictions of Devonshire

<size=45>3 Time-Limited Magic</size>

scripts.say: Port - Amusement Park
Surrounded by the tunes of various attractions, I search for the marked location in the park.
I think... this should be the spot.
In the plaza, there's a fairy-tale-themed parade full of floats luxuriously adorned.
When I take my eyes off of the procession, I hear an excited voice.
Cinderella mode engaged. Your Highness, you're late...
A hand reaches out from a curtained float, takes me by the arm, and pulls me in.
Huh?
Don't be nervous. This is just for the story.
Letting go of my arm, Devonshire takes a step back and performs an exaggerated curtsy.
I've been waiting for you, Your Highness...
May I have this dance?
Now?
Now. I've already gotten the music ready.
Or will you refuse me after I spent so much time diligently practicing?
I'd never.
Good...
A slow waltz begins to play. Devonshire extends her hand toward me, palm facing upward.
Let's dance.
I take her hand, and we dance in tune with the music. Her Cinderella dress billows out like a flower in bloom.
Amidst the elegant melody, the distance between us slowly shrinks.
To be quite honest... dancing in a public place is a novel experience for me.
I spend a lot of my time walking around with trays and standing quietly behind you... so being able to dance with you is exciting.
You dance really well.
Thank you very much... and I'm grateful that you were willing to join me in this little role-play.
If only we could dance forever...
As the music draws to a close, she stops.
What's wrong?
Forgive me... but my Cinderella magic has a time limit.
When the clock strikes midnight, my pumpkin carriage and beautiful dress will go back to normal.
I'll go back to being a maid who spends her time washing dishes and counting donuts.
She takes my hand and puts it to her chest. Through the fabric of her dress, I feel the rhythm of her heart.
Your Highness, if you want to be with me forever...
You must find the real me before midnight.
I'm sorry. I must go.
Before my magic fades...
She releases my hand, winks playfully, and makes her exit.
The warmth left on my hand is my only proof that everything just now was real.

sequence:
The Facts and Fictions of Devonshire

<size=45>4 Mystery of the Tarot</size>

scripts.say: Port - Park
Following the map, I arrive at a fortune-teller's booth next to a large tree.
Warm, golden light spills out from behind the curtain. I hear a hushed voice.
Lost wanderer, drawn by the threads of fate... You've finally fallen into destiny's trap... Ahem, I mean, its domain.
The fortune teller parts the curtains and beckons me inside.
Your eyes betray curiosity... but at the same time, a sense of composure, as if you believe you don't need a fortune teller.
Very well. Let the stars' revelations dispel your curiosity... I hope this divination satisfies you.
She takes a deck of tarot cards out of her sleeve and places it atop the black velvet cloth.
Envision the future you most wish to see.
Once you are ready, give me a sign.
I close my eyes. In the darkness, I sense slight tension emanating from her.
I put my hand on Devonshire's and feel slight hesitation.
...Now, I will begin the ritual of fate.
She guides my hand, placing it alongside hers atop the deck.
Your first card reveals the past.
She looks down slightly. Together, we draw the first card and flip it over.
The Magician Upright... This symbolizes creativity, skill, and new beginnings.
Hmm... Somebody has put together a stage, props, and script... all to perform a one-act play for a certain someone.
Her tone sounds less like an analysis and more like her personal feelings.
The next card reveals the present.
She puts her hand on mine, and we flip over the second card together.
The Tower Reversed... Somebody has built towering walls, locking themselves into a safe stage. However, they wait for somebody to break those walls.
I feel Devonshire's gaze from beneath her hood.
Lost soul, if you ever crossed paths with this somebody... would you become the person to break those walls?
Of course. If that's what she wants.
That's a sweet answer... I'm almost tempted to give you extra points.
The fortune teller giggles to herself. I can't help but feel like it ruins the mystery of the situation a little.
Finally, this card reveals the future–
Wait a second.
When she reaches for it, I grab her wrist to stop her.
I want to flip this card.
Oh, but wait!
Umm, the thing is...
Heedless of her warning, I flip over the card with my free hand.
Stars shimmer on its face.
The Star? Wait, this card...
What is it? Is it bad?
No... But if this is true, then...
There's still a very long road ahead of you and that somebody...
She wants to reach the finish line as soon as possible, but things can't be so simple...
Maybe some sights are only worth seeing because the journey is so long.
Comm... I mean, lost soul... What are you saying? This wasn't part of my plan–
Realizing she's misspoken, Devonshire becomes unusually flustered.
No... This isn't something I should say in fortune teller mode.
You are genuinely special, lost soul... I have other matters to attend to, so I must take my leave now.
Wait, Devonshire!
She pulls her hood over her face and disappears into the darkness of the night.

sequence:
The Facts and Fictions of Devonshire

<size=45>5 Where the Date Goes</size>

scripts.say: Port - Theater
It's 11:50 PM. The brightly lit theater is faced by an audience of none.
Devonshire stands alone behind the curtain and gazes at her pocket watch.
Only ten minutes remain until the perfect ending I've planned...
I hope the Commander wasn't scared off by my clumsy attempt at fortune-telling.
I misplaced the cards I'd prepared in advance, too... I knew I shouldn't have picked that stupid fortune teller mode.
After returning the watch to her pocket, she crosses her arms impatiently.
What an unexpected mishap, though... My mistake was panicking.
But maybe this was fate's doing, too...
Or did the Commander see through my tricks and just play along for my benefit the whole time?
No... If that were true, you'd be here now.
She surveys the empty seats once more, and her eyes stop on one seat: the prime vantage point in the center reserved for the Commander.
I meant to put the Lovers card in a conspicuous place, but I must have ruined the order when I was shuffling.
If I ever get the opportunity to plan a date again, I'll have to resort to librarian mode...
The minute hand inches ever closer to midnight.
Maybe the magic really will fade at midnight...
Mourning the thought that her meticulously prepared ending might go to waste, Devonshire gazes up at the spotlight above.
But this is fine...
GONG... GONG... GONG...
The clock reaches midnight. When the final gong ends, the stage lights all turn off at once.
This is the end...
Devonshire turns around and heads backstage with calm footsteps.
Instantly before her fingers can touch the doorknob, a hand reaches out of the darkness and gently grabs her arm.
It's too early for a curtain call, Devonshire.
Ah... C-Commander, how...
Act Three isn't over yet. I don't want to miss the ending.
Donut chef, Cinderella... and a mysterious fortune teller.
Was this the card you wanted me to flip over?
I went back to look for it. That's why I almost missed your third act.
Moonlight streams down from the windows above, illuminating the Lovers card.
The date you planned for us was really fun.
Is this the stage where the ending plays out?
Yes... You've seen right through me.
I prided myself on having made the perfect plan, but you brought it all crashing down...
You need someone special to break those high walls of yours, right?
But the clock has struck midnight, the lights are out, and the finale I prepared... will go unseen.
Is it really over?
You're here right now, Devonshire.
To me, that's all that matters.
Beneath the moonlight, she gazes at the Lovers card, fingers tracing its edges.

sequence:
The Facts and Fictions of Devonshire

<size=45>6 The True Devonshire</size>

scripts.say: Theater - Backstage
Devonshire takes a seat on a cushion by the wall and urges me to sit by her side.
What was your planned final act, anyway?
Per my original plan, I was going to show you all of my different modes when the stage lights turned on.
There are two modes I haven't shown you yet, aside from the chef, Cinderella, and fortune teller you've seen already.
Then, at the end, I would ask you a question... Which of the modes you've seen so far do you like the most?
I see. All of the personalities from earlier were interesting.
But along the way, I realized something.
I wanted to meet the true Devonshire.
...Have you found the answer?
Your magic faded when the clock struck midnight.
We're not a chef and her guest, a princess and a prince, or a fortune teller and a lost soul.
It's just me, the Commander...
...And you, the true Devonshire.
The one who tries her hardest to plan dates, but sometimes makes mistakes and agonizes over unforeseen mishaps.
Is that true, though? What if that's only another of my modes?
For example... sweetie mode engaged. Master, today was sooo hard on me~ Help meee!
Maybe now, yes.
But I'm certain of one thing. I much prefer the real Devonshire to any character you try to play.
She falls silent for a moment before eventually sighing.
You really... threw all of my plans into disarray.
I prepared a dozen backup plans for every possible mishap, but not a single one accounts for this situation.
I guess I'm not as adaptable as I thought~
So? What mode will you handle this with?
Devonshire stands up and walks into the moonlight.
I don't need modes anymore... Consider this Devonshire mode.
With no role or script to follow, no faked expression...
But prepare yourself, Commander.
She turns, approaches me, and leans in slightly.
The real Devonshire might just be harder to deal with than any mode you've seen yet.
Despite that... are you willing to continue this date, unscripted?
I'd love to.

sequence:
The Facts and Fictions of Devonshire

<size=45>7 The Real Punishment</size>

scripts.say: Theater - Dressing Room
Devonshire takes my hand and leads me through a maze of costumes and props until we reach the dressing room.
The light is off, so only silvery moonlight illuminates it.
Commander, this is the final door.
Once you step inside, you will be able to see the true Devonshire – one who doesn't play any character.
Are you ready for this?
I was born ready.
When I open the door and step inside, she giggles and locks it behind me.
Now, as promised... today's date enters its final phase.
No script, no roles, and no pre-written plot.
All I have now... are the words I want to tell you, and the self I want you to see.
She slowly approaches until both of us can feel each other's breath, and she places her fingers on my collar.
Do you get it yet? The reason I played so many characters and contrived so many scenarios today...
...Was because I wanted you to look at me alone.
You and me...
And...
Our most authentic selves, which we can only share with each other.
Pushing me up against a mirror, she braces herself with her hands on either side of me.
Her fingers graze my collar again, undoing the top button of my shirt.
In this moment, I'm not a chef, a princess, or a fortune-teller.
It's just... you and me, as we are.
The Devonshire... who wants to keep you here forever.
Are you trapping me here?
No... I'm only expressing that I wish this moment could go on forever.
She reaches for the costume rack, retrieves a length of ribbon, and ties it around our wrists.
Now that I've shown you my true self... I'll keep you by my side from now on.
Once the ribbon is tightened enough to keep our wrists together...
She raises her head so that she's face-to-face with me again.
You know... I hate surprises.
They tend to disrupt my plans.
But all of tonight's accidents have brought us closer together.
That's made me change my mind. Rather than the perfect script... I might like this unexpected ending with you even more.
Still, you need to be punished for disrupting my plans.
Punished?
From now on, you'll have to get used to the true Devonshire.
I'll be selfish at times, I'll be jealous of your attention, and I'll try to go on dates with you when we have time alone... You'll need to get used to all of that.
Devonshire lowers her head slightly and rests it on my shoulder.
Will you accept me as I am?
As someone who's imperfect, inelegant, and maybe a little greedy...
With my free hand, I stroke her hair.
That's the Devonshire I've been waiting to see.
*sigh*... I'm supposed to be the one leading this date, but it feels like you're the one caring for me.
As clouds cover the moon and block off its light, the two of us lean close.
Promise me. From this night on, every version of me that you see – be it maid, assistant, or the true Devonshire...
Whoever I may be, I want you to accept me.
I promise.
Her arm circles around my waist, and she presses her knee against me to hold me in place.
Warm breath touches my ear, and fingertips grasp the bottom of my shirt.
Your heart is racing, Commander...
If I got closer... I worry you'd forget how to breathe.
Her fingers trace a slow path upward.
Tonight's punishment... is more than a little lecture.

sequence:
The Cloudy Mask

<size=45>Chapter 1: The Outset</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Slave! I'm bored.
I accepted the secretary position expecting it to be interesting, but all I do is sit locked up in this tiny office of yours.
And you, lowly slave, dare ignore your master and process those documents without speaking a word to me?
Find some way of entertaining me, or I'm leaving! This is an order!
I appointed Deutschland thinking it would appease her, but she's acting the same as always.
I refuse. A lowly animal isn't worthy of my help.

options.content: "I'd appreciate it if you'd help me."

scripts.say: Plead all you want, it won't do you any good!

options.content: "Please, master, I humbly beg for your assistance!"

scripts.say: ... Hmph! What a helpless dog you are, begging your own master for help!
But since you're so loyal and I'm so benevolent, I'll hear you out and help with your work!
Umm... Commander?
I'm here to deliver the mission report...
N-now then, if you don't have any new orders for me, I will take my leave...
I wanted to thank Juno, but she left my office in a hurry before I could even say anything.
Ahahahahah! Did you see that, slave? The look of fear in that destroyer's eyes?!
Ahh, it was incredible! I want to see that again!
If it means I get to feast upon that sight every day, then fine! I'll remain your secretary!
It seems she's found a way to enjoy herself as the secretary.
But I think someone has to do something about that mindset of hers...

sequence:
The Cloudy Mask

<size=45>Chapter 2: True Nobility</size>

scripts.say: Deutschland and I were on a stroll around the port, and that's when we came across...
Bel, why do I need to attend today's exercise?
Because you have been assigned to the exercise fleet for the time being, Your Majesty.
I'm not in the mood for it today! Have Warspite do it in my stead!
Your Majesty, please, you must not be selfish.
How interesting, the queen of the Royal Navy is being lectured by one of her own servants! An Iron Blood leader would never be lectured by her servant!
Ah, is that Gneisenau over there? Perfect. Slave, stay here and watch this!
Hey, Gneisenau!
Hello there, Deutschland. Do you need anything?
I don't want to do that exercise tomorrow. Get someone else to do it for me!
... Very well, that won't be an issue. I will inform Tirpitz that we're changing the composition of our exercise fleet.
Now then, if you'll excuse me...
Gneisenau left the scene to convey Deutschland's wishes.
Ahahahahah! See, slave? That's the level of authority I have!
I have this hunch like Gneisenau isn't so much obedient to her, rather she just doesn't think Deutschland's attendance is required...
Her response gives me the impression that she's long since gotten used to Deutschland's arrogant attitude.
This is yet more proof of the fact that I'm Iron Blood's most respected spiritual leader!
... But I suppose there's nothing really wrong with that.

sequence:
The Cloudy Mask

<size=45>Chapter 3: Dissonance</size>

scripts.say: I shall now announce the exercise winners in descending order of performance.
Listen closely, slave. Wait for the moment my name, Deutschland – the most magnificent armored ship in the world – is read aloud!
Fifth place: Rodney.
... Hmph, I was out of shape today. But no matter, the Big Seven are a class of their own, but I would never fall short to any other battleship type...
Thirteenth place: Queen Elizabeth.
... Grrrr...
Twentieth place: Takao. Takao is the sole heavy cruiser that made it to the top 20 for this exercise. Let's give her a round of applause.
Not so fast! What about me?!
Ah, Deutschland, let's see...
You were faster than all others in the moving target shelling category, but there is room for improvement in your accuracy and firing posture.
In my opinion, you could use some more training.
London continues reading out names where she left off.
Training is for dogs and circus animals! I'm perfect, I don't need to train...
I don't... need to...
Slave! I'm more powerful than anyone, aren't I?! Yes, I'm just in bad shape today! That's all it is, right?!
She's on the brink of tears. I'd better...

options.content: Flatter her so she'll calm down.

scripts.say: So that's how it is... Now I see...
I'm not actually powerful at all... Everyone's just been playing one big trick on me...
Ahah, eheheh, hahahahaha...
She looks depressed as she runs off on her own somewhere without answering my call, like she didn't even hear me.

sequence:
The Cloudy Mask

<size=45>Chapter 4: Devastated</size>

scripts.say: Office work hours have begun but Deutschland still hasn't shown up, so I decided to head to the Iron Blood dorm to look for her.
Iron Blood Dormitory
You're here, slave? What do you want?
I opened the door to Deutschland's room to find her all by herself, huddled up in a corner.
Now I'm worried about her...
You need a secretary? Get someone else to do it then...
Just leave me alone. I'm no use to you anyway...
I'm such an idiot. Everyone around me thinks I'm a clown, and I never even realized it.
They say I'm powerful, which makes me think I actually am, until I'm convinced I'm superior to everyone and act high and mighty...
... She brushed my hand away.
Don't touch me!
I've slowly realized something ever since I came here. I'm not like the girls from the other factions.
I'm different...
And you're like them. You made me your secretary just so you could laugh at me when I screw up, didn't you?
Of course you'd lie...
I don't think she'll listen to anything I say in her current state.
It looks like I'll have to ask her fellow fleet members what happened.

sequence:
The Cloudy Mask
