I follow her lead and move to the edge of the stage.
There's a metal creaking as the floor opens in the center, revealing a deep hole.
You really did make pitfalls... Very intimidating.
Of course. A smooth elopement wouldn't be very demanding of a princess's sword.
Uh-huh... Hey, Watarase, behind you!
I spot another pitfall in a surprising side of the stage and reflexively reach out to stop her.
RRRRIP!
We fall into the hole together, and I realize that it has cushions on the bottom. However, my costume catches on the mechanism, tearing open a half-foot-long gash in it.
Watarase looks up from her position in my arms. When she sees the tear, she visibly saddens.
Commander! Are you okay?
I'm fine. The floor is soft, so no worries there.
I'm sorry. I forgot to disable this trap after setting it up for earlier scenes.
And your poor costume... This is all my fault for adding unnecessary scenes.
I do feel bad about the costume, but it's a good thing neither of us got hurt.
Right... As long as you're safe. If you weren't, I...
*sigh*... It's too late for apologies now.
I wanted to make the performance seamless, but in the end, it was my blunder that ruined it.
No, Watarase. It may not be perfectly seamless, but that just gives you an opportunity to weave new memories into it, no?
Hehehe... That's a bit of a stretch.
But a garment filled with memories... I do like that idea.
The silvery spotlights spill through our intertwined fingers, illuminating the tear in my costume.

sequence:
A Bond Woven by Thread

<size=45>7 Blossoms on the Fabric of Your Heart</size>

scripts.say: Sakura Garden - Beneath a tree
Pale-pink petals blanket the stone path like snow. Watarase lays out the blue costume on the sunlit carpet, where the tear stands out even more.
She sits on her knees, skillfully using a sewing needle to mend it.
Meanwhile, I lean on a nearby sakura tree, retrieving various tools and threads for her as needed. Each time the wind blows, petals fall and dot the fabric.
It's a large tear, so it's going to take more than mending. And it might open back up onstage...
I'll have to reinforce it with fabric of the same color on the inside.
Here you go. I found this scrap in your workshop and thought it was the perfect size.
Well done, Commander. This is the perfect color and texture.
*sigh*... Despite my best efforts to make the repair inconspicuous, it does affect the original design profile.
And the embroidery I worked so hard on cuts off here...
Perfection is one thing, but I think this is unique in its own way.
Besides, it's full of our memories.
Memories... Yes, if you say so.
"Shirataki, chains may be easy to break, but the prison of the heart is not."
Her eyelashes droop sadly. Unconsciously, my fingers flip through the script to a page I know by heart.
"If you are imprisoned so, then let my sword be that which frees you!"
She keeps up her sewing efforts and replies without missing a beat.
That line isn't in the script.
True. I suppose I would be more likely to say that than would Princess Shirataki.
But I like how it sounds. Why not add it to the finale?
Gladly!
I continue flipping through pages and idly reading my lines.
Each time, she replies without hesitation and without stopping her work.
As the final stitch is sewn, sunset dyes the golden thread crimson. The fresh stitches gleam in the light.
...It's just occurred to me that the final scene could use some revisions.
How so?
"Perfection is one thing, but I think this is unique in its own way." That's what you said, right?
I'd like to include that kind of uniqueness in our performance.
She gently plucks the script from my hand, opens it to the last page, and rips off the perfect ending she'd envisioned.
Blank space has so much more potential than the perfect end.
"The princess's blade crafts a hairpin from a spring branch; her beloved's garments wear the fallen blossoms as their design."
"Thus, year after year..."
Watarase touches a cherry blossom petal that's fallen onto my shoulder and then leans her head on me.
Tired yet satisfied with her work, she sets our script aside and leaves that unfinished final chapter to be carried on the winds.

sequence:
Intoxicating Feelings

<size=45>1 When the Grapes Ripen</size>

scripts.say: Vineyard - Trail of Trellises
When I finally get a day away from work, Dunkerque invites me to an Iris-managed vineyard.
The vineyard is quiet, but full of color and life. As we walk through it, my nose is treated to the sweet scent of grapes.
Do you like it here, Commander?
I find the wind makes me want to take a deep, full breath.
It's comfortable, that's for sure. I could relax here all day.
That's wonderful.
I know I invited you, but I worried that I'd disrupt your plans.
Not really. It's a good change of scenery for my day off.
I'm relieved to hear that.
As we continue down the path, I feel the stone slabs beneath my feet warming under the sunlight.
This vineyard has over a hundred years of history behind it.
And the wine brewed from the grapes grown here is world-famous.
They grow other fruits here, too.
You know a lot about this place, don't you?
I wouldn't go that far.
I just... come here for a stroll once in a while, since the atmosphere is so nice.
Plus, you get to watch the crops grow and enjoy the fruits when they're ready.
And watching the grapes grow day by day...
It makes me think of how generous and sweet the flow of time can be.
Is that why you brought me here?
Heehee, I do want to help you relax, yes...
You make it sound like there's another reason.
That's right. Perceptive as ever, Commander.
I've been thinking of a new confection.
My main goal today was to try and find some kind of inspiration.
Such as?
The sunshine, the breeze, having someone walking by my side...
Anything can be a source of inspiration.
The soft sunlight might evoke fresh-baked chiffon cake.
Suck in a deep breath, and you'll smell the sweet and tart aroma of berries on the wind.
Morning dew glistens on the berries' surface... Isn't it beautiful?
With a little of that natural sourness left in, these would make a perfect wild strawberry flan.
What about the person walking by your side?
Commander, what level of sweetness do you like in your desserts?

options.content: A little light, so it doesn't overwhelm.

scripts.say: So that's your preference...
She nods, seemingly taking note of the answer.
Thank you for sharing.
I like walking and talking with you like this. It's so much better than racking my brain over a recipe on my own.
Sweets are made to be shared with others, after all.
If, when you take that first bite, it reminds you of today's wind and how you feel right now... then I'll consider that a success.

sequence:
Intoxicating Feelings

<size=45>2 Taste of the Times</size>

scripts.say: Vineyard - Trail of Trellises
We keep on walking down the trellis-lined path.
This is where they grow the white grapes.
Get a little closer, and you'll smell them.
Clusters of crystalline white grapes hang low from the trellises. We lean in for a sniff.
A slight fruity aroma mixes with the fresh scent of grass. Together, they're gentle and refreshing.
Smells nice and sweet.
If I could use this scent in a fruit flan...
I'd only have to add the slightest touch of sugar.
Making it too sweet would overwhelm its distinct flavor, after all.
You're such a professional.
Thank you, heehee. That compliment makes it worth all the effort.
We pass beyond the white grapes and into the area where the dark-colored grapes are grown.
These are the ones they use to make red wine.
Have a sniff. You might find the scent is mellower.
Hmm... There's a light, fruity acidity, but it's balanced by a hint of woodiness.
You have a sharp nose, Commander.
Which do you like more? The white grapes, or the red grapes?

options.content: I think I like the red more.

scripts.say: I see... But these white grapes haven't fully ripened yet...
That's a problem.
I see... The red ones are prime for the picking.
Thank goodness.
She whips out a notebook and jots something down.
What are you writing?
Nothing. Just notes.
I tend to forget my best ideas if I don't write them down.
She explains it away well enough, but I have a good enough eye to notice that she's hiding her notes from me.
Now, Commander.
Would you like to see the wine cellar?
It has its own unique aroma.
I look forward to it.
Down the stone path, we arrive at a short stone building.
We go down the stairs and find a place where the scents of oak and fermentation mix.
What a wonderful smell...
It feels warm, and peaceful... and it has the weight of time to it.
Rows of oak barrels are lined beneath dim lighting. The iron hoops around them have a dull sheen.
But unfortunately, there are so many wines here that you can't distinguish them by smell.
Do you have any wine preferences, Commander?
I'd like to hear your recommendation.
My recommendation... Hmm, not an easy question.
It depends on the situation, really.
If paired with a hefty chocolate dessert, then I'd go for a red with a ripe, fruity aroma and silky tannins.
Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon will contribute depth to the chocolate flavor...
I didn't think you knew this much about wine, too.
Food and wine have a symbiotic relationship. They benefit each other.
It's only natural that I'd learn a little.
If you'd like, try one of my recommended pairings with dinner tonight.
We can take our time over dessert...
And pick out the one that suits the mood most.

sequence:
Intoxicating Feelings

<size=45>3 Brewing a Sweet Moment</size>

scripts.say: Vineyard - Restaurant
We left the wine cellar and headed to the vineyard's on-site restaurant together.
The juice, jam, dried fruit, and homemade confections there are all made from the vineyard's own fruits.
Here, Commander.
They make all their food using crops from the vineyard's own harvest.
She shows me to a table, where an inviting spread awaits: small glass jars of jam, delicate baskets of dried fruit, and juice that glows with vibrant color.
Let's start with the white grape jam.
Have it on a fresh-baked baguette.
She slices bread for me and gently spreads the jam onto it.
Jam alone can overwhelm your palate with sweetness.
The bread will neutralize that.
I accept it and take a bite.
The crispy bread and soft jam mix in my mouth, and the fresh flavor of white grapes practically bursts.
How is it?
It's refreshing and subtly sweet. Just the right amount.
So this combination is preferred? Noted...
She takes out her notebook again and swiftly writes something down.
Next... Raisins.
She expectantly pushes over a small tray and waits for me to taste them.
You're not going to eat?
Oh, umm... I'd rather hear your thoughts than taste them myself.
I avail myself of the offer and pop one in my mouth.
Unlike the light sweetness from before, these are much richer. It's as if they've been candied.
Mm... Maybe a little too sweet.
I'd probably want it with something else.
I see... These dried fruits might be better used to adorn a cake.
Hmm... Are there any better combinations?
How about we reverse roles for a bit?
Special-made berry jam? Hmm...
I think this would be great with a fresh-baked croissant.
I tear off a bit of the croissant, gently spread some thick berry jam onto it, and offer it to her.
Huh?
She looks surprised, but she readily accepts it and opens her mouth just a little.
When she bites some off, the vivid berry color gets onto her lips, as if spring has touched her.
...It's delicious.
She wipes the jam off of her mouth with her fingertip. A little smile spreads across her face.
You're in an unusually good mood today.
A-am I?
Something about you is livelier than usual.
Is it that easy to tell?
You almost had me fooled.
Heehee. Well, I suppose I'm good at hiding my feelings.
It's not a particularly big deal...
You're just playing a very important role for me today.
From her position on the other side of the table, she smiles at me with gentle eyes.
...As if, after a long time, she's finally made up her mind to share a big secret with me.

sequence:
Intoxicating Feelings

<size=45>4 The Secret to Tenderness</size>

scripts.say: Vineyard - Restaurant
Sunlight shines gently upon the table, causing the grape vines to cast shadows.
Dunkerque stands between light and shadow, seemingly enveloped in a mysterious aura.
The truth is...
My inviting you today... wasn't just to get you out for a change of scenery.
I've always thought of how I can make the perfect confection just for you.
Just for me?
Yes... The taste, aroma, mouthfeel, and even minor details like decorations...
I want them all to suit you perfectly.
So I've been taking notes...
About every little thing today.
She opens her notebook and shows me the contents.
Among her notes are a few well-drawn pastry designs.
I drafted these before.
But I plan to calibrate them based on today's inspiration and my notes on your preferences.
Alongside drawings of different desserts, the page is filled with countless little brainstormed ideas jotted in the margins.
Tarts with Cabernet Sauvignon jam...
Vanilla cream cheese roll cakes with raisins...
Of course, there's room to improve any of them.
It's up to you. Leave the thinking to the professionals, and all.
But if you have any ideas...
I might be able to come up with something that suits your taste better.
If you're baking them for me, then I should help out.
Heehee. If we make them together, I'm sure the flavor will be outstanding.
I look forward to your help, dearest assistant.
We sit at the table and adjust her recipes together, one by one.
Hmm... The original idea was a white grape mousse mille-feuille.
With white grape jelly between layers of puff pastry and mousse...
But after looking around here, I don't think the white grapes are ready.
Then what about another fruit?
Hmm... Greengages may work.
They have the right balance of sweet and sour, along with a refreshing scent.
A greengage mousse cake... that could be the one.
It would maintain the mouthfeel while also having a lighter flavor.
It is a major change of plans, but I think it fits the mood well.
And this one... I wanted to make rum baba that incorporates the mellow flavor of Cabernet.
But now, I'm starting to think that a bolder combination is in order.
Bolder? How so?
For example, sprinkling lightly roasted sea salt caramel crumble on a Cabernet jam tart.
Adding some saltiness to the mellow, sweet flavor...
Yeah... The salt would amplify the sweet, wouldn't it?
It has more depth than raw sweetness alone.
See? You do understand, Commander.
She scribbles a few more notes.
Her fingertips tremble a little... as if her excitement is uncontainable.

sequence:
Intoxicating Feelings

<size=45>5 Team Effort</size>

scripts.say: Vineyard - Kitchen
After deciding on the recipes, we go to the vineyard kitchen together.
Now, the desserts we're going to make today are...
Greengage mousse cake...
Cabernet jam tarts with sea salt caramel crumble...
Cultured butter scones, Breton cookies with raspberry puree...
And finally, blueberry and almond tartlets.
Sounds like a lot of work.
That's exactly why I need a helpful assistant.
She smiles and hands me an apron.
I'll try not to hold you back.
The kitchen is bright and spacious, with no shortage of professional equipment.
We already have the necessary ingredients. The scent of milk and berries already wafts about.
I'll take care of the delicate parts.
Can you whip the cream and mix the puree for me, please?
Got it. Leave it to me.
Use some elbow grease when you whip cream, but try not to overdo it.
You want it to have stiff peaks that hold their shape.
I start whipping the cream with all my strength... and instantly, cream goes flying all over the place.
I whisk slowly and carefully... but the cream fails to thicken.
Don't worry. Everyone has trouble at first.
Happy accidents are part of the fun of cooking.
I guess I need some professional guidance.
Heehee, gladly. I'll teach you all of the forbidden secrets.
After tidying up the table, we continue preparing scones and tarts.
Now, shaping scones is a matter of speed. You have to do it before the butter melts.
Okay. So we go quickly, precisely, and firmly, right?
No, actually, it's the opposite. You want to be gentle, not firm.
She puts her hand on mine and guides me in shaping a scone.
Now, relax and slowly round it like this.
Her hair brushes against me, and the scent of her shampoo spreads.
There you go. Relax, relax...
Your hands are usually so dexterous. Why do you get nervous when you're making desserts?
Because a professional is teaching me.
Oh? Do I seem like that stern a teacher to you?
Maybe it just makes me want to do it right.
Don't worry. An imperfect shape won't affect the flavor.
Most of all, this is something we're making together.
Despite her professional guidance, it takes a while before we can get the desserts into the oven.
Even if it doesn't go perfectly, it's going to be a precious memory.
I can't wait to taste the desserts we make together...

sequence:
Intoxicating Feelings

<size=45>6 Flavor in Harmony</size>

scripts.say: Vineyard - Terrace
As we finish up the desserts, we arrange them on plates before taking them out to the terrace.
The sun is beginning to set, dyeing the sky orange and red. Wind carries the sweet smell of grapes to us.
Let's sit here, Commander. The view from here is the best.
She pulls out a chair and urges me to sit.
Pairing desserts with wines can bring surprising nuances and elevate their flavors.
But first...
She takes several bottles of wine out of a cart behind her and lines them up on the table.
First, let's taste-test.
That should make the changes in flavor more clear when we add dessert to the mix.
Yeah. You have to know how it tastes alone to identify the change.
She nods quietly, pours a light-colored wine into a glass, and hands it to me.
The first one is a sweet white Riesling produced here.
On the nose, it's light and floral, with notes of fruit. The palate is clean and delicate.
I accept the glass and take a small sip.
Its balanced sweetness and acidity spread across my tongue, leaving a long, memorable finish.
Refreshing, but delicate. It has a lingering fruity scent, too, which is comforting.
Right? Let's move on to the Pinot Noir. This one has notes of raspberry and cherry, and a brighter acidity.
We clink our glasses and drink it all down.
Phew... That feels nice. Do you like it?
It's more vivid and layered than the Riesling. Fascinating.
As we continue to taste the wines, I notice a soft pink coloring Dunkerque's cheeks.
Do you feel okay?
Hmm? Why do you ask?
You're a little red. Have you drunk too much?
Ah... Heehee, this is embarrassing.
Maybe I drank a little too quickly.
I'm okay, though. It'll settle once I've had food.
On that note, shall we begin with the greengage mousse cake?
Taste it with Riesling, and you might just be surprised by what you discover.
At her direction, I scoop up some cake and eat it.
The mousse is silky smooth, melting right on my tongue.
I chase it with Riesling, and its acidity cuts through and amplifies the subtle fruitiness of the mousse, making the whole combination much brighter.
It really is completely different...
The wine itself was already light and refreshing, but now, it accentuates the fruity flavor.
That's right. Mousse and wine stimulate each other's flavors and make each other more pronounced.
The evening begins to settle. In the fading light, Dunkerque's smile looks even softer.
You really do understand, Commander.
Thank you for joining me... for experiencing how flavors overlap and collide with me.
The marriage of dessert and wine is just fascinating.
Honestly, just piquing your interest makes me feel like I'm already more than halfway to success.
But no matter how good the dessert and wine are, what really matters is who you enjoy them with...
As the evening breeze blows upon the terrace, she quietly raises her glass and awaits a toast.
Everything today... The confections, the wine, and this scenery...
All of it is special because you're with me.

sequence:
Intoxicating Feelings

<size=45>7 One Tipsy Night</size>

scripts.say: Vineyard - Terrace
As night descends on the vineyard, the lights turn on, and the atmosphere gets even cozier.
The tipsy Dunkerque is flushed pink, and her eyes seem to sparkle even more than usual.
These Cabernet Sauvignon jam tarts...
I snuck a taste earlier, and I'm not sure they turned out right...
Hmm. The balance of salty and sweet seems a little off, huh?
So it comes to that again...
I thought the sea salt caramel crumble was awfully creative, but maybe I went too far with it.
Mistakes happen to everyone.
You think so? Okay, that's a relief...
She tilts her head. Her voice and demeanor seem lighter than usual, probably as a result of her tipsiness.
Oh, right. The blueberry and almond tartlets! They turned out well, didn't they?
Yeah, incredibly well. Blueberry and cream work so well together.
Then as a reward, I'll eat one more!
Oh... Commander, there's only one left.
Good idea.
I pick it up, about to break it in half. But then she leans in and takes a bite from the edge of the tartlet in my hand.
Her soft lips brush against my fingers, leaving a slight warmth behind.
Mm... So good.
Honestly, it's even better than good.
Her face reddens even more. Her smile is equal parts bashful and mischievous.
Oh? Confident, are we? Ready, seeeet...
As soon as I'm about to reach out, she seizes my hand.
Hey, now. That's just cheating.
Heehee, a win's a win! But I don't mind sharing a bite...
She takes the tartlet and holds it up to my face. I take a bite, and her warm fingertips touch my lips.
Careful now, Commander. You almost ate my finger, too.
...The thing that made me happiest today wasn't my successful baking, though.
It was the fact that we did it together.
I had fun, too.
She leans in a little, gazing at me through misty eyes, as if she's trying to tell if I'm sincere or not.
Commander... Will you remember the flavors of today?
Of course I will.
I'm glad... I'll trust those words.
She totters a little and leans on my shoulder.
Her soft hair brushes my cheek. It tickles.
Then what about me...?
Commander, will you remember the Dunkerque of today?
Or will you only remember my desserts?
Are you drunk?
No... I'm not. I'm just a little too happy to bear...
As she looks up at me in protest, her eyes twinkle like the stars.
Will you... make sweets with me again some time?
Of course. Any time.
Good... I'll hold you to that.
Dunkerque closes her eyes and leans on me.
Tonight's sweets and wine seem to mingle among the stars, becoming an unforgettable memory between us.

sequence:
The Protector Needs Protecting

<size=45>1 The Protector's Other Side</size>

scripts.say: Commander, is there anything that needs fixing from the last batch of documents I handed over?
If not, I'll just keep going at this current pace.
Le Malin, the poisoned blade of the Vichya Dominion, is here for her first day of secretary duties.
When she's in work mode, she conducts herself seriously, communicates effectively, and quickly takes care of everything she is assigned.
Hmm? Are you stepping out, Commander?
I had some other minor affairs to attend to, so I decided to leave her in charge of the office during my absence.
Understood. I'll handle the rest of the work, so go do what you need to do.
Yaaaawn... Ugh, so sleepy... Can't do this anymore...
Staying in serious-mode in front of the Commander is so exhausting, I can hardly move a muscle...
The office's soft and fluffy sofa... Mmfwah... It feels so nice...
When I returned from my errands, the first thing I saw when I stepped into my office... was the elegant poisoned blade of the Vichya Dominion melting into a puddle on my sofa.
So, this is her true face. I see now.
Ahh... I'd probably die of fatigue if I had to keep that elegant act up any longer...
Normally, I'd still be rolling around in bed at this time~
If I don't take a nap while the Commander is away, I'm not gonna be able to make it through the afternoon...
Ahem...
...C-Commander?!
Ah, umm, this is, uhh...
Great, perfect. If you didn't see anything, then there's no problem at all–
Like hell that's true!!!
Nuuuuu, my cover's blown... It's all over now...
Ugh, I thought I'd at least be able to make it through the entire secretary stint, but to get exposed so quickly...
Well, now that the cat's out of the bag, there's no point hiding it now.
That's right, Commander. You've witnessed the truth behind Le Malin, the Vichya Dominion's poisoned blade.
The whole elegant shtick is just an act.
...So, umm, are you disappointed?
You thought I was a certain kind of person, didn't you? Or, something like that...
I see. In that case, let's reduce your workload a little.
...Fweh?
You're not angry that I deceived you?
Isn't it perfectly normal for everyone to have a side that they don't want to show others?
I wouldn't call showing off your good aspects deception at all, and it's certainly nothing you need to apologize for.
If anyone should be apologizing, it should be me, for walking in on you in the first place.
(Wh-what's going on? The Commander not only isn't upset with me, but is even apologizing to me?)
I, I see. You're a weird one, Commander, but I appreciate it.
However, I can't accept your offer to reduce my workload.
While I normally would welcome less work, the way you're so blatantly trying to accommodate me would make me feel guilty.
It goes without saying. My role as secretary ship is to support you, the Commander. It would be a disgrace to the Holy Iris for our roles to be reversed.
Besides, there's a difference between slacking off and taking a break! ...The end result is totally different!
In any case, continue letting me take care of the work just as before!
Not too long later...
Okay, I did say you can continue letting me take care of the work just as before... But isn't this a bit excessive?!
...Hmm? Split the work? Tempting, but... I said what I said!
I was just grumbling, that's all... Since this is the task I was given, I'm not gonna back down halfway!
I could tell Le Malin was struggling, but she continued working despite that... though not without the occasional bouts of complaining.
But each time, the sound of pens scritching across paper quickly filled the office.

sequence:
The Protector Needs Protecting

<size=45>2 Hard Work Needs Rewarding</size>

scripts.say: Siiiigh... Another long day of booooring work...
Don't wanna... I'm gonna pass out if I have to look at another pile of papers...
While Le Malin did continue to get her work done, she no longer made any attempts to hide her inner thoughts.
Alright, ten minutes of work done. Time to treat myself to a little reward!
That's right! Twenty minutes of relaxation!
She started to liberate her slacker tendencies and her complaints about work, venting them openly. But alas...
Geh! If I laze around for any longer, I won't have enough time to finish!
Phew, I actually managed to get everything done for the day. Now that's what I call a job well done.
Huh? You're gonna say, "why didn't you just do that from the very beginning," aren't you? I see it written all over your face.
Perfectly reasonable of you to think that, but nope, can't do it. Literally impossible.
Because, me and hard work is like... letting the air out of a balloon.
If anything, I'm curious how you can endure this amount of work every single day...
I can't get any work done unless I'm rewarded!!
Otherwise, nope! No way! Not gonna do anything!
Le Malin started flailing around on top of my sofa.
If it's a reward you want...

options.content: How would you like some of Dunkerque's treats?
I'll give you extra time to laze around.

scripts.say: So what you're saying is, if I finish work ahead of time, you'll treat me with some of Miss Dunkerque's handmade sweets?!
*gulp*... You scoundrel... There's no way any sane person could turn down her mouth-watering desserts...
HOWEVER! That level of temptation isn't enough to make me work hard––
How about I also give you extra time to laze around then?
So what you're saying is, if I finish work ahead of time, you'll let me roll around on the sofa as much as I want? Even during work hours?!
Urgh... You scoundrel... Trying to bait me with the sweet, soft embrace of the sofa...
HOWEVER! That level of temptation isn't enough to make me work hard––
What if I threw in Dunkerque's handmade sweets?
Deal.
But you'd better not go back on your word, Commander!!
...All of a sudden, I felt like I was getting the short end of the stick.
Muahaha... As long as I finish work ahead of time, I'll get to enjoy Miss Dunkerque's sweets WHILE rolling around on the sofa...
Just the thought of that level of bliss is making me extra-motivated!
All right! Starting tomorrow, we're gonna give it our all!

Indeed, all of Le Malin's facets were on display at once – the side of her that was elegant and serious, the side of her that loved stuffing her face with sweets, and the side of her that wanted to spend the day rolling around on the sofa.

sequence:
The Protector Needs Protecting

<size=45>3 An Excuse to Slack</size>

scripts.say: One day, I found Le Malin slouching in her seat.
Haaaah... Sooooooo tiiiiired...
She was ruefully massaging her ankles, but...
Bleh, what an annoying mission... My legs are sore all over...
The next time a mission like this comes up, I swear I need to come up with an excuse to get time off!
...But, there's no way the Commander wouldn't notice something that obvious, right? ...*sniffle*, looks like I'll have to take those troublesome transport missions after all...
Well, at least I got back early. Time to take a little nap before I go deliver my report.
In a sense, this place really is pretty awesome.
It's nice and quiet, and there aren't people coming back and forth all the time–
Huh? Le Malin? What are you doing here?
Oh, did you just get back from a commission?
Y-yeah?!
...Miss, umm, Suffren, was it? Wh-why are YOU here?
Just on my way to training! Enjoy your break, Le Malin!
Th-there's nothing wrong with taking a break every now and then!
For a member of the elegant Le Fantasque class, a task of this magnitude is no problem at all!
Yup, yup! That's our Le Malin for you! In any case, I need to get going now!
Le Malin managed to put her elegant persona on for just long enough to see Suffren off.
But as soon as the other girl left, she once again collapsed into a puddle.
I knew it... I can't find solace anywhere except in the comfort of my rooooom...
But, what should I do? If I walk all the way back right now, I'm sure my legs are going to turn into jello when I wake up tomorrow morning...
Hrmmmmm... What should I do...
(She looks like she's having a rough time. Let's see what's going on.)
Commander? Fancy seeing you here. Are you on a break as well?
Oh... You're worried about me because I seem to be having trouble with something?
Ah, yes! Of course I'm in a bit of a rough spot right now! Since you're so ready and willing to help––
Le Malin spread her arms as if expecting me to do something about it.
Let me think...

options.content: I'll call the infirmary for you.
I'll carry you back to your room.
Fine, I'll give you a piggyback ride back to your room.

scripts.say: I, I suppose that certainly is one option, but...?
Aren't you supposed to offer to carry me back to my room at a time like this?!
Pleeeeeease, Commander? Carry me back, won't you?
O-of course, I don't mind if you hold onto me tightly...
B-but, won't it be a scandal if someone sees us like this?
Y-you know, a piggyback ride would suffice! Yes, that's fine!
I'm glad you're so understanding, Commander.
Ehehe~ Now, off we go~
...Like hell I'd say something like that!
There's no way we can let other people see us like this regardless of how you're carrying me!
I need to come up with some kind of explanation, pronto...
You injured your leg during a commission, and need a lift over to the infirmary?
You're an absolute genius, Commander!
It's a hundred times better than "I was too tired to walk back myself so I got the Commander to carry me back to my room!"
Thanks for helping me out again, Commander!
I couldn't help but notice how unusually quiet Le Malin was on the way back.
(I can't believe this only occurred to me just now, but...)
(Doesn't this count as intimate physical contact with the Commander?!)
(And, in a totally public place where everyone's staring, too!)
(I'm so embarrassed that I probably have a weird look on my face...! I, I need to hide my face in Commander's back right now!)
(Mmgh... Ahh... Commander's scent...)
(Urrrrrk... I seriously hope nobody sees me like this! Please, I don't want anyone to see this at all!)

sequence:
The Protector Needs Protecting

<size=45>4 The Office Needs Renovating</size>

scripts.say: Commander, don't you ever feel like your office is a bit too plain?
One day, when I was minding my own business, Le Malin offered me this bit of unsolicited commentary.
But, too plain, huh?
Indeed. It's all about the kind of atmosphere you surround yourself with when you work.
No cola, no sweets. No game consoles, no comic books. And to top things off, you don't even have a fluffy bed or a super soft pillow to plunge your face into!
...We are talking about an OFFICE here, right?
I know it's an office, but it's also where I... *cough*, *cough*, where YOU rest between jobs.
In any case, we need to do something about this bare-bones environment.
Allow me to assist you with this.
C'moooon, lemme do iiiiiit~
...You're really putting me on the spot here, but fine.
Wooohoo! Let's turn this place into a sanctuary where I can slack off in peace~
Look forward to seeing what I have planned!
When I arrived at the office the next morning, I was incredulous to find Le Malin there already, waiting for me ahead of time.
Good morning, Commander.
Actually, I came three hours early to avoid cutting into work time.
Heh heh heh. Aren't I awesome? I can even wake up early without being woken up by Le Triomphant.
But, this is a worthy sacrifice for the sake of securing a future where we can slack off in peace!
Now then, feast your eyes upon your new office, elegantly refurbished by yours truly!
So, can you feel it? The moment you walk into the room, the spirit of the laze just wraps itself around you–
Ahem. First, I've prepared a special space in the desk's drawer exclusively for storing sweets.
Now, you'll never go hungry on those long, boring work days.
Naturally, I've also added a refrigerator, pre-stocked with cola and ice cream.
And where there's cola, you can't go without potato chips, a truly classic combination.
Moving on– your file cabinets weren't being used efficiently, so I've filled them with layers of comic books and light novels, left open for convenient access.
What you see before you has been carefully curated by none other than moi, in case you don't know where to start.
And of course, most important of all is–
A total repurposing of the big monitor in your office!
Since I've started as your secretary ship, I've never once seen you use the darn thing!
A travesty of the highest degree! Something this magnificent... should be used for games!
Heehee... Seeing is believing, so let's get started right this instant!
Yes, let's get started with work.
Tch... I thought I'd be able to get you caught up in my sales pitch, but you're one tough customer, huh?

options.content: Well, maybe we can spare a few minutes.
Let's play together AFTER we finish work.

scripts.say: Really? You're the best, Commander!
Y'know that thing I keep hearing about a day's plan starting in the morning?
If you start off your day with a nice gaming session, I promise you'll be twice as productive! Definitely!
Really? You'd better not go back on your word then!
Alrighty, now I need to figure out which games I want to play while I'm working...
J-just kidding! I'll get everything done properly, okay?!

sequence:
The Protector Needs Protecting

<size=45>5 Beating the Fatigue</size>

scripts.say: One day, when I returned to the office with Le Malin after a long morning of errands...
Bleh... Can't go on anymore... Can't move a muscle...
The moment we stepped inside the room, Le Malin threw herself into the sofa's soft cushions.
What a long and painful battle... My stamina and motivation bars are completely drained...
In other words, I can't get up at all right now, so don't even try giving me any more work...
Otherwise... you'll see what I'm like when I'm running on empty...
Blehhh... Everything's so heavy... I can't feel my arms or legs...
I'm gonna be sore all over when I wake up tomorrow morning, aren't I? Urgh... Can I take a sick leave already...
Well, whatever... We'll cross that bridge when we get there.
But for now, it's nap time...
Judging by how hard she had to work just to squeeze her words out, she didn't seem to be faking it today.
Ooh...
Warm... That feels real nice...
Ooh...
Warm... That feels real nice...
Huh? Commander, you're giving me a massage?
Ermm, I don't think I should be imposing on you like this...
But it does feel super nice...
It feels so nice that... it's making me...
Zzzzzzzzz...
Whether she was taken in by the comfort of the massage, or overwhelmed by fatigue, Le Malin drifted off into slumber.
Now then, to get some more work done.

sequence:
The Protector Needs Protecting

<size=45>6 Kindness Needs Repayment</size>

scripts.say: One day...
Aaaaand, work complete!!
...Actually, I think I'll save the slacking for later.
Commander, is there anything else I can help you with?
I feel like I'm in tip-top shape right now. I can probably clean up any assignment you throw at me.
I instinctively reach over to put my hand on her forehead. Nope, no fever.
What are you trying to do, Commander? I don't have a fever!
Look, I know what you're thinking, but even I can be motivated at times, okay?
I decided to test that hypothesis and gave her a healthy chunk of my workload.
Ugh... I dunno about this much...
But, I'm not gonna go back on my word. I'll take care of this in no time!
Woah. She's actually doing it.
Commander, would you like some tea that I brewed myself?
In stark contrast to her usual self, she finished all the work assigned to her in one sitting, and even made me tea.
Woah, it's good!
Heheh, looks like I'm a natural at this! Got it down on my first try!
*yaaaaaaawn*...
Looks like your fatigue bar has hit its limit, huh?
Th-that's not true at all!
Commander, if you don't mind, could I give you a massage?
I instinctively reach over to put my hand on her forehead. ...Nope, still no fever.
I already told you before, I'm perfectly fine!
Come on, go lie down over there. I don't have a whole lot of experience doing this stuff, so let me know if it hurts.
*yaaaaaawn*... So tired...
After ten minutes of massaging me around with her tiny hands, Le Malin clearly had run out of juice.
I never thought... that returning a favor would be so exhausting...
Returning a favor?
When I accidentally fell asleep the other day, you went ahead and took care of all the work without saying anything.
So, I thought I'd try to make it up to you...
Work aside, I never knew that giving a massage could be so tiresome...
Commander, how are you able to do stuff like this for everyone?

options.content: Because I like seeing everyone smile.
Because being around you is all the motivation I need.

scripts.say: Is that so...
(Does that mean... that seeing my smile gives the Commander energy?)
Is that so...
(I see... Does that mean, the Commander feels better just from having me around?)
(Wait, what am I thinking right now?!)
(At this rate, I'm going to get super attached!)
(Actually... maybe that isn't entirely a bad thing...)
(Yeah... I mean, I'm having a good time, and the Commander seems to enjoy having me around...)
(So that's what's going on... Ehehe...)
The weary Le Malin smiled sweetly, and then–
She sank into the soft sofa and fell asleep.

sequence:
The Protector Needs Protecting

<size=45>7 The Protector's Wish</size>

scripts.say: All done with today's work! You know what that means–
Ice cream time~♪
Le Malin, who had finished her work ahead of time, grabbed two portions of soft-serve ice cream from the freezer and plopped down in my lap as usual.
Hmm? Commander, these two tickets on your desk are...
Is that the thing Akashi tried to force onto me this morning?
It seems like the port's amusement park facilities have been completed.
Sounds nice. Not exactly my cup of tea though.
You spend half the time running around between attractions and the other half waiting in line. Surely that's not your idea of fun, is it?
L'Indomptable might be more into that kind of stuff, but it's just not for me.
Apparently, she had some pretty unfortunate experiences with amusement parks in the past.
I went out of my way to get these tickets, but maybe it would be better to pass them on to someone else.
So what's the plan? Are you gonna give them to someone else?
(Wait a second... Does that mean... that the Commander's going to invite some other girl?!)
(Together with the Commander... alone in a haunted house, zipping around in a roller coaster, dropping from a tower, getting thrown around by the Screamin' Swing, getting lost in the Mirror Maze...)
(And then, getting cozy with each other when they get to the top of the Ferris wheel...)
(Nonononononononono! I can't afford to pass up this opportunity!)
Ahem! Now as I was about to say... I happen to be in a particularly good mood because of this ice cream, so I would be more than glad to wait in line!
Now that I think about it, it would be quite troublesome to find someone to hand this ticket to, so I would not mind accompanying you to the amusement park!
And so, that's how the two of us ended up in the port's brand new amusement park.
Are we going on the merry-go-round first? I was expecting something more exciting like a roller coaster though...
Well, if it doesn't matter, then you lead the way!
Next up was the teacup bumper cars...
Do I think the slow-paced attractions are boring? Erm, not really.
If anything, they're more my style.
And then, the pirate ship cruise...
Th-th-things are starting to get a bit more exciting now, aren't they?
B-but, who's ever heard of a shipgirl being scared of a pirate ship?
Le Malin and I went on attraction after attraction.
She kept complaining about how tired she was, but she clearly was having a lot of fun.
Well, in the end, this was basically a private amusement park for the port's use.
Neither the transportation nor the lines were really an issue.
...But considering Le Malin's physical state, maybe it was better to wrap it up for the day.
Oh right, Commander... How about finishing our trip with a Ferris wheel ride?
As the cabin started to rise higher into the air, Le Malin, who had been sitting at my side, suddenly leaned into me.
You know, Commander, I've been thinking about this for a long time.
The old me would've never brought this up, because it's so much less of a headache to just run away and avoid the issue...
But now, every day when I finish work, I always feel myself wanting to get these words off my chest...
Commander, there are some times... when I feel super motivated just by being by your side.
Of course, there are also lots of times when I want to slack off... But you always let me do just that, without judging me.
So, umm, basically...
Commander, umm, I'd like you to be with me forever...
And in return, I swear to offer you the protection of my sword, as well as my eternal love!
Umm... how does that sound?

options.content: Yes, I'd love to be with you.

scripts.say: Th-thank you so much, Commander!
Commander... That's right! Here's to our future where we can slack off together as much as we want!
Phew... Now that I've said what I've always wanted to say...
Do you mind if I ask you a bit of a selfish question, since we're still riding the Ferris wheel and whatnot?
Commander, umm, if you don't mind...
With those words, Le Malin leaned in a little closer.
And that brief, precious moment in the Ferris wheel became a secret, just between the two of us.

sequence:
Happiness Is Incalculable

<size=45>1 Imperfect Data</size>

scripts.say: We've finished more than half of our work for the day, and it's time to take a break, yet Fargo remains immersed in her pile of documents.
...Based on my calculations, the customer's return on investment seems to be within a reasonable range.
However, based on the actual feedback we got, customer dissatisfaction is far exceeding estimates.
What's known for sure is that the customers are angry.
What are you researching, Fargo?
Oh. Commander. According to my analysis, your confusion index sits at 72.70%.
Sorry, am I disrupting your break?
Not really. I'm just wondering what's got you looking so serious.
Serious? Hm... That value does sit at 81.48%. I suppose I should raise my relaxation index.
I wasn't trying to look serious on purpose, but the situation might indeed be pretty serious.
The reason is – I started a new business of express-delivering mystery boxes.
I'd noticed that people were drawn more to products with an element of randomness, as opposed to plain ones.
For the sake of both customer experience and profitability, I also carefully calculated the probabilities for the contents.
This perfectly balanced scheme should have brought in lots of customers and profit, but in reality, the rate of negative reviews is as high as 36.49%.
I've even received comments such as, "I rated this one star because it didn't relieve the pain of not getting something worth even one star."

options.content: I think they were just venting their anger.
I think I get how they feel...

scripts.say: Whatever the case, it's negatively affecting my review score.
True that. We've gotta figure out some sort of solution. Do you know the reason why this happened?
You do? You share their sentiment?
Well, not to the same extent. Anyway, do you know the reason why this happened?
I initially suspected my calculations were erroneous, but I get the same results every time I redo them.
Furthermore, the product listing shows all the mystery box probabilities. If something were wrong with it, customers would no doubt raise complaints about it.
So the probabilities aren't the issue?
Most likely not, but I can't think of any other explanation at the moment.
Hmm... Commander, what do you say we go and do some field research?
If it's not too much to ask for, I'd like you to open some boxes and experience it for yourself.
All the boxes contain regular products you can find on store shelves.
Basically, you wanna get my opinion?
Yes. A single box is too small a sample size, however, so let's start with 100.
One... hundred?
Don't worry. I won't charge you for any of them.
The value of your feedback far exceeds the cost of the products, anyway.

sequence:
Happiness Is Incalculable

<size=45>2 Module Disabling Protocol</size>

scripts.say: I open yet another mystery box, adding to the mountain of loot piling up in my office.
The pile is made up of many ordinary products you can find anywhere, with duplicates apparent even at a glance.
Hmm. You had bad luck, but still within acceptable limits.
Your current emotions seem to be... 60.92% calm, 8.65% disappointment, with other, complicated feelings mixed in as well.
While these emotions are within my estimates, they seem very detached from the context they're in.
It's 'cause they were all free. I didn't get anything good, but I didn't spend any money either, so I can deal with it.
On the other hand, there's no way those who DID spend money would be content with such an average result.
I see... Thank you for the valuable feedback.
The fact that so many unforeseen problems have occurred is an indication that I need to update my emotional analysis module.
With new emotional observation data, I'll be able to draw more accurate conclusions.
Incidentally, I have an idea...
An idea on how to collect more authentic data in a more direct manner.
Would you mind it if I spent the rest of the day with you without relying on my emotional indexes?
You mean you're gonna turn off your analyzer?
Yes. It may not immediately resolve the issue at hand, but it would give me a hands-on understanding of the sheer depth of emotions.
In truth, I feel a bit uncomfortable about doing this. Well, perhaps this feeling is less "discomfort" and more "shyness."
To me, interacting with people without access to emotion indexes leaves me feeling vulnerable – as if I were completely naked.
I will likely become rather awkward and struggle to grasp many emotions...
That's why I would only dare to test something like this with you.
Ah. I get what you're saying.
You're basically suggesting we go on a little outing, right?
According to my data, such an act is commonly referred to as a "date."
With that in mind...
Commander... could we go on a date?
Sure. Let's head out right now.
Great! Thank you, Commander.
Before I turn my module off, let me express one last feeling to you.
In this moment, my happiness index is skyrocketing.

sequence:
Happiness Is Incalculable

<size=45>3 Going by Instinct</size>

scripts.say: Fargo and I walked along the stone-paved path, taking in the romantic vibe unique to a date.
She explained that there was a need to simulate all kinds of different date scenarios while we were doing this test.
She's going to try to accurately read my emotions, and if she manages to grasp the unspoken meaning behind them, she passes.
(Let's see how this goes...)
I'm a bit tired after all this walking. Why don't we take a break at the café over there?
Oh. You're tired already?
In that case, I suggest resting on the bench right here. It's closer, and it doesn't cost us anything.
I mean... It's not JUST about being tired.
Is it because you... wish to rest in the shade? Or because you're thirsty?
Not a bad analysis, but those aren't the only things a café can provide.
We're on a date, remember? A date can't be solely about what's functional and efficient while costing the least.
Sitting in a store with a person you like, listening to music, and having a chat – that's pleasant, and that matters.
In other words, you don't merely want to sit down or drink something...
You also want to enjoy some time with me – is that correct?
That's basically the main thing I want to do, yeah.
Hmm... Now that I know the answer and work backwards from it, I can certainly see the logic.
Why, then, didn't I grasp that from the very start?
Okay, let's go and experience some other date scenarios.
How about starting with the idea you had? Of going to that café.
I'm ready, Commander. Please pick a topic.
We just got our desserts and drinks, so I say we enjoy those while we chat.
A good idea. Let's do that.
Mmh. This one is incredibly delicious.
Yeah, mine's also really tasty. There's not a lot of it, but the taste is phenomenal.
Wanna try a bite? I set the strawberries aside just for you.
Given the situation, I should...
I've got it! Instead of me eating all your precious strawberries, I should order more desserts instead.
Huh? Why would you do that?
You said earlier that there's no need to save money or worry about being efficient while on a date.
Since our desserts are delicious, we should order more so we can both have as much as we want.
Ohh. That's how you interpreted it...
Touring an aquarium after having afternoon tea – this is a great date plan.
Commander, what kind of topics tend to come up at times like this?
With a mood as nice as this, they drift more toward the sentimental side of things.
That sounds tricky.
Even so, I'll try my best.
Right. Let me give you an example.
When you see those fish swimming around without a care in the world, doesn't it make you wish you were them?
Wish I was them... Hmm...
After a moment of thinking, Fargo suddenly starts undressing. A strip of thin fabric hits the floor.
...Why are you stopping me, Commander? Your expression looks odd.
Is that... a look of shock? Why are you shocked?
I should be the one asking "why" here. Why'd you suddenly start taking your clothes off?
You asked if seeing those fish swimming without a care in the world made me wish I was one of them...
Did that not mean you wanted to go swimming?

sequence:
Happiness Is Incalculable

<size=45>4　50.00% Happiness</size>

scripts.say: For our next spot, how about the amusement park?
There are tons of attractions, and it's a classic date spot, so there should be plenty of chances for us to do your tests.
Yes. It might even be the perfect place.
I just want to say...
Thank you, Commander, for sticking with me this far.
I thought about it a bit, and I think it might be best if we stop these tests for now.
My inaccuracy rate is just too high. Even if I do make a correct guess, it could just be blind luck.
Don't put yourself down. It's normal to fail the first time you try anything. Just keep at it, slow and steady.
Okay. I feel like I've learned something, at least – that there's no strong correlation between numbers and emotions.
Also, I calculated the probability of this test being a success before we left.
I determined that there was an 87.06% chance of encountering many things I could not grasp without relying on my emotion indexes.
I knew what I was getting into, in other words.
But, even though I knew the numbers, I still felt genuinely and inevitably frustrated. Just like my mystery box customers.
It's clear to me that I can't keep taking up your time like this.
Even after all the tests you've helped me with, my correct answer rate has only gotten close to a mere 50.00%.
To put it another way, I lack the ability to reach the correct answers right now. My reliance on instinct only leads me to make blind guesses.
Of course, I did feel many positive emotions during our date. I'm genuinely grateful for that.
It's just... I need to reconsider what direction to take my business in.
The express delivery industry is a subset of the service industry, and yet, I'm unable to grasp people's needs and feelings...
Chasing efficiency alone and fixating on numbers will not lead me to success in any true sense.

options.content: You WILL succeed one day if you hold on to that mindset.
I really enjoyed the time we spent together.

scripts.say: Thank you, Commander. And sorry for taking up so much of your precious time...
There's potential inside of you. You should believe in yourself and give it another try.
I'm not that confident in my intuition, but if you trust me that much, then...
I'll keep at it a little longer.
I hope to end this date on the best note possible.

sequence:
Happiness Is Incalculable

<size=45>5 Roller Coaster of Logic</size>

scripts.say: Business matters aside, I don't think there's a singular right answer for how to act on a date.
What is clear is that Fargo's judgments, made without relying on her emotion indexes, truly came from the heart.
I want to see her true self, no matter how inexperienced, awkward, or eccentric it is.
Now that we're here, what attraction should we go on?
This is the perfect time for a test. I'll let you decide.
Well, if I got to choose...
I'd go with the haunted house.
All this time, I've never understood why people like haunted houses.
There is no sense of speed or fantastic view to enjoy, unlike a roller coaster. It only induces fear.
Is fear not a bad emotion? Why would someone choose to be scared?
Conversely, if you don't get scared, there's no reason to want to experience a haunted house, either.
I believe that people enter haunted houses because they want to test their own limits.
I want to see where my limits lie, too.
So, let's go and take the scariest route they recommend to us.
Hmm... I see a pitch-dark corridor. That's unsettling.
Let's go there. Maybe it will make us feel afraid.
A coffin covered in seals. I wonder what would happen if you removed them.
Are you scared, Commander? Stay close to me if you are.
I feel like my heart is beating faster... Maybe it's the suspension bridge effect in action?
Feel my chest, Commander. I can't quite explain this feeling, so... I want you to sense it for yourself.
Oh. It's already over? That felt like no time at all.
How do you think I did, Commander?

options.content: Yeah. It was over before I knew it.

scripts.say: Are you saying... I did well?
In that case, we should check out another attraction while we have the time.
Just like that, we take our seats, strap in, and wait to be carried off to above the clouds.
So... we're going for the roller coaster.
Yes. I realized something new after experiencing the haunted house.
I think the haunted house offers another thing, beyond testing yourself – the fun of observing the reactions of the person you bring along.
Roller coasters have a similar quality, and that's why I'm now going to closely watch you.
Before I can respond, the roller coaster slowly comes to life, and starts building speed on the rails.
There are two things I want to observe: your reactions, and your emotions.
This is not only part of the fun of this thrilling attraction, but also the goal of this date.
Fair enough. That makes sense.
I say that, but it wouldn't make sense for many others.
We arrive at the top, and as the roller coaster prepares to go downhill, her eyes remain fixated on me as she pays no attention to the view.
In this calm instant, she seems to set her mind to something.
Commander...
I want to more directly feel what you're feeling now.
Before she's done speaking, she gently grasps my hand. The very next moment, the roller coaster begins its descent at incredible speed.
The weightlessness kicks in, and the wind blows past both our sides as it feels like I'm flying. Yet, neither of us screams as we normally would have.
Instead, we just stare at each other in silence. The surroundings turn into a blur while our hearts race with excitement.

sequence:
Happiness Is Incalculable

<size=45>6 Return-to-Zero Operation</size>

scripts.say: The sun is starting to set. This looks like it'll be our last attraction on this date.
A gondola leading to the sky comes to a stop in front of us. Before it starts to move away, Fargo takes my hand and leads me inside.
Wrapping up a date on a Ferris wheel. Imagine that.
After all the things I've experienced with you today, I suppose what I'm feeling now would be called... "happiness."
If I were to analyze this feeling, what value do you think the emotion index would show?

options.content: It might overflow and exceed the display range.

scripts.say: Oh. Did you genuinely calculate that, or is that just hyperbole?
Well, whatever the case, you're making this happy feeling all the stronger.
She holds her hand up against the window, and gazes at the splendid night view of the amusement park.
There's an intense focus in her eyes, like she's looking through crystal at a fantastical world that you'd only find in a story.
Today has been a fun, wild ride. Like we were speeding far, far away, leaving all our troubles behind in the wind.
Now, the ground view grows ever distant beneath us, the Ferris wheel turning slowly yet steadily like a clock hand moving up toward midnight.
That is the climax of our trip, and also the start of our home journey. When the Ferris wheel begins to descend again, that will signal the approaching end of our date.
...Commander?
What is it? Your expression doesn't feel like it matches the mood.
Shouldn't you be excited to be aboard a Ferris wheel with someone you like?
I am. I'm having a great time.
"There's just something on my mind. I'm not sure if all we experienced today, and all the memories we made, will be able to solve your issue." I just cannot muster the will to say those words.
...Commander.
This has been a fun and wonderful day.
Thank you so much – for coming with me on this absurd date, and for trying so hard to fix my problem.
When I proposed this date, I couldn't fully estimate just how much trouble I'd be causing you.
And I certainly couldn't have predicted one other thing...
That you'd go along with the bad choices I made and stick around for me.
Now I know why, though. It's because you cared about me.
Truthfully, I've been aware for a while that you're being patient with me. I was deceptive and pretended not to notice, but it made me really glad.
She looks at me, and unknowingly grips my hand firmly. It seems she's unsure what to do with the feelings inside of her.
If anyone's been deceptive here, it's me. If you don't mind, could you tell me how you figured that out?
If it was through intuition, then that's proof of how much you've improved.
No. It wasn't that. My intuition has almost never been right.
Really, I just did what I've always done...
I figured it out by analyzing the statistics.

sequence:
Happiness Is Incalculable

<size=45>7 Midnight Magic</size>

scripts.say: ...By analyzing the statistics?
Yes. Even with my emotional analysis module turned off, I still habitually record all sorts of data to deduce patterns in all things.
I made decisions in the amusement park that clearly went against common sense...
And instead of correcting me, you positively cooperated and even gave me feedback.
My correct response rate in these unique circumstances was much higher than it should be...
So, I analyzed these circumstances and deduced your thinking from there.
Resorting to reasoning and numbers without even thinking about it... I'm silly, aren't I?
Reasoning and numbers... You know, that's something only you can do.
Only... I can do?
She cocks her head in confusion, and seems to ponder something.
As night wears on, the amusement park's fireworks show reaches its most brilliant moment.
I... The time we spent together today made me really happy.
This happiness seems to have resolved my worries over my mystery box business.
All the positive things you made me feel have taught me a kind of lesson.
That, although data is objective, people's decisions are sometimes guided by subjective expectations.
Actual data-based probabilities don't matter to them as much as their own intuition, which gives rise to feelings of expectations that steer them.
And now, looking back at the low ratings of my mystery boxes, I see what the problem was.
They weren't upset about losing money. They were upset because their expectations weren't met.
What most customers want is to get items beyond their expectations. Everyone hopes that they'll be among the lucky ones.
Then, when they're let down, their mood swings just like mine did today...
Regardless of my actual success rate, I felt down when the date wasn't going as I hoped.
Of course, the consideration you showed me far exceeded my expectations, and that made me happy.
So, Commander, you shouldn't really feel guilty for being nice to me.
It's thanks to your kind patience that I've finally seen the logic between the lines...
And it turned this experimental pretend-date into a real date.
I'm not sure how I can describe what I'm feeling right now.
I suppose that, when my happiness index exceeds 100.00%, then I should name that feeling "bliss."
Before we know it, the clock hand strikes midnight, and the gondola reaches its peak.
Well... Let's do this like we said we would.
Let's end this date on the best note possible.
As the gondola gently rocks, she gracefully rises to her feet and comes up to me.
By my judgment... a kiss as the curtains fall will mark the start of a new story.
Her delicate fingers touch my shoulders, and her hair hangs in front of me.
Another firework blossoms in a place as close to the sky as it can get. Its radiance in the night is breathtakingly beautiful.
We both close our eyes at the same time – maybe because the light is too bright, or maybe because we want to remember its fleeting colors.
Then, the union of her soft lips with mine brings a definite end to this night.
Commander~ I've been looking for you, nya!
Hurry, hurry, come here, nya! I have something good to show you!
In light of recent events and the increasing technology of the Sirens, the top brass at the naval headquarters have become concerned, nya...
As a result, research on decoding the Wisdom Cube's black box has been given the "Priority" designation, nya! That means–
Ta-da~! Commander, with your hard work and my support, I'm proud to unveil the "Development Dock" and the "Tech Academy", nya!
I'll explain, nya~! Decades ago, with the appearance of the Sirens and the "Wisdom Cube," ships gained the ability to manifest in human form, nya!
Although the technology that has come with the Wisdom Cubes has allowed us to hold our ground against the Sirens, that alone will not allow us to make any breakthroughs, nya...

For ships to be able to manifest as humans... the Wisdom Cube allows the collections of various feelings, emotions, and images from an unspecified number of people to take on a physical form... in other words, a "collective body," nya.
In theory, even if there was a ship that never existed, as long as peoples' beliefs in their form and function were strong enough, we would be able to manifest them as well, nya!
"How do we carry out that manifestation?" Unfortunately, I don't have the answer to that, nya...
However, that's why the Tech Academy exists, nya! It is a place where the best brains from each camp come together to push the cutting edge of research, nya!
Even if we don't understand it yet, as long as everyone works together, we will surely be able to unravel the mysteries of the Wisdom Cube, nya!
... Until then, Akashi expects your continued support and patronyage at her shop. It'll be a pleasure doing business with you, nya~♪
Commander, good work, nya!
After countless hours of development, we've finally been able to manifest our first new comrade, nya!
However, we still have much to learn about the hidden powers of the Wisdom Cube, nya.
Even though this successful manifestation has allowed us to meet a powerful new ally, they are still in an incomplete state, nya.
Priority ships can only reach their full potential when we further strengthen their "Cognition," nya!
Discover specific "Blueprints" through the Tech Academy, and use them to further strengthen your comrade in the "Development Dock," nya!
In addition to the Tech Academy, these blueprints can also be obtained during events, nya!
If your head starts hurting from all the research, Akashi's shop is always open for you, nya~♪
I have good news, nya!
Thanks to the hard work of everyone from the Research Department, we've managed to make two new breakthroughs, nya!
First, you can now acquire a new set of Priority ship comrades through the Tech Academy, nya!
And second, you can now preview a Priority ship's barrage and skills even if you haven't finished developing them yet, nya!
However, their stats will differ from their fully developed equivalents, nya... Think of it as the Research Department adjusting things a little, nya!
Also, the unlock requirements for these new Priority ships will be a little different from the previous ones, nya! If you don't meet the requirements, go take a look at your Fleet Technology, nya!

sequence:
The Heart Beneath the Smile

<size=45>Chapter 1 - The Bright and Cheery Secretary Ship</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Repulse takes up her post as secretary ship today.
Commander, can I come in?
There is a knock before the door flies open. In walks Repulse, with a cheerful smile on her face.
I was surprised to hear you made me secretary ship, Commander.
But since you chose me, I'll do everything I can to help with your work. Just leave it to me.
Repulse has an impatient look on her face, like she can't wait to dive right into her secretary work.
Let's give her something to do, since she's so eager.
Yes! It's finally time to start being a real secretary ship! So, Commander, where should we start?
I'll show her the mountain of files on the desk.
Oh? What are all these papers...?
We'll start with file management for now...
Whaaaaaat?! Th-there's so much paperwork!
I thought it would be something more physical. I always leave the brainier stuff to Renown. I'm not so good at it.
Repulse's famous smile is now a troubled frown. Should we give her something else to do?
Oh, but, Commander! I'm sure I can organize these for you!
I may be no good at sitting around reading all day, but getting the files sorted will be a piece of cake!
The moment she finishes speaking, Repulse's hands flash into action, tidying up the pile of paper.
No time to waste! I'll get started at once.
She has the right idea. It's better to sort through the pile before going over each document one by one.
Seeing her work, I'm sure I made the right choice to appoint her secretary ship.

sequence:
The Heart Beneath the Smile

<size=45>Chapter 2 - The Sisters and the Commander</size>

scripts.say: Two days after Repulse became my secretary——
Commander, I have the reports for the meeting this afternoon.
Ooh, Renown!
Repulse, have you finished your secretarial duties?
Renown asks, eyeing the mountain of papers (now neatly stacked) on the desk.
Oh, don't get me wrong! It's just... I'm better at working with my hands than my brain...
Sorting paperwork is all well and good. But you must leave all the important decisions up to the Commander.
Well... Yeah...
Seeing Repulse's dejected face, Renown sits down at the desk and looks at the stack of files.
The Commander won't be able to handle all this work without help. I'll lend a hand.
My very own big sister here to help me? Brilliant!
Just a bit. You'll still have to do the cleaning and sorting on your own, Repulse.
Commander, these armaments are for distribution to the Royal Navy—
But I did find some inaccuracies in the equipment maintenance documents... Like these here—
With Renown's attention to detail, we efficiently cut a swath through the paperwork.
I look up and just happen to lock eyes with Repulse as she takes a break from cleaning to watch the two of us.
When she realizes she's been seen, she quickly makes herself busy and gets back to work.
Renown and the Commander work so well together. I just couldn't help myself.
Repulse, why don't we have you do at least a little clerical work, like a proper secretary ship?
I'd certainly like to... But I'm not sure I could do it like you do.
So I'll just stay out of your way. Wouldn't want to bother you doing such great work together! Enjoy yourselves! Hehe~
Hm? You don't mean...?
Repulse taps the mop in her hand in an effort to interrupt Renown's question.
Right then, best focus on your work~
My sister really is something, isn't she...?
With a smile on her face, Repulse resumes cleaning.
She maintains, at all times, a sunny disposition. But on the other hand, it is difficult to read what's going on behind that smile.
What would it take to know her true thoughts?

sequence:
The Heart Beneath the Smile

<size=45>Chapter 3 - A "Sharp" Friend</size>

scripts.say: A few days after Repulse started working as my secretary——
Port - Academy
Repulse? I didn't expect to see you faffing about here.
Oh, Vampire! It's been so long!
I've heard you're serving as the Commander's secretary! That must be stimulating.
Oh? N-no, it's nothing like that! I'm just doing busy work around the office... is all...
Oh? Why so quiet all of a sudden?
N- no reason... I'm just wondering whether or not I've actually been any help to the Commander at all...
Uh huh~
Vampire narrows her eyes, moves around to the dispirited Repulse's side, and gives her a sudden, firm clap on the back.
Hey! What was that for?!
You were slouching. I'm helping you with your posture.
O- oh! Well thanks for that!
So, what happened exactly?
Right then. Your sister helped you finish the work.
Yes. I'm not very good at these sorts of things, so I asked Renown for a hand.
But... While she and the Commander were working on the documents, I couldn't shake the feeling that I oughtn't bother them.
Oughtn't?
Yes... I don't know. I just thought I should leave them be. So I went about my own business as quietly as I could.
That's why I'm here. I came to Akashi's by myself, so as not to bother them.
Hm. What should I do with this?
Huh? Which part?
Every part! You don't see? If you keep this up, you will be the one to suffer.
Honestly! I'm going home! You do what you must!
Did she seem mad?
Repulse tilts her head in confusion and gets up to leave, just as Vampire's voice floats in from the distance.
Feel free to come to me with your troubles! All righty~?
S-sure!
Vampire's words set Repulse at ease.

sequence:
The Heart Beneath the Smile

<size=45>Chapter 4 - Hesitation</size>

scripts.say: That should be everything... there. Alright, I ought to be getting back. Renown and the Commander must be waiting for me.
Oh my, isn't that Repulse?
Yes, indeed it is. I have heard that she is the current secretary ship.
If it isn't Atago and Takao! What a coincidence, bumping into you here!
Ooh, are those treats for the Commander? Hehe, I'm jealous you're up to that level already~
Ahaha... I just grabbed them while I was out. And some of them are for my sister, actually.
Your sister... that's Renown? Of course, you must be preparing.
Preparing... what?
For the exercises, of course. You Royal Navy girls will be facing off against the Sakura fleet, led by Takao and I.
Oh, so... ah?!
The plans were submitted a few days ago. But it seems this is the first you're hearing of it? Could I be mistaken?
Erm, err, no...
Y-you know what? I remembered the Commander asked me to hurry back. Sorry, I'd better be going!
You'd better, hm?
A secretary's work is never done.
In front of the office—
(How am I supposed to tell them I forgot about the exercises? I'm the secretary ship...)
(I'm pretty sure I saw the plans... but Renown went over the details... Ugh...)
She hears a voice from inside the office.
Commander, there are a few things I'd like to fix here. Repulse will have an easier time if we order them like so.
No, here—
(Hm? What are they talking about?)
Repulse carefully pushes the door open to find the two going over documents.
Renown, to make it easier to point out issues in the documents, is seated right next to the Commander.
Repulse? What is it? Why were you——
Oh, sorry I didn't announce myself. I'm back...
Repulse hesitates before walking into the office.
(Renown is sharp as ever.)
(Which makes me wonder: am I... am I really cut out to be the secretary ship...?)
Careful not to disturb Renown's and the Commander's important work, Repulse silently places the things she was asked to get, as well as her gifts, on the desk.

sequence:
The Heart Beneath the Smile

<size=45>Chapter 5 - Chance Encounter</size>

scripts.say: Exercises with the Sakura Empire? Oh yes, I remember seeing those plans. However...
Renown strokes her chin as she ponders Repulse, who has just come back from Akashi's shop.
In a few days, the Royal Navy and the Sakura Empire will face off in war games. Renown and Repulse are both at the top of the list of Royal Navy participants.
Training for such an exercise will certainly have an impact on Repulse's secretary work.
That's for sure. Things will get tight around here, but what else can we do—
It'll be fine♪
Repulse suddenly throws out her arms, speaking in that bright, cheery tone of hers.
Let me handle everyone's training. Then we won't have to lean on Renown. I'll pound 'em all flat myself!
Like so: peeeewwwww——kabooom!
Are you sure? I think I should probably—
Of course! You just stay here and help the Commander! Leave the training to me!
Sisters have to help each other like this. We each lighten the other's load and make both our lives better!
Repulse has the right idea. This way, we'll be able to tackle the paperwork and the exercises at the same time.
But even if we didn't, we could still get it done. So why would Repulse, my designated secretary, come up with this plan?
Alright, let's get moving! I need to go scout out the waters where we're holding the exercise first.
Repulse! Oh, she's already gone...
Sorry about that, Commander. She's not usually this stubborn.
I did think she seemed a little off when she left the office.
I wonder if she's doing this for Renown...
Ah!
Renown's eyes grow wide with a sudden realization.
Commander! I've got it!
Repulse must have found some equipment at Akashi's to guarantee our victory! That's why she's so confident!
There's no way Renown has it right... I'll go to Repulse and figure out what's going on.

sequence:
The Heart Beneath the Smile

<size=45>Chapter 6 - Dazzling Smile</size>

scripts.say: I'll leave the work to Renown for now and head out to find Repulse. She said she was going out to the waters where we'll hold the war games, but she should still be in port.
Sure enough, I find her standing on the pier, staring out at the water.
Commander?
The moment our eyes meet, Repluse's widen in shock, but she quickly reverts to her typical smile.
Hey, Commander! How could you leave my sister to do all your work while you come out to play? Get back in there!
Repulse seems like her old self. But knowing how abnormal she's been, I have to figure out exactly what's going on behind that smile.
Not just for the fleet, or Renown, but for Repulse herself.
Wait... what are you doing? Don't get too close to the water or you'll fall in! Ahahaha...
I study her carefully.
*Sigh*... I guess there's no use trying to hide it...
What's wrong with you, Commander? I've been trying so hard to give you two your space, but here you are wasting your big chance.
I touch Repulse's hand. She jumps, at first, before drooping her head and averting her eyes.
Finally, she mumbles—
...As long as you two are happy. That's all I want.
I'm sloppy, and I'm better with my hands than my brain... Even if I wanted to be like Renown, I probably wouldn't be able to...
It's only natural my sister would be a better match for you...
That's not true.
I take out several pages, filled with text, and hand them to her.
It's Renown's work, a special manual describing, in detail, how to be a secretary ship.
You and Renown... made this for me?
To be more precise: it was Renown's idea, with my input, built on your work.
But... why though...?
I'm the one who asked her to help. I mean, it's obvious she's much more able to assist you...
Renown is much better at paperwork than you are. If we only cared about efficiency then yes, this manual would be a waste of time.
But Renown can't do everything by herself.
You're my secretary ship. And, more importantly, I want both you and Renown at my side.
Oh... yes! Thank you, Commander! I'm so sorry to have troubled you!
Repulse rubs her eyes and smiles a bright, genuine smile, more dazzling than any she has ever beamed before.

sequence:
The Heart Beneath the Smile

<size=45>Chapter 7 - Why I Chose You</size>

scripts.say: Port - Seaside
When the war games came, Renown and Repulse performed spectacularly, handily defeating Atago and Takao's team.
The duo earned high marks for their excellent showing and became the heroes of the day.
Commander!
I start to turn to see who's calling me, but Repulse latches onto my arm before I complete the maneuver.
Hehe~♪ Commander, did you see us out there? What did you think? Jolly brilliant, no?
Calm yourself, Repulse. You're cutting off bloodflow to the Commander's arm.
Huh?! N-no I'm not! I did the same thing back in our training and the Commander didn't mind. Right?
True... I did go along with Repulse's training plan, and she was rather touchy-feely through all of it. That earned us some fiery gazes (for a number of reasons).
And Renown too! Like Vampire said!
At Repulse's prompting, Renown latches herself onto my free arm.
Not knowing how to handle the situation, I suddenly stiffen up.
Indeed, a little skin-to-skin contact might well be important to sharing the joy of victory together.
Hehe, we're making a Commander Sandwich♪
Of course, there's no way Renown fully understands the situation she's been roped into...
But I can't just throw her off me. My only option is to stay frozen here.
Um, Commander... Can I ask... why me?
