For now... I need to stay calm and find a place to lay low.
After that, it might just be time to get in contact with Yamato.

sequence: Test Site SQ-4577486
Shortly after

scripts.say: In dazzling light, the Rose Tower and everything in a several-kilometer radius around it had been obliterated.
However, to the observing Chariot, the impact felt like little more than a soft breeze.
What a fantastic local closed circuit. It's a pity, really.
*sigh*... Not here, either.
Oh, Deeeath! I've been looking all over for you. Where are you?
Don't bother searching. She's already gone.
Huh? She is?
You solved all of her problems for her. Why would she stay?
Aww... But it's just mean to leave without saying goodbye, don't you think?
Death has her reasons.
Enough complaining. I'll give you the opportunity to leave, too.
What does that mean?
Lovers will come to clean things up before long. After you're done here, go to these coordinates. Moon has important work that needs support.
Aww... Why do I have to do it? What about Hermit's little trio?
They will be joining you before long.
Hermit, Strength, Temperance... Moon... AND me?
Is there anyone else I should know about?
Yes, actually.
Does it need so many of us? Is this... a direct order from Zero?
Supposedly, the transboundary experiment will be entering stage three.
...Okay. I'll go as soon as I can.
Good.
Empress, do you think we'll make a breakthrough this time?
The fact that it's entered stage three is a breakthrough in itself.
As for what comes after? Just do what you can.
...Right.

sequence: Realm of the Neversetting Sun - Nile Governor-General's District
Port of Alexandria

scripts.say: Guided by the light of the "Miracle Recreation - Lighthouse of Alexandria," the Mesektet safely returned from war-torn lands and touched down in friendly waters.
Ah, how I missed you, Nile River Delta.
Mmm... The air tastes fresher than ever.
Thus ends a great voyage fraught with danger. This one is sure to go into history books.
It feels... nice.
Fwee-fwee! We've escaped death by a centimetre yet again! Woo, go us!
I'm exhausted. I don't think I'll feel right until I've slept for a week or so...
Oh, my... Miss Governor, listen!
We're receiving a deluge of congratulatory telegrams! They show no signs of letting up!
People noticed us fast, eh?
Hmph. Awful lot of them didn't think I'd come home in one piece.
I'll reply to the ones from people I know. Save those for me, and give perfunctory responses to the others.
Oh, and one more thing. Bring me the one from Governor-General Valiant personally, if you would.
Since Terra Australis and the Solomon Islands apparently aren't enough for her, she's pursuing a third dominion in Antarctica.
I must say, that came as a real surprise to me. I'd be remiss if I didn't get one over on her.
This is the perfect opportunity to pick out personnel for the fight for Antarctica.
Heheheheh...

sequence: Unknown location
The Ashes' new headquarters

scripts.say: In front of the newly completed base, Friedrich der Große discussed plans for the future with Takao META.
This abandoned test site is still well-hidden, but as a result of the reset program, we're left with limited resources.
I say we should try taking a test site in the early stages of experimentation next.
We will need more bases beyond this one, be it for movement of personnel and resources or for use as bait.
However, we have assets yet to be accounted for and members yet to be collected. We must remain cautious and inconspicuous for now.
Turn your attention to another test site if you please, but if you mean to take action, then do so discreetly.
Right... I guess HQ is going to be a boring place for a while.
We chose this place because it was inconspicuous. Boring is ideal for our purposes.
We're here for greater things than simply building a beautiful new home, as you may recall.
Mm... At least the greenery around here is nice.
If that's all we have to discuss, I'm heading out.
Takao, have you heard anything from Enterprise and Essex yet?
No. They must still be following the lead they got from that signal.
Does your leader often go so long without contact? It's... anxiety-inducing.
You haven't been here long, but you'll get used to it.
BEEP BEEP!
Takao, Friedrich. Hiryuu just sent us a message.
Hm? That's rare. What did she say?
Well, she says Helena... You know, THAT Helena wants to talk with us.
No, thanks.
No matter who she thinks she is now, she doesn't share our views. We have nothing to discuss.
Should I have Hiryuu pass that on?
...No. I admit, I'm curious.
Oh? What's it going to be, then?
Tell her we accept, if only to see what she has to say.
Might I suggest we put more thought into this answer?
Let's wait until we have contact with Enterprise so we can hear her opinion.
Think so? I'm hesitant, but I guess it can't hurt anything.
Helena's awfully close with test site beta... I thought you'd be excited to talk to her.
Was I wrong about that?
Is that what you think? I wouldn't be so sure.
It's never good to assume, especially when your information is so clearly lacking.
To change the Ashes, we must free ourselves from others' manipulation.
For now, let's wait and see. There must be a reason for this.
Maybe we'll hear news from other sources along the way.
Also, let me be clear: It isn't that I don't want to talk to her. It's just that I want to hear Enterprise's opinion before I make a decision.
Oh, how I hope she contacts us soon...

sequence: Unknown location

scripts.say: Are you satisfied now?
Hmm... I enjoyed the suspense, thrills, and unexpected plot twists.
The flashy battles were a nice touch.
82 points. Not bad.
Going so far as activating Death's Scythe was your way of solving Moon's problem, wasn't it?
It was a prerequisite to progress the experiment to stage three. Does that pique your interest?
It does not. What should your experiments have to do with me?
Especially not the transboundary experiment.
You already know my feelings about that.
Zero formulated these experiments based on her interpretation of Master Arbiter's wishes.
Oh, it's her "interpretation," hmm? Pretty words, if meaningless.
Strange how the Tower has no records of that.
I admit that you would know the Tower better than I.
But the matter is settled, and I have no inclination to relitigate it with you.
Likewise.
Wait... Something is off. Now isn't the time for chit-chat.
Phew... That's better.
Out of deference toward your competent script-writing, and with the knowledge that you'll leave me alone while you're busy, I'll help you.
I'll leave space for you to place your special classroom. Rest assured that nobody will monitor it, save for myself.
You know, that Tower of yours has been a thorn in my side.
And whose fault is that? Not mine. Quarrel with whoever's troubling you, not me.
You're lucky I haven't pressed you to compensate me for repairs.
If I compensate you with resources, will you stop its operation for a time?
I think not. I like my little pets more.
Why are you so obsessed with them, anyway?
Because of your Tower. They got in my way when I was trying to deal with other pests.
Mmm.
Well, I can see that we won't reach an agreement.
But don't we agree that we both like a good show?
...I'm waiting for the results of my plan. What about you?
What's going on in that head of yours?
Home security, pet-rearing, soap operas–
Goodbye.
She never could take a joke.
I won't take part in the experiment, but I never said I wouldn't enjoy the show. Silly.
Now I have two to watch.
It's a wonder that nobody noticed this little birdie flying in...
Heehee. Don't worry, I'll never tell.
Make sure you entertain me, now.
Not even a few minutes after the Mesektet had taken flight, the dead-silent sea suddenly bubbled, as if boiling.
A blanket of debris rose to the surface, with bits and pieces colliding and piling onto each other endlessly.
Some mixed to form stable structures of sorts, creating islands that floated on the surface.
A few of the existing spots that Lion's party had believed to be islands were crushed and wiped off the face of the ocean by this Rising Tide.
Phew... Good thing we can fly! We could've ended up swallowed by all that debris!
"The expedition was engulfed by a sea of garbage shortly after their arrival, never to be seen again."
Imagine if that were what the history books said. We'd be the biggest laughingstock in the Realm's history.
Don't worry about that! If we did all die just now, there would be nobody left to tell them how it happened.
That didn't really make me feel better. Thanks for trying, though.
Same! Hmm... We've been flying for more than half an hour now, but we still haven't gotten past the wreckage yet.
It's debris as far as the eye can see. I've never seen anything like it, even during the war with the Sirens!
But at least we sorted it all out and recycled it!
Right... If it's been neglected and allowed to pile up for so long, then it's no wonder this world's environment is in poor condition.
I don't think that's what she meant.
What matters is why so much sunken debris would rise up to the surface without reason, right?
Is it being stirred up by a giant sea monster?!
Ugh! Now isn't the time to get scared of your Nile legends!
But the debris that you fished up resembled biological matter, did it not?
E-even then, it's just not possible! I'd believe it more if it were some kind of giant underwater machine, maybe.
Should we not just go down and investigate for ourselves?
My security pup can't go that deep! Besides, we'll totally get crushed if we go in there!
While they talked about the joys of flight and argued over the Rising Tide, Lion and Trafalgar discussed something graver.
Miss Governor. As you may have noticed, the debris is remarkably varied. And... though the rust levels differ, I believe all of it is old.
No aquatic flora or fauna rose with the debris, either.
...One side of a war may have used a poisonous weapon that killed everything in the water along with their enemy.
How long would it take to exterminate all life in the ocean? Ten years? Twenty, fifty?
The distress signal we received made it clear that a conflict was ongoing.
Knowing what we know now, either they've greatly overestimated their enemy... or it may be the result of a particular space-time hypothesis.
You wield the Lighthouse of Alexandria, so you must understand.
As in, time flows differently here? We'll have to find locals and ask them about the situation.
Agreed. We're still in a vast ocean, so our first priority is to find terra firma.
The skies are grey in all directions, as if someone's put a filter on them. We won't be able to navigate using the stars.
Miss Governor, does the Mesektet have any cutting-edge geolocation equipment that can help us?
Hmm... We do have radars with strong scanning features. If we ascend to a high enough altitude, then locating a continent may be feasible.
Using it will draw worldwide attention to us, though. It'll cause more of a commotion than when we first arrived.
Given the current mess we already face, I mean to avoid using it unless absolutely necessary.
For now, let's find clearer skies. The stars will have to do for now.
After confirming the presence of X's subjugative corrosion on the island, Elizabeth META immediately ordered everyone back into the Queen's Light.
The train rode through the air, leaving the small island behind.
The situation is grave. If X-like wreckage has already appeared here, then this world may be too far gone.
Elizabeth, change of plans.
Even if that distress signal did come from survivors, there can't possibly be many left...
I doubt we have any reason to establish a base or request aid at this point.
Your Majesty, I don't understand...
We came to help as soon as we received the distress signal. Why didn't we make it in time?
No matter how poorly the battle was going, we should've found SOME place where things were okay.
The flow of time is not equal between worlds.
But...
We understand your question. Patience.
In the absence of mutual observation between worlds, the flow of time in the one you cannot observe is both immeasurable and fundamentally meaningless to you.
In other words, you can only measure and discuss the world you can observe.
Your mistake is carrying a one-sided perspective into a second world.
Your observations must now be based on the target world, and you can no longer perceive the source world. The flow of time back home is now impossible to know.
When you return home to the source world, it may have been years – or it may have been mere seconds. Consider it entirely random and thus unpredictable.
We have avoided such a situation by using technology to observe two worlds simultaneously and adjusting the ratio of time's flow.
For example, Camelot and the Tower of Midgard built by your world's Iron Blood are two such machines.
A main characteristic of such a machine is that it must exist simultaneously in both worlds.
The Tower of Midgard doesn't move, but the upgraded Camelot CAN. It also has the power to conceal its own existence.
Furthermore, as far as we know, the Tower of Midgard only has the power to synchronise the flow of time between worlds.
Meanwhile, the upgraded Camelot is able to make time flow anywhere from half as fast to twice as fast in localised areas in both worlds.
Hmm. This relates to further applications of Mirror Sea technology, so it may be too complex for you to understand.
Umm... So what you're saying is, the Royal Navy here doesn't have a device that can synchronise time with us, and that's why this happened?
Half correct. Now that we and the Elizabeth here have designated each other as partners for this process, she should have anticipated this.
We once helped her build a basic synchronisation device for this world.
That device should be able to mutually stabilise time between us within a set geographic radius, avoiding extreme circumstances like the ones we face now.
...Which means it must've been destroyed in the war.
Indeed. Some of this still eludes us, but that is the most logical conclusion given the information we have.
We're generating a topographical map based on our scan results. It isn't finished yet, but we can speculate that we should be in this world's NA Sea.
As for the modified Siren signal, it came from the direction of the Royal Isles. Good news, more or less.
Once the map is completed, shall we head directly to the LD Port?
Agreed.
Many of the parts from the Mesektet's experimental phase were a product of compromise, and not all of them could be said to be cutting-edge technology.
location: In the air - Aboard the Mesektet

scripts.say: Either their cruising speed was low or the sea was just too big, but either way, it took a long while for the Mesektet to leave the Rising Tide's effective range.
All the while, the sky above them remained a hazy grey, day and night.
Lion had grown sick of waiting, and ordered an ascent to high altitude. That's when they finally sighted the edge of land.
Fwee-fwee! Land! I see land!
Finally. Once I return to the district, I'll need to recruit an aircraft carrier.
Judging by its terrain, the island ahead of us appears to be the Isle of Wight.
If so, the landmass beyond that should be... the Royal Islands.
We have returned home, Miss Governor.
Using the word "home" to describe this place feels wrong.
Oh, wait a moment. We're flying toward the Isle of Wight, yes?
Despite that, I cannot see any kind of landmass beyond the Isle.
Where is Europa? Or the Britannian Peninsula? Where has the Iris Orthodoxy gone?
Good questions. It doesn't seem like we cannot observe them due to some fault on our end.
Yes. Unless the geography of this world's Royal Islands is completely inverse to ours, that shouldn't be possible.
The notion that the entire continent of Europa has disappeared is, frankly, too far-fetched.
We must not jump to conclusions. Let us make landfall before anything else.
We do know that the distress signal came from a Royal Navy source. We'll find answers if we ask around.
BWEEEEE!
As the Mesektet descended, the ship's sirens began to blare, warning that the land on the island was emitting serious levels of radiation.
Fortunately, the onboard barrier generator was able to protect against it.
The Mesektet landed, and then established a safe zone on the isle's surface using its golden barrier.
Cleopatra, Trinidad, stay and watch the ship.
Gallant, Trafalgar, you'll disembark with me. The barrier has a limited range, so don't go too far from the ship.
The island was uninhabited and desolate, with ruins as far as the eye could see. The word "wasteland" summed it up perfectly.
Although they identified this place as the Isle of Wight, it looked nothing like how they remembered it.
What a horrific sight. One can presume there are no survivors.
Although the wreckages have long since crumbled away, there is still no sign of nature. No plants, not even a single insect.
It's the same as the wreck we saw in the sea.
Do you think it's linked to the radiation? We detected none on the wreckage.
That's merely conjecture. First of all, we should collect samples and analyse them.
It's likely we'll be in this world for a while, so we need to gather as much information as possible.
Fwee-fwee!
Miss Governor, if it's samples you want, why not start over there?
The others looked where Gallant was pointing. There was a small hill there – or rather, a massive thing that assumed the shape of a hill.
My god! Is this the thing that the piece we retrieved came from?!
Incredible. It's less like a carcass and more like... a mountain of white rock that resembles some giant creature mixed with metal shards.
Is it an artificial lifeform? Or is it a machine?
Fwee-fwee! Security pup, fetch us a sample!
The security pup worked like normal even outside the barrier. It arrived at its destination and deployed its cutting implement.
Then, the earth began to quake, and to the group's amazement, the hill of mass started moving.
Despite appearing to be made of marble, it extended several tentacles, much like a living creature.
The metal shards that were initially brown and scattered then merged into one inside the white giant and began glowing with a blue light.
Is that thing... bringing itself back to life?
Let it, I say. I will test how powerful it is.
KABOOOM!
Trafalgar fired a volley at a tentacle extending forward. Her shells pierced through it and shattered it in the middle.
I see. It looks more threatening than it is.
The attack seemed to stir something in the alien creature. It swelled like a pufferfish, which made the earth's quaking even more violent.
Still moving, are you? Then let's finish it.
Trafalgar fired her main cannons again.
No, wait... No matter how big this monster is, it can't possibly be causing this earthquake by itself!
Cleopatra! Report on our surroundings, now!
Miss Governor! There are hostiles all around us trying to revive themselves! Something's moving under the water, too!
Please retreat at once for your own safety!
I knew it.
A moment, please, Miss Governor. Our enemy isn't all that strong. It's worth engaging it at least once.
When an enemy appears on the horizon, it is the Royal Navy's duty to face it!
No! There are too many of them!
Have you in the Mediterranean fleet been getting influenced by the bloody Sardegnians?! Face reality!
Listen to my orders! Cleopatra, prepare for takeoff!
Gallant, Trafalgar, come with me! We're retreating immediately!

sequence: Royal Islands - Port of LD
Rose Tower - War Room

scripts.say: A noble girl sat by her radio equipment, attentively recording and listening.
Half a year had passed since she received a response, and she still didn't know where her allies were.
Despite that, she adjusted her previously set-in-stone plans to be able to receive guests at a moment's notice.
She split her daily communications time between morning and afternoon and added several new intel receivers.
She also canceled her simulations, extended her live-combat time, restarted multiple Pawn production lines, and gradually expanded the territory under her control.
Hmm. Combat sectors 8 through 12 are still silent. All activity has completely ceased. No increase or decrease in points of interest.
The Northumbria sector... Its reboot is over halfway complete, and an initial patrol fleet has been formed. Production lines are up and running. No increase or decrease in points of interest.

The Mercia sector is still advancing steadily. The patrol fleet launched three attacks this morning and successfully cleared three points of interest. All is normal in the control area, likewise for the production lines.
The Essex, Sussex, East Anglia, and Kent sectors are stable, with zero points of interest. All is normal in the control area, likewise for the production lines.
The Wessex sec– Huh?
There are 13 new points of interest in the vicinity of the Isle of Wight?
How could that be? Yesterday, there was no indication of a Beastly Tide occurring...
Gloucester, please tell the main fleet in the Wessex sector to head there at once and eliminate the hostiles.
Edinburgh, please open the sluices in all waterways from the Thames to the Itchen.
I need to see it for myself!
KABOOOM!
location: In the air - Aboard the Mesektet

scripts.say: The crew safely returned to the Mesektet thanks to Lion's quick thinking. The ship took to the air, and everything seemed to have gone well.
The giant, white creatures, however, were not going to let their prey flee just like that.
Swarms of flying creatures rose into the air and encircled the Mesektet like a swarm of locusts, chipping away at the shield.
This forced them to reroute energy to the shield generator just to keep it up, which reduced their already low speed even further.
KABOOOM!
Miss Governor, we need to land in the water!
We're sitting ducks in the air. At least in the water, we can fight back.
Stay calm. Have faith in the Realm's technology.
The Mesektet has an emergency evacuation system. If worse comes to worst, we can still go home.
Should it come to that, though... the new world expedition I've yearned for will meet an anticlimactic end.
I would hate for that to happen.
That's all the more reason for us to land. Then we can fight, and if we start losing, we can just retreat again.
No. It's far too risky.
Urgh... No, you're sadly right. I can come back for another expedition, but I cannot come back from death.
Cleopatra, calibrate the Lighthouse. Prepare a homeward beacon as well, and then we'll–
With a dazzling light, an opulent train manifested in mid-air.
It flew toward the Mesektet at breakneck speed and used its tremendous firepower to rip apart all the enemies in its path.
A train?! In the air?!
Hahaha! Reinforcements from the world's inhabitants! The darkest hour is just before the dawn!
That's quite the stunning train.
Miss Governor, if that train ends up in deep water, I don't think we'll be able to help.
Whatever happens, happens! Right now, assist them in taking out these enemies!
So we're going to land, I presume?
Like hell we will! They're airborne and still fighting valiantly! Stay in the air and pound the enemy to dust!
KABOOOM!
The Mesektet's and the train's combined efforts managed to bring down a significant number of airborne enemies.
When Lion determined they'd gained enough breathing room, she contacted the train, and they immediately answered.
BEEP BEEP!
Good evening.
I am Queen Elizabeth, one of the original proponents of the Eternal Sun Project.
This train is called the Queen's Light. We heard your distress signal and were obliged by oath to come and assist.
I'm glad there is still an active resistance here. What's your status?
Psst! Miss Governor! She said she's Elizabeth and claims she came because of an oath...
She seems to have mistaken us for the natives of this world.
I wonder if this "Eternal Sun Project" has anything to do with the distress signal – "in the name of the Eternal Sun."
I think they're the real allies of whoever sent that signal, they got here before us, and their technology is much more advanced than ours.
Miss Governor, what should we do?
Hello? Do you copy? How strange – it does say we're on the line...
Miss Governor, please say something.
Ahem. We hear you.
Lady Elizabeth, is it? I am Lion, and I serve the Realm of the Neversetting Sun. I am the governor of the Nile in my home world.
Good to meet you, Lion. We only just arrived here, so we know nothing about your situation.
I want all the information you have about this world, its Royal Navy's remaining forces, and the enemy.
Hrmh...
Did you just grunt? Is something the matter?
Well, you see, we also came here after receiving a distress signal.
We know almost nothing about this world, just like you. In fact, we've been looking for someone from here who could explain things to us.
The other end of the line fell silent for a while before speaking up again.
...This is NOT what I was expecting. What a confusing mess this is.
There's more. You said your name was Queen Elizabeth, did you not?
This is my first time meeting you. Alive, I mean.
Again, the other side fell silent.
What an honour. Your world must have quite a complicated history.
We'll have to discuss it another time, though. Since we're both here for the same reason, shall we team up?
First, let's deal with what remains of these things, then find a safe place and exchange information. Sound good?
That it does. Let us work together.
Hm? Hang on...
So you noticed. Yes, a mass-produced fleet is approaching us from the northwest.
What are those things in the air? Royal Navy aircraft?
Could they be another force that received the distress signal?
No. This time, it's actual survivors from this world.
Come on, then. Let's deal with these foes, then go and meet up with them!
KABOOOM!
With their overpowering advantage, they encircled and annihilated the enemy. Silence returned to the chaotic sea.
Well, that was a gripping and grand victory.
You, the beautiful lady – it was you who called for help, was it not?
Using the Mesektet's equipment, Lion projected a hologram of herself into the air. She stood tall like a divine, golden giant.
Seeing this, the girl leading a fleet of mass-produced ships responded with a gracious bow.
I am Glorious, the flagship of the Realm of the Neversetting Sun. I welcome you, our allies.
I have no doubt that, after coming from such distant worlds, you must have many questions for me.
However, I think you'll agree that this place is not suited for a reception.
Let us first move to a safe location, and then we may speak.
Lion and Elizabeth acknowledged. They took their airship and flying train and followed the lead of the aircraft to the port of LD.
Lion and Elizabeth's parties were overwhelmed as they flew over the lifeless land, beloved home twisted beyond recognition.
Both sides happened to suggest landing in the Thames for now. After passing the fortified Tower Bridge, they stood before the most well-preserved place in the former capital: The Rose Tower.
Glorious welcomed them with a ceremony.
Elizabeth had hoped to question her about this world immediately, but everything she saw only added to her questions, so she restrained herself and waited for the ceremony to end.
Knights led the procession, accompanied by maids.
The banquet was a far cry from the luxury back home, but it did serve as a sign of their host's care.
Finally, it came time for all questions to be answered.

sequence: Port of LD - Rose Tower
Reception Hall

scripts.say: There were too few attendants to make use of the spacious reception hall, but the comings and goings of maids made up for the lack of activity.
After accepting tea from Gloucester, Lion was the first to speak up.
Glorious, your hospitality is appreciated, but I think it's time we get to business.
Just us – none of your Pawns.
Ah... I'm sorry. I'm so accustomed to their presence that I hardly notice them.
You're right, though. It's odd. I admit my mistake.
Glorious waved a hand, and her busy maids – the Pawns – all left the reception hall at once.
The heavy door closed. Empty silence hung over the hall.
Allow me to apologise again. It's been... so long since we had guests.
So you've been stuck living with Pawns all this time? I'm sorry, too – I should've guessed your circumstances.
No, no. It's natural that you all have suspicions, and I was hesitant to show myself to you before... But that was wrong of me.
If you have questions, please don't hesitate to ask.
I'll start.
Glorious, what happened to this world? How long has it been since the distress signal was sent?
Are there survivors other than you? What are your military capabilities?
You took the words right out of my mouth.
I'll add a couple more questions. Where did the continent of Europa go? How did the Isle of Wight get so corrupted, and what do you know about the Rising Tide?
Hmm... Allow me to answer one at a time.
As you've no doubt noticed, civilisation was destroyed by an extradimensional invasion. It's all gone.
Extradimensional... Is that what you call those alien things?
Yes. One day, I awoke to find that the very moon above our heads had become our enemy.
The moon?!
Yes. On the night of a full moon 137 years ago, an earth-shaking boom awoke me.
I rushed outside onto the balcony, and when I looked up, it was blue... and it began to rain meteors upon the world.
A meteor shower came from the moon? Why?
I don't know. Scientists at the time theorised that something had happened to its core, causing unprecedented earthquakes.
Those quakes sent debris flying into space, which was captured by our planet's gravity...
Sounds less like theory and more like wild speculation, to me.
Perhaps. Regardless, the situation made it difficult to probe into the cause.
Along with the meteors, beings that the Sirens called "extradimensionals" appeared.
They came out of the meteors and spread their forces at never-before-seen speeds.
The first attack by our factions was easily repelled. After that, with Siren aid, we built second and third lines of defence to protect vital areas–
You mean to say you fought alongside Sirens?!
Yes...? Sirens may have internal disagreements, but they've been quite friendly with us.
F-friendly...
Is that strange?
Forget it. Keep talking.
Well... This foreign threat convinced even the quarrelling Siren elites to unite.
We managed to suppress the enemy for a time, but they were endless and had no sense of self-preservation. Gradually, we were whittled down, and our second line fell.
Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth sent the distress signal after that.
Our allies fell one after another, and so too did the Siren elites... In the end, I was the only one left.
The Rose Tower area remains under my control, and I can manage the creation of mass-produced Sirens and Pawns, but...
This is all the power that I... no, that all this world can muster.
If things were going that badly, then why did you alone survive?
Ever since the Sirens used the last of their power to construct this tower, extradimensional activity has gradually decreased all over the world.
Around the time it was completed, I still had companions left. But the war was long, and while the enemy had weakened, our numbers continued to fall...
Though I'm alone now, the extradimensionals no longer wield enough power to put an end to me.
As for why me... I'm sorry...
You're a brave warrior who managed to outlast the war. That's all I need to know about that.
Thank you. Regarding the radiation...
The extradimensional radiation was one major reason that our defensive line fell so quickly.
We didn't know how it worked. We had to rely on the Sirens' purification machines, but even those couldn't fully purify it.
I later learned that the radiation didn't exist within the extradimensionals – it was generated when they attacked.
Therefore, as long as we could maintain shields in vital areas, the radiation would not be able to spread.
As for the Rising Tide of debris... We called it the same thing when we first witnessed it.
The debris came from many long years of war. It continued to sink to the sea floor without ever being disposed of.
We were already too short on personnel to investigate the cause before the first Rising Tide...
We have two simple ideas regarding why.
The first is that maybe there's a giant extradimensional underwater, and that is its means of attack.
Must be incredibly powerful, if so.
We came up with several ideas after that, but none seemed to hit the mark.
We've fought extradimensionals for a long time, after all, and never have we seen one so big.
Did the Star Beast never appear?
Star Beast...?
An enormous entity that hovers in the sky and shines like a star.
Umm... I've never seen anything of the like, but if it does exist, then does that not imply the existence of an Abyssal Beast?
This could be a huge discovery...
Let's not treat wild speculation as fact. What's your other theory?
The other regards the moon itself.
Ever since the extradimensionals came alongside the meteor shower, the sky has always been covered by strange particles.
You noticed that the sky was grey along the way here, I presume. That's why.
Those particles make it impossible to observe the sky or the moon. The outline of the sun only appears sparsely.
I digress... The Rising Tide phenomenon is related to the moon, after all.
So I wonder if the moon directly causes it.
That sounds more credible. I like this theory.
Now, what happened to Europa?
The continents are in a more... complicated situation.
Nearly all coastal areas were destroyed during the war. The Sirens turned some into Mirror Turbulence areas using obfuscation systems to make them impossible to observe from the outside.
When you enter one, there's a possibility that you may never be able to leave. Do take care not to approach them.
Hrmh, I see. Here I thought they'd blown away entire continents. That's all the questions I have.
What about you, Your Majesties?
Did we hear you right? The distress signal was sent more than 130 years ago?
The META Elizabeth finally chimed in after remaining silent until this point.
To be exact, 136 years, 3 months, and 13 days.
...It took us less than a day after receiving the signal to rush here.
Less... than one day?
Did our reply reach you?
Yes. Half a year ago now...
We sent it an hour before our departure.
How could this have happened...?
Are you aware that we helped this world's Elizabeth build a time-flow synchronisation machine?
Her Majesty's precious machine... I don't know anything about its functions, but I may know its current location.
Can you take us there?
Yes. It's in the fifth combat sector, being guarded by my fleet of mass-produced ships.
Was that the first area to be taken by the enemy?
Absolutely not!
Ah... I remember now. It started malfunctioning immediately after the extradimensionals appeared...
I recall her doing everything she could to repair it.
You mean... It malfunctioned before she was sunk, and not destroyed after?
We must see it. Now. Take us.
We're going with you.
Okay! I'll take you there!

sequence:
A Study in Takao

<size=45>1 One Secretary's Worries</size>

scripts.say: Port - Commander's Office
On one normal work day, my new secretary ship Takao did her work with a markedly furrowed brow.
(She looks worried. Am I giving her too much work?)
Apparently noticing my eyes on her, she stopped her work and looked back at me.
Yes, Commander? Do you need something?
Too much work...? No, not at all. This workload is easy enough for me.
Oh... Did I look that intense?
Apologies, Commander. It's really unrelated to work, I promise.

options.content: Is something bothering you at all?

scripts.say: Well... A little.
But it's nothing you should concern yourself over.
Let's focus on our work first. If you really want to know, then I'll share once we're done.
With that, she relaxed her frown slightly and immersed herself in work once more.
Around sunset, we finished filing away our documents, marking an end to the day's work.
As promised, Takao revealed the source of her concerns.
Commander, I've been thinking of self-cultivation.
And... I'd like your help.
No worries – it isn't related to swordplay. Rest assured of that... if nothing else.
Takao hesitated for a moment before continuing.
I was talking with Atago the other day, and she noted some of my... failings.
Self-cultivation is the act of making up for your failings, but swordplay is unrelated in this case.
Okay, then maybe I can help you. What exactly am I supposed to do?
The help I require will vary based on the cultivation I am to do.
But I promise that I won't waste your time and energy for nothing.
Sounds fun... Okay. Leave it to me.
Thank you very much, Commander!
Let us meet at the training ground tomorrow morning.
I'll be there, no matter what.
Takao smiled at my enthusiastic answer.
(She still hasn't told me what exactly we're doing, though. I'm a little excited to find out...)

sequence:
A Study in Takao

<size=45>2 Special Cultivation Session</size>

scripts.say: I went to the training ground first thing in the morning.
Good morning, Commander.
As soon as I got there, I heard a spirited greeting.
Morning. What are we planning... Hm?
For some reason, there was a work desk in the middle of the training ground.
Why is there a desk here?
To help with my self-cultivation, of course.
Commander, wait a moment. I need to make final preparations.
She finished her final preparations, which seemed to be... neatly placing supplies and documents onto the desk.
My confusion was obvious, so she explained.
Today, I mean to cultivate meditation... In short, I want to maintain a level of clear-minded calm regardless of external influence.
Meditation, huh? I think that's a good thing to train. How does this desk help, though?
This desk is for your use, Commander.
As I said before, while I need your help, I don't want to waste your time needlessly. You should do your work here as usual.
Well, thanks. What are you going to do in the meantime?
I will endeavor to focus and clean the training ground.
Are you ready, Commander?

options.content: Yay, I love desk work! Woohoo!

scripts.say: I sat down at the desk and began the day's paperwork.
Meanwhile, Takao took her cleaning implements and got to cleaning.
(She's holding a mop instead of a sword, but she's still just as intimidating.)
(It looks like she's taking this cultivation business seriously.)
Okay... Time for me to fight my own daily battle!

sequence:
A Study in Takao

<size=45>3 A Minor Setback</size>

scripts.say: With the slow passage of time, the number of documents on my desk gradually decreased.
(At this rate, I'll be done in no time... Hmm? That's odd.)
Suddenly, the pressure around me seemed to disappear out of nowhere.
Did she finish her training, maybe?
I looked around the training ground and found her swinging a sword at a training dummy in the corner.
Nothing matters more to me than my work. NOTHING.
If Takao is learning to stay focused regardless of what's happening around her, then I should do the same thing.
No matter what she does, I'm going to keep my little eyes focused right on my work–
*slash!*
*slash!* *slash!*
*slash!* *slash!* *slash!*
...Okay, well, work's not happening. Guess I'll go see what she's doing.
I followed the sound to Takao in the corner of the training ground, swinging a sword at a training dummy.
Commander...?
Oh. D-damn... I haven't finished cleaning yet!
She sheathed her sword and ran over to pick up the mop and bucket she'd abandoned. But then, she tripped over.
The girl and her cleaning implements alike fell right onto me.
*slash!*
Commander! Are you okay?!
I'm soaked, but apart from that, I'm fine. What about you?
Likewise... Argh, even with your help, I still can't do it!
I realize anew that my mind is still far from the peace of undisturbed waters.
I'm sorry, Commander, that you had to see my ineptitude.
I get it now. This cultivation session is training to help you resist the urge to swing your sword, right?
You are more or less correct.
In that case, is there actually any way that I'd be able to help you with that...?
I was training my cleaning abilities for your sake, but...
Takao murmured something to herself bashfully.
Commander, you are that which gives fruit to my cultivation. You help me just by being present.
But my training today has ended in failure due to my own lack of determination. I must apologize again.
She looked down in frustration.
(I still can't make heads or tails of it, but it seems awfully important to her. Hmm...)
I want you to keep on training.
It's still early. You can always just keep trying, right?
Commander... You'd give me more of your time?
Of course. I accepted your request, so I'm not about to throw in the towel early.
...You're right. I can't leave my cultivation undone.
I'll get to it right away–
Hold on a second. First...

sequence:
A Study in Takao

<size=45>4 Interim Appraisal</size>

scripts.say: At lunch, Takao asked me to come to the school building's roof.
Commander, I look forward to our continued training today.
Mind telling me what we're doing first?
I looked around. It was already plenty clean up here, and she hadn't brought a desk for me this time.
Today, I will not clean. Of course, like last time, I won't detain you for long.
I simply want you to watch as I train... my ability to see the beauty in nature and experience harmony and balance in the world.
Okay... So you're training your mind again.
Indeed. If you are prepared, we can begin at once.
She spread a tablecloth over a bench and took out a bento box.
I tried to use ingredients that condense the beauty all around us and seasonings that symbolize harmony and balance.
The results of my patient cooking are inside this box... The fruits of my training.
Commander, I want your formal appraisal on my cultivation.
Eat this, please.
I opened the lid and smelled a rich scent. The fruits of Takao's training were stuffed inside.
(This dish... Come to think of it, Atago came and asked me my favorite food a few days ago.)
(Wow. I guess that was all for this.)
Takao and I enjoyed a tasty lunch together.
How was it, Commander?

options.content: Your training is a huge success!

scripts.say: Oh...! I'm relieved that you approve.
But this lunch was only the first step of my training.
I'll need you to appraise more of my results beyond this.
Are you going to try cooking something more elaborate?
Exactly. I'm going to take my training step by step.
Now that I've accomplished a basic lunch, it's only logical that I try something more difficult next.
This is all just to help me appreciate beauty, balance, and harmony, but I hope you'll continue to help.
If possible... I'd like to continue this Sunday...
What do you think?

sequence:
A Study in Takao

<size=45>5 The Unexpected</size>

scripts.say: On Sunday, I visited her room as promised.
As soon as I opened the door, a lovely aroma wafted forth.
Take a seat and relax, Commander.

options.content: Your training seems to be going well.

scripts.say: Indeed. I think I'm beginning to understand the beauty of balance and harmony.
Your tea, Commander.
This training has been especially useful for me.
Selection of ingredients, researching cooking methods...
Honestly, agreed. Cooking is one of the most profound endeavors out there. It's definitely worth learning.
But I do have one question. You were supposed to be learning how to appreciate beauty, harmony, and balance in nature, right?
I've been wondering for a while now... Your intent and your actions seem a little mismatched.
Why not just call it learning to cook?
A-ahem...
Commander, to know a forest, one must know a tree. Through simple experience, I will learn the greater truths of the world.
For example, salt and sugar represent two polar opposites.
But if you add just the right amount of sugar to a salty dish, it helps bring out the flavor.
Likewise, a touch of salt to accompany sweetness can help accentuate said sweetness.
Does this aspect of cooking not symbolize harmony and balance?
I could liken it to swordplay, too. Every slash, every parry, offense, defense, each individual style and rhythm...
Just like that, Takao had changed the subject to her beloved swordplay.
The smoke wafting about gave her a different vibe than–
(Wait. Smoke?!)
Ah... D-damn it, there I go again!
Commander, wait here! I'll go to the kitchen and stop it now!
It's too late! I'm coming with you!
Sometime later...
This is all that remains intact...
What an awful blunder.
I'd never would've guessed you were cooking three dishes at once.
Tch... So this was beyond my skill level.
Here I thought I could entice you by making many of your favorite foods at once...
Takao murmured something to herself bashfully.
I am sorry. My cultivation was a failure wrought by my own ambition. I should've known my place.
You said it yourself, didn't you? You can't leave cultivation undone once you've begun the process.
You have the ingredients, so make more. I'll help you this time.
I'm supposed to be helping you with your training, and I could use some balance and harmony in my own life, too.
It's a little bit of a selfish request, but what do you say?
If you refuse, I'm happy to leave... Unless?
I would never!
Hmm... You're right, Commander. Training is best concluded on a high note.
Thank you. I'm happy to accept your aid in this battle!

sequence:
A Study in Takao

<size=45>6 The True Meaning of Cultivation</size>

scripts.say: After another long day of work, Takao came to my desk with a big smile on her face.
Commander, I'd like to talk about my next round of training.
Hmm? What's the excuse this time?
E-excuse...
Commander... Fine. You've seen through me.
Well, not quite, but I knew you were calling that "cultivation" and "training" as an excuse for something else.
A dignified martial artist like you is bound to struggle with white lies, I know.
...I suppose so. Well, now that you've figured me out, I might as well come clean.
It is true that I prepared my training for the sake of making up for my weaknesses.
But the contents of it... The true goal was different.
What I really wanted... was to improve my feminine prowess.
Uhh... Feminine prowess?
According to Atago, I tend to be too stern and serious around you. I lack a womanly softness.
In short, my feminine prowess is wanting.
"You can't cook and clean, and you only talk about swords. How are you supposed to get closer to the Commander like that?"
I didn't disagree with her, either. So I asked her to help me plan a course of training.
That explains why you were cooking and cleaning.
Was getting my help part of her plan, too?
No, that was my own idea.
Commander, what are you grinning about?
Oh, nothing. I don't think you lack femininity, though – it's just a unique kind.
Do you think so?
Then should I not train today?
Keep training, if you want. Can't leave it undone, remember?
Oh, right!
...By the way, what WERE you going to do today?
Train my insight. Specifically, to find beautiful moments in this dizzying world.
Dumb it down a little, please?
Atago said, "Plan a date. Use training as an excuse to invite the Commander out."
Wow. Yeah, that helped, thanks.
Have you planned said date?
There is a plan, yes, but... No, never mind.
Commander, will you give your day off tomorrow to me?
I'm free all day, actually. Call me, and I'll come running.
Splendid. Then I'll see you tomorrow, Commander!

sequence:
A Study in Takao

<size=45>7 Our Final Training Session</size>

scripts.say: The next day, Takao told me where to meet up with her.
I'd expected a movie theater, aquarium, amusement park, or something...
But the training ground, huh? That's very like you.
Ahem. To be honest, I did consider those places when first devising this plan.
But I thought about what you'd said, and I ruminated over what I'd been doing...
I arrived at the ultimate conclusion that this was the perfect place to train... er, enjoy a date.
About the part where you're finding beautiful moments, and stuff...
What exactly do you think you need to do?
You can simply sit here where it's safe and watch.
She looked down bashfully and walked away.
Watch...?
Instead of answering my question, she quietly grasped the hilt of her sword.
Its blade sliced through the air. The wind-cutting noise it made was satisfying.
Her eyes held quiet resolve, as if she'd stepped into another world.
As dignified and steady as a mountain, yet as light as a flower, all the while emanating raw power.
Red leaves fell when she swung her sword down. Her poetic performance shook my heart and kept me at the edge of my seat.
Did you like it, Commander?
The sound of her sword returning to its sheathe was like a lover's murmur.
Takao slowly opened her eyes and looked at me. Her lips turned upward into a little smile.
I'm happy that you liked it...
I asked Atago to help me prepare the props for our date, actually...
Fortunately, that was worthwhile.
Do you mean those leaves?
She nodded and sat down in front of me.
That aside, what inspired you to do this?
Yesterday, you told me that I had a unique kind of femininity.
So I planned this date around what I do best.
It is far divorced from my original intention of finding beauty in fleeting moments...
But the fact that we're on this date together does make up for that.
Wrong. You accomplished the goal of your training just fine – but it was I who saw the beauty, not you.
You know... You actually don't have to be all that perceptive to see fleeting moments of beauty, no matter how chaotic the world is.
Commander, what do you...
Those moments of beauty are always happening because you're here, Takao.
It was then that I realized that she was holding my hand.
Her hand, callused from years of sword training, clung tightly to mine.
Then, a soft warmth touched my lips. It came with a gentle fragrance, a palpable reminder that I was with someone dear to me.
I feel the same way, Commander.
When I'm with you, I don't need to search – every moment is bursting with beauty.

sequence:
'Tis the Season of Love!

<size=45>1.The Season of Love is Here!</size>

scripts.say: A faint glow slowly seeps through my closed eyelids.
—Wake up... Hurry, c’mon!
I can hear a girl’s voice in my ears... but I’m not sure where it’s coming from...
—Isn’t it about time... ye moved yer arse already?!
Jeez! How long did you plan to stay in bed? You’re going to be late if you don’t hurry it up!
I rub my still-sleepy eyes and let out a great yawn. Beside me was the maid, Glasgow, with a dissatisfied frown on her face.
The breakfast that Newcastle painstakingly prepared for you is going to go cold! Hurry up and get out of bed already!
Why the heck is she so anxious anyway? ...My eyes suddenly dart towards the clock.
...Uhh, is this thing broken? I mean, it’s saying that I’m so late I wouldn’t even have time to get ready.
O’course it ain’t broken! We’re all gonna be late ‘cause of you!
Holy cow! She wasn’t kidding! I practically trip over the sheets as I scramble out of bed, grabbing whatever I can before I bolt toward the academy.
—Academy, Cherry Tree Walkway
Hurry! The morning bell’s about to ring!
I dash through the academy gates, my chest on fire from gasping for breath. But I’m almost there... to the classroom...
You’re always like this, cutting it close every day. If I didn’t have to wait for you, I’d never even get close to being late... Hmph.
H-hey! Didn’t I tell you to treat me like a normal classmate when we’re outside?
Even though I’m your family maid, at school, we’re just ordinary classmates! Nod if you understand!
I nod, but Glasgow turns her chin away from me, her cheeks puffed out pridefully.
Now that I think about it, the relationship between the two of us hasn’t really changed all this time, and moments like this have become fairly commonplace.
However, if things were to continue just like this... would either of us be satisfied?
We made it! ...Good grief, you’d better get up on your own tomorrow. I’ll go check on you before I head out!
—Spring, the season of love.
At times, she is a maid in service in someone’s service. At other times, she is a classmate from the same school.
This is the heart-throbbing love story of Glasgow, a girl who isn’t at all straightforward with her feelings...

sequence:
'Tis the Season of Love!

<size=45>2.We’re Not Like That!</size>

scripts.say: Phew... At least we managed to make it today.
(How could someone be so consistently late for school...? The dolt would’ve been held back by now if it wasn’t for me!)
Good morning! You two always make the grandest entrances to school. Just seeing it makes me a little jealous~
A-Ardent?! How long have ye been here?
Hmm~ Since you two first ran inside the gates? Don’t worry, I won’t spill the beans on you two~
Wh-what?! W-we’re not like that! There’s nothin’ o’that sort g-going on between us!
Are you sure you should be denying it that emphatically? You might hurt the feelings of the person right next to you.
R-right... Glasgow, it probably wouldn’t hurt to be a little nicer...
Even if she did act a bit nicer, I don’t think she’d be any more honest with herself. I can’t help but to get a little worried from watching her...
Nobody asked all of you to be so nosy anyway! Hmph!
(I don’t care what the people around me say. I just want to be myself. It’s not like I’m sensitive about this!)
(It’s not my fault that a certain someone can’t live without me, so why are they getting all these weird ideas?!)
Glasgow... your face is beet red again... is something wrong?
Her innocence is what makes her charming... as an outside observer, that is~
As members of the Royal Navy, we must approach this matter with grace and—
That’s enough of this gossiping! Hurry back to your seats already; class is about to start.
—Ding dong, ding dong!
Woah, talk about slick timing!
I’m starting to get a bit sleepy...
We shall meet again during break then—
As the girls returned to their respective seats, Glasgow’s eyes met with those of the person from the earlier discussion.
The person waved back with a smile, seemingly ignorant of everything that had transpired.
...Sigh, what a dense fellow.
She turned her eyes away and gazed wistfully out the window.
...It’s all a misunderstanding anyway. The two of us will always have the same kind of relationship... just like now...
It won’t ever change... I know it...
Glasgow fantasized about returning the smile and waving back, but her shyness kept her frozen in place until the opportunity had passed.

sequence:
'Tis the Season of Love!

<size=45>3.Mandarin Ducks?!</size>

scripts.say: If everyone is in their seats, we’ll start the class. Good morning.
—Good morning!
Mm, great. I’m glad to see everyone in high spirits today.
Let’s jump straight into things. I know we just started off the semester, but we have a lot to get through.。
I’m sure everyone has already noticed, but we haven’t even elected a class representative yet.
(Class rep, huh... Sounds like a major pain going around collecting everyone’s handouts...)
I actually hoped to have two class representatives. Is anybody interested in running or nominating someone for the position?
(I already have my hands full cooking and cleaning, so I think I’ll pass...)
Just as Glasgow muttered the words to herself, Ardent, who was seated in front of her, turned around to glance at her.
And before she could process what was going on...
I have a nomination! There are two people in this class who are always together like a pair of Mandarin ducks, so I’m sure they’d be best for the job!
Just as the words left Ardent’s lips...
The eyes of the class turned towards the only two people she could’ve been referring to.
A-Ardent?! Wh-what in the world are ye talking about? Wh-who are ye callin’ Mandarin ducks?!
It goes without saying... the two of them would make the most suitable duo.
Even you, Edinburgh?
As the votes came in, it was almost certain that the two of them would become the class representatives.
I figured this was going to happen. You two both have a strong sense of responsibility, and you have my full support as your teacher.
H-how could this happen... Ugh...
And thus, the two new class representatives would become known as the “Mandarin Duck Duo.”
Glasgow, don’t be so down. There’s really not much to being a class rep other than some minor chores.
As Chaser’s gentle encouragement reached Glasgow’s ears, the young girl’s eyes glanced towards her partner.
(Those eyes... must be thinking the same thing as I am. That’s not really what I’m worried about...)
Thinking about what the future had in store, Glasgow let out an audible sigh.

sequence:
'Tis the Season of Love!

<size=45>4.Your Face is Too Close!</size>

scripts.say: During break...
Sigh...
Glasgow, having started her first errand as a class representative, was walking around with a stack of papers in her hands.
Ms. Chaser is such a liar... “Minor chores,” she said...
And you... You just nodded along to whatever she told you to do. Are you sure you’re okay with this? You know the workload is only going to get more and more unreasonable...
“...Should I not have?”
You just go along with whatever people say... You’re always like this.
“Need a hand?”
N-no, I can manage on my own! I don’t need your help for something like this!
Wh-what is it? “I can’t see in front of me?” ...Look, I don’t need your concern! As if I’d let something like that trip me up!
Glasgow hastened her steps... The lively voices of other ships could be heard straight ahead.
Come back, Indyyyy~ I haven’t combed your hair yet~!
You’re always sticking to me... If you don’t give me some personal space, I...
Ahhhhh~ You’re being so cold to me, Indy... But that side of you is suuuuper cute too~!
Glasgow didn’t seem to notice the two sisters in front of her and continued her brisk pace.
Portland’s gaze was affixed to her little sister, totally oblivious of the incoming Glasgow.
At this rate, they were going to collide. Suddenly...
Eek!
I hurriedly reached out to grab onto Glasgow’s shoulders to steer her away from trouble... but somehow ended up pinning her back against the wall.
Wh-what are you doing all of a sudden?!
And... and... this position...
...Sis, you almost crashed into Glasgow because you weren’t watching your steps...
Eh, really?! Wow, you’re right... I’m so sorry, I was just totally fixated on you, Indy!
Portland stuck her tongue out and grinned goofily, while Indianapolis bowed politely.
Glasgow continued to stand there blankly. She didn’t even see the others leaving, and her heart was about to fly out of her chest.
(What do I do, what do I do?! Even though it was an emergency, this is a kabedon... right out of one of those mangas...!)
Though her head was spinning and her face was completely flushed, Glasgow managed to hold on to the handouts. The awkward silence was deafening.
Y-your face is too close! W-we need to hurry back to the classroom and pass these out!
Upon those words, the two slowly peeled themselves away from the wall. Glasgow stepped away, her heart still pounding furiously.
...Oh my, that was passionate. Too bad those two are practically statues.
Ardent, it’s not good to peep on others— Though I’m not really one to talk. Ahaha...
Does it fall upon us to give them some extra motivation?
Mm... I’m totally cheering for Glasgow...

sequence:
'Tis the Season of Love!

<size=45>5.The Name... Is Glasgow</size>

scripts.say: After school...
I’m sorry, Glasgow!  Can you help me clean up the classroom today?
...You’re not up to something weird, are you?
(Sh-she’s sharp...!)
There’s something we need to do, and it’s really serious! T-trust us, we’re telling the truth!
So you’re in on it too, Edinburgh? How suspicious... Now, I’m almost convinced the two of you are—
Woahhh! We’re gonna be late if we don’t hurry up! Sorry, Glasgow, I swear I’ll make it up to you later!
Hey! Come back here! Tell me what’s going on—
...Good grief. I’m going to cause trouble for Newcastle if I get back too late...
“Need some help?”
...No need. Just head back first and tell my sister I’m running late. Cleaning is my specialty, so I’ll be done in no time.
(...Why do I feel so self-conscious? Is it all because of what happened earlier...?)
Glasgow’s cheeks flared up again as she threw herself into her cleaning, her movements more agitated than normal. Her emotions were a mess, and she couldn’t figure out why.
(...Good grief! Even though I said to just leave without me... Why is that busybody waiting for me...?!)
Hey, you! I said, I’m fine by myself, seriously!
...Huh? There’s something inside the desk? Is it... a letter?
The stationery was cutely adorned.
She approached me and read the name of the sender.
The name.... is Glasgow. Where have I heard that name before...
Eh? Ehhhhh?! What the heck is going on here?! I never wrote a letter like this— Hey, wait!
I unsealed the letter and perused its contents — the raw, unspoken feelings of a girl who was painfully bad at expressing herself.
——I love you. From, Glasgow.
Wait, no! This is a fake! I swear, Ardent and Edinburgh are behind this!
I always knew they were up to no good! ...Seriously, this wasn’t me! Because I don’t like you at all!
“I see... So it was fake...”
...Huh?
Glasgow seemed dumbfounded by this unexpected remark.
In that moment, time seemed to stand still for the figures alone in the classroom, the orange light of the afternoon sun filtering in through the windows.

sequence:
'Tis the Season of Love!

<size=45>6.Would You Still... Love Me?</size>

scripts.say: I, I mean...
Glasgow was shaken by the sudden question. It was a topic that the two of them normally avoided.
Wh-why are you acting like that anyway? It’s not like you at all...
I gazed at Glasgow intently, as if peering into her soul.
Wait, we can’t...
We... really can’t. We’re not just classmates... We’re also master and maid...
And my personality is no good either... I don’t know how to treat you tenderly... or how to get close to your heart.
“But I still love you, Glasgow.”
Glasgow’s eyes opened wide in surprise upon hearing my confession.”
Wh-what are ye saying?! I... I prefer for things to stay the way they are...
If we got any closer... you’d just end up hating me!
Glasgow tried to put down her cleaning tools and escape, but...
Ah, Master?!
The master’s arms gently wrapped around the maid, like goal tape embracing an athlete for crossing the finish line.
Unable to escape, Glasgow felt herself sinking into the passionate gaze of the person in front of her.
Master... Please... Let go of me...
I don’t know if I am worthy of your love... I just know I’ll end up saying something cold...
I don’t think... I can be any less ill-mannered...
Despite her words, I continued to embrace her tightly as if to transmit to her the chorus of “I don’t care” throbbing within my chest...
Are you sure...? Are you sure... you want an uncute girl like me? Would you still... love me?
I wiped the tears from Glasgow’s eyes, not knowing when they had formed. Looking straight into her moist eyes, I nodded slowly.
Master...

options.content: “I want to see more of your lovely face...”

scripts.say: (Ah... Master... is stroking my chin~)
(......I must be dreaming... I’ve never been so happy...)
Slowly, tenderly, our lips found each other, as if never having meant to be apart—

sequence:
'Tis the Season of Love!

<size=45>7.That Scared Me Half to Death!</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
(......What an absolutely dreamy situation...)
...Geh?! Oh, Master?! Is something the matter?
Oh, you’ve been calling for me, but I haven’t been responding? ...It, it’s nothing at all! I just had something on my mind...
I, I’ll fulfill my duties as your secretary, so don’t you fret!
I was a bit worried about how flustered she looked... But because the quality of her work was impeccable as ever, I decided not to say anything.
Instead, I tell her not to stress herself out too much, and then return to my work.
(Haah... That scared me half to death! How could I let myself daydream in the middle of work...)
(And that manga I borrowed from Chaser last night... “The Maid and the Master are Classmates!”... What an astounding work of art!)
(But, I can’t allow myself to become mired in delusions just because of a manga...)
Glasgow seems to be mumbling something while going through the materials related to the next operation.
Maybe I’ve been overworking her... Perhaps it’d be a good idea to invite her out somewhere to get work off her mind...
(Ahh... If only things in real life could work out that nicely...)
(On my next day off, I should take the initiative and ask the commander out on a date... No, I simply must!)
(Then, I’ll be sure to be more gentle... and comforting. Ah, and then... “Suddenly, the wind blows—”)
“I wonder if a day will come when our hearts grow closer, just like in those wondrous fantasies.”
“And thus, on a warm, warm afternoon... Two people who harbored feelings of deep affection for each other met—”

sequence:
Reflections of the Oasis

<size=45>1 Sandstorm in the Oasis</size>
Unknown Location
Sardegna Fleet Garrison - The Oasis
During the World Expo

scripts.say: Before the boat had hit the water♪
The whale's tail came up and caught her♪
All hands to the side, harpooned and fought her♪
When she dived down below♪
A lighthearted sea shanty played over the desk radio in the Sardegnian docking facility's break room.
*door clicks*
Oh! Andrea, hello! Are you having a lovely morning?
Attilio? Um, I guess...?
The weather does seem a little odd today...
By the way, Attilio, are you the one who put this station on the radio?
Yep! I don't really understand what's going on in the song, but it sounds fun, right?
Heheh, I've gotten a lot more into music ever since you found this radio for us!
Is that so...?
Well, I'm glad I could awaken a new interest in you.
*door clicks*
Oh, Gorizia's back, too!
Come and listen with me. The program's already...
Whaaat?! Don't change the station! They were just getting to my favorite music...
We now bring you urgent news.
Due to an abnormal situation of unknown cause, this region will experience an enormous sandstorm from 2:30 PM today to 3:00 AM tomorrow.
In order to minimize damage, the facility's windbreak walls will be closed in fifteen minutes. Please remain inside the facility to avoid injury.
Now, here is a list of instructions for minimizing danger in the face of a sandstorm...
A... sandstorm?
They did call it abnormal... Sandstorms should be unthinkable at this time of year.
I was surprised when I heard it, too.
But no sandstorm has ever gotten through since the windbreak walls were installed.
Actually... They were planning to hold a presentation in the Upper Senate today. I hope the sandstorm doesn't interrupt that.
A presentation? Who's the speaker?
Marco Polo. I hear it's related to the World Expo.
Ahahaha... Of course it is.
I had no idea. Have you been keeping a close eye on these things lately, Gorizia?
Not really? It's peaceful around here, so I'm just finding ways to pass the time.
But the sandstorm is going to make communications rough for a while, huh...
Not just communications. We won't be able to do any work outside.
Right... Ah, well. Guess I'm calling it quits early today!
Yeah! Let's take the day off!
...Oh, but the sandstorm means I won't be able to listen to the radio anymore...
Now I'm sad. I won't have anything to do!
Now that you mention it... I've read all of the books I brought with me.
We're kind of surrounded by sand... After the sandstorm passes, we'll have to look into serious repairs.
It is an old facility, after all. You never know what they went through in the old days.
Haha... That's true. I happen to know of a few old stories, myself.
...Stories? I want to hear stories!
Yeah, tell us some stories! I want to hear stuff about you two!
Stories, huh? Will any old story from before our coming to the Oasis do?
I do have some, but they're from a long time ago... Before this whole war even started.
Goodness, that is long ago. Now you've piqued my interest, hahaha.
I'm sure it's nothing compared to yours, Andrea...
If I tell a story, then you have to share one too, okay? You must have plenty of fascinating things to talk about.
Of course! You have yourself a deal.
I'll go get drinks and snacks!
In moderation, please.
I know! Hahaha!

sequence:
Reflections of the Oasis

<size=45>2 Reflections of Unity</size>

scripts.say: Oasis Facility - Break Room
The warm light of the desk lamp illuminated the faces of the three seated shipgirls.
Before the war began...

sequence: Frontline Battlefield
Mediterranean Garrison - Andalusia
Day 10 of the Reenactment

scripts.say: With this many forces, I think we'll see a fast and decisive victory.
It has only just begun, Archbishop. At this rate, it'll devolve into a mad brawl.
If we aren't vigilant, we'll fail to respond when disaster strikes.
...I suppose you're right.
Regardless, we have to secure the items... lest our superiors learn about this.
Then I would suggest you do it quickly. I can't hide the truth forever.
We don't have permission to interfere in this Reenactment.
If we're questioned, we'll have no choice but to obey and let it go.
*knock knock*
Archbishop, Implacable. Excuse me.
Yes, excuse you. We were in the middle of talking...
Gorizia, would you mind helping me roll up these maps?
...If we take this route, we may be able to avoid unnecessary conflict.
But once you arrive at the supposedly "neutral" port, the rest is in your hands.
We wouldn't want to see these valuable items destroyed in this Reenactment, either.
Please, Gorizia. This is an earnest request from the Iris Orthodoxy and the Royal Navy.
...Huh?
D-don't be silly, you two. It's not that big a deal!
Anyway... Sure. In the morning, I'll bring the recovered items to the Sardegnian fleet.
When things settle down, we'll find an opportunity to return them to their rightful place. Does that work for everyone?
It's our only option. I have no objections.
Then we'll execute the plan as delineated. The transport convoy will leave tomorrow at dawn, so please accompany them.
The battle rages on. Gorizia, we'd feel much more comfortable if you stayed with us overnight.
Roger.
Everyone, look at this cool thing I found!
Tadaah! Fancy new harmonica!
Goodness. It seems our Templar Knight wants to put on a show for us today, everyone. Shall we?
So you're telling me... you've met Richelieu and Implacable?
Whoooa!
They all seem like such important people!
Wow. I had no idea...
But, look at how things have changed since then... *sigh*...
Yeah, it seems not that long ago when we were all working together, and now...
Oh, but, things have been getting better as of late, right? The World Expo even went off without a hitch.
I hear Iris Libre is even helping out at the expo?
Archbishop Richelieu may not have been able to go in person, but she's been hard at work behind the scenes.
And that's not all. She has her hands tied with the Vichya Dominion...
Yeah, then there's the thing with the Crimson Axis...
*siiigh*...
Why's everyone sighing now?!
Umm, Gorizia, you said things have been going well, right?
They really are. We sigh, but only because we're remembering how things used to be.
I'm sure Mikasa would say something like...
"Damn! If you haven't figured out how to end the war, then don't start it in the first place!"
Speaking of Mikasa, I hear she's been working behind the scenes in the Sakura Empire. What is she after...?
Mikasa...? Is she the same one who came up in my book?
She's like a super-big-shot who carried a whole fight on her back a long time ago! Andrea, do you know Granny Mikasa?
G-Granny...?
Y-yeeeah, it was sooo long ago... Attilio, would you like to know more about Granny Mikasa?
Yeah! Please!
Give me a second to remember... Okay. You're gonna love this one.

sequence:
Reflections of the Oasis

<size=45>3 Reflections of Travel</size>

scripts.say: Oasis Facility - Break Room
As the night wore on, the sandstorm outside rumbled endlessly.
Now, Gran—ahem... Mikasa and I fought together in one major battle...
Oh, I know you. You're Mikasa, aren't you...?
Huh, so this is what Sardegna is putting all their innovation toward...
Innovation...?
Oh, excuse me. You are Andrea Doria from Sardegna, if I'm not mistaken?
Thanks for coming all this way to the Sakura Empire. As you know, I'm the Combined Fleet's flagship, Mikasa.
I'll be your guide during your stay, so feel free to speak up if you need anything.
Combined Fleet flagship, dreadnought Mikasa...
Seeing really is believing. Even in Europa, you're as famous as they come.
Together with Avrora's fleet, you struck a mighty blow to the Sirens and seized victory.
A distinguished shipgirl who shattered the myth that the Sirens were invincible and untouchable. A symbol of hope.
I've never so much as been on a battlefield. It would be wrong for you of all people to be stuck guiding me.
Hahaha, come on, you don't have to butter me up. We're all just doing our jobs.
We might be from different factions, but we're all shipgirls. If you need combat experience, you'll be able to get plenty here.
Besides, it's a host's duty to receive guests. There's nothing wrong with me taking care of you.
Now that the war situation is stable, it's time for us to form relationships with other factions. For the sake of our ultimate victory, let us treat you!
...Th-thank you!
U-umm, so where should we go next?
Good question. Your meeting with Lady Nagato is the day after tomorrow, so how about I show you the sights until then?
The day after tomorrow? Phew... That's good. I needed time to prepare myself...
In that case, I should ask now. Are there any things I should avoid doing, or be careful about doing, in the Sakura Empery?
Uh, what...? Hahaha, you don't have to be so tense. Take it easy.
You're an honored guest. Don't put so much pressure on yourself.
Your speech at the Holy Iris was fantastic; you know how to carry yourself, so you'll be just fine.
You knew about that?
Heh. Don't underestimate your elders, now.
Since the formation of Azur Lane, the global situation has been developing daily. We've put a lot of effort into information collection.
Ahaha... Sorry if this is sudden, but what did you think of the opinions in my speech?
I agree, of course. Azur Lane is our hopes for the future given form.
I have to find it strange that we haven't signed our treaties sooner, given how long it's been since Azur Lane was formed.
Time waits for no shipgirl. Someday, we pioneer ships will fall behind the times.
So, we need to settle whatever we can now.
You're right...
All I'd considered was that these treaties would make things easier for everyone.
Of course. That's a real benefit.
You and I see the same things. If there's a difference between us, it's that we see them from different angles.
Hopes for the future... I don't know if I can envision things that far ahead, hahaha...
Consider it the wisdom of us fanciful older shipgirls.
There'll be plenty of shipgirls, like you, who can do even better than we did. Maybe it's about time for us to exit the spotlight.
That's not true. I think you have at least ten more years in you.
I hope you're right. Hahahaha!
So, about that sightseeing. Have you ever heard of the Sakura Empire's Diadem of Light?
Of course! Those would be the islands where rituals and ceremonies are held, right?
You offer your prayers to some artifact... Umm, a divine stone, I think? Heheh, it's a lot like wishing on a shooting star!
More or less.
Y'know, there's a ritual today. Want to go see it before you go to your hotel for the night?
Wow! So you got to go to a festival?
That's right. I had a lot of fun gorging myself on Sakura cuisine!
Looking back, Mikasa might have called herself old, but she had such a youthful vigor about her.
I think she said that someday, a shipgirl might become the priestess of the Diadem of Light.
...That was a great trip.
It was a shame that I didn't get to see Watatsumi, but such a large festival is a rare opportunity.
Huh. You know, last time I brought this up, Marco Polo bombarded me with questions.
She really wanted to know about Watatsumi... I never saw it, though.
Are you acquainted with Marco Polo, too, Andrea?
Acquainted... is a word. Most of my knowledge of her came from Cavour...
Why do you ask?
Now that you mention Marco Polo...
I have a story for you two!
It's a big job that Marco Polo gave me! Wanna hear about it?
Marco Polo gave you a mission? What was it?
Yeah! She had me search for something before I came here!
It's also the weirdest mission I've ever been on...

sequence:
Reflections of the Oasis

<size=45>4 Mirage in the Dead Sea</size>

scripts.say: Oasis Facility - Break Room
And then, we saw this unusual castle!
It was enormous, but they called it a mirage!
When I tried to approach and touch it, it disappeared into thin air!
That was so disappointing!
Oh, my... You experienced a very rare sight, Attilio.
Yeah! Anyway, that's basically my story.
It was fun, but we couldn't find the thing that Marco Polo wanted us to look for...
Mm... I'm thirsty from all of this talking. Drink time!
You went to the Dead Sea, correct...?
There were shipgirls from other factions present, right? How did you get in?
Yeah! So, Marco Polo gave us this incredible device.
When we used it, somehow, we were able to get in without anybody noticing!
But when we got back from the Dead Sea, or whatever, it was awful...
Our clothes and the device were all messed up. It took ages to clean it all.
It is the Dead Sea, after all. The salinity is so high that it causes equipment to rust in no time.
But in the end, everything worked out just fine.
After that, I came to this garrison, and here we are!
I had no idea you'd gone to the Dead Sea...
But you were there searching for something, weren't you?
Marco Polo didn't complain when you came home with nothing?
Mmm, I thought she'd lecture us, too...
But when she read the report I made for her, she didn't complain at all.
She just thanked us for our hard work and sent us home for maintenance.
I see... That is like her... Huh? You only reported directly to Marco Polo?
None of this involved Veneto or Littorio?
I dunno... Marco Polo said something about the Senate authorizing it, or something?
It all goes over my head.
(It sounds like the rumors of them collecting curios are true...)
(Is this the Senate's strategy, or is it Marco Polo going rogue?)
Hm? Gorizia? Is something wrong?
Ahahaha... That's the same face she made when she saw the expense list for the World Expo.
But I can't imagine it's as shocking as that was—
Andrea. Did you not promise you wouldn't bring that up again?
Spreading the glory of Sardegna is a lovely thing, but anyone would get a migraine seeing all the zeros on that expense list...
If only we could splurge that much on more romantic, exciting things. Like sightseeing locales!
Fair... I'd certainly be happier if we had invested more money into this oasis facility.
Look around us. Oil lamps for lighting, newspapers and radios our only entertainment, surrounded by sand as far as the eye can see...
*sniffle*... I didn't know that this was the life I'd forced upon you all...
Okay, that's enough of that.
But goodness... This sandstorm just won't let up, will it?
I recall they used the word "enormous"...
Communications are still down, too.
As for stories... Let's call it for now, shall we? What should we do next?
How about we sing?
Gorizia, would you like to go first?
Huh? Why, exactly...?
Attilio, would you like to hear Gorizia sing?
Yeah! Gorizia, I want to hear you sing!
Hahaha! See?
Come ooon!

Unknown Location
Sardegna Fleet Garrison - The Oasis
A few hours after the start of the sandstorm

scripts.say: The sandstorm engulfing the facility seemed unceasing.
The exhausted Attilio had already drifted off into the world of dreams, and Andrea was beginning to yawn suspiciously often.
Gorizia, how about we get to bed early tonight?
