Granted, we don't have anything TO store at the moment, but still.
I say we get started now, so that our rescuers have a good place to anchor once they arrive.
Let's start by making a small pier, then expand it into a big harbor, and finally, build a storage depot.
Does that sound good, Commander?
"Yes. Logistics are a problem we must solve before we can further develop the island."
"I'm impressed, Z23. We only just arrived, and you've already thought this far ahead."
Thank you. The more you plan ahead, the better.
By the way, I found several spots where we can gather materials during my survey earlier.
Shall we go give them a look?
"Sure. Securing resources is our top priority. If we can map out the island's terrain at the same time, that's two birds with one stone."
Absolutely! Come with me!

sequence:
Uncharted Summer

<size=45>Of Mining and Crafting</size>

scripts.say: The giant volcano has caught my eye since we set foot here. I decide to go check it out.
Oh, Commander. Did you want to explore the volcano too?
At the volcano's foot, I run into Ayanami. She's squatting, looking intently at something on the ground.
Volcanos have a way of drawing people closer, yes.
If only I had a diamond pickaxe right about now...
Not stone, per se, but minerals.
I found this one just a minute ago. You can have it.
Yes, exactly! Your game knowledge is up to scratch.
I've already asked Javelin to gather the wood for me.
I'll use that to make a wood pickaxe, mine enough iron to make an iron pickaxe, then use that to mine for diamonds...
Give it a few days, and I'll have enough materials to make a palace fit for a king.
With tons of underground passages, of course.
Oh, by the way, I found this mineral just a minute ago. You can have it.
She hands me a small shard of obsidian.
Little fragments like this are all I can get at the moment, since I don't have a way to mine...
Although they are small, they're still dazzling. I'm gonna decorate my tent with them later.
"It is quite the gem. No pun intended. Also, this volcano must've erupted at some point for there to be obsidian lying around."
"There's a high likelihood there are other kinds of minerals and gemstones to be found here."
Yes, I think so too. Should we take a look around together?
Ayanami and I briefly search the area for materials before we retrace our steps back to camp.

sequence:
Uncharted Summer

<size=45>Welcome to Camp</size>

scripts.say: As the sun starts to set and I make it back to camp, I discover that the girls have already pitched up tents.
Moreover, everyone is working double-time to get all the essentials set up before nightfall.
After adding my gathered resources to our pile, I decide to give them a hand.
Deserted island - Provisional camp
With everyone working together, we finally manage to light a campfire on the coast.
Bonfire lit. Camp level 1 achieved.
And we all have proper places to sleep tonight, too!
The fire is so cozy... I'm dying for some barbecue...
Be patient. The mushrooms and fish need to roast a while longer.
Oh, and Commander, I managed to reestablish contact with the port.
I already told them about our predicament, and they're going to send a rescue team that will arrive tomorrow.
"That's great news. Then we can enjoy this barbecue in peace, knowing help is on the way."
Now the sun has set, night has come, and it's time for bed.
While my food digests, I consider what to do next...
I take the communicator out of my tent, face the ocean, and make a call.
Oh, Commander? Cruddy sleeping bag making it hard to fall asleep, I assume?
...Not quite? You're just worried about us back at the port?
Please. If anyone SHOULD be worried here, it's us. You're all alone out there.
For a storm to appear out of the blue like that... I still can't believe it.
Rest assured, the girls are working overtime right now to rescue you as soon as possible.
Z23 told me about your plans for the island, by the way. We'll bring manpower and supplies to help with that.
Ah, Saratoga just messaged me. I'd better get back to preparing the rescue team.
Get some rest, Commander. You'll need it for the coming days.
Good night.
A calm breeze blows across the beach, marking the end of our little barbecue party.
The fire crackles softly as all of us retire to our tents for the night.

sequence:
Uncharted Summer

<size=45>The Winds Bring Good Tidings</size>

scripts.say: As the morning light paints the beach a golden color, a battleship appears over the horizon.
Avast, ladies! Our destination is in sight!
And boy, what a bloody brilliant sight it is!
Lemme thank you all for being such gracious hosts! The food was scrumptious.
The cheek on you. Don't you feel the least bit responsible?
The Commander wouldn't have gotten stranded had you not sent that letter. Care to explain why you did it?
What's there to explain? All I did was share information with my first mate.
We share secrets, so what's wrong with sharing knowledge on some treasure?
I don't remember you ever being that close.
Let's say we grew on each other quickly during last Halloween♪
By basically keeping the Commander hostage? Sounds like Stockholm syndrome.
So? Is a pirate not allowed to take hostages? Hahaha!
Besides, the Commander CHOSE to go on this treasure hunt. I didn't force anyone!
I'm glad the Commander went, though. Sailing into uncharted seas in pursuit of adventure takes a lot of courage! Courage that I envy!
Oh, to seek the meaning of life amid tempestuous storms. THAT is the pirate life!
Not that I expect some desk jockey to understand~
Watch your mouth...
Calm down, now. On the bright side, nobody was injured.
At the same time, everyone gets to forget their troubles and have a leisurely vacation.
I say let the Commander decide how to deal with Royal Fortune while we enjoy ourselves.
Miss Memphis, Miss Royal Fortune, may I interest you in a cup of tea?
Cheers, darling.
*sigh*... Thanks.
When you think about it, the Commander's made an amazing discovery. A whole uninhabited island.
Hey now, the Commander didn't do it alone! I deserve credit too!
I guess so. The shipwrecked thing could've been avoided if you'd mentioned a storm in your letter, though.
Err, well, I was so focused on making a fitting poem that I forgot.
At any rate, the Commander DID get in touch with us! It took nearly a day, but...
Alright, I'm sorry! I won't do something like that again.
Good. But if you do, I'll personally bring you to the Commander to answer for your criminal negligence.
(Blimey, she's terrifying!)
Ladies, we've sighted the Commander and friends by the shoreline.
They built a whole camp in just one day. Talk about impressive.
Hm? What are these coordinates? The supply drop-off point?
I think I see what they're going for. They plan to build a pier.
A splendid idea.
I have to agree. It would be much easier to load and offload cargo and people with a pier.
It sounds like a fun endeavor as well. Everyone, let's get ready to disembark.
To be frank, I'm all but floored by the girls' enthusiasm.
They set out to explore the island almost as soon as they set foot on it.
If we keep this pace up, I think we'll have the resort built in close to no time.
But before that, I need to deal with a certain someone who led me here in the first place.
Ahoy, matey! How ya been, Commander?
Missed me? Wanted to thank me?
"Sure, but first, there's something I wanted to ask."
I know what you're thinking. I promise I didn't mean for you to get hurt, on my honour!
On one hand, my carelessness got you shipwrecked, but on the other, it led you to this pristine piece of resort real estate!
So, I'd say we're square, right? I mean, surely?
...Oops, I just remembered I have a meeting with my Tempesta mates. I've got to scurry back home.
Don't worry, I'll be back in a few days. Meanwhile, go on and explore the island!
Until then, keep me in your thoughts – and heart.
And remember, the treasure hunt has only begun. Toodles!
In a reprise of our Halloween encounter, Royal Fortune disappeared just like that.
I'm not quite sure that she's telling the truth about there being treasure, but for now, I'll focus on looking around the island.

sequence:
Uncharted Summer

<size=45>Beachside Daydream</size>

scripts.say: A beautiful woman stands alone on the beach, bathed in the sun's golden glow.
I daydream of sitting down to appreciate the scenery... until her voice calls out to me.
Ah, this weather is perfect – perfect for a date with you, my Commander~
Taihou wraps her arm around mine and takes me on a stroll through the empty beach.
I'm so happy to have you all to myself today~
Oh... You can't take your eyes off my swimsuit – off me, hmm?
By all means, stare as much as you wish. In fact, DO stare. I love it when you do♥
It seems this swimsuit is a winner, because it has already captured your heart♥
And yet, now your gaze is darting from place to place... Are you looking for someone else?
I'm afraid you won't find another soul out here. The only people on this beach are you and me♥
Do you know why?
Because I've reserved the whole beach♥
She leaned in close and teasingly whispered that right into my ear.
And do you know what that means?
That there's no way to run from my love♥
Heehee~ Seeing your anxious face makes me want to tease you.
Yes, it won't do with you passively staring at me. That won't deepen our bond at all.
That being the case...♥
I'll make the first move myself.
Before I can attempt to wriggle my way loose, she grabs hold of me.
You needn't do anything, my Commander. Allow me to take the lead.
Your desires, your body, your spirit... I'll take care of them all♥
Now, close your eyes...♥
It's not been that long, yet the beach is again buried under garbage brought in by the tide.
This pile of waste is an eyesore getting between the natural beauty of the sky and the sea.
Garbage has washed up again, Commander...
We've got to clean the beach again...
Come on... For the turtles...
You take out an apple you picked in the forest and give it to the little fox.
It promptly wolves down on it, and when it's finished, the fox looks up at you with eyes that seem to yearn for more.
The rain shortly stops, and the weather clears up again. You go on your way, leaving the shelter behind.
You feel nothing special. It was just an insignificant encounter in the rain.
Feeling bad for the little animal, you offer it another apple.
It's even bigger than the last one. Its stomach must be full after this one.
Once again, it promptly wolves down on it, and when it's finished, the fox looks up at you with eyes that seem to yearn for more.
This is a greedy little creature. You don't want to indulge it any more.
You pay no attention to the fox, which looks at you with a lovable expression.
The rain stops. You leave the shelter behind, and the insignificant encounter recedes into the back of your mind.
You offer it a triply extra-large apple and swear to yourself not to give it any more after this.
The rain keeps falling. The fox happily eats the apple while you sit there, bored.
After it finishes eating, the fox wags its tail at you, seemingly very pleased, before disappearing amidst the rainfall.
The rain stops, and the skies over the island turn clear once more.
Out of nowhere, a little red critter appears before you. It's the fox you fed the apples to, and it is holding a gift in its mouth..
This is its way of repaying the kindness you showed it during this off encounter in the rain.
It seldom rains on the deserted island, yet it is pouring down. Your clothes will get soaked at this rate.
You decide to look for shelter.
A while later, you notice that a lone, rain-drenched baby fox has sought shelter in the same place as you.
Its ears are drooping, and it seems to be either hungry or sad.
You gave the godlike manjuu your answer.
Is that so? Was it really the golden one?
...Actually, to be frank with thee, I forgot which one it was.
No matter. In light of thy sincerity, I shall give thee the golden manjuu. Treat the little peep well!
You gave the godlike manjuu your answer.
Is that so? Was it really the silver one?
...Actually, to be frank with thee, I forgot which one it was.
No matter. In light of thy sincerity, I shall give thee the silver manjuu. Treat the little peep well!
In the spirit of the fairy tale this is seemingly inspired by, the right thing to do is say neither; it was a normal manjuu.
However, you are so taken aback by what you're seeing that you cannot answer properly.
Doth thou mean to say it was neither of them, hmm?~
Indeed, thou art an honest one. Worry not about the little peep, for I already saved him before posing my question.
In light of thy outstanding honesty, I shall give thee both the golden and silver manjuus. Treat the little peeps well!
The god-manjuu hands you both the precious manjuus, then disappears beneath the surface.
As you're exploring the island, you stumble across a manjuu that appears to be drowning in a small river in the forest.
Plrblrblrbhh! Help! Help me, peep! Blrlbrph...
Just as you get ready to jump in the river, a manjuu seemingly with the aura of a god emerges from it.
O, wise and kind warrior, I commend thy willingness to put thyself in harm's way to save a manjuu.
So, tell me, which manjuu fell in the river? This one of gold, or this one of silver?
Look, Otto, I'm as eager to find the hidden treasure on this island as you are...
But you need to watch your step. Remember what I told you about the vines?
What vines?
Ahem... "The creep vine lurks in the forest's dark corners. It ensnares reckless travelers who pass by it."
Creep vine? Yeah, right. That's just a story meant to scare kids who–
Before she could finish speaking, Otto felt something squirm under her feet.
Aaaaahhhh!
In the blink of an eye, the vine has suspended her in the air.
Well, well... A predatory vine. Just like the reports said.
Its morphology is also quite unique. I should bring a sample back for study.
Seriously?! You knew this vine hangs around these parts?!
Well, yes.
Then you could've warned me about it!
I literally did not even a minute ago. You chose to ignore my warning.
Urgh... It's tightening its grip... Don't just stand there! Get me down!
As you're passing through a clearing, you come across some unusual creatures.
You there, traveler! Come over here and play a game with us peeps!
One of us peeps is hiding a rare and shiny gem.
If you guess the correct peep, the gem is yours!
In truth, we don't really have a gem! Us peeps just want to play.
Zzz... Peep...
"A guessing game, eh. Let's see if I can pick the right one."
Formidable and you are walking along the cliffs of the mountain while a white mist ripples beneath your feet. The view from here is astonishing.
That's when all of a sudden, you catch sight of an orange rectangle.
It's in the distance, but if you had to guess, it's a warning sign that was put up recently.
Hmm... I can't make out what it says on account of this mist.
I'll get a bit closer and try to read it, Commander.
I will. Now let's see here...
"Unstable foundation. Beware of rockslides"...
There is an ominous cracking sound, and suddenly, the ground beneath Formidable's feet collapses.
Aaaahhhh!
Oh! *pant*... *pant*... Thank goodness there's a vine here, or else I'd been done for...
That sign is worthless where it's placed now! ...C-Commander, come and help me up!
*burp*... I'm hungry. Do you have any food, Comrade Commander?
Grozny and you are surveying the expansive forest. It's been quite the trek, and she looks exhausted.
I could eat anything. Heck, I might just take a bite out of you.
"Please don't. I don't taste good."
Take it easy. I'm just kidding with you.
"If memory serves me right, there should be a camp stocked with rations just a stone's throw away from here."
"I'm fairly sure the exploration team left behind some meat."
Ooh, meat! That's perfect for a barbecue!
Her eyes glimmer with eagerness.
While we don't have any vodka or borscht, the thought of juicy barbecue alone is enough to make my mouth water...
You can rest and I'll man the grill, Comrade Commander.
You're going to fall in love with the taste of Northern Parliament-style barbecue!
After a long walk through the snaking cave, you eventually find wooden boards and stones with clear signs of handicraft.
It seems this cave was once used for storage.
And there's no fluffy pillows to be found. Sad...
What were you expecting? Please use your common sense, Laffey.
A surprising find – you obtained a small quantity of crafting materials!
Continuing deeper through the dark, dank cave, you come across another surprise.
Halt, everyone! I just heard something!
The deafening roar of an animal echoes from further in.
I-I think we've angered the cave's resident! Let's get out of here!
This does look like an animal's den, even if it's too dark to see inside.
It could be dangerous for all you know. Best to play it safe and turn back.
An uneventful step on your journey – nothing happened, but that's fine. Every adventure needs a little downtime.
As you're exploring the island, you come across an eerie cave.
Something inside it is radiating a curious light.
Looks creepy... Do you think a ferocious animal might live in there?
There might be an unexpected find in there... Like a fluffy pillow...
You won't find a pillow out in the mountains... But, there's often lootables inside caves in video games. Like treasure chests.
I don't see any signs that it's inhabited. It's probably stood empty for a long time. What do you think we should do, Commander?
Nothing ventured, nothing gained. You decide to...
You jump into the river to rescue the helpless critter.
The water is cold, but this only fills you with determination. In the end, you manage to rescue the animal, but you pass out on the riverbank afterwards...
When you wake up, you find a token of gratitude left beside you.
It must be from the animal you rescued. You've been rewarded for your heroic act.
As much as you want to save the animal, you don't want to put yourself in harm's way. What if you need rescuing next, after all?
It's wiser to call for someone nearby to help.
With your friends' help, you manage to rescue the little critter.
It runs off, leaving behind a token of gratitude. You've been rewarded for your level-headed response.
You are walking along the river when, out of the blue, you hear repeated splashing.
You turn your head to the source of the sound and spot a small animal, trying its hardest to stay afloat. It seems it fell into the river.
The river is so deep you can't see the bottom. The animal flails about, desperately crying for help.
You steel yourself and decide to...
The unprocessed wood you offered gives off a brilliant light, and then...
You found a treasure in the bird's nest!
Do you want to try again?
The unprocessed ores you offered give off a brilliant light, and then...
Nothing. Your materials disappeared without a trace...
For want of more treasure, you put in additional materials.
However, nothing happened. Your materials remain in place, as you'd expect them to.
The strange voice has vanished, and it seems you can't get any more treasure this way.
The unprocessed wood you offered gives off a brilliant light, and then...
Nothing. Your materials disappeared without a trace...
Do you want to try again?
The unprocessed ores you offered give off a brilliant light, and then...
You found a treasure in the bird's nest!
Do you want to try again?
The unprocessed ores you offered give off a brilliant light, and then...
Nothing. Your materials disappeared without a trace...
Do you want to try again?
This voice is obviously untrustworthy and should not be listened to.
You turned back the way you came, leaving the dubious bird's nest behind.
Do you want to try again?
The unprocessed wood you offered gives off a brilliant light, and then...
You found a treasure in the bird's nest!
For want of more treasure, you put in additional materials.
However, nothing happened. Your materials remain in place, as you'd expect them to.
The strange voice has vanished, and it seems you can't get any more treasure this way.
The unprocessed wood you offered gives off a brilliant light, and then...
Nothing. Your materials disappeared without a trace...
For want of more treasure, you put in additional materials.
However, nothing happened. Your materials remain in place, as you'd expect them to.
The strange voice has vanished, and it seems you can't get any more treasure this way.
The unprocessed ores you offered give off a brilliant light, and then...
You found a treasure in the bird's nest!
For want of more treasure, you put in additional materials.
However, nothing happened. Your materials remain in place, as you'd expect them to.
The strange voice has vanished, and it seems you can't get any more treasure this way.
An enormous bird's nest, almost as big as a cloud, catches your attention.
You approach it, and suddenly hear a strange voice inside your head.
"Cock-a-doodle-doo... I shall trade with you..."
"Leave an offering... buk-buk-buk... and be rewarded..."
These mushrooms look as poisonous as it gets, but they should be safe to lie down on.
You sit down on the cap of a mushroom and rest. Its surface is velvety soft, and gently beckons you to dreamland.
When you open your eyes again, you find yourself inside a cave packed with treasures.
Among them, an old-fashioned but ornate treasure chest atop a tall pedestal in the cave's center catches your eye.

options.content: This is a dream. Snap out of it.

scripts.say: These mushrooms look as poisonous as it gets.
You give them a wide berth for the sake of your well-being.
Who's dumb enough to pass up free treasure? Not you.
You open the treasure chest and find that it's filled to the brim with priceless gold and jewels.
You wake up. The cave, the treasure chest, and the precious booty are all nowhere to be seen.
It seems what you saw was merely a dream induced by that weird mushroom you slept on.
Who's dumb enough to pass up free treasure? Not you.
You open the treasure chest and find that it's filled to the brim with priceless gold and jewels.
You wake up. To your surprise, you are cradling the treasure chest you found in your dream.
Filled with joy over this miracle, you open the treasure chest...
Strangely, it's filled not with gold and jewels, but rather a few handy items.
While there's no denying you got nice stuff, you still feel a bit disappointed.
You shake your head and manage to wake up.
The cave, treasure chest, and of course the valuable booty are all gone, and you find yourself back atop the giant mushroom.
With it in hand, you walk off, leaving the strange place behind.
You shake your head and manage to wake up.
But, strangely, you feel a weight between your arms. Unbelievably, it's the treasure chest from the dream.
With it in hand, you walk off, leaving the strange place behind.
You got lost during your adventure and wound up deep inside an unmapped forest.
All around you are giant, unusually-colored mushrooms that give off a faint light. You decide to...

sequence:
Cinnamon Roll on a Rainy Day

<size=45>1 Sweet as Sugar</size>

scripts.say: Early morning - Outside the office
I was nearing my office, and that's when I saw a familiar figure right by the door.
Good morning, Commander. I'll, um, be your secretary starting today.
I thought I should wait for you before stepping inside, so... Here I am.
Right, today was the day Helena would start as my secretary. I then noticed she'd brought a big stack of notes with her.
Okay, first thing's first – sorting paperwork.
Helena placed her stack of notes on the table and started flicking through them.
Paperwork, paperwork... Ah, here it is.
She withdrew a sheet with gorgeous handwriting and adorned with a colorful stamp, to boot.
...Hm? Are you wondering what my notes are for?
They're a list of secretary tips I compiled by asking girls around port.
I figured their advice would help me perform my job better, so yeah...
Talk about playing it extremely safe... To be fair, she has always been like that.
Ah, crap, I haven't made you a drink yet. Do you want tea or coffee?

options.content: "I'll have some tea. The usual strength."

scripts.say: The usual strength... Got it. I'll be back in a minute.
She anxiously skimmed her notes until she found the page she was looking for, then left the office.
Helena came back a while later with a kitchen scale in hand.
This? It's so I can make exact measurements.
Based on the size of your teapot, it'll take about five grams of tea leaves for the right strength...
...It's done. Here you go, Commander.
I had a sip, and... it was just my cup of tea. Literally, I suppose.
However, seeing how meticulous she was made me worry if she cooked like this too. I prayed she wouldn't turn the kitchen into a science lab.
I'm done sorting your papers now. Have a look.
She was already performing impeccably as a secretary. Then, all of a sudden, someone came knocking on the door.
Hey, Commander. We're just here to drop off yesterday's after-action report.
Ugh. Couldn't you have carried these papers yourself, Louis?
It was St. Louis and Honolulu. What a coincidence.
What's up, Helena? Starting to get the hang of this yet?
L-Louis? Um, hi.
Sorry, I just remembered I have to go return this scale. I have to go...
Goodness, she left in a hurry.
Anyhow – she's a great help around the office, isn't she, Commander? My little Helena is a diligent girl.
"She definitely is. Though 'diligent' doesn't quite do it justice. More like 'fastidious'..."
I get what you mean. She's a bit like rock candy, you know?
"Rock candy? In what way?"
Sweet, but sticky, I suppose.
Well, seeing as we're done here, it's time we get going. Keep at it, Commander~
The analogy didn't really hit home, though I had a feeling it would make sense in due time.

sequence:
Cinnamon Roll on a Rainy Day

<size=45>2 A Storm is Coming</size>

scripts.say: Later that evening, a drizzle descended upon the port.
It's starting to rain, Commander. Should we call it a day now, before it gets worse?
"There's still work left to do. I can't leave before it's all done."
"You can go home early if you want to, though. You've already finished your job."
I could, but... I'd hate to leave without you...
"And I'd feel bad if I let you down. I'll try to finish up quick, then."
While I was chipping away at my work, the rain had whipped up into a complete downpour.
Gales rattled the windows while thunder boomed in the distance. What began as an evening shower had grown into a storm.
"Now I remember... Yesterday's forecast warned there could be a big storm coming."
A storm? Oh god...

options.content: "Seems I got tunnel vision over my work. Sorry."

scripts.say: Don't be sorry, it's fine. We can just wait for it to pass.
Thunder rumbled outside, and my stomach growled almost as if it were echoing it.
"Hmm... I think it's time for dinner. I've got instant noodles and snacks in my drawer..."
Oh. Yes, please.
Helena and I both reached for the instant noodles, and our hands made contact.
Err... I-I'd like to do the preparation. It's what a secretary should do...
Okay, first I set the timer to three minutes, and then...
She again flipped through her notes while seemingly reciting a recipe.
It seemed like she'd written down tips for every plausible occasion...
Dinner is served. Bon appetit, Commander.
"Wow, this is really good!"
"Seriously, this is great. Where'd you learn to cook like this?"
Well, it's actually a recipe I got from a Sakura Empire friend of mine. Dried plums and potato chips have surprising culinary utility.
The fact she even knew what snacks I keep around the office shows just how far she went to gather intel to prepare for the job.
If you'd like, I could ask around for more recipes to add to my–
BRRZT...
*gasp*! Wh-what was that?
A shockingly loud thunderbolt struck, and the lights in the office all went out.

sequence:
Cinnamon Roll on a Rainy Day

<size=45>3 A Light in the Darkness</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Helena and I relied on the backup lights to find our way to the breaker room.
A scorched smell lingered in the air when we got to the power station. Whatever broke here, fixing it wouldn't be quite so easy.
Commander, I think we have a small generator over in the depot.
If we can get it online, we should be good on power... for a while, at least.
Let's head there together, shall we?
This building's confusing layout was only made worse by our inability to see anything in the dark. Getting lost seemed an inevitability...
"Is it this way? No, that leads to the archives... What about that way? Wait, that's not right either..."
The depot is this way. Or at least, I'm pretty sure it is...

options.content: "Do your notes include a blueprint of this place, or...?"

scripts.say: Oh, not exactly. It's just that I've been here once before, so I know roughly where to go.
If I remember right, we just have to turn right here, then left, then left again, and then...
I let Helena lead the way, and after just a short while, we'd made it to the depot.
Did she really memorize such a complex layout after just one prior visit? That was amazing, if so.
"Well, we're here. Now the question is, how are we going to find a needle in a haystack? The generator could be anywhere."
I'm fairly sure it should be over in... aisle twelve, first shelf.
Ah, there it is! Thank goodness my memory didn't betray me.
She even remembered its exact location. I was stunned.

options.content: "You've got a memory like an elephant."

scripts.say: Please, that's not true. I just had a gut feeling it would be here.
Also, uh... We're going to need some fuel for the generator.
Even in near pitch-black darkness, I could tell my compliment made Helena smile.
We found some fuel and got the generator started. The office lights lit once more.
That takes care of that. Now we should probably–
Eek! Oh god! Did I do something wrong?
"No, it's fine. I doubt that flickering was because of you."
"The generator's probably just gotten weaker over the years. Let's turn off all the non-essentials and use my desk lamp for light."
The office was bathed in the faint glow of a lone light bulb atop my desk. Helena and I found a cozy spot to sit down and rest for a bit.

sequence:
Cinnamon Roll on a Rainy Day

<size=45>4 Warming Words</size>

scripts.say: Thanks to Helena's efforts, I finally managed to wrap up my work for the day.
"Well... The storm doesn't seem to be dying down. Why don't we talk about stuff to kill some time?"
Talk about... what stuff?
"I guess for starters... What's your favorite thing?"
Hard to say... Maybe my SG radar?
"Your radar, huh. I had a hunch... What about something more general?"
Hmm... Nice clothes, I suppose?
I made a mental note to buy some nice clothes later to thank her for her outstanding performance today.
"I see. What about... something you consider a shortcoming of yours?"
A shortcoming? Well...
She gazed into the floor and went quiet for a short while.
Um... I dislike going into battle...
Because every time I see my friends get hurt, it feels like my heart is coming apart at the seams...
I really wish I was stronger so I could do something to prevent that, not just watch powerlessly while it happens...
A somber look formed on her face, and she fell silent again.
In retrospect, I should've asked a different question instead...
Dropping the topic, I got up and poured a cup of tea for each of us.

options.content: "Sorry for asking about such a touchy subject."

scripts.say: For me? Th-thanks for the tea.
...Thanks, Commander.
Cup of tea held in her hands, she gazed through the office window, brooding for a considerable time.
Eventually, after gathering up enough courage, she turned around and threw me a decided look.
What about you, Commander? What's one of your shortcomings?
And what do you do to try to make up for it?
Knowing you, you must have some good advice for fixing your own flaws.
...Why are you shaking your head? Are you saying I don't need to fixate on that?
"Yeah. You'll be just fine if you work on it at your own pace."
"I should've said it sooner, but you've been a lifesaver today. You deserve a huge thank-you for that."
"So thank you, Helena, for going above and beyond."
Y-you really think so?
I'm... I'm delighted to hear those words from you.
Her expression lightened up a bit.

sequence:
Cinnamon Roll on a Rainy Day

<size=45>5 Shattered Glass</size>

scripts.say: CRAAACK!
*gasp*! What was that?!
A gale sent an object crashing through the window, letting the fierce storm winds blow through the office.
Commander, are you okay?!
"I'm all right. I can't say the same for the documents, though..."
"Or the rest of the office, for that matter. That gust left a mess in its wake."
It really did. We should do something about that broken window.
First thing's first – the documents. She took a heavy book and placed it atop the stack of papers so they wouldn't be blown away.
That should do for now. There should be a folded-up cardboard box behind the bookshelf – can you get it?
Indeed, there was one. I fished it out and brought it over.
Great. Just put it over the window and I'll fasten it with some duct tape...
There. Now let's get the wet papers off the floor. Hopefully they'll still be legible after they've dried.
After covering up the broken window, we picked up the documents spread around the office.
The wind howled outside, buckling the cardboard in an attempt to break through.
"It's not going to hold for long. The winds are too strong."
Then we'd better move these documents someplace safe, quick!
Eek!
Her foot slipped in the dark, but luckily I caught her before she fell over.
Th-thanks. That was close... The floor's wet, so watch your step. Wait here – I'll fetch some mops.
It struck me just how proactively she took care of one problem after the next.
She likely didn't notice it herself – but I definitely did.

sequence:
Cinnamon Roll on a Rainy Day

<size=45>6 Sweet Respite</size>

scripts.say: After carrying the documents to a safer place, Helena and I mopped the floor.
We were both tired after dealing with so much in such a short timespan, so we lay down on the couch to rest for a bit.
KRRCH-BOOOM!
The thunder kept on booming. I suspected the storm wouldn't let up until the morning.
All of a sudden, Helena grabbed my hand and held it with a trembling grip.
S-sorry. I just need a little something to help me relax...
I can let go, if this is making you uncomfortable...

options.content: "Not at all. I'm here for you."

scripts.say: The shaking in her hand calmed down little by little, giving way to a comforting warmth.
The warmth was soothing to my heart.
The office became like a cozy lighthouse in the eye of a turbulent storm.
Fatigue had finally caught up to me after such a long day. My heavy eyelids were closing on me... That's when Helena's head brushed against my shoulder.
Zzzzz...
I don't blame her for dozing off on me. Her first day on the job had been incredibly hectic.
It wouldn't be long before someone came to check on us. I decided to get some shuteye...

sequence:
Cinnamon Roll on a Rainy Day

<size=45>7 The Calm After the Storm</size>

scripts.say: Port - The next day
*sigh*...
Come on, sleepyheads, that's enough. Wake up.
Opening my eyes, the first thing I saw was... Helena's thighs. It seemed I'd asked for a lap pillow at some point before dozing off again.
Ahem. What the hell are you two doing?
Huh...? Honolulu? Louis? Why are you here?
To check on you. You never came back to the dorm last night.
We figured it was because of the storm, so we waited for the rain to let up first.
Care to walk me through what happened? Please don't tell me any funny business went down.
Uhh, sure. It started late in the evening...
...Hmm, all right. I'll take your word for it.
Now that the sun's up... Geesh, the storm made a worse mess of the office than I thought.
We need to order a new windowpane, replace fried wires, tidy up the place... There's a lot to do to better prepare for the next storm.
Commander, should I go ask Akashi if she can provide new electronics?

options.content: "Go ahead. I'm sure you can work something out."

scripts.say: All right. I'll see you in a bit.
With a blush on her face, Helena made her swift exit.
Something's fishy here... I'm going to have to press her for the real answer about what went down last night.
How about we say they had a sweet moment and leave it at that, hm? Heehee~
Commander, be a dear and keep looking after Helena for me.

sequence:
Set Sail! An Inspiration-Seeking Journey

<size=45>1 Writer's Block</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Commander, I've brought you the itinerary for next week. Please go over it.
Hai Tien, the newly-appointed secretary ship, hands me a schedule for the upcoming week as well as the corresponding task list.
The schedule is packed with detailed notes, and the task list is numbered in order of priority. Everything is logically arranged and beyond reproach.
However–
The super-focused girl doesn't seem to notice that there are some peculiar strips of paper stuck to the documents she just handed me.
("She leaps as hard as she can into the arms of the one she loves..." Scribbles. "Her lover's embrace is so strong, yet so very warm..." More scribbles.)
(Scribbles... "The rain surrounds the two of them like a silken veil, casting the illusion that nothing exists between heaven and earth except for each other..." Scribbles.)
(Huh. Is this a story that Hai Tien has been working on?)
(There are a lot of things scribbled out, and she clearly threw the paper into a shredder... Maybe she's been struggling with her work?)
(Though, writing a novel is a time-consuming process. Formulating the story's framework is no easy feat...)
After gathering my thoughts, I decide to...

options.content: Give Hai Tien the rest of the day off.
Ask Hai Tien about the matter.

scripts.say: Mm. According to the itinerary, I should be able to take care of everything on my own today.
Why don't you go back and get some rest? Oh, but I don't mind if you'd like to stay in the office to get your personal work done.
(There's no point making wild speculation. I might as well ask her since she's already here...)
Hai Tien, has something been bothering you lately?
Huh? What do you mean by...
D-did I do something to displease you? Have I failed to meet your expectations as secretary ship in any way?
That's not it at all. If anything, you've been doing remarkably well considering you were just assigned the job.
You've already helped me in a whole lot of ways, so I'd like to take this opportunity to return the favor.
Umm... If that's the case, I will accept your gracious offer.
...So that's basically the gist of things.
I've been going through a bit of writer's block, and now I can't come up with anything remotely satisfying anymore...
Have you tried drawing inspiration from other works? Maybe a song or an old masterpiece of some sort?
The girl shakes her head helplessly.
I already tried that, but it didn't do anything.
Oh, I've got just the thing! You know how in the olden days, people would take long journeys through the rivers and mountains to draw inspiration for their poetry?
Why don't we go on a camping trip of our own and give that a try? Maybe you'll find your inspiration somewhere along the way!

sequence:
Set Sail! An Inspiration-Seeking Journey

<size=45>2 Camping Preparations</size>

scripts.say: Hai Tien was more than glad to accept my invitation for a camping trip, and we started making preparations for our next day off.
After wrapping up the remainder of the work, the two of us head out to the port's shopping district for our day off.
Commander, I've consulted all my other peers and compiled a list of camping supplies. Let's follow this list when deciding what to buy.
Sounds good to me!
Woah, if it isn't Commander and Hai Tien! Are you guys out here to stock up for a camping trip?
I'm quite familiar with that stuff, y'know, so feel free to gimme a holler!
If memory serves me properly, don't you run a produce store, Miss Owari? I'm not sure you'd be able to help us with camping supplies...
Hmm~ Well, yeah, but fruits and veggies aren't the only things we sell. We've got a whole bunch of other useful stuff too.
After all, doin' business around the port is no walk in the park. You've gotta branch out and expand your market share if you don't wanna strike out.
Nya? Did I hear someone say they were shopping, nya?
As if we had spoken forbidden words of power, a familiar green cat suddenly popped out right in front of us.
Let's take a look at that shopping list you've got there, Hai Tien... Hrmm, hrmm... I see, I see, nya.
Looking for camping supplies, nya? You'll find everything you're looking for, and more, in Akashi's store, nya~♪
Wait, hold yer horses! I was the one who found these customers first! This is practically daylight robbery!
Nya? In the end, it's the customer who decides where to do business, and with whom.
That being the case, why don't we both bring our wares and let Commander and Hai Tien decide, nya?
You're on! Practically took the words right outta my mouth!
Some time later...
*pant*... *pant*... Feel's like my tongue's going numb just explainin' all the different products...
Why does Akashi look like she's not havin' a hard time at all?!
Mwahaha... Well, well~ it comes with the turf, nya~!
Drumroll please... and tadah! An 'oral spray that keeps your mouth hydrated no matter how much you talk', nya!
An absolute essential for anyone who wants to do business! And, it can be yours for a cheap, cheap price of 9,999 coins, nya!
Woah, that sounds crazy useful! Gimme two canisters!
(...What's crazy is how she's had the tables turned on her completely. And how does anyone fall for that shady sales pitch anyway?)
Thanks for your patronyage!
Now then, you two, have you decided on what you want, nya? Since it's your first time camping, you might want to make some extra preparations by buying everything. Just in case, nya~♪
Exactly! Supplies aside, you'll also want to make sure you have a first aid kit and some non-perishable food on hand~
Err... Why don't you give us some time to browse on our own first?
Miss Owari certainly brought up a good point. While there seem to be a lot of things on the list, unforeseen circumstances can always pop out...
I'd like this, and this. And all of these over here!
- Thank you, thank, nya! You are most generous, Hai Tien! - Thanks a ton for supporting my biz! Come back again next time~♪
I wasn't able to stop Hai Tien from going on her shopping frenzy, nor did I want to rain on her parade either. In the end, we bought every last thing that Akashi and Owari brought.

sequence:
Set Sail! An Inspiration-Seeking Journey

<size=45>3 Set Sail! An Inspiration-Seeking Journey!</size>

scripts.say: I brought all our freshly-purchased wares back to the office and spread them out on the floor to organize them–
A tent, a tarp, two camping chairs, a foldable sunbed... Insect spray, wet wipes, sunscreen...
Wait, what? Why is there an axe here?!
Um, well, just in case we need firewood or encounter a ferocious beast... It's better to come prepared, right?

options.content: There shouldn't be any wild beasts around the port, I think...
I'm not sure how much of a threat wild beasts pose to cannon-toting shipgirls, but...

scripts.say: Y-yes, you're right...! We can leave the axe behind, and the crowbar as well...
After returning a whole bunch of items we didn't plan on using such as walkie-talkies, a folding clothesrack, and a chainsaw...
Hai Tien and I finally set out on our camping trip in search of inspiration.
A bit later, in the woods behind the port...
Phew... The air here is so crisp and refreshing. My mind already feels totally refreshed.
I haven't had any flashes of inspiration yet, but at least my body feels lighter than before.
Hai Tien has a smile on her face as she speaks. A squirrel hops down from the tree trunk, circles around her, and then darts off deeper into the woods.
Want to try following the squirrel?
That sounds like an excellent idea! Thank you!
The two of us head deeper into the woods as well, following the direction of the squirrel.
It seems that we happened to go on our camping trip during the flowering season. A kaleidoscope of flowers are in full bloom everywhere we look, and I inadvertently slow down to admire them.
Have these flowers piqued your interest, Commander? I happen to know a thing or two about them, if you'd like to learn more about them.
Hai Tien's eyes are shimmering with anticipation. She clearly wants to demonstrate her knowledge to me.
You're my teacher today, Miss Hai Tien!
The scenery here is certainly beautiful, but...
...But?
It pales in comparison to your beauty.
*cough*, *cough*... Geez, Commander, please don't tease me like that...
But, she is unable to hide the faint blush on her cheeks.
Now that I think about it, you didn't come here just to hear me yap about flowers...

Oh, right! Commander, have you ever heard of the Flying Flower Game? It's a game where we take turns reciting poetry verses around a particular word or theme, and the loser has to play a punishment round.
Sounds interesting. Definitely a good way to spruce up our stroll.
Alright, let's do this!
Heehee. Allow me to begin, then: "Before the Calyx Tower, spring is in full bloom."
(According to the rules, I have to respond with a poetry verse that includes a flower-themed word)

options.content: "Beneath the swirling petals, glasses clink and feelings deepen."
"Flowers and spring showers? Naw, we gon' make it rain!"

scripts.say: Wow, that's a great response, Commander, I'm surprised.
I shall continue then.
Um, Commander... I believe we might be going a bit off-topic...
Ahem... Oh, is that so? It, uhh, might just be... yeah, a poem you've never heard before!
Hrmm... Really now? Well, it matters not. I shall continue then.
Bring it! Let's see what you've got!
"As moon waxes, floral shadows fall before the window."
"There rests a beauty, like a flower wreathed in clouds."
"Clothes like dancing clouds, cheeks like a rosy blossom."

options.content: "The spring breeze gently caresses the steps, peonies even more beautiful in the rich dew."
"And upon the branches bloom countless pear flowers."

scripts.say: Hmm... Commander, are you sure this verse connects with the previous one?
I guess not, but... When I look at you, it feels like everything wants to connect back to the starting verse...
"If not a fairy descended the mountains, she must be a goddess bathed in moonlight" ...I think those words describe you perfectly, Hai Tien.
Um... I, I guess I can overlook this and not count this as your loss...
Well done! Let's keep it up–
"As song comes from boats, flowers line the shore."
Let me think... Urgh, I don't think I can come up with anything else...
Heehee. It appears that I'm the victor. Now then... "A flower must be harvested when the time is right. Wait not until the branches are empty."
Commander, would you mind making me a flower crown?
(A flower crown? That shouldn't be a very difficult request...)
I nod my head and agree to go along with Hai Tien's request.
Just as I am hard at work scavenging for flowers and branches, weaving them together into a circlet large enough to rest atop her head...
I feel a slender, soft hand slide into my own, gently dropping a carefully-crafted ring of grass into my palm.
My eyes turn towards the hand's owner. It is not just her cheeks that are bright red this time – even the tips of her ears are dyed an adorable pink.
This is... my way of thanking you for the flower crown.
Her voice sounds tender, almost wavering.

sequence:
Set Sail! An Inspiration-Seeking Journey

<size=45>4 A Short Story</size>

scripts.say: Hum hum~♪
Hai Tien walks next to me with a sprightly spring in her step, wearing the semblance of a flower crown that I had crafted on her head.
As I follow her, I also wear the ring of grass she had made for me on my left hand.
We continue to pass through a tiny trail in the forest, and eventually arrive at a pleasant clearing that seems perfect for camping.
Commander, shall we pitch the tent? I'd be glad to help out.
Sure, good idea.
Though this is the first time camping for both of us, we still manage to get the tent set up without any difficulty.
(Hmm... The sun might get pretty intense soon. Maybe I should throw up the tarp?)
Commander, is there anything else I can help with?
Uhh, I think I'll be fine. Here, I just finished unfolding the chairs. Take a breather and see if you can come up with any inspiration.
I can put up the tarp by myself.
Well then, I'll leave it to you.
As I go to set up the tarp, I suddenly hear Hai Tien's voice.
No, not like that! The emotion here is completely off! There needs to be more intimacy in your expression!
Yes, yes, that's it! That's exactly how you should be looking at your crush!
(Hmm? That's weird... I don't think there's anyone else here, so who is she talking to...?)
Curiosity gets the better of me, and I stop what I'm doing to head back to where Hai Tien is–
At some point, a whole bunch of squirrels had lined up in front of her.
And Hai Tien is... enthusiastically teaching them to act.
When I listen in a bit more, I notice that the content of her "playbook" seems to be from the novel she was working on before.
Squeak, squeak!
Squeak! Squeak squeak squeak!
You're doing great~ That's exactly the emotion you want! Next, the storm scene is about to start!
Hold your lover tight, and let her feel your heartbeat–
There's a certain magic to her fairytale-like story that puts a wide smile on my face.
The question is, how is Hai Tien able to teach the lines to the squirrels? Does she know how to communicate with them...?

sequence:
Set Sail! An Inspiration-Seeking Journey

<size=45>5 An Unseen Scenery</size>

scripts.say: I finish setting up the tarp and then come back to watch Hai Tien for a little longer before the squirrels scurry off.
Your story's pretty captivating, Hai Tien.
Oh, umm... I got a bit carried away in the moment. I forgot that you'd be able to hear me.
By the way, are you able to talk to squirrels?
Huh? I definitely can't...
What? The way they were moving and responding to you made it seem like you were able to communicate with them...
I think they were just responding to me being nice to them...
The reason it looked like we were communicating is probably because of some preconception on your part, Commander~
Since you've been working so hard, why don't you take a seat and rest for a while? We can take another walk around the area later.
Actually, I'm good to go still.
I put down the work tools and start taking Hai Tien around our campsite.
Hmm? Do you see that little trail over there?
I look in the direction she's pointing.
Looks promising. Want to head over and take a look?
The path leads to a grassy clearing, and there's even a little lake in the distance.
"Winding paths lead to secluded beauty" ...I'm not sure this saying quite captures the essence of this place, but...
This scenery is quite different from what we've seen so far in the woods.
That's true.
Heehee. That's an interesting idea. You certainly have a way with words, Commander.
"Willow threads sway in the wind, the grass' garments trimmed by the rain"...
I never expected to see such beautiful scenery here.
Commander. I've got it. I think I just had an epiphany.
The girl next to me gently gets up on her tiptoes, and rests her head against my shoulder.

sequence:
Set Sail! An Inspiration-Seeking Journey

<size=45>6 The Distance Between Us</size>

scripts.say: Hai Tien and I continue our leisurely stroll through this wonderful new scenery.
Oh, I really should head back to the campsite soon.
Shall we go together, Commander?
Sure thing.
Just at that time, rain starts to fall from what had been a seemingly boundless blue sky just moments ago.
We are still a fair distance away from the campsite, and even if we try to hurry back, the trail would be muddy and slippery by the time we get there.
To avoid any potential accidents, the two of us decide to take shelter nearby and wait for the rain to pass.
Looks like luck hasn't completely abandoned us after all. I didn't expect to find a cave like this so quickly...
Heehee. Might this be the "promising" thing that you mentioned earlier?
Hai Tien covers her mouth and giggles in a mischievous way that I've rarely seen from her before.
It isn't until then that I notice, her casual clothes are drenched in rain and clinging tightly to her body.
Maybe it's because the fabric is slightly transparent, but, I can't help but to marvel at her skin, almost as fair as pure white snow.
*cough*... Oh, umm, there are some rocks and dry twigs here.
Let's try to make a fire and dry our clothes out.
After much effort, I am finally able to start a fire.
It's getting a bit dull sitting around waiting for the rain to stop... Want me to tell you a fairytale to pass the time?
As Hai Tien nestles up to me, the light from the bonfire flickers in her eyes, making her gaze even more dazzling than usual.
Is it a story that you wrote yourself?
Not this time. Commander, have you ever heard of the "Legend of the Umbrella Lent Upon a Lakeside Sojourn"?
I can't say I have.
In ancient times, there once was a man named Xu Xian who was sweeping tombs during the Qingming Festival. When he reached West Lake, it started raining all of a sudden.
During the heavy rain, he met a white snake spirit that had transformed itself into a young girl.
The two shared the same boat, and began to fall in love with one another...
Hai Tien cups her cheeks with her palms, smiling softly as she continues her story.
By the time the boat reaches the shore, the rain has still not let up, so Xu Xian lends his oil-paper umbrella to the girl.
And that umbrella becomes a symbol of the love between them.
Unfortunately...
Hm?
Unfortunately, even though we're caught up in the heavy rain, I'm unable to be like the snake spirit-turned-girl and borrow something from you...
Huh?
I hold out my left hand to the confused Hai Tien and show her the ring woven from grass that she had given me earlier.
That's... the ring I made for you today...
Wait, Commander... Does this mean...?
Suddenly, as if a realization had just dawned upon Hai Tien, the girl leaps straight into my arms.
Umm, Commander, you're still soaking wet, and even if there's a bonfire here, it's still quite cold inside the cave...
I apologize for my indiscretion, but... this is for the sake of your health!
The constant pitter-patter of the rain seemingly cuts the two of us off from the outside world.
The light from the flame suddenly dances in a flurry, and my vision is temporarily obscured by the flight of the girl's damp clothes–
And all that I see next is lustrous, moist skin, as fair as pure white snow.

sequence:
Set Sail! An Inspiration-Seeking Journey

<size=45>7 Wellspring of Inspiration</size>

scripts.say: Perhaps it was the heat from the bonfire, or perhaps it was the warmth of our bodies pressed together.
I'm not sure when it was that we fell asleep, but when I next open my eyes, the rain had already stopped.
Hai Tien?
The girl next to me still has her eyes shut, her lips curled into a slight smile, a look of contentment on her face.
As I call out to her, she slowly begins to stir.
Huh...? Commander?
When she realizes how "close" the two of us are, a familiar blush once again spreads across her cheek.s
Um, I'm so sorry for what just happened... I don't know what came over me...
It's fine, don't worry about it.
C-Commander... Since the rain has stopped, umm.. sh-should we put out the fire and head back?
The embarrassment from her words is so thick that it's almost palpable.
Mm, sounds good to me.
We step out from the cave, back into the picturesque scenery we had accidentally discovered.
After the rain, the sun shines brightly once more. A rainbow streaks across the clear, blue sky.
"The seven-colored bridge cleaves the rain, the autumnal sky pristine and clear. Upon the mounts' brow, fresh verdance doth appear."
Though the seasons don't quite line up, the scene that this poem describes really resonates with me.
I'm so glad that I was able to enjoy such a splendid view together with you, Commander. Going on this camping trip truly was a worthwhile experience.
Last but not least, I've found the inspiration to continue my story.
Oh, right. You did say you had an epiphany earlier when we were taking in the scenery.
Yes, that's right.
The inspiration only came to me because I was with you.
More importantly... When love nestles within your heart, words will flow forth freely like a fountain.
In other words, the wellspring of my inspiration... is none other than you, Commander.
Hai Tien takes my left hand and gently strokes the ring that she had woven herself. Her adorable smile blooms as brightly as any flower.

options.content: Ah- looks like she ran out of steam this time.

Hammann~♪ Let's play~

... But forget about all of that! Right this instant!

Didn't this only happen in the first place because you can't give a proper apology?

Wait, what am I going to do? ...That's right, you should ask Yorktown!
Good point! If anyone would know what to do, it's Yorktown...! Thanks, Sims! Look after the office for me, okay?

Ah... there she goes again...
