<size=45>2 Secret Sanctuary</size>

scripts.say: Okay, so... How exactly are we supposed to find props for the show?
As I follow Fleuret's light, rhythmical steps, I ask a question that's been on my mind.
Heheh, they're all in my secret sanctuary, of course!
And it's exactly where I wanted to take you today, Commander!
When she opens the door, I'm overwhelmed by the combined scent of old wood, cloth, and paper.
Though the room is dimly lit, the items lined up inside are dazzling.
Is this like a warehouse?
Ding-ding! It's a storage room for my magic props!
Look! This is a box you use for the Sub Trunk illusion! And that prop is for putting coins through glass!
Every single prop here has its own unique function.
While she explains it all, curiosity drives me over to a very plain-looking wooden cane.
What about this cane? It looks pretty normal to me.
Heheh! That one has a secret compartment with a bouquet of flowers inside!
She rushes over, takes my hand, and has me grasp the handle.
Take this, twist a little, and...
Poof! Out comes a bouquet of bright-red roses. At the same time, a smile blooms on Fleuret's face.
Hmm? Something wrong, Commander? What's with the suspicious look?
VERY suspicious... Wait a minute, I know what this is.
You must have a crush on this glorious magician!
I was just struck by how happy you are.
All of these props of yours seem so... professional. By the way, which ones are we using for the show?
Umm...
Her expression turns serious as she approaches a large, old-fashioned box. It's black and heavy-looking.
The surface is wrapped in worn leather with inlaid brass latches and hinges. Several small holes are also poked in the sides, likely for air flow.
Is that it? No wonder you came to me for help. That thing even LOOKS heavy.
It was used for escape magic, so it's made to be super sturdy. There are some mechanisms on the inside that make it so you can open it from within.
So the plan is to use this to show off your escape magic?
No... Not quite. The essence of magic isn't all found in elaborate contrivances.
It's like the card trick from earlier. What matters isn't the cards themselves, but the surprise and mystery they evoke.
Props are only there as a bridge to help the magician convey those feelings.
That's not to say they're meaningless. Higher-quality props help make the magic more exciting and communicate the magician's intentions better.
Back on topic, though... It's thick enough, the construction is simple, and most of all...
Look how spacious it is! This bad boy could fit TWO Commanders in it!
True... Wait, don't tell me.
Heheheh! Have you pieced together the incredible trick we're going to perform?
I have a feeling...
Oh really? Maybe you do have what it takes to be a master magician!
You've already read my mind, after all.
Alright, spill the beans. What's it going to be?
Heheh... Tell me, are you ready to get stabbed in the heart?

sequence:
Magician of Flowers and Swords

<size=45>3 A Floral Stage</size>

scripts.say: With the magic tricks for the show planned out, we took the box to a secluded garden.
The afternoon sun cast dappled shadows through the branches and leaves, and the wind carried the scent of flowers.
Look, Commander! This is the stage I chose!
You're going to do it here in the garden?
Yep. The sunlight, breeze, and flowers make for a more relaxing stage than even the most elegant auditoriums.
I think the sheer wonder of magic will stand out better here than anywhere else.
Besides, don't you think the lighting is perfect for a sort of mysterious mood?
Is the mood that important for this kind of trick?
Of course! Mood-making is one of the most important parts of magic.
Even thrilling tricks like my Commander Heart-Stabberoo are no exception.

options.content: Wasn't it called the Sword Box illusion?

scripts.say: Scary name... Any chance we can change it?
Heheh, nope! That's how magic tricks are supposed to be named.
Like "sawing a woman in half" or "water torture escape." Simple, easy to remember, AND attention-grabbing!
Wasn't it called the Sword Box illusion? Why are we going and changing the established name now?
It's a little different! Because I specifically wanna pierce your heart!
Heheh. Just wait and see!
Am I in danger?
Don't worry! I carefully calculated the holes' positions before making them, so you'll definitely be safe!
All you have to do is stand exactly where I marked.
Then, I'll use these sharp-looking prop swords to stab stickers that I've put over the holes...
Stab! Stab! Stab! By the time I'm done, the box will look like a hedgehog from the outside, and people will think I've run you through!
But in reality, the swords will be inserted diagonally to create a safe space inside... right?
You got it! I'll take the swords out, open the box, and bam! The Commander's alive and well!
Everyone in the crowd will be astonished!
Quit worrying so much! This might be my first time doing this trick, but magic tricks are basically all the same when you get right down to it!
I'm REALLY looking forward to getting to put on a show with you, okay?
But we can't show everyone else yet. Not until it's perfect.
So Commander... Today, you're gonna be my personal assistant and guinea pig!
We're gonna practice, practice, practice here in this secret location until we've had it down pat.
Until I can guarantee that you can come out without a scratch, AND have fun doing it!
Because that's the most important part of a magic show – even more important than the audience's applause!

sequence:
Magician of Flowers and Swords

<size=45>4 Precise Positioning</size>

scripts.say: After a full afternoon of preparation, we managed to set up a simple but convincing stage and curtain in the garden.
Phew... Stage, check! Curtain, check! Lighting... Hmm, natural will do!
It sure feels like a magic show now. I'm glad our efforts were worthwhile.
Heheh. A stage is a bridge between the magician and their audience.
From the curtains and lights to every word they say, all of it carries the intention of conveying wonder to the viewer.
It's really touching... to see this empty space gradually turned into one that carries the potential of magic.
Commander, thank you so much for helping me create this wonderful stage! Hehe... What kind of reward would you like?

options.content: I'll have to think about that.

scripts.say: If you're happy, I'm happy. That said, it still looks far from complete...
Don't worry about it! You've already done enough for me.
A reward, huh? I'll have to think about that.
Hehe! Take your time. When you have an idea, you know where to find me.
Now, we still need to do the most important part: setting up this magic box in the right position!
Tricks hit best if they're positioned just right.
I'm ready! Let's carry it up to the stage together.
The box is heavier than I expected, but with her help, we slowly but surely begin carrying it to the middle of the stage.
She carefully walks backward with it, all the while thinking of our coming rehearsals.
When we rehearse later, I'll call out, "Assistant!" That's when you come out from behind the curtain and get into the box. Make it a little theatrical, okay?
I'll stand right here and strike a cool pose with my sword...
Perhaps too focused on her plans, Fleuret trips over a board protruding slightly from the stage floor!
Ack!
She screams, loses her balance, and nearly falls...
Though she tries to hold the box tight to right herself, that only ends up dragging it along with her to the ground.
Fleuret?! Oh, man!
It all happened so fast. I tried to catch her by the hand, but before I knew it, her momentum pulled us both straight into the open box.
Due to the impact of the fall, the lid slams shut with a shudder-inducing click.
Then it all ends, and the box is filled with nothing but stifling darkness and silence.
I'm half on top of Fleuret. In this cramped space, we can only hear each other's ragged breathing.
C-Commander? Are you okay?!
Yeah... I'm fine.
Don't panic! Let's assess the situation.
I manage to calm her down, straighten up, and push on the lid of the box. However, it doesn't budge no matter how much force I put into it.
Are we... locked in here?

sequence:
Magician of Flowers and Swords

<size=45>5 Alone in a Black Box</size>

scripts.say: In the small, dark box, the air gradually becomes thick and hot.
Fleuret's basically in my arms at this point. Though the initial panic has subsided a little, we can't help but blush at the situation.
*sniffle*... I promised I'd show you the coolest magic trick ever, but now... it's all ruined.
Don't worry about it – I know it was an accident. Besides, this is plenty astonishing.
Are you making fun of me right now?
You're not wrong, though... Who knew I'd end up locked in the box I made? And with you, at that... Uuugh...
Like I said, it's fine. Everybody makes mistakes.
Are you scared of the dark, by chance?
Why do I ask? Well, she grabbed my hand the moment we got locked inside, and she hasn't let go since.
After a while, I'd decided to return the favor to reassure her.
It's normal to feel apprehensive when you're stuck in a dark place and can't get out.
That's not it... I was scared before, yeah, but not because it was dark.
What I'm really afraid of... is for something we both worked so hard on to be wasted all because of my stupid mistake.
That won't happen. All we have to do is find a way out of this.
Don't worry. We'll get out of here.
Okay... I think I see why the best magicians need serious mental fortitude.

When the curtain rises, the spotlights turn on, and all eyes gather on you... The sheer pressure of having to meet their expectations and fear of the unknown... That's what really makes you feel locked up.
But holding your hand now, I know I'm not alone. It helps me feel at ease.
Maybe that's why the best magicians need assistants.
Not just to draw the audience's attention, but to share the heavy loneliness that comes from being on stage and not knowing what might go wrong.
To share the loneliness? That's one way to put it... A really devious way...
In the darkness, I fail to see the bashful, yet happy smile on her face.
Fleuret... Are you sure we can't open this from the inside?
Well... It's made for escape tricks.
So it's impossible to force open the main lock from the inside! That's like the whole gimmick!
Her voice regains its usual vitality, but it still has a faint, embarrassed tremble to it.
But a TRUE escape artist would always leave a loophole! Remember that little mechanism I mentioned?
What mechanism?
One to open a secret door, of course. Right below me... There's a small board you can move. It needs a special key, though.
A-and, well... The key is in a secret pocket in the lining of my jacket...
After much hesitation, she reluctantly produces a noticeably warm key.
Commander... The keyhole should be... behind you.
In the darkness, she leans forward. As she fumbles the key into the hole, her bewitchingly warm breath tickles my ears.

sequence:
Magician of Flowers and Swords

<size=45>6 Pierced Through the Heart</size>

scripts.say: With a gentle click, the secret door on the bottom of the box opens.
A flowery scent and cool night air flow into the cramped space, relieving us of the stifling air from before.
Fleuret scrambles out of the box, sucks in a deep breath of fresh air, looks up at the sky – and screams.
Wha?! I-it's already dark out!
Oh, no! We haven't even rehearsed yet! Commander, we're running out of time! We're gonna have to go do it off the cuff!
As soon as I crawl out, she seizes my arm and drags me behind the curtains.
In the dark of early night, her cheeks are still flushed – but her eyes gleam with the confidence and excitement of a master magician.
Have faith in me! Just like you did in the box!
All you have to do now is follow my orders.
Let's make tonight a miracle together!
Alright!
After that, she rushes onto the stage like a gust of wind.
With an elegant twirl, she puts on a show for an audience of none – or rather, an audience of the flowers and stars.
Ladies and gentlemen, and our dearest Commander!
Welcome to Fleuret's Night of Miracles! Prepare to witness the thrilling sight of countless swords piercing one heart!
Assistant, please step into this box! Yes, right now!
Well done! Now, if you'd please lean to the left a little... Lower your head... Good! Yes, that angle is perfect! Just trust me.
Let the first sword pierce illusions!
Let the second pierce fear!
Two right off the bat?! This isn't what I was led to expect!
Worry not! These two are only meant to frame the following ones! As long as you don't touch them, none of the others will hit you.
Before she even finishes speaking, wooden swords pierce through the holes in the box one after another.
From the outside, it must really look like a hedgehog!
Now, Commander, lean left a little. Remember to steady your center of gravity!
Left, huh... Like this?
Perfect!
See? We're totally in tune with each other!
Which way is left, again?
If you're nervous, then just trust your intuition!
Yeah, just like that... You're doing great, Commander!
Let the seventh sword bear witness to indomitable courage!
And finally... Close your eyes, and listen to your heart...
She takes a sweeping look across the garden, inhales deeply, and stabs the last sword. Her voice is a mix of excitement and just the slightest tinge of nervousness.
Let the final sword pierce the dark and usher in a miracle!
Now, let us welcome the hero's safe return!
Commander, take my hand! Together, we'll meet their applause! Well, except for the fact that there's nobody around except the moon and flowers.
I take her hand without hesitation, and she guides me out of the box.
Even when I'm on my feet again, she doesn't let go – in fact, she holds on tighter. Meanwhile, she raises her other hand high to point at our surroundings.
Then, like a magician finally unveiling her secrets, she speaks up with tenderness and pride.
Commander, look! That's the real magic I prepared just for you – the Commander Heart-Stabberoo!
When I cast my eyes over the garden again, the sight takes my breath away.

sequence:
Magician of Flowers and Swords

<size=45>7 Swords, Flowers, and You</size>

scripts.say: Buds and vines that had been closed and drooping earlier today begin standing upright and blooming beneath the moonlight, right before my very eyes.
Beautiful white flowers bloom in unison, exuding a soft luster and comforting scent.
In the space of a few minutes, the entire garden is covered in countless moonflowers, like a river of moonlight spreading across the land.
So, Commander. Have the floral swords around us finally managed to pierce your heart?
The moonlight washes over the sea of flowers and flows quietly around the two of us.
Heheh, do you like it? This is my real magic trick – making a whole garden of moonflowers bloom all at once.
It's way more astonishing than that dumb old box, isn't it?
I prepared this big trick just for you, just for tonight.
Was this your plan all along? You know, I had a feeling you were hiding something from me.
When she sees my genuine surprise, Fleuret raises her index finger and wags it playfully.
Heheh! Do you get it now? A true magician can't be confined to simple props like boxes or swords!
The moon, the earth, the dormant flowers... All of nature is my stage and my props!
She takes a step forward and looks up to the sky. Moonlight flows into her eyes.
The magician holds her arms out, as if picking up the entire garden, and gently brings it over to me.
This sea of moonflowers is my real present to you, Commander! It's unique, it's just for you, and it could've happened only tonight!
What do you say? Isn't this magic a million times more moving than cold props and tricks?
Tell me, is your heart pounding like a drum?
Yeah. It was astonishing... Thank you, Fleuret.
Yeah. It was beautiful... Thank you, Fleuret.
My words make her eyes sparkle even more.
She sidles closer with exposed shyness and expectation.
Did you know, Commander? Every flower has its own unique meaning.
Like a magician's hand gestures, they all have special little messages that only some people know...
Try guessing... what the moonflowers here all mean to me...
The wind stops, and the moonlight dims just a little. Our breathing and the gentle wavering of flowers were the only signs of motion in the garden.
...I don't know. Why don't you tell me, magician of flowers and swords?
She quietly releases my hand. While I watch her in surprise, she takes a half-step back.
Then, she bows elegantly – not to an imaginary audience, but to me alone.
Moonflowers... symbolize a bond that will never falter.
Fleuret straightens up again, places a hand on the hilt of her sword, and strokes a nearby flower with the other.
Her posture is simultaneously reminiscent of that of a knight attending to her liege, and of a magician ready to reveal her final trick.
What I mean to say is...
My sword, the flowers that have bloomed tonight, and my heart...
All of them...
I offer to you, Commander.
That's the miracle I wanted you to witness♡
Port - Dragon Empery Dorm
Lady Veneto, we have arrived.
Oh! Look at all these decorations. My, the Empery holiday mood is in full swing here.
I'll have to make note of this... And that...
See? I told you it was worth a visit. Since we have plenty of time to look around, does anything catch your eye?
Hmm... No, I can't seem to think of anything in particular.
Then let's just walk around. Who knows, maybe we'll come across something interesting?
Something like...
BANG!
What?! What was that?
It came from over there! Come on, follow me!
The Sardegnian shipgirls followed the cloud of smoke rising into the air and soon arrived at its point of origin.
Greetings! ...Oh, I don't see you girls every day. Do you have business at our dorm or something?
Ah! If it isn't Hu Pen and Fei Yuen. It's been a while.
It's the Sardegnians! The cuisine-knowers! Hello hello!
Yat Sen said anyone who visits is a guest, so just come to Lady Yuen if you need something!
Um... thank you? I should mention that we aren't here on a formal visit or anything.
Rather, we're here to watch and learn from how the Dragon Empery celebrates its holidays.
Indeed. I hope we're not intruding on anything.
See, many of our fellow Sardegnians have expressed an interest in your holiday customs.
We would like to decorate our dormitory in the same style as yours and perhaps even have some fun together.
Aquila here is our most knowledgeable lady when it comes to your culture, so we brought her along.
Please, my knowledge starts and ends at what I've read in comic books.
I see! I understand perfectly!
You've come to the right place, my friends!
But, your timing isn't the best. We have our hands full in the kitchen and nobody's available to give you a tour right now!
That's fine. We'll just wander around and see for ourselves.
One thing we're wondering about, though – was that an explosion just a minute ago?
- No! - It wasn't an explosion!
It was a culinary experiment, that's all!
A what...? Oh, yeah, what she said! She's trying to come up with a new dish!
With a kind of stir-frying. The kind that goes "bang"!
Oh, I've read about this in a comic! It's the "big flame, ample oil" technique, no?
You crank the heat up, use copious amounts of oil, and fry like you're trying to make the food blow up. That explains the noise we heard!
It does...?
I mean...
Y-yeah! I'm surprised you know one of our country's most well-kept cooking secrets!
If you don't believe us, we'll cook a feast for you tonight! That's sure to help with your own festival prep.
Sounds like a promising idea. What's your take, Veneto?
No objections here. While we're at it, though, can we invite others to join us? Us Sardegnians surely aren't the only ones interested.
Go right ahead! We'll make enough of this new dish to feed every last guest! You have Lady Yuen's word on this!
A bold proposition. We accept. Now, if you'll excuse us, we have other places we want to check out.
Sure! See you later!
Phew...
They would so have caught on to us if it weren't for my quick wit...
We can NOT let the other factions find out how bad of a cook Chi An is!
Ahahahah...
To be honest, I'm worried about her.
Worried? Why?
I mean, she just made the kitchen go kaboom, so...
Wait, Chi An?! Err, um... I was just kidding!
Y-yeah! We both know you would never intentionally blow up the kitchen and leave a huge mess!
Um, that's kind of rude.
What we're saying is: it's okay! C'mon, Fei Yuen, say something!
Huh?
Oh, uh... Chi An, your kitchen adventure was astonishing! It almost moved Lady Yuen to tears!
*sniffle*... I can't believe this!
Look what you did. You made her cry!
Let's clean this place up before poor Chi An feels any worse!
After moving through the kitchen like a cleaning tornado, the girls eventually got it looking like it did before.
Whew... Good as new. Thanks, you two.
Don't thank me. As long as you're happy, I'm happy!
No, you deserve it. I DID blow up the kitchen and cause a mess for you to clean up. I'm sorry.
It's not like it's the first time...
Ah, forget it! We have more important things to focus on!
True. The Sardegnians are visiting for dinner tonight.
Right, right! They're real gourmands, so we need to plate up a whole feast!
Yes, but who's going to cook?
Lung Wu, obviously!
When it comes to cooking, you can trust her to deliver!
Speaking of Lung Wu, I haven't actually seen her all day. Do either of you know where she is?
Hm... She's not at the port today.
She, Yat Sen, and a few others are out buying things for Lunar New Year. Did nobody tell you?
Now that you mention it... She DID tell me to get my food from the canteen today.
Hold on, doesn't that mean there are no good cooks available?
Then how are we supposed to serve dinner to the Sardegnians tonight?!
No, calm down, Lady Yuen... You've been in this situation countless times... Just calm down and think about it...
I've got it! Let's go ask the Commander for advice!
Port - Dragon Empery Dorm
Looking up the words "Huan Ch'ang" written on the door plate, I couldn't help but wonder... How did it come to this?
Commander's office, 30 minutes earlier...
SLAM!
We're in trouble, Commander!
Lady Yuen needs your help, Commander!
The door to my office is thrown open, and in jumps two little shipgirls.
Seeing the anxious looks on their faces makes me tense up.

options.content: Let's take a deep breath now.

scripts.say: Okay, let me explain...
Some Sardegnian girls came to visit, and I ran my big stupid mouth and promised them a huge feast tonight...
It's not your fault, Yuen! You didn't know all our cooks were away today. I didn't either, or else I'd have stopped you!
But what's done is done, and we need your help, Commander!
Not only are we known for our delicious food, we also finished our holiday preparations the earliest so we have no excuse to delay!
It's gonna bring terrible shame to our name if we serve our guests food that tastes like crap!
(Sardegna came to visit? Oh, yeah, Veneto did say something about wanting to celebrate Lunar New Year.)
(They probably came to the Empery dorm, then this and that happened...)
(Wait a second, something feels odd here.)
(Why did she "run her mouth" to begin with? Was she just boasting, or was she covering something up?)

options.content: Why did you invite them to dinner to begin with?

scripts.say: Well... Ahahaha... You know...
It's complicated...
They were forthcoming a moment ago, and now they're reluctant to share anything, looking back towards the door.
I follow their gazes and spot a figure in the hallway – Chi An, peeking in through the gap.
Oh dear... Why me...
Ahem... Good morning, Commander!
Ah, right! You have to forgive me, I've been rather forgetful as of late.
Lunch? Not yet.
I was actually making lunch earlier, but I had a small... accident.
As a result, it's on hold for now. Heehee!
(I get it. The Sardegnian visitors saw this "accident" and Fei Yuen invited them to dinner as a coverup.)
(Knowing these three, they only made it harder to ignore what happened.)
I shoot Chi An a look of doubt – among other feelings – as she tries to act cute.
Don't look at me like that... It hurts my feelings.
I tried, okay? I really tried to cook something.
I just need to keep practicing and practicing. I'll be able to make good food one day, I'm sure of it!
Yeah, right...
Ahem! Sorry, that's a distant future issue. We've got a near future issue to deal with! Like, TONIGHT near-future!
You're a good cook yourself, aren't you, Commander? What if we just let you handle the...
...I'll take that as a no.
I think the Commander wants to say we got ourselves into this mess, so we should solve it ourselves.
Don't you know your way around the kitchen, Hu Pen? You're always helping Lung Wu with her cooking.
Oh yeah, I do.
While I'm no five-star chef like her, I certainly can make some good eatin' with the right ingredients!
The problem is – we don't have the ingredients...
Let's ask Huan Ch'ang! She'll get the bagua to point us in the right direction!
I don't think that's such a hot idea... She won't like diving a solution to a problem of our making.
But... what if the Commander asked for us?
If anyone can persuade her, it's the Commander!
Chi An, say something! Convince the Commander to do it!
Okay... Commander, do it for me? Pleeease?
(Dang it. I got caught up in a mess.)
(Probably.)
Who is it?
Huan Ch'ang's Place - Living Room
Have a seat.
My divinations told me unexpected visitors were coming, but I sure didn't think it would you and an entourage of Empery girls, Commander.
What brings you here? Do you need my help?
So you knew we were coming! That's our bagua fortune-teller for you!
And yeah, that's exactly why we're here!
See, we're actually in a real pickle here...
We invited another faction to dine with us tonight, but Lung Wu is away and I'm the only one who can cook the food.
And I'm not even half the chef she is!
But! I can make up for it if I can just get some good ingredients!
Which is what we need help with! Huan Ch'ang, can you please divine where to find ingredients that'll make delicious food?
In order to do that, I need to know the cause and consequences of the events that led you to this point.
You'll need to give me more details.
For a start, why did you suddenly invite them to dinner if Lu Wung wasn't there?
...It was because I ran my mouth and made a promise I couldn't keep. Sorry.
Please don't be mad at Lady Yuen...
L-look, what's done is done!
We can't let down our guests, or we'll sully both Lung Wu's name and the rep of our cuisine!
Chi An, are they telling the truth?
Um... Umm...
It's okay, little ones. I know you don't want to be rude, but you don't need to walk on eggshells for my sake.
In truth, this was all my fault. I was in the kitchen, and–
You insisted on cooking, caused an accident, and just by pure bad luck, the Sardegnians happened to be visiting at the same time. Is that right?
Huh? Wait, did you divine all that?
No, it doesn't matter. Yes, you're exactly right. I caused an explosion in the kitchen.
It's fine. You can laugh at me.
I can?
Yes.
Heh... Heheh...
You actually blew up the kitchen. Wow. I knew you were a bad cook, but this is something else.
Hmph. It's not THAT funny.
Just because I'm from the Empery doesn't mean I was born with great cooking skills.
That's a stereotype, you know.
What I lack in talent, I'm trying to make up for with hard work and practice. I'll get good at it eventually.
Of course. Keep at it. Now, how do you want me to help?
It's simple. We'd like you to divine where to find the ingredients Hu Pen needs.
Just to be sure – you're not going to "help" in the kitchen, are you?
Heehee, no. I know my limits.
One last thing, then. Commander, as the one who knocked on my door, what is your opinion on this?
The heavens discern not between matters great and small, good or evil.
I'd like to hear a reason for me to call upon the bagua.
(Is she asking me to give the final push?)
(Alright then...)

options.content: We already have the right time and right place. What we need is the right person.
We'll never know what the heavens decide if we don't at least try.
I need your help, my lovely Huan Ch'ang!

scripts.say: Such sophistry...
But, given the current situation, I suppose it's not beyond the realm of possibility...
If you insist...
So you're leaving it to me?
But, given the current situation, I suppose it's not beyond the realm of possibility...
If you insist...
...Wow.
Hey!
Wh-what's with you? You don't say that in front of people...
Ahem... Alright... I'll start divining now...
Of paths fiftyfold, only forty-nine may be divined. The hidden truth is...
...I've got it.
You can catch good fish at the port's freshwater lake.
For some reason, she shoots me a glance when she says that.
(Hm? Is she talking about the same freshwater lake where we went fishing the other day?)
(Does she want to fish some more?)
Really?!
Hooray! Let's get going, then!
I'll come with you.
Since the bagua pointed us there, now I'm curious to see what ingredients we'll get.
Port - Freshwater Lake
Huan Ch'ang led the way, bringing us beneath a canopy by the lakeside.
Here we are.
Whoa! I never knew we had a place like this by the lake!
This looks like a great spot for fishing!
Oh, shoot! Lady Yuen forgot to bring a fishing rod!
I did.
As they say, plan ahead for rainy days. Opportunities come only to those who prepare for them.
Huan Ch'ang produces a fishing rod seemingly out of nowhere.
That's a looong rod!
Hey, do you come here to fish often, Huan?
Only sometimes. To clear my mind. I wouldn't call it "often."
In addition, I'm not the only one who comes here to relax.
Huan Ch'ang shoots me a glance.
(The cat's out of the bag.)
Oh! The Commander brought one, too!
Hang on, there's not just a tackle box under the canopy. There's a cooking stove and a fridge as well!
You could set up camp here, or cook food for a picnic!
Gosh. Huan Ch'ang's "divination" sure led us to a special spot, hm?
Ahem...
It IS a nice place. It's got a great atmosphere, it's compact, and it has all the equipment you need.
Say, do you come here often with the Commander?
Well... occasionally.
Right. "Occasionally."
The first time really was a coincidence!
I came out to fish one day, and it suddenly started raining.
I knew it was going to, because I divined it. I came prepared and set up under the canopy.
Then, just as I thought I was going to be fishing alone, someone came seeking shelter...
My only catch that day was a fishing buddy. I couldn't go home emptyhanded.
Ever since then, the canopy has stood right here.
As time went on and we fished more together, we slowly added more amenities and upgrades.
Ahh, no wonder...
Wait, "couldn't go home emptyhanded"? You didn't catch a single fish that day?
Well... Fishing is about doing all you can and letting fate run its course.
The fact that I didn't catch anything just means the heavens didn't ordain it! Do you understand?
I don't...
It's fine if you don't...
Enough talking! Can I fish now, Huan?
Of course. The whole reason we came here is to catch ingredients for your dinner.
Lady Yuen wants to try, too!
Yay! Thanks, Commander!
Heheh! Watch this! I'm gonna catch the biggest fish you've ever seen!
Easy, now. Fishing is a matter of patience.
Hold your rod steady. Don't scare the fish off, or they'll never–
Nibble! I got a nibble!
Me too!
Huan Ch'ang's advice is interrupted by the girls both getting something on the hook. They reel in their catches – two large fish.
WHAT?!
This has to be beginner's luck...
It's ginormous! You were right, Huan! These are good fish!
Got another on the hook!
A... Another?
Is this your luckiest day of the year or what?!
Shocked by their success, Huan Ch'ang starts quickly divinating.
No... The bagua isn't aligned right... How are you catching so many?
Unless... the lake itself...
...Have people been overfeeding the fish?
But even then, that doesn't explain how you've caught so many big fish in a row.

sequence:
Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard

<size=45>1 Cannons, Sails, and Engineering</size>

scripts.say: Lights!
Music!
Greetings, everybody! Welcome to my secret shipyard!
Well, the effects were brilliant, but the speech could use some work.
Let's try that again...
Ahem! Greetings, everyone! This is the start of my great journey across the seven seas!
Welcome! Welcome to my secret shipyard!
Yeah! That's more like it!
Before we go on, I'd like to ask you all a question...
What is a sailing frigate?
Now, ya don't need to answer right away. Just scrounge up all the knowledge about them ya can think of.
Go through every little detail. Analyse your answer, and when you're confident in it, present it!
That's right! As its name suggests, it's an armed ship that uses its sails to harness the power of the wind to propel itself!
Its hull is larger than a typical sailing ship, and it even has armour plating and several decks.
Put some cannons on one, and you've got a fortress that can sail on water!
Where we Tempestas come from, sailing frigates are the undisputed rulers of the sea!
Yup – you're in the presence of a mighty battleship. Doesn't that make your heart race?
But enough telling, it's time to show. Let's get hands-on!
Because we are gonna build our own sailing frigate!

sequence:
Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard

<size=45>2 A Keel, a Soul</size>

scripts.say: Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard - Keel laid down
The keel is an oblong structural part located down the middle of the hull's underside. It connects with the ship's sternpost.
Its most important role is to function as the ship's load-bearing structure.
From an engineering mechanics perspective, the keel bears the hull's longitudinal bending moment.
In other words, an excellent hull is the proof of a ship's structural soundness.
Furthermore, the keel enlarges the ship's side surface area, which is really important when sailing in a headwind.
Its weight stabilises the ship, keeping it steady from heeling and unexpected turning.
To put it simply, the keel is the cornerstone of a ship.
And to a sailing frigate, it's like her core, or even her soul!
Of course, a keel alone cannot support an entire ship.
I want you to remember that its relationship to the ship's other components is just as vital.
Now, let's move on to the next step!

sequence:
Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard

<size=45>3 The Reinforcing Ribs</size>

scripts.say: Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard - Ribs connected
The ribs are vertical structures which link to both the inner walls of a wooden ship.
Their role is to support the hull, protect the hull's form, and absorb water pressure coming from the ship's sides.
They're what allow a sailing frigate to cruise steadily, and prevent the hull from deforming due to rocking and heaving.
Ships obviously want to be able to sail even when the seas are rough, and that's why they need top-rate ribs.
And to maintain a large fleet of them, you need a steady flow of good shipbuilding wood!
Believe it or not, some trees need to grow for centuries before they can be used to build a warship.
Luckily for us, we have just the wood we need at this shipyard!
With the ribs done, it's time to get started on the hull!

sequence:
Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard

<size=45>4 Stringers and Their Role</size>

scripts.say: Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard - Stringers installed
You need more than just the ribs to sufficiently support a hull.
And that's where the stringers come in!
Stringers are support structures placed lengthwise inside the hull. They're installed perpendicularly to the ribs and help form the ship's frame.
The point of stringers is to make the ship even more stable, and to further improve the hull's structural integrity.
The larger the ship, the more ribs and stringers it's going to have. The largest of them – first-rate ships – are like true oceangoing fortresses!
Granted, those are also stupidly expensive to maintain♪
Anyway, that's enough chitchat. Let's get back to construction!

sequence:
Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard

<size=45>5 Learning About Anti-Fouling Paint</size>

scripts.say: Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard - Hull exterior boarded
"Only those who journey far will know where their limits lie." The same is true for ships.
It doesn't matter if you use the best wood around – it's still gonna rot if it spends too long in the sea.
There are both visible and invisible organisms that attach to the ship's surface below the waterline.
While they do give it a pretty colour and create value from a visual standpoint, for the ship itself, they're bad news.
The organisms not only corrode the ship's bottom, but they also affect the cruising speed.
If ya don't do anything about 'em, they'll leave even a good warship riddled with holes in less than a year.
And that, my friends, is why we invented paints that protect against these organisms.
What we'll use is a mixture of rosin and tar that's called "black material." While its performance is average, it's pretty darn cheap!
Sadly, the coating will only last a year at most even if you lay it on thick. You're gonna need to repaint the ship every once in a while.
So, what have we learned? That the key to a ship staying seaworthy for a long time is regular and thorough maintenance!

sequence:
Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard

<size=45>6 Cannons Are Might</size>

scripts.say: Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard - Gun deck finished
At last, we've reached this exciting moment!
Cannons! The symbols of a sailing frigate's might!
The section where the cannons are installed – called the "gun deck" – comes in two different arrangements.
It's easy to tell them apart. It's about whether their cannons are arranged continuously along the sides, or if they're spaced out.
The number of cannons also determines the ship's rate – its ranking, essentially.
For example, compared to a fourth-rate ship, a first-rate ship typically has two more gun decks with continuous cannon arrangements.
A fourth-rate ship, meanwhile, has around 50 cannons less than a first-rate.
A nation commanding even one first-rate ship is proof of its navy's might!
Although, first-rates don't mean much to pirates, of course. Hahah!
On the open sea, speed is everything. Having way too many cannons will only slow you down.
And that is why any respectable fleet needs smaller ships as well.
A wise admiral builds their fleet according to the conditions and who they're fighting against.
That's a fact that still holds up after many centuries.

sequence:
Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard

<size=45>7 All About Decks</size>

scripts.say: Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard - Upper deck completed
There we go! The decks and the mast are finished. It's almost time to set her to sea!
But before that, I'd better give you a rundown on decks in general.
The main ones you should know about are the forecastle deck, the main deck, the quarterdeck, and the poop deck.
The forecastle deck lies at the very front of the ship.
The main deck is right above the gun deck. Or gun decks, in the case of larger ships.
The quarterdeck is situated just a bit ahead of the stern.
And the poop deck, as funny as it sounds, is located at the very rear of the ship.
It's the highest deck on the ship, and is usually where the helm and the captain's quarters are located.
Obviously, the position and structure of these decks will vary depending on the size of the ship.
That's the long and short of it! Let's hoist sails!

sequence:
Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard

<size=45>8 Hoist Sails!</size>

scripts.say: Royal Fortune's Secret Shipyard - Sails rigging finished
Everything's in order to set off, but there's one last thing I wanna tell you about.
You guessed it – it's about a ship's sails.
From bow to stern, you have the jib, the foresail, the mainsail, and lastly, the mizzensail.
When all these sails are raised at the same time, it's known as a "full sail."
And that is when the ship can cruise at its top speed.
But, ships usually lower some of their sails to adapt to the sea's often turbulent whims, a technique known as "reefing."
When the wind is weak, they raise sails to catch more of it, and when the wind is too strong, they do the opposite.
Doing this allows a ship to sail at a comparatively stable speed.
Knowing what to do in a storm is also required knowledge in order to sail.
When a storm blows, you raise only your topsail and keep all other sails lowered.
That way, your bow will stay raised, and you won't go off-course 'cause of any strong winds.
You could argue that mastering the art of raising and lowering your sails is THE most important part of sailing.
Then again, I reckon you folks already know that, no?
Now... Hoist sails and weigh anchor!
Let our great journey begin!

Port - Office

Heehee. Unable to reach a consensus on where to go on vacation, are you?
Pittsburgh walks in through the office door, holding an envelope between her index and middle finger. She waves it around to get my attention.

But the rumors say only the founder of the gang, the Commander, has a gun with that mark...
A-are you saying... that this is the Commander in front of us? Able to traverse the most dangerous places with just brain and brawn?
The one who disappeared right after becoming a legend? THAT Commander?!
(This wasn't in the script, but I guess that was my backstory.)
Ahem. Hey, are you really the Commander?
Don't bother refusing, because I won't believe it!
That's right! This is definitely the real deal!
You mean it? Okay–wait, I don't even have pen or paper!
We'll have to wait 'til we're back in town...
Hmm... What brings you around to these parts anyway, Commander?
Before I answer that, can you two tell me why you're dueling?
Ah, that was nothing. We just wanted to see who could draw their gun faster.
Not that it matters now. Isn't that right, Hornet?
Heheh, yep! What's more important is... Commander, how's about you join us?
When I started my journey, I vowed never to join another gang. I'm not interested in any more fighting.
Ahaha! Don't worry about that! We're not inviting you to a gang!
Look over there, Commander. There's a small town up ahead.
She points in a direction. The silhouettes of buildings are barely visible through the dust.
Heheh. The stuff going on there is a hundred times more interesting than any gang war.
What would that be?
While we talk, the cloudless sky suddenly darkens.
The wind roars chillingly. Sand whips up in the distance and begins closing in on the town.
Oh, no... Another sandstorm.
They've been so common lately... Forget it. Commander, can that horse still run?
Sure can.
Then get on that horse, ride into town as fast as you can, and take shelter!
We'll catch up with you later, Commander!
The girls wave, jump onto their own horses, and ride bravely into the rising sand.
I shouldn't hesitate, either.
I climb on, stroke my horse's mane, and plant my feet firmly on the stirrups.
Yah!
Then, we rush toward the sand-mired town without a second thought.
We manage to reach town before the sandstorm can consume us.
However, every door is locked, and every window is shuttered. Beneath the dark sky, it's impossible to find a hotel.
I might be better off asking a resident to shelter me for now.
Before I can knock, the door opens a crack.
No matter how much I knock, nobody answers.
But I can just barely hear the sound of a music box inside.
Just then, the door of the house to the left opens a crack.
You, stranger... Come in.
The house is dark, its only source of illumination being the lamp in its owner's hand.
Ahem... Know me as Bristol. Stranger, have you too been drawn by the allure of bounty?
Bounty?
(Is this what Herring meant when she said things here were more interesting than gang wars?)
Your reaction tells me that you know something is happening in this town... but not what. Is that right?
Allow me to tell you – about this town, the bounty, and the curse...
Many decades ago, in the town mine...
Do we really need to blast it? I'm tired.
Sure, the gold mine is blocked by rocks, but just let someone else do it...
All we have to do is fill it with explosives, right? There... Done. I'm going to sleep now.
Part of me feels like the cast is all wrong... Anyway, it's dangerous here. No sleeping!
Wake up! I'm about to detonate the explosives!
Counting down!
Dupleix... W-wait! Impero put too many–
Three, two, one...
*BOOOOOOOOOOOM!*
The overly packaged explosives cause a cave-in, catching the miners in the wreckage.
Aah. I curse you. A curse upon gold mines and hard work.
I'm cursing it, too... Anyone who touches this gold mine will turn into a bunny...
Why a bunny?
...Because they're cute?
Okay, is our scene done now? Yaaay, break time.
That's a pretty... random curse.
Ahem... Well, ever since the cave-in, the town's curse has spread.
Bristol shows me to another part of the building.
Behold, stranger! That bunny right there is proof of the curse!
The feeble light of the lamp barely illuminates the inside of a closet.
I like this role...
Zzzzz....
Um?
This sleeping bunny was once Laffey, niece of Mayor San Diego.
She didn't believe in the curse. So she went to the mine, and this is how she came out...
Ever since, the mayor has promised a bounty to anyone who can put the spirits of that mine to rest.
Hmm... A gold mine cursed by spirits, huh?
I ponder it for a moment. Bristol seems to mistake this for interest in the bounty.
After shooting a quick glance out the window, she pushes me out of her home.
Farewell. Hopefully you can display your value amidst this chaos... Commander.
Wait!
Ignoring my calls, Bristol slams the door shut in my face.
A harsh gust of wind blows, making it hard to keep my eyes open. Afterward, the sandstorm passes.
I look around again and find that the buildings have changed.
Hm? That house just turned into a tavern. It's like I'm in a whole new place...
My horse absentmindedly chews on some hay in the stable behind the tavern.
(When did I stable you? I don't remember doing that.)
The lamp-wielding Bristol and mysterious sleeping rabbit are gone, too.
Was that all just an illusion?
Well... Let's see if the tavern has any clues.
When I go into the bar, I get a warm welcome.
Welcome~ I'm Bell, your server today!
Come in, sit down, order a drink~ Here's your menu! When you're ready, just give me a shout!
After pushing a tattered, handwritten menu into my hands, Bell runs off while balancing a tray.
Hey there! Took you long enough, Commander. We've been waiting for ages.
C'mon, get over here!
When I notice Hornet trying to get my attention, I get up and walk–
Hm? Hornet, did you just call this person... Commander?
Commander? Heheh... It looks like that bounty hooked one hell of a big fish.
Pleasure to meet you. I'm Indiana, a bounty hunter.
I came here to lift the curse on that mine. Commander, how about working with me?
The two of us can split the bounty, 40-60. You get the 60, of course. What do you say?
So eager to win over the Commander... Are you just going to ignore me~?
I thought you weren't interested in the bounty, Pittsburgh.
Weeell, I know I said I wasn't interested in any curses. But the Commander? That's a different story.
She sits on the edge of the table, casually twirling her revolver around.
Hey, read the room!
We already got dibs on the Commander! Isn't that right?!
See? Straight from the horse's mouth! Now give up the ghost~
What?! You already forgot about us?!
Anyway, we got to the Commander first! If you need to recruit, there are plenty of other candidates here.
Yeah. That nun drinking tea over there would be a good fit.
Hornet points at a corner of the tavern.
It's then that I realize that this tavern isn't just packed – it's full of ferocious fighters.
(A nun, a maid, and a witch...?)
(What an odd breadth of occupations.)
Heheh♪ At this point, I'm happy to let the Commander choose... What do you think, Indiana?
Our plan's already failed~
Too bad. If you won't join us, then we'll just have to treat you as a rival!
I'm confident we can win that bounty first. Curse, spirit, whatever it is – I'd like to see it stand up to my gun!
With a hearty laugh, Indiana swaggers over and claps a hand on my shoulder.
We might be rivals now, but I'd love to work with you sometime, Commander.
Heheh~ Now, now. Give these girls back their partner, please.
I'd like our relationship to remain a little amicable, wouldn't you?
Pittsburgh hops off the table, grabs me by the arm, and pushes me over to Hornet.
Whoa... She's even worse than the first one...
Heheh, don't worry. I'm not interested in the curse. All I want is to observe your little trio's work, that's all.
That's cool and all, but we don't even know where to begin.
Can't exactly stray too far from town, either, given how often the sandstorms are these days.
Only the pizza from this tavern can make me feel better... Mm! Yeah, every pizza needs pineapples on top!
When Hornet takes a big, happy bite of her slice of pizza, people in the tavern angrily protest her claim.
You can praise the pizza, but maybe pick better phrasing...
Huh? Why? If you say so, Commander... *munch*... I'll be more careful!
Anyway, I'm running short on cash. Fast.
Same here. If I can't get that bounty, I might have to resort to robbery...
Have you been here for a long time?
Thanks for waiting~ Five cups of Pittsburgh's mixed juice. That'll be one thousand gold coins, please~!
We'll pay at the counter after.
Okaaay!
Bell's conveniently-timed entrance answers my questions.
See? These prices are way too much for any normal person to afford!
Has it always been this expensive?
How should I know? It's been like this since we got here, at least!
Heehee♥ It's okay, Commander. If money is what you need...
Pittsburgh gulps down her drink and sidles over to me, seemingly tipsy.
Ahem. Uh, I appreciate the thought.
Are you shy~? How cute...
Sorry. That's enough teasing. I'll have you know that once upon a time, prices here were normal.
It was only after the mayor issued her bounty and sandstorms ramped up that prices started to rise.
(Hm? Another person saying that the sandstorms suddenly ramped up...)
By the way, is Laffey – the mayor's niece – the only one cursed to be a rabbit?
Or are there others?
Ooh! Now that you mention it, Bristol ended up that way when she investigated the accident decades ago!
The tavern's waitress was apparently next to me for a while now.
Bristol?
(The person who let me in during the sandstorm was named Bristol. Is this a coincidence, or...?)
Yep! She went missing at the mine. When someone finally mustered the courage to go looking for her, they just saw a single bunny nearby.
Ever since then, the townspeople have kept their distance from the mine. The loss of its gold led to a gradual decline...
Laffey wanted to prove that it wasn't cursed, for the sake of the town's future. And... Well, we know how that ended.
But I heard all of this from U-556! I only moved into this town recently, so...
If you're curious... Oh, she should be coming with a delivery soon. Ask her when she comes!
The spirits' curse, Bristol contradiction, high prices, and growing frequency of sandstorms.
Several different key phrases are involved in this mystery. But just when a vague idea comes to mind, something new comes to throw me into disarray again.
While we wait for U-556 to come with her delivery, I tell Bell that I'm going for a walk and exit the tavern.
During said walk, I find a flyer regarding the curse bounty. I take it off the wall and try to glean some valuable information from it.
"We are offering 20% of all gold mine proceeds to whoever can rid us of this curse."
So the bounty isn't even a set sum. It's just the promise of a new revenue stream.
(If they really wanted to get rid of this curse, then they'd offer some advantage to people who came seeking the bounty.)
(Like discounts on facilities... or at least not charging exorbitant prices.)
W-watch out! Get out of the waaay!
A girl's panicked voice interrupts my train of thought.
I realize that I've wandered close to a pasture. The cows around me quietly munch on hay, save for...
Waaaah... P-please help meee...
The girl, riding one cow, desperately tries to keep her balance.
W-wow...! You stopped it with just your eyes!
I whip out my revolver and fire a few shots at the grass in front of it.
Whoa... It stopped because it sensed the danger...
With her crisis resolved, Kersaint alights and thanks me.
It was no big deal. By the way, why were you riding a cow...?
O-oh! When I was changing their hay, this one suddenly got rowdy...
I tried to calm it down, but it threw me onto its back, and... Ooh...
Hay? The same that they normally eat?
I don't know... I was just told to change it. Fargo's the one who knows this stuff...
Hmm. Where is this Fargo, then?
She's right over there.
Kersaint shows me to a nearby cowshed.
Commander approach confirmed. Happiness index increasing by 25.22%.
Changing mode to "super friendly."
Good morning, Commandeeer!
You look like you're wondering how I know who you are! Haha☆ I've got secrets to keep, sowwy!
Okay... I won't ask. Can you tell me if the hay you're using in the pasture is the same as usual?
Sure is. Ever since the sandstorms started, we've had to rely on U-556 for all of our supplies.
She delivered the hay, too.
U-556 again, huh...
Oh, but there wasn't enough hay yesterday, so I went and harvested some myself.
From the mine, that is.
*gasp*
Commander, why are you here?
I hear a familiar voice behind me.
Indiana?
I was wondering why Pittsburgh suddenly asked me to look for you... So Fargo's been keeping you, huh?
I haven't done anything wrong. I'm simply answering the Commander's questions.
Fargo's voice is emotionless again. Apparently, her "super friendly" mode has been disengaged.
Hm?
Don't worry about it. She's harmless for now.
Pittsburgh and the others are waiting. Let's hurry back.
When we return to the tavern, Hornet quickly starts a lively conversation with Indiana and Pittsburgh.
Weren't you rivals before?
We still are, yep!
Yeah. Being rivals doesn't mean we have to hate each other.
That's right~ Things are a lot more relaxed now than when you left.
While everyone chats, I hear the sound of approaching hooves.
Prairie Knight U-556 has arrived with a delivery!
While the townspeople unload the goods, I jump on the opportunity to approach her.
Courier duty, huh? You must be like a hero to the townsfolk.
Heheh~ This is nothing, nothing~ Did you just come into town recently?
You could tell I was an outsider?
Yeah. Almost everyone's left this place, except for the ones moving in recently.
Anyone else is sure to be a bounty hunter.
But that's fine. It helps the economy here, after all.
Excuse you. This economy is beyond helping!
And with all the sandstorms, nobody can ever leave!
Don't act like it's our fault.
These sandstorms weren't a problem before. They only started because you outsiders came and angered the spirits!
Hold on. You're saying there weren't any sandstorms before?
Yeah. They started popping up after the first batch of bounty hunters blew in!
And the more people came in, the more frequent they became! It's definitely because the spirits are mad!
She's just given me an important piece of information without realizing – and it puts an idea in my head.
I think it's time I go see this so-called curse in person...
With a decision made, we decided to go back to the tavern on Indiana's suggestion.
Wait a second. Why are you acting like you're part of the team now?
Following you all seems like fun. Besides, I had a feeling this bounty business was a little fishy, too.
Agreed. Apparently, there were other bounty hunters who came before you all.
Where did they go? And... why have you made no gains whatsoever despite being here for so long?
Huh? You're right... I never even noticed.
I guess because something weird would happen every time we tried to investigate...?
Now that you mention it, it is weird.
Every time we tried to do something, some other idea would come up at a weirdly convenient time and wash that away.
Heehee... Maybe that's why I have so little interest in the bounty.
The way you're talking makes it sound like you know something, Pittsburgh. Mind sharing?
Unfortunately, I don't know any more than you. I've just felt vague suspicion here and there.
Spirits living in the gold mine, people turning into rabbits, being distracted from our plans, sandstorms whipping up whenever we try to leave...
What do YOU think the curse is, honey?
Or... do you think all of those coincidences are real?
She lowers her voice. There's a strange, seductive glint in her ruby eyes.
It's a mystery how you're unaffected, though...
Would you mind telling us your little plan? Com-man-der?♪
Got it. Pittsburgh and I will stand by here.
Geez. Here I thought I'd get to come along... Leaving me to bring up the rear is just rude.
But it's fine. I'll just pray that all goes well tonight.
Night falls, and Herring, Hornet, and I spring into action.
Weird. It's not like it's hard to find the mine, so why haven't we bothered trying yet?
I just realized something... We haven't met Mayor San Diego since we came to this town, have we?
Yeah! How'd I forget something so important?
Hush. We're almost there.
While they talk, we approach the mine.
There's an overgrowth of wild grass, but there are definite traces of it being culled by a sickle.
(So Fargo wasn't lying. The problem is the grass here... What makes it different?)
Upon careful investigation, I find blackish marks on the grass near the entrance to the mine.
(Are these black marks related to the curse?)
(Well, nothing to do but go in.)
Ahem! Commander... Uh, a-are you really planning to go in there?
If the curse is real, and we're turned into rabbits...
Calm down, Herring! The Commander knows there's no curse. That's how we got this far, right?

options.content: Let's become bunnies and live a lazy life!

scripts.say: Yeah! The Commander's words fill me with determination!
Huh? You're getting cold feet NOW?
Commander? Are you serious right now?!
Leaving the veracity of the curse aside, there must be other secrets hiding in here.
You don't want to be stuck in this town forever, do you?
No, but...
Then let's go.
The dark, cramped, and damp cavern winds on for seemingly forever.
Hornet leads the way with a small kerosene lamp in hand.
Well... We've been walking for a long time now, and nothing has happened. It's almost as if there's nothing going on in here.
Herring grumbles. Just then, we hear conversation in the distance ahead.
Hornet quickly turns the lamp off, and we all slowly approach.
Uh... Are you sure this is fine?
Of course, nya. You don't have to worry about a thing, Mayor, nya!
But Laffey... Akashi, are you REALLY sure this is fine? Really, really sure?
Trust me, nya~ Laffey became a bunny because she wanted to, and business is better than ever, nya!
That's true! It's growing like never before! Someday, it'll be as brilliant as the good old days!
Nyahahaha... There you have it, nya! And I'm gonna make bank, nya!
Let's ramp up the output, nya~ Increase the fake sandstorm frequency, and make it so nobody can ever leave again, nya~
By the way, Akashi... Sandstorms are one thing, but that stuff you're putting into the food and water doesn't have any weird side effects, does it?
Of course it's fine, nya~ The Akashi brand has a reliable track record~
It's harmless – it just makes people dream based on simple suggestions, nya~ That's why the curse rumor spread so easily, nya!
Rest assured that you're in good hands, nya. Stay here, and I'll use your title to make this town flourish like never before, nya!
Thanks, Akashi! I'm such a genius for letting you do business here!♪
Nyahahaha... I didn't think it'd be this easy to fool... I mean, I didn't think you'd be so trusting, nya!
The tunnel up ahead has been rearranged like a workshop.
One green cat skillfully operates the many mysterious machines within.
There's also a single cage mixed in with the machines.
The red-haired girl in the cage, Mayor San Diego herself, happily hums a tune.
(That's the mayor! Why is she in here?)
(And Akashi, too... Are those machines and whatever she's putting in the food the real "curse"?)
Hmm? I feel like I'm being watched... Staaare!
San Diego suddenly stands up inside the cage and turns toward us. We make eye contact.
Akashi! We've got visitors!
Nya?!
(Oh, no!)
We run through the damp, narrow tunnel as fast as we can, but we can't shake off Akashi's pursuers.
*pant*... *pant*... So does that mean...
The sandstorms, the curse, and our memory loss... Akashi was behind it all?!
Yeah! The gold mine was just a trap to lure us here and squeeze us for all we have!
If we ran out of money, we'd have no choice but to stay here and live in this town!
What a scheme...
But if those sandstorms are an illusion made by Akashi's machines... that means we don't have to worry about them at all, right?
As the light of the exit comes into view, we finally manage to escape the pursuit.
Let's just get out of here for now! We need to go tell everyone the truth!
Right!
We make it back to the bar safely and tell our rivals what we learned about the mine.
Now that the secret of this town's been exposed, there's no reason for us to stay any longer.
Damn right, nya! 'Cause I'm gonna get rid of all of ya, nya!
The green cat appears out of nowhere – with her lackeys from the mine in tow.
Akashi's always got a backup plan, nya!
I built a tunnel under this town just to keep people like YOU from getting away with my secrets, nya!
Heh. So you wanna fight? Right here, right now?
Sure do, nya!
Music to my ears. Bring it on!
On Indiana's words, the sound of gunfire rattles the tavern.
Pittsburgh and Indiana whip out their guns at lightning speed.
You ready, Commander?
Any time!
*BANG!* *BANG!*
After two gunshots, two of Akashi's pursuers fall to the floor.
The tavern descends into chaos almost instantly. Tables and chairs go flying.
Ooh, I hope the tavern can handle replacing all this stuff...
I recommend invoicing Pittsburgh for recompense.
Tch, Indiana's stealing my spotlight... Don't underestimate me, dammit!
Time to prove which one of us is faster!
Hell yeah!
I've had ENOUGH of pineapple on pizza!
Yeah! I'm fighting for real, authentic pizza!
Seemingly ignited by the gunfire, the other people in the tavern gradually join in the mad melee.
Bullets fly in all directions. The sounds of chairs and tables flying, and the tavern being destroyed, are ceaseless.
At the end of it all, when dawn finally came, the tavern had finally calmed down. After that last gunshot, silence had returned.
Uugh... I lost, nya...
Town rules dictate that we'd hand you over to the mayor, but...
The mayor's in cahoots with her, anyway. Though I guess it did look more like she was getting tricked than anything...
Not sure what to do here...
This is a big scandal. I think we need to elect a new mayor~
What if we just lock her up until a new mayor takes office and then hand her over then?
I can fix all this! Just don't lock me up, nyaaa!
So many business opportunities still await, nya!
Save it for the new mayor, please~
Pittsburgh tightens the rope around Akashi's wrist.
What will you do now, Commander?
Why even ask? Our only option is to make the Commander our new mayor~
You as the mayor, huh... Now that would make this town legendary!
That's exactly why I need to leave.
Commander?
You'll understand someday, Hornet.
I gaze into the distance. The dilapidated town has taken on a more lively air under the dawn sun.
Are you really going to leave us?
Yeah. New journeys await me.
Heehee. Of course... Then I'll pray for your good fortune.
Goodbye, Commander.
I take the reins from Indiana and climb onto my horse.
After a gentle kick, it begins to walk.
As the town gradually fades in the distance behind me, I realize the adventure ahead of me is long and perilous.
(But that's just fine by me.)

sequence: END

scripts.say: Aboard the express...
Readings indicate that everyone's collective happiness index is 67.11% higher than usual.
I suppose the act of going on vacation has that effect on you.
If I want to blend in, I should raise my own happiness index accordingly.
At the same time, I'll also increase my pleasure index by an appropriate 23.64%.
No, no, Fargo, you're doing it all wrong!
This one has ample vacation experience. You can use that for reference instead!
Adjusting values does not equate with true understanding of emotions.
Analysis: You must study emotions just as I did.
If you want to go about it more efficiently, I think I can help you with that.
By overwriting her emotional understanding with a program? Hardly an ideal solution.
No, Fargo, what you should do is study this one's emotion module. It is handy... even if it overheats easily.
I gaze out the window at the Wild West scenery passing by while overhearing the girls chattering merrily amongst themselves.
Some others, though, aren't in such a merry mood.
Uggghhh... It makes me SO anxious when I remember that my workload is gonna INCREASE during this vacation...
But at the same time, if I don't take my work with me, I'll never get to enjoy some time with the Commander...
I can empathize to a painful degree. Still, you should just focus on enjoying the present.
Trust me – the last thing you should do is let work spoil your vacation!
Yeah... You're right.
I can do overtime or all-nighters for weeks once I'm back at the port! Vacations are for relaxing!
Attagirl!
Hey, folks, we're almost there now.
Pittsburgh strolls down the train corridor and announces that we'll be arriving shortly.
Already? It feels like we only boarded a minute ago.
This is a short-distance express train, so yeah.
The reason why we boarded a train to begin with was so you could soak in the western mood for a while first.
Ah. It's no wonder the train was dressed in period-appropriate furnishings inside and out.
It even has that classic steam whistle...
Exactly. If you're gonna call something a Wild West vacation, you've got to go all out to make everything match the theme.
Hey, is that why you've been sitting here all by yourself? Because you were taking in all the details?
If so, I've got something way more interesting for you to look at.
With a cheeky smile, Pittsburgh takes the empty seat next to me. I immediately pick up a sweet, fruity smell coming from her.
Is that juice I smell?
Oopsies, I gave it away! Don't tell Indiana and Enterprise or they'll fry my bacon, okay?
FWEEE! FWEEE!
Before I can say anything else, the train's steam whistle cuts me off.
I look out the window again. At the end of the black train tracks bisecting the wilderness, I see the outline of a small town sticking out in the night.
Looks like we'll be there any minute now.
Yeah, but–
BANG!
BANG! BANG! POW!
(Was that... gunshots?)
We're settling this right here, right now! Only one gang gets to rule this town, buddy!
Who went and made them the rules? Screw that, let's team up and squeeze the townsfolk dry instead!
Two riders on horseback gallop by outside the window.
Hey, that's not a bad idea...
You, the Commander! Fork over your valuables now! Or else...
(This has got to be some kind of farce. No matter – I'll play along for now.)
Or else... what?
Or else you're getting a li'l present from me! Mwah!
The moment she blows me a kiss, the train starts to shake violently.
What was that? Did you plant bombs on the train?
Hahaha! Who doesn't love a good explosion, right?
Hurry up! Leave your valuables behind then get off the train!
Doing as told, I leave my baggage on the train, after which Herring escorts us to the town... for some reason.
We pass through the smoke and dust raised by the explosions and the gunfight, and the town finally reveals itself in full.
To little surprise, we find Indiana and friends waiting for us at the town's entrance, all with warm smiles on their faces.
Alright, that's the end of our bit. Welcome, folks, to the frontier resort town of Parisek!
Hahaha! Good that you finally made it.
So, how'd you like the act? It's as Wild West as it gets, right?
While it's not as wild as I imagined the Wild West would be, it was still a decent opener.
I've not had such a unique welcome in a while. My hat's off to whoever came up with that.
Hear that, Enterprise? I told you the Commander would be okay with it!
Hm? Was this your idea, Essex?
It was! Heeheee. I thought we should treat you to something special after flying all the way over here.
Took a lot of rehearsals and a lot of fine-tuning the direction.
In the end, we settled on this comparatively gentle one.
It's just a shame that we all had our hands full when we decided to do this.
We were gonna have a bigger shootout, with more people robbing the train. As it is now, it didn't hit nearly as hard as it could have.
It really is a shame. It would've been so cool if we could've had dozens of masked bandits riding along both sides of the train, shooting at each other.
That's a good idea!
What is?
What you just said! Dozens of bandits riding side-by-side, having a huge shootout!
That'd be like, THE clippable scene if it were in a movie! Right, Commander?
Let me guess – inspiration has struck you.
Exactamundo! Let me paint you a picture...
Wildnerness as far as the eye can see. The main character wanders through the lonesome lands, thirsty and hungry, and that's when they set foot in a remote frontier town...
Then they get caught up in the town's trouble! Exciting hijinx ensues! Something like that!
Okay... Even assuming everyone's fine with using the town as an open set, you don't have the equipment to film a movie. Also, who's going to write the script?
I mean, we kinda DO have the equipment. Any presenter worth their salt always brings their gear with them!
So you brought filming equipment with you on a vacation...
What about it? Everyone films their vacations! I want to capture those beautiful moments in time!
Anyway, as I was gonna say – Hai Tien can be the scriptwriter.
M-me? Um, I'm not particularly well-versed in this genre...
I COULD write it, but I'd need some of you to review it for changes and suggestions.
No problemo! That's easy to arrange.
So, we've got film equipment and a writer, and that's all we need. Let's make a film!
Not so fast. I want to see the schedule for the next few days first.
I don't want the film-making to collide with events that the others planned.
Don't worry about that. We only have two special events planned for you.
You'll have tons of free time to explore the town at your leisure, so the filming shouldn't collide with anything.
As for the events themselves, well... You'll find out more tomorrow!
If anyone's worried about their luggage, don't be. U-556 already brought it all to the town inn.
You're now free to explore the town at your whim. Go and enjoy yourselves!
Early in the morning, I receive a message from Yorktown to come meet her outside the town.
The event we have planned for you today is – the full settler experience.
Ugh. I'm getting tired just from hearing those words...
Don't even think about sneaking away. A Chevalier does not shy away from hard work.
I can broadly guess what it's about from the name alone, but what, specifically, are we going to do?
We're going to settle the wilds. Or, to put it another way, make this place feel more inhabitable.
Yup! It's about growing the settlement into a village, then from a village into a town.
That should give you an idea of what to expect.
Yes. That means finding food and water and creating a place to live for yourselves.
It takes luck, manpower, and a sense for community development! All of them are important!
In essence, you want us to build a new town from scratch, yes?
Magnificent!
I like the sound of that! I will make a town that serves as a beacon for Sardegna's glory!
Uhh... Sure? This is just to give you a taste of what it was like, though, so a small wooden hut will do just fine.
While there are plenty of materials to build with, you will need some carpentry skills.
Don't worry – we have prepared tools for you to work with.
Isn't there more to it than this? This feels a little easy for a first-settler experience.
Because there's more! You'll need to design and build your shelter as well as find food and water, and there's a time limit on all of them.
You need to secure all the essentials you need to survive, and you only have so much time to do so.
Only those who've obtained it all by the end can call themselves true pioneers!
Whoa, whoa, this is getting really hard really fast.
If it gets too hard, ya can always skip looking for food.
I've got plenty of canned stuff to go around!
It's the dreaded canned herring, isn't it?
Dred-dead... I don't know that word, but I wanna try it!
I'm just saying – if ya wanna lower the difficulty, come to me to get your can of food.
Being a settler wasn't easy, and your options are limited!
Fair enough... I'll keep it in mind as a last resort.
One thing is clear to me now. Failing to finish your hut within the time limit will also leave you with less time to find water and food.
Thus, your only option if you don't want to starve is to eat canned herring.
Sounds a lot like a punishment to me.
I'm only trying to motivate the rest of you. You should do like THEM and start designing your huts.
Clemenceau points toward two shipgirls, pen and paper in hand.
It's Dupleix and Strasbourg, frantically sketching up blueprints.
No way in hell! I'd sooner die than eat canned herring!
Well said! I fear no overtime – but that stuff? It scares me!
Seeing them work springs the rest of the girls into designing their own huts.
Heehee. THIS is how an event should be.
Good luck to you, Commander.
Well, personally, I would love to feed you some canned herring, but still.
Clemenceau smiles at me, then takes a sheet of paper and starts drawing.
(I'd better get to it...)
Sometime later...
Uh, Laffey, why have you only drawn a single triangle?
Because some planks glued together are good enough for me.
As long as I can get inside and sleep, that's all I need... Zzz...
Hmm... Perhaps I should convert the confessional into a prayer room.
Then again, a confessional leads to much more fun scenarios. Heehee.
This narrow plot of land isn't nearly big enough to demonstrate my creativity!
It really isn't! How do they expect me to be content with some shabby shack?
Sounds like you're all having fun, and we're still only in the design stage!
New Jersey looks around at the girls, then walks up to me.
What've you sketched up, honey? Can I see?
I give her my blueprint.
Hang on... Isn't this layout just like your office?
Don't tell me you're STILL in work mode. Are you not enjoying the vacay?
She shoots me a concerned look.
No, it's just that that's the only idea that came to mind as far as designs go.
Look at it this way – you all come through my office at some point, right? That makes it a starting point, in a sense.
So, without thinking about it, I just copied my office layout.
Heehee. That sounds almost like cheating.
Now that you mention it... Royal Maids, help my servant build that Wild West office!
As you wish, Your Majesty.
With a lot of extra help, my wooden frontier office is now complete.
Not bad. Not bad at all. However, we spent so long building it that we couldn't find any food or water...
You know what that means! Caaanned herring!
Wait! Let me try one last thing first!
Fu Shun picks up bits of wood scattered on the ground and makes a stack of them.
She constructs a very modest throne, then takes a seat on it.
Upon the altar of the justiciar shall I sit; toward the heavens and the seven stars shall I raise my sword!
Well, I don't have a sword, but still.
What are you doing?
What does it look like? I'm trying to borrow divine powers! Have you heard of the Empery expression, "borrow the east wind"? You can borrow food in the same way!
Let there be wind! Let there be rain! Let there be food!
...Hello?
Crickets. No wind blew, no rain fell, and no food appeared from thin air.
The tumbleweeds, however, heard her call and hit her directly.
C'mon, just accept the fact you'll be eating herring.
Herring goes around and gives everyone a can of herring.
We all gather on the floor of my frontier office and dig into our very modest meals.
With my breath held, I open the can and find not herring inside, but rather ordinary combat rations.
Huh? Did you replace the contents of these cans with regular rations?
Heh, I sure did, since nobody else appreciates the greatness of canned herring.
It was worth it to see the looks on your faces.
Hey! How come MINE has actual herring in it?
Oops, I forgot to mention some of them really are the real deal.
Ahahaha... Well, this isn't exactly what I expected...
But it did leave us with an unforgettable memory, wouldn't you say, Commander?
I give Yorktown a small nod, then turn my eyes on Herring, chasing Fu Shun around the office.
Unforgettable being the keyword.
And so, our trial of the settler experience concludes while the scent of canned herring hangs in the air.
It's the next morning. I received a message from Hornet to come meet her at the plaza.
Hah! You're actually just in time, Commander! I thought you had a rep for arriving early.
I'm guessing you must've overslept because your bed was too comfy.
Equating being on time with oversleeping... What a terrible thing to say to someone.
Anyway, let's move on!
The event we have planned for you today iiis... gold scrounging! I've prepared some equipment to get you all started.
"Equipment"... You mean pans and shovels? I asked Essex about this just yesterday.
Those are the go-to, but that's not all we have. Indiana wanted to make it a little more fun.
See, if you want to look for valuables in the river, we've also got powerful magnets for you to use!
Magnets?!
Yeah, it's called magnet fishing. Instead of a hook and fishing line, you use a nylon rope and a powerful magnet to pull up metallic stuff from the riverbed.
Those who want to try magnet fishing, come to me to get your ropes and magnets.
And those who wanna do it the old-fashioned way, come get your shovels and pans here!
Ooh! Magnet fishing sounds more fun than panning!
So... The magnet hooks onto anything even remotely magnetic, right?
Yeah. You're bound to catch SOMETHING. I think it's perfect for you.
It is. At least I won't be going home empty-handed this way.
Pick whichever you feel suits you best!
Once everyone's geared up, Bell and I will take you to the river.
(Hmm... Which one...)
If you want to experience the authentic Wild West, you've gotta stick with tradition!
The temptation of a guaranteed catch is hard to resist. Let's do it the new way!
I take the equipment and follow the guides to a river not far from the resort town.
Y'know, it kind of dawned on me that scrounging for crumbs of metal isn't the most exciting thing...
It's just menial work repeated over and over. Should we spice it up by creating two teams and see who gets the best haul?
Competing over who gets the most doesn't make the work itself any more interesting.
In that case, why don't we make the act of looking for gold more interesting?
For instance, by letting everyone use whatever they have at hand to modify their tools. Within the spirit of gold-hunting, of course.
Ah. You mean allowing them to use their creativity to improve efficiency.
Exactly. That will make the work less repetitive, I believe.
It's a good idea. Hornet, tell the others about it.
On it!
Testing, testing... Alright, our first-ever Wild West Gold-Hunting Competition is well underway!
I'm Aoba, your on-the-scene commentator for this event!
Looks like the contestants are making some solid progress out there... Oh? What have we here?
It's da Vinci! She used her ingenuity and whatever was at hand to create a Fifty-Fifty Goldy Sifty Machine!
Weird... How come there's nothing but pebbles left?
Something must've gone wrong... Oh! That gives me another idea!
