(The fact that Terminal received a signal there would've happened irrespective of anything Sawai did.)
(Our reason for going there to begin with was to find a lead on the skelebeasts and the ghost fleet.)
(Of course, there was nothing linking them to the Fountain. It was just a Siren machine, now completely looted.)
(But, the monster and the fleet have appeared everywhere we go, from Whydah's hideout to this holy site...)
(The undead creatures and the concept of "immortality"... Perhaps there's more than meets the eye here.)
(What even is the Goddess? The deity of storms and the sea? Or is there more to her?)
(And why does the Church consider this place of all to be a holy site?)
(What if, like the Fountain of Youth, the Goddess is a machine of some kind?)
Sawai, what is the link between this site and the Goddess?
Sorry, who are you?
A-ha! Let me do the introductions!
This is none other than the founder and vice-leader of Tempesta! {playername}, the Commander!
Ahh, it's no wonder why you're asking insightful questions.
Normally, I wouldn't tell you a thing, much less allow you to come near a holy site.
However, you found and came to this place by yourselves, and you did rescue me as well.
Those things considered, I'm willing to tell you...
Assuming, of course, that you'll keep it a secret.
Simply put... this is where the Goddess lives.
Where she... lives?
Oh, perchance it's more apt to call it her "body." You see, the name of this place, the Sleeping Sea, refers to "the place in which Goddess sleeps".
I'll explain the rest at the temple that's here. Come with me!
If my theory is correct, the temple is where we'll find the answer to all these strange occurrences.
After linking up with our fleet, Ganj-i-Sawai leads the way towards the temple in the Sleeping Sea.
Though enemies continue to appear along the way, they are no match before our combined firepower.
There! The temple is on that island!
In the distance, the temple sits on a frozen-over beach, radiating a cold glow.
Hundreds of ghost ships have already started gathering in the waters around the island.
Talk about a chilling congregation... There's so many.
How're we supposed to break through that? Reckon we should just give up.
That relic won't be any use to us if we die nabbin' it!
We know where it is, we've seen it, and even just the tales of this journey will earn us a nice guinea.
What if we split in two? One group lures them away while the other makes landfall.
It's a nice plan, buuut... isn't it really, really dangerous?
We broke through their lines getting here, and there are still pursuers on our trail.
Whoever has to do the distracting will get surrounded in the bat of an eye.
True... Apologies, I didn't consider that.
I know, I know! How about we swim and go UNDER the water?
That's even more dangerous than going through the surface. The waters are brimming with skelebeasts.
I could swim there easy-peasy!
Okay... And what will you do then?
I'm gonna steal the relic.
...That sounds like it could actually work.
It won't. You need a high-ranking Church member to be present to get inside the temple.
Hmm... There has to be another way inside if this place demands such tight security. Is there, Sawai?
There is... but you can only access it from the inside.
So we're completely locked out is what you're saying...
Commander, think of something!
Right, first of all, forcing our way through is our last resort.
Secondly, Portsmouth made a good point. All of you here came only to investigate matters, remember?
Sure, getting the relic and solving all problems in one go would be ideal, but nobody's saying you have to do the impossible.
Hey, hang on a second...
Yeah... My commission is simply to investigate the strange stuff and kill skelebeasts, not to resolve the situation.
So since I know what the root cause is, that's mission complete. I can just go home with all the bounties and spoils!
Exactly. We can always come back later to deal with the ghost fleet.
Also, considering how big this whole incident is, I'm sure the Church and the cities will take it seriously.
Once we're out, we can contact all the parties and organize a joint fleet, then lead them back here and finish things for good.
Yes, true...
Ganj-i-Sawai gazes at the temple and lets out a sigh.
It's the only way. Um, please don't tell the others about the Goddess' body in your commission report.
The Church will muster some ships to deal with the ghost fleet. Don't worry about that.
Suddenly, the sound of the sea breeze tickles my ear.
The wind's blowing?
No, wait... That's the sound of a storm!
Dark clouds begin to swirl overhead. Gales rage and rain pours down.
(This storm formed WAY too quickly!)
(It has to be because the Goddess' power has weakened... Storms can manifest in the blink of an eye!)
(I shouldn't have let my guard down just because there was no wind!)
Quick! Hoist sails and get us out of there!
Commander! Get inside the hold!
Dammit, we won't make it! Just grab my hand!
A massive wave slams into the ship, knocking me off my feet.
The feel of Royal Fortune's hand is gone in an instant as I plunge into the salty sea, the cold raindrops whipping my body.
COMMANDEEEEER!

sequence: Order is... collapsing...
...lapsing... Order is... collaps...
Rebooting... Failed...
Scan... Failed...
Connecting to server... Failed...
Failed failed failed failed failed...

scripts.say: Drip, drop. I hear droplets hitting the ground.
Something cold yet soft and smooth strokes my cheek... or so I think.
Nnh... Ugh...
Nnh... Ugh...
Hello, human.
A thing in the shape of a human looks at me with a forced smile.
I am Fancy. A being of the abyss, born from the imaginary.
(A being of the abyss? What?)
(She does have a very... "unique" look about her, compared to the Tempesta girls I've seen.)
(And yet, I just get this feeling...)
(Yeah. She's still a shipgirl.)
Thanks for saving me, Fancy.
You're "welcome."
Let's get moving.
Without any warning, one of Fancy's tentacles perks up and coils around my body.
This is faster.
Okay, uh... Where are we going?
To fulfill your mission, human.
What mission?
The Goddess guided you here, just as she guided me.
Therefore, the Goddess has a mission for you, just like me.
("Guided me"? Is she talking about what Grimoire Terminal said?)
(Didn't it say something about "connecting to a server"? What was that about?)
(Maybe there really is a link between the Goddess and the Sirens.)
Hang on. I want to check something.
Hoping for a miracle, I take Terminal out of my backpack. It's still the same as before.
I should've figured it wasn't working again.
Just as I stow the tablet back into my backpack, Fancy takes a few soft steps toward me.
Oh, this? It's a multipurpose tablet called "Grimoire Terminal". It's sort of broken.
Terminal? As in a computer terminal?
You're familiar with computers? How do you know about those?
The Goddess granted me this knowledge. She granted me this mission.
Computers, grimoires, terminals – these are extensions of the will of the Goddess' central unit.
I, too, carry her will. Perhaps you could say I'm a grimoire and a terminal, too?
She tilts her head to the side and thinks about it.
Don't worry. You obviously aren't.
Very well. Then let us move.
Her tentacles start to slither all around.
Wait up, there's one more thing I want to know! What even is this place?
The Kingdom of the Goddess. Her domain.
You are in the Goddess' central unit. You are inside of her.
(Central unit... The pieces are falling into place!)
(The Goddess is no imaginary being, nor is she a transcendent god. She is simply a Siren machine.)
(Then that means... all this time, the people of this world have worshipped a thing the Sirens left behind?)
(More importantly, how does Fancy know about it?)
(She could have ties to the Sirens... in which case, she must have all kinds of info.)
Is the Goddess' central unit... self-aware?
Huh?
She cocks her head, puzzled. It doesn't seem like she understands my question.
Different question, then. What does her central unit typically do?
Control the sea's climate and suppress the curse of the deep.
(I've never heard "climate" and "curse" used in the same sentence before...)
Many system errors accumulated within the central unit over its endless purges, and one day, the curse infected her with a virus.
This virus has seized control of the unit, allowing the dead to appear all across the sea.
(Although her explanation sounds bizarre, I now fully understand the situation.)
In other words, you and I need to remove the virus to restore the seas to normal – did I get that right?
Not me. You.
I know of no way to remove the virus. My mission is only to take you to the central unit.
Oh... Then I'll just have to figure something out.
Alright, let's walk over.
Once more, the tentacles slither around me.
Umm, I said "let's walk over," not "please carry me." You know what "walk" means, right?
You would prefer to use your lower limbs?
Fine. I understand.
Come along.
Fancy and I walk through a massive mechanical structure.
Our journey is smooth and unimpeded as the double doors slide open one after the next.
After passing through a corridor, we arrive at a vast, open place, as blue as the ocean.
A thin mist extends everywhere, and across it, I can see purple lights twinkling like little stars.
This is the Misty Pond.
I'm surprised... Even they have come back.
Come back? Who?
The lights. The silent souls.
They know we're here.
Then, great beasts appear among the mist, swimming across the surface.
Those silent souls... don't they look a lot like skelebeasts?
They are the essence of the skelebeasts as well as their source of power. It's how they move.
In fact, they are linked.
They must be running rampant on the outside for there to be this many of them.
So if they're linked, what will happen to the skelebeasts if we destroy them all?
They will lose their power and minds, becoming but empty husks. What they ought to be.
However, consuming all of them will take considerable time.
Do they taste like anything?
No. They taste neither good nor bad.
Want to try one?
Her tentacles start to squirm.
Thanks, but I'll pass.
At the same time, I don't think you can do this alone.
Hang on – if you took out all the skelebeasts on the outside, what would happen?
Without bodies to control, the souls fall silent.
Why? Will you tell your allies on the outside to deal with them?
That's the plan. The question is how to get in touch with...
Wait, how do you know about my allies?
I saw them with my own eyes.
You saw them?
Take my hand. I will show you.
She sits down by the side of the pond and dips her feet in the water, then extends a tentacle to me.
Dodging the tentacle, I grab her hand and suddenly find myself in a new place.
Skelebeasts swim past one after another in the ocean's deep, dark recesses.
All I can do is watch, like an observer without a physical body.
After a while, I'm brought to a different location.
Then yet another.
(Is this some kind of equipment the Sirens used to monitor the sea?)
(Did she hook up her own sight to it?)
One scene transitions into the next, flickering by in just the blink of an eye.
Then I see a fleet of sailing ships at sea – and a girl in red wearing a pirate hat.
The Commander's underneath the island? Seriously?
I can hear her voice clearly.
(If this can connect directly to the monitoring equipment, maybe it can send audio, too.)
(Won't hurt to try!)
The Commander's underneath the island? Seriously?
Standing on the deck of the Great Royal Fortune, the pirate girl asks a question.
Yeah! I'd recognize that voice anywhere! It's below the island.
Then we must make landfall.
Luckily, the ghost fleet is in disarray thanks to the storm. We have an in.
Tempesta, can you hear me?
I have seen your sins and I shall judge you!
Ahem. Tempesta, can you hear me?
What is that? I hear a whisper. Does anyone else?
It's not just me! I thought the bottle was speakin' to me!
So it wasn't just my imagination?
Hang on, wasn't that the Commander's voice?
Commander! Where are you? I can't see you!
Long story short, I told them I was fine and relayed my plan to them.
See? I said the Commander was under there! Heehee.
So if I got that right, we just gotta take out as many foes as we can, yeah?
Easy-breezy! I've been rarin' for a fight!
Allow me to lead the charge, then.
Just so you know, there are loads of traps down in the temple. Be careful!
Come on, Tempesta! It's time to save the Commander!
Tempesta gets to work, dispatching the monsters. The lights in the mist begin to disappear at a perceivable pace.
Those are powerful allies you have.
It's about time that I did something, too.
Yes. To flex my muscles a bit.
Yes. Just a little bite to appease my cravings.
The air around Fancy bursts into purple flames that spread out like waves.
Her blindfold turns to ash, revealing the inhuman eyes below.
Lips parted, she thrusts her blazing tentacles into the sea of mist.
HISSSSS!
The deathly shrieks of the so-called silent souls echo.
This is my true form. My true form as an abyssal being.
It's a pleasure to see you, Commander.
Water sloshes, explosions boom, and mandibles rip and chew. The lost souls are devoured with nothing left behind.
Temple Underground - At the Central Unit of the Goddess
At the center of this vast room stands a colossal machine, towering toward the heavens.
An irregular, metallic shell encases it, covered in patterns and designs carved with gold.
(What are these gold patterns? That's very unusual for the typically-utilitarian Sirens.)
(At any rate, I'm glad this machine isn't THAT big.)
(Here I thought we'd have to deal with a city-sized structure, like the elite Sirens have.)
There is the central unit, human. Fulfill your mission.
Fancy stands in a corner of the massive room and gestures to the machine with a tentacle.
Everything appears to be safe.
(I've never directly operated Siren machinery before... but it shouldn't be too hard to at least extract some info from it.)
(Besides, what else should I do? Nothing?)
BEEP BEEP! BEEP BEEP!
As soon as I approach the machine, the tablet in my backpack starts to beep. Terminal comes back to life and lights up all of a sudden.
Terminal? Are you back?
Terminal on standby.
(It just... started working again? Or did it activate by being in close proximity to the machine?)
Run a self-diagnostic.
Charging field detected. Engaging charging mode.
(It was just out of batteries this whole time.)
(Whydah didn't say anything about charging it, so it should work fine after this.)
(Siren tech is mighty convenient.)
Examining it, I quickly locate the visual interface you often see on Siren machinery.
I need access privileges. Terminal, can you hook me up?
Orders received. Processing... Processing complete.
Verification complete. I'm Central Unit - Compiler's Wings, at your service.
(It worked!)
(Interesting. "Con Pyler Swings." Is that the Goddess' name?)
(I don't remember any of the books in this world alluding to her name before, but maybe...)
(Wait... Con Pyler Swings...)
(Is it... "Compiler's Wings"?)
(Last time, it was Tester who'd gone nuts. It must be Compiler this time.)
(I'd bet every Siren in this place has a few screws loose.)
I want to ensure the virus won't interfere, so I start by running a security check.
(The status bar says the last self-diagnostic was performed two hours ago.)
(Weird... It says it's "working as normal"?)
(There should be a virus infecting the central unit which gave rise to the skelebeasts, if Fancy is to be believed.)
(That can't possibly be how the system is meant to operate.)
(I'll run another self-diagnostic, just to be sure.)
Once the task is complete, I pull up the logs and examine them for any useful information.
Look at these files... The Atmospheric Circulation Adjustment Project... The Deep Sea Life Enhancement Project...
The Tropical and Subtropical Marine Climate Adaptation Experiment... Silent Souls – Research on the Development of Wisdom Cube Applications...
(It sounds like Compiler's machine has been running experiments by itself.)
(Safe to say, everything that's gone wrong with the "Goddess" links back to these projects.)
(Although, there are a few things this doesn't explain.)
("Adjusting the climate" doesn't whip up storms in an instant, and this research into the silent souls makes no mention of ship parts or skeletons.)
(That makes me think what's actually happening in the world is misaligned with what the Sirens had in mind.)
The self-diagnostic concludes, and the screen only shows the words, "Nothing unusual."
(Maybe it's not a virus... Maybe someone has tampered with the system?)
(But then, who?)
Remembering the computer knowledge Ingraham and Helena taught me, I scour the system for any clues that might've been left behind.
Despite my best efforts, I realize after a while that it's beyond my abilities.
(No dice...)
(The only people who can do anything are me and Fancy... Actually, is it possible that she did the tampering?)
(No, that makes no sense. She wouldn't have led me here if she did.)
I turn around and look at her. She seems to shrug with her tentacles.
(This is a temple. A holy site dedicated to the Goddess. It's not out of the question that some internal sabotage took place within the Church.)
(Or maybe someone just touched it without knowing the consequences and broke something.)
(If it was someone from the Church, does Sawai know about it?)
(I suppose she could know as little as I do...)
(Oh yeah, didn't she say there was a secret path that connects to the outside?)
(I just need to find that, then lead all the others in here.)
With Terminal's help, I unlock the secret passageway leading to the outside.
(They say the Goddess has been a part of this world longer than anyone remembers.)
(If these experiment logs are to be believed, the Sirens have actually helped keep the world in balance.)
(The influence of the "Goddess" only weakened very recently, so with that in mind...)
Terminal, is it possible to revert the experiment plans and restore the system to an earlier version?
Yes. Would you like to do that now?
Not yet. Later.
This is Tempesta's world, and it's up to them to decide what to do with the Goddess machine.
Commandeeer!
I greet the girls as they rush inside the room hosting the central unit.
Oi! I'm the leader, that means I get first dibs on hugging the Commander!
My darling! I'm so glad you're safe.
Looks like the plan worked in the end.
Even if it was a real pain...
Commander, you gotta hear what Portsmouth did!
She took her ship, right, and then she just... Ahahahaha!
Said we could take care of 'em any way we wanted, didn'tcha? So I took my ship 'n' rammed the buggers!
You're such a kid. Why do I work with you again?
It's good to see you again, Whydah the Magnificent.
No way! Terminal!
You fixed it, Commander?
Whydah runs up and pulls the tablet into her embrace.
Terminal, my beloved!
Who is that, Commander?
Martinho's words get everyone else's attention. The girls all look at Fancy, who's next to me.
Well, she's the one who saved me from the storm, put me in touch with you, and showed me to this place.
Her name is Fancy. She's a shipgirl and an abyssal being.
Fancy raises her chin, satisfied with that introduction.
She might even have ties to Ganj-i-Sawai and the Church.
Pardon?
I don't know what you mean. I've never seen her before.
That aside, Grimoire Terminal allowed me to have a look at the Goddess' central unit.
Let me run you through what happened and what the deal is with this huge machine.

sequence: I explained the gist of everything I had learned.
The silent souls, the cause behind the monsters, the reason why Fancy is here.
Although, I withheld some details about the central unit and its status.
All I told them was that someone had tinkered with it, leaving the Sirens completely unmentioned.
As you'd expect, they were all shocked, especially Ganj-i-Sawi on account of her Church involvement.
I finished by bringing up a few ideas on what to do about the central unit.
Now it's time for Tempesta to decide the fate of their world.

scripts.say: Can you believe it? The Goddess was an ancient artifact, just like the Fountain of Youth.
To think her graces were just nothing more than an attempt to maintain balance...
The Church must've known that for ages. Why didn't you tell us?
You say that, but her protection IS real.
Also, don't you like her more now? Isn't this better than a real deity who judges you from the heavens?
Hmm. That's true...
So now that you know the truth, won't you join the Church? Come and praise the Goddess with us!
What's with the sudden recruitment attempt? You join Tempesta first and I'll think about it!
I'm not going to let outsiders to the Church decide what to do with the Goddess' powers.
Unless you join, I won't accept the results of anything you vote on.
At the same time, you'll no longer be outsiders if you join, and you can vote with the rest of the Church on what to do with the central unit.
Sod that. I'm not joining any bloody church.
Besides, whether we join or not, we all have the same idea of what to do with the unit.
I don't remember stating my take on what we should do.
You didn't. You just gave us the facts.
But let's not forget I know you better than anyone else here.
Assuming this thing really is a threat and a burden, why should we waste time voting on what to do with it?
Royal Fortune winks playfully at me.
So! What's it going to be, folks?
Do we bring it back to normal, or do we wreck it?
Let it be restored so the wind and the sea will protect us once more.
Agreed! Better to have a Goddess than not, in my opinion.
The Church will be greatly indebted to us if we fix it!
It's an ancient artifact. Repairing it is the best option.
I don't really care either way.
Is there a "Portsmouth can have it" option?
No!
Damn. Fix, then.
Fixing it is the obvious thing to do.
Let's fix up the Goddess!
Alright, nine support fixing it, zero want to break it, and one just doesn't care.
See, Sawai? It's unanimous, and nobody even had to join any church!
Wonderful! On behalf of the Church, thank you all for your resolution!
That's that. Terminal, proceed with the system backup plan.
Orders received. Starting system restore program.
Estimated time until completion: 15 hours and 23 minutes.
This is gonna take all day!
Well, seems we'll just have to wait.
*yaaawn*... You do that... I'm gonna catch some z's...
Oh, right, I just remembered!
Fancy! Fancy, ya there?
Pardon?
You live in this place, yeah? So ya gotta know this place inside out.
There a pantry or pub 'round here? Got any grub 'n' spirits?
Spirits, you say?
Yes. Those are everywhere.
Jackpot! Get in there! Where're they at?
You want to consume them, too?
I'll show you to the Misty Pond.
Brilliant name for a bar! Let's go!
(Port's mouth is in for an adventure.)
BOOOM!
A mighty rumble shakes the entire temple.
Bloody hell! What was that?
Portsmouth Adventure appears in the corridor, Fancy's tentacles wrapped around her.
Heehee. Have you had enough "spirits"?
Blegh... Now's really not the time, Amity!
Serious talk – that an earthquake, or what was it?
Oh, I thought that was you. I suppose not.
The Commander is examining the Goddess' machine. Shall we see what happened?
Temple Underground - Central Unit
Whoa... Was that an earthquake?
There goes my nap...
The monsters are squirming. They're putting up one final struggle to stay alive... or stay undead, I guess.
There are still ten hours to go. We'll have to defend this place to the death.
For ten hours? There's no way.
Perhaps there IS a way.
We can move the unit to my ship and flee rather than fight.
Move it? How?
The shipgirls all stare at the colossal machine.
It's possible to perform a ritual that removes the seal upon it and move it to a new location.
Of course, it takes time. I'll need an hour to complete it.
An hour is doable. It's worth a shot!
Alright, I'll help!
I'd prefer help fending off the beasts on the outside rather than with the ritual, thanks!
Terminal is still performing the ritual of restoration. Let me stay here and keep an eye on it.
I'm staying if Terminal is staying.
Whydah...
I'll stay. You should back the others up outside.
Yeah, but...
It'll be fine. They're out there. If anything happens, I'll sound the alarm at once.
Okay. Be careful, Commander.
Following a quick strategy briefing, the shipgirls take the secret passage up through the temple.
The only ones left in the vast room are me, Fancy, and Ganj-i-Sawai.
Well, have you any questions for me?
That's my line. Don't you have anything to ask?
In fact, I do! You're a mysterious stranger from across the storm. I'm very curious about you!
Having said that, now is certainly not the time for pleasantries.
Let us concentrate on doing what we need to.
She casually trots over to an empty part of the room.
With a silent song in her mind, she then takes the first step of a graceful dance.
Vivaciously she moves, dancing with the sublimity of a flower blooming in the early spring.
Her ornamental bells chime softly while her sleeves draw beautiful curves through the air.
As she breaks into dance, a glowing golden pattern emerges on the floor.
It flickers gently, seemingly in resonance with the pattern on the central unit's shell.
Orders received. Executing command.
(Whoa, even Terminal is glowing gold...)
(Is it really a part of the central unit's transfer ritual?)
(That... actually makes sense.)
O Goddess, let this prayer carry you to a safe place!
She offers a prayer, and the central unit begins to shrink rapidly until it becomes a metal box no larger than Terminal is.
The ritual is finished, Commander! Let's board my ship and get out of here!
After escaping from the temple, I'm invited to a feast aboard Ganj-i-Sawai's ship.
I haven't had a chance to stock up on spices, so this may taste a little bland.
Still, it should be better than the grub Fancy offered!
I hope you'll like it, Commander.
The dining hall is furnished appropriately for a ship named "Exceeding Treasure," and the table is lined with lavish meals.
The gently flickering candlelight and the exotic aroma in the air lend the hall a definitively mysterious ambiance.
But, on the other hand...
KABOOOM!
On the outside, the ship's cannons fiercely bombard the sea.
(Such might... Each shot is equal to an Enforcer in power.)
(Sawai has felt... different ever since the central unit was placed aboard.)
Don't worry about your friends. What enemies are left outside aren't a big threat.
Clear your mind and enjoy the feast.
You're right. One thing, though...
Let's dig in and continue from there, shall we?
Sure.
I grab a small loaf of bread on a plate in front of me and take a bite.
Hmm... Curry bread?
Now then, what did you wish to talk about?
I won't beat around the bush. Were you after the Goddess' machine from the start?
Indeed! I was surprised you agreed to my plan to transfer it to my ship.
If I hadn't, we'd all be in danger.
Hmm. Maybe...
Wait, you don't think I put the enemies around the island so I could take the machine for myself, do you?
Because I didn't. Let's not forget they targeted me, too.
No, no, I don't think you were playing both sides for this.
It's just that I have my reasons to not fully trust the Church.
Tell me, what do you want from the machine?
Nothing outrageous. Just the power to crush any foe.
Like this!
KABOOOM!
Her cannons light up the night sky in a show of might.
Let me ask something different.
How long has our group been a part of your plan?
Ever since you rescued Whydah and learned about Grimoire Terminal?
Or even before that? Were you gunning for Terminal all along and "saved" her?
It wouldn't have been possible to move the central unit without it, after all.
My, my, you really are a sharp one.
And you're a great actor.
I really did think it was a coincidence that Terminal gave us that map.
Heehee. Thank you.
How much does the Church know about what's been happening?
Furthermore, how much does it know about ancient artifacts?
Now, now, I've not done anything to hurt you this whole time, have I?
No, but you did undeniably deceive a whole bunch of people.
And I promise that's the full extent of my sins. Won't you keep it a secret between us?
Why should I?
Because you haven't told the whole truth either, have you? About the central unit.
(She knows?!)
Listen. I'm not your enemy.
As for your other concerns... they're not so important now, are they?
She shrugs and forces a slightly awkward smile.
Come on. Relax a bit and enjoy the feast.
Don't let this candlelit atmosphere go to waste!
As soon as I hear the words, "Relax a bit," an overwhelming sleepiness comes over me.
Sawai... Did you...?
Forgive me. I used a little medicine in place of spices.
It wasn't in the food – it was in this aroma.
Sweetly and graciously, she smiles at me.
Urgh...
My eyelids grow heavy and my sight becomes cloudy.
Don't worry. Your friends are safe. I swear it on my honour.
As my consciousness recedes into the darkness, I feel a warm embrace around me.
Good night, Commander.
There is no need to say farewell.
Because we will meet again.
Somewhere, in an unknown location...
When I open my eyes, I'm met with an endless expanse of blue.
The compass glows faintly as it casts its light in a certain direction.
The compass...
Ah, that light... It's time to go home...
The light grows brighter and brighter until eventually, it engulfs everything.
The next time I open my eyes, what greets me is the familiar ceiling of my home.
I check the alarm clock beside my bed. Not much time has passed since I lay down.
And yet, I know that the adventure I just had was no dream.
The proof is right there – in my hand.
It is the golden compass, shining lustrously.
My pirate adventure really did happen.
And, it certainly won't be my last.

sequence: Tempesta and the Sleeping Sea - The End?

scripts.say: Through some miracle, I manage to board Royal Fortune's vessel.
Seeing my battered ship sink below the waves, I breathe a sigh of relief.
I've missed you, Commander!
Royal Fortune comes running up to me with open arms. Before I know it, I find myself squished into her bosom.
Yeah! It really has!
How come you knew I was out here?
Is it because I summoned all of Tempesta?
Which included you, I guess?
Wait, you did what?
You called them to the middle of a storm?
A storm is nothing we can't handle! It's in our name!
It was a joke! Don't look at me all angry like that!
Actually, this place was pretty calm up until a few moments ago. Then this storm showed up out of nowhere.
Maybe the storm appeared because you showed up?
Speaking of which, how'd you end up here anyway? I'd love to think that you're at my beck and call, but...
I saw a compass in my dream, and followed it.
A compass? You mean the one you gave me, and then I gave back to you?
No, the one you gave to me and that I later gave to you.
What? But I don't have a compass. I gave mine to you, remember?
You said you saw it in your dreams... Does that mean you don't have it on you?
Like I just said, I gave it to you!
Oookay... So where is it now?

options.content: Your guess is as good as mine.

scripts.say: Welp, I guess only god knows now...
But you see, the thing about lost items is that they tend to crop up when you least expect it! Like how it showed up in your dreams.
On another note, I'm investigating some strange events. Since you're here, might as well help me out!
You, too? What a coincidence.
I know an ace investigator. I'll get her on the case.
If you can, by all means!
Although, the passage between your world and mine is pretty unreliable... If only it weren't, you could bring in your unstoppable fleet to solve all our problems.
That's true. Unfortunately, I'm stuck on this pirate ship with only you to rely on.
Don't lose hope! You're a part of Tempesta, and I'll look out for you while you're here!
...Hey! What's so "unfortunate" about me and my ship, huh?!
Just a little banter. Anyway, tell me about these strange events.
There's been stories of rumbles in the deep, sea monsters that eat everything in their path, and terrifying so-called skelebeasts...
The rumour is that something strange has happened beneath the surface.
Whatever it is, a growing number of people have witnessed and suffered at its hands. Now even the routes between our cities are under threat.
That's why I've called the rest of Tempesta to deal with the problem.
For the good of humanity? That's awfully benevolent for a pirate.
"Benevolent"? We're doing it to ensure the smooth flow of commerce! How will we trade otherwise?
I'm not doing it for free, either. I went 'round and collected commission fees to do this from every city before I set out.
Smart! That way if your ship sinks, you can immediately afford a new one.
"If it sinks"? Hah! Not with ME at the helm, matey!
BWOOOOO!
A horn is blown, and the next moment, a fleet of ships breaks through the storm.
Heheh! The gang is all here!
Let's go, Commander! It's time for a captain's meeting!
A whistle blew and sails were hoisted. The weather was ideal for a voyage.
The treasure hunters of Tempesta stand on the deck, their red hair blowing in the wind.
Aahh! Nothin' beats the sea breeze!
Whatcha gonna do now, Amity?
Figure out what the Church is up to.
It feels like we were played like a fiddle.
Uh, were we?
Ganj-i-Sawai said the Commander went back home, but if there's one thing I know, it's that that one wouldn't leave without saying goodbye.
Eh? Didn't Royal Fortune say everything went fine?
Then that means that our leader is hiding something from us.
Don't you want to know what?
If there's no money in it, not really. Or what, are ya gonna blackmail one of our own?
Because I'm NOT doin' that!
Then what about becoming famous?
What? Famous?
You heard me.
Greater fame means more ruins to explore and more ancient relics we can get. Also more adventure.
Heehee. First, though, we'll have to get our names out there.
By spreading the story of Tempesta and the Sleeping Sea.
Sometime later, at the Tempesta meeting spot...
You won't believe this! I heard loads of people talking about our adventure in the Sleeping Sea while I was on the way here!
I've heard the tales, too. The word has gone quite far!
Which means our fame is growing!
From what I've heard, it was two treasure hunters who spread the word.
Ah, Dolphin! How did that probe go?
Pretty good! Here's what you asked Whydah to find out.
Fantastic!
Also, you said "two treasure hunters"... Could that be Portsmouth and Amity?
If so, they're doing us a real favour out there.
If our fame keeps spreading at this rate, then the next time the Commander shows up...
Who knows? Maybe we'll be several dozen strong by then!
Really? I think that's unrealistic.
Ugh! Don't be such a killjoy, Martinho!
...You don't have bad news for me, do you?
No. Nothing of the sort.
I just have a hunch that our ranks won't grow much.
Think of it as a curse placed upon us.
Not one more word about curses! It's frightening how plausible that is!
However, our luck may turn around, should the Commander return.
What makes you say that?
A hunch.
Incidentally, I heard you escorted Sawai to the Church. How did that go?
It went well. Few things can threaten someone like her.
Did she tell you anything?
No, but she did give me a curry bread recipe that's quite good.
She said the Commander liked it at her banquet, so I'm trying to make it as well.
Ooh! Whydah's gonna love what you just said!
Can I be excused?
You're leaving? You don't wanna go drinking with us?
No thanks! I already finished resupplying while you were talking.
Whydah's asked me to do a bunch of stuff, so I need to get going!
She's working you like a dog... Should I tell her off?
I can handle it. Plus, I love visiting her!
She knows all kinds of cool things and has all these plans going on...
Oh, but don't tell anyone! It's a fun secret.
She also says we're all gonna go on more amazing adventures together soon!
It's gonna be so much fun!
Somewhere, in an unknown location...
A shipgirl was performing a ceremonial dance in a vast room.
O Goddess, let this prayer carry you to a safe place.
As the light withdrew, Ganj-i-Sawai's dance came to a stop.
So, too, did the mysterious ritual she was conducting.
The Goddess' first miracle – Compiler's Eyes.
Wings that give shape, eyes that discern...
Soon, the Goddess shall return to us...
The sound of waves could be heard from somewhere within the room.
The Star Wayfinders have caught on to us.
I'll clean up our tracks. Keep them busy in the meantime...
...O faithful one.
Understood.

sequence: Tempesta and the Sleeping Sea - The End

scripts.say: Aboard the Great Royal Fortune - Captain's Cabin
As the various members of Tempesta gather, the din and hubbub of the cabin grows louder and louder.
Fortune! What were you bloody thinking, putting our meeting spot in the middle of– Why's the Commander here?!
Commander?
Oh, my! What brings you here, my darling? Did you miss me?
You're ALL here because I called on you! That includes the Commander!
Um... So your call went all the way to another world, did it?
Adventure Galley, São Martinho, and Golden Hind raise many questions, so I recount everything I've learned up to now.
I see... It seems that we once more need your leadership for the battle ahead of us.
Yes... To put it another way, destiny has brought us together again! Heehee♥
That explains the storm. Wherever the Commander goes, tempests aren't far behind.
São Martinho, you're still with the navy, yes?
I am. I serve as a Nebula Guardian, which suits me better.
Works better for us, too! Having navy connections makes pirating easier.
In addition, some of the commissions that Royal Fortune accepted were posted by the Nebula Guardians.
It therefore makes sense that I be present to supervise her.
Yeah, yeah, cheers for keeping an eye on me and all that. Now, who wants some nosh?
"Nosh"?
...Already put the stove on, I see.
The storm hasn't stopped and we're still waiting for people, so yeah, I say we have ourselves something to eat!
Plus, we've got to celebrate the Commander being here!
All too true! I'll just help myself to these skewers.
Sure, eat all you want!
I caught these... Uhh, I actually dunno what they are, but they're delicious and I caught 'em just this morning!
You, too! Try these, Commander!

options.content: (Take a bite of the mystery skewers.)

scripts.say: (Unappetizing texture, strange taste...)
I don't dare to savor the taste any longer, so I forcibly swallow the food – if you could call it that.
Pretty good, right? Have another!
(It smells and looks really unappetizing...)
(For my own safety, I'll have to decline.)
Not hungry? Fine, just hold it, then!
I'll eat it for you! Nom!
By the way... Are these "skelebeasts" edible?
What?
You think I cooked and skewered one of THOSE things?
Does this smell and taste like a sea monster to you?
Also, just think about the name! If these WERE skelebeasts, shouldn't they be all bones and no meat?
Wait, do you even know what the skelebeasts look like?
That's one of the things we're here to find out!
Rest assured, I can confirm that this is not the flesh of a skelebeast.
Then why'd you phrase it like that?! Way to freak me out!
I wanted to remind you about our objective here, since you were being so casual about this commission.
Lest we forget that our target is a monster that threatens all trade between our cities.
Supposing that this is a dangerous and elusive creature, we must take it absolutely seriously.
Yes, yes, whatever you say, ma'am.
Bleh... My appetite's all gone...
Mine, too.
How unfortunate. In that case, I shall eat the rest of the skewers.
You what?
Let's get back to business, shall we?
Fortune, you said you're on an investigation, but to where?
Well, I have a few places in mind. There's the place where the last attack happened, so I'm thinking about checking that first.
That is, once the gang is all here. Until then, we wait.
Who's missing?
Whydah said she's not coming, so we're just missing Mary.
So if I got that right, the gang consists of Whydah, São Martinho, Mary Celeste, Golden Hind, Adventure Galley, and lastly you.
Am I really not missing anyone? Didn't you say you'd recruit more members?
...Why are you all looking at me?
Believe me, I HAVE been getting the word out and trying to recruit people! It's just not gone very well!
In fact... I think someone has been sabotaging our efforts!
Whydah is looking into the who and why as we speak.
She'll uncover something any day now, so don't blame me for–
KABOOOM!
Royal Fortune is interrupted by the sound of an explosion.
Looking out the cabin window, I see the red glow of a firework in the distant sky.
That's her!
It's Mary's distress signal!
Looks like our saboteurs have escalated! Now they're engaging in full-on raids against us!
Girls, get back to your ships! Prepare for battle!
Tempesta's vessels get into a neat formation and sail forward. It's not long before we reach the site of Mary's distress signal.
KABOOOM!
Mary is outmatched two to one.
They only have two ships? Then let's back her up and make it a five versus two!
Marinho, you and Golden Hind go take care of the big one!
Galley and I will blow the small one to bits!
Wait. Don't sink them, just neutralize them.
Why? You got plans for them, or something?
Do you know who the attackers are?
Uh, no?
Okay, and what are the odds that they knew about your meeting point and waited here to ambush you?
That's basically impossible. Although, considering that they've been working in the shadows this whole time...
If they knew about your rendezvous, why didn't they attack when you came here alone?
What are you suggesting? That they just happened to be in the area?
That doesn't really make sense. Why would they pick a fight with Mary in the middle of a storm?
You came here to investigate those strange events – maybe the attackers play a role in them.
Can't deny that. They might know something.
Right, you lot heard the Commander! Change shots and aim to cripple, not sink!
KABOOOM!
Guh! Stone me! She wasn't lyin' 'bout reinforcements bein' on the way!
Let's retreat. We'll get another chance.
Hah. Tempesta's biggest ships are here, and you think you can retreat?
Wuzzah? Tempesta?
You heard me. You scared now? What happened to "giving me a whooping," huh?
Hang on... You sayin' you DIDN'T command those those big-arse monsters into attackin' us?
The only "monster" I control is Argo, and besides, YOU attacked first!
Oh. Yes, come to think of it, I only saw a single monster in the water during our battle...
Bollocks. We mucked up 'n' went after the wrong one...
You what?
Oi! You scallywags! We have you surrounded!
Lower your weapons and surrender and we'll spare your lives! And your assets, I guess!
Alright! We surrender!
Otherwise, we'll– Oh. That was easy.
We'll hold you to your word – spare our lives and assets.
Say, could we take shelter aboard your flagship? The wind is really picking up.
Also, we're quite hungry. You'll share some food with us, won't you?
Oi... Why are you acting like we're friends now?
Are you trying to trick me into letting you board the Great Royal Fortune to stab us in the back?
You're NOT setting foot here! Make do with your own ships!
Let's let them explain who they are, then we can decide what to do with them.
Oh, right... They ruined my flow and I lost focus.
So, who are you people? Why are you here? Why did you attack our ally?
Well, Portsmouth, looks like we've run into an interesting group.
Somehow, I get the feeling that the red-haired girl is staring at me.
Name's Portsmouth Adventure! This lass here is Amity!
We're treasure hunters. We didn't plan on comin' 'ere until this storm appeared outta the blue!
So we tried to escape the storm, then monsters attacked us all of a sudden!
Monsters, you say?
Were humongous, I tell ya! Knew they came from the deep the moment I saw 'em!
In fact, they were 'bout as big as your Miss Mary's giant pet!
You assumed I was controlling it and you attacked me? Is that it?
Yeah. We'd just made it out alive, then we saw you commandin' another beast.
Simply put, we jumped to conclusions! Sorry!
So... I'm innocent in all this?
Yup. Unless you're hidin' another monster somewhere.
You know, we have five ships and you have two, so...
Like I said, we're sorry! We'll compensate ya for the harm done, promise!
There's no harm to speak of. You never even hit me.
Ah, Mary, but there was harm and you're overlooking it.
There's the damage to the sails and ropes, then the cost of the cannonballs. That adds up to quite a lot for five ships.
You'll pay the current market price to replace these things, won't you?
Blimey... Ahah... haha...
We can talk about compensation later. I have a more important question to ask.
Yeah? Go on.
You mentioned a monster from the depths... Is THAT what you were referring to?
The waves churn on the horizon. Giants rise from the deep one after the next.
GRAAAAGHHH!
Th-that's them! The monsters!
Let's get outta 'ere!
The monsters pursue us at incredible speed, smashing through the waves.
There's at least a hundred of them! Could this get ANY worse?!
On the contrary. We're quite lucky.
This gives us a heap of information, and right on our first investigation.
Ah, all too true, milady! Could Your Invincibleness then please go and capture a specimen for us?
Exactly. See, it's only called an investigation when we have the initiative – when they do, it's called a battle to the death!
At least we know now the strength of our enemy.
Hey, Cap'n? We can't exactly run forever, so let's take to land 'n' seek refuge, yeah?
I endorse this suggestion.
Well, we WERE gonna make landfall at Eisenblech to resupply anyway...
It's not that far from here, and the Goddess does watch over the island.
Let's go there! Should be safe enough!
Eisenblech Island – Port – Sometime later
On the shore stands a faintly-glowing statue of the Goddess.
The skelebeasts had suddenly stopped pursuing us just a few nautical miles off the coast. In addition, the island seems unaffected by the storm we just braved.
Phew... We're still in one piece!
Yes. For now.
São Martinho gazes up at the statue.
A portion of its face is battered and worn, a massive crack running along its back. One of its wings is missing as well.
The Goddess statue has been destroyed... Who could have done this, and why?
Moreover, how is the island still receiving her protection if her statue is ruined?
No man did this. It simply fell apart on its own one day.
This has happened across many islands... This one is just one of them.
What do you mean, "fell apart on its own"?
The Goddess' protection is growing weaker. That is evident from the arrival of these storms.
The head of the Nebula Guardians must be informed of this posthaste.
Oi... You suggested this island as a resupply spot so we could investigate this statue at the same time, didn't you?
As a reminder, doing this is a part of our commission.
Wait... Really?
Did you even read the terms of the commission before you accepted it?
I will make note of the statue in my report.
Okay! I'll leave the writing to you!
So she accepted a commission from the Nebula Guardians to earn some money for investigating the attacks that she was going to anyway.
Meanwhile, the Nebula Guardians combined that investigation with another one about the statues.
So, is there any chance that the statues and the attacks are connected?
There is.
The reports about the skelebeasts and the ruined statues came in nearly at the same time.
Naturally, this raised some eyebrows.
So you admit it! You lumped the commission together to get two for the price of one!
...Really?
That's what you care about?
Hey, I care, too.
As do I. These things matter!
Ahahaha! You lot are a funny bunch!
I'd keep my gob shut if I were you! We haven't forgotten you attacked us just half an hour ago!
You said you were treasure hunters, yeah?
As promised, I won't take your lives or assets... but I WILL make you spill the beans on all the treasure I don't know about!
Yeah! Give us the deets, NOW!
The promise of treasure gets all the pirates riled up.
Well, I heard a rumour a while back.
Supposedly, a ghost fleet appeared from the depths of the sea.
They say this ghost fleet returned through the power of a very special relic.
In fact, we were chasing this ghost fleet until we were caught up in that storm.
That legendary relic won't be an easy one to find!
A ghost fleet? I've never seen anything like that.
First skelebeasts, then storms growing stronger, broken Goddess statues, and now a ghost fleet?
Ugh! This is getting more convoluted by the minute!
And what's this about a "special relic"?!
Nobody knows what it looks like, or even if it exists in the first place...
If the Goddess and the storms are connected, then who's to say the skelebeasts and the ghost fleet aren't connected as well?
Whatever the case, we should treat these as two separate anomalies.
I see the connection between the Goddess and the storms, but what links the skelebeasts to the ghost fleet?
It's just a gut feeling. I think they have in common the trait of being undead.
Seeing as skelebeasts spawn from shipwrecks, they're sort of like zombified ships. That's a lot like the ghost fleet – wrecked ships coming back to life.
Wrecked ships coming back to life... What if this all leads back to our old friend, the Fountain of Youth?
Not in any obvious way, if so. There are still many mysteries surrounding the Fountain, though.
Sounds like we should investigate, then!
Porty, Amity, what will you do? You coming with us?
Last I heard, the Fountain of Youth has been totally looted, so not much reason for us to go there.
But, since it might lead to clues on the relic, we're goin'! To the Fountain of Youth!
Then we have a plan! We'll resupply then be off!
Before we do that, let's find Whydah and borrow Grimoire Terminal. Anything could be waiting for us at the Fountain.
Good idea. Once the resupply is done, we'll meet up with Whydah!
I have a question. Which one of you is the leader of Tempesta?
Me! That should go without saying!
I see, I see.
Tempesta arrives at Whydah's hideout, having avoided storms along the way.
Thankfully, it was an uneventful journey.
New World - Whydah's Hideout
An ashen fog has engulfed the once-calm sea.
A field of broken and charred planks covers the surface, extending as far as the eye can see.
Bloody hell... THIS is where your friend lives?
I smell the remnants of a battle... And the stench of decomposition.
Where's Whydah?! Is she alright?!
BANG!
A signal flare goes off, bursting into a blue light.
I sent out a signal. We just have to wait for Whydah's response.
KABOOOM!
There is no response from Whydah – only the first salvo of an enemy that lies in wait.
It's an ambush!
One ghost ship after the next emerges from the water, making the sea look as though it's boiling.
Well! 'Ere they are! They're real ghost ships alright!
Talk about lucky! Wasn't expectin' us to run into them out 'ere!
Yes, lucky us. Since you're so lucky, why don't you go and capture one of them for us?
Can I? Aw yeah!
Wait, you'll do it?!
Amity, we're going with Porty! And remember to try to aim this time!
KABOOOM!
Tempesta! Give 'em hell!
GRAAAAGHHH!
Skelebeasts incoming!
KABOOOM!
Listen up! We're running away! If you like living, you'll do the same!
Because you're burned bread if those monsters surround you!
Dammit! I nearly got one of the buggers, too! Amity, let's book it!
The shipgirls hoisted sails and, after a long while, finally shook off the pursuers.
While they're out of the woods now, they haven't turned their backs on Whydah's hideout yet.
We can't just leave Whydah there. We have to go back.
Whydah's smart. Knowing her, she left that place long ago.
Then why did the enemy lie in ambush for us rather than pursue her, huh?
Beats me. Maybe she escaped without them noticing?
Besides, there's no reason for them to linger if they've already sent her to Davy Jones's locker.
She could be hiding somewhere not far from here.
If you're all staying here, fine! I'll go after her myself!
Whoa, whoa, hold on a moment! Nobody's said we're NOT gonna rescue Whydah, okay?
Rushing in blindly is not the way to do it, though! We need a plan!
While the girls hold a heated debate aboard the Great Royal Fortune, an abrupt event shakes the sea.
BOOOM! BOOOM!
A magnificent and enormous battleship emerges from the fog, thundering explosions from its guns tearing through the air.
Dozens upon dozens of cannons erupt with black smoke, firing red-hot cast iron balls at the enemy.
In but the blink of an eye, the ghost fleet and the skelebeasts are decimated.
Isn't that... Ganj-i-Sawai? The treasure ship?
Ganj-i-Sawai? That girl who sails around, lugging tons of gold and silver?
Yes. That's her.
Bloody hell... Have a gander at that. How much treasure ya reckon she's haulin'?
I wouldn't go after her if I were you.
She is a high-ranking member of the Church of the Goddess. Attacking her will have dire consequences.
Wasn't even considerin' it, angel! I was more thinkin', "Oi, aren't we saved now?"
Looks like she's running and gunning. Is that what she's doing? I think she's pulling it off well.
I've spoken to her when we did business a few times before. She's not a bad apple, don't get me wrong...
It's just you can never know what's going through her mind.
While the girls talk, Ganj-i-Sawai herself appears on the deck of her massive vessel.
O Goddess, put these weary souls to rest...
She looks skyward, her face a reflection of pure reverence, and whispers a prayer.
Next, she turns and looks at us with a beaming smile.
That was close! I'm shocked there are such dangerous foes out here... Are you all okay?
We're fine! Thanks for coming to our help.
Oh, think nothing of it! I just happened to be in the area, you see.
Here, allow me to return these sweeties to you.
Catch!
WHOOSH!
She picks up two little girls and throws them our way.
AAAAAAHHHHHHH!
Wheeeee! I'm flying!
They sail in a perfect arc through the air. Whydah hits the deck like a sack of potatoes.
The other girl, meanwhile, nimbly lands on her feet next to me.
Heehee! Another happy landing!
*cough cough*... Much stronger than she looks, that woman...
Whydah, are you okay?!
Okay enough. She came to my rescue as soon as the fighting started.
What are you all doing here, anyway?
We're going to investigate the Fountain of Youth again, and the Commander said we should bring your Grimoire Terminal along, just to be safe.
The Grimoire, huh...
Ah, you're going to the Fountain?
Are you also hoping to get your hands on that relic that can revive the dead?
"Also"?
Sure are! Got any info ya could share?
That I do! But in exchange for what?
Uhh... Amity, how much dosh do we have left?
Porty, please. Do you think she would tell us anything if she wants the relic for herself?
I certainly would not!
As far as I'm concerned, you're my rivals!
Don't expect me to give you any useful info, and even if I do, you shouldn't take it at face value.
All I'll tell you is this – do go to the Fountain!
Sure, it's been looted bare, but who knows? Maybe there's still something you can uncover!
Now, if you'll excuse me, I'll be on my way.
When she finishes, she turns her ship around and starts heading off.
Just a moment, Sawai!
I think someone is using the relic to manipulate monsters and ghost ships into attacking people. I doubt they'll just hand it over if you ask nicely.
Your best shot at getting it is to work together with us.
I'll be just fine! The Goddess is watching over me!
The rudder of her great vessel turns, and she vanishes into the mist in an instant.
Even the Church has become engrossed in hunting for treasure...
Despite the fact that these monsters and ghost ships pose a threat to all of our cities.
I think getting rid of the threat and confiscating the relic are the same thing to her.
On the bright side, based on what she said, it all but confirms that the relic is no mere rumor.
What's more... she probably knows much more about it than we do.
Should we go after her?
We'd better hurry if we're gonna!
I'm not sure we'll be able to catch up to her even then.
I can.
On your own? That doesn't help. We've ALL gotta go after her!
Relax. We're not going after her.
She called us her rivals. She might take it as a threat if we start following her.
Really? She seemed like a nice lady to me.
Nice has nothing to do with it. We're clearly no friends of hers, so it's best to be cautious.
All that is to say, we'll go to the Fountain of Youth as planned.
Aye-aye. Tempesta, get your things in order!
Set sail for the Fountain of Youth!
Set sail for the Fountain of Youth!
Nice! That's the energy I want to see!
Wait...
Who are you?
Who are you?
Royal Fortune stares dumbfoundedly at the little stranger who landed on her deck along with Whydah.
The girl, Dolphin, tilts her head slightly to the side.
Heehee. I was wondering when you were gonna ask!
Hi, fellow captains. I'm Dolphin. I'm the new blood.
Come again?
Really? We finally got a new member?
Ohh, you're a new recruit. I'm Royal Fortune! I'm your leader!
Wow! The leader! Hi there!
Hold on a minute. I thought ya were a treasure hunter?
Dolphin! I've heard that name before! Didn't think she'd be as small as li'l Whydah here, though.
Heeey! Hands off my hat!
Whydah's the one who let me join, actually!
You've been dying for a new member, haven't you? Well, this little girl came here from far away, and she's honest and adorable, to boot.
She's from far away?
Yeah! I became a fan when I heard you discovered the Fountain of Youth, and I've been looking for a way to join you ever since.
Then I found Whydah, but immediately after, all those baddies surrounded us and we had to run.
That's when Ganj-i-Sawai came to rescue us, and the rest you already know!
Did you hear that? Our little Whydah got us our first-ever new member!
Ugh! I worked my arse off, and Whydah just gets one for free!
Still, I'm impressed you found her. She's our second-hardest-to-find member.
Heehee. That's all thanks to my special ability.
If Whydah's the second-hardest... who's the most?
Why, it's none other than...
Royal Fortune points her finger at me with a snap.
My vice-leader, {playername}, the Commander!
Ohh! So you're Tempesta's commander. I'm Dolphin. It's nice to meet you!
The little girl takes my hand and shakes it with all her strength.
No, you got that wrong... It's just "Commander." Not "commander of Tempesta."
Not your commander... Just "Commander"?
Dolphin slightly cocks her head and shoots me a confused look.
Ugh... Look, it's complicated! It'd take too long to explain!
All you need to remember is that I'm the NUMBER ONE leader of Tempesta! Okay?
She prefaces with the phrase "number one" to make this point absolutely clear.
(She really wants to hammer in who the boss pirate is to the rookie, huh.)
Okay.
Dolphin nods in understanding, and Royal Fortune hands her a thick book titled, "The Tempesta Pact."
And so, we resume our journey to the Fountain of Youth, with a new member along for the ride.

sequence: <size=64>And so, an uneventful 12 hours pass...</size>
Aboard the Great Royal Fortune
Commander's Cabin
Night

scripts.say: Hey, you've not left your cabin since dinnertime.
Doesn't it wear you out, working around the clock?
Blimey. Your work must be dreadful.
She gives me a sidelong glance while I fill out another mission-related paper.
You know, I don't think you've had a moment's rest since you got here.
If you want my advice, take a nap. You can work after you've had your beauty sleep.
And if you can't sleep, or if you're feeling lonely... I can sleep with you, if you want.
This whole situation is complicated, and I want to go through all the information again.
I'll be just fine. You can hit the hay if you're tired.
I mean, I'm not really. Plus, watching you work is entertaining.
I'll stick around a while longer, in other words. It's not like I have anything else to–
CLUNK!
The cabin door opens, and a large pirate hat comes into view as Whydah peeks in.
Hey, uh, I've brought Grimoire Terminal.
Said you wanted to borrow it, right?
Yeah. Thanks.
You can hold on to it. As long as we're ready for surprises at the Fountain of Youth, it doesn't matter who has it.
Well, uh... It's been acting up for a while now. I've tried to speak to it, but it won't respond.
See? Nothing but crickets.
Maybe you can fix it, somehow...
(It worked just fine before... Do Siren electronics break that easily?)
Let me have a look.
She hands me the "Grimoire." I examine it up-close, from top to bottom.
(It looks undamaged, and I don't smell any fried wires.)
Terminal, boot up!
Alas, nothing happens.
(Hmm. It could be a software error, or some internal component has broken.)
(Alternatively, it could simply be out of battery.)
What's goin' on in here, then?
That little thing ya got there break, or somethin'?
Want me to smack it? Who knows – might fix it!
Portsmouth starts twirling the bottle in her hand.
Nooooo! Don't do that!
Ahahaha! I'm just kiddin'! Don't get so worked up, lass!
(If only Akashi were here. She might be able to fix Siren tech.)
(I doubt we can get this thing working again on our own.)
So, any ideas, Commander?
I can't figure out what the root issue is. It won't be easy to fix.
Darn...
Whydah hangs her head in low spirits.
I do have an idea, though. Do you mind if I keep it for now? I'll find a way to get it working again.
Sure. You can have it as long as you want if you fix it!
If you need replacement parts, let me know and I'll find some.
THUD!
Huh?
Whuh?
Did... Did the desk just move?
I think it did...
THUD!
I knock on the desk, and it jumps again.
What is this? Is it haunted?!
Are we dealing with a ghost?!
There's ALREADY a ghost on your ship.
THUNK!
Then, the cabinet doors under the desk fly open.
Are you looking for something?
I can help with that!
Why is there a compartment under the desk?
Because I saw some New World designs and got inspired!
It makes cleaning easier if you can just pop it right open!
Why are you in there, Dolphin?
I'm looking for treasure!
On my ship?
Yeah! I can sense there's some amazing treasure here.
That is true... The Great Royal Fortune carries loads of treasure, and some of it is even exceptional...
But that doesn't mean you can just take them!
I know, I know. I'm just looking around and studying the ship's structure to kill some time.
Anyway! What were you all looking for? I'm an expert at finding things!
Nothing at the moment. There's no telling what replacement parts you need without opening this thing.
(Besides, replacement parts for Siren technology aren't exactly easy to find.)
Ohh. Okay.
Do you wanna sleep with me, then?
HUH?!
What? Ya mean like... nappin' together?
R-right, that reminds me! It's late! You should all go to bed!
Nighty-night! Sleep tight! Go on, back to your cabins now!
Eh? Feels like I'm missin' something 'ere...
Maybe, maybe not? I can't tell!
If ya say so. Then I'm off to have myself 'nother drink!
Shrimpy, you stayin', or you comin' with?
First of all, I'm not a "shrimpy."
Secondly, I'm going back to my cabin.
And lastly, you're the last person I'd drink with!
Royal Fortune, Whydah, and Portsmouth Adventure all leave the cabin one by one. Only Dolphin remains, sitting under the table.
You still haven't answered my question.
I asked if you wanted to sleep with me, and you never said anything.
My hands are tied with work, so...
Well, go to bed early tonight! You can always work tomorrow.
Finally, we arrive at the ruins of the Fountain of Youth.
As they gaze at the ransacked islands, looks of amazement appear on their faces.
There it is! The Fountain of Youth! This was worth the trip!
Although... pretty different from what the rumours say, innit?
I was gonna say! It's completely different!
Wasn't it, like, a big island of machinery last time we were here?
Yeah, there was machinery everywhere.
And now there's nothing but rocks left!
What happened? Where'd all the technology go?
It's been almost literally stripped bare... It seems we underestimated the draw of the rumours surrounding this place.
Will we even find any leads here?

options.content: We're already here. Might as well try.
We'll just have to look around and see what we find.

scripts.say: That's true. You're here, so maybe we'll get lucky!
True! Although, it's not like we have any other choice.
Let's split up to cover more ground.
You do that. I'll stay here and stand guard.
Nuh-uh! You're coming along!

sequence: <size=64>And so, we split up into teams to search across the islands.</size>
Our search range grew and grew while the sky overhead darkened.

scripts.say: Somewhere, in the ruins of the Fountain of Youth...
You can't see anything when it's this dark outside.
Since we're not going to find anything, we'll just have to call it for tonight...
BEEP BEEP! BEEP BEEP!
Is that...?
All of a sudden, Grimoire Terminal starts beeping from inside my backpack.
I take out the tablet. There are a few glowing dots displayed on the screen.
The light of the Goddess is fading... Her core is decaying...
The tide is rising... Order is collapsing...
Only by putting the dead to sleep once more... can peace be restored.
The flickering dots change shape, assuming the form of a map of the sea.
A bright spot stands out on the map – it is clearly some sort of destination marker.
"The Sleeping Sea"...

sequence: Aboard the Great Royal Fortune
Captain's Cabin
Sometime later

scripts.say: ...And that concludes the briefing!
Royal Fortune displayed the map of the sea copied from Termina's screen. She briefed the others on what I told her earlier.
Sleepless Sea... Doesn't ring any bells. I don't think the books of the ancients made any mention of it.
Also, the map places it at the very edge of the boundary between the Old and the New World.
That sounds very dodgy to me.
I have a question. Are you SURE it was Grimoire Terminal speaking to you, Commander?
You tell me. It's never booted up by itself before, and I don't remember it sounding like that the last time.
Maybe it wasn't Terminal speaking, but rather someone else was speaking through it.
Using... magic, I guess.
That little thing is one big enigma...
Supposing that it wasn't Terminal speaking, then who? Are they friend or foe?
There's no way to know, is there?
But if we don't know, this will make for an exceedingly risky voyage.
To hell with it! We can talk ourselves sore, but what good will that do?
Make up your minds! Are we goin' or not?
Commander, what's your take?
On one hand, it's a potential lead. On the other, it could be dangerous. I say we decide by vote.
I'm in favour of going!
Same here!
- Let's check it out!  - I support it.
Personally, I'm against it.
As long as I can stay behind and stand guard, I don't care one way or the other.
If the Sleeping Sea does exist, that in and of itself will be a massive discovery. I support going there.
So that's five in favour, one against, and one abstaining. Commander?
If I must choose, I'm leaning toward going there.
That's six in favour! An easy, qualified majority!
We'll set sail for the Sleeping Sea in three hours!
Hang on a minute! Don't me 'n' Amity get to vote?
This is a vote among Tempesta only. If you want to have a say, you'll have to become a member first!
So, will you join?
Can we get honorary membership, like Martinho?
Yeah, sure.
Then we'll join. Also, we both support going there.
Gotcha. That's eight in favour, even though we already have a qualified majority.
Amity and Portsmouth Adventure, welcome to Tempesta!
Now let's set off! To the Sleeping Sea!
And so, the curtains rise on a small conflict.
The victor will seize the treasure, whilst the loser will walk away empty-handed.
This conflict, compared to the immeasurable vastness of the ocean, is unbelievably tiny...
Fire! Fire!
It's the early bird who gets the New World booty!
KABOOOM!
Amid thundering cannon fire, the warship's opponent turned tail and fled.
Hahaha! I won!
Another glorious victory to my name, another heap of–
CRACK! BOOOOOM!
Whoa!
What was that?! A storm out of the blue?!
I need to lower my sails, right now!
Dammit! I won't make it in time!
This is NOT the kind of high-octane adventure I signed up fooooor!
The warship, with all her sails hoisted, hurtled headfirst into the storm.
In light of our change of course, rather than pick up the pace, São Martinho maintains a set distance behind us.
It's as if she expects us to wander into the Windless Sea and is waiting for it to happen.
Then, suddenly...
...The wind stopped.
The air is heavy and the seas are calm... Uh-oh.
This isn't the Windless Sea...
KRR-BOOOM!
It's a storm! A storm's coming!
We need to find shelter, now!
...But where are you supposed to find shelter on the open bloody ocean?!
In the blink of an eye, our ship begins being pelted with rain and rocked with gales.
In a storm like this, it matters not whether you're in the shabbiest sloop or the best clipper – the waves will pummel your hull either way.
As it goes with the Great Royal Fortune, so too does it go with our pursuer.
Gah...!
She's gotten separated from her galleon... Good!
I doubt she'll make it far like this!
Oi, you stubborn prat! Give up the chase and go away already!
São Martinho winces, but shows no intent of breaking off from us.
She is determined, but the storm is apathetic to her resolve.
(I can't just leave her to her fate!)
What? Are you seriously thinking about saving her?!
She can't even save herself... Bah, fine!
Despite her objection, Royal Fortune grips the helm and pulls it hard.
I need your help, too, Golden Hind!
São Martinho! Come here, quickly!
Grab my hand!
Ugh...
Mrrghh...
Come on...!
The waves are coming! Look out, Commander!
Almost there! Don't let go!
Comma... wave... too strong!
We're... turn...!
The furious thunder drowns out their voices.
I do the only thing I can – hold on to São Martinho's hand like my life depends on it.
Heheh~♪
Sooo... you're sure about this?
Okay... I feel like the happiest girl alive!
But, living with me's not gonna be easy. You can't just change your mind later, ya hear?
Alright, then take my hand...
SLAM!
Oi! What are ya doing?!
I open my eyes and see Royal Fortune at the cabin door, having just thrown it open with force.
What does it look like? We're tending to the Commander~
Shh. Not so loud. The Commander just woke up.
Okay, okay...
WAIT, NO! THIS IS NOT OKAY!
The Commander is MY crewmate! Looking after the crew is MY job!
And you! Out of the way!
Famous ghost ship or not, you're in MY seat!
Well, well~
I thought I heard someone aboard this clipper was dying to meet a ghost ship~
Who might that be, hmm~?
Ugh! I hate you!
I don't care about those anymore!
I did not imagine my day would start with a catfight wake-up call...
Fair enough~ Come sit next to me, Royal Fortune~
Hmph. "Thanks."
She sits down angrily on the bed and grasps my other, unheld hand.
*sigh*... Let's get the important question out of the way.
Where's São Martinho? Is she okay?
Aye. Safe and sound, thanks to your selfless bravery.
Yeah. She told me she WASN'T after us in particular.
Because why would she be? That whole chase only happened because Golden Hind misled us!
Well, in my defence, it's only natural to be alarmed in that situation.
Can't argue with that.
São Martinho feels conflicted about this whole thing. She pursued you all, and you ended up saving her. Must be a hard pill to swallow.
Still, I think she'll let you off the hook. Your hand's so warm, anyone would–
Oi!
I see you! Don't you even try!
Hahahah! You've got a funky crew here, Commander. Hang on to it.
My name's Mary Celeste, by the way.
I'm the true face behind the ghost ship legend of New World.
Mhm. She helped by guiding us into the eye of the storm.
I figured you should know, since she probably wouldn't tell you herself.

options.content: Thanks for saving us. How can we repay you?

scripts.say: No need to. You and your crew earned the rescue.
Brave people like yourself deserve to see grand voyages to their end. I only did what I thought anyone would have.
As a ghost ship, sailing to the eye of a storm is an instinct imprinted on my hull.
Speaking of the storm, it'll abate in a few hours. You can sail away safely after that.
Will you be coming with us?
Excuse me?
Don't I creep you out? I'm a ghost ship, for god's sake.
Come on. You're just saying that.
No, the Commander means it.
The Goddess of Thalasso has nothing against you, so why should we?
You are cordially and sincerely invited to join the crew. We want you with us on this adventure!
Isn't that right, Commander?
(Come on, say something!)

options.content: Damn right! Took the words right out of my mouth, my queen!

scripts.say: O-okay, you don't need to agree THAT hard...
Hmm... Give me a while to think about it.
By the way–
KABOOOM!
Suddenly, the sound of cannon fire rumbles through the cabin window.
What was that?
Oh, dear. It's the Echo Fleet.
And São Martinho is already engaging them. We should back her up~
In a hurry, we leave the cabin and set foot on the quarterdeck.
Debris from the ship litters the deck, even though the storm that broke the pieces off is already dying down.
No, not just dying down – the storm wall encircling us is dispersing right before our eyes.
The storm is going away? How?
I thought it'd pass in hours from now, not minutes!
Golden Hind, didn't ya say the Goddess commands the sea and the sky?
Has the Echo Fleet taken that power from her, somehow?
They couldn't control the bloody weather, last I heard! Clearly, they can!
I'm afraid I wouldn't know. It's possible they sussed out Mary Celeste's true form and decided to attack.
Otherwise, I can't see why they'd want to kill the storm.
They're here because of me?
Huh... I don't know what their beef with me is, but sorry for getting the rest of you involved.
Start sailing out of here. I'll draw their attention away from you.
Thank you! You're a lifesaver!
...Is what you thought I'd say, didn't you?!
No! I have principles! Principles like not abandoning a single member of my crew or fleet!
From now on, that's part of my pact!

options.content: Since when did you have a whole fleet?
Since when did you establish a pact?

scripts.say: Since now!
Now shut up! I'm trying to sound cool here!
Hahahah! You all are a funny bunch.
Tell you what – I'll come along on your adventures.
Welcome aboard! Literally!
First of all, we have to win this battle! São Martinho needs our help!
The Echo Fleet is tough, but we've already beaten 'em once before!
Now, set sail!
It was a long and hard battle.
The Echo Fleet fought us head-on, coordinating and using tactics, not so much as flinching at the hail of cannon fire we unleashed on them.
Despite that, though, I managed to lead our side to victory.
May the golden light shine evermore... The Echo Fleet has been annihilated.
You, Commander, are a force like a raging storm. I commend you.
After weathering that fierce battle with us, São Martinho finally is willing to talk eye-to-eye.
I do not. I mean every word.
My view of you has been glowing since you saved me.
Why don't you board my ship, so we can talk further?
A kind offer, but we must refuse~
While I know you only came across us by happenstance, I will not let you poach any of our crew.
If it's my darling Commander you just can't get enough of, how about you join our fleet instead?
Oi! Phrasing! It's not "our" fleet, it's MY fleet!
Also... I found this odd flag among the Echo Fleet's wreckage. Does anyone recognise it?
Flag? Let me have a look~
Oh, my... Why, this is the Black Wolves' flag!
Indeed it is. I've seen more like it very recently, too.
Those, too, were among Echo Fleet wreckages.
Hang on, I thought the Black Wolves were treasure hunters?
What's the Echo Fleet got to do with them?
Well, consider that the Black Wolves "perished" decades ago.
And after many years, they've suddenly reappeared again, as if brought back to life.
While they use the same old flag, we know nothing about who they are now, not even who's their leader.
So, what I think is that the Black Wolves aren't back, but rather that someone is controlling the Echo Fleet and sails under the guise of the Black Wolves' banner.
Hmm... I can see the logic behind that.
The Echo Fleet has been raiding shipping lanes more frequently over the past few years.
They've gotten more daring and begun attacking cities, too.
It's anyone's guess what their goal is, but if they're after the same thing as the Black Wolves...
(This is an interesting inquiry...)
(The Sirens are more than capable of manipulating the weather.)
(Assuming this Echo Fleet is in fact the Sirens, it explains their habit of attacking shipping lanes when they get separated into smaller units.)
(They were organized when we fought them just earlier. That can only mean one thing...)

options.content: Their master has come back to life.

scripts.say: Their... master?
Surely you jest, my darling? That's ridiculous.
There is the folk theory that their fleet is a relic from the past, but...
...They did attack the city where the map for the Fountain of Youth was.
...And they have the means to dispel a storm, like what's said to guard the Fountain.
What if they ARE after it, and intend to take the power it contains?
Whether the legends that surround it are true or not, we need to put a stop to them.
Let us sail for the New World at once, my darling.
The sooner, the better.
The Great Royal Fortune has faced many challenges but still stands firm as she sails into the lonesome night.
Moonlight dyes the jigger topmast a silver color, giving the flying jib almost a snow-white silhouette.
It's a beautiful sight wrapped in tranquility – hardly befitting us seafaring adventurers.
The silence is broken by a shout coming from high up in the crow's nest.
Ahoy! I can see land!
There's land!
The ship's crew – which is, admittedly, just me and a small handful of shipgirls – all immediately gather on the deck.
All of us take turns with the telescope, our gazes focusing in the direction Royal Fortune gestured towards.
With bated breaths, we wait for the moment that land pokes up over the horizon.
It is not land that comes into view, however, but rather a shocking entity.
That isn't land... It's the Echo Fleet!
Flying the Black Wolves' banner, at that. They really have taken the treasure hunters' flag as their own.
That's not all. Judging by their heading, I think they're headed for a New World port.

options.content: How long until they reach it?

scripts.say: Around an hour, I'd say.

options.content: What defenses does that port have?

scripts.say: None that'll arrive before morning, since it lacks the facilities to fully facilitate navigation at night.
Which is to say, it'll fall before sunrise if anyone attacks.

options.content: Then all we can do is to lure the fleet away.

scripts.say: We certainly can lure them away. Driving them back, though? That's another topic~
We need reinforcements, my darling. Say, while we keep them busy, could you do something for me~?
Engaging the Echo Fleet was always going to be a steep uphill battle, even if only as a distraction to lure them away from the port.
It's already clear that they can't be reasoned with. The only way to get their attention is with an exchange of cannon fire.
On one side, Mary's team fights with the fury of a tornado. On the other, São Martinho fights relentlessly on the frontlines.
Onward! Onward! The golden light's banner shall never fall!
Fire! Fire! The golden light's glory shall never wane!
Resound and applaud! The golden light's hymn shall never stop!
The enemy attacks come in violent waves, but São Martinho does not flinch. Her bravery shines like a star in the dark night.
They're tough, I'll give them that...
Thank god we have São Martinho on our side.
She's led the surrounding Echo Fleets away from the shoreline. We should retreat now.
Nuh-uh. Now is not a good time.
They'd have chewed us up already if São Martinho hadn't gone in first.
Showing them our backs now would be suicide.
