Yes. It was all quite shocking.
So, I suppose that the Commander indeed was "forced to leave," if you want to put it that way.
For the record, I had absolutely nothing to do with these skelebeasts that attacked out of nowhere.
If I could control them or somesuch, I wouldn't have had to put myself in such danger back in the Sleeping Sea, would I?
There is one thing I haven't told you before, though.
The true reason as to why the Church came to these islands isn't to search the ruins or anything of that nature.
We have received intelligence that a Goddess-level ancient relic is hidden on Islas de Libertád. What we're here to do is to retrieve it.
Oh, and the appearance of the skelebeasts has only lent even more credibility to our intelligence.
They are drawn to the Goddess-level relic on these islands, just as they were drawn to the Goddess's central unit in the Sleeping Sea.
"Goddess-level"? You're saying there's something here that's on par with it?
That I am. We suspect that a fragment of the Goddess lies out here.
Well, Monsters DID appear in Mar del Demonios before you even got here...
Dolphin also said there's some super-duper ridiculous treasure somewhere around here...
Given that, it does all add up.
Do you believe me now? I never had any evil intent to begin with.
Ahaha... Guess my hunch was way off. Sorry!
No, no, I'm just glad that we cleared up this misunderstanding.
There's a chance that the treasure Dolphin spoke of is the same one we're after. You wouldn't already happen to know where it is, would you?
If we're able to seal that relic away, the skelebeasts will have nothing to stick around for, and they'll scatter.
We've got it down to a few potential locations, but nothing more than that.
Well, since we're still under attack, even being able to narrow down our search radius would help a lot.
Just leave the rest to the Church and our secret arts.
Time waits for no one, so let's go treasure-hunting, shall we?

Following her search from several days ago, Dolphin had been able to pin down the "mindblowing treasure" to one of three locations – the ancient temple on the main island, a metallic cave on Isla Segunda, and the great lighthouse on Isla Tercera.
Royal Fortune decided to bring Ganj-i-Sawai to the main island, where the ruins were preserved the best.
On the way there, as they were passing by the Nebula Guardians' temporary base...
Royal Fortune, Ganj-i-Sawai, I thank you for your help.
We owe it to you that we made it without sustaining major casualties.
We're all allies here, so it's what anyone would've done.
Yeah. We're friends, so don't sweat it.
Friends, you say...
You're right. From now on, I consider you to be my friends.
Then, as friends, I will give you some advice.
Don't be lulled into a false sense of security. These islands still face danger.
Our supplies are limited. The monsters may be repelled for the time being, but we cannot hole up here forever.
We ought to prepare a breakthrough assault before supplies run out and morale drops.
Right! As it so happens, Ganj-i-Sawai and I were just looking for a way to repel them.
If it doesn't work out, I'll tell Anne we need to break through the siege.
The Nebula Guardians will take the vanguard.
I'll do everything in my power.
But, if it comes to plan B, I'm counting on you.
Of course. I will prepare for the eventuality of a battle.
The two bade goodbye to the Nebula Guardian, then headed toward Queen Anne's Revenge.
Once she was informed of the Church's plans, she took her treasure map and went along on their treasure hunt.
They searched every nook and cranny of the ancient temple. Ganj-i-Sawai and Dolphin even found a couple of hidden chambers along the way.
However, the ancient relic they were looking for was nowhere to be found.
*sigh*... It seems the temple was a bust.
As one would expect, you won't find a miracle on your very first attempt...
We can't give up already! There's the metallic cave to check out next!
Let's save that for tomorrow. I'm sure we're all exhausted after our battles earlier today.
Pearl and I will fine-tune our secret arts, and hopefully raise their efficiency a bit.
I have to agree. They won't breach our defences anytime soon.
Alright, then how about we all stop by our base and have supper?
I stocked up on loads and loads of supplies before coming here! We've got curry from Crownpolis to go around!
Just bring some ingredients you want to add, and we'll be good!
See you all there!
Om, nom, nom...
Come again? Islas de Libertád?
It was evening, and the members of Tempesta were feasting on a lavish supper in their grand villa whilst sharing rumors.
Yeah. Heard the Vengeful Queen's discovered some unclaimed isles past Mar del Demonios.
They named 'em Islas de Libertád and made them their own. What do you think happened after?
Did they start settling the isles, perchance?
Did they find some ludicrous treasure that set them up for life?
Not even sort of close. What they did was send invitations to people across the world. "Seekers of liberty, come and let us explore these ruins together."
Ohhh. What an interesting choice! They sound like a decent lot!
My, what a bold proclamation. Such perfectly preserved ruins are bound to attract countless people.
It will give a tremendous reputation boost to the Vengeful Queen Fleet as well.
You bet. Crazy to think there are still unclaimed islands in this day and age.
This might just stir up a wave of sailing adventures around the world!
*knock knock knock*
Ooh! Smells yummy! Seems I came at a good time!
If it isn't Tempesta's own adorable little messenger! Yes, this is a good time! Come and dig in!
We made whale meat roasted with curry from Crownpolis!
Whale... curry? No! No thank you!
She insisted on it, I'm afraid.
It's not about the whale meat, it's about it being curry made with spices from Crownpolis! They were a right pain in the bum to procure, I'll have you know!
Tonight, it's whale meat, and tomorrow, it'll be shark meat! The day after that, maybe we'll do octopus! It'll all be scrumptious!
Oh, uh... Sure it'll be! They all sound yummy! But I'll still have to pass!
Right, I nearly forgot – what brings you here? Whydah ask you to deliver a message?
No, nothing like that. I'm just here to deliver this invitation from the Vengeful Queen.
Wait, from them? Blimey, could it be...
Let me see!
A-ha! It IS what I thought!
Come on, share it with the class. What does it say?
Exactly what you told us a minute ago. The Vengeful Queen lot has invited us to a treasure hunt on Islas de Libertád!
It's a direct invitation, no less! Seems we've made quite a name for ourselves, mateys!
Hell yeah. So, when do we set off?
Before anything else, you need to call Whydah back to–
Uh, I don't think we'll need to! She said it's too far away and it'd be such a pain, so she won't come!
Sounds like she's telling us not to disturb her, whatever we do...
Alright! Then contact São Martinho and Adventure Galley instead.
Tell them to meet us at Limestone Island, the last supply stop on the way to Mar del Demonios. Once you've given them the message, go there and wait.
Aye aye! I'll be off, then!
Hey, no need to rush. Sit down with us and have some of this whale curry!
Uh... oh...
Late was the hour, and the skelebeasts' onslaught still continued.
Amidst the roaring of the ancient battery's cannons, Royal Fortune clutched her wooden compass as she dreamed a dream.
Tranquil seas. A calm beach. The breeze was mild, and the sunlight was warming in this lovely dream.
Such a peaceful dream... Well, guess that's pretty nice!
As long as you ignore how there's a battle going on in reality...
Royal Fortune walked down the beach, feeling the invigorating waves while she picked some coconuts.
Mmm! So sweet!
I love dreams with flavours! Would be even better if I had some good nosh, but hey.
Hm? What the...?
She suddenly realized that her wooden compass was faintly glowing.
The light converged on the tip of the "needle," pointing in a certain direction.
Whoa! It's glowing!
Wait, this is a dream, so how come it's glowing?!
Oh! Maybe if I follow it...
She turned in the direction indicated by the compass and broke into a sprint.
After running for a while, she eventually came across someone who was sleeping in a beach chair.
Zzzzz...
HUH?!
W-wait...
Commander?!
...Where am I?
When I come to, I'm on a beach for some reason.
Before I fell asleep... Right, I saw that compass glowing on the bookshelf.
Did the compass beckon me into this dream?
That voice I just heard was oddly familiar, too.
By the time I recognize the voice, Royal Fortune has already run over to me.
Waaaah! Commander, it's really yooou!
I haven't seen you in so long! I never dreamed I'd see you in... well, a dream!
The girl calling out to me is none other than Royal Fortune, captain of the Tempesta fleet.
It has been a while... Did the light of the compass lead you here, too?
Wait, but it's in my possession now. How did you come here, then?
Huh? You've got the compass?!
Bloody hell, that's brilliant news! With the compass, you can come visit me any time!
As for how I came here myself... Heh, you were right. The compass lit the way!
Did you find another one for yourself?
Not even. I chiselled it from wood myself!
Behold!
She proudly produces a wooden compass and waves it around in my face.
See? Perfect, ain't it?
Hmm... If I squint really hard, it's kind of similar, sure.
Hmph! You don't think it's similar at all! Forget how it looks, though – what matters is that it works!
I've got a lot of questions for you, and I'd wager you have a few for me, too.
We used this opportunity to exchange a bounty of information.
Royal Fortune and I discussed how the flow of time differed between worlds and how a fleet back at home encountered the treasure hunters.
She divulged the details of Tempesta's treasure hunt in Islas de Libertád and their hairy encounter with wreckage skelebeasts.
That included the fact that the Church of the Goddess was searching for a Goddess-level ancient relic, of course.
Looking back, I disappeared in the middle of eating with Ganj-i-Sawai. Did she say anything about that?
Yeah, she did! I was really suspicious about it, but she convinced me when she shared her side of the story.
Don't tell me... Was she the culprit after all?!
Well, I mean... I won't say no to that, but... Forget it. It's not important right now.
I have something I want to give you.
Whoa. Terminal?!
It's all yours. When I first saw the compass glow, I decided I should take it along in case it was an omen of things to come.
I'm kinda surprised I was able to bring it into the dream.
There isn't much material help I can offer, but if you're searching for Siren ruins, it may come in handy.
The waves turn quiet, and the world around us begins to dissolve.
Looks like the dream is ending.
Guess so...
I'd be happy to take Terminal along. Bet it'll be a great help!
And you, Commander? Don't undersell yourself – you might be helpful, too.
How do you reckon?
If I can take Terminal with me, then who says I can't take you, too?
Kinda like... THIS!
She rushes over and pulls me into a bear hug.
If I hold you tight enough, maybe you'll still be there when I wake up...
My vision turns blank white as she whispers into my ear.
When the light dissipated, Royal Fortune awakened in bed.
Mmnh... Am I awake?
Commander?!
She shot up, nearly sending Terminal flying in the process.
However, nobody else was there.
Not here, huh...
Damn shame... Who knows when I'll see you again?
After that complaint, she slapped herself in the cheeks a few times.
Cheer up, you twit! At least the Commander sent you back with Terminal!
You're exploring the metallic cave and the lighthouse today. Treasures abound, and they WILL be mindblowing!
While she gathered personnel and prepared for the day's adventure, a commotion happened to break out at the main island's gathering place.
Yesterday's sudden crisis had led to an impressive display of teamwork among the isles's fleets.
However, the coming of a new day made them restless and rowdy once again.
Fights broke out over patrol schedules, distrust over the Nebula Guardians and the Church of the Goddess, and perceived unfairness in resource allocation.

Fortunately, Queen Anne's Revenge was well prepared for this. She resolved these issues swiftly. Armed with overwhelming support from the various fleets, she established a set of provisional regulations for Islas de Libertád.
Once all was settled, she left them and set sail for Isla Segunda with the Tempesta and Church of the Goddess fleets in search of the day's treasure.
Sheer rock cliffs towered a hundred meters high, forming a natural barrier around the second island.
However, the treasure map opened the way inside for the well-equipped explorers, revealing its secrets.
The island's interior was ancient ruins, and the rock walls were a mere facade that concealed them.
Labyrinthine passages stretched in all directions, even to the clifftops above and depths below. That explained half of why Queen Anne's Revenge had dubbed this place the metallic "cave."
Following a preliminary investigation of the area above, we've managed to find some valuable supplies.
This is where I found the star map drawn on the invitation – the Resonant Star Chart.
It was after I discovered these items resembling entry tickets that I thought to send the invitation.
Huh? I thought they came from the ancient temple on the main island!
Well, you were wrong. My theory is that this cave was used as a warehouse.
Unfortunately, even I don't know if it conceals any hidden rooms like the ancient temple.
That's a job for the Church's secret arts!
Hah, don't even bother. I have a more efficient solution!
Terminal, scan the cave's structure and discover any hidden passages for us!
Even better, generate a map!
Orders received. Scanning the structure of the immediate area.
Local database detected. Accessing.
Reading stored data.
Data analysis complete. Displaying facility layout of Compiler's Fortress III's Central Corridor, Section T-02.
All except for Royal Fortune watched on in slack-jawed surprise as a map of the area was projected in mid-air.
Anne, did you draw a map last time you came here? Let's compare them for differences!
Upon comparing the two maps, the group discovered several differences between them.
With Terminal's help, they took a quick tour of all the hidden rooms.
They found veritable troves of ancient relics, though their uses were unclear at best.

Their greatest rewards, however, were a bounty of high-quality ancient alloys and ancient crystals – objects that could power the Polises' walls, Temples of the Goddess, and virtually all of the ancient ruins sites in Islas de Libertád.
And though by accident, Dolphin managed to deploy the massive cannons hidden in the rock walls, bolstering the island's defenses.
However, the Goddess-level relic that Ganj-i-Sawai spoke of was nowhere to be found.
This left just one final place to be searched.
Later that night, after an exhausting day of searching the metallic cave, Royal Fortune took her wooden compass in hand and drifted off to dreamland, hopes high in her heart.
In an endless stretch of ocean, rows of tightly-packed Echo Fleet ships stood in line.
This enemy, once thought invincible, had now been forced into a desperate situation.
I am... Compiler...
No... I am a ▇▇▇▇▇!
You invaded the ▇▇▇▇▇'s system and altered my ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇'s memory...
Who in the world are you?!
Up in the heavens hung a ball of light that glowed even brighter than the sun.
Inside the light were practically countless, giant eyes that stared down at all the threats below with cold indifference.
As the voice's words grew increasingly unintelligible, the ball of light in the sky suddenly ballooned.
The world was enveloped in light.
*pant*... *pant*... What the hell was that dream?! That freaked me out!
Awoken by sheer shock, Royal Fortune almost dropped her wooden compass.
That little one called herself "Compiler," didn't she?
But... isn't the Goddess a machine?
And what was that ball of light?
It kinda reminds me of the runes the Federation uses in the Blessing for the Guardian...
But most importantly, why the hell did I dream about it?!
Oh no... All I wanted was to grow my fleet, sail the seven seas, and go on all the adventures I wanted...
Commander, please... Please protect me from getting dragged into this weird stuff from ancient times!
Royal Fortune somehow fired herself up, and went to the great lighthouse on Isla Tercera.
En route there, she overheard people talking about the Nebula Guardians proactively wiping out the enemy in nearby waters.
These heroics sparked a fighting spirit in many of the fleets. Morale on the islands was high, despite them now being three days into a siege.
Royal Fortune and company passed through the defensive barrier, and arrived at the foot of the lighthouse.
So this is the great lighthouse. What a mysterious aura it exudes.
This is where I sensed it was most likely we'd find a mindblowing treasure!
We still don't know how to get up it, though.
Our original plan was to launch me to the top with a cannon so I could lower a rope for the rest of you, but, well...
That's when the skelebeasts attacked, and we never got the chance to try it.
Heh! Now we have Terminal, and we don't need no cannon or rope!
Terminal, open the door!
Her trusty companion did not let them down.
After just a quick scan, Terminal activated a set of hidden doors, allowing the group to search the lighthouse's interior.
To their surprise, however, there was absolutely nothing inside it except for a spiral staircase leading upward.
Hmm... We're almost at the top, yet we've not found a thing.
Dolphin, is your treasure sense tingling?
Nuh-uh. I think the treasure's higher up!
My Church arts are pointing further upward as well...
Therefore, what we're looking for must be at the top of the lighthouse!
And so, the group arrived at the summit of the lighthouse.
They found no lamp there in the center, only a pillar made of a black, metallic material.
The first to begin inspecting it were none other than the two envoys from the Church of the Goddess.
"O Goddess, lend us your wisdom to see through this mystery..."
Ganj-i-Sawai scooped out a handful of liquid flame from a lantern she had brought, smearing it on Pearl's forehead and palms.
Pearl then set her sights on a particular spot of the pillar and gently touched it with her left hand.
The pillar let out a buzzing sound.
Countless metallic plates began to shift up and down and split apart, beginning from the spot that she touched.
They were like the throbbing scales of some enormous beast made of steel. Through the cracks, a red light slipped in and out of view.
"O Goddess, may your light illuminate the path..."
Ganj-i-Sawai took out another handful of flame from the lantern, this time applying it to Pearl's staff.
Then, Pearl held the staff up, and firmly struck the spot she had touched with her hand.
The strike from the staff made the metallic plates vanish instantly in a burst of flame, revealing an object hidden within the pillar.
What the...
A metallic ball?
Oh! This is it! The mindblowing treasure!
Compiler's Eyes...
Oh no! Ladies, look out!
With the wall of metal gone, the metallic sphere so-named "Compiler's Eyes" lay itself bare.
Without any warning, it shot out a dazzling beam of light toward the sky.
The beam dispelled the abnormal night sky hanging above Islas de Libertád. This also ignited a ferociousness within the blocked-out skelebeasts.
Ah! The night-sky barrier's gone!
Oh no! Look! The skelebeasts have all gone mental and are coming for us!
I understand now. The metal pillar of the lighthouse is a device meant to confine Compiler's Eyes.
Its sealing effects were waning after so many years, and that's why the skelebeasts were drawn to it.
Now, with the seal completely undone, they've begun rampaging.
Lyme and São Martinho are still out there, fighting!
They're gonna be surrounded any minute now! We have to hurry and help them!
...I'll call in supporting fire.
We should probably split up. The rest of you, go and help those two. We will stay and prepare a ritual to reseal Compiler's Eyes.
If we're successful, the skelebeasts should be left with no reason to attack this place. They'll be gone before long.
Well, be quick about it! Girls, follow me!
KABOOOM!
Amidst a veritable wave of skelebeasts, Lyme and São Martinho dashed forward with great courage.
This scene... It feels familiar.
Heh. It does.
Without the supporting fire from the island's batteries, this would've been a nightmare.
Not so much anymore.
We have the upper hand. Our opponents may be numerous, but we just have to stay calm and kill them one at a time.
Oooi! Lyyyme! São Martinhooo!
Something's thrown the monsters into a frenzy! We've come to help you get out of here!
Ah, Tempesta. Good timing.
Do you see the Lord-class skelebeast up ahead? Let's cut it down together.
Uh! Sorry if I wasn't clear, but we've come to get you the hell out of here!
There's no time to turn around. Charge it head-on!
What?! Okay, fine!
KABOOOM!
Amidst booming explosions, the colossal Lord-class skelebeast sank beneath the waves.
Following this, the maddened and rampaging other skelebeasts began to gradually settle down. Seeing their leader defeated, they scattered one by one.
It was at this time that the group realized that the light shining from the great lighthouse was gone again.
Phew... Seems Ganj-i-Sawai's sealing ritual worked!
"Sealing ritual"?
Ah, well, basically...
Royal Fortune briefly explained what happened over at the lighthouse.
I see. So it was sealed off.
Okay. Let's head back.
With Compiler's Eyes sealed anew, the skelebeasts that had besieged Islas de Libertád now dispersed.
The strange starry sky hanging over the isles also disappeared along with the veil that once protected them.
However, bright sunlight washed over the islands now, lifting the haze that had hung over them and making them a more comfortable place to live.
With this, danger had finally passed.
After a grand celebration, everyone resumed their daily routines... that is, until Queen Anne's Revenge summoned everyone for a great announcement.
Friends, adventurers in search of freedom, comrades in arms!
location: Islas de Libertád - Main Island's Harbor

scripts.say: On the dawn of our great victory, I must ask you.
Do you remember why you first set out for adventure?
For fame? For fortune? For a life of freedom? For all of these reasons and more, perhaps.
But how did you feel along the way?
All of us seek freedom, not bloodshed, yet the Federation of Polises has continuously oppressed us.
Ever more rules, ever more restrictions. They choose to give us only two options.
We can either be subservient to the Federation of Polises, to be used at their behest and discarded at their convenience...
...Or we can let their rules tighten around our necks like a noose, little by little, and let them wring us for all we're worth.
As for me, I don't like either option.
That's why I chose not to monopolise Islas de Libertád for myself. Why I invited you all to come and share in their bounty.
The results speak for themselves, don't you think?
We are strong. Before our combined might, even hordes of monsters are dust in the wind.
Before our combined might, the Federation of Polises and Church of the Goddess cannot deny us sovereignty!
Yes, we have lost the curtain of stars that guides us as a result of our battle.
But let that symbolise the freedom to make a new path. Let anyone who craves liberty be free to come and join us.
These are Islas de Libertád. Just as I named them, they are a home for all who yearn for freedom from oppression!
And they will become our own Polis. The archipelago of Libertypolis!
Thus, I hereby declare the establishment of Libertypolis, a nation for all adventurers who desire freedom!
All who love liberty and are willing to abide by our laws will be welcomed and honoured as citizens of our free state!
The crowd stirred.
The sailors of Islas de Libertád were naturally overjoyed, but there were others who felt it necessary to speak up – especially Lyme.
Queen Anne's Revenge, have you lost your mind?
The Federation of Polises won't stand for this act, and they certainly won't acknowledge the sovereignty of an illegal Polis.
You're making an enemy of the entire federation, you know.
Then let them be my enemy.
I never asked anyone for permission to establish a free state, least of all the corrupt Federation of Polises.
Since you contributed to our victory, and I consider you a guest for now, I'll let that remark slide.
Of course, you're more than welcome to a reward based on your contributions. Does that sound fair?
Not interested.
If that's all, we'll be leaving now.
Goodbye.
Watch yourselves, sailors of the Vengeful Queen...
As expected, the Nebula Guardians departed without delay. Queen Anne's Revenge then turned her attention to the Church's fleet, who'd watched on in silence.
The Church typically doesn't meddle in inter-Polis affairs.
If the Federation formally acknowledges your sovereignty, then you will naturally become our allies.
If they do not... well, things could take an ugly turn.
Hmm. Well, I won't detain you.
I am well aware of the Church's contributions to the success of our war effort.
Would you like a token of our gratitude before you leave?
I heard you gifted a small island to every fleet that came to the isles. Is that right?
What if you were to offer one to the Church as well?
Building a temple on your land would let us offer direct aid to those in need... and may serve as a useful bargaining tool in the future.
I have to apologise, but as I alluded to before, we only welcome those who love freedom.
That would exclude the clergy of the Church of the Goddess.
You may request something else.
...Ugh. Then I would ask that you allow us to take the ancient relic back to the Church for proper storage and care.
As you're well aware, the seal on the relic must be reinforced regularly, and only the Church can perform the sealing ritual.
If neglected, the seal will eventually weaken and attract monster hordes yet again.
...You considered that a "Goddess-level" relic, didn't you? I understand it's very important to you.
It would only beckon danger in our hands. Take it.
Thank you very much.
Incidentally, about the reward you intended to give the Nebula Guardians... May I deliver it to them in your stead?
They've suffered their fair share of casualties in these past few days' conflict.
Lyme refused out of stubborn pride, but she will be in a very difficult position if she returns home empty-handed.
Well, aren't you just the sweetest? Be my guest. Make them owe you one.
We have no shortage of treasure, so load some up onto your ships before you go.
Thank you. We'll prepare to depart at once.
After successful negotiations with the Church, Queen Anne's Revenge shifted her focus to the Tempesta fleet.
Royal Fortune. Do you support the establishment of Libertypolis?
Huh? Me?
Umm, well, I think everyone knows how the Federation of Polises has treated you.
They've only gotten more overbearing, so it's good to have a safe haven like this.
But, you know, managing a city-state takes more than just passion...
Of course. That's why I intend to craft our laws based on the Tempesta code.
Say what?!
For people who love freedom, all we need is a basic level of common understanding and rules. Isn't that right, everyone?
The crowd cheered in response.
Let's drink the night away, everyone!
To the birth of Libertypolis! Cheers!
Ooh... Ch-cheers!
Cheers!
Whatever the future may hold, on this day, Islas de Libertád were all feast and revelry.
The establishment of Libertypolis would mark the first chapter of a new age in Federation history.

sequence: Tempesta and Islas de Libertád - The End?

scripts.say: A shipgirl was performing a ceremonial dance in a vast room.

scripts.factiontag: The Priest of Wind and Rain
scripts.say: "O Goddess, let this prayer carry you to a safe place."
As the light withdrew, Ganj-i-Sawai's dance came to a stop.
So, too, did the mysterious ritual she was conducting.

scripts.factiontag: The Priest of Wind and Rain
scripts.say: We have the eyes that discern... All that's left are the wings that give shape.
The area revealed by the Goddess mainframe is dangerous.

scripts.factiontag: The Priest of Wind and Rain
scripts.say: I know, I know...

scripts.factiontag: The Priest of Wind and Rain
scripts.say: Our next move demands a more thorough plan.

scripts.factiontag: The Priest of Wind and Rain
scripts.say: With the eyes that discern, creating the ideal plan should be an easy feat.

scripts.factiontag: The Priest of Wind and Rain
scripts.say: Something elaborate, yet foolproof...

scripts.factiontag: The Priest of Wind and Rain
scripts.say: No matter what, the Goddess must make her return.

scripts.factiontag: The Priest of Wind and Rain
scripts.say: Otherwise, our future holds only death and destruction.
Yes.
After returning home from Islas de Libertád, Tempesta got to work moving.
Tempesta Island...
Heheh... Our own island... Tempesta Island!
Terminal... *sniffle*... Terminal, you're finally home...
I'm never letting you out of my sight again!
With a whole island to ourselves, we can build whatever we want.
Maybe I'll make a luxurious underwater suite for Argo.
...We still can't abandon this trading post, but if people flock to Islas de Libertád, then business will boom, too...
What if we move HQ over there?
Just a what-if, since we don't know how the Federation will react.
Meh... We can only take things one step at a time. First things first, we set up a trading post on Tempesta Island...
Everyone dreamed of the future, some excited and some anxious.
Just then, there was a knock at the door. Dolphin had returned with news from afar.
So Galley says the Federation of Polises is taking action?
Yep! The Federation Council is gathering representatives from every Polis to a big meeting in Crownpolis!
Galley's going with the representative of Stellapolis. She said not to move to Islas de Libertád until we know what the Federation's plans are!
Ugh... Can't they just get over it?
They're using the illegal establishment of a Polis as an excuse, but they really just want the land and ruins there...
But hasn't Vengeful Queen already taken over the islands' defensive facilities?
Even the Federation of Polises has to baulk at those huge cannons...
Hmm... Whatever the case, we're already in an alliance with Vengeful Queen. There's no ignoring this now.
I'm going to Crownpolis myself! You all take a break at Limestone Island and wait for word from me!
When the light fades, I see my bedroom ceiling again.
Guess it couldn't be that easy, Royal Fortune.
Still feeling her lingering warmth, I look around my room.
The compass has stopped glowing, and Terminal is gone.
At least I managed to deliver Terminal to her. Hopefully that will give Tempesta the extra boost they need to make it out of danger.
All I can do now is pray.
The Virtual Tower acting up, people constantly flooding in and out from other worlds, and now Tempesta...
If our world has such a thing as a boundary, then it must be getting weaker by the day.
DOS...
...Fine by me. If danger comes, then we'll stand and fight it.
There's no point in agonizing over things that might never happen. Gotta live in the moment.
Time to wash my face, eat breakfast... and get to work.

sequence: Tempesta and Islas de Libertád - The End

scripts.say: This wasn't Royal Fortune's first rodeo. She didn't expect this adventure into ancient ruins to go without a hitch.
location: Fleet Meeting Spot - Late at Night

scripts.say: As such, she decided to call in her fleetmates who were operating elsewhere and spend several days stocking up on all the supplies and weapons that she could.
And not only that...
What... are you doing?
Golden Hind gave a look of confusion to Royal Fortune, who was focused on carving a piece of wood.
I lost my compass, remember? It's made it a pain in the arse to travel between our two worlds.
Sometimes our method for entering the storm works, and sometimes it doesn't.
That's when I got an idea: Since I don't have a compass, why not just make another?
Check it out! Can't tell it apart from my last one, eh?
Royal Fortune showed her freshly carved wooden compass to Golden Hind.
I can't say I saw your last one, but even so, isn't this a little too crude?
Oi! I worked really hard on this!
Maybe it's not perfect, but it at least generally LOOKS like a compass!
Tell you what – let's give this baby a trial run and see how she works!
Royal Fortune blew off the wood shavings stuck to the compass, placed it on the table, and then put her hands together and said a prayer.
Doesn't seem like that did anything.
Yeah... Should've figured it wouldn't be that easy.
Oh well! You never know – it might start working out of nowhere.
Anyway, it's getting late. You should hit the hay. We've got loads of shopping ahead of us tomorrow!
After three days of preparations, the well-stocked Tempesta fleet finally departed on a course toward Islas de Libertád.
The winds on their route were gentle, and the skies were fair and clear.
They sailed for 10 days without incident, and eventually reached their last stop before entering the sea of Mar del Demonios, where she and her companions would meet up – Limestone Island.
They anchored their vessels and headed for a tavern on the island. There, they decided to gather intel whilst waiting for their fellow members.
Once they'd conducted a bit of sleuthing, a piece of concerning information reached their ears.
Shhh. Did you hear the rumors about Mar del Demonios?
They say that three fleets have already come back with heavy losses. No wonder we saw so many battered and bruised ships at the docks...
Mhm. Also, while I was asking around, the tavern owner warned me to stay away from Mar del Demonios.
The surviving crewmates even said they not only got caught in the most terrible weather, but also that they were attacked by sea monsters.
As much as I have faith in our fleet, the idea that Islas de Libertád may very well be a trap is giving me second thoughts.
Dammit... Guess they don't call it Mar del Demonios, the "Sea of Demons", for nothing.
Are you saying someone's gone and used the Vengeful Queen's name to lure us into a trap?

Can't think of anyone who'd have reason to do that... Even the Federation of Polises would have to consider the ramifications. They didn't invite just established fleets, but indie adventurers as well.
Also, if sea monsters show up and attack out of nowhere, isn't that more proof that Islas de Libertád are real, if anything?
I mean, remember the skelebeasts and the Goddess's central unit from that time we went to the Sleeping Sea?
If there are loads and loads of ancient ruins around Islas de Libertád, that might explain why there are sea monsters around here.
We've still got time, so why don't we verify it with the survivors?
Yeah, good idea. Even better if they can confirm they were skelebeasts, and if so, what kind!
Sunset arrived, and the group went back to the tavern one by one.
Although they failed to get any notable information, they did meet up with Dolphin, who had just arrived.
Captain! It's me! I'm here!
Brilliant of you to show up! Why is it just you, though? Where are the others?
Adventure Galley was busy promoting the Star Wayfinders in Stellapolis, so she couldn't come.
Same with São Martinho. Also, they told me to pass on a message: "The Nebula Guardians seem interested in Islas de Libertád, and have some sort of plan for it."
Also, "Try to steer clear of them." That's all!
Nebula Guardians meddling in stuff. Must be a day ending in Y.
Whatever. The rule is first-come, first-served with unclaimed islands, AND we've already been invited to a treasure hunt.
We'd be bonkers to sit this one out!
Crew, rest up well tonight! We're setting off tomorrow!
As the curtain of night fell, so too did raindrops begin to fall on the fleet.
Royal Fortune was in her lavish bed aboard her own vessel, thinking to herself.
Mar del Demonios... Named such because it's home to demons who lure in sailors with their songs, then drown them.
I can't believe those are actually real... Well, I haven't seen one in the past two days, but still.
And to think that Vengeful Queen lot found a bunch of new islands in a place like this.
"Let the stars guide you," eh...
She raised the written invitation with her hand, holding it in front of her dim lamplight.
The light suddenly illuminated a star map drawn onto the invitation, revealing a course that could bring them to their destination safely.
Such intricate craftsmanship... Doesn't look like something her crew could produce.
Maybe they made it with something they found in the ruins?
...Bah. No use thinking about it. I'll find out when I ask them myself. Time to sleep!
Fierce winds and violent waves struck the vessels in the fleet. Tempesta's ships were at risk of sinking at any moment.
What the–?!
Oi! Mary! Golden Hind! What the bloody hell is going on?!
Captain, we're under attack by a group of skelebeasts!
And things aren't looking great. We may have to abandon ship.
Bail out! Bail ooout!
Nooooo!
Not my beloved shiiiiip!
NOT MY BELOVED SHIP!
Royal Fortune awoke in her nice bed, dim light illuminating her cabin.
Just... Just a nightmare? Damn ill-boding, ever for a nightmare...
Doubt I'll be getting any more sleep tonight...
She took out her wooden compass from underneath her pillow, pressed it between her palms, and offered a prayer.
Commander, please protect me so I can finish this treasure hunt safely, and let my ship go unscathed...
Okay... That should do. Time for an early morning patrol!
Six hours later, it was eight in the morning of their third day in Mar del Demonios. Despite this, the sun had yet to rise.
Something's not right. It's cloudy, but it shouldn't be THIS dark.
Hell, I didn't even realize it was morning 'til I looked at the clock.
Yeah, blimey. Has Mar del Demonios always been like this?
Long ago, I went through this place a few times with some merchant ships, and it certainly wasn't this gloomy then.
Means it's probably got something to do with the Vengeful Queen lot, then. We're lucky the rain's still only a drizzle, and there've been no storms or sea monsters yet.
Since we're in the clear for now, let's have some nosh!
Today, we're having curry with–
I've got cod! Freshly caught!
Brilliant! Cod with curry it is!
Bleh...
The time was two in the afternoon. The rain had stopped, the clouds had cleared, and the stars were brightly shining on their course.
Hang on, why are the North Star and the Southern Cross visible at the same time? Shouldn't that be impossible?!
This night sky doesn't sit right with me...
Oh! I KNEW the star map in the invitation looked odd!
I thought it might've just been artistic flair at first. Here we are, looking at those same unusual constellations!
Things're getting weirder and weirder. Should we keep sailing?
Seems a whole lot likelier now that we'll run into trouble.
Of course we'll keep sailing!
We've not run into any sea monsters yet, despite all the weird stuff. I don't know about you, but I don't want to be known as a coward who scurried off home already.
Besides, think of the treasures just out of our reach. The crew of the Vengeful Queen are waiting for us!
Another half a day went by, and as midnight rolled around, the outline of an island finally appeared on the horizon.
Captain! I see land!
Attention, ship to our bow! You are about to enter the waters of Islas de Libertád!
I am Royal James, member of the Vengeful Queen Fleet! State your names!
Once the group spotted the island, a warship that had been standing by in the area quickly caught notice of them.
I am Royal Fortune with Tempesta! We came here on an invitation from you!
Oh! Royal Fortune? And you're with Tempesta?
Well, that changes things! Welcome to Islas de Libertád!
I've been waiting for ages out here, and you're the first group that's ever shown up!
I was starting to get worried that there was something wrong with the invitation, and nobody would come here!
Our captain, Queen Anne's Revenge, is waiting for you! Follow me!
Tempesta's fleet followed Royal James, passing by a few unusually shaped islets while avoiding dangerous reefs along the way. Eventually, they reached the pier of an especially large island.
Anne, I've brought Tempesta with me!
Ah. You must be Royal Fortune. Your name's been knocking about lately, and I was hoping to meet you.
Welcome to Islas de Libertád. Think of it as our base, and make yourself at home.
Once they arrived at the pier, the group was welcomed by Queen Anne's Revenge, the captain of the Vengeful Queen Fleet.
After exchanging a few brief words with them, Royal Fortune began surveying the island before her.
I've seen ancient ruins before, but these are something else. They're so much bigger and better preserved.
Remarkable, isn't it?
From finding the treasure map that led us here to making the journey itself, it was hellish to get to this place.
These ruins are enormous, and exploring them just by ourselves would be too dangerous and too big a faff. That's why I sent out those invitations.
But, I sent them three months ago. Three whole bloody months...
And in all that time, you're the only ones who came here! I don't believe it – I really don't!
Well, it's not that nobody else TRIED, it's that... none of them made it here.
Come again? What do you mean?
Royal Fortune relayed the things that they learned on Limestone Island.
...Sea monsters? Yes, I suppose your run-of-the-mill fleets and adventurers don't stand a chance against those.
You know, I included a safe route in the invitation so people wouldn't be scared off by the weird night sky. Some good that did, I suppose.
Right, going out on a limb here – the stars looking odd had something to do with you, but the sea monsters didn't?
Kind of?
Let me explain. The treasure map I got supposedly also functions as a key. Using it will let you open a path to the main island's ancient temple.
Well, we did that, and when we did, the sky got strange all of a sudden. I suspect it's some sort of device meant to camouflage these isles.
By the way, by "main island," I mean the one we're on. It's the largest, and located in the centre, so it makes sense.
It's also my first suggestion for a treasure hunt. The buildings are preserved the best here.
As for the "ancient temple," I'm referring to the giant structure up on the mountain over there. I presume you can see it.
If you're wondering about the cannons and the defences next to it, those have been activated.
There should be no shortage of unexplored areas on the island I could activate with my treasure map, but I haven't gotten to them yet.
Queen Anne's Revenge pointed to the various landmarks and explained them one by one.
Besides the main island, there are four large-to-medium-sized islands and another, oh, 214 islets in unusual shapes.
There are ruins on those as well, but the further out you go, the more deteriorated they get.
I doubt they were always like this. If I had to hazard a guess, they got destroyed in a battle long ago.
214 islets... You've really done the maths.
We were bored out of our minds while waiting for others to come!
And it's all because of those darn sea monsters! They weren't there when we first got here! What made them crawl out of the depths all of a sudden?
You've not seen any sea monsters this whole time?
Not a single one. It's been graveyard-quiet around here for the three months we've been here.
What about you? Did you do in a load of sea nasties on your way here?
No. We didn't run into a single one either. Maybe we got lucky?
Strange. I suppose we'll never know.
Since you managed to make it, others should be able to as well. I say we wait a little longer.
Ah, right, I'll give you an islet as a present.
...You what, mate?
Pick any islet you want – excluding the main one and the comparatively larger four – and it's yours.
Make it your base, or do anything you like with it. I don't mind.
You're GIVING us an islet? Blimey, that's generous!
We can't hoard them all when there are this many. Might as well give them away.
I'll be giving another to whichever fleet makes it here next.
They're expecting a treasure hunt, and I wasn't kidding when I said there was one.
I will lead the exploration of the five largest islands. Anything you find on the smaller ones belongs to whoever owns it.
Everyone is free to explore, and whatever treasures you may find, our fleet won't start a barney over it.
You first pick an island, then you go look for treasure on it! It's fun in that it's almost like playing the lottery!
Yeah! That DOES sound like a lot of fun!
I, uh... don't really know what you should say when you're suddenly gifted an island...
Anyway, cheers!
From now on, you're all close friends of ours!
Sometime later...
location: Aboard the Great Royal Fortune - Meeting Room

scripts.say: Hmm... While I do trust those girls, we've only just arrived in this place. We haven't explored the area yet, and can't choose an islet until tomorrow.
Spending the night on land seems kinda risky, so I suggest we stay on our ships tonight!
A prudent decision. Spending the night aboard our ships will also let us respond more quickly in the event that something happens.
Mary, would you be a dear and station your pet near our fleet to keep watch?
Sure thing. I'll do that!
That's meeting adjourned, then! Get yourselves some rest!
Dolphin, I remember you've always wanted to feed Argo. Why don't we do it together?
Just a minute! I'm almost done drawing!
Whatcha drawing? A map or something?
Yep! A map of Islas de Libertád!
It's mostly blank since I haven't had much time, but I'm gonna fill the whole thing in later!
Ever since we got here, I've gotten this feeling like there's some super-duper valuable treasure hidden here!
I've just got to find it!
It was the next day. While Tempesta was looking around Islas de Libertád, another group was off in Mar del Demonios...
KABOOOM!
Ahahahaha! Got another one of 'em!
Right stupid, those skelebeasts are! Tryin' to steal MY bloody ship!
You make it sound like we're winning, when the truth is we're being chased.
Heh! Because we're treasure hunters who go with the wind, lassie! Not prats who tackle the enemy head-on!
Took care of 'em all to our bow! How's it goin' with 'em to our stern?
They've been dealt with. That was the last skelebeast just now. We've shaken them off.
Whew... This course has been bustin' our arses, eh? Been fightin' from dawn 'til dusk now!
...Hang on. Something isn't right.
Look at the clock. It's still morning, so how come we can see the stars?
Whuh? Damn, you're right!
Ya reckon this has got somethin' do with Islas de Libertád?
The odds are extremely high, yes. Remember when we went through a storm and found the Skynexus Tower?
Then, just as now, the space around us changed drastically when we entered it.
Therefore, I'm pretty sure the Islas de Libertád ruins are the real deal.
Also, look at these constellations. Don't they match up perfectly with the strange star map in the invitation?
Bloody hell, you're right! The star map's gotta be for showin' the right course through this place!
Now things're gettin' interesting, ain't they!
Whaddya think'll happen if we go off-course?
I don't know, but let's not find out.
Hahaha! Yeah, figures.
Startin' to seem like that Vengeful Queen lot got their hands on the discovery of the year, dunnit?
Onward! Full speed toward Islas de Libertád!

sequence:
Hidden Charm

<size=45>1 A Girl Without a History</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Good morning, Commander.
I'm Suruga. Starting today, I will serve the role of your secretary.
Suruga entered my office and gave a brief introduction. My first impressions were that she's quite dignified, but also standoffish.
I felt her watchful gaze analyzing me. It was a little... unnerving.
If you don't mind... I'd like to ask a question right off the bat.
"Sure. What are you wondering?"
Why'd you appoint me as your secretary? Why me of all people?
That was a complicated question. I debated whether or not to answer it...
*sigh*... Really? Is this how you do things around here?
She breathed a deep sigh which took me by surprise. I worried if I'd offended her, and wondered what I should've said instead.
See, what you SHOULD have said is...
She continued before I could say anything, phrasing it like she'd read my mind. I withheld comment as she took a deep breath, preparing to elaborate.

(Ugh! It's so obvious why I was picked for this job! "Because the commander knows you," you might think, and you'd be totally wrong! The answer is: blueprint ship bias! And that's despite the fact I'm nowhere near the level of a PR, let alone a DR!)

(I never even asked for this position! It makes me stick out like a lit Christmas tree at night! All I want is to quietly do my job and go unnoticed! Is that so much to ask for?! God, I'm so close to having a nervous breakdown right here and now...)
...On second thought, never mind I said anything.
A few seconds passed without a word from Suruga, and yet somehow, I had this feeling like she'd just roasted me to a crisp.
Let's get back on track. What's on the agenda today?
Her tone of voice changed noticeably. I took it to mean she'd had a change of heart.
I can perform any task you need done. Within reason.
She spoke with a sense of great gravitas that meant to reassure me, but at the same time, I sensed there may be some workplace friction between me and her before long.

sequence:
Hidden Charm

<size=45>2 What's on Suruga's Mind</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Work was progressing smoothly, in no small part thanks to Suruga.
Let's see...
Hmm... Hm.
Every now and then she'd mutter a few words to herself, but beyond that, she did her job in total silence. In that regard, there was nothing to complain about.
However, not everything was perfect. The mood in the room was just as tense as when we started. I didn't know what was going through her mind.
I've completed the task you assigned me, Commander.
"Good to hear. You did a great job."
What's next? I can see there's a lot of work on the back burner. Shall I take care of some of it?
"It's all right. You don't need to concern yourself with these particular tasks."
Uh-huh. I see... Do I take that to mean you're reluctant to assign me any important work?
That wasn't at all how I meant it. There was some hostility in her tone, and her question put me on the spot.
I answered not with words, but with a nervous gaze, hoping she'd understand.
(Oh no... Way to go, Suruga. You couldn't have made that more passive-aggressive even if you tried.)
That wasn't at all how I meant it. There was some hostility in her tone, and her question put me on the spot.
(Just from looking at her, all signs point towards me having offended her in some way.)
(I'll bet the commander's furious with me... Which is a normal reaction to that attitude I just put on...)
(If it's only going to get worse from here, it's time to reconsider the whole thing...)
Maybe I should resign as– Wait, what?!
Strangely enough, we both got the same idea.
(Actually... Resigning would be a terrible idea.)
(I'd be teased to no end if people found out I quit only hours after becoming secretary...)
In the end, I decided against discharging Suruga. I reasoned that we just needed time to get to know each other better.
It seemed to me she felt the same way. And so, we both agreed to do our best to get on amicable terms.

sequence:
Hidden Charm

<size=45>3 Not Standing Out is Hard</size>

scripts.say: Port - Shoreline path
Suruga continued serving as my secretary, even if we had our awkward moments together.
We were heading to the exercise area that day, passing by a fair few familiar faces along the way.
That's when a realization hit me. Neither of us were saying a word to each other, and simply stared at the ground as we walked.
It was in stark contrast to the talkative people we passed by. We stuck out. And if there was one thing I knew about Suruga, it's that she hates sticking out.
S-say, um... H-how about we talk about something?
She sounded terribly nervous. It seemed I was right.
Please, you choose the topic. It can be anything.
That being the case, I decided to ask about her distaste for being in the spotlight.

options.content: "Why are you so anxious about sticking out?"

scripts.say: Wow, um, talk about getting straight to the point!
I suppose, all things considered, you deserve to know. Allow me to explain.
I was keenly interested to hear her answer.
It's easy to become socially distant when you're like me, but rest assured, I still have people I consider my friends.
...I'm going to take that only the way you intended it.
Anyway... Among my friends, one of them in particular just loves to be the center of attention.
"And you think something bad's going to happen if you get more attention than she does? Is that about right?"
You're quick on the uptake, aren't you? That's the gist of it all. I'll give you the whole story sometime later.
The next thing I knew, we'd arrived just outside the exercise area.
Suruga was going to participate in today's battle. Looking at the lineup, it seemed her opponent was someone close to her.

sequence:
Hidden Charm

<size=45>4 To Be a Kii</size>

scripts.say: Port - Exercise Area
To all who are joining us on this day: thank you for coming.
After coughing a few times, one of the Sakura Empire's brightest minds – Amagi – addressed the crowd.
Of course, that includes you, Commander. Your presence is greatly appreciated.
I hadn't been invited just as a friendly gesture. There was an important role for me to fulfill.
I was to serve as the referee for this naval exercise. It would be a friendly battle between Amagi's great apprentices, and other shipgirls connected by the threads of history.
Well, well! You came after all, Suruga. Congratulations on taking the first step!
{namecode:80}……
Yeah, me again. Ready to get whooped again?
You know, it's just like you to count your chickens before they've hatched.
Tension was building. Kii and Suruga were about on par in terms of rigging specs, but it sounded like Kii had an advantage from the get-go.
It's time to begin. Commander, if you would.
After taking a look across the spectators, Kii, and Suruga, I gave the starting signal.
Let's give the audience what they came for! Say goodnight!
Kii immediately sprung into action. She held nothing back, firing several volleys at Suruga in an effort to take her out quickly.
You've used this strategy a million times already! Get new material!
Suruga dodged the volleys while firing back with sharp remarks the likes of which I'd never heard from her before.
Whoa, what?! What's changed with you between now and last time, Suruga?
Kii was taken aback, but kept firing even so. Despite Suruga's evasive maneuvers wearing away at her stamina, she now went on the offensive.
(This time will be different! I'll win, I swear it!)
Suruga's desire to win could be felt even from the spectator rows. Her heart was on fire.
Of course, Kii burned with a similar desire, but Suruga's passion stood out particularly much.
YOU'RE MIIIINE!
Hmph! Nice try!
After much passionate fighting... It seems we have ourselves a victor.

sequence:
Hidden Charm

<size=45>5 The Things We Tell Ourselves</size>

scripts.say: Port - Exercise Area
It was clear-cut who had won. Suruga was my secretary, but I couldn't let that influence my judgment.
Ahahaha! Victory is mine!
Kii lured Suruga closer with a series of feint shots, securing the victory by scoring a hit at point-blank range. Her strategy had been executed flawlessly.
The crowd burst into applause, congratulating Kii on her result.
Whew... That's that done with.
Suruga, on the other hand, was indifferent about the whole thing. If anything, she sounded like she'd gotten done with a boring chore.
"Done with"? You sound like you weren't even trying to win!
...And? So what?
And that's lame, that's what. It wouldn't kill you to give it 100% in a duel with me.
Do that, and I'll be able to give it as much as 120%! We've still got time for a round two, y'know. C'mon. You had fun, and you know it.
*sigh*... Would it kill YOU to show some basic consideration?
I'm also working as the secretary now, remember? I've got huge amounts of work to do today and tomorrow. I don't have the energy for a no-holds-barred duel.
Damn, girl, okay! Don't let me keep you then.
This, however, wasn't true. Suruga's workload for the day and the next was nothing out of the ordinary. She was making excuses for herself.
Maybe she was bitter over her defeat. I felt I had to say something to her.
Please... It's best you don't.
I rose from my seat, but Amagi stopped me and adviced against it.
Not long after we returned to the office, Suruga's anxiety abruptly boiled over.
Urgh... I gave it my all. I really did. But I still couldn't beat Kii...
At least, if I'm destined to wallow in mediocrity forever then it's not my own fault... I'm just cursed, simple as that...
Her sobbing grew little by little into a bawl, and then something completely unexpected happened.
Plop! Ploop! Flissshhh!
She blurted strange words in an even stranger voice. But strangest of all was the fact she grew a furry tail, and her horns morphed into big, fluffy ears.
They looked like they belonged to... a raccoon.
Oh dear, oh dear! Suruga has dropped her disguise and shown her true form! Commander, you must evacuate!
Shimakaze burst into my office as if she'd predicted this turn of events. She took me by the hand and dragged me outside...

sequence:
Hidden Charm

<size=45>6 The Weakness Kept Inside</size>

scripts.say: Port - Evening
Shimakaze, being one of Suruga's friends, likely had an explanation for her transformation. I decided to ask her about it.
She'd prefer it if you'd keep what you saw a secret.
Suruga maintains a constant tough girl act, you see. She goes out of her way not to seem cute or delicate.
And here I'd come to adore that cool side of her...
Look at these horns, Shimakaze. What do you think?
Wooow! I'm simply stunned!
As in, stunned that you've managed to disguise your real ears beneath them. They look so... so different!
"I'm simply stunned" would've been plenty for an answer, you know!
Sorry. At any rate, rest assured, I think you look awesome with a capital A!
Heheheh... I sure do! This new look will finally give me the confidence needed to truly excel!
...And that's the story behind them. Sadly, they still weren't enough to take her to the absolute top.
As a result, Suruga set her expectations lower and lower. She'd settle for 2nd place, then 3rd, and it only got worse.
Kii holds some... quite strict beliefs. "Defeat comes from not trying hard enough. All losers do is make up excuses for it."
She doesn't know Suruga in and out. The only reason she associates with her is for her looks...
"Now I see the greater picture... There's only one thing I can do."
You're going to try to console her?
There was Suruga, my secretary, and then there was Suruga, the Kii-class battleship.
There was Suruga, brimming with valor in the exercise area... and Suruga, vulnerable and exposed.
I learned something important that day. Suruga had two sides to her.
When I returned to my office, Suruga had not only stopped sobbing, she'd seated herself at her desk and started working again.
Oh. There you are, Commander. You were out for quite some time.
She spoke casually and straight to the point, like nothing had happened before I left. It was a sly tactic, and seemed... a little like what a raccoon might do.
If you have any work lying around, just let me at it. I could use something to clear my mind.
Her eyes were still faintly red after weeping for so long. Instead of assigning her work, I decided to tell her something to raise her spirits.
The sea?! But that's not on tomorrow's schedule?
Unless... you mean in the after-hours, then I suppose that could be arranged...

sequence:
Hidden Charm

<size=45>7 The Road to Improvement</size>

scripts.say: Port - Exercise Area
Pl-please! I've asked you not to touch my ears! Err, horns, I mean!
After finishing our work for the day, I invited Suruga to participate in a mock battle using a mass-produced ship.
...You'll show a preview of your steering skills before we begin? Are you that confident in them?
Well, go ahead, I suppose. I'm not sure why you– Oh... OH!
Suruga's jaw dropped – I had just performed a maneuver characteristic of Kii's fighting style. I'd spent the whole previous night practicing to learn how to imitate it.
(You went out of your way to stage a mock battle against basically-Kii... just for me, Commander...?)
With a hesitant gait, she seemed to come closer to me.
Don't tell me you arranged this, hoping it would make me happy?
Though she made it sound like she wasn't pleased, I could sense she was.
(Crap... I can't hide how obviously overjoyed I am.)
The tables had turned – now I could read HER mind, clear as day.
"My goal with this whole endeavor is simple. I want to make you comfortable with being yourself, and not who you think others want you to be."
Are you trying to say you actually LIKE my raccoon features? Are you just into exotic things, or something...?
"Your appearance is part of it, but it's not all."
"More importantly, I can't bear to see you keep losing to Kii. This will help with that."
Aha! I see you've started! Are you having fun, Suruga?
Sh-Shimakaze?! You're not taking part too, are you?
Hm? No, not at all. I just completed a mission and I'm simply passing by to say hello. Isn't that right, Commander?
(Wait a second... Did the commander get Shimakaze's aid to make this happen...?)
You know... You really didn't need to go through all this effort just for me.
The fact of the matter was that I wanted to. Suruga was precious to me, and it was only natural I'd want to convey that.
I know that look! You're thinking of cheesy stuff right now, aren't you?! Ugh, it's giving me second-hand embarrassment!
She turned red as an apple from ear to ear and fired a volley of training shells at my ship.
As I maneuvered out of their path, I smiled and hoped for our now-amicable relationship to continue just like this.
Oh no you don't!
It's time we get serious! Come here and I'll show you what I'm really made of!

sequence:
Crosswave

<size=45>Suruga, Sally Forth!</size>

scripts.say: Port - Exercise Area
In this exercise scenario, our fleet will ambush another fleet led by the Commander.
As I'm sure you all know, this will be similar to the friendly spars we've had with the Royal Navy and Eagle Union in the past; it is merely an exercise.

However, its goal isn't solely for our fleet to gain more experience; it's also meant to strengthen bonds among factions, and more importantly, to expose us to different combat formations and unexpected scenarios.
And so, as per Mikasa's advice, I shall serve as the commander of the Sakura Fleet since I have not become a full-fledged member of this naval base yet.
I'm sure many of you who have never seen me before are confused or upset by this decision.
But I, Battleship Suruga, promise to dedicate my body and spirit to carry out this task!
Now, let's get ourselves ready and see this exercise through to the end!
That was a rousing speech, Suruga. I knew it wasn't a mistake to summon you here.
Thank you. I shall give it my all to ensure that this joint exercise is conducted successfully.
Of course. For this exercise, you are the one in charge, not me. I trust that you will be able to fully display the Sakura Fleet's majesty and honor to the Commander.
Next, I shall announce our combat strategy and formations...
Wa ha hah! Just call upon Yukikaze the Great, and Commander's fleet will fall in the blink of an eye!
We can't have that happening. I have waited for this exercise for so long, and I want to truly savor each moment as my Commander's opponent.
Suruga, would you please have me deployed to the area where my dear Commander will be waiting for me?
I will take it into consideration. I'm aware this is simply an exercise, but my deployment decisions must be based on logic and take the mission's goal into account...
Hmm, very well. We must do our best for my Commander, after all.
I hate to admit it, but this fleet is called the Suruga Fleet, not the Yukikaze Fleet... so just this once, I'll follow your orders, Suruga!
R-right... I shall do everything that I can...
Sorry for putting you through all this trouble.

sequence:
Crosswave

<size=45>The Lucky Ship's Initiative</size>

scripts.say: Port - Exercise Area
I'm astonished. They responded to my strategies by immediately redeploying their forces and adjusting their weaponry with precision.
Perhaps that's not very surprising, though. Who would be more familiar with this fleet's capabilities than the Commander, after all?
Suruga, how does the battle fare?
We are in an engagement on the frontlines. As for how it's faring... not quite as expected. Our opponents are advancing faster than I expected.
Though it would be possible to sortie our main fleet to meet theirs head-on, avoiding that engagement to lure them deeper in might be the wiser option.
Ah, you plan to wait until their advance is at its breaking point to strike them full-force.
Indeed. However, I still haven't decided who would be best suited to lure the opponent towards us...
Perhaps it would be best to withdraw our vanguard fleet...
There's no need for that!
Yukikaze?
If you need someone to lure our opponents in, then Yukikaze the Great will do it! Just give me the order!
I appreciate your initiative, but considering the speed of the opponent's advance, our fleet wouldn't even be ready to intercept them.
In other words, we'll also need some way of buying time while luring them. Do you have any ideas on how to do that, Yukikaze?
Heheh! We don't need any cheap tricks for that! This is nothing that cannot be solved with Yukikaze the Great's extraordinary luck!
... Come again?
Well, that's what I would normally say, but I'll be counting on you to back me up if anything goes wrong.
I, I see... Then, I will do whatever I can to support you.
Hahahah! You two seem like quite the promising pair! Now go out there and seize victory!
You can count on Yukikaze to get it done! Wa hah hah!
... A-affirmative!

sequence:
Crosswave

<size=45>A Leader's Prowess</size>

scripts.say: Port - Exercise Area
They got meeeee!
Another dead end... Yukikaze, fall back to our line of defense! Taihou and I will cover you!
You certainly know how to work someone hard... Yukikaze, now!
Understood! ... I mean, consider yourselves off the hook for now!
Somehow, we managed to fend off the Commander's onslaught... But as the battle gets drawn out, we'll surely get whittled down...
Grrr... How is it possible that not even Yukikaze the Great could put a halt to the Commander's fleet...
It seems we're at a loss. We can adjust our strategy all we want, but Commander's fleet seems to always be a step ahead of us.
There are Eagle Union ships that have managed it before, you know...
And, while I wouldn't mind suffering a crushing defeat at my Commander's hands, that would reflect poorly on the Sakura Empire's reputation...
I'll admit, one's motivation starts to diminish when a battle feels as one-sided as this... Having said that, we must not resort to using cheap tricks, like Yukikaze said...
They're forcing my hand...!
Taihou, Yukikaze, please listen. I have an idea for how we can turn this around.
But how? And let me just get this out of the way; I might be lucky, but even I can't magically triple our fleet power!
There's still a way for us to get the upper hand in this situation?
Yes. By ignoring all the other opponents and going straight for the Commander.
No way! Not even Yukikaze the Great could plow through to the center of that massive fleet...
You won't be alone. We'll bait the ship the Commander is on to come here, then attack all at once.
It doesn't matter if you use cannons or bombs, just take out that flagship! Got it?
But how do you know where the Commander is?
Why, I thought you of all people would know, Taihou... Would you mind doing some recon for us?
Me?! ... Need I even answer that question? I would absolutely love to locate the Commander!
Appreciate it. I'll give you specific instructions later, so for now just try not to let the Commander catch wind of our plan.
Set sail!

sequence:
Crosswave

<size=45>Crossing New Waves</size>

scripts.say: Port - Exercise Area
Good. Keep this up, and we'll be able to lure them over before they breach our last line of defense.
We still aren't done?! Yukikaze the Great may be second to none, but even I don't have limitless stamina!
Just hold on a bit longer! But we're also nearly out of time! Taihou, any news?
I can smell it! This is my dear Commander's fragrance... Hehehehe...
Great! Yukikaze, once you're at the location I told you about, turn around and head back at maximum speed! We'll get them in a pincer attack!
Understood! And how's it going for you over there?
I'm drawing closer to the opponent! ... *Sigh*, and I wish I wasn't. Why did I agree to this in the first place...
But it's fine... At this range, everything turns into an all-out brawl, and it'll be impossible to keep track of what every ship is doing. This is my best opportunity.
Taihou, do you read me? I've transferred my flagship status to you! The moment my gunfire stops, send your bombers over to my location!
Are you seriously going to thrust deep into the Commander's fleet all on your own?!
This isn't what you promised! Didn't we agree I would be the one to dive straight into the Commander's heart?!
You're a carrier; that's not happening! And keep your mind on your recon! If we lose sight of the Commander, the whole mission will fail!
Fine! But just this one time!
D-did you just get Taihou to back down?!
Wait, is this really the right time to be cracking a joke?
Thank you for having faith in my command, Yukikaze, Taihou!
Now's the time! I'll show them what a Kii-class battleship is capable of! Chaaaaaarge!

sequence:
Crosswave

<size=45>Suruga's Saga</size>

scripts.say: Yukikaze, Taihou, and of course, Suruga, you've all done me proud. Even the Commander has praised your outstanding performance during this exercise.
You had me worried at the end there! Thank goodness we only use blanks for exercises!
And you got within such close range of my Commander... I demand you give me that privilege the next time, Suruga!
Ahahahah! It's fantastic to see you in such high spirits immediately after an exercise! I say we have Aoba write a special news report on your exploits today.
A... a whole report?!
Sorry, but I would MUCH prefer not to!
(Looking back, I really wasn't expecting all this to happen...)
And so, as per Mikasa's advice, I shall serve as the commander of the Sakura Fleet since I have not become a full-fledged member of this naval base yet.
(I only agreed to it because I was expecting that position to be purely honorary and not require me to make any decisions!)
Heheh! We don't need any cheap tricks for that! This is nothing that cannot be solved with Yukikaze the Great's extraordinary luck!
(Ugh... I really can't deal with these empty-headed optimists who can't seem to take anything seriously...)
(But, you know, we're still in this together, which means I can't just throw her under the bus! And that in turn means I have to work even harder!)
And, while I wouldn't mind suffering a crushing defeat at my Commander's hands, that would reflect poorly on the Sakura Empire's reputation...
(You don't say! And how in the world could I have known the Commander's fleet would be so powerful?!)
(Of course they'd mop the floor with us if I didn't pull out some clever trick! I had no choice, you know? Do you really think I like standing out like this?)
(Oh, and the Commander knows all of you well enough to see right through your plans, right? But as an outsider, things were different for me.)
You had me worried at the end there! Thank goodness we only use blanks for exercises!
And you got within such close range of my Commander... I demand you give me that privilege the next time, Suruga!
(An outsider... That's what I am... But nobody here treated me like one...)

sequence: <size=51>What if... this is where I belong...?</size>

scripts.say: Correct. There is no gap between ships that have a service history and those that lack it.
So what do you say, Suruga? Won't you become an official member of our fleet?
Considering your exercise performance, you might get accustomed to life here even quicker than those girls from the development dock. Hahaha!
You have plenty of time. Ponder it for a while and do what your heart says is right.
(She's right. This might be where I, and that speedy, annoying little destroyer belong...)
Let us meet again soon...

sequence:
The Melancholy of a Princess Chevalier

<size=45>Chapter 1 - Teatime Visitor</size>

scripts.say: One afternoon at the port...
Master, Lady Triomphant, please enjoy.
Le Triomphant and I showed up to join the Royal Navy's tea time.
I'm honored to have been invited to your famous afternoon tea time.
As she spoke, Le Triomphant took out a cutely-wrapped present.
Hmm... So you're the new arrival from Iris Libre?
Good, I see that Iris Libre also cultivates some fine young ladies.
And you, the commoner over there! You should be more thankful, since I went out of my way to invite you!

options.content: Thank you very much! Long live the Queen!

scripts.say: It seems that Le Triomphant had made a good impression upon Her Majesty.
If you wanted to look at it a certain way, they certainly seemed to give off the same vibe.
Commander, you were thinking of something rude just now, weren't you?
The chief maid, Belfast, was pouring tea for everyone.
This aroma is... Darjeeling?
Yes. This particular batch was freshly picked in the spring. It's Her Majesty's favorite.
I see, so that's why it's so refreshing. I've always heard that the First Flush of Darjeeling is one of the most precious teas.
Heh heh, precisely! I can see that you have discerning tastes~♪
Being here reminds me... of the tea parties we used to have back in Iris Libre...
Le Triomphant's eyes seemed to swim with a mix of affection and loneliness.
Perhaps it would be nice to have a tea party with the Vichya girls as well.

sequence:
The Melancholy of a Princess Chevalier

<size=45>Chapter 2 - Do Your Best, Le Triomphant!</size>

scripts.say: Port - Commander's Office
Commander, here is a list of the ships participating in today's joint exercise. Please have a look.
Really, have you already forgotten? According to the plan that we made a while back, we would conduct a joint exercise between Iris Libre and the Royal Navy as a part of our ongoing daily training.
As the commander of the fleet, everyone's counting on you to keep things together. Come on, please hurry and check the list.
After getting scolded by my secretary ship...
I made a few small modifications to the list.
You'd like to adjust the list? Let me see...
Huh? You'd like me to lead the vanguard fleet?
It's because you want everyone to see my combat performance?
Heh. If that's the case, then I readily accept!
Commander, I'll be glad to show you - and everyone else - just how powerful the Le Fantasque-class is!
Afternoon - Training Grounds
Make sure to match each others' pace! Don't charge forward on accident!
Stay calm and collected. This isn't a solo operation, so don't be afraid to ask for help!
... Good work. We've finished this area, so let's go support our allies in the next area!
Due to Le Triomphant's successes, Iris Libre's team started off with a strong score.
Heheh, thank you very much, Commander.
What'd I tell you? Are you impressed with how powerful the Le Fantasque-class is?
That said, we're still working on the basics.
If my sisters were here...
Le Triomphant seemed to be immersed in her memories again...
Ahem! Nevermind! In any case, let's all review the results of today's joint exercise...
Ahh, what an exemplary secretary ship.

sequence:
The Melancholy of a Princess Chevalier

<size=45>Chapter 3 - Le Triomphant, Sortie!</size>

scripts.say: Operation Sea Area
Torpedoes incoming from port! Watch out!
Please keep firing!
Line ahead! We're going to break the enemy's formation!
Requesting assistance from the main fleet!
Are preparations complete? Please provide us with aerial support!
You'll find that the speed of the Le Fantasque-class is not easily matched!
Commander, operation complete! We'll be able to come back home soon, hehe~!
With Le Triomphant's leadership, the combat operation was a great success.
Port - Harbor
It's only natural! It comes with being an elegant Le Fantasque-class destroyer.
However, this victory would not have been possible without everyone's hard work.
That includes you too, Commander. Your instructions were also important!
I'm glad that I was able to be a part of such an excellent fleet!
So once again, good job on the operation, everyone. Commander, would you like to join me for some tea before we get back to work?
Ahh, what an exemplary secretary ship. Truly without equal.

sequence:
The Melancholy of a Princess Chevalier

<size=45>Chapter 4 - Cheer Up, Le Triomphant!</size>

scripts.say: Le Triomphant and I were patrolling the port together.
All right! Let's prepare ourselves for another fine day of work!
She seemed to be quite energetic today.
Ah... it's Commander... Terror, come here and greet the commander!
Hello, Le Triomphant... and Commander...
We had bumped into Erebus and Terror.
Good day, Miss Erebus, Miss Terror.
Thank you, Le Triomphant. After sortieing with you, Terror seems to be a lot more confident in herself.
Thank you...
There's no need to thank me. Terror has always been very capable, all I did was give her a little support.
I'm terribly sorry, but we're going to have to get going. Too much sunlight is bad for Terror's body. Terror, want to go get some sweets?
Sure...
With that, Erebus lead Terror off.
Self-confidence, huh...
Oh my, Le Triomphant? Are you on patrol with Commander today?
Good day, Miss Lexington, Miss Saratoga.
Eh? Ehhhh?! How'd you find me? I was gonna sneak up on Commander and get a real good reaction!
I'm sorry, Miss Saratoga... I seem to have made a mistake...
Knock it off, Saratoga. You're a member of the Lexington-class, so you should take some lessons from Le Triomphant about being responsible.
I know, I know.
Well then, Commander, Le Triomphant, thank you both for your hard work. Good luck with those patrols!
Bye bye! Oh, by the way, Lex, did you hear the rumors?
Being responsible...
Le Triomphant seemed a little down...
H-huh? Is something stuck on my face...?

options.content: Pat her gently on the head

scripts.say: C-Commander...
Le Triomphant smiled at me, but she somehow seemed distant and lonely.

sequence:
The Melancholy of a Princess Chevalier

<size=45>Chapter 5 - Listen to Your Heart</size>

scripts.say: I asked Le Triomphant what was bothering her while we walked around port.
Commander, did you know that I'm the youngest sister of the Le Fantasque class?
Yes, as you might surmise, I have several other older sisters...
Before that war, we were all very close. I thought that things would be able to stay like that forever.
Even when war broke out, I had nothing to fear as long as my sisters were with me...
But reality was much harsher.
There were a lot of complicated circumstances; everyone started to go their separate ways...
Even though we're all aiming for the same goal, why did we end up having to fight each other...?

options.content: You'll be able to overcome your differences one day.

scripts.say: Since coming here, I've managed to regain some of my hope thanks to you, Commander.
