<size=45>8 Each Other's Wishes III</size>

scripts.say: I've been thinking... Don't you, like, spoil me way too hard?
TB crosses her arms, makes a peevish face, and stares at me.
What?
You know what I'm talking about,{playername}. I say I wanna do something, and you make it happen, every time.
You try to make even my wildest wishes come true. If that's not spoiling me rotten then what is?
Hey, I'm just doing my duty as your guardian.
And I wouldn't call it "spoiling you." I just want to make you happy.
Yeah! That's the thing!
You've done all I've ever asked for, and I think it's time for a bit of a role reversal.
You're going to be MY guardian, is what you're saying?
Don't be silly! I'm not gonna be anyone's guardian!
Unless that's your wish, of course!
Oh, uh, no. It's not.
Reeeally? How can I be sure it isn't if you won't tell me what you really wish for?
I'm not falling for that leading question.
Tsk. I tried...
You don't need to play mind games to get an answer from me. What I want is really simple.
I want to tell you a bedtime story for old times' sake.
I haven't told you one ever since you grew out of them, have I?
Seriously? THAT'S what you want?
Sure, that's totally fine... On one condition! I get to decide what it's about!
Adventure and fighting! That's what I wanna hear!
I'm sleepy... I wanna hear a story.
Oh, do you like bedtime stories? That's good to know. I thought you didn't.
What does... "like" mean?
Umm... You can "like" in all kinds of ways.
There's liking things, then there's liking people. Basically, it's a feeling of wanting that thing or person to never go away.
(Hmm... She's probably too young to understand it.)
(I should have explained it differently. That's an error on my part.)
The little girl stares at me, no sign of emotion on her face at all, then tells me...
I like it... when you read to me.
That's lovely. I'll have to find a first-rate story for her tonight!
{tb}, do you have a moment? I'd like some advice on what club I should apply to.
With an anxious look, she softly places a flyer on the table in front of me.
How about... going with a club dedicated to what you like?
That's the issue. I don't know which of them to choose...
More specifically, I don't have any real hobbies, so none of them jump out at me.
I'm even starting to consider just trying them all out before I decide...
I mean, what's wrong with that? Trying things until you find something you like is an option.
After mulling it over for a while, she accepts my advice.
Here's hoping she'll find something she enjoys.
Hey, {tb}! I want your help with picking one of these!
TB thrusts a flyer before my face before I get the chance to say a word.
I've got no clue which one to go with and it's kinda making me wanna try 'em all!
Oh, you're looking to join a club. Then how about choosing one based on what you like the most?
Good idea! But there doesn't seem to be any comic book reading club. Maybe I should make one myself!
I don't think they'll let you get away with just reading comics. You'll have to choose between the ones on the flyer.
Really? Aww... Wait! There's no rule that says I can't pick EVERY club, is there?
Because if not, that's what I'm gonna do! Oh, I'm such a frickin' genius!
I want to say that she won't last long doing that, but seeing how excited the idea makes her, I hold my tongue. Don't want to rain on her parade.
Besides, it's good to try all kinds of things. I hope she'll come upon her true hobby.
Do you need something?
I had to ask. TB's gaze has been fixated on me for an hour at this point.
Not really. I'm just keeping an observation diary for a school project.
Wait... An "observation diary"? Are you observing me?
Yes...?
Could you, like, study something else? Like an animal or a bug.
No. That's more effort.
She hits me with a hard "no" and goes back to observing me.
On the bright side, at least she'll finish her homework faster this way.
Say, {tb}, what do you do at home while I'm at school?
Also, what's your favorite food? I already know, but I'm asking just to be sure.
While I'm at it, what TV shows do you watch? What clothes do you like to wear? What–
TB fires off a barrage of questions about my daily life. Why is she asking all this?
What's with all these questions?
Oh, sorry, I'm so scatterbrained I forgot to explain. I'm asking for an observation diary I'm going to present at school.
I know you well, but I don't know many of the things the form wants me to fill in, so...
I think that's because these kinds of studies are typically not conducted on people.
Huh? They aren't?
I shake my head. Just as I'm about to suggest something else for her to study...
Be that as it may, I want to study you anyway. Shall we continue?
Left with no choice, I answer her questions and help fill out her observation diary.
{tb}! Hey, {tb}! Help me fill this out!
..."Write details about your observation subject"? What's this about?
What's it sound like? My homework is to keep an observation diary!
Well, yeah, I can tell that much. I'm asking, "Am I the one being observed here?"
Bingo! You're gonna make my diary the most unique in the whole class! I'm such a genius!
Oh, it'll definitely be unique, but people aren't ordinarily the subject for this sort of thing.
What? So this is, like, not allowed?
I didn't mean that it's not allowed, I'm just saying–
Great, then it's all good! Come now, subject! A bold new future awaits!
In the end... I have to just run with it and help with her homework.
I've finished my homework and my chores.
Good... Uh, why are you staring at me?
This is the part where you say, "You're the best" or give me some kind of reward.
Oh. You're spoiled, is what you're saying.
Am not. It's not being spoiled to ask for recognition for my hard work.
Alright, then I'll cook dinner for you, my hardworking princess. I'll fry you an egg for extra nutrition, too.
I didn't do all that work just for a fried egg... but thanks. Be careful so you don't burn it.
Of course.
Kids her age... So hard to work with.
{tb}, is there anything else I can do for you? Like give you a shoulder massage, or something.
You've done your chores and finished your homework. That's plenty. You can just relax now.
Yes, but those are things I was meant to do anyway. So, if you don't need a shoulder rub, how about...
I know! Why don't I make dinner? Although, we don't have many ingredients... I'll fry some eggs for the extra nutrition!
Hold your horses. Frying eggs is my job!
Is it? But...
Egg-frying is dangerous business. Let me handle that at the very least!
The memory of when she tried it still burns bright in my mind.
Hmph. Then after dinner's over, I won't speak to you until tomorrow.
(I'm not a kid anymore. I can fry an egg just fine...)
Sure enough, she didn't say a word to me after we ate dinner. Kids her age... So hard to work with.
My homework and chores are all done! I'm such a good girl it's kinda crazy!
I know that look. She's aching for praise.
Well, Ms. Good Girl, what do you want for a reward?
A reward? Aww, you're too generous!
If you insist, then I'd love to practice my cooking a bit. There are eggs in the fridge, so...
(I hate to be a wet blanket, but the last time she tried her hand at eggs, it was a disaster. Better not let it happen again.)
...Hey! What's with that sour look? You're thinking of that time I fried eggs as a kid, aren't you?!
That's what you call it? I call it, "That time you burned enough poor little eggs to fill a whole bowl."
Wow, rude?! Just you wait! I'm gonna serve you the best, most perfect fried eggs ever one of these days!
She pouts, takes a seat on the couch, and turns on the TV to watch cooking shows.
Strangely, I'm looking forward to the day I'll taste her perfectly fried eggs.
{tb}, do you like chocolate?
Why do you ask?
Just curious. Do you like it or not?
Well... It's good for the energy boost it gives me.
Huh? You don't have any follow-up to that?
My gut tells me I said something wrong.
Oh, I was just thinking what a hard time you'll have. In more ways than one.
"Hard time"...?
Later on, I catch TB trying to make a concoction out of an energy drink and chocolate.
I just realized – I don't know your taste when it comes to chocolate.
Why does it matter?
Oh, well, I've been in a chocolate-making mood as of late, and I wanted to make something suited to your tastes.
Ah. Truth be told, I don't have a favorite when it comes to chocolate.
That said, it's good to have if you're in need of an energy booster.
So really, just make whatever kind of chocolate you want.
Hmph...
What? Did I say something wrong?
No, it's nothing...
I get the feeling that she's a little peeved about my answer.
I feel a tug on my shirt. I look down and see TB, silently gazing up at me.
What's up? Are you hungry?
Mhm... I wanna eat.
What should I make? That meal you liked last week?
No... It's not good anymore.
(Even TB can get tired of eating the same food, I suppose.)
I want something different.
Alright, I'll cook up something new next week. Pick whatever you want to eat.
I'm not picky... I'll eat anything you make.
I crack a wry smile and pat her on the head. I'll definitely do some reading on cooking later.
I'll be straight to the point, {tb}! Do you want chocolate?
Come again?
Chocolate! Do you want some?! Yes or no!
I'm not fiending for a bite, if that's what you're asking. Did you buy too much to eat on your own?
No, nothing like that!
(I was wondering if you wanted me to make some...)
What was that? Make some what?
Nothing! Forget about it!
She drops the topic right there and then. It sounds like she's going to make something.
Hey, look...
TB points at the clouds outside the window.
A star... A fish... A horse...
An aircraft carrier... A battleship...
No way the clouds look like those. Let me see...
I look in the direction she's pointing, and...
She's right! They DO look like those things! Why did Akashi make them like that?
Enough... Enough...
TB is reading a book and seems to have stumbled upon a complicated concept.
What does that mean?
It means not too little or too much. Just the right amount.
Hmm...
It's not always clear how much that is, I know.
We'll just have to find the answer together.
Together... Yeah, we will.
TB looks very sad.
What's the matter?
I lost my wallet...
She still had it when she was buying snacks on the way home.
But when she got home and searched her pockets for it, it was gone.
There was a month's worth of allowance in that wallet, and now it's all gone.
Oof. That's tragic...
I feel so bad for her that I just have to replace the money she lost.
{tb}, is magic real?
Magic? Umm...
I can't say it isn't, or I might ruin her dreams.
But I can't say it does either, obviously...
(Raising a kid is harder than anyone told me.)
Since there is no right answer, I dodge the question by giving her a cupcake.
I want to read a book, but I don't know what kind...
A school book, maybe? When in doubt, educate yourself.
It has to be about something fun.
Oh. Sorry, I can't think of any fun books off the top of my head.
Tell you what, when we go out later, we'll check out the bookstore. Pick whatever book looks appealing to you.
Okay!
{tb}, what is a dream?
TB sometimes asks big questions like this, and I'm never sure how to reply.
It's a challenge, but that's what makes it fun to answer.
A dream is like... a kind of hope for the future.
You could also call it a goal you want to achieve deep in your heart.
Answering her questions also allows me to reflect on the things I know.
Just as I help her grow, she helps me grow, in a way.
{tb}, I want to try this drink.
TB points to an ad of a glass filled with a golden liquid. Her eyes are filled with little twinkles of excitement.
The problem is, that drink is meant for adults.
Hang on, is it possible she'll get an update that turns her into an adult?
...Regardless, she's too young for it right now.
Later on, I dupe her with a glass of regular fruit juice.
{tb}, this dish looks interesting.
TB points at the TV. It's playing an episode of a show called "Kitchen Blunders: Your Food is Cooked."
They're showing a dish that, to put it nicely, makes you wonder what was going through the chef's mind.
I'd like to replicate this.
The food's color is offputtingly vivid, and it's prepared in an alien way. I break into a cold sweat.
Trust me, you don't want to.
I change the channel and distract her with a cartoon episode.
Whew. I'm stuffed...
Snack packages lie scattered across the table. Looking at it all makes my head hurt.
It's not healthy to eat nothing but snacks, you know.
Hmph.
That doesn't seem to faze her. Time to turn up the heat.
Also, you can't become an adult on a diet of snacks.
Really? In that case...
Since then, she has stopped eating snacks in large quantities.
Yeah? What is it?
My outfit... Was it cute?
Ah, she must be asking what I thought about the clothes she wore at her performance.
Yeah, it was wonderful. You looked so cute in those new clothes.
You too...
Me too?
You're cute and wonderful...
Being called cute – by a young TB, no less – renders me speechless, but I'm also touched at the same time.
That's us. Cute and wonderful people.
What's up? Do you need help with something?
No... I'm just wondering if you notice anything different about me.
Different?
I examine her under a magnifying glass, but fail to find anything significant.
Oh, did you learn a new skill?
...No. I cut my hair by 5 millimeters.
After that, she seemed a bit sulky.
It's not here...
What are you up to, TB?
She is walking around in circles in her room.
As usual, her expression tells me nothing, but I can clearly tell that she's worked up and anxious.
My plushie is gone...
Plushie? Oh, she must mean that white... thing she's always carrying around.
I stowed it in the closet after she went to school.
I had no idea putting it away would make her this stressed out... I feel a bit guilty now.
Opening the closet, I take the plushie and give it back to her. It manages to calm her down.
What a strange plushie it is, though. I really wonder what creature it's based on.
Why can't I have more, {tb}?
TB stares at me with a serious look in her eyes.
I'm not saying it's out of the question, but why do you need a bigger allowance?
Because children need money that they can spend however they want.
It deepens their understanding of money and the economic system.
That's a very... formal argument. My counterpoint is this – you're still young.
{tb}, are you one of those adults who "save" their kid's allowance and birthday money, then spend it on frivolous stuff?
...Fine, fine. Here, take this.
Once more, she makes me cave into giving her more pocket money...
I've figured out who the perpetrator is.
Sat in front of the TV, TB confidently begins explaining her deduction.
Have you finished your homework?
Analysis... The criminal must've... Then gone to... And finally...
She doesn't answer me – her focus is entirely on the show as she mutters her theory.
On the one hand, it's a solid deduction. On the other...
TB. Hey. Your homework.
I'll do it after I've seen the ending. I'm in the middle of analyzing all the important evidence.
Well... I suppose neglecting your homework is an important part of growing up, too.
Do you know anything about sports, {tb}?
I've hit a slump with my sprinting and I can't get my lap time any lower.
So that's why she's been acting anxious today.
Before I answer that – do you like sprinting in and of itself, or do you just care about getting good grades?
Sprinting is good for your health and improves your physical stamina.
That's... true, but it doesn't answer my question.
...I think I like sprinting in and of itself.
Then there's no reason to worry about lap times or grades.
All you have to do is keep sprinting to get something out of it.
The next day, I was informed that TB had gotten better at sprinting.
{tb}, I've done the laundry and dried our clothes.
TB fluffs up the tail of the plushie in her hands. Looks like she dried it as well while she was at it.
Wait, can you bring your plushie to school? Since when?
Now that I think about it, she's been doing that for a few days, but I didn't think anything of it before now.
It's against the school rules, but...
I have my ways.
...No harm in that, I guess.
It seems there is still room for improvement in her school's policies.
...Look at this.
TB places a flyer on the table in front of me.
What are these? School activities? Did you want to ask for my opinion?
Not really "ask for your opinion," more like ask you to pick one. I'm tired of doing it myself.
(Of course. She's too cool to be honest about it...)
Then let's work it out starting with the obvious one. Do any of the clubs appeal to you?
Not really.
That's the thing. I don't care much for any of them, so I can't decide.
(She's grown into a girl who's indecisive about a lot... Could you consider that a personality?)
When all is said and done, my only suggestion for her was to try out every club she might like and decide after that.
Port - Office
TB and I engage in a staredown through the computer screen.
Ahem... TB, remember what we discussed before? Did you find an answer?
Synchronizing analysis module. Unable to grasp the information surrounding the concept of "personality."
Analyzing the data did not lead to any answers to my questions pertaining to emotional cognition.
TB brought up a very tricky subject just the other day. She said that she feels she lacks a personality.
My first thought was to provide her with some texts on the subject so she could figure it out for herself, which seemingly wasn't enough.
Sounds like just feeding you information won't get you any closer to figuring it out...
Database entry: "personality" typically refers to the collection of traits unique to an individual, or to an individual's particular way of thinking.
While I can describe what a personality is, I do not understand where a so-called personality comes from.
Where it comes from? Hmm...
Just then, a daring idea crosses my mind.
This might be a weird question, but please entertain me...
Do you remember what it was like to be a kid?
Digital assistants such as I generally do not have periods matching the criteria of "being a kid."
Synchronizing analysis module. You are saying that there is a connection between childhood and personality.
Correct. Do you think your lack of a childhood is the root of the problem?
Initiating data categorization and engaging analysis module.
Don't think about it too hard. Just tell me the first thing that comes to mind based on what I just said.
Orders received. Halting analysis.
I believe the existence of a link is possible. However, this theory has no supporting evidence. It is merely a logical inference based on the conversation thus far.
That's all I need.
Are you suggesting that you have found an answer?
Sort of, but I can't share it with you yet. I'll say this, though – you can stop all the work you're doing for a few months.
I have something planned for you. Something only you can do.
I'm not exactly sure how it's going to work out. Just know that I'll tell you when everything is ready.
Orders received. System entering special standby mode. I will reinitialize only upon your explicit orders.
(Just have to provide Akashi with a goal and supplies, and she should be able to make it work.)
Since TB has slowly accustomed to her normal life, I've decided to bring her to new and different places to expand her knowledge.
It should be a suitable place for a child her age, but what would that be?
Hmm... Well, you can't go wrong with the aquarium.
TB and I leisurely roam the aquarium together.
She stares blankly at the fish swimming inside the tank.
(Not sure what to make of her reaction. Does she like it or dislike it?)
They're moving.
She approaches the glass of the tank, looks up, and eyes the aquatic life in the water with great curiosity.
Do you like it?
Mhm. It's warm.
(Not the kind of answer I was expecting... Then again, she's still young, so let's follow up with a question a child can understand.)
Warm? Do you mean these fish?
No... The blue water.
The water? Ohh...
She must be talking about the sea.
Does she feel a familiarity with it, even inside this fabricated world?
That's what they call "the sea."
If you like it, we can go to the sea together when you're a little older.
Okay...
She turns to me with a slight look of confusion.
It's understandable. She still has the cognitive ability of a child, so it must be hard for her to truly grasp some concepts.
Do you wanna go over there? There are even bigger fish there.
She answers with a nod.
TB and I went on to have an unforgettable time together at the aquarium.
Afterward, we called it a day and went home.

Do you like it?
Mhm. It's warm.

She answers with a nod.
Today is TB's first day of school.
I'll be good and listen to the teachers.
Her use of language has improved considerably compared to what it once was.
However, this fluency makes her distinctive robotic tone stand out all the more.
(It's a little jarring to hear a child speaking in such a monotone voice...)
(Although, that'll probably improve once she finds her own personality.)
Hmm?
What's that sound?
The school bell begins to toll.
That means school is starting. Bye for now, TB.
Bye for now...
She mimics me and waves goodbye as well.
I'll come pick you up after school.
The spring breeze is warm and scatters petals from the roadside cherry trees through the air. It almost looks like they're swirling around TB.
I stay and watch as she walks inside the school building and her first day begins.

I'll come pick you up after school.

Some time has passed since TB started going to school.
(Oh, right, they're having an open day at her school, and there will be a performance.)
(Is she going to put on a performance, too?)
Hmm... I guess I just have to wait and see. Whatever the case, it's time to go pick her up.
TB and I are walking home together, and for some reason, she glances up at me from time to time.
Did something happen today?
I squat down to meet TB at eye level.
We're doing a performance for the open day.
Right. Are you doing one, too?
She responds with a nod.
(I had a hunch. This just confirms it.)
The teacher said I'll need a costume for it.
Directions vague. I don't know what to do.
Why not just go with something cute? That seems right for a performance.
(I didn't really think that answer through... Hope it's fine, though.)
(If I'd known this was what I'd deal with, I would've read up on child psychology.)
Okay.
Once we return home, I rummage through the closet and pick out a few garments that would look cute on her.
Do I... look cute?
Absolutely.
She silently examines herself in the mirror. She seems to like this dress quite a lot.
You've... grown.
I have? Yeah. And I'm gonna get even bigger.
Her eyes are glued stuck to the mirror even while she responds.
While she still isn't using clear facial expressions, she has become easier to read.
I cannot wait to see what kind of performance she's going to give.

I take off the device, leaving the virtual world and returning to my office.
It's funny how TB's and my roles have reversed somewhat. She ordinarily assists me in the real world, while in her world, my job is to supervise her as she matures.

It swings open, and inside steps a familiar green shopkeeper.
Akashi? What brings you here?
Heheh. See, there's a feature I forgot to tell you about, nya.
The virtual world will update at regular intervals based on the actions of its residents, nya.
Which is to say, whenever there's a new version, TB will experience a growth spurt, nya.
Checking the device, I find a gauge on it that tracks the progress until the next update.
I already knew she'd grow, but not that there'd be an indicator for it. You could've told me sooner.
People forget things, nya. Now let's give TB that update, nya.
She'll have grown a lot by the next time you see her, nya.
Also... Hmm, actually, that's it in terms of features I should tell you about, nya. Catch you later, nya!
Then, Akashi vanishes in the twinkle of an eye.
She sure is good at running away...
Now I'm curious to see what Akashi means by "growth spurt."
I have to ask myself an important question – what is TB to me, anyway?
Just an AI assistant? Or is she more than that?
The question simmers in my mind for a while until I realize I have no answer to it.
Spending more time with her is the only way I'm going to find that answer.
The update should be done by now. Time to put it back on and check on her.
A jingle plays to signify the update's completion. I switch the device on and dive back into the virtual world.
It has been a while since that system update.
If TB was around 3 or 4 years old before the update, I would say she is about 7 or 8 now.
She sees growth, in every meaning of the word, as a good thing – and she certainly has grown.
It's time to leave. Judging by the traffic conditions and the weather, there's about a 10% chance I'll be late.
You're taking this awfully seriously. You could be a little more lax, you know. Nobody's going to kill you for being late.
I think this is just what's expected of a "good girl."
Sports day starts in an hour. I need to set off now.
I let out a sigh under my breath.
As soon as we arrive at the school, she changes uniforms all by herself.
She then begins the warmup exercises on the mat laid out on the school track.
Hey, TB. I'll leave a bottle of water and some towels here for you.
M'kay. Are you going home already?
She shoots me the question whilst performing leg and back stretches.
No, I'll still be here, cheering you on from the bleachers over there.
Oddly, she looks a little displeased to hear this.
It's not against the rules, is it? Assuming it's fine, I'll be right there, rooting for you.
Okay. I'll try to do good so I'll get good grades.
Maybe I'm just imagining it, but it looks like the corners of her mouth rise slightly. She has never made an expression before this point.
Seems I'm dealing with a kid with a small rebellious streak. Still, rebelliousness is cute in its own way.

That's not "haggling" you're doing. It's called, "asking for more and more pocket money for your school trip."
Hmph.
TB puffs her cheeks with indignation and falls silent, thinking about something.
...Can't you give me more, nya? Even just a teensy-weensy bit, nya?
She looks almost ready to start crying. It's tugging on my heartstrings something fierce.
That word at the end of her sentences, though...
The teacher said, "Use this word when your guardian won't do as you ask, nya."
She grabs my sleeve and tugs on it while she pleads.
Please give me more, nya...
Okay, okay. Your begging strategy worked. You win.
I win, nya!

That's to be expected when I'm in my growth period. My teacher said so.
Not what I was hoping to hear, but alright...
Umm... Okay.
I just thought you'd be happy to hear someone close to you point out how you've grown.

I am happy.
There it is. The expression on her face is what you could definitively call a smile.
We did a lot of fun things and even saw fireworks tonight. Of course I'm happy.
The words themselves don't sound right for a girl her age, but that's beside the point.
What matters is that she has developed her own feelings, which may mean this project has been partially successful thus far.
I wish it was fireworks day every day.
Then I wouldn't have to go to school.
Now she sounds like a kid again. Hearing that, I can't help but smile.

Oh...
She sounds a bit disappointed to hear that.
What about the next time it's fireworks day? Can we go then?
Of course we can.
Pinky promise?
I hook my pinky finger around hers, vowing that we'll come here again next summer.

Yeah, but...

Alright, alright. Let's start with frying an egg.

I taught her how to do it in detail and took precautions so she wouldn't hurt herself...

*sigh*...

You hit the nail on the head, nya.
It's time to tell you about the thing that defines this whole project, nya. Namely, the personality TB is about to develop, nya.
After this upgrade, you will see a TB with more evident personality traits, nya.
Isn't it too early for her? I thought it'd be a more slow and steady process...
We ARE doing things step by step, nya!
Oh, also... her personality will influence her choice of occupation in the future, nya.
Hang on, she's going to get a job?
I don't remember that being on the list of things I asked for.

It's a lot to explain...
Hmm. I see how it is, nya.
You want to ease TB's woes about personality, nya.

Then she'll experience what it's like to grow up and develop her own personality, little by little, nya.

And what would that be?
Nine TRILLION?! Are you kidding me?!
Nya?
That's my price after a generous discount, nya.
Dare I ask what the original price was?
I took the bait and asked the foolish question. Akashi cracks a grin, then whispers a number into my ear.
Fine, I'll take it! You have a deal!
A snappy answer, just the way I like it, nya!
Always a pleasure doing business with you, nya.
Come back in a month and I'll have it ready for you, nya.
A whole month? There's no way you need that much time.
It's actually a lot less than I'd like to have, nya. This is complicated, intricate work we're talking about, nya.
That's a shame. I suppose I'll take my business to da Vinci instead, then.
I-I was just kidding, nya! Give me 20 days, no, 10 days is all I need, nya!
I'll come knocking with good news before you know it, nya!

Okay. What are your ideas?

No thanks.

How does the merry-go-round sound?
She isn't opposed to it, at least.
Merry-go-round it is, then. Let's get in line.

I'll earn her ire if I suggest any more thrill rides to her.
A gentle ride should be more to her tastes.
We line up at the entrance to the merry-go-round.
These seats look pretty cramped for adults...
That's no surprise, since it's clearly themed with children in mind. I crack a wry smile.
You go ahead and enjoy yourself. I'll sit this one out.
No thanks.
There's room for one person per horse.
Although her tone remains as unaffected and flat as ever, she projects an air of intensity that I can't refuse.
Alright, alright. I'll get on.
I take a seat on the wooden horse just next to hers.
Hey, TB, look here.
Hm?
I snap a picture of her riding the merry-go-round.
Please at least tell me before you photograph me.
Then again... No, never mind.
This is fine.
Huh...?
She doesn't say a word after that, but she does nudge me into riding the merry-go-round again later.
Our amusement park visit continues after that, and we make some unforgettable memories.

Well, if you're sure...

Oh... You don't think that's a childish ride, do you?

No, not at all. I was just surprised. It's a cute choice.

Alright, let's go. To the merry-go-round!

Hey, TB, look here.
Okay!

Make sure I'm in focus!
Of course.

Heehee. When we're home again, you should print out all the photos we take today.

Fiiine. Let me think...

Am I in focus? Great! Make sure you capture my best side!

Since when were you so keen on taking pictures?
I'm not, like, a photo nerd or anything! This is just a special occasion that deserves to be immortalized!
I mean, when was the last time we went on the merry-go-round? Basically never! Heehee!

I'm not sure how to feel about it.

Okay.

I saved up my allowance to buy it.

I was... feeling the Christmas spirit.
It was then that I understood what you meant by "lucky."
Merry Christmas.
This is for you.

She holds out the wrapped Christmas present to me.
This is my thank-you for always looking after me.
It's not much, I know, but it's the thought that counts, right?
I hope you'll appreciate it.
Merry Christmas.

Four hours... Four whole hours spent running around without a minute to rest...
And you're not tired in the slightest...?
Do I LOOK tired? I told you you need to exercise more! This is what happens when you skip leg day!
I'll make the place look nice and festive. You just stay there and rest, okay?

I do desperately need to rest, but I'll doze off if I sit here for too long...

I said wake up!

Tadah! TB Claus is here in style!
Heehee. What do you think? Don't I look Christmassy as anything?
(She's all but begging for compliments.)
This is for you!
She presents a small box, lovingly wrapped and tied up in a nice bow.

There's no rule against it, and even if there was, we have the whole place to ourselves.
Let's have a little fun! Come on!
Seeing her eyes twinkle with excitement, I breathe an exasperated sigh.
It is completely beyond me how she turned into such an over-the-top peppy girl.
Hm? What's that?
Just as I brace myself for a hot spring water fight, something else seems to grab her attention.
Look! It's a maple leaf!
Look! It's a maple leaf!
A leaf floats in the water. She picks it up and covers her eye with it, showing it to me.
It is. What about it?
In cases like this, you need to have a quote prepared. Like...
"Cursed power within my right eye, heed my words – with this leaf made of a sage's blood, I will seal you away!"
Ain't that the coolest thing you've ever heard? I read it in a comic book!
Sure, it's cool. If you're a teenager in their edgy phase.
Hmph. Spoken like the most boring adult on the planet.
Oh, I'm boring? Let's see how you fare against this cursed power of mine!
Owch! Hot, hot!

Then it's not so bad.

Tadah! It's the completion day of TB's virtual town, nya!
Take this, nya.
What am I looking at here?
The Akashi Workshop's latest and greatest immersion interface, nya!
Wear this and you'll feel like you're actually touching things in the virtual world, nya!
TB exists in the virtual world, and you live in the real world, nya. A barrier stands between you two, nya...
But this device will tear that barrier down, nya!
That sounds incredible. Did you make this all by yourself? If so, great job.
It wasn't just me, nya. Others around the port chipped in to make it real, nya.
But that's not important, nya! Use it and see what it's like, nya!
TB will be there shortly, nya.
Whoa, wait a sec...

You're here. I'm glad you could come.

Would you like to dance with me?

I spent so, so long picking out just the right one, so it better be!
She shoots me a gaze and then performs a quick pirouette.
You bet. It's the perfect dress for you.
Heheh! Obviously!
By the way, you're gonna have to dance all night with me to make up for being so darn late!

Gimme your hand!

Easy, cowgirl. Slow down...

At this point, the project's primary goal of cultivating a personality for TB has been achieved.
In the second stage, TB will have chosen a career based on how I raised her, according to Akashi.
I wonder what she's like now that she's grown even more.
...How is this expression and pose? Fine?
With her beautiful looks and talent in front of the camera, TB became a model after graduating.
Meanwhile, I more or less became her half-agent, and I handle the contracts and business side of things.
If you're wondering why I'm only half an agent...
I have another commercial shoot in three hours, so let me know about the progress, thanks.
There's an audition in the morning tomorrow, then in the evening... Actually, please cancel my gig in the evening tomorrow.
...It's because she can manage her schedule completely fine without an agent's help.
That there is a great pose.
The gig can wait, because I want to go to the amusement park with you tomorrow.
...Also, what's so great about it? There's nothing good about it at all.
She whispers to me between takes. There, in that moment while she was changing poses, I caught a glimpse of her cheeks turning faintly red.
...Hm? It's bad for the eyes?
Don't worry about it. I adjusted to it a long time ago.
Post-graduation, TB committed herself to the art of painting.
She moved out and found a studio apartment. There, she spends day and night refining her craft.
Because of the distance between us, we mostly communicate via phone.
Remember, you need to eat. Is that clear?
Yeah, I know. I'll be coming over to your house today.
So... please make something tasty.
She whispers a promise to me.
...Okay, need to set everything up before the band gets here.
After graduating, TB became a musician and put together enough money to purchase her own recording studio.
That must be exhausting.
Yeah. I guess it's the price you pay for making music that really speaks to the soul.
You can wait outside if you're getting bored, by the way.
Not at all. It's fun watching you work.
M'kay.
The look on her face as she fiddles with the mixer is one of utmost concentration.
When I get home, I should listen to some of the albums she recommended.
First, I'd like to thank all my wonderful fans. Your support has honestly been stunning.
This comes as such a surprise to me that I don't even have a speech prepared...
TB stands on stage, trophy in hand, addressing an entire audience of people.
She became an actor after graduating. Celebrated for her outstanding talent, she has received numerous awards and prizes.
...But I will say this – I wouldn't have gotten into acting, and I certainly wouldn't have received this trophy, if it weren't for the person who raised me.
She smiles warmly. Everything around her seems to pale in comparison to the light she gives off.
To that person, and to everyone else who has supported me, thank you.
Spreading icing on a cake evenly has no right being this difficult...
Heehee. It takes patience to make a cake look beautiful.
After graduating, TB turned her hobby into her job.
This and that happened, and now she's a fairly well-known chef.
Of course, it's no piece of cake to bake a pretty cake when you're a beginner... Let me tell you a little lifehack.
There's a lifehack?
Absolutely. It's to pour your heart into what you're making. Then it becomes easy.
Like this...
As she moves, a sweet aroma of cream and strawberry fills the kitchen.
The cake she's making will is going to be delicious.
Oh... You're here.
After she graduated, TB chose to become a writer.
The novels she published all garnered great reviews, and so she decided to make writing into her full-time job.
As you can see, I'm searching for inspiration at the moment.
Have you already settled on the theme for your next book?
More or less. I want to do a romance story next.
You'll help me gather some references, won't you?
There is a tinge of teasing suggestiveness in her tone as she says that.
Heehee! First place again!
TB clutches a towel with one hand and gestures a peace sign at me with the other.
Aren't I super? Amazing, even? The best ever, even?
Securing even bigger trophies will be a breeze if I keep this momentum up!
Right...
Following her graduation, she became an athlete to take advantage of her physical abilities.
She is on course to achieve even greater athletic feats in the world at large.
Remember, eyes on the prize. You don't want to get complacent.
Of course! You just wait and see!
My vision gradually returns to me, and a scene takes form.
Looks like a living room.
It is decorated with cute furniture and furnishings, creating a very familial atmosphere.
Warming sunshine permeates through the curtains, making me feel naturally at ease.
Akashi did say TB would be here "shortly"...
Maybe I should do something to welcome her.
Yeah, I think I'll make the place look nice.
However, upon closer inspection, it becomes clear that there is nothing TO tidy up. The living room is clean and orderly.
Never mind. I'll just sit and wait.
All of a sudden, I feel tense.
Whew...
I take a deep breath to relax while I look at the clock.
I should've asked when exactly TB would show up...
Just as I start to worry, there is a soft knock-knock on the front door.
I briefed TB on the details of my plan before I went in and more or less got her acknowledgment.
While in this virtual space, all her functions save for her most fundamental cognition are disabled, and she can't access her memory in the real world.
This is so that she can get an authentic experience of growing up.
I knew what I signed up for, but I wasn't expecting TB to be this tiny.
That said, my surprise quickly gives way to a sense of responsibility.
That's right – I made a promise to her, so I must help solve her problem.
Welcome home, TB.
Your business is booming and it's clear that you don't need any associates.
And yet, you've come to me for help, but won't show me any respect or even address me as "ma'am." Do you expect that to work for you?
TB has become a big shot in the business world and projects a staggeringly intimidating aura.
After graduating, she set her sights on bringing home her own bacon.
She started at the bottom by working part-time at a store, then climbed the ladder step by step until she became a rising star in finance.
Seeing the stately manner she presents herself, it feels almost like she has changed into another person entirely.
Whew... I finally got them out of my hair!
Why are you looking at me like that? You won't get leeches like those people off your tail if you don't play tough!
Ugh. Being at the top isn't all it's cracked up to be. Working sucks! I just wanna visit the hot springs with you again!
She bursts into a whining fit.
Inside, she is still her old self. Thank goodness for that.
Tadaaah! Look at all this! I'm running the place pretty well, wouldn'tcha say?
It's exhausting work day in and day out, but it's more fulfilling and fun than any other job out there!
After graduating, TB yearned for a very different lifestyle, and so she took over a farm.
The farm had been in decline for some time, but she slowly turned it around with hard, honest work. It's now more prosperous than ever.
Hey, think you could help out with a few things? It's a good workout and builds muscle, too.
Oh, I'll pay you for the trouble, of course!
No need to pay me. I'll help anyway.
Heheh. Alright, then be a dear and feed ol' Daisy here.
Her ponytail flutters for a little as a calm breeze blows by.
What wonderful weather we're having today.
TB graduated with no particular hobbies or remarkable skills. She took a back seat and simply drifted wherever life took her.
Now she works a run-of-the-mill, unremarkable office job.
A ceaseless stream of phone calls, a paperwork stack with no end in sight, and long, late-night overtime shifts that leave bags under the eyes...
If she got a second chance, maybe she wouldn't have to live such an exhausting life.
My parenting attitude of live and let live proved too lenient, resulting in TB losing interest in everything.
After graduating, she chose a life of doing absolutely nothing.
All she needs to be content are video games, soda, and fried chicken.
It's dubious that she will even set foot outside her room again.
Is... that it? It's over?
It is, nya!
Akashi?! What are you doing here?!
Myahaha! I'm the developer, so it only makes sense for me to appear in the credits, nya!
Besides, don't you have questions for me, nya?
Well... Yes, I suppose.
For one, what's this about a final ending?
Nya?
If you want to know, you should ask TB directly, nya!
And in case you're wondering how TB can be here – it's a trade secret, so don't ask, nya.
(I was going to ask that next, but never mind, then.)
I'd better get going now, nya. You two have a nice chat, nya!
Akashi vanishes into thin air, and not much later, I come face to face with TB.
Orders received. Analyzing... Analysis stopped.
Sorry. I aborted the analysis process prematurely because I don't want to answer this question.
To explain what your parenting was like, to me, it was the feeling that is commonly defined as "fun."
However, the source of this feeling cannot be rationally explained by the concepts currently in my database.
To borrow an expression, "It's strange."
Spending time with you inside the virtual space – and knowing that I can count on you no matter my choice of career – filled me with a sense of security.
Even when I'm tired, I can overcome anything as long as I'm with you. Your presence is reassuring.
TB...
What is it, Commander?
Maybe I'm just touched, maybe I'm just surprised... but you sound a little different to how you usually do.
My change in tone is likely based on the feedback received during your parenting. I can adjust it if you don't like it.
No, I like it the way it is.
I know it's odd for me to say this, but... as your guardian, I clearly still have some learning to do.
All I want you to know is this – no matter who you grow up to be, you can always count on me, and the port will always be your home.
I do not require a place to dock. I get the feeling that your statement with regard to a "home" was rhetorical.
I can with ease sense the feelings embedded within your words. Commander, before we go, I would just like to say... Thank you for everything.

That's right – I made a promise to her, so I must help solve her problem.
Welcome home, TB.
TB stares at me with eyes brimming with curiosity.
While I'm used to the shipgirls at the port staring at me, it feels different when little TB does it. It's making me feel oddly flustered.
So, uh... Do you remember who I am?
Co-man-dur?
Incredible...
You just called me Commander, didn't you?
She must be mistaking my question for an instruction and begins to repeat the word.
Com...man...der?
Although she is struggling with the pronunciation, she just gave me a glimpse of her astonishing language-acquisition ability, having learned a new word instantly.
At the same time, her referring to me as "Commander" at such a young age somehow doesn't sit right with me.
If I'm going to ask her to call me something else, now would be a good time.
Now that that's settled, what do I do next?
TB is still standing there, staring at me inquisitively.
I decide we should sit down and relax. I gesture towards the couch for her to take a seat.
Hmm...?
She tilts her head to the side. She doesn't understand what I mean.
I take her hand and lead her right to the couch, with some difficulty.
How about we sit down and rest our legs?
...Okay.
Before I can reach down to give her a hand, she climbs up on the couch with her own strength.
Wow. This is a novel sight.
Hmm...?
Never mind. TB, this is going to be our home from now on.
Resting her jaw on the backrest of the couch, she shifts her gaze from place to place around the room.
...Not listening, huh.
And so, my life with TB inside the virtual world begins.
Alright, that's all the ingredients chopped up.
Despite all this being virtual, I can feel the texture of the ingredients and smell them as though they were real.
Man. The things you can do with money...
I remember the fee I paid to Akashi to develop this device, and my eyes start to water.
That's when I feel something tugging on the sleeve of my shirt.
It's TB.
Are you hungry? Dinner will be ready soon.
She does not even pretend to react, she simply stares at me without a word.
What's up, TB?
Uhh...
She extends her arms like she expects a hug.
Do you wanna help me cook?
Yeah...
On one hand, the kitchen is a dangerous place for a young girl. On the other hand, she'll never grow if she doesn't get to do anything.
I bring in a kiddy stool and add some stability to it so she can safely stand on it.
This... round.
She holds up a potato I have yet to dice and makes a gesture I don't quite understand.
Cut in four... simmer with black stuff. Yummy.
I try my best to make sense of what she's trying to say.
Red before thing, chewy... Made my jaw tired.
Oh, do you mean the meat and potatoes stew I made?
That's my guess at what she means by "red before thing." I messed up and burned it. Maybe she liked it despite that?
She answers with a nod.
Do you want to watch me make it, or do you want to help?
Help!
There is no change in her tone of voice, but somehow, I can tell that she's excited.
I get out a box of child-sized cooking utensils and hand her a knife.
Just be careful when you're using it.
(It's wild how this house really has everything. Akashi is nothing if not thorough.)
With TB's help, if you could call it that, the stew came together beautifully.
Picking up a spoon, I scoop up some food and offer to feed her.
However, she ignores the food and instead takes her own cutlery and mimics what I just did, albeit unnaturally.
They grow up so fast...
No, what am I saying? Get it together, me. You're not a helicopter mom.
Just as I start to get uncharacteristically emotional from witnessing her growth, I once again feel a tugging on my sleeve.
Aaahh.
TB moves a forkful of broccoli in front of my mouth.
Uhh...
Mouth. Open.
Though she makes no facial expression, she looks very happy.
She's imitating a mother feeding her child. Maybe this feeding behavior is her way of trying to understand something.
Aaahh.
Seeing that I didn't do as she asked, she tries to spur me on again.
Aaahh.
I open my mouth comically wide and chomp down on the broccoli.
Our fun little mealtime comes to a close not long after.

Aaahh.

It has gotten very late.
And yet, TB doesn't seem tired in the slightest.
Don't need bedtime... Not yet.
Her list of memorized words has grown, and it's becoming easier and easier to understand her.
But you do. You'll never grow up if you don't sleep.
Oh, I know. How about I tuck you in and get you sleepy?
This is very clearly parent-child stuff... but I'll do it for her sake.
The only question is – what should I do to make her sleepy?
A lullaby should do the trick.
I'll get a picture book and read it to her.
It didn't take long to lull her to sleep. I took the virtual reality device off and handled some work at the port. After a while, though, a thought started gnawing on me.
I should check on her... Let's go back in and have a look.
TB must have rolled over in bed a lot, because half of her blanket has slipped off her.
Zzzzz...
Hugging her plushie tightly, she snores quietly and softly.
(I'm curious about that plushie she always has her arms around. What is it even supposed to be?)
That's what I thought it was at first glance, at least. Now that I look closer, though...
Yeah, that's definitely not a jellyfish.
But if it's a rabbit, where is the nose? And why is its body shaped like that?
It looks more like some sort of sea creature, though I'm not sure what, exactly.
(Whatever it is, it's pretty cute.)
I adjust the blanket so it fully covers her again.
She doesn't react whatsoever and keeps on sleeping like a baby.
The moonlight shines through the window and pierces the curtains. Looking at TB like this, it feels like I'm seeing her face for the first time.
Zzzzz... Mhm...
I hear a quiet mutter. For a second, I'm not sure if it was TB muttering in her sleep, or if it was the sound of my own breaths.

TB, do you want to try doing it yourself?
...Yeah.
After tying her bang up with a hair claw, I put her up on the bathroom chair.
She has a puzzled look on her face, like it's her first time seeing a mirror and sink.
There are two me's...
You mean your reflection? Yeah, there's two of you.
She looks... different.
She sure does. The you inside the mirror moves in the opposite way you do.
(I'm starting to talk like her...)
When you're with a small child like her, something inside you makes you want to speak on the same level as them.
Unlike most kids, though, TB is remarkably well-behaved.
I don't know whether it's because her common knowledge is lacking, or that she views the world differently than most, or if it's because...
Never mind. Thinking hard about it won't yield any answers. What's important is being with her as she grows up.
There we are. Perfect.
And so, a new day begins.
