*knock knock knock*
Strange... Her Majesty should be in her room with Belfast around this hour...
Pardon, Your Majesty. I'm coming in.
Warspite opened the door to Queen Elizabeth's lavish office.
However, the queen was not there, and neither was the maid who accompanies her almost at all times.
She searched all over Scapa Flow, but could not find a trace of Her Majesty. The concerned Warspite called for a meeting.
Yesterday, the ceremony to celebrate Scapa Flow's reconstruction was cancelled. Today, something even worse has happened...
Her Majesty has gone missing, along with Belfast, Sheffield, and several of our blueprint ships.
Now, this has happened before. During the last major operation at Scapa Flow, she took the Royal Maids with her to survey a Singularity.
This time is different, however. She's left no written message explaining her absence. Assuming she has already left these islands, she could be anywhere right now.
Ladies of the Royal Knights, do you have any idea where she may have gone?
Afraid not. As you said, Her Majesty took the Royal Maids with her during her expedition into that Singularity. The Royal Knights entrust them with matters of secrecy by a matter of precedent.
Vanguard, you're part of Her Majesty's palace guard. Did she tell you anything before she left?
She did not. Being the head of the patrol fleets here, I can however say that she did not sail out of Scapa Flow.
Yesterday's air raid put us on high alert, so I deployed additional patrols around the area.
Even if she snuck out very early in the morning, there is not a chance she could've left undetected.
Especially not considering she made off with an entourage of maids and blueprint ships.
The fact she took the blueprint ships with her is puzzling. The Royal Maids should be plenty for a covert operation.
So, if nobody saw her leave Scapa Flow, yet she is nowhere to be seen, that leaves only one possibility... The Singularity.
You're saying she went through the gate to that Mirror Sea we've discovered?
"Camelot," was it? Why would Her Majesty go there?
After the battle, we continued investigating the Mirror Sea and found a teleportation device that seems to lead to a number of other places.
The name Camelot applies to not only the Mirror Sea, but also to the teleportation device and all facilities connected to it.
And the way to it is through the gate we have here at Scapa Flow.
In essence, our gate here at Scapa Flow is the bridge to a hub world of sorts?
Correct. I suspect the reason Her Majesty left, then, is to search for a cure for Hood's illness in Siren territory.
In that case, I have a theory as to why she took those blueprint ships with her.
If we assume that the Black Cube corrupts the foundation of our hulls, the defense mechanisms of regular shipgirls like us may be insufficient to deal with these effects.
On the other hand, the hulls of blueprint ships are imprinted in a completely different manner that may allow them to fare better.
Do you think Her Majesty planned this expedition in advance, and that's why she invited them to the ceremony?
I wouldn't go that far. Her Majesty couldn't predict Hood would become bedridden from her illness.
True. If Hood had a say in the matter, she would never let others risk their well-being for her sake. Yet, we cannot simply stand by and watch.
Of course not. But rushing on an expedition into a Mirror Sea with no support is just reckless.
I agree. This is quite unlike how she conducted herself during the last operation.
That one was much better organized. Her Majesty had the Iron Blood's cooperation as well as information about the META, giving the Royal Maids a chance to conduct a preliminary survey.
Their thorough preparation was the only reason the Naval HQ was deceived into thinking that Friedrich had captured Her Majesty.
Indeed. This time, she has no such advantages, and we have no idea where Camelot leads to.
She must have a good reason to have done all this...
Last evening, I informed her it would take very long to survey Camelot. I hope that had nothing to do with it...
Let us make doubly sure before acting. Vanguard, have you heard of unusual activity in any of Scapa Flow's facilities?
I have not. The guards I assigned to this building claim Her Majesty retired here for the night without incident. Naval HQ's representatives have done nothing out of the ordinary, either.
It seems Camelot is our only bet, then. We've no other leads to go on.
Let us not be too hasty, King George.
If we find Her Majesty in Camelot, all is fine. However, if she has used the teleporter to go to a different Mirror Sea, then what we're facing is a major emergency.
Precisely, which is why I'm so concerned about Her Majesty's wellbeing.
You misunderstand. I am saying we must not act without thinking first.
Vanguard is right. We need to plan ahead for the possibility that Her Majesty cannot be located within Camelot.
To add to that, Naval HQ would become deeply suspicious if both you and King George went missing in addition to Her Majesty.
So allow me to make a proposition – you two shall stay here, and I shall lead a small search party into Camelot.
My fleetmates and I make up a formal Mirror Sea expedition fleet. We've been briefed on them and should be able to respond flexibly to whatever we encounter.
Upon my honour, we will find and bring Her Majesty back safely!
In the meanwhile, I ask that you provide us with all the support you can, and that you keep the gate to Camelot guarded and maintained.
Hmm... You make a good case. I'm in favour of entrusting the task to a select few specialists.
Sending in all the search parties we can muster wouldn't be more efficient. It would only result in chaos and many casualties.
Indeed it would. Vanguard, you face a monumental task, but I put my faith in you.
Seems we have our Mirror Sea expedition team. Vanguard, Indomitable, Jervis, Janus, Revenge, and Bellona.
I should feel confident that Vanguard is leading this fleet, but I still can't shake my sense of unease.
I fear that she may lose herself in the fighting and lose sight of our goal...
You've nothing to worry about. Yes, she rarely gets to fight and becomes a little overexcited as a result. But...
In times of crisis, she knows what must be done and she does it. She wouldn't put herself over what's important.
Now, changing topics... We need to come up with an excuse to explain Hood's and Her Majesty's absence.
I'll deploy a reserve fleet outside Camelot, just in case we need it.
The fact remains that it's Siren territory, even if we have explored Camelot before. Better to be safe than sorry.

sequence: It wasn't long ago the events at Scapa Flow unfolded.
The Iron Blood rebelled against the Sirens, igniting a battle that would finally bring an end to one of their leaders.
This sent shockwaves across not just the Azur Lane and the Crimson Axis, but the entire world.
While they all processed the news, the Royal Navy embarked on a secret expedition into their Singularity.
Now they set out once more, in search of a cure for the Black Cube's corruption.
Vanguard leads the foray into the unknown, in pursuit of the missing queen.
What awaits them inside the fabled land of Camelot?
The Holy Grail? Or something even greater?

scripts.say: Location unknown - Teleportation device
Here we are at the second set of coordinates... I already see equipment similar to what's in Camelot littering the place.
The last location was covered in woodlands. This one has some sort of structure instead.
They don't look Royal in origin. They're more reminiscent of something from the Eagle Union.
I'm reminded of the place the Commander described seeing during that visit to the Northern Parliament. Arcana something?
Safe to assume they're Siren structures connected to Camelot and the META in one way or another.
We have a real laundry list of things to report once we get back. The METAs we met, the samples, this place...
I don't get the feeling we'll find people here, though. The building on that island sticks out to me, so let's go there first.
Vanguard, excuse me, shouldn't I do some aerial reconnaissance before we go anywhere?
Oh, right. Sorry, I'm a bit out of it after parting ways with Renown and Repulse.
You're the leader here – you mustn't go all absentminded on us. Pull yourself together, please.
You're right. Let me get my bearings straight, then we'll continue.
Get your planes to a high altitude ASAP. If the Commander's intel is right, these structures have advanced defence systems.
What in the world...? Forget any defences, I just laid eyes on something far more bizarre.
Huh? What?
That island you mentioned? There are Siren mass-produced ships anchored there.
Blimey... Don't tell me we've got a hornets' nest in our hands here.
But wait, there's more. There's an entire fleet of merchant vessels from all factions parked just next to them.
This reminds me of the time Sardegna investigated that maze... Do you think they could be ships the Sirens captured?
It's possible. The good news is, the Siren ships are all ancient models. We can take them on and win with minimal damage.
Any trace of Her Majesty?
None that I can spot from this high up. We'll need to search the structure's interior if we're to find anything. How annoying...
...Hang on! I can see signs of fighting over by that island!
That has to either be a Siren experiment, or a clash with the META.
Vanguard, shall we have a look there first? We're at a disadvantage if we're caught in a firefight inside the structure.
That, plus we need to remove any potential threats to the gate's integrity.
We're all doomed if we find Her Majesty but lose our ticket back to Scapa Flow.
Sounds like we have a plan, then. Thank god this way I can cruise instead of having to travel on foot.
Cruising beats walking, but fighting's way more tiring. Unfortunately for us, it's looking like we'll need to do just that.
Location unknown - Mirror Sea
It seems they dispatched them quickly. There's not a Siren left in sight.
I hope it was Her Majesty's fleet.
We'll know before long. There's a battle taking place just up ahead.
Look's like it's... Monarch! Why is she all by herself?
Strange. Her Majesty, her maids, and our other blueprint ships aren't with her.
The question is if she's truly our Monarch, or someone else... Her identification signal checks out, for what it's worth.
If it is her, that means Her Majesty has gotten separated from one of her escorts... A bad sign.
Salutations! I am Vanguard, head of Her Majesty's Mirror Sea Expedition Fleet! Monarch, please confirm that is you!
Vanguard! So it was your fleet Warspite referred to when she spoke of that "expedition team."
Phew. It really is you. How did you get here? Through Camelot, like us?
Yes. I can only assume the situation must be dire if they sent you into this place.
Tell me, do you know where Her Majesty has gone?
We were hoping you'd know. She, Belfast, and a number of blueprint ships were declared missing just this morning.
I did see Her Majesty not long ago, actually. I activated Camelot to go to a Mirror Sea, where I encountered an indescribable foe.
Her Majesty and her entourage ended up there as well. We fled together, but after warping to a random location, I found myself here, alone.
It sounds to me like there's a very good chance Her Majesty is somewhere in this place as well. Don't worry, we'll find her – it's why we're here.
Indomitable, tell Janus to send in reinforcements. I don't know who this "indescribable foe" is, but I'm not taking any risks with someone who forced Her Majesty to flee.
Will do. Incidentally, this is my first time seeing a blueprint ship in person. It's a pleasure.
They're a rare sight, as they seldom get to participate in regular operations. Well met, I'm Jervis.
It seems you've been injured. Allow me to patch you up.
Thank you. I feel emboldened, knowing I have you all to watch my back.
Well, well, it seems a challenger has appeared.
Challenger? Um, Bellona, now's not the time for a duel...
I know you'd like to spar with Monarch, but this is a Mirror–
She's not talking about me, Revenge. Look.
About time you all showed up! What took ya so long?
Oi! It's Purifier!
Yeah, it's me, what's up.
Don't answer that – what's up is, on top of you being late, you smashed up like six thousand ships when we were SUPPOSED to do this on the quiet!
I suffered the headache of plotting a safe route for you, and you pay me back by putting an entire patrol fleet outta commission!
What, did you think nobody would realize if you just sank everything in sight? Assholes!
What in god's name is she on about?
*sigh*... What's done is done, yada yada. Let's get this show on the road.
Put on your booties, stow away your planes, and form a line. We're going on a field trip, children.
You! The destroyer! ...Are you even a destroyer? Hella stacked for one.
Hang on, this ain't the lineup I heard about. All right, roll call! Raise your hand when you hear your name!
Renown! Repulse! Vanguard! Jervis!
...Some of you called in sick, huh. Oh well, whatever.
Listen up – we're going straight to Point Berth. No detours, no bathroom breaks, nothing.
You're under Antiochus' command while you're here. Don't start anything if you don't wanna sully the good Doctor's name any further.
C'mon, it's time to go see Elizabeth. Y'all ready?
Umm... Was she talking to us this whole time?
No clue. For all I know, she just spent the last minute monologuing.
All I caught was "Elizabeth." Maybe she can point us in the general direction of Her Majesty...
All right, ladies. Let us follow this Siren and see what she has in store for us.
There ya go. Follow the teacher, children. AND DON'T! SHOOT! ANYTHING! I swear to god if you do!
Led by Purifier, the fleet made its way into a great facility on an island.
Good gosh, look at these mass-produced ships and defence structures... I've never seen a Siren facility this well-guarded before.
What's more interesting is how they're seemingly completely unaware of us.
It appears she wasn't lying about plotting out a safe route. We are indebted to your mastery of the art of stealth, Purifier.
Aww, you're makin' me blush!
...Am I the only one who's feeling even a little tense?
Me, I've given up on trying to make sense of what's even going on.
Don't worry your pretty little heads. This here permanent anchorage is perfectly safe.
The security here's so tight, even those edgelords won't come near it.
Permanent anchorage? What, for shipgirls? Why would you Sirens need that?
Humans totally flipped out after the Richard incident, remember? So, Antiochus started gaining traction because we don't go nuts like your kind.
In any case, once you've picked up Elizabeth, scram back to port and don't ever come back here again!
Also, I'm only gonna say this one more time! DO! NOT! SHOOT! ANYTHING! You already owe us for the damage you've done!
The Doctor's reputation is at stake here!
This is as far as I can go. The permanent anchorage is just up ahead.
You'll find Elizabeth in there. Steer clear of the surveillance cameras and you'll be fine.
Go get her then make a break for it. Don't go messing with stuff, and don't make a damn scene!
Not to be rude, but you've been making a scene since we first met you...
What was that, you little–
<Protocol revision. Task "Mainframe Protection" has been prioritized over "Reenactment." Immediate action required to preserve branch.>
...What? You gotta be shittin' me, Observer! You want me to take THAT thing on by myself?! Ugghh!
Purifier suddenly became possessed, and just as suddenly went back to normal. Without saying another word, she turned her back on the shipgirls and ran off.
Vanguard, I have a clear shot. Shall I?
Hold your fire. She's up to something, but rescuing Her Majesty comes first.
Deep inside Point Berth – a mysterious permanent anchorage within a Mirror Sea – the search party finally located their missing person.
Your Majesty! Please forgive us for not finding you sooner!
If it isn't Vanguard! And Monarch, too.
I commend you for all your efforts.
Your Majesty, are you all right? Please allow me to tend to any of your injuries.
I'm fine. Go give a hand to Cheshire and Neptune in the kitchen instead.
Your Majesty, it is unwise to remain here for long. Kindly follow us back to Camelot.
No need. There may be no clear way out of here, though it is extremely safe.
I know what you're thinking. "But this place is crawling with Sirens." Yes, it's normal to react that way. It took me a while to grasp the situation as well.
In short, this facility – nay, this very Mirror Sea – is for conducting Reenactments.
All of it? Was our encounter with Purifier just before all part of the act as well?
That's right. She's just another vessel for the script, so to speak.
Neptune, Cheshire, and I decided to play along, and she brought us here just like that.
Now, Vanguard and Monarch, fill me in on what happened on your end.
I see... You heard Her Majesty bemoan how hard it'd be to find a cure for Hood, so you decided to take matters into your own hands?
Yes. After activating Camelot, it took me to a destination where I ran into a goblin by the name of Bon Homme Richard. Then Her Majesty appeared and saved me.
There's no defending such recklessness even if you had noble intentions! You nearly got Her Majesty killed!
You're right. There is no excusing it, and there is no denying this was my fault.
My selfish desire for acknowledgement nearly cost us everything...
Please tell me you had some sort of plan! Or did you rush headfirst all alone into a Mirror Sea, expecting to find a lead on a Black Cube?!
I don't have to remind you how dangerous handling one is. Did you think being a blueprint ship makes you immune to–
That's enough. She has already expressed remorse for her actions.
Besides, everyone made it out alive, and your expedition team has procured information pertaining to a cure for Hood. Everything worked out in the end.
There are only two things I'm wondering about... First, Monarch, what exactly were those coordinates you saw?
And second, what drove you to jump into Camelot without any support or supplies?
I'm wondering as well...
It goes beyond plain curiosity. The teleporter cannot be operated by one person. How did you manage to use it?
To answer your questions, the coordinates were already entered on the terminal when I found it.
I hardly even touched anything. I just stepped onto the platform, and the warp sequence initiated by itself.
When it finished, I was in that Mirror Sea with Richard. She urged me to "become META," and when I refused, she attacked me.
Or rather, she subjected me to haunting visions, then she summoned a giant tornado out of thin air.
And just when it was about to take you, Her Majesty appeared, huh.
Correct. After our arrival, Richard did something to Camelot's energy output, causing it to fluctuate horribly.
The tornado would've annihilated not only us, but also Camelot in its entirety if we hadn't resorted to drastic measures to get out of there.
Whoever this Richard is, she has made it clear that not only is she a great threat in her own Mirror Sea, but also that she can manipulate Camelot.
I've no doubt in my mind the whole teleporter incident was a trap laid by her.
(But then... where did the other coordinates leading to those META ships come from?)
Hmm... I've changed my mind. Vanguard, tell Janus to prepare the gate to take us back at once.
Yes, Your Majesty!
Some time later...
"Point Berth"... Bah, it's just a detainment facility with a fancy name. That talk about "the other Elizabeth" being here is all nons–
Elizabeth put her cup of Neptune's tea to her lips, and before she could finish speaking, her vision faded to black.
What's going on...? This isn't where I was a minute ago...
For some reason, Monarch found herself transported from the Siren facility and into the Royal Navy's training grounds she was so used to.
"Gunnery practice finished. Moving on to weapons inspection and maintenance."
This feeling in my head... It's the same as when I met Richard. Bastard! Stop making visions out of my memories!
"That's that done. Next, refining my swordsmanship."
"HAHH!"
The vision showed Monarch hoisting her sword and swinging down with great force.
She is a blueprint ship who sees herself as the embodiment of excellence. Yet she was not allowed to fight side by side with George and Wales. This fact caused her misery.
"If I were as carefree as Cheshire or Neptune, I would never have reached this level of mastery."
"I cannot be like them. I am Monarch. I've pledged loyalty to Her Majesty, and my duty is to one day become the paragon of glory."
"After a day of training and patrolling, the sun sets upon the horizon once more."
"Her Majesty has lauded my potential, but does she truly expect anything from me?"
"It makes me wonder... What is my purpose? Why do I exist?"
The only thing I've done today is disappoint Her Majesty and everyone else...
How am I supposed to redeem myself...
"Why, hello there, Monarch."
"Wales said you'd been hospitalised. What happened?"
"Don't worry, it's just my old wounds acting up a little. I'll be cleared to leave in just three days."
"You brought me lunch? My, you're too kind."
A different memory this time... What the hell is the point of this, Richard?
"I'm afraid this is a bit much to eat alone, though... Oh, I know. Why don't you stay and enjoy it with me?"
I stuck around and decided to confide in Hood after a while of conversing with her.
"No, it's nothing in the way of romance... It's just... I feel miserable, always being kept away from the frontlines."
"We are shipgirls, we are Her Majesty's swords. What purpose do our lives have if we cannot fight?"
...And what purpose is there to my training, if I will never get to see the battlefield like my sisters in arms?
"Hood, you must have an idea of what Her Majesty wants from me. I need to know – how can I seize glory for the Royal Navy?"
Hood did not return an immediate response to Monarch abruptly opening up.
Not because she couldn't sympathize – quite the opposite – but because she wanted to give Monarch a minute to sort her own emotions out.
Hood's style of solving problems is to let her conversation partner speak their mind in full, then she offers her advice.
"...S-sorry. I lost my composure there."
"Don't be. I understand why you feel the way you do."
"All I'll say is this. Glory is not always something tangible that can be grasped."
"What... does that mean?"
"The glory you seek is the feeling of being needed by others – of being admired by others."
"As for what I seek... That would be elegance, of course. Hehe~"
Hood giggled, and Monarch looked strangely reassured. Then, the memory of the patient room slowly dissipated into mist.
"Thank you for coming. It would be my pleasure to contribute to this operation with a speech and tactical advice."
Morale was high among the Royal Navy during Operation Siren. They were eager to join arms with the Eagle Union and repel the Sirens from the NA Ocean.
This goes further back... The other blueprint ships and I were put in the reserve and ordered to guard the Royal Islands.
"Another operation where I don't get the sortie order..."
The handful of girls who weren't part of the operation proper were gathered in a briefing room on the Royal Islands.
"I recognise her... That's Vanguard, of Her Majesty's palace guard."
"*sigh*... Stuck here again while the others brave the frontlines."
"Standing guard during Her Majesty's meetings is an important duty, sure, but I was hoping for a little action."
I felt a strange sense of closeness to her after overhearing her little monologue.
She scarcely sees any action as she's usually tasked with VIP protection... I, meanwhile, am a blueprint ship who is next to impossible to field.
"...It makes me wonder. What is 'glory' to her?"
"As a shipgirl and a Royal Knight, she must yearn to fight alongside her compatriots as well."
"We've both been relegated to benchwarmer duty, it seems."
"Hm? Yeah, apparently. I'm going to be restless for a good while."
"Likewise. Say, you know about the upcoming exercise? Why don't we have a friendly duel around then?"
"I'm up for that. Let me just check if my schedule allows for it..."
"...Oh, it seems sadly not. I have important business on the day of the exercise."
"But rest assured, we will have our duel the next time the circumstances permit it!"
My chance to ask Vanguard how she felt about being excluded from Operation Siren slipped me by...
Looking back at it now, what even was that "important business"?
"Her Majesty may be powerful, but she cannot conveniently summon Sirens out of thin air."
"Therefore, it falls on us to repel the imaginary invaders."
This time, Monarch was shown a memory not hers. The time was right after Elizabeth had made the call to cancel the ceremony.
Huh... This must be when George's fleet set out to intercept the Sirens.
"We've never played the role of Sirens before, but our first portrayal must be convincing."
...What? Does this not mean the Sirens were never responsible for the air raid?
"Hood's illness has flared up, and she cannot deliver her speech."
"To conceal this fact, and to corroborate our coverup story of an air raid, we will need to sink a few of our own mass-produced patrol ships."
Her Majesty truly went to great lengths to keep Hood's declining health a secret...
I'll accompany them on this sacrificial battle. As thanks for giving me this information.
"Make sure their wrecks are left with absolutely no recoverable data or damages that can be traced back to us."
"As for our alibi, it is as follows – we left Scapa Flow and shot down the Siren aircraft, but not before they took out some patrol ships. Understood?"
"Good. Just a few more, and that should do it."
Confirming we've entered the Mirror Sea.
And my, it feels like we've stepped into a fairytale. Sunshine, green pastures, and a silver castle. It doesn't look anything like Scapa Flow.
Because we're not in the Mirror Sea version of Scapa Flow. Change the coordinates on the gate, and it'll take you elsewhere.
In this case, to what they've dubbed "Camelot." That castle means we're in the right place.
It's like being back home in the Royal Islands, strolling through the countryside. The familiar name definitely helps sell the idea.
Indeed. In fact, this place looks almost exactly like how I'd imagine the Camelot from the Royal Knights' stories to look.
Really makes you wonder why the Sirens designed a Mirror Sea like this in the first place...
Who knows? We can come up with whatever reasons we'd like, but the truth is, we can never really understand the Sirens' motivations.
If their goal was to replicate a vista from the Royal Islands, they certainly embellished the details with such an ornate castle.
Assuming they have a motive, the only one I can think of is that they made it this beautiful so we wouldn't want to destroy it.
It sure beats the cold, purely functional architecture we're used to seeing from them. I'll give them that much.
Th-the breeze is so nice and cool...
Watch your step, Janus. You might trip.
It's all right. I'm watching where I'm going.
Ah – these flower petals vanish when you touch them.
Luckily the castle doesn't vanish when you touch the brick exterior. Though it feels more like metal than brick to me.
It's a Siren facility – appearances are only superficial. We're not in the Royal Islands, and definitely not in the Camelot of legend either.
This is a foreign place, and our mission is to explore it. Remember that, and be on your toes.
Now, first order of business – finding the teleporter inside the castle.
The one Her Majesty used to warp to another Mirror Sea, correct?
We don't know that for sure yet. Though I doubt she came here just to smell the roses.
Plus, she surveyed this area before we did. Safe to say she hasn't gotten herself lost in her own second backyard.
Tallyho, ladies. Let's bring Her Majesty home in time for tea.
The flash of a cannon broke the vision into pieces that rearranged themselves into a different scene – the patient room from before.
Hood...
Monarch leaned over Hood in her sickbed and whispered her name, expecting no response.
Medical devices littered the floor all around them, screens showing Hood's weak vital signs updated in real time.
The room was dead silent, save for the sound of Hood's faint breaths.
The sickness caused by the Black Cube had reduced her to this. If someone didn't find a cure for her, the sickness would soon take her.
Before Monarch left for Camelot, she swore a promise under her breath.
"My glory is the feeling of being needed by others... of being admired by others."
"Even when all is lost, my valour to be remembered by none..."
"Need I give my life for the good of all... it shall be done."
Yes. This is just after I'd reached the teleporter.
"So this is Camelot. The Mirror Sea beyond the gate, hidden within Scapa Flow..."
"And this seems to be the device that 'links it to other areas.' Must be a teleporter of some kind."
She paid no mind to the gorgeous greenery around her and instead went straight into the castle hall, as if led by an invisible hand.
"Coordinates? Did Her Majesty leave these? ...No, I know where these will take me."
"Somewhere in this place is a lead on a cure. And I'm going to find it..."
I'm never making the same mistake again. Your visions will not lead me astray.
I am Monarch! I am excellence given form!
Mirror Sea - Castle Dining Room
I guess it's just us two again, sis.
Nothing's changed in the end. Though it was pretty all right having guests over.
Can you believe they came all the way out here to save a friend? Sirens probably have them on their knees.
Indeed. It's a shame there's nothing we can do to help anyone anymore.
Nothing? Vanguard said they have a way out of this place. Their gate, remember?
I'll bet we can catch up with them if we head out right now.
...Wait, you're saying we can leave?
...Oh, lord. I'm such an idiot!
Yes, we must head out immediately. Those girls are likely going to need our help.
If we can relocate the rest of the Ashes so we can fight alongside them, we may– AGH!
What's happening...?! My head... Is this the work of–?!
KABOOOM!
Sis, how'd we get here?! And why the hell did Vanguard just shoot at us?!
"Well, my execution was fairly good, but the last part was sloppy."
This... doesn't seem to be an illusion conjured by Antiochus. Look at our appearances – we seem to have gone back in time.
"I'll need to work on it a bit more, but hey, practice makes perfect. I'll nail it soon enough."
"Thanks for taking the time to help me practice my special move today."
"Don't mention it. Your technique is very unique... Would you mind performing it again someday? I'd like to study it for myself."
"Uhh... Yeah, sure. Someday."
"Truth be told, I learned it just from watching someone else. I don't think I can teach it directly, per se."
"That's fine, and thank you. I want to explore its potential as a flashy feint. It could work on some opponents."
...I don't think they realise we're here. You reckon this is one of Vanguard's memories?
I'd suspect so. Perhaps that's why we look the way we did pre-METAmorphosis – Vanguard only knew a Renown and Repulse by these appearances.
"Better start wrapping things up. Someone needs to guard Her Majesty."
"The Royal Maids are plenty for that... but I digress. A Royal Knight must not be picky about her assignments."
"Hope Bellona won't ask who exactly I learned the move from... If anyone finds out it was an anime character, my life is over."
"...You know what, better not use it at the next exercise. Too risky."
"Good, honest practice and hard work win battles. Not flashy special moves."
Scene change, eh. Whose memory is it this time?
"...Yup, that's traditional stargazy pie, made the same way it has been for hundreds of ye–"
"Please, you don't need to sugarcoat it. It's crystal clear that you think it's nasty."
Seems like there's no branch where it tastes good.
"*sigh*... How deplorable after I spent a considerable amount of time making it."
Oh yeah, it does take a while to make. I'd nearly forgotten.
"I'll ask Repulse for some pointers before I try it again. Renown has told me she knows how to make it good."
Me? Sure, I can show you how to make it.
It's still going to taste rubbish regardless of how you prepare it, though.
Sis, I know you complimented the flavour and all, but you didn't have to clean your plate just to be polite.
Pardon? I wasn't being polite. It was genuinely delicious.
You're serious? Then you've got some very unusual tastes.
"Erp... Forgetting about the pie for a second, what's for supper tonight?"
She'll be starving when that rolls around. What DID Jervis make for supper back then?
Lasagna, was it? Filled with stringy Sardegnian cheese. I only remember it 'cause we all loved it so much.
"...Sardegnian lasagna? All right! I can hardly wait!"
Hang on, this feels familiar... It's one of our memories, isn't it?
"Eyy. Right on time."
"Actually, you're late, Antiochus. Or should I call you Purifier?"
"Uh, no? You guys just got here early."
"And without smashing up our stuff on the way, at that. Wish ol' Enterprise would be as well-behaved as you."
"Now remember, this is a stealth mission. I've got a safe course plotted out that'll get ya right past security and inside Point Berth."
"Wonderful. The less I have to fight, the better."
"If you're not raring for a fight then stow away your damn planes! You wanna save Elizabeth, you gotta holster your weapons!"
"All right, all right. Goodness, you Antiochus sure have gotten expressive over time."
"Excuse me, melon mounds, I've been expressive since day one."
"I meant in terms of your personality. You used to be so robotic and alien."
"Oh, that. That's 'cause Observer's been promoting learning more about human civilization and culture and stuff."

KABOOOM!

*yaaawn*... It's all so tranquil it's making me sleepy.
