Oh, if it isn't you, Master. With an entourage of Sakuran ladies, I see. Are you here to ride the merry-go-round?
Gloucester nimbly hops off the horse, lands right before me, and bows her head.
That was a professional stunt. Please don't try to replicate it.
Hah. Don't do it, huh? Watch me.
With a fearless grin and an acrobatic maneuver, Kaga jumps onto the still-moving merry-go-round.
Miss Kaga...
Heehee. I never knew you had a playful side, Kaga.
Well... Let's get on, shall we?
Aye. Let's.
Once the merry-go-round comes to a stop, each one of us picks a horse and sits.
Then, the ride slowly spins up again, going round and round at a gentle speed.
As I start pondering what ride to go on next, a firework goes off in the night sky above.
Oh! The first fireworks round has started!
Seemingly in response to that, more fireworks shoot into the sky.
Their light paints everything around them in beautiful vivid colors.
There you are, Commander!
Ark Royal appears out of the blue. I couldn't hear her coming since the booms of the fireworks muffled everything else.
Oh, hi. Were you looking for me?
Not just her, lots of people have been looking for you!
Come on, follow us to the castle! There's no time to lose!
Trust me, you won't want to miss the best part of the fireworks show!
The veil of night descends, and the park's lighting shines even brighter.
If I remember right, it should be riiight... here.
Yaaay! The spinning cups!
Mutsuki jumps for joy and runs toward the attraction at full speed as soon as she sees it.
Watch your step, or you'll trip!
Akagi looks at me and Amagi and hesitates for a moment, then runs after Mutsuki anyway.
Heehee.
What?
It's nothing. Seeing her like that, I just couldn't help but laugh.
True. Also, there's a thing I've been wondering about...
It started as just a vague hunch, but seeing you smile, I'm sure about it now.
Oh? What are you sure about?
That you didn't create this dream just for me to review redesign plans for the amusement park. I'm right, aren't I?
If you feel you're certain about it, then there is no need for me to answer.
You already know it in your heart. You know how I think.
She looks at me with clear eyes that make no attempt to conceal a smile.
Commander! Dear sister!
Come here!
Of course. I'll be right there.
Let's go, Commander. Akagi and Mutsuki are waiting for us.
Right.
When we arrive at the spinning cups – technically, they're honeypots, but I digress – Mutsuki's eyes already gleam with anticipation to get on.
They're like cotton candy – big, round, and sweet!
I wanna ride them!
Settle down. You have to wait for them to stop first.
Okey-dokey!
The attraction comes to a stop, and she boards a cup immediately.
Ride with me, Akagi!
Does it HAVE to be me?
She doesn't display this affection for you every day. Why not indulge her, right?
Yeah! Play with me, please!
Fine, if you insist...
Akagi shakes her head reluctantly, then sits in Mutsuki's cup with an exasperated expression.
We should ride it, too. Give me your hand and I'll help you get in.
Certainly. Thank you.
All of us take a seat, and the cups start to gently spin around.
What's the matter?
Ordinarily so calm and collected, Amagi looks both tense and confused for some reason.
Oh, it's nothing... It just occurred to me that this feels somewhat like a date between us.
Although we were alone in the castle before, the mood feels quite different now than it did then.
Meanwhile, in the background, the second round of fireworks begins all of a sudden.
Their vivid lights illuminate the dark sky. From their light, I can see myself reflected in her mirror-like eyes.
Commander, this has been a wonderful day and a wonderful dream for me.
A tinge of pink crosses her fair cheeks.
She stretches out her hand and meets mine, locking fingers with me.
I swear that I will never, ever leave you.
Not in this perfect dream, nor in reality once we awaken.
Comainder, Amagi, what are you doing?
Ah!
Caught off guard by having her name called, she instinctively tries to pull back her hands.
But, after a moment's hesitation, she just wags her tails and hides our joined hands.
We're talking about the fireworks. Look, over there.
Whoa! Fireworks! So pretty!
Heehee! Riding the spinning cups with the Comainder is so much fun!
You're not with the Commander, you're with ME, remember?
Yeah, but... Hey, are you upset?
No. Not really.
The cups come to a complete stop and we get out. Mutsuki, however, still hasn't had enough fun.
I wanna ride something else!
Sorry, but we have to go home. It's closing time.
Alas, it's over already...
Akagi sounds vaguely disappointed about this.
Not quite, Commander. There are a few quick things we could still do.
Allow me to look after Mutsuki.
Yaaay! I get to have more fun! Heehee!
In return, please keep Akagi company.
Wait... Me?
Amagi smiles and pats Akagi on the hand, then takes Mutsuki and leaves.
Alright, well... Should we go somewhere?
(She hatched a plan so I could be alone with the Commander... Thank you, dear sister. I will not let this opportunity go to waste. Heehee...)
Yes, let's! I'll gladly accompany you no matter where we're going♡
Oh, but if I may make a suggestion – next time, won't you ride the Ferris wheel with me, please?
There'll be no one to disturb us. We'll be all to ourselves. And then... Heehee...
(Once we reach the peak of the Ferris wheel, I'll kiss you and pledge my eternal, unwavering love to you.)
Alright. I promise we'll do that.
It's going to be so wonderful! Hehehehe...
She lets out a sweet laugh, then extends her hand and wraps her little finger around mine.
It's a pinky promise! We've officially struck an agreement, you and I♪
Her reddish tails wag joyously while brilliant fireworks burst in the sky.
This moment feels like an eternity.
Port - Office
I wake up bathed in gentle morning sunlight. After a big stretch, I lightly rub my sleepy eyes.
Memories of Dream Park are still fresh in my mind. I can still clearly remember specific details of it.
(I have so many good memories from that dream.)
(But now isn't the time to reminisce. I need to go tell Akashi to stop what she's doing.)
I waste no time and call the cat.
Good morning, nya~ Anything wrong, Commander, nya?
It's about the amusement park remodel. I came up with a new idea I'd like to move forward with.
You don't need to make those demos we were discussing anymore. Get some rest.
Nya? A new idea?
Okay, nya. Then I'm gonna take a little cat nap, nya...
Sorry for canceling all of a sudden. I appreciate your work.
If you need a favor, let me know.
Nyahaha~ That's all I needed to hear, nya!
I hang up, pick up the pen and paper left on my desk, and try to replicate the park I'd dreamed of.
But I'm interrupted by a knock at my office door.
Come on in.
A familiar friend opens the door and enters with a kind greeting.
Commander, good morning.
Heehee... I see you've made your decision.
Yeah. All thanks to that dream.
But I would appreciate some help nailing down a few details. I'm not sure if my idea is complete enough.
You, of all people, asking for my help? Why, I'm honored.
Unfortunately, I've already brought in someone more suitable for this matter.
Oh?
Planning facilities and rides will require more detailed documentation than a dream can provide, no?
Not long after, Akagi and Kaga enter with thick bundles of documents in hand.
Akagi and I slapped together this documentation today. Surely this should be enough.
It's still early. If you want, I'd be happy to reorganize them again for you~
Akagi, is there anything you wouldn't do for the Commander?
Sure. That would be great.
Heeheehee... My pleasure♡
My office is filled with the sound of rustling papers for a while.
Staring at papers all day is no good for the eyes. Commander, might I suggest a break? I can make tea and sweets for everyone.
Sounds good to me. Thank you.
By the way, Commander... I had an odd dream last night.
Oh? Tell us more.
Well... At first, it was a nightmare about an amusement park. But it turned into a good dream along the way.
I don't remember the details, but when I woke up, I felt oddly happy.
Heh, what a coincidence. I had a dream like that, too. At the end of it, I think I was watching fireworks...
Might be because the Commander was telling us about that park redesign plan?
I hear people tend to dream about what they thought about during the day, so it's possible.
While the three of us chat about dreams, Amagi casually strolls in with a tray holding sweets and a kettle.
After putting the tray down on the table, she produces teacups out of seemingly nowhere and pours tea for everyone.
What were we talking discussing?
The dreams we had last night. By the way, did you dream at all?
Me? Hmm... Yes, I had a lovely dream.
Was yours about a park, too?
Indeed it was. But I've forgotten all about what happened in it...
Strange that all of us dreamed about amusement parks... I'll have to ask Shinano about that.
Consider that proof of just how excited we are for the park.
You may be right. Still, that dream felt so intensely nostalgic...
Amagi grins slightly and offers me a cup of hot tea. Then, she whispers into my ear...
I think everyone left with lovely memories of their time.
Agreed. All thanks to you.
Our eyes meet. We smile.
Hm? What are you whispering about over there? You're not plotting something, are you?
Kaga sounds just a tad exasperated.
Not at all. Amagi was just proposing a secret attraction. Sorry, but it stays between us... for now.
That's right, Commander.
This is one secret that can't be revealed just yet.
After leaving the castle behind, I go for an aimless walk around the water area.
Milooord!
I turn to where the voice is coming from, and I see Ryuujou rapidly going down a big water slide.
Just as it looks like she's going to land in the water, she leaps into the air and does a forward somersault, landing on an inflatable pool toy.
Behold! The Meandering Megamanjuu Dragon Slide! The most popular attraction at the park's water area!
Each time I slide down it, I feel the might of the winds that grace our port!
Although, I think this slide might be a little too much for you. Hmm, what else could we do...
She pauses to think for a moment, then snaps her fingers like she hatched an idea.
I know! There's a magic show coming up, and from what I've heard, it's going to be good! Let's check it out!
Follow me and I shall take you to it!
Ryuujou leads me away to the performance stage situated in the water area.
The front rows of the bleachers already seem to be packed with people.
Ah, how nice of you to bring the Commander along, Ryuujou.
Watarase stands right up and graciously bows her head to me.
Would you like to sit next to me? The seat is vacant.
Ayase and Suzunami are with me as well, and we'd love to watch the show with you.
Y-yeah... I think it'll be more exciting with you... The show, I mean...
F-forgive me, I'm getting way ahead of myself...
Here, Commander. Go on.
Suzunami pats the seat between her and Watarase, urging me to sit down.
Very well! Then I shall sit right behind you!
Sounds good to me.
I plop myself down. Watarase extends a handkerchief toward me.
Your hair is a little wet. I assume you just got here from the pools.
Please hold still. I'll dry you off.
With a smile, she pats my hair dry.
There, all good now.
B-by the way, Commander... you'll be at the banquet at the castle tonight, right?
There's a banquet happening?
Wait, you didn't know that? Do you not have the park's schedule?
I've got a spare flyer. Here.
Thanks.
So after the show, there's a parade, and then that banquet at the castle... and the day ends with a fireworks display and lights show. Got it.
That's everything! Y-you'll check them all out, won't you?
I know you will. This night is to be relished.
Just then, music begins to play from the stage.
Hey, everyone! I'm Z35, the magic idol! We're gonna make miracles happen today!
O, shining stars! Take my magic and passion and bring color to the world!
Z35 waves her magic wand, and the stage comes alive with glamorous lights.
She then recites a spell, turning water spouts into rainbows and gemstones. The crowd wows in amazement.
Oh my gosh! That was amazing!
Looks like they upgraded the stage tech again.
Shush, you! Don't talk about tech when there's magic happening!
Yes, those stage effects would be sweet when you're playing games.
Whatever tech they have, I want it for myself.
Me too...
Don't be silly, you two. This is way too big for either of you to fit in your rooms.
While I marvel at Z35's amazing performance, a familiar voice rings in my ears.
Chosen one, please lend me your strength.
Huh? Sheffield?
I'm not just Sheffield – I'm Sheffield, the magical girl maid. Come, help me take down the forces of evil.
What forces of evil?
She hardly even gives me time to react before she drags me along, bringing me up on the stage.
Then, all of a sudden, she puts one of her guns in my hand.
Commander, our hero! On my command, use the magic weapon!
You heard her, Master. Prepare to take down those monsters.
Aim for the screen and shoot the foes as they appear!
It was chaotic and confusing, but with Z35's and Sheffield's help, I brought down the evil army.
Woohoo! Amazing job, Commander! You helped us save the world!
Well, I sure didn't expect to be part of the show...
Your courage was truly a thing to behold, Comrade Commander.
You were cool too, Sheffy and Z35! But will you consider adding more superhero stuff for next time?
Think about it – a super magical girl hero! Double the pain for the bad guys!
What? No! That doesn't sound cute at all!
If lack of cuteness is the issue, how about making the villains more adorable?
What if, for example, they were based on Arctic hares? Just an idea...
Yeah, let's save the brainstorming for later...
Like over a bite to eat. I'm hungry. Anyone coming with me?
Oh, I know just the place! They have delicious food in the break area not far from here!
We're in! We're coming with you!
What about you, Commander? Are you coming?
Of course I am.
And so, we all head off for the nearby break area.
When I leave the break area, I spy Yamashiro running toward me in a panic.
Ah, Milord! Now isn't the time to stroll about! Hurry, hurry!
You'll be late for the parade!
Hmm? The parade shouldn't be for a while, right?
Well, yes, but we won't get the good seats if we don't hurry!
I follow her to the starting point of the parade, and we manage to secure good seats.
The music starts as the floats drive over.
Whoa! Hey, Commander!
Guam, star of the port, notices me. She and the other idols on the float wave at me.
Heehee, my Commander's looking at me.
This technically isn't a real idol performance, but I must take it seriously regardless.
I have to make the Commander think I'm perfect...
Noshiro brushes her hair behind her ear, revealing that it's flushed a tint of pink.
Heheheh, thine eyes are already fixed on me!
Hmph! As the queen, my intention was to lead the parade myself.
But Guam was so enthusiastic about organizing all of this... How could I refuse her?
Servant! Stop sitting there and follow my float to the end. Your queen demands it!
Yeah! This parade won't be any fun if you don't follow along and liven things up with us, Commander!
When I get up to follow, I'm interrupted by a roar from the float behind them.
I turn and see a giant, dragon-shaped contraption. Blücher hangs from it by one arm.
Heheh☆ Commander!
It looks dangerous up there. Do you need help getting down?
Heheh☆ Surprised?
This is just a stage effect. Safe as can be!
When I wave at her, her face lights up with joy.
Heheh♡ Do you like it? Awesome AND intimidating, am I right?
I'll admit that it's realistic, but intimidating? I dunno.
Heheheh☆ Y-you don't have to be mean! Aww...
Ooh, do you wanna touch it? It won't bite, I promise!
Immediately after, I hear another voice from atop the float.
Role-playing mode engaged.
Hmph. Bow before me, mortal, and submit to my demands!
Devonshire, dressed in her greater demon outfit, looks down at me chillingly.
Grrr... Why do I have to dress like this?!
I didn't wanna be on this float in the first place! I don't even match you girls!
Heedless of Pamiat's complaints, the parade marches on.
I hop out of the stands and walk alongside the floats.
After Guam and Blücher's floats, the third one approaches...
Commander! How's about an old-fashioned Wild West showdown?
Or you could do something a little more fun with me.
A Wild West float, a demon-themed float, a fairy-tale float...
The parade carries on until it reaches the final float.
This one is like a moving garden, adorned with many cute ribbons, flowers, and the like.
Commandeeer! Get on my special float, nya!
Amagi prepped this Grand Premium VIP Service just for you, nya!
It's this float right here, nya!
Get on this bad boy and dance with us, nya!
Akashi jumps off the float. Before I can answer, she impatiently pushes me toward it and makes me get on.
Everyone else will be here before long, nya!
After a while, the girls from the other floats all gather on this one.
Be careful not to fall, everyone!
Ahaha! Piece of cake for a star such as yours truly! Come on, everyone!
Come and dance with me, servant!
My Commander, why don't you and I make some very special parade memories together?
Heehee. You won't be getting a head start on me!
Waaargh! Too many people!
Shipgirls flood onto the float one after another.
I hope you don't plan to leave us out of the fun!
Awawawa... C-Commander, I'm not good with crowds...
It's okay. Don't be nervous.
Commander, today's parade was a source of inspiration for me.
I have the perfect idea for a new outfit for you. Don't worry – it won't be too flashy.
Cheery music mingles with my friends' voices as they echo through Dream Park.
Yeah... This is a nice dream.
Commander?
Sorry, it's nothing. Let's just enjoy the moment, eh?
We're going to make this the best park vacation we can.
I arrive at the castle near the park's center. The fireworks display has reached its climax.
One by one, they launch into the sky and burst into brilliant flowers of light against the backdrop of the dark sky.
The streaks of red and golden light spread out and fall back down to earth like shooting stars.
Wow... It's like watching stars fall...
Huh? Yeah, good analogy.
I know there are two more rounds of fireworks, but the first one is just the most exciting one!
Yeah!
Look, sis! They're so pretty!
Aye. This view is excellent.
Nagato gazes up at the colorful explosions in the sky. She may not know it herself, but she's cracking a smile.
SNAP!
Whuh?!
Aww! Your smile was so cute I just had to take a pic!
Man, for a polaroid, this sure looks good. Guess that comes with being a photojournalist!
Check it out, Commander!
Alfredo waves her polaroid camera around and hands me the developed photo of Nagato.

options.content: You're right. That's a cute smile.

scripts.say: Heehee! I knew you'd agree!
C-Commander... *blushes*
(It's a shame we can't bring this photo with us. It's just a dream, after all...)
I turn and look at Amagi. She gives me a nod with a sorry look.
Before I know it, the first fireworks round starts coming to a wrap.
One final dense column of fireworks shoots up, painting a wonderful picture in the sky.
What? It's over already? I thought there was gonna be a lights show.
That's what I was told as well.
DING!
Right then, all the lights shining on the castle go out save for one corner of it, leaving it pitch black.
A moment later, lights and shadows start dancing on the castle's surface, reenacting some good old memories we've had.
Are these... the times we've spent together over the years?
Seabreeze Island, the hot spring, the Wild West town, and the cruise ship...
My, my. Whoever planned this show put a lot of thought into it.
*sniffle*... All the fun things we've done... *sniffle*...
D-don't cry... *sniffle*... or you're gonna make me cry as well...
Hahah! All that footage I took came in handy!
After all that fun we had earlier, now we can look back on the sweet memories of the past.
Yes. These memories remind us that even ordinary days spent with the Commander are precious and worth remembering.
The lights and shadows continue changing, synching perfectly with the music. Together, they recite some wonderful stories.
Gradually, the light grows in intensity, illuminating not just the castle but also the smiles on the faces of everyone around me.
Finally, a special firework bursts in the sky, bringing the lights show to a perfect close.
Wow... That was incredible...
Heehee. It was truly a one-of-a-kind experience.
Having said that, I will still watch the second and third rounds of fireworks. The first round gave me some ideas.
Then I suppose we could each do whatever we want next.
Okay! I wanna stay and watch more fireworks! I wanna find better seats for the next round!
Then I have a good idea for you.
Oh, really? Tell us!
The girls discussed things they had to do before the park closes, then went their separate ways.
However, at least one of them remained in the central area.
Comainder! I wanna go on more rides!
Really? Aren't you tired?
Nuh-uh! This fun park is great!
Alright, then let me think...
(It must've taken Amagi considerable energy to build this dream, and Akagi's stay in the nightmare must've been draining.)
(Those two must be exhausted by this point.)
Are you wondering if me and Akagi have enough stamina to continue?
Rest assured, I still have the energy and the will for some more.
Likewise. I've not had enough yet.
Yippee! Let's have fun!
(Well, that's good... Me, though, I'm going to need a less-taxing attraction.)
I skim the list of attractions I've seen, and I find a suitable one.
Here we go. Let's check out this one.

sequence: Beneath the neon lights, people drape themselves in lies to survive, staking their lives on a game.
Who's playing out the script, and who's writing the ending as the flames of explosions light up the streets?
There is but one truth waiting to be uncovered.
By the special advisor of the police force.

scripts.say: Nyahaha, we're finally starting, nya!
So, dear main character, do you remember your lines, nya?
Yes, you're the main character and you have lines, nya.
Have you been so busy that it escaped your memory, nya? That's fine, nya!
Let's skip the rehearsal and go straight to filming, nya!
Wait, slow down. I really haven't even gotten the script, and nobody told me I had a starring role.
All I got was a call from Aoba to come and help her get some material for...
Oh. You two were in cahoots!
Nyahaha! The best kind of script is no script at all, nya!
You're playing yourself, and that's what'll make this such a hit, nya.
Here's the gist: You're a special advisor for the police, and I want you to put your keen deductive skills on display, nya.
Calling all teams, nya. Our star is on set, nya!
Three, two, one... Action, nya!

sequence: <size=25>Chapter 9 - So, Who is It?</size>
<size=25>Scene: Police station meeting room</size>
<size=25>Time：8:05</size>
<size=25>Date: June 27th</size>
<size=25>The next day, you gathered all the suspects in the meeting room, including Instructor Azuma and Officer Zenker.</size>
<size=25>You had already drawn a conclusion in your mind, and now, the whole group was waiting for you to make your judgment.</size>
<size=25>It's time to reveal the results of your sleuthing.</size>

scripts.say: Seven pairs of eyes turn to look at you the moment you set foot inside.
You're greeted by the faces of Police Chief Impero from Criminal Investigations, Officer Zenker from Section Zero, Assistant Officer U-552 from Section Zero...

Officer Neptune from Criminal Investigations Division One, Assistant Officer Z13 from Investigations Division Two, Police Sergeant U-37 from Traffic Control, and Instructor Azuma from the police academy.
Did they all really need a second introduction? Are you getting paid per minute or something?
It's called narrative echoing. It also serves as a reminder for the audience.
Ugh...
Gathering us all in one room first thing in the morning. Again. Found the rat yet, advisor?
It's about time we put an end to this. C'mon, tell us whatcha got. My favorite show's goin' live in a few minutes.
You really live up to your rep, Advisor! I'm impressed you pinned down the infiltrator within just a few days!
That crook will pay for setting fire to our station. So, tell us, who is it?
It's Instructor Azuma! The evidence is clear! Why won't you call her out?
Advisor, remember what I told you last night. Put yourself first.
Regardless of your answer, I'll always be on your side.
Well, what do you have for us? The brilliant Chief Impero waits with bated breath.
The time has come to make the final call. In the end, who is it?
No, it's not.
The time has come to make the final call. In the end, who is it?
You announce the result of your investigation – that there are no infiltrators.
There... aren't any? Are you sure?
Interesting. So that's the answer you've arrived at?
Hang on a minute! How can you say there isn't one? Someone blew up the archives, and that's a fact!
Yeah! And Instructor Azuma attacked me! Why would she do that if she WASN'T an infiltrator?
The answer is: This was all part of an extremely realistic security drill drafted by our superiors!
The fire in the archives was indeed a serious matter, but we put it out quickly.
As for all the suspicious intel we've seen in the past few days, it was bait that the Police Commissioner planted to reveal potential weak links within the station.
All this is to say, there weren't any infiltrators in the first place.
So that's how it was... That information I saw was no more than a red herring.
Officer Zenker, I'm sorry for what I did.
I don't even know what to say... The people at HQ must really have nothing better to do.
This was not only a waste of time and resources, but it also strained our relationships.
...I'm sorry, Instructor Azuma. I had the wrong idea.
Glad we managed to clear up this misunderstanding.
And so, with the fear of the station being infiltrated dispelled, you decide to return to headquarters to give your report.
Well, ladies, this is where I say goodbye. Hopefully, I'll see you again.
Stay safe on your way home, Advisor. I hold you in high regard. May we meet again.

sequence: You bade a warm goodbye to the group and started making your way back to headquarters.
You gave your report to the Police Commissioner, who simply nodded in acknowledgment of it.
Half a month later, it was announced that the Commissioner would go into early retirement and be succeeded by Impero.
Following that, you resumed your work as a regular employee, steadily making your way up the ranks and building your career.
"Focusing on your job and moving up ain't so bad, is it?"
The Neon City Investigator - The End

scripts.say: Aaand cut, nya!
You announce the result of your investigation – that all of them are infiltrators.
A-all of us?! Are you seriously saying everyone in the room is a rat?!
Hold it right there! You can't just say that even as a joke!
Exactly! And let's not forget I'm a victim here! Why are you branding ME as an infiltrator?
You know, this kinda makes no sense!
Over the past few days, you've all been working together to mix up the truths and lies in the info you've given me, sowing confusion. You were trying to throw my judgment off.
Luckily, Instructor Azuma came forth and gave me the truth, which exposed a weakness in your conspiracy.
While it's true that she was responsible for blowing up the archives, the information she provided me with was all factual.
She wanted out of your organization, so you used her as a distraction to divert my attention away from the rest of you.
Isn't that right, Chief Impero?
Impressive, Advisor. Very impressive.
How did you figure out MY involvement in this, though?
Because you're the highest-ranking and least suspicious person of the bunch, yet you tried to get me on your side and convince me to stop.
...And here I thought you'd be smart. What a shame.
Oh well. No helping it now that the cat's out of the bag.
Ya won't be leaving this place. I locked the door.
And I switched off all the security cameras. My advice? Don't try to resist arrest.
Don't worry, we won't kill you. We'll just lock you up for a bit.
Had a feeling it'd come to this. However, you're not the only ones who came prepared.
I AM leaving – through the window!
You're up, Interpol! Get 'em!
Freeze, all of you! We have the building surrounded! Resistance is futile!
Excellent work, Partner! The route to the garage is clear. Hurry on over.

sequence: You turned to the morning sun and jumped out of the window.
As the infiltrators looked on in shock behind you, you slid down the sloped glass and safely escaped the police station.
Not long after, Interpol arrived on the scene.
You were given a medal from the Police Commissioner for a job well done.
Although you had won, you now feared that the remnants of the crime syndicate would seek retribution.
As such, you went off to live a happy life in anonymity in a little-known place under Interpol's protection.
"A normal but happy life ain't so bad, is it?"
The Neon City Investigator - The End

scripts.say: Aaand cut, nya!
You announce the result of your investigation – that you, yourself, are the infiltrator.
Everyone in the room fell into a frigid silence.
YOU'RE the infiltrator?
Come on, Advisor. This isn't the time or place for jokes.
Since I've lost all my memories before this point, it's theoretically possible that I'm the infiltrator, isn't it?
You... do have a point, but you couldn't possibly have blown up the archives, could you?
Remember, I have amnesia. It's theoretically possible that I did it, isn't it?
Okay, but what about the fact that Instructor Azuma attacked me? That had nothing to do with you, did it?
Again, amnesia. It's theoretically possible that I threatened her into attacking you, isn't it?
Hmm... I mean, I guess it's not outright impossible?
Heh. You are a real comedian, Advisor.
I like this bit you're doing. It's genuinely hilarious.
What now, then? Are you going to report back to the Police Commissioner? Or are you just considering ways to escape this place?
I don't know what you mean.
Hrmh... You know what? Forget it. You should get back to headquarters.
There's a car waitin' for ya, Advisor!
I'll come with you, Advisor.
Come again? The Advisor has a report to submit, but you don't have any business there, do you?
And so, having concluded your investigation in a truly astounding way, you got into a car and went back to headquarters.
Well, ladies – until the day we meet again.
Be safe, now...

sequence: The mood was ever-so-slightly awkward as you bade goodbye and set out on the journey back to the police headquarters.
En route, you flipped through the papers Instructor Azuma gave you and made a call to the Commissioner.
But then, just as you did so...
Boom! Your car burst into flames and careened off a cliff.
The next day, the self-incriminating testimony you had left reached the Commissioner's desk. Your fiery death was written off as a suicide fueled by your guilty conscience.
Half a month later, it was announced that the Commissioner would go into early retirement and be succeeded by Impero.
Then, the world simply kept spinning. As though nothing had happened.
"Some jokes are more than just a laugh, y'know."
The Neon City Investigator - The End

scripts.say: Aaand cut, nya!
You announce the result of your investigation – that the Police Commissioner is the infiltrator.
...What? Sorry, Advisor, I just don't follow.
You're... kidding, yes? I refuse to believe that it's the Commissioner.
Now you have my interest. What's your reasoning?
It's a common trope in detective dramas that the criminal is one of the first characters introduced, you know?
Assuming that's true, wouldn't that make the inspector general pretty suspicious?
They were the first named character, yet there were no clues pointing to them this whole time.
Nobody knows their name, their face, or anything about them.
It all raises the question – who ARE they?
Aoba is the inspector general.
Now THAT'S suspicious!
Aoba's also the one who tricked me into coming here under the pretense of "providing some material"!
If that's not sus, I don't know what is!
I hear you. So, what are you thinking?
I'm thinking we should team up, find her weakness, and overthrow her!
Hmm... The brilliant Impero likes that plan.
Alright – head back and be on your guard. Wait for me to contact you, then we'll take her down together.

sequence: The mood was bizarrely soft yet ardent as you set out on the journey back to the police headquarters.
On the way there, you received a top-secret call from Chief Impero.
With her help, you submitted a vague and clever report that wrapped this investigation up with an impeccable bow.
Later on, you and Chief Impero successfully uncovered evidence that Commissioner Aoba possessed a huge fortune of unknown origin.
Aoba was dismissed from her position and arrested. Impero was officially appointed as her successor.
Thanks to your "unique connection" to the new Commissioner, you rose through the ranks at blazing speeds.
In less than three years, you had become the next Police Chief.
Everything was great, and so it went.
"Until the world ends, life is good."
The Neon City Investigator - The End

scripts.say: Aaand cut, nya!
You announce the result of your investigation – that the film's director is the infiltrator.
The director is the infiltrator? Are you serious?
Dead serious.
After being here on the set for the past few days, I've fully figured out the dark undertone of this screenplay.
I know I need to accuse someone of being the infiltrator if I were to follow the script.
But, I refuse!
If you were to force me to just accuse someone, then I'd choose the director – Akashi!
Nyaaa!
Scene, cut, stop, nya! Stop the cameras, nya!
Heh. You think I haven't been preparing for this?
This is no longer just YOUR movie, Akashi!
...Nya? What are you talking about, nya?
I see! So the movie is gonna completely break the fourth wall and get a surprise twist!
This story's scope will also be expanded, with richer plotlines added.
The same cast, the same sets, but with a brand new script! Pretty neat idea, if you ask me!
I actually already have some ideas for the script. Allow me to be the screenwriter.
We should add a ton more cuts, too! And fill the story with adventures!
And special effects, and intense fight scenes, and car chases!
Might even be able to squeeze in some superhero stuff!
I vote to put in vampires somewhere!
Grrr... We can't forget about the fantasy adventure elements!
Yes. I'm ready for just that.
The legendary team of adventurers...
Has come back together!
Yeah... Zzzzz...
The detective drama parts stand to be improved. More big scenes, more international flavor!
What... are you doing, nya?
My film... My precious film, nya...
You're... making it more interesting, I think, nya?
Alright, team! Let's start shooting those extra scenes!
Action!
Eventually, all the filming was done.
Nyahaha – that's a wrap, nya! Great work, team, nya!
We're done already? Aww, I was hoping for more scenes with the Commander!
I was nervous for the entire shoot... I should start making more backup plans.
Nicely done, Commander!
Ah, Memphis, good timing. I wanted to ask you something.
Oh? What?
WHY MEEEEE?!

sequence: <size=25>Chapter 1 - An Alarming Explosion</size>
<size=25>Scene: Police station meeting room</size>
<size=25>Time：19:25</size>
<size=25>Date: June 25th</size>
<size=25>You are a special advisor dispatched from headquarters who's been tasked with finding an infiltrator from a criminal organization within the force.</size>
<size=25>Under the Police Commissioner's orders, every potential suspect has been gathered in the meeting room under the pretense of a safety inspection.</size>

scripts.say: So, new advisor, are you ready?
Azuma? Why are you here?
That's Instructor Azuma to you.
I heard from the Commissioner that my former student was back. Heehee. Did you not want to see me?
(Ah. She's already in character.)
Of course I did. I'm glad to see you again.
Heehee. As am I.
Come on, let's not waste any more time on chitchat. Everyone's waiting inside.
With a smile, Instructor Azuma urges you inside. You steel yourself and enter the meeting room.
(Uh-huh. I see they're forcing the story to progress.)
(Well, I guess it's better than getting no hints at all.)
Six pairs of eyes turn to look at you the moment you set foot inside.
You're greeted by the faces of Police Chief Impero from Criminal Investigations, Officer Zenker from Section Zero, Assistant Officer U-552 from Section Zero...
Officer Neptune from Criminal Investigations Division One, Assistant Officer Z13 from Investigations Division Two, and Police Sergeant U-37 from Traffic Control.
(Thank god for the explanations.)
Ahem. The reason we've really gathered you here is because of an anonymous tip we received about the possibility that a member of an international crime syndicate has infiltrated the force.
I'd like to hear everybody's thoughts on this.
Seeeriously? Ya called us all here just for that?
You just gonna take that tip at face value? Hell, I could just say the Commissioner's our rat, then!
She has a point. The tip lacks credibility if the source doesn't even know of Section Zero.
You know, the people over at Section One's HR department should have detailed records on us. Why don't you start your investigation with them?
(Ah, the HR department. I'll admit, I'm critically short on information right now.)
Where are these records kept?
If I'm not mistaken, I believe they're in the adjacent building.
KABOOOM!
The very moment Officer Neptune finishes speaking, the building that houses the archives explodes with a loud boom, reducing it to a pile of rubble.
As a fireball erupts, the deafening ring of alarm sirens fills the police station.
Wh-what the hell?! Did someone just blow up the archives?!
While we were all gathered here, no less. That means it can't have been any one of us.
Might be able to recover something if we get to it before the flames do. Ugh. Sounds like effort.
One of our very own buildings, blown up before our eyes. They've signed their own death warrant!
That explosion's timing was way too convenient.
I'm leaving to check on the scene. Let's call this meeting adjourned.
Kindly hold on a moment, Advisor! I'll round up Division One and we'll come with you!
Aaand cut, nya!

sequence: <size=25>Chapter 2 - Officer Bunneptune Is on the Case!</size>
<size=25>Scene: Outside the police station's archives</size>
<size=25>Time：20:08</size>
<size=25>Date: June 25th</size>
<size=25>You rush to the site of the explosion, hoping to find clues before they all burn to ashes.</size>

scripts.say: Step aside, officer comin' through!
Have you found any good clues yet, Advisor?
I just got here thirty seconds ago. I've hardly started searching yet.
But now that I've seen the damage, I'm not expecting much.
*cough*... Judging by the smoke, it hasn't finished burning yet. Let's go in and see if anything is still intact.
The building is still on fire, though. Do you think anything will be left once the fire department is done with it?
Suddenly, you hear thunder in the distance. Mere moments pass before a heavy rain begins to fall.
Fantastic news, Advisor! Even the weather is on our side! Now we can begin our investigation.
(Don't comment. You'll only make trouble for yourself.)
Now, let's split up and search for clues. What do you say I take the left and you take the right?
(She wants to split up at a time like this?)
(If Neptune is the infiltrator, then that would be the ideal opportunity for her to destroy evidence and clear her name.)
(Still, acting alone might give me the opportunity to make a breakthrough...)
I've already found something! How are things going on your end?
I-infiltrator? Me?!
How dare you, Advisor? If that's a joke, it isn't funny!
Then what are you hiding behind your back?
Behind my back...?
Forget that – check out these documents. I found Section Zero work records and a letter of grievance!
Aaah! Your back's on fire!
Huh?! Wh-what's going on?! I still haven't...
Yoink!
Let's see here... Twenty chicken kabobs, three servings of wagyu beef, and five bottles of beer?
It's... just a dinner bill?
See? It didn't matter! That's why I said to forget it and focus on these documents!
Aww... Just deceiving this poor, adorable bunny wasn't enough for you? You even accused me of being the infiltrator...
Maybe YOU'RE the big bad, after all.
Sorry. Let's get back to work.
Okay! Let's refocus ourselves and find every last piece of evidence!
Nothing here. What do you have?
Heheh, I got one heck of a bounty. Check it out!
Is this... Section Zero's work record?
Well, the writers didn't do a very good job. One of them is practically blank, and the other one only left a table of contents.
As for the other one, it's a letter of grievance that's too burned up to see anything apart from the complaint itself: "I was arrested for 'walking too fast.'"
Unfortunately, I doubt either of these will be of much use.
Hmm? You've been hiding something behind your back for a while now. What is it?
This is just, umm...
Oh nooo! It's caught on fire! How careless of me!
What?! Give it here!
I'm sorry... I think I got too close to a place that was still burning. It's burned up without a trace.
I waited to show it to you because I hadn't read it for myself yet.
(Suspicious.)
Well, what's done is done. Let's keep looking.
Right. Let's search this place from top to bottom!
Aaand cut, nya!

sequence: <size=25>Chapter 3 - Strategic Date Solution</size>
<size=25>Scene: Police station office</size>
<size=25>Time：08:23</size>
<size=25>Date: June 26th</size>
<size=25>You've determined that the explosion is linked to the infiltrator, but clues are sparse.</size>
<size=25>However, you discover that recent surveillance footage has been tampered with, leading to inconsistencies in the timeline of events.</size>
<size=25>You visit the office of Assistant Officer Z13, who works closely with surveillance, to get to the bottom of this.</size>

scripts.say: Well, well, if it isn't the special advisor!
Just so you know, I'm not slacking on the job! This is what's called a strategic break period!
A break period... Do people normally play computer games when they're on break?
You don't do this at the port, too, do you?
AHEM... Not sure what you mean by "the port." Did you come here just to confuse me?
You've heard of work-life balance, haven't you?
Now get your butt over here, sit down, and game... I mean, take a strategic break with me.
Chief Impero herself approved this!
She did?
Yeah! Heck, she'll go and take strategic break periods at the pub during work hours.
Impero, of all people... Actually, I can see her doing that.
See? So, you're here during work hours. That must mean you're up for a strategic date.
(Do I get straight to the point, or do I let her take the indirect route?)
Careful where you lay those baseless accusations, friend. That's a serious claim.
Let me ask you this, then. When your supervisor goes off-premise during work hours, how do you know where she's going?
You must have seen it through the surveillance cameras.
If you're surveilling everyone at all times but haven't reported anything, then you must be the infiltrator.
Or maybe I'm just a hard-working officer? Have you considered that?
Hard-working, you say?
Okay, then are you aware that the surveillance tapes here have been tampered with?
What? Are you serious?!
Well... Yes. You're the one who did it, no?
That's not even physically possible!
Let's approach this differently. Are you able to investigate who did it?
Hmm. Nope. Also impossible.
All I can do is watch the monitors here. That also means that I do nothing BUT watch them.
But when the explosion happened, well, you were there. I had to go to the meeting like everyone else.
Right. Let's pull up yesterday's video, then. We can watch it together.
Hmm... How do I do that, again?
Sure. You know what would make for a fun date? Me getting a look at that encrypted data.
Huh?! What kind of date are you imagining?
A strategic one, of course.
Hey, no teasing!
Hm? Oh, you want to use my computer directly? But there's only one chair.
Wait, I know! You sit in the chair, and I'll sit in your lap, alright?
I can stand, thanks. What's the password?
Ooh, is this part of the date? Try this: I AM YOURS.
Incorrect password.
Try adding my name to it!
Come on. I'll put my hand on yours while you do it.
Doesn't that get the heart racing?
Just between you and me, my cubicle is in a bit of a blind spot, so we can get up to anything we want and nobody will ever know!
Nope. Incorrect password.
So, umm, Advisor? The thing is... I forgot my password.
Huh?
How about you try just putting in whatever?
Okay... PASSWORD it is, then.
Wait. It worked?
Whaaat?!
Aaand cut, nya!

sequence: <size=25>Chapter 4 - Keeping Peace in the Streets</size>
<size=25>Scene: Police station parking lot</size>
<size=25>Time：09:31</size>
<size=25>Date: June 26th</size>
<size=25>After much effort, you manage to recover the original video. A dark shadow in the shape of a person appears onscreen.</size>
<size=25>You recognize that speedy figure, but you can't place who it is.</size>
<size=25>Unable to get any further on your own, you decide to consult with the experienced members of Section Zero.</size>

scripts.say: A familiar figure, zipping by in the blink of an eye...
Forget the investigation, I've figured it out.
Aoba is the infiltrator!
Bzzt. Wrong, sorry.
Alfredo or Gridley, then?
Bzzt. Wrong, sorry.
Fu Shun? Fei Yuen? Fu Po? Bristol? Gallant?
Shimakaze? L'Audacieux? Le Malin? Le Terrible? Le Triomphant? L'Indomptable?
All of your guesses are wrong. And thanks to your incoherent mutterings, you've attracted the attention of a nearby patrol.
Advisor, whatcha doin' here in the parking lot? Are ya taking your investigation off-site?
You look a little flustered. Need a ride, maybe?
I have some questions for the personnel of Section Zero. Do you know where Officer Zenker and Assistant Officer U-552 are?
I'm not privy to that information. Did you find a clue, or something?
Try me. Maybe I can help ya out!
Aren't you just a traffic cop?
Yeah, what of it? I'm still a real cop! You sound biased as hell, Advisor!
Just recently, I stopped a violent biker gang with nothing but this bad boy!
Anyway, hop on. We can ride and talk.
Where are you taking me?
I'm still on duty, so we're goin' on patrol, of course. Can't get caught slackin' off.
Uh, good work ethic, I guess.
But...
Say what?!
You'd suspect ME when you've seen how seriously I take my work?!
I don't know if I believe you.
Can this dinky little machine actually keep up with biker gangs?
I'm not sure you could keep up with bicycles, frankly.
I can if the gang is walking!
Umm... A walking biker gang?
I mean, can pedestrians actually become a violent gang?
They exist, seriously! That's why someone's gotta do justice!
You know... I'm starting to see why someone filed a grievance for being arrested for walking too fast.
No shot. Someone filed a grievance against me?!
Don't worry about it. It burned up, anyway.
Phew... Good thing.
So basically, you assert that you take your job as seriously as one can reasonably expect.
Hell yeah! Now hop on, already. We're goin' on patrol!
Can this thing handle two riders? We won't be violating traffic laws, or anything?
Of course not, silly. We'll take that patrol car over there!
Let's go, already!
Uh... Aw, man, where'd I put the key...
You were trying to get me on that dinky scooter a minute ago.
Do you break traffic rules all the time?
How... DARE you?!
I'm the best patrol out there! Every year, I get commendations!
True... I haven't heard of you committing any traffic violations.
But that's even more suspicious.
It just means I follow the rules!
Quit overthinkin' this stuff! I'm goin' back to my patrol, so you get back to work, too!
Aaand cut, nya!

sequence: <size=25>Chapter 5 - The Core of the Issue</size>
<size=25>Scene: East Coast sightseeing train</size>
<size=25>Time：17:34</size>
<size=25>Date: June 26th</size>
<size=25>One way or another, you found out where Assistant Officer U-552 from Section Zero is.</size>
<size=25>You board a sightseeing train that loops around the coast and find her. She's sleeping.</size>

scripts.say: Assistant Officer U-552? Why are you... sleeping on this train?
*yawn*... Commander, remember, I'm not an officer right now – I'm a tour guide.
"Commander"?
Oops. My bad, I just woke up. I meant to say special advisor!
I guess since you're here, why not have a little nap?
I'm not tired. So, are you undercover or something?
Yep. I'm dressed as a tour guide and gathering top-notch intel.
*sigh*... I wish I didn't have to work.
Need to act the part. Ahem...
Hello and welcome aboard our sightseeing bus.
Today, we'll be... Uh, what was my line, again?
You sound awkward. Not used to service work, I take it?
Spot on. The reason I picked this job is because no actual tourists ride this thing.
Most people who come on board have some intel. So, basically, I went for the most low-effort thing available.
That makes sense, but...
What? Is being lazy reason enough to get suspicion cast on me?
Not saying that I WAS being lazy. It's just that this sunny weather was... perfect for a nap.
Uh-huh. So, did you hear any juicy intel?
Look. Espionage takes knowledge and, above all else, patience. Being from Section Zero, I need to put more importance on staying hidden than relaying information.
In other words, you haven't.
The core of the issue isn't whether I have or haven't.
What IS the core of the issue is... finding the core of the issue.
And what exactly is the issue at its core?
To find the issue at its core, you first have to find the core of the issue.
Okay. Have you found it or not?
*sigh*... Fine, I admit it. I was slacking off, okay?
But trust me, Advisor, I had a reason for it. Don't make me a suspect just because I was a little lazy.
I DO have intel. I just don't have it on me right now.
So, you have it, but you don't have it?
Exactly! The intel exists, it's in my possession, but I don't have it on hand!
Ahem... I've already sent in everything I've gathered.
It's written on paper, so I can't just show it to you. Sorry.
Who'd you send it to?
Officer Zenker. She should be at this train's final stop by now.
Go talk to her and she should clear my name for you!
...But what?
No, forget it. The weather IS perfect weather for a nap, so I can't blame you.
This isn't a bad opportunity to take a break.
Glad you understand, Advisor.
Although, since there's a passenger on board now, I've gotta fulfill my duty as a guide.
Ahem... Here, special advisor. Please have the latest edition of Tourist's Digest.
Everything you want to know about the local tourist destinations is listed here.
There is also a variety of food and drinks for you to enjoy during the trip. We hope that you'll be satisfied with our selection.
We wish you a pleasant time on this journey.
I'd be even more satisfied if you had any intel for me.
Still, I'm eager to see the fruits of your work.
Uhh, did you have to change the subject like that?
Just try to focus on the sightseeing, okay?
As I was gonna say... Dear passengers, please take your seats. We will be departing shortly.
Aaand cut, nya!

sequence: <size=25>Chapter 6 - Blah, Blah, Blah</size>
<size=25>Scene: Downtown warehouse</size>
<size=25>Time：19:20</size>
<size=25>Date: June 26th</size>
<size=25>With the hint that Officer Zenker possesses crucial information, you stepped off the train.</size>
<size=25>You pursued the address stated in the hint and arrived at a warehouse in the downtown area.</size>
<size=25>After entering, you hear the cry of Officer Zenker from further within the building.</size>

scripts.say: H-heeelp! Somebody heeelp!
Oh, phew. You're here, Advisor. Get me out of here, quick!
Is that you, Officer Zenker?
Isn't this supposed to be Section Zero's secret base? How'd you end up as a captive?
*sigh*... It's a long story.
It all began on a rainy night 13 years ago...
Sure sounds like a long story...
(I can stick to the script here, or deviate from it...)
E-excuse me?!
No, I'm not! You know who it is!
(Talk about a sudden development.)
Who?
Instructor Azuma from the police academy! She's the infiltrator!
She attacked me in order to fabricate evidence and pin all the blame on me!
She's behind all of this! Even the explosion in the archives from yesterday!
Understood. I'll take it from here.
That was a dark, windy night. It's been so long since then, and I still can't forget the things that happened that day.
I was still in middle school back then, and me and my friends were at a party at an amusement park. We had so much fun that we lost track of time.
When I decided it was time to leave, it had already grown late.
It started raining, and since I was alone, I was startled and anxious, so I wanted nothing more than to be home as soon as possible.
So, I ran around in the dark and ended up getting lost.
Sometime later, I spotted two shady figures in dark clothes standing under a dim streetlight.
It looked like they were doing some kind of transaction.
My curiosity got the better of me, so I snuck up to them to try to get a look at what they were doing.
That was when–
While you were focused on them, you didn't realize there was a third person behind you.
They drugged you, and when you woke up, you realized you'd shrunk down to the size of a kid. Correct?
What? No, nothing like that. Although, they did catch on to me.
As I was walking, I accidentally kicked over a can, and they heard the noise.
I got scared and started running, and they chased after me.
No matter where I went, they kept chasing after me, and all I could do was keep running for dear life.
I don't know how long I ran for, but I came to a stop when I blindly bumped into someone.
Instead of getting mad at me, though, she asked me what happened. I explained, and she fought off those two.
It wasn't until later that I realized that the person who helped me... was none other than Instructor Azuma.
Ever since that day, I wanted to be a police officer.
When I got into the academy, I asked for her to be my instructor.
3 years passed in the blink of an eye, which brings us to 10 years before today...
(This is really starting to drag on.)
(Camera film costs money. Money that comes out of the port's budget.)
Hold it, Officer Zenker. Just give me the important parts, thanks.
Who attacked you? How did your assailant get inside the base?
It was Instructor Azuma! I let my guard down, because I never thought she'd attack me!
She's the infiltrator! She was behind yesterday's bombing, too! She attacked me in order to fabricate evidence and pin all the blame on me!
If you're wondering how she knew how to get inside, well, that all started six years ago.
Back then–
Stop! Don't. You've told me more than what I needed.
Last question: When did she attack you? How long has it been since she left?
It was... 30-odd minutes ago! It started when–
Okay, that's enough! I'll take it from here!
Okay! I'm counting on you!
Hey, wait! Before you go, let me loose!
Aaand cut, nya!

sequence: <size=25>Chapter 7 - Discussion Class</size>
<size=25>Scene: Police academy classroom</size>
<size=25>Time：20:42</size>
<size=25>Date: June 26th</size>
<size=25>Thanks to your rank within the police, it wasn't particularly hard to look into Instructor Azuma's activities.</size>
<size=25>You arrive outside the empty classroom, where a familiar figure has been quietly waiting for you.</size>

scripts.say: To think you'd find me this quickly. You really are outstanding.
What should I call you? "Special advisor? Or maybe you prefer, "my precious model student"?
(I can stick to the script here, or deviate from it...)
I don't know – are we talking as colleagues, or as instructor and student?
Heehee. Turning the question back on me. That's my student.
If only the rest were as excellent as you.
You mean Officer Zenker?
Maybe I am. Maybe I'm talking about others.
It doesn't matter. The reason you're here is because you've already drawn a conclusion, no?
You believed what Officer Zenker said?
Then, what if I told you that I'm not the enemy? Will you believe your old teacher?
I'm not about to take either of your words without a pinch of salt. I can't reach a decision without proof.
Speaking of proof, Officer Zenker gave me circumstantial evidence that you orchestrated the archive bombing. What do you have to say to that?
What is true is that I did go to the archives yesterday.
The reason for that, however, was to look for a file for you.

Since I knew you were conducting an investigation, I feared that the crime syndicate may go to some extreme lengths to destroy evidence. That's why I acted in secret while you had the suspects' attention.
As for the results, this is what I found yesterday.
Thank goodness I left quickly, otherwise I doubt these records would've survived – or I, for that matter.
Azuma gives you a file. It contains records that detail how the entirety of Section Zero has long since become a stronghold for the syndicate's several infiltrators.
Even more shockingly, it hints at an even deeper level of infiltration within the police.
My god... This is why you attacked Officer Zenker?
Not entirely. Some of the records in there are actually from their base, recovered by me.
I didn't anticipate that she'd come back in the midst of my search. Luckily, I was the physically stronger one between us.
So that's how it went down... Why didn't you report it, though?
Because, by all accounts, this syndicate has been spreading its roots amongst us for many years now. You're the only person who'd even believe me.
You need to be extra careful now that you've gotten your hands on this evidence.
Trust no one. Anyone could be an infiltrator.
Aaand cut, nya!

sequence: <size=25>Chapter 8 - Night in the Neon City</size>
<size=25>Scene: Downtown bar</size>
<size=25>Time：22:59</size>
<size=25>Date: June 26th</size>
<size=25>After leaving the classroom, you sooner or later wound up outside a bar after having worked out your next move.</size>
<size=25>It had been a long day, and your stomach rumbled at you.</size>
<size=25>Director</size>

scripts.say: (A dinner scene in a bar. I was waiting for it to happen.)
Barkeep! I'll have a deep-fried burger, naval curry, grilled sausage, a plate of Schweinshaxe, escargot simmered in wine, stargazy pie, a Margherita pizza... oh, and an Empery full course banquet!
As soon as you entered, you ordered meal after meal, none of which were even on the menu.
The bartender turned a deaf ear to you. On the bright side, you caught the attention of someone you know.
Mmh... Advisor?
Did you just... finish for the day?
Good timing, then... Come here and drink with me!
Infiltrator? Yeah, that's me... The brilliant Chief Impero is your infiltrator!
Go on, arrest me... I've worked so much I'm starting to feel like I am at my limit... I don't wanna do this anymore...
Do you think being arrested will get you out of having to work?
Hrmh... Guess not... On second thought, don't arrest me...
Let's keep the cuffs off and just driiink!
Yeah... Just got done working overtime.
I've been getting more and more of it lately, and it's seriously killing me.
And you, Chief? How rough do you get it?
Heheh... On paper, I'm working overtime right now...
In reality, though, I'm taking a strategic break.
*gulp gulp*... Ahh! Oh boy, I'm getting light-headed...
You know, Advisor... It's hard enough just coming in to work every day, so why do you have to do overtime on top of that?
I don't get it...
Wow. I respect that, I really do...
In fact... let me raise a toast to you!
Hey, listen to me for a sec, Advisor...
Work is a thing that's... best done in moderation.
Remember, you only get one shot at life...
The time spent not working... that's when you're really living...
When work gets you down... come to the Akashi Bar and have a drink...
TRUE! So true! I'll drink to that!
Hey, listen to me for a sec, Advisor...
Work is a thing that's... best done in moderation.
Remember, you only get one shot at life...
The time spent not working... that's when you're really living...
When work gets you down... come to the Akashi Bar and have a drink...
Listen, the beer at this place is something else... The folks at the Akashi Beer Studio use a 72-hour, incremental cooling fermentation process...
It gives their beer an amber color, and the bubbles it produces are as smooth as champagne...
And the meat they use for their skewers? Comes from cattle raised the traditional way and delivered straight from Akashi Farm...
Uh... How much is she paying you for this?
Not a dime – just all the beer and skewers I could want!
I'll leave you to it, then. I'm heading home.
Don't drink too much, and stay safe on your way back.
I'll be fiiine... Juuust... fine... *hic*... Zzz...
Good luck... catching those... infiltrators...
Nya, nya! Cut, nya!
Eagle Union Mainland - NY City (Post-Siren attack)
Good winds, check. Calm waves, check. Today's looking like it'll be smooth sailing!
Yup. If nothing else, we'll have a nice journey on our way to the Canal Zone. We'll be busy after that though, because that stronghold isn't gonna protect itself!
Saratoga and I will have our hands full with a separate mission, so we won't be able to accompany you. Still, someone has to keep watch on our territories when our defenses are weak.
Don't you worry. If any Sirens show up, they'll get a welcoming present from my 8-inch guns.
You should start setting off now. Good luck out there, and stay on your guard.
Yeah, we ought to get going as well. Good luck, Enterprise, Saratoga.
It's no biggie, we're just checking out a remote stronghold! Anyhoo, safe travels to you all!
All righty, Sara's gonna go ahead and link up with the Commander~
I wonder how things are going up there in the Bering Sea. I heard they were going to investigate an iceberg fortress.
Think so... I think it's a bit suspicious how they invited the Commander out of the blue, when the Northern Parliament has been handling it by themselves so far.
So I want to be on the safe side and come along to ensure everything's fine!
In the meanwhile, you just need to hold the line here and await our triumphant return!
Roger that. Good luck, and give my regards to the Commander.
Will do~!
Canal Stronghold - Eastern Region
A dense mist enveloped the seas. All was painted white as far as the eye can see.
A Mirror Sea! Those damn Sirens are pulling the same trick on us again!
Attention, everyone! Enter battle formations and maintain a safe distance! Prepare for engagement with the Sirens!
The Eagle Union fleet found themselves in a Mirror Sea whilst they were en route to the Canal Stronghold. They readied themselves for a Siren ambush.
Helena, you see anything on your radar?
No, it's not been detecting anything...
We all but know there are Sirens here, yet you can't detect them?
Radio waves get jammed in Mirror Seas. We'll have to rely on our other sensors and plain line of sight to spot them.
However, with this mist obscuring our view, even that might be nigh-impossible...
I feared a Mirror Sea was coming just after I heard about this dense fog...
My premonition proved right, I suppose.
This is my fault. I shouldn't have kept us on course through the fog and sailed into a Siren trap.
What's done is done. Besides, we have to pass through here to get to our objective. So, what do we do now?
It's obvious; we fight our way out of here. Which, funnily enough, we might've needed to do later anyway, if these Sirens were gonna attack the Canal Stronghold.
Right. A flawless plan, assuming it goes as we hope...
By the way, Helena, would you please see if you can contact with Canal Stronghold? I suspect we're being jammed, but it doesn't hurt to try.
I'll give it a shot... Oh, I think my message went through! It looks like our communications are *not* being jammed!
Wait, seriously?! How in the world... Seems this Mirror Sea is different to what we've dealt with before...
Canal Stronghold - Region unknown
(Beep... Beep... Beep...)
Was that...?
Everyone, hold! My radar just detected something!
Didn't you say it wasn't functioning earlier?
(Beep... Beep... Beep...)
Hang on, I'm getting something too. The signal's weak, but it's definitely *something*.
It seems they have an allied identification signal... Maybe they're transport ships who got caught in the mist too?
The odds of that are low. I've heard nothing about active supply convoys in this region.
Furthermore, since our comms equipment still works, they should be broadcasting an SOS if they really are allied.
When you put it like that, it sounds more likely to be a trap laid by the Sirens.
Very likely, I would say.
Okay then. Let's go investigate.
Yeah, let's go in– Wait, what?!
Do you have a plan, Baltimore?
I do. We've got 2 options; either we make a beeline for the fortress, or we "take the bait," so to speak.
We can't exactly just leave this mist hanging around even if we head straight for the stronghold, and we can't be certain our compasses are pointing us in the right direction either.
Either way, it sounds like we have to shift our focus to the Sirens...
Obviously, I don't intend to just walk into a trap here. Helena, do me a favor and contact NY City. Ask them to send reinforcements.
Roger!
This is just a hunch of mine, but I doubt the Sirens' plan is as one-dimensional as it looks.
Let's proceed cautiously and uncover what they're really doing here.
Now, I'll admit I'm no master strategist, but isn't this really risky? I think we should head for the fortress instead.
That was my first thought too, but consider this: what if that signal really is coming from an allied convoy?
Then... we must help. We can't just leave them to their fates.
The more likely scenario is that it's a Siren ambush, though...
Whichever it turns out to be, we have to exercise caution because of all this fog.
Everyone clear on what to do? Then let's go!
Location unknown
Are those... the wrecks of mass-produced Siren models?
Could that signal really have come from an ally?!
As the fleet approached the origin point of the signal, they started finding Siren wreckages littering the ocean's surface.
Memphis, Helena, either of you heard anything over your comms?
Nope, I've heard nothing.
I've... Hang on... The Sirens have started jamming us!
So *now* they're jamming us... They must be getting ready to strike!
Our comms have been down in every Mirror Sea we've come across, which means...!
Slow to catch on, ain'tcha!
You never heard what the old maritime legends say? That Sirens lurk in the mist?
It's you, Purifier...!
Yuup, it's me! The crowdpleaser, the one and only Purifier! Hello there, my little test subjects~
I noticed you tried to send some messages to your pals. Thanks a bunch for the secret intel!
Didn't think for a second that maybe there's a reason why you could still use your comms, eh?
Oh, and the messages themselves? Guess what: never arrived!
Purifier snapped her fingers, and just like that, the fog all around them vanished and exposed the sky above.
Would you look at that! This thing's pretty nifty for a subprogram device!
By the way, your comms weren't all we messed with. Check your navigation systems, you're in for a treat!
We're in... the Bermuda Triangle!
What dirty scheme are you up to this time, Purifier?
It's something we've been working on for a long time! Sorry, buddy! Don't wanna spoil the surprise!
Baltimore, I just received a transmission from the stronghold! We've–
Hold it, you're not going anywhere!
Purifier snapped her fingers again, and the dense mist returned.
You're staying right where you are until the stars of the show turn up!
Dammit! Everyone, get ready to engage!
Good idea! We've got plenty of time to kill, so let's have ourselves some fuuuun!
Canal Stronghold - Eastern Region
*pant*... *pant*...!
D-do you think they're still after us?
We need to hurry!
Faster! Everyone needs to know what's going on out there!

sequence:
Warmth in the Storm

<size=45>Mischievous Storm</size>

scripts.say: Port's Surrounding Waters - Patrol Vessel
Mogador and I are en route to an island near the port for a survey mission.
Ugghh... I can't believe I'm forced to wear this thick cloak when it's this sunny outside...
Imagine if we could both change into swimwear and go on a holiday. Heehee, I'm getting giddy just thinking about it♥
Mogador steps closer and leans against a railing on the deck.
Just then, the sea breeze suddenly picks up, ruffling her hair.
What's more, the clouds seem to have grown a bit heavier.
Yeah. You deserve a vacation after all your hard work lately.
Once this survey is done, we'll both take some time off and go on a holiday.
Heheheh... Getting to spend time together with you, breathing in your smell...
That's not hard work to me – that's heaven♥
In fact, I wish you'd make use of me more often. For things other than office work, I mean.
Ugh, this cloak is such a bother... I wanna take it off...
You can't strip when you're still on the clock.
Heheh. I know, I just had to say it.
You know, there'd be no need to wait for a holiday if it wouldn't affect the Tribunal's image or whatever it was.
It's so crazy hot today, almost tempting enough for...
Ahem...
It might be hot now, but the weather around here is very erratic.
It gets especially cold at night. You'll catch a cold without clothes.
Try to bear with it. Both for the task at hand and your health.
You're that concerned about my health?
Aww... Getting coddled by you wasn't on my bingo sheet today.
You make me wanna expose my... heart to you.
What, you mean to get something off your chest?
Ahahaha! Straight to my chest, eh... I wanna take it nice and slow today, though.
We'll have all the time in the world to enjoy ourselves...
Heehee... I'm getting shivers thinking about all the stuff we'll do...♥
...Oh! You were right – the weather here IS erratic!
Right as she says that, a strong gust assaults the deck.
The ship starts to rock violently, and Mogador stumbles while the wind lifts her cloak.
I think a storm's coming.
Time to change course. We need to get on the island immediately!
Although the storm grew more tempestuous, we did manage to make landfall before it got really bad.
Unfortunately, our clothes got soaked, which makes things a little awkward.
Sorry, Commander. I think some of my sweat got on your hand when you held me...
Well... We're both so soaked... It's hard to tell where the sweat stops and the water starts...♥
Call me bold for saying this, but I wish we could cuddle more often like this, and not just due to circumstances...
...Oh. That sounded weird, didn't it?
It's fine. Gotta act quick when there's an emergency.
Well, uh... What now? Are we stuck on this uninhabited island together?
Perhaps. I'd better radio the port first of all.

sequence:
Warmth in the Storm

<size=45>Ghost Rumors</size>

scripts.say: Port's Surrounding Waters - Unexplored Island
Uh-oh. There's no signal whatsoever.
The weather out at sea is a fickle mistress. As if this sudden storm blocking our return route wasn't bad enough, it has also cut off all our signals.
It looks like we'll just have to stay on the island until the connection is restored.
It's okay. We just have to wait out the storm.
Let's find a safe place to seek shelter...
True. My cloak is soaked through and through. It's stuck to my skin and it's gross...
You're sopping wet, too... We'll both catch a cold at this rate.
Might as well take off our clo–
I immediately stop her before she can strip down to her birthday suit.
If I remember correctly, the scouting fleet that first discovered this island set up a provisional base before they left.
Let's go there and catch our breaths.
We're going indoors? Fine by me.
Provisional Base - Indoors
Ahh. Four walls and a roof. Now we don't have to put up with the rain.
Although, it feels like it's getting colder and colder in here, somehow...
It's so dark... Commaaander, let's stick together. Just in case something happens...
Good point. Let's first find a generator and see if we can get the power on.
Okey-dokey. Heheheh...
Try to keep a little distance, though. And be on the lookout for danger.
Okaaay...
We go forward, fumbling our way through the darkness in search of a generator.
I can barely see anything, yet your presence feels so much stronger...
Heehee♥ My heart races every time we– Oh, watch your step here, I mean...
(The Commander's still drenched... I wanna come closer♥)
(If only... No, no I shouldn't. Need to stay focused. But...)
(The Commander's scent... It makes it impossible to stay calm...)
A while later, we arrive in the room housing the base's generator.
We scan the room under the emergency lighting and happen upon some writing that someone has left on the wall.
Commaaander, there's some writing on this wall here...
"The island's ghosts awaken during the storm. Anyone who stops here must obey the following rules:"
"One: Return to your ship at once if you see or hear strangers. No people live on this island."
"Two: The sea wind is a gentle being, and its storms never rage on the island itself..."
"If a storm hits, head to the break room and stay put until it passes."
"Three: There is no shower in the break room."
"If, however, there is a shower room, there should also be two beds."
"If there is a shower room and only a single bed, you must ◼◼◼◼"
The rest is unreadable... What is this? Some kind of ghost story?
Part two of it has kinda come true already, so...
Do you think it has any weight to it, Commander?

options.content: Ghost stories are just that. Stories.

scripts.say: Someone who came here before us probably just wrote it as a prank.
When we get back, I'll have to check if Bristol was here.
What do YOU think?
I think it's well written for a ghost story. Especially with this atmosphere...
If it IS real, I'm curious to see what comes next. Heheheh...
(Real or not, I have a hunch something will happen during our stay here.)
(Ahh... You look so composed, so gentle under the moonlight, Commander...)
(You know what? Maybe it's fine if it stays dark♥)

sequence:
Warmth in the Storm

<size=45>Searching for the Break Room</size>

scripts.say: I power up the generator. Slowly, a dim light illuminates the lengthy and narrow room.
Antiquated machinery and piles of random objects cast long shadows on the walls.
Oh, there's the light...
Thanks to the light, I can now finally get a look at Mogador.
Although her clothes have dried a little, they still firmly cling to her skin.
Commaaander... Look how wet I am♥
She pulls on the fabric, which outlines the contours of her body down to the fine details.
The play of light and shadow makes her bumps and curves all the more pronounced.
Your uniform's heavy, so I bet it feels even more uncomfortable on you♥
She places her hands on me and is about to start undressing me, but then...
There's the click of the power breaker failing, and darkness envelops the room once more.
...Can you hear that, Commander? Someone's talking...
She's not wrong. I can hear a whispered conversation coming from a corner of the room.
I listen closely. Amid the hushed words, I hear a faint laughter.
Startled, Mogador huddles up next to me, gripping the sleeve of my coat and looking around warily.
Could this be... what the first rule warned us about?
Is that ghost story... true after all?
Her breath feels especially warm against my ear. Maybe it's because the temperature is starting to drop.
It's a bit creepy, I won't deny that. Let's just hope your main guns can handle any ghosts that might appear.
But any ghost-busting will have to wait until tomorrow. Let's head for the break room for now.
And if you get scared, well...
I'm a judge of the Tribunal. I ain't afraid of no ghosts...
...Actually, on second thought, I'm really scared!
Uh, okay...

options.content: (Let her hold on to your sleeve.)

scripts.say: I extend my hand to her. She grabs it without a moment's hesitation.
Her cold fingers run across my palm, then interlock with mine.
Thanks... This really helps a lot.
Your... sleeve...
Can I wrap my arm around yours instead? That'd be more reassuring...
Her cold fingers brush against my hand. Once she sees I'm okay with it, she immediately wraps her arm around mine.
Thanks... This really helps a lot.
Glad it does. Now let's go.
As we move through the darkness, her body sometimes leans right against my arm.
Even through her cloak, I can tell that she's trembling slightly.
(Sheesh... I didn't think it'd get so cold at night on this island...)
(At least the Commander's hand feels so warm. I don't wanna let go of it...)
*sigh*... This is why you should wear clothes.
Hang in there. We'll find a way to warm you up once we find the break room.
Don't worry, I'm really resilient. I don't get sick easily.
...Err, I mean, I'm freezing cold! Brrr!
I'm gonna turn into a popsicle... You need to warm me up now, Commander!
She wraps her whole body around me, squeezing tightly like I'm a stuffed animal.
It'll take us longer to get there if you cling to me like this...
I'm not in a hurry... At least doing this keeps us both warm♥
Right then, a strong gust throws open a nearby window, interrupting our conversation.

sequence:
Warmth in the Storm

<size=45>Bring Me a Towel</size>

scripts.say: An eerie breeze stirs up dust and old papers. That, combined with the moonlight, makes it almost look like there's a ghost with us.
Mogador tightens her grip on my hand.
Don't be afraid. It's just the wind.
I wrap my arms around her shoulders and pat her back to calm her down.
My comforting helps. She relaxes and leans against me.
(Ahh... An excuse to embrace the Commander...)
(Such a warm coat... I wish I could be held like this forever♥)
(I love ghost stories now...)
She caves in to her impulse and slips in under my coat, clinging to me.
(I can't move like this...)
(Ugh... Need to close that window.)
After the minor "incident" in the corridor, we arrived inside the break room.
Only one bed. We'll just have to make do...
(We have this place all to ourselves... Heheheh...)
Okay, I just had a look around the room. The doors and windows are all firmly shut, so there won't be any repeats of what happened in the corridor.
(We'll be sleeping in the same room... Heheheheh♥)
The power works and there's running water, so the shower room should be usable. You go ahead and take a shower to warm up.
(Drats... I need to think of a way to drag the Commander with me into the shower...)
There are plenty of rations and even candles for emergencies. I'll set things up and prep some food.
(Food and candles... A candlelit dinner on a desert island...)
Mogador? Hello? You look a bit distracted.
Oh, uh, I'm fine. You really plan for everything, Commander!
Thank the girls who came here before us. I didn't bring the supplies – they left them here.
Of course. They're all so diligent!
Anyway, I'm gonna take a shower. Be back in a bit!
She runs off into the shower room without a moment's delay.
What's up with her...?
The sound of the shower ceases, and a hand pokes out through the gap in the door.
Commaaander, there's no towel...
(Don't tell me this was her plan...)
One sec. There should be one among the supplies.
I get up, find a towel, and just as I reach out to give it to her...
Rather than take the towel, she takes a firm hold of my wrist.
Commaaander... You've been drenched for a pretty long time now...♥
Come in here and let me take care of you♥
Before I can even react, she pulls me inside the shower room.
The room is thick with warm steam. Fortunately, there's a translucent shower curtain separating me and her.
You must be exhausted! Let me help you wash with some hot water. It feels sooo good, trust me...♥
She grabs the curtain, getting ready to pull it aside.
