The first time heading inside the Singularity was pretty rough, but now it feels more like a roller coaster ride than anything else!
Hmm. So it's been about four hours...
Magdeburg, have you heard back from the Ashes?
Nope. I tried contacting them a few times, but...
What about you, Elbe? See anything?
Haven't found anything inside my observable range. The Sirens have shot down any recons trying to fly beyond that though.
I see. She's not coming then.
Let's prepare to withdraw. The entrance won't stay open for much longer.
...Please wait.
What is it? We can't really fix up your injuries while we're inside the Singularity.
...You're not going to wait for a response?
The fact that we're not getting a response is good enough. Given the difficulty communicating between worlds, expecting anything was already optimistic.

It doesn't really matter whether or not Enterprise ignored us, had a change of heart, or simply decided not to get you involved. Whatever the end result is, the fact that we can't get in touch means that she's not coming.
But from how aggressively the Sirens are shooting down your recons... they're surely hiding something.
Whether or not I'm hiding something, I'd shoot down enemy recons regardless. Plus, the Sirens are always hiding something, and there's always next time.
...I know I'm not thinking logically right now, but I want to see if something happened.
So, you think the Sirens' behavior has something to do with Scharnhorst not returning yet.
That Scharnhorst... is not my real sister. But despite that...
I understand how you feel, but when we're at risk of being attacked by an Arbiter Vessel, I can't risk you putting all of us in danger.
So... tell me the real reason, Gneisenau.
...Scharnhorst is still somewhere inside the Singularity. I can feel it...
Even though she's not the Scharnhorst you knew, you still want to save her... That's what you're saying?
Yes. It's the same for me with Bismarck, and the rest of you in the Iron Blood.
I understand. How about the rest of you?
Woah, Gneisenau finally asked us for help! That's the kind of plot arc I'm down for!
Mm, yeah. I wanted to go check things out as well. Didn't seem to me like Scharnhorst was the type of person who'd ghost us.
That's right! Not even a bad girl like me would do something like that. Let's go find her!
I just brought over some supplies on our mass-produced ships, so let's do a quick field maintenance before we get going!
Guess that means it's a go. We're short on time, so this will be the last search in our operation.
I'd prefer not to drag someone who's injured back into the fray, but we'll be counting on your intuition, Gneisenau.
Don't worry about me.
U-1206, relay this message to Peter: "Affirmative, send in the reserve team." Let's finish our preparations and get moving.
Sure!
You wanted this all along, didn't you, Ulrich?
All ships, refuel and turn course. We're heading out to look for the Ashes!
Only a few hours remain until the Singularity maintenance limit––
Inside the Singularity - Near the Tower
Hey, Elbe, don't take this the wrong way, but... Couldn't you have chosen a different route?
This place was spooky enough when all the wreckage was on fire, but now... it's like even worse?
It, it's not like I picked this route just to mess with you! And gosh, why is it so cold... Brr...
The temperature feels normal to me... Wait, didn't U-1206 say something about getting a weird sensation when we first came through here?
Hey, U-1206, what was it you were talking about earlier?
Uhh, U-1206, are you still alive?
Shhh! Did you hear that just now? It sounded like the kind of noise that'd come from a constructions site...
Nope, nothing... Well, you're underwater, so the vibrations must be transmitting better. Guess that's why subs tend to pick up on more things.
So? Where's the sound coming from?
From all over? Like... inside the wreckage?
Just as everyone perked up their ears to try to figure out the source of the sound, a large explosion rang out just in front of them.
You heard that, didn't you?!
Clear as day! Wait, could these sounds be...
As if responding to the first explosion, the other charred husks in the area began to creak and groan.
Ugh... What is that cacophony...?
We might've not come out here specifically to look for a fight, but...
If it'll get these assholes to stop making so much noise, I'm down to throw down!
We're really going to need to upgrade our radars... I'm tired of getting ambushed like this.
I feel so bad... I can't believe I failed to spot the enemy twice in one mission...
It's not your fault. We know they're here, but we can't do anything until they make the first move anyway.
We're not used to being constantly at risk of attack, but that's all the reason to proceed carefully.
But what are they doing inside the wreckage? ...If they were really trying to ambush us, would they really be making so much noise?
And I don't think that explosion was caused by U-1206 firing a torpedo, right?
Hmm... If you look closely, some of the wreckages have been cut cleanly.
Why would they do that? To recover resources? Have the Sirens ever needed to do that?
If they're not attacking us, just ignore them. We need to save our strength for when it matters.
(If Scharnhorst ended up encountering the Arbiter Vessel, I'm not sure that our forces are sufficient...)
Heeey, look! Someone's over there!
It's the Ashes' Scharnhorst!
The Iron Blood fleet found their target inside a small "lake" of mangled shipwrecks.
The gravely-wounded Scharnhorst laid there motionless, her rigging barely holding together.
U-1206 hurried over to the unconscious girl's side.
Hang in there, Scharnhorst! We're here to help!
She cried for her with all of her might, but there was no response.
It's no good... She's completely lost consciousness...!
What in the world happened here...?
Who knows. Judging from the wreckage around here, she probably ran into the Arbiter Vessel...
Let's bring her back, and hurry. The Sirens will surely be back soon to finish the job.
Too late, they're already here! So is this what the Sirens were doing in that pile of wrecks? They're trying to retrieve her!
Like hell we'd let them get away with that! Get ready for battle, everyone!
.....Nngh... Arghh!
Calm down, Gneisenau.
We'll escape the Singularity once we take care of these guys. We have no intention of leaving Scharnhorst here.
U-1206, secure Scharnhorst. Everyone else, intercept the Sirens!
Don't pursue them if they run. Once we break through their line, we're heading straight to the Tower. Understood?
...Got it.
Siren bastards, this ammo is wasted on you lot...!
There aren't any Sirens on our tail anymore! We lost them!
What about the wreckage in front of us?
Don't worry, I won't mess up this time!
There aren't any Lurker-type Sirens ahead of us, either!
(Hmph... I've got a bad feeling about this. Things are going way too well.)
(If there was an Arbiter there, why didn't they just finish Scharnhorst off? And, why aren't they chasing after us?)
An Arbiter should be more than a match for a force of our size, so why...?
Keep... up your guard... The sea is still...
You're hurt real bad! Don't talk, and more importantly, no sudden movements!
I'm alright... I've been through worse... I can fight once you treat me... Ugh!
Fight?! In this condition...?!
Yeah. The main engine still works... and my main gun too... One of them, anyway... Heh, hehehe...
Why did you guys... even come here? Didn't you expect... for this to be a Siren trap...?
Well, of course we knew it was a trap. But Gneisenau insisted that we come save you.
Gneisenau...
You aren't acting like yourself. The Scharnhorst I knew would have been able to put up a good show, even in this state.
You're... one to talk...
Look how beat up you are...
That's because... she insisted on charging into the enemy headfirst to try to get to you before they did.
Even if you're not the Scharnhorst from my world, you're still Scharnhorst... Just as there must have been a Gneisenau in your world.
If I let you sink here... I wouldn't be able to look the other Gneisenau in the eyes.
Gneisenau... Heh. I'll... remember those words...
If you can't return on your own, come to our base until you're all healed up. We won't try to keep you there if you don't want to stay.
I don't know if we're able to repair Ashes ships, but... we're willing to try. ... And you might be interested in our leader.
It's not like... I'm in any position... to refuse...
There is one thing I want from you in exchange though. Tell me what just happened, and any information you have on Arbiter VI.
It's... the first time I encountered that Arbiter.
Enforcers aren't a big deal, so I underestimated them, but... they're a pretty dangerous bunch...
The Enforcers... aren't a big deal?!
We are pretty used to fighting them... So I didn't think they'd pose much of a threat to Gneisenau either...
Oh, uh, I see! That doesn't make me feel bad at all...
The Enforcers' combat ability and style depends on their corresponding Arbiter... and the compatibility between them...
Basically, they'll either take you out by outnumbering you, or with sheer force on their own...
Which one happened to you?
Both... I hate to say it, but I still haven't figured out a way to deal with them.
In the first wave of attack, they overwhelmed me with sheer numbers... and then after, the Arbiter completely overpowered me on her own...
I see. I didn't think any number of Enforcers alone would've been able to take you down.
It's as you say... In the end, Enforcers are just Enforcers... Even you guys should be able to handle them just fine...
But, the Arbiter Vessel... No, Arbiter VI's true form...
A huge armored structure appeared in the sky... and that's the last thing I saw before losing consciousness.
So you were taken out in an instant. If Gneisenau hadn't come looking for you, the Sirens would've "salvaged" you...
...Just like what they're doing with the rest of the wreckage.
That may well be a part of the Arbiter's powers... Taking control of the Singularity to create Mirror Seas...
Once she finishes... No, she might already be done...
She will be able to deconstruct and reconstitute herself at will, using the resources from the endless seas of debris to regenerate herself.
And her Enforcers have likewise become more and more durable... and until we deal with them, we have no hope of getting to the Arbiter.
That is the Arbiters' power... The weapon they use to hunt down the Ashes.
So those Sirens were retrieving resources for the Arbiter...?!
This entire singularity... is the Arbiter's domain...
Yes... This was once a world branch that they turned into a testing site... They won't show us any mercy.
Hold on, so the reason I was made to fight here was...
Yes. They wanted to test your power... Or perhaps simply "erase" you from existence...
Gneisenau, I'll leave Scharnhorst in your hands. The rest of you, stay vigilant. The enemy may strike at any moment.
...Understood.
The wounded should stay in the back and offer fire support. I'll clear the way.
I would've been able to give a better showing if I was in better condition...
Sis– I mean, Scharnhorst... Stay with us.
Only a few hours remain until the Singularity maintenance limit––
Humanoid Sirens incoming! It's the Enforcer we fought earlier, and a model we haven't seen before!
That must be the infamous close-quarters model.
Yeah. Do not mess around with that one or it'll be the end of you.
Ulrich! The sea way over there is looking quite unusual!
Must be abnormal weather produced by a Mirror Sea.
Most likely. Guess they're trying to turn this into a game of cat and mouse... You'll get hurt just by sailing through that area.
Dammit... To hell with it! Full speed for the Tower!
Tower of Midgard - Pier
Is everyone here? It feels like we're missing someone?
Oh, it's probably Adalbert. She's probably off stretching somewhere before the operation.
Gosh, imagine being as carefree as her. The operation's starting soon, too!
She's so in her own world, she won't even show up for lunch unless you call for her!
Oh well, she's only got herself to blame if she goes hungry!
You called? Also, whose funeral?
Err...! Nobody's, just talking to myself!
Yo, where the hell've you been? Somethin' happen at one of the structures?
Nah, we're still in the green. We've got active camo, remember?
Granted, that's gone as soon as we make that Singularity. We'll basically be broadcasting ourselves to all the Sirens nearby.
Oh, and since you asked, I was just getting my stretches in. Wouldn't want to get a cramp during battle, ya know?
Well, do whatever you need, but don't go running off once the actual operation starts.
Anyway, it's almost lunchtime. You comin'?
Sure. Hang on, where'd U-1206 go? She called me and everything.
My guess is she went straight for the cafeteria.
Unlike Elbe. I see you hiding back there, girl.
Dang it. Here I was hoping I could sneak up on you un– Owch! Ow-ow-ow!
Adalbert ran up to Elbe at breakneck speed and pinched her cheek.
Okay, sorry! I should've known better than to try to pull pranks on you!
Moments later, a pair of voices echoed from across the pier.
Is this really it, Z46? Today's the big day, right?!
You needn't shout, Heinrich...
Sorry! I'm just excited to finally get some R&R once we wrap this thing up!
And thank god for that! I'd die from boredom if I had to go one more day with no action whatsoever!
Do not get too excited. Your respite shall only come once this is over.
Aww, look at Eisen! He's looking restless too. Poor boy needs a vacay just as much as I do!
He appears that way only because you will him to...
Heyo, Heinrich.
Oh! Sup, Adalbert! What's brought you all the way out here?
I mean, what do you think?
Uhh... I dunno? Should I know?
You... You did read the mission briefing, yes, Heinrich?
On paper, yeah! In reality... nope. But that's no biggie, I'll be just fine with Strasser's guidance!
Classic Heinrich. Never change.
Basically, we're gonna go take a look around that Singularity.
But right now we're just chewin' the fat while waiting for lunchtime.
Ah, gotcha! Meanwhile, I just got done running a final inspection on some equipment.
Heard we're getting started once Strasser and Ulrich finish their meeting.
By the way, is that still going on?
Seems like it. Ulrich might seem all grumpy and unsociable, but she's actually quite thorough with these things.
Huh. I guess you really can't judge a book by its cover...
Fearsome indeed will her fury be should you not know what the operation entails.
...On second thought, I think I'll read the mission briefing! See you girls later!
Hey, are you not gonna eat before– Welp, guess not.
You needn't worry about her. She will catch up with us soon enough.
Now, let us make way to the cafeteria. We can fetch some food for Heinrich too.
There are so many humanoid Sirens! I just can't stand these things!
There aren't that many. It shouldn't be too hard to deal with them.
Gneisenau, Scharnhorst, let's hurry.
Yeah!
There's a submarine type Siren over there! Be careful!
They're taking advantage of the fact that we're missing an escort fleet... What a troublesome bunch.
Prepare for anti-submarine warfare. Gneisenau, Scharnhorst, how are you two holding up?
We're fine... Did you forget that we're used to fighting on our own?
You're saying that, even though you were hit by a submarine? Was that data we had collected not of any use?
And what about you? Your anti-submarine equipment is destroyed beyond any use.
All due to your signature recklessness.
Maybe we should call Magdeburg's group over. If it comes to it, I can...
It's fine, leave it to me. Take Scharnhorst and go ahead first.
No need to worry about me, this is nowhere near enough to take me out.
I'll catch up with you guys later, rush over to the Tower!
...Hurry! There's no time to waste!
The only obstacles left in our way... are that Enforcer and its fleet.
We'll arrive back at the Tower soon. We don't have the time to spare though. Break through by force!
Then I'll take the lead—
Don't put on airs. You're hurt, leave it to us.
Ugh...! Are you telling me to sit by and watch while you guys put your lives on the line?!
Exactly that. That's objectively our best course of action given the situation.
It'd be a different story if you weren't injured, but the Iron Blood does not make futile sacrifices.
...But I'm not even Iron Blood. I'm with the Ashes.
If the Ashes leave their members to die, then I'll have no part of it.
Speaking of which, you mentioned that you've been through worse before. How did you make it through that time?
I don't believe that the Sirens just happened to lose track of you... right?
It was thanks to Enterprise... When I was about to succumb to despair, surrounded by the wreckage of my friends... Enterprise showed me a new path.
...Then we will do the same for you.
You're not Code G! There's no way you can take on those guys on your own!
Not everyone was born strong. And don't worry, I'm not doing this path on my own...
Ulrich, we've taken care of our pursuers!
Not quite taken care of, but we've led them away.
And Gneisenau has regrouped with us~
Jeez, you almost hit me with that anti-submarine round!
...There was a bit of a problem with the data analysis. Besides, didn't we agree not to talk about that anymore?
I said I wouldn't talk about it after we made it back safely!
They've all sustained heavy injuries from fighting against the Enforcers...
That's why we need to pool our efforts. Let's break through and make it to the tower! Everyone, we're at the last stretch!
I can see the light emanating from the Tower, Ulrich!
We don't have much time left... but as long as we can keep up the pace, we should be able to make it!
B-b-b-but, there's something frightening behind us...
Don't look back! Run, with all your might!
That's right! We're almost there!
Ulrich, the reserve team is in position! Leave it to us!
My, what a precious express you have, Ulrich. I've never seen you frazzled before~
Your timing couldn't have been better... Is it just you two?
Are the two of us not good enough for you?
Just kidding. There are others behind us. We can call them in if necessary.
Friedrich called back some of our forces, but we should have ample firepower to take out the Sirens.
Scrap that idea. This entire Singularity is already under the control of an Arbiter. We need to withdraw immediately.
...Understood. We'll hold them back, so make your way to the Tower.
I guess so. It'd be more fun if we all fought together though~
Let's see how scary you actually are, Arbiter!
W-when did she get here?!
That instant materialization...! It's the Arbiter! She's here!
Scharnhorst and... Gneisenau? Wait, the two of you are...
There's no time to explain. If we don't take care of her and the Tower is destroyed, we'll be stuck here for eternity.
Roger. Engaging in combat with the Siren higher-ups is part of the plan... We'll support you!
By the way, Ulrich, I'd keep the Ashes out of this if possible.
Yeah. The Sirens were after them from the very beginning, and we must get them back to our world safely.
Gotta look after our allies after all. Make me proud, mass-produced ships!
Enough chit-chat. See you back home.
Ulrich entrusted the two new allies to the reserve fleet, and turned back to face the Siren threat.
Just at that time, a massive figure formed in the sky, its gargantuan white rigging casting a shadow across the Tower.
That's... Arbiter VI?
There was no answer. The massive construct looming overhead seemed unable to speak.
But its response was thundering. Lasers swept across the waters as the rigging revealed its arsenal of optical weapons.
Doesn't look like they want to talk. Guess there's only one thing left to do, Mainz.
Naturally. I didn't come all this way to have a tea party.
Only 10 minutes until the Singularity maintenance limit! Don't get carried away!
Of course, I know~ Hehe... Let's have some fun!
Battleship Ulrich von Hutten firmly grasped the massive scythe in her rigging, unleashing her full powers in a decisive stand against the Sirens.
KABOOM–––––––!!
The combined onslaught of the Iron Blood ships began to take a toll on the Arbiter Vessel.
Blow after blow rained down until finally, the armor split apart.
The Arbiter, as if unable to comprehend the damage she had taken, stared at the place where her armor had been pierced.
Our attacks are working! Let's make that thing bleed!
Don't get ahead of yourself. As long as we're inside the Singularity, she can continuously repair off any damage we do inflict.
It seems like it's more of the defensive type. And while we've been focusing on the Arbiter, the Enforcers have started to move again. That's fine though – I've been wanting to test my limits.
Wait... Look where her muzzle is pointed... She's trying to destroy the Midgard Tower!
As a bridge between worlds, getting hit from one side shouldn't be enough to collapse it...
A greater amount of energy is needed just to keep the bridge open. But, if the Arbiter can somehow output even more energy than that...
You're right... Roon, Ulrich, we need to pull back, lest the unthinkable actually does occur.
Fine by me. Adalbert, after you~
Sure~ Then I'll be heading out first.
Protected by the fire of the mass-produced ships and her allies, Adalbert disappeared in the torrent of light.
And after her were Ulrich, Magdeburg, Elbe, U-1206, and Mainz...
The last one left was Roon, who used the impact from one of the Enforcer's attacks to push her through the exit in the nick of time.
The torrent of energy held together by the Towers at both ends of the Singularity suddenly distorted, instantly atomizing the Enforcer that had approached too closely.
Both the gateway and the Tower... Bifröst itself – like a fleeting rainbow in the sky – vanished without a trace, as if it had never existed at all.
The emergency cutoff was a success! Th-that was too much for my heart... I thought we were all going to get squished into space dust...
But we got everyone back safely, right? Wait, Adalbert's unconscious...?
Roon and Mainz too! Ahhhhh! Did something go wrong during the transfer?!
The transfer could've been handled with more finesse... but at least they avoided the Arbiter's attack.
Y-yeah! All's well that ends well, right?
Eisen over here chewed through some cables though! You're working too hard, Eisen!
Oh, Roon twitched a bit right now! What a relief...
Mm... Let's bring everyone to the rest area.
The aftermath of this operation, the saga of Ashes and META... will surely be most interesting to hear about.
And the best part about the operation... is always what comes afterwards! Vacaaaaation time!
Probably not this time. Given the state that the control room is in, we may have to all write an official apology.
Uh oh... I hope that's not what this incoming message is about...
Same here. I'll have to explain what happened to Peter as soon as possible.
Help meeee, Viersechs! I'll never be able to write an apology note all by myself! Save meeee!
To be relied on is comforting indeed, but...
For you to grow as an individual, you must learn to confront your weaknesses.
Ughh... My head... Where... am I...?
When Adalbert woke up, she saw the familiar sight of the facility in the floating fortress.
Relieved, she promptly fell back down, exhausted from the mission.
Adalbert! Adalbert! Oh... she's out cold again!
No, I'm fine... It's just that... I pushed myself a bit too hard at the end there... Hey, Heinrich, can you request some time off for me as well?

sequence: "So this is how the Tower's functionality test concludes."
"Indeed. It's almost as if we've angered the Divine."
"...If they attack us, then we shall respond in kind."
"We will need my child's assistance."
"We'll fire the first shot. And we'll pave a new path."
"I'll make sure that your wish comes true, Bismarck."
"You're as reliable as always, Friedrich."
<size=51>「Eisen und Blut über alles」</size>
...For the sake of our great victory, and the Iron Blood's bright future.

scripts.say: Somewhere in the Sardegna Empire
That's all the information from Friedrich's report on the Singularity expedition.
The Tower of Midgard, huh? What a droll naming sense... Plus, there was nothing about that thing that even resembled a tower.
And what's the deal with Midgard? If they wanted to emphasize that whole deal with transcending God, they should've gone with the Tower of Babel or something.
*sigh*... Stop being a smartass...
In any case, what are you going to tell the Iron Blood?
Just tell them, we've read the materials. And congratulations on a successful operation.
Understood.
By the way, Cavour. Have you heard of the Vichya's Skybound Wall?
Haha, you're talking about the weapon they used against Richelieu in Mozambique?
Yeah, that! Don't you think that would be a treasure that would truly show off Sardegna's true splendor?
The Eternal City christened with glory... a manifestation of divine majesty that displays the dignity of God...
That basilica is currently in the hands of Richelieu. It'll be hard to negotiate with them.
That's right... Then, how about asking the Vichya or the Iron Blood for blueprints of the weapon? If they can make it, Sardegna should be able to too.
And once that's done~ Hehe, hahahahaha~♪
Understood. I'll keep it in the back of my head.
Good~♪
*Sigh* ...When Veneto and the others were trapped in the labyrinth, the Sirens attacked the capital...
And now we're missing a lot of our higher-ups. But I guess it's thanks to that we can make our moves relatively freely...
I don't know, it just feels a bit weird... Doesn't it bother you, Marco Polo?
Not at all? It's just coincidence anyway, and Zara was able to drive the Sirens away.
Oh, by the way, this is something about Iris Libre and Vichya, but.
Are you talking about the Crown, one of Iris Libre's divine treasures?
Yep, exactly! Did you find out where it was?
I'm not a skilled intelligence officer, but... I've heard a rumor two about it.
For example, that it went missing during a botched Reenactment.
They lost it? The Iris Libre? That Richelieu?
I guess that means they are less worthy than us to be its safekeepers... Hehe...
You're overstepping your bounds, Marco.
Veneto's directive was to increase the prestige of the Sardegna Empire, not to loot and plunder.
Just saying. Plus, it's not like that'd actually decrease Sardegna's prestige.
Look, it's not like I care that much if Richelieu holds on to it. I just think, it'd be put to better use in our hands.
Anyways, I'll let you get back to work.
Everything in moderation, Marco Polo.
I guess someone has to do the chores. See you around.
The attack on the capital... It was significant, but it happened when Veneto wasn't around.
And it wasn't the Royal Navy who came to our rescue, it was the Iron Blood... Either the Senate decided to put on quite the self-serving theatrical performance, or...
For some reason, the Royal Navy wasn't able to come to our rescue...
Veneto has her own way of doing things, but I, Marco Polo, have far grander ambitions!
First, the Basilica's sacraments... and the then the sources of "power" that every faction is so keenly interested in...
What better way is there to spread the glory of Sardegna while the Senate is paralyzed?
The Eternal City christened with glory... a manifestation of divine majesty that displays the dignity of God...
Yes, it is time... to gain "God's" allegiance. Hehehe~♪
PH Base
What is all this... and that? And then more of this?!
I don't get it... I just don't get it!
What the heck is going on over there?
Back at base, Saratoga was holding her head in her hands.
Several piles of paper were scattered precariously around her, threatening to engulf the small girl at any time.

The lack of results was inevitable. The Iron Blood prided themselves in their secrecy, and it was impossible to know if the Naval HQ had doctored what little else was available. Nobody would be able to grasp the truth under these circumstances.
The only conclusion we could draw from the appearance of the Singularity, the movements of the ships, the operation that had suspiciously occurred at the same time as An Shan's investigation, was...
...that there wasn't enough information to draw a conclusion.
Oh, I found it! A picture of the device of the Tower! I knew it had something to do with the Singularity, Commander!
The list of ships deployed were... Ulrich von Hutten, and Peter Strasser.
I wonder what they found though... Do you have any ideas, Commander?
I'd better ask them directly... I won't be able to find out with just what's over here.
"If anything, maybe we should ask the base at Antarctica for materials from that time period."
Yep! I can see that there was a big energy reading at that time!
We lost contact for a while and it was pretty freaky...
Wait, hold on... You've got an emergency communication from the Northern Parliament...
Let's see here... "We've sent this message to the Commander directly to Naval HQ..." Wait, what?!
What the heck are you doing, Northern Parliament?!
Commander, hurry and read this!
Northern Parliament sent a message for you directly to Naval HQ!
And looking at these contents... It'll be a huge issue if the Naval HQ and NY City find out!

sequence: "Dear Comrade Commander."
"I hope you are in good health."
"There is much I would like to say, but I will get straight to the point."
"Thanks to the aid from the Azur Lane, we were able to turn the tides against the Sirens."
"The time is ripe."
"Once again, we will begin our counterattack against the Iron Blood."
"We hope for your participation."
—Sovetsky Soyuz

scripts.say: Observer, the analysis of the Mirror Sea is complete.
The experiment time was consistent with our calculations. The bait has been retrieved, and no abnormal phenomena were detected.
Allow me to report on the task I've been entrusted with.
After analyzing and verifying all observational data, we've detected activities from exactly three Arbiters.
...But I must ask again, are we seriously investigating the Arbiters?
This is our testing site. Everything that appears in it is a variable.
Well, it's not like that's any of my business.
Let me check one of the permissions in my function profile though.
Branches are forbidden from interacting with each other. The Iron Blood's creation of a Singularity should be a major violation.
Should we start the destruction protocol of this branch?
Even had the Iron Blood not done so, the Ashes... and the KAN-SEN that had undergone metamorphosis, would have been drawn to this world branch. There are many ways to open a Singularity.
Destruction of this branch is forbidden. It is still too early, for now.
I didn't give them the technology for creating Singularities. So it must have been you, Observer.
Can't you tell from watching the Arbiters? This branch is very adept at learning.
When was the last time you received instructions from Zero?
The last time I received instructions from Zero, Compiler.
Let me ask you something as well.
What happens when a branch, a world that was the subject of a natural deductive experiment, is destroyed?
I've never seen any materials related to it. This branch's material should all be transmitted through your network mainframe, Observer. Shouldn't you already. know that?
Yes. All of the data is transmitted to Zero. What I want to know is, what will happen to me.
Basically, what will happen to the Siren observations, experiments, systems, battle... everything related to the terminal when a branch is discarded...
Does my soul return to the eternal sea, or will I become something else, like Theseus's ship? Will I still be me, or will I become something else?
The only one with a connection to the main frame is you, Observer. What you don't know, there's no way for a Compiler like me to know.
Besides, it's annoying to have to find out.
I will go back to allocating resources to the development of new weapons. Working is pain.
...Next time, if you need someone to run your errands, get Purifier instead. She hasn't been on the experimental field in quite some time.
Appreciate it. Bye.
Tower of Midgard - Pier
Not long after the girls finished their meals, the ground began to rumble.
Hey, who put the facility on vibrate?
That's just the Singularity generator powering up. Nothing to worry about.
Hi there, Strasser! Just making sure: we've gotta go stand guard around the facility, right?
Correct, and you are to stay on guard until Ulrich's team finishes and returns from the Singularity. Understood?
You got it! And if it goes well, Eisen and I will finally get some time off!
The key word is, "if." The Sirens will start coming for the Tower now that we've lost our active camouflage.
Not a problem! I could use some after-lunch exercise.
This is Weser. I have a report to make.
The Sirens have indeed noticed us and are on their way to attack.
Already? They're faster than I expected.
Sooo, there's good news and bad news. Which do you want to hear first?
It makes no difference. Just tell me.
Okay, the good news is, the Siren forces consist of mostly mass-produced ships.
And the bad news is... they're all heading straight for us, almost like they're being pulled in by gravity!
I see... So you were scouting all this time? Is that why you weren't at the cafeteria?
Yeah. I saw Weser head out, so I thought I'd better tag along!
So neither of you have had lunch...
Nah, we just went and ate at a different cafeteria!
Anyway, we can't really enter the Singularity yet, can we? Sirens come first, right?
Indeed. We must seize the initiative against them.
Your team, however, will proceed to the Singularity's entrance. Ulrich is waiting for you there.
You sure you don't need our help?
Would you not waste time questioning my orders? My mission is to ensure you get inside the Singularity.
And your mission is to explore the Singularity and return safely. Remember that.
You're the boss... Then let's not keep Ulrich waiting.
Let's go, Elbe, Magde, and U-1206.
Oh, and Heinrich, good luck with the Sirens and all that.
Thanks, but I don't need luck! I've got a belly full of food and I'm ready to do some damage!
Time to go! Let's get 'em, Eisen!
Tower of Midgard - Singularity Generator
This is how a Singularity looks, eh... Didn't expect it to be this shape, whatever it's called.
Yeah, what is it called? Can't remember.
If I'm not mistaken, I think it's a halo.
Or a donut, with the shimmering layer being the glaze.
Halo! That's the word! And what the heck do you mean "donut"?! There's no "shimmering layer" either!
Adalbert clearly has food on the brain. We just ate, too.
I'm no expert on the names of shapes, but even I can tell ya that ain't no donut.
Let's just put this whole topic to rest. No more talking about food.
Fair. Feels like we should be doin' something besides twiddlin' our thumbs while the others defend the Tower...
Be patient. It's only taking longer than expected because our defensive installations are drawing power.
That's what I'm sayin'! Shouldn't we be out there helping 'em?!
Stop worrying. Everything is still proceeding as planned.
Helping them would only waste energy and resources. We can't just get a replacement for you after we enter the Singularity.
Besides, dispatching those Sirens should be a breeze for someone of Strasser's caliber.
Well... All right, if you say so!
This is Strasser. Sorry I took so long.
How are things on your end?
We're almost done with them. The Tower's turrets will make short work of the Sirens once Heinrich's team softens them up.
I'll reroute power to the Singularity generator now. Just hang on a bit.
Understood. We'll get ready.
Everyone, run a final equipment check, then prepare to enter the Singularity.
Hey, Ulrich, what shape do you think the Singularity is? Like a donut?
Here we go again...
You're viewing it through a perspective both too limited and too childish.
It is no donut – it is a tower. A tower that extends into other worlds...
You lost me... How is it like a tower?
Never mind that. It's not important.
(Above, the domain of the gods. Below, the land of the dead. And betwixt the two... Midgard.)
What matters is directionality. If this is a tower, and not a bridge, then we will either go up... or down.
Soooo... Singularities are like the layers of a cake?
Who can say? We know hardly anything about how Singularities function. The only way we'll learn more is by going inside.
With a thundering great rumble, a maelstrom whipped up at the facility's center. It erupted into the sky, turning into a radiant cyclone.
Good. The Singularity looks stable.
But it won't stay that way forever. The clock is ticking, and you must come back before time runs out.
I can't stress this enough: if you run out of time, you are as good as dead! Waste not a moment getting ready to enter the Singularity!
I know. Now it's time we play our part.
Starting countdown. Listen up, everyone! Your orders are as follows...
Enter in formation. U-1206 goes first, Magdeburg and I follow, then Adalbert. Elbe takes the rear, leading the mass-produced ships forward.
Keep one eye on your monitoring equipment and the other on your surroundings. We have no idea what to expect in there.
The future of Iron Blood – if not the future of all mankind – hinges on this operation. Failure is not an option.
Operation begins NOW!
When the signal was given, U-1206 sprang into motion, followed by all the other members of the team.
Are you sure about this?! I'm not sure I'm quite ready yet!
Time waits for no one, girl! Doesn't matter if you're ready or not!
One by one, the shipgirls's faded as they crossed over the Singularity's event horizon.
Yo, Heinrich, I'm going in now.
Gotcha! Break a leg!
Talk to you inside, Elbe.
Of course. Godspeed.
After notifying her sister, Adalbert proceeded into the Singularity.
Here's hoping all these mass-produced ships can, at the very least, serve as a distraction...
I have no idea what's waiting for me inside... yet somehow, that's making my heart beat with excitement.
Strasser... Weser... Trust me, when I return, there'll be trumpets blowing to celebrate my success!
I don't expect you to conquer another dimension with your planes, but... well, I wish you the best of luck.
As do I. I look forward to seeing your findings.
*sniffle*... All right, I'm off now. Bye!
Finally, Elbe – the last member of the team – entered the Singularity, with a stunning column of mass-produced ships in tow.
The girls cut off from their comrades, the operation had officially commenced.
The air was scorching, but the water was freezing – it was like being in two places at once.
An overpowering odor hung in the air, sapping the girls' strength. This place was unlike any Mirror Sea.
And of course it would be. After all...
Hey, Ulrich? You okay?
...Yeah, I'm fine.
Looks like we made it.
Seems so. And what a weird place this is...
One moment we're in familiar waters, the next we're here. Saw you stagger just a sec ago. I think all of us did too.
Must have been because of the drastic change in environs. We should've sent the mass-produced ships in first...
How are the others doing?
All good.
Our monitoring equipment works like normal. There's water and oxygen, and luckily enough, not a Siren to be found. I'd say our entry went about as well as possible.
Now onto the surveying part. Where're we goin' first? Lots of ground to cover here.
Well, my recon planes spotted the wreckages of mass-produced Sirens. They seem like pretty new models too.
So I say we follow the breadcrumb trail of wrecks to start with.
Sounds good to me.
Elbe, I just wanna point out...
There's another Tower of Midgard right behind us!
U-1206 was right. There, in the place they emerged from, stood the same towering structure and swirling maelstrom.
That's the same facility, and the same counterclockwise vortex...
Oh, I get it! This is our way home, come the time for us to leave!
So this is the exit? Gotcha! Feels smaller than the one we came from, though...
Smaller? Ah, that's because this Tower doesn't have the defensive turrets. They're separate from the Singularity generator, so that's probably why they're not here.
That makes sense! I'm glad we have a smart, good girl like you along, Elbe!
I am NOT a good girl! Say that again and I'll feed you to the sharks!
Too bad I'm not scared of sharks, so hah!
U-1206 swept in behind Magdeburg and stuck her tongue out at Elbe.
Sounds like you're acclimatizing well to this place. Listen, I'm going to repeat our objectives here.
Objective one: conduct a preliminary survey of the area and gather as much information as possible.
Objective two: find members of the neutral "META" faction and persuade them to join us.
Hang on, what?! The briefing didn't say anything about a second objective!
That's because it's not on the record.
And why's that, exactly?
It's a classified objective, which is why I couldn't tell you about it until we entered the Singularity.
That's not much of an explanation at all, but whatever I guess...
How are we supposed to find META ships, though?
For that matter, are you sure they're neutral, or that they're willing to talk to us?
We don't have any concrete way of finding them, but it's possible we will as we survey this area. That is our job.
As for how we know they're neutral... The Commander has defined them as such.
Hmm... In that case...
Any more questions?
Nah, not from me anyway.
If anyone else has one, ask it now. I cannot have you doubting the mission's purpose in the midst of a battle.
No doubts here. Now, are we heading for the wrecks I spotted earlier?
Yes, we are. U-1206, lead the way.
Got it! Diving down now!
Do not forget this operation is ultimately about gathering intel and negotiating. Avoid pointless conflict if at all possible.
(If we are to fight... It should be with a purpose.)
I've spotted a humanoid Siren! It looks to be... a new model entirely.
Surprised we've come across a new Siren model already.
Wonder if our attacks'll work on it... Good opportunity to find out!
Should I blast it, or go in for a punch?
Neither, you idiot! Let's not tempt fate! Moreover, something is strange with it...
It's alone. Usually Sirens come in groups, don't they?
Looks like it's on wreck-retrieval duty or somethin'.
Don't take that for granted. Sirens, especially humanoid ones, hardly ever work alone.
Heads up, Ulrich! I've spotted functioning mass-produced Siren ships among the wrecks!
What?! Agh! I must be blind for somehow missing those!
Hey, don't beat yourself up. Anyone could hide a ship among this many wrecks.
This either means these Sirens are capable of using tactics, or that they have a command unit leading them.
Whatever the case, what are your orders, Ulrich? Fight, or flee?
Supposing they're lying in ambush for us, they must possess sensor equipment outranging ours.
Ergo, avoiding them is not an option. Prepare to fight.
Oh sweet, our first-ever battle in a Singularity. Let's mess 'em up!
Hold it. They could be stronger than we expect. That being the case...
Send in the mass-produced ships first. We will not waste precious ammunition on Sirens if we can help it.
Inside the Singularity - Unknown Location
The Iron Blood's mass-produced ships moved in. Instantly, the Sirens hiding among the wrecks all emerged and opened fire.
Their firepower was truly staggering. The Iron Blood's ships were obliterated, and so their front was wide open.
The hell?! They melted our ships in an instant!
We juiced 'em up for fighting in the Singularity, but I guess that made no difference!
I had a feeling they'd only work as a distraction... Ulrich, let me do this!
Go ahead. We need aerial support.
C'mon, Mag. We've gotta step up.
At least we know what we're in for now. Time to take off the kiddie gloves!
Ulrich! The Sirens have submarines too!
Of course they do... Have you found their command unit yet?
Can't say for sure, but I couldn't see anything that looked like it!
(It seems approaching these Sirens like any other isn't going to work... But can we really afford to use our trump card already?)
(But, we might not have a choice, considering our mass-produced ships are as good as worthless.)
While Ulrich pondered her next decision, a violent explosion went off at the center of the Sirens' fleet. It happened without warning.
What... What was that? Did you see that, Ulrich?
Who did that?
No idea. I don't know what even happened.
It came from way over there! Someone or something hit the Sirens directly!
Look! Another one's coming!
Several high-speed projectiles appeared above the horizon, smoke clouds trailing behind them like the tails of comets.
They crashed into the Siren fleet, engulfing their ships in flames.
Cannon shells...? No, those were something else!
Whatever that was, it left their formation in ruins! Should we go in and start doin' damage, Ulrich?
(Those were obviously targeted attacks... That means there's someone else out here fighting the Sirens.)
(Either it's those META girls, or backup sent by the Commander. There's only one way to find out who...)
(By going straight to the source.)
Change course. We're finding out who fired those projectiles.

sequence:
The Many Lives of Maids

<size=45>The Maid on Her Last Legs</size>

scripts.say: I'd wrapped up the day's work and decided to pay a leisurely visit to the Royal Navy's teahouse in port.
Apparently, Vanguard was helping out around the store as part of the teahouse's maid trial program. Maybe I'll get to see her, I thought to myself.
Wouldn't you know it, there she was. We made eye contact.
Wh-why are you here, Commander? Err, excuse me, I forgot to say the line...
Ahem... "Welcome back, M-Master."
You're not the first to say that...
I'm honoured. Thank you. Assuming you mean it, anyway...
*sigh*... I'm so not cut out to be a maid. Who thought putting me on this programme was a good idea...
I'd just sat down to have a break since there were no customers, and then you show up.
Oh well... What would you like to order? I'll tell the kitchen staff to ready up.
Well, yes? People would be right mad if they caught a Royal Knight slacking around the Commander.
I guess I could have my break after you've ordered something. Not like anyone could complain then.
So, what will it be? I can recommend the house's scones and a glass of orange juice.

options.content: "I'm not really sure what I want."

scripts.say: Great, thanks. I know everyone raves about the tea, but our freshly squeezed orange juice is quite good as well.
I'll be back in a minute. Just kick back and get comfy.
A cup of tea then, as always?
Ugh... "Thank you for ordering, Master. We'll have your stargazy pie ready soon."
"Please make yourself at home until then. I'll be back shortly."
"Thank you for your patience. Here is your order. Bon appétit."
Oops. Brain got stuck in maid mode there. Enjoy your meal while I go lie on the sofa in the next room over.
I told you before, I'm NOT cut out for this bloody job. "It's great stress relief," they said... Yeah, right, my stress is going through the roof here!
Hats off to the Royal Maids who do this every day. I'd go mental if I had to.
God, I need something to unwind from these past few days... Do me a favour and let me sortie tomorrow, Commander.

options.content: "You're almost through with this. Hang in there."

scripts.say: Awesome! I knew you'd show compassion!
Just need to get through today, then I'll finally get to vent some steam!
You're kidding, right?
I mean... If you really enjoy having me as a maid, then I guess I'll bear with it...
Don't expect me to put on this uniform too frequently, though.
...Anyway, the sofa's calling! I'm going to have my break now. Take your time and enjoy the food.

sequence:
The Many Lives of Maids

<size=45>The Maid with the Distaste</size>

scripts.say: It was just before closing time at Scharlachroter Tresen – the Iron Blood's café.
What? Who's visiting this late in the– Oh! It's you.
W-welcome back, Mast– Ah, forget it! I'm not doing it. So, what's brought you here?
Ägir greeted me at the entrance. Her new uniform took me very much by surprise...
What are you gawking at? Does my outfit offend you?
Or is it the fact I'm lying down? I'll have you know I'm enjoying a break after cleaning all day.
...Y-you're just surprised by how good I look? Well, thanks...
That aside! I assume you want to order something. You're lucky we're still open a while longer.
So, I'm listening.
Let's hear your order. If it's on the menu, I'll have it done in a flash.
Everyone's favorite. As you wish.
Wait right here. This will just take a second... unless I fumble.
Excuse me? That's work fit for a secretary, not a maid.
Even if I say "sure," there's no guarantee I'll do a good–
Wait a damned minute! That's not even an item on the menu!
For god's sake... Stick to what's on it, or I won't bother with you.
If you really need documents sorted, ask me again after I've finished my job here.
Tell you what, I know something you'll like – I'll pour a glass of that.
Wait right here. This will just take a second... unless I fumble.
Here's your drink. Get comfortable and take your time. If that'll be all, I'll be over here resting on this couch.
I sat down with my drink, but held off on sipping it. I could feel Ägir's gaze on me...
What do you think? It's child's play for me! No trouble at all...
...You know what, let's not kid ourselves. It's obvious I'm not in my element.
August persuaded me into this, insisting it would be "a pleasant role reversal."
That may be right up her alley, but I feel a fervent distaste toward being ordered around as a maid!
I'll stop myself now before I grumble myself hoarse. This will all be over once you leave anyway.
Then I can close the book on this humiliating chapter of my life and go back to being myself again.
Ägir subjected me to a short rant, which wasn't very pleasant on the ears. On the bright side, the drink she poured for me was excellent.

sequence:
The Many Lives of Maids

<size=45>The Maid in the Night Mood</size>

scripts.say: Prinz Eugen invited me to visit her at a hillside café with a gorgeous view.
Right on time, Commander.
Guten Abend~ How do you like the view? Pretty good, am I right?
Silly, I'm talking about the skyline, not myself. Heehee~
Now... What would you like to order?
Come on, can't you take a hint? Look at me. I'm your personal maid for tonight.
Got to act the part, you know?
Why the surprised look? Let me guess – you don't think my uniform looks very maid-like?
Or is the view so incredible you just forgot all about the girl in front of you?
Aww, that hurts. I get into character and pick out nice clothes, and you ignore me?
Heehee. I'm just teasing you. I know you're not one to neglect your partner on a date.
So, let's start over. What would you like to order, mein Schatz? If you're in a wine mood, I can fetch the house special.
I thought you'd say that.
She took out a bottle sat ready behind the counter and poured a glass of wine for each of us.
Let's have a toast. To you, and to this beautiful night. Prost!
We gently clanged our glasses together and then had a sip from our glasses.
You can't chug wine like you chug beer, but that's fine. This night calls for a drink you can savor.
Oh, seems we've emptied our glasses already. Want a refill? I'm thirsty for more.
It was then that I remembered Eugen has a slight drinking problem.
Heehee... I know what you're thinking. It's written on your face.
Puh-leeease. I can hold my liquor. Let's not spoil the mood by counting glasses.
Besides, the night is still young~
Whew... I'm tellin' ya. Bismarck, me, everyone's changed so much since we took up post here~
An' you know who's to blame? Yeah, you – for making us all feel so whole and stuff~
You've given me somethin' I can't ever be without again... *hic*... I'm addicted to you, mein Schatz. You'll always be here for me, won'tcha?
She was officially drunk as a fish. It had gotten pretty late as well. Letting her have any more would've been a bad idea.

options.content: "Come on, Eugen. It's time to go."

scripts.say: Aww, alreadyyy? I was just gettin' started!
Waait... Heehee, I get it now! We'll go someplace else then drink some more~ That's whatcha mean, right? Sillyyy, you could've just said it. Be straight to the point, like me!
She'd clearly had too much already. I gave her a hand and led her back to the dorm...

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids! (Part 3)

<size=45>1 The Third Exercise</size>

scripts.say: Do you understand, Illustrious? This exercise is a sublime opportunity to gauge the strength of our latest carriers!
Both sides are to consist of three carriers each, plus a small escort fleet.
The Royal Maids did an exemplary job demonstrating the Royal Navy's excellence in the previous two exercises. You lot have a high standard to live up to, but I expect you'll do just fine!
One last thing: As this is an aviation exercise, neither I nor the Commander will be in charge.
...Those were Her Majesty's instructions.
The Royal Navy's exercise fleet will be centred around Centaur, Perseus, and Albion.
As for the opposing fleet, I'm told it's up to you to determine its composition, Commander.
"I see. It'll be hard to narrow down my picks when there are so many qualified candidates."
"Is there anyone you'd recommend, Essex?"
I do. The Essex class has plenty of combat experience, and I believe we'd make a worthy opponent for the Royal Navy.
If you're looking for specific names, how about Intrepid, Shangri-La, and Bunker Hill?
*knock knock*
Sorry for showing up uninvited, but I heard you're planning a carrier-on-carrier exercise?
How do you feel about giving Sardegna an opportunity to participate? We seldom get opportunities like this.
"I don't see why not. Though, Sardegna currently only has two carriers stationed here – Aquila and Impero. That leaves one slot to fill..."
I have no issues working with someone from the Eagle Union. Essex, what do you think about an Eagle Union-Sardegna Empire joint task force?
Well, it's certainly an ambitious idea and will pose an interesting challenge for everyone involved.
Commander, if you don't have any issues then I'm in favor of it.
"No objections here. That still leaves the question about the final carrier, though."
Intrepid might be the best fit, in my opinion.
"Then Intrepid it is. Also, I'm appointing you as the task force leader, Essex."
M-me? As you say! I promise I will not disappoint you!
Great. I'll inform Aquila and Impero at once.
Oh, and I trust you to assemble the escort fleet, Essex. Now, if you'll excuse me...
Okay then... Illustrious, has the Royal Navy already worked out its escort fleet composition?
Yes. We've chosen Manchester of the Royal Maids and Janus, a trainee maid.
Alright. In that case, I'm going with Reno as our light cruiser. We'll also need a destroyer...
"There's a candidate right here. We need at least one maid per side, don't we?"
...Me? Is this some kind of joke, Commander?
I may have taken some maid training courses, but that doesn't make me a full-fledged member of the Royal Maids, does it?
"Maybe not, but I'd say you know more than enough about the Royal Navy's tactics to fill in that role."
"Essex, Illustrious, are you two on board?"
I always trust your judgment, Commander!
Likewise. I believe she's just as qualified as any of the Royal Maids.
"Then that settles it. Jervis, you're on the escort fleet."
Uhh, I see... If you insist, I'll do as you say.

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids! (Part 3)

<size=45>2 Wings Above the Field</size>

scripts.say: This is the Royal Navy carrier task force. Connection established. Awaiting instructions from Elder Illustrious.
Has the fleet arrived at the coordinates?
Yes, they just reached the objective. Fortunately no signs of hostiles yet. Unfortunately, the weather looks quite poor...
Poor weather affects both sides equally. We just have to locate their fleet first and seize the advantage.
Has your fleet launched reconnaissance planes?
We have! Elder Perseus is currently surveying the area. We should find something shortly.
Please send over the data and I'll help with analysing it. In the meanwhile, contact me if anything happens.
I'm impressed, Albion. You gave off the impression of a skilled frontline commander during that call.
Thank you, but I still have much to learn, Elder Centaur.
My modest capabilities will be put to the test today. The joint Eagle Union-Sardegna task force will pose a considerable challenge.
Yeah, but it'll be a brilliant show of the Royal Navy's strength if we DO beat 'em, wunnit?
That is true. To that end, we'll all need to give it our all.
Course, heheh! I've got your flanks covered!
Albion, I just received some coordinates from Perseus. I believe she may have spotted the enemy.
"May have" spotted them?
Mhm. She said they are like, quote, "a flock of sparrows laying waste to a wheat field"...
I see. It must be some sort of code. Elder Perseus is wise to encrypt her messages.
If she has spotted them then it is only a matter of time before they spot her.
In other words, we must hurry. Onwards to the coordinates she sent!

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids! (Part 3)

<size=45>3 Manchester's Peculiar Tastes</size>

scripts.say: Elder Perseus! We've come to aid you!
Albion and Centaur draw their bows and launch their aircraft skywards, joining the battle with the enemy's own aircraft.
Wow, they're like a swarm of locusts fighting over territory.
Didn't you liken them to a flock of sparrows earlier?
Same idea. Fun fact about locusts: they're actually regular grasshoppers who undergo physical change and turn into locusts when the conditions are right.
Really?
Yeah! I've heard about that.
They make a decent snack, too. But they taste nasty when they swarm, so remember to go for the solitary ones.
People... eat locusts?
Well, yeah? You never had one?
If I may, I've never considered the idea either.
Neither have I...
So I'm the only one? That's a bummer, innit.
I was gonna offer to make some for ya after the exercise, but Belfast has banned me from doing that...
See, I made a plate for her once. She had one bite and told me to never cook again.
The most objectively correct decision I've ever heard, hones–
Owch! Hey! They just scored a hit on me!
It would seem they've broken through. Our carrier Elders are truly living up to their reputation!
We must not let them hit us again. Elders, enter a circular formation and neutralise the remaining fighter planes!
Remember, their task force members aren't used to each other's doctrines. We are better coordinated than them.
So teamwork is our key to victory, yeah? Tell ya what, I've got a plan...

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids! (Part 3)

<size=45>4 The Ruse Cruise</size>

scripts.say: Somewhere in the Exercise Area...
Enemy ships spotted! They're heading straight for us.
I'd suspect they'll try to disrupt our formation while we're unable to respond immediately.
It's a reckless plan. Only Manchester could've come up with that.
It's not reckless! At least call it "brave"!
Well, I suppose charging right at us with only Janus for backup is nothing if not brave to a fault.
Regardless, I'm afraid it's not going to work. Reno?
I agree. We've got planes on the way, so surrendering would be your best choice here.
Planes on the way? Heheh...
Our sides both have the same aviation strength to make it a fair fight. You can't have planes on the way if they're already all locked in a dogfight.
Huh? But Impero said she'd send some. Hang on, I'll have to check with Intrepid...
Now's our chance, Janus! Full speed ahead!
R-right! Sorry, Jervis, but I'm coming through!
Wait, wha–? Jervis, stop them!
...Dang it! It's too late to catch up to her now.
I can't believe you fooled us with that bald-faced lie...
When the enemy shows you their weakness, you've gotta exploit it!
Uh, Reno, Jervis? There's a destroyer coming towards me.
Without you to watch my flanks, I'm kind of a sitting duck here, sooo... send help.
Impero radioed for help in a lazy tone. Jervis turned off her communicator without a word.
...Jervis? Aren't you gonna help Impero?
There's little I can do for her. By the time I catch up to Janus, it'll already be too late.
What we should do is keep Manchester preoccupied so at least she can't come any closer to our carriers.
Smart move, but that means we'll be staring each other down until the exercise ends, dunnit.
Welp. I think we've pretty much lost already...

sequence:
Fight On, Royal Maids! (Part 3)

<size=45>5 The Victor is Determined</size>

scripts.say: Later, after the exercise's conclusion...
"The exercise was a great success. The Royal Navy, Eagle Union, and Sardegna Empire all fought brilliantly and learned much from each other, both as combatants and as allies."
Yes, yes, but who won? You can't just leave that out!

options.content: "The team with a Royal Maid trainee."
"The team with a Royal Navy destroyer."

scripts.say: Ah, that clears up the ambiguity... NOT!
Both teams had one of those, you dolt!
"Does it really matter that much who won? It's not like your reputation is at stake since you didn't participate."
Well, yes, that is true... but it DOES affect my reputation as a leader whether or not the Royal Maids brought home the victory.
"It's not about victory or defeat, it's about the journey."
*knock knock*
Commander, may I come in? ...Oh, excuse me for interrupting your conversation.
You're excused. My servant and I are done talking. Go on, tell us why you're here.
Thank you, Your Majesty. I've brought the exercise after-action report. Please give it a look.
Albion hands me the report. I start flipping through the pages.
There's quite a lot to read. Her reports are always much, much more lengthy and detailed than everyone else's.
Now if you'll excuse me, I'll be taking my leave. I hope you can both attend our celebratory banquet later in the evening.
"Wait, celebratory banquet?"
You can bet on it. I'll personally ensure my servant here doesn't get caught up in work and lose track of time.
Wonderful, Your Majesty. I'll be waiting for you at the venue! There will also be a lavish feast, courtesy of Elder Manchester.
...On second thought, I'll go right now! As the banquet organiser, I must be on location to ensure everything goes swimmingly.
Albion, you'll stay here and see to it that my servant makes it to the banquet on time.
Very well, Your Majesty... Are you certain the Commander won't mind?
Quite certain! My servant wouldn't object!

sequence:
The Queen's Ordinary Day

<size=45>1.An Ordinary Morning</size>

scripts.say: The sun rose over the Royal Islands on a quiet yet busy morning.
Birds chirped from atop their tree branches, their song flowing across the empty streets below.
Sunlight filtered through the curtains of the Queen's castle, marking the beginning of another wonderful day.
Royal Islands - Queen Elizabeth's bedchamber
Zzzzz...
Your Majesty, it's time to wake up. Please, Your Majesty.
Zzz... Five more minutes, Bel... Zzzzz...
You said the same thing five minutes ago. No work is going to get done if you stay in bed all day...
Nnngh... Oh, it's you, Newcastle... That's right, Bel isn't here right now...
*yaaawn*... Okay, time to get up!
Some time later, in Elizabeth's office...
After getting dressed and washing her face, the little queen sat down at her work desk.
Cup of morning tea in hand, she went through reports from her subjects all around the world.
Per Your Majesty's orders, we sent replicas to our exhibit at the World Expo. As predicted, several of the originals have since gone missing.
The data we gathered suggests META involvement, though the specific readings do not match anything we have on record. Furthermore, we are unable to trace how these infiltrations took place.
Moreover, sporadic Siren attacks were detected around the same timeframe the exhibition items were stolen.
While there may be some connection between the two events, we do not have any hard evidence to link them as of yet.
For the time being, all we can do is continue investigating.
I shall inform you if anything new comes to light.
Hmm... The Sirens targeting the World Expo was well within my expectations.
But, what does this unidentified META want with our Royal Islands?
Their motivations truly make no sense to me – and that goes for both the Sirens and the META.
(We've dealt several blows to the Sirens, both in the NA Ocean and through Friedrich's ploy. We've also made contact with certain META ships through Camelot.)
(So why is all of this happening now? How are they attacking us while hardly leaving any evidence behind?)
(I have a bad feeling about this... If there are META ships colluding with the Sirens, that could spell disaster.)
(Even the Ashes are not a monolithic faction. It isn't inconceivable that they would have members among them working with the Sirens.)
(...In any case, I can't just sit around and wait for reports to come in. Think, which parties might be interested in getting their hands on cultural artifacts?)
Newcastle, summon Gloucester. I want a report on Sardegna's and Iris Libre's recent movements.

sequence:
The Queen's Ordinary Day

<size=45>2.The Usual Lunch</size>

scripts.say: Elizabeth's Office - Noon
Your Majesty, it's almost lunchtime. Would you like to eat?
Let me finish what I'm doing first. Give me thirty minutes.
As you will. I shall wait until then.
Your Majesty, here's the report you asked for.
Finally. Let's make this quick.
Tell me your most important findings.
Of course.
Starting with Iris Libre, Richelieu's campaign in Africa is proceeding smoothly.
Her fleet has been steadily growing in strength and is expected to become a considerable force in the near future.
Meanwhile, the Vichya Dominion has been abandoning their territories one by one and redeploying their forces in mainland Europa, suggesting a change of strategy.
As for the Tribunal, we've learned that several of its members have left the continent of Europa to partake in covert operations.
However, due to the organisation's secretive nature, we've been unable to determine their means or objectives, and need to remain vigilant.
Are there any reports of the Tribunal attempting to reach out to Iris Libre?
Not as of yet. However, as both the Vichya Dominion and Iris Libre have set up pavilions at the World Expo, it is highly likely the two parties have interacted in secret.
Sheffield may know something, as she is on the scene.
I take it she's maintaining the appearance of a neutral party?
That's correct. Furthermore, we have not seen any movements from the Holy See in response.
If any new information comes to light, I will inform you at once.
I appreciate it. Speaking of which, what information do you have on Sardegna?
To the best of my knowledge–
Wait. On second thought, let's ask Illustrious instead. She's there in person.
Certainly, Your Majesty. I will contact her right now.
Illustrious, do you hear me?
Your Majesty? Yes, I hear you loud and clear. How may I be of service?
I want a word with you. Where are you right now?
I'm in the restaurant of the Royal Navy's pavilion. I'm afraid you caught me in the middle of dinner.
Please do forgive me. I will head to my lodging and call you back at once.
No need. I just wanted to know how things are over there.
I presume the Sardegna incident has been dealt with. Has everything gone well since?
Indeed it has. There have been no further problems so far.
Sardegna has done an excellent job maintaining order and keeping the event on schedule. In general, the mood here is quite festive.
Glad to hear it. I suppose that makes things easier for you.
What about Veneto and Littorio? Have you seen them?
I have, both during the opening ceremony and a few more times after that when they paid a visit to our pavilion.
I saw Littorio as recently as yesterday when she attended our banquet.
Alright. Finally, have you had a chance to speak to Marco Polo, the organiser of the expo?
Now that you mention it... No, I've not caught as much as a glance of her.
Hmm. Interesting.
Oh, I have one important thing to report, Your Majesty.
It seems the Dragon Empery delegation will be leaving the World Expo ahead of time, though I'm not sure if they're planning to return home just yet.
Hmm... Why would they do something like that?
Illustrious, when is the closing ceremony of the World Expo? They might know something we don't.

sequence:
The Queen's Ordinary Day

<size=45>3.Desserts After Lunch</size>

scripts.say: Castle Training Grounds - Noon
Let's see you parry this!
Hah! Not bad, but not quick enough to land a hit on me!
Now it's MY turn!
You may be quicker, but I've figured out your fighting style!
You blocked that?! Tsk... But you won't block–
Hold it, Vanguard! We are being watched.
Watched? Actually, yeah, I've been feeling that too...
I sense it from over there. Look. Is that... Her Majesty?
She's tiptoeing along the tree line. I can only assume she's trying to sneak out of the castle.
Well, she can't sneak past us.
Let's go talk to her. We'll call this duel a draw.
Your Majesty! Do you require help in any–
No, I don't! I'm just passing through!
Get back to your training. Don't waste your time worrying about me!
I'm afraid I can't do that, Your Majesty. It is my job to protect you, and to that end, I must know where you're going.
If I may ask, why are you sneaking around? If you're going on an outing, you need only tell me so.
Erp! Well, um...
There you are, Your Majesty.
Vanguard, you came at just the right time. I believe Her Majesty intends to leave for Scapa Flow by herself.
Newcastleee!
Scapa Flow?! Your Majesty, you cannot be serious!
What's wrong with that? Plus, lower your voice already!
With all due respect, it wasn't long ago when you reprimanded Monarch for the same reckless behaviour!
Fine, fine! If I must be held to the same standard, then you two come with me.
Yes, Your Majesty! Monarch, get yourself equipped.
There's no time to waste. Catch up if you're coming along!
Your Majesty, wait! Please give us a minute!
I've already given you one! I will not be late on account of you!

sequence:
The Queen's Ordinary Day

<size=45>4.A Stroll Through the Courtyard</size>

scripts.say: Mirror Sea - Camelot
Hey! If it isn't Her Majesty.
It is an honour to see you again, Your Majesty and company.
Yes, it's been a while. Is everything ready?
Yes, Your Majesty. Once the designated time arrives, the rest is up to you.
Got it. You two, follow me to the control station.
Your Majesty, may I ask what you intend to do? Are you going to use the Gate to teleport to another Mirror Sea?
Nothing of the sort. We can't risk drawing the attention of that Bon Homme Richard girl by activating the gate again.
Until we've completely ruled out any possibility of danger, use of the Gate is off-limits.
A wise decision, Your Majesty.
Whatever that monster taking the form of Bon Homme Richard really is, leading her to this branch would prove catastrophic.
That much is clear. We could barely even hold her off last time, and that was with outside assistance.
Hmm... But, we're not the only ones researching translocation through Singularities, right? If Iron Blood doesn't stop their experimentation as well...
I've contacted the Commander to hopefully get them to stop. None of us can afford to make any rash moves while we don't know what we're up against.
But, that doesn't mean we can't use the Singularities at all. Today, we're here for a completely different purpose.
That being...?
Establishing a communication hub through space-time.
Instead of creating one large energy signature by opening the Singularity for fleet travel, we'll basically poke holes in a bunch of different Mirror Seas for data transmission only.
This way, that Richard girl won't be able to trace us back to a single point of origin, assuming she even picks up on our minuscule energy footprint in the first place.
That's all well and good, but what even is your goal?
Simply stated, searching for friends.
If the Ashes can make allies, there must be SOMEONE out there willing to ally with us.
How do you know it's going to work?
I don't, but we'll never know until we try.
What's the alternative? Continuing to play along with the Reenactments? Fighting amongst ourselves forever?
To hell with that. I will not sign away the lives of my subjects in an unending, unchanging war.
And, neither will the Commander.
Protecting our azure lanes is our duty as shipgirls. Fulfilling it requires ending this war and ushering in a lasting peace.
And in order to defeat those who would make an enemy of peace itself, we must have a full hand of cards to play.
Your countermeasures are as magnificent as your ideals, Your Majesty.
If all goes well... I can hardly imagine how bright the future ahead of us will be.
Hmph, if only the power-obsessed leaders of Iron Blood shared your same vision.
Despite how things may appear, the situation is not so black-and-white. I believe we are ultimately working towards the same goal.
Every faction has its own strengths and weaknesses, as well as interests and ideals. Iron Blood is no different.
We are capable of things they are not, as is the Sakura Empire capable of things the Eagle Union is not.
We may all have been dealt different cards, but all we can do is play our cards to the best of our abilities. That is true, regardless of which side of the table one may sit at.
...Ahem. At least, that's what my servant would say.
I suppose all of us, across all factions, have been forging our futures in secret.
You could say that. Granted, I, too, was clueless once.
Clueless of many things. The nature of the Reenactments, the Singularities, the Crimson Axis, and even the Commander–
I could not tell good from evil, friend from foe.
To be honest, I don't even know how this plan will pan out. We have neither the knowledge nor the technology to predict that.
But one thing is for certain – this is better than doing nothing, isn't it?
...It's almost time now.
Hurry up onto the platform. We've got work to do.

sequence:
The Queen's Ordinary Day

<size=45>5.Afternoon Tea</size>

scripts.say: Mirror Sea - Camelot
*yaaawn*... Still nothing, hours later.
Nobody said it'd be straightforward, but that doesn't make this less boring.
Sis, Your Majesty, I'm gonna patrol the area for a bit.
Om, nom... Hawrigh. Fwake kherr. *gulp*...
Newcastle, may I have seconds?
Certainly. Just a moment.
You're sure you don't want a Royal Maid stationed here? It must be exhausting doing everything yourselves.
While I'm grateful for the offer, I must politely decline. We're used to our isolation and would need time to readjust to the company of others.
Of course, you may feel it necessary to leave a force here in the unlikely event of an enemy attack.
However, I believe Repulse and I alone are sufficient to prevent anyone from invading your branch.
All that is to say, we will manage on our own.
If anyone could use more protection, I would say you do during these visits, Your Majesty.
If I may interject, I also strongly discourage any more trips by yourself, Your Majesty!
Yes, yes, I know! Stop pestering me about it.
How absurd it is that the Queen must tiptoe around territory that rightfully belongs to the Royal Navy!
Curse that Bon Homme Richard... I WILL find a way to deal with her...
BEEP BEEP!
Your Majesty, did you hear that?!
I did! We must check the communicator at once!
Good lord... We've done it!
We've found a potential ally already?!
No. Settle down, Monarch.
We've managed to connect to some terminals out there, but we still can't send any information yet.
But, let's see... Good, the connection is stable and it doesn't seem we're being traced. We might just be able to receive data.
While there's much room for improvement, this is excellent for a first attempt!
Your Majesty, we should prepare to leave.
What? Oh, yes, it's gotten late.
That will be it for today. Renown, please analyze the results of our test and conduct any necessary debugging of the equipment.
Very well, Your Majesty.
One more thing. An unidentified META infiltrated our museum warehouse and left behind what presumably is beacon data. I'll send it your way.
We weren't able to match these data traces to anything in our database, but you might be acquainted with this individual.
They appeared... in a museum?
The beacon data will tell us if it's someone we know. Each META has a unique data signature.
Whoever it is, I hope you will be able to identify them. I look forward to hearing from you.

sequence:
The Queen's Ordinary Day

<size=45>6.A Hearty Dinner</size>

scripts.say: Royal Islands - Elizabeth's office
With her work for the day complete, the queen leaned back in her comfortable chair.
She leafed through a few reports on her desk, tossing finalized documents into a big pile.
BEEP BEEP!
Ah, Bel. What do you have for me?
Your Majesty, I have received a report regarding Vichya's movements.
Their mass-produced fleet stationed at the Kerguelen Islands has evacuated, effectively leaving it and its Basilica facility deserted.
Iris Libre appears unaware of this fact. Shall I contact Lady Richelieu?
No need. She'll go running over in no time.
...Wait a moment. Why would they even station that many mass-produced ships near the Antarctic region?
Bel, tell the fleet in the region to capture the islands and investigate the Basilica at once.
Find out what's inside, before the Tribunal gets to it!
As you command. I shall see to it.
(The Basilicas are said to represent the authority of the Iris Orthodoxy... but that's not the whole story.)
(The island that Richelieu occupied before contained a secret weapon called the Skybound Wall. There's a chance those facilities are the Holy See's research facilities.)
(If we get to it before the Tribunal does, we might be able to get a step ahead of the Naval HQ and assist Richelieu in the process.)
It's already getting late. Newcastle, we should head back now.
Just bring dinner over to my bedchamber. I don't want anyone bothering me this evening.
Understood. Shall I cancel your visit to the Coronation Abbey?
There's STILL more work to do? Ugh, let me rest for half an hour first...

sequence:
The Queen's Ordinary Day

<size=45>7.News Before Bedtime</size>

scripts.say: A luxurious, old-fashioned carriage slowly rolled through the gates of Queen Elizabeth's castle as the sun fully submerged beneath the horizon.
The carriage came to a stop, and an attending maid stepped forward to welcome the esteemed passenger.
Good evening, Your Majest–
Her Majesty is fast asleep. Please take her bags while I bring her to her bedchamber.
Very well, but what shall I tell Lady Warspite?
She's still waiting to hear from Her Majesty. Apparently, she has an urgent report to make.
That's a conundrum. I wouldn't want to wake Her Majesty...
I'll speak to Lady Warspite and ask her to leave a message. I'll inform Her Majesty in the morn–
Mmgh... Warspite...?
What was that about Warspite?
Oh, Your Majesty! Well, she's on the line for you with important business.
I considered answering on your behalf and forwarding her message to you tomorrow. Shall I do that?
No need. I'm awake now anyway.
I can't believe she's still up at this hour... I'll talk to her myself.
As you wish. Then what about the meeting with high command tomorrow?
It will go ahead as planned.
Very well...
Gloucester, did anything of note happen while I was away?
Yes. Sheffield had a report to give you, but I did not forward it to you at the time as your connection channel was not sufficiently secure.
That was the right call.
Newcastle, change of plans. Tell Warspite to hang up.
I'll call her myself after I've read Sheffy's report. Save my supper for later.
Yes, Your Majesty. I shall bring the communicator to your office.
It had already been a long day for the queen, but it was not quite over yet...

sequence: This is the story of an ocean in which battles come again and again.
Of a cerulean stage upon which steel-clad girls dance.
