You know, I think it shows the Commander's thoughtfulness~ to put us all together like this, all from different camps, and letting us shine. It's nice.
Well, if my Commander wishes it, I suppose I can muster up some motivation.
Directives received. Switching functionalities.
Now... I don't actually know where to begin...
Anywhere's good, right~ Let's try this: the first song, "cœur." Ready? One, two, three...
And so, with a little hope and a lot of unease, the newly formed group, Polaris, practiced their hearts out...

sequence:
One day, with Polaris...

<size=45>One day, during a break...</size>

scripts.say: One day, after rehearsal...
Phew... what do you say we call it a day?
Yes, there are limits to both time and stamina...
If that's how you feel, then I suppose we can take a break... But it's not like I'm tired or anything.
Observation: Hipper is in an abnormal state. Current Condition: Exhausted.
Haah?! Wh- who's exhausted?! I barely even broke a sweat!
Hehe, another day of hard work complete~ I think it's time to visit my Commander for a well-earned reward!
I'm a little curious what exactly you think that reward will be... Actually, I'd rather not hear the details...
Since we're done for the day, I'll go get us some drinks. Who wants what? Oxy-Colas? Coolant?
Gascogne requires coolant.
Tea... Actually, let me accompany you. Serving drinks is in fact a maid's duty.
I've heard you Royal Maids struggle under the yoke of a very strict Head Maid, eh...? In any case, I'll have a coffee.
I can't believe you Iron Bloods actually pour that filthy swill into your mouths... Hehe, I'd like tea. One of your splendid Royal Maids' teas.
Haah?! Coffee is the choice of a refined lady!
Here we go again.
Ahahaha... it's nice to see Hipper and Akagi getting along.
Haah?! Who the hell would get along with HER?
Hehe... Since it has nothing to do with my Commander, I suppose I can let you have it. Just don't let me see you slurping down your coffee and we won't have a problem~
I will fetch your beverages then. Kindly wait a moment.
Hey, I'm coming too! Gotta get me an Oxy-Cola on the way~
And so, the Polaris girls grew another day closer after a long practice session...

sequence:
Azur Anthem - Side Story

<size=45>4 Lessons</size>

scripts.say: One day, on the port's temporary stage...
Wow... Cleveland looks so cool up there onstage!
Big sis... is incredible...!
Sheffield... You have brought honour to the Royal Maids.
Aww, I want to get out of work too! Err, I mean, I want to do something to bring honour to the Royal Maids too!
Oh...? Well done. I can't wait to see the real thing, "Dear Sister." Hehe♪
The stage is yet another battlefield, Akagi. And I will watch your battle with great interest...!
Hah... I never thought we'd draw a crowd like this. I'm actually getting a little nervous.
And I never thought Belfast would come to this kind of show...
Hehehe... If I treat it as a special performance, just for my Commander, I can do great things~
Phew...
All that practicing was enough... Why do we have to get up on stage and do it again?!
Initial performance... Gascogne: physical parameters abnormal. Is this... "excitement?"
Stage fright and excitement go hand in hand. That's the thrill of a live performance!
You seem quite knowledgeable, Cleveland.
Aaagh! Fine! Here we go!
Executing song number one: "cœur."
And so began Polaris's first onstage performance...

sequence:
Captain Pompey Has You Covered!

<size=45>1 The All-Capable Secretary</size>

scripts.say: As the morning sunlight peeked in through the office windows, there was a soft knock on the office door.
Captain Pompey the Great has arrived! I'll be serving as your secretary, moving forward.
Good morning. You came at just the right time.
Of course! So, what's on the schedule today? Not that it matters, I'll take care of it all!

options.content: If you're sure. It's all up to you!
Well, things will be a little different today...

scripts.say: And so, the Commander left the port to go on a one-day business trip.
Pompeo was left all by herself and, as the acting secretary, had to deal with each and every one of the port's issues for the day.
What?! Hey! W-wait, Commander!
In a panic, Pompeo hurried after the Commander.
Meaning, there's much work to be done? Don't worry! With me by your side, it'll be done before you know it!
While that's reassuring, by "things" I mean that I have to leave on a business trip today.
I'll be away until tomorrow, and I need you to look after the port in my absence.
Okay! I can do that!
Wait, YOU'LL BE GONE A WHOLE DAY?!
I give Pompeo a series of encouraging pats on the shoulder.
I've already made arrangements for almost everything, but it's possible I forgot something or made an error.
If something urgent comes up, use your authority as the secretary to resolve it.
You can message me if you absolutely need my approval on something, but I might not reply immediately if I'm in an important meeting.
B-but I'm just... I can't...
You can. People say nothing but good things about you. You're reliable and capable.
Really? They say that about me?
You bet they do.
Hah! Well, if it's my help you need, then you shall get it!
Leave it all to me! I promise on my great name that I'll finish everything flawlessly!
Great. I'm counting on you.
As you should! Rest assured, nothing will go awry on my watch!
(Though I wish I could have you by my side...)
Hmm? Did you say something?
N-nope, nothing! When are you leaving?
In just a minute. Could you get me my briefcase?
Sure, here. Good luck, and I'll see you when you come back.
Thanks. Remember, you're in charge now. Don't let me down!
Please don't put more pressure on me than there already is!
Hahah! Alright, it's time for me to go.
Just a sec! Let me come along and see you off!
A soft breeze fluttered a curtain as Pompeo left the office and closed the door behind her.
Chatting casually, she and the Commander walked through the corridor, their voices growing more and more distant.

sequence:
Captain Pompey Has You Covered!

<size=45>2 Your Signature Here</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Pompeo Magno sat behind the desk. Her arms crossed, she was brooding over something.
This is lousy.
I thought "being in charge" and "looking after the port" meant doing something...
All I'm doing is keeping the bench warm!
No, no, I can't think like that. The Commander trusted me and asked me for help.
Need to get it together... L-let's have a look at this paperwork to be done.
There were two stacks of documents in front of her. One was a true pile of documents, with labels attached to them visible from the side.
The other stack was much thinner, and the topmost paper had a sticky note attached to it that read, "Due today."
Here we are. Let's see here...
Uhh... Um...
What did the Commander say I should do with these, again?
Right, I never asked about that...
You know what? I'll leave this for later. In the meantime, there's the...
..."Port Hygiene Inspection Report"?
"Please sign here if the report's findings are satisfactory."
That's all I have to do? Pfft, easy-peasy! Let me do that right awa–
Pompeo's hand stopped abruptly before the pen touched the paper.
Hang on! Whose name am I supposed to write? My own? Or should I write, "Commander checked and approved"?
Doesn't the document become invalid if I write my name on it? But it doesn't feel right to write, "The Commander says it's fine" either...
I-I'll leave this one for later, too.
Let's see what's next...
Captain Pompey put her all into processing the paperwork due that day.
And after all that effort, the pile had not shrunk even one bit.

sequence:
Captain Pompey Has You Covered!

<size=45>3 Way Over Budget</size>

scripts.say: *knock knock*
There was a knock on the office door.
Commander, you there? It's me, da Vinci!
Da Vinci?!
Hm? Is that you, Pompey?
The door opened, and into the office stepped da Vinci, the local inventor.
Hey, Comma– Huh? You're the only one here? Where's the Commander?
Out on a business trip. Left the port just this morning.
If you need anything, it's Captain Pompey you should talk to!
Ahh. You're the acting secretary today.
That I am! So, since you're here, what is it you need? Don't be shy, tell me and I'll have it done in a flash!
Heheheh... The Commander's not here, eh...
Ahem. See, there's actually a favor I wanna ask of you.
It's about a grant. Remember the Doggo Cattron 3000 I made a while back?
You mean that cat toy that barks like a dog?
Yeah, that one!
But it's not a toy, you hear? It's the culmination of my hard work!
...So, what about it?
Well, I wanna mass-produce it!
Okay...?
And to do that, I'm gonna need some money. I figure about this much...
Using her index finger, da Vinci wrote out a number in the palm of Pompeo's hand.
Whaddya think? Can you do it?
Request rejected!
Awww! Why?
That grant is the most insane ask I've ever heard!
Do you even realize how many digits that is?!
You're only saying that because you don't see the genius of my invention.
The Commander would say yes in a heartbeat!
The Commander would reject it before you were halfway done writing!
You don't know that! Nothing is impossible! Anyone would approve it if they just knew what's so innovative about the Doggo Cattron 3000!
Doesn't matter, because the answer is no! Hell no!
Come ooon, Pompeo! Don't be such a naysayer. All I need is one little seal of approval!
Lend me an inkling of your time and I'll make you see why this project is so important!
Rejected, and that's my final answer!
Pleeease, Captain Pompey the Great!
No, no, and again, NO!
The "negotiation" between the two went on for quite some time.

sequence:
Captain Pompey Has You Covered!

<size=45>4 Why in the Library?</size>

scripts.say: Sometime later...
Sat at the desk, coddled by the warm afternoon sunlight, Pompeo began drifting off to sleep.
Just a short break to rest my eyes...
Mmh... I guess I dozed off.
At least it's not even been an hour... It would've affected my work if I'd slept any longer.
Zzz...
Pompeo heard gentle snoring coming from somewhere. She bent forward over the desk and searched for the source.
And there she was, on the couch, sound asleep.
...Impero?
Hey. Impero. Wake up.
Mghh...
Come on, wake up. When did you even get here?
*yaaawn*... I heard you'd been appointed the secretary for today, so I came to have a look.
I knocked several times to no response, so I came in and saw you sleeping like a baby at the desk.
So I thought, "Screw it, I'll just have a nap too."
Makes sense... Wait, no! Why did you come here in the first place? What business did you have with me?
Oh, I remember now. I was gonna ask you to install beds in the library.
Excuse me? Beds?
Yup. I fall asleep when I read, and Littorio's always bugging me about how I'll catch a cold if I keep that up.
So, if we put beds in the library, I could sleep under a warm blanket and not have to listen to any nagging.
Is that a "no"?
It's not. First of all, though, please sleep in the Sardegnian dorm and not here. I'll write your request down and present it to the Commander.
*yawn*... Thanks. Then if you'll excuse me, I'm gonna resume my nap.
I just asked you not to...
Hey, this couch is comfy.
*sigh*... Fine, whatever. Let me get a blanket for you.
Thanks. You're a good secretary.
Heheh...

sequence:
Captain Pompey Has You Covered!

<size=45>5 You're Not Alone!</size>

scripts.say: Sometime later again...
Although at a snail's pace and with missteps along the way, Pompeo was chipping away at the pile of documents.
To think the Commander has to go through this much time-consuming work every single day...
I never noticed just how much it was, despite working here for so long.
Now that I'm processing it myself, the sheer volume of work to do is really sinking in.
Whew... Let's see how much is left to do...
Seeing how much remained, her morale took a nosedive.
I-I've not even made a dent in it!
There is no way I can finish this by myself...
The Commander said I'm reliable and capable, that people say good things about me...
If the Commander finds out THIS is all I managed to do, I'm so done for... Everyone's going to hate me...
Nobody is going to hate you, Pompeo.
Yeah, they will... I was expressly trusted with this job, and I'm failing fantastically...
Think about it this way – the Commander doesn't work alone, so why should you have to?
What are you suggesting?
It's quite simple...
The source of the voice stepped forth and gently moved aside the documents obscuring Pompeo's view.
That when something seems impossible on your own, you should ask someone for help in good time.
That's right – I'm here to assist.
Aquila...
I know you're in a bit of a pinch, and I'd like to ease your burden.
Is there any work I can help with?
Thank god you're here...
Yeah, there's tons! For a start, could you review these documents for me?
These, you mean? Sure thing.
By the way... Da Vinci said she'd stop by to help in a while.
She had gone around claiming that you'll permit anything while the Commander is absent, which is why Impero came to visit you earlier. She shouldn't have done that.
Don't worry, though. I've already nipped that rumor in the bud.
And let's just say I "asked" da Vinci to come help as a way of atoning.
Thanks for doing that. Dealing with her was a pain because she just wouldn't back down.
Think nothing of it. Also, shouldn't you be working now? I believe these documents are due today, so...
Ugh... We've got a long road ahead of us.

sequence:
Captain Pompey Has You Covered!

<size=45>6 Teamwork Makes the Dream Work</size>

scripts.say: Evening was drawing near. Though it took considerable effort, the girls eventually managed to escort the sleepyhead Impero to her dorm room.
Now the three remaining Sardegnians were waging war on the hill of paperwork to be finished before the day.
Da Vinci, have we gotten inventory on the depot yet?
Not yet. Akashi said there's just too much stuff in there, so it's gonna take a while longer.
It's been three days since the lights in the academy's corridor broke. Why haven't they been replaced yet?
Oh, one of the documents mentioned that. Ingraham was in charge of maintenance that day, but then she got assigned an urgent mission.
She missed the opportunity to replace them as a result.
Okay then. Da Vinci, do you reckon you could do it?
Sure. I'm on it~
Wait, right! I need to issue you a certificate of supplies withdrawn. Where was that again...
Here. I've already filled one out.
Oh! You're way ahead of me!
Alrighty, I'd better head to the academy before it gets dark.
Take care!
Will do!
Now for the next thing to deal with...
Apropos of nothing, I heard from Veneto that when signing documents, the secretary may use either her name or simply write, "Request approved."
In that case, I'll write Captain Pompey the Great!
Umm... I'm not sure that will fly with the admiralty.
Oh... Okay, I'll just write Pompeo Magno, then!
There we go. Just sign here and you should be good.
Pompeo... Magno... There! Okay, next.
Thanks to everyone's efforts, Captain Pompey the Great had evaded the fate of a forced all-nighter... or did she?

sequence:
Captain Pompey Has You Covered!

<size=45>7 It's Not a Toy!</size>

scripts.say: Office - The following day
Pompey?
Pompey, are you in there?
No response. Time to go in and check.
On the desk by the window, papers lie organized into neat stacks.
Several cute little smiles have been drawn on the sticky note that reads, "Due today."
Zzzzz...
Pompeo is asleep on the couch. I softly walk over and adjust her blanket for her.
She looks so sweet, sleeping with her cap substituting for an eye mask. An urge to mess with her crosses my mind.
I reach towards her hat, but before I can take it off...
Hey! My cap is not a toy!
At just the right time, she wakes up and dexterously puts her cap back on.
Commander, you're back!
What are you doing, sleeping in my office?
Don't tell me you had to work late to finish everything.
Not at all! Getting it done was a piece of cake.
Well, not really... In truth, I have Aquila and da Vinci to thank for helping me.
Oh, sorry if I wasn't clear – we got the work done way ahead of time!
The reason I slept in the office was so I could welcome you back as soon as possible!
I knew messaging Aquila was the right call.
Messaging Aquila? You mean...?
A certain someone here did promise on her great name that she'd finish everything flawlessly.
Commander...
A blush takes shape on her face.
Either way, you did a great job. What do you say we go get breakfast?
Sure!
Wait, one thing! I can't go outside just like that. I need to wash my face first.
I'll be done in 30 minutes... no, 20!
She hurries out of the office to find a bathroom somewhere.
I take a seat at my desk and pick up the note with the smiling faces drawn on it.
The next time I get called on a sudden business trip, she'll manage to hold the fort even better.
Okay, I'm ready, Commander!
She returns with a lightness in her gait.
THAT was quick. Didn't you say you'd need 20 minutes?
Heehee... I'm always faster than the estimate!
By the way, shouldn't Captain Pompey the Great expect something more than just breakfast as thanks for her hard work?
I think I deserve something, you know... great.
Very well, Captain Pompey – what is your desire?
Ahem. I'm glad you asked! I don't ask for much. All I want is 24 hours by your side!
Which is to say, I want to spend this shared day off together with you!
And not just for breakfast, but for lunch, teatime, dinner... and whatever comes after that, too!
Got it, Commander?
If so, you need only present thy appendage! Come on, give me your hand~
As she asks, I extend my hand.
She extends her own as well, locking her fingers with mine. Our palms touch.
This is a part of my reward, silly. Heehee~
Now, let us set off on our magnificent date together!

sequence:
A View For Two, With You

<size=45>1 A Girl and Her Telescope</size>

scripts.say: Emanuele Pessagno, reporting for secretary duty.
A girl lugging a giant telescope around stands at the entrance to my office.
Today is her first day working as my secretary ship.
Good morning, Commander. Umm... May I enter?
"Of course. Come on in."
Pessagno—who we've taken to calling Ema for short—tries to take a step, but she suddenly freezes up.
That was close... I almost smashed my telescope against the door frame.
S-sorry! Just a second...
She backs off, frantically takes the telescope off of her back, and enters my office holding it with both arms.
The poor girl is even more nervous than usual now.
And compared to her small figure, the giant telescope stands out even more.

options.content: "Is there something special about that telescope?"

scripts.say: Hm? Are you curious about it, Commander?
It may just look like an antique monocular, but it's actually special supporting equipment.
It's important for both navigation and combat... Oh, and of course, it naturally works just fine as a normal telescope.
With this, you can get a perfect view of even the most distant scenery!
I just love immersing myself in... Oh!
Sorry. I didn't mean to go on a whole monologue...

options.content: "It's good to be passionate about things. I like your telescope."

scripts.say: (She's not as nervous now. I'm glad I brought it up.)
...Thanks, Commander.
I was so worried about being given this job.
People tell me I'm not very good company, they can't tell what I'm thinking, I don't express myself enough...
It made me nervous thinking that you would feel the same way.
But I'm okay! Now that I know you like telescopes, too...!
(That's what matters to her?)
Da Recco was right. There's nothing to worry about as long as we're with you, Commander.
"I'm glad you think so. Now, are you ready to get to work?"
Yeah! Leave anything to me.

sequence:
A View For Two, With You

<size=45>2 The View Through the Lens</size>

scripts.say: Is that all of our work for today, Commander...?
"Quick double-check... Yes, I'd say that's about it."
Okay. Then may I...
Ema glances at the telescope on the other side of the room.
*stares*... *fidgets*...
*stares*... *rocks back and forth*...
You mean it? Thanks, Commander! Umm, while I'm at it, would you like to join me?
Wh-why are you looking at my telescope, too...?
Oh, do you want to take a look through it? I'll set it up right now!
Ema excitedly prepares the telescope and teaches me how to use it.
...That'll do it. I doubt you'll be able to set up manual focus on your first try, so I put it on auto-focus for now.
Here you go! Have fun.
I look into the eyepiece, and a distant part of the port comes right into view.
(Blue skies, white clouds, the busy wharf... and oddly, Alfredo Oriani sneaking around.)
(She's hiding in the tall grass... and sneaking pictures of Elizabeth out on a stroll?)
How do you like it? You can see all the wharf from your office. Awesome, right?
You can almost feel the sea breeze, right?!
(Whoops, looks like Sirius found Alfredo in the middle of her candid photo session.)
Your office has a good view, so I've wanted to try this ever since I learned I'd be your secretary... Heheh...
(Alfredo tries to escape, but Sheffield blocks her path! Alfredo's in huge danger!)
(Too bad! Her big scoop is all but lost!)
...Commander? What's wrong? You haven't said a word.
Heheh, are you too engrossed by what you see?
"It's so interesting that I can hardly take my eyes off of it. Maybe you could call that being engrossed."
Not wanting to monopolize it for too long, I reluctantly let Ema take a turn on the telescope.
Ema frowns at what she sees.
Is that... Alfredo? Why are the maids dragging her off?
And she's throwing a peace sign this way?
D-did she think we were snooping like her?
...Wait a second. Commander, is this what you were staring at so intently?
Geez...
*sigh*... Anyway...
I'll set it up so we can look at REAL scenery this time.
She adjusts the telescope and admires the view.
Ooh, yeah... This is really pretty...
Ema carefully adjusts the telescope's positioning, moving along with it. She has a big smile on her face, clearly taken by the scenery.
Can we? Like, right now?
She smiles happily. There's more to scenery than what you see through a lens, after all.

sequence:
A View For Two, With You

<size=45>3 Out of Focus</size>

scripts.say: The door to my office slowly opens, and one dejected Ema appears.
Hi, Commander...
After weakly greeting me, she takes a seat and stares vacantly at the documents.
So I organize these files... And then these...
(I don't think she realizes that she's been sorting the same pile of documents over and over.)
(She's clearly not all here... Something must be wrong.)
...Huh?
Oh, the files!
Sorry... I'm not getting any work done at all, am I?
"It's not a big deal. Checking and rechecking your work is good practice."
"If there's anything bothering you, though, I'm happy to listen."
Well...
She's still sad, but Ema tells me what happened.
Earlier, at the port...
(Morning at the port is pretty in such a different way! Good thing I took this little detour.)
(Oh, what just jumped up that tree? A squirrel...?)
Whoooa, big telescope!
Whatcha looking at? Something cool?
(I hear someone talking, but... I doubt they're talking to me.)
(Focus on that tree... You might find a little house of squirrels!)
Now, now. Don't disturb her.
Aww... Yeah, I know I shouldn't.
But now I really wanna know what she's looking at!
(Hmm... Are they talking to me?)
Oh! You two are from the Northern Parliament, right...?
Yes. I'm Avrora, and this is Pamiat' Merkuria. You would be Sardegna's Emanuele Pessagno, yes?
Right! Sorry... I didn't realize you were talking to me.
Umm, do you need something...?
Me and Avrora here were just investigating this area.
With that huge telescope, you must know which places have a good view, right? Any recommendations?
Recommendations? Umm... For what, exactly?
Duh—for a date with the Commander, of course♪
D-date?!
Yeah! I need date ideas!
C'mon, tell me any places that you can think of!
U-umm, well...
(I have gotten curious and looked for fun date destinations, but...)
(A first date would be... There, of course. And after that, erm... Right, I'd have to recommend...)
(Then, if you had time, you'd go there... Oh, and you can't miss that one... Hmm...)
Hellooo? You there?
...Yeah, forget it. She's overheating so much, her head's gonna start smoking.
(This is bad... I already have the perfect route in mind, but how do I even begin to tell them...)
Kuku, it's not nice to tease. We're sorry for disturbing you.
Ahaha... Yeah, my bad. We actually just happened to be passing by, y'know.
I was kidding about the date thing! Calm down a little.
Okay! Geez, Avrora, I'm coming! You don't have to pull!
I wasn't really worried or unwilling to tell them...
There are so many places I want people to know about, but I just don't know how to communicate it...
Ugh, come on, Ema...
I really wanted to tell them, but for some reason, the words won't come out.
Maybe it's true what they say...
I'm not very good company, it's impossible to tell what I'm thinking, and I don't express myself enough...
(She's only making herself feel worse. I should do something.)

options.content: "Is there anywhere you'd like to go?"

scripts.say: Y-yeah!
But... *sigh*...
(I was able to get her mind off of it, if only for a moment. Let's keep this up.)

sequence:
A View For Two, With You

<size=45>4 Out of Sight</size>

scripts.say: Ema and I climb a nearby mountain together.
Thanks for coming with me, Commander.
I've always wanted to show someone the scenery from here.
Umm, anyway, I'll set up the telescope right away!
"So you've been here a few times before."
Yep. It won't take long for me to set up.
"In that case..."
"I think I'd prefer not to look through the telescope this time."
While we're at it, you can... Huh?
I want you to tell me what you see, through your own words.
Oh, I get it... You want me to practice my communication.
But are you sure, Commander?
We went through all the effort of climbing up here, and you just want to... listen to me describing the scenery?
I'm really... not good at this stuff...
"Everything is hard at first."
"Besides, I can see plenty without the telescope already."
"Not everything you want to see has to be beyond the lens of a telescope."
That sounds oddly philosophical...
Okay. If you're really sure, then I'll do my best to describe everything as best as I can.
Uh, wait just a second...
...Huh?
Wh-why...? I can't get it to work automatically or manually!
The focuser is malfunctioning...
A-aww, man...
This is all my fault. I use it so much, but I've been slacking on maintenance.
I wanted to look upon all the scenery...
And tell you all about it, and how I feel...
I mustered all my courage and resolved myself, but now...
The telescope malfunction hurts her feelings more than I'd expected.
"There's nothing we can do about it now. It's a shame, but all we can do is go back."
Okay...! As soon as we get back, I'll ask da Vinci to repair it for me.
Once it's ready, we'll come back together! Promise me!

sequence:
A View For Two, With You

<size=45>5 Close-Up</size>

scripts.say: Three days later...
Hi, Commander...
The door to my office slowly opens, and once again, one dejected Ema appears.
Da Vinci's taking so long this time...
Y-You don't think she's adding some weird features to my telescope, is she?!
Worry... Fear... Concern...
Even as she mumbles about her feelings, she never stops organizing documents.
(I need to put a stop to this. It's about time for a certain invention of da Vinci's to take the stage.)
The... Scenery-Spiffying Telescope Mk.II? Th-thanks, I'll give it a try.
...Hm? Uhh... It doesn't have any lenses?
How are you supposed to look at the scenery...?
Are you saying I should look at what's around me, instead of seeing everything through a lens?
Yeah... Maybe you're right.
Telescopes let you see distant things with such clarity.
I end up getting so focused on those things...
It made me forget all about everything close to me.
To communicate with others, you need to see them head-on. I've always missed this simple, but vital truth.
Yeah... I'll give this one a try, Commander!
Hmm, so this is the seat you always sit in...
Every day, you sit here and do your work...
This is your coat rack, where you put your hat and jacket...
Hmm... Those are some interesting books on your shelf. I'd never noticed...
And over here... Eep!
Sorry, Commander! I should watch where I'm going...
*knock* *knock*
Yoohoo, Commander!
Hey, it's the telescope dork, too!
U-Umm...?
Ema, was it? Sorry for her...
Heheh, my bad.
Uh, it's... fine...?
We met before, didn't we? The girls from the Northern Parliament?
I'm sorry I couldn't be more helpful last time. Do you have business here?
Yes, we have some documents that we'd like the Commander to check.
And... Not to be rude, but why are you looking at us through a telescope?
Umm, i-it's a long story... Sorry you had to see me like this...
Don't be silly. As far as I can tell, you're not Ema without a telescope!
Weird that you've got it pointed inside instead of outside, though.
Hahah! Does that mean I'm part of the scenery?
(In a way, she's actually right...)
U-Umm, basically, this is...
Don't worry about it! No need to force yourself to explain everything.
We're just here to report to the Commander. Once we finish, we're out.
Heheh♪ I get the feeling we're gonna hear all about Ema's favorite spots soon~
You mean the date destinations?
I'll do my best to get better at communicating, so just give me a little longer...
"What's this about dates?"
Whoa whoa whoa! That was a joke, I swear! A joke!
Gosh, why is this girl so serious about everything?!
Oh, yeah! I just remembered we're here for a thing! Avrora, show them the thing!
And there she goes...
Did I say something weird?
Pamiat' will be just fine. Shall we get back to work?
Now, regarding this document...

sequence:
A View For Two, With You

<size=45>6 A Columnist's Debut</size>

scripts.say: One week later, during lunch...
Phew... Thank goodness. Da Vinci didn't add any weird features to my telescope.
After thoroughly inspecting her repaired telescope, Ema breathes a sigh of relief.
I'll need to thank her properly later. This telescope is really important to me...
Just then, with a bang, the door to my office is thrown open.
Ema, are you here?!
Yes, but...
Alfredo, make sure you knock before entering next time.
Also, keep your voice down during breaks.
Sorry, sorry! I just got great news and wanted to let you know ASAP!
I'll be more careful next time.
(If it has Alfredo this worked up, then...)
Heheh... Listen, and be amazed! Ema and I did a collab column in the port newspaper, and it's a big hit!
Collab column...?
C'mon, work it out. We made a column on scenery together!
She writes like she's serving you a slice of the real deal. Readers say we've given them a sense of immersion so good that it feels like they're actually there!
It's just our first one, but it's already the talk of the port!
Of course, it's partially thanks to my own pizzazz. Check out this title: "Behold, Hidden Vistas! Seven Secrets of the Port You NEVER Knew!"
Wait, Ema! You did a really good job, so why didn't you tell the Commander?!
U-umm... It slipped my mind?
Ahem. Here's my next manuscript. That's enough small talk, so you'd better get it ready soon.
Ooh, another spectacular article! New sales records! I can see it... I can see it!
Heheh, geheheheh... By the way, Ema, you've changed since you became a secretary ship.
Before, I never would've dreamed of YOU inviting ME to do something together.
And you keep giving me these awesome articles!
By the way, I brought the reader survey with me!
Heheh, we've already got letters about your debut column!
This one says "to the telescope dork," so I could tell at a glance that it was for you.
O-okay... Leave it there, and I promise I'll read it later.
Don't you think you should get back to work? I'm sure there are plenty of huge scoops with your name on them.
A-alright, just stop pushing me!
Bye, Commander! I'll bring the next one as soon as it's ready! I'd better get going for today!
Okay, that's enough goodbyes... Be on your way, please!
Ema chases Alfredo out of my office, blushing bright red all the while.
Alfredo always says too much... *sigh*...
Erm, I couldn't find the right timing... B-besides...
Aww, don't look at me like that... I just didn't mention it because...
You don't need to go out of your way and read the columns...
I-I mean... I'm right here next to you.
If there are any sights you want to know about, I'm happy to tell you...
Ema closes her eyes tight and manages to squeak it all out.
She blushes as she goes back to her seat. Then, she goes back to work as if nothing happened...
...All the while ignorant of the bomb she just dropped.

sequence:
A View For Two, With You

<size=45>7 Beautiful Sights</size>

scripts.say: A few days later, Ema invites me out again.
Thus, we climb to the top of the same mountain.
Wait a second... I still need to adjust the telescope a bit.
She single-mindedly focuses on the view, adjusting the telescope through the lens. Sometimes, she writes something in her notes.
Even now, she loves seeing distant sights through her telescope. But...
She's also learned how to appreciate what's right in front of her.
And no matter the distance, she does her very best to convey what she sees.
...There. It's done.
Commander? You look happy. Did you get good news today?

options.content: "I'm just excited to see the sights."

scripts.say: For me...? Where's this coming from?
U-umm... Thanks, I think?
Yeah! Me, too...
I've been looking forward to today...
Ema takes a deep breath, as if steeling her resolve. Then...
She circles behind me and gently pushes me toward the telescope.
It's important to see things in the distance, but you can't neglect what's close to you.
Thank you for helping me realize that, Commander.
Because of you, I can see so many things that I'd overlooked before.
And... I want to return the favor.
I set up the perfect vista for you. One that I've always wanted you to see.
Also... Umm...
While you look through the telescope, I'll view the same scenery without it...
And I'll whisper what I see... into your ear...
Ema gently leans against me.
Yeah... Let's enjoy the scenery, both near and far, together.

sequence:
Like a Soaring Apsaras

<size=45>1 Like a Soaring Apsaras</size>

scripts.say: I was trudging along a stream running through the mountains–
When suddenly, the melody of a pipa echoes around me. Its soothing tones seem to permeate me, melting away the fatigue of my long trek.
I continue on towards an open area, eventually reaching the destination Hai Tien and I had agreed upon previously.
Commander, I appreciate you coming all the way out here.
I've been waiting for you. The tea is ready, so let me get it for you right away.
"By the way, I heard the sound of a pipa earlier..."
Oh, umm... I was just getting some practice in. I didn't think anyone would be able to hear it...
I originally was planning a surprise performance for you, but you'll have to forgive me for fumbling it.
...Hm? Hearing me play was enough to make your fatigue melt away?
Ahaha... You don't have to go out of your way to console me...
(Ugh... I was so preoccupied with creating the right atmosphere for our date that I didn't consider how tiring the trek up here would be....)
But, if my music was enough to make you feel better, I am relieved to hear that.
In any case, Commander, I called you here today because I wanted to show you the dance that I've been practicing for quite some time now.
It's called the "Soaring Apsaras"– an acrobatic combination of dance and music. I do hope you'll find it to your liking.
...Hmm? Was there something you wanted to ask me, Commander?

options.content: "What kind of music are you going to perform?"
"Can you tell me more about this dance?"

scripts.say: It's a bit embarrassing to say this... But it's my original composition.
Ever since I first met you, each and every day has been filled with joy and excitement. Before I knew it, you became the first and foremost thing on my mind.
I can't do anything about these overflowing feelings, but I at least want to put them down in song form... Hopefully, you won't find it strident to your ears...
Commander, you should already know that I'm not very athletic.
But this time, I'm going to overcome my limits. Just thinking about performing in front of you makes all the difficult hours of practice feel like a distant memory.
Who knows? Maybe I'll be able to capture that same feeling you felt when you heard the sound of the pipa~
Heehee. In any case, you're the reason why I'm able to show these things to you today.
In the mountains, the stream burbles beneath the shade of great willows. The flowers are in full bloom, and the wind is refreshing.

When music reverberates, everything becomes more melodious and magnificent. My performance then blends into the scenery all around us, creating a dreamlike, mesmerizing mixture of movement and stillness.
But to be entirely honest, the beautiful scenery around us probably compensates for the inadequacies in my performance. Please bear with me, Commander.
Now then, relax and take a deep breath, and then we'll get started–

Sometimes as violent as a sudden hurricane in the summer, at other times as gentle as a newborn's breaths... The sound of the pipa, along with the stream flowing right next to me, seemed like reminders from the heavens to leave behind the material world.
I can't take my eyes off Hai Tien. It's as if I had stepped into a fairyland depicted in a storybook.
How was it, Commander?
I'm so glad to hear that! All my hard work has finally paid off!
Oh, um... Ahem, sorry I got carried away there. Please forget you saw that...
If you don't mind, would you mind staying here with me a bit longer?
Since you already came all the way up here, why not enjoy a cup of tea while taking in the scenery?

options.content: "Do you think I could learn that dance?"
"Woah, so that's how you play the pipa!"

scripts.say: ...Huh? Wh-what did you just say?!
I'd be honored to teach you if you really are interested in learning!
Though, um, I'm not sure I'd be able to do a good job getting the point across with words alone...
Hai Tien suddenly shoots up and slides over to my side.
Ah, umm... this is just to teach you the dance moves...
Now then, please excuse me–
Oh my, you've picked up on it so quickly. As expected of someone as accomplished as you, Commander.
That being the case, allow me to make a suggestion–
How about you improvise a melody, and I'll dance to it? Only if you're up for it, that is.
Since you're improvising, don't worry if you make any minor mistakes. In fact, I... I'd prefer it if you could keep your eyes on me...
Oh, but having that said...
Umm, if I stumble over my own feet and bump into you because I'm a bit of a klutz... Please don't hold it against me, okay?
Somewhere in the Northern Parliament - Conference Room
You’re early than I expected... It must have been difficult to rush over here, Belorussiya. How is your health?
Truly no rest for the wicked in times like these. Still have a faulty power system, and my turret might need an overhauling, but that’s what happens when you rush back from the front lines.
It’s all minor stuff though, and more importantly, I’ve made it back in time. By the way, where’s Sovetsky Soyuz? Wasn’t she the one who sent out this emergency assembly order?
Unfortunately, she had to set out for another meeting in St. Petersburg yesterday, so now I’m in charge over here.
Guess it’s that time again, huh... But given how we’re besieged on all sides, I guess it doesn’t matter if she’s here or not, eh?

As of late, the Azur Lane has been preparing for a large-scale operation in the NA Ocean. Whether our navy participates in this operation,and if so, through which means and to what extent, are all major decisions that require the input of Sovetsky Soyuz.
One moment, she’s fighting on the front lines. The next, she’s fighting the bureaucrats in back rooms. I don’t envy the responsibilities of our fleet leader.
Let me guess, the reason why I was called back urgently is because it’s finally time to take that commander to the Arcana Sanctum?
Precisely. Through our time working with you, Comrade, you’ve not only proven your worth as a commander, but also demonstrated exceptional strength of character.

You have proven that you are willing to look beyond prejudices and are not beholden to any of the various factions you’ve worked with in the past. The ability to set aside your own preconceptions and strive towards the survival of humanity truly embodies the ideals of the Azur Lane.
You have more than earned your title of “Comrade,” but I am not here to flatter you. We believe you are the key to unraveling the unique phenomena we have seen in the records from the Arcana Sanctum.
By all our indications, you are ready to learn the secrets we’ve discovered.
This matter is of great importance. Sovetsky Soyuz had planned to take the commander there herself, but there’s no shrugging off summons from St. Petersburg. That’s where we come in.
We can wait a couple days for the meeting to end before taking the commander over, can’t we? There’s no reason why we need to rush things so much, is there?

Mmm... I’m not sure if you’ve noticed, but the situation in Europa has been very strange as of late. After the attack on Scapa Flow, we were expecting a full-blown engagement between the Royal Navy and the Iron Blood. Instead, both sides have been eerily quiet about this matter.
That does sound suspicious. Do you think the two sides managed to broker some kind of deal?
Hard to say. The Iron Blood has a roundabout way of doing things, and knowing the Royal Navy... In any case, because the situation has eased up, they want to bring the commander back.
Tsk... What a demanding bunch.

We’ve received intel showing that they’ve begun significant preparations for this purpose. Because we no longer have any reason to keep delaying, our hands will probably be tied once their convoy arrives.
Hmm... Got any specifics about their preparation progress?
We’re not exactly sure which route they’re taking, but they should be here within the week.
Are they in that much of a hurry?! I guess we really are in a race against time. What’s the plan?

We’ll launch a joint attack. The Sirens in the Arctic front seem to have finally discovered the purpose for us keeping the commander here. After all this time of being fairly ambivalent towards our “Secret Room,” they’ve finally started to direct their attacks there.
After the operation begins, I’ll draw the Sirens away. Use that time to escort the commander to the Arcana Sanctum, and complete our mission.
We won’t have the commander for much longer, and the Siren offensive is also becoming more intense. This might be the only chance we get, so failure is not an option.
Don’t worry. It shall be done.

sequence: <size=51>“Zero, do you know how to design a worthwhile treasure hunt?”</size>
<size=51>“First, you need an intrepid Scavenger.”</size>
<size=51>“Then, you’ll need a keen Observer to oversee the game.”</size>
<size=51>“Of course, you’ll need a Compiler to record the whole thing.”</size>
<size=51>“Finally, and do pay extra attention here...”</size>
<size=51>“Make sure they never meet one another.”</size>

scripts.say: ...The icebergs floating here must be hundreds of meters high...
From 50 to 200 meters, to be precise, and their surfaces are flat and smooth.

As we all know, most of an iceberg’s actual mass is hidden under the surface — in theory. Based on our observations, however, the icebergs here do not have substantial underwater structures. Rather than “floating,” they seem to be suspended within the water.
Are these icebergs all a part of the Mirror Sea...?
That’s not all! The Mirror Sea periodically produces Siren defense modules around these parts! These modules are rather dated, but we can’t just ignore them either.
Per our orders, we have to return here periodically to sweep any enemies that might spawn, and these icebergs sometimes get split apart by stray fire...
But... after we leave and come back, the icebergs simply reform as if nothing ever happened!
The ice is capable of regrowing...?
That’s right~! Pretty spooky stuff, right? So that’s why we still have to carry out lots of experiments. When the icebergs are lightly damaged, they regenerate into their original forms.
If we blast ‘em to pieces, the fragments disappear, but then an identical iceberg will float up to take its place soon afterwards!

So far, the Mirror Seas we’ve encountered can be broken up into two categories: one, arsenals for making Pieces as well as mass-producing ships; and two, experimental research facilities for creating unfathomable weapons.
Of all the Mirror Seas discovered by mankind, this may be the first that does not fall into one of those categories.

We’ve conducted extensive long-term research on this place, gathering as much data as possible and analyzing any samples that we can get our hands on. However, we still have no idea what the purpose of setting up a Mirror Sea like this might be - a hidden underwater facility that seems only to preserve a landscape.
Finally, we made a hypothesis... Comrade, what if Mirror Seas were not originally meant to be tools of war, but were designed to be tools of stealth and evasion?
What do you mean by that?
Generally speaking, Mirror Seas are unrecognizable from the outside until you’ve actually entered them. The single thing that all Mirror Seas have in common is their concealment.
On the battlefield, the Sirens often directly convert a portion of the ocean into a Mirror Sea, suggesting that whatever device they use to do this must be portable.
As for all the attacks we’ve seen both from and inside the Mirror Seas, those might just be products of the equipment stored inside.
As someone who formerly stayed in Iron Blood, I can attest that they started researching Mirror Seas very early on.
The impression I got was that initially, Iron Blood wanted to monopolize the fruits of their research on Siren technology, and refused to join the other major powers in the Azur Lane for that reason.

At first, Iron Blood was not a primary target for the first wave of Siren attacks. Ironically, their meddling into Siren technology stirred the sleeping beast, so to speak, and they suffered devastating losses as a result.
Mhm. Iron Blood has always been obsessed with Siren technology, through and through. Even before I left, they already managed to disassemble components of the Mirror Sea.
I assume they’re still ironing out technical challenges for the various modules, but I don’t know how much progress they’ve made.
What I’m taking away from all this is that we have to distinguish between the Mirror Seas we encounter in battle, and the actual concept of a Mirror Sea, right?
An actual Mirror Sea is just a technological device designed for absolute privacy and portability, whereas what we see in practice is like an upgraded, personalized version of that?

That sounds about right. Though Mirror Seas can be a pain in the ass when used offensively, we are able to destroy them directly as long as we have the numbers. But what if Mirror Seas are used to hide away places just like this one? We may never find those places... or know how many there are.
That does sound plausible. Perhaps the Sirens’ main base, which has never been pinpointed so far, is hidden somewhere in the depths of the ocean in a similar form?
We reached the same conclusion, but because we’ve never found a second Mirror Sea that shares the same conditions as this one, we need a lot more evidence before making that logical leap.
(...Wait, if the Sirens are hiding underwater in well-concealed Mirror Seas, how was the Northern Parliament able to seize control of this “Arcana Sanctum?”)
(I can’t help but feel that there’s more to this story that they’re not telling me...)
Careful, a Siren guard fleet has appeared.
Seriously? We cleaned out this place not that long ago...
Those look like some seriously outdated models.
The enemy models in the Arcana Sanctum have never been upgraded. They’re the exact same as they first were when this place was discovered decades ago.
Back then, the Sirens that wrought such destruction and suffering upon humanity... looked just like this...
But now, enemies like these are hardly worth our attention. Comrade, time is precious. Let’s end this quickly! Uraaa!
The fleet made its way to a massive iceberg, easily dispatching the enemies in the way. It is said that this iceberg is the only facility here with an internal structure, and also houses the “Gate.”
This place is where we first recovered some truly revolutionary information. Isn’t it spectacular, Comrade?
The first time, we had to fight our way here. Countless comrades became martyrs in these very waters before we finally managed to clear out the swarming Siren forces.
But considering what we got out of it... their sacrifices were not in vain.

It can be said that what we discovered here was a turning point for fate. The intelligence we recovered from here was the reason why the Northern Parliament, then on the verge of collapse, managed to hold its tattered line of defense and then claw its way back into becoming one of the major world powers today.
But that’s not all. We also discovered a sliver of the Sirens’ secrets...
The Sirens’ secrets...?

What I’m about to tell you has never been made public. After so much information has been leaked, we’ve completely lost trust in the ability of the Naval HQ to maintain confidentiality, but we do think you need to know this information.
I assume I’m also to keep this a secret from the Naval HQ?
That’s not our intent, no. However, I do hope that after listening to everything, you will utilize your best judgment in deciding what to disclose.
All the information you learn in the Arcana Sanctum today should be treated in that manner.
I can agree to those terms.
We’re almost convinced that the Sirens were not spontaneously “born” from these oceans, in any sense of the word, but rather came from a distant place.
As for their true purpose, it is not something as simple as trying to eradicate humanity.
Since the very beginning, most of their actions have been aimed at driving wedges between our major factions and amplifying those conflicts, plunging us into a state of endless war.

Looking back at everything that’s happened, the Iron Blood had the deepest ties to the Sirens. Their splintering from the Azur Lane, sudden betrayal, and formation of the Crimson Axis, all reek with the Sirens’ lingering influence.
And perhaps, us too in the past, no... Even right now, we might have walked straight into a trap set by the Sirens.
It’s not just you. Both the Eagle Union and Royal Navy have been somewhat aware of this.
Somewhat aware, perhaps. But they still continued to fight, whatever the reasons may have been. In the end, everything still happened as the Sirens desired. This is the true nature of their power.
As for where the Sirens came from and what they’re actually after... Unfortunately, we still haven’t found the answers. But we’re sure that the answers can be found behind the Gate.
We’ll reach it on the other side of this great hall. Let’s keep moving.
So, the reason you need me is because you haven’t been able to open the Gate.
Correct. We believe that your natural attunement to Wisdom Cubes will aid us in opening this dusty Gate.
We’ve scoured the entire Mirror Sea, but have not found any device that can control the facilities here. We can’t even control the Mirror Sea or access its maintenance device.
The most suspicious thing is this console up in front.
Ahead of us in the middle of the great hall is a metallic console that looks like some kind of control device.
There’s a groove in it where you’re supposed to insert a Wisdom Cube, right?
Hmm, seems like it... It does look like some special device that requires a Wisdom Cube to activate.
However, all the Siren devices and facilities we’ve encountered so far have been powered by a special energy storage device. Why would this thing here require a Wisdom Cube to activate?
We may never know until we see what’s on the other side of this door.
An infinite loop, huh...
We’ve conducted a series of experiments to try to activate the console, but everything we’ve tried has resulted in failure. It won’t respond at all.
So you believe that this device will only respond to special individuals?
Mhm. Comrade, the tests you took when you first became a commander showed that you have the highest attunement with Wisdom Cubes that this world has ever seen.
All the science we have today cannot explain why you are able to produce benign changes to Wisdom Cubes, but even you should be aware of this phenomenon.
Mhm. I’ve always wanted to know... Why me?
But where is this “Gate” that you keep talking about? We’ve reached the end of the great hall, but I don’t see any doors here...
Ah... Sorry, sorry. I forgot to tell you one little detail about the Gate~
The wall of ice in front of you, right at the end of this hall, is what we call the “Gate.” We’re confident that if you’re able to activate this console, this will open up into another passage.
Just from its size and texture, there’s no way something like this could have formed naturally. But I can’t see any kinds of mechanisms inside... It seems like just a sheet of ice.
And that’s where you’d be wrong, Comrade. There’s much, much more to it than that.
Gromky, let’s do a little demonstration for the commander. Shoot at that corner over there.
Aye aye! Everyone, please keep a safe distance! Commencing fire!
The shell discharged from Gromky’s gun slammed into the wall of ice and erupted in a cloud of smoke and steam... But when it cleared, there wasn’t a scratch on the wall...
As you can see, we can’t damage the wall even with this amount of force.
Of course, we’ve tried many other methods. Using larger-caliber guns, having the entire fleet fire salvos, using explosives, using heavier explosives...
But nothing has worked so far. All the firepower we’ve been able to muster to date, and still not a scratch on this wall.
I guess you really do have to work from the console... Hm? Wait, this insignia here... it’s not what the Sirens use to represent themselves... I’ve never seen this before.
Huh? That’s weird... I don’t think we would’ve glossed over something like that...
What...?! Impossible! I’m certain that symbol was never there before.
In other words, the console changed in a way we’ve never seen before?
Sure enough, mysterious things start to happen as soon as the commander sets foot in here... Here, use this Wisdom Cube.
Don’t keep us waiting. Go ahead and give it a try.
There’s nothing else on the console that can be operated. Might as well start with the Wisdom Cube first——
...Woah, the console’s actually reacting!
Woaahhhh... It’s glowing!
As soon as I pressed the Wisdom Cube into the groove, the device began to vibrate and hum. The Wisdom Cube seemed to dissolve, replaced by a ball of light that expanded above the console.
The structure of the Wisdom Cube is reflected in the motes of light... as if they’re trying to deconstruct the cube...
...Belorussiya, looks like our hypothesis might be correct.
Yes! The Gate has also began to change shape! Now, show me what lies behind this wall of ice!
The Gate gave way to a new path, but in a way nobody had expected.

The wall of ice became thin and translucent, as if turning into a gossamer membrane that could disappear at any time. And on the other side of the veil, a radiant city comprised entirely of light rose from the formerly empty Mirror Sea.
My jaw dropped once more at the indescribable majesty shimmering before my eyes.
Incredible... A truly unexpected development...
Woooow... It’s so pretty...
Holy... this makes the towering icebergs we saw before seem insignificant in comparison...
It’s like a fairytale castle straight out of the storybooks...
Those streams of water above us actually turned out to be suspended tracks leading to the city...
The Sirens truly hid a magnificent work of art here. I can’t imagine their ugly sense of aesthetics giving birth to something this beautiful.
The buildings here... they don’t look like Siren architecture... Rather, there’s something... human-like about them...
Not even the most advanced countries can pull off an engineering marvel like this... not to mention, this entire city seems to be composed entirely of light.
But you have a point... this doesn’t feel like something the Sirens would do...
Now this is an unexpected development. Instead of getting some secret backroom or lab, an entire city of light materializes out of nowhere, and we don’t have any clues as to who built it.
Comrade, now that you’ve seen this, will you continue this expedition with us?
Of course. I’m also searching for my own answers here.
Then, let us pass through the Gate and discover what awaits us in this city of light!
Loud alarms blaring through the air... the burning stench of gunpowder choking my lungs... waves of scorching heat flaying my skin... I’ve experienced this before.
This must be... the defensive line... at NY Harbor...?
Why am I here...? What was I doing...? Why can’t I remember anything?
Hey! Why are you still here?!
Didn’t we agree that you’d be heading to Samos with the others? Why are you here all by yourself?
The voice in the distance, calling to me... It feels so familiar, but also so alien... Who could it be...?
We were crushed terribly in our last-ditch counterattack, so this place will fall soon.
You were supposed to go to Samos because we had anticipated this possibility...
Our defenses are still holding for now, but that cannot last much longer. They will come again with even greater numbers and raze this place to the ground, just as was planned.
You were there when the plan was drafted, weren’t you? Did you vote for it, or against it? ...So much has happened, I can’t even remember the details anymore...
Forget it... In any case, even if you wanted to stay with me, I can’t accept that.
I’m not important, and you’re still needed elsewhere... Let’s see if any evacuation fleets have yet to leave. Good grief, so stubborn even at a time like this...

sequence: <size=60>“Hurry. This place will fall as well.”</size>
<size=60>“Unfortunately... I won’t be able to keep our promise.”</size>

scripts.say: What...?!
Hey! What are you doing, staring off into space by yourself over there? The battle isn’t over yet, so you can’t be wandering around outside!

options.content: The others will come back and save you.

scripts.say: Hm? Surely not. If they’re following the plan, there’s no way they’d be able to leave.
They’ll come back... I’m sure of it...
Well, that complicates things. I wanted to make this deal without them finding out...
So...
Are you finally awake, Comrade?
...My head still feels fuzzy. Did I pass out just now?
Only briefly. The fleet has managed to cross the Gate.
That’s good... Were you the one who brought me back to the command ship?
Unfortunately not... As soon as we crossed the gate, we were scattered across this sector, with no sign of the control room or where we came through.
While regrouping, we found you unconscious on the submarine.
Hah, it’s nothing worth apologizing over. Rather, we owe you an apology for taking you into an unknown and dangerous battlefield.
It’s my fault for not working with the fleet...
Ahaha, words fit for a hero, Comrade.
At least, you weren’t the only one affected by passing through the Gate. Each of us experienced a short period of malaise as well.
Yeah, it felt like someone clubbed me hard in the head or something... Ugh, this place is weird...
However, the city of light is still glowing brightly in front of us, so at least we can be sure that we passed through the other side of the gate.
Do you think that all these strange phenomena were set up by the Sirens? ...Well, it’s best not to dwell on it. We’ve seen enough Mirror Seas to know that pretty much anything is possible.
The huge floaty icebergs are also totally different! Look, strange glowy lines are running through them now, just like the console when it was activated!
As I suspected, it was no accident that the icebergs in the Mirror Sea continued to regenerate themselves. Everything, including the icebergs, is an indispensable part of this giant city.
You’re right... Everything the light is touching is being repaired.
Look, the tracks above us are glowing so prettily! Imagine how fun it’d be to slide all the way down from up there!
Those tracks seem to provide access throughout the whole city. We’ll have the best shot of finding our bearings if we take control of it.
Of course, before we get pulled in too deeply, we should at least find our way back to the control room, just so we have an exit strategy.
Agreed. Unfortunately, we don’t have the luxury of aerial reconnaissance here, so we’ll have to gather whatever information we can while looking for a way back.
Hum~ dee dum~♪
Gromky seemed to be enjoying this a lot.
Gremyashchy, on the other hand, looked no different than before, even beneath the splendors of the city of light.
Why are you staring at me again? ...Do you need something?
Gremyashchy, it’s not good to be so grumpy around Comrade Commander! You’ll be able to get along better with others if you just put a smile on your face~!
I’m not grumpy. This is just the face I was born with. Besides, I’m here as an escort ship, not a therapist. Mm, that’s all.
Aww, why do you always have to be like this? Fine then! Comrade Commander, if there’s anything you don’t understand, I’ll be your Gremyashchy translator~
Hmph... Well, that’ll be all.
Look, look, she’s blushing!
Gremyashchy might act all cold, but she’s actually happy that she gets to work with you!
You two really understand each other, huh.
Heheh, we sure do! We used to be in the same fleet, but I was assigned to defend the Sanctum later on. It’s so nice to be back together!
Naturally, it’s as if we were never apart! Right, Gremyashchy~?
Yeah, yeah... So, can you let go of me already...?
No can do! I’ve missed you a tooooooon, so you owe me a bazillion hugs! You should come join in too, Comrade Commander~!
The hugging session was quickly cut short by the piercing sensation of Gremyashchy’s icy gaze.
Oh, you’ve returned? We’ve finally made some progress. There seems to be a passageway that goes deeper into this research facility, from this point here on the iceberg with the control room.
Hm... Weird stuff happened when we got across the Gate. Do you think we’ll be able to leave the way we came through?
We’ll never know until we try.
If we adopt this plan, there may be a chance of success.
However, we must ensure that the jamming device remains operational as long as possible. In the meantime, we’ll have to hold the line while evacuations are carried out.
In other words...
We already know this, Dr. Aoste. We’ve taken it upon ourselves to build upon this framework.
...I understand. But even if that is the case, everyone has already sustained heavy losses. The actual feasibility of the timeframe you provided must still be carefully evaluated...
If the “Light of Dawn” is ever extinguished, then Laplace’s Demon will cease to be. If we have not reached the evacuation threshold at that time, our future operational plans will be impacted.
Worry not. I will also help buy time for you.
...Dr. Anzeel?
I’ve already issued too many communications through the process of commanding the operation, and they’ve likely already identified me for destruction.
As long as I can continue to draw their attention, I should be able to alleviate the pressure in other places, giving you more time to implement the plan.
But, what will happen to you then?
After such a fiasco, someone always has to bear the responsibility. Only now, there aren’t many people left who can shoulder that burden.
I see... You can bring your KAN-SEN along as well. However, I would like Code G to accompany my Antiochus if possible.
Very well. You can have Enterprise, and whoever else manages to survive.
However, take them as far away from NY City as you can. Never let them return here.
...Without you here, I’m not sure I’ll be able to control them...
What happened to the ever-so-wise and stoic Magister? You have no choice but to give those children both a purpose and the responsibility that comes with it, right?

...Even after you “betrayed” us, I still believe we see things eye-to-eye. And I think what you’re doing is just. I completely understand you, and I trust that in their hearts, they understand you as well...
I’m sure they’ll need some time to accept it, but they will come to understand you one day...
Yes, I’m sure of it...
The whole atmosphere around us has changed!
I’m sure we’re at the same place, but nothing else about this facility matches what we saw before. I don’t think this is the same console from before.
Doesn’t this feel familiar? This seems more like one of the Northern Parliament’s command centers rather than what we saw before.
That’s also the impression I’m getting. Belorussiya, I don’t think I’ve seen that insignia anywhere before. Ring any bells?
I can’t say I recognize it either. This place really is full of mysteries.
Look at all those doors ahead of us! Why don’t we go explore them all?
I don’t think anyone’s home anyway~ Surely nobody will mind if we take a little peek inside~
Besides, it’s not like we’re doing anything else right now...
Everything here must have been hidden away for a reason. I, for one, am in favor of getting whatever valuable intelligence we can.
There must be something around here that gives us more information about this Mirror Sea, and how to control it.
...Having said that though, we don’t have the time to look through every single room.
How about starting from the big picture and working our way down?
I agree. If this is some kind of command center, then there must also be a conference room, a records room, and some information about what this place was used for.
Ah... Look at that room up ahead! Don’t you think that fits the bill?
After entering the curious room, we were immediately greeted by a huge display screen on the opposing wall.
Hmm... Why would something like this be here?
This is a chart that seems to track the course of a battle of some kind... It seems to be of... an island defense?
Hmm... the red star in the middle must represent an important target, and a defensive line has been erected all around it.
Trying to defend such a small island in this manner seems like a fool’s errand.
Indeed. You can buckle down all you want, but anyone trying to defend this island will be at a huge disadvantage due to the lack of maneuverability.
You might be able to use some of the smaller surrounding islands as a buffer, but even so... Assuming each mark represents the same amount of forces, the defenders are outnumbered several times over.
“The purpose of this operation is the absolute defense of the island’s facilities, and to prevent the enemy from establishing a foothold in the region.”
This place must’ve had some greater importance we’re not seeing. Otherwise, it wouldn’t make sense to defend this place so desperately at such an overwhelming disadvantage.
“Use the fleet's speed to fight back. Even if it’s impossible to overcome the difference in numbers, we can still buy more time...”
“There is still a glimmer of hope in this operation. We were expecting to be crushed, but luckily, the enemy’s forces seem to be getting diverted elsewhere.”
“We will hold the line until our last breath.”
“We’ve done all that we could. Your dedication and sacrifice shall not be forgotten.”
...That sounds pretty tragic...
Thank you for your dramatic display of oratorical flair, Murmansk. We can already see all that information on the screen.
What’s wrong with embellishing things a little bit~
...Huh? Gremyashchy, what’s the matter?
Wait...
We’re not alone... Something is watching us. Do you feel that as well?
Eh? I don’t feel anything...
Me neither... Jeez, Gremyashchy, stop saying spooky stuff like that.
I will admit... I’ve had an uneasy feeling ever since I stepped into this room...
Eh? You feel it too, Comrade?!
It's weird, isn't it? Nobody's been here for ages, but the monitor is still on, like everyone just up and disappeared.
More than weird, it's kind of creepy, even... Like we've entered a haunted house.
Ahaha, how unscientific of you, comrade Murmansk! Besides, how could the Revolution falter before some ghosts?
That said, since several of you share this suspicion, I suppose we should proceed under the assumption that we are indeed being watched.
Stay close, everyone. Nobody is to wander off on their own, lest we risk getting lost, or worse yet, walk into a trap.
Good morning, Comrade~ Have you been enjoying your time here with us, away from the front lines?
My eyes are still having a bit of trouble adjusting to how white it gets when it starts snowing, but other than that, the hearths are warm and the food is delicious.
Also, I’m discovering that bears can be unexpectedly cute...
Hehe~ See? I knew you’d come to appreciate how great our bears are. Cuteness and power in one package!
How are things going on your end? I heard the fighting in the front lines is still tense.
It should be fine. It’s never easy being on the front lines of course...
We’ve been locked in what seems like an endless tug-of-war with the Sirens. Our current deployment strategy focuses on outlasting the enemy with minimal losses...
After being at war for so long, knowing how to relax is just as important as knowing how to fight.
That's right. But today, we're not here to relax.
Then, we're going to look for a way to break this stalemate?
Well said! Now then, Comrade, are you ready to go on a trip with us?
Our destination this time... is that secret facility of yours, right?
Mm, you could say that.
Tallinn, what’s the status of the area around the Sanctum?
We’ve managed to repel a good number of the Sirens, but there’s no end to them. Without a doubt, they’ll start launching even more vicious waves of attacks.
If the Sirens have found out about this facility, is it going to be safe?
Don’t you fret, dear. Tallinn and the others are dependable. Even if the Sirens were to muster their main forces, they’ll find our defenses difficult to break.
Commander, after you’ve taken charge here, the apparent leader of the Sirens, Omitter, seems to have fallen into a state of madness after a series of setbacks.
Even if we can hold the line here, we can’t guarantee that the Sanctum won’t become collateral damage.
Mm, make every second count. Let’s get this over with.
According to the plan we agreed upon, Kirov and Gremyashchy will act with the commander and rendezvous with Tallinn’s garrison fleet before entering the Arcana Sanctum.
Sovetskaya Rossiya, Chapayev, and Tashkent will lead the Polar Fleet in an offensive on Purifier’s old nest at the Winter’s Crown, drawing away the Siren fleet to buy us additional time.
I’ll crush any enemies that threaten the commander’s safety. Mm, that’s all.
The Sirens will likely see through a maneuver as blatant as this, but if we commit enough of our forces, Omitter will be forced to turn the fleet around to defend the Winter’s Crown.
I won’t be able to protect you, so please stay safe. Let’s crush our enemies together, dear comrade.
Commander, I wish you the best of luck. Let us begin the first phase of our combat preparations.
You too. Come back safely. We’ll handle whatever is inside that Sanctum.
Everyone, I wish for your success and safety in this operation.
The fleet moved in a single group through the complex corridors. There was much ground to cover, but not infeasibly so, now that we got through some of the biggest rooms.
Comrade, I’ve found something amazing here as well!
Ehehe... Let’s go explore in that room and see if there’s any more treasure~!
Hehe~ Sounds like fun. Let’s all go on a treasure hunt~♪
I didn't find much in the way of treasure. All I recovered was this stack of misprinted documents.
Let me have a look. Hmm... "Summary on Bluepoint Ships"?
Actually, it must be "Blueprint Ships." It's barely legible, but that looks more plausible.
"Blueprint Ships" rings a bell...
I think that was the term the Naval HQ came up with after we first saw a ship called Gascogne at the Battle of the Basilica.

That's right, but I remember coming across this term some earlier reports from the Iron Blood and Royal Navy. Bismarck's aide, Friedrich der Grosse, seems to have taken this classification for herself.
Friedrich, huh? We have practically no information on her other than what you just said...

Immediately after our campaign to suppress Bismarck, a mysterious new leader took command from the shadows and stabilized the situation in the Iron Blood. It is believed that the Royal Navy also started pursuing this technology as a countermeasure.
I've been thinking about this, Comrade. What kind of existence is a blueprint ship supposed to be?
We have always thought that a ship's foundational hull is inseparable from its history. In essence, this history is supposed to be a sum of humanity's perceptions and notions about the ship.
A hull is widely considered a prerequisite to a ship's construction, even for mass-produced ships. By extension, a history is a prerequisite.
All this is to say, a shipgirl's history is her proof of existence. Even if she was only dreamed up in blueprints.
...That's an interesting point. Soyuz, Rossiya, and I all fall under this category. We were just never given forms.
This is hardly a unique occurence and yet we've never been referred to as blueprint ships, whereas Freidrich has.
Based on how rarely the term comes up, I think there are a small number of blueprint ships in existence.
Yes, and this raises another question: What makes one a blueprint ship? Is it not something determined by the Wisdom Cubes that constitute our foundational hull?
Through whatever means, the Wisdom Cubes already contain the data that makes us who we are. To build a ship, you must extract this information.
But what if there is not enough information within the Wisdom Cubes to give form to a ship? What would happen if you "edited" another reality into the Wisdom Cubes?

It's a lot to take in. If I understanding this right, Wisdom Cubes contain the "essence" of a shipgirl, and building them is the process of giving this essence a physical form, right? In contrast, blueprint ships...
Are you saying that someone is capable of inserting their own "history" into Wisdom Cubes and manifesting them...?
Who knows? This is just a theory of mine, but if it is true, what restrictions are there on the kinds of history you are able to edit into a Wisdom Cube?
And finally, what is a blueprint if not a plan for the future? Whose plan is it, and what is it they were trying to do?
It seems our search has grown in scope, Comrade. We started out looking for an exit, but now we're also searching for the truth behind the Sirens, and behind our very existences.
The Sirens may have a deeper connection to the Wisdom Cubes than we first realized, but let's not jump to conclusions until we've fully explored this place.
These documents may not tell us all that much, but it's clear that the Sirens know much more than we do.
I'm certain that what we've learned so far is only the tip of the iceberg...
We stepped into another room, this one even bigger than the command room we found earlier.
Hundreds of seats lined both sides of what appears to be an auditorium, its roof well over 20 or even 30 meters above the floor. At the far opposite end of the room, there was a podium.
A few enormous monitors hanged on the wall behind it. These ones were turned off, projecting not a thing.
First a control room, then a conference room, and now an auditorium. Not too surprising, I suppose.
This must be the heart of the facility. Unlike the control room though, the screens in here are all turned off.
It's not hard to imagine they simply switched off the power here after they'd evacuated everyone.
Just looking at it makes me think... Soyuz is probably having her meeting in a room much like this one right now~
I really hope we'll get to see her soon~
That can be arranged. We could throw a party as soon as she gets back.
Ooh, a party! Wouldn't that be nice, Gremyashchy?
It'd be cool. Mm, that's all.
But I'm not good with situations where I need to pay extra attention to what I say and do. Especially not in front of a crowd of people.
The commander especially should know how that feels.
I see how that could be off-putting, but we're all friends, aren't we? You shouldn't have to feel nervous in front of your friends.
"When you're in my position, you sometimes don't have a choice. I at least know how you feel."
Oh, you poor thing. It is part of your job though, so don't expect to garner too much sympathy.
Tallinn threw me a cold remark, but interestingly, followed it up with a friendly smile.
It's easy to forget how influential you actually are from the way you talk, but I appreciate how easygoing and approachable you are.
"Since my job also includes even more stressful things like negotiating with faction leaders, it helps to make a good impression on others..."
Now you've got me interested~ I don't think I've ever seen you giving a public speech though~
That would be because commanders generally spend more time attending confidential naval meetings than they do talking to the public.
"True, but I think we've gone completely off-topic at this point. Let's get back on track and have a look around the auditorium."
We're just chatting! What's wrong with that? As I was gonna say... Don't you ever wish you got more recognition for all your hard work?
I mean, I can only imagine how tough your job is. You must work day and night to make sure everything goes smoothly, right?
Rather than acknowledge Murmansk with a response, I instead pulled back an empty chair at a desk and examined its spine.
It looked a lot like the chairs we sat in during a meeting at Naval HQ quite some time ago. They had buttons on the back that would power on the screens.
Interestingly, this chair also has something like that. I wonder if it works the same way...?
...More electronic interference? How is that possible? We are deep below the surface and should be immune to any kind of jamming.
Zero, survey the surrounding waters and determine if there are hostiles approaching.
Nothing of the sort? I see. Well done, child.
It seems to have been an equipment malfunction.
And you fixed it? Thank goodness it was nothing more than that.
Why would there be a hardware failure now though...? Diagnostics were performed on the system yesterday and everything was in working order... There must've been some reason for it...
Yes, you're right... We'll look into the source of the malfunction later. It may well have been the result of the solar flares we've experienced of late.
Apologies for that. Our equipment suffered a malfunction, but the issue has been rectified.
Rest assured, this auditorium is completely closed off from the outside. No electronic signals can get in or out. Furthermore, we are safe with Antiochus's fleet guarding the perimeter.
With that behind us, let us continue where we left off. Standing with me today is the leading expert on the study of Wisdom Cubes.
This individual may have a solution to the issue of metamorphosis which plagues us so. Allow me to introduce–
Hurry, Commander! We've gotten all the info we can, so it's time to get out of here!
Are you serious? You're either the bravest person alive, or the dumbest, and I can't tell which.
