Whatever you did, this place's entire security entourage is here. I've never seen so many undocumented types of enemies before...
Belorussiya took the others out to intercept them, but we need to hurry up and grab as many documents as we can before getting out of here.
...Did you forget?
We're surrounded, and we still haven't found the way out! We're in deep, deep trouble here!
What should we do, then? We'll be annihilated for sure if we remain here.
If we head in the opposite direction of the Gate, we might just find the exit. It's better than awaiting our doom, at least...
Then what are we waiting for? Fire up those leg-engines!
Not so fast. If we flee now, we'll be putting the commander's life at risk.
I can cover for myself, but I cannot guarantee the commander's safety if a firefight breaks out in these cramped corridors. We must reduce the enemy's numbers until it's safe enough to leave.
Mm, I guess that's a plan.
Gremyashchy, you and Comrade Commander will stay here and gather up everything we've found! The rest of you, follow me!
Now do you remember?
I do, but... why did I forget in the first place? Why did I only remember just now?
Never mind that, Belorussiya just gave us the signal. Come on, we have to–
All of a sudden, Gremyashchy vanished without a trace, as did the flashes of the firefight happening outside. They were simply gone, like they had never existed in the first place.
Simultaneously, the auditorium's monitors sprung to life, showing me what appeared to be footage of Northern Parliament girls doing battle with strange enemies.
They were enormous beasts made of black steel, but even through the high-resolution screens, their shapes were blurred as if light itself was repulsed by their grotesque forms.
The Northern Parliament girls were similarly blurry. All I could tell from looking at their contours was that they were not Kirov or Belorussiya.
Whatever the screens were showing me, it did not seem to be live footage of the battle outside. In any case, I had to contact Belorussiya.

That was when I realized that the button on the communicator was stuck, and no amount of pushing on it did anything. I could not contact her, and even if I could, it seemed extremely unlikely that I'd get a response.
It seemed almost as though... time had stopped.
The auditorium's exit was not physically blocked, but I couldn't go beyond its open doors. It's as though there was an invisible barrier, locking me in here.
<The computational system has encountered an error. Security mode has been activated, and will shut down in 19 minutes and 7 seconds.>
Suddenly, a hologram appeared, breaking the dead silence in the frozen room.
<Negative. You are speaking to this facility's administrative program. Responsibilities include data recording, processing, simulation, and playback.>
Those ships on the monitors, who are they?
<The ships are KAN-SEN belonging to the Revolutionary Front.>
What is the Revolutionary Front?
<Your query returned 0 results.>
Who are they fighting?
<The ships are fighting the enemy.>
Is the enemy the Sirens?

<Negative. The entities shown on the monitor are simply holograms created from computational models and simulations, in turn derived from logged data. Unable to reproduce a clearer image at this time.>
Then what ARE the Sirens?
<Your query returned 0 results.>
Who is Antiochus?
<Your query returned 0 results.>
Who is commanding this fleet?
<Your query returned 0 results.>
What happened to those girls?
<Your query returned 0 results.>
Were they fighting to... protect something, or someone?
<That is correct.>
Similar to what my fleet is doing, then?
<The fleet that you control is of much, much, much smaller size than the fleet that appears in the records.>
<The enemy that you are fighting is of much, much, much smaller size than the enemy that appears in the records.>
Is there any way to leave this facility then?
<There is none.>
There... isn't...?
<Please fight until the last light has faded.>
KABOOOM!
Oof! These enemies don't mess around!
Yeah, not to mention they're covered in some sort of... weird mist...
They look like Sirens, but there's something very different about these things!
If they look like Sirens and come attacking us, then as far as I'm concerned, they might as well be Sirens!
Well said! Either way, there's but one thing for us to do: dispatch them!
That's the Kirov I know! Hahaha!
Right you are! I cannot and will not rest until the revolution has come!
They are neither immune to our cannon fire, nor too fast to hit! We need only keep firing on them until they sink!
Blow them to dust, comrades! Hold the frontline until Comrade Commander and Gremyashchy have evacuated!
Commander! Gremyashchy!
You finished at just the right time! I'm dying to return to the surface!
Murmansk! Tallinn! It's time to fall back!
Will do! I was just starting to worry we'd never make it back!
Commander, this way!
KABOOOM!
Damn... My second turret's been disabled! How's the rest of the fleet?!
Gremyashchy and Gromky are still resting... And we're about to run out of ammo.
Murmansk and I have suffered varying degrees of damage, but we're still able to fight.
We've lost nearly all of our mass-produced ships except for the icebreaker, but... we didn't have that many to begin with, and they don't have the same maneuverability as we do.
We'll have to make do without. I didn't expect to make it this far in, so I didn't bring as many mass-produced ships as I could have.
We can't keep this up forever. How are we supposed to maintain our defenses while also holding the evacuation point?
Damn, I can't believe the Sirens got the best of us... I thought it was impossible for there to be enemies like these still hidden after all the surveying we did!
This is a terrible failure on our part, but we shall assume full responsibility. Even should we all fall, Comrade Commander must not be lost here!
Kirov, Tallinn, Gremyashchy, take the Commander aboard the icebreaker and make for the exit. Everyone else, we make our stand here!
Sorry, Belorussiya, but I don't intend to sink without seeing what's on the other side of that iceberg!
We might have a better shot if we all stick together and press forward. What's your opinion, Comrade?

options.content: "I disagree with both of those options."

scripts.say: ...I know you don't like making sacrifices, but the world cannot afford to lose you here.
If this is actually a "Reenactment," then there is no escape route anyway.
Reenactment? How were you able to come to that conclusion, Comrade?
Reality is a harsh mistress. I've already tried lining up the map to the information we recorded before, and I'm not seeing an exit.
I see... As much as I don't believe in giving up, I don't think I have the strength anymore to search for the control device for this Mirror Sea...
I'm sorry, Comrade. This might be it for us...

options.content: "I've accepted this possibility from the moment we arrived here."

scripts.say: Is there any way to leave this facility then?
<There is none.>
There... isn't...?
<Please fight until the last light has faded.>
The lights of the city are gradually dimming, one by one!
You're right! So, we're supposed to hold until all the lights go out?
Judging by how things are going, that might take a few more hours at this rate...
Will everything disappear once the lights go out? I don't think we can hold on that long...
Don't give up so soon! We may be cornered, but we must grasp onto this lifeline and hold on to it no matter what!
Instead of trying to retreat, we'll focus on buying as much time as possible. Commander, please continue to lead us!
I'll protect you, even if all I have left is my flail. Mm, that's all.
Everyone...

options.content: "It's been an honor to fight alongside all of you."

scripts.say: The feeling is mutual, Comrade.
Now, fight with everything you have until this false light is extinguished! Go!
Where am I...? Back to the place where I first inserted the Wisdom Cube into the console...?
The others are scattered across the hall, collapsed around the floor in deep slumber. None of them appear to be injured.
Their rigging is unblemished as if no battle had taken place, and their breaths were soft and quiet like dreaming children.
But what about the city of light? I remembered passing through the Gate, and...
I looked towards the place we had passed through. The passageway to the city of light had been closed off, a wall of ice with a surface that resembled a cracked mirror in its place.

I remembered searching around a mysterious facility, and interacting with some kind of terminal. I remember fighting against the Reenactment of a Siren foe... but then what happened...? My memory might be a little fuzzy because I just woke up...
—"Please fight until the last light has faded."
...What happened at the end of that battle?
In my hand was a small box of materials collected from the facility. Above all else, my friends were safe and sound.
Let's not worry about anything else right now.
I peered inside a box, and on the very top was a document with the words: "Project Dawn."
Northern Parliament “Arcana Sanctum” - Offshore
We're finally back! Oh, how I've missed you, fresh air~!
Ugh... My head is still throbbing like crazy... Is everyone alright...?
My memory also feels incomplete... I remember entering a mysterious facility in the City of Light and recovering some data, and then we ended up in a desperate battle against the enemy...
What happened at the end though? What exactly were we fighting, and how did we get back to the entrance?
I don't know... The recording equipment I brought in is completely blank. It's been running the entire time, but there's nothing but noise from the time we entered the city of light...
Our riggings have also been fixed, as if a battle had never taken place.
But, the Commander and Gremyashchy managed to retrieve some data, right? What exactly is going on...?
Let's not worry too much about the complicated stuff~ We have experts for that after all! Now, let's just be thankful we're all safe and head back to port~
Hey, don't just leave Kirov behind... Wait, what are those ships coming towards us?
A large fleet began to appear over the horizon. Lifted above them were the banners of the Eagle Union and Royal Navy.
Did the Azur Lane schedule a joint exercise in our waters? I don't remember hearing anything about that...
There definitely isn't anything of the sort. What have our outposts been doing, letting such a large fleet sail through without notifying us?
I was told they'd be coming, but I didn't expect them to be here so soon.
I see, I see. Well, I can understand why they'd be in such a hurry.
What do you mean, Tallinn?
I'm talking about their beloved Commander, of course. It's been a while, hasn't it?
That makes sense. I was afraid that our greatest secret had been compromised.
However... I must say I'm impressed by how quickly and decisively they put together this operation.
I'm sure they suspect something. If the Iron Blood and Sakura Empire also got involved, we wouldn't be able to keep any secrets for long.
Hello, my lovely friends of the Northern Parliament! Commander, I've missed you sooooo much~!
To what do we owe the pleasure, comrades? I do not recall the Northern Parliament requesting aid from the Azur Lane.
Hmm... I wanted to see my Commander so badly, I just couldn't wait~☆ And besides, these are technically neutral waters, right? Nothing wrong with Sister Sara here passing through, right?
Ahaha, of course not, comrade! We were simply doing a bit of sightseeing before bringing the Commander back to port! Would you care to accompany us?
We'd be glad to, but could I ask you to transfer Commander to one of our ships first?
Quite interesting to see you "sightseeing" on such a strange... ship. Is this the vessel that the Commander is on?
Now now, let's not be in such a hurry.
While Sovetsky Soyuz did request the presence of Comrade Commander, the decision to stay was ultimately not ours alone.
Where would the "freedom" be in not hearing out your Commander's own desires first?
No doubt the Northern Parliament found a reason to keep the Commander around longer...
What do our friends of the Royal Navy think of this?
Her Majesty has already given her seal of approval. "My loyal subject is permitted to go to the Eagle Union," she said.
Very well. What do you want to do, Comrade?
(What should I say...?)
(Or so I'd like to say... But I don't think there's a way to keep this from turning ugly...)
Oh my. Nobody told me that we'd have guests over.
Soyuz? Weren't you supposed to be at a meeting?
Yes, and at the meeting, an urgent request for the Commander was brought up.
From Her Majesty? Ugh...
After much deliberation, the Northern Parliament has agreed to transfer the Commander to the Eagle Union.
What...?! How could you make a decision like that?
Belorussiya, I will explain the details to you in full at a later time.
Commander, thank you for everything you've done for the Northern Parliament. May we fight again side by side.
I guess that's it, then. Don't get yourself killed out there.
You're always welcome here, Comrade! Maybe next time, you can come visit as a tourist!
...Thank you. I won't forget my time here.
Looking back upon their warm hospitality and the arduous battles we had overcome together, I felt a pang in my heart from having to leave my new friends. However, the Eagle Union needed me...
Commander, let's head back to port with the others!
I heard you've made a major breakthrough in your research, Dr. Anzeel.
You heard right. I finally have some insight into the phenomenon of cognitive awakening.
That again? This "cognitive awakening" is nothing more than a flight of fancy. Higher emotions cannot exist within these simulacra of yours.
Or, did you finally find evidence to show that this "cognitive awakening" is real?
Not yet... But soon! I just need a little more time...!
...How many times have you said this?
I'm sure of it this time! *cough* *cough*...
If we can find a human with high enough attunement to the Wisdom Cubes... then I'm sure we'll be able to...
Comrade, you’ve been unusually quiet this whole time. Is something troubling you?

I’ve been trying to piece everything together... The operation briefings laid out the specifics of the operation as well as the necessity of my participation in great detail, but any references of the Arcana Sanctum itself have been extremely vague. It’s almost as if the information has been tampered with.
What are you able to tell me about this "Arcana Sanctum?"

Hmm... The best way of putting it is, the nature of the Sanctum is extremely unique, to the point where we have to be cautious even in our internal briefings. If unredacted information was somehow allowed to spread...
Of course I’d be willing to explain things to you, Comrade, as long as you don’t record anything down.
Now, where do I begin...
Comrade, do you know when and how the first shipgirls were born?

Let’s see if I remember my history... After the Siren invasion, various countries came together to form the Azur Lane and assembled the world’s resources to develop the Wisdom Cube. From there came the shipgirls that were able to turn the tides of the war, right?
That would be true, according to the information that has been publicly disclosed. But this explanation is only a half-truth.
It’s not quite accurate to say that the Wisdom Cubes gave rise to the shipgirls. Rather, the two appeared at roughly the same time.
What? Are you saying... the appearance of the shipgirls wasn't due to the invention of Wisdom Cubes...?
Where did you get this information?
Haha, it's just a fanciful conjecture. But assuming that what we just told you is true, Comrade, who do you think was the first shipgirl?
Long story short, after we discovered this information, we returned to the sector to conduct an in-depth exploration, and that’s when we discovered the existence of the Arcana Sanctum.

Turns out, we later discovered that the Sanctum was actually a Siren stronghold. Perhaps the Sirens weren’t prepared for the forces we had on hand, but we were able to seize control of it through a surprise attack.
The reason why the Northern Parliament was able to make such a miraculous recovery after being devastated by the Sirens previously... is because of the contents of the Sanctum.
I see... And is this why the Northern Parliament has been tiptoeing around the issue of how to handle Siren technology?
The Royal Navy and Eagle Union will never understand what it feels like to desperately struggle for air when being strangled by an overwhelmingly powerful enemy.

In any case, around that time, the Naval HQ managed to successfully develop and mass-produce the Wisdom Cube, and the rest is history. Various countries utilized the Wisdom Cubes to create their own fleets, eventually tipping the scales in our favor.
Are you implying that the development of the Wisdom Cube hinged upon whatever was in that Sanctum?
No, that’s not quite what I’m getting at. We had no hand in the development of the Wisdom Cube, and the resources recovered from the Sanctum didn’t have any records of Wisdom Cubes either.
If anything, I’m inclined to say that the two are unrelated. However, Wisdom Cubes appeared at around the same time as the first shipgirl,and this alone is something worth thinking about, is it not?
Who knew that such a shocking revelation would lie beneath something long-considered common sense? I’ll have to thoroughly comb through the files at the Naval HQ when I get back.
Through our expedition into the Arcana Sanctum, we've all seen firsthand how anomalous an existence the Commander is.
The Commander's attunement to Wisdom Cubes not only affects shipgirls, but also devices powered by Wisdom Cubes.
Lasting changes have already been observed in the Sanctum, something we could not bring about despite all our efforts.
Do you think that the Commander is the "seed of change" mentioned in the documents?
I cannot say for sure. We may arrive at a clearer understanding after analyzing all the data we've collected.
Whether or not the Commander will become this seed... is not something that we can decide.
Now that there are no outsiders here, I shall speak frankly.
As long as the endless war between the Northern Parliament and the Sirens persists, there can be no future for our people.
Even with the advantages we have currently, the Sirens' infinite adaptability will eventually overwhelm us.
We've used everything to try to secure our future. The aid of the Azur Lane. The technology of the Crimson Axis. Even the secrets of the Sirens and the Ashes.
But now we know, the Commander has gained the "Key" from the Arcana Sanctum.
We must now turn this key together and grasp the possibilities that open up before us.
If that is the case, why didn't we pull some strings to keep the Commander here a bit longer?
The Royal Navy and the Eagle Union have not yet grasped the Commander's true worth. Were they to do so... I fear we may not ever meet again.
We are viewed with distrust from the outside, but the Commander has given us a way forward.
...You're right. We can't squander this opportunity that the Commander earned for us.
For the sake of the Northern Parliament, nay, for humanity itself, we must seek every advantage.
To these ends, the Commander's assistance is indispensable, and we must squeeze everything we can from this "Key."
But that is something reserved for the future. For now, we must be practical and do the things we ought to do.
Study these materials well. Do not waste the light of dawn that the Commander has given us—
And the conclusion...?
The one known as the "Commander" is in fact unique.
Three times, the one known as the "Commander" vanished from this world, albeit for a few microseconds.
Disappeared, then reappeared, with no fluctuations in energy. As if the world was rejecting its existence, then re-accepting it.
This timeline did not diverge then, but rather is being pruned...
If this phenomenon is real, then there is much for us to consider.
Indeed.
Your other intuition proved correct as well. The Observer's Reenactment was compromised.
The work of the Arbiters cannot be detected by even the most unique of Observers... Even the one in this timeline.
Continue to monitor the experiment, and stay concealed. You are forbidden from interfering in it. Another Arbiter will be sent to deal with Code G.
A large number of variables that cannot be empirically determined have begun to converge upon a single timeline. We must handle this situation with extreme caution.
What exactly did you see... "Commander?"
The path is clear, Commander. You can continue forward.

Gremyashchy was the perfect representation of the stoic fighting style of the Northern Parliament, expressionlessly mowing down the enemy ships that occasionally appeared in our way. Among all the destroyers I’ve commanded, Gremyashchy’s combat capabilities were absolutely top-notch.
Think nothing of it. I’m just doing my job. Mm, that’s all.
Hah. You sure know talent when you see it, Comrade. Gremyashchy here has been given the prestigious title of “Guardian.” She’s the ace up our sleeve!
Now that you mention it, I do remember something about that...

options.content: “That’s a very rare reward, isn’t it?”
“You’ve done well to serve your country.”

scripts.say: That’s right! Very few ships in the entire Northern Parliament fleet are given this prestigious title!
Even when I was back at the Eagle Union, word had spread of the outstanding reputation of the Guardians.
I don’t really need the honors. All that matters to me is doing my job well.
Gremyashchy, a good warrior should also know how to acknowledge the praise of others.
Um, thank you... Umm, y-yes, that is all...
Considering how exceptional of a fighter she is, it’s a bit strange to me that I haven’t seen her active until this point.
Gremyashchy’s mostly been active in the Arctic naval routes, and we only recently had her transferred here to aid with our current operations.
It’s only fitting that she would come down to guard someone as important as you, Comrade~
I really appreciate it. Let’s all try to make it back in one piece.

Unlike the other destroyers I’ve worked with, Gremyashchy doesn’t solely rely on her gunnery and torpedo strikes. She prefers to quickly close the gap on her enemies before dispatching them with a swing of her massive, comically exaggerated chain mace.
In addition to her snow-white naval hat and coat, I also found her scarf to be very distinctive.
And when she courses through the waves at high speeds, the scarf flaps behind her like the wings of an angel.
What are you ogling me for? Are you... some kind of creep?
Northern Parliament “Arcana Sanctum” - Offshore

Good morning, Comrade~ I’m Murmansk, from the fleet in charge of the Sanctum’s defense. The flagship of the defense fleet, Tallinn, is currently busy commanding, so I am in charge of making sure you all docksafely. Right this way~
How’s the current situation?
Hmm... Sovetskaya Rossiya might have already begun her offensive. The Sirens started to significantly change their behavior today.
But, we haven’t seen them pull their forces back as we were hoping. Instead, their attacks have been more ferocious than ever...
After launching an attack on their base, Omitter did show some signs of being flustered, but instead of turning her fleet around, she’s doubled down on the offensive...
This is indeed the best decision for the Sirens, given their lack of concern for casualties. We may have underestimated her decisionmaking just because of her comical demeanor.
She is the mastermind behind the Sirens in the Arctic front, after all... Hmph, but there’s nothing more to it than that.
In the face of our mighty Polar Fleet, clarity of mind is not enough to account for the fact that they can’t sufficiently reinforce their front lines.
As long as we clear out the remainder of their forces here, the Sanctum will no longer be in danger. After that, we can start doing the things we came here for!

Mm~ That’s what Tallinn had in mind as well. Our fleet is currently holding the enemy back from several directions. I’d love to play it cool and say we have everything under control, but to be honest, the fighting is really fierce out there and we could use the help...
So... Comrade, I hope you’ll be able to lend us your aid and protect the Sanctum!

options.content: “Of course. That’s what I’m here for.”
“Sure, I didn’t come here to sightsee.”

scripts.say: Thanks a ton! It’s an honor to fight by your side, Comrade~!
Ehehe~ Fortunately for you, the view inside the Sanctum is simply stunning. After we clear out the enemies, I’ll show you exactly what I mean~
This is our regularly-scheduled transmission. Dear comrade, we’ve already reached our destination, and are now holding our positions.
I haven’t seen any higher-tier Sirens like Omitter yet, but I’m sure they’ll be forced to come out as long as we keep fighting.
How are things on your end, dear comrade?
The Sirens here haven’t gotten any stronger. I’d say your gamble was a success. However, the Sirens around the Sanctum haven’t pulled back either, and we’re currently engaging them.
I see. Well, I believe in you. Teach them a harsh lesson for me. Over.
Seems like the assault on the Winter’s Crown is going smoothly. Unfortunately, we’re facing more resistance here than expected...
The more times we clash with Omitter, the more incongruous her behavior seems. The way she acts says little about the way she commands.
I concur. I have witnessed their cunning ambushes time and time again along the Arctic routes.
It is hard to picture such ruthless and cunning attacks coming from that clown. Mm, that’s all.
I do have a theory though... Commander, the Sirens are supposed to be some kind of program, right...?
Mhm. Though there’s much we don’t understand about the Sirens, based upon the Naval HQ’s classifications, Sirens are more structurally similar to machines than they are to organic lifeforms.

Normally, lower-level Siren combat units are simply mindless tools of destruction, whereas higher-tier humanoid Sirens exhibit both knowledge and intelligence, and have absolute command over the lower-level units.
Almost like a hive of bees commanded by a queen...
“Right, that’s the impression I get.”

In theory, you can eliminate the treat of a Siren fleet by taking out their command structure. But in reality, the Sirens often have multiple command units, and each command unit can use special flagships to remotely relay their orders.
Theory rarely stacks up to the reality of the battlefield.

Given that fact... there’s obviously a better way for the Sirens to communicate that would not only be more efficient, but also be more machine-like. Why would they need to take on human personalities?
Hmm... I can’t say I’ve considered this before...
Perhaps they’re trying to exploit our empathy to create an advantage on the battlefield...
What’s your take on this, Comrade?

options.content: “Maybe it’s a disguise used to approach us...?”
“Are they trying to cast themselves in our image...?”

scripts.say: Mm... Obviously, lower-level Sirens are unambiguously menacing in their appearance. As for their leaders, they not only are rich with emotions, but also take on the appearance of young girls.
Given the Sirens’ pragmatism and precision, it’s understandable that they would seek to reach out to us in a form we can relate to.
Oh, that reminds me... Kirov, has your latest work been related to this kind of stuff?

Uhh, I guess? As we continue to encounter these Siren commanders, a growing number of Siren-worshipping cults have begun to appear across the world, their members perhaps bewitched by their alluring forms. A most disturbing trend.
“Siren worshippers, huh? I’ve also heard about this...”

Comrade, we can’t allow this trend to continue! The Northern Parliament has been monitoring this development closely, but the Naval NQ needs to recognize the seriousness of this situation and act accordingly.
“I’ll make sure they get the memo.”
The bodies of young girls, and massive ship riggings... These Siren commanders are similar to us in many ways.
Do you think the Sirens might be a product of humankind?
Though we don’t have that kind of technology, I’d say it’s quite likely that the Sirens were constructed. In any case, whoever created the Sirens... must know us very well.
You make a very interesting point...
And the purpose of designing them in this manner... must surely be some kind of disguise to let them get closer to us.
They sound like us. They look like us. The Sirens exploit these similarities to subconsciously influence our thinking and interfere with our judgment, even without us being aware of it.
This battle is proof of that. We misjudged the battle situation based upon an assessment of Omitter’s outward personality.

Wearing emotions as a disguise to give us the illusion of having common ground, of being able to communicate... when in fact, underneath those expressions, they are cold-blooded killing machines. How terrifying...
Like demons that adorn themselves in the trappings of men... but humans are their victims.
Indeed... Just like what the name they’ve been given symbolizes...
Speaking of which... did humans name them “Sirens,” or is that what they call themselves?
When I entered service, the Sirens were already known as Sirens. Mm, I don’t know anything else beyond that.
I don’t think I remember either... But most likely, whoever discovered them named them “Sirens,” as mysterious enemies that emerged from the ocean.
Just going off of destructive potential, wouldn’t it have made more sense to call them “Leviathans” or something? ...Why Siren?
You have a point... But they’ve just been called that for so long, I’m not sure anyone actually has an explanation for the origin of that name.
(The Ashes keep referring to something as “Antiochus”... Could that have something to do with the Sirens’ true identities...?)
Murmansk, your questions have been unusually on the mark today. Have you recently changed your hobby from observing small animals to perusing tomes of philosophy?
Whether you’re observing nature or reading books, a thirst for knowledge goes a long way~
Ehehe... Did I just say something totally quotable? To be honest though, I suddenly thought of all these things after meeting Comrade Commander today...
I see... I can only hope that the answers we seek lie behind the doors of the Arcana Sanctum.
(I can only pray... that the solution to our problems also lies behind those doors...)
That should wrap things up over here. I do believe this is my first time meeting you in person, Commander. I am the flagship of the Secret Room’s defense fleet, heavy cruiser Tallinn.
And I’m sure you already know Murmansk.
Zdravstvuyte! You look even cooler in person than through the communicator, Comrade! Ehehe~
And over here is another member of the defense fleet, destroyer Gromky.
Hehe~ Well met, Comrade Commander! My name is Gromky, a destroyer from the Northern Parliament! I hope I’ll be able to assist you in this operation!
I didn’t expect the Sirens to call our bluff and ignore our offensive on the Winter’s Crown... Fortunately, the worst is behind us, and the Sanctum is safe.
Commander, though this is our first time working together, I need no further convincing about your abilities.
“I’m glad to hear that.”
Don’t get me wrong - this isn’t some attempt at flattery. I’m merely stating objective facts.
(I could sense a domineering aura from Tallinn. As the flagship of a fleet that had been fighting tooth and nail, on top of her experience in the Iron Blood, she was a force to be reckoned with...)
So, when you say that the Sanctum is safe, does that mean it’s around here somewhere?
You guessed it, Comrade. The Northern Parliament has kept a very close eye on this place!
...We’re still surrounded by icebergs and freezing winds. It’s somewhere in these waters then?
(All around us are the husks of Siren ships destroyed during previous engagements, and the various logistics forces trying to clear them away.)
(When I look into the distance, all I see is the frozen sea being blanketed by endless white snow, with no traces of platforms, facilities, or any other manmade object for that matter.)
(As far as I could tell, there’s nothing here that makes it stand out from the other places I’ve seen across the Arctic.)
The commander looks completely lost. Did none of you say anything?

Oho, do you remember how shocked we were the first time we came here? It wouldn’t be fair if our Comrade missed out on that rite of passage. But don’t worry, Tallinn, everything has been taken care of.
I established a connection as soon as the battle ended. Judging by the time... we should be about ready.
Ready for what...?
We’re going underwater, Comrade Commander! Don’t just stare out into the distance - make sure to watch your feet as well!
Under... water...?
CRAAAAAASH—————!!
Not far from me, a massive object could be seen ramming the ice from beneath.
CRAAAAAASH—————!!
What the hell is that?!  Is that...?
Ahaha! A hail of cannonfire may not be enough to faze you, Comrade, but seeing this really caught you off guard, huh?
Indeed... I never expected to see something like this here...
That roaring sound... is that some kind of vessel? It’s coming straight out of the ice...

The mechanical roar, the violent cracking of the ice, and the surging of the ocean beneath... A symphony of sounds rushed together as the world around me shook, as if I was witnessing the summoning of an otherworldly beast.
When the weather is warmer, this area doesn’t stay frozen over like it is now.
But as fate would have it, we now get to use this icebreaker submarine to carry out our grand mission!
An icebreaker submarine... I don’t think the Naval HQ, or any of the other factions, have ever seen a vessel like this.

Of course they haven’t~ This is our latest multifunctional tactical submarine, developed independently by the Northern Parliament! But as you can see, due to its size, you can’t just call it a submarine anymore! It’s a submersible ship!
Sovetskaya Rossiya should already have taken you to some of the laboratories used to test the Wisdom Cubes’ power supply.
What you see in front of you is one example of the fruits of that research. Powering it with Wisdom Cubes ensures this behemoth’s power and endurance.
Of course, it is more than capable of fighting as well. Though it can only be used as an icebreaker while surfaced, it can transform into an underwater combat platform when submerged.

The huge arsenal it has on board provides us with excellent firepower coverage. Combined with its ability to freely navigate through the Arctic region, including parts of the sea covered in ice, and the long time it is able to stay submerged, we have high expectations for this new class of ship in any future conflicts.
A huge underwater combat platform with the ability to engage in anti-submarine warfare... Is this the reason why we didn’t see many Siren submarines in the previous battle?
You got it~
And if we need to take a submarine, I suppose this Sanctum is underwater?
More or less. Belorussiya, Commander, please board the submarine so that we can prepare to dive.
Let’s go, Comrade! You are able to see the reason why we have brought you here!
Comrade, we’ve arrived at our destination.
It feels like we’ve already been underwater for a long time... Do we need to switch into smaller expedition vessels if we’re exploring underwater ruins or something?
It’s not that complicated. We can just walk off from this ship.
Walk off? Aren’t we still underwater?
To be precise, this is a unique space that resembles a Mirror Sea, except underwater. The specifics are a bit more complicated, but you’ll see once you get out.
An underwater Mirror Sea...?
Comrade, welcome to the Northern Parliament’s Arcana Sanctum!
After exiting the hatch,  I was surprised to discover that there was no water pressure. A wide, spacious area stretched out in front of my eyes.

When I looked down at my feet, I could see a layer of calm ocean water coursing beneath me. Lifting my head, I could see that the dome of stars that should’ve been above me was now replaced by the expansive sea.

Around me, icebergs cut neatly into titanic slabs floated overhead serenely, and two tracks swirled overhead as they spiraled toward the surface. Not even in my wildest imagination would I have been able to envisage such a surreal dreamscape.

At first, I expected this “Arcana Sanctum” to be some sort of naval base. Then, I thought it was some abandoned underwater facility. But this... could something so spectacular truly exist in this world...?
It’s been some time since I last came here. A marvelous sight to behold, as always.
Heh. You look completely speechless, Commander.
Ehehe~ I was just like that the first time I came here... It takes a while to let everything sink in, you know~
Comrade, we need to get moving. You’ll find even more wondrous things deeper inside.
Take this submarine as your command ship. The rest of us will spread out and enter an escort formation as we head through the first Gate.

sequence:
For the Perfect Smile

<size=45>A Pressing Problem</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Afternoon sunlight streams through the big windows, gently illuminating my document-filled desk.
As I wrap up the last of my work, I put down my pen and take a moment to breathe, subconsciously rubbing my brow.
During this moment of rest, I feel eyes on me. Plymouth stands in front of my desk, staring down at me.
Plymouth? Need something?
Good day, dear Commander.
If I may say so, your brow has been awfully furrowed as of late. Is something troubling you at work?
Is it that easy to tell?
There's nothing in particular that I'm struggling with... It's just been a lot of crunch lately.
I see...
No wonder you seem so stressed.
It's no big deal. A little rest, and I'll be just fine.
But I am still concerned. You work yourself to the bone to ensure that everybody else can live happy lives.
That's why... I've always hoped for your happiness.
I appreciate the thought, but really, there's no need to worry.
That won't do! Now that I know the truth, I cannot turn a blind eye to it.
If I failed to notice the shifts in your spirits, then I would be a poor excuse for an aide.
She lowers her gaze, as if in thought.
After a while, she looks up again with resolve burning in her gentle eyes.
Dear Commander, do you have plans tomorrow?
Tomorrow? Not in particular... Why do you ask?
Then please, let me have you for the day.
I'd like to prepare a special relaxation plan for you.
From morning to nightfall, I will do all in my power to help you rest and recharge.
If all goes well, then... by the end of tomorrow, you will have a much sunnier visage than you do now.
You're awfully serious about this.
Because it's important. I will make sure to eliminate anything that could possibly interrupt your relaxation.
I will be your most devoted personal supporter for the day.
I'd feel bad letting you go that far...
Don't. I'll have you know that I'm more than delighted to plan this for you.
Besides, I want to see the look on your face when you're truly at ease.
Alright. Tomorrow, I'm all yours.
Lovely! Please leave it all to me. I'll put my heart and soul into ensuring that you have a lovely day.
Please look forward to what I have in store for you tomorrow. Heehee!
She pinches the hem of her skirt and performs a perfect curtsy. Her usually docile expression betrays a rare look of anticipation.
Thus, with that earnestness and composure, she exits my office.

sequence:
For the Perfect Smile

<size=45>Perfect Knifework</size>

scripts.say: Port - Plymouth's Room
The next day, I visit Plymouth's room as agreed.
As soon as I open the door, I'm greeted by a faint aroma. A tea set and fancy sweets line her table.
Good day, dear Commander.
Welcome to your first stop on today's route of rest and relaxation.
You will be eating breakfast with me. I hope you enjoy it.
You started early. Thank you.
It was no trouble. All that's left is to prepare the salad. While I do that, please do partake of the sweets.

options.content: Don't push yourself too much, okay?

scripts.say: Need some help?
Only if it involves you sitting and patiently waiting. Remember, Commander, your job today is to let me care for you.
Please relax and let me handle it.
Don't push yourself too much, okay?
Heehee, please don't worry. If it means getting to see you relax, then my efforts will be more than rewarded.
She smiles sweetly and heads back into the kitchen.
Just as I reach for a pastry on the table, I hear an unsettling sound coming from the kitchen.
BZZZZZ!
Plymouth? What's going on?
*cough* *cough*... D-dear Commander...
I-I'm chopping the vegetables right now. Please step away...
When I rush into the kitchen, she leans over the cutting board, staring fixedly at something.
However, she's holding no ordinary kitchen knife – it's a piece of laser-cutting equipment.
Plymouth, what are you doing?
Ah, dear Commander, please don't come any closer. You don't want bits of food flying onto your clothes.
Aren't you just cutting vegetables? Is industrial equipment really necessary?
Of course it is~ Laser cutters don't put pressure on the food, creating the perfect cut without affecting the shape or causing waste.
Please watch this.
With a fork, she spears a sliced carrot and offers it to me.
It shines in the morning sunlight, the cut surface so smooth that I can hardly believe it's a real vegetable.
Isn't the cross-section strikingly clean?
When you eat it, I hope it'll feel like silk on your tongue.
Go on. Try it!
Plymouth leans closer and feeds me the slice of carrot.
Seeing her earnest expression, I obediently open up.
Mmm...
How is it?
It's definitely unique. The texture is silky smooth, but it's also crunchy.
Good... It turned out exactly as I hoped.
Do you feel a little happier now, dear Commander?
Of course. Just you doing this for me is already enough to make me happy.
That's wonderful to hear.
She winks at me and smiles contentedly.
But instantly after, her eyes focus on my brow.
Yet it still isn't enough.
Hmm? What isn't?
Oh... Nothing at all.
There is still much more for us to do today. I will continue to endeavour for the sake of making your expression just a little bit sunnier!

sequence:
For the Perfect Smile

<size=45>The Park Sharpshooter</size>

scripts.say: Port - Amusement Park
After breakfast, Plymouth takes me to the amusement park as per her plan.
Dear Commander, this is our second destination for the day.
According to my data, amusement parks are great places for people to quickly improve their mood.
Just walking around with you has put me in a good mood already.
Upon hearing that, she looks up at me for a while, as if inspecting me.
Then, she shakes her head.
That won't do, dear Commander.
It's not good to be considerate at times like this.
That furrow in your brow still hasn't smoothed out yet. I must keep doing my best.
You don't let up, huh?
Heehee. I am your dedicated secretary ship and most devoted supporter, after all.
Now, where should we begin?
Something leisurely? Something thrilling? I'm happy with either.
So she says, but I sense hesitation in her words. When I follow her gaze, I spot a roller coaster reaching the peak of its track.
As it plunges downward, screams echo throughout the park.
The roller coaster? We can think about it later.
For now, why don't we take a little walk?
Very well. Let us start by easing into a relaxed pace.
As we walk down the park path, I catch sight of a shooting game stall.
Colorful balloons are set up as targets, with a huge bear plushie in the center of the prizes.
The sign reads, "Hit all 20 targets to win the grand prize!"
Looks fun. Wanna try it?
A shooting game? Okay...
If you're interested, then I would be happy to.
Plymouth approaches the stall and picks up the toy gun.
The gun's balance is rather lacking, and the sights are misaligned... It would be a tall order to reliably hit every target.
But worry not. I anticipated this might happen, and I prepared the ideal method to ensure a perfect score.
Huh?
In no time, she produces a scope, stabilizer, and rangefinder module from her bag.
Surely that's against the rules...
Do not worry, dear Commander. I studied the rules beforehand, and they only said that the stall's gun had to be used.
Leave the rest to me. As your devoted supporter, I promise to deliver the grand prize to you.
Initiating mission... Eliminating balloons.
BANG! BANG! BANG! BANG!
With each gunshot, the balloons burst one after another.
Not a single one misses, wiping out all twenty in the blink of an eye.
Whoa...
Mission complete. Targets eliminated.
I believe I have earned the grand prize?
She heads over to the prize window. Before long, she returns with the bear plushie, which is nearly as big as her.
Please confirm my results, dear Commander.
Thanks... I didn't think you'd win.
It's a gift for you. I hope it makes you happy.
It sure does.
Plymouth smiles slightly in response.
But her gaze once again drifts to my brow.
And yet... it is still not enough.
Huh?
Even a teddy bear of this size is not enough to satisfy you, is it?
Or would you be happier with a higher quantity of prizes?
No, no, this is plenty.
Calm down, Plymouth. I feel great now – I mean it!
I see... Then I'm glad to hear that.
If the amusement park is working for you, then let us proceed with the original plan.
I'll keep doing my best, heehee!
She stands by my side, happily cradling the giant teddy bear.

sequence:
For the Perfect Smile

<size=45>Unwelcome Rain</size>

scripts.say: Plymouth and I continue to check out the amusement park attractions, from relaxed ones to more thrilling rides.
Time passes in the blink of an eye. When we arrive at the observation deck in the center of the park, night has already fallen.
We're here, dear Commander. This is the perfect spot for viewing the fireworks.
I took everything into consideration, including the view, wind direction, and crowd density.
Did you put that much effort into researching this?
Of course. Tonight's fireworks are a vital part of my itinerary.
I want you to make genuinely happy memories of this place.
Thanks, Plymouth.
As she gazes into my eyes, I notice hers wavering ever so slightly.
Something seems to be on her mind, but she keeps her lips shut and smiles.
Yes... However, the day is not over yet.
As such... I would like to prepare just a little more joy for you.
As she speaks, a cold droplet falls onto the tip of my nose.
Hmm?
I look up. The sky, which was full of stars just a while ago, is suddenly obscured by dark clouds.
More drops fall in quick succession as it begins to drizzle.
It's raining.
In just a few seconds, it turns into a merciless downpour of big raindrops.
It's not getting better. Let's go find shelter.
Oh, no... I checked the forecast, and it was supposed to be clear skies all day.
As Plymouth stands there stunned, I take her hand and lead her under the awning of a nearby stall.
Though we got moving quickly, our hair and shoulders are already soaked.
Dear Commander, I'm so sorry for this...
She takes out a handkerchief and wipes the water off of my shoulders.
And your hair... If you get sick because of this, that will affect both your health and your mood.
I'll be fine. You're soaked, too, you know.
That doesn't matter. What matters most is...
The girl looks up at the night sky obscured by endless rain. Mere moments ago, we'd hoped to see fireworks up there.
Attention, all guests. Tonight's fireworks display has been cancelled due to inclement weather.
Again, tonight's fireworks display has been cancelled due to inclement weather.
No surprise there... That's a shame.
I'd expected as much, but when I hear the announcement, I can't help but feel a bit disappointed.
Today was still a lot of fun, though.
Even if we don't get to see the fireworks, I'm happy.
Do you mean it?
Plymouth fixes her eyes on me, as if trying to catch the slightest shift in my expression.
No... You are disappointed. I can tell.
Plymouth...
I can tell. You're only saying this because you don't want to worry me.
But we came here with such high hopes...
I came so close to letting you see that sight, but we're forced to leave with regrets because of silly luck...
She looks down sadly. Her tone of voice is as gentle as ever, but it's clear that she's feeling down.
I cannot stand for it.
Commander, please wait here a little longer.
Tonight... I promise, I will make fireworks for you.
With that, she turns and runs off into the rainy night.
Where are you going?!

sequence:
For the Perfect Smile

<size=45>Steel Fireworks</size>

scripts.say: The rain continues to intensify. All I can do is anxiously watch in the direction that Plymouth ran off toward.
But shortly after, the cloud-laden night sky is suddenly torn open by a flash of light.
KABOOOOM!
Huh?!
It wasn't lightning. I could identify that sound anywhere.
I watch the sea as golden streaks of light cut through the rainy night, ascending toward the sky.
Shells burst high overhead. Their explosions mix with the brilliant streaks of tracer rounds.
They burst magnificently between the clouds, transforming into a cluster of fire.
Golden, red, and blue trails radiate outward, drawing dazzling arcs against the black canvas.
Plymouth...
Bursts of light continue to bloom up above.
They're not quite as gorgeous as real fireworks, but they possess a certain grandeur made possible only by the mix of steel and firepower.
When the glow finally fades, a familiar figure runs toward me through the rain.
Dear Commander... I'm very sorry you had to wait.
Did you create those fireworks just now?
Yes. Since the display was cancelled, I devised a backup plan.
I can't perfectly recreate the show, of course... but I wanted to provide a worthy substitute for you.
Hahaha! That's the kind of solution only you could come up with.
Did you enjoy it, dear Commander?
I loved it. My time with you today was more memorable than any fireworks display.
Upon hearing my words, she finally relaxes, as if a weight has been lifted off of her shoulders.
Plymouth looks up at me. Beneath her wet eyelashes, she smiles sweetly.
Thank goodness... This time, I think I've truly managed to make you happy.
You have. But don't push yourself so hard next time, okay?
You got soaked just so I could see some fireworks.
I reach out and brush her wet bangs aside before draping my coat over her shoulders.
It was no trouble at all. I got to see you smile, so I've been more than compensated for my efforts.
Good grief. You're something else.
Heehee. If we get another opportunity... I would like to see real fireworks with you.
It's a deal.
Let's come back on another day when it's not raining.
Let's.
When that time comes, I will remain by your side as your most devoted supporter.
Plymouth leans in closer.
Though the steel fireworks have faded into the night, the lingering warmth of this day can still be felt between our palms.

sequence:
For the Perfect Smile

<size=45>Trouble with Feathers</size>

scripts.say: Port - Plymouth's Room
We return to port late at night.
On the way back, Plymouth is much quieter. She seems to be deep in thought.
It's getting late. Let's get some rest soon.
Not yet... I have one more plan for you.
Please join me for the last part of my itinerary, dear Commander.
Gladly.
What is it, exactly?
Umm... Well, I was hoping to keep it a surprise.
I've made some slight adjustments to my room, you see.
To your room?
I start to feel a tiny bit uneasy.
Please, come right this way.
You are about to see the ideal sleeping environment devised just for you.
The scene before me is almost dazzlingly white.
The bed, chair, and floor are all blanketed in fluffy down.
Would this be the adjustment you mentioned?
That's right. To replicate the sensation of sleeping on clouds, I opened up every down pillow I could find in the storage building.
Judging by their soft, yielding texture, I believe I've approached the ideal sleeping conditions.
You mean... all of them?
Indeed. I did thorough research on the quality of sleep, and I learned that a sufficiently soft sleeping environment will relieve tension in nerves and muscles.
Do you like it, dear Commander?
If you're unsatisfied in any way, I am happy to adjust it.
No, this is more than enough. I think you'd better not go any further.
I see...
Still, you won't know its effects until you try it for yourself.
Please lie down, dear Commander.
She takes my hand and guides me to the bed.
Before I can take a closer look, the down beneath my feet gives slightly. It feels like I'm being swallowed up by that white softness.
There's a strange, weightless sensation to it.
How does it feel?
Is it helping you relax a little more than usual?
It is soft... but maybe a tad more than I was expecting.
I'm glad to hear that. If it made you happy, then my preparations were not in vain.
Don't think about anything right now, dear Commander.
Surrender yourself to the softness and relax.
I will take care of you tonight.
Plymouth...
Perhaps because of the down feathers drifting in the air, or perhaps because of how close she is...
When I open my mouth to speak, something tickles the tip of my nose.
Ack...
Ah... Achoo!
The instant I sneeze, down feathers go flying.
Sorry, Plymouth... Can we go outside...?
Oh, no...
My research materials said that down feathers would be the most relaxing.
Could I have only made you feel worse?

sequence:
For the Perfect Smile

<size=45>The Furrowed Brow</size>

scripts.say: Port - Outdoor Garden
I sit down on a garden bench for a while, sneezing for what seems like forever.
The cool night air helps soothe the ticklish sensation still lingering on my nose.
I'm very sorry, dear Commander.
Maybe... I went too far this time.
Plymouth...
From breakfast, to the amusement park, to my room...
I prepared everything in hopes of making you happy, but everything ended in disaster.
She falls silent, as if trying to compose her feelings.
When she speaks again, she sounds clearly dejected.
In the end, your brow is still a little furrowed.
Don't be like that.
Everything you did for me today was effective.
The breakfast, the prize, those fireworks... All of them are precious memories to me.
Do you mean that?
Of course I mean it. Today was fun all the way through. There wasn't even...
Suddenly, I realize something, and I point at my brow.
When you said my brow was furrowed... was this what you were talking about?
Plymouth is taken aback for a moment. She leans in and stares intently at the spot.
It's... a little red.
Yeah, I think I got bit by a mosquito. It's been itchy, so I think I've been furrowing my brow and rubbing it without realizing.
To you, it must've looked like I was unhappy because of that.
It was... all because of a mosquito?
Yeah. Just a mosquito.
It wasn't because I was unhappy with your plans at all.
Quite the opposite, in fact. You being here made it a lot of fun.
She gazes at me for a moment, letting those words sink in.
Her tension melts away all at once.
Oh, my goodness.
You're saying I didn't let you down at all...
And today's plans really did make you happy?
Don't be so sad, alright?
You're the one who's been working so hard all day.
A smile – softer and sunnier than any I've seen yet – blossoms on her face.
Thank you. If that's really the case, then I can relax and share in your joy.
With that, she retrieves a small jar of ointment and squats down in front of me.
Lower your head please, dear Commander.
Now that I know the cause, I'm ready to treat it.
She gently applies the ointment to the bite on my face.
A chilly sensation spreads from my brow. In no time, the discomfort that has been plaguing me all day disappears.
Please continue to rely on me, dear Commander.
The next day, as soon as I step into my office, I'm taken aback by the scene before me.
Inside, several pieces of laser detection equipment are quietly running.
Er... Plymouth, what is all this?
Oh, dear Commander! Good morning.
After identifying the root of your problem last night, I took some preventative measures.
If any bug approaches you, mosquito or otherwise, these devices will eliminate it posthaste.
She smiles sweetly at me.
Because your smile must be protected at all costs, Commander. Heehee!

sequence:
Bonded Together

<size=45>Giving Up Command</size>

scripts.say: Zoo - Entrance
After a period of overwork, I'm freed from documents and meetings for a rare day of free time.
I'd planned to do nothing and relax, but Chapayev invited me to the zoo, and I couldn't turn her down.
(Some of those documents still need final touches. When I get back later...)
Commander~ You're not thinking of work right now, are you?
I shake off those dark thoughts and realize that her blue eyes are focused on me rather than the animals.
Oh? You looked awfully lost in thought. Heehee, let me guess.
Are you thinking about time? About the idea of using your one and only day off to make your work even more efficient?
I'm sorry. It's hard not to...
Is it? Well, Commander, you have to resist it. Your time is mine today, and I'd like you focused on me.
With that, she snatches the map out of my hand, gazes at it for a moment, and closes it with a smile.
Allow me to chart our course.
If you'd like... I could even take the lead all day?
Be my guest.
Oh? You'd give up authority to me so easily? It's almost unbelievable.
Heehee, beg enough, and I might give it back.
Ahem... No, it's fine. I trust you, Chapayev.
Really? I'm almost disappointed. Here I thought I'd finally get to hear you beg...
Let me be clear: I want you to enjoy our date today as best you can.
If you find your mind wandering toward work again, I'll drag it back. Even if it means using force.
Chapayev tugs on my collar, not too hard yet not gently either, with her slender fingers. It's not aggressive – more suggestive, perhaps.
Yeah. I'm excited to let go of work and have fun with you.
She leans against me and looks up with happy eyes. I can tell she expected those exact words.
Heehee. Much better.
(Question that last part.)
Her smile deepens, and her grasp on my collar tightens just a little.
For example... I could make it so that you can't leave my side? And I do mean physically... Heehee.
She says it gently and sweetly, but part of me thinks she's being serious.
Did you have this all planned out?
Heehee. It's my day with you, Commander. I'm sure you've braced yourself for what you know will come.
Well... I have given you authority over the date. So, where are we going next?
She looks down at the map intently. The light shining through the trees illuminates her profile, and her bangs blow slightly in the wind. The whole sight makes her look softer than ever.
After a while, she points at the Polar Habitat. Its title on the map has a cute drawing of a penguin next to it.
How about the Polar Habitat? We Northern Parliament girls tend to feel an affinity for animals that live in the cold.
So you like penguins, huh?
"Appreciate" might be a more apt word.
Penguins are such loyal creatures. Once they find a life partner, they never leave. I think that's admirable.
What about you, Commander? Are you loyal?
Her eyes linger on me for a moment before she looks away and giggles.
Before I can formulate an answer, she takes my hand and leads me forth.
There's no need to rush. Our date's just begun♪

sequence:
Bonded Together

<size=45>Loyalty and Possessiveness</size>

scripts.say: Zoo - Polar Habitat
When we get to the exhibit, chilly air touches my cheeks, taking all of the heat and tension out of me.
Through the glass I see a flock of penguins. They sway, cuddle, and waddle leisurely about, leaving little footprints in the snow.
The breeding area is particularly lively. In small, fenced-off areas, penguin couples warm their eggs. There are also some fuzzy little chicks snuggling in for warmth and chirping for attention.
Doesn't it sound like fun? Always in pairs, inseparable for even a moment...
It's like they're possessive of each other. Is that what you like about them, Chapayev?
I tease her while we watch the penguins in love.
She slowly turns to me. Her blue eyes are emphasized in the cold air, and her grin seems to deepen.
Maybe. Don't we all want things just for ourselves? Particularly... our lovers?
That last word comes out like a sigh. It seems probing, though it's hard to see what she's after.
(Ask what she's getting at.)
Her lips curl up into a meaningful smile.
Hmm, is there? Since you asked so directly, maybe I should say it outright.
(Point out her use of "lovers.")
She giggles, leans on me again, and returns her attention to the penguins.
I just said what came to mind. Have you never felt the same way?
There's a short moment of silence. Chapayev gazes at a loving penguin couple before turning and snuggling into me.
Her movements are so gentle and natural that, before I know it, I'm hugging her back.
Commander, wouldn't you say... that we're a lot like those penguins?
Are you imitating them?
Yep♪ Snuggling close to you is relaxing.
It's like animal instinct. Nobody tells them to do it, but they naturally find out how to reassure themselves and each other.
And I think your arms... are the most reassuring place for me to be♪
Her voice is filled with immense satisfaction.
I subconsciously relax alongside her and enjoy the intimacy of the moment.
Penguins can't communicate as well as we can, but they understand each other.
Forever inseparable... Heehee, is that too clingy for you, Commander?

options.content: People and penguins aren't the same.

scripts.say: Love is fostered by togetherness, so I prefer it that way.
She raises an eyebrow and grins at me.
Heehee... I'll remember that.
People and penguins aren't the same.
When she hears my answer, she seems oddly fascinated.
Oh, really? If only we could be as simple as them.
Without another word, she turns to look for something.
After a quick glance at me, her eyes finally stop on a nearby sign.
Okay, that's enough of a break. Back to our date~
She suddenly leaves my arms and takes a step away. Then, she turns and offers me her hand.
The interactive area will be even more fun. Don't you want to see these adorable animals up close and personal, Commander?
The penguins watch on curiously as I take her hand and walk along with her.

sequence:
Bonded Together

<size=45>Gift of the Penguins</size>

scripts.say: Zoo - Polar Habitat
The interactive area of the Polar Habitat has no glass barriers, allowing us to get close to the penguins.
A few of them waddle closer, looking up at their new visitors with abundant curiosity.
They're interested in you, Commander.
I bet they're looking forward to me feeding them.
We put on gloves and pick up a bucket of small fish to feed the penguins.
Watch this. I'm an old hand at taming naughty animals♪
Right on cue, the penguins gather around her at once. But she doesn't feed them – instead, she raises the bucket out of reach and smirks.
If you want snacks, you have to learn to beg.
I don't think the penguins will understand that...
But you did, didn't you? Heehee, show us all what a capable master you are.
Chapayev offers me the bucket and watches expectantly.
I experimentally remove a fish, and the penguins rush me with mouths open wide. For now, I just put it into one of their mouths.
You're spoiling them. You have to make it clear which one of you is in charge.
She takes another fish out of the bucket and throws it far away, causing the penguins to waddle-stampede over at it.
One manages to catch the fish, stretching out its neck to swallow it before bobbing its head in satisfaction.
Very good♪
While the fight for the fish continues, one male penguin ignores the food and stares fixedly at a female.
Then, he picks up a smooth stone and places it in front of her.
Hmm...?
Heehee, we've been blessed with a rare sight.
That's a courtship signal.
Penguins give carefully selected stones as gifts to prospective partners.
Isn't that just romantic?
Sure is. I hope he wins the girl.
After that, the female picks up the stone and takes it back to her nest.
So... She accepted it?
That's right. She judged him a reliable mate.
It's just an interaction between penguins, and yet...
Part of me envies them.
When will I get my own stone, I wonder?
Well, Commander?
She makes it sound like banter, but her blue eyes sparkle expectantly as she waits for my reply.

options.content: Is a stone all you want?
You want me to give you a rock...?

scripts.say: Surely you want more than a silly rock...
Not at all! Love can be found in the little things.
If you gave me a stone, I would cherish it.
You want me to give you a rock...?
My, Commander, do you think I'm joking?
Of course I want a present from my special someone.
If you're too embarrassed to do it, I'll gladly take the initiative.
The initiative? What, you'll give ME a rock?
Heehee. A rock, hm...?
She giggles and traces her index finger over my lips, down my neck, and to my chest.
I won't stop there.
I want to give you... something that you'll never forget.
It'd be more fun if it was a surprise, don't you think?
I guess, but don't go too far, okay?
Heehee. Desire and expectation really do add spice to the excitement.
Expectation is a great emotion, especially when it's directed toward your desire.
What do you desire, Commander? I'm sure it won't be hard for me to guess♪

sequence:
Bonded Together

<size=45>Held Hostage</size>

scripts.say: Zoo - Polar Habitat
After we'd finished feeding, the penguins lost all interest in us and just milled about. It was getting time for us to leave.
Just as I turned to do so, though, something pulled at my pants suddenly. A penguin had grabbed on with its beak, with a surprisingly steadfast look in its eye.
Hm?
Uh... Does it want something from me?
I think it wants you to stay.
Heehee, even penguins can't resist your charms!
I try to walk again, but the bird stands firm and even begins beating my leg with a wing, as if trying to warn me against making any sudden moves.
The other penguins notice the hostage situation. Some watch curiously, and some approach to help this one out.
Well. I guess I'm a hostage now.
Hostage? Don't be silly. Maybe they just want you to be their friend.
Instead of helping me, Chapayev crosses her arms and watches in fascination.
Not gonna help?
Heehee. Isn't this the perfect time to show your diplomacy skills?
You monster...
I sigh, squat down, and try negotiating with the stubborn bird.
I can't walk like this, buddy. I really need to go.
(Try to save yourself with food.)
The penguin cocks its head, as if considering the trade.
However, it flaps its wings again in refusal. I doubt it'll be that easy to win a compromise.
Your bribery is coming off as insincere, methinks. Heehee!
(Threaten to use force.)
Despite my threats, the penguin tightens its grip. It seems determined to keep me here.
I won't say that's not an option, Commander, but try not to ruin your pants.
The stalemate continues on until Chapayev bends down and gently pets the bird.
There, there~ Don't bully the Commander, now.
She coos gently, soothing my captor.
It's then that the penguin finally lets go, looks up at her, and chirps softly before backing off.
So it listens to you, huh?
Maybe because I fed it a moment ago.
I stand up, relieved to be free again, but I'm interrupted by an unexpected attack.
The penguin leaps into a nearby pool, splashing water everywhere... and soaking me.
Ugh...
I think it still wanted revenge on you♪
What a... friendly little guy.
I need a change of clothes now.
Hmm... The map says there's a gift shop the next room over.
I bet they sell nice souvenir clothes!
Goodness, now I get to dress you up... What an exciting opportunity to see you in new clothes.
I owe that penguin my thanks!
She giggles, apparently looking forward to playing "dress-up."
I sigh and make my way to the gift shop. Chapayev's practically giddy from this turn of events.

sequence:
Bonded Together

<size=45>A Fashion Crisis</size>

scripts.say: Animal-related products line the shelves of the gift shop.
A polar bear onesie, or a hoodie with a shark fin... Which one do you like more, Commander?
Do they have anything less... cute?
It's a zoo, Commander. Do you expect them to have tactical gear, or something?
No, but something more low-key would be appreciated.
You don't like being cute? I think they're perfect for a comfy day off. And best of all, they'll turn heads!
I can't walk around in those...
Okay. So you prefer serious and low-key, I see.
Not necessarily. I just don't want to deviate from my usual image too much.
Usual image, hmm? But from whose perspective? Everyone else's? Or one specific person's?♪
Doesn't matter. Normal clothes, please.
I look around and eventually choose a black and white outfit. It does have a penguin pattern, yes, but it's not TOO ridiculously conspicuous.
You really did choose the plainest one.
This is fine for now. It's more like me.
Really? I wonder if you don't know your style as well as you think you do.
What does that mean?
Heehee, don't worry. I'll prove it before long.
I pay, take the outfit to the dressing room, and put it on in favor of my soaking-wet top.
When I exit, Chapayev is already waiting by the gift shop entrance. I notice her pocket is bulging.
Did you buy something?
It's a secret.
That just makes me more curious...
Heehee. If you must know, then wait until we get back, okay?
Do you enjoy keeping me in suspense?
Not at all.
A surprise is more fun when it comes at the right time, don't you think?
Okay, then. I'll just assume you bought it for me, then.
Ah. Commander, your collar–
She reaches up to my collar. A cold chill runs through my skin when her fingertips brush against my neck.
Very smooth change of subject there.
Do you want to know that badly?
If you do... Heehee, all you have to do is search me.
I'm happy to let you do it any time.
She takes my hand and presses it against her chest. The softness and her rhythmical heartbeat make me hesitate, but I manage to pull my hand away.
Maybe when we get back.
I'll consider that a promise♪

sequence:
Bonded Together

<size=45>Late-Night Farewells</size>

scripts.say: Port - Pier
After our fun at the zoo, we return to the port as the moon rises overhead.
The sea breeze is cool and humid. Chapayev walks slowly, seemingly trying to buy time.
Can't help but notice you're a little clingy today...
Aww. Do you not like that?
That's not it. I just feel like you're acting different from the usual, is all.
Maybe you don't recognize what's "usual" for me? Given how deeply you immerse yourself in work all the time.
I doubt that...
Well, I don't. I recognize that furrowed brow of yours.
You look like that when you're thinking of what work you'll be doing when you get back. I don't like it.
Sorry. I just realized I have leftover work...
That's exactly what I mean. Your work has tamed you.
I have to escort you home myself, or else I know you'll be consumed by work again.
Hahaha... Here is fine. You go back to your place, okay?
Oh? I'm right, aren't I? You don't want me to know that you're going straight back to work.
Or maybe... are you worried something "unexpected" might happen if I go all the way with you?
The thought never entered my mind.
Despite you saying that you might search me later?
You're not going to let me off that easily, are you?
Oh. So you remember that...
I'd never forget such an offer.
Anyway, let me take you to your office. I'm going to hold you to it♪
She bulls her way through, so I sigh, shake my head, and go to my office.
Heheh, you folded so easily... I think you were looking forward to this.
No, I wasn't...
You don't look very conflicted about it to me.
It's not like you to get embarrassed this easily.
Chapayev turns to me, apparently enjoying the sight of me, as she walks by my side.
Was today fun for you?
Yeah. Much more fun than paperwork, for sure.
So it was half a success, then.
Half?
Having you get used to me so that you'll spend more time with me, I mean.
Getting used to you...
Good. Then you wouldn't be able to escape me even if you wanted to.
You're unusually straightforward.
Heehee. I just wanted to see how much I could make you blush♪
Port - Office
Here we are.
So I've escorted you. Now...
She stops in front of the door, gazes at the knob for a moment, and then looks back at me.
Now...?
You remember the present I got for you, don't you?

sequence:
Bonded Together

<size=45>Proof that You're Mine</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
I close the door and turn to Chapayev. She's leaning against my desk and smiling expectantly at me.
Now can you tell me about this present of yours?
Wow, how forward you are behind closed doors.
Or are you at the limit of your restraint?
So you want the pat-down after all, huh?
Heehee. That was the promise.
How do you plan to do it? Where will you begin?
Her tone is provocative. Without hesitation, I reach my hand into her pocket and find the gift – a fluffy collar.
The metal clasp on it sparkles faintly in the light.
Do I wear this?
Heehee. Figured it out already?
This is surprising...
Oh? What did you expect, then?
Something tells me you're not very bothered by it~
She takes the collar, slowly lifts it up, and gazes at my neck.
So? Want me to put it on you, Commander?
You make it sound like a big deal...
If I do, it's because it is a big deal. Come on, don't be shy~
Her fingertips brush against my neck, and with a cool touch, the metal clasp is fastened.
There... Mhm. It suits you even better than I'd imagined.
Suits me... How, exactly?
I mean that it's exactly what I expected.
She smiles meaningfully as her gaze travels down to my chest.
Guess you win this round.
You say that as if you've lost♪
When Chapayev leans forward, her breath brushes against my ear, leaving a soft whisper to linger within.
Now that you've accepted being mine... How about I come closer?
Her fingers trace from shoulder to collar clasp, before tightening it slightly.
Chapayev...
Yes?
Keep this up, and I will fight back.
Oh? How, I wonder... I can't wait to find out♡

sequence:
Another Leader?

<size=45>Chapter 1 - An Unexpected Savior</size>

scripts.say: Port - ???
As I opened my eyes, an unfamiliar scenery slowly began to spread before me...
An ornate, imposing ceiling. A somewhat nostalgic fragrance. The opulence was reminiscent of the heart of the Royal Family...
Heheh... Thou hast awoken at last?
(This voice... Duke of York...?)
(By the looks of things, I was taken to her room...?)
Prying into a lady's motives, how sinful thou art.
It is hard to believe that someone in thy line of work would have no knowledge as to why I resorted to such... forceful measures.
(She seemed to be serious, but what did she mean by "my line of work?" Had I done something wrong...?)
Ahaha, thy tender expression, so full of innocence and confusion... how I wish to devour it so...
Did thou truly think to escape from me by hiding behind "that" woman?
(Not Wales, but "that" woman...? She can't be talking about...)
Commander, your deliverance has arrived.
The voice that echoed across the halls belonged to that of the newly-appointed secretary, King George V.

The thick aroma of Duke of York's incense, coiling around my senses like shackles, robbed me of my defenses as it pulled me deeper into a sweet darkness... Until suddenly, my savior cut through it in a flash of light.
Curses... why you bloody...!
The normally imperturbable Duke of York seemed at a loss.
Hmph. You can't hide anything from me, dear sister.
Now, work is about to begin, so I'll have to bring the Commander along with me. If you have something to say, you're welcome to come to the office.
With that, King George V swooped over and–
Commander, hang on tight.
... picked me up in a bridal carry, all the way back to the office.
... What a colorful way to start off the day.

sequence:
Another Leader?

<size=45>Chapter 2 - An Affable Personality...?</size>

scripts.say: Port - Main Plaza
In other words... you're asking me why Duke of York is so afraid of our sister?
After what happened this morning, I went to see Prince of Wales for an explanation.
Heh... Heheh... Hahahaha...!!
The normally unexpressive Prince of Wales suddenly burst out into laughter.
Let's see... One could say that King George V is that snake's nemesis.
... Nemesis?
Unlike Duke of York, her power does not stem from "individual strength," but rather from "Noblesse Oblige," the charisma she holds over others. Ah, good timing — see for yourself, Commander.
Sis, are you still hung up on that one time...?
No way! As long as people continue to say that I have no personality, I won't give up!~
Uh, Sis, that's what being hung up means...
Precisely! If you'd like, I could offer some words of advice?
You're... King George V, from the Royal Navy!?

Pardon me for eavesdropping on your conversation. Ms. North Carolina, you stated that you have no personality, but if I may be so bold, I would offer that your noble search for a personality is in fact your personality.
In other words, you must first accept who you are before you can move forward.
B-but... who would acknowledge a personality like that...?
Me, of course!
Huh?
What's the issue? If you are looking for someone who accepts you for who you are, then I shall be that person.
Therefore, you have nothing to worry about. Take pride in yourself and smile — don't you think that suits you better?
... ... (Seems to be desperately trying to suppress her laughter)
Hm... If you put it that way, that does make me feel a bit better! Thanks for hearing me out!
See, Commander? That's just the type of person she is.
Her presence is like the sun, bright and indiscriminate. Whether for better or for worse, she can't stop radiating charisma.
For Duke of York, this is someone who she absolutely cannot handle.
...For once, I seemed to understand what Prince of Wales was talking about.

sequence:
Another Leader?

<size=45>Chapter 3 - Her Majesty</size>

scripts.say: Port - Royal Navy Dorms
One day, I suddenly heard Queen Elizabeth's distinctive voice as I passed by the Royal dorms.
What's the meaning of this, George!?
To say that the Queen was not very happy would be an understatement, and the target of her anger was... King George V?
I had to see what was going on.
When I entered the room, I saw Queen Elizabeth flushed and sweating profusely, trying to fan her tongue as she sat in front of a plate of supernaturally red food.
Wh-wh-what is this dish? You said it wouldn't be spicy at all and I believed you!
Bel! Hurry and get me water, right now!
As you wish.
Your Majesty, this is authentic "mapo tofu" recipe I learned from the girls of the Dragon Empery.
They told me that "you'll stop tasting the spiciness after your mouth goes numb." Perhaps I should have relayed that message, Your Majesty...
Probably would have been a good idea...
Ughh... so spicy... but there does seem to be a nice flavour lingering in my mouth...
Your Majesty, the water.
Queen Elizabeth gulped down the glass of water, and immediately afterwards, continued her showdown with the mapo tofu.
Your Majesty, I've actually learned a variety of different dishes from the various camps here.
We'll talk about it later! Ack...! I can't feel my tongue!
In that case, excuse me. Please enjoy your meal.
Oh, what's this? Were you watching us?
Ah, it is but a small hobby of mine. Have you heard of the saying, "an army marches on its stomach?"
Having that said though, even if we're just eating to survive, it can't hurt to make things a bit tastier, right?
At that time, I swore I could almost see the warrior-chef's soul burning bright in her chest, full of loyalty for her Queen.

sequence:
Another Leader?

<size=45>Chapter 4 - The Knight Commander's Leadership</size>
