Kronshtadt?! H-how did this happen?!
Huh...? How'd I get here? I was on the bridge just a moment ago...
What is happening here?! Did I doze off and start dreaming?! Kiev, come here and pinch my cheek!
Oh no... I don't like this one bit...
Those same clear blue skies. The warm sunshine. The tranquil sound of the sea. This place was seemingly the idyllic holiday resort.
And in less than a few hours, all of it would be engulfed by that horrific black tsunami.
That is, unless someone put a stop to it first.
(After all this, it's time to let them in on the truth.)
Everyone calm down and listen. This is now our third time in this place. Let me explain...
You have got to be kidding me! Your story has too many holes in it! It's simply not possible!
That's a bit too farfetched even for me to believe, I'm afraid...
It's impressively elaborate for a story you made up to ease our minds, I'll give you that much.
It's not, Arkhangelsk. I swear on my honor and reputation that it's the truth. You have to believe me.
Well... You are the leader, and I don't think you'd lie to us.
Assuming you're telling us the truth, that still leaves some unanswered questions.
You said on the first visit we were engulfed by a black tsunami, interrupting the synchronization process and sending us back to the Suliko.
Then the second visit, the tsunami got us again and the synchronization process was interrupted.
And now it's our third visit, and yet you're the only one with any recollection of what happened. Why?
Hmm... Wait, I know! The answer has been right under our noses!
It's the headset! Only Kronshtadt has worn it, right?
It must somehow let her retain her memories of what happened in this place! Without it, you forget it all!
Now, that doesn't explain why the rest of us get dragged into the dream as well, but my hypothesis is that the machine "hooks on" to the mind of anyone within range and drags them in!
Then when it disconnects, it takes your memory of the dream with it, but the headset, dare I say, synchronizes your real and dream memories!
It's a stretch, but it does connect the dots.
Even if we forget everything that happens in here, we'll always trust you.
Just explain it like you did just now, and we'll believe you no matter how many loops we forget!
Yeah... It'll be fine.
Thank you all for believing me. I'll explain it all as many times as needed, but let's try to finish the mission on this loop.
You know, now that I'm aware this is all a dream, suddenly I can't help but feel creeped out by this place.
After processing your explanation a little, some things you mentioned stood out to me.
You said during the first and second visits, that Richard girl looked different, but everything else was the same.
That, to me, suggests she plays a pivotal role in this dream. Hell, her appearance might continue changing.
Then there's that black tornado – and tsunami – that sends us back to the Suliko when it gets us. That's the failure condition, right?
What we should do then is pursue options that extend the dream for as long as possible while we gather new information.
Easy. We travel away from the exercise area and explore some other place.
Good idea! And if that Richard girl appears, we should just avoid her altogether. I don't trust her.
I'm in favor of a change of pace from the last loops and traveling the opposite direction! We aren't far from the Eagle Union's east coast!
If we get far enough away from the exercise area, the black tsunami won't reach us even if it does manifest!
Plus, we can observe it from a safe distance and gather data! What do you say?
You make a good case... Let's do it. Third time's the charm.
Once the waves have subsided, we can take our sweet time exploring this place.
Ahh-ha-ha-haah! A genius always makes genius suggestions! Now, let us set off!
Taking a different approach to the last two loops, this time the girls sailed away from the exercise area and towards the Eagle Union's east coast.
...Should happen any minute now.
What should?
I kept an eye on the clock since we arrived, and it's around this time the black tsunami appears.
Had we done the same as before, it'd be rushing towards us right now.
But we're not seeing one, soooo... does that mean we did it? Did we get around the tsunami?
Hell yes! My plan worked!
Don't pop the champagne just yet. That tornado and subsequent tsunami are so massive they can be seen for miles and miles.
So if they do form despite us being nowhere near, we'll see it.
Uhh, yeah, about that... It's getting pretty foggy pretty fast out here, isn't it?
So foggy... it's hard to see anything.
*inhale*... *exhale*... *inhale*...
What are you doing?
Practicing my breaststroke, just in case the tsunami reaches us!
...You won't swim your way through a tsunami, you know.
It's a joke, you're supposed to laugh! If Kronshtadt couldn't withstand that monster of a wave, I'm as screwed as a nut on a rocket hull!
On a serious note, this fog is getting thicker at an alarming rate. The horizon was clearly visible just a minute ago...
This is abnormal even for the Bermuda Sea. Someone has to be manipulating the weather.
For all we know, there could be Mirror Seas even in this dream world. Be on your guard, everyone.
Volga, can you see anything from above?
Sadly not... It's like the whole sea became covered in a layer of fog.
It'll be impossible to stay oriented like this...
Hey, you there! This area's off-limits!
Eek! Wh-wh-who the hell are you?!
Back off!
A girl outfitted with ship rigging suddenly emerged from the fog, right in front of the Northern Parliament girls.
Kiev responded immediately with a volley. The girl dodged and circled behind Soobrazitelny, who was still reeling from shock.
She melted into the fog again before making the same entrance, suddenly appearing right before Kronshtadt.
Richard...?
Yup, that's me!
Lower your weapons, everyone! Do not attack her!
Kronshtadt ordered her comrades to stand down before walking with a brave stride towards the girl only known as Bon Homme Richard.
Come on, lady. Is this any way to greet someone?
Why are you here?
Hey, that's what I'm wondering. Why are YOU people here?
The outline of Bon Homme Richard was clearly visible even through the fog.
Though she was equipped with her rigging, she showed no signs of hostility, her demeanor disarming as always.
However, Kronshtadt viscerally felt something terrifying hidden beneath that smile.
The reason was that...
You're not the Richard I know. She didn't look like this.
Answer me: Who are you really?
You're a strange one, lady. You just called my name, didn't you?
Bon Homme Richard.
What...?! But how...
Hmm?
In Kronshtadt's head, the image of the girl standing before her shifted rapidly between the one she knew before, and the current one.
Arkhangelsk! Describe how this girl looks to you, right now!
Her hair color, eye color, and the length of her hair!
White, blue, and semi-long, respectively!
I'm seeing the same thing! Why, are you seeing something different?
What's going on? Why am I the only person seeing something different?!
But this world is my... My...
Answer me! Who the hell are you? And how are you messing with my mind?
You're looking at the real Bon Homme Richard, lady.
Actually... Heheheh, I'm more curious about how I appear to you through your eyes.
Richard continued to chuckle bemusedly, a sense of fear awakening within Kronshtadt.
She wracked her brain, sifting through her memories... Following the trails left behind through the dreams to anything pertaining to the person in front of her.
Right... That photo! We took a photo!
But... we didn't meet this time, so there wouldn't be a photo...
Oh, are you talking about that photo? I have it right here~
What...?
Kronshtadt looked at the photo Richard held in her hand.
Despite the familiar, friendly setting of the photo, the girl's inhuman red eyes gazed back at her with a gleeful emptiness.
This isn't what happened before... I'm sure of it...

She tried to stay calm, sorting through all the possibilities in her head. For someone so used to controlling all sorts of information, the inexplicable and illogical drove the seeds of fear deeper into her heart.
Are you okay, lady? You don't look so good~
(My comrades aren't noticing anything strange about Richard. I need to compose myself and get information out of her...)
I'm fine. Can you tell me about the restricted area up ahead?
Hm? Are you talking about this exercise area?
Exercise area? I thought we were heading in the opposite direction!
Ahaha, what are you talking about? This entire place is the exercise area! You wouldn't want to miss our exciting wargame, would you?
Well, not that you'd be able to anyway~
Look, it's about to start right now! Hehehe... Ahahahaha!
Suddenly, Richard's ordinarily amicable voice turned grating and maniacal.
I still don't know who you are or what you're after...
But if you intend to block our way, then we will show you no mercy!
Don't be so trigger-happy, lady. Hold it in a bit longer – there's plenty of fun to be had~♪
Though Kronshtadt already stood poised to start shooting, Richard continued to ramble mirthfully, as relaxed and carefree as ever.
(What's with this girl...? I feel as if I'm being watched... by thousands of people, not just this one girl...)
(Whatever she is, she's dangerous! And at this rate, we're going to become her prey!)
(We need to get out of here, fast... But how? Think, think!)
(That's it, that's the only answer. We have to defeat her. We have to defeat her and get out of here as quickly as possible!!)
Huh? Kronshtadt, what are you doing?
Everyone, fire! Unload everything you have into that girl!
KABOOOM!
Kronshtadt's main gun roared to life before she even finished her command.
Following her lead, the other members of her fleet started to unload into Richard as well.
...But, their attacks seemed to pass right through her body, incapable of leaving even a dent.
Time's up~♪
Heheh... Hehehe... Ahahaha! Ahhahahahahahahaha!
It's starting! Yes, yeeees! It's starting again! Ahahahahaha!
The girl's cacophonous laughter seemed to split through the fog covering the area in the blink of an eye.
Under a sky darkened by black clouds, countless mass-produced ships stood lined up, preparing to face each other.
What? Where'd all those ships come from?!
C'mon, lady, let's have lots and lots of fun!
The girl spread her arms wide, pitch-black water coalescing around her in a roaring vortex.
Peals of thunder and flashes of lightning greet her dark storm, the same black maelstrom re-forming around her.
Kronshtadt fought to suppress the fear tickling her throat back into her heart, clenching her fists tightly to muster what power she had.
The swirling mass in front of her could make the very ocean answer its sinister call. She steeled herself for the waves that would come to smash her consciousness to bits.
Everyone, get behind–
The force of the impact engulfed Kronshtadt entirely. But instead of being devoured by it...
"It... doesn't hurt...?"
"I see. This would be the third time... Maybe my body's gotten used to it..."
"Or does this mean... I've grown stronger?"
"This power flowing through me... It feels surprisingly... good."
"Ah... Imagine what I could do to my enemies with this power... How I'd love to sink them, annihilate them..."
"I am a weapon. I want to destroy everything... Missions, duties..."
"...My enemies... Where are they?"
*cough* *cough*... Everyone, are you all right?!
Urgh... Somehow, yeah... What in the world was that ridiculous tsunami? My body's hurting all over...
Wait, it's not over yet! We haven't been pulled back to the submarine yet!
I'm getting a bad feeling about this... We need to get out of here...
Seconded. My rigging's gonna come apart if I get by something like that again!
Kronshtadt, are you okay? Kronsh–
"Targets... sighted."
"...Yes, those are my enemies. Look, over there too."
Kronshtadt silently turned around and pointed the muzzle of her gun at her "enemies."
"Preparing... to engage the enemies..."
(No... What am I doing...?! Those are my friends!)
Her main gun discharged. Then her secondary guns. Every tool of violence on her rigging vomited fire and brimstone, an uncontrollable lust for destruction pouring out without end.
Something in front of her collapsed to the ground. That something desperately clutched at the hem of her clothes.
But she didn't stop shooting. She could not stop shooting. She could see nothing, hear nothing, feel nothing, think nothing.
Run... Run... away...!
Kronshtadt could only squeeze a few words out with the last bit of her strength before her consciousness was once again swallowed by darkness.
FATAL ERROR.
██████ PROGRESS: 89.9%
Kronshtadt opened her eyes and scanned her surroundings. She was back in the Suliko's synchronization chamber.
We just... barely made it out...
She rose to a sitting position and combed her hair in order with her hand.
...Arkhangelsk? Where are you?
Volga? Hello?
Kiev? Kiiieeev?
Even you, Soobrazitelny...?
Her friends were nowhere to be seen.
Strings of letters passed by on the screen in front of her while the faint whirring of a computer fan continued in the background.
I'm alone? Where did everyone go?
Suliko Interior - Bridge
There's no one here either... And it looks like the sub is set to autopilot.
She doesn't seem to be malfunctioning, at least. But I can't turn the autopilot off...
I'll try my communicator... Sigh, no response.
After searching every nook and cranny of the Suliko, Kronshtadt dragged her weary body back to where she started.
Ugh... Headache. Plus now I'm getting dizzy.
I'm the only one left. But I can't possibly pilot and maintain a submarine all by myself...
We... I have failed. The mission is a failure.
Seems my ultimate fate is to be written off as missing in action, along with the Suliko.
...What a miserable climax to my life.
Stranded at the bottom of the ocean, soon to be forgotten by everyone... And I deserve it for betraying my comrades.
She turned her gaze to the data on the screen. Ordinarily she'd feel like trying to decode it, but now, that felt meaningless to her.
...No, it can't end like this...
She remembered the glimpses she caught of Arkhangelsk before being sent into the dream, and the final step she did to initiate the synchronization process.
It's not too late. I'll finish this mission even I have to do it by myself...
I refuse to be forgotten, to perish as a traitor...!
The only thing worse than dying in that dream...
Is to do at the bottom of this abyss all alone!
Suliko Interior - Bridge
Ugh... My head hurts...
Is this... the submarine's bridge?
Anyone alive? Kiev? Volga? Arkhangelsk!
...Too noisy. Shush.
Nnngh... Did I fall asleep?
Mm... I had a really lifelike nightmare...
We were trapped in a dense fog... then a black tornado appeared... After that, we were all knocked out by a huge wave...
Yeah, I had the same dream...
Woah, what are the odds of that? Did we all have the same dream?
Oh right, Kronshtadt said the same thing, didn't she? She was talking about being in a dream, then getting jolted back to reality by that black wave...
Now that you mention it... Were we able to come back to reality because we were swallowed by that wave?
That incredible pain... Kronshtadt must have endured it those other times as well...
But, why do I remember now? Shouldn't we forget about the dream after we come back...?
I'm not sure, but maybe Kronshtadt has some answers for us!
Suliko Interior - Synchronization Chamber
Kronshtadt?
She... doesn't seem to be conscious yet.
Arkhangelsk pointed to Kronshtadt's immobile figure within the synchronization chair.
What's going on...?
I don't know. When I woke up, I saw her next to me in this state...
What a strange dream... Do you remember anything, Arkhangelsk? Kronshtadt mentioned something about a black tsunami.
Yes, including what happened during the first two loops.
And, during this last loop, she...
Pointed her guns at us, right?
Yes... I remember that still...
That couldn't have been the real Kronshtadt! She wasn't acting like herself!
But more importantly, why hasn't she woken up yet? Don't tell me she's trapped inside that dream still!
I'd hate to be stuck in that place...
Hmm... Do you think we could just wake her up?
Something's telling me that would be a terrible idea.
Huh? Why?

The device likely interfaces with her brain during the connection process, right? So if we were to sever the connection forcefully, it might cause her psychological damage! Maybe there's a way to stop the process...
I already thought of that... But I can't get it to stop...
Ugh... So that's not an option either, huh? But we can't just leave Kronshtadt like this!
Wait, that's it! If Kronshtadt is trapped inside the dream, why don't we go back in and "finish" it for her?
Uhh... I don't think we have the time for that...
The Sirens are starting to resume their patrols in this area.
You've got to be shitting me! Did the Sirens notice us already?
Maybe we should head back to the research base? It's a bit of a gamble, but we can't just leave our comrade behind.
It's not a bad idea on paper, but the synchronization is only made possible by connecting with the meteorite. I have no idea what'll happen if that connection is broken...
Oh, right...
And didn't Kronshtadt mention the other problem as well? If the Sirens find us while we're ascending, we're goners!
If the submarine goes down, Kronshtadt's gonna be the least of our worries!
What should we do then? We still have plenty of supplies, but... can we only wait for help?
C'mon, genius mechanic, think! How do we all get out of here alive?
And how do we rescue Kronshtadt from her dream? Graaaaaaah!
All right, we've got to go the distance here. If ascending is not an option, there's only one way to go – deeper!
I dunno how much pressure this submarine can handle, but at least the meteorite's gonna be fine!
Every second we keep diving is another second that we can keep the Sirens from noticing us!
Not like there's anything else we can do... But here's the problem – even if we do manage to bring Kronshtadt back, then what?
Wait... I'm picking up a signal! An... An SOS signal?!
Huh? That's impossible, there's no way our comms would work at this depth...
Wait, what? Didn't we originally locate the meteorite thanks to a mysterious signal?
Does that mean it's coming from the meteorite then?! If we can find some way of amplifying it, then it'll be picked up by the research base, and our comrades will know about it!
Next, if we can increase the strength of the connection, we might be able to find a way back into Kronshtadt's dream!
Wait. Who's going to pilot the submarine then? If you strengthen the connection, we're all going to get pulled inside the dream, right?
H-haha... Time to pray that the sub's autopilot function actually works?
Well, maybe I can throw together a quick routine to help it avoid Siren detection... But it won't be good for long.
What other choice do we have at this point? If we don't try something bold and daring, we'll just be waiting for our doom!
Understood. How long does it take to do all of those things?
Heheh! Faster than you can say "Soobrazitelny, the galaxy-brained mechanic!"
Surrounded by enemies, the Northern Parliament fleet rushed to finalize their desperate measures.
Inside the synchronization chamber, Volga monitored Kronshtadt's condition while keeping an eye on the operation of the connection device.
On the bridge, Kiev was fine-tuning the Siren avoidance routine while Arkhangelsk focused on amplifying the meteorite's signal from inside the communication room.
In a monumental feat of diligence and discipline, the Northern Parliament ships worked together seamlessly to finish their preparations in no time.
With the completion of Soobrazitelny's command, nothing would keep them from their crucial mission.
All righty! That's a real genius mechanic for ya! Did you see that?
How about the signal from the meteorite? We're casually doing all kinds of revolutionary things here, but I hope Soyuz at least manages to get the signal...
There's no guarantee. All we can do is send out the signal to draw in anyone who's paying attention. Also, you never know what might bite.
Hopefully we'll have Kronshtadt back by then too...
I don't want to think about losing another comrade ever again...
Anyway, are you sure everything's ready to go, Soobrazitelny? We can take some time to double-check things if needed.
Way ahead of you! When I'm surrounded by such beautiful machines, it'd be a shame to perform only a single check on them!
Heh. I guess that's true. You still want to head back to the research base and take another look around, right?
Kronshtadt's going to have to put in a good word with Soyuz for you, so you'd better make sure she comes back to us safe and sound!
All right... Let's go bring her back, together!
Are we ready to connect then? Let's make ourselves comfortable first~
After confirming that all preparations were complete, Volga resumed the boot sequence of the connection device.
See you on the other side, my friends!
An alien scenery spread out before Kronshtadt's eyes.
...So this is the climax of the show.
Flames danced atop water. Twisted metallic headstones adorned the surface. Unworldly weather raged above the exercise area from before.
An abandoned sector of the sea, ravaged by an unfathomable storm that consumed everything in its path.
The grand fleet that had once dotted the horizon was now nothing more than a graveyard, a solemn witness to the calamity that had passed over it.
Flames, smoke, and blackened waters. Even the very air choked the senses in this apocalyptic hellscape.
Only one thing continued to dance in the gala of death and destruction.
It seems... alive.
No, it always was...
Flames and storms raging all around her, Kronshtadt took aim with her main guns as she approached the black tornado.
Kronshtadt knew she had to confront it. No matter how many tries it took or how much time passed.
If I defeat you, then the operation... My mission... can finally end...
She turned her eyes towards the figure at the heart of the maelstrom – Bon Homme Richard.
Kronshtadt could not see the girl. But she could feel her presence.
As if answering her, a laughter began to ring out in her head, both innocent and maniacal.
Defeat me? Why would you want to do that?
I must complete my mission.
Why? Is that mission really that important to you?
I will defeat you, put an end to this dream, and return to the Northern Parliament with my comrades.
Comrades? No, no, Kronshtadt. Don't you remember how you hunted them down yourself?
There is no camaraderie in this world. Only temporary alliances out of convenience.
Your Northern Parliament is no different. They only support you when they need something from you.
Friendship. Factions. Loyalty. You don't need those things. You don't need any of those things.
Shut your crazed, lying mouth!
I will defeat you, solve the mystery of this meteorite, and bring my comrades back...!
Hahah! Is that so? I see, I see.
Even if you manage to defeat me, all that proves is that you have great power.
But power is fearsome. That applies to countries, to factions, to organizations, and to people.
People seek power for themselves, but when they get it, all that power does is breed fear.
Isn't that ironic? Isn't that hilarious?
Face it, Kronshtadt. Even if you defeat me, no glory awaits you. Your "comrades" won't ever come back.
You are all alone. Forlorn. Shunned. Denounced. Destroyed.
No, you're wrong! You know nothing about my comrades or the Northern Parliament!
You are the one who knows nothing.
Everything is a lie, a convenient excuse to use you... to use the KAN-SEN.
Yes... Kindness, support, respect. It's all a lie.
The glories afforded to you are cheap tokens to buy your loyalty, good for nothing but manipulating you.
The moment they realize they are unable to control you...
Is the moment they will come for you to destroy you. After all, what is an unusable weapon but a heap of scrap metal?
If you still won't admit it, then show me that power.
Defeat me! Destroy me! ERASE MY EXISTENCE!
Kronshtadt pumped shell after shell into the black tornado, resuming the symphony of destruction with a new movement.
"Die! Die! DIE!"
She had lost all control of her emotions, becoming a puppet to her pure lust for destruction, her existence reduced to unload her entire arsenal at her target.
The tornado, meanwhile, simply took it all. It did not retaliate or even defend itself.
(How laughable... Am I really trying to kill a storm?)
(It's a force of nature, not a living being. I'm making a fool of myself...)
(But... Pointless as it may be...)
Her assault did not let up.
Is that the best you can do, lady? You've not left as much as a dent on me!
"Shut up! You've not seen the start of it!"
Her identity was being overwritten. Her consciousness began to wane.
Soon destruction would be the only thing she could think of. Soon she would be no more than a living weapon.
Her comrades, her allegiance, her duty, her mission – everything she held dear was being reduced to forgotten memories.
Never before had something felt so reprehensibly wrong. And yet she couldn't stop firing. Her power grew and grew without limit.
"AHAHAHAHAHAHAH!"
"Prepare to meet your end! Drop dead already! DIEEEEE!"
Richard was right there, standing right in front of her.
With a smile like a fallen angel, she pressed her little head against the barrel of Kronshtadt's cannon.
You've almost got me, lady.
A little more should do it~♪
No... No! This isn't like me! I would never...!
Despite her rejection, she could not stop firing. The world turned pitch black, and she realized then that she was on the brink of METAmorphosis.
But then... a ray of light shone through to Kronshtadt.
(What... happened to me...)
The black tornado was no longer there. Nor were Richard, the wrecks, or the exercise area.
Kronshtadt instead found herself in a strange, concrete hall.
Columns of lamps illuminated her surroundings with a faint light.
(Maybe I've finally arrived at the gates of heaven...)
Kronshtadt wandered out of the hall without any sense of purpose, trudging into a corridor. Suddenly, a plain wooden door caught her attention.
(Huh, I wonder what's in here...)
The moment her fingertips brushed against the doorknob, the white concrete hall transformed into a dimly-lit room.
Books and scraps of paper littered the floor, and opposite her in this horribly cluttered room sat a woman at her desk, writing something.
I don't understand... How did this happen?
Her Wisdom Cube... Why did that happen...?
I've never seen anything like it before...
I don't understand... I just don't understand...
BANG! She swung her fist without thinking, knocking over a stack of books.
(Watch out!)
Kronshtadt instinctively rushed over to shield the woman from the falling books, but they slipped through her body and crashed all over the desk and the floor.
Damnit... That hurt...
If only I could see the test data... But I don't have any clearance anymore...
I'll have to count on Dr. Aoste then... and focus on doing what I can do right here!
Don't give up! If anyone can crack this problem, it's you, Anzeel!
Kronshtadt tried to reach out to the woman, but the moment she did so, the scenery around her warped and whisked her back to the previous hallway.
(Was that a researcher? What a slovenly lifestyle... Not that I have any right to judge others though...)
(I don't know who she is or what she's doing, but I hope she succeeds.)
Continuing down the corridor, she came across another door.
(What's behind this one? Another vision?)
This room was lit even more dimly than the last. Kronshtadt could just make out the silhouettes of an adult man and a young girl.
Magister, your calculation has been completed.
It's finally done?! What are the results?
The results indicate that the proposed safety lock mechanism is able to satisfy project specifications.
I see... This is great news. We've finally done it.
I will consider the task complete, then. However, I could perform further calculations if you would like a more stable alternative.
No need. What we've got now strikes the perfect balance between stability and energy output ratio.
Stability comes at the cost of output – limiting it too much would be to put the cart before the horse.
Do you not have faith in Antiochus as a contingency plan?
That's not what I'm saying. I'm just biased towards those girls, perhaps because Anzeel sees so much in them.
Her incessant gushing has piqued my curiosity. Now I, too, want to observe this "Awakening" process that unlocks their latent potential.
What of the Bon Homme Richard incident? Do you believe it to be an example of an Awakening?
Don't be ridiculous. That was the opposite of an Awakening – it was more akin to the girls reverting to their original selves.
That is to say, their Wisdom Cubes underwent the process of degenerating into Origin Cubes. Knowing Anzeel, she's brainstorming a snappy term for it as we speak.
And if she is, she really should be working on something more important.
You know how it goes. When Anzeel slacks, I have to watch her back.
Oh, that reminds me. It's about time I had a talk with our assistant.
When the conversation in the dimly-lit room wrapped up, Kronshtadt found herself back in the white corridor once more.
(Another researcher? Huh... Who was that "assistant" he mentioned?)
(Surely not the little girl? She looked young enough to be his daughter. Far too young to be a lab assistant.)
(Beyond that, I didn't get a word of what they were talking about. Sigh... If only Soobrazitelny were here. She could make sense of it.)
(Wait... If only who were here? Who's Soobrazitelny?)
(I've never heard that name before, and yet... It feels familiar, for some reason.)
(Soobrazitelny... Soobra...zitelny... Oh!)
Repeating the name buried in the back of her mind caused an unexpected third door to appear right before her.
The vision on the other side seemed to be set in some sort of assembly hall, or a theater.
Should we leave some sort of message here?
This is the final stage of the safety lock. If they got this far, they should already have Awakened... or they're on the brink of doing the opposite.
I mean, why not write something at least? It'll be like a fun little Easter egg.
They might read it and gain the strength they need to overcome a great tragedy.
Frankly, that notion is almost too silly to entertain. Nevertheless... I'll put my faith in that genius instinct of yours, Anzeel.
You should be the first to leave a message though, not me.
Oof... Dumping the toughest task on me, huh?
"Heya, little shipgirl! Good job finding this message! Hope you have a great day!"
I hate to be a critic, but maybe you could... tone it down a little?
Yeah, I guess you're right... Okay, how about this:
"Hang in there, child of the Creator."
"Your very existence is a miracle born from the hopes and hearts of countless people."
"Face the darkness, but don't let it consume you! Mama's cheering for you!"
Better?
Serious, yet light-hearted at the same time... I'm not sure what kind of message that'll send.
Look, I'm a researcher, not a writer! This is the best I can do!
Now it's your turn to write something!
I'm not sure I could come up with something in the spur of the moment... Can I sleep on it first?
Nuh-uh, you're not getting off that easy! You're doing it right now!
Fine... Let's see then––

options.content: "For those you love, and those who love you, don't give up."
"Chin up and keep fighting. Everyone back home needs you."
"I too would like to meet you, perhaps in another time or place."
"If you make it back to port, drinks are on me."

scripts.say: Don't give up...? What have I given up on?
Home...? I still have a home to return to?
Meet me? Excuse me? Is this a pick-up line?
Famous last words to tell a comrade on the battlefield...
How do I restart it? And what application even is this?
Sigh... Out of all the things you could say, you chose nothing?
These people are... interesting, even if I still have no clue what anyone's talking about.
I recognize one of them. She's the female researcher from before, I think.
And the other person... Nope, doesn't ring a bell. Must be someone important, though.
Mentioned something about a "genius instinct," though... That reminds me of how Soobrazitelny always goes around calling herself a genius.
And then there's Kiev, Volga, and of course, Arkhangelsk...
My... My comrades...!
Yes! I remember now! I remember all of it!
I would never forget about my comrades! And they would never forget about me!
What am I doing here... I've got my duty to fulfill, and the Northern Parliament to return home to!
I know you can hear me! Get me out of here and put me back where I belong!
Take me back home, to where I belong!
FATAL ERROR.
ORIGINATION PROGRESS: 99.7%
ORIGINATION PROGRESS: 83.5%
ORIGINATION PROGRESS: 65.9%
ORIGINATION PROGRESS: 41.6%
ORIGINATION PROGRESS: 10.2%
ORIGINATION PROGRESS: 0.0%
Kronshtadt's fractured senses pieced themselves back together, her consciousness clawing its way out of the void.
Next came her humanity, then her emotions, flooding back into her being.
*cough* *cough*! Wh-which loop is this?!
Enough is enough, please... I think I've endured enough punishment already...
Kronshtadt! You came back to us!
You wouldn't believe how long you slept. Frankly, I considered waking you with brute force more than a few times.
That explains why my whole body hurts... Violence is never the answer, Arkhangelsk.
I only said I considered it. Maybe I'll give you a friendly whupping after we've returned to reality, though.
Heheh. Hit me with your best shot.
So, what now? Everyone's gathered in one place – do you have a plan?
Yes. I've gathered all the intel we'll need. All that's left is to finish this just the way I like it.
Please pace yourself, okay? We'll gladly take part of the burden off your back.
Exactly! You have a genius mechanic at your disposal – use her!
All we have to do is beat this big thing up, right?
No, we're not doing that. You can't beat a force of nature.
Then what? If we don't strike now while it's sitting around, it'll overwhelm us with its waves again!
The black tornado was still spinning, but its intimidating presence and air of madness were gone. Now it was no more than a destructive storm.
(It's lost its menacing edge... You've shown me everything you had to show, is that it?)
(Or is this just the aftermath of it all, and it's our job to take care of it?)
(If so, it's a humiliating reminder of how stupid I was to think I could fight a tornado with cannon fire.)
It doesn't matter. I will finish this mission no matter what and go home with my comrades and the data we gathered!
And if anything or anyone tries to stand in our way, we will fight until it is no more!
All ships! Aim for the tornado's center! Hit it with everything you've got!
"Prototype submarine Suliko approaching maximum depth."
The Suliko hit the seafloor, sending out shockwaves that rippled through the meteorite and the surrounding environment.
Seemingly in response, the Sirens in the area adopted more aggressive behavioral protocols.
The raised threat level posed a significant challenge for search parties in the area. This, coupled with the confidential nature of the mission, put a temporary stop to major rescue efforts.
But, at no point did any shipgirl from the Northern Parliament forget that their comrades were out here, somewhere.
Their search continued for any lead that might lead them to the girls' whereabouts. They waited, restlessly, for a chance to rescue their missing comrades.
Beneath the endless ice, an echo continued to emanate from the depths, an abyssal refrain waiting to be heard.
The following day...
A small, isolated train station came into view among all the snow, and the convoy finally came to a stop.
They parked next to the station building, from which emerged a woman donning a distinct Northern Parliament coat.
Hello, everyone. How are you all feeling after such a long and arduous journey?
Well, if it isn't Avrora! I'm feeling just fine!
I recognize this station. Quite the historic building, isn't it?
That it is. It had fallen into disuse, so we repurposed it into a stopover point. It's quite useful, actually.
Is it? There's nothing else around here, though.
There isn't, but do you see this map? If you follow it... Well, it won't take you to your destination, but it will lead you to the last leg of your journey.
Wow, Kronshtadt sure was right about the base being far out of the way...
Mhm. That's all the help I can give, I'm afraid. Good luck on the rest of your journey!
Northern Parliament - Secret Naval Base
The convoy followed the markings on the map, traveling for hours through the snow.
Arriving at their destination, they found a small naval base with several out-of-use facilities... and a gigantic submarine berthed in the nearby waters.
Who would've thought we built a port all the way out here...?
One that doesn't freeze over, at that. I suppose this is the place we're meant to patrol?
Look there! What is that giant mech– No, wait, it's a giant submarine?! I've never seen anything like it before!
Kronshtadt, you know something about this, don't you? Mind telling us?
I've heard some rumors. They say this was used in the exploration of the Arcana Sanctum, but that can't be true.
Sometimes rumors do stem from the truth. Well done making it out here.
Soyuz?! Is that you?!
Yes, it is me. Welcome to our command submarine development site.
I'm somehow not surprised by your subdued reaction. You already knew about this project, despite its top-secret nature.
You may think you simply stumbled across the intel, but I believe one of the higher-ups leaked it. I'll have to look into this matter more closely at a later date.
No, truly, all of what I know about the project is guesswork and speculation–
There's no need to explain yourself. Knowing you, you heard of it purely through some strange accident. Am I correct?
As embarrassing as it is to admit... Yeah...
I have to say though, this submarine is a marvel to view in person. Our mission here is going to involve it somehow, right?
Indeed it is. You are going to pilot it yourselves.
But first, I should tell you a little more about this beauty. Please listen closely.
She is a special type of submarine, designed to analyze Siren relics deep beneath the sea.
In place of armaments, she has a vast array of instruments and equipment that makes her better suited for deep-sea environments.
She can fulfill the role of an icebreaker on the surface while retaining all the capabilities of a full-fledged submarine, making her the ideal vehicle for our purposes here.
Her massive internal space allows her to carry a large amount of equipment and weapons without sacrificing the comfort of the crew.
There is only one in existence as of now, which will serve as the Commander's escort vessel, but I do plan to mass-produce this model.
Great Scott! So this giant beast is something of a prototype, isn't she?
Correct.
Like all mass-produced vessels, she's a poor substitute for a shipgirl. Still, I am very confident in her usefulness as an auxiliary vessel.
Gathering data on how she operates in practice will be part of your mission here.
Never thought I'd one day serve as a submarine test pilot...
Of course, I've done everything I can to attune your research equipment, reinforce the hull armor, and calibrate onboard life support systems...
But I'm afraid you won't get many opportunities to investigate Siren tech without the Naval HQ breathing down your neck.
But that's just what we're going to do, right? Pilot this submarine and investigate a Siren facility?
That's right. You have a daunting task ahead of you, but I will pray for your success.
There is a decoy research base in this region. You will head there as part of this operation, but your real objective lies–
Woooow, this submarine is AWESOME! I NEED to see how it looks inside!
Permission to enter her, please! Please?
Denied. Please let me finish explaining.
Kronshtadt may already know most of this, but I don't believe you'll be able to fulfill your mission without knowing what it is you need to do, Soobrazitelny.
R-right... Haha, sorry...
...As I was about to say: your real objective lies deep beneath the surface.
The research base I just spoke of is only a glorified stage prop, but it does house important equipment that you are to bring with you to your real objective.
Your visit to the base serves to create an alibi while also diverting attention from the true purpose of this operation.
As for what your real objective is... Well, I'm sure you already know.
You'll find instruction manuals inside the submarine. They'll tell you how to operate the equipment and where you need to go. I suggest you all read them on the way there.
Now, I'd like to reiterate – we likely won't get another opportunity like this.
The Northern Parliament's future rests on your shoulders, everyone. Bear that in mind all throughout this mission.
Good thing this is exactly the kind of mission I've been looking forward to.
You can engage any Sirens you come across if you so wish, but please do everything in your power to return safely.
Relax, Soyuz, you've picked the right person for the job.
You have other business to attend to, don't you? You shouldn't keep the others waiting.
Indeed I do. I'm putting my faith in you here, Kronshtadt.
You won't have much time to complete your mission, but don't make rash decisions. Proceed forward calmly and carefully.
Got it. We'll be back before you know it.
Best of luck to you all.
Wait! Before I start tinkering with the sub... Does she have a name?
Ah, she does. Apologies, I forgot to tell you.
Her name is Suliko.
It reflects her purpose – to record data, analyze technology, and discover the source of our "souls" as shipgirls.
A nice name, wouldn't you agree?
Northern Parliament Research Base - Nearby Waters
The Northern Parliament's submarine followed the signal into the depths of the ocean.
The time had finally come. With the Commander's aid, the Siren activity in the Polar region was finally curbed enough to allow the search to continue.
Belorussiya, there are some Siren submarines up ahead.
Take them out, Tashkent. Don't miss.
Yeah, yeah. Ready, steady... fire!
3... 2... 1... Direct hit confirmed. The target is down.
Heh... Good thing we didn't come here defenseless. The data Commander provided for us was invaluable.
This vessel is a more polished product than the Suliko.
But, the Suliko still should have enough energy and supplies to keep those girls alive...
It's hard to say. While there should've been enough supplies to last for a year, no ship should be able to continuously operate in these conditions...
At this point, we can only pray for their safety...
Look, there it is! Kronshtadt's submarine!
...Let's get ready.
Prepare to approach the Suliko, Belorussiya! Let us go greet the heroes of the Northern Parliament!
Back at the Northern Parliament
Sovetsky Soyuz reunited with Kronshtadt at a grand parade celebrating the return of the long-lost heroes.

The fact that they were able to return home safely brought relief to the hearts of many, but just as importantly– the information they gathered while connecting with the meteorite would surely pave a new path for the Northern Parliament.
Some things never change, huh? It's good to be back home.
Indeed. This is the place where we belong, and it will always await us with open arms.
How was your trip back?
I guess I got the first-class treatment? In any case, I slept through most of it.
Somehow, our resident genius mechanic still had the energy to go back to the research base.
Honestly, I never thought I'd be able to see my home again.
Yes, it was a miracle for us as well to find that you were still alive. We've never stopped thinking about your disappearance since that time–
So, time didn't seem to be flowing normally inside the chamber?
Correct. Apparently you stayed asleep inside the chamber the entire time until you were found. But nothing else had changed.
It was as if time stood still.
...Let's set that aside for now. No matter how deep the submarine dove, there's no way that time itself would freeze over inside the chamber.
But, if that had anything to do with the Siren technology we were using, it becomes clear why they are so keenly interested in the meteorite.
...So what do you plan on doing next? Do you want some time off, or do you plan to resume your training?
I am always prepared to give more for the Northern Parliament, Soyuz.
We appreciate your service, comrade.
Welcome home, Kronshtadt.
*sigh*... Hah, it's good to be back, my friend.
...Sorry to have kept you waiting!
Royal Isles - Queen's Palace
Suffolk was running through the palace's corridors, a stack of documents in her arms.
She had set the alarm to wake herself up earlier, but slept right through it after having slapped the snooze button repeatedly.
Thus, she had no choice but to try to take some shortcuts through some unfamiliar halls.
Ugh... I'm going to make a fool of myself in front of Her Majesty...
*pant* *pant* ...Huh? Did I make a wrong turn somewhere? This was supposed to get me there faster...
W-wait, did I get lost?!
She noticed that she was no longer surrounded by the palace's brightly-decorated corridors, but instead had entered a strange place with unnatural-looking walls.
She had never seen any place like this before, but assumed it had to be somewhere beneath the palace.
Ugh... Did I somehow end up getting lost in the palace basement?
If the Head Maid finds out about this, she's going to give me an earful...
Oh my, if it isn't Suffolk. I wasn't expecting guests today~
Eep?!
Wh-who's there?!
There's no need to be alarmed, heehee~ I was just thinking how rare it is to see a member of the Maid Team get lost~♪
Miss Neptune! What are you doing here?
Wait, I need to deliver these materials to Her Majesty right away! S-sorry!
I see, I see~ You're on some important business, aren't you?
That being the case, allow me to show you the way~♪
Really? Thank you so much, Miss Neptune! You're a lifesaver!
Phew... Maybe I can avoid sitting through the Head Maid's lectures at this rate...
I wouldn't be so sure about that. You ARE late, after all.
Sheffy?! Bleh, I was afraid this was going to happen...
More importantly, did you come looking for me? How'd you know where I'd be?
I was trying to get these materials over to Her Majesty, but ended up getting lost and wandering my way here...
It happens. This place was relocated in a hurry after all, so the passages might not be reflected in our existing maps.
Huh...?
Don't worry about it. We planned to turn this place into a storage place for some of Her Majesty's toys. Let's head somewhere less clammy first.
Thanks a ton, Sheffy!
It's no big deal. Oh, and one more thing...
Her Majesty said that this area is to be kept secret. Speak not a single word of it.
Got it! Anyway, let's get those documents to Her Majesty before she gets angry! Let's pick up the pace, Sheffy!
Eagle Union - NY City
After receiving the Naval HQ's response regarding the "Reenactment," Saratoga locked herself in a conference room, thinking hard about the next step.
The risk of communications between factions breaking down. The possibility of a Siren counterattack. The Commander's response...
It would not be until several hours later when Saratoga finally decided to make her move.
This probably isn't the brightest idea, but I don't see any other way...
If things are left to continue down this path, we're all going to be in danger, including the Commander.
This has got to be the only way! I'm sure of it!
At least, things can't get any weirder than they already are right now!
Saratoga took out a communicator used only for top-security protocols, and started to connect to a certain channel.
Communication line confirmed. Checking integrity of intel security... Confirmed.
Checking authorization of the correspondent–––
Identity confirmed as CV-3 Saratoga, Eagle Union.
Authorization confirmed. Please state your query.
Please connect me to Alaska in the "Sea of Stars."
It's about time we show the Commander some secrets of our own... Hehe~♪
Polar Region - Northern Parliament Waters
Speed and angle looking good... Engine output stable...
Wow! This is all incredible! Oh, how I'd love to take this beauty apart and examine the components!
Goodness me, you're like a kid in a candy shop~
A kid in a candy shop her parents own...
Oh boy, I wonder what happens if I tweak these parameters just a smidge!
She's too engrossed in the machinery to even deny the fact she's acting like a kid...
Having fun with the sub, are you, Soobrazitelny?
Yes! I'm having the time of my frickin' life!
...Wait, I forgot that we're on the clock! We have a job to do!
Before we do, I have a question for you, Miss Genius Mechanic.
Let's hear it! Assuming it's about machines, I know everything there is to know!
No, it's about the port the sub was docked in.
Specifically about the fact it wasn't frozen over. Geographically speaking, that should be impossible, no?
Should it? Hmm... Wait, I think I know the answer!
Remember those little buoy-like things we saw floating in the water back at the port?
My theory is that they are machines which regulate the water's temperature to stop it from freezing!
See those cables extending to the surface? I bet they connect the heating element to some sort of machine further down below!
That... makes a surprising amount of sense. I really didn't expect you'd have an answer.
Didn't you hear me? I know everything there is to know about machines! Ahh-ha-ha-haah!
...Wait, you weren't expecting an answer? So you asked just for the hell of it?
Yeah, and I learned something new for it. While we're on the topic of machines...
Don't you think it's astonishing how things once thought impossible were made possible thanks to Cube technology? Including warming the waters around an entire port.
All that energy, generated by a device small enough to fit in the palm of your hand. I can't even imagine a world without Cubes.
The port certainly could not exist without them! This region has neither the geography nor resources to support one without the usage of Cube technology.
Maaan, now I want to get my hands on one of those buoys, take it apart, and see what's inside!
Don't even think about it. The buoys are Northern Parliament property.
Having fun with the sub, are you, Soobrazitelny?
Arkhangelsk said almost the exact same thing...
Yeah, I'd take off like a rocket if it wasn't for the fact that I have a job to do! Speaking of which...
Moored vessel spotted to our front! It appears unarmed – most likely an icebreaker!
Let me have a look... I can just make out its name. "Mikoyan."
Exactly where the mission papers said it would be. This icebreaker will guide us to the research base.
Get in gear, everyone. We're about to arrive.
Does anyone else wonder why we're still fielding icebreakers when we've got those heating buoys?
"In with the new but keep the old," I suppose. Maybe the research base will be a mix of old and new as well.
There's no need to retire the icebreakers if they still work, no? That'd be a waste.
I wonder what we should expect to find inside the research base... Do you know anything about it, Kronshtadt?
What I do know is hard to explain... Don't worry though, you'll soon see for yourself.
Polar Region - Northern Parliament Research Base
The girls sailed onward, using the moored icebreaker as a landmark. Not long after, an enormous structure reared its peak over the horizon.
Its hypermodern design was reminiscent of a majestic chapel, or perhaps a rocket launch pad. It towered silently over the ice field surrounding it.
It seems safe to assume that's the research base.
Doesn't look like something built by humanity... It feels threatening...
No surprise you get that impression, considering who DID build it.
Huh...? What do you mean by that?
Simply put, this used to be a Siren facility. It was abandoned and in ruins when we found it, so we decided to rebuild it.
We did what? That sounds way too risky!
It was worth the risk. This place is vital to our operations out here.
We don't have the resources to build a facility from scratch, but we need a base to function as a stopping point in order to dive down.
The Sirens gave us free real estate here; it would be foolish not to take full advantage of it.
Do I have to go inside? I'd rather stay out here...
Why? What are you afraid of?
I'm not afraid. It just feels like it's dangerous to go near it.
That's what it means to be afraid, Kiev. Tell you what – everyone who's going in, assemble on the deck.
Kiev and Soobrazitelny, you'll stay here and guard the sub. You never know when Sirens might appear.
And Volga, you're on babysitting duty. You can all patrol the sector if you want, but don't get lost. This place is bigger than I expected.
Okay. We should be fine if we use the icebreaker as a landmark.
Good. I'd be astonished if you managed to lose track of an ordinary vessel in an area littered with Siren structures.
Then we have a plan. I'll start scouting the waters around the submarine after we've dropped you off.
I can see the base's pier! Initiating docking sequence!
Perfect. Time to get cracking, team!
Northern Parliament Research Base - Submarine Anchorage Point
Whew... I'm done loading the equipment! Kiev, do you have the courage to at least get up on the pier?
I'm telling you, she's a complete scaredy-cat. Sure it's an ex-Siren facility, but so what? It's been rebuilt from top to bottom!
I'm not a scaredy-cat, I'm just cautious... Did you notice anything unusual inside the base?
Nope! But I did find a whole factory's worth of broken machines. I wish I could hole up in there and tinker on them for three months straight!
We've GOT to return here after this mission's over!
The question is whether we'll get permission to... It could be worth asking Kronshtadt about it.
Not now though, since she's in a meeting with Arkhangelsk. Based on how serious they both looked, I think they're discussing the mission...
Suliko Interior - Lounge Area
...Interesting. I never would've guessed that's what's going on in the Royal Navy.
Shocking, isn't it? Tell that to a member of the aristocracy and they'll spit their tea.
What about you? Have you heard anything that'll amaze me?
I hear about all kinds of things. You're going to have to be more specific than that.
How about something I don't already know, for starters?
...How am I supposed to know what you don't know?
Now you're being silly. How would I ask a question about what I don't know about?
You're missing the point. How would I know what you do or do not know?
For the love of... I don't know what to ask about because I don't know what I don't know.
Well, this isn't getting anywhere. Let me try phrasing it differently... How about you tell me something that only you know?
Why didn't you say that in the first place?
Why didn't you just answer a simple question instead of dancing around it?
It's called rhetoric, my friend. It's an important skill to have if you plan on dealing with those aristocrats.
Anyway, no more games. You are someone I can trust with what I'm about to tell you.
Something that you would have no knowledge of, something that only I know–
One way you can make black tea taste better is by putting a whole slice of lemon into your teacup and letting it rest for–
Adding lemon to black tea?! That's disgusting! Nobody in the Royal Navy would do that! Who told you this? The Iron Blood?
That's classified. But I can tell you this is apparently a popular practice in the Iron Blood.
Thinking about it now, that may be a signal used by those in my field... You should watch yourself around anyone who adds lemon to black tea, Arkhangelsk.
Believe me, I'd steer clear of anyone who poisons their own tea like that. Yuck.
Honestly? You should keep this to yourself, lest you get put on the Royal Navy's wanted list for crimes against tea.
I don't plan on sharing it with anyone else. This information is only meant for those in the know.
Although... by divulging it to you just now, I've already let an outsider in on the fact...
I've no reason to think you WOULD leak this information. I trust you, but you must be very careful so as to not accidentally give it away to an agent with...
...Why the weird look? Are you not taking me seriously?
The sudden blaring of sirens interrupted the banter between the two ships.
What's happening?!
Kronshtadt! We're picking up Siren signatures! They're headed our way!
How many? Volga, have you sent out any recons yet?
I have! I'll try to get some more out in a moment–
It seems there's only a handful of them. What's more, they don't appear to have their course set on us – we just happen to be in their path.
I believe our mass-produced ships stationed at the research base will be enough to deal with them.
Most likely. Still, we ought to eliminate them ourselves. Think of it as a warmup.
Warmup for what?
Our objective – that Siren relic – is bound to have more than a handful of Sirens guarding it, so why not test our tactics in a comparatively safe environment?
She's right, you know! We need to get into the swing of fighting while defending the Suliko!
Kiev and I agree wholeheartedly! I'll keep my planes on them so we don't lose track of–
Hey... Everyone, look at the sky!
The girls gathered on the deck looked up and saw a night sky with curtains of silver-blue light slowly fluttering high above.
An aurora! What a spectacular and rare sight!
Agreed...
Say, Kiev, believe it or not, but I have a question for you! Do you know how auroras are formed?
This is admittedly a gap in my knowledge and I thought, "Hey, Kiev is the quiet type, so she likely knows more than she lets on!"
...That's a stereotype about introverts. Quiet people aren't always smart.
Shh! The genius mechanic asked you a question! What you just gave me is not an answer, but a sidenote!
...It so happens I do know. Auroras are the result of fast-moving charged particles from the sun colliding with air particulars in the planet's magnetic field. Does that make sense to you?
The explanation is lost on me, I'm afraid. All I know is these lights are gorgeous~ I should make a wish to the aurora!
Volga put her hands together and whispered a wish to the sky.
(Please, watch over my friends and let our mission here go without a hitch.)
At that exact moment, the Suliko's sensors picked up a distress signal from an unknown source...
Northern Parliament Research Base - Nearby Waters
This is it... The place the distress signal came from.
Is everyone all right? You're not hurt, are you, Kiev?
We're all fine, I think. I made sure of that.
"We're all fine, I made sure of that"... In the most reckless way possible! You'd have gotten seriously hurt if we were fighting a real Siren fleet!
Don't parrot me.
Listen, I'm trying to tell you not to rush in alone or you'll get yourself killed!
But I didn't get myself killed, so it's fine.
Seems the warmup was to everyone's benefit. That was some nice teamwork out there.
And the Suliko didn't get as much as a scratch! All in a day's work!
I was a little nervous at first, but in the end I managed to gain control of the skies~
Hmm... No signs of a fight, and no wreckage either. As crazy as it sounds, I think the signal is coming from underwater.
Right, the signal. Its signature didn't match anything used within the Northern Parliament, so it's anyone's guess as to who's calling for help.
Not even you have any idea who it could be? Goodness...
What's strange is that the signal's source isn't far from the objective... Reckon that's a coincidence?
Oh, you're right. It's practically close enough to park the submarine next to.
So what do we do now? I doubt we'll find any leads here on the surface.
What do you think? We must go deeper, of course!
We could be walking into a Siren trap, but the only way we'll find out is by diving with the sub and investigating. So I propose we do just that!
True, and we have to test her diving performance anyway! Let's get ready to go down.
(Good thing we eliminated all the Sirens first before going underwater. Because once we do, we can't fight back.)
(Smashing up the place, then vanishing without a trace. Just the way I like it.)
Hold on tight, everyone! Initiating diving sequence!
Investigation Site - Depth: 200 Meters
Current depth 200 meters, holding steady!
Terminating diving sequence and switching to manual steering!
Manual? You sure that's a good idea?
It'll be fine! There's still a ways to go until the objective, and this is a good opportunity to get some steering practice in!
Do you remember what the operator's manual said?
There's nothing to worry about! Did you forget I'm a genius mechanic?
Do you remember what the operator's manual said?
Uh... I said it'll be fine! I've piloted mass-produced subs in the past!
Do you remember what the operator's manual said?
I'll... go read it again...
Didn't think so. Go on, shoo.
I'm a little worried... Our riggings are no use underwater...
If Sirens turn up, we'll be sitting ducks...
We knew the risks when we took on this mission. Worst-case scenario, we'll just resurface at once and fight them above water.
Mhm. If the Suliko sinks, we go down with her, so no underwater engagements.
Let's see what the notes say... Interesting. "The specimen is unstable. Do not attempt to move it outside the site of discovery."
Unstable? Are we dealing with something radioactive here?
Not quite. Apparently, if you move the meteorite – i.e. the specimen – far from where you found it, its unique properties vanish.
"Fragments of the meteorite display this same unstable behavior; when removed from the site of discovery, they too undergo structural change."
"For this reason, it is theorized that the specimen can only be studied in a research site constructed on-location, or through remote observation."
And that's why they're sending us down in a submarine. We don't have much other choice.
Wait, I'm getting confused... What are we studying? A relic? A meteorite? Could someone please explain?
You know, I think I'll have another look at the mission briefing...
No need. Stay here and I'll explain so we're all on the same page.
Kronshtadt may be able to weigh in with what she knows too, but at this point I don't trust her to have all the facts straight.
Your words sting like a branding iron...
To start with the meteorite, that's our objective. Once the submarine reaches the coordinates, we're going to analyze it.
I see...
We would simply haul the meteorite back to the surface if we could, but apparently it likes it down there.
So instead, we'll come to it and study it with our instruments to gather data. Am I on the mark, Kronshtadt?
Everything you said is correct. Now let me interject and tell you what I know about the meteorite.
Its story begins just before the last Great War took place, when a massive explosion went off over the Northern Parliament.
I've heard about this! Apparently, the explosion was so big that the shockwave shattered windows even a thousand kilometers away.
Yes. Its butterfly-shaped blast pattern had scientists believing it was caused by a meteorite for the longest time.
This was backed up by eyewitnesses who reported seeing a giant fireball fall from the sky, as well as the discovery of what seemed to be a crater at the explosion's epicenter.
But upon further examination of the crater, researchers were unable to find any meteorites or even traces of an actual impact.
A meteorite impact was the only sound explanation, but without any evidence to support this theory, it quickly fell out of favor.
Now, what I'm about to tell you is strictly classified: a few days before the explosion, "Sirens" appeared near the blast zone.
Following the explosion, unidentified flying objects were seen passing over the site, later thought to be Siren aircraft.
Sirens? Out there...?
Of course, humanity didn't know about the Sirens back then. As such, the reports were regarded as typical UFO sightings and largely written off.

Some time after that, the Siren base we visited earlier was first discovered. However, it wasn't until after the war with the Sirens broke out that people made the connection between them and that huge explosion.
As for why nothing was found at the site, the Sirens likely got to it before we did.
Which finally brings us to what we're looking for. According to my sources, the original meteorite broke into several fragments, one of which fell into the sea.
You'd think the Sirens would've recovered it too by now, but since its unique properties vanish when it's moved, I suppose they decided to leave it be.
And since it's not going anywhere, they probably decided that it's also unnecessary to keep a permanent defensive system around it.
...Or at least, that's my best guess from reading between the lines of our mission briefing.
So... The Sirens built a stronghold to guard the meteorite, but later realized that's not necessary and abandoned it?
I believe so, yes. Back in the last Great War that Avrora fought in, humanity captured several Siren strongholds, and even discovered a few Siren ruins after the war.
The base we visited is one of them, as is the underwater city. I believe it's named... "Arcana Sanctum."
As nobody knew about the meteorite back when we captured the base, our researchers focused mainly on the tech the Sirens had left behind.
The tech they successfully reverse-engineered was then integrated into the riggings we use now.
Later on, with the discovery of the meteorite, we finally realized why the Sirens built that stronghold in the middle of nowhere. And that's how this mission came to be.
I've no doubt in my mind Soyuz must've languished for ages over how to reach the meteorite while avoiding the Sirens and Naval HQ's prying eyes.
The opportunity she'd waited for finally presented itself with the completion of the Suliko and the waning Siren presence in the area.
I never knew the base played such an important role...
Now I feel bad for thinking so little of it before...
I don't blame you for it. We've already salvaged everything worth analyzing from it anyway.
As powerful as Siren tech is, we mustn't forget its ruinous influence. Just look what it did to the Crimson Axis.
However, we needn't pursue Siren tech in our quest for answers. Where do Sirens draw their strength from? Where do we shipgirls draw OUR strength from? Finding those answers is of great importance.
And Soyuz... The fact that she personally traveled to meet us instead of sending an envoy shows just how important she thinks this mission is.
That explains why she put a big shot like you on the case, too.
Excuse me, but... how did we discover that there was a meteorite out here anyway?
Well, it was found–
By complete accident. You won't locate a meteorite chunk in an ocean using divers and sonar.
Remember the huge explosion I spoke of earlier? Scientists observed that the insects and trees around the blast zone were suffering from abnormalities.
"And?" you ask? These strange phenomena were also observed in the species endemic to this area where the meteorite rests.
Fish had begun mutating and coral reefs were turning into crystal. Just like what happened to those insects and trees.
This prompted a team from the research base to follow the bread crumb trail of abnormalities, who then pinpointed the meteorite's location.
I reckon it was around this time they also found out that bringing meteorite bits outside the area they're discovered turns them inert.
The briefing says those specimens can, optionally, be recovered. I say we might as well, even if it's not our main goal here.
So, if you were only half-paying attention, in summary...
One: the meteorite in this region is only a chunk from a bigger one, and for some strange reason, doesn't want to be moved much.
Two: that research base is simply a prop for our cover story. With no more tech left to salvage from it, it's practically worthless.
Three: our mission here is to examine the aforementioned meteorite chunk up-close and gather data on it. Any questions?
None from me~ Thank you for the outstanding explanation, Kronshtadt! Thumbs up!
...Wait, I just thought of one. By "examine" you don't mean literally staring at it through the Suliko's windows, right...?
Obviously not. We're going to use the specialized equipment we retrieved at the base before.
Speaking of which, that equipment is all 100 percent Siren tech. Handle it with caution.

Howdy-do, Lex, Sara!
Hey, Sandy!

I'm feeling great, hehe~ So, Sara, what's up with that outfit?
Heh heh, you're keen as ever! Sara's almost done retrofitting, that's what!
Yup yup, I'm as keen and sharp as a shack! Also, what's a "retrofit"?
A retrofit... *Ahem*! A retrofit is the fruit of much blood, sweat, and money poured into one single goal! To me, it's like my rebirth as an idol!
Wooow... I don't know what that means, but that sounds awesome!
Hah hah hah! Now I must go and see what new pranks– I mean, new abilities I've gotten! To the Dormitory!
Sara! Don't run off without– *Sigh*, what am I to do with her... San Diego, don't take after her, okay?
Hmm... Retrofit, huh... I wanna know more...

Me neither!
Me neither!
It certainly i– Wait, am I really the only one who worked so hard?!

Zzzzz...
Hey, who's that behind the tree over there?
Oh! HEEEEY, NICHOLAAAAAS!
WAAAAGH?! Jeebus, what was that?! An earthquake, an airhorn, or both?!
Nope, just me, San Diego!

Heyo, Hammann!

Useful to the Commander?

Oh, okay! I think I'm starting to get it now!
If that's all, then I'm going back to sleep now... Good night, or morning, or whatever it is... Zzzzz...

Upbeat is my middle name~! You gotta be beaming with energy all day or else your brain'll turn to mush, you know!

My own pace?
Yeah. Everybody learns new things and grow as people every day. How they do it differs from person to person.
Retrofitting is the same. Don't think too much about everyone else's, focus on what you want yours to be, and you'll surely break free of your personal limits one day.
W-wow... I'm kinda dumbstruck, but it feels like you just gave the best motivational speech I've ever heard!
Glad to help someone second only to me in battle stars. Good luck with your goal, San Diego. I believe in you.
Wow, I'm feeling super-duper motivated now! It... it almost feels like I could retrofit right here, right now!
Have San Diego's efforts and her friends' advice brought her to the climax of this story? Has her dream of retrofitting come true? Find out now – go to your Dock and check on her!

You did all that? Even the supply manifest?

Your work's done, Commander. Come lie on my shoulder a little longer, if you'd like. Ooor... I'd be happy to let you lay your head in my lap, too♪
Thanks for your help. I thought I'd be up all night again, so that's a relief.
Now now, you don't have to thank me. I couldn't help myself because I just love looking after you!
I made sweets, too. If you don't want to rest any longer, at least consider enjoying a little midnight snack.

<size=45>2 Is the Secret Good Food?</size>

scripts.say: When I arrive at my office the next morning, I find San Jacinto already single-mindedly focused on paperwork.
The second supply manifest needs a second pair of eyes on it.
The port's overhead crane has broken down, too. We'll need to have it repaired.
Oh, Commander? You're just standing at the door... Are you entranced by the sight of my work?
Haha, I'm just kidding~ Don't be so bashful, Commander...
No. I'm just surprised that you got here so early, San Jacinto.
I think it's only right for a secretary ship to arrive before her Commander.
More importantly, did you sleep well last night?
Yeah. Thanks to you, I slept like a log for the first time in a long time.
That's lovely~ By the way, I can help you... in ways other than work, you know.
San Jacinto puts down her documents, rests her chin in her hands, and smiles meaningfully at me.
Heehee, come on in already. Your breakfast is getting cold.
Breakfast...?
Confused, I approach my desk. I realize a luxurious breakfast has been put there without my noticing.
I made your breakfast full of nutrients! It won't just give you energy – it'll heal your exhaustion, too!
You scrape by on convenient instant foods when you're busy, don't you? From now on, we're having no more of that!
You must eat balanced, nutritious meals on time.
Most of all, good food is the secret to curing exhaustion♡
I sound a little too proud, don't I? I just hope my home cooking is enough to soothe your heart, Commander~
You shouldn't go out of your way for me...
That's not true at all.
As your secretary ship, it's my duty to support you both in your work and in your private life!

sequence:
The Secret to Curing Exhaustion?!

<size=45>3 Overnight Operation ♡</size>

scripts.say: After finishing San Jacinto's homemade breakfast, I focus hard on work.
But even after half the day has passed, half of my desk is still taken up by work waiting to be done.
Goodness, time flies.
I wanted to be with you a little longer, but it's almost time for the joint exercise...
You've already helped me plenty.
She glances at the pile of documents hesitantly.
This much is just fine. Believe in me for once.
I don't mean to doubt your abilities, but... Look how much there is. It'll take time even for you to handle all that.
I'll be back as soon as the joint exercise is over. Consider taking a break for now, okay?
I brought sweets again, so consider it an impromptu tea time~ Come on, Commander. Slack off a little once in a while, would you...?
San Jacinto leans in close. Her hot breath tickles my ear.
What do you say?

options.content: As Commander, I can't just slack off...!
I have to set a good example as the Commander!

scripts.say: Heehee~ I knew you'd say that. That's part of what I love about you, after all.
But don't put yourself through too much, okay?
Let's work together again as soon as I'm back from the joint exercise.
(San Jacinto takes her secretary work so seriously...)
(I guess I'd feel bad if I didn't let her help out.)
Okay. If I'm not done when you get back, then I'll have you work overnight with me.
Aww~ The Commander's inviting me over for a night together♡
Your secretary ship wouldn't dare disappoint~
I hope you're as excited as I am!
The door is suddenly flung open. Behind it is Independence, who stares into the room, stunned.
What did you just say? A... A night together...?
Yep! The Commander wants to spend a night with me♡
Y-you don't mean you'll...
Well, that depends on the Commander's wants!
(Okay, can't have her misunderstanding any more than that. I'd better explain things.)
By "a night together," I mean that I'm having San Jacinto help me out...
That's right. It's a secretary's duty to make sure her Commander's needs are met!
With mutual consent... right? Nobody's forcing anyone to do anything here?
Of course not. I'd never force her to do such a thing.
(It IS secretary work, and San Jacinto offered of her own free will, so I don't think I'm forcing her...)
I promise you, I'm serving my Commander purely out of my own desire.
Though I do think every secretary SHOULD do it~ Heehee~
H-hold up! Is that actually a part of the job?
Independence blushes madly, and her eyes swim all around the room. Eventually, they stop on the sweets San Jacinto brought.
(Okay, fair. Making sweets isn't exactly part of the job description.)
We started doing this last night. She saw that I was exhausted, so she did that for me.
It's my secret to helping the Commander work to the fullest~
Independence's confusion only grows.

sequence:
The Secret to Curing Exhaustion?!

<size=45>4 How to Wake a Sleeping Beauty</size>

scripts.say: After getting one very confused Independence to leave, San Jacinto left for her joint exercise, and I immersed myself in work again.
By afternoon, the pile of documents on my desk has shrunk considerably.
Already that time, huh? It's about time for the joint exercise to end.
Helping me work, participating in joint exercises... San Jacinto must be exhausted, too.
I'll go out to the port to meet her.
When I search the wharf where the exercise was held, though, I find no sign of her.
Am I too late?
While I search, I run into someone I saw very recently.
Commander? Why are you here? Shouldn't you and San Jacinto be... Ahem!
(Is it just me, or is she looking at me weird...? No, I'm probably imagining it. I've just been working too much.)
I'm looking for her right now. Do you know where she is?
Huh? You didn't bump into her?
After the exercise, she was in such a hurry to get back to your office.
I don't think I've ever seen her in such a hurry...
Is she getting ready for our all-nighter...?
M-maybe... *blush*
Thanks for letting me know.
Now that I know San Jacinto and I missed each other, I rush back to my office again.
When I get back, I see that the pile left on my desk is just a little smaller.
San Jacinto is asleep, face-down on my desk. The gentle smile on her face is almost picturesque.
(Didn't she say sleeping like that is bad for your spine? She must be more tired than I thought.)
(If I leave her like that, she'll have some bad aches when she wakes up. I'd better help her out.)
Carrying her over to the couch and laying her down there wouldn't be too difficult.
Doing that without waking her, though, seems nigh impossible.
I think about it for a while and decide to carry her princess style.
Gently, I lift her from the chair and lower her onto the couch.
(Let's get back to work. There's still plenty of paperwork left to go around...)
When I try to leave her there, though, the girl I'd thought was asleep reaches out and grabs my shirt.
No fair, Commander~
Sorry. I tried not to wake you up, but I guess that didn't work out...
What's not fair, though?
You promised we'd stay up late together, didn't you? Did you already forget?
I can't possibly make you stay up with me after seeing you fall asleep in the middle of work.
Naps ARE good at helping you recover from exhaustion, but...
Commander, are you sure that was enough?
Hmm?
When you're waking a sleeping beauty, don't you need the magic of love? True love's kiss, was it?
That's how it works in the fairy tales...
You went through the trouble to princess carry me. And then you go back to work like nothing happened? That's just mean~

sequence:
The Secret to Curing Exhaustion?!

<size=45>5 Is the Secret Vacation?</size>

scripts.say: Despite San Jacinto's petty complaints, we work late into the night.
This is the last one, Commander.
Finally over, huh? Good work today.
I can only imagine how bad it would've been without your help.
You're still so mean, Commander~ Do you think a compliment is enough now that we've come this far?
She teases, but there's a hint of expectation in her eyes.
I'm off tomorrow. Do you want to go out somewhere together?
We could call it relaxation.
Are you saying you wanna go on a date with me?
Heehee. I'll take that as my reward, then.
(She did say she wanted a reward, but...)
(Just going out together doesn't seem like it's enough. I should commit more than that.)
What's the matter, Commander? You're staring...
Tomorrow's date isn't a reward. It's a request from me to you.
I don't want to use an off-handed comment to disguise that.
As my secretary ship, you've helped me both with work and with my life and health.
It's only natural for your Commander to try to repay you a little.
If there's anything you want to do tomorrow, I'd appreciate it if you let me know in advance.
Huh...?
I'm not sure if it's just my imagination, but San Jacinto's ears look a touch pinker.
Mmmnh...
Th-this is... so sudden...
Is that your plan, Commander? Turning my request back around on me is so unfair♪
Not that I like you any less because of it...
