I would be delighted if it rid us of the netherworld, but that is a matter for the distant future.
We performed the ritual for a more pressing reason.
To be honest, we don't know what results the transcension ritual is meant to yield.
All I know is that, with the Holy See vacant, the ritual is a prerequisite for a coronation.
A coronation? The Holy See is vacant?
Isn't that surprising? The throne of the Holy Unitas Empire has been vacant for many years now.
Currently, major decisions are made by the Archbishop of Köln, while lesser matters are left to individual lords. Unfortunately, as the netherworld threat grows...
I don't know if Carabiniere has told you this yet, but the Apennine Peninsula that lies just beyond our borders has already been consumed, taking many of our comrades with it.
But the coronation must be overseen by the Holy See.
Thus, we performed the ritual in hopes of finding another solution to conduct the coronation.
Uniting the Empire's strength for another solution...
You don't have to dwell on it for now. I'm just chatting, in a sense... I've never really been cut out for this stuff.
You should go to Brandenburg. Köln will take care of you from there, I'm sure.
It's getting late. Activating the divine waterway comes with danger, so consider resting here for the night before you depart.
I'm okay with that, but what's this about "activating" it? What IS the divine waterway?
It's one of the miraculous feats of engineering left from the time when God still walked among us. As a network of canals, it connects all of the Empire's major cities.
The entrance lies on the other end of the city. I'll escort you there tomorrow.
As for tonight, you could go directly to our guest quarters to rest... or hear out a proposal of mine.
Let's hear it.
I am to lead my troops to Vienna to bolster the forces there. Tonight marks our pre-departure party.
The city's most prominent figures will be there, including some who may be able to provide you with more information.
You might even meet some fascinating individuals. You need to know more, don't you?
You're right about that. I'd be happy to come, if you'll have us.
Commander {playername} of the Visitors from Beyond, it would be our honor to host you.
On the night of the party, there was a fierce debate in the castle study.
Regensburg's forces are marching to the border tomorrow, so this party is likely to be our final chance.
What do you all think? Do we make our move?
Heeehehehe... I say your plan is already too conservative by far.
Stealing a seal and forging a few orders? Could you be any more boring?
The Empire is already sick to its core. We need a more potent remedy if we hope to cure it.
I would think that forgery of a letter of recommendation is already brash enough...
Heheh. What I'm trying to say is... If we want the Deep-Dive Scrolls, then what better way than to go raid the treasuries ourselves?
As far as I know, there's one hidden away in Regensburg Cathedral, with at least seven more in Nuremberg City's treasury!
Stealing them directly skips all the silly bureaucracy altogether!
Are you saying we should plunder the Cathedral and Imperial Treasury for the sake of HELPING the Empire?
Better we use them than let them keep collecting dust!
Don't worry, I'll take responsibility for it!
Well, no. You wouldn't be able to bear quite all of that responsibility.
We should stick to my plan. The seal will be stolen, but the Deep-Dive Scrolls will be formally borrowed on that pretext.
That only lets one person in to investigate. We can't make a team out of one!
Umm... What if we just make enough for everyone?
When we arrive at Nuremberg, we can forge another set of orders...
That's an idea. Let's do just that. Once the party begins, we'll all spring into action.
*knock* *knock*
Just as the discussion reached a conclusion, there was a knock at the door.
A key slid into the lock, and the study door swung open.
Ah, Archbishop. Are the preparations for the party going smoothly?
Don't insult my intelligence. I heard everything.
Let me warn you: the next time you decide to conspire in secret, try doing it somewhere OTHER than your mark's own study.
You know full well why I've denied permission to form your little investigative team. Using the Deep-Dive Scrolls will weaken the Empire's defenses.
Need I remind you that they're already hanging on by a thread?
But...
I understand that your obsession with deep-dives comes from a desire to analyze the netherworld and predict its attack vector.
That's why I sat idly by while you used the one that Prinz Moritz happened to "acquire" just recently.
As I recall, it was U-2501 and Z15 who took the scroll and broke off from the rest of your force.
Ulp...
I won't press you for any further details.
Come with me – there's someone I must introduce you all to.
We may have the solution to bolstering our defenses close at hand... and if so, I expect you all to prove your worth.

sequence: Regensburg City
Castle's Banquet Hall
Shortly later...

scripts.say: I joined in the pre-battle banquet on Regensburg's invitation.
I've been to plenty of parties, but never one that feels right out of a medieval epic.
Blending in won't be easy.
Indeed...
Adapting to one's environment can be a difficult task.
Meanwhile, Eugen and Clemenceau have integrated into the culture here effortlessly.
They're leveraging conversations with the locals to get information on this world. As for me, all I can do is watch and enjoy the food.
Is the party not to your liking?
I know how you feel. They're not really my thing, either...
Anyway, let me introduce you all. These three here are the freelance mercenaries Götz von Berlichingen, Prinz Moritz, and Z14.
Regensburg gestures to each of the three shipgirls.
Hello there, Commander {playername} of the Visitors from Beyond mercenaries. My name is Götz von Berlichingen.
I've heard that you'll be making for Brandenburg to address the roots of our Empire's troubles. May we join you in your cause?
Götz explained her plan to investigate the netherworld.
Just as our defensive barrier was enough to allow us to fight atop the netherworld's waters, the inside wasn't necessarily impossible for living beings to traverse.
With the Deep-Dive Scrolls – relics that appeared inside each cathedral upon the first emergence of the netherworld – one could safely "dive" into them.
The mercenaries' goal was to use them in order to gain a greater understanding of the enemy.
However, their use came at a cost: using the scrolls would weaken all of the Empire's barrier.
As a result, they would have to wait until the defenses were stable – which meant waiting until the problem of the coronation was solved.
If you're going to Brandenburg, then I suggest you take them with you.
The challenges ahead of you will involve more than just reading some dusty texts inside of a cathedral or two...
What do you say? Deal?
The next day, the four freelancers joined us on the Tribunal's Hand. We arrived at the Regensburg City entrance to the divine waterways.
Though called divine by the locals, they were really a network of canals left by the Antiochus.
This canal network did more than just connect the Empire's major cities – it also featured various so-called "divine relays" along its route, aiding in long-distance communication.
Large, high-speed transport vessels were positioned within as well. Since the Tribunal's Hand fit inside, we opted to travel that way.
The waterways were technically owned by the Emperor of the Holy Unitas Empire.
However, management of them was delegated to specific people.
Regardless of these details, traveling from Regensburg City to Brandenburg meant passing through three other cities.
These were Strasbourg City, Mainz City, and Magdeburg City, in order.
Based on our speed so far, we would reach Strasbourg City this evening.
There, we would rendezvous with U-2501 and Z15 to bring them along.
Commander, we've received confirmation that the route ahead is clear. We may launch the transport ship now.
Then let's set sail for our next destination.

sequence: Holy Unitas Empire
Strasbourg City
Evening

scripts.say: The transport ship arrives at Strasbourg City, bathed in evening light.
Elbe, the person in charge of this waterway, comes to greet us at the entrance. U-2501 and Z15 are with her.
Unfortunately, they come with bad tidings.
We finished our investigation, everyone!
The state of the netherworld is, uh... not great!
U-2501 discovered enemies preparing for a big attack underwater.
There lurks something even more ominous deeper below...
Ugh... As if we didn't have enough trouble on our hands.
I'm sorry we couldn't bring better news...
(Something more ominous deep below, huh?)
(During the World Expo, Marco Polo was setting up something underwater, too...)
(That was why enemies kept appearing endlessly.)
(As I recall...)
(Hmm... She was converting the phenomenon of "faith" into a physical entity, was it?)
(I wonder if something similar is at work here.)
By the time we've settled our business in Strasbourg City, the sun has already set below the horizon.
Like Regensburg, this place has electric lighting – which they call "divine mechanisms" – in the castle and cathedral. However, the rest of the city is lit by sparse torches and oil lamps.
As such, the city is almost entirely dark at night.
When I go to meet Clemenceau and ask about the underwater device at the World Expo, I'm stopped by someone unexpected.
Greetings, Commander {playername}. I am Elbe. It's a pleasure to make your acquaintance...
Hello to you, Elbe.
You look unwell. Is something wrong?
I appreciate your concern. You see, I was hoping to speak with Clemenceau regarding Elector Mainz.
But now... I believe that issue has become less complicated.
What a turbulent night it's been...
On my way here, I received urgent news... They say the netherworld offensive has intensified, just as we were warned.
Is the front line holding?
Things have become dire in the city of Reims... The Archbishop of Trier and her guards have all fallen. It's only a matter of time now until the Hagiobull Alliance's defenses crumble.
Another elector has fallen... This is a grave loss.
I suppose this does eliminate the Mainz issue.
Can you share exactly what that's supposed to mean?
It concerns her status.
As the name implies, electors are powerful lords who have the power to vote for our new Emperor.
By the decree of the Hagiobull, there are seven electors in total. Succession to these titles is typically based on inheritance.
When the Empire is faced with grave danger, the system is changed to prioritize shipgirls.
The Archbishop of Trier was one elector, and the shipgirl Mainz is next in the line of succession.
In short, she will become an elector tomorrow.
Even though we're not of this world?
That won't be a concern. What matters is how she responds to the omen...
In other words, whether she is willing to aid us.
Of course. That's the whole reason we're here.
Setting aside the political situation...
The Hagiobull Alliance is a joint military made up of the Holy Unitas Empire and surviving allies, right?
Does Reims need shipgirls? Can they survive the night?
Hmm... The majority of Iris territory has been engulfed by the netherworld, but the Reims defensive line has remained stalwart.
All of the remaining Iris forces are concentrated there, so they should be able to withstand one more night.
As for how many more after, well...
I've summoned reinforcements to come overnight, and I hope to have them dispatched within two days...
That may be too late.
We'll go there to help them first. Can the waterways be used at night?
They can be used if maintenance work is interrupted... I'll have them activated at once.
Let the others know, Clemenceau. We depart at once.
Already done. The mercenaries will accompany us on the mission, too.
Everybody should be on their way to the Tribunal's Hand.
Got it. Let's join them.
It's time to see the threat this world faces with our own eyes.
I leave the Reims situation in your capable hands. May God's light guide us to victory...
Beneath the lightless night, a black torrent washed relentlessly over us.
The boundary between the world and netherworld blurred, undulated, and shifted, with the netherworld encroaching ever closer.
We've finished off the seventeenth wave... What a night this has been.
We're like a breakwater fending off a flood. No matter how long WE hold out, the land behind us...
We have to stand fast, Hardi. Like a flood, it will eventually recede.
I'm surprised to hear you being encouraging for once.
But of course! It's any holy woman's duty to maintain faith in the darkest of nights.
*sigh*... We haven't been able to send or receive communications since the netherworld swallowed us. There's no telling whether reinforcements will come, at this rate.
This is one of its biggest assaults yet. The Holy Unitas Empire will surely notice we're in danger.
It's only a matter of time... It may take more than two days for reinforcements to arrive.
Two days! As long as we focus on holding the line, that'll pass in no time.
Exactly! If things get especially dire, we always have the option of using our divine relics.
They'd turn even the mightiest army of demons into dust in the wind.
I sincerely hope it doesn't come to that.
Everyone, a new wave is coming.
Ugh... That makes eighteen. Hang in there, everyone!
KABOOOOM!
Commander, we've cleared the enemy forces up ahead. We can proceed.
Great. Let's press on.
Clemenceau, send more recon drones. We have to find the Iris fleet as soon as possible!
After traveling all through the night, we finally made it to the Empire's western front.
I witnessed the clash of steel weapons against Sin Shadows, along with the unwavering resolve of those who sang God's praises throughout their struggle.

I also learned that the Iris fleet was deep inside the netherworld, preparing to execute a ritual called the Sacred Purification. In the process, they'd issued a retreat order to all forces on the defensive line.
A full retreat... I hope that doesn't mean their ritual is mutually assured destruction.
We have to find them – quickly!
KABOOOOM!
Commander, our drones have located the targets! But... there's something wrong with our visual feed!
Routing it to you now...
The footage transmitted by the drone reveals the Iris fleet, unaccompanied by mass-produced vessels.
They floated in a perfect circle atop the sea.
The center of the circle radiated golden light, keeping enemies at bay while also turning the surrounding water from black to grey.
That must be the Sacred Purification ritual. Commander, can you see into the light?
Into the light...
I look closer and see a rectangular object suspended in midair, glowing with a divine golden light.
What is that?
How many shipgirls do you see, Commander?
Hmm... Five?
No, wait. I see five corporeal figures, but also... five apparitions?
So you can see them. That means my hypothesis may be correct... I believe those are Origin Cubes.
Golden Origin Cubes?
Their technology must be akin to the Black Sun device in my possession.
When the device is activated, the Origin Cube at its core turns golden... albeit only for an instant.
This test site may provide the answer to the mystery.
Leave the rest to me. I have a plan to interrupt the ritual and rescue them.
The Black Sun hangs in midair.
Beneath that symbol of judgment, the army of Sin Shadows is instantly reduced to dust.
Huh?
What is that...?
Am I... dreaming?
Flagship of the Vichya Dominion, Jean Bart, calls for the attention of the fleet!
Casablanca has fallen! Now, the pagans will surely bare their fangs at the heart of our motherland.
The Iron Blood and the Sardegna Empire have banded together to tear at our bodies and partake of our blood.
Even our leaders seek the destruction of the Vichya Dominion!
Yes, the same was true of that fateful night at Mers-el-Kébir...
Though Dunkerque and the others showed no signs of hostility...
The craven attack by the Azur Lane told me everything that I needed to know!
These cowardly hypocrites shall never see us bow our heads in obeisance!
These beasts seek to sever the lifeblood of the Vichya Dominion... and they surround us in great numbers. But we shall never become their playthings!
In the name of freedom, hear my final order! All ships, you are to sink yourselves!
I was defeated. For the sake of whatever pride we had left, I ordered my friends to sink themselves.
Battleship Jean Bart sank at Casablanca on that day... That should have been the case.
Yet, I am conscious, and something feels wrong.
My consciousness, which should have returned to nothingness, still continues to "exist" in some way.
So, is this heaven, or is this hell? Perhaps that is the wrong question.
As a ship, perhaps another destination awaits me...
At least I can confidently say this infinite black void all around me is nothing like what's described in the Iris Orthodoxy.
"...All that comes into being must also cease to be. Grieve not over the passage of life, for that is the truth of the providence of rebirth."
"One day, I will wake up as a different me."
"When that day comes, I still wish to praise God. For giving me life in such a wonderful country."
"Thank you for bestowing upon me a life of happiness,"
"And thank you for welcoming me into the seas of Heaven."
"I pray that this glory will be passed down to all who walk the path of the Iris after me."
Within the darkness of the void, only my consciousness offers any illumination... Strangely, when I try to call out, a voice echoes back to me.
However, I am forced to accept that even as a ship, I am scarcely different from any other mortal being.
The Vichya Dominion... Iris Libre... and my sister, Richelieu...
...All the things that I hold dear, now so distant from me.
...If only I could meet everyone again...
Vitals stable. D'accord. You should be regaining your five senses soon enough.
...That voice... Who are you...?
Who I am is of little importance. What matters is you, Jean Bart.
What matters... is me...?
Indeed. Now that you're coming to your senses, shall I explain the situation to you?
Now think, where do you last remember yourself?
Casablanca... Yeah, that should be the place where I sank.
That's right. You ordered the fleet to preserve the Vichya's autonomy, for everyone to sink themselves so that they would not become pawns of the Iron Blood or the Royal Navy.
Yeah, I remember that clearly...
But your decision was nothing but an escape. Your sinking cannot change the cowardice of the Senate, the Royal Navy's treachery, or the fracturing of the Iris Orthodoxy.
However, one can say that your efforts were brave, comical, or tragic. Future generations are sure to reflect upon it in different ways.
But you already knew that, didn't you? Your history... Even knowing that, you'd make the same choice, wouldn't you?
The life of Jean Bart, the battleship, ended at Casablanca. But Jean Bart, the person, has yet to take the first step of her new life...
...You can close the channel now.
...What a load of crap. Le Terrible...
Now I remember it clearly. I tried to sink myself back then, but I was rescued.
Which I guess means that I'm awaiting my recovery while listening to your blathering... right?
I'm pleased to see that you're as sharp as ever, Miss Jean Bart.
I too was in the same situation, but I recovered just earlier. Algérie entrusted me to take care of you.
Jean Bart, do you truly believe that you are in the clutches of death?
...Yes, that is what I chose. I know that my body rests at the bottom of the ocean, and only my consciousness has wandered here. There is no doubt that I have crossed to the other side.
But as a ship... is it necessarily finality that awaits you on the other side?
...What do you mean?
Nothing in particular, Miss Jean Bart.
Reflect upon everything you've left unfinished. Reflect upon all the anger you've yet to vent.
Reflect upon your faith, and upon the power that belongs to you.
Now arise, my "Sleeping Beauty." The wondrous Iris skies await you.

sequence: <size=51>"Lift your head to the heavens, and look closely at the clouds that rise high over you."</size>
<size=51>"How much does each mistake you make cost you in the eyes of God?"</size>
<size=51>"What would it mean to repeatedly turn your back against God?"</size>
<size=51>"Even if your life is just, what would God grant upon you?"</size>
<size=51>"And what would God receive from your two hands?"</size>
<size=51>Cast your eyes skybound and gaze at your insignificance.</size>
<size=51>Alas, what sinful creations we are...</size>

scripts.say: The Basilica Isle - Shortly before engagement with Richelieu's fleet
"Any further trespass upon Vichya waters shall not be permitted. Change courses immediately. Any further advance shall..."
How unfortunate...
It'll be hard to separate their forces if they're moving so closely together. The Royal Navy must be trying their best if they're willing to hand over the command like that...
Now, what should we do next?
*beep beep*
As expected, Richelieu does not want to fight us.
However, things rarely unfold the way we'd like them to. We need to stay vigilant as well.
Vauquelin and the others... should be deployed somewhere safe.
As for me...
(Just to be safe, about the Basilica's "secret"...)
All production-type ships, forward! Intercept the enemy's fleet!
The Basilica Isle - Surrounding Waters
Explosions tear through the waters as the battle rages on.
They're so strong, even though they're just mass-produced ships...!
We're at a disadvantage fighting under the supporting fire of the coastal artillery installations... We should continue the fight outside of their range.
Our enemies are much tougher than I expected... We're not making much progress here.
Why is the Vichya going to such lengths...
Their alliance with the Iron Blood may have something to do with it, but these defenses are on a whole different level from what we saw before.
If we don't advance carefully, we'll risk being focused by their coastal defenses...!
Was this part of Algérie's plan...?
Algérie was not only one of the Iris Orthodoxy's best fighters, but also a skilled tactician.
Nothing was more reassuring than having her on the same side, but to face her as an opponent...
Miss Richelieu...
One more thing. Those mass-produced ships seem to have received some tuning-up.
Ordinarily, performance shouldn't change within the same mass-produced model. However, these clearly have higher specifications than normal.
Not all of these ships have been upgraded, but the fact that they've mixed them together is enough to cast doubt into our battle plan.
Because they look the same, that introduces an element of confusion.
What a tough trial this battle is... does God's protection extend even to these mass-produced ships?!
No, this feels more like it's Algérie's doing...!
O, Saint Michael, why must we be tested like this?
Does this have to do something with cognitive chips...?
That's a possibility...! Wait... there's been no verified evidence of cognitive chips having any effects on mass-produced ships...
Wait. Could this be… the Basilica's doing…?
The Basilica…?
(While it's true that cognitive chips have been a significant technological advance in drawing out the power of wisdom cubes, we still don't know much about their exact mechanisms…)
(Her Majesty has talked about this on occasion, but is Iris Libre hiding something we're not aware of…?)
(I'm curious about it, but there's no way I can broach the subject right now…)
(If there's some joint research between the Royal Navy and Iris Libre… it'd be best to consult Hood about it.)
(The Royal Navy certainly should already be involved if there's any secret research going on… I'll definitely have to look further into this.)
The Iris Orthodoxy was conducting some research on cognitive chips since the Great War, but I heard that it was halted partway through.
…I think the Cardinal is saying that there's no point in pursuing this line of thought any further.
I see…
I'm sorry to interrupt, but… don't you feel something… unsettling about these waters?
It's as if something is encroaching upon us…
Now that you mention it…
I... I feel it too…!
What? I'm not sensing anything, though?
Me neither… is this some sort of strange spell...?
I'm not noticing anything either. If anything, my reactions feel even sharper when I'm operating my aircraft.
Perhaps being an Iris Basilica, there's something about it that only affects outsiders?
(This gives off the same sensation as the Basilica's sacrament...)
(Is it possible... that the Vichya Dominion already uncovered it...?!)
Fortune, how are you feeling?
I-I'm feeling a little weird...
(If these mass-produced ships are being strengthened by the Basilica... I need to get in contact with Algérie as soon as possible...)
Miss Richelieu...?
The Basilica Isle - Surrounding Waters
In the midst of battle...
...It makes sense now! These aren't very strong, but they sure are durable! They're trying to stall us!
There's no spell to get rid of them all, is there... Algérie, why are you doing something like this...?
I'll try to approach the Basilica myself, but it's going to take some time.
Good, let's hang in there.
In other words, Algérie's plan is to wear us down?
Most likely. In a negotiation, you must always look to strengthen your position.
In essence, they're trying to decrease the power disparity between our forces as much as possible.
(If they intended to annihilate us, they would've used that first message to lure us in before launching a surprise attack. I doubt they have any intent on fighting us to the bitter end.)
Let's keep taking out the trash while avoiding the enemy supporting fire then!
Fortunately, their numbers aren't too great, so we'll be able to conserve our strength.
But I'm going to get tired of the grind...
I wonder if Algérie is going to show up soon...
Don't worry, Tem... We're fated to meet again... I think!
Based on the current situation, she'll probably make her appearance before long.
That seems to be the case. My planes have detected a larger Vichya fleet approaching us from the direction of the mass-produced models, led by Algérie.
Miss Richelieu, what would you like to do? Should we attack...?
Oh my... Miss Algérie has left the formation and is approaching us alone.
Hmm... Finally something to be relieved about.
Everyone, stand down. I'll go talk to her.
It's been a while since we've last spoken, Cardinal.
Indeed, it's been too long, Algérie. I believe the last time was...
A sunny day in the garden, surrounded by flowers and sweets. Something like that, right?
Yes, that brings back fond memories.
One of Le Téméraire's and L'Opiniâtre's "magic" tricks went astray and almost caused a gunpowder explosion...
Dunkerque came in just the knick of time and even brought some fresh confections with her...
Dunkerque...
I wonder if you still remember the taste. Sweet and fluffy, soft and gentle... almost unimaginable when you think about what she's like on the battlefield.
And then there's Strasbourg, Provence, Bretagne, and Jean Bart...
I wonder... how they're doing now...
Yes, as you already know, they didn't sink... They were rescued and are now under the care of the Iron Blood.
Unlike the Royal Navy, the Iron Blood will not betray us.
The true enemies of the Iris Orthodoxy are those who invaded our homeland – the Iron Blood. There is no reason for blood to be spilled between us.
We should live to honor the Lord and protect the Iris Orthodoxy, not to wage war against each other.
Please, Algérie. Come back to us, and let us work together to restore hope to our country.
And what of those who already betrayed us? Would you still cooperate with them despite that?
It's certainly true that Iris Libre and the Vichya Dominion should work together rather than fight.
By allying yourselves with the Royal Navy, you are the ones who betrayed the Iris Orthodoxy. But I'm sure the others will understand how you feel.
How about you join us instead? If you really feel sorry about what happened to Dunkerque, it's not too late to atone.
I will not make excuses. What happened to Dunkerque is my responsibility.
Sure, but that's not all I'm here to talk to you about. The Azur Lane is not the same as it was during the previous Great War.
Even if the Iron Blood is far from just, they are rational and do not betray their allies.
...Even if we can't convince anyone else, that'd be fine. I swear in the name of the Templar Knights that the Iron Blood shall not lay a finger on you.
We are in need of your guidance.
Those who devote themselves to the restoration of the Iris Orthodoxy should not obey that which has become an agent of the Iron Blood invaders.
Only by expelling the influence of the Iron Blood, purifying the tainted throne of the puppet state, and restoring the independence of the Iris Orthodoxy can everyone become whole once again.
After all, this is the will of the Iris Orthodoxy.
For that purpose, we are willing to work with the Royal Navy.
...Heh. It seems like we're traveling down two parallel lines.
...So it seems. But, that won't deter me.
My intent is the same. I have no desire to fight you, but sometimes the world doesn't work out the way you want it to.
In that case, Cardinal, best of luck to you.
The knight of the Vichya Dominion gave her blessings before turning around.
The cardinal watched her leave in silence before also turning around.
I hope that one day, we'll be able to have another tea party...
Seems like someone let all the air out of you, huh?
I guess so. But I have no intention of surrendering.
...I was just messing around, but whatever. How'd it go with Richelieu?
She hasn't changed one bit. Charismatic, dignified, and uncompromising.
The others were looking on from a distance, but they seemed to be doing well.
I'm glad that they're not being mistreated by the Royal Navy.
...Maybe that's 'cause Richelieu is with them? Or it could be something else...
There's no point in us worrying about that, right? In any case, has Vauquelin moved into position?
She just did. But, isn't this different from what we had planned?
Yes, because this Basilica has changed our victory conditions. I'll have to look into it a bit further...
Does it have to do with that black thing you showed me earlier...? The thing that powered up the mass-produced ships?
No matter how high the stakes, there's no way you can do everything alone. Are you sure you'll be fine?
Everything will work out. I talked to Richelieu, and neither of us have any intention of fighting the other to the death.
As long as she's in command, the Royal Navy will have their hands tied.
All right... I'll try to draw them in a bit more, so make sure everyone is in position.
Got it. Take care of yourself, Algérie. You hear me?
The Basilica Isle - Surrounding Waters
*beep beep*！！！
Main fleet, continue to bombard the enemies! Light ships, help the anti-air fleets with target selection! Everyone, advance with the blessings of the Lord!
(Sorry, Algérie, but no matter how much you've strengthened these mass-produced ships, there's no way we'd lose in a direct engagement.)
Illustrious, Béarn, as I detailed earlier, please focus on neutralizing Algérie by disabling her rigging.
Of course. The holy light will guide us. Hehe~
As you command. Lady Illustrious, allow me to be your escort.
Ngh...! This anti-air fire...!
Looks like there are additional anti-air installations hidden on shore. They're not going to let us have a straightforward battle.
What a fearsome opponent...
Don't worry, we can keep pushing forward! Momentum is on our side!
The Vichya fleet has begun to retreat!
Is Algérie trying to flee?
Wow, they're all starting to scatter...
All right, let's utilize our speed to catch up to them!
Algérie isn't the type to retreat so easily... Surely this is a trap to lure us in.
Really...? This is our strong suit, though...
Illustrious, what should we do?
Excuse me, let me check with my planes first.
Their movements are too orderly for a retreat. Rather than leaving the battlefield in a hurry, they seem to be reorganizing into a small fleet.
I can't rule out the possibility that they're trying to thin out our forces, but... should we go after them?
If we split up, the enemy will have the numbers advantage. Remember, there's always a risk of being focused by the artillery installations.
In that case, should we go after them one by one? The Basilica isn't too far away, so we could always deploy a portion of our forces to head there...
Lady Richelieu, your orders?
...All ships, we're going to switch course to the Basilica.
Since we cannot confirm the location of Algérie and her forces, let's secure the Basilica first.
The vanguard fleet should not pursue the enemy, and instead retreat to rejoin the main fleet. Taking the Basilica will now be our primary objective.
(If your goal is to protect the Basilica, then you can't ignore this move. It's your turn, Algérie.)
Casablanca Harbor - Past
The warm sunlight, the familiar scent of the sea breeze and the sand, all sweetened by the aroma of Dunkerque's desserts...
Today's shaping up to be another fine day.
Le Terrible, good morning. *cough* *cough*... Sorry, the magic spell I was working on with Tem seems to have failed...
Actually, that was my fault! I was just trying to pull a joke! Also, Tartu, why didn't you stop Tem sooner?!
Uhh... Sorry, Vauquelin... Did you say something just now?
Ahhhh, good grief, I can't count on you for anything! I'll give everyone a hand myself!
*cough* *cough*... Thanks a ton, Vauquelin~!
Is Dunkerque in the kitchen? Time to find out! Let's head over there and take a look!
*sigh*...
Here I am, rusting up from boredom while everyone else is out having fun...
Le Terrible, do you know where Richelieu is?
The Cardinal? She should be sitting at that table over... Err, guess not...
Miss Richelieu headed towards the church.
Oh, merci~
Algérie, y'know, there's something that's been bothering me...
...Isn't this tea way too hot...?
Who's there...? Oh, it's La Galissonnière and Algérie. Good day.
Oh, if it isn't Le Malin! You didn't go to the tea party?
I wanted to, but... Ahem! I mean, I'm on patrol today and could not join you this time.
But don't worry about me. Le Terrible brought me some snacks.
Really? That's fine, but isn't it more fun when you're with everyone else?
By the way, Le Malin, have you seen the Cardinal?
Hmm, Richelieu should be by the...
She headed over to the headquarters. I can send a message if you need her.
Oh, Jean Bart? It's really no big deal though. I was just worried that the host of the tea party wouldn't be coming back.
I see... Well, you should hurry back and enjoy the tea before it gets cold. There's some other stuff I gotta attend to.
Thanks, Jean Bart! We'll be heading back then~
The tea you make really is something else. I just can't seem to get the hang of it.
Anyone can do it as long as they calm down and put their mind to it. With how fidgety you are, I can see how that would be hard, though.
Really, huh? Well, even if I don't do it, someone else will take care of it.
Hehe. So, what did you need to see the Cardinal for?
I heard from a certain friend that the Iron Blood has begun to move.
I'd get told to mind my own business if I told HQ about it, so I haven't bothered with that.
But I was wondering if Richelieu knew anything about it. Just out of curiosity.
"The possibility of war breaking out with the Iron Blood"...
(Thinking about it makes me shudder, but Richelieu and Jean Bart did both mention it before.)
It's still peaceful for now, but things are about to get fun real soon. I can already smell the smoke.
Are you sure that isn't just L'Opiniâtre's magic? Anyway, care for another cup?
Hehe, sure.
The Basilica Isle - Just a while ago
...Why am I reminiscing about the old days again...
Vauquelin and La Galissonnière are doing their part. I need to hurry and finish my preparations too.
When Algérie turned to leave the room, a figure blocked her way.
Algérie of the Templar Knights, the Vichya Headquarters wishes to confirm your receipt of the top-secret orders.
...From the headquarters? I should've known that you were no simple helper.
The expressionless Gascogne handed a small box to Algérie.
The handcrafted box was old-fashioned and decorated elaborately, but seemed to give off a strange sensation.
(A very old box from the Iris Orthodoxy... the seal of the Vichya Dominion was attached later. There's no sign that it's ever been opened, and this girl doesn't seem to know what it is either.)
Algérie opened the box, revealing a device along with some notes.
(A secret order from the Vichya? What could they want...?)
What...?!
The Basilica Isle - Near vicinity
The combined Iris-Royal fleet ignored the maneuvers of the Vichya ships and headed straight towards the Basilica.
Despite being hindered by the various coastal defenses, they soon successfully reached the Basilica.
There are a lot of smaller defensive structures concentrated here. It seems that they tried to turn this Basilica into a fortress.
All that bombardment from earlier wasn't even their trump card...?
No, but they did place their defenses at all the crucial locations up until now, making their firepower extremely efficient. However, there's still no sign of their surface fleet...
If we can just capture the Basilica, it wouldn't make sense to be fighting out there, right?
I guess Miss Algérie really didn't want to fight us...
I also want to believe that, but Algérie is a knight of the Vichya Dominion. She wouldn't kneel before us so easily.
Although the Iron Blood should not be able to enter these waters, we cannot rule out the possibility of their intervention either.
But I'm still wondering, why would they allow us to approach like this? If they were trying to spread our forces thin, there had to be a better way.
...I have a bad feeling about this.
...I agree. What if they're trying to lure us in range of the Basilica's defenses before turning their fleet around to surround us?
However, if we were to fight here, that would pose the risk of stray shots damaging the Basilica.
Miss Richelieu, the Vichya Fleet...!
So they've shown themselves at last. As Richelieu said, there's no way they'd let us capture the Basilica for free.
Vauquelin is leading a fleet of mass-produced ships. Vanguard fleet, please intercept them, but don't chase too far.
The main fleet will continue to press forward. If we reach the Basilica, this pointless battle will end.
Fortune, I'm well-protected here. You can fight with Iris Libre's fleet if you'd like.
U-understood!
Richelieu, Illustrious, see you later!
Indeed. Please be careful.
Hahah! Behold the Vichya Dominion's enhanced, indestructible Mass-Production Corps, led by the unvanquished Vauquelin!
What? The unvanquished Vauquelin? Enhanced and indestructible...?! Why must God test us with such tribulations...!
Uhh, I was just trying to think of something cool to say, so you don't have to take it so literally! That's super embarrassing... *blush*
Haha... But I must ask you once again, please return to Iris Libre! There's no reason for us to have to fight!
I-I'm glad you feel that way, but as one of the Vichya's glorious Templar Knights, I can't just hang up my gear and say, "sure thing!"
...Besides, I don't want to fight you either. As Algérie said, if I can get you to turn around or convince you to join us, I won't have to fire a single shot.
...Sorry, but that's off the table. We have something we must do...
Mm... What should we do then...?
Ah, I know! How about, instead of fighting with our rigging, we joust the old-fashioned, knightly way?
You'd like to settle this with the sword? Very well. I, Jeanne d'Arc, shall not hold back...
Wait, wait, wait! I'd totally get my butt handed to me! Um... I was just blurting out some ideas!
Really? That's too bad though, since this is a battlefield after all...
Fine, I'll take you on then! Wait, Tem, you're coming at me too?!
If you don't want to duel me one-on-one, we'll just fight the usual way!
Ehhhhhh?! F-fine, let's do this!
What's wrong, Opie? Your magic seems to lack its usual kick today!
So you've figured out how to dodge my spells? Let's see how you deal my serious sorcery...!
Hey, I don't want to deal with that at all! I mean, uh, come at me!
KABOOM!
Vauquelin keeps bobbing and weaving around in close range! It's too hard to get a clean shot at her rigging's power source!
Did they decide on these maneuvers beforehand? Surely Algérie would've planned for something like this.
(But uncovering their strategy won't win the battle for us. We've got to eliminate the mass-produced ships and encircle Vauquelin!)
Everyone, please report your current situation!
Le Téméraire here, in good condition! I've taken some minor damage, but I'm good to go!
I'm fine as well. I can continue fighting without any issues.
Um, this is Fortune... My second turret... and my motility unit have been damaged...
Fortune...
(Even though the bulk of the vanguard fleet consists of Iris Libre ships, the majority of the damage has been sustained by the Royal Navy. In other words...)
Ugh...
Vauquelin, why are you doing this...?
Sorry, Richelieu, but we're going to have to change our strategy! In addition to focusing on the power supply, please also try to disarm them!
We can't let them keep targeting our Royal Navy allies...!
In the seas surrounding an area near the Southern continent, untouched by the conflict with the Sirens...
Many cultures thrived in this vast continent, distanced from the large-scale conflict between the major maritime powers and the Sirens.
But these peaceful waters did not know of the dark undercurrents that would usher in the horns of battle...
A fleet was crossing the ocean, approaching a remote island located off the continent.
Mozambique Strait
Th-there's a Siren fleet ahead of us...! One, two, three... no, there's even more!
We've only just entered the strait, and they've already gathered here in such large numbers?
It shouldn't have been that long ago...
Since the Vichya Dominion extended their influence to this area, it's not unusual for there to be Siren interference.
During Operation Catapult, why were the Sirens working under the Vichya Dominion...
Back then, Dunkerque mentioned something about being "puppets of the Iron Blood"...
Ah, my apologies, I didn't mean to open past wounds...
Don't worry about it. Back then, it was only natural for everyone to feel distrust towards the Royal Navy.
All these problems still stem from the fact that we were invaded by Iron Blood. Now that our homeland is divided and at war with each other, we have no choice but to face reality.
This time... We, Iris Libre, will persuade the Vichya Dominion.
Miss Richelieu, I still have my reservations regarding your direct participation in this operation...
No, I must. I must prove if the accusations that I am a hypocrite are true or not. To my own heart, to God, and to the Vichya Dominion.
There is no reason for those who have inherited the former Iris Orthodoxy to be at war with one another.
Upon saying that, Richelieu briefly flashed a bitter smile.
Yes, just like back with the Azur Lane, when we didn't have to fight one another...
Algérie, um... I don't think I can deal with their entire vanguard by myself...
I know, you've been given an impossible task. However, focus on evading, and take aim at the Royal Navy ships if you get an opportunity to fire.
I can do that, but... what if they don't stand down...?
I'll back you up at that point. Ah, please keep an eye on the submarines.
Submarines? Did we have any submarines stationed around here?
Well, who knows? In any case, just keep your eyes peeled.
Got it! Your strategies have never failed, so just leave this to me!
KABOOM!
(I said I'd focus on dodging, but they're coming after me a lot harder all of a sudden!)
(They seem to have figured out that I was only aiming for the Royal Navy ships... but since they're allies, of course they couldn't just let that slide...)
(In any case, Algérie said she'd be following up any moment now, so I'll have to find the right timing to make a retreat!)
Taste my true sorcery! I mean, uh, fiiire!
(Woah?! Did Opie close the gap on me while I was thinking about Algérie's strategy...?!)
Daydreaming at a time like this? Vauquelin, did Tartu rub off on you?
Don't be worrying about me! Anyway, it's about time for me... to make my exit! Whoosh!
Vauquelin! ...What's this...?
It's a smokescreen! She's trying to run away?!
Of course I am! There's no way for me to win!
Wait! Vauquelin!
L'Opiniâtre! Remember what Richelieu said about not overextending ourselves? Get back in formation!
What did Vauquelin come here for then...?
I don't know. Richelieu and the others should already be at the Basilica, and none of us seem to be injured... Wait, no...
Ah, um...
What's wrong, Fortune? Does it hurt?
I... I'm fine... Thanks for your concern... and sorry for making you worry.
What's wrong? Why did you start crying?
Um, well, Hood and the others... did a terrible thing to those Vichya girls... right?
It pains me to say this, but as a member of the Royal Navy, um...
Despite all that, you still fought alongside us, and protected us... even against your former companions...
I know that... even if I apologize now, I won't be able to change what has already been done...
But, I'm so sorry... for everything that's happened...!
Yes, we're aware of all of that. But Richelieu still decided to work with the Royal Navy.
It is true that what happened to Dunkerque indeed was the responsibility of the Royal Navy, and Richelieu does bear a portion of that burden. However...
We shall not be stopped here if we are to reclaim our homeland.
The Iris Orthodoxy should be made whole again. There is no future ahead of us in the hands of the Iron Blood.
...That's why, right now, we stand together.
Jeanne... Thank you!
Since the Vichya fleet is retreating, Richelieu and the others should be getting back to us soon... Wait, what...?!
The Basilica Isle - Near vicinity
We've received a message from Jeanne. They've successfully repelled Vauquelin and are coming to join up with us.
The enemy forces seem to have focused their fire on Fortune, causing her to sustain slight damage, but she is still able to fight.
Phew... Thank you for looking after Fortune... Miss Richelieu...
Just what are they trying to do here? The Vichya forces have gone through all this trouble to defend this Basilica and to try to push us back... for what purpose?
Does this Basilica have anything to do with those cognitive chip-enhanced mass-produced ships?
(I heard from Béarn that the Royal Navy has launched its own investigation... Am I not going to be able to hide it any longer?)
To be frank, this Basilica holds the great sacraments of the Iris Orthodoxy, which–
Before she could finish her sentence, a dazzling light erupted from deep within the island and poured into the surrounding waters.
Above them was a dome of light, shimmering like the vaulted ceiling of the Basilica, touched by the hand of the Divine.
It's... so beautiful...
The array of light was breathtakingly beautiful, as if witnessing a work of God.
All who cast their eyes to the skies were captivated by this otherworldly phenomenon, their engines inadvertently grinding to a halt.
The "Skybound Wall," the divine barrier only referenced in this Basilica's most esoteric scriptures...
The secrets of this Basilica transcend our wildest imagination...
Miss Richelieu, do you think this is what the Vichya Dominion and the Iron Blood were after?
That is a possibility... But it's not something I wanted to believe...
(This barrier bears a great resemblance to the technology of the Iron Blood... But why...?)
Richelieu... The "Skybound Wall" really existed all along?! This path has been completely sealed!
Calm down, Jeanne d'Arc.
Y-yes! ...I apologize for being overcome with emotion...
We know that the "Skybound Wall" was mentioned in the Iris Orthodoxy's literature, and it would not surprise me if there were plans to reproduce it.
To the best of our knowledge, no weapon of that nature has been found so far. Therefore, we should think thoroughly about the situation without being caught up by its appearance.
