(Is she a part of Amagi's soul which the corruption absorbed? Is she a phantom conjured up by the corruption? Is she a puppet controlled by Akagi? Is she Akagi herself, distorted and warped by the corruption? The possibilities are many.)
(Personally, I doubt that she's either simply a puppet or a corrosion entity with identity issues.)
(What we know for sure is that she's extremely dangerous and not to be taken lightly.)
(...Thanks for this, Nagato. Be safe out there.)
Eagle Union Samoa - Sometime later
Base at Kiritimati. No response.
Base at AF. No response.
Port at PH. No response.
Base at SD. No response.
I've tried to contact each and every one of our bases across the Pacific now. None of them answered.
Shimanto wasn't kidding, then... This situation is far, far more serious than I thought.
It IS possible that our communicators simply don't have the signal strength necessary since we haven't fully lifted the illusion yet.
For all we know, the bases may be unreachable due to plain jamming.
That's true.
But also, how can you tell that we've not eliminated the illusion fully yet?
My recon planes spotted an approaching fleet. Affiliation unknown.
Their external identifiers match with Sakuran mass-produced ships, but only by 35.75%.
They're shrouded in black mist, making further identification impossible.
Here's a picture my planes took.
They're covered in black mist alright... Looks a lot like those corrosion entities the Commander told us about.
Only thing is, that intel said they can't be identified at all, yet you said you recognize at least part of 'em.
Back this data up just to be safe. We'll send it to SD once we've got signal again.
I know.
Y'know... when we were "dreaming," or whatever, didn't we say some Sakuran tourists were coming soon?
Looking at the clock, I think our "tourists" are the enemy!
You might be right... If we hadn't snapped out of it, that might have been the end for our base here!
But we DID snap out of it. The enemy's lost the element of surprise.
Let's give 'em a head-on battle! Don't stop shooting until they're all fish food!
BEEP BEEP!
Commander, the fleet is in position. I can see the Sirens' defenses from here.
Chen Hai, Hwah Jah, what's your status?
In position, ready and waiting to start firing at your command.
Ditto. We've arrived at our designated location, awaiting your order to open fire.
BEEP BEEP!
This is Sovetsky Soyuz, reporting to the Empery and the Commander. Our Antarctic Fleet and Blueprint Fleet are in position and awaiting orders.
Are you commanding the fleets yourself?
I am. Our objective, after all, is to take the Mariana Islands and destroy the machine that creates the Storm.
To that end, I feel I should be on the ground with my troops. Well, on the water, but you know the saying.
I have blueprint ships and Kirov META accompanying me. I hope they'll be of service to you.
Admiral Nakhimov here. I'm glad to be fighting with you all.
Bringing several different factions to the same battle... Very interesting. I'll be watching and learning from your commanding style.
BEEP BEEP!
This is Peter Strasser of Iron Blood.
You called, Officer, and the Floating Fortress Fleet has answered. We will help you capture the Mariana Islands.
Hindenburg speaking. We're waiting, Contract Binder. Give us your orders.
Heheh. I could never turn down a request for aid from you.
I expect this to be a rousing battle. As always.
The Royal Navy's South Pacific Fleet has arrived.
We encountered an Orthodoxy squire along the way. She wants to talk to you, so I'll put her on.
I am Forbin, Templar Knight of the Orthodoxy! I'm here to partake in your operation on Cardinal Richelieu's orders!
Wait, Forbin? Are you able to signal Richelieu all the way from here?
Well, I was! I received a very brief transmission from the Cardinal. She said she's dealing with the illusions in Europa as we speak!
(That's good news. Means Shinano and Clemenceau are handling things well. That's one less thing to worry about.)
BEEP BEEP!
This is Nagato. My fleet is in position.
Excellent. Thanks for letting me know.
Hey, Hornet here! With my Type II and all! I'm on the way!
Yorktown's staying at SD, so she handed command over our fleet to me!
Good call. She helps the place run, so it's best that she stays there until all the problems caused by the illusions have been sorted out.
Yeah, that's what she told me! Oh, and that she's sad she didn't get to meet the Commander, but there's always next time!
Man, you three are so close. Commander and Enty and Yorky, sitting in a tree...
Hornet.
Uh-oh! That's my cue to shut up! Sorry!
Ahem. Commander, our fleet will arrive in an hour. Unfortunately, Hornet's fleet will need two hours even at top speed to get here.
We don't wanna give the enemy too much time, so let's launch the attack in an hour. The Eagle Union will lead the charge – the other fleets can follow our trail.
No problem. The attack will start in one hour, then.
KABOOOM!
Harutsuki! You okay?
I-I'm fine, thank you!
These Type IV Sirens mean business. Don't let your guard down.
Okay! I'll be careful.
Come with me. We're gonna regroup with the Sakurans.
As you say!
Wait! Indiana, behind you!
God dammit! Turn around for one second and they rush you like hyenas!
Think you can catch me off guard?!
KABOOOM!
Another Tester vessel destroyed. One point for me.
Phew. Sure looks like that enemy stronghold is getting cooked.
This'll be done in no time at this rate. Hahah.
Got a report from Chen Hai! They've destroyed what they believe to be the Storm's control device!
Also, the coordinated attack on the stronghold is going well! The mission objective should be completed pretty soon!
Alright! Once the fortress is destroyed, all fleets will pull out of the area. Destroying Tester's mainframe will have to come another time when we're better prepared.
Well, about that mainframe – I think she's exposing it to us.
Sending you the recon data I took. Take a look.
Hornet sends me a picture and a set of coordinates.
The picture depicts a great rupture suspended above the sea, almost like someone punched a giant hole through space.
On the other side of the hole, there are thousands of faintly glowing lines, and in the background, a sprawling city of steel situated in a sea of electronics.
Is that really it? Her mainframe?
She's showing it for the whole world to see?
Invasion prevention plan must be executed... Storm must be reconstructed...
Actual test site values... far exceed projected values...
Requesting local cleanup authorization...
"Cleanup"? That sounds bad!
Very bad. Compiler tried to initiate the same thing when we breached her mainframe.
Our forces are too spread out to take her on. I say we retreat before she can activate it.
Why the hell is she escalating like this?! We aren't even after her damn mainframe!
Maybe it's not us... It's someone else!
REQUEST DENIED.
YOUR VESSEL IS SHOWING SIGNS OF MANIPULATION. SUBMIT TO A SELF-DIAGNOSTIC.
A self-diagnostic NOW?!
I'm perfectly fine! Do I look like I'm malfunctioning?!
Look-look-look-look li-li-like mal-mal-mal-mal–
KABOOOM!
Oh dear. You should see a repairman about that.
From seemingly nowhere, the Amagi doppelganger appeared.
With that, the final Tester vessel on the path toward her mainframe was destroyed instantaneously.
I'll make good use of your mainframe, if you don't mind.
Dark tendrils pulsated forth from her fox mask.
Black mist shot through the air, aiming for the rift in space where the wrecks of Tester and her ships lay.
But, just as they were about to enter the rift, they hit an invisible wall, sending sparks flying.
Meanwhile, more of the black mist had covered the wreckages of the mass-produced ships. It pulled them together, transmutating them into a single, enormous vessel.
BEEP BEEP!
It's her! That's the Shadow of Corruption!
She is trying to seize control of Tester's mainframe and connect the Watatsumi to her false Sacred Sakura!
Commander, you must stop her IMMEDIATELY!
Computational resources. A soul. A body...
Now I have them all.
Orochi! Reveal yourself to me!
The sea was blanketed in the black mist of corrosion. It first became a gust, then a tornado, then assumed its final form as a corrosion entity.
The colossal battleship dubbed "Orochi" radiated a foreboding crimson light, its form distorting.
Then, it shrunk down, taking the form of a human.
First, there was one, then two, then three, ten, a hundred...
Finally, a crimson crowd of people stood there ominously, like an army of Pawns.
Those... things... they're not shipgirls.
Nor are they Pawns, nor are they ships... and they're certainly not people!
This is mad!
What have you done?! You've horribly misused the Watatsumi's power!
Ahahahahaha!
I've done it!
I'm so, so happy!
Cacophonous laughter echoed across the sea.
Abnormal weather detected! Corrosion entities are appearing... and mass-produced ships... My god, there are so many of them!
The impostor's strength is still growing... How? She should have no power outside of an illusion...
The mainframe! That's it! If need be, we must put our lives on the line to stop her from reaching it!
But how? That corrosion storm is too dangerous to get close!
There is a solution! That storm is very similar to the one we destroyed just earlier! What's more, it's already very unstable!
I believe we can dissipate it using the Dongyus' rockets!
Doesn't hurt to try! Do it!
Dragon Empery units, target the corrosion storm with your Dongyus! Iron Blood units, protect them!
Enterprise, Bunker Hill, Pittsburgh, disperse the crowd of Amagi doppelgangers!
We'll head for Tester's mainframe and stop the head Amagi from getting in at any cost!
KABOOOM!
With your blasted corrosion storm gone, you cannot move as you please!
Give up! Your plan has failed!
The Dongyus were successful in eliminating the corrosion storm – the very thing that sustained the army of the Amagi doppelganger. Without it, the Eagle Union readily eliminated them all.
You look so awe-inspiring now, Lady Nagato. I'm surprised.
Do not speak using Amagi's voice, you fiend.
You can think whatever you like, because – guess what? I've already succeeded.
"Succeeded"? You're lying to yourself about being satisfied with creating these abominations.
Do you think THAT'S what Akagi would've wanted?
Not at all. The fates of these creatures were sealed the moment they were made.
Tell me, Nagato – when you look at them, what do you see?
A herd of impostors that shan't ever, ever reach the truth.
Interesting. Impostors of who, exactly?
What do you mean, "who"?
A falsehood can only exist if a truth exists. Imitations owe their existence to an original. Whose hull are they based on, and where is its owner?
The owner is long since dead!
Dead? Is she? Why?
Close your eyes and think about it, please. Have you not found a way to cure Amagi's illness?
What are you talking about? That was a dream – a vision produced by the illusion.
A dream, you say?
You are in reality right now. Yet you cannot forget the memory of that perfect dream you had.
You can't be serious...
Where there is cause, there is effect, and vice versa.
The impostor is the effect, the original is the cause. It's only logical.
No... You implanted memories within us, then used the Watatsumi to make them real... That's it, isn't it? That was your plan all along!
Heehee... AHAHAHAHAHAHA!
The figure with the red fox mask turned around and walked inside the rift in space, laughing triumphantly.
As the last traces of the corrosion storm faded away, the portal to the mainframe closed up.
Dammit! We were THIS close!
No. We were not. That impostor was already in possession of a body able to exist outside an illusion.
She let herself be attacked. She pretended as though she could not reach the mainframe. All to make a mockery of us.
She wanted to flaunt her victory to me...
Commander... I must talk to you...
A crowd of shipgirls had gathered at the entrance to the Mirror Sea housing Tester's mainframe.
The space ahead of them appeared empty. They all knew, of course, that this was only camouflage.
I closely examined this place before you all got here.
The route to the mainframe is undoubtedly here. However, an extremely intricate barrier protects it. It will take some time to dispel it.
A barrier, eh... Hmm...
Given the context, do you think she's talking about a Mirror Sea?
Likely. When Sakurans use the word "barrier," they sometimes refer to a special kind of Mirror Sea known as a locked Mirror Sea.
Locked Mirror Sea? Go on.
Well, the first of its kind was discovered in–
It's a kind of Mirror Sea whose inside is hidden! Ya gotta know the right procedure to actually get inside!
...That's the gist of it.
Yes, that does seem like what this is.
What's that? I think I just heard something interesting!
Our researchers have had success cracking the code to get inside those locked Mirror Seas! This sounds like a good opportunity to test some theories!
What do you say, Commander?
Hmm. The Sea of Stars' computing power would help us find the key much faster.
Perhaps we can help. Our supercomputer – the Celestial Tower – can share the calculation burden.
So we've got a Sakuran expert on the subject, an Empery supercomputer, and our own Sea of Stars...
This should be a piece of cake.
Aye. This will go much quicker if we work together.
Alright, then I'll be the crier!
The what?
Y'know, the one who shouts something when you use a talisman.
I figure we'll need a dedicated crier for this Mirror Sea, so just say the word and I'll be there.
I... What?
Wait, do you NOT need to do that? But Shimanto did it when she threw HER talismans!
That's... simply a habit of mine.
A HABIT?! So I recorded all those cringy lines for nothing?!
Oh god... They've been playing ON LOOP inside so many illusions!
Yeowch. That's embarrassing.
Uuuggghhh! Kill me now!
Hah! Well, let's put that aside and get started.
All fleets, restock and resupply, then prepare to invade the mainframe.
While Tester herself is incapacitated, we should be ready to run into the Amagi doppelganger. Do not let your guard down.
BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP!
What? An energy pulse?
It looks like it's coming toward us at high speed...
Warning: Massive energy pulse was detected 30 seconds ago, originating from the Sakura Islands.
Energy pulse shares 96.4% similarity with that of the creation of a Singularity.
The size of this Singularity cannot be determined due to all nearby monitoring equipment having gone offline.
The Sea of Stars suggests giving this Singularity the provisional name "Naraka."
Based on calculations using available data, Naraka is believed to affect the entirety of the Sakura Islands.
Threat level: Cataclysmic.
WHAT?!

sequence: The tables were completely turned as one side was on the cusp of victory.
The players moved their pawns while the spectators stood on the battlefield.
Be cautious at every step and plan for everything before you act.
Know yourself and your enemy and you needn't fear the result of a hundred battles.
The battle being waged by every faction goes on.
Whilst the echo from across the starry seas whispers into their ears.
To Be Continued

scripts.say: Scapa Flow - Tourist Area
The streets were abuzz with people. It was another ordinary, peaceful day.
Hey, does anyone else think this vacation has lasted ridiculously long?
What's so bad about that? No orders to return home means endless vacation!
Yeah! I mean, who DOESN'T like a long vacation?
Look... In the sky.
Did you spot a fancy cloud or– Oh my gosh! Girls, look!
A black sun, quietly burning in the dusky sky.
This is your queen speaking! My loyal subjects – wake up!
You're in a sweet but deadly trap, so snap out of it!
Y-Your Majesty, why are you in the sky?
THAT'S the first thing on your mind?
Owch... My head hurts...
So this whole vacation was nothing but a dream... I can hardly believe how realistic it seemed.
Because it's not entirely a dream. Dreams are natural, whilst yours was fabricated!
It'll be alright, though. This newly developed anti-conceptual weapon will tear down this illusion in only three minutes.
If you feel dizzy or have a headache, that's fine. It'll be gone when you open your eyes.
I'm off to the next illusion now. You lot just focus on waking up!
Let's hope the girls manning the gate haven't done anything stupid...
Sardegna Empire - Taranto
Blue skies, blue seas, and sparkling waves as far as the eye could see. It was another ordinary, peaceful day.
Mmmh. This weather is so wonderful.
It makes me want to sail out and practice formations with my aircraft. Will any of you come to watch?
Allow me to accompany you as your escort!
Yeah, I'll come along! I've been meaning to test out the new glider I invented.
Hehehehe... You girls go and enjoy yourself... I'll stay right here...
Sure, we'll– Uh, what's that in the sky?
A black sun, quietly burning in the dusky sky.
Ahem. Veneto here. Can you hear me? I'm speaking to you through unorthodox means.
A black sun... I remember that! It's that conceptual weapon Marco Polo used!
That thing?! Oh no... Don't tell me someone's trying to cause another superimposition event!
Clearly, this is not who we think it is, then!
You! You're merely an impostor claiming to be Veneto! Who are you really, and what do you want?
Huh?! But Aquila, it's me... Vittorio Veneto.
I don't believe you. Marco Polo already tried this trick once! It didn't work then, and it definitely won't work now!
Nothing you say will make me trust you! Ladies, prepare for battle!
Wait, Aquila! I know you must be confused since I awoke you so suddenly. Um...
Please don't be rash. Just take a deep breath with me... It's really me, Veneto. I've borrowed this conceptual weapon to break the illusion and get you out.
Y'know, that DID sound a lot like what Veneto would say...
You think so?
What is this "illusion" you speak of? I don't understand what you mean.
Have you not been having unusual dreams? Maybe you've run into strange people, or noticed odd things happening.
Uh, no? The weirdest thing that's happened lately is you...
So... nothing strange has happened there whatsoever?
What about from abroad? Have you received any calls or unusual messages?
No. All our communications with Rome and nearby fleets have been perfectly normal.
(Did the illusions have absolutely zero impact on our country?! There's no way that can be true!)
(Oh, I get it! The perpetrator was so afraid of Sardegna's glory that they dared not touch us!)
(Yes, that explains it!)
In a Tribunal hideout, shipgirls who had awoken from the dream were having a meeting.
Elizabeth and Veneto are steadily dispelling illusions across Europa. All that remains is the Northern Parliament.
Ah, them... I've heard that Soyuz transferred the chain of command over to the Pacific.
This move seems calculated. I think we should refrain from employing our conceptual weapon on their shipgirls.
Next topic, then. I've received intel that some circumstances behind the illusions have come to light.
There is no dancing around it – fragments of the Watatsumi played a role in this incident.
It must be stated that the Sakura Empire had no plans for any incident such as this...
Nobody is suspecting your country. It's Akagi who's suspected.
Akagi?
Let me fill you in. Many people have reported seeing someone who goes by the name of "Amagi" in their dreams.
Amagi. The lead ship of her class and sister to Akagi.
Correct. Friedrich and I looked into her once. For what's relevant to this conversation, Amagi died.
When she passed on, this affected Akagi in a substantial way. She was a battlecruiser and was reborn as an aircraft carrier.
Wait, Amagi... died?
Yes. She was to be a major contender for the flagship position of their Combined Fleet.
Sadly, she was born with a hull defect that weakened her body. It only got worse, until it one day claimed her life.
She is, to date, the only case of a shipgirl dying to a hull defect.
Akagi took the loss of her sister so harshly that she was unconsolable for a while.
Once she got better, she was a changed person. She built influence on par with her sister and became a substantial leader of the Sakura Empire, along with Kaga.
Not long after, the Sakura Empire allied itself with the Sirens, and the rest you already know.
Amagi... Many Sakurans grieved over her death...
Still, the memory of her faded as time went on... Now, scarcely few can claim to vividly remember her...
That's not everything, though, is it? Wasn't talking about her considered taboo?
That it was... It only made her seem more forgotten... This one must ask – how do you know all this, Bismarck?
Friedrich, as I said. She told me a lot about her.
Is there reason to believe that her hull defect was implanted by the Sirens?
It's not out of the question. That's why Akagi never fully trusted them.
Perhaps allying herself with the Sirens was only a means to an end for her. Perhaps she wanted to exploit them, as we did.
To summarize – not many know about Amagi, the real one, or that she passed on.
Therefore, when she appears before people in an illusion, it gives the impression that she is, in fact, alive and well.
From this, we can infer that Akagi's goal is to propagate knowledge on a global scale about a shipgirl known as Amagi being alive.
The Watatsumi is capable of bringing ideas to life – and Akagi wants to exploit this power to revive Amagi.
But once a shipgirl has been given form, she shouldn't be able to recover from severe hull damage...
The Commander is already trying to find a cure for that, too. Why would Akagi do this?
If she achieves it, it'll be an unprecedented breakthrough. The risk, however, is extremely high.
Onto something more pressing – the Commander and the Empery are fighting in the Pacific as we speak. I think we should aid them.
This one agrees... However, the Pacific is so unfortunately far away... We would not be in time even if we set off now...
I wouldn't say that. There is a Watatsumi fragment we can use, no?
In the Orthodoxy's capital, within an Eagle Union consulate, a group of awakened shipgirls were trying to get a grasp on what was happening.
(No way... That was all a dream!)
(Okay, need to stay calm. I've snapped out of the illusion, so now I need to figure out what's going on, and fast!)
Shangri-La, has our connection to NY City fully come back online yet?
Not yet. According to Orthodoxy intel, a lot of equipment has gone haywire, even if the illusion itself is gone.
I'd assume that's the reason why.
Damn it. They really caught us off guard...
Then again, we're used to communications going down, so it's not the worst. Start writing a report and send it as soon as we have signal again.
Hey, hang on. Look at this. Does the center of the NA Ocean look weird to you, too?
My, these monitoring values are shooting through the roof...
I'll try to get in touch with New Jersey and ask her to investigate.
BEEP... BEEP... BEEP...
Huh? It's not connecting.
I've got a really bad feeling about this.
That makes two of us...
Call Richelieu and let her know about this. We need to find out what's happening in the NA Ocean ASAP.
I'll send out recon planes and see what I can find!
Somewhere, in the Antarctic Ocean...
Hm-hmmm-hmmm-hm♪
Pamiat' Merkuria META straightened out her cap and coat, humming cheerfully all the while.
Around her, a massive graveyard of wreckages lay turned over like dead animals.
Silly little Observer. You're disconnected from your mainframe, and you thought you could stop me?
Not even your weirdo META with a weirdo Pawn could save you.
See, the only reason I lost last time was because I got too careless! When I put on my serious gloves, that's when it's time to run.
Hm-hm-hm-hmmm♪
Your test site is in chaos right now. I could do anything and nobody would know it was me.
This is gonna be so easy!
Easy? Are you sure about that?
Oh, look, another one of Observer's bodyguards. Who is it this time?
Just hurry up and do your thing! I've got stuff to do, so make it quick!
Data separation – activate!
A torrent of blue data rushed forth from the Tower and filled the sky and sea.
A vast stretch of space filled with stars stretched on in all directions.
What... What is this place?
YLTVCL HUK LEWLS
Ugh... You blocked my access to my resources! Who the hell are you?!
You don't need to know. Rodney, deal with her.
The time has come – for your demise.
Pamiat' Merkuria META was gone without a trace, almost like she was deleted from reality.
You did a good job, waking the Commander up.
But, now you've served your purpose. It's time to get off the stage.
Impressive work. Is she gone for good?
I doubt it, though this will keep her quiet for some time.
Let's go. We have things to do in Antarctica.
The Eagle Union fleet tore through the enemy with overwhelming momentum, coming face-to-face with their leader.
KABOOOM!
Heads up! I've sighted their command unit!
Come now, reveal your true self to us.
All cannons! Fireee!
KABOOOM!
Heehee...
The instant before the shell could hit, the being donning a fox mask vanished in a cloud of pink smoke, leaving not a trace.
She disappeared! How?!
We're not dealing with any regular old Pawn here.
A META, then? Or a new kind of Siren?
It seems our "visitor" was going to be someone known as "Amagi."
Does anyone have any information on this person?
Nope. There's no one named Amagi among the Sakura Empire's current leadership.
Yeah, sorry, I don't do politics or whatever so...
Aren't you our local Sakuran expert, Bell? Do you know anything?
I mean, I only watch their movies and read their manga... I've never heard of anyone named "Amagi."
Guess we'll have to reestablish contact with SD before we can figure out who she is.
Catch your breaths then we'll head out again. We're going to Kiritimati.
Why Kiritimati?
Their radio equipment is more advanced than what's here. Maybe we can reach another base from there.
That's not all. Did any of you notice where those misty things were coming from?
Just from their bearing, chances are pretty high they came from Kiritimati.
If true, that could also mean the fleet stationed there is in some deep shit...
We're the closest allied fleet to them, so we're obliged to assist.
As the fleet approached Kiritimati, the dark clouds overhead suddenly and instantly cleared.
Figures. The weather anomaly ignores the laws of nature. Fargo, what do you see on the island?
Nothing abnormal. My recon planes don't see any signs of fighting, or anyone preparing to fight, for that matter.
They didn't answer our calls, though.
That's true. My confidence index is at 94.75% that the effects of jamming would be eliminated at this close range.
Then it's pretty safe to assume they've got it just as bad as we did back on Samoa.
The things we saw with our own eyes, the photos taken by the recon plane, the sea and the sky changing in the blink of an eye – it all points to this place being affected by the illusion.
If Shimanto didn't wake up the people stationed here, there's a good chance the island's already been taken over.
Then we gotta get in there and save 'em!
Yes, but carefully. We know that the illusion distorts your very perception of the world.
It might paint us as the enemy, like how it tricked us into thinking those enemies were Sakuran tourists.
If it comes to that, we'll just have to stick these talismans to their foreheads.
It worked on us, so it should work on them, right?
How do we even get close to them, though? Shimanto used a torii gate portal, and that ain't exactly Eagle Union standard issue.
Bell? Got any ideas?
Why do you all keep turning to me? I'm just a girl who likes Sakuran movies and manga!
Actually, wait, I DO remember watching a movie where they made a portal.
They held the tag between their fingers, then threw it forward while shouting something cool. It could work!
Bell took one of the talismans and placed it between her fingers just as she had seen in the movie.
Amazingly, the talisman began to pulsate with cherry pink light at a set rate, like it was breathing.
Th-that actually worked! I can't believe it!
Don't forget to yell something.
Right, yeah! How about... Sakuran talisman, dispel this dream!
The talisman turned into a glowing arrow and flew across the water's surface.
It vanished in the air, and in its place appeared a torii gate.
So this is how they showed up out of nowhere. I hope they don't mind us copying them.
Hell yeah! Good job, Bell!
Don't thank me, thank Shimanto for giving us these talismans.
Good job both of you, then. Let's go through the gate and save some peeps!

sequence: Pacific Ocean - Kiritimati
Nearby Waters
Inside the Illusion's Borders

scripts.say: Smoke so thick it blotted out the night sky hung above. Warning sirens rang through the air. From sea to land, everything was ablaze.
Judging by the topography, this appears to be the Long Island defense line near NY City.
NY City? I thought we were going to Kiritimati.
Doubt it'd be so simple. We're playing by the illusion's rules. Fargo, can you see anything else?
There are supposed to be way more defensive structures ever since the front line was attacked. Those are nowhere to be seen.
If I had to guess, this illusion is a recreation of the day of the attack.
That's the day when the Commander, Baltimore, and Victorious pushed back Tester...
Dewey's station was on Kiritimati back then, and she just so happened to be at the defense line.
Maybe the illusion latches on to past trauma... If so, Dewey is in danger! Not just her, but her whole garrison!
Where are they?
I'm still looking. Let me expand the search range.
Judging from my latest recon footage... the Sirens have all been wiped out.
No offense to Dewey and her fleet, but they couldn't possibly have fended off all those Sirens by themselves.
Yeah, I doubt it. Something's up.
Found them! There's a fleet heading to land. I can see Dewey, Halsey Powell, and even Hazelwood.
Thank god. We should link up with them imme–
Wait. There's a stranger among them, wearing a mask.
That's not all... I see those same quasi-Sakuran mass-produced ships from earlier.
Oh no. Those girls have no idea...
There's still time. Charge in there and let's save 'em!

sequence: Pacific Ocean - Kiritimati
Eagle Union-Sakura Empire Joint Fleet
Present Time

scripts.say: The motley fleet sailed gently onward through the blazing seas.
The defense line had suffered catastrophic damage following the intense fighting.
Though the shipgirls fought for dear life to try to prevent this, their best simply was not enough.
Why... How could this happen?
We defeated all the Sirens, and still they caused all this damage...
The line fell all because of us... We were weak...
No, that's not true. It wasn't your fault.
There were so many of them, and so few of you. As important as this line of defense is, you could've never protected it alone.
You not only survived the battle, you even repelled the first attack. You should be commended for that.
Thank you... Thank you, Amagi.
And thank you for helping us. Without you, we'd be on the bottom of the sea by now!
You're welcome. My conscience wouldn't let me stand by and leave an ally to their fate.
You know, this wouldn't have happened if you had more support. Instead, your higher-ups rerouted forces away from here.
I saw the writing on the wall and came here, hoping to resolve your manpower shortage... Alas, I was too late.
The Sirens' next attack could come at any minute. We should leave as soon as possible. Come with me and we'll retreat inland.
BEEP BEEP!
This is Indiana. Dewey, what's your status?
I-Indiana? Why are you here?
What do you think? To save your asses! Pittsburgh, Fargo, Herring, and Bell are here with me.
We're glad you came for us, but I'm afraid it's too late...
Although we managed to push back the first wave of Sirens, the defense line has been utterly destroyed.
Worse yet, we're unable to reach anyone nearby. You're the only ones who have come to help.
You shouldn't stick around! The Siren command unit has yet to show itself, so their next attack could come at any second!
We're going to pull back with the Sakuran delegation. You should come with us.
We need to retreat and regroup, then we can mount a new defense!
What was that? You're gonna retreat?
Affirmative! I hate to admit it, but we are woefully unprepared to fend off another assault at the moment.
The Sirens are going all-out. This line is only one of the many, many fortifications around the Eagle Union that they're attacking.
To think that the capital fleets are so far away at such a crucial moment...
Regardless, staying here is foolish. Retreating and conserving your strength is your best option.
Nobody asked for your advice, "Amagi."
Yeah. Keep it to yourself, you manipulative monster.
M-monster? But she saved our lives!
No. Listen up, Dewey. None of what she did for you is real.
This is a dream – an illusion she conjured up to exploit your weakness!
My fleet wasn't there when the line was attacked, but we looked into what happened after the fact.
The Sirens caught you off-guard. They caused serious damage to the line. That's all true...
But that's not the whole story, is it?
The Sirens sent a huge force at you, but you stood your ground, fighting until the end. None of you even thought about giving up.
Despite having no backup, despite the huge gap in strength, you held the line – with the aid of one person in particular!
One person? Wait...
Farragut-class destroyer, Dewey, reporting for duty!
I'm another Farragut-class destroyer, Aylwin. Reporting for duty.
Are you two from the defense line?
Yes we are, Miss Victorious.
What about the others?
The diversion force managed to draw the Sirens' attention away, giving us the opportunity to retreat with the wounded. But after that...
We'd like to check back with the others, but the Siren fleet is blocking the way back.
It's too much for just us to handle...
B-but... as long as you're here, Commander, you'll think of something, right?
Yeah. It'll be fine.
Don't worry. You've done well. With the Commander's help, we'll get through this.
The goddess of victory is with you! We'll keep you two safe – just stay behind us!
V-Victorious! We received a transmission from Juneau and Birmingham, informing us that they made contact with an elite Siren!
Commander, we should go save them!
I remember now! The Commander fought with us and we WON that day!
No Sakuran delegation came by back then, either!
But then... Who are you?!
Heheh. So you've opened your eyes.
Even with outside help, I didn't think you'd wake up so quickly... Memories can be powerful things, I suppose.
This is interesting. VERY interesting.
Now that you've awoken, enjoy your perpetual stay.
The moment her fake identity was stripped away, the masked person laid bare her rigging while black mist coiled up around her body.
The similarly sinister mass-produced ships, too, began radiating a foreboding aura the very next moment.
O-oh no!
Gone was the warm embrace of safety the dream gave them, replaced entirely with a bursting lust for blood.
All of a sudden, a torii gate appeared in the sky with a flash of pinkish light. Their savior leaped out from it.
Leave!
Our!
DESTROYERS!
ALOOOONE!
Relentless cannon fire rained down upon the mass-produced ships, forcing the masked figure to back off.
What?!
Did she just jump out of the sky?!
That's SO COOL!
If you've got something to say, say it to me, monster.
Girls! The wolf in sheep's clothing has shown her true colors! Let's kick her ass then get the hell out of here!
The masked figure didn't put up too much of a struggle, as the arrival of Indiana's fleet caught her by surprise.
She fought back merely for form's sake for a while, ultimately disappearing in a pinkish mist just like last time.
With their command unit now gone, the rest of her fleet quickly fell into chaos and was disposed of. The illusion's grip on the island disappeared.
By the time the shipgirls returned to Kiritimati, it was already evening.
We're back to Kiritimati! Gosh, that was TOO realistic for just a dream...
We're sorry we failed you like this – by falling for the illusion...
If you hadn't been here, I fear we wouldn't have survived.
Don't feel bad about it. You fought valiantly against an extremely cunning enemy.
Truth be told, we also fell for the illusion and had to be saved. In our case, it was Shimanto and Harutsuki.
Those two were the real deal. Not like that fake fox lady.
The Sakurans saved you? Why were they in Samoa?
They were also attacked by an unidentified enemy, just like we were.
Also, the enemy disguises themselves as Sakurans, so they wanted to get to us first before any misunderstandings could happen.
Worst-case scenario, the whole Pacific has fallen for this illusion... but as long as we can keep fighting, things'll be okay.
I hope so!
Oh, I've got a question!
You used some cool portal thingy to get here, right? What was that?
Hahahah! That was a torii gate made with a special talisman Shimanto gave us. They're for getting inside these illusory dimensions.
And also for removing the effect the illusion has on your mind. We didn't even need to this time, though.
Oh yeah! We didn't even use 'em.
I didn't really do anything "cool," I just copied what I saw in a movie once...
If you'll excuse me for butting in, I've finished reconning the area.
I'll cut to the chase. Most of the automated production facilities have fallen into enemy hands.
Also, as far as I can see, they're using Kiritimati as their base of operations to dispatch forces to other islands across the Pacific.
I estimate there's a 99.95% chance the fleet that attacked Samoa came from here.
Then they're running a coordinated operation here. We can't let them just walk all over us.
Dewey, you're coming with me. We'll recapture the island's command facilities and get in touch with HQ.
If anything gets in our way, we'll smash it!

sequence: Kiritimati
Command & Communications Facility
Sometime Later

scripts.say: In the end, the superior communications equipment on Kiritimati still couldn't connect them to their base at SD.
But, luckily for the girls, they received a call from a surprising person.
This is Enterprise, flagship of the Pacific Fleet.
I thought we'd completely lost Kiritimati... Thank god you're still alive and kicking.
Whoever's in command, could you brief me on the current situation?
Enterprise?!
Ahh, you're okay... That's such a relief.
Well, to make a long story short...
I see. Not even Samoa was safe from the illusion.
You handled the situation well.
We sortied as soon as we realized that Kiritimati was on the brink of falling. En route to your location as we speak.
Any idea what's happening in the Pacific? Do you know who the enemy is, or what's happened to our SD base?
I don't know a thing, sorry. I was hoping you did.
All I can tell you is that there's jamming all across the entire Pacific and that all of our bases have been affected by the illusion.
It's not limited to the Pacific, though. It's affecting our SD base, NY City, and even DC. We can't reach any of them.
While it's possible that's just due to the jamming, I think we should assume the worst case has come to be.
My god...
Did the illusion affect you, too? And you escaped it?
Yeah. I had a dream about...
Flames. Flames as far as the eye can see.
Among the inferno – a stranger, yet familiar all the same...
Come to have a chat, huh?
No... There are still things I must do. I don't have any time to waste.
Hmph. Okay.
Leave. It's time to wake up.
The woman shook her hand, enveloping everything in flames.
Just like that, the illusion was broken.
Actually, it's not important.
What matters is that the illusion isn't unbreakable. We're all awake and trying to win this battle.
There have to be others. In DC, NY... There must be other people who've awoken.
For now, we just have to do what we can and have faith in our comrades.
Agreed.
I'm transferring command to you. What's our plan now?
As we've established, contact has been lost with practically every base we have in the Pacific.
That includes the bases at PH and AF.
They have massive amounts of supplies and equipment, and plenty of personnel, too, but I've heard nothing from them.
If those two bases fall into enemy hands, the situation will get much more difficult for us.
Our top priority should be to help those we can and build up the forces necessary to recapture those two bases.
Understood.
Bunker Hill and some others are currently engaging the enemy. They came from the base on the Marshall Islands.
I suspected it was a Sakuran surprise attack on account of their looks, but I've completely eliminated that possibility thanks to the intel you just provided.
I've forwarded the intel to Bunker Hill and given her orders not to provoke any Sakuran bases.
Until we recapture PH and AF, we're stuck playing defense.
Fortunately, you bought us a lot of time by retaking Kiritimati. You might even have saved our rears.
Once we've verified that all our bases have survived, we'll focus on waking up as many people as–
Let me stop you there. I agree that waking people up is high on our to-do list...
But the enemy has a huge upper hand on us, AND we can't contact anyone. Spreading our forces too thin is way too dangerous.
I know. My plan accounts for that.
We're not going to split up. We'll just send out aircraft to awaken people.
The planes can use one of those talismans to create an entrance into the illusion, drop another one to awaken someone, then strike at the enemy when possible. How does that sound?
Yeah... that's easier said than done. It'd take inhuman precision to drop a talisman right onto someone's forehead.
I think a more effective approach would be to contact those under the illusion directly, like we did with Dewey's group.
True. That's not an easy drop to make...
Not many options, then. We'll just have to spread out as little as possible while carrying out our objectives by order of priority.
Even then, there's the risk the enemy will detect us and eliminate our isolated rescue fleets...
If all we need to do is reach out to them, my drones are more than enough for the job.
My Fargo Direct Drones can airdrop packages of talismans and can even play audio.
Our aircraft can concentrate on escorting our forces and eliminating stragglers. My drones will handle the rest.
This affords us greater operational precision while we rescue people at the same time.
Using their onboard equipment, the drones can also enhance our communications, facilitating intel exchange and letting us relay tasks and orders.
A combination of drones and aircraft working in tandem... It's worth a shot.
Alright. Our aircraft will deal with any enemies we come across.
Once you're ready, we'll set off for PH and AF.
Got it. Let's give those bastards hell!
Amid the sunset glow, a girl performed her final checks surrounded by drones.
Destination: Base at SD. Changing voice pack to NINJABELL. Setup complete.
She placed a talisman inside the drone's storage compartment, and then it took off, getting in formation with the aircraft.
Next. Destination: Base at Panama Canal. Changing voice pack to NINJABELL. Setup complete.
Next. Destination: Easter Island...
One after the next, the drones take to the skies and link up with the aircraft, their wings carrying both cargo and hope.
If this goes well, it will turn this whole thing around.

sequence:
Adventures in the Forest of Fables

<size=45>1 Into the Forest</size>

scripts.say: Good mornyan, Commander!
Akashi came into my office on my day off.
That's my question, nya. Why are you spending your day off in the office, nya?
There are so many better things you could be doing, nya. So many more fun things, nya.
Already I could tell where this was going...
Remember the escape room we made just a while ago, nya?
Me and the others have designed a new esca– I mean, a new attraction for the port, nya! And we want you to test it, nya.
It'll be free of charge just like last time since you'd be doing us a favor, nya.
Hehehe... You're just aching to try it now, aren't you, nya?
Great, nya! I knew we could count on you, nya!
I'm afraid it's now or never, nya. Everyone's already prepped and waiting for you over by the set, nya.
I've asked a Royal Maid to brief you this time. If you have any questions for her then don't be afraid to ask, nya.
Now let's get going, nya~
After arriving at the place Akashi pointed me to, I was greeted by Enterprise of the Royal Maids.
Without further ado, allow me to explain this attraction.
This is the Forest of Fables, where our tale is set. You are a lone person who has gotten lost in these woods. That's it – that's the premise.
The staff are all ready to begin, so please just make your way past the entrance.
I couldn't see anything resembling an "entrance," as Enterprise called it, only a straight path that continued into the forest.
Is something the matter? The Royal Maids set up all the greenery here, so rest assured, there are no booby traps or anything of the sort.
"Wait, am I not getting a communicator this time around?"
Correct. Staff members will join your party during this adventure, and they will essentially try to guide you down the right path.
I'm sure you don't want to listen to me talking all day long, so please head on inside and have fun, Master.
It wasn't really clear what I should expect from this attraction, but since I didn't have much other choice, I went into the forest.

sequence:
Adventures in the Forest of Fables

<size=45>2 The White Rabbit and the Cheshire Cat</size>

scripts.say: As I was walking deeper into the forest, I suddenly caught sight of a familiar face.
Comma– I mean! How strange to find a human out here!
No, no, I'm not Shimakaze! I'm the White Rabbit!
Hello, hello! My name is White Rabbit!
Forgive my forwardness, but I urgently need your help!
Jin– I mean, a vicious wolf prowls these woods at night! I simply must get back to my house before it turns dark!
The problem is, I have lost my way, as I'm sure you can tell...
So please, help me get back home! I don't want to be wolf food! I'll do anything you ask in return!
Shimakaze – or should I say, the White Rabbit – offered to accompany me deeper into the forest.
It seemed my mission for the opening act was to help her find her house.
After walking for a while, we came across a cabin amid the trees. On the other side of the door was a place lined with mirrors in all directions.
I'm afraid we'll need to go through this maze to find my home.
Unfortunately, I've completely forgotten which way leads out of it!
You must help me find the correct path, or else the two of us will be stuck here forever!
Everywhere I looked there were doors and corridors reflected in the mirrors, and there was no telling which led to the exit.
I knew we would get lost in a heartbeat if we walked around at random.
Leaving a mark on paths we've taken wouldn't work either, because we'd still lose all sense of direction after turning just a few corners.
While I stood there, trying to think up a plan, I suddenly heard the sound of rapidly approaching footsteps.
Owneeeeer! I'm right over heeeeere!
(Wait, please! Cheshire! You're supposed to stick to the script!)
Glomp! Ahem... A human and a rabbit. What an odd combination indeed!
Tell me, why do you need to traverse through this maze?
Because my house is through here! My grandma is worried about me!
This person here – who I assume wants to leave this forest for whatever reason – is helping me get there! Would you happen to know the path forward?
I see, I see. It so happens I'm in a good mood today, so tell you what – if you play with me, I will take you to the exit.
You will?! That's so kind! But I wonder – how long do you wish to play?
How long, indeed? I never specified a timeframe, did I?
Could be five years, maybe even ten if I so desire! It all depends on my mood~
If that's how it's going to be... Human, let me handle this!
You know what else you didn't specify? WHO will be playing with you! So I volunteer for the task!
Hey! But I want to play with my Owner!
(That's enough, Cheshire. Let's keep things moving along.)
Hrmmph... Worry not, I was only kidding!
Besides, it wouldn't be fun to keep the human trapped in here forever. My Owner can go, while the rabbit stays and plays.
The exit is right that way. You're free to leave.
"What, just like that? I didn't do anything, and you're letting me move forward?"
Don't sweat the details! It's better for one of us to make it out than for both of us to be trapped in here!
Oh, one more thing just before you go!
When you find my house, would you mind relaying a message to my grandma? Let her know I'm just fine so she has no reason to worry.
And that I'll be there after I've finished playing with Cheshire!
Also, please take this watch with you! I'm sure it will come in handy on the next leg of your journey!
After I received her pocket watch, she and Cheshire ran off elsewhere.
At the same time, a passage previously blocked by mirrors opened up, revealing a path to what presumably is the exit.
And so, I proceeded to the next act.

sequence:
Adventures in the Forest of Fables

<size=45>3 The Lover in the Castle</size>

scripts.say: After exiting the mirror maze, I came upon a small castle.
Up on its balcony, a figure emerged and beckoned me.
You've come, my love, my dear...
Biloxi's sentence trailed off, and she looked to me to finish it.
Now hurry inside the castle, please. We haven't much time.
Now come into the castle, quick. We don't have much time.
She dropped down a ladder from the balcony to me.
The ball today is our last chance to escape this place. Come on, be quick!
I climbed the ladder and entered the castle. Inside I saw what looked to be a banquet hall, where weapon-wielding Meowfficers were patrolling the area.
You see the guards, no? We can't let any of them spot us, or they'll all come after us.
And if we get surrounded, we're never gonna make it out.

options.content: "Can't we just... use the ladder to leave?"

scripts.say: They're a measure the head of this castle employed to prevent me from seeing you.
Afraid not. The guards will be hot on our heels as soon as they find out about it. Then it's game over for us.
To get away, we need a plan that will buy us some time.
I've heard the guards change shifts at set times of the day. We'll be home free if we can just exploit that gap in their rotation.
The problem is, I don't how long it is until their shift change, and there's nothing in this hall that tells the time.
Comman– I mean, my love, do you have any ideas?
The plan would only work if we could tell the time... That's when I remembered the pocket watch I got from the White Rabbit.

options.content: "I have just what we need right here."

scripts.say: A... pocket watch?
Perfect! That's our ticket out of here!
The guards will rotate iiin... five minutes! Follow me, my love!
Biloxi led me through a series of dark, twisting corridors. We somehow managed to avoid all the guards and eventually made it to the castle's backdoor.
We're almost there, my love! Freedom is just past this door!
Just as we were about to sprint for the exit, a figure emerged from the shadows to block us off.
Well, well. I thought you'd try to leave through the rear entrance, and lo and behold...
If I said this is as far as you'll go, what would you do?
Dammit. This is it... Of all the people to capture us, it's Algérie her-fricking-self.
Heehee. Yes, I am the queen, but you needn't fear capture at my hands.
You see, I'm willing to let you go in exchange for a favor.
Favor? What do you want?
You'll find a girl named Snow White not far from here. Take this poisoned apple and have her eat it.
Wicked queen... So you are after Snow White's life after all.
My love, we have to take this deal, or else neither of us will ever get out of here.
Take the apple and go on without me. I'll stay behind as insurance so the queen won't go back on her word.
Let us hear your answer. What do you say?

options.content: "Feed someone a poisoned apple? I don't think so."

scripts.say: A wise decision. Then take the apple and be on your way now.
What you think is unimportant. You will do it. Exercise caution, as Snow White is not so easily fooled.
Now take the apple and go.
Algérie handed me the poisoned apple.
Wait. Take my mask with you. That way I'll still be with you even if I can't follow you.
Best of luck, my love!

sequence:
Adventures in the Forest of Fables

<size=45>4 Snow White and the Poisoned Apple</size>

scripts.say: I left the castle, poisoned apple in hand, and walked through the forest once more. Arriving at an open field, I encountered Snow White.
I know your kind... You're an assassin, ordered by the queen to take my life.
Very well...
Before I could even move a muscle, she pointed a sword at my throat.
You're sorely mistaken if you think I will simply let you kill me.
Lying is a sin. A grave one, at that.
Before I could even move a muscle, she pointed a sword at my throat.
You can't deceive me. You aren't the first assassin I've come face to face with.
Be frank with me. What trick is the queen trying to pull on me this time?
I took out the poisoned apple and explained the queen's plot to Snow White-slash-Joffre.
I see. So she has turned to deception now that it's clear a frontal attack will not work. I've about had enough of this wicked woman.
Listen, I'm planning to gather reinforcements and assault the castle. However, her cohorts will doubtlessly catch on to me without a disguise.
A mask? It will hardly hide my identity, though I suppose it's better than nothing.
I must say... You're quite upstanding for an assassin.
Am I correct to assume you didn't want to assassinate me, but rather you were roped into it?
Don't you worry. Once I've dealt with the queen, you'll be relieved of your orders.
"This sure is different to the version of Snow White I remember..."
Thank you for assisting me. It's time we both went our separate ways now.
You should hold on to that apple. There are many dangers lurking in the forest, and that apple may just come in handy against them.
The absurdly battle-hardened Snow White bid me farewell, then began heading for the castle with a leisurely stride.
"Okay... How is a poisoned apple going to help me in these woods?"

sequence:
Adventures in the Forest of Fables

<size=45>5 Little Red Lying Hood</size>

scripts.say: As I kept walking past the open field the greenery became sparser and sparser until eventually I found myself in some sort of village.
"I wonder if one of these houses is where the White Rabbit lives."
There was only one way to find out. I went up to a small house with a red roof.
You've entered Little Red Riding Hood's house. Who are you? The Big Bad Wolf that's come to eat me?
Needless to say, I had not found where the White Rabbit lives.
What I did find was a bizarre sight. For some reason, Little Red Riding Hood was lying on her bed in wait for the Big Bad Wolf.
Because I'm a defenseless girl.
And I'm trying to get into my role by assuming the most vulnerable position such a girl would be in.
I know the wolf is around here somewhere.
Search the other houses and you will find it.
Yes, I'm sure of it now – you're not the wolf. You don't even have jaws big enough to eat me.
And even if you were to try, I'd simply gut you with my lance.
So, you may leave. I must get back to rehearsing my defenseless girl act.
Remember to close the door on your way out. Le Malin insisted I should rehearse in solitude.
Close the door for me, and you may take that spare red hood by the entrance for yourself.
Little Red Riding Hood sent me out of the house, though I did get a red hood as a parting gift... for whatever reason.
"I guess I'll have another look around for the White Rabbit's house."
"That wolf could mean danger, though. I'll need to be on my toes..."

sequence:
Adventures in the Forest of Fables

<size=45>6 The Wolf is Out of the Bag</size>

scripts.say: I found what looks like a wolf's footprints just outside the next house. If the wolf was anywhere, it was sure to be in there.
There was a second pair of footprints as well. Did they belong to the White Rabbit? Was she already inside?
I opened the door as quietly as I could, and that's when I heard voices coming from inside.
Hello! I'm baaack!
Why, if it isn't the White Rabbit! What took you so long?
Well, I encountered Cheshire on the way here and she demanded that I play with her...
But now I'm home at last, Jin– Err, I mean, Grandma!
Welcome back, dear. Did you get the mushrooms?
Oh! I became so distracted with trying to find my way back that I completely forgot to pick any mushrooms!
I'm terribly sorry, Grandma! Allow me to go find some right now!
Don't worry about it, dear. It's late. Rest your weary bones.
Come near so Grandma can have a better look at your face. My, you've grown again, haven't you?
For some reason, the White Rabbit and the wolf – putting on a grandmother act – were having a conversation in the house.
As much as I wanted to interject, they sounded really into it, and I didn't want to ruin the mood.
Wow, Grandma, what big ears you have.
All the better to hear you with, my child.
Huh... and you have such big eyes too.
All the better to see you and make sure you do not get into any trouble, my child.
And those great big arms?! What are they for?!
All the better to hug you with...
Gosh, this sure is a true-to-life wolf outfit you've got, Grandma!
What about your mouth? Why is it so big?
All the better... to gobble you up with, little rabbit!
Graaghh!
The wolf dropped her grandmotherly facade and got ready to pounce on the White Rabbit.
That's when I decided to...

options.content: Wait until the right time to act

scripts.say: What?! You were the Big Bad Wolf all along?! No! Please don't eat meeeee!
The White Rabbit, having finally seen through the disguise, made a mad dash toward me, with the wolf following closely behind.
A red hood...? So the Commander's playing the role of Little Red Riding Hood...
Here I thought Shimakaze's appearance was down to a mistake, but it seems everything is in order!
The wolf abruptly changed targets and made a beeline for me.
Now, Commander, let's see how you'll get out of thi– Hmph?!
This apple... it's poisoned...!
I acted quickly and took out the poisoned apple, which the wolf bit down on. She keeled over fell and flat on the floor.
Phew... Thank you for saving me, Commander!
"So I just used the apple meant for Snow White to kill the Big Bad Wolf... What a plot twist."
Owneeer! There you are!
Lookie! I found Biloxi locked up in a castle, so I rescued and led her here!
We're finally reunited, my love.
You won't believe this – Snow White arrived at the castle with an army. While they and the queen's troops were busy fighting, that's when Cheshire and I fled.
I'd lost all grasp of the story at this point, but it seemed like all the characters' problems had been resolved.
In other words, the story came to a close.
Congratulations. You've completed the Forest of Fables.
What did you think of it, Master?

options.content: "It was pretty enjoyable, all in all."
"It was the most fun I'd had in a while!"

scripts.say: I see. One could say that's more or less the response we expected.
This attraction is the product of a myriad of ideas from the production team, so it's unavoidable that some liberties would be taken with the source material.
Be that as it may, I believe that was worth it as long as you and everyone involved had fun.
But we can make it even better. Next time, we'll invite some more people and make a bunch of improvements.
When that time comes, you'll be welcome to play again, Master.

sequence:
Where the Sun Doesn't Shine

<size=45>The Unmotivated Girl</size>

scripts.say: Today is a day off. Rays of light shine through the window, dyeing the floor with a pleasant golden glow.
It's a bright, cheerful day. For everyone but me, that is.
I stare at the pile of paperwork on my desk and let out a sigh. There's so much work to get through still.
As for the reason I have all this work to catch up on... she's sitting over there in the corner.
Torricelli, my secretary. Squeezed into a corner of my office, she looks lost in thought.
Sometimes, she produces some sort of lab report and writes something down. She rarely ever talks unless spoken to first.
She reminds me of a mushroom, growing quietly out of sight.
I think I'll base this report on the office's internal layout... Hehehe...
...Hm? What is it, Commander?
She senses my gaze and slowly turns to look at me.
Work? You mean... sorting those papers?
I did that long ago. It felt like plain busy work... Hehehe... You underestimate me, don't you?
Here. Everything's in order...
I skim the folder she gave me. Not only is it neatly organized, but it also includes easily readable annotations. However...
Why didn't I give it to you earlier? Well, you never asked...
I'm not sleeping on the job... Communication isn't my forte... that's all...
Now if you don't mind, I'd like to be left to my devices...
When you think about it... Staying out of your hair counts as helping you do your paperwork, right?
It may not look like it, but I am assisting you, as a secretary should...

options.content: "Doing nothing does not count as helping."
"I've got more papers for you to process."

scripts.say: Dang it... You saw right through me...
Ugh. Talking to people is such a chore...
Look, I'll be here if you need help... Don't talk to me unless it's important, thanks...
She takes back the organized folder, then shuffles back into her dark corner...
W-wait... THIS much?
Fine... I don't wanna, but if you insist...
Suddenly I don't feel like surveying your office anymore... Oh well, I'll go back to my corner and get to work.
Don't call for me unless it's something important...
She takes back the organized folder, then shuffles back into her dark corner...

sequence:
Where the Sun Doesn't Shine

<size=45>Out of Sight, Out of Mind</size>

scripts.say: It's a new morning. The sun is already high in the sky, lighting up the road.
I woke up later than usual, since I worked overtime late into the night yesterday.
By the time I sit down in my chair, exhausted, it's already past the time I'm supposed to start working.
After a quick survey of my office, I can safely say there's nobody around.
"Phew... I've got to keep at it. There's still no shortage of work to be done."
I stack my finished documents into a small pile, unable to enjoy the achievement for even a moment due to my aching shoulders.
The clock says it's time for a break. All this time later, Torricelli is still nowhere to be seen. Where is she?
Commander... Are you almost done?
A sudden voice makes me jump. I turn around and find Torricelli, sitting quietly in the corner.
"Were you here the whole time, hiding just out of sight?"
Yeah, I've been here all morning... Hehehe... I like sitting in shady corners. They're nice and quiet...
I didn't say anything because you were focused on your work, and I didn't wanna disturb you... Hehehe...
"You're lying. It's written all over your face. You just wanted an excuse to sit around."
"I will interpret your silence as conclusive evidence."
...L-let's change topics! Need to take a break, Commander? We could chill out together...
"Together? I was under the impression you preferred being alone."
Usually, yeah... I feel like I'm being watched when I'm around people...
But not around you, for some reason... I feel at ease when I'm with you...
Plus, you're a hard worker and look after people, so yeah... Hehehe... Being around you is pretty nice...
S-so, to show you my gratitude... I will try to relieve your fatigue...
Starting with a massage... I learned it from a book. It should work...
She starts massaging me. I try to enjoy it as much as I can... And by "enjoy" I mean "wrap my head around this novel experience."
While I know she's trying her best, she doesn't quite know how much force to apply.
Umm... Does it not feel good...? In theory, this should be the perfect amount of pressure to use...
Maybe... Maybe the theory is wrong...?
"Not necessarily. You need some degree of experience to give a great massage, and that's something you can't just get from a book."
Ohh, I see... I'll incorporate your feedback into my own theory, then...
Also... There's no deep meaning behind this massage... I'm rewarding you for your hard work, that's all...
I still prefer being alone... That fact hasn't changed, just so you know... Hehehe...

sequence:
Where the Sun Doesn't Shine

<size=45>Vacation after Sunset</size>

scripts.say: Huh? Go outside? You mean... now?
I... I can't... It's too bright. I'll melt under the sun...
It's time for a break, so I raise the idea of going on a stroll with Torricelli. To my surprise, she doesn't want to.
"But why? The sun is shining, the breeze feels great. You couldn't ask for better weather."
Th-the sun is the problem...
I just... I prefer cool, dark places where people won't look...
It sounds like she won't budge on this. I decide to ask her again in the evening.
Noon has passed, and I've now finished all my work for the day.
The sun has begun to set, and before long, it'll be Torricelli's favorite time of the day – dusk.
So, I take her outside on a stroll. Despite the fact there aren't many people walking around, she trails right behind me, as though avoiding others entirely.
"What's the matter? Do you dislike crowded places?"
Not really... I just don't want to run into someone I know, because then I'd have to say hi and that stuff...
If I could choose, I'd rather be alone in my room...
Um, that's not to say I don't like going out with you. That's different. But...
...No, I think you're right. Crowded places make me anxious...
"I understand. In that case, let's go to a place where there aren't many people."
My initial plan was to take her to the amusement park, but that's a lively place, so it's likely not something she'd enjoy.
"How about..."
An aquarium is a great place to tour with someone. Besides, I'd be surprised if it's crowded at this hour.
Hmm... It's probably barren right now, so that sounds like it'll be fun...
Best of all, fish won't try to strike up a conversation with me...
She might be into stargazing. It's nearly nighttime, too.
The observatory... The idea of looking at the stars with you sounds strangely romantic... Hehehe...
Hardly anyone visits the observatory on weekdays, so nobody will get between us... Hehehe...
Although... Like I said, I'd rather be in the comfort of my own room...
...Be that as it may, she needs some fresh air. Let's see where the night takes us.

sequence:
Where the Sun Doesn't Shine

<size=45>Mushroom Banquet?</size>

scripts.say: *wheeze*... I'm so tired...
I'm already well past my recommended exercise limit... I'm gonna fall apart...
After I took her to the aquarium first, we then stargazed at the observatory.
"It really wasn't a long walk, yet you're THIS exhausted? Do you not get much exercise?"
I do research... I rarely need to go outside...
I thought as much.
"Should I ask the Sardegnian dorm managers to make an exercise program for you?"
...No thank you...
Night rolls around. After all that walking, I decide to treat her to a restaurant dinner.
Whew... Finally, some rest... I can barely think from how hungry and tired I am...
I feel alive again...
Hey... Do you mind if I order for us both?
I have a bad feeling about this... Still, I tell her to go ahead.
Hopefully, I won't have to eat any questionable food. Then again, this is a restaurant – their menu should be perfectly fine.
Let's have this... this... and this.
She selects a few curious menu items; salted mushroom skewers, creamy mushroom chowder, and mushroom cake...
It can't be a coincidence that she picked three mushroom dishes.
"You really like mushrooms, huh?"
Yeah... Hehehe... They like the dark and hate the sun, just like me. Plus, they're tasty...
They're also perfect subjects for study, since they grow in clusters and never make a sound... There's a lot to learn about them.
"Let's add one more thing to our order."
Meat is good too, but I really want you to try these mushroom dishes...
Once you've had a bite, you'll never forget the taste... Hehehe...
"That's a very ominous way to phrase it..."
Oh, you like mushrooms too? Great minds think alike... Hehehe...
"I'm not especially fond of them, I just want to keep the mushroom theme going, I suppose."
...The dishes she recommended were good. Once our slightly unusual dinner is over, we retreat home for the night.

sequence:
Where the Sun Doesn't Shine

<size=45>Showing She Cares ?</size>

scripts.say: Somewhere in the Sardegnian dorm, there's a small, ordinary-looking room. But, looks can be deceiving.
In reality, it's a secret laboratory. Inside, there is a girl tinkering with tools, working on some sort of invention.
Nice... Looking good so far!
That's when someone knocks on the door.
What's the passphrase?
Observation and testing is the root of all deductions.
Ah, Torricelli! Come on in.
The door opens for Torricelli, who bears a somewhat distressed expression.
What brings you here this late? Sudden hit of inspiration? A new idea to share?
Maybe to borrow some machinery to develop new weapons? Speaking of which, I still haven't gotten the last batch we agreed on.
Not quite...
Ahh, wait – one of my inventions broke? But that's theoretically impossible... Whatever the problem is, it has to stem from your prototype!
No, da Vinci, it's nothing like that...
Listen for a sec... Supposing you wanted to give the Commander a gift... what would it be?
...Come again?
Nooow I get it. You want to return the Commander's kindness in some way. Hmm...
(You're asking the wrong person! My forte is inventing things, not interpersonal relationships! Heck, I WISH I had the answer!)
You know, I'm really surprised you're asking about gifts.
In your case, shouldn't it be enough to say, "I'm glad I have you to look after me"?
...Ugh.
Ahem. Back on topic... I'm not sure what to tell you, other than, "Get something the Commander would love."
It doesn't have to be expensive or exotic. What people like most is receiving something they really needed.
Something... they really needed...
Yup! Sadly, I have no idea what the Commander needs...
Yup! Sadly, I have no idea what the Commander needs...
You're right...
That's it... Now I know what to get. Hehehe... Thanks, da Vinci.
You're welcome!
(Phew! I didn't lose face, even if all I did was tell her the obvious...)
(Still, it's good that I did! If I hadn't, who knows what dangerous stuff she might've given the Commander!)
(Hope it goes well, Commander.)

sequence:
Where the Sun Doesn't Shine

<size=45>A Pleasant Surprise</size>

scripts.say: A few days later...
As Torricelli has begun adapting to her responsibilities as my secretary, my workload has gotten lighter.
She is so proficient at sifting through data and sorting documents, she could it in her sleep.
"I know we're not always on the same wavelength, but the work you do is more than satisfactory."
Hehehe... I like the acknowledgement... More, please...
She tilts her head slightly downward, presenting it to me. She must want me to do something.
Mmh... Keep doing that... Hehehe...
Her cheeks seem to turn red, which I don't think I've ever seen from her before.
M-my hair is messy as is... Don't make it worse...
"If you'd always worked this well, I could've enjoyed some time off not long ago."
Th-that's in the past now... Let bygones be bygones...
Ahem... Let's change topics. Have a look at this, Commander!
She produces a big box encased in wrapping paper.
A gift, from Torricelli? I wasn't expecting that.
There's a carefully-crafted machine inside. It looks like it's made to sort paperwork.
It's a present... I-I figured you wanted something to help with your work...
I asked Da Vinci to design it. It automatically organizes documents according to their tags...
It's sure to make that part of your job quicker... and give you more time to spend with me... Hehehe...
"That's actually quite useful. Maybe a bit TOO useful. Won't this machine effectively do your job for you?"
Exactly, which means I don't need to work... I can just relax all day and sit in my cozy corner...
"It also means my workload will never get any lighter than it is now..."
"Still, it's a kind gesture. Thank you for the gift."
Hehehe...

sequence:
Where the Sun Doesn't Shine

<size=45>True Warmth Comes from Within</size>

scripts.say: Commander, is your work nearly done? Hehehe... Then come relax with me...
I've also come up with a plan to retrofit your desk... It'll give it all sorts of added functionality...
I've been working with Torricelli for quite a while now. Not only have we grown closer, but our spare time together has become more enjoyable as well.
My first impression of her as a taciturn, gloomy girl was wrong. She's very friendly once you get to know her.
How about we go out earlier than usual today? I've had plenty of rest, so I think I can go for a longer walk... Probably...
"You sure? There's a long while to go until sunset."
I know... I meant AFTER sundown, but we can discuss where we'll go before then, right...?
There's no way I'm going out in broad daylight... I'd melt in minutes...
"I think you have more in common with a snowman than a mushroom."
It's not just about sunlight... I don't like places where people can see me, either...
That's why I like dark, damp, isolated places... Just like mushrooms do...
Oh, and I can think more clearly when I'm by myself...
I guess one way to put it is... "Geniuses are born lonely," or something...
"On the other hand, you sort of cling to me like a wet towel."
Hehehe... You're different... You make me feel at ease...
You don't make me feel nervous, like others do...
The more I see of your caring, hardworking side... the more I want to stay with you forever...
I think... I've caught the Commander dependency virus...
"Sounds like it. I don't mind, though. I'm happy to be relied upon."
A-anyway... I want to thank you... for always being so nice to me...
And if you'll let me... I'll gladly keep relying on you to look after me...
Hehehe... That restaurant we ate at was incredible... Can we go again today? I want to try more mushroom dishes...

options.content: "You're on. Let's see who can eat the most."

scripts.say: Hehehe... As time goes on, we become more like each other...
Awwww... Then I'll have to keep trying. One day, we'll be like two peas in a pod...

sequence:
Days of Tranquility

<size=45>1.Sound of the Waves</size>

scripts.say: A warm breeze – notably warmer than normal – greeted me when I stepped outside.
It was a wonderful day. The sun was out, the skies were clear. I decided to make the most of it and go for a walk to the pier.
Upon arriving there, I found U-47. She sat there, feet hanging off the pier and dipping into the water, just enjoying the solitude.
That's when she noticed I was there. She turned around to face me.
"What are you doing out here all by yourself?"
Not much... Just listening to the waves.
I sharpened my ears and listened in. The sound of the waves washing onto the shore gave me a sense of peace and quiet.
For a moment, I forgot all about the stress of my job. I sat down next to U-47 and appreciated the calming sound.
After a while of silently gazing out at the sea, U-47 turned and looked at me with a puzzled look.
You're an odd one, Commander. But in a good way.
You're the first person to hang out with me and keep quiet. Most people I know just make a racket.
I've gotta go now, though. Submarine meeting thing around this hour. See you later.
She bluntly announced her departure, then got up to leave.
Just wondering...
Right as she started walking, she suddenly stopped in place and began to pose me a question.
Is it quiet in your office?
"Quiet? It's pretty far from the dorms, so I suppose so...?"
I see... Good to know.
She gave a concise response, then resumed her walking and left the pier.
She seemed uninterested in me from start to finish, but I didn't get the impression that she disliked me.
And then, it was just me. I stuck around for a while longer, simply taking in the sound of the waves.

sequence:
Days of Tranquility

<size=45>2.The Quiet Visitor</size>

scripts.say: I was doing work in the office, when suddenly someone came knocking on my door.
I wasn't expecting a visitor at this hour, but I decided to let them in. I was surprised when I saw who it was.
Huh. Interesting place you've got here.
U-47 entered and had a look around. I asked if she had any business with me.
Nope, I'm here just because. I can leave if you're in the middle of something right now.
"It's fine, I'm not doing anything particularly important. You can stay as long as you want."
Oh, thanks. Then I'll just have a seat and read some books.
It had been a while since U-47 and I said anything. I focused on my work and kind of forgot she was there, which I hoped she didn't take offense to.
She was just sitting on the couch by the door, not making a single peep. Feeling curious, I walked over to check on her.
Zzz... Zzzzz....
An open book lied in her lap. Her snores were so quiet that I could only hear them up-close.
I picked up the book and looked at the cover. It was on a complicated topic a bit above her comprehension level.
It made sense to conclude she'd gotten drowzy while trying to digest it. I retrieved a blanket and tucked her in.
For a moment, I thought I'd woken her up. Fortunately, that was just her turning her sleep a little.
As I got back to work, I made a mental note to leave out a perhaps more accessible book.

sequence:
Days of Tranquility

<size=45>3.Milky Goodness</size>

scripts.say: This is for you, Commander.
U-47 came by the very next day after her first visit to my office. She brought with her a small carton of milk.
The packaging sported a depiction of a brawny cow, an allusion to the widespread belief that milk promotes bone growth.
A small thank-you for the blanket yesterday.
"Ah, you're welcome. By the way, do you have a straw? There's none on the carton."
Oh, darn. Must've dropped it at some point... But it's still good, whichever way you drink it.
She shrugged, then started scouring the bookshelf for something to read, like yesterday. Meanwhile, I got a glass and poured the milk into it.
I took a sip, and immediately I could tell this was not your run-of-the-mill milk. Its taste was extraordinary. I commented on this to U-47.
Mhm. It's my favorite. Imported, too. I wouldn't share it with just anyone.
Also, got anything you need help with? I wanna make myself useful this time around.
"There's nothing I desperately need your help with, but I appreciate the offer. For future reference though, what do you excel at?"
Stealthy stuff.
"I see... I'll let you know if any missions like that crop up."
'Kay. Please do.
She was content to leave it at that, and then pulled out a paperback from the bookshelf.
I took a brief glance at the cover to see what she picked.
It was titled, 'Catalogue of Navy-issue Postage Stamps.'
Pretty sure this wasn't here yesterday... Could be cool.
Just like yesterday, she sat down on the couch and began reading in silence.
I had put out the new book more or less at random, and was surprised to see she had taken an interest in it.
I've said it before, but... you really are an odd one, Commander.
I don't help around the office, but you still left this book here just for me. You're really quiet, too.
Don't get me wrong, I don't want you to start running your mouth. I like peace and quiet, so I'm fine with that.

options.content: "You don't need to exchange words to enjoy each other's company."

scripts.say: Mhm.
She briefly echoed my sentiment, then focused her attention back to the book.
Not much of note happened after that, and yet, a comfy mood enveloped the quiet office for the duration of her stay.

sequence:
Days of Tranquility

<size=45>4.The Loudmouthed Visitor</size>
