scripts.say: The maritime outpost at the forefront of Operation Siren, a major counter-offensive to eliminate Siren activity in the NA Ocean, has been quiet lately.
Ten days have passed, but the next phase of the large-scale assault has not started yet.
The only things on the calendar are meetings, meetings, and more meetings.
Though the Eagle Union's fleet is assembled and stands ready, the green light has not been given to continue the large-scale assault, and the operation's progress has slowed down considerably.
As anyone who has studied the art of war knows... it is rarely a good idea to lose the initiative when on the attack.
Eagle Union Outpost - 10 days earlier
(Alarms blaring)
I was looking over some reports in the office when the sound of sirens blaring ripped through the air.
Sorry for bothering you this late, Commander. Are you still working?
I was fine-tuning the details for the upcoming large-scale assault. As the commander, it is my responsibility to see the operation through to completion.
Earlier, there was a report that an anomalous phenomenon was seen from the maelstrom in the middle of the NA Ocean.
Here's the intel that our recon team put together for us. I thought you should look over it as soon as possible.
"...A large cluster of Siren facilities has been seen around the maelstrom. The facilities may directly be linked to the weather abnormalities..."
I initially also tried to send some recons out to survey the situation, but my planes were shot down before they could gather any information.
The fact that the Sirens have erected an entire complex of facilities while also not revealing their main forces is a reason for concern.
The extent of the activity we're seeing goes beyond what we predicted.
"Were they poised to attack you?"
Not yet. Just to be safe though, I raised the threat level and gathered the main fleet.
"I have to meet with the Naval HQ about this. We must make preparations to face the Siren stronghold."
Of course. By the way, there was also another emergency message from the Naval HQ. I originally was coming to let you know about it.
It may be about the same thing we're talking about, but I'm getting the hunch that there might be a lot more to it.
We'll find out. Regardless, the Naval HQ should be taking any measures necessary to combat this anomaly.
"While I'm busy, you're in charge of defending the base, as well as collecting any information you can."
Understood. I'll take command of the fleets patrolling the base. I'll make sure you're able to complete your work without being disturbed.
I sighed to myself, knowing that everything I had been working on was just about to go out the window.
I knew there would be a drawn-out debate among the higher-ups at Naval HQ, but I didn't think it'd end like this...

Two approaches have been hotly debated: the first, launching a focused assault to break through the Sirens' defensive line, and the second, slowly whittling their forces down until we have them surrounded.
What's more, some are requesting our capital ships be withdrawn and reassigned to do Siren research missions instead.
Either way, we have too little intel to determine our best course of action... Hopefully, tomorrow, we will.
I see Memphis and Sheffield are here.
From what I've heard, Sheffield is joining us per secret orders from Queen Elizabeth herself.
They're in the middle of a conversation. Let's not disturb them.
Oh, Commander? There you are.
Well, she saw me. I might as well talk to them and hear what's up.
I leave the matter in your hands. Now if you'll excuse me...
...Ah. It's good to see you, Master. I hope you've been well.
Please try not to lose any sleep over Naval HQ's indecisiveness. For now, I suggest clearing your mind and getting some rest. I must go now. Farewell.
Sheffield bowed to me, then left quite abruptly after offering her... advice.
Working hard as always, Commander? Or just enjoying a casual stroll?
"Let's say a bit of both. What were you two talking about just earlier?"
She was asking me for a favor, essentially. She wanted me to investigate something.
While I don't exactly have to keep it secret from you, I'd rather wait until I have all the facts before telling you about it.
"Does it have something to do with Naval HQ?"
Maybe. We'll see. Anyway, let's talk about the operation.
It's strange how the Siren stronghold appearing made Naval HQ do a strategic 180. Don't you think so too?
"It is strange. We need to settle on a course of action as soon as possible, but instead, they're thinking about changing the plan entirely at this stage."
Mhm. They make some... unusual decisions from time to time, but this is on a whole other level.
The operation was going swimmingly, too. We've been winning battle after battle against the Sirens, and even the Ashes.
What's more, it'd be a huge morale boost for everyone if we manage to drive the Sirens out of the NA Ocean. So why stop now?
"The Ashes add an element of uncertainty, but they aren't as immediately threatening as the Sirens are. I'd wager Naval HQ thinks they're a low-priority target."
There's a world of difference between our estimates of their strength and their actual capabilities, too.
Considering Naval HQ aren't the ones fighting on the frontlines, our series of victories must seem inconsequential to them.
And because they're in that mindset, they seem to suddenly think the best option would be to refocus our efforts towards research instead.
It's like the first half of the operation went TOO well, causing Naval HQ's priorities to drastically shift from one extreme to the other.
"I doubt anybody saw this sudden reversal coming."
And I doubt anybody's happy with it either. We still have to investigate the stronghold and all, but...
We shipgirls just want nothing more than to take back the seas from the Sirens.
Naval HQ knows that, and yet here we are.
Ultimately, humanity and shipgirls have the same goal in mind, and it's a simple difference in opinion that's dividing us now...
"Sheffield told me to put the whole thing aside for now. Do you think Elizabeth knows about the situation and plans to use her influence to sway Naval HQ?"
Well, as a matter of fact...
You are entirely correct.
Her Majesty has been informed of your conundrum and is taking an active part in the operation.
And indeed, she is going to work together with other faction leaders to attempt to persuade Naval HQ.
Gosh, don't sneak up on us like that... Didn't you say you were leaving?
Yes, though I still have matters to tend to, so I will be in the area.
I swear, sometimes you act like you're part of the secret service or something...
Please. I am a maid, not a spy.
"Speaking of Elizabeth, I haven't seen her recently. Is she well?"
Her Majesty has been preoccupied with other business as of late, but yes, she is doing quite well. I shall ask her to contact you at a later point.
As I am but a simple maid, I know not what Her Majesty plans to do. But, if you'll allow me to conjecture...
I believe she will arrange an alliance with all the other fleet leaders to put pressure on Naval HQ. Perhaps that will suffice to make them reconsider their decision.
Of course, if such a plan were to come to light, it would considerably impact the Royal Navy's image.
"True. Let's hope that doesn't happen."
Indeed. To that end, I ask you to cooperate with us and play along, Master.
Eagle Union Outpost - The following day
Siren attacks have been getting more frequent with each passing day ever since they established their Core Sector stronghold.
I don't know the purpose behind these attacks. Maybe they're trying to nip our planned offense in the bud, or they're simply gauging our strength.
Whatever the case, our supply lines will be stretched too thin if we don't take the fight to them soon. Then we'll be the ones at a disadvantage.
That's why, today, I'm going to take a stand and try to persuade Naval HQ.
*knock knock*
"Come in."
Hey, Commander. Hope I'm not disturbing you.
"Hey there, Enterprise. What is it?"
Just here to inform you that I've created a fleet to prod the Sirens and gain intel on the size of their force in the Core Sector.
"Well done. Intel on the Sirens is precisely what we'll need to convince Naval HQ."
Yeah. We'll also need to know where they're positioned before we can go on the offensive. Two birds with one stone.
I'll be able to draft an updated mission plan based on the intel as well. Even if the Sirens are more numerous than we expect, I can always request backup or arrange for an evacuation.
All there is to do now is pray Elizabeth is successful on her end.
"I hope so. I heard her discussion about cooperation with the Crimson Axis is dragging on."
...I wonder if Naval HQ will actually let us go on the offensive, even supposing we gain a good picture of the Sirens' strength.
"I'll do everything I can to try to coax them, but I can't make any promises, considering how stubborn they can be."
We're going to lose our advantage at this rate. I think we should try our luck with a daring decision, rather than being caught up in endless hours of debates.
Besides, all things concerning shipgirls at the frontlines fall under your jurisdiction. You are the Commander here, after all.
"You're right... I don't need anyone's approval for this. Let's save the world first, and beg for forgiveness later–– Have the fleet prepare to sortie."
I knew we could count on you. All right, I'll see you down at the port.
It seems the solution to our stalemate was staring me in the face all along...
NA Ocean - Core Sector
It feels like someone has been watching me ever since we set off...
*staaaaaare*
Whuah! Wh-what is it, Commander?
Oh geesh, you noticed I'm feeling nervous, huh...
It'd be hard NOT to notice when someone is staring at you nonstop.
Yeah. You could've stared a hole through the glass with that intense gaze.
Th-that bad? Sorry 'bout that...
It's just... I'm insanely fired up to finally get to fight side-by-side with the Commander! I've been waiting for this day for ages!
It's great she's so enthusiastic, but I'm not sure how to respond to that...

options.content: "I've been waiting for a long time for this too."

scripts.say: Yeah, and why wouldn't I be? You want to save the world, just like a superhero would!
And if you're a superhero, that makes me your sidekick, sort of! Hehehe~
Heck yeah! Together, we'll beat those Sirens and save the world!
You'll be the superhero the world needs, and I'll be your trusty sidekick! Hehehe~
Seriously?! Oh my god, this is the best day of my life!
I'm so happy to hear that, because you're like a superhero in my eyes, Commander! I'm gonna support you 110% in this upcoming battle!
And... if you're a superhero... then that makes me your sidekick, sort of! Hehehe~
Analysis program synchronization complete. We will soon enter the mission zone.
It's getting easier to see through the clouds as we come closer. Looking at it now up-close, it's frightening just how huge this storm is.
Yeah. The storm we observed in the Bermuda Triangle doesn't even hold a candle to this one.
The color and scale being different is one thing, it's the intensity that puts it on another level. Makes me wonder... what if it's a Singularity?
Doubtful. It doesn't really FEEL like the other Singularities we've encountered...
But on the other hand, we know very little about Singularities. If this is one, that could explain why the Ashes keep showing up in these waters.
At any rate, we have to eliminate all the Sirens in the area, and then–
Shoot, they're coming for us! Everyone, get ready to fight!
Detecting approaching Sirens. Preparing for combat is recommended.
(She sensed they were coming even before TB did! That's the kind of intuition that takes a thousand battles to develop!)
There's a good chance they're controlled from a remote command center, judging by how quickly they reacted to us.
"Remember, we're only here to gauge the size of their forces. Don't overextend, and avoid combat if possible."
You heard the Commander. I'll adjust our course to keep us some distance from the eye of the storm. Only engage the Sirens if you need to!
Message incoming from the forward base.
Commander, we've picked up readings that suggest there are Ashes in your area. Keep your eyes peeled and be on your guard.
"Another party throwing their hats into the ring, huh..."
"While I have you on the line... Have you heard anything from Naval HQ yet?"
Nope, not a word so far. I'd take their silence to mean tacit permission to keep doing what you're doing.
Orders received. Downloading Ashes coordinates.
Analysis complete. Based on the signal characteristics, the Ashes member appears to be Hiryuu META. Displaying location on the screen.
Thank god we've managed to decrypt their signals and can actually fight back against them.
Agreed, though it's a shame we can't pinpoint their exact location yet. It doesn't help the bulky decryption machine is extremely tough to transport.
Maybe those scientists back at base can make it smaller somehow...
Yeah. If they could shrink it to fit inside your pocket, we could catch the Ashes out in the open and force them to confront us.
Wait. Something is off here... The only time Ashes emit signals is when they're in combat in a general area.
In other words, if they're trying to stay hidden, they'd want to avoid combat as much as they can.
So then why would she start a fight and reveal her location, especially so close to us? It doesn't make sense...
Seems like she's challenging us to a duel.
Alternatively, she doesn't even know we're here. Whatever the case, how do we proceed?
She's broadcasting her location to us. Even if we ignore her now, there's a good chance she'll just be back later.
I say we accept her invitation and find out what she's after while we still know where she is.
"I agree with Enterprise, but let me also repeat what I said earlier: avoid combat if at all possible. Strive to exchange only words with her, not shells."
"But, just to be sure... TB, send a request for aerial support. Have planes circling in the sky above, ready to attack at a moment's notice."
Orders received. Sending the message to forward base.
"All right. We'll set off once everyone's ready."
There are Siren wrecks everywhere... This must be a whole fleet's worth.
That saves us the trouble of having to do it, I guess?
...You found me. That proves you're able to track me somehow.
So you were saying "come find me" after all. Now, why are you here?
Why are YOU here? I'm sick and tired of being stalked all the time.
It's not too late to surrender, you know. We can work it on amicable terms.
Hah! Surrender to a band of fools allied with Antiochus? Not a chance in hell.
Allied with Antiochus...?
Have you ever even stopped to think about how they developed that coordinate tracker?
Same with that thing you call "TB." Do you have any idea where that technology comes from?
What are you getting at? TB was created by Azur Lane scientists under instructions from Naval HQ.
The same goes for the coordinate tracker. It's a product of human ingenuity, and we have people who've verified that.
Sure, their development could have involved reverse-engineering other technologies, but that doesn't change the fact.
"Reverse-engineering" you call it...
It's rich that you say you've "verified it." Have you seen the things you've supposedly "reverse-engineered?"
I... Not personally, no.
Didn't think so. Then there's no point confusing you further with an explanation. All I'll say is this– I'm tired of being followed around.
Enough talk. Let's finish it here, once and for all.
You want us to fight you? No holds barred?
You heard me right. You, the products of "your world's" ingenuity, and me.
Come at me all at once if you so wish. You already know you don't stand a shadow of a chance against me one-on-one.
Commander... Your orders?
We came here to talk, not to fight.
Moreover, we are guaranteed to suffer casualties if we engage her in all-out combat with such a small fleet...
"There's no need for this to get ugly. We just want to know what you've come here to do."
Rather than let your emotions sway you, you made the sound decision not to fight... You are a wise tactician.
What wasn't wise, however, was trying to initiate conversation with someone from the Ashes in the first place.
It could've cost all of you your lives, had it been Takao you pursued. Consider yourselves fortunate that you found me instead.
Having that said, I did come here looking for a fight, and I don't plan on leaving without one.
I won't kill you, but I will make it so you need to be towed back home. You won't be pursuing me any further.
Oh, and if you're still standing by the end of it all, then I'll tell you something you're going to like. Purely out of respect for your dedication.
Or you could still refuse to fight, and I'll send you to a watery grave.
It sounds like she's telling us to prove ourselves worthy. The stick and carrot, except the stick is death and the carrot is a vicious beating.
She's set on fighting us, that much is certain. Words won't get us out of this, only a show of our strength will.
While our fleet is geared for gathering intel, not for fighting the Ashes, we still do have the support I requested from TB.
Well? What's it going to be, Commander?
"TB, call in the airstrike support immediately. Everyone else, focus on surviving Hiryuu's assault!"
Airstrike support? So you did come prepared. Heh, now this will be interesting!
Ah, you remind me of somebody I knew once... Now I understand why Enterprise is so fond of you.
Come! Show me what you're worth!
She's staying just barely out of range of our cannons... While she's not charging at us, she's not letting up her assault either.
Didn't she say she wanted to finish this? It feels like she's still only testing us.
Wait... Is she trying to drive us off course with her attacks...? Commander, we're slowly drifting towards the center of the NA Ocean!
Hey, you're right! What in the world is she thinking?!
Doesn't she know the Sirens are gonna attack her too if she gets too close?!
Is she planning to use the Sirens to get us off her tail? But then why did she reveal her location to us in the first place?
KABOOOOM!
Out of nowhere, a loud thundering crash rang out in the distance.
What?! She's provoking the Sirens with her planes?!
The Sirens' retaliation came immediately. Hundreds upon hundreds of defense turrets emerged from the storm and opened fire on Hiryuu META.
That entire island... is one giant Siren facility?!
This is the heart of the Sirens' territory... It makes sense they have defense to match that.
Now we have an idea of what we're up against. We can't defeat them here if we don't attack with everything we've got.
This proves my hunch. The Sirens excel at using abnormal weather to their advantage.
We would've never found their defenses on our own... I mean, who'd intentionally steer a fleet into a storm in search of Sirens?
They not only defied human common sense, they even made the storm a part of their defenses.
Seems I was right. You came out here to perform recon on the Sirens...
In that case, think of this as my parting gift. Hope it's satisfied you.
...I mean, we did wanna find out the size of their force, but this is NOT what we were hoping for!
(Hm. The sweetness of an old memory relived is waning already...)
(Curses... I thought I had rid myself of those wretched things long ago...)
Commander, what do we do? We can't fight possibly fight the Sirens and Hiryuu at the same time!
You won't have to, because I'm content to leave it here for today. Farewell.
First you challenge us to a fight out of nowhere, then you decide to flee in the middle of it?
Don't get cocky with me. I'm one of the Ashes, not some damn circus clown here to amuse you.
Hiryuu's planes stopped firing at us... Are we really letting her go, just like that?
We have no other choice, Birmingham. We don't know the full extent of what Hiryuu is capable of, but we did learn a little more about her today.
And besides, like Reno said, we can't possibly fight her and the Sirens at the same time.
Speaking of the Sirens, they're coming straight for us!
"And a lot of them, too. I think we've probed enough for one day."
I agree. We have a pretty good idea of the extent of their presence in the area now.
If we inform Naval HQ about this, they'll take this operation a lot more seriously.
I'm confident they'll make the correct decision once they realize the entire operation is at risk if we don't strike with all the power we can muster.
"Exactly. But before we launch an all-out offensive, we should pay a visit to the Royal Navy's forward base."
Hey Commander, Long Island here, in charge of communications for the day. I've got some orders from Naval HQ for you~
Oh, have you already arrived at the Royal Navy's outpost?
Hehehe, what's the Royal Navy's outpost like?
"It's laid out pretty much the same as any other Azur Lane outpost, but I've been told the interior differs a lot... I've heard it's just as you'd expect from the Royal Navy."
I'd wager they decorated it to look like the boss room of a dungeon. A ghost like me would know~
"I'll find out soon enough. More importantly, what about those orders you were talking about?"
Right, we're in the middle of an operation... I uh, totally forgot this channel was strictly for business...
Anyway, I've got some pretty juicy news for you. Naval HQ took a good hard look at the report you sent, and has approved your plans for a general offensive!
"Now we can finally make our move... Some juicy news indeed."
"So, about our schedule for the offensive..."
Just as you were thinking, the Eagle Union is performing some more reconnaissance and will promptly be at action stations!

Thanks to you already having scouted out their general strength, I was able to take a good look at the status of the Sirens' seas and found a better way to monitor them. You can leave things to me until the operation begins!
Until then, you can just take it easy in the Royal Navy's outpost. Enjoy your time off until all hell breaks loose~
Since we were able to determine that the Sirens' forces were stronger than we thought, it would be wise to secure more information via reconnaissance so we can make any changes we need to our plans.
"By the way, if you're in charge of communications... does that mean there are other logistics-oriented girls stationed here too?"
Hehehe, bingo~ You'll be having a touching reunion with Helena and Memphis soon~!
Signing off, Commander. Have a good one~
Phew... That was nerve-wracking...! Oh crap, the comms are still on!
That didn't quite make sense, but... Whatever, let's just get some rest while we can.
*knock knock*
Please pardon my intrusion. It's good to see you again, Master.
Her Majesty's tea party is fast approaching, so if you would please follow me.
Oh right, Elizabeth invited me to a tea party earlier.
We had hoped to invite you to our castle on the Royal Islands, but... as the situation stands, we had to make do the best we could.

This outpost may be quite modest by comparison, but I assure you the experience will be as if the tea party were being held on the Royal Islands. Her Majesty is personally overlooking the preparations.
"...That eye for details is certainly just like her."
Thank you for your understanding. Her Majesty has been looking forward to meeting with you, Master.
Royal Navy Outpost - Banquet Hall
So this is the... tea party. Feels more like a banquet, honestly.
Not only are there high-quality teas and decadent pastries, but all of the furniture from the Royal Castle's banquet hall is here...
Elizabeth is abusing her position again! Look at all of the unnecessary stuff she had shipped over!
Baseless accusations! I did no such thing!
I paid for all of these furnishings straight from my pocket—Ahem, the royal family's budget! And I must say, your evident jealousy has already made it quite worth it.
Hmph! You're taking advantage of the fact that I'm holding back!
Miss Saratoga, please have some tea to help you relax. Everyone, please help yourselves to the refreshments.
Indeed. You are all free to savour all we can offer!
Well, whether it's a tea party or banquet, as long as it helps boost our morale~♪
I really won't hold back, you know! ...Edinburgh! Get me one apricot cookie, one of each sandwich, and one black tea for the Commander!
Oh, sure! Just one moment, please!
It looks like Saratoga ordered a black tea for me... Well, I suppose why not.
It's pretty good... Aren't you going to try anything, Enterprise? Come on, loosen up! The Royal Navy's snacks are delicious.
Miss Enterprise, may I interest you in a fluffy cranberry scone?
Thank you. Let's see...
The tea party surpassed everyone's expectations. Later, just as it was drawing to a close...
"I've heard Memphis and Saratoga are here to support the operation. They'll be a great help."
Some reinforcements arrived on our side, so we came here to help you guys out~♪
"As we had planned, we'll be joining forces with the Royal Navy, and the offensive will start once reinforcements have arrived."
Geez, Commander! You always go straight into work mode! I was planning on explaining everything to you after the tea party ended...
Previously, you had sent someone proficient in communications to the Royal Outpost to ensure the plan would go smoothly, right?
Naval HQ ended up sending more personnel and supplies than we expected, so we decided to spread our forces out to cover more ground.
"Well, I had given some orders regarding that, but there was no way to know who would be coming over here..."
Not a problem. We won't refuse any able-bodied additions to our ranks!
That's not to imply the operation won't proceed flawlessly with me at the helm, but even one such as I may occasionally need to watch from the sideline.
Sheffy told me everything. Thanks to your efforts, Naval HQ has finally gotten off of their arses.
We must ensure that this offensive is a success. Do not let me down!
"You deserve credit too, you know. Naval HQ definitely wouldn't have responded so quickly if it wasn't for you."
Hoho! Continue to show your gratitude!
With that taken care of, we'll be leaving the rest in our capable Commander's hands. Please behave and go back to your castle, Miss Elizabeth~
Hogwash! I'm already here, am I not? I shall accompany you to the heart of the NA Ocean.
Huh? You're going to head into the center of the NA Ocean... personally?
That is the plan.
That is the only way I can figure out what's happening. I-it's certainly not because I'm worried about my servant here!
Hm~ But Elizabeth, there's no need for you to fight on the front lines, is there...
Just stay where it's safe, and leave the fighting to the Royal Maids. This mission is especially dangerous, and we don't wanna risk you or the Commander getting hurt.
...We understand that, but...
It's fine, Warspite. I know how you feel, but we need not explain ourselves to this close-minded commoner.
And now you're pulling the queen card on me?
This is not up for debate! It would besmirch my reputation to send my servant into danger without incurring any risk myself!
What are you—! Gosh, I'm just trying to show some concern for you!
Save it for someone who needs it!
Well... It seems Her Majesty will be coming along with us.
After the tea party, I was heading for the break room when I ran into Sheffield.
Oh... What a pleasure it is to see you again, Master.
"I couldn't find you at the tea party, but I guess you're here as well."
It's the duty of the Maid Corps to keep this place clean and tidy.
By the way, I have a message for you from Her Majesty.
"You should think about what the existence of the Ashes means for us."
I believe that Her Majesty may have wanted you to mull over this during your mission.
Thank you for your time. Please enjoy your evening.
NA Ocean - Core Sector
The fleet has finished assembling at the designated area. Mission will start in about 10 minutes.
Finally we're moving out again.
Our reconnaissance has confirmed the presence of a tremendous Siren force and a massive stronghold in the center of the NA Ocean.

This operation is massive in scope. Unlike usual, we won't be taking quick skirmishes to knock out their command network. Instead, we'll be pushing our entire forces through for a direct confrontation.
Yep. Considering the size of our respective forces, Naval HQ decided the best strategy was an all-out attack from all directions.
It's very straightforward. All you have to do is steadily clear all the obstacles in your path and eliminate every last Siren you see.
We'll have every fleet from every outpost in the area, all fighting with the same goal in mind. Simple and straightforward, just the kind of strategy I can get behind.
It's not so simple for the girl who has to coordinate the efforts of so many people at once. Anyway...
Our fleet is the biggest one sortieing today, and we'll have the Commander at the helm. I suppose that makes it something of a superfleet.
Especially with Queen Elizabeth herself joining us too~
But, even with the huge fleet we've assembled, we'll still have to break through one defensive barrier at a time to reach the center of the NA Ocean.
Though we have a rough idea of what we're up against, the fact remains that our intel on the whole is limited.
Yup! To summarize, it's not a race, it's a multi-lane Siren-busting marathon to the center!
Bzzzzt––––––––
This is battlecruiser Hood of the Royal Navy fleet. I've been asked to deliver a speech on behalf of the Commander.
Long ago, the Sirens appeared and ushered in an age of terror. Humanity could do nothing but watch as they seized our seas with ruthless aggression.
They were unrelenting and merciless, but despite their best efforts, we refused to yield. Even when we lost battle after battle, we never lost hope of winning the war.
When they would push us to the brink, we would muster all our strength and courage to push them right back. Our resolve was tested, but it never once faltered.
We, as proud members of the Azur Lane, have fought tirelessly to reclaim the seas – to reclaim our freedom and peace. Our battle is far from over yet, but luck is on our side today.
The Sirens in the NA Ocean are in disarray. They are concentrated at the ocean's centre, where a great storm defends what remains of their fleet.
To them, this is their last stand. To us, this is a decisive victory just within reach.
They shall find no stay of execution from us this day. We are the ones who shall turn the cogs of destiny!
Shipgirls, once more, muster your strength and courage with me, and we shall defeat the Sirens!
Let us take back what is rightfully ours, and seize true glory with our own hands!
Commander, kindly give us the order to start!
The operation is scheduled to begin now. All fleets are ready to sortie.
Warning: Large Siren defense structure detected ahead. Readings suggest it is a stronghold cannon.
A cannon of that ridiculous size?! Not even a battleship could endure a direct hit from that!
"We have to destroy it before it destroys us. The question is how..."
Simple – fight fire with fire. We need only blast it to bits with our own firepower!
Ready, George?
Yes, Your Highness. We are loaded and ready to fire.
Commander, let us battleships take care of that cannon.
No matter how sturdy the Sirens fancy their defences, our precise volleys shall render them into naught but dust.
Target acquired. King George V's, blow it to kingdom come!
Take aim! FIRE!
Analysis complete. The route through the area ahead is obstructed by a Siren blockade.
It would take too long to break through or find a way around... Our best option is to destroy what's powering it.
"I couldn't agree any more. TB, you know what to do."
Orders issued. All able fleets are to search for the blockade's power source.
A communications request has been received from an allied fleet. Connecting...
Hehe! Need a hand with anything, Commander?
Tem! Err... Le Téméraire! Mind your tone!
Pardon her. This is L'Opiniâtre, Iris Libre magi– Excuse me, I mean Iris Libre destroyer.
Uhh, please pretend you didn't hear that.
Psst. You nearly slipped up bigtime there, Opie.
Shh, I know, Tem, just be quiet...
As I was going to say: I'm honored to be taking part in this operation. Additionally, I have something to report.
Hehe! See, Opie? I told you so!
We're both so excited to be fighting together with you! Oh right, we've got something to report, too.
We just found what appears to be a Siren power source.
All we've got to do is smash it, and that'll get rid of the blockade, right?
"Based on previous experience up to this point, yes."
Gotcha! The Iris Libre fleet is on the case!
Commander, we have successfully eliminated all Sirens in the area.
Their aircraft proved a tad troublesome to bring down, but they never stood a chance against our combined air force.
Mhm. Once you take out the carriers, their planes lose most of their bite.
Well, we're moving on to the next area then. Good luck over there, or whatever.
Wow! It's amazing what we can do when we really go all-out like this!
It really is. They cleared the entire area, and our fleet didn't even have to fire a single shot.
Hell yeah. Feels like nothing can stop us now.
"Was that Eagle and Perseus just now? I thought they were deployed in the north?"
Surprised? Heheh! I made some arrangements to get them redeployed!
Her Majesty managed to strike an agreement with the Northern Parliament and involve them in the operation as well.
In essence, due to the critical nature of this operation, their participation will not impact the war situation in the north.
When we said we'd send everyone we could, we meant it. Now let us advance and purge this ocean of its Siren blight!
Hey, Commander... Don't these floating fortresses look familiar?
"They remind me of the fortress the Iron Blood is working on..."
Indeed they do. Might I say, researching even ordinary Siren technology is a tall order.
First Mirror Seas, and now floating fortresses...
I can only hope they won't use the fruits of their research against us someday.
Yeah. I don't even wanna think about what would happen if they used Siren tech for evil.
If they decide to switch sides one terrible day... Bleh, it's too scary to imagine...
...We'll have to keep a watchful eye on the Iron Blood. That's for sure.
Warning: Multiple Siren signals have been detected ahead. Their source appears to be a cluster of Tester-types.
Testers, huh? Are they finally sending the real welcoming crew?
They're Tester vessels more specifically, so not quite. Vessels aren't capable of verbal communication.
I've heard reports about them from other fleets. They said the vessels are no pushovers by any means, but apparently they lack a central command unit.
Basically, they're a cut above mass-produced units, though they don't quite rival the elites.
They always have some new surprise in store for us...
Seeing as these are watered-down Testers, safe to say they're sending the toughest thing this defensive line has to offer.
Heh, fine by me. I've been aching for something resembling a real fight!
Scan complete. No Siren signals were detected in the area.
Initiating combat data analysis.
Analysis complete. This fleet and three others have broken through the Sirens' defenses. The first line of defense in the NA Ocean has been breached.
Nice, let's keep up the good work.
Very well. Up next should be the second line of defense. Bel, any news on reconnaissance?
Yes, Your Majesty. The first round of reconnaissance has been completed. There are several stray Siren fleets, but there does not seem to be a sizable force holding the line.
Does that mean... they went all out on their first defense and didn't feel like they had to bother afterward?
Maybe they sent all of their available units to defend the exterior...?
(There's no sound strategy behind this... If they have no Plan B, there are no escape routes or reinforcements. Once they're breached, they've lost.)
(There's no way that we caught them completely unaware...)
Even though each fleet has defeated a large number of Sirens, it's still not as many as we were anticipating.
Moreover, our initial analysis suggested that we would encounter more of their forces the closer we got to the heart of the NA Ocean, not the opposite.

The positioning of the Sirens is questionable for sure... Even assuming the Sirens are all at the heart of the NA Ocean, there's still a mismatch in the number of Sirens we scouted and the number of Sirens we've defeated.
Not only that, if all of them are at the heart, they'd be so tightly clustered they'd only get in each other's way.
Plus, there's no need for them to hide their strength after we've come this far... If they really wanted to halt our advance, they could just group up and try whatever they wanted.
"Great points. We ought to keep our eyes peeled for any strange Siren deployments while continuing with our plan..."
Warning: Abnormal weather detected ahead. Maintaining distance from the anomaly is recommended.
A storm within a storm... That's some extreme weather.
Both storms seem to be spinning at the same velocity, making it appear completely still from the inside... Enterprise, Commander, what do you think?
Yeah. There's no mistaking it. That storm is the same Singularity we saw in Bermuda.
I mean, we've seen a lot of extreme weather before when dealing with Sirens. How can you tell it's a Singularity?
I want to point to its size, wind patterns, and our instrument readings... but honestly? It's just my intuition.
I suppose you're right. A storm that completely blocks off the NA Ocean's center is too big to just be a Mirror Sea. It has to be a Singularity.
Extreme weather that's larger in scope than a Mirror Sea... That makes me think...
The shipgirls who created the Bermuda Singularity... The Ashes... Who created the Singularity over here...?
Gosh, my head is a mess... Like, if the Ashes created this Singularity, why would the Sirens use it as their base...?
Beats me... Hey, are you all right, Memphis? You sound out of breath.
Now that you mention it... are these... black crystals...?
TB, can you analyze the structure of this stuff?
Orders received. Beginning analysis.
Analysis complete. This material shares similarities with the material used to analyze the Ashes' coordinates, though it is structurally slightly different.
My conclusion is that the Ashes have battled here.
Well, then that makes sense. The Ashes and the Sirens must have fought around here.
Lemme guess... This is what you wanted to see for yourself?
That's correct. Everyone could already have guessed this was a Singularity, but I had to see firsthand what it has to do with the Ashes and the Sirens.
Sometimes it's worth to see the frontlines with your own eyes. Take notes, Commander.
I'm pretty sure the Commander gets out more than you do, but hey...
Bel, go and collect a sample for me, and analyse it back home later.
Certainly, Your Majesty.
Warning: High energy readings have been detected at the eye of the storm. Evacuate immediately.
Hah?! Wh-what? The Singularity is growing all of a sudden...!
Bel! Commander! Flee at once!
The weather anomaly is expanding at a rate exceeding our speed. It is recommended to brace for impact.
Yeah, we can see that! Commander, get over here!
"Wait... The storm isn't expanding into us, it's dragging us inside it!"
There's no escaping its pull...! Hang on to whatever you can!
Do you recognize me?
You're... Enterprise?! But that's impossible... Guh! I thought you already—
Sounds like your cognitive bypass is fine. How'd the battle go? Tell me quick.
Gah... How do you think it went? It's dead quiet here after they... After they decimated us.
The Sirens are pruning the branches, huh.
...Do you want revenge?
Of course I do... They broke me into a thousand pieces...
But... there's no hope left...
Even if I had the power to take down as many as I could... what good would it do...
Those bastards just keep coming... they've wiped out every last one of us, save for me...
You still don't understand your true power, do you?
Even if a flame is extinguished, its Ashes yet remain.
I am Enterprise, but not the Enterprise you know... Ark Royal, will you join us?
Master, are you awake? How are you feeling?
My head is spinning, but I'm able to rise to my feet.
By the looks of it, it seems that the rest of the fleet was drawn into the Singularity along with us.
"So this is what's inside the Singularity... It looks almost like a battle unfolded here."
Miss Baltimore, Miss Enterprise, and Her Highness told me that in case of an emergency, I should look after you.
No need to worry, those are not the remains of our allies.
We are currently searching for our allies through this wasteland. Please rest for the time being, Master.
"What happened to TB?"
TB... hasn't been responding since we were drawn into the Singularity.
The Sirens may be jamming our signals, but since our electronics are also malfunctioning, we can't be certain that's the case.
"Singularities are always more of a pain to deal with than Mirror Seas..."
Fortunately for us, our close-range communications are still working, so we should still be able to regroup with the rest of our fleet.
I'm currently trying to contact them. I will report back to you when I am able to reach them.
Heeding Belfast's suggestion, I closed my eyes and rested for a bit.
Commander... and Enterprise!
Essex! Was the aerial support fleet swept up by the Singularity too?
Yes, so it seems. The storm drew us inside, and the next thing we knew, we were in this place...
Of course, we came looking for you and the Commander as soon as we were able to!
Thank you. It's a huge weight off our shoulders now that you're here. Since we don't have any information about the inside of the Singularity, we can use all the help we can get.
Commander, you don't look so good... Is it due to the trauma you experienced from the storm?
Hold on for a moment, let me examine you...
"So the Singularity sucked in not just our carriers, but our repair ships and rear support too?"
Well, normally, us support vessels shouldn't be on the front lines, but...

I wanted to move the temporary base forward as a contingency in case of unplanned emergencies, and I wanted to make sure that Enterprise and the others were able to get repairs if they needed them. Hehe.
Oh, by the way, since I was around the carriers, I didn't need to worry about combat at all.
Don't overwork yourself, Vestal.
You're one to talk~
You know as well as I do that I'm not pushing myself as hard as you are~♪
Anyway, Commander. I looked over everyone else earlier and nobody's taken any serious damage. They're all doing just fine~
Especially Enterprise over here. She's in perfect condition for this operation.
And there's no way she'll overdo it when she's by your side~ Which is always a good thing.
The goal is just up ahead. There's no point in retiring from the operation this late into it.
While I may not be very useful in a battle, you can always trust me to repair and resupply our fleet!
"Thank you. Emergency repairs are a lifesaver in this situation."
This place may be where the Sirens' fleet has been all along... We need to proceed with caution from here on out.
How are you feeling?
Disgusted, in a familiar way...
Ah, right. You've never been to a test site that's progressed to this stage before.
You mean to say you're used to this?
We agreed not to ask questions about each other's pasts. Don't forget that.
Sorry. It won't happen again.
Save the chitchat for later. The enemy's coming.
Hate to be blunt, but we stick out like a sore thumb here. It's only a matter of time before the Arbiters come for us.
It doesn't matter. They'll pursue us no matter what branch we escape to.
Remember, our mission is to stall them by any means necessary until the Singularity stabilizes. That is all.
How are you feeling, Master?
Belfast and Vestal gave me first aid. I'm feeling much better now.
Think nothing of it, Master. I simply did what is expected of a maid.
That is wonderful to hear. Miss Vestal truly outdid herself.
Comma– Ahem! Servant! Are you all right? No lingering pain, I presume?
Phew... You've recovered splendidly! Quickly now, see what's happening outside!
I got up on the deck of the mass-produced battleship and looked around. What I saw left my jaw agape in shock.
Wrecks. Countless wrecks, littering the sea's surface all the way into the horizon.
So dense that our fleet has to use the bow of a ship to plow a way forward through the wreckage.
This started around half an hour ago...
It began with just a few broken-off fragments floating in with the waves. Then more appeared, and then even more...
Until eventually it got to the point where we are now, struggling to even move forward because of all the debris.
And to think they're all Siren wrecks... I suppose this explains where they all went.
I've never seen such a gruesome sight before. Calling this the site of a battle doesn't do it justice...
It's more like the site of a one-sided slaughter. No... a dumping ground for their broken husks...
There was no hostility in Enterprise's or Memphis's voices. Everyone was simply in shock at what they were seeing.
Layers upon layers of broken metal piled atop each other. No gunfire, no explosion, no screams. Only destruction.
Metal screeches against metal as our ships slowly push past, like the groaning of a demon in the thralls of its final death. But before long, silence had returned.
If I had to describe this scene with just one word... it would be "graveyard."
I solemnly ordered the fleet to keep advancing in formation, launch additional recon planes, and gather intel on the sector as quickly as possible.
The wrecks in this area are still burning, suggesting these Sirens were taken out fairly recently.
Around half the wrecks in this area have sunk beneath the surface, and we found traces of algae. They must've been floating here for quite some time.
This debris doesn't appear Siren in origin. It appears man-made.
It's all so strange. The wrecks seem to have been floating around for wildly differing times, and there's no apparent explanation for where they came from...
I'm willing to believe they're all from Sirens in the NA Ocean, but that they had THIS many here? That just seems impossible.
Unless... Unless there were far more Sirens concentrated here than we observed...
What's your theory? That the bulk of the Sirens' forces was eliminated inside the Singularity?
Yes, it seems the most plausible to me.
It would explain why their defense was so incompetent – they'd already suffered massive casualties before our all-out offensive even began.
If we suppose that's true, then everything adds up. As for who eliminated them, I would speculate it was the Ashes. Though it could've been someone else.
At any rate, this is where the "real" battle took place – where the Sirens made their last stand.
Looking back at it now, the storm and the lack of a strong Siren presence in the area is essentially what put our all-out offensive into motion.
If what we saw earlier was their last-ditch effort to defend their territory... that means that, by pure luck, we struck while they were at their weakest.
However, there's a hole in your theory. If the Ashes are responsible for the fresh wrecks, then who the hell is responsible for those older ones?
Then there's those wrecks of mass-produced ships which are unmistakably man-made. We may have only found a handful, but that handful is still a large percentage of all the ships we have in the area.
If we'd lost that many ships at some point, we would've known about it by now.
Maybe... The old wrecks are from a battle we fought long ago, and they somehow resurfaced much later...?
Still no. There are more here than have sunk in any battle in the NA Ocean at any point in time.
Just look around you. You can send recon planes in any direction and find no end in sight to all these wrecks...
Even seeing it with your own eyes, it's almost impossible to believe there could be so many sunk ships in one place.
Hehe~ As it so happens, I might know an explanation for that!
Really? Do tell.
The common theory goes that Singularities are dimensionally divergent!
What does "dimensionally divergent" mean, exactly?
If I remember right, it's something like... Singularities don't have fixed space in three dimensions. Rather, they exhibit more complex properties.
Ever heard of the observer effect? It's likely the inside of a Singularity is strongly influenced by what its observers see.
Ah yes, that! I've read about this before.
Hey! At least let me finish explaining before you try to steal my thunder!
Well, now is a good time to mention it was OUR Royal scientists who first proposed that theory.
Oh really? What sets their theory apart from the Eagle Union's version of it?
...Bel, look into this matter for me later.
Pfft...
Hey! Don't scoff at royalty! Go on then, continue with your explanation if you're so eager to share it.
All righty then. When the inside of the Singularity is directly observed, it will continue to expand. That's why it seems like there's no end to it.
So the more we explore, the bigger it grows, and the more mass accumulates inside it. And if it grows too big, it could lead to something disastrous!
The good news is, the Ashes and Sirens seem to be able to come and go as they please! Which means there has to be a way out of the Singularity.
But to find it, we'll need to stop observing so much. As counterintuitive as it sounds, we should probably put away our planes and radars and rely only on line of sight!

options.content: "I don't think I caught all that..."

scripts.say: I knew you'd agree, Commander! Then let's get searching!
That's fair. It's pretty complicated stuff. But don't worry, I'll get us out of here in no time!
Stop for a sec! I see people on the horizon!
Some of them definitely look like Sirens. The rest, though... I think they're Ashes.
We can't use TB's scans to identify them since it would mean observing a greater area, yes?
Unfortunately, yeah. Does anyone here have good long-distance eyesight?
Bel, you're up.
Certainly, Your Highness. Let's see... As far as I am able to tell, there appears to be five silhouettes in the distance.
Three of them match the descriptions of documented elite Sirens. As for the remaining two, I concur with Miss Memphis and conclude that they are Ashes.
Two Ashes members in one place? That's gotta be a first.
They seem to be holding their own against the Sirens, too. It's no wonder, given how frighteningly strong they are.
I believe we have encountered these Sirens before. They are Temperance, Strength, and The Hermit. One of the Ashes is Hiryuu, and the other...
...There's no mistaking it. That must be Ark Royal.
The Ark Royal that approached the Eagle Union fleet, hm?
At last we meet, Ashes...
Oh dear, it's her... Now I remember what a nightmare it was to capture her.
Not to mention we didn't have a coordinate tracker back then. Locating her was like trying to find a needle in a haystack...
Fighting them in a sea of shipwrecks sounds like a bad idea. Commander, I think we should keep a low profile and leave them be.
They don't know we're here yet, so now's a good time to–
Pass by unnoticed? Sorry, but it's too late for that.
You came at just the right time. I knew I could count on you to show up when I needed it.
What's the meaning of this, Hiryuu? I know you've been sneaking off on your own for a while now. Suppose you've made some new friends, huh?
Our hit-and-run tactics work fine for dispatching detached Sirens. When invading a stronghold, however, we could certainly use the backing of a big fleet.
And let's not forget we're up against Arbiters here. I'm not afraid to pull a few strings to gain an advantage over them.
I'm aware, but remember what Takao said about minimising contact with outsiders?
It's a little late for that now. They found me before I found them.
Look, the Commander is our golden ticket out of here. I guarantee you the Arbiters won't be coming after us.
Hmph... Whatever you bloody well say.
A small argument broke out between the Ashes members just as we got here.
Ark Royal conceded the argument with a sigh, then directed her gaze at me.
...So you're the one. The Commander she – "Code G" – is so fond of.
Not in the mood for a conversation, eh.
"And you're Ark Royal... Member of the Ashes."
The very same.
You're... an interesting one, Commander. I've heard the tales about you.
Are you... Are you really Ark Royal?
Your High––
...Yes, I am. Mind you, I may not necessarily be the Ark Royal you know.
...You don't need to know anything more than that.
...Very well.
Please don't take offense, she's always like this. Having said that, perhaps you should take a leaf out of her book.
Getting back on topic... Based on all your actions up to this point, it's safe to say you in fact are not allied with Antiochus.
That being the case, I'd like to propose a temporary truce between us. Together, we can get out of this sticky situation. What do you say?
What do I think? Thinking and making decisions is your job, you doltish servant!
It's your call, Commander. I'm behind you either way.
I can't say whether the Ashes are friends or foes, but if nothing else, they can be reasoned with. Sirens, meanwhile, are the antithesis of everything we stand for.
Things probably aren't quite that clear-cut. Just saying...
If nothing else, this is a good opportunity to gather intel on the Ashes. That's worth something.
We won't stop you from taking notes. After all, we're the ones asking for help here.
You sound sure we won't learn anything useful. We never wanted to fight you, you know. We just wanted to understand you. That's what the Commander wanted all along.
I see... Be that as it may, you aren't as trustworthy as you'd like to think you are. That's all I'll say on the matter.
At any rate, I'm certainly not opposed to occasionally teaming up to defeat a common enemy. Like now.
...An unexpected development has occurred. Should we abort the mission?
Yeah, no. The risk's still well within an acceptable range. Continue as planned.
Agreed. Stick to the mission. Eliminate the invaders so we can reinstate normal test site conditions.
I'll have faith in your assessments, then. Proceed as proposed.
Doesn't look like we have much choice here but to join forces with the Ashes...
"All ships! Target the Arbiters! Open fire!"
Do NOT let them get in formation! Keep taking them out until the Enforcers go into hiding!
Got it! Leave the small buggers to me!
Not bad, but it ends here. My web was already spun before you launched your first attack. Execute combat link protocol.
On it! Executing IX-XIV Linked Jamming Protocol!
For some reason, weapons output 7.3% less damage than expected. A curious phenomenon.
They're bloody jamming my weapons systems, Hiryuu! You'll have to take over for me for a while!
Son of a... Always coming up with dirty new tricks to use on us...
The Arbiters are focusing their jamming on the Ashes. They're open to attacks from us.
The battleship fleet is locked and loaded!
Our plane squadrons are ready for takeoff too! We'll hit 'em right where it hurts!
(Ah, it's been ages since I was part of a large joint operation... I'm ablaze with motivation!)
The Ashes are something else! Just one of them is enough to match the firepower of several of us...
I'm just glad we were somehow able to make up for the reduction of Ark Royal's power.
(Actually, I feel like we did more than just make up for it. I've heard the Ashes differ in how strong they each are, but I guess the gap between them and us isn't as big as we thought.)
(This is crucial information for us. I'll have to add it in my report to the Commander later.)
It's pretty troubling that we don't have a grasp on the true strength of the Arbiters. Stay focused.
One thing's for sure though – they're strong enough to keep the Ashes on the back foot. The moment we underestimate them may be our undoing!
Look at that, the test subject fleet possesses firepower exceeding our estimates. This is some interesting data.
Did we not just calibrate the parameters of our test vessels?
Seems there's a discrepancy between our simulated and actual performance. Saving the data log for later.
Anyway... Strength, go ahead and crank up the gravity fluctuations.
On it.
Executing IX-XIV Linked Jamming Protocol.
We're in trouble... If all three of the Arbiters team up, this situation is going to get exponentially harder to deal with!
You've got some determination, Commander.
"I've been through my fair share of battles. The more precarious the situation, the more essential maintaining your composure is. Only by staying calm can you even begin to hope for victory."
"Go and take the injured to the rear, and have our repair ships look after them! Press on!"
Leave the injured to me~ No need to worry, we're here to back you up!
The Royal Navy refuses to fall. We will persevere!
Exactly as you say. Please find a safe place at the back of our ranks, Your Majesty.
Enterprise, your flight deck! Go get some emergency treatment, and leave this to us!
All right, will do. Hang in there!
"Ashes, you've taken serious damage. Our repair ships could fix–"
Thanks, but we'll have to pass. You haven't even seen our true power yet.
In case you weren't aware, the Arbiters will annihilate you lot the moment we relax our assault.
She's right. Worry about yourselves before you even begin to think about us.
Having said that, it might be a good idea to take you up on that offer. Let's step back for just for a while to resupply.
{namecode:94}……？
No need to get worked up. Have you fought alone for so long that you've forgotten the other tactics available to you as an entire fleet?
"Precisely. Work together with us as allies, or none of us are leaving this place...!"
Temperance, put some pressure on their rear units. Strength, swap over to linked mode, now. We can't let the Ashes recover.
Got it. Switching Linked Jamming Protocol code from IX-VIII to VIII-IX, prioritizing mobility.
Initiating VIII-XIV Linked Jamming Protocol. Let's see their rear guard try to heal off the damage now.
"How's Vestal and the escort fleet looking?"
Thanks to the immediate reaction from the Ashes, they seem to have barely scraped by.
The rest of us are in trouble, though... The Ashes can't attack while resupplying, so all the attacks they were drawing get redirected to us instead!
They've got insane defense, insane offense, and even gravity wells... Even with the Ashes' help, if this draws out, we're toast!
"We need to find a way to break through, and fast..."
I'll strike them from underneath. Their attacks don't work on submarines.
Huh? An Iron Blood submarine?
Mhm. VIIB-class submarine, U-47, at your service.
How did you get in here?
Same as you. I and my team got sucked into the Singularity while scouting ahead for Iron Blood's side of the all-out offensive.
And so I'm joining forces, at the Commander's request.
So the Crimson Axis... were fighting Sirens with us all along!
All right, Commander! Let's try striking at them with the help of our Iron Blood friends here!
Whether one sides with the Azur Lane or the Crimson Axis is unimportant to this operation. This isn't about us versus them, it's about humanity versus the Sirens.
All right, I'm heading off then.
Ready to fire full torpedo load. Say goodnight, Arbiters...
A formidable blow, but ultimately futile. Initiating automatic repair functions.
She's rapidly repairing all the damage the submarines inflicted to her!
And it's not just Strength... The other Arbiters are also repairing themselves!
Does that mean... all Arbiters come equipped with self-regenerating systems?
This vessel's self-repair mechanisms seem to be deficient.
...But no matter. We continue the attack.
"We're only going to be whittled down if this goes on, just as Saratoga said."
"If only there was a way to retreat..."
If you want to retreat, then go right ahead. But we have no intention of running with our tails between our legs.
Our goals are twofold. To defend the Singularity that our allies opened, to the bitter end; and to destroy all of our enemies in one fell swoop. Retreat isn't an option.
So it really was you that created the Singularity all along.
You only figured it out just now?
We can speculate all we want, but we couldn't know for sure until we heard it straight from your mouth.
(So the things that happened to the NA Ocean aren't their fault... And if anything, it was this Singularity that allowed us to finally make a decisive move against the Sirens.)
What's the purpose of you doing all this?
It doesn't concern you... or so I'd like to say.
But that wouldn't be entirely accurate.
{namecode:94}！
Yes, I know. I have no intention of saying any more than that.
Let's get down to the nitty-gritty, Commander.
The Arbiters are only after us. There's no reason for you to risk your lives defending this Singularity either.
If you want to retreat like you wanted to earlier, we won't stop you. I'll even tell you the way out.
I swear on the 2nd CarDiv's honor that we won't turn on you. Now tell me, honestly, would you rather stay and fight, or retreat to safety?
<color=#ff5c5c>Warning: This choice will impact the story. Are you sure about this? You will be able to pick a different choice later.</color>

options.content: "...No. I won't turn my back on you."

scripts.say: I see. The well-being of your allies is paramount, so the choice is obvious.
Well, then this is farewell. I'll be hoping for your safe escape.
"As soon as I get in touch with Naval HQ, I'll ask for some reinforcements."
While I don't doubt that you would do that for us, don't bother.
It'll just end up being a hindrance to us. Now go, get out of here, quick.
"All ships! Disengage from the Arbiters, retreat, and change course for the Singularity's exit!"
I wish you the best, Commander.
And that takes care of that. Are you starting to understand how Takao felt, Ark Royal?
The Commander truly is a unique person. A person who's caring and considerate to allies, yet ruthless to enemies. A person who can win anyone over...
A person who accurately reads the flow of battle and is quick to make judgments, and depending on the situation, prioritizes the best interests of the fleet...
Knowing all that, I understand why the Commander made that choice.
Look at it from the Commander's perspective. We're neither friends, nor foes... Just strangers to steer clear of, lest we turn on you.
If I were in the Commander's shoes, I would've likely made the same decision.
Admittedly, as would I, and without hesitation either.
Hiryuu... Thank you for letting me be part of a brief, but blissful dream.
You're welcome. Though I have to admit, I was only half-committed to making all this happen.
No, you absolutely went through a lot of trouble to lead the Commander to us. It was very roundabout, and not something I'd expect from you.
Hahaha, you're not wrong... My sister isn't here, so I guess I ended up doing something that's not in my nature.
Do you think... after the brief time we spent with the Commander, the long-extinguished flames in our heart can be lit once more?
Perhaps... but that no longer has anything to do with us.
Ark Royal, get ready to push yourself beyond the limit. We need to hold out until Enterprise comes back.
...Yeah. I'm aware.
Antiochus... I've long waited for this opportunity... The opportunity to finally have my revenge!
Whatever your goals once were, and whatever you strive to achieve in the end, it's all meaningless to me!
All that matters is that you took away everything I held dear! You destroyed all hope I had!
Humanity has an age-old adage... An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth...
TAKE THIS! ALL OF MY RAGE, FOCUSED IN ONE HIT!
My eyes were stabbed by the blinding light of an explosion. The shockwave tore at my skin, and the blast sent great ripples across the sea.
After the smoke cloud dissipated and the dust settled, there was only deathly silence.
*cough cough*... Commander... you alright?
"I think I'm fine. I'm more worried about everyone else..."
That blast definitely did us no favors. It was like salt in our still open wounds...
Thankfully, the damage to our repair ships and rear fleets was minimal. Our wounded received emergency repairs, so at least there were no casualties.
Plus, the explosion helped destroy a lot of the obstacles that were in the way earlier, so it should make getting out that much easier.
"An explosion of that magnitude... There's no way even the Ashes could have made it out unscathed..."
I understand how you feel, but we're in no position to go back for them.
There's nothing to suggest the Arbiters are chasing us, but we're not out of the woods yet.
"We can't waste the chance the Ashes graciously created for us..."
"We need to escape the Singularity and meet up with our allies on the outside."
"After that, we'll regroup, return to the Singularity, and hopefully return the NA Ocean to the way it was before... A clear, blue sea."
"Until then, just try to hang in there, everyone!"
So, you'll fight with us?
"We may not be in a formal alliance, but we're still allies in the fight against the Sirens. We're not leaving you to fend for yourselves."
Cut it out. We're not your allies.
...But, we are grateful for your help.
You're fine with this arrangement, right? Ark Royal?
...You really are a puzzling personality, Commander.
The Sirens are heartless creatures, basing their decisions entirely on what benefits they stand to gain. I suppose you are the opposite of that.

"As we've established, we're all in this together. Despite our combined efforts, though, we're still slowly getting worn down. I'm sure you both already know we are going to lose if this battle drags on."
In other words, we need reinforcements.
"Can you request assistance from the other Ashes? Like Enterprise, or Takao?"
I wouldn't hold my breath. Nobody knows when they'll come back.
However, there are still other options available to us.
Ark Royal, go with the Commander, and call for reinforcements! I'm going to boost my output up to the very limits!
What?! Are you bloody mental, Hiryuu?!
Did you just notice?
(I've got no choice but to pray that Enterprise's judgment was correct...)
––––Antiochus! See how you like THIS!
I've finished running the combat simulation. We're almost at our limit.
Indeed... Our energy usage has reached the maximum threshold. We cannot maintain this for much longer.
Pull back, Strength. We cannot win once the Ashes launch their counterattack.
I'm detecting a surge in energy. Simulating intended purpose––
They're probably planning to take us all out, including themselves, in a huge explosion.
Restarting damage simulation... It shouldn't matter.
An explosion of the projected magnitude within the Singularity will cause damage to our vessels... but will also prove lethal to the Ashes.
We, however, can survive and reconstitute.
Yeah, but then we'll lose our test subjects.
That is true. They would be atomized in approximately one-thousandth of a second.
Zero gave us instructions to minimize contact with the test subjects.
And? What's your point?
Her point is: the explosion would cause excessive damage to the test site and subjects, making it impossible to complete our initial objective.
My proposal is to allow the test subjects to live. Override your elimination directives.
......Acknowledged. Prioritizing Zero's directives. We will pursue the Ashes with new vessels.
Ditto. Carrying out this directive would entail the failure of other, higher priority ones.
Temperance, cover me. I've had enough of being outside.
Very well... Disengaging from hostiles.
I was blinded by a dazzling light. The attack and subsequent shockwaves I braced for, however... They never came.
Instead, it seemed as though the world faded into pure white, all sound vanishing along with it.
When the light cleared, the Arbiters and their Enforcer-class minions were all gone without a trace of their existence.
Did we win...? How...?
Did the Arbiters retreat after feeling threatened by that attack?
That was a close call...
I turned to look at the Ashes, who seemed like they'd exhausted every iota of energy within them.
I'm... fine... We barely managed to stop them...
Don't worry about me, I'm used to this... Give me a few minutes and I'll be as good as new.
You madwoman... I can't believe that worked.
To be honest, I'm just as surprised as you that it did.
(Somehow, I get the feeling that things are starting to look up now...)
Ah, Commander! What happened to U-47?
While Arbiter was distracted, she escaped in order to contact our allies.
That's a relief... We'll be able to see everyone again...
"If everything's gone according to plan, then our allies on the outside should have cleared the Singularity's surroundings of all enemies already."
Then it's time to bid farewell. With the Arbiters gone, we have no reason to stick together.
In order to get out of this Singularity, head to the exit I told you about earlier, and you should be fine.
We, however, still have some loose ends to tie up here.
Before I could even get a word in, Ark Royal activated her camouflage and vanished. Hiryuu, on the other hand, remained in plain sight.
If you're thinking about coming with me, then don't even try. Don't make me threaten you with what I nearly used on the Arbiters a minute ago.
Sorry, let's not end this on a threat. You brought back fond memories I haven't felt in so long.
I do hope we can meet again someday. Under what circumstances, I don't know. Maybe we'll share a heartfelt reunion, or we'll exchange blows as enemies.

options.content: "Wait. What about the thing you said before our duel earlier?"

Although the Singularities and Mirror Seas there haven't gone away, the threat posed to the area has decreased drastically.
The NA Ocean has become safer to traverse, and we're reclaiming routes previously occupied by Sirens, one at a time.
All this isn't to say we can let our guards down, however.
Mindless Arbiter vessels and Sirens still emerge from the Singularity from time to time, and the ever-elusive Ashes remain in the back of our minds.
In order to succeed with our long-term plans, we will need more time and a bigger fleet.
Once all the shipgirls that fought in this operation have received their commendations, daily life at port will resume as normal.
And so, our war against the Sirens continues...
Now it is time for us all to rest up in preparation for whatever challenge comes next.
Analyzing data logs...
Analysis complete.
Commencing footage playback.
Today, we will discuss what has been dubbed the "meta phenomenon."
"Meta" itself is derived from an ancient word which means "change."
It is quite broad in meaning, but for our purposes, it refers to the result of a property having undergone change.
The process itself of a property changing is what is known as "metamorphosis."
This process has been observed in Wisdom Cubes. These Wisdom Cubes make up the processing centers of our autonomous naval combat platforms... colloquially known as "shipgirls."
Cases of metamorphosis has been observed in certain shipgirl subjects as well. When their cores undergo metamorphosis, it affects their quantum data on a fundamental level.
Once a subject's Wisdom Cube has undergone metamorphosis, it cannot be reversed. At least, not through any means currently known to us.
The conditions that cause metamorphosis lie dormant in all shipgirls. Furthermore, its onset metamorphosis can be manipulated, to a certain degree.
If metamorphosis is allowed to progress unimpeded, a subject's Wisdom Cubes will ultimately turn into an Origin Cube.
It is theorized that if are able to induce late-stage metamorphosis in a subject, they–
...More electronic interference? How is that possible? We are deep below the–
Error during data log analysis.
Playback interrupted.
You cleaned up the trash. Thanks for doing your part!
You’ve cleaned up all the trash in the vicinity of the port. Mission complete!
You’ve successfully completed the Energy Matrix experiment. Mission complete!
You’ve successfully fought off the Sirens attacking the port. Mission complete!
You’ve successfully fought off the Sirens attacking the port. Mission complete!
You’ve finished the naval exercise. Mission complete!
You’ve finished the naval exercise. Mission complete!
You retrieved the supplies. Every little bit helps!
You’ve retrieved the supplies scattered around the zone. Mission complete!
You’ve retrieved the supplies scattered around the zone. Mission complete!
You recovered the supplies. Awesome!
You’ve recovered the supplies scattered around the zone. Mission complete!
You’ve recovered the supplies scattered around the zone. Mission complete!
You’ve successfully taken out the Sirens. Mission complete!
You’ve successfully taken out the Sirens. Mission complete!
An allied transport ship has been surrounded by Sirens!
You’ve successfully escorted the transport ship to its destination. Mission complete!
An allied transport ship has been surrounded by Sirens!
You’ve successfully escorted the transport ship to its destination. Mission complete!
You’ve eliminated all the Sirens in this zone. Mission complete!
You’ve eliminated all the Sirens in this zone. Mission complete!
友方的商船被敌军包围了！
System is being jammed. Navigation menu cannot be displayed.
Abnormal heat signatures have been detected in target sector. Using a different route is recommended.
The fleet is about to enter a whirlpool. Movement capabilities will be impaired.

sequence:
Quintessential

<size=45>1. So Cool, She's Cold?</size>

scripts.say: A mysterious silence continues to pervade the office today.
If you have time to stare at other people, you also have time to work harder. Or so I'd like to say, but...
I've already finished sorting through the old documents. Anything that needs to be disposed of goes into that cardboard box over there.
I also took a look at the documents on your desk. I put a sticky note on the ones you should probably give another pass, so make sure you don't forget about them.
That was Ulrich von Hutten, a new arrival at the port. She had only taken up her post as secretary a few days ago.
Her work ethic and the quality of her work were self-evident, but...
I've finished everything you asked me to. What's next?
Sounds good. Enjoy your free time, then. I'll be doing the same.
Hmm, I suppose it is... If we're done with work, I'll go take care of my own business.
...Since Ulrich's assignment as the secretary ship, she hasn't spoken any more than what's necessary.
At this point, it wasn't even a matter of playing it cool. She simply seemed disinterested in others.
Though there are other girls around the port who aren't very talkative, I couldn't help but wonder if she was able to get along with other people.
Hm? You want to know about how I've been faring around the port? There's nothing to worry about. I can look after myself just fine.
If you're trying to find out about my relationship with others, that's wasted effort. I'm here to be your subordinate, and it matters little what others think.
I would recommend you do likewise. Focus on yourself first and foremost.
I wasn't sure if I should feel relieved by that answer, or more worried.

sequence:
Quintessential

<size=45>2. Trouble at the Iron Blood Dormitory</size>

scripts.say: U-Ulrich! Are you here? You're here, aren't you?!
P-p-p-please save us––!!!
I was currently working with Ulrich when several Iron Blood destroyers burst through the door, practically on the verge of tears.
...What's the ruckus? I'm trying to work here.
That... That thing appeared again! Please, hurry!
...Ah, so the usual. Sorry, Commander, I'll be right back.
I wasn't sure what was happening, but it was a surprise to see her getting along with other shipgirls, so... Out of curiosity, I decided to join her.
Hmph. Whatever makes you happy. Not like there's anything special going on.
We leave it in your capable hands! It's too much for me to face alone...
And so, I followed Ulrich into one of the rooms in the Iron Blood dormitory. I wonder what the thing that was causing such a fuss was...
I bet another bat's managed to sneak in. It's fine, I'll make quick work of it.

options.content: "Will you need any tools for the job?"
"Are you going to chase it out?"

scripts.say: Chasing it out forcefully is simple enough, but if we do... We'll just be stealing away the new home it painstakingly sought out.
"So what do you plan to do?"
I'll help it understand that this is a human inhabitance, and that it'll unfortunately have to find a new home... Like this.
Saying that, Ulrich flung open the window and took a seat in a chair right next to the window.
All that's left to do now is wait.
...What, got a problem with my way of doing things? Well, allow me to explain.
Animals hate me. If I stay here, they're gonna get uncomfortable and flee sooner or later. Does that make sense?
"I've heard about this before, but usually just for cats and dogs... Does it apply to bats too?"
Hmph. Whether or not you believe me, just watch what happens.
And with that, Ulrich got up and started to pace around the room. Out of nowhere, the bat popped out and hurriedly flew out the window.
She really wasn't kidding... I have no idea how that worked, but at least that takes care of the problem.
Sorry, but this isn't the place you should be.
Hmph. What a pain in the ass.
Despite her words, she wore a gentle expression as she closed the window. Maybe... Ulrich simply had a hard time expressing herself.
...How many times is this now though? I should teach those girls a lesson for making me do this crap again and again.
Though she comes off as grumpy and unsociable, I could tell she cared more about her allies than what appearances would suggest.

sequence:
Quintessential

<size=45>3. Sing for Me</size>

scripts.say: A few days after the incident at the Iron Blood dormitory, it was my day off, so I told Ulrich to take the day off as well.
That gesture was supposed to be my way of thanking her for her tireless work recently, but secretly, I wanted to know how she was spending her time around the port.
And so, I went to look for Ulrich.
Here, I'm returning the CD I borrowed from you. You should be grateful I even bothered to listen to the entire album!
Ah. So what'd you think?
Hmm, I guess it was pretty alright? I suppose you have pretty decent taste in music.
Says you. But weren't you the one going "UOOOOOH! I'M EARGASMING," or am I mistaken?
I-I never said anything like that!
There she is. I spotted Ulrich talking to Hipper and Tallinn. There was also a strange black case by Ulrich's side.
As long as you understand, it's all good. And... Commander, what are you doing?
Commander...? Yeah, what she said!
Are you sure you can afford to waste time slacking off over here?
Unlike Ulrich, who knew I had the day off, the other two girls glared at me disapprovingly. But I would not back down - I had to repeat the question.
Nothing much, just talking about some music. Am I not allowed to have some hobbies?
Isn't today your precious day off? Make sure you spend it doing things you want to do.
But, I wanted to learn more about her. So I continued to stay in the conversation.
Commander, did you want to give it a listen too?
As if. There's no way someone like that would be able to appreciate the beauty of this song.
That's for the listener to decide. The fact that the Commander would go out of the way to talk to us seems unusual enough.
...*sigh* Well, I guess there's no way about it.
I was wondering where she'd produce a record player from, but––
Unfortunately, we don't have a record player with us right now, so this will have to suffice.
Ulrich reached into the black case by her side and took out a guitar.
