Enough talk! You die now!
I'll defeat you... not just to avenge my sisters, but for the sake of a bright future for the Admiral Hipper class!
PUZVSLUA PUZLJAZ
BZZZZT!
When she leaves the safety of the barrier, the Star Beast launches an attack.
However, the crushing noise is erased by soft light.
Bullying poor Hipper? Not on my watch.
Heheh☆ Hipper! Let's punish this big lug together!
Two people thought long lost appear on the scene.
The girls on Hipper's flanks point their guns in the same direction.
Eugen, Blücher... Shouldn't the two of you be...
No way. This isn't real...
Are you ghosts? Hallucinations? Or...?
Geez~ Settle down, Sis!
You're not wrong, but that doesn't mean you're right!
Well, uh, maybe you are actually wrong...
Aargh, I don't understand it well enough to explain!
Eugen, help me out here!
Basically, your wishes took form as us.
You wished to make a new future for the Admiral Hipper class. How could we let you do it alone?
Is it... really you?
Yeah, we're back. Only for a while, though.
Hipper... Thanks for all you've done in our stead.
P HT AOL ZAHY ILHZA
NBPKPUN AOL ZAHYZ KV P HWWLHY
ILHYPUN AOL ZAHYZ KV P SLHCL
AOL DVYSK OHZ ILLU ZBSSPLK
IBYU PA KVDU P ZOHSS HUK PA DPSS IL YLIVYU
Blinding light condenses beneath the starry sky.
Tch... Interrupting our touching reunion? You're as dense as they come.
Hey, you big lug! I'm gonna beat the tar outta you!
Wait! Eugen, Blücher! Get back in the barrier!
You two can't take that thing on alone!
Don't worry about us. We have each other.
Yeah! Let's win this together!
KABOOOOM!
That which I'd seen destroy the world before was halted by a gentler force, which weakened it more with every passing second.
Silence took over the battlefield, engulfing all.
Ages seemed to pass in this moment.
When the light disappeared, so too did the Star Beast.
Did we... win?
It was a perfect victory.
Heheh☆ Our bond can beat anything!
I swear, I must be dreaming... We really, really won?
Blücher? Eugen?! Have you come back to life somehow?!
It's been a while, Rumey. Who knew you'd become the leader of the Resistance?
Sorry, but we haven't. Consider us just a fleeting illusion born from hopes and dreams.
A fleeting illusion... Does that mean you're leaving me?!
The future you dreamed of is reality now. Our job here is done.
Oh... Well, knowing that you two live on in this state is still a relief.
When can I see you again?
Take care of yourself and keep getting stronger, and maybe then...
You might just be able to find us... Or you might even realize that we've been with you all along.
Doesn't make much sense to me. But okay... I'll take care of myself. I'll get stronger. And someday, I will find you two!
We're cheering you on, Hipper!
Sure are. And keep an eye on your nutrition, got it?
You don't have to tell me that!
A sea breeze blows through, and Prinz Eugen and Blücher begin to fade.
It's time for us to go... Thank you all for taking such good care of our sister. Keep her safe for us.
No worries there, Eugen. We will win this war.
I believe you.
SHUFFLE...
There's the sound of shuffling cards again. But it's softer and slower, as if giving me time to prepare before I'm taken away.
It's time to say goodbye.
Everyone, we've achieved a great victory today.
From now on, the Star Beast is no longer a sword hanging over the world – it's a symbol of victory and hope.
Congratulations, Fritz Rumey. Your counteroperation has taken a great leap forward.
Commander... Thank you.
You're not leaving too, are you?!
...I am.
Will we ever see you again?
Of course. I'm certain of it.
You will forever be the Commander of the Iron Blood Resistance. Take care of yourself.
Heheh... Commander.
Long time no see... Or perhaps should I say, "I'll see you soon."
(What?!)
After the light faded, the headquarters, Eternal Stars, and Star Beast alike were all gone.
I was slumped over a classroom desk, bathed in warm sunlight. When I sat up, it felt as if all that had happened was a dream.
But I know very well that all I'd experienced was real. Eugen's words are still fresh in my mind.
(Long time no see. See you soon.)
Thinking about something? Or just feeling strange now that you didn't have to die this time?
I'm thinking about what Eugen's phantom said to me as I left.
Who cares? Why bother agonizing over something if she doesn't find it important enough to tell you directly?
You know something, don't you?
Let's get back to talking about you.
Your little search has finally come to an end. Are you satisfied?
I'd call it a happy ending.
What about you? What have you been after all this time?
There's one thing I'd like to know.
...Did isolating you from your memories of test site beta make it easier to explore who you are and what you've experienced?
I can't deny that. Pieces of the puzzle came together like never before. I remembered some things, too.
But...
You just don't like my method.
Yeah, I really don't. I can overlook your manipulation of me to an extent, but I draw the line at manipulating my friends' memories.
Really? Even if some of your own memories in test site beta are falsehoods?
Doesn't matter. My memories are from test site beta – that's what matters.
No matter what came before, that's where I belong.
It's not an easily discarded test site to me. It's my home. Or one of them, at least.
To be honest, I wouldn't have been able to get out of this if not for my bonds with my bonds.
The answer I gave is no doubt different from the one you intended, right?
Exactly. I planned to have you choose a different route.
Having me complete Jörmungandr, I presume.
Why do you think so?
The Sirens' role is the key. I think your ultimate goal here was to make me change my opinion on them.
You wanted me to fail over and over until I was willing to cooperate with the Antiochus... or you'd convince me to take a similar deal.
If I accepted, you'd tell me how to complete Jörmungandr and provide the resources. With that, we'd defeat the Star Beast...
...And with that, I would have a new impression of the Sirens – that they're my ally. Isn't that right?
It means nothing now. You chose a different path, after all.
Magician... You don't remember me, do you?
Why do you ask?
You've been trying to teach me things, though in a roundabout way. But you've kept so silent about my true identity.
While I searched, you wanted to observe me and try to figure out who I am. Am I wrong?
Heehee. Perhaps. Or did I simply manipulate you into presuming as such?
Either way, I understand your thoughts now.
I won't toy with your memories anymore. I'll promise you that, if nothing else.
No more suddenly yanking me out of my world?
Hmm... Depends on my mood, I'm afraid.
Then promise me that you won't interfere with their world anymore. I want to be able to see them again.
Very well.
We don't have much time left, so let's do something special.
Suddenly, we're inside some kind of fortune-telling tent.
Pick three cards, if you'd please.
On the purple tablecloth is a deck of tarot cards spread face-down.
Are we doing divination now?
Past, present, future. Three cards, please.
Go on.
Your first card is The Star, reversed.
The Moon, upright.
Your third... Well, isn't this interesting?
How so?
I'm not telling yet. I'd much rather keep you in suspense.
Yet another secret, huh?
I only let you choose. I never said I'd share the result, now, did I?
Besides, what good is knowing the future if it means limiting your options?
Heehee. This has been a lot of fun.
I look forward to meeting you again, Commander.
I was finally reunited with my friends in the magic circle, surrounded by a kaleidoscope of butterflies.
Commander!
- You're finally home! - I've been waiting for you!
Ahem... Sorry for the long wait. It's over now.
It hasn't been that long.
We're honestly surprised how fast you were. Have you already finished everything you needed to do?
...Fast?
How much time has passed since we last talked?
Less than three minutes.
(Time passed at a different speed there?)
(...Did Madam M do that out of consideration for these two?)
(I had no idea one of the Arbiters could do that.)
Commander? You just froze up... Did you forget something you needed to do?
No, no. I'm fine.
I'm fed up with this little business trip. Let's go home and leave the discussion for another time.
Yes, let's!
I'd be happy to accompany you, Commander.

sequence: "Journeys intertwined."
"Encounters unexpected."
"The chaos has ended, the danger passed."
"From now on, life will be peaceful once more."
"Or... will it?"
Substellar Crepuscule - The End

scripts.say: The next day...
It was late by the time I arrived at the base, so I was promptly escorted to the guest room.
Now it's the next day, and I'm going to meet Fritz Rumey at lunchtime today. Before that, though, I got a call from Duisburg on my communicator.
Good morning, Commander. It's Duisburg.
We've made a few discoveries that I thought you should know about. Our engineers found some rather valuable components among the things we salvaged yesterday.
These will let us finally accomplish our goal of fixing our radiation purgers.
They also managed to decrypt plans for improving the device from the data core of a science vessel.
I heard those are really going to come in handy.
Rumey has always had plans to reclaim the surrounding island bases if we managed to repair the purgers.
Thanks to all these discoveries, we'll be able to put our big plan into action at once.
The plan will be publically announced today at noon. We'd love it if you came to listen.
Once the announcement is done, I'll bring you to Rumey's office. Then you can talk secrets with her.
Later, at noon...
Shipgirls gather at the base's square and hoist their banners.
Atop the high ground, a woman clad in the naval attire of Iron Blood makes her gallant appearance.
My compatriots!
I presume you've all heard that a Class V Rising Tide has appeared.
Yesterday, our scouting party returned from it with spoils in tow.
With the equipment they recovered, we will finally be able to restore our three radiation purgers to working order!
At last, we will be able to reclaim the surrounding bases that were lost!
YEAHHH!
The silent crowd erupts into cheers, like a long-dormant volcano.
However, Rumey raises her hand to quell their jubilation.
It is not yet time to celebrate.
The data core we recovered contains upgrade plans for the radiation purgers as well as blueprints for mass-producing them.
This means we will be able to reclaim not just our islands, but also restricted areas on the mainland!
YEAHHH!
The crowd cheers even louder than the last time.
Therefore, in three days, I will launch our first operation to reclaim our lost territory!
The first to be reclaimed shall be area IB-AX-104, the Silberstern – the Silver Star.
Our goal is to seize the island, restore the base's functionality, and establish a logistics line between it and our headquarters.
We must reclaim this island to secure vital materials needed for the upgrade of the radiation purgers.
Furthermore, it will serve as the springboard for future recapture operations...
Rumey's announcement continues.
Her briefing on the salvage mission turns first into a series of operation announcements, then into specific orders for her troops.
These rapid-fire proclamations had me confused at first, but it makes sense now that I think about it.
(This IS their forward operating base, so I assume everyone here is involved somehow.)
Once the announcements wrap up, Duisburg escorts me to Rumey's office.
The leader of this place just finished her speech, and now I will speak to her face-to-face.
You must be the outlander – {playername} – or should I say "Commander"?
I've been told about you. Did your memories return to you following a night's sleep?
I shake my head in response. Without any change in expression, she cuts to the chase.
I'll get straight to the point. Won't you consider joining us?
As you've seen around the base, we need every pair of hands we can get.
You would be of extraordinarily great help to us, especially considering your ties to other outlanders – the Sirens.
Unfortunately, I cannot promise much in the way of tangible resources in exchange for the knowledge and intelligence you possess...
However, if you work with us, I promise that you will be treated as an ally of the Resistance.
No, more than just that – you are an excellent leader, I've heard.
I will also give you our highest degree of trust and the space to fully display your tactical ingenuity.
Naturally, if you wish to join another one of humanity's force, I will not stop you.
Still, in a personal and official capacity, I sincerely hope you will choose to stay with us.
Please, Commander.
(A frank but succinct request. It's hard to say no when she's pleading so earnestly...)
(You sure know how to persuade, Rumey.)

sequence: Time: Unknown
Location: Unknown

scripts.say: For several days now, Helena has gazed endlessly at the panel before her and worked without pause.
Only one system hour remained until she would find test site beta's coordinates.
She had captured the core device of the phantom test site three system hours prior.
It's almost going too smoothly...
Magician must have set a trap. That much is clear from the fact that Miss D's appearance in test site beta isn't kept confidential.
Besides, the Tower and Camelot need to maintain a constant connection for this to work...
This would be the perfect time for her to launch an attack, and yet...
Why isn't she doing anything?
Was this the whole point? Just delaying me for a few days, and nothing else?
BEEP BEEP!
Right on cue, the situation took a turn for the worse.
A strong impact came from seemingly all directions. The bait that Helena had prepared was destroyed in the blink of an eye.
Is that all?
No... She was never after the Tower. She wanted to disrupt time-space and delay my contact with test site beta!
Observer, are you done over there?
I'm still selecting a location for the mainframe. How fast do you think I am?
I see. Then put that on hold for now.
...You're not about to tell me to go fight Magician, are you?
Me? Fight an Arbiter? You must be kidding.
Shut down and go into hiding at once – before she can seize control and take us unawares.
Otherwise, I'll be forced to dispose of you.
Ugh... Fine, I'm out of here.
Phew...
Requesting access to Antiochus database: Arbiter System Information.
Reading Arbiter IV to XIV backup data. Building simulations.
Magician... I've always considered you an eyesore.
It's time I made a move!
My disappearance came to be known as the Day the Stars Faded.
For a few days after, I stayed in the Sakuran pavilion due to safety concerns.
During my stay, I submitted my report on the incident, contacted my allies across the world, and confirmed that everything was back to normal.
After that, I contacted Elizabeth on an encrypted line and learned that the Ashes' reinforcements had never come to the NA Ocean Singularity.
She also informed me of the situation with test site beta and how the META Helena was hard at work on it.
I still couldn't reach Helena herself, and Camelot had lost contact with her.
Given what I knew so far, there was no doubt that she and Madam M – The Magician – were in the midst of a fierce battle.
I'd have had no way of intervening, and knowing their power, it seemed unlikely that either of them would come out seriously hurt.
All I could do was pray that their battle ended soon.
And finally, it was time for Akagi to return to the Sakura Empire.

sequence: Sardegna Empire
Former World Expo Venue
Sakura Empire Pavilion

scripts.say: You may leave me here, Commander.
This is a big moment for you. I don't mind coming with you if it makes it easier.
You'd... really come with me?
Of course. I have two or three days free, and I can make more time if I need to.
You mustn't. This is an internal matter, so it must be decided by my people.
If you were there, they may be too kind to me. I won't get the punishment I deserve.
Besides... Lady Nagato, Musashi, Mikasa – they're all working as a united front now.
But...
I'll be fine. I'm prepared for whatever may come.
Don't worry, Commander. I'll be there as well.
I've been away from home for a long time, but I believe I still have friends who will show deference to me.
I haven't forgotten our promise to travel together.
When this is all over, Commander... I'll be waiting for you. In the Sakura Empire.
Thanks, Akagi.
Commander. Friends. The Sakuran fleet will hereby take our leave.
I look forward to seeing you all again.
Thus, the Sakura Empire fleet departs.
There they go...
Getting a little sentimental?
She risked her life alongside us.
At first, I found her a little extreme... Now that we've spoken, though, I think differently of her.
There's more to Akagi than her mistakes. I hope she's able to atone for her past actions.
Goodness. Don't you think you should worry about yourself first?
Hm?
Don't go telling people you can make all the time in the world for them!
Ugh, get your priorities straight!
Oh... You mean the reformation?
Yes, that is what I mean! The reformation is back on the table thanks to all of this, and it's looking better than ever!
Siren forces are more disorganized now, too, with the loss of the mainframe... You have endless work to do, you know!
The winds of change are coming to the Azur Lane...
I have to think about the test site, too.
Now that the Experimental Framework is gone, should the truth be publicized?
How will the future shake out without the Sirens' intervention?
Problems that I'd thought "future me" would have to deal with are piling up in front of me right now.
The Sirens have brought war and destruction, but at the same time, they've pushed us to solve the X problem.
With their mainframe gone, that pressure is gone.
What of the people who don't know about the X? They're relieved by the reduced Siren threat, but how will they feel?
Does the Azur Lane truly have a reason to exist anymore?
We've been so focused on defeating the Sirens all this time.
But now that the Experimental Framework is gone... It doesn't really feel like we've won.
There are still Sirens who threaten the safety of this world.
The Arbiters watching us. The mysterious Observer Zero.
As long as their experiments continue – as long as we suffer as their guinea pigs – peace with the Sirens is impossible.
What's more, our true threat still lurks in the dark. The risk of it encroaching upon our world is ever-present.
This is no time to sit on our laurels.
We can't tell all the world everything about our enemy...
They'll be celebrating this false victory and fighting over the spoils for a time to come...
There's nothing we can do about it. We just have to protect the world.
The Azur Lane, Sirens, and our test site...
I suppose I won't have much free time, after all.
Right. I should return your handkerchief. It turned out to be a big help.
Oh... That's okay! It's a gift!
I thought it was your favorite?
Don't worry about it!
If you really want to thank me, then get me a new one.
Also... You said you're free for the next two days? Why don't we all go out together?
I can't wait to see a Sardegnian holiday!
An upbeat singing voice echoed through the boundless, starry night sky.
La la la la la~ Let's sing a little song~♪
La la la la la~ Sing it all day long~♪
Sing with me~ It's easy as can be~♪
If you're feeling down~ Turn that frown upside-down~♪
La la la la la~ I'm gonna get you bastards~♪
La la la la la~ Every last one of you~♪
Nothing would make me happieeer~♪
La la la la la~
Hmm?
What's this?
Fascinating...
Heeey! Don't run away from me!
Get back heeere!
Through the city, I walk.
Buildings line the streets.
Upon the earth, I walk.
Mountains and rivers intertwine.
Atop the seas, I walk.
Coastlines stretch on eternal.
In the skies, I walk.
The sun dyes the world white.
In purest white, I walk.
Through heaven, I walk.
Upon me, your eyes gaze.
On my ears, songs of adoration echo.
P HT AOL OPLYVWOHUA
"I am The Hierophant."
NVCLYUVY VM OHYTVUF, WYVTVALY VM KPZJVBYZL
"Governor of harmony, promoter of discourse."
JOVZLU MLD, NHAOLY HYVBUK
"Chosen few, gather around."
HJJLWA TF WYPUJPWSLZ, HUK LEAVS TF UHTL
"Accept my principles, and extol my name."
Following the conclusion of my meeting with Fritz Rumey, I formally became a member of the Resistance.
Not that I had much of a choice though, given that I'm stranded in this world.
On the bright side, they did have knowledge pertaining to my situation that they could share.
The records I've read say that cases like yours – an outlander suddenly vanishing into thin air – have happened numerous times before.
A popular theory from the time is that the outlanders returned to the worlds whence they came.
Since that is the case, I think you needn't worry about returning home for now.
As for what comes next, we'll take it one step at a time.
We also discussed the threat that this world faces, that being the so-called extradimensionals.
The way they were described reminded me of X.
Their surface-level looks are different, however. To find out more, I'll just have to fight them and see for myself.
I also brought up the Antiochus, and the response was interesting.
..."Antiochus"? I've never heard that word before. An unexpected alias for the Sirens, to be sure.
If you want information on them, I can provide that.
For, when you trace things back to their origin, they are inextricably linked with the development of our world as well as my very birth.
Rumey told me that the Sirens appeared out of nowhere in this world roughly 200 years ago.
In stark contrast to the extradimensionals, they came in peace.
It was thanks to these friendly aliens that the world's technological development accelerated exponentially.
As time went on, however, even the Sirens weren't spared from the hostility among the factions of the world. They were divided as well, sometimes even getting pulled into small-scale conflicts.
Even so, humanity believed that this golden age of rapid development for civilization would continue forever.
And so it did – at least until the extradimensionals struck.
As soon as their existence came to light, the whole world united under the banner of the Sirens and fought countless battles, until the Sirens' ultimate defeat.
Yet despite their victory, the extradimensionals strangely went no further. Their advance halted, and their power even seemed to subside.
That is how humankind's resistance organizations have managed to survive up to this day...
*knock knock*
Mandy! You there?
Z11 – another member of the Resistance – knocks on my door.
What's up?
You haven't had dinner yet, have you?
Nope.
Nobody eats dinner at four in the afternoon.
Good! Perfect! See, Duisburg is throwing a welcome party and you're invited!
Welcome party for who?
For you, duh! You're the guest of honor, so you can't, like, NOT attend. The girls would be literally heartbroken!
So, you coming or not?
Of course I'll come. Lead the way!
Huh? Wait, uh, umm... Don't you, like... know where our hideout is?
Why would I?
Right, of course... I guess I just have to, uhh, escort you...
Gotta make this as quick as possible...
*huff puff*... *huff puff*... Okay, I'm all good! Let's get going!
Something fierce inside her suddenly breaks out, and she drags me out of the break room at breakneck speed.
Sometime later...
On a beach you could hardly call pretty, Duisburg and her friends stand silently while watching the sunset.
Oh, there's the Commander! And Z11! You finally showed!
*pant*... *pant*... My work here is done... Can I go home now?
C'mon, are you serious? You're already here, so what reason do you have NOT to stick around for the party?
Aha... Ahahaha... You're doing the thing again, aren't you?
Z9, are you attending?
I mean, it's for the Commander, so... *sniffle*...
Ooof course... Fine, I'll stay!
Sweet!
Heehee. Your face just screams completely obvious. Let me explain.
Look over there. What do you see?
Duisburg points toward a fairly large island sitting in the periphery of the headquarters.
The two are connected by a bridge, and on that island stands a great structure that rivals the headquarters building in size.
That's our energy tower. It's our lifeline that powers not just the whole base, but also the Mirror Sea and even the Eternal Stars.
They say it's home to many secrets that still haven't been uncovered after many years, so it's just been left sitting there.
Is that where your hideout is?
What? No. It's got something to do with what we're about to do, though.
I'll let you in on a secret – there's a fish farm inside the tower.
Seriously?
Yeah. Since you're not keen on tube food, I was planning to politely borrow some fish to grill.
By "politely borrow," you mean steal?
It's called taking with appreciation!
She smiles a gentle smile.
Alright. How are you going to return the fish?
(Unless she plans on having us regurgitate them like birds...)
It doesn't matter as long as the population doesn't shrink.
She maintains her unwavering smile.
They'll spawn more, sooner or later!
So, you wanna come with and borrow some?
Well, it sounds fun, and I could use some work experience in this world.
Thought as much. Time to set off!
H-here we go!
Sometime later...
Whew... Good job, everyone. Have some coffee!
The fish will be done in just a minute.
Your clothes should be dry now, too, Commander. Those were some lively fish, huh?
(Operation Polite Catch was a success... and fun.)
(When was the last time I had this much fun?)
(Dammit... I really can't remember because of this cursed amnesia.)
Aaahhh! I messed up! Help, help!
Eek! Wh-what happened?!
I threw some gasoline on there 'cause the fire was looking weak, and, well... our food is getting burned!
Oh, for crying out loud... I SAID not to do it yourself.
One moment, Commander. I'll deal with this!
And so, me and the members of the Resistance had a fun night together.
Three days passed in the blink of an eye. The time to fight has finally come.
Commander {playername}, Rumey has directed me to relinquish command of this fleet to you.
But given the fact that this is your first mission, may I serve as your second-in-command?
I'd be happy to have you.
Duisburg knows a million times more than I do about these seas and so-called extradimensionals.
I wouldn't dream of turning down an offer like that.
Heheh. I'll make you proud.
Z52's recon fleet is en route from IB-AX-108 to 110, and Rumey has already set sail with her main fleet.
The amphibious and escort fleets are still on standby.
As for our own hunting fleet, our job is to secure the supply route at IB-AX-104, eliminate every enemy in sight, and collect samples from them.
But to think that we would need a sample from an extradimensional, of all things, to fix our radiation purgers...
IB-AX-104 is vast, but it's long been seen as relatively safe.
Recon shows nothing out of the ordinary as of eight hours ago, as well.
Well, isn't that convenient...
(If it really is safe, then dispersing our fleets makes for a more efficient search, yes. But something is fishy here...)
Anyway, we'd best get going.
After a smooth journey to IB-AX-103, we ran into them – the extradimensionals.
KABOOOM!
ROOOOOAR!
That's one heck of a horde! Is this what you call safe?
Not at all. This is the most we've seen in years!
But why today?
Commander, I urge a swift retreat! We can't fight off those numbers!
Agreed. Give the order to all ships to cover each other's immediate retreat. Contact our allied fleets and headquarters as well – Rumey needs to stop the mission at once.
Roger that!
KABOOOM!
ROOOOOAR!
As time passed, the horde only grew in number.
Things had turned from hopeful to hopeless in practically minutes.
We did everything in our power, but we lost contact with ship after ship.
Even retreat seemed an unlikely luxury at this point.
No... Why did it have to be today of all days?
Why...
A mission that we'd expected to be an easy success had ended in tragedy.
Duisburg's voice trembles from pain, sadness, and regret.
Commander... We're done for, aren't we?
I'm sorry for getting you involved in this. I...
KABOOOM!
Deathly silence fills the air.
Am I... dying?
Right here? This easily?
I haven't accomplished anything. I haven't even been able to get my memories back.
But this is how it ends...
KABOOOM!
Amidst the explosion of the mass-produced ship, my consciousness is thrown into the empty abyss.
SHUFFLE...
Then, I hear the sound of cards shuffling.

sequence: Time: Unknown
Location: Unknown

scripts.say: In a giant ship, one blue-haired girl gazed upon the galaxy before her.
Naraka and the NA Ocean Singularity are connected, and the Commander did enter the Singularity.
But something is tampering with the exit.
Memphis is off in another test site, and the Commander is missing...
No... It's as if test site beta has become an illusion altogether.
I can't find it anywhere. Where has the real test site beta gone?
Helena's cold eyes showed a hint of pain.
Passive radar and regular scans show no abnormalities. Our defenses haven't come up with any notifications, either.
If not for the Tower's resources being diverted to active scanning, I never would've seen through the test site's camouflage.
Something transferred the real beta elsewhere.
The ability to not just change its coordinates, but to make a branch-sized illusion and even jam the Tower's observational capabilities...
There's no doubt about it.
The Empress and the Magician...
So they've teamed up.
The glint in her eyes turned even colder.
Soulless beings lurking in the dark, coveting the Commander...
Add another grudge to this long-simmering hatred... Very well. Let's have at it, then.
BEEP BEEP!
Jintsuu. It's me.

sequence: Sardegna Empire
Former World Expo Venue
Sakura Empire Pavilion

scripts.say: After the Commander's disappearance, Akagi led the fleet who'd escaped from Naraka to Sardegna, hoping to get Amagi some necessary recuperation.
The Sakura Empire pavilion at the World Expo was left intact, owing to its popularity during the event.
However, much like the other pavilions of the World Expo, Shinano's new quarters were more than meets the eye.
Barriers everywhere...
Amazing that even the flowers in the garden are being cared for by the barriers.
I couldn't have imagined that such a simple pavilion would be so complex.
Perfectly defended, as well...
And would you look at that? It isn't just the building – there are layers going all the way from earth to sky.
Shinano, are we sure this is a Sakuran mansion and not some kind of Eagle Union doomsday bunker?
This one only oversaw construction, not design...
Oh, I suppose you're right.
Now that we're inside, have you received any more word from Yamato?
Wait, please...
She says the defenses are but a precautionary measure. Do not mind them...
They prevent interference of the mind, as well, so we may prepare without worry.
She intends to perform the Rite of Return in two days...
Eliminating the corrosion in Naraka, undoing the disturbance of the world's concepts, reviving those who fell in battle...
In the process, possibly even removing the mental interference being done to the Commander.
But before the rite, we must find the rupture in the world that was created by the Commander's disappearance...
By repairing it with the correct memories and concepts, those which only we have...
We can greatly bolster our chance of success.
Treating our Sakuran allies and rescuing the Commander. Two birds with one stone, indeed.
However, if the Rite of Return is in only two days, then that puts a lot of pressure on us to find and repair that rupture.
Leave that to Helena and me. Information processing is what we do.
That's right. I'd do that and more for the Commander's sake!
Of course. We all harbor the same love for the Commander, yes, but our skills are quite different.
I-I guess...?
Ryuuhou and I will help, too!
Gladly!
Heehee. Let us all endeavor for those we love.
Ah... She also says that it may help if we have any objects that connect us to the Commander.
Objects that connect us... Oh!
The brooch from Clemenceau... No, better yet! The handkerchief I gave the Commander!
A handkerchief... Perfect! Our chances of success rise ever more...
What a lucky little coincidence.
Also... Yamato says that, since Kaga's soul is secure, she must be returned to normal soon...
The mind will remain hers, but incorporated with memories beyond the limited scope of the sample...
As long as I'm still me, I don't mind.
Then we must begin preparing the rite per Yamato's instructions...
I must agree with my sister. Let's do our best to bring our Commander back.
The light recedes, and I find myself inside a bright classroom.
*pant*... *pant*... *pant*...
The chill from my brush with death still lingers around me. The warm sunlight is enough to make me dizzy.
What happened?
Did I dream up all of that? Or is this the dream?
Heehee. Death is not at all a pleasant experience. Take your time getting used to it.
A purple-haired woman walks forward from the teacher's podium, smiling as she does.
I remember you. You and this classroom.
I've been here before... haven't I, Madam M?
Sounds like some of your memories are back.
Can't remember much more than that, though. Are you responsible for my amnesia?
...They say that seeing an old friend's face can help an amnesiac recover some of their memories.
Are you saying you're the old friend here? You don't feel like it to me.
I don't? What a shame.
So she says, yet there isn't the faintest trace of disappointment in her expression.
Anyway, let's move on to discussing your current problem.
Yes, let's. What in the world is going on?
Do you remember the two things I guaranteed you? The right to search, and the opportunity to choose.
Are you ready to make your choice?
There you go, talking nonsense again. How does that have anything to do with figuring out who I am?
It depends on what you manage to take from your search.
Take the Sirens, for instance. What are your thoughts about them?
The Sirens, huh...
Their arrival in that world ushered in a technological golden age, and they must've played an instrumental role in their battle against the invaders.
Although their efforts ended in failure, the things they left behind helped with humanity's resistance.
Wait, are you trying to hint that the Sirens and those extradimensionals are natural enemies, and that's why they were defeated?
I'm not hinting at anything. I just love seeing your mind at work.
What was it all, then? An elaborate illusion you created for me?
That depends on what you think. If you think it was real, then it was. If you think it was fake, then fake it is.
Expressionless as always, she utters yet more esoteric drivel.
Reality or fiction? This question isn't particularly important.
Excuse me?
I'm saying that it doesn't matter one way or the other to us.
You're not concerned with the veracity of things, are you?
This search came to a tragic end for you. Supposing that I said it was all real, what would you say then?
I'd say I regret making such an atrocious mistake, but I'm grateful for being rescued.
If I'd known more about the enemy and shared some thoughts with Rumey, I might've been able to concentrate our forces and achieved a different result.
Then if I were to tell you that it was all smoke and mirrors, would your thoughts on the matter change at all?
No, but this and that are two different matters.
If it was real, then it was a complete and irreparable tragedy.
But, if it was fake, you could call it an extremely valuable simulation.
Should I face a similar situation in the future, I'll have greater odds of weathering the storm thanks to what I learned here.
Those are the same thing.
If you want to retry it, then just give it another shot and try something different. Why wait for the future to come?
What are you saying? That I should revisit your illusion and make better choices?
I don't remember saying it was an illusion.
Well, if it was real, then what's done is done. How could I start over?
That's what I'm wondering. What you should be thinking about is this: If you do get a chance to start over, will you take it?
Of course I will. I'll keep on changing things until there's no more sadness.
Then that's what you should do.
The light outside the classroom windows grows blindingly bright, enveloping everything in pure whiteness.
You will always have freedom of choice.
And when you're not sure which choice to make...
Exhaust all options until you're confident in your answer.
As the bright whiteness fades away, my consciousness is cast into the darkness.
When I open my eyes again, I'm greeted by the ceiling of the break room, instilling in me an awareness of the flow of time.
The communicator by my bedside is blinking. I press the on button and hear a voice message from Duisburg.
We've made a few discoveries that I thought you should know about.
Our engineers found some rather valuable components among the things we salvaged yesterday.
These will let us finally accomplish our goal of fixing our radiation purgers.
They also–
She enthusiastically told me about the fruits of their salvage operation. It was all the same as before day three.
6 AM... I'm back, just like Madam M said I'd be.
I've got to make use of this second chance.
(Six hours to go until Rumey's address. Nothing will change if she announces her operation and assigns missions just like before.)
(That means six hours is all I have to alter Rumey's plans.)
(A lot of things to do, with a tight deadline, to boot... First thing's first – coming up with a new strategy.)
Since I already had many ideas, I managed to finish the battle plan in roughly three hours.
The next thing I did was call Duisburg and ask her to schedule my meeting with Rumey earlier.
Although she was naturally stunned by my sudden suggestion, she nevertheless passed my word on to Rumey out of curiosity.
Approximately 30 minutes later...
...A change to my operation plan?
Since I already knew how she thinks, I rushed through the introductions before immediately presenting my revised plan.
Hmm. This is an interesting direction.
My revisions focus on three things: The concentration of our forces, additional scouting of the area, and units committed to collecting samples.
These will improve our probability of completing our main objectives at the cost of potential secondary gains throughout the operation.
You came up with all of this solely because Duisburg called you?
You must have been truly a one-of-a-kind commander prior to your amnesia.
Needless to say, she is oblivious to the reasons behind this new plan.
I decide not to say anything in response to her compliment to avoid introducing more complexity.
Still, your plan seemingly takes the presence of an enemy ambush for granted.
Why is that?
Better safe than sorry. The opening phase of a counteroperation is especially crucial.
Her gaze holds me under scrutiny, but I calmly reply with my prepared response.
(She'd think I'm crazy if I told her I've already seen what's going to happen.)
(My amnesia is cause for suspicion enough. The last thing I want to do is declare myself a prophet.)
I... see.
Thankfully, my identity as a commander from a different time and place lends me enough prestige for Rumey to accept my proposal.
Your plan is a most valuable one. I will include your changes to mine.
Furthermore, I want you in command of my main force during the operation in three days. Will you accept the responsibility?
It would be my pleasure.
Excellent. For choosing to stay with the Resistance, I am much obliged.
Let us speak again later. Right now, I must concentrate on my address.
Roger that. By the way, there's one more thing I want to discuss...
Despite my slight hesitance, I tell her about my idea to investigate the Eternal Stars and gather intel on both our enemies and the Sirens.
To my surprise, she readily approves of it.
(While my memories are hazy, I'm confident that I'm inextricably linked to the Antiochus' systems.)
(If I can get a full grasp on the weapons they left behind, they'll be a powerful insurance policy in the battles to come.)
(What information we'll gain from investigating the Eternal Stars over these three days will be key.)
Camera settings... Check!
Parameter adjustments... Check!
Recording... Now!
Gooood morning to everyone working in the Sea of Stars! The current time is a fresh n' early 0410, but...
Doesn't it feel a bit early to be saying good morning?
Well, whatever~ By the time you see this show, the sun should already be high in the sky!
So, good morning it is! We'll roll with that!
...But wait, you never know what sort of freak accidents might delay the broadcast... Say, what if we moved things to tomorrow morning instead?
No, shoot, that defeats the entire purpose! ...Okay, cut! We're just gonna start from the top!
Let's try this again! Gooood morning to everyone working in the Sea of Stars!
I'm Eagle Union CB-2, Guam, the beautiful shipgirl presenter you all know and love!
The current time is 0410 in the morning! Even the busy hangar area is all empty right now. Ooh, there might be spooky monsters in hiding!
Now! As the more perceptive among you may have guessed...
"No way, Guam. Are you about to investigate spooky ghost stories?"
Exactly! You would be correct!
Some of you may not be aware of the rumors of hauntings in the Union's own Sea of Stars research facility, so let me tell you all about it.
We're here to pick up a teammate, Guam, not to film a show.
Plus, I don't recall hearing about any ghost stories around this place.
Ooh! You know, you're right! We DID come here to greet a friend!
As for the spooky rumors, they're all made up! Trust the science, everyone! Don't fall for hoaxes!
That's probably the least authoritative statement I've ever heard....
I choose my words carefully, you know~♪
By the way, the liaison craft is about to arrive. You should probably put away your camera.
No can do, Northampton! This is the moment I came for – to capture the plane's touchdown on camera!
San Jacinto was practically begging me to get footage of Princeton arriving~
Something to the effect of, "I wanna see that stuffy-and-serious Princeton get all starry-eyed like a little kid!"
Who was I to turn her down? Of course, I don't offer my services for free.
As payment, I had her leak me Constellation's itinerary for today. I am SO not getting stuck in another one of those meetings!
...You'd better hope Constellation doesn't hear that.
It's fiiiiiiine. Besides, I can always edit it out later.
Shhhh. You hear that? I think the liaison craft's here.
According to the app... we're supposed to go this way...
What an enormous hangar... I was told they built a facility deep inside the mountains, but isn't this just overkill?
Now then... Do I go down from here...? Or keep heading down this hallway in front of me? Ugh, it feels like a labyrinth in here...
Laffey, stay close to me. Feels like I might never find you again if we get separated.
Okay...
But seriously, how did they even manage to build an enormous megastructure like this...
And these walls, too... I don't think I've seen this kind of high-tech material used anywhere else before...
Ugh... Maybe I should try asking for directions after all. Can't make heads or tails of this place...
I think there's someone up ahead... Hello? Excuse me?
Wait, it's Louisville! Have you been assigned to the Sea of Stars, too?
Princeton and Laffey? Is something wrong?
Umm, we're on our way to the Rigging Design Department... Hercules, I believe?
Actually, I was just stationed here, so I don't exactly know my way around either.
But, now that you mention it, I also happen to be headed for the same place.
Huh, that's convenient. Then, uh... shall we join forces?
It's Louisville! And Princeton and Laffey came, too!
Better get my shot ready...
Three, two, one... Surprise!
*pop!* *pop!* *pop!*

- Aaaaah! 
- Wh-what was that?!
Welcome... to the Sea of Stars!
I'm Guam, the beautiful shipgirl presenter of this facility! And here with me is Northampton! The two of you were just assigned here, right?
Yes, ma'am! I am the Independence-class ship Princeton, and I've been reassigned from the NY City Fleet! From today onward, I will be stationed at the Sea of Stars!
Allow me to introduce Laffey. And...
My name is Louisville. It's a pleasure to meet you.
You didn't just get here today, did you, Louisville? Uh... Anyway, thanks for coming all the way to this facility. We'll show you around.
Thank you! Incidentally, why the cameras...? Are you filming something?

- Yep! 
- No.

- It's a special program! 
- Guam planned all this just to skip meetings...
- You should help me film! - Ignore her. Let's get going.
U-umm...?
H-hey, it's fine~ We were going to show you two around anyway, so it's not like it really matters one way or the other♪
I've been here for a long time, so I know a lot about this place!
From showing you the facilities to spooky ghost stories, leave it all to me♪
Ask me anything, anytime!
...In that case, I do have one question...
When will I get to meet Saratoga?
Saratoga? She's not here.
...Huh?
Th-then what about Alaska? She's in charge, right...?
Alaska? Uh, she does work in the Management Department, but... Saying she's in charge sounds kind of misleading...
Well, it is a secret research facility, so I guess it's to be expected that outsiders won't know much about it.
Alaska's out on official business, so she isn't in the Sea of Stars right now.
...Really?
And the Commander is in Europa, too... Hmm...
Whoa, you look crushed... Don't tell me. Did you ask them to assign you here just so you could meet Saratoga and Alaska?
Oh, not quite. I was assigned here to help research Type II Independence-class rigging.
If they aren't here, then I'll simply accept that... Guam, may I ask questions about work as well?
I've put together a list of questions that arose during the information-gathering process. I'd like you to take a look, if you don't mind...
(Did this girl just pull out a whole notebook?! Wow, that writing is DENSE!)
(Oh, no. I can't handle super serious people like her...!)
Umm... I'll let Northampton handle those questions. She's good at that stuff♪
Which one of us told her to feel free to ask "anything, anytime," again?
Yes, it was me! And would you look at that; she asked me stuff! I didn't say I'd definitely answer all of her questions!
Anyway, that's enough standing around...
I'll show you around and handle the camera, and Northampton can explain the facilities...
How's that for dividing the labor! Let's get going!

sequence: This is Fortress. Correspondence attempt number 182.
No response.
"I see... Try again in two hours, please."
Princeton, you've been working for seventy-two hours straight.
You should rest, for the sake of the well-being of yourself and others.
"Fine. I'll leave the fleet in your care."
Orders received. Good night.
"Good night."

scripts.say: NY City Simulation - Testing Area
Regulation reminder: four, the simulation will be terminated if you attempt to communicate with the Arbiter vessel in any way, shape, or form.
Please acknowledge.
I know. We'll stick to the rules.
Acknowledgment received. Generating Arbiter vessel and commencing combat performance test.
A hulking beast clad in black armor approached from the horizon.
There was a massive tank hung on the beast's back, filled with a liquid substance that vaporized into a red steam that blanketed the area.
At its front was an armored protrusion, like a knight's helmet...
And atop it sat a little girl wearing a black, frilly dress.
So, before we get this thing started, a quick self-introduction.
My model ID is The Devil XV, but you can just call me Devil.
I'm a second-generation Antiochus specializing in battlefield support. Frankly, taking head-on fights isn't my forte.
The purpose of today's experiment is to gauge how Antiochus and KAN-SEN fight both against and alongside each other. Mostly the latter.
(She's talking to us, like a civilized person?)
(That's unlike what I've come to expect from the Sirens...)
Hm? What's the matter? Aren't you gonna say anything?
I'll hear out your questions, if you have any.
So you don't talk much. That's fine, I–
KABOOOM!
What the hell?! Don't shoot me before we've even started! Have some decency!
(I don't like this... I'm starting to feel kinship with a Siren.)
(Why is she so different? I don't think we've fought any Arbiter as talkative as her before.)
KABOOOM!
Fine! I'll just come at you with all I have!
Good. Engaging Annihilation Mode!
KABOOOM!
Ugh... It's so unresponsive...
...Ah. You haven't figured out all the ins and outs of your rigging yet.
Guns and torpedoes alone won't do. Use your drones as well.
And Princeton, while your attacks and support are on point, it's time to bite the bullet and change gear.
I'm way ahead of you in terms of damage caused... yet, for some reason, the system has declared ME the loser.
So whatever. The test is over.
Why are you still here? Don't you have things to do?
(That's weird. TB should appear now that the test is over.)
Laffey, keep your guard up. I'll contact the control room.
Okay.
BEEP BEEP!
Nobody's answering...?
(What do we do now? Is this normal in the Sea of Stars?)
(No, what am I saying? There's nothing normal about our communications being down!)
(Dammit... I've seriously got caught up in an incident on my first day here...)
(How are we supposed to fix this?!)
Oh. Can't get in touch with HQ, is that it?
Let me give it a shot. Testing connection, calling exercise coordinators...
...Nope, mine doesn't work either. We're all cut off from them.
Nothing is wrong with this area itself, so maybe you've had an equipment malfunction back home.
Glaring at me won't solve anything.
I already admitted defeat, okay? I'll escort you back to your base. Come on, hop on my rigging.
Okay, you clearly don't want to hitch a ride.
Maybe I should get a new rigging that's less frightening to children...
I get it already! Let's all just wait here if that's what you want!
The connection is only temporarily unstable anyway. It should come back if we give it some time.

sequence: This is Fortress. Correspondence attempt number 1853.
No response.
"Hey, do you think we'll ever be able to go home?"
I can't give a definite answer to that question.
But I can say this – don't lose hope.
There is always hope.
"You're right... It's funny – I never expected you to cheer me up."
You're welcome.

scripts.say: Unknown Simulation - Unknown Location
A pure white light blinded Constellation. When her vision returned, a landscape covered in ice and snow unfolded before her.
Beyond the horizon was a colossal structure made of metal and ice, towering toward the clouds.
Surrounding it were shards of ice, decorating it. This was the Crown.
Reality Lens connection is stable... I've safely entered the abnormal data.
I'm... guessing this place is where the Crown of the Polar North is. It's a long way from the Coral Sea...
This is a surprise, to say the least.
Why was there data on the Crown amongst what we recovered from the Coral Sea?
It doesn't make any sense...
This is baaad, Constellation. I think we've lost connection with the control room.
What? But that shouldn't be possible in the Reality Lens...
No, wait. I think that happened when the Commander was investigating Anchorage's hull abnormalities.
The Commander connected to the Reality Lens, lost connection with the control room, then wound up in a different simulation...
It's a good thing we came here. There HAS to be something hidden in the abnormal data.
TB should call us when the connection is back online. Let's inspect the area until then.
I think... this Crown isn't the same as the one we're familiar with.
For sure. It has energy surging inside of it. It almost looks like it's alive.
That's what's odd about it.
The Crown we know of is an inactive Singularity.
Amid a Reenactment between the Royal Navy and Iron Blood, Enterprise META – who the Sirens call "Code G" – tried to activate it.
But, as we later found out, the Sirens managed to stop her.
And ever since then, the Crown has been under Siren control.
But, for some reason...
This Crown is up and running.
Remember, we're in a construction based on abnormal data gathered from a simulation. This Crown doesn't HAVE to be the same one we know about.
That would make the situation even worse.
Because if so, there has been a second Crown this whole time that we didn't know existed.
But at the same time... how did it fly under not just our noses, but the Northern Parliament's noses as well?
Even a Mirror Sea wouldn't be able to hide an active Crown. It releases way too much energy.
Active, inactive... It's not active right now, and yet it's also running...
What if it's an artificial Singularity, like Iron Blood's Tower of Midgard?
Like, it's not active at this very moment, but it was at some point in the past, and we didn't know about it...
You're saying this data is from the time the Crown WAS active?
That does make sense, and it IS possible. But we don't have hard evidence that it was.
There is no way there was a lapse in monitoring across every single faction, and even if the Crown was hidden inside a Mirror Sea, energy would leak out of it if it was activated.
The only conceivable explanation is that it was activated before we had all established systems to monitor the Crown.
What I don't understand is – why was this data in a simulation of the Coral Sea?
Did it travel through time and–
KRRRGGHHH!
A booming rumble broke the silence of the night, interrupting Constellation's train of thought.
Wh-what was that?!
Good lord... Constellation, look! A black tornado!
A storm formed from pure malice appeared out of nowhere in the distance.
Not long after the initial rumble subsided, a dark barrier stretched from the seas to the heavens.
Dark clouds rapidly spread across the ocean and the sky, leeching the light even from the energy in the Crown's heart.
It's coming toward us!
Quickly, Jacinto! We need to get out of here!
Meanwhile, inside the Sea of Stars control room...
Warning: hostile data detected in Reality Lens.
Warning: quarantine sequence could not be initiated.
Warning: processing load of defense systems is approaching critical levels. Risk of hostile data breach increasing.
Warning...
Warning sirens blared while the control room was flooded with error messages, painting it a strobing red.

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: Aaahhh! It's red... The screen has turned red!

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: TB, what's happening? What do we do?
The Galactic Core's systems are under attack by a hostile program.
Emergency quarantine measures have been initiated.
The attack is coming from within the Sea of Stars and is propagating at an extremely high rate. The defense systems will cease functioning shortly. Our only option is to initiate crisis mode.

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: Crisis... mode...?
Affirmative. Please break the emergency glass on the third control panel.
Specifically, the glass panel with a red frame immediately under your right hand. Please break it and push the biggest button.

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: Red glass, red glass... There!

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: Break the glass... Push the button... Okay!
Orders received. Verifying credentials...
Credentials verified. Executing emergency orders and putting all systems in crisis mode.
Commencing hostile program countermeasures.
Princeton and Laffey were still in the NY City simulation, only now the city had been so devastated as to render it unrecognizable.
The buildings on the horizon were burning and crumbling. This was the work of a black tornado, appearing suddenly and ravaging everything in mere minutes.
Did the Sea of Stars generate that black tornado, too?
But... why? Why do that?
Just for show? This IS a testing area, so it's not like it's any harm done...
Princeton, there are enemies coming toward us...
Enemies?
Huh... All I see is mist. I have no idea if those are ships or not.
Oh, wait, the Commander's files said something about this!
They were described as hostile entities that took the form of mist, appearing at the same time as a black tornado did.
So... we're fighting mist now?
No, but it sounds like that if you didn't read the files.
To put it simply, that mist is a projection of something or someone from a higher dimension.
They're not in our dimension, per se, which is why they look so hazy. It's also why we can't take measurements of them.
Got it. I'll be careful... Get ready to fight.
KABOOOM!
Princeton, you okay?
Yeah! Thanks for the cover!
But with these numbers... Plus, they show up out of nowhere and won't get off our tails.
It's okay. I'll deal with them somehow.
I'll keep you safe.
Sorry I couldn't catch up with you sooner. I suddenly remembered a bunch of stuff at once.
I see. So, you've been using my data to run your simulations.
Typical... Leave it to Tower to muddy the waters.
(What the...? She sounds so different all of a sudden!)
You're not a simulation... are you?
Uh-oh...
Princeton, remember the regulations...
Regulations? So THAT'S why you wouldn't say a word.
Well, I've already broken them, so it doesn't matter now...
Devil, I don't care whether you're real or a simulation. I'm taking you down.
Taking me down? Now?
...Say, do you have any idea how much of a mess you're in right now?
We're going to take you down... no matter what it takes.
Oh boy... If you think getting a game over here will bring you back to reality, I have bad news for you.
...What are you talking about? Once the simulation is over...
Do you know where you are right now?
Inside a simulation created by the Sea of Stars' systems?
And, do you know where that simulation space is located?
Actually, let's go on step further. Do you know how the "Galactic Core" is even able to generate simulated worlds in the first place?
I-I don't know. I just arrived at the Sea of Stars, so...
Really? First day on the job, and you got caught up in this mess. Ahahah!
How interesting. It really does make me feel better knowing there are folks out there with luck even worse than mine.
Since I'm in a good mood, I'll let you in on a little something. You see...
...Don't tell them? And who are you, telling me what not to do?
...Ah, of course. You've gotten good at concealing yourself.
...Fine, then I won't tell them. I'll just watch what happens.
...You'll really set me free if help you out?
...I already have a plan – to run off amidst all the chaos.
...That's a good idea. We have a deal.
Who are you talking to?
Nobody. My speech synthesizer was just on the fritz.
Listen up – I hate dealing with those Harbingers as much as you do.
So I'm going to help you out this one time.
Help you as much as this vessel is able to, anyway...
It's a cheap knockoff, but it's better than nothing.
I'll do something about those mist entities. You two run that-a-way in the meantime.
Yeah, toward that glowing thing. I'll send Laffey the exact coordinates.
Go through that and you'll be able to exit the simulation. Now go.
L-Laffey?
Yeah, the communications system sent me some coordinates. Glowy coordinates...
Seems we have no choice but to go and check it out.
You're off the hook this time, Devil. Let's go, Princeton.
In the Sea of Stars control room, TB's battle with the hostile data raged on.

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: TB, it glowed again...

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: I'll break the glass!
Don't worry, Anchorage.
In crisis mode, I have full control of all resources within the Sea of Stars.

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department

scripts.say: In other words, there's no need for you to break the glass.
Status report: I've successfully isolated the hostile data within a sandbox.
At this time, it is impossible to delete the data.
Due to the hostile data's attack on our communications system, I've taken the system offline to physically isolate it from said data.
It will be impossible to leave the control room or communicate with the outside. I'm sorry.

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: It's okay. I'm right here...

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: TB, go!

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: Fight that data!

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: I'll draw you a picture!
Thank you for that.
Question: why have you mentioned the act of drawing?

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: Huh? Don't you draw, too?

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: You drew that on the screen. It's cute.
On the screen?
That is no drawing. It's simply a visual display of the affected area.

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: But it looks like a drawing...

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: Umm... Like a beacon?

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: And letters... U, C...
Beacons, letters... Synchronizing analysis module.
Performing visual data verification. No similar patterns found.

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: TB... You don't see it?

scripts.factiontag: Advanced KAN-SEN Research and Planning Department
scripts.say: It's okay... I'll draw it!

sequence: This is Fortress. Correspondence attempt number 3122.
No response.
"I didn't expect them to run into Harbingers... What's the damage report?"
Three Raptor-class ships were moderately damaged. One Klyatva-class ship was lightly damaged.
The shields of flagship Calabrian Pride have been overloaded.
"The situation is still under control. Engage Ixion III to initiate repairs."
"You'll have to handle Calabrian Pride's shields yourself."
"Really, do they even know what a flagship is? The point isn't for it to rush in at the front."
I've detected a space-time distortion in the surrounding area.
"Will we be able to go home?!"
Warning: Distress signal received from a Council beacon.
Per protocol, we must go to their rescue immediately.
"A United Council beacon...?"
"Then... We received communications from home?!"
Coordinates pinpointed.
"Let's change course. We're going home..."
"No. We're going to SAVE our home!"

scripts.say: Somewhere, in an unknown location...
The twilit sea was covered in a veritable layer of wreckage.
...We got away.
Princeton, where are we?
...Princeton?
Princeton... Where are you?
Nobody answered Laffey's calls. There were no signs of life on the sea, so calm that it looked like a mirror's surface.
Princeton... is gone...?
BEEP BEEP!
Laffey, can you hear me?
Guam...?
Phew... I saw that ray of light come down from the sky, but I didn't think it would be you...
Are Princeton and Northampton with you?
Northampton left the exercise early...
Princeton was with me until just a minute ago.
We were running from the black tornado, and then she was gone...
Running from a black tornado...? So were we!
Wait, you and Princeton got separated?!
Laffey, don't move a muscle! I'm on my way!
...When I went to the coordinates the Arbiter gave us, I was warped here.
It sounds almost supernatural...
*sob*... I thought this was a simulation, but then Devil suddenly started talking... It was so scary...
Argh... All this crazy stuff is happening, and I can't even broadcast it!
Princeton was going with Laffey to the exit, but she disappeared when Laffey warped here!
We can't reach her over comms. Maybe she was warped somewhere else!
Why do I feel like I've been dragged into a hot mess?!
Aaaaaaaaah!
San Jacinto, wh-where's the tornado?! It's not chasing us, is it?!
Phew... I don't see it around... I-it looks like we managed to get to safety.
...Constellation?
...Huh?
Wh-what's going on? Louisville? Flasher? Laffey? Why are you all here...?
More importantly... Where are we?
Uh, so it's a long story...
Do I have to explain everything again...
If you don't mind, Laffey! Pretty please!
Laffey's group was in the NY City experiment zone, while Guam's was in the Coral Sea. Both were chased off by the black tornado...
There must have been a major malfunction at the Galactic Core.
Could it have happened while I was investigating the abnormal data...?
Everyone, I'm sorry.
It's all my fault. If I wasn't so anxious to make progress...
Everyone tried to stop me, too, especially poor Flasher...
If only I'd been more careful... *sniffle*...
*sob*... I-it's okay... As long as you're okay, Stella, everything's gonna be fine...
Yeah! Hear that, Stella? We're fine as long as you're fine!
...Why are you calling me that, too?
Just livening up the show as any good star should!
There's no use crying over spilled milk. What's done is done.
Besides, it's not like it's the worst-case scenario.
TB said there wasn't any danger when you analyzed the data, right? So there was no way of knowing this would happen when you used the Reality Lens to study it.
Unless you just never studied it, this would've happened sooner or later.
It sucks that so many of us got wrapped up in it, but that just means we can all help each other out of this mess!
Imagine if you were the only one connected. Now THAT would be the worst case.
...Th-thank you for trying to console me...
Not even! This is rational analysis. You mentioned the Commander before you connected, too.
What kind of situation did the Commander get into? What adventures awaited, and how did the Commander escape danger?
You gave an example, and I say we should learn from it. Right?
Either way, no feeling sorry for ourselves! You know the Sea of Stars the most of all of us, so we're relying on you!
But you wouldn't all be in danger if I hadn't done anything, so relying on me is just...
Fine, then. Constellation, take responsibility and get us all outta here!
Ahahaha... You know how to hit her where it hurts.
Heheh. Do I?
Cheer up, Stella... I know you can get us all home safe!
Right! You can do it, Constellation!
We should find Princeton, too... *yawn*...
O-of course... I don't have time to feel sorry for myself right now...!
For the sake of those who believe in me, I have to do everything in my power to take everyone home!
There you go! You're on fire!
And don't you worry – I'll record all of your efforts for you!
Things might not be great right now, but it's cool if I record, right?
Of course. Those recordings will be necessary later.
Record as much as you like. When we get back, I'll have the Analysis Department go through the footage. I'll see that it's returned to you once they're done.
Woohoo!
Sorry to put you on the spot, but what's the plan, Boss?
U-umm... First, let's... search our surroundings? Yes, let's do that.
There must be a reason we were brought to the same place from simulations made by different machines.
Let's look around and find some clues!
Stella, my salvager is picking up a strange reading!
I knew there had to be something that gathered us all here in one place.
The signal source is underwater... I'll go have a look-see!
A while later, Flasher resurfaced with a metallic object in hand.
I'm back, Stella!
I found this th-thing!
Wait, I thought your salvage gear was designed to retrieve data?
Are you saying it can do regular salvage, too?
Ordinarily, you'd use the salvager to scan an object's data and send it to the Sea of Stars, but there's no telling if the Sea of Stars is operating at normal capacity now...
And there's no analysis device here, so... I just b-brought this thing up with me...
You've got a point. Analyzing it ourselves is our only option in this case.
Stella, this object gives off readings pretty similar to the abnormal data we found in the Coral Sea simulation!
It does? Let me have a look...
Flasher handed the device to Constellation, who began to inspect it.
Hmm... Metallic exterior. Structurally divided into two parts.
The stand is ten centimeters and the main unit is thirty. It looks like some sort of transmitter.
Considering the material, it's quite lightweight... The panel is damaged, leaving its circuitry exposed. It's clearly broken.
Manufacturer information... No, the letters are too worn to read.
Have you figured anything out?
Only that it's horribly destroyed. So, nothing useful.
Judging by the stand, I believe it's a floating transmitter. Meaning, it's a small beacon.
A... beacon?
Yes, the kind that aids in navigation. It might be what's responsible for warping us all here.
The strangest thing about this place is that, unlike those other simulations, it doesn't exist amongst the data we have.
So how in the world did we end up here? The only thing I can think of is that the Sea of Stars and the Reality Lens are linked to that future the Commander got sent to, but...
Uhh, I'm not following you. What exactly are you talking about?
Why we got warped here. All I have now is speculation, though.
At any rate, we have a clue as to how we got here. The next thing is to figure out what this place is.
Jacinto, did your aerial reconnaissance find anything?
I'll cut to the chase. There is absolutely nothing in the sea or on the islands.
There are no fish in the water or animals on land. Nor are there any signs of vegetation, insects, or even fungal life.
Finally, the thing that looks like a mountain range in the distance is actually a huge heap of trash.
To put it in other words, this space is made up almost entirely of man-made stuff.
Oh, and there is a flying artificial island not far from here. Almost looks Siren-made, if you ask me.
Here's a photo.
Oh... I recognize this. That's one of the Sirens' floating fortresses.
What's that tucked away in the corner? Some kind of materials storehouse?
It seems the Sirens are carrying out a huge resource collection project in this sea. Or maybe they've taken to recycling.
Either way, I've never seen anything like this.
Oh! What if we've happened upon a secret supply base of theirs?
That gives me an idea! Hang on a sec...
Guam cupped her hands together, scooped up a handful of seawater, and drank it in one gulp.
Wh-what are you doing?!
Um, there's water right here if you're thirsty, Guam.
Drinking water from the sea could make you sick...
I wasn't sure if the simulation ran that deep, but it was worth it to test my theory.
Jacinto, you must've gotten a good view of this area with your planes. Are you sure this is a sea?
Well... Yeah? Why do you ask?
Because I couldn't taste the sea in the seawater. It just tasted like water.
Really? I need to see for myself...
...You're right. It's no different from regular tap water. I don't like what that implies.
Flasher, did you bring any equipment that can analyze water?
Y-yeah, I did!
Great. Run an analysis on this sample.
Stella, it's done...
Not even trace amounts of minerals, let alone any salt. Nothing more than two hydrogens and an oxygen.
In other words, this entire ocean is made of distilled water.
That's so weird. Did the Sirens, like, filter out all the minerals?
Then this would be purification on an unprecedented scale. Seawater consists of around 3% salt, so...
BEEP BEEP!
I'm getting weird readings on my IFF system...
Weird readings? Can you glean anything from them?
Nope... Only their identification signals.
At least they're within radar detection range.
The terrain here is rather messy, so maybe the signals are from a Siren fleet in hiding?
Broadcasting ID signals isn't something Sirens typically do.
Though I guess they could be doing it to lure us into a trap.
I'm getting another signal, but this time it's different. I can't identify it...
If I may ask, how come only you are able to receive these signals anyway?
Might be because her rigging isn't her original rigging, but rather built on simulation data.
If I were them and I was waiting in ambush, I wouldn't want to put my target on high alert by sending signals to them.
Whoever's broadcasting these is most likely trying to tell us that they know we're here.
...At any rate, we won't get anything done by standing around.
Laffey, send an identification signal back. We'll see how they respond and go from there.
Sea of Stars - Accessway
Every block in the Sea of Stars has a codename based on a constellation family.
Take the Rigging Design Department, for instance. It's part of the Engineering Block, and therefore falls under Hercules.
So, that's what it means when you hear something like the "Hercules Rigging Design Department."
It's also where the three of us will be working from now on.
Meanwhile, our lovely presenter here, Guam, is a part of the Secret Service Block's Special Operations Force. She's basically a glorified mercenary.
Hey, that's uncalled for! I fight for what's beautiful and right, thank you very much!

Grouping the various departments under distinct constellation families is an interesting concept. It really fits the theme of this place!
Sure is. All the science, experiments, and related things happen over in the Research Block, dubbed Perseus.
And the Directive Block, Heavenly Waters, is associated with medicine, intelligence, decision-making, and the like.
There are so many departments in the Sea of Stars that it's difficult to remember what they all do, but the codenames should at least help you narrow down their general purpose.
I'm sure you'll pick up on the individual names in due time.
If you don't mind me asking, what department does Saratoga belong to?
Oh, she's not actually a part of any specific department. She's more like an advisor to the administrative board.
Unfortunately, I don't know much else beyond that.
I see... What about Alaska, then?
She is a part of the Sea of Stars administrative board, and also a member of Argo Navis, a special subdivision of the Directive Block also known as the Strategic Department.
