I knew all along that Wisdom Cubes and those crystals were completely different.
But, even if they don't work like Cubes do, maybe – just maybe – they have the power to fix her hull.
Lex has been debilitated ever since that battle, and we've still not found any way to cure her.
And while we don't know any cure, maybe the Sirens or whoever controls them does.
You have to understand... I'm desperate, Commander. I need something that can save her.
So desperate I was willing to walk into a trap all on my own... But people came with me, and I couldn't just tell them it was a trap...
And now they're all here, and it's my fault... Because I didn't have the courage to tell them...
Listen to me. You're not the only one to whom Lex is important.
She taught me so much when I was studying at the academy, and she was always there during my stint in the Eagle Union.
She isn't just a shipgirl under my command. She's a friend and a person close to my heart.
We made a promise, you and I. To save Lexington, whatever it took. I would never go back on that promise.
So trust me when I say this – you can't carry this burden all by yourself.
But... It's too late now...
Lexington's condition is stable. We WILL find a way to cure her.
But the sun, it's... N-never mind.
Ahem! Commander, I really, reeeally need your help!
It'd be one thing if we were fighting mass-produced Sirens, but a swarm of Gazers this big is too much for our fleet to deal with!
Remember your lesson on the Antarctic Treaty? It lets you command not just us shipgirls...
But also all the defensive weaponry that exists around Antarctica!
...Thanks for trusting me, Sara.
Of course. I've always trusted you!
Okay, I'm handing control of our fleet over to you now!
Do your thing and lead us to victory!

sequence: Iris Orthodoxy - Tribunal Headquarters
Temporary Command Center
Sometime later

scripts.say: As I expected, Clemenceau immediately approved my request to borrow the Tribunal's base.
I finished my call with Saratoga and went to the command center. There, I saw that the Eagle Union and Northern Parliament were already done setting up a chain of command.
Commander, I set up a new rendezvous route for Saratoga's and Soyuz's fleets, like you asked.
Also, the research station is orchestrating an evacuation as we speak. It's going smoothly so far.
Good. Then I can finally breathe for a bit.
*clap clap clap clap*
Winning a battle thousands of kilometers away. Imagine that.
This has been a magnificent display of your legendary leadership skills, Commander. If you ever retire and become a politician, you'll be the face of your party.
You're exaggerating. I've not "won the battle" yet, I've only just begun repositioning fleets.
I'm not proud about the distance thing, either. If I could, I'd teleport to Antarctica right now.
But enough about me. Have you done the Bismarck thing?
Yes. Just as you asked, I've prepared a closed comms channel to her. That's what I came here to tell you.
It's over in our secret room. Nobody else will be able to hear what you say.
Nobody else besides you, I'm guessing.
Heehee. I don't know what you mean♪
She's on the line, but I can reschedule the call if now is a bad time for you.
Now is as good a time as any. Lead the way.
Of course. Right this way.
Tribunal Headquarters - Secret Room
This is not how I was hoping we'd meet again, but things are what they are. Greetings.
While we have publically spoken face-to-face before, well, as you may know...
Showing my face in the capacity of a leader in a private conversation is... quite different.
I will say, I'm surprised you'd go out of your way to contact me like this.
If I'm to guess, this is about transferring command down in Antarctica, right?
What? Did Clemenceau not tell you anything?
All she told me was that this was about sharing intel and cooperating in Antarctica. Her tone was quite "figure out the rest yourself."
It sounds like she withheld what she knew from you as well.
That sounds like Clemenceau alright.
Long story short, here's what we're dealing with...
It was YOU who relayed the discovery of that Antarctic crystal to me and Soyuz?
So you've converted Clemenceau of all people to your side?

options.content: Yeah. She can't say no to me.

scripts.say: You never cease to amaze, Commander.
It's no wonder why Friedrich would sing your praises on a daily basis. Hahahah.
Unfortunately, I couldn't predict that we'd run into Gazers.
If they're not dealt with, we'll have a disaster on our hands on par with the World Expo... No, maybe even bigger.
On the bright side, we've fought them once before, and the superimposition hasn't begun yet.
Manifesting a concept like Marco Polo did then will be much harder on Antarctica. Even if it does happen, the concept's foothold should be weak.
If all factions engage it as one, we have a fighting chance.
That, I agree with.
Obviously, opinions differ from one faction to the next. But we need to set those aside and coordinate our efforts.
For that reason, I would like to take command of your Southern Ocean fleet.
Of course, I could also use any other forces you have in reserve. Knowing you, I'm certain you have some at the ready.
I do. I moved some people around as soon as I received word about the jamming.
Here's what's going to happen.
I will give you immediate control over our forces in not just this battle, but all future battles as well.
This, I hope, will help you forge the future that you dream of.
All future battles? You're allowing me to control whenever I see fit?
Thank you so much, Bismarck. This will help greatly.
You're welcome. As long as you're up for the task, you can give orders to our shipgirls on the front whenever you want.
Use their strength as though it were your own.
Right. I will not abuse this power.
Thank you. Until next time.
Tribunal Headquarters - Corridor
Oh, you got done sooner than I expected.
Seems like it went exceedingly well. Color me impressed.
Who could have predicted she'd give you THAT much leeway, hmm?
Was I, really? You can never be sure.
Heehee. I'll take that as a compliment♪
But enough joking around. I got in touch with the Royal Navy's fleet.
It seems they anticipated the Gazers' arrival, though they're still scrambling to figure out what to do.
PTSD from the events of the World Expo, perhaps.
Won't you be a dear and get them to calm down?
Remember, you can always pull the Antarctic Treaty on them.
Say something like – "As the Commander of the Azur Lane, I have unrivaled authority over Antarctica and its ocean."
"I request that you transfer control of your fleet to me immediately and that you cooperate with other fleets under my command until the battle is over."
Not to be pushy or anything, but I could send that message on your behalf.
No thanks. I'll speak to them myself.
Aww. That's too bad♪

sequence: Tribunal Headquarters
Temporary Command Center
Sometime later

scripts.say: Thanks to the hard work of Helena META as well as the shipgirls on-site, the jamming in Antarctica had been reduced to all but a non-issue.
The command system was now getting everyone's positions, compositions, and statuses. Stable strategic communication had become possible.
All faction fleets reorganized, creating a single, unified fleet under my command – the Azur Lane fleet.
Reinforcements came in, too. Not just the ones Bismarck had prepared, but backup from the Eagle Union as well.
The excuse given for the latter's presence was that, "They just so happened to be in the Southern Ocean." Yeah, right...
Sara – or should I say, Miss Saratoga – really brought her entire fan club.
She even got Enterprise's friends to come all the way out here...
Ahem. Anyway...
Let's start with reviewing the evac from Antarctica.
The Eagle Union's and Royal Navy's bases are far from the action and their staff have already withdrawn.
Königsberg is headed for the NP's research station right now. She'll evacuate after linking up with Soyuz's group.
The fleets attached to each station will escort their members to safety. They won't partake in the operation until the evacuation is complete.
On the Divine Vestige front, there have been no sightings of the cocoon that brought forth the Arbiter last time.
The Gazers have been spreading the Divine Vestige, but only at a glacial pace compared to the time of the World Expo.
So far, my theory has been correct.
Pamiat' Merkuria META didn't plan ahead like Marco Polo did. She's apparently just been winging it.
She is the key to all this. If we can neutralize her, it should end the crisis right there and then.
As long as we stop the superimposition, we can take our time neutralizing the Gazers and drones.
Luckily for us, it seems Soyuz has a big fan in Pamiat'. She's been pursuing them this whole time.
All while ignoring how I've been rapidly redeploying our forces.
All we need to do is lure her into an ambush and we can wipe out her and her Gazer army in one fell swoop.
Soyuz's team is on the case, moving from the snowmelt area and toward the ambush point.
With the Union's air support on our side, everything should go according to plan.
Hell, the trap should be even more effective if we can push Pamiat's buttons and get her to run into our ambush completely blind.
According to Soyuz, the girl is pretty emotionally unstable. It shouldn't take much to agitate her.
Alright. Forces lying in ambush... Iron Blood has Brünhilde, Hindenburg, and Felix Schultz, to name a few.
On the Union side, Saratoga's fleet is also en route to the ambush site.
They've got battleships Washington, North Carolina, and the Colorado sisters. For carriers, they're bringing Saratoga herself of course, Ranger, and Independence.
Add to that a few dozen cruisers and destroyers.
Over in the Southern Ocean, there's the Royal Navy's Southern Ocean fleet led by Implacable, as well as an Iron Blood support fleet with Prinz Heinrich among the ranks.
Finally, there's the Union backup fleet that "just happened to be there"...
All in all, we have a really good shot at victory.
Antarctica - Ice Fields
Soyuz, do you read me? What's your status?
Damages are within estimates. We will reach the destination momentarily.
The air support is almost there! Just hang in a little longer!
I appreciate the support, it's just... aircraft will only deal quite limited damage to the Gazers.
Who's saying I've only brought aircraft?
I've got a whole arsenal of stuff ready! You'll see later!
Soyuz, our fleet is in position. All there is to do now is wait for the target to come.
And the reinforcements are coming in at full speed!
C'mon, Eisen! Faster, boy!
...I'm Bunker Hill. Eagle Union Southern Ocean fleet. En route at max speed to objective.
Same with the Royal Navy's Southern Ocean fleet. We'll arrive in three hours. It's an honour to be fighting alongside you.
This is Ingraham. We're done evacuating all the Union and Royal Navy forces. The escort fleets will now join you in battle.
NP's and IB's evacs aren't finished yet. I'm working on it as fast as I can.
Thank you all for the status reports.
We'll continue to our destination and report back when we've arrived.
Sheesh. The Commander is leading everyone flawlessly, despite being across the world.
Yes. And under circumstances not even I could have predicted...
But... that's what makes Comrade Commander so reliable, don't you think?
I shall be the bait for Pamiat'. Everyone else, please follow the orders you've been given.
Nighttime fell upon Antarctica, and the showdown was drawing near.
An aurora shone overhead whilst the grand chase finally came to a close.
Well, well. I was wondering why you stopped fleeing. Of course you had an ambush prepared.
Eisen, that's the bad guy! Let's get her!
Get a whiff of that one. Smells like danger.
And what are we, harmless little kittens? We're just as dangerous.
Heard you've been starting shit here in Antarctica. Get ready to pay the price!
The Knights of the Sea are done letting you run rampant!
It's not too late to stop. Surrender peacefully and we might just let you off with a stern beating.
Wooow. Those are big words for a bunch of mice drawn to the big cheese.
Observer couldn't have predicted this would happen. Not in a million years.
I mean, of course she couldn't. Being disconnected from your mainframe does that to you.
...She has lost connection to her mainframe?
What, you didn't know?
C'mon. Put the pieces together.
Do you think Observer would've just let Compiler get terminated if she was operating at normal capacity?
She cut herself off from her OWN mainframe. Can you believe that?
Something in your branch has made her go cuckoo, methinks.
She hasn't connected to her mainframe for a very long time now. Why? I don't know.
But at any rate, she can't get updates, can't access the Natural Calculation System, and can't use the resources of Laplace's Demon.
The only things she can use are her mainframe's nodes and her vessels.
Like, at this point, why would she even bother? She can't do jack!
It's no wonder, then, that she hasn't shown herself for so long.
Has she really become so weak she can't even deal with a threat right next to her mainframe?
That's right.
The funniest thing of all is that she thought she could hide it from me!
You can't hide a weakness as glaring as that! Hahahaha!
I would like it if the enemy of my enemy were my friend... but you don't seem keen on an alliance.
You clearly don't like Observer either, though. Why don't you take it out on her and we can all part on peaceful terms?
No can do. In case you forgot, I've got things to do here.
(Right, her three goals... Laying the Divine Vestige was only one of them.)
We have stopped an invasion such as this once. We will do it again.
Whatever your plans are, they will not come to fruition. This I can promise you.
Really, huh? Let's put your promise to the test. I mean, I've already come this far!
If you wanna stop me then you'd better give me your best shot! Ahahaha!
KABOOOM!
With a loud explosion, another Gazer toppled over.
Thirty minutes had elapsed since the battle began. Already, the shipgirls had gained an overwhelming advantage.
This Pamiat' is just a weak imitation!
She doesn't stand a chance against our firepower!
That's 'cuz we've got, like, a million people whalin' on her! It helps that we've got the Commander and ME, of course!
But isn't she a little TOO weak? You'd think the head honcho would put up more of a fight!
Compared to that World Expo hag on her flyin' throne, yeah, I guess she's kind of a pushover.
I think the Tribunal deployed a superweapon to deal with her in that case.
In this case, though... it almost doesn't feel right with how easily she's going down...
(It IS odd. Beyond using Gazers as meat shields, she is making no attempt to avoid incoming fire.)
(Rationally speaking, she's only digging her own grave... Yet, I remember one of Kronshtadt's reports described a fighting style just like this.)
(One "Bon Homme Richard" similarly wasn't afraid of damage, and used it to erode the minds of her attackers...)
(No... Could she be doing the same?)
Pamiat', why are you fighting so hard for your obsession with the past?
I can understand looking back on the past and basking in nostalgia. What I cannot understand is trying to replace the future with the past.
You've suffered a lot, fought hellish battles, but at the very least, you survived.
As a survivor, you should bear the hopes of your fallen comrades. You should live on, and fight for the good of all of us.
Look what you're doing now. Do you think they'd be proud of you?
You are trampling on not just everything they fought for, but everything YOU fought for as well.
Hahahaha! "Obsession"? Do I look like someone driven by an obsession?
No! I'm doing this because it's what my fallen comrades would have wanted!
Haha... Ahahaha...
AHAHAHAHAHAHAH!
Pamiat's terrifying laughter rang through everyone's communicators. It sounded wrong, like someone was laughing THROUGH her.
Oh, gosh! Do you hear that?! It's like her laughter's coming from inside my head!
Is it just me, or is it gettin' cold as hell all of a sudden?
Condensation is forming on my chains... Soyuz, I think she's healing herself!
Not on my watch, she isn't!
KABOOOM!
Soyuz fired a volley at the girl possessed by some evil spirit.
The shells flew through the air, but stopped short of their target, plunging into the sea like rocks.
A pulse of sheer cold radiated outward from Pamiat', freezing everything in its path at an unbelievable rate.
The sea froze faster than the shipgirls could react. One by one, they were frozen in place.
...So this was your plan all along.
You knowingly walked into our trap and allowed us to attack you.
Ahaha... A small sacrifice to make, to be able to finally come into contact with the font of essence.
By plucking the fruit from the prime branch, I have at last found... the true past!
Look at this – the Revolutionary Front! All I ever knew about it was what little that one person told me.
And now... it's like I was actually there myself.
Ahahaha... I see it in the fragments... Very, very interesting.
Wouldn't you know it – your Ring of Whatever isn't just a doomsday bunker.
It's also where you store that device based on data you recovered from the RF.
If it wasn't for that, you wouldn't have built a bunker all the way out here. Isn't that right, Soyuz?
Ahahaha! Oh, what a laugh!
And you called ME driven by obsession! You should have a good look in the mirror!
Project Dawn is the biggest obsession of them all!
You think it's your ray of hope? You couldn't be more wrong. It's an express ticket to your downfall.
Just being close to it brings misfortune.
Do you know what happened to the people involved in this project? I can tell you.
Don't answer. I'll tell you either way.
The project planner went out with a fleet to test a new experimental device. Then... Poof! None of them were ever seen again!
Then the project was suspended and became an accessory to a separate project.
And when that project started, our entire fleet, as well as our last admiral, were all sacrificed! Not a single survivor!
"Fight until the last light has faded."
That's what they all said. They all fought to their deaths and let someone else have their chance to live!
This is what Project Dawn is! This is the obsession that's been passed down!
It's sacrificing yourself and dumping everything on those who survive!
Now it's yours. Do you want to do the same as them?
The same as Antiochus, the same as the Ashes – carrying the hopes and dreams of the fallen and suffering for all eternity!
You've already seen what that turned them into.
This endless cycle only creates more tragedy... and must be put to an end.
If you were given a way out, why would you NOT take it?
You may have chosen a way out. At least, so you may believe...
But looking at you now, it's clear you haven't been set free.
All you've done is escape the fate of being controlled by one Siren in favor of another one. You're still being controlled.
Ahahaha! No, Soyuz, you're wrong! Antiochus are not all the same.
Look at humanity itself. They're not a monolith, and neither are Antiochus.
You've got low-level programs, blindly following orders, and then you've got the Arbiters.
Killing that first group is easy. The second one, though? They're as unkillable as unkillable gets. Especially... her.
One thing you should know about me is that I'm nobody's lackey. We're cooperating as equals.
We're partners who see each other eye to eye, searching for the answer together!
Is "escapism" the best answer you could come up with?
Call it whatever you want, but it sure beats a pointless suicide pact!
That isn't what we're choosing. We aren't trying to end our own lives or follow the path to destruction.
We are searching the unknown, carving a path to the future. That is the indomitable human spirit – which has brought us to this very point.
We may stumble along the way, we may get caught in a storm, but every hardship and challenge humanity faces becomes a lesson for its development.
Perhaps Project Dawn did fail in the past. If so, that is a failure we can learn from.
We will fix its faults and try again with care so as to not repeat the same mistake.
Even if we perish in the process, we must believe that, someday, someone will come and succeed where we failed.
You're still on about this...
Fate, the future, the cycle – those will all end one day.
Your fate has already been decided for you. I've seen it myself.
There is nothing, NOTHING good in that future you can't stop gushing about!
The good days are all in the past!
You're wrong! Nobody decides our future for us!
The future is ours to choose, not yours!
I pressed the button to call the girls, to cut off that ear-piercing laughter, but then...
...Helena. So you heard it, too.
Then I might as well ask you. Is what she said about Project Dawn true?
Yes and no. It is how she remembers it... It is reality, but only one reality.
Reality and truth are not always one and the same.
What I can say is this – reality can only become truth if enough faith goes into it.
"Reality can only become truth... if enough faith goes into it."
Let's not worry too much about the philosophical stuff right now. There's still a battle going on.
I've protected you against Pamiat's cognitive influence. You won't be affected by her voice.
Thank you. Next thing to deal with, then, is that ocean-freezing power of hers.
From what I can tell, it's not an Arbiter or META ability. It's simply a bluff, right?
Yes. She certainly could use the Tower's power to freeze the sea in an instant...
But this freeze is only surface-level.
It's a trick meant to fool you. Nothing to be afraid of.
She isn't as strong as everyone thinks she is.
The forces you have right now are more than enough to win against her.
It's time to get back in the fight. Good luck.
Tribunal Headquarters - Temporary Command Center
Helena's defense against the cognitive influence and Soyuz's decisive action in battle gave us the edge we needed to fend off Pamiat' META's attacks.
As we'd reasoned out, the thin layer of ice was hardly an obstacle to our fleet.
Simply firing at it with machine guns or even raising their main engine output and moving a bit more vigorously was enough to break through it with ease.
To compare this Pamiat' Merkuria to other META we'd encountered so far, she was probably between Scharnhorst and Hiryuu.
A powerful foe, yes, but nothing compared to the awesome might of the Arbiters.
Our allies continued to strike down Gazers, all the while cornering the mastermind.
(This is all wrong. It's going TOO well.)
(If she's imitating Bon Homme Richard, then she must still have an ace up her sleeve.)
Haha... Ahahaha...
AHAHAHAHAHAHAH!
Her eerie laughter echoed through my mind.
Helena was protecting me from Pamiat' META's attacks on my mind, yes, but ONLY me.
What if Pamiat' META attacked the command structure itself instead?
(If I lose contact and can't command our allies anymore, that's effectively the same as getting rid of me...)
(Memphis and Helena need to raise the security of our command network! If I don't tell them now...!)
KRRRHHHH...
For just a moment, I heard interference in the communicator.
Damn! She pivoted to jamming already?!
Helena, Memphis! Prepare for enemy attack–
Did that light just flicker?
Hm? There are some odd readings on my monitor...
Excuse me, Algérie? Can you help me troubleshoot this right away?
Huh? It was fine during my daily checks this morning... What in the world?
Umm, hey... Is it just me, or is there black mist oozing out?
Black mist?
Tch... Everyone, get away from the communicator!
It's an enemy attack! Algérie, sound the alarms!
Lock down this facility at once!
Yes, ma'am!
Under Clemenceau's command, our Iris allies began an emergency evacuation.
Black mist gradually filled the command center.
(This is definitely an enemy attack... But how do you get gas through communication lines?)
Clemenceau, Soyuz! Be ready to take command!
Seemingly alerted to my presence, the black mist turned its tendrils to me.
While my consciousness turned hazy, I heard the faint sound of wind chimes.
In a world of pure white, at the far end of my vision, stood a single door.
(I know this place. I came here when I was investigating Anchorage's hull at the Sea of Stars...)
(That's not all. When we fought the Arbiter at the World Expo, I was warped to this space again, too.)
...Comrade Commander?
Are you there, Comrade?!
Is that you, Sovetsky Soyuz?!

options.content: (Isn't she in Antarctica right now, though?)

scripts.say: Yes, it's me. And I'm relieved to see that it really is you, Comrade Commander.
Something uncanny is happening, that much is clear.
I was in Antarctica, and you were in Europa – and yet we've been warped to the same place at the same time.
Soyuz, did anything strange happen before you were brought here?
...Actually, yes. The enemy META released a black shockwave.
The power of the impact did more than just break our formation – it knocked out our communication systems.
Same here. Black mist started spewing out, and our communication equipment all started malfunctioning...
And before you knew it, you were here. Just like me.
It would be reasonable to presume this is the result of an enemy attack, then.
Actually, it might not be. I recognize this place.
Is that so? Incidentally, so do I.
Shortly after I came to Antarctica, when I touched that strange crystal, I was warped here.
I went through that door and witnessed an unusual sight...
Comrade Commander, if you have any clues regarding the truth of this place... I'd certainly appreciate you sharing.
Mm. This area appears connected to the Wisdom Cube's information space.
I think that door leads to the data preserved at the Wisdom Cube's inception.
Data preserved in the Wisdom Cube? Does that mean... that what we know to be "essence" is an account of things that actually happened?
Indeed. This is in fact a record of reality, though in a branch separate from ours.
From our perspective, however, it is but one of infinite possibilities.
Like you said, this branch has its own past and present.
More importantly, it has its own future.
Comrade Commander...
Nothing will happen if we just sit here. Let's think of a way to escape.
Oh. This is just anecdotal, but I think the passage of time here is different.
Haste makes waste here. Since we're stuck here, we might as well keep calm and take our time.
First things first, let's see what's behind that door.
Soyuz and I opened the door in front of us.
Beyond it lay a palace reminiscent of the Imperiya.
La la la~ Hum da dum~
Foie gras~ Venison~ Roast chicken~
Truffle and nut souffle♪
I've returned, Mademoiselle Pamiat' Merkuria.
*sniff* *sniff*... That smells good!
Thank you for all you do, Pamiat'. Heehee, would you like some help?
Aww, I'm fine. I can handle it myself!
Heheh. But I know something you can help me with...
I haven't found the right wine to go with it! Mind going down to the cellar to pick one out?
Say what? You can't find a drink in the Summer Palace, of all places?
I said the RIGHT wine!
I'm having Iris cuisine today, so I wanna try for a different vibe this time.
What does it matter as long as it's potable? Unless it's vodka we're talking about, anyway!
It DOES matter!
Yeah! It does!
Alright, Sevastopol. I'm counting on you to find the perfect wine for tonight!
The recording ended, and the world turned white again.
We entered the door once more.
Great work on your mission, Avrora!
You must be tired. Empty that brain and take a little break!
Thank you! Mm... The air here is just so lovely.
But Pamiat', I'm not entirely sure if horseback riding is the best way to take a break after a long trip.
Ahahaha♪ Actually, I had you come with me because I had a little surprise to show you!
A surprise?
Check this out!
Tadaaah!
You've modernized your rigging... You got a retrofit! So the new technology proved a success?
A roaring one, as you can see!
Heheh, and I'm the first shipgirl to get one, too!
Awesome, right? I am so awesome!
The recording ended, and the world turned white again.
We entered the door once more.
Gangut... Sevastopol...
Why... did everyone have to die...
Why... am I the only one left...
Why... did you try so hard to let me live?
Her tears had dried up. Her voice was hoarse.
Behind her, the two-headed eagle flag collapsed amidst the flames.
It was over.
The recording ended, and the world turned white again.
We entered the door once more.
In the moonlight, a damaged ship quietly kept watch.
From her silhouette and her visage, you managed to recognize who she was.
She exuded coldness and loneliness, but also the joy of hope and the noble pride of one who'd fought through and survived a great war.
The recording ended, and a fifth door appeared before us.
Was that... the past of the other Pamiat' Merkuria?
Seems like it. But that ship from the last one...
Comrade Commander... Do you know what manner of being she was?
No...
This is the fifth door. Do you want to keep going?
Of course. It's just a feeling, but I think this one is the last one.
We're about to find the truth of this place.
Comrade Commander... Is this what I think it is?
Antarctica. Not where you were before you came here, but...
When we went through the door, we found a place quite similar to where Soyuz had been.
It wasn't a memory or a recording. The scenery here was just too vivid.
In the center of the battlefield was Pamiat' Merkuria META, engulfed in that black mist.
I saw our allies around her.
However, everything was motionless. It was as if time had frozen in the Antarctic cold.
When I looked up, there was one more witness.
It's frozen because it's happening right now, in the present.
You're... the Pamiat' Merkuria from back then, aren't you?
Nope.
Like yeah, I am Pamiat', but I'm not that one. I'm not any of the Pamiat' Merkurias you've ever known or will ever know.
Umm, I guess you could say I'm like every Pamiat' ever all balled up into one.
Does that make sense?
In other words... you're the culmination of the concept of Pamiat' Merkuria?
Oh, wow! You're smart. Guess you need to be, if you made it this far.
Anyway, this incarnation was just born, so it's not quite perfect yet.
Even though the shipgirl Pamiat' Merkuria has existed for a long time now?
A long time? Mm... Sorry, but time doesn't really MEAN anything, does it?
We can't just pop out of thin air willy-nilly, you know. There are conditions for our birth.
...What would happen if we were to take you down right now?
Hmm... Gotta say, I'm curious myself!
But unfortunately, I'm not going down here. Neither will either of you, though.
That's just... the rules, or whatever.
Don't worry too much about the battle, alright?
See? Take a look, and you'll get what I mean.
You've already cornered the poor girl. You're this close to a total victory.
If you went back right now, you could seize victory just like that.
So just leave it alone, and everything will be just fine!
Instead, have a little chat with me!
You must have tons of questions!
I don't mind chatting, but let's make one thing clear first.
Are you our enemy or not?
Strictly speaking? I'm not on any side.
Will I take a side? Well, I have my own plans♪
Work with me, and I'll call you a friend. Get in my way, you're my enemy. Sound good enough?
So, who the heck are you?
Uh, the Commander of the Azur Lane...?
Come ON, I already know that.
I don't want your title. I want to know who and what you are!
Something about you is all nostalgic... I just can't remember why, for some reason!
I mean, look. I'm not perfect, but I'm Pamiat' Merkuria in the purest sense of the name.
Don't you think it's a liiittle weird that there's something I just can't remember?
Meh. You probably don't know, either.
But then I have to wonder – why are you here?
Just so you know, I didn't bring you here. I don't have any crazy powers like that.
It wasn't you? Then it must be the black mist...
Wait. Do you hear those wind chimes?
Wind chimes? What are you talking about?
The sound of wind chimes rang in my ears again.
Wait! I still have questions to ask!
Dazzling light awakened me.
(Now what... Light, a lamp... A wire?)
(This isn't the Wisdom Cube's information space. Am I back?)
Commander! You're finally awake!
Thank goodness... Your vital signs were fine, but you just wouldn't wake up.
Do you feel okay? Are you hurting anywhere?
(I think the black mist coming at me woke me up...)
Where are we?
A Tribunal medical station.
How long was I out?
Thirty whole minutes!
What about Soyuz... Did our comrades in Antarctica win their battle?
How did you know...? Wait, shouldn't you be more worried about yourself?!
Now, now. I'm sure it's a good thing that the Commander has the energy to worry about others.
Clemenceau, how's the situation?
All is well. Soyuz has things under control.
Is the command center safe?
You don't need to worry about that. By the way, we have a call from Soyuz.
Through normal channels...?
A secret line. I promise I'm not eavesdropping this time.
Comrade Commander, we've secured victory.
We've also confirmed the disappearance of the Gazers, and the Arbiter invasion has been thwarted.
All of this is thanks to your support, coordination, and command.
This combat operation is more than just an execution of the Antarctic Treaty – it serves as a model example of all factions working together against a common enemy.
I speak for all of the Northern Parliament when I say thank you, Commander.
No matter what choice you make in the future...
We hope to stand with you and help you in any way we can.
I look forward to seeing you at the victory celebration banquet.
With the META threat defeated, the distant battle in the Antarctic had ended in our victory.
We had prevented Antarctica from facing a worst-case scenario.
However, some doubts lingered.
Why had Observer severed her connection to her mainframe? What exactly was that Pamiat' Merkuria in the memory space?
What were those wind chimes, and why did Helena META want to help me so much?
Project Dawn and the strange crystal contained their fair share of mysteries, as well.
One thing was for sure – more sleepless nights lay in store for me.

sequence: Southern Ocean
Operation Area
30 minutes earlier

scripts.say: KABOOOM!
*cough cough*... How are you still moving?
No... Don't tell me that had zero effect on you...
Your test site means business, huh. It's no wonder you held off her invasion once. You're capable.
This is the end of the line, "Pamiat'."
Yeah, looks like it. The time for resculpting is over...
You got me! I lost!
But hey, it's no big deal. I'm satisfied that I even got this far.
...And now, maybe we can finally talk.
It has been bothering me how so many of your actions here don't make sense.
Initially, I thought your goal here was to brainwash me in order to gain control of the bunker.
You were able to blend in smoothly, hardly raising any suspicions since we first saw you. You clearly have skill.
And yet, your attempt to persuade me was lukewarm, and you willingly lifted your cognitive influence on me.
Then, there's how you told us all that information about Project Dawn without any prompting whatsoever.
There are simply too many inconsistencies.
What is your goal here, really? Why did you come to our world?
Who knows. Maybe I just wanted to see my old comrades. Maybe I just wanted to atone for old sins.
Or maybe I wanted to chat with an old friend to get drunk on false hope again?
At any rate, you girls might have won, but that doesn't mean SHE has been defeated.
The battle is far from over.
...Of course. Your three objectives.
Yeah! I'm glad you remembered.
Laying the Divine Vestige must've been the first. What were the remaining–
Okay, that's enough talking! You need to start fighting for real or you'll actually die!
Buuut then again...
You DID fight off this invasion and live to tell the tale.
Maybe you'll meet a girl with the same tragic past as me who also carries the wishes of her comrades.
Me and her, we are fundamentally at odds with each other. I'd say we're pretty much mortal enemies.
But you, Soyuz – you can help her. I know you can.
So if you ever cross paths... take care of her, alright?
...I don't have any reason to honor your request.
Come ooon! I went easy on you AND gave you intel! She's a comrade and – unlike the cutie you're talking to – she's really powerful!
What more reasons do you need?
(Hmm... If Comrade Commander were in my shoes...)
That's it for me! Now don't get squashed without a fight!
The future depends on it! Yours, the Northern Parliament's, and the Imperiya's!
I'll be watching you from somewhere far, far away...
And strike whenever I see the chance!

sequence: Iris Orthodoxy - Holy Capital
Azur Lane Provisional Base
After the battle's conclusion

scripts.say: It would be another sleepless night, just as I had been fearing.
Amidst victory celebrations, reports of Siren attacks started blowing in like a snowstorm.
Large Siren fleets had been sighted nearly everywhere, from the South Atlantic to the Antarctic and its surrounding ocean.
They were all converging upon a single point in the Southern Ocean.
It seemed like repelling Pamiat' Merkuria META gave Observer the breathing room to launch a counterattack.
To make matters worse, the Gazers were still lurking somewhere beneath the snow. We would have to take care of them before moving on to the Sirens.
However, I could not let the shipgirls remain in Antarctica. If they did, the fighting would surely get chaotic.
For that reason, I ordered the immediate withdrawal of all forces present on the continent.
I instructed the Combined Azur Lane fleet to move to safe waters, then spread out and return to their faction's area of control.
Now, having done all this, it was time to contact the girl who'd helped me so much during this operation...
I closed my eyes and allowed the cognitive influence into my mind. A galaxy full of stars spread out before me.
Hey. Here to ask me something?
Yeah. About the crystals. While they do exhibit some resonance with riggings, the amount is just not enough to be practical.
They're worthless as a cure for hull damage, and we can never hope to get more of them than the bunker managed to produce.
Mhm. They were just bait Observer used to lure you.
Be that as it may, the crystals DID restructure Soyuz's rigging. Why is that?
I think that was just another trick on Observer's part. Seeing is believing, and she made you believe by removing what was inhibiting Soyuz. It was the quickest way.
I see. So it was something different to the "resculpting" that Pamiat' spoke of.
Is there anything you can tell me about that, actually?
"Resculpting" is... Well, it's a special stage of METAmorphosis, fraught with danger and instability. I don't want to tell you too much.
But, to give you a hint – by now, you've met several girls whose METAmorphosis changed them somehow.
Why do you think they changed? Where do the energy and data that turned them into what they are come from?
Data from the "prime" branch, huh... When I was attacked by that black mist, it sent me into another Wisdom Cube information space.
This time, it led me to a girl who claimed to be the "culmination of the concept of Pamiat' Merkuria."
We talked about some things, but got interrupted by the sound of wind chimes.
I've heard those chimes and visited information spaces multiple times now, yet I still know next to nothing about either.
I don't reckon you have all the answers, but maybe you can tell me a thing or two?
I can't, since I don't know what things you truly saw in there.
If we ever get the chance, though, I'd like to see it with you.
The sun's activity is on the rise, so I know this won't be our last meeting.
What was that about the sun? What does that have to do with anything?
Unless... it's not the sun itself that's important, but rather the concept of the sun...
Correct. Conceptually, it represents weakening, and weakening facilitates coalescence.
It comes with some danger, but also with opportunities.
Sorry for being so vague on the details. I'll tell you everything in due time.
...I have to ask – are you really not worried about that Pamiat'?
She told you herself. She'll attack again whenever she sees the chance.
When the Arbiters strike, we'll be ready for them. We'll be ready for that girl, too.
I sure hope so. Your branch is currently under constant threat.
You stopped her from accomplishing her first objective. She still has two more.
Be on your guard, Commander.
The battle isn't over yet.

sequence: Iris Orthodoxy
After the battle's conclusion

scripts.say: Heeheehee♪
I TOLD them the battle was far from over!
Okay, the target should be under this building. Inside a dungeon...
Ugh. Dungeons. This is gonna be a pain to look through.
Well, well. A trespasser? Did no one teach you to ask for permission?
Oh. It's you, Clemenceau.
So you knew I'd be here. Interesting.
It wasn't hard to figure out you'd come here. Though I am puzzled by HOW you did it.
Getting rid of you won't be that easy after all.
Oh, well. At least this is a good chance to test how well-prepared we are.
Well-prepared for– Wait, is that...?
Heehee. An uninvited guest.
Already made yourself at home, huh? Get ready for the reception party!
The submarine's voyage continued. Meanwhile, the girls had all gathered in the mess hall.
Thank you!
Is this... juice? Seriously?
Duh. We can't get drunk on a mission!
I'd love a drink as much as the next girl, but we should stay alert. The liquor stays in the cupboard.
Well, Soyuz? Everyone's seated. Let's hear the answer to Svirepy's question!
Right. I'll now tell you about the history of Antarctica.
Sovetsky Soyuz also raises the glass of juice to her lips, but her mind has already begun to embark on another voyage.
In the last great war, before the Azur Lane splintered, the factions of the world came together to discuss who would control Antarctica.
After many long debates, humanity finally reached an agreement – one that came to be known as the Antarctic Treaty.
The treaty had many provisions. First and foremost, all claims made over Antarctica's territory were suspended.
The entire continent would not belong to any single government, but would be under the management of the Azur Lane.
The construction of research bases or naval outposts to defend against Sirens would only be allowed with permission from the Azur Lane.
Furthermore, the command structure in Antarctica was to be equal to or higher than anti-Siren operational areas in each sea sector.
Even after the Crimson Axis was established, the Azur Lane's attitude toward Antarctic remained the same.
The Azur Lane may also, for any reason, freely take command of fleets or ships belonging to its member states stationed in Antarctica or its surrounding ocean.
It may also intervene in any and all armed conflicts within its borders.
Does that include... Reenactments?
It does.
In other words, the Commander's power is infinite here?
"Infinite" might be an overstatement, but it is true that Comrade Commander's authority is greater here than anywhere else.
Such is the power of the naval commander of the Azur Lane.
On paper, this authority supersedes that of the governments around the world, though in practice, it has yet to be exercised.
There are no Reenactments around Antarctica, and there have never been any significant encounters against the Sirens here either.
If anything, one could say that the Antarctic Treaty is a forgotten remnant from the last great war.
Back then, the Sirens had such an insurmountable advantage that even certain coastal regions were hard to defend. The strategic value of a place as distant as Antarctica... was less than zero.
Essentially, things boiled down to this simple principle: "We won't touch it if nobody else does." Rarely are things so straightforward on the international stage.
And so it remained... until after the war, when the Azur Lane split. Then, things began to change.
It started with Iron Blood, which took advantage of the "anti-Siren outposts" part of the treaty to construct military bases.
Thanks to the knowledge they'd gained from reverse-engineering Siren technology, those bases got finished in the blink of an eye.
Then, as part of a gambit by its higher-ups, the Eagle Union built a military stronghold and stationed a permanent fleet in the area.
The Northern Parliament, Royal Navy, and Iris Orthodoxy all attempted to follow suit with our own bases, but due to the ensuing Reenactments, none of us made any real progress.
Afterwards, the Iris Orthodoxy was split into two, forcing them to withdraw any claims on the continent.
The Royal Navy downsized their forces, eventually giving up their goals of maintaining a military base on Antarctica.
As for us, we largely abandoned our hopes of militarizing our research bases and shifted our attention back towards more pressing issues in the Arctic North.
There are recorded incidents of the governments of the Eagle Union and Iron Blood exchanging blows through mass-produced ships, but beyond that, no major conflicts have broken out.
However, you must take note that a single truth underpinned all these events – that Antarctica had no strategic value.
Which brings us to the current day.
As you all know, the Azur Lane and the Crimson Axis have reached a comprehensive ceasefire agreement.
As we speak, representatives from all over the world are gathered at the reunited Iris Orthodoxy to discuss the reformation of a single Azur Lane.
Naturally, one of the terms for this process would be that all parties would assume their roles in upholding the existing treaties and agreements of the Azur Lane.
And of course, the Antarctic Treaty would be no exception.

Having all that said, regardless of how this negotiation process actually goes, as long as all of the factions are still willing to come to the table, there shouldn't be any major power shifts in Antarctica.
The Royal Navy, Northern Parliament, Eagle Union, and Iron Blood – these are the factions that still have research bases in Antarctica.
Of these factions, only the last two have any sort of military presence here.
Yup! Also, fun fact – our research station was made in collaboration with Iron Blood!
Wait, what? That's news to me!
I never knew that, either. Our Intelligence Bureau must keep that fact close to the vest.
Pamiat' is correct. Our station was indeed built with borrowed Iron Blood technology.
It's not strictly confidential information, just a little-known fact.
We knew about the Reenactments and shared our intel with Iron Blood. Around this time, we decided to build a base hidden from Naval HQ's prying eyes.
Me, Friedrich, and many others... we all came together in preparation for the coming war with the Sirens.
This included building our own research station in Antarctica.
We built it because this war with the Sirens will one day be over.
We built it because the world still has so many discoveries waiting to be made.
We built it because the future holds countless possibilities.
We built it because, if human society dedicates itself solely to war...
Then what will we do once there is no more war to fight?
This is why we built the research station. In preparation for a better tomorrow.
My... Really makes you think.
Okay, so if I got this right...
Nobody lives in Antarctica, so the Sirens don't attack it.
The Sirens don't attack it, so nobody really cares about it.
Nobody really cares about it, so humanity signed a treaty, agreeing to just share it.
And because nobody cares about it, the research station gets away with doing stuff in secret. That right?
Pretty much!
(Huh? When'd Pamiat' get here?)
Also, while it's true no PEOPLE live there, it's still home to a whole ecosystem.
On that subject, now it's my turn to play the teacher! Can anyone name an Antarctic animal?
Me, me! Penguins!
Round penguins! Cute penguins!
Will we, um, get to see any of those here?
Most likely. The research station isn't far from a penguin habitat.
Hooray! Heehee... Hm? What is it, Svirepy? You look like something's on your mind.
Round means fat. Fat means ancient people probably ate 'em.
And they lay eggs, don't they? Betcha somebody's made a penguin egg omelet.
Whuh? But penguins are such cute little things... How could anyone be so cruel?!
Round penguins. Tasty penguins. I wonder if we can catch one...
Let me stop you right there!
Remember the Antarctic Treaty? Yeah, it explicitly says all Antarctic animals are protected, whether they fly in the sky or walk on land!
Don't even THINK about eating any of them! It's not gonna happen!
Damn. You live to see another day, penguins...
Phew... That's a relief to hear.
You won't have to worry about food. In addition to the supplies for our expedition, we're also bringing rations to resupply our research station.
Please don't do anything to the little penguins other than adore them, Svirepy.
Yeah, yeah, I know.
Ahh, I get it.
We've come all the way to Antarctica, and you'd hate to leave without trying some of the local cuisine, right?
Yeah? I guess?
Then have I got good news for you! All the animals that fly or walk on land are off-limits...
But all the ones that swim in the water are fair game!
Like krill, for one! It's pretty good!
And don't feel too bummed out about the penguins. According to ancient Antarctic hunters, it hardly tastes any different from chicken.
If you're REALLY craving chicken, then I can roast one for you. You'll just have to make do with that!
Or I could make krill noodle soup. Royalty used to have that at their banquets long ago, so it's gotta be delicious.
Granted, they didn't use krill back then, but still!
Doesn't SOUND that good, but like they say – don't knock it 'til you've tried it.
Wait, you never said you can cook, Pamiat'!
Well, I do! Sometimes. I make old dishes to keep the taste alive in my memory!
BEEP BEEP!
This is research station Mirny.
Kalinka, your signal has been verified. Welcome to Antarctica.
Thank you. It's been a while, Comrade Tallinn.
We've brought you supplies – and gratitude from back home for your commitment to the motherland.
Yeah, thanks. I'll have to cook up something special tonight.
Have to say, you were the last person I was expecting, Soyuz. I really didn't think you'd visit in person.
One sec... There. I sent you the latest map data. There's your route to the station.
Look out for icebergs and hold on to your wheel. I'll come meet you outside the station.

sequence: Iris Orthodoxy - Holy Capital
Northern Parliament Embassy
After the battle's conclusion

scripts.say: Thank you for coming all this way, Commander.
Soyuz told me you had something important for me.
That, I do. It's about the Ring of the Wise – our Antarctic bunker.
You were given information on it during the battle. We had, however, omitted a few details.
Soyuz asked me to provide you with the complete records.
You mean there's even more to it?
I knew that was no mere doomsday bunker, but even what I knew wasn't the full story?
Indeed, it's not. Its true duty has to do with... geomagnetic fields.
The details are all in here. I suggest you read it for yourself.
You cannot bring these documents with you, however. Also, please don't speak a word of this to anyone but me or Soyuz.
So this is some of the most classified stuff the Northern Parliament has.
It is.
Understood. I'll give it a read.
Please do. And thank you, Commander.

sequence: Somewhere in the Southern Ocean
Unknown location
One day after the battle

scripts.say: Tsk... Damn Tribunal and their secret weapons...
Guess rescuing Marco Polo is on the back burner.
New priority – weakening the low-level program presence in this area!
Purifier's mainframe should be somewhere around here...
Come out, come out, wherever you are! Mama's got business with...
...What the heck is this?
A Pawn?
What's a Pawn doing out here?
And why is nobody ELSE here?
There's no way she left the defense of her mainframe to a single Pawn, right? She wouldn't send ALL her units to Antarctica!
Whatever, let's deal with you.
KABOOOM!
I've got places to– Whoa?!
KABOOOM!
A-an attack?!
Shit, that was powerful! Who did that?!
Y-you... What are you?!
Where'd you come from?!
Nobody said I'd be dealing with YOU!
G-god, test site beta is a frightening place!
KABOOOM!
Somewhere, in an unknown location...
A report from Implacable. Concerning the battle in the Antarctic, eh...
Is what you brought Belfast in for earlier?
This is quite an interesting thing indeed.
Heh. Another day, another splendid job.
This is why I'm always saying what a good servant I have!
I've already told Bel to give her full assistance to the Commander in any and all upcoming matters.
Now what, then?
What do you mean, "now what"?
...Hmmmm.
What? Wipe off that smug grin and explain!
We're just wondering how long you're going to stay here.
We did invite you, but not to stay permanently.
You've met Ms. D and you've asked your questions. What else is there for you to do here?
In fact, we thought that little maid was coming to pick you up.
Hmph! I'm the queen! I'll stay until I'm content to leave!
And since I'm here, why don't you bring me along on the next of your "hunts"?

sequence: Sakura Islands
Mikasa's Residence
After the battle's conclusion

scripts.say: God, I'm sooo tired... Feels like I haven't come home in forever.
But now I am! And it feels good to be back in the Empire!
I'm curious why Lady Nagato would summon me here on such short notice...
Then again, I've got a lot of things to report, anyway.
*knock knock*
Shoukaku! Great Veteran! Lady Nagato! I'm here!
...Hello? Anybody home?
...I didn't get the wrong place, did I?
Where IS everybody?
BEEP BEEP!
The call is connecting... but nobody's answering.
What the heck is going on?
Somewhere, in the Bermuda Sea...
...This is the place.
It sure wasn't easy getting here.
Why did the damn Arbiters set up such strong defenses at the outskirts of this branch?
No problems have sprung up in this test site from what I can tell...
You don't think the Arbiters already beat her, do you?
Because if so, that saves us a lot of trouble...
Nah, there's still the chance she hasn't made a move yet.
For the time being, let's gather what intel we can then wait and see.
...Huh? What's that? That's a bear instead of the Imperiya's two-headed eagle.
Wouldn't hurt to check it out...
...Actually, forget it.
Well, ladies...
The sun's activity has flared up.
We'd better wrap things up here quickly then get out.
The strikingly white landscape grew clearer and clearer as the submarine approached Antarctica.
Hazy white monoliths sharpened into icebergs with defined edges, and black spots scattered along the coast clarified into buildings. The research station, too, revealed itself.
So that's Mirny. Our destination.
It's bigger than I thought. And sticks out like a sore thumb.
Sticking out makes it easy to find in an ocean of white. Like, can you imagine trying to locate it on a ship or a plane if it was camouflaged?
It's not about staying hidden from the enemy, it's about being findable by your allies.
Besides, it's not Sirens or other people you should be afraid of out here. It's the environment.
So it's the same idea as paintin' a big red cross on a hospital ship? Got it.
Uh... No, not exactly.
It's not?
Lookie! Tallinn is waiting for us at the pier!
Talliiinn! We're heeere!
Quit shouting! She can't hear us from inside the cabin anyway!
Oh, right! Oops!
Settle down, girls. We'll be anchoring in a minute.
It's extremely cold outside, so don't even think about going outside until you've put on extra warm clothing.
Research Station Mirny - Cargo Loading Pier
One step, two steps, three steps!
Tadah! We've officially touched down in Antarctica!
This is, what, ten thousand kilometers from our base in the Black Sea? What a journey it's been.
It's a miracle we got this far.
Ah... Ahh... ACHOO!
So windy... I'm freezing my face off here!
I KNEW you were going to say that! Here, put this on.
Huh? What the heck is that colorful jacket?
I covered it in lots and lots of adorable accessories! Isn't it cute?
No! It's hideous!
Rude! I think it's cute!
Fine, I'll just hug you then! A nice hug should warm you right up!
Put that thing away first! The thought of gettin' hugged with that gives me chills!
Ah, forget it! I'll just turn on my rigging's engine. Oughta warm me up.
Sounds like you girls have energy to spare even after such a long journey.
Once more, welcome to Mirny, comrades. I'm Tallinn, I run this place.
Don't worry about the cargo. The pier's automated system will handle it.
Come on, let's head inside. You must be freezing out here.
Mirny Interior - Break Room
A thick door closed, isolating the girls from the icy winds outside. Now inside, the Mirny's heating systems slowly warmed them back up.
Phew... I feel alive again.
The difference between in here and out there is crazy. It's two different worlds.
It's nothing but chills and howling winds outside. Here, it's cozy vibes and hot tea.
Hey, doesn't this feel like a doomsday shelter?
When you put it like that... sort of?
There's nothing "sort of" about it.
Outside these walls is unfiltered, brutal nature.
If we were exposed to the elements in this place, we'd freeze to death within the hour.
Which is to say – yeah, this station is absolutely like a shelter.
Anybody else notice how Pamiat' is awfully chatty today? Ain't that weird?
Weird? I think she's very insightful! I like a chatty Pamiat'!
Soyuz, don't you and Tallinn have important things to discuss?
We can't leave these two by themselves. Tell you what, why don't you talk while I give the kids a tour around the station?
Who're you callin' a kid?!
I think she's talking about you, Svirepy!
I'm NOT a kid, ya hear?!
Alright, alright, sorry! Now come on, follow me.
Hooray! We're going on an adventure!
It ain't an adventure! We're only lookin' around and eliminating threats!
Kids, I swear... Hey! Wait for me!
Well, they're gone.
Pamiat'... She's acting strange.
Strange?
Yes. It's only in the little things, but she's not entirely like her usual self.
I suppose she seems a bit different. I wouldn't say it's much of a difference, though.
Maybe the environment is having some effect on her. Who knows.
It's cold and snowy just like our motherland, but even worse. It's been especially stormy here as of late, too.
It's not unusual for sensitive people to respond negatively to the immense isolation out here, either.
So it could simply be the environment...
...Let's dive into the main subject now.
Tallinn, give me a situation report. And a briefing on this unique crystal, please.
Yes, ma'am. A few things have happened during your journey here, actually.
Starting with the crystal. It seems to affect not just riggings, but the environment as well. Snow has started melting substantially faster in the area where it was discovered.
So, logically, we've started calling it "the snowmelt area."
As for the crystal itself, we've collected samples of it from numerous different places around the snowmelt area.
Every sample we've tested demonstrated the same rigging resonance effect.
Precision improved, same with reload time, targeting time... Every variable we tested saw a positive increase. Here are the details.
Now for some bad news. The Eagle Union has dispatched survey teams to the snowmelt area.
No problem with that, you might think. Well, they've sent a lot, and I mean A LOT more shipgirls than I expected.
Yesterday, I saw a massive fleet arrive at their station.
Honestly, it wouldn't surprise me if they were preparing to wage a war.
Wage a war?
But there aren't any Reenactments in Antarctica, and the Sirens have close to zero presence here.
If they're getting ready for a fight, then with whom?
I do not know. Perhaps they have access to some intel that we do not.
What I do know is that this will significantly complicate our mining operation...
Tallinn, have there been any engagements with the Eagle Union?
No, of course not. Just some peaceful back-and-forths in the snowmelt area.
And the fleet that arrived yesterday hasn't even left their station yet.
Whatever they're planning, they're working behind closed doors. Like us.
Any covert activity is off the table, I suspect. They wouldn't have amassed such a large force if stealth was their goal.
Tell me about Iron Blood next. I believe they were the first to discover the crystal.
Have they been up to anything of note?
Nope. I haven't seen any sign of them in the snowmelt area.
Granted, their fortress base is much closer to the area than we or the Eagle Union are.
Maybe they completed their investigation long before we did. It's hard to say.
Oh, but I can say that, unlike us and the Eagle Union, they haven't sent in new forces.
At least, not in public, they haven't.
They haven't sent new forces to Antarctica?
...I see.
I'd like to examine a sample. Could you show me one?
Sure. All the samples we've collected are being stored in the testing area. Follow me.
Mirny - Testing Area
Soyuz was shown to a room illuminated by dim lights. There, protected inside a glass case, she saw a crystal giving off a faint blue light.
Is this one of your samples?
It's enormous compared to what I read in the reports. Why is that?
Ah, well, the initial samples we got were all pretty small.
After some physical tests, though, we discovered that the crystals would merge with others under particular circumstances.
That's not all. The larger the sample, the more strongly it resonates with riggings.
That one is our largest yet. It's the result of merging many samples together.
It's fascinating. May I have a closer look?
Soyuz, do you... Alright.
If you really want to, then me and Poltava will wait outside. Otherwise we might disrupt the resonance process.
I'll lower the glass remotely in a sec. Feel free to examine it all you want.
And don't worry, it's safe. I've tested it myself.
Thank you. I won't take long.
Tallinn and Poltava left the room. A short while later, the protective glass lowered, granting Soyuz direct access to the crystal.
She took a step closer, examining the glowing sample in great detail.
(It looks like a gemstone found in nature. No impurities as far as I can tell.)
(It feels cold, almost like ice... And this blue glow – I wonder if it's somehow related to Wisdom Cubes.)
Associations flashed in her mind, restructuring into ideas that she sorted through.
She looked inward, trying to sense the crystal's effect on her rigging.
(It isn't resonating with my rigging like how the report described. I'm this close to it, and yet, nothing...)
(Maybe it really is true. My hull lacks something critical that everyone else has.)
A moment of hesitation. She shrugged it off and steeled herself.
One step closer. Two. Three. She was now only an arm's length away from the crystal.
(The only thing left is to touch it.)
(Let's see what happens...)
Extending her hand, she softly touched the surface of the sample with her fingertips. Then...
A blank, featureless space. In the middle of it, a door silently stood.
...A door?
I suppose I'll... enter it.
Wow, this transmission quality is pretty good. Even slips past the problem of external monitoring.
Gotta hand it to Aoste, this plan is wild.
He's not the only wild one. You're using your private jet to implement said plan, Dr. Anzeel.
Ahaha! Use it or lose it, right?
*sigh*... Thanks a bunch for forcing me on a business trip. Like I wasn't neck-deep in work already.
You'd have to do it sooner or later. Look on the bright side – traveling with me, you get all the benefits of being on a private jet!
The service is way better than you'd get with the trade union.
Besides, I REALLY need an assistant after Aoste took mine away!
Uggghhh...
In any case, there's no turning back now.
We have around two hours until we're out of signal range.
Time is precious, so let's get down to business, Ms. Creator.
Who are you calling "Creator"? Don't you start mimicking Aoste now!
Oh, my apologies. It's just that I remember a certain someone here started using that word during our last meeting.
I believe we were talking about embedding and adhering concepts, and someone said that a concept and an impression can exist separately for a certain time...
Ugh, stoooooop!
Do you remember?
Look, I came up with it on the spot and just threw the idea out there! I told you not to take it seriously!
Forget about it, will you? It's not worth remembering.
Of course. Sorry for getting us sidetracked. Let's get back on topic.
Sovetsky Soyuz, the ship with a name that was never fully constructed...
What was all that...?
Argh! Aaghh...
Suddenly, a surge of energy pulled on Soyuz's fingers.
Its power was immense, dragging her toward the crystal – as though it was sucking her inside.
Oh, shit...
Urgh... Need to... pull my hand away!
She deployed her rigging. Mustering all the strength she could, she tried desperately to fight the crystal's power.
Maybe seconds passed. Maybe minutes. Maybe even hours.
So exhausting was the struggle for Soyuz that her perception of time was warped inside out.
Her effort was not in vain, however. In fact, she won. The crystal's power let go of her.
Once the blinding blue light had faded, the crystal had shattered into many pieces. Only dim lights lit the room once more.
*pant*... *pant*...
It's over...
It's finally over...
The report said nothing about a phenomenon like this...
It was like... a demon took control of me, and...
...Huh?
What... What happened to my rigging?!
A thunderous sound boomed inside the room, coming right from her rigging.
The beast made of steel let out its first roar – an ice-breaking cry to celebrate its birth into the world.
Its awe-inspiring yet terrifying presence sent a tremble coursing through Soyuz's body.
I can't believe my eyes...
It's... a new rigging...
This output, this ability... It's stronger than even cutting-edge riggings!
Did the crystal do this? That can't be. It's still there; it wasn't consumed... just like a Wisdom Cube.
If it didn't materialize it by converting energy and mass like a Wisdom Cube, then my rigging must've been created through that power alone.
No... It didn't CREATE my rigging.
What it did was restructure my hull...
That is why this rigging doesn't feel alien. It explains the strength I feel coursing through my body and into my rigging.
Most of all, though, I feel like the hole inside my hull has been filled.
I've been made whole...
Unfortunately, that doesn't answer the many questions I now have...
Like how I reached this conclusion. What that vision I saw was about. Why it happened as soon as I touched the crystal...
And those strangers I saw in the vision... They said my name.
It sounded like they were talking about creation through a ship's hull... That's the only thing I know now.
I need to learn more...
BEEP BEEP!
Hey, Soyuz. Sorry to interrupt.
It's alright. I've finished my testing anyway.
Is something the matter?
Actually, yeah. I got a call from Iron Blood's base while you were examining the sample.
They said their fleet came under attack by an unidentified enemy.
They've raised their security level and suggested that we do the same.
...An unidentified enemy? As expected, the Eagle Union didn't muster that force for nothing.
Please ask Iron Blood for specifics about this attack – and relay this news to the Eagle Union as well.
I'm interested in hearing if they "know" anything about what we're up against.
A-an enemy? In Antarctica?!
I TOLD ya this would happen! This is why ya need patrols around the base!
Look who's back. Did you see anything unusual?
No? Nothing out of the ordinary.
Good. Then we'll raise the security level and be on standby until new intel comes–
Hang on a sec. Iron Blood's base is pretty close to the snowmelt area, isn't it?
Then since we're going out to collect samples anyway, we might as well go just a little further and help them out.
What's the alternative? Folding our arms and waiting to see what happens? That's being too passive.
Imagine if it was us instead. Wouldn't you wish someone would come help?
Yes, you're right. If the situation in Antarctica is worsening, we must complete all the goals of this trip before it's too late.
Tallinn, you'll stay here and watch for news and enemies. The rest of us will travel to Iron Blood's base.
Got it. Be careful out there.

sequence: Antarctica
Ice Field
Sometime later

scripts.say: Soyuz, got a minute? I wanted to ask you something.
I know Iron Blood gave us a hand with our own base, and that we should help those in need...
But nobody said you yourself need to go, nor that you had to go at once.
They've built a fortress out there, like the Eagle Union. I think they're able to defend themselves.
You're right.
Iron Blood does not need our assistance. That was clear from the moment they sent us advice instead of a request for help.
Having said that, I see this as a good opportunity to do some reconnaissance.
Now that Bismarck has returned, what strategies does Iron Blood employ? What is their organization like out in this vast desert of snow?
Are their projects from the Friedrich era still ongoing? Has their stance on cooperating with us changed?
These are just some of the things I'd like to know. Things you can't just ask through regularly scheduled messages.
Thus, I want to be proactive and emphasize upfront that cooperation is in both our best interests.
They won't have any reason to refuse help since, naturally, this follows Comrade Commander's principles.
And then there's the mysterious enemy that attacked. I must look into that sooner or later anyway.
Yeah, exactly!
Basically, it's gettin' a lot of shit done at once. Efficient! However you cut it, there's no loss in Soyuz going.
Hey! Look! There's a bunch of buildings over there! I think that's Iron Blood's base!
The girls cast their gazes to where Ognevoy pointed. There was a cluster of Iron Blood buildings, rising from the ice field like concrete shells.
It certainly looks like a military complex. Compare that to our little research station.
Ain't it kinda overkill, though?
Like, ya don't need a sturdy fortress in Antarctica. Siren attacks are so rare out here.
It seems unlikely that it's JUST a research station or a safety measure in case of a Siren invasion.
(Something about this is fishy. Perhaps Friedrich is still in our branch...)
Heehee. Something happened in Antarctica, Soyuz.
Do you wanna know what?
Huh? What are you talking–
...about? What is this?
Pamiat'?
Soyuz was standing completely still, yet the scenery around her changed in an instant.
Pamiat' and the rest of her comrades were gone. In their place, a city made of steel towered in the distance.
Its scale was almost unbelievable. It wasn't so much that the ice field surrounded the city, but rather that the city surrounded the ice field.
Its border stretched from horizon to horizon, and it didn't stop there. Soyuz looked down and realized she was standing not on snow and rock, but rather on metallic pavement.
She was on the edge of a city that was still growing, consuming the silver landscape around it.
(This entire expanse... has become a fortress.)
(No... Could this be the original form of the place where we're standing now?)
Soyuz could not help but be astonished by this sudden thought.
(That's impossible... This cannot be real...)
The scenery changed once more, allowing her no time to digest the thought.
This time, the ground was ablaze and the city was crumbling.
In the sky, a shimmering aurora. The daunting yet splendorous city had collapsed in the blink of an eye.
(What is this? Antarctica's essence? Its truth? Its... future?)
Yet again, thoughts formed from the blank space in the back of her mind.
Yes. This is my story. One of the possible futures for this continent.
Phew...
(Was I just hallucinating? Everything is back to normal, looking as it should...)
Hum-de-dum♪
Pamiat', what exactly did you mean by "your story"?
My "story"? What are you talking about?
Me and Ognevoy were just having a chat. You must've misheard something I said.
Misheard? But...
Are you alright, Soyuz? Are you hearing things?
Not just hearing things. I saw something, too.
Audiovisual hallucinations, eh... You did touch that crystal earlier. Maybe that has something to do with it?
Could be! Her very rigging did get restructured. That takes a huge toll on your body and mind.
Yes... You're probably right.
Are you sure you're okay? Should we stop and take a break?
I'm fine, I promise. The base isn't far now, so let's get out of the cold.
Iron Blood's base was on high alert, ready to respond quickly in case of an enemy invasion.
Getting inside would've been difficult for Soyuz's party, but luckily, a message from Tallinn allowed them inside without much fuss.

sequence: Antarctica
Iron Blood Military Camp
Sometime later

scripts.say: Greetings. I am Königsberg, the head of operations at this base.
Allow me to sincerely thank you, Sovetsky Soyuz and company, for offering us your assistance.
You don't need to thank us. What's the situation?
You've generously come to our aid, and so the least I can do is tell you the facts as they are.
To be honest with you, the situation is quite bad.
(What now? Soyuz said she wanted to do some reconnaissance...)
(Shh! Don't say everythin' out loud!)
As I wrote in my message to you, we have lost contact with the research station near the snowmelt area.
The last message we got from them was, "Engaging unidentified enemy."
Shortly after, the signal started being jammed, and we haven't heard anything more from them.
To make matters worse, we also lost contact with our nearest supply base. The jamming cut us off from them, too.
Due to all these problems, I'm afraid we're in no position to provide any hospitality.
I wasn't expecting your group to come all the way out here to speak to us, let alone offer us help.
I see you've also gotten a new rigging, Soyuz... Congratulations.
What brought all of you to Antarctica, anyway? The new crystal that was discovered in the snowmelt area?
I see word about it reached you quickly.
(That confirms it. It WAS the crystal that the Tribunal was talking about.)
Indeed, it was. However, I also wanted to investigate the phenomena that arose following its discovery.
As you know, abnormal weather is often an omen of an impending Siren attack.
Even ignoring that, it's extremely likely that the unidentified enemy is part of a plot against you.
Perhaps it's a Reenactment, perhaps it's a conspiracy...
Whatever the case, I'd like to know how Iron Blood plans to respond. What will you do?
It depends. We've dispatched a team to the site. What they report back will decide our next move.
If I may ask, what do YOU plan to do?
We are going to head straight for the snowmelt area and conduct an investigation.
It's clear that the abnormal weather and the unidentified enemy are linked to the crystal.
Therefore, a direct investigation will hopefully bring a swift end to this situation.
That's quite brave of you.
I sadly don't have any intel to share on the mysterious enemy, but I will say this...
Please be careful out there.
If I find out anything new, I'll contact you immediately.
Thank you. Likewise, we will let you know if we find anything of note.
Also, I have a proposition to make.
Given that Antarctica is fairly isolated from any faction's sphere of influence, it's hard to argue humanity has a strong presence here.
In the event that a problem arises, I believe all factions present should unite to deal with it.
To facilitate this, I propose an agreement to share what information we gather with other factions as well.
I'm sure that, if present here, Comrade Commander would've suggested the same thing.
Sure. I'm okay with that.
To think you brought up the Commander... Well, I suppose hearing it does convince people.
I'd also like to propose an evacuation plan, in case of a disaster.
We have a special submarine that has the capacity to evacuate all the personnel stationed here.
If we can control the situation, I would like this place to serve as the stronghold from which we conduct all our plans to neutralize the enemy.
But, in the worst-case scenario, I suggest that everyone stationed here gathers at our research station. Then we may evacuate using our submarine.
That is very generous of you.
To tell you the truth, this fortress relies almost entirely on automated defense systems. I'm the sole shipgirl stationed here.
Defending this place without the prospect of reinforcements is, frankly, a bad idea.
To put it another way, this is not a hill worth dying on.
I agree to your evacuation plan.
Should this situation develop into a crisis, I will head straight to your research station.
Thank you. I'll tell Tallinn so she can make arrangements for your arrival in advance.
That should be everything, I think. We will now make our way to the snowmelt area.
Good luck. Do teach the enemy a thing or two about attacking us.

sequence: Antarctica
En Route to the Snowmelt Area
Sometime later

scripts.say: Pfft...
Ahahah! I can't believe Königsberg believed that!
She really thought Soyuz's rigging just got a little upgrade, rather than being rebuilt from scratch using that crystal!
I bet she'd also believe it if we said this gear is all mining and survey gear!
It didn't seem like she knew the Eagle Union had dispatched a huge fleet either.
Either the signal jamming has left her completely clueless, or she was hiding something from us.
Then again, Iron Blood's base is the closest to the crystals, so maybe she's just been blinded by overconfidence.
...You know, I still can't believe the Eagle Union sent such a large fleet. And not just mass-produced ships either, but shipgirls.
Soyuz, I know there's something you're not telling us.
This isn't just about the crystals. You're looking for something else near the snowmelt area.
...So you realized.
I knew something was up. You wouldn't travel across the world with a nonfunctional rigging just to see a quarry.
Tell us already. What ARE you here for?
I'm sorry. I should have told you sooner. Königsberg, too.
In fact, I was supposed to explain this shortly after we arrived on the continent.
This led to that, and, well... But you've brought it up now, and we have some time before we reach our destination.
Let me start by saying that the Eagle Union almost certainly doesn't know what I'm about to tell you.
There is a shelter beneath the snowmelt area. Its construction was a joint effort between us and Iron Blood.
It is a doomsday bunker a thousand meters below the surface. It was built to protect all the people inside no matter what calamity was unfolding on the surface.
Its name is, "The Ring of the Wise."
Naturally, I have no reason to believe it had anything to do with the discovery of the rigging-enhancing crystal...
However, it might just be the reason why the snow on the surface has started melting.
I'll be damned.
A bunker of ours was responsible for the snowmelt.
Königsberg seemed completely unaware of it. I take it this is highly classified intel, then?
It is. I suspect that even you had never heard a word about it until now.
As it should be. Owing to its secret nature, only a very small handful of shipgirls know about its existence.
A bunker's the cause of it, eh... I thought we had another unsolvable case on our hands.
Happens all too often that a cool mystery has a boring explanation.
Let's not jump to conclusions. We don't yet KNOW if the Ring created the snowmelt area.
It shouldn't be able to. It's in a dormant state right now.
The only way it could cause snowmelt on this scale is if someone deliberately activated and modified certain facilities.
Then there is the unidentified enemy and the crystal. Those obviously weren't there during the construction or planning stage.
(If other factions are allowed to investigate freely, it's only a matter of time before they discover the bunker.)
(Even if the Commander covers for us, Naval HQ will nail us for it.)
