Especially now that the Watatsumi's power has nearly run out.
Danger approached the courtyard, the final safe haven left by the Great Sage.
Now that the seal was broken, the dark mist grew stronger. It now tried to encroach upon the last pure land in the Prime Sakura's sanctuary.
Indeed, just as the moon up above was eroded by shadow...
A lunar eclipse...?
The shipgirls gathered by the lake that served as the entrance to the abyss.
That rift lettin' the black mist in is gettin' the moon, too... But that's a whole lot of mist!
Before long, the fleeting night sky had been almost fully engulfed in black mist.
It solidified into the shape of crows and carrier-based craft that flew through the black.
Get behind me, everyone!
Owari, do you still have ammo?
Just a li'l! I can still fight a while!
How 'bout you all?
Of course!
I shall fight, too!
Natori, protect Zuihou! We'll show you what we're capable of together!
Their main guns roared like thunder, shaking their surroundings.
Meanwhile, real thunder crackled beyond the rift.
Purple lightning shone upon the full moon, warding off the black mist.
Lightning, symbolic of the Guardian Fox's authority, flashed multiple more times.
Musashi!
Divine lightning struck the courtyard from above.
Air that had once been filled with black mist cleared up all at once, causing all of the black to disappear in the storm.
The rift in the sky shrunk, and the black mist that had seeped through was sucked back into it.
After peace and calm had returned to the courtyard, Musashi appeared before the shipgirls.
Musashi, it really is you!
Owari, Zuihou, Asanagi, Hatsuzuki. Is that everyone?
Am I to assume that nobody else is here?
Oh... Right!
I dunno if she was the real one or an illusion, but the Great Sage was just here a minute ago!
I see. So the Great Sage is alive and well.
Listen well. The one who created this seal, and thus the Prime Sakura, was not the Guardian Fox. It was the Great Sage.
When disaster fell upon the Prime Sakura long ago, Lady Nagato and I worked with the Great Sage to empower the black mist's seal.
However, due to the Reenactment of Watatsumi, the Great Sage was forced to remain here.
Lady Nagato established the sanctuary outpost in order to research how to rescue the Great Sage, find out how to expel the darkness, and keep an eye on the seal.
Now that the seal has begun to rupture, those who monitor the sanctuary at the outpost...
So we're, like... free from duty now?
Hmm... Now that you mention it, what was that illusion I saw before?
Just to be sure, WE didn't break the seal or anythin' crazy like that, right?
I doubt that. We didn't really help much though, did we...?
I'll have to disagree. The message Owari sent to Kii and the signal flare you fired both helped to notify everyone of this situation.
Thanks to your drive to struggle to the very end, we've managed to barely maintain the sanctuary's seal.
What's this...?
Lady Nagato's charm?
Yes. Use it, now.
Musashi handed it to Hatsuzuki.
When she accepted it, the charm burst into flames and burned up in almost an instant.
Musashi? Wh-what happened?
I didn't do anything wrong, did I? O-or did I mess it up...?
Urk... I burned Lady Nagato's precious charm, just like that...
I've really done it now... Ugh...
You did nothing wrong. This allows Lady Nagato to know where we are.
Light shone from above—that was the signal for teleportation magic.
"It will be but a shell, exhausted of its power, but it should still help you change this nation's future."
Great Sage... No, you are no empty shell.
Consciousness—a blank, white space constructed only of a simple mental image.
To annihilate the black mist is to return it to nothingness.
Not a conflux of heaven and earth, not a harmony of yin and yang. A complete removal.
As if it had never existed in history to begin with.
That is the end of Watatsumi – the end of you and I.
No, perhaps it isn't an end. For we'll have never existed at all.
I, born to bear human wishes. You, born to give them form. Our essence is fundamentally the same.
Am I wrong?
Hmm. Perhaps my attempts to bear the concept of Watatsumi have changed me.
I still can't forget the people I met that night...
With this power, I've seen countless branches destroyed.
I finally realized that this was the only way to ensure survival.
Annihilation. That's the only way.
I know that.
I do.
That is the will of Watatsumi and the Great Sage...
That is the resolve to confront fate, a resolve that cannot be shaken...
Yet I only exist... because my resolve was shaken.
Because I wanted to feel this ever-so-beloved world... To bathe in its sunshine and savor its seasons.
To let the wanderlust take over, to see the smiles of other people.
To throw myself into this beautiful world, just as I did on that rainy night when the wisterias danced.
And... I want to be reunited with you.
That is the reason I am here, after failing to bring the Reenactment to bear.
Waiting for one miraculous moment, not as Watatsumi, not as the Great Sage.
My one desire...
Is to be able to meet you again.
That's all I need.
...Have they made it out of the seal?
Hmm. Perhaps my attempts to bear the concept of Watatsumi have changed me.
That's wonderful.
I've already made up my mind.
First, a swing. Cutting the dark mist's clouds aside, using the momentum to leap forth.
Second, a stab. The blade pierced the enemy's heart and dispersed it.
Black mist condensed once more into the shape of a human.
The Shadow of Corruption reflected her figure, her features, even her presence.
Third, a sweep. The two opponents' swords clashed, sending sparks flying.
Fourth, a quick-draw. She took a half-step back and sheathed her blade. The moment the shadow showed an opening—
She loosened her sword slightly and unleashed a powerful blow upon the defenseless mist.
Haaaah!
The sword drew a crescent moon arc in the darkness of night.
Her strike, affixed with the concept of the seal, cleansed the wicked mist.
All is futile.
As if taunting her, the darkness formed an army and roared as it closed in from all directions.
She jumped straight upward, causing the army to collide and collapse into itself.
She then pulled back her long, flowing clothes, keeping them out of enemy reach as she danced out of range.
All is futile.
She weaved between black figures, aiming for the core—one that emitted a red gleam.
Found you.
She instantly accelerated, aiming her blade tip toward it.
Prepare to be annihilated.
Though the thrust was backed by all her strength, the blade was stopped just short of the core.
This is...
Made not of flesh and blood, the black body emitted an ominous aura.
The Shadow of Corruption seized the blade in its hands and roared.
The end... of me and Watatsumi...
Arm after arm lunged from the black mist, trying to rip the blade away.
The sword broke, and a black shockwave exploded throughout the sanctuary.
Powerless and limp, she fell pitifully onto a floating mass of rock and soil.
The mist's core was once again concealed, and it condensed once more into a horrifying monster. The beast opened its maw and swallowed the sanctuary's protector.
Why have you come again?
No matter how many times I face destruction, I will appear here again.
Because I am you. I am Watatsumi.
Then pass that burden to me.
I... cannot.
This is my duty. Something that only I can do.
The destiny I believe in is different.
Countless times I have seen visions of entire branches, wiped away. Countless times, I have seen them come to fruition until I had no choice but to understand.
Destruction is inevitable. Your efforts will only amplify the pain and misfortune.
Only by abandoning the self and choosing annihilation can you prolong this world's existence.
I see...
Is this my belief as the Great Sage, rather than that of Watatsumi?
How noble it is to bear the weight of the world upon your shoulders. To become a martyr.
But that is the duty of a god, not that of a human.
Who am I to transcend above the mortal realm, looking down upon creation like some sort of god? No salvation can come from that.
I must be... not a bystander of this world, but a member of it... A single grain of sand among many.
Even if all of my effort is in vain...
Even if inevitable destruction comes...
All that I've done to defy destiny will remain as proof that I was human.
In this mental space, she offered a hand to "herself."
Watatsumi, Great Sage... Join me.
As one will. One concept. One shipgirl.
Let us purge the dark mist that threatens to burn the world down.
She held fast to her volition and adjusted the concept that anchored her existence.
In the white space, a kaleidoscope of butterflies surrounded, approached, and crossed between them.
No longer were there two figures confronting each other—they were one now.
In the center of the seal, a shikigami dragon curled up its giant figure.
It made a cocoon, wherein a new being was born.
The light symbolizing the concept of the sanctuary seeped in through the gaps in the paper cocoon.
The concept recorded in her hull bubbled to her surface.
In her rigging, she saw her existence in a new light.
Collected thoughts, engraved memories, defined moments.
Her rigging, though it affixed to her as a mere item, was given life as an essential part of the concept that was her new self.
This is my rigging.
I am... the heavy cruiser Unzen.
Her time as the Great Sage that protected the sanctuary, her time as Watatsumi, had come to an end.
She had taken back her identity as the shipgirl Unzen.
Why, it already fits me like a glove.
The shikigami dragon floated away slowly as another shipgirl appeared before Unzen.
Great Sage... No, Unzen.
I am the blueprint ship, Shimanto. On Musashi's orders, I have come to release you.
Like yourself, your rigging is an embodiment of ideals brought into reality, and that made it difficult for me to gather information...
But my tireless efforts have borne fruit, and your powers have finally been restored.
Now, you are no longer the Great Sage, but a shipgirl of the Sakura Empire just like us.
Without Watatsumi, the seal is extremely unstable, but that also means you are no longer bound to be its steward.
...In short, you've been saved by the great Dragon God.
Well, Owari helped too, but the sudden rupture of the seal meant I had to adjust my plan on the fly.
Sorry. To make it up to you, I'll pass on the offering this time. Call us even.
Great Dragon God, allow me to correct you about one thing.
While Watatsumi indeed played an important role, it was not the only thing maintaining the seal.
For me... No, for all of the Sakura Empire...
This battle is not over yet.
That's right.
However, now that I am no longer the Great Sage, it will be much more difficult to control the sanctuary's power.
I can confirm that the Guardian Fox is deploying the ritual, but there isn't much time left to destroy the black mist's core.
To that end, I humbly beseech your assistance.
Say no more!
Behold– the might of the Dragon God!
The concept of the seal had weakened, and Unzen now confronted the black mist with Shimanto's support.
Shimanto protected herself with her shikigami dragon, supporting Unzen from afar as she sailed through the void sea.
Despite the paper-like appearance of her rigging, Shimanto was easily able to repel the attacks from the black mist.
Unzen, now!
Now, may this place be cleansed by my flames!
The explosive impacts of her artillery fire caused the shadows to reel back.
The corruption is gathering... It's going to unleash its full might!
The serpentine heads of the beast created by the creeping shadows continued to grow longer and longer.
The leviathan's coils continued to grow and expand, casting a profound darkness across all who turned who would turn their heads upward at it to wallow in their utter insignificance.
No effect. In that case...!
The Dragon God struck again, but her attacks were not even enough to cause a ripple in the infinite darkness.
The next moment, another of the leviathan's heads erupted from the water's surface, bearing its unfathomable form down upon the shipgirls there.
The beast seemed inevitable.
The paper dragon placed itself in the path of the mist's onslaught, but shattered the moment it came into contact with its yawning maw.
All seemed to be futile–
Impurity be purged!
In a flash, only a single blade of cold steel held the threshold before the abyss.
Back off, you two!
Using the massive beast's momentum, Ibuki parried the leviathan's head aside and sent it hurtling into a nearby island.
Just as quickly as she had appeared to save the day, Ibuki disappeared beneath the eruption of debris, leaving the other two to scramble for cover.
Unzen and Shimanto looked at each other with tacit agreement. They had to find a way to mount a counterattack, and fast.
Lady Nagato doesn't have much time left... Unzen, do you have a plan?
When asked, Unzen thought for a moment before releasing her rigging.
That part of her being became butterflies of light that disappeared into her left eye.
Shimanto, I have a request.
Sure. I'll do whatever it takes!
If we can break the "core" of the black mist, we'll be able to fend it off long enough to restore the seal.
But that involves jumping into the depths of that darkness. We'll only have one chance.
I will need to call upon the Prime Sakura to make that moment count–
Understood. Before that though, I'll do my part–
...and clear a way to the core!
Outside the sanctuary...
Sakura Empire - Nagato's Abode
It was just before dawn, and the horizon to the east was beginning to brighten.
The Guardian Fox's little sister, Mutsu, opened a silk pouch and retrieved the roll of paper from within.
Inside was a message from Nagato. A mere few lines of text.
Huh?!
Lady Mutsu, where are you going?
We have to help Nagato! Kawakaze, get ready, fast!
Send a message to everyone in the Sakura Empire! We need to light the lanterns!
In almost no time at all, a massive lantern rose in the sky above the castle's ramparts.
It ascended higher and higher, carried by the Prime Sakura's power, shining more brilliantly than the brightest star.
After a long night of guard duty, Sakawa witnessed the lanterns' rise from her bedroom.
She rushed outside, to the site of Musashi's own giant lantern, where she ran into Kii.
W-woah, what's the occasion? Did someone start a festival without me or something?
Unlike Sakawa, who was still scrambling to order her thoughts in her head, Kii was quite calm in comparison – almost even excited.
We only light the big lanterns to notify everyone of an emergency, right?! Then that means...
Lady Nagato calls for aid!
And the Sakura Empire will answer.
Let's light the giant lantern!
Another lantern ascended skyward.
Before long, others began to rise in response. Lights began to dot the horizon, as far as the eye could see.
One after another, the lanterns rose into the skies, forming their own galactic river in the early morning sky.
And, as if guided by said river, they slowly floated toward the Prime Sakura.
Nagato...
Mutsu gingerly placed one hand on the sacred tree, its dry bark betraying its spent power more clearly than ever before.
The Sacred Sakura trees, symbols of human wishes – their indomitable will to dream – were all connected by their roots to the Prime Sakura.
While corruption could spread through these roots, so too could the heartfelt wishes that nourished the Sacred Sakura.
Countless hands from all over the Sakura Empire extended toward the Prime Sakura's sanctuary, gently holding its withered roots and imbuing it with vitality.
Nagato...
This has to help you somehow, Nagato...
Nagato, please be safe.
A flash of a sword dispersed the thick, black mist.
Lady Shimanto, Lady Unzen, leave this place to me!
Ibuki?
Yes! I had resumed training for the sake of my master, but the way the air had changed made me suspicious, so I entered the sanctuary...
I-I do know that I shouldn't enter the sanctuary without permission, but I was just so worried about what was happening in here.
Anyway, long story short, I came running to help you all.
As a fellow member of the Sakura Empire, I cannot overlook this situation!
I may not be much help, but I offer what protection I can give!
Unzen faced the rampaging beast anew and tightened her grip on her twin swords. A new power flowed into them and coalesced around her blades, giving them a new form.
She recalled the sight of her own countless failures in past dreams.
Her swords hadn't been broken yet, and she now had others by her side.
Light gathered around her, creating many swords with the power of the concept of cleansing.
They created a wall of flashing steel around the shipgirls, repelling any shadows that dared encroach.
Closer...
Just a little closer...
She channeled all her focus into a single point as she continued parrying and warding off the darkness, drawing ever nearer to the core.
No matter what attacks the enemy threw at her, she knew that she was not alone.
Shimanto and Ibuki had been beside her this entire time.
Lights from bursts of flame and glints of steel continued to dance and weave together, never wavering while she was yet to complete her work.
Unzen!
We're not going to be able to hold out much longer!
Unzen!
Lady Unzen, you'll have to go the rest of the way yourself!
Shimanto's shikigami dragon had already caught on fire, yet it still tried to throw itself in the way of the enemy.
Ugh... My blade's about to give out...
Ibuki cast a single glance at the notches that the shadow's teeth had left in her dulled blade, before anointing it once more in the flames of battle without hesitation.
I mustn't subject you to any further danger...
Soon, my blade will reach the core!
Lady Unzen!
I must withdraw!
Finally, the place where Ibuki once danced her flurry of blades fell dark and silent.
Unzen was all alone.
The leviathan of shadow looked down upon the tiny speck of light within its domain of endless darkness with the contempt of a god.
「Meaningless. Futile. Hopeless. Worthless. All is in vain.」
You're wrong.
Nothing lasts, like bubbles on the water's surface. Wasted effort, like a castle of sand before the inevitable tide.
It isn't futile at all.
I've witnessed the destruction of countless branches.
Each time, I made the same decision.
I believed it was the Great Sage's destiny to be annihilated from existence along with you.
I believed it was Watatsumi's destiny to be the cocoon from which fate hatched.
But I am not the Great Sage, and I am not Watatsumi.
Redundant. Ostentatious. Unavailing. The incoherent mutterings of someone lost in dreams.
Indeed. I tried to banish my emotions so that I could become the vessel through which the Reenactment would bear out.
But now, my hull is full of emotions that never should have been let in.
Yearning for another, the desire to see them again...
Doubt, hesitation, indecision, irresolution.
All of these emotions define who I am, here and now.
I am a shipgirl, and I am a human.
...am no god.
And neither are you!
The released power of the sacred tree filled the seal and became a sword of energy that pierced the sky.
Both the cloud canopy and Shadow of Corruption alike were split in two, showing a glimpse of a different-colored sky beyond.
The leviathan of mist writhed, as if feeling real agony.
Already having lost its form, the mist began gathering in one place.
Instead of launching a counterattack, or even displaying a hint of malice, it was actually trying to flee.
Unzen!
Shimanto, are you alright?
Heheh, remember, I am the Dragon God! That was nothing to me...
We mustn't let the core escape us!
The corpse of the beast spat out a black mass that emitted dark-red light as it passed over the shipgirls' heads.
Is that... the core?!
We can't possibly catch up from here!
It was then that the clouds covering the sky opened up.
That was the sanctuary sky that Sakuran shipgirls knew. The sight outside of the seal.
Seemingly of its own volition, the core ascended toward the opening in the clouds.
In that case...!
Unzen fired her cannons, but the core had already escaped just beyond her range.
At this rate, the calamitous black mist would reach the outside world—
Haaaaaah!
The core collided with a glowing, pink pattern—the seal.
The glyphs of power spread like ripples on water, engulfing the entirety of the black mist.
The moment it had the mist in its clutches, the seal condensed into the roots of the Prime Sakura, the center of the ritual.
Time seemed to flow backwards. The withered Prime Sakura and the islands of earth floating in the air all began returning to their original form.
Thus, the black mist was sealed once more.
Lady Nagato!
I-I made it...
Great Sage... I've repaired... the seal...
No sooner as those words left her lips, Nagato collapsed to the ground, unconscious.
The nearly-escaped core had been dragged instantly back into the seal. Now, its presence was seemingly gone.
Lady Nagato!
Ibuki rushed to help her.
...Phew. Thank goodness, it's just fatigue.
Even for the Guardian Fox, performing a ritual of such scale by force...
How much did she have to push herself for that? Phew...
I sure do have a long way to go.
Exhausted from the fierce battle, Shimanto collapsed to her knees to take a break.
Lady Nagato, Shimanto, Ibuki. It's an honor to have fought with you.
Unzen stabbed her swords into the soil. As the sacred tree's remaining power had returned to the sanctuary, the swords disappeared as well.
It's almost time.
One blue butterfly landed by Unzen, followed by hundreds, no, a thousand more.
The light cast by their wings extended slowly toward the Prime Sakura.
Voices of the other shipgirls in the sanctuary reached them from afar.
Amidst the cherry blossom-colored rain, the Prime Sakura also slowly merged with the light...
Floating along the river towards destinations unknown.
When they turned back, Unzen was already gone.
When the Great Sage began the ritual, the scenery before them changed.
The magnificent Prime Sakura abruptly began to wither, the flowers and leaves upon its intricate branches falling as if all life had been drained from it.
Lady Nagato, now! Go into the seal!
Before the impure darkness could overwhelm them, they stepped into the Prime Sakura.
The earth shattered, and a black haze spewed forth like a geyser.
Chunks of ground that had been thrown into the air continued to float, as if gravity no longer had any effect.
They were now in the Prime Sakura, where the Watatsumi star fragment lay.
Light shone from what seemed to be the tree's roots.
The deeply-embedded roots were yanked out of the ground before rising up into the air with the rest of the massive tree.
Lumps of earth looked like shining pink crystals as they reflected the dazzling light around them.
Despite knowing that not everything they saw was necessarily reality, the group was overwhelmed by the sight of the inner seal.
Such power...
Is this Watatsumi...? No, the core of that crystal—
Huh?! Lady Nagato!
Sensing danger, Musashi rushed over to Nagato's side with sword in hand.
Even as the devouring darkness threatened to swallow the two of them whole, Nagato focused herself entirely on communing with Watatsumi.
She closed her eyes tight, focusing every fiber of her being into feeling the star fragment's lingering power.
She reached for the light in the distant darkness, like navigating towards a lighthouse on a dark stormy night, like grasping for a tree's roots when caught in a flood.
Then, finally...
Shard of the fallen star! Shine your light upon my path forth!
Lady Nagato!
With a violet spark, the dark mist reaching out to seize the girl from behind was snuffed out.
That was too close... Thank you, Musashi.
I've made contact with Watatsumi. Now, we can proceed to the center of the seal.
As a result of the ritual, the void around the shipgirls changed. Now, an invisible sea spread out beneath their feet.
This will make movement and fighting easier. I'll lead the way now.
Musashi, stay on guard. Something is eroding the seal, trying to break through.
Countless rays of light slowly extended from Watatsumi in the center of the darkness, drawing some kind of pattern.
An enormous gate, symbolizing the sealing ritual itself, had appeared before them.
I'm going into the center now... Huh?!
Main cannons, prepare for salvo!
Nagato fired her cannons, crushing the approaching black mist. However, she did not erase it entirely.
Right rudder, sharp turn!
Huh?!
The dark haze took the form of a giant beast, opening its maw to attack.
Urgh...!!
Musashi immediately materialized her rigging and used her turret's plating to stop the beast's bite.
Hold it back!
Musashi's main guns fired shells that exploded in mid-air, sending pellets forth in a fan shape that tore through the beast of black mist.
Lady Nagato!
I know! Type 3 shells...
Main cannons, prepare for salvo!
Another thick hail of shells struck the beast, causing its physical form to disperse back into the darkness.
Look out, Musashi! It's a trap!
The dispersed darkness tore into Musashi's armor like a giant maw, a shower of sparks erupting as a portion of her rigging was torn straight off.
Nngh...
So you created just a maw instead of an entire body that we can shoot at, huh?
Not bad... Looks like even monsters are capable of learning...
But I won't let you interrupt Lady Nagato!
If cannons won't work... How about facing my lightning?
–––KRRZZSHHH!!
Faster than the eye could react, Musashi's sword had already found its way through the dark mist.
Where lightning flash met darkness, the mist seemed to melt away into nothingness.
It sputtered and sizzled with a hoarse screech, like droplets of water sublimating on a hot iron plate.
I thought we had been cut off, Great Sage, but I see you're still protecting us.
The mist is weaker here now. Lady Nagato, let's move on!
Musashi shed the rest of her rigging and rushed forward with her blade drawn.
Then, she looked to the black mist blocking the way forward and readied her sword.
Thunderbolt that shines through eternal night, gather upon my blade.
With this strike, I carve a way forward!
Lightning shot from Musashi's katana, brushing aside the darkness and clearing the way in front of them.
It won't hold for long! We must press on!
Past – Somewhere in the Sakura Islands
The special exercise to decide the new flagship, along with the events with Kaga, Amagi, and Akagi, had passed.
How is Lady Nagato doing?
Presumably safe and sleeping in the Prime Sakura?
However, I don't think that's what it's for...
Don't ever breathe a word of this to anyone again.
...Yes, ma'am.
Anyway, are you sure I should really just write that Lady Nagato gave up her position as flagship because of the Reenactment?
If she's hurt, then we should really tell everyone...
We don't know how others might act if it's known that the Sakura Empire Combined Fleet's flagship is wounded and unable to battle.
Lady Nagato herself has expressed that she would like it to be known as simply part of the Reenactment.
You and I are here to obey.
Seemingly understanding, Kii quickly nodded and left the room.
Musashi looked at a little girl sitting behind the curtain—particularly, at the treasure in her hands.
"Can what the Great Sage gave us really change the Sakura Empire's future...?"
Yes. I'd thought it a Wisdom Cube, but it displays wildly different characteristics.
So far, there is little that I know about it.
"Hmm... What of Shinano?"
It seems she has inherited some of the Great Sage's dream powers...
She cannot fully control them, making the boundary between dreams and reality fuzzy for her. This is why she hasn't woken up.
"Then let's move her to the Diadem of Light. It's far from our mainland, so that will keep her far from the trouble stirring here."
"If Shinano wakes up... then offer her my blessings on my behalf."
Yes, gladly.
Mmnh... Lady Musashi? Is it already over...?
Then I'm gonna go change clothes and go to bed...
Of course. Make sure you brush your teeth first.
Good night, Minazuki.
What are you planning, exactly?
...Yamato.
The light fragrance of mugwort tickled her nose. Warm rays of sunshine caressed her cheek.
In a world of comfort, Unzen awakened.
Nnh...?
Her mind was still a mess, and her eyes had yet to adjust to the bright light.
Good morning, Unzen.
Ibuki helped her sit up.
It seemed she was in a Sakuran room, and a rather fancy one at that.
Are you thirsty? Heheh, how would you like some mugwort tea?
Ibuki handed her a cup of tea, just barely steaming. This was the source of the fragrance.
Allow me to introduce myself properly. I'm Ibuki, and I've been tasked with taking care of you here in the sanctuary.
Fragmented memories finally began to connect.
Once the black mist had been sealed again, Unzen's body had begun to disintegrate.
I'm so glad you're okay, Unzen.
Out of joy, Ibuki sat on the bed and grasped Unzen's empty hand.
The texture of her hand told Unzen that this wasn't a dream.
Ibuki, where's Watatsumi...?
The star fragment she'd given Musashi had once been the backbone of the seal, but now, it was believed to be powerless.
While the seal was being repaired, the Prime Sakura had already begun to disappear. When Unzen looked outside now, she saw no trace of it.
More precisely, what once had been the Prime Sakura had reverted into a sapling.
A figure with a red parasol stood on the shore of the lake surrounded by pink crystals.
Are you curious about the Prime Sakura?
After we found you in the middle of the lake, a new tree started to grow where the roots of the Prime Sakura were.
Heheh, Amagi goes to visit every day.
Amagi? But I thought she already...
About that... Well, it would be best if you asked her yourself.
Oh, but you're still recovering, so don't push yourself too much.
If you want to just take a light stroll, I can get your clothes ready for you. Would you like that?
Yes, if you wouldn't mind.
I'd be happy to, Unzen.
Past Sakura Empire – Nagato's Abode
Wanderlust would be an apt word.
As the Commander of a fleet, it was common for me to travel to other places.
I got many opportunities to travel all over the world and learn the customs of various lands.
However, the responsibility on my shoulders made it difficult for me to relax and have fun.
I open up the itinerary and check my plans for the day.
A packed schedule, a whole mountain of notes left by my friends... It's enough to make me dizzy.
But, I signed up for this, and I can't let something like this discourage me.
Plus, I happen to have a little bit of free time before my next engagement.
Maybe it would be a good idea to take a breather.
Now that I think about it, the Sakuran tour guide showed me around various places and introduced me to quite a few shipgirls.
We'd visited places together, tried all kinds of foods...
Worked, sat through endless meetings...
Looking back, I had to give speeches and manage the proceedings, so I was focused the whole time...
Whoops. Can't let those kinds of thoughts get to me too much.
I tidied up my clothes and made my way over to the dinner venue Nagato had invited me to.
The dinner party was in full swing.
We were here to have a peaceful, friendly time together, but the party had gotten a bit rambunctious for my tastes.
So, I came up with a reason to slip away from the venue to catch a breath of fresh air.
Being out in the courtyard in the cool evening breeze was refreshing to say at the very least.
I even decided to check out a little side trail.
I walked around, slowly and aimlessly, under the moonlight.
Certainly, much better than the stifling feeling of being inside.
Just being there in the moment felt so peaceful for some reason, like I was liberated from all the stuff I constantly have to think about normally.
I lost track of how long I had been walking for, and how many corners I had turned.
But soon, the dark and narrow path opened up into an elegant courtyard.

Everything there, from the architecture to the arrangement of the decorations to the landscape, seemed to have been placed deliberately and tastefully. The dim glow of a lantern gave it a delicate yet profound atmosphere.
A calming, comforting scene.
I took a few steps, and saw the moonlight reflecting off the surface of a little pond.
And next to the gleaming water was a shipgirl clad in white.
She might be the owner of this place... Should I apologize for entering without permission?
Did you find our cuisine satisfactory?
Ahh, umm... I'd like to apologize for barging in first.
No worries. The way here is rather jumbled to begin with.
To pass through my barrier, you had to overcome the realm of possibility to arrive here.
Hmm, perhaps I should say... that this is fate?
She seemed to speak in riddles, as if pondering to herself.
You look rather worn down by the banquet. My condolences.
Am I being that obvious about it?
Well, that isn't all. You're different, in many ways.
You're one to talk...
Hmm... I wonder what makes you say that.
A brief look of astonishment flashes across her delicate features.
Then, our eyes met.
I saw within them something akin to joy and loneliness.
Unexpectedly, I felt myself getting jittery and had to break eye contact first.
She was a shipgirl, of course, but staring at each other too long might lead to misunderstandings.
In any case...
Are you waiting for someone here?
It felt awkward just standing there in silence, so I tried changing the subject.
...No, I was just lost in thought.
Really?
If something's wrong, you can talk to me about it.
It didn't take long for me to regret my thoughtless offer.
This was my last day at the Sakura Empire. I was supposed to start packing after the dinner party.
Despite my job and ability to travel, I didn't know when I'd meet her again.
Add the war with the Sirens, and this might be the last time I'd ever see this stranger.
Oh, but if you're not in the mood to talk about it right now, we can another time.
Another... time?
I'm kind of sating my wanderlust right now. It's just, you know, it'd be nice to meet again someday.
Wanderlust...
People talk about once-in-a-lifetime encounters, and all, but we should always be optimistic where we can.
I mean, look. I already slipped through your barrier and met you this time.
This time, she was the one to turn away bashfully.
Under the moonlight, the two of us gave ourselves up to the passage of time.
Neither of us said a word, but we were comforted by this silent time together.
Eventually, I told her that I'd best get back to the dinner party. When I turned around to do just that...
She grabbed my hand and gestured with her eyes up to the moon in the sky.
...The moon is lovely tonight, isn't it?
Her beautiful, yet fleeting smile would be forever burned into my memory.
Commander?
Commander, we're going to land soon.
Essex? Why are you still here?
If you want to attend Richelieu's ceremony at the Iris as an Eagle Union representative, you'll need to hurry and get ready.
I prepared new clothes for you, so let's go change, okay?
And Commander, I think you should get ready, too.
My friends' voices faded along with their footsteps.
I've been steeped in nostalgic memories for a little too long.
Today, I'll be in Europa...
There was a loud rumbling, followed by calm. It seemed we'd landed without issue.
I still had far too many plans today.
Things are going to be busy for a while...
I closed my eyes, trying to squeeze out every moment of rest.
The face of the woman I met that night, along with the scenery of that mysterious moonlit encounter, came to mind.
Yeah... I'm sure we'll meet again. Somewhere, someday.
Great Sage of the Sakura Empire... Unzen.

sequence: "One step closer are you to revealing the truth of this world."
"While you have shed the penumbra of the past,"
"The true darkness is yet to come."
"Trees seek quietude, but the wind refuses to stop blowing."
"Now then, how will you proceed?"

scripts.say: They reached the center of the seal and attempted to perform the ritual. However...
The barrier's defenses still resist the erosion...
We must continue to protect Watatsumi until the Great Sage's ritual is complete.
If Watatsumi is destroyed first, the seal itself will break.
Indeed. However, it seems easier said than done...
Musashi looked upward, beyond the withered Prime Sakura's trunk.
At the canopy, the giant eyes of the black mist beast glowered down at the shipgirls.
That ominous being was none other than the shadow of calamity.
And when she looked further up, toward the sky...
A shooting star? No, is that the Great Sage...?
"Once upon a time, a star fell from the northern sky." So this is what the legend meant...
She's merged with the concept of Watatsumi and reinforced it. Now, she's trying to eradicate the darkness herself...
Musashi, that legend said that the stars set themselves ablaze!
Does she mean to burn out her own life—
Cutting off Musashi's words, the star falling from the sky struck the Prime Sakura.
The light emitted from Watatsumi was as brilliant as a jewel.
...Am I hallucinating?
What remained was a fragment of memory.
A sea of clouds. From the dark clouds emerged an eldritch beast, devouring all in its path.
The Prime Sakura was wreathed in flames.
The black mist, now in the form of a shadowy leviathan, was tearing at its trunk with its fangs.
(RUN...! RUN, NOW...!)
Is this... one of our cities...?!
Lady Nagato, look!
Amidst the raging windstorm, the dark mist eroded the boundary between land and sky.
Beneath a blood-red moon, ordinary citizens scrambled for safety from the conflagration roaring around them.
From the highest point in the city, the roof of the castle tower, a woman clad in white stepped forth.
She looked down across the surging, roiling mist, a deep sorrow etched upon her face.
The Great Sage...
Before Nagato could call out to her, the Great Sage leapt from the tower and became a flash of light that pierced the mist.
What formed was a mirage of memories.
The mirage changed again, this time into the scene of spring they had witnessed before entering the sanctuary.
Blue skies above, a gentle breeze caressing their cheeks.
Atop a tall hill in this peaceful world, the woman in white awaited Nagato and Musashi.
Great Sage...
What was that vision? Are you... okay?
Guardian Fox. Musashi.
You two had the same dream, as I recall.
Some say that dreams are an extension of reality, while others call them a reflection of your mind.
Unlike you, however, I dream of potential futures.
To be honest, I've dreamed of that same future of destruction countless times.
Tens... No, hundreds of times, even.
I was able to act of my own will, so I investigated various things throughout the dreams.
That beast of black mist that withers the Prime Sakura and brings calamity to the Sakura Empire...
I call it the Shadow of Corruption.
While Watatsumi, that which fell from the heavens, gives us the wisdom and power to expel evil...
The Shadow of Corruption, too, will inevitably become the calamitous darkness.
...Did Watatsumi and the black mist come at the same time?
Yes. Like two sides of a coin, like light and shadow.
Wherever there is light, there is also darkness. Normally, they maintain balance instead of leading to ruin, but...
But due to this anomaly, you've witnessed our future.
The more Watatsumi's power is used, the stronger the darkness's influence becomes.
No, even if Watatsumi's power isn't used, as Wisdom Cubes grow stronger...
I... don't understand what you're saying.
Are you saying that Watatsumi and Wisdom Cubes are one and the same?
To be more precise, they're similar but different. As time passes and branches shift, our names for them change as well.
Regardless of the name you call them by, they tap into the same wellspring of power that gives form to our hulls... In other words, a conduit to a root source.
Humans may wield this power and manifest it in different ways, but this primordial wellspring is far beyond their ability to control.
Nevertheless, if we do not define it in terms of human cognition, we would have no way of understanding its scale on a cosmic level.
What do you mean to say...?
A miraculous entity born of countless wishes, interwoven with the laws and truths of countless worlds.
That is Watatsumi. That is me.
"Once upon a time, a star fell from the northern sky."
"Darkness spread from the sea in which it fell. The stars set themselves ablaze to create a blinding light that sealed the darkness into this sanctuary."
KABOOOOOOM!
Thus, Watatsumi struck the Sakura Empire. Its enormous power radiated from the point of impact.
Amidst scorching light, pink crystals emerged from the shattered earth and accelerated upward into the sky.
This is...the Prime Sakura...
The sanctuary that seals the dark mist...
The vision faded, and Nagato and Musashi saw the current spectacle within the sanctuary once more.
The Shadow of Corruption, created by the Reenactments and given form by the black mist, seemed to writhe in agony.
The ominous black fog closed in from all directions.
Musashi tried to cut it away with her purple lightning blade, but the severed darkness only reformed again to attack.
Bear witness! Haaaah!
Materializing her mental imagery, Nagato's prayer became a guiding light that drove off the darkness.
However, it was weak, and it only managed to slow the darkness's encroachment temporarily.
We only have one choice now.
Musashi, I'll entrust the last of the Guardian Fox's power to your blade. Strike true, and cut a way out of this situation!
...You mustn't.
Even if I were to escape, you...
It is my duty as a miko to protect the Sakura Empire.
I vowed to do so, and I showed you my resolve during our game.
Bear witness... to the Guardian Fox's power!
The young woman forcibly pushed the sheathed sword into Musashi's arms.
In the next instant, the blackness engulfed Nagato.
Lady Nagato...!
Pure nothingness—a world devoid of sound or light, home only to endless darkness.
Nngh... What was all that...?
In the distant future, one girl would witness these events in a vision.
Past – Nagato's Abode
Before the Great Sage would become the foundation of the new seal in the Prime Sakura's sanctuary...
In a room for treating guests, Kawakaze, a disciple of the Guardian Fox, placed white cups of fresh tea in front of a guest.
Though her etiquette was rather simple, the refreshing aroma of the fresh tea was proof that the host would never neglect their guests.
After repeating this process several times, Kawakaze bowed, opened the sliding door, and gracefully exited the room.
Great Sage, I'd like to talk about the withering of the Prime Sakura you informed us of.
I've looked into it, and I've received one other report of a Sacred Sakura withering...
Are these two situations related?
I have to apologize. There's something I haven't disclosed to you two.
The roots of every Sacred Sakura in this empire are all connected to the Prime Sakura.
If the roots are severed by the erosion, even these hallowed trees will not be able to recover.
They will be cut off from nutrients, and eventually wither.
As for the report you received, its cause can be traced back to the Prime Sakura itself.
A breeze blew through the window, bringing in some flower petals.
One of them happened to fall right into the Great Sage's teacup.
Even this one petal of the Sacred Sakura...
...Shows that the erosion is spreading throughout all the nation.
If left alone, the Prime Sakura and all of its children will wither.
Hmm... If that is true, then we have to resolve this as soon as possible.
Great Sage, can we presume that the source of the erosion is somewhere within the Prime Sakura?
I suppose you could say that it is "somewhere" inside of it, yes...
The Great Sage said, evasively, before continuing to speak.
More precisely, the Prime Sakura itself is the source.
What...?!
Nagato was surprised, but the Great Sage offered no further explanation. She simply stared at the petal floating in her teacup.
*knock* *knock*
Kawakaze?
Lady Nagato, the dinner party is ready. Everyone is waiting for you.
...I'm sorry to cut the conversation short, but I have important guests to entertain over the coming days.
I understand you're a wanderer, but would you please stay here until I'm done? We can plan to deal with the Sacred Sakura problem then.
After the Guardian Fox's request, the Great Sage closed her eyes in quiet thought for two, three seconds.
The sound of wind chimes traveled through the window and into the spacious room.
...I would like to take you up on that offer, Guardian Fox.
Nagato's expression softened slightly. That was exactly what she wanted to hear.
After drinking down the tea given to her, she stood up and followed her aide.
Once the little girl's footsteps had faded into the distance...
Musashi, I'd like to ask you one more thing.
How is Shinano doing?
...I see there's no point trying to hide anything from you.
Sorry to trouble you. But... Could you let me meet her?
If that is your request, then I won't decline.
But it's too late today. Let us plan for another... No, I'm sure tomorrow will do just fine.
Thank you. Tomorrow is perfect.
Now, I have other business to attend to, as well. Spend your time as you please.
Finally, the Great Sage was left alone in the room.
She had no plans for some time, so she decided to enjoy the rest of her tea as she admired the courtyard.
It was already evening. Golden light reflected on the lake water.
Perhaps she ought to pay a visit to the dinner party.
Past – Musashi's Abode
The next day, on Musashi's invitation, the Great Sage visited Shinano's room.
When she listened carefully, she heard faint breathing behind the screen door.
She carefully opened the door, trying not to make a sound, and glanced inside before closing it again.
Could Shinano be related to the Sacred Sakura's withering?
No, I believe it's due to the influence of our roots – our hulls.
That isn't something particular to Shinano, but at the same time, it isn't exactly easy to solve.
Does this mean... Amagi too...
Yes, but...
There may be no way to reverse an injury of that extent.
The Great Sage went into the hallway, put a hand on the fence, and finally looked back to Musashi.
The Prime Sakura's sanctuary.
Please pay me a visit there. Bring Lady Nagato, if you'd please.
We may be able to talk now, but my real body cannot leave that sanctuary.
If possible, I'd like to talk about the most important matters there.
Come to its trunk, and I shall tell you everything.
Great Sage, I understand your wishes...
But leaving me aside, why Lady Nagato... Why did you choose us?
As the inheritor of the Guardian Fox, Lady Nagato has a power that nobody else has.
As for you, Musashi, I would simply be more at ease if you protected her.
She is the miko who protects the Sacred Sakura, and you...
(I hope you... will protect Mizuho's seas and skies once I'm gone.)
Present Day – Prime Sakura Sanctuary
In a corner of the Prime Sakura's sanctuary, shipgirls on guard duty were enjoying their work.
Where did Hatsuzuki go off to?
One bored little girl glanced occasionally at the Prime Sakura from the guardroom she was cleaning.
She claimed she went off in search of Owari, but I assume she's simply bored.
Really? She looked kinda pale when she left...
Pale? Hahaha!
Why, anyone would look pale if they were plagued all throughout the night by nightmares!
Hmph... She could've talked to us about it.
This is the first time she's just up and disappeared.
You worry too much, Zuihou.
Nothing will actually happen in this boring little outpost.
Think about it. This is the Prime Sakura's sanctuary, a sacred place in our empire.
Taboo aside, this place is protected by the Guardian Fox's barrier.
Why, you could go out and play all alone, and nothing bad would happen to you.
And really, I think it's for the best that nothing happens.
Shh!
Geez, Asanagi! You can't let Owari hear that!
She doesn't say it, but she takes this job REALLY seriously!
"It's like, nature, y'know? Nobody as far as the eye can see, it's all just grass and little animals!"
"Kinda like we're livin' in the sticks!"
"For me, you can't get much more nostalgic than that!"
That's what she said! Not that it made a lot of sense to me...
Oh ho. So that's how it is...
Regardless, that doesn't mean she cares about the mission. She just enjoys being in this environment!
E-either way!
As protectors of the sanctuary, we have to do our job!
That means you, too, Asanagi! If you're bored, then let's go search for Owari and Hatsuzuki!
If anything happens, our homeland Mizuho...
Just then, they heard a girl calling out from outside the guardroom.
The girl, clad in red and black, jumped out from the horizon and rushed toward the courtyard.
What was that sound?
Look! There's Hatsuzuki!
She's in a real hurry. Is someone chasing her?
*BEEP BEEP BEEP*
The communicator's beeping!
Zuihou snatched up the communicator and listened in close with Asanagi.
*rustle* *rustle*
H-hurry and get ready...!
Hatsuzuki's breathing was ragged, and her voice faltered.
Don't panic! Calm down!
I-it's too late...
Zuihou, Asanagi! Are you still listening?!
Taken aback by Hatsuzuki's ferocious speed, they failed to notice her shouting through the communicator.
Despite the fact that she was moving with her rigging, she looked like she was dashing as fast as she could.
Hatsuzuki's really going fast...
I'm amazed that she can run so fast with her rigging on...
Maybe I should try... Whoa! Now isn't the time to think about that!
Hatsuzuki, are you okay?! What's too late?!
When she finally reached the beach outside of the guardroom, Hatsuzuki hit the brakes and drifted up the shore from inertia.
*pant*... *gasp*... *WHEEZE*...
While Hatsuzuki panted and gasped for air, Zuihou ran over with broom in hand—
...But Hatsuzuki held out her hand, gesturing that she was fine and prompting Zuihou to stop.
It's too late now.
After some deep breaths, she returned to normal and said with a sad look on her face.
It's just too late!
Lady Nagato, Musashi, and someone else...
They're here in the Prime Sakura sanctuary!
Lady Nagato and Musashi? ...Hmph. That isn't a very funny joke.
They would never come here out of nowhere.
Whoa, whoa! I-I gotta hurry up and finish sweeping the courtyard!
Hey, I'm not joking. I saw them with my own eyes!
While I was looking for Owari, I suddenly saw them sailing, too.
I'd never mistake the figure of the Sakura Empire's Guardian Fox!
...Y-you mean you were serious?
I've BEEN serious this whole time! Maybe I'd be happier if I was mistaken, but...
Oh, no, no! Wh-what do we do?!
I'll send my carrier-based aircraft to search for Lady Nagato now...
Hatsuzuki, go in and rest! Asanagi, wake up Natori, and... And make her clean her room!
We need to make tea, too... If we hurry, we might make it in time!
B-but if I start getting ready now, what if I'm so focused when they get here that—
Argh! Why are you all just standing around doing nothing?!
Right! I'll get going right away!
The once-peaceful outpost was livened up by the presence of uninvited guests.
(I-is this related to Owari? What in the world is going on...?)
In an empty plot of land in the outpost, Asanagi took a broom in hand – a rare sight to see.
She began sweeping the ground haphazardly and hurriedly, but sweeping it all the same.
It was pure curiosity that was driving her to do this. She wanted to know what was happening inside the house.
Psst! Hatsuzuki!
With a hushed voice, she approached the building and addressed Hatsuzuki, standing in the passageway.
Three there were, you said. Where is the third? I've seen only Lady Nagato and Musashi.
I don't know where she is. It's always possible I was wrong...
No matter. Do you know why the two of them are here?
You know what I know? That it's rude to eavesdrop!
Asanagi put down her broom and tried to enter, but Hatsuzuki hurriedly stopped her. At the same time, somebody emerged from a room opposite them.
It was Zuihou. Tray in hand, she nimbly turned around and gave a quick bow.
If you need anything, just let me know!
Then, she stepped aside and slid the paper sliding door shut.
Phew...
Zuihou! Come here!
Tell me – what is happening in there? What are those two discussing?
Take it easy! Give her a moment to compose herself.
Zuihou was shaking like a leaf. She dropped the tray off in the storeroom before Asanagi hauled her off into another room.
Gosh... That was nerve-racking...
I've never spoken face-to-face with Lady Nagato or Musashi before.
I wasn't the least prepared for it either, and I nearly spilled their tea on the floor...
Thank goodness nothing happened.
When I nearly spilled the tea, Lady Nagato had this dead-serious look on her face, but at least Musashi shot me a comforting look.
It was nearly a disaster...
Yes, yes. Did they speak of anything relating to Owari?
Huh? Uh, Lady Nagato said something about "going to the Prime Sakura."
Are you certain of that? THE Prime Sakura?
Asanagi gestured with a finger towards the giant Sacred Sakura at the sanctuary's center.
Yup.
That's where she is? Then it's no wonder Hatsuzuki could not find her.
Why do that, though? Why would she go to the tree?
Oh! Shoot! I forgot to report that Owari has gone missing!
Now I've really messed up... What if Lady Nagato or Musashi get hurt because of it?
While Asanagi and Hatsuzuki held their heads in their hands and Zuihou lost her composure, another person cut into the conversation.
No harm done. Moreover, we learned that Owari is safe just moments ago.
Our companion will show her back to the outpost shortly.
M-Musashi?! Um, I...
No need to be so stiff. It's alright. Also, Lady Nagato has a special mission for you three.
You are to gather some materials we will need for a ritual.
Musashi produced a slip of paper from her sleeve to give to the outpost girls.
The three, however, stood motionless, paralyzed by Musashi's sudden appearance.
Hatsuzuki?
Y-Yes, ma'am?!
So it was you I saw earlier.
S-sorry for not introducing myself earlier! None of us were expecting you, and the chance to say hello passed us by...
"It happens," said a voice belonging to none of the girls. It came from just behind Musashi.
If it isn't Hiranuma... Or rather, Natori.
Pardon me. I was supposed to wake you, but carelessly forgot about it when Lady Nagato and Musashi turned up.
I ask you for forgiveness as well, Musashi!
It's fine. You have nothing to apologize for.
Musashi turned on her heel and directed Natori toward the rest of the girls.
Zuihou, I trust you to find the materials.
There's still time before the ritual. Until then, let's discuss the outpost and the sanctuary, shall we?
After wading through the darkness for who knows how long, a ray of light finally shone through to Owari.
Mmgghh...
Her head was heavy. She had been subjected to far too many apparitions, or possibly visions of the past.
She ran her hand along her nape and felt the back of her head. No signs of injury.
Strangely, though, it felt as though her feet weren't touching the ground.
It didn't feel like she was standing, but rather lying down – suspended in the air like with strings, something gripping her waist.
The heck is this... The wind? Did a hawk capture me or somethin'?
Can't even open my eyes. Dammit...
Startin' to think this is some kinda sleep paralysis... Or a nightmare...
What was I doing before this? I can't remember...
Her memories were a jarbled mess. It was a struggle to remember much of anything.
Oh, right!
I remember seeing Lady Nagato and Musashi over by the Prime Sakura!
And they were, like, fighting something? Wait, nah, that's not right...
That ain't one of my memories, it's an event the Prime Sakura recorded waaay back.
Why would it show me that, though? Something, something, "come to the tree"... Sounds creepy.
A headache came over her and she was forced to stop thinking.
Some time passed, and eventually, the feeling of being suspended wore off. She could feel the sanctuary's soil beneath her feet again.
...Am I back on the ground again?
This time when she opened her eyes, her vision had returned to her.
Flowing rivers, lush fields of grass, and the Prime Sakura's great pink canopy all laid before her.
Guess I'm back? Some weird-ass nightmare that was...
Got the feelin' something ain't right. I'd better hurry back to the outpost.

sequence:
Slacking Off with the "Good" Girl

<size=45>1.Busy Days</size>

scripts.say: Port - Commander's Office
Coming iiin. Your secretary ship is here right on time, Commander. Lucky you!
My... You don't look too hot, Commander. Are you okay?
...Good. Then I will help out as usual... with the easy stuff, of course.
Phew... It got dark in no time, didn't it?
Still, despite how much I've been helping you, your work backlog hasn't shrunk at all. Why is that?
Well, I suppose all I can really do is find typos and the like... The actual decision-making falls to you, in the end. Okay! Good work today, Commander.
Aww, you appreciate all my hard work? In that case...
Commander, do you ever find yourself wanting to be a little lazy?
Of course, I don't mean just abandoning your work wholesale. After all, a girl as good as me would never neglect her duties.
What I'm suggesting is... resting, in moderation.
I've noticed that you've been making a lot more typographical errors lately. It seems to me like you're losing concentration due to a lack of rest.
"I-I can't refute that..."
Ergo, I propose laziness in order to raise your work efficiency!
Though, really, all I'm suggesting is that you totally turn off for two hours on a specific day. As long as there aren't any emergencies, you're forbidden from working.
As for what you'll do while you're off work, this good girl will gladly find something for you.
This isn't a naughty excuse; it's a way for good Commanders to raise their efficiency. Persuasive enough, right?
Hahaha! I knew you'd understand.
Why don't we give it a try tomorrow morning?
You don't need to do anything; leave it aaall to me.
So it's settled! I'd best take my leave now.
Oh, I forgot to add one thing. Staying up late is for naughty Commanders, so get to bed early tonight, okay?
I watched Jade leave as I cleaned up the rest of my documents.
"I guess I'll have to go to sleep early tonight..."

sequence:
Slacking Off with the "Good" Girl

<size=45>2.Time to Get Lazy!</size>

scripts.say: The next day, Jade carried out her plan to make me slack off.
Thanks for waiting!
When Jade called out to me, I turned around to find her bringing a big collection of snacks over.
Our first round of slacking is quite simple, as you can see.
I call it... The Max Guilt Snacks Party!
Indeed, I have brought you all of your favorite snacks, Commander.
Oh, but if you ate so much that it made you too full to work, that would make me a bad girl for ruining your productivity.
As such, you'll have to choose just one to start with.

options.content: "I'll take the chips that look like cones."

scripts.say: Oh, do you like these, Commander? Spee recommended I try them a while back.
I don't think she likes them because of the taste, though. It's more likely because they're fun to put on your fingers.
Like this... Rawr!
Jade put the chips on her fingers and showed them off like an animal stretching its claws out.
Z24 told me that dark chocolate is like a symbol of maturity.
And then, she threw the whole piece into her mouth and went, "Eww..." It was just hilarious!
But of course, I'm sure this is nothing to you, Commander.
Ahaha! You know exactly who loves these, don't you?
That's right: U-110! The two of us cracked a cipher together, and we were given these as a reward.
These cute gummy sharks might not suit someone as mature as you... Is this what they call "gap"?
Hahaha, I think they'll be a little too sweet for you, but give them a try!
I tried eating the one I picked out.
Oh, hold on a sec.
Didn't I tell you to leave it aaall to me? That includes this...
Open up, Commander.
I was taken aback by the sudden turn of events.
Go on. Open up like a good Commander...
(I'll have to just obey orders for now.)
(Mm. That's not bad.)
That look on your face says you like it. Would you like another?
Say "ahh."
Heehee, it feels like I'm feeding a little animal.
By the way, are you thirsty? I brought canned fruit juice and soda with me. Which would you like?
Okay. Then I'll take the other.
By the way, can you open the cans for me?
"No problem."
Thank you. You're such a good Commander.
Aaah... Doesn't it feel like junk food and drinks aren't quite enough?
Do you have any fun stories? For example, hidden treasure in your office, or anything?
Haha, that's just an example. I'm a good girl, so I won't invade your privacy. That's a promise.
Hmm... Okay. Until we think of any fun topics of conversation, let's continue what we were doing before.
Open up, Commander!
We've only just begun, so let's take it slow, okay?♪

sequence:
Slacking Off with the "Good" Girl

<size=45>3.Loafing Around with Friends!</size>

scripts.say: Port - Commander's Office
Hello, hello! It's your scheduled slack-off time!
I brought Elbe with me this time. When she heard she'd get to hang out with you, she came running.
Naturally! This isn't just a chance to hang out; it's an opportunity to waste the Commander's time and make work even harder. I wouldn't miss this for the world!
Let's waste your valuable time together like the naughty people we are!
Or... So I say, but are you sure it's okay for me to take up the Commander's time, Jade?
It's okay. You aren't taking up time; you're using it together to be lazy. The Commander understands and consents.
As you can see, our slacking will be a little livelier than usual today. In other words...
Today, we're playing Old Maid with a punishment game on top!
The rules are simple. The first winner gets to choose a punishment for the loser to undergo.
But keep it clean, okay? Nothing cruel or unusual!
Now, let's get it started!
Before long, our first round had reached the final battle.
There are two routes at this point. If the Commander pulls something other than the Joker, then Elbe loses.
But if the Commander pulls a Joker, then it'll be Elbe's turn... Of course, that could be fun in its own right.
Bring it on, I say! I'll make sure you take the Joker!
I tried reaching out for the card on the right to see what would happen.
Elbe was clearly anxious. It'd be harder to not know which one was the Joker at this point.
As expected, I pulled the Joker.
Woohoo! Now it's my turn!
Please no Joker, please no Joker... Anything but a Joker... Here goes!
Yaaaay! Phew... Now I don't have to take the punishment...
Hahaha. You're too soft on Elbe, Commander.
In accordance with the rules, you will now have to take a punishment of my choosing, since I was the first to win.
I know... How about you bark like a cute puppy three times? Easy, no?
(This is what I get for letting Elbe win. Well, rules are rules.)
"Woof, woof! Woof!"
Aww, good doggy~ Here's a little scritch on the head.
Th-that's all? If I won, I'd have picked something that would really embarrass the Commander...
As expected, Elbe lost.
Wh-what?! How did you know?!
Heheheh~ Elbe, just admit defeat.
Don't worry. As a good girl, I won't make things TOO bad for you.
Urk...
Now, for your punishment...
How about you kiss the Commander on the cheek? Easy, no?
Wh-wh-wh-why that?!
I-I-I could never do that! That's too embarrassing!
Hahaha! I was just teasing you, but I didn't expect you to get so flustered... Out of deference to the Commander, I'll choose something else.
Hmm... Meow like a cat. That's an easy one.
Y-you bully... It's embarrassing, but that's at least better... I-I'll do it!
A-ahem. Meow, meow...
There you go! Well done.
Now, it's about time we get to round two.

sequence:
Slacking Off with the "Good" Girl

<size=45>4.Mindless Scrolling</size>

scripts.say: Port - Commander's Office
It's that time again, Commander.
Today's theme will be surfing the web!
Come and sit on the couch with me, Commander. I brought snacks again.
Jade took out her phone and tapped away at it with experienced hands.
First, we'll search "Commander"...
Sort by new, and... "Spotted the Commander checking supplies in the warehouse! Are you ever not busy?"
Hmm... Well. As far as I can see, everyone's posting about how busy you are these days.
They have no idea that you're slacking off with me... Heehee!
How about we search for something else... Hm? A new message?
It's nothing private. I'll reply now, so wait just a moment.
Our supply of snacks is running thin faster than usual? Hmm, what could that possibly have to do with me?
Really, Elbe can't do anything without me, can she?
Done! Thank you for waiting, Commander.
Heheh, this time, I'll search the words Jade and Commander together.
"Zero search results?"
Nothing at all... I suppose you've been so occupied with work that nobody knows we're spending time together.
I'm glad our little secret is still safe♪
Besides, being so absorbed in work must mean that you haven't been able to keep an eye on the situation around port.
If you have any questions, I'm always willing to search for you.
For example, if there's anyone you have your mind on... Or if anything just piques your interest.
Hahaha, we still have plenty of time today. Let's really dig into you and the things that are on your mind!

sequence:
Slacking Off with the "Good" Girl

<size=45>5.An Eventful Day</size>

scripts.say: Port - Commander's Office
Phew... This is a good stopping point for the morning's work.
Just in time for us to begin our usual slacking session!
*knock knock*
Pardon me. Commander, there's an urgent matter.
The research department's run into a bit of a problem. Yuubari and da Vinci alone can't handle it, so we'd really appreciate your help.
Are you available right now?
"Sorry, Jade, but I should really go..."
If it's urgent, don't worry about me. It can always wait until you get back.
...Better yet, allow me to come with you.
If it's related to the communication modules, I might be able to help.
"Well, that's finally done and dusted..."
Excuse me, Commander? There's a problem...
Ack! Commander, there you are! It's an emergency! P-please, help me out here!
Sorry, Commander. I happen to need your help with something...
After being pulled back and forth by emergency after emergency, I dragged my tired body back to the office.
When it rains, it pours, hm? That's our Commander for you; despite all of the problems presented to you, you dealt with them with aplomb.
It seems like our recent slacking sessions haven't dulled your skills at all.
...Of course, I think my presence contributed, too♪
Oh, but it's already so late... I think our plans for today have been ruined.
It's not your fault, Commander. If you feel bad about it, then that defeats the point of me trying to help you.
By the way, it's almost your day off, isn't it?
Heehee, what if I were to borrow your day off to make up for today?
Just like our slacking sessions, you can just leave everything to me.
Sounds like a plan. See you then!

sequence:
Slacking Off with the "Good" Girl

<size=45>6.Idleness: Back with a Vengeance!</size>

scripts.say: Port - Outdoor Pool
My, you're early. So you're the punctual type? What a good Commander.
It's too hot out, so I went ahead and changed into my swimsuit!
Would you like some of my popsicle, Commander?
*lick* ♥
Jade first licked her popsicle before holding it out to me.
Hahaha, too bad. It's about to fall apart from the heat, so maybe another time!
Aww. You can be a little naughty sometimes, y'know.
There are more popsicles in the cooler next to the pool, so take as many as you want.
By the way, I heard this rumor...
People say you're so good at swimming that you can keep up with the submarines.
I'd love to see your swimming, if you don't mind.
It doesn't have to be top speed. All I want is for you to push me and my swim ring around the pool.
(That rumor seems just a little bit embellished...)
"If that's all you want, I don't mind."
That's it. Keep it up!
Your reward will be watermelon. It's seedless. Now open up!
Hahaha, this is fun. It feels like I'm refueling my engine!
While we're here, why don't I take a picture? Look over here, Commander.
Three, two, one... Cheese!
Maybe I should post this on Juustagram... No, I won't. I'll just save it in my "Slacking with the Commander" album, as usual.
Hm? Commander? You're slowing down. Are you already tired?
Would you like to get out and take a break? I brought plenty of snacks along with the popsicles.
I've reserved this whole day with you, so we can take things nice and slow.

sequence:
Slacking Off with the "Good" Girl

<size=45>7.I Am a Good Girl, You Know</size>

scripts.say: Port - Commander's Office
I had a wonderful time on our date.
The pool, the amusement park, the arcade, and a café... That was enough fun to last!
And you even carried the stuff I bought! Here's your reward... *lick* You can have my popsicle!
Your complexion looks much better these days. I think our lazy time together has been quite effective.
Hm? You'd like to keep slacking off with me?
Oh, if I must. As a good girl, I can't sit idly by while you're struggling.
And you wouldn't refuse my busybodying, now, would you?
Besides, you've had plenty of chances to refuse until now.
You could've always justified refusing me by saying, "No, I'm busy." Yet you didn't. And that means...
We're both good for caring so much about each other!
Haha! Let's make more fun memories together from now on, okay?
Say, Commander, could you close your eyes for a moment?
Don't open them until I say so, please.
*sigh*... You're obedient to a fault.
You're so sweet that I don't know whether I really look like a good girl or a bad girl to you.
But I'm not the kind of person to worry about that, so let me give you my own answer... I'm the kind of girl who wants your attention.
So if I said... that I loved you, would that make your heart skip a beat? Or would you be more startled?
*mwah*
I don't plan to let anyone take my time with you.
There. That's all from me!
It's dark out, so I'd better get going.
Oh, and... You can open your eyes now♪
Port - Commander's Office The next day...
...That summarizes my report of the commission.
You're in an unusually good mood today, Commander.
I don't know what you're so happy about, but congratulations on whatever it may be.
Anyway, thank you. I'll take my leave now.
(That's all for the morning's work. Now it's time to kick back and—)
*knock knock*
A familiar voice called from beyond the door before coming in with snacks.
Oh, my. I just came along because I'd hit a good stopping point in my work, but it looks like I'm right on time.
I don't suppose I have to explain what we're going to do now.
Shall we get to slacking off together?

sequence: Iron Blood Embassy, Iris Orthodoxy
Dinner Party

scripts.say: I received an invitation to a formal banquet from Bismarck, and now Memphis and I have come to their embassy.
While hosting a banquet in an embassy isn't exceedingly unusual, it certainly is when it's in an Iron Blood embassy.
This place, usually solemn and deathly silent, is brimming with life tonight.
After verifying my identity and going through the embassy's main gate, a well-maintained lawn lined with trees comes into view.
This is a fairly large banquet. The venue spans from the hall indoors, past a roofed and semi-outdoor space, and all the way into the garden.
People come and go, glasses cling, and the buzzes with laughter and conversations. The celebrations are in full swing.
Wow... This is nowhere near as formal and lifeless as I expected it to be.
Granted, I've never been to an Iron Blood banquet before. I just thought their parties would be like their army.
But no, they're actually hosting a leisurely event here. Never judge a book by its cover.
Maybe the Orthodoxy's romantic vibe has influenced them a bit?
Hmm. Yeah, probably. I take back what I just said.
So much for that. More pertinently, have you seen the Kingdom of Tulipa's delegation?
I don't see any of Bismarck's entourage either.
The Tulipans are the stars of the show tonight. You'll probably find them wherever the crowd is the largest.
Let's head inside, shall we? It's cold out tonight.
I enter the hall and my ears are met with an impassioned symphony.
In stark contrast to the graceful atmosphere in the courtyard, the hall and all its furnishings are far more lively.
Memphis and I fortify ourselves with a light meal, and before long, Bismarck approaches us from afar, the delegation of Tulipan representatives trailing behind her.
Commander, Memphis, I'd like to introduce you to some people.
I was surprised by how many delegates had come from Tulipa.

In addition to a military rep whom I'd met only once before to discuss shipgirl-related business, the delegation also included a spokesperson from the Tulipan royal family and several members of their parliament.
The point of this banquet is apparent – to deepen the Iron Blood's ties to me as well as the Tulipans – but Bismarck also has obviously has some other, personal stake in it.
During my conversation with the representatives, I noticed something interesting.
The military reps were very positive about the inclusion of shipgirls in their fleet. Their enthusiasm was only matched – and surpassed – by the royal family's representative.
On the other hand, the members of parliament were certainly polite and formal, yet always maintained an air of distance and prudence.
Despite that, they were always the ones guiding the conversation.
Much unlike the royal family of the Royal Islands, which has a direct say in their navy, the royal family of the Kingdom of Tulipa are little more than figureheads.
Or at the very least, that's how it seems to me.

Perhaps as the Tulipans' plans of expanding their fleet with shipgirls progresses, their royal family would follow the example set by the Royal Islands and regain power by incorporating shipgirls into their dynasty.
Be they kings or congressmen or generals, as long as they treat shipgirls fairly and can guarantee them their due status and power, I have no reason to meddle excessively in their internal affairs.
That is the position that I, as well as the Azur Lane, hold firmly.
Finally, our conversation which was 10% sincerity and 90% lip service came to an end.
The Tulipan delegates set their respective sights on other targets among the guests, and quickly began on their next task.
Once they had dispersed, Memphis compiled a list of tonight's guests.
Meanwhile, Bismarck and I made our way to the conference room she had prepared ahead of time.
All it took was rearranging the layout of the tables and chairs to instantly turn the formal conference room into a quiet, private room.
The room is lit by a gentle light, and there is even food ready. It gives a candlelit dinner type of atmosphere to the place.
We didn't have much time to speak earlier, so let me say it now: It's a pleasure to meet you again, Bismarck.
How has your health been? Any changes since then?
It's been wholly fine. Thank you for your concern.
Now, let us have a toast to the smooth progress of our cooperation with the Kingdom of Tulipa.
Heehee. I hope you'll like this wine.
Don't you think this place is much more conducive to a calm dialogue? It's rather rowdy and hard to have a face-to-face out there.
Yeah, it's a huge step up. Thanks for planning for that. Say, is this the privilege of being the banquet organizer?
Indeed, it is. Although, it did mean you had to leave Memphis behind.
Don't worry about her. She'll enjoy the party.
That's good to hear. Now, let us get down to business. What do you think of this diplomatic banquet?
I was surprised to see your embassy hosting it. The invitee list had names from factions across the world, too. That was a thrilling sight.
The organizers and participants all seemed overjoyed, and I was pleased to see different factions mingle and laugh. Some had ulterior motives for being here, sure, but none of them showed it.
It felt like I'd gone back in time to before all the fighting began.
Is this what you believe our new order should look like?
...We won't be poised to deal with future threats if we merely go back to an old status quo.
Is that so? The last time we met, I knew you had some ideas, but you lacked the conviction you have now.
Let's just say I've been through quite a lot.
Some of them are things you know about, some of them you don't. Some happened here and now, others in a far-off place long ago...
Hmm. A very thought-provoking manner of speaking. A good change, I'd say.
Ah, forgive me. I didn't mean to put on airs.
Heehee. Let's put the past aside for now and focus on present matters. For instance, the complete ceasefire agreement between the Azur Lane and the Crimson Axis.
So something finally came of those endless meetings.
Things wouldn't have gone this smoothly if you hadn't expertly resolved the crisis of the Sakurans.
I can't claim all the credit. That was the result of us all working together.
From what I've heard, you've finalized the framework and are ironing out the details – correct?
Yes, and tonight is the groundwork for that. I've directly spoken to a few factions already.
As of now, all of them are in agreement on two things: Firstly, that the Azur Lane and the Crimson Axis should seek an immediate, complete armistice and an end to all-out war.
Secondly, that the spheres of influence of all factions be restored to fundamentally what they were prior to hosilities beginning.
A formal vote on these two points will be held at the next conference. It should pass without issue.
To elaborate on the ceasefire a bit...
All matters such as restoring old borders, troop transfers, reconstruction, and compensation for war damages will be dealt with by asking the other factions to sign separate supplementary agreements.
The Azur Lane and the Crimson Axis will both provide full support in the facilitation of this process.
Yeah, that's the right approach. At long last, this war is coming to an end.
It couldn't have been done without you, the one who brought all the factions together and ensured the success of our joint operations.
I really look forward to seeing how the war's end will change the world.
Thank you for the kind words, but personally, I remain cautiously optimistic about the world's future.
Reforming the Azur Lane... It's a real swamp.
We'll take that one step at a time. Rome wasn't built in a day, after all.
On another subject, the Lower Countries Treaty is formally being signed next month. Would you mind being there to personally witness it?
Ah, that treaty...
(By signing it, the three constituents of the Kingdom of Tulipa will pull out of the Iron Blood's shadow and regain its neutral position.)
(Although, when faced with the Sirens, neutrality is a pie in the sky.)
(All it really means is that Tulipa will be treated as an observer state by both the Azur Lane and the Crimson Axis.)
(It will stay that way until a final judgment on the Azur Lane's reformation is passed, after which further discussion will take place.)
Of course. I'd love to see it, assuming circumstances permit me to.
It's our first step into a new age, and a sign of enormous progress for the reformation of the Azur Lane.
Let's discuss that matter later.
Right. Let's have another drink. To the Lower Countries Treaty.
Cheers.
Bismarck and I discussed all sorts of things.
Interfaction affairs, Siren movements, META organizations in other branches, the Iron Blood's nature, climate, and culture, and so on and so on.
All this talking reminded me that behind that tempered exterior of hers lies a woman who is surprisingly eloquent.
Time had completely flown by, and the banquet was approaching its end.
Ah, before you leave, there's one last thing I'd like to tell you.
About the Tulipan shipgirl fleet that you came up with and the factions of Europa worked together to build...
There will soon be a chance for you to meet those girls in person.
Come again? But I don't have plans to go to Tulipa anytime soon.
