Ah, wait, are you hinting that they'll be present at the signing of the treaty?
That, I'm not at liberty to say. You'll see for yourself tomorrow.

sequence: Iris Orthodoxy - Capital
Commander's Office
The next day...

scripts.say: The day following the banquet, an operation briefing from my higher-ups gave an answer to the question Bismarck left me with yesterday.
I can't believe they're launching the NA Ocean Purification Campaign so soon... What's more, the Tulipans have a fleet participating in the first phase.
They don't have any experience with fighting Sirens. Is this really a good idea?
Everything has to start from somewhere.
The enemies they'll be up against aren't especially threatening. That's perfect for a first battle.
Following the departure of the Sirens' experimentation division, our world entered a new, post-Siren age.
Unfortunately, the self-detonation of their mainframes was so sudden that it left us with many problems to deal with.
Among them, the biggest and most serious is the NA Ocean.
Since Compiler's mainframe was not self-detonated, but rather destroyed by us, its restructuring program initiated very soon after.
To make matters worse, when Observer issued the self-detonation command, Compiler's mainframe still hadn't come back online, so it never received that order.
If we don't do anything, then it's possible that a new Compiler mainframe will take shape within the NA Ocean within the year. That's a future no one wants.
Therefore, cleaning up Compiler's remaining forces in the area became the top priority between all of the world's factions.
To that end, the Azur Lane and the Crimson Axis formulated a cooperative plan to neutralize the recovering mainframe as well as the lingering Siren forces.
They dubbed this plan, "The NA Ocean Purification Campaign."
The plan originally only included the Royal Navy, the Iris Orthodoxy, the Iron Blood, and the Northern Parliament.
However, the shipgirls of the Kingdom of Tulipa were added to this roster after they demonstrated promising results.
(...And since I had a hand in the creation of their fleet of shipgirls, the task of commanding them fell upon me.)
(The mission itself isn't that difficult. All that needs to be done is eliminate the enemy Mirror Sea sitting near the coast of Tulipa.)
(We'll also be accompanied by a support fleet consisting of vessels from both Tulipa and other factions. That will reduce the danger further.)
(What I'm not sure of yet is whether their inclusion in this mission was an attempt by my superiors to place the Tulipans, or an attempt by Bismarck to train them.)
Commander, the briefing said to "go to the Kingdom of Tulipa, review their fighting capabilities, and determine whether or not support from other factions is needed."
But, well... the Northern Parliament have already stated they'll provide support.
Should we politely turn them down?
No. Regardless of the impression it gives, I'll gladly accept anything that gives us more leeway in battle.
Understood. When are we leaving?
I want to learn more about the Tulipans before the mission. Let's leave as early as we can.
Okay. How about going there by train tomorrow?
Sounds good.
Alright. I'll contact the Tulipan command and let them know!

sequence: Kingdom of Tulipa
Train - Commander's Cabin
The next day...

scripts.say: Memphis quickly arranged everything for me.
The day after I received my mission briefing, I set off to Rotterdam – the Kingdom of Tulipa's second-largest city and its largest port city.
Bumping every now and then, the train ran through cities, grasslands, forests, and hills, until eventually windmills, dikes, and colorful flower fields filled the scenery past the window.
Time passed slowly while my heart was enraptured by the beautiful sights. Before I knew it, the train's whistle sounded and its speed gradually dropped.
After a roughly three-hour journey, I had arrived at my destination – the first stop of my journey to the country.
As soon as Memphis and I disembark the train, a girl carrying the country's flag approaches us.
To her sides are two girls donning the distinct uniforms of the Northern Parliament.
Commander, Memphis, thank you for coming all this way. Welcome to the Kingdom of Tulipa
I am Evertsen, an Admiralen-class destroyer of the Kingdom of Tulipa.
Thank you, Evertsen.
Your country lives up to its name. I was bewitched by the beautiful sights of all the blooming flowers on the way here.
You, too, are quite a stunning representation of this new era for the Tulipan navy. I look forward to seeing you bloom on the battlefield.
(The Tulipans are really doing well with their shipgirls.)
(This aura of nature and greenery must be their trademark trait.)
I promise you that our fleet will live up to your expectations.
Say, who are these other ladies? Kazan and Oleg, correct?
It's good to see you again, Commander.
She and I are here to assist the Tulipans on orders from Saint Petersburg Base. We'll be under your command for this mission.
It's a pleasure to fight by your side again.
Yeah, we only got to speak briefly during the last battle. This time we can finally take our time and work together comprehensively.
The burden on the Tulipans' fleet will be lessened with you two around. I can't wait to see you in the field.
Heheh! My heart already races with anticipation! Do look forward to our stellar performance!
Now then, we're going to drive to an anchorage located on the city's outskirts.
If you have any questions about my homeland, don't be afraid to ask on the way.
The car is waiting for us. Please follow me.
The car takes us westward. While the gorgeous flower fields and windmills are a given, there are also enormous dikes built along the river. Their presence is not lightly felt.
These dikes are bigger and taller than ones I've seen anywhere else... They even have buildings attached to them.
And those massive mechanical structures built on top of the banks...
Are those part of the famous flood control system that took the country many years to build?
I didn't expect it to be so large in scope. They've fortified not just the coastal areas, but the banks of inland rivers as well.
Correct. Since our country is on such low elevation, we have not just a long coastline, but also an extensive network of waterways.
As such, we place a bigger emphasis on banks and dams than other countries. We're also in a class of our own when it comes to building them.
When the Sirens first appeared, Tulipa was immediately put in danger as it didn't have shipgirls to protect it.
Instead, we opted to weaponize our embankments.
We devoted our full efforts to up-arming the banks that span our whole kingdom and created a vast and complex defensive installation that can protect our most important positions.
Of course, while it's inadequate for dealing with a proper Siren fleet, it did give us the ability to defend ourselves against threats like stray mass-produced ships and regularly sized air raids.
Now, the banks that protected us from the sea also protect us from the Sirens.
(Fortifying your land and concentrating your population where the defenses are the strongest...)
(That's how the Tulipans defended themselves during the war against the Sirens, whilst staying out of the spotlight and having no shipgirls.)
(This strategy has limited effectiveness, but I suppose they had no other choice.)
(Hmm. Speaking of the Sirens...)
Your country's future is looking brighter. The Sirens' experimentation division has been destroyed, and now you have a fleet of shipgirls.
Yes. I believe a better future is ahead of us.
The sun set and dusk silently enveloped the city as we drove. Soon, we arrived at the harbor, where Tulipan shipgirls and a mass-produced fleet were anchored.
That building up ahead is sparkling... Was it built just recently?

Yes. While implementing our shipgirl program, some advisors sent by the Northern Parliament informed us that shipgirls do not operate quite like a conventional navy. As such, we decided to construct this new harbor.
It was completed exceptionally quickly thanks to the Northern Parliament's substantial aid.
Heheh! As a matter of fact, I contributed a little to its construction.
I'm somehow not surprised to hear you're already getting involved in their construction projects.
All we did was help people who needed assistance.
It's not limited to Tulipa, either. Now that the war in the polar regions is over, the Northern Parliament finally has the flexibility to help other countries.
Post-war reconstruction is indeed a crucial task.
There is still fighting to be done, and we need to help each other to get through it.
My apologies for the delay. I am De Zeven Provinciën, light cruiser of the Kingdom of Tulipa.
Commander, Memphis, Kazan, and Oleg – welcome to Nieuwe Haven Naval Base.
Zeven, I told you to be ready to greet the Commander. Why were you late?
I was just filling in our exercise schedule, then all of a sudden the machine started spewing smoke...
So I had to put out the fire... which took quite some time.
Not again... It may be for the best if you simply don't touch any machinery from now on.
But I'm the fleet's flagship! I'm also the harbor's overseer.
Let's save this for another time. More pertinently, what was that about an exercise? I wasn't informed of this.
I wanted it to be a surprise, since I figured the Commander would be interested to see us in action.
A surprise is the last thing we need right now. Our schedule is packed. There's simply no time for a surprise exercise.
Tell me, what do you see anchored in the harbor?
A mass-produced fleet? What of it?
And what about those ships in the front?
I mean... they're our riggings.
Exactly. They've been fully deployed in the harbor in vessel form in order to conduct inspections and maintenance.
How, pray tell, do you expect to hold an exercise while that's happening?
With... magic?
...Is that not going to work?
No. It's not going to work.
Are you sure? Is it super-duper not going to work?
It's not going to work! Period!
Aww... Okay, I understand.
Zeven, Evertsen, may I suggest saving confidential matters until AFTER we've entered the base?
Oh, right! Forgive me! Please come with me – I'll show you to the reception party!

sequence: Kingdom of Tulipa
Nieuwe Haven Naval Base

scripts.say: After the party, Memphis and I were curious about the Tulipans' dam defense system, so went to the nearest one to have a look.
Thanks to my status and position, we made it there without much hassle.
After a short while, we were strolling on the embankment, made of concrete and rebar and covered with steel armor.
In terms of structural strength, it looks on par with our Panama Canal fortifications.
Even though this is just a place to walk, not a strategic location.
I suppose Tulipa was very serious about it when they built this dam defense system.
Yeah. You can even see signs of repairs all over the place. Sirens must've hit this place several times in the past.
The Sirens' Mirror Sea is pretty close to the coastline. I'll bet that's where they attacked from.
BEEP BEEP!
Hm? Who's calling this late in the–
The light fades, and the familiar sight of the night sky unfolds before me.
I called you in advance this time.
Not with the best timing, sadly. I was just with Memphis and–
I know. You were taking a walk on the embankment.
Don't worry. I made it so the time flows at a ratio of 360:1 this time, so this won't take more than a few seconds.
Is there some sort of issue with Marco Polo?
No, there's just something I wanted you to know about your next move.
You mean my incursion in the Mirror Sea off the Tulipan coast?
Yes. How much did they tell you in your briefing?
Upper command said it's Compiler's forward operating base for keeping an eye on and blockading the Kingdom of Tulipa.

Ever since Compiler's defeat, the base's defense systems have remained offline, and the fleet within it has remained idle. It's the perfect place for the Tulipan shipgirls to get some fighting experience.
Let me guess... our intel is wrong, isn't it?
Heehee.
Then how much of it is wrong?
That's not an FOB. It's a weapons test site previously overseen by Omitter. It was used to develop and test all kinds of new weaponry.
The defense system works like normal, and the test programs inside are still running, despite the detonation of her mainframe.
So, how much of your intel do you think is wrong?
...Sounds like our intel department will need a lot more time to figure out the experimentation division's structure.
Don't worry, that's exactly what I'm here to help with.
I got the data on their new weapons from Observer. I'll send it to you later.
You'll need much more than two Tulipan shipgirls to deal with that place. It's really lucky that the Northern Parliament sent those reinforcements.
And to think I was going to split the fleet in two so they could gain more experience...
You saved my skin with this intel. Thank you.
No need to thank me.
Well, that's everything from me. Enjoy your nightly stroll.
Hmh...
Hrrmmmh...
When I can see again, my vision is filled with Memphis' face.
You blanked out for no reason for a minute there, Commander.
I, uh... My mind just wandered for a bit.
Your mind wandered. Right. You weren't talking to someone?
It was her again, wasn't it? Helena META.
Gosh, does she even know how dangerous it is for her to do this?!
What if she did it while you were driving, huh? Or in the middle of crossing a road?!
It's fine. She knows when not to do it.
Let's hope she never misjudges her timing, then.
So, what did she tell you?
It was about the–
Shh. Wait. Someone's coming.
...Commander? Memphis?
I wasn't expecting to come across you here. Are you out on a walk as well?
Excuse me? I radioed the base and said we were going out.
Uhh, well... My communicator did receive a message, but as soon as I picked it up, it stopped working...
And then... smoke started coming out of it...
So Evertsen brought in the technical team to assist...
It's no big deal! Luckily, I stumbled upon you out here!
Are you anxious about your upcoming battle, Zeven?
...You see right through me, Commander. Yes, you're correct.
I have done lots of training and I have the essentials of combat carved into my memory, but even so...
This will be my first real battle as a representative of my country, and I feel so nervous about being the flagship...
That's normal. Nothing is easy the first time around.
I know what you're capable of. You'll be fine as long as you fight like you did during your training.
Okay! Thank you for the comforting words, Commander! I'll strive to do my best!
Oh, one more thing! My favorite park lies just at the end of this embankment. Would you like to come see it with me?
I wish I could, but time is short. The mission is taking place the day after tomorrow and I need to get back and start preparing.
We can certainly go and see the park after we've won.
In two days, then! Why don't we walk back to the base together?
...Right. Let's head back.

sequence: Sea Near the Kingdom of Tulipa
Joint Fleet
Two days later...

scripts.say: On the day of the Tulipan fleet's first battle, their flag flutters in the gentle sea breeze.
Zeven and Evertsen deploy their rigging and set sail first.
They're followed by my command ship, which is then followed by the imposing mass-produced Tulipan fleet.
Kazan and Oleg have joined me on the command ship so that the stars of the day can keep the spotlight to themselves.
That said, though the parade is flashy, it is a short affair.
Not long after we leave the port, Zeven and Evertsen put away their rigging and join the Northern Parliament's mass-produced fleet waiting close by.
The fleet changes to a circular formation centered around the command ship, and we make way for our destination.
Shortly later...
Kazan, is it just me, or is the Commander a little too cautious?
The experimental division's big shots are gone. I bet Sirens would be easy pickings for our fleet.
I'm sure the Commander has good reasons.
Besides, you've seen how nervous the Tulipan girls are.
Oh... Yeah, now that you mention it...
It will work out... It won't work out... It will work out... It won't work out...
Aww... This is no good. Let me try again...
It will work out... It won't work out...
Keep pulling out petals, and that wand won't have any flowers left.
Ah... Th-then I'll just grow more...
Not a good use of your powers.
O-okay, I'll just go get more flowers...
That's not the problem – ugh, forget it. I'm wasting my breath.
If you really can't settle down, might I suggest a round of patrols?
Oh! That's a good idea. Shall we go now?
Wait a minute, I heard that!
You're acting as part of a fleet. No individual action without approval!
I'm sorry. I guess I didn't think things through.
Okay, they're getting TOO tense.
This isn't normal... It's almost shipgirl instinct to maintain discipline in battle, isn't it?
Are they under too much pressure? Or could it be... because of their special Wisdom Cubes?
Aha! That must be it!
After the investigation of the Arcana Sanctum, everyone's Wisdom Cubes had changed in subtle ways.
Their structure is still stable, but they're extra active. They were there for a long time, after all.
So we'll get to see the Tulipan fleet using the power of those cubes... I'm getting even more excited to see them in battle!
Commander's Vessel - Command Deck
*sigh*... These people are such a mess.
Don't worry. There's still time until we enter the danger zone, so let them get acclimated.
Weren't you like this during your first operation, too?
Goodness, no!
I was calm and collected, and I sunk countless mass-produced Siren ships to boot.
Why, my heroic acts left an unforgettable impression on everyone there.
...What? If you don't believe me, then go ask Honolulu.
That's not it. I'm just thinking about how time flies.
Hm? Are you calling me old now?
Not at all.
Hmph. We shipgirls are forever young!
BEEP BEEP!
Whoops, there we go.
Commander, we have intel reports.
Our route remains clear. If we continue at our current pace, we should enter the Mirror Sea in approximately 45 minutes.
Time to get into formation, then.
BEEP BEEP!
Evertsen, can you hear me?
Evertsen speaking. Commander, what are your orders?
Let me ask one thing first. Have Tulipan communication devices been prepared to deal with the jamming in Mirror Seas?
I'm sorry... You won't like the answer.
Oleg, what of the Northern Parliament's?
It's possible in theory, but I can't make any promises. Sometimes, they fail.
Understood. All units, listen carefully.
In forty-five minutes, we will enter the Mirror Sea. Communications with the outside will most likely be cut off. This is expected – remain calm.
Memphis will give you orders to adjust your formations, so listen to her and prepare for battle.
Roger!
(Things are just like they used to be. It's almost disconcerting.)
(I should ask Helena META if she has any tech she can share with us...)
(Worst case, I can have her reverse engineer it at the Sea of Stars. I doubt she'll say no to that.)
KABOOOM!
The Tulipan fleet is engaging the enemy.
Shell after shell loaded with fury ignites one hideous foe after the next.
The Sirens are ablaze.
All the blood shed since the destruction of our kingdom's fleet... can be seen in these flames.
We finally did it... The Kingdom of Tulipa finally did it...
It's not time yet to be overcome with emotion, Evertsen.
Our journey has only just begun. We only planted our flag in this ocean mere moments ago.
You're right... This is only the beginning.
Our new future... begins now.
KABOOOM!
Enemy reinforcements incoming.
We'll lead our mass-produced fleet in and pincer them. Eliminate them as quickly as possible.
Let us show them our might. Our first battle must end in victory!
KABOOOM!
As time went by, the Tulipans conquered their initial awkwardness and gradually became accustomed to fighting.
The advantage we had since the very start had developed into an overwhelming superiority.
Mirror Seas used to be so dangerous, and now we can just bulldoze through them.
And our fighting force isn't even first-rate...
Seems like we've accomplished the transition from quantity to quality.
You realized that just now?
I've had an inkling for a while. Data doesn't lie.
It's just that the enemies have been getting stronger at the same as we did. Chances to really feel our growth were surprisingly rare.
This one time is different. They're still weak while we've changed greatly.
I estimate we'll complete this mission in under 12 hours, including time spent searching for hostiles.
If we hurry back to the harbor, we should even make it in time for lunch.
(True. The mission is proceeding very smoothly, and it looks like the Tulipans got into the swing of things.)
(That said, no report is better than seeing something with your own eyes. There is something special about these girls.)
(The ivies appearing out of thin air, this everpresent feeling of nature... Could this be a type of cognitive materialization?)
(Their strange powers and these unusual phenomena must have something to do with those unique Wisdom Cubes.)
(After my trip to the Arcana Sanctum, there was an unidentified but positive change in all the Wisdom Cubes the Northern Parliament had at the time.)
(They developed all kinds of theories to try to explain the origin of this phenomenon.)
(Some say the cause was the Arcana Sanctum's unique environment, while others say my Wisdom Cube aptitude had that effect. Others, still, say it was a combination of both of those.)
(Whatever the case, that phenomenon hasn't reoccurred since.)
(That's not all. Whenever new shipgirls are born in the Northern Parliament, they use those unique Wisdom Cubes as part of the process.)
(Despite this different procedure, those shipgirls don't display any differences. It's as though they did it using regular Wisdom Cubes.)
(In contrast, the Tulipan shipgirls exhibit astonishing changes.)
(I hope we'll be able to figure out the root cause...)
(Because if we do, we might be able to further raise the strength floor of our world!)
BEEP BEEP!
Commander, the Northern Parliament fleet has finished its elimination mission.
We're now starting to surround the Mirror Sea's central control tower from the southwest. Expected to be in the designated position within an hour.
Likewise, Commander, the Tulipan fleet has completed its own elimination mission. We are currently surrounding the tower from the southeast.
We'll begin an all-out attack once we link up with the Northern Parliament's fleet!
Fantastic work. Keep it up.
BEEP BEEP!
What's wrong, Commander? You look displeased, despite how well things are going.
Remember back at the embankment, right as Zeven approached us? I was going to tell you that Omitter used this Mirror Sea to test new weapons.
I heard it straight from Helena, so I have no reason to doubt its veracity.
Huh? But we haven't seen anything you could call a new weapon so far...
That's what worries me.
There should be one, so where is it?
KABOOOM!
The battle for the central control tower wasn't particularly tough.
All resistance to our overwhelming firepower proved futile, and the tower that maintained the Mirror Sea was destroyed very quickly.

The abnormal weather and terrain within the Mirror Sea gradually faded away, and soon, the jamming that impeded our communications disappeared, and we started receiving messages from the outside again.
Wow, that's a lot of unread messages.
...Commander, I have terrible news.
Not long after we departed, a Siren fleet launched an attack on the Tulipan coast!
My bad premonition came true.
Helena META's intel was correct – this place was indeed a Siren testing site for new weapons, and it had been operating as normal.
Apparently, as soon as I took the fleet in to destroy the Mirror Sea, its commanding AI sent forth a fleet armed with new weapons and attacked the now-defenseless Tulipan coast.
Scheming to strike at us even if it meant sacrificing itself... How cowardly!
Our dam defense system is engaging the Siren fleet, and it's now on the brink of falling apart...
Commander, we have to retreat posthaste!
Hold up. While we did destroy the machine sustaining the Mirror Sea, there are still Sirens in the general area. Our mission isn't over yet.
Be that as it may, the enemy is attacking our country directly!
I know, but we can't just leave. This is a joint operation between the Azur Lane and the Crimson Axis.
And as operation participants, we have to prioritize the mission.
Even if our country is burning?
Believe in yourself, believe in your compatriots defending the dam, and believe in the Commander.
You have to keep cool no matter how dire things get.
Remember, we have the edge in firepower. As long as each of us carries out their role, the Commander will always lead us to the best result.
*sigh*...
You're right. Forgive me, Commander. I lost my composure.
Since the situation has changed, we'll have to redeploy our forces.
We've successfully eliminated the Sirens within the Mirror Sea and taken out its control tower.
However, there are still hostiles in the area, so our mission isn't finished just yet.
While it's true we have to deal with them, not ALL of us need to stay here.
A part of our force will split off and head to the coast.
Zeven, assemble a fleet consisting of you, Eversten, and your mass-produced ships. I'll bring my command vessel and provide support.
Thank you, Commander! I'll start regrouping at once!
Kazan, you'll take command of the NP fleet and stay here to mop up the enemy. Don't let a single one get away.
Got it. It will be done.
I'll request backup from the Royal Navy fleet nearby. They should help us clean up this area.
Once the area is clear, immediately return to Tulipa and provide backup.
This battle must be finished quickly and conclusively.
There are your orders. Eliminate all enemies before Tulipa suffers further casualties!
Roger!
The fleet sailed on at full speed, and soon the Tulipan coastline lit up by cannon fire came into view.
location: Kingdom of Tulipa Coastal Waters - Dam Defense System

scripts.say: While there was fighting all across the dam defense system, it didn't seem as disastrous as was assumed.
The defense line was holding, and the battle was going far better than expected.
Leipzig, Nürnberg, coordinate with the Tulipan defensive installations and destroy the enemy's vanguard force.
- Yes, ma'am! - Roger!
Spee, don't focus solely on their biggest units. Our goal isn't swift elimination, it's to repel them from the coastline and keep structural damage to a minimum.
Okay... I'll bear that in mind.
Oh. It seems the Iron Blood had the same idea as us.
Murmansk, Grozny, we're going to assist the Iron Blood's fleet and push the frontline back into the sea.
- Roger, roger. - Let's beat the crap out of 'em!
Ally reinforcements on the coastline!
Thank goodness. They're still holding out!
Those are the domestic Iron Blood and Northern Parliament defense fleets not participating in the operation.
They're actually going out of their way to assist...
A good sign of things to come. It means all our hard work up to this point wasn't for nothing.
There may just be hope for the Azur Lane's reformation.
Yeah!
Then there are THOSE things over there... They must be Omitter's latest weapon.
According to intel, those are Sphyrnidae, super-dreadnought-class eradicators.
We have to defeat them to complete this mission in any real sense.
Commander, the Tulipan fleet awaits your orders!
Right. Coordinate with the coastal defense forces and allied fleets and eliminate the enemy!
KABOOOM!
Commander! Haven't seen you since the NA counterattack operation!
Royal Navy destroyer Grenville, head of the search-and-destroy fleet, reporting in!
The battle hasn't yet resulted in significant casualties. It seems we've arrived at the perfect time!
We're done mopping up the stragglers. I'll join up with you and the Royal Navy soon, Commander.
Whoa-ho! Those must be the biggest foes I've ever seen!
Heheh... I'd love to pick their wreckages apart!
What're we waiting for? Get 'em! Chaaarge!
At long last, peace and quiet returns to the shore.
The first light of dawn shines down, and a new day begins.

sequence: Kingdom of Tulipa
Nieuwe Haven Naval Base
Two days later...

scripts.say: Across the land scorched by fire, new life springs forth in droves.
After less than a day of examination and statistics, the Kingdom of Tulipa immediately started repairing its dam defense system.
Meanwhile, in the corner of the busy construction site...
Whoooa! They're growing! I can see the growth with my own two eyes!
They're getting bigger and bigger, longer and longer...
They can even lift those stacks of steel plates with ease!
Fabulous! Simply beautiful!
Are you satisfied?
Satisfied and then some!
Ah, sorry, it just hit me that I made you put on a show for my sake.
Don't be sorry. I'm just doing what has to be done anyway.
It makes an incredible amount of sense to put life and nature to use in reconstruction.
Our dam defense system is very important and directly linked to our country's safety. As a Tulipan, I should naturally give reconstruction efforts my all.
Well spoken! Ah, that makes me think...
Heheh... Mwahahaha...
What's so funny?
Nothing, I just remembered something joyous!
You've shown me the wonders of biotechnology. Soon, I will show you the staggering might of INDUSTRIAL technology!
We defended these embankments together, so the Northern Parliament should also have a role in its reconstruction!
In fact, the giant construction machines I requested will be arriving by transport ship at this harbor today!
Hahahaha! Together, we'll rebuild it stronger, bigger, and better than before!
Have to say, I'm impressed by how the Tulipans rebuild.
Admiring the impassioned workers at the construction site from afar, Memphis and I walk along the embankment.
On another note, I heard the Sea of Stars sent a request for a few of those special Wisdom Cubes for research purposes.
Do you think the Northern Parliament will approve it, though?
Probably. Since the Tulipan fleet already demonstrated its unique powers, there's no reason to hide the Cubes anymore.
(Although, I wonder if the Sea of Stars will be able to research anything until they figure out how the Cubes work.)
BEEP BEEP!
It's Bismarck. She has many things to talk about, including but not limited to the mission's results.
I'll go and take a walk over there.
I heard you achieved another stellar victory, Commander.
Now that the Tulipan fleet has a win to its name, the going should get easier for them.
While the mission was a success, I wouldn't call it flawless.
Despite our overwhelming military advantage, Tulipa still suffered damage in this battle.
Damage which happened despite my learning in advance that our intel was wrong and revising the plan accordingly.
If it hadn't been me at the helm, or if I hadn't realized the intel was wrong, then who knows how the battle would've gone?
Even with the Sirens' experimentation division gone, we still can't ignore the threat that the remaining Sirens pose.
I think we've come to let our guard down after winning too much.
You're right. The Sirens are no less dangerous than before.
This direct attack on the Tulipan mainland serves as a warning for those of us who've become complacent.
...You know, I just remembered that the Sirens and the Iron Blood used to have a handful of Mirror Seas for cooperative testing purposes.
Please. That's in the past.
We live in a new age. A unified age where people help one another.
A better age. Wouldn't you agree?
As I walk aimlessly while on a call with Bismarck, I suddenly realize that I've arrived at the park Zeven mentioned a few days back.
I spot Memphis waving in the distance. She points at the communicator, then at a gazebo nearby.
Wrapping up my chat with Bismarck, I go up to the gazebo.
There, I find Zeven waiting for me.
Commander. What a coincidence! I wasn't expecting to meet you here.
How do you like the park?
You'll find the beautiful sights of Tulipa in many more places than just here. Since the mission is over now, and you find yourself here, why not stay in the country and relax for a while?
I and my countrymen all would love to have you here.
Well... The plan is for me to return to the Iris Orthodoxy tomorrow.
For another all-but-pointless meeting?
You've been working like a dog lately. It's time you took some time off.
Heck, I can write your vacation request for you. There's no need to burden yourself with that.
You say that, but my work is important.
If it really is important, they can call you about it. You can do it remotely!
Alright, if you insist...
Glad you agree! Time for a well-earned vacation!
Zeven, let's put together a schedule!
The two of them start merrily chatting away about a holiday schedule for me.
As I savor the joy of temporarily getting away from my work and the excitement of a vacation, I take one last look at my communicator.
That's when I notice there is a single unread message.
The sender – Queen Elizabeth. It arrived at nearly the same time as my call from Bismarck.
(From Elizabeth? Why would she message me at this time?)
(Maybe it's a "congratulations on your mission completion" message? One of her fleets DID participate.)
(Only one way to find out...)
I open the message. As expected, it does start with some congratulations, and even briefly touches on the developments on the front the Royal Navy has been assigned.
What comes after that, though, hits me like a freight train.
Queen Elizabeth META and Miss D returned safely to Camelot. They were successful in their whale hunt.
The catch is that although they have the whale, Miss D has forgotten how to use it.
Due to the exceptional familiarity Miss D showed toward me, and the astonishing cooperation between her and Helena META in the Martyrium, she is now inviting me to come to the Royal Islands.
Along with Helena META. She hopes that, together, we'll be able to shed some light on this whale of theirs.
(An invitation I can't refuse...)
(I'll have to contact Helena sometime today and start preparing in advance for a visit to the Royal Islands.)
Commander! How does the Tulipan capital sound for our first destination?
Err...
...Why the grim look?
What happened? Show me that!
So... yeah.
We'll accompany Grenville's fleet to the Royal Islands tomorrow.
No.. My vacation... My vacation plans...
ELIZABEEEEETH!!!

sequence: Toward Tulipa's Seas - End
Sub-Antarctic Ocean - Kerguelen Islands
Royal Navy Antarctic Fleet
Basilica Investigation Forward Team
Basilica Lighthouse Tower

scripts.say: Have you found anything abnormal, Royal Oak?
I-I think... everything is as it should be?
I've patrolled this area many times before, and I still can't believe how gloomy it feels... Did Vichya really have a fleet stationed here?
That's what our intel says.
However, it seems they all evacuated before we got here.
Perhaps they shared your sentiment and couldn't stand the dismal conditions anymore.
Maybe. At any rate, this facility is under our control now that they've abandoned it.
A shame there's not a shred of valuable information to be found.
We've searched every nook and cranny for the tiniest crumb, just as Implacable instructed, and all we've found is a map of the building.
It would make us look bad if we returned to Her Majesty emptyhanded, but...
Her Majesty is certain beyond a doubt that there's something here. We just haven't found it yet because I'm dead weight...
You're not dead weight at all. If failing to find anything noteworthy is a crime, then I'm equally guilty of it as well.
No, no, no... I can't let you be my scapegoat, or it will haunt me for the rest of my life...
That cannot happen. I'll search again, but twice as diligently this time!
(I was going to propose we search again together, but that's not what she needs to hear now...)
Calm down, Royal Oak! You know everyone cares about and respects you!
If we didn't, you wouldn't have been Her Majesty's first pick as the team's flagship.
The only reason Implacable is leading this operation is because you passed on that honour.
But if I had accepted, I would've invariably disappointed Her Majesty.
Because, I'm slow and have no stamina or grace. And worst of all, terrible luck...
Please don't berate yourself like that.
As Her Majesty said, there has to be something in this Basilica. Otherwise they wouldn't have had a force stationed to protect it.
I promise you, we will find it. We just have to keep looking for... Wait, what?
Royal Oak, did you notice any strange movement? Something just tripped an alarm.
Huh? Wait, that wasn't a stray bullet? Something's moving?!
Stay calm and report the situation! Panicking will only make things worse!
I'm fine, I just heard what sounded like footsteps... It couldn't have been a ghost, right?
Well, I wouldn't be surprised if a ghost took up residence in a dreary place like this.
So it WAS a ghost?!
No! Forgive me, I only meant it as a joke!
Hang on, I'll start up the security cameras. Let's see, you're over by... There, I've got it.
Now to find the feed for the room you're in...
That's strange... It seems to be offline.
Oh, I'll check it myself. Just give me a minute!
That should do it. Argus, is the alarm still sounding?
Not anymore. However, the security camera remains unresponsive.
You mean this? Let me have a look... *cough cough*!
Looks like the cable has been cut. Judging by all this dust, it seems it's been left like this for a long time.
How long has it been like this? Whoever was in charge of this place before was way too inattentive...
Maybe. Do you think the alarm was a false positive too?
It wouldn't surprise me. Some of the oldest records of this island date back to the Naval Holiday period.
A false alarm doesn't explain the footsteps your heard, though.
*gasp*!
Th-this is Royal Oak of the Royal Navy! Show yourself!
Huh? Did you encounter an enemy?
Not exactly... I just thought someone might come out if I yelled.
I see... Also, I think I should do a more thorough system inspection. We might find something new.
If I remember the phrase right, it should be something like...
Basilica System, initiate a full facility self-diagnostic.
Orders received. Initiating full facility self-diagnostic. Time remaining: 60,000 minutes.
60,000 minutes?! We'll be here for an eternity!
That's how it is when you're dealing with a facility this old.
Hang on, there's a sysadmin message on the screen.
System override in the case of an emergency... Grants administrator privileges... Thus activating the facility's defences...
Okay, I've got an idea! I'll log us both as admins and briefly enable the Basilica's automated defences.
This way, we'll immediately know when anyone comes or goes.
Wonderful. If it can deal with intruders as well, we'll be safe until the rest of the team arrives.
Mhm. I'll give it the order now.
Orders received. Entering emergency defense mode. Powering up production center.
Wait, what?
Royal Oak, it seems we have a problem in the production centre!
Yes, I can see it over here as well. A lot of devices are spitting out error messages.
It's getting worse! Oh goodness, what do we do?! One thing after the next is failing!
Error: Failed to initialize emergency defense mode.
Error: Failed to initialize recovery program. Retrying... Failed. Retrying... Failed.
Warning: Significant data corruption. Please reconnect to system host.
Something has gone terribly wrong here... Let me try to update my admin privileges...
What the...? I can't! It says I need higher clearance!
But that's impossible... What could possibly be higher than the sysadmin?
Royal Oak, we have a problem! Get out of there and regroup with me!
...can't... you... too many...
...ambushed... fighting...
Royal Oak, do you hear me?! What's happening over there?!
...Our comms are being jammed. Don't tell me... we're in a Mirror Sea?!

sequence: On a remote island in the frigid Antarctic waters...
A number of Iris Orthodoxy Basilicas stood like beacons of faith.
Yet beneath the veneer of pious glory,
flow whispers of intrigue and technology untold.
While all eyes are on the World Expo,
an investigation fleet suddenly arrives at the distant island.
What began as simple orders from the Queen
would soon capture the interest of sinister eyes.

scripts.say: Basilica Blanc Control Center
W-we've gained control of the main passages along the east side!
The southern bridge has also been secured.
And I've already finished conquering the north side~☆
Thank you for your hard work, everyone. I'm not detecting any more enemy signals.
How are things on your end, Cardinal?
Done. Looks like we've cleaned up the last batch of Pawns over here.
Béarn, how's your situation?
The infection index in the purification system has dropped to normal levels, which means this area is effectively safe.
Excellent.
I'm not sure if I'm just imagining things... but this place doesn't seem as claustrophobic and dreary as it did before.
If anything, it has a bit of a calming, reassuring atmosphere now...
Now that you mention it, I think I feel it as well.
Woah, and that's not all – look, the dense fog that was obscuring the horizon has completely disappeared as well!
The gilded inscriptions on the Basilica's white spires are so majestic... Magnificent works of art in their own right.
Incredible... Just a slight change in the atmosphere can completely alter the way I perceive this place...
Don't get distracted from the fact that this place was functionally designed to be something akin to a military stronghold or factory.
Tell me, Cardinal, you wouldn't have happened to retrofit Basilica technology onto your warships, would you?
...Indeed, the Tribunal did have such plans in the past, and managed to build one prototype using their own resources.
I believe it was classified as a Mechanicus Confessor.
Oh? Did something like that really get built? I wonder why I haven't heard anything about it until now...
It's practically ancient history by now. And shortly after the Confessor was completed, the Tribunal sent it to the front lines.
Unfortunately, its maiden voyage was also its final voyage.
That's a pity. I would've liked to see it...
So, are we done with this Basilica? Shall we move on to the next one?
Yes. Our next destination is Basilica Rouge. Please follow me, everyone.
Basilica Rouge – Main Plaza
Hmm? Is the plaza here the same as the one saw before?
The only difference is, it seems to be a bit bigger...?
That's correct. Although the four Basilicas have their own unique layouts, they are similar in general design.
Similar plazas can be found in front of every Basilica. As you pointed out, this one is slightly larger in size.
Furthermore, the Main Plaza of Basilica Rouge is the only way to access the command center, and also serves as an ideal location to engage the enemies.
Right, we'll have a significant advantage if we can set up a defensive line out in the open.
Good, you're quite perceptive. Just keep in mind that as this is the largest facility, we'll also be up against the most Pawns here. A tough fight lies ahead of us.
(Hmm... This undeniably is an advantageous combat location.)
(But, it's a bit too wide-open...)
Is something amiss, Lady Implacable?
Ah, it's nothing. Please do continue.
I've already said everything that I needed to say. If you have nothing you'd like to add...
Umm... Since you're putting me on the spot anyway, I'll just say a few words.
Everyone, remember Her Majesty's words. Always keep the duties she has given us front and foremost in your mind.
As long as we cooperate with our friends and allies, victory will be ours!
KABOOM–––!!
The cannons of battle rang out the instant the first Pawn broke through into the Main Plaza.
The events unfolding below were clearly visible from the observation platforms rising above the plaza.
Pawns exuding an ominous red mist continuously broke through into the plaza, but were quickly felled one after another by a dense barrage of bombs and cannonfire.
Despite the enemy's terrifying numbers, the overwhelmingly advantageous position held in advance by the defenders made the battle a completely one-sided affair.
Implacable continued to bombard the enemies as they lurched forward, until she finally had enough time to sift through various possibilities in her mind.
(Blanc, now Rouge... After we clear out this Basilica...)
(..."And thus did the first horn of Judgment sound.")
(Speaking of which... This Basilica was originally built during the first counterattack against the Sirens, though it seems to have been expanded several times since...)
(I see, so that's what's going on...)
The wreckages of crimson-colored Pawns lay strewn across the ground, stacked one on top of another.
From a higher vantage point, it seemed as if this sanguine mat could stretch all the way to the ends of the world.
Implacable, the battle is over. Cardinal Richelieu led Béarn to clean up the mess, and Scylla went with them.
We had a flawless victory, sustaining no injuries in the process. How are you doing?
No problems on my end either.
Thanks to the Cardinal's understanding of this place's terrain, we were able to destroy a massive army with almost minimal effort.
If only she'd actually tell us the truth...
...What do you mean by that?
Oh, don't worry about it. That was just some of my idle musing.
Argus, when you and the others were on patrol a few days ago, do you remember the state of the facilities and if anything unusual happened?
Umm... Everything looked really run-down, and the equipment looked like it hadn't been maintained in a really long time.
As for unusual occurrences... I remember there were a few electrical explosions, which isn't something you'd normally see in a place of worship, right?
What else?
Other than that... I don't think anything particularly noteworthy happened, which is also what I put in the report.
I'm not just talking about your objective findings. Let's talk about something a bit more... spiritual?
I can't exactly put this into precise words, but did you experience any emotional or spiritual abnormalities?
Hmm... Well, I did feel a bit rather depressed when I got here, as if I was in a constant state of anxiety. That was probably just due to the suffocating atmosphere of the building though.
Royal Oak said she had a similar experience.
And that was a persistent sensation, correct? Not just one that occurred after the subsequent incident?
That's right... Though, that feeling did grow stronger after that close shave.
After the purification system was activated, that feeling of oppression completely went away...
I'm not sure I'm describing it in a very helpful way either, and it might've just been all in my head as I said earlier.
Let me know if you experience something like that again. Mental problems can sometimes be a greater cause for concern than physical ones.
In any case, let's head to the next Basilica.
Hmm? Did Lady Richelieu already tell you where we'll be going next?
No, but I've already figured it out.
We will be going to Basilica Noir.

sequence: Basilica Island Inner Facility
Basilica Noir Control Area
Joint Basilica Investigation Team

scripts.say: Die, die, die~☆
You're nothing more than lowly mob monsters, but why is it so much fun chopping you up~?
Umm... P-please get back in formation! Y-you're getting ahead of us too quickly!
Don't worry. Just focus on keeping up with her. I'll cover your rear.
In the middle of the storage facility, a fierce battle had broken out between the investigation team and the army of infected Pawns gathered there.
Though the enemies were numerous, there were not as many of them as had been at Basilica Rouge.
It did not take long for the battle at Basilica Noir to also wind down smoothly.
Lady Implacable, Royal Oak and I might've discovered something out of the ordinary...
Details please.
Through the course of the battle, we realized that the size of the battlefield was far more spacious than it should've been...
In other words... the area inside the Basilica is larger than the space it occupies on the outside!
Excellent. So you've finally noticed it as well?
My sincerest apologies. We have not had time to thoroughly survey the area to confirm our findings.
Don't worry, I did not mean to cast doubt on your abilities. I simply am glad to have someone else's confirmation.

Actually, this phenomenon is not readily noticeable to the untrained eye. Whoever built the Basilicas incorporated a number of optical illusions to obfuscate this fact, and not every Basilica shares the same design.
Some were built to be massive, while others only expand in space under certain circumstances.
I've been carefully observing this as well before finally coming to my conclusions.
Scylla, did you notice Richelieu and Béarn doing anything unusual while they were cleaning up the battlefield?
For example, trying to cover something up?
My apologies, Lady Implacable. I saw nothing of the sort.
I see... Well, so be it. The two of us are on good terms, so I suppose I can directly ask her myself.
Cardinal Richelieu, how goes the purification process?
The third purification station is operating normally, and should finish running within fifteen minutes.
An army of mass-produced Pawns, and a space larger than the actual size of the building––
This entire Basilica is a piece of Siren technology, isn't it?
Indeed. We've achieved these feats through recycling Siren technology.
...Oh? So, you admit it readily?
After all, I am in the mood to casually give away valuable information today.
Besides, you've been fighting in the Basilicas long enough to know that this phenomenon is commonplace. I never intended to cover it up in the first place.
Then why didn't you bother saying anything?
Because you never asked.
That is the first reason, but there's also a second – you seem like the type of person who genuinely relishes in piecing together the truth.
Plus, you've had your Royal Maid keeping an eye on me the whole time, so why would I go and threaten my standing with the Royal Navy?
That aside, was everything here made using Siren tech?
Not everything. That would require us to go back through history, to the time when this Basilica was first established.
A long time ago, the Iris Orthodoxy sent a small expedition to this island during the course of its war against the Sirens, in hopes of establishing a strategic foothold in the area.
However, it did not take long for the Sirens to invade and completely level the expedition base.
Generally speaking, conventional wisdom holds that the Iris fleet should've withdrawn for good – and live to fight another day.
But for whatever reason, the Holy See issued a declaration that day: retake control of the island, at any and all cost.
The Tribunal would soon dispatch another fleet to attack the Sirens' entrenched position.
They carried out their orders faithfully, and after paying a harrowing price, managed to wrest control of Kerguelen Island from the Sirens.
After regaining control, we found a number of non-combat installations left behind by the Sirens all across the island.
Apparently, they were trying to convert this place into a stronghold with logistical functions, but the blood price paid by the Orthodoxy fleet that day caught them off guard.
Perhaps that was not simply a stroke of fate. The Tribunal may simply have had information nobody else was privy to at the time.
So you continued to build up the military fortress on the foundations of the Siren stronghold, and took control of it in the form of a Basilica?
What you see in front of you has changed appearances multiple times before reaching the scale you see now.
Of course, there were various twists and turns along the reconstruction processes, but that would be the gist of it.
I see. That makes sense. What about the meanings behind these four colours?
What do you mean exactly?
Blanc, Rouge, Noir, and Vert.
The bow, the sword, the scales, and the sickle.
Conquest, war, famine, and death.
What the four Basilicas truly represent... are the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, the harbingers of the Last Judgment.
Were you also planning to tell me that from the beginning?
I must admit, that is one piece of information I was not planning to impart.
It's true, the Iris Orthodoxy was involved in eschatological research on behalf of the Holy See. It would've been quite embarrassing for them had word gotten out.
But, when I led you and your team here, I came to terms with the reality that you'd figure it out sooner or later.
Our faiths may be different, but they ultimately trace back to the same roots.
None of this symbolism is foreign to me.
My question for you is this – what did the Orthodoxy hope to achieve with this research? To pass Judgment upon this world?
Hardly. We created this symbolic system to streamline the process of controlling our four armies.
After the Holy See took control of the Siren stronghold here, we did manage to get our hands on a full suite of facilities for producing Pawns.
However, that did not come with the technology needed to control them. That's something only the Sirens know how to do.
After extensive research, our engineers came up with a set of devices that borrowed the imagery of the Four Horsemen to operate the four fleets.
And those are the four Basilicas you see now.

So, each of the Horsemen corresponds to the division of the fleets based on function, and the concept of Judgment allows you to issue combat orders to exert a semblance of "control" over the Pawn fleets...
A remarkably innovative solution.
Or so it seemed on paper, but the execution did not pan out in the end.
The reason why it failed was the infection problem we discussed earlier.
In other words, the infection of the Basilicas is not a malfunction per se, but rather a conceptual misalignment?
That explains a lot. No wonder why I've never seen Sirens struggle to command their Pawns.
And yet, you managed to create your own version of the Sirens' control system from scratch, relying solely on these bulky machines?
That's right. Béarn was the chief engineer during the second phase of the Basilica's construction at the time, and many of the devices inside were brought to fruition thanks to her.
So, she's the chief engineer, huh? No wonder the two of you knew everything about the Basilica's installations along the way.
Is the purification system also derived from the imagery of Judgment Day?
Correct. It represents the cleansing of all sin from the "world."
Now, only one Basilica remains. Once we reactivate the purification system there, Béarn and I will handle the rest ourselves.

sequence: Basilica Island Inner Facility
Basilica Vert Control Area
Joint Basilica Investigation Team

scripts.say: Hmm... What's going on here?
What's wrong, Miss Béarn?
Things are much worse than I had anticipated.
This was originally the first Basilica built on top of the Siren facilities, so it's also the oldest.
I already knew that the level of infection would be the most severe here.
But, I didn't expect it to be so severe that it'd generate its own Mirror Sea.
Wait, so the Mirror Sea didn't appear because Argus activated the emergency control system?
By the looks of things, that's right. All she did was cause the existing infection to spread.
This problem has been going on for far longer.
And to make matters worse, this Basilica's factory has been running nonstop this entire time.

This might be the real reason Vichya abandoned the island... The facility had already gone out of control, and instead of trying to get the equipment back under control, they sealed it off and allowed it to continue running...
We're fortunate the seal has managed to hold up until this point, but...
Eventually, the Pawns will overflow from this place and mindlessly spread "death" as their symbolism implies...
In other words, this would've turned into a major crisis sooner or later.
Had Her Majesty not sent us...
You would've had to take responsibility for whatever fallout came of this Basilica. Isn't that right, Lady Richelieu?
...Yes. While I did not account for the Royal Navy coming here, your assistance is the best thing I could've asked for.
Her Majesty would naturally want us to look after our allies~
Say, you mentioned just now that the factory has been producing Pawns nonstop. Where have they all gone?
On the contrary, we haven't encountered any resistance at all since we entered the Basilica. Things are going smoother so far than in any of the other Basilicas.
I can't give you a definitive answer without doing a bit of investigation myself, but they might've been sent deeper into the catacombs–
Béarn...
Ahem. Sorry, I spoke without thinking. I need to investigate whether the purification system will still be able to function as normal, so please excuse me for a moment.
...Quite an uncharacteristically intense look in your eyes, Cardinal.
What are these "catacombs" that Béarn mentioned?
...One of the Basilica's facilities, responsible for breaking down and recycling the Pawns manufactured here.
The situation down there probably isn't very optimistic either, but it doesn't change the task at hand.
Once we reactivate all four purification stations, that should resolve the most urgent part of this problem.
As long as we work together and seal this place back up, there won't be anything for you to worry about.
(I can't afford to get any more outside parties involved in this mess... Especially not the Commander.)
I'll trust your assessment of the situation then.
Naturally, as these facilities belonged to the Iris Orthodoxy, the Cardinal should have the final say over what to do with them.
There's no need to be so formal. Though I've had to choose my words carefully, do let Queen Elizabeth know that I am extremely grateful for her assistance.
Heehee. I'll do just that.
Much obliged. Now, all we need to do is to wait for Béarn to finish reactivating the purification system.
Miss Scylla, would you mind preparing some snacks for us in the meantime?
As you wish, Lady Richelieu.
Basilica Island Inner Facility
What on earth is this place? I don't remember it being here when we surveyed the island.
This is the Tribunal's fortress. It only rises out of the ground when all other purification systems have come online.
Its presence confirms that the purification of Basilica Vert has been completed.
Unfortunately, I don't know much about this fortress either, as it was always one of the Tribunal's most closely-kept secrets.
Can I also assume that the Tribunal was directly responsible for the construction of the fortress? They seem to have had big plans for this place.
That's correct. As a matter of fact, the Tribunal's Mechanicus Confessor sank not too far from here.
At the time, the Tribunal had invested a massive amount of resources into that ship's construction, managing to create one of the most powerful conventional warships at its disposal.
As it was one of their prized vessels, there was technically no reason for it to have participated in the battle in the first place.
However, they still sent it to the front lines as part of their mission to reclaim the island at all costs.
What's more, it actually did play an instrumental role in that battle against the Sirens.
It truly is a pity, just as you said.
...I see Vichya hasn't replaced these flags. They're still in the Orthodoxy's old design.
Yes, I suppose some good did come of their negligence to maintain this place.
A sight for sore eyes indeed. May the Holy Iris's blessing be upon us all...
Do you wish to pray? I can leave you alone for a while if you'd like.
No need, resolving this situation is still our top priority.
There will be plenty of time for prayers later.
Béarn, begin the final purification. Carry out the Judgment procedure.
As you wish, Cardinal.
Béarn pulled the lever on the purification system, spurring it into action.
In an instant, the ambiance lightened, as did the anxiety gripping all the girls' hearts.
So... Is that it? We've finally done it?
Okay. Hero, return the bow to the Cardinal. You don't need it anymore.
Give it back? Heck no. This is loot and I earned it.
You WILL give it back, and that's that. We're not in the business of looting sacred relics.
If she wants it, she may keep it.
That bow is only a replica for exhibition purposes anyway.
Sweet! Cheers, Cardinal~
Well, if you're sure. Cardinal, I'd like to take this moment to thank you again, on behalf of the whole Royal Navy.
Were it not for you, Royal Oak and Argus would still be in danger and this crisis would continue to threaten our forces in the Antarctic region.
Once we're back home, I will relay everything that happened here to Her Majesty.
If you'd like me to forward a message to her, please tell me now.
No, I should be thanking you. You helped us regain control of these Basilicas, and let me see our old, glorious flag as it once flew over this island.
You needn't tell Her Majesty anything specific. Just give her my sincerest thanks.
That's all? Alright, I'll–
...Cardinal, what's that in the sky?
The sky...?
And thus shall the lightless purgatory manifest above the skies, a portent from beyond the realm of Man.
An all-devouring void, the sign of the arrival of the End Times.
Raise your eyes to the Apocalyptic Sun, for Revelation has come.

sequence: <size=29>"I watched as the Lamb opened the first of the seven seals, and there before me was a white horse."</size>
<size=29>"Its rider held a bow, and he was given a crown, and he rode out as a conqueror bent on conquest."</size>
<size=29>"When the Lamb opened the second seal, another horse came out, a fiery red one."</size>
<size=29>"Its rider was given power to take peace from the earth and to make people kill each other. To him was given a large sword."</size>
<size=29>"When the Lamb opened the third seal, there before me was a black horse."</size>

<size=29>"Its rider was holding a pair of scales in his hands. Then I heard what sounded like its voice, saying, 'Two pounds of 
wheat for a day's wages, and six pounds of barley for a day's wages, and do not damage the oil and the wine!'"</size>
<size=29>"When the Lamb opened the fourth seal, before me was a pale horse."</size>

<size=29>"Its rider was named Death. They were given power over a fourth of the earth to kill by sword, famine and plague, 
 and by the wild beasts of the earth."</size>

scripts.say: Where... am I...?
What happened? I don't understand...
Don't fear, Implacable. Take deep breaths and calm down.
*huff*... *huff*... Eurgh, I feel awful.
One moment I'm looking up at the sky, the next, the world is spinning like I'm inside a washing machine.
Shadowy reflections were cast upon the stained ocean. High above, a black sun hung above the sky like an unending solar eclipse.
Did we... get sucked through a Singularity?
Implacable looked around blankly. Basilica Island had completely disappeared, replaced with a sprawling network of intricate buildings reaching all the way to the skyline.
This feels like somewhere we aren't meant to be...
Cardinal, do you know anything? Are we "beneath" the Basilicas?
I believe so, yes. We've somehow entered the catacombs.
Catacombs? You mean Mirror Sea, don't you?
I doubt all the technology in the Basilicas could've created something like this.
Not only is this clearly Siren territory, but it's also been here for a long time.
Yes, you're probably right.
How did this happen? You said it'd be over once we activated all the purification systems on the island.
It SHOULD have been over, but it seems I was mistaken... I can only guess the system malfunctioned in some way.
That, or this was an elaborate Siren trap from the very start.
Regardless, I shouldn't have assumed the Mirror Sea was limited to the island's surface layer. A foolish error on my part...
Don't blame yourself. The Sirens have ways of catching even the most cautious among us off-guard.
Let's focus on getting out of here. Does anything about this place resemble its real-world equivalent?
I can't say for sure. If I notice something, I will let you know.
...Why did we get sent down here to begin with?
Is it because we now know too much, and the Tribunal wants to silence us?
That seems unlikely. If they wanted to get rid of us, we would've been sent down when we activated the very first purification system.
"Unlikely" means it's not out of the question, but I'll take your word for it. For now.
If I remember right, you said Pawns are broken down and recycled in the catacombs, correct?
So if we're not being silenced, maybe the facility sees us as "outside invaders" and is trying to eliminate us.
As far as I know, the catacombs and the purification process have no bearing on one another.
It should also be stated the catacombs are almost entirely separated from the surface layer. Béarn and I don't know any way to reach them.
That is to say, I fear you may be right in saying that we've walked into a trap.
That would make it one of the most despicable I've ever seen.
Whoever's behind it knew that people would investigate if they just withdrew the island's defense force.
Then, the Pawns would easily dispatch whatever mass-produced ships were sent in, forcing us shipgirls to do the job.
The Royal Navy wouldn't be able to activate the purification systems or escape the Mirror Sea, and would eventually succumb to the Pawns.
Meanwhile, the only people in Iris Libre who could activate the purification systems would be sent to be dealt with down here...
...We need to get moving, immediately.
Huh? Why? Are Pawns on the way?
No, something far worse. By the look of things, the catacombs are completely out of control.
If we don't act now, we'll be in grave peril.
Implacable! Implacableeeee!! We need to get the heck out of here!!
There's a huge-ass mecha-knight coming straight towards you!
Mecha-knight? Did I hear that right?
An emergency call interrupted the girls' analysis of the situation, shifting their attention towards the distance.
There, they saw Hero, fleeing while desperately firing her cannons at the rapidly approaching threat.
A massive mechanical knight, clad in black armor with a set of heavy scales in hand, galloped across the water. An ominous, deathly aura followed in its wake.
...Mechanicus Harbinger - Famine.
It looks very different from what I remember, but that is definitely one of the Four Horsemen!
Royal Navy, intercept the target!
No, Implacable! Make no attempt to fight it! It is far too powerful for us!
Béarn! Search for a nearby conceptual anchor! We must retreat at once!
Understood, Cardinal! I will look for one!
Retreat? Why? Isn't it just an oversized Pawn?
It is nothing of the sort! We have to run!
Look, I'll explain what it is and how to deal with it once we've made it somewhere safe!
You need to trust me, Implacable!
Alright, alright. You know this place better than me, so I'll just follow you!

sequence: Mirror Sea - Unknown Location
Joint Basilica Investigation Team
- Data Corruption//- Fatal Error Detected//

scripts.say: Led by Béarn, the girls fled into a derelict building.
Phew... Many anchors appear to be broken, but at least this one works. We should be safe here.
You sure? How's this regular old building gonna protect us from that knight?
Please tell me there's some kind of secret weapon stashed away here...
There is not. This is just an ordinary building.
It is the conceptual anchor's sanctity that protects us. The knight can't come near us.
First something about anchors, now "sanctity?" Care to explain what's going on?
Sanctity, much like purification on the surface level, is a concept we use to control the Basilicas.
Conceptual anchors, meanwhile, are things which strengthen that sanctity. They are Sacraments that have been buried deep underground.
Sanctity has a range inside which no infection can occur, and Pawns which have already been infected cannot come near it.
The purification systems let us regain full control of the surface facility, while these conceptual anchors help us retain some semblance of control down here.
Also, while the anchor is working for now, I'm not sure how long it will last.
All I got from that was one thing – that there is equipment down here which you're familiar with.
In short, yes. As for the... um, "mecha-knight," was it?
No need to dumb it down. Tell me everything you know about that thing first.
That knight you saw was, originally, a natural entity that came into being in these catacombs.
It is one of four in total – Conquest, War, Famine, and Death, each appearing in its respective area.
A... natural entity? What?
Yes. It is neither Pawn nor shipgirl, but rather a being born from the Orthodoxy's beliefs.
A non-Siren entity, brought into existence by a Mirror Sea... That's completely unprecedented.
Forgive me, I should clarify one thing... The Four Horsemen were not always present here.
Their origin dates back to when the facility had just been opened...
A lot of the Siren technology the Tribunal discovered could not be controlled and were deemed too dangerous to research, yet they also did not want to destroy these hard-won spoils.
As a result, they piled all that technology in the Mirror Sea lower layer while shifting their focus towards researching the comparatively safe technology on the surface.
Just like the factory you saw, which was a powerful tool that could be used almost immediately.
However, once Pawn production was in full swing, Pawns began appearing down here as well for reasons nobody understood.
By the time we received word that something had appeared in the catacombs below, the research team stationed here had been wiped out, and the Four Horsemen had already been born.
At first, they did not pose a significant threat, and the Tribunal successfully captured the underground layer with only a modest force.
But things have changed significantly since then.
As long as the factory continues producing Pawns, the Four Horsemen will continue to be reborn.
To make matters worse, the worse the Infection problem in the upper layer, the stronger the Horsemen become each time.
It was initially thought that the Horsemen were avatars which control the Pawns, and that reinforcing their respective concepts would let us control them.
In reality, they may have been the ones controlling us, using the Basilicas to make themselves stronger.
...That may well have been the Sirens' plan from the very beginning.
It wouldn't surprise me if they let you "capture" this base on purpose.
But, if you knew about this problem, why didn't anyone destroy the entire Mirror Sea and all the equipment along with it to resolve the issue once and for all?
Well... That's because there is no central control unit in this Mirror Sea.
What? That's impossible.
The Tribunal searched the catacombs numerous times, but were ultimately unable to find a way to dispel the Mirror Sea.
They also tried to take out the Four Horsemen on multiple occasions, but they kept coming back stronger and stronger.
It soon dawned on us that if we kept producing Pawns, we would essentially be putting four Siren superweapons into our world.
And so, we halted all production and sealed off the catacombs.
That is when Béarn proposed the idea of installing conceptual anchors in an attempt to weaken the Horsemen.
It worked... until the Orthodoxy split in two.
And because Vichya neglected to maintain the Basilicas, the factory eventually malfunctioned and resumed production.
Then came the infection, making the Horsemen only grow stronger and stronger.
Correct. I am truly sorry that things ended up this way.
It's not your fault. You're not the one who built this place or let it spiral out of control.
But, you are eager to get things back under control, aren't you?
When Béarn let the word "catacombs" slip, you interrupted her because you hoped to personally deal with the Horsemen yourselves. Is that right?
Yes, because with the purification complete and Pawn production stopped, the Horsemen will not get any stronger. Their days are numbered.
On the contrary, had we done nothing and let the infection grow unimpeded, the Horsemen would one day break out and render the Antarctic waters impossible to navigate.
We can blame Vichya for being neglectful all we want, but at the end of the day, this is a calamity that could affect the entire world – one that we, as shipgirls, are sworn to prevent.
This was supposed to be Iris Libre's battle, but now that the news of Vichya's withdrawal has gotten out...
So that's why you were being so secretive about this place.
Even if you can't get rid of the Mirror Sea, stopping the production of Pawns and destroying the Four Horsemen for good would already be enough.
That's right, and Iris Libre must shoulder that burden.
Eliminating Pawns associated with a particular Horseman's concept seems to have the effect of weakening it.
Rest assured, Implacable. I swear upon my name as the Cardinal to do whatever it takes to regain control of this place.
But first, I'm going to get you all home.
I do need to correct you, however – you need not shoulder this burden alone.
You'll fall behind in the long run if you pour all your resources into solving this without outside help.
I say let's work together to resolve your Horseman problem. Then we can all go home.
We're allies, and whether you wanted it or not, we're in this together now.
That's... a favor too tremendous to ask for.
Ask for it anyway. You know we'd gladly help.
I'll need to think of a way to repay you.
You'll have plenty of time for that later. Let's deal with the more pressing issue.
That being, finding the way out of here.
As much as I'd like to take the Horsemen on, I don't think we stand a fighting chance at the moment.
About that... Sadly, I have no idea where to even start looking.
I beg your pardon?
This is the first time I've personally seen this Mirror Sea layer with my own eyes.
The Tribunal's reports always stated that the situation here was under full control.
They didn't even bother to include small details such as how to enter and leave the lower layer...
Small details, huh...
Ahaha... The Tribunal, despite its tremendous service to the Iris Orthodoxy as a whole, also served as an extension of the Holy See's influence.
Their allies are many, and even I have difficulty comprehending their motives at times.
Béarn, it was you who proposed the conceptual anchors. Perhaps you know the catacombs better than I do?
I'm afraid not, Cardinal.
While I did come up with the idea of the anchors, I know the layout no better than anyone else here.
Even ignoring the Mirror Sea's inherent effects, what structures remain here have changed drastically since I was personally involved.
I can't say whether that's due to Siren intervention or Vichya modifications, but it matters little.
This wouldn't be much of a trap if we could simply walk out of it.
Worst case scenario, there simply is no exit. If so, we just have to find and destroy the central control unit.
As I said, we already tried that a long time ago...
That doesn't mean we won't succeed this time. After all this time, we all have more experience dealing with the Sirens' tricks than before. Maybe we'll notice something you overlooked back then.
Besides, what other option do we have?
I'll launch my recon planes and see what I can find. If you don't have any better ideas, you might as well at least pray for my success~♪
Basilica Island Catacombs
Lady Implacable, Lady Richelieu, this is the layout of the entire area. Please take a look.
Efficient as always. Thank you for your hard work.
Hmm... You're right, I don't see any sort of control device here, and the entire place is crawling with enemies...
Wait, this is odd... Cardinal, didn't you say that each of the Four Horsemen controlled a set of Pawns corresponding to their respective concepts?
Yes, each Horseman basically functions as a fleet leader.
Whenever a Horseman is reborn, the facilities here will automatically produce another Pawn fleet for it.
Things don't add up then. There are four different-coloured Basilicas corresponding to each of the Horsemen, but I'm only seeing one type of enemy here – red.
Where are the other three Horsemen's Pawn fleets?
I see a large number of wreckages of unknown origin around this area. Maybe the Four Horsemen fought amongst each other, and one of them came out on top?
Fighting amongst themselves? Has anything like that happened in the past?
No, but we've also never been in this exact situation before either.
Furthermore, it's not unheard of for Sirens to have Pawns fight each other for experimentation purposes.
Based on my experiences, that does sound somewhat plausible...
But even if we accept that premise, it shouldn't lead to these results.
Do you remember what we saw at Basilica Vert's factory?

Despite it being the largest facility and most severely affected by infection, there were very few Pawns on the upper level. If what you said is true, shouldn't the Horseman of Death have the largest fleet and be the strongest of the Four?
So my question is – why are they not down here either?
Ooh, let me take a stab at that!
Since only the red fleet is still remaining, that means the Horseman of War was simply stronger!
That's begging the question, Hero. What evidence do we have?
We don't know if there's any inherent differences in strength between the fleets.
If the Horseman of Death had the largest fleet and should have been powered up from the infection, how did the Horseman of War come out on top?
Uhh... I got nothing for ya!
Do you think this has something to do with "concepts?" Just like how the concept of sanctity kept us safe earlier, do you think something here is amplifying the concept of War?
Good, I reached the same conclusion.
Cardinal, I will now conduct a little experiment to test this hypothesis. If I start to show any signs of abnormalities, please stop me by any means.
...What are you trying to do?
We'll find out if I'm on the right track soon enough.
Implacable closed her eyes, took a deep breath, and began to chant in an almost imperceptible voice.
"When the Lamb opened the second seal, another horse came out, a fiery red one..."
"Its rider was given power to take peace from the earth..."
As the words of power flowed from her lips, a red mist began to diffuse from her body, just like the Pawns around them.
Wait... Stop this right now, Implacable!
Even as red mist flowed from her, Implacable ignored Richelieu's words and continued her chant.
"...and to make people kill each other. To him was given a large sword..."
Lady Implacable... Lady Implacable!!
Tch... I apologize for this!
KABOOM––!!
...Aaaaargh! That hurt like hell! What in the world just happened?
I hit you with a blank to snap you back to your senses. How are you feeling?
Terrible, thank you very much! My mind's all foggy, like someone just hit me in the head!
But, uh, my little gamble paid off, right? When I was reciting those lines from the Scriptures, something started happening to me, right?
Yes, your body started giving off the same red mist coming off of those Pawns, and you wouldn't respond to me.
Almost as if I was being possessed by the concept of War, right?
You said earlier that this space brought the Four Horsemen into being based on the Iris Orthodoxy's beliefs. What you just saw was a manifestation of the power of concepts here.
And if the Four Horsemen are fighting over control of this area, then the concept of war would permeate every corner of this space.
What about the concepts of Death and Famine? For Pawns and mass-produced machines, these concepts do not exist at all.
As for the concept of Conquest, that would likely depend on whether or not they were given orders, correct?
That seems likely. In other words, this space imposes a completely different set of rules on the Horsemen compared to up above.
By the way, how did the Orthodoxy try to fight against the Horsemen back then?
