You mean, tactics-wise? We didn't really have the luxury to pick and choose our fights, so we had to suppress them as we saw them.
If you want further details on the exact nature of those operations, you'd have to look through the Tribunal's logs.
I don't think that'll be necessary. You had us activate the purification stations at each of the four Basilicas in a specific order, right?
If that symbolises the breaking of the seals from the Scriptures, what do you think would happen if we defeated the Horsemen in the opposite order?

We'll follow the order of Vert, Noir, Rouge, and then finally Blanc. Given the diminished strength of the first two Horsemen, we should also take advantage of that opportunity to learn how to best fight in this space.
Also, we can use the conceptual anchors to wait for opportune times to attack and avoid unfavourable fights.
What do you think about my proposal, Cardinal?
It's certainly worth a shot. We have more resources at our disposal now than we ever did back then.
Excellent. In that case, let's move out while we can still seize the initiative.

sequence: Mirror Sea - Death's Territory
Joint Basilica Investigation Team
- Data Corruption//- Fatal Error Detected//

scripts.say: KABOOM––!!
Hero has arrived at the quest objective~☆
Hehe! Come out, my dear Horseman! I'm gonna turn you into juicy EXP~☆
However, Hero's energetic taunts were met with only silence.
This is supposed to be the part of the Mirror Sea corresponding to Basilica Vert, right? How come it's so quiet...?
We only ran into a few stragglers along the way here, roaming around as if they didn't have a commander at all...
Quite unusual... I have a bad feeling about this, so let's stick together and try to figure out what's going on.
It did not take long for the group to come across a series of remains in an open area.
What formerly was a suit of armor was strewn across the water, seemingly crushed and torn to shreds.
An intricate scythe was discarded nearby, leaving no doubt that this is where Vert, the Horseman of Death met its demise.
What in the world happened here...?
S-sorry, the armour was destroyed so badly I couldn't distinguish it from the other wreckages in my previous recon report.
We have one fewer giant mecha-knight to go up against. Isn't that a good thing?
No... Quite the opposite, actually.
The whole point is that we're trying to defeat the Horsemen in a certain order.
Scylla, are you able to analyse the traces left behind to track who's responsible for this?
Certainly. The most conspicuous damage comes from Siren shells, and these lacerations came from a massive slashing weapon.
Neither Pawns nor conventional mass-produced ships are able to cause this kind of damage, so that most likely narrows things down to two of the remaining Horsemen.
Given what we know about the armaments of the other Horsemen, War most closely fits the bill.
For machines that do not know the concept of "Death," this space seems like a particularly unforgiving place to fight.
Actually, you forgot another group that could've inflicted damage like this – the METAs.
I did consider that possibility, but the beacon tracker hasn't picked up anything as of yet.
(That's assuming all the META ships play by the same rules... Not a bet I'm willing to hedge. Though, things would admittedly be much simpler if the META aren't involved.)
What led you to bring up META all of a sudden, Implacable?

Hmm... I'm not sure if you've heard the news yet, but not too long ago, we detected an unidentified META signal after a break-in at one of our repositories, where a number of cultural relics were stolen.
Not a Siren? There's a META out there currently targeting the Royal Navy?
That certainly is a reason for concern. Thank you for sharing that bit of information with me.
You're welcome. But, the problem still remains that Death has already been defeated.
It's clear that we're no match for the Horseman of Famine we ran into earlier, so we should continue to steer clear of it for now.
I'm actually more curious about the status of the other Horsemen now. We didn't pick up on either War or Conquest during the previous recon.
We've been fortunate that we only have to deal with the War's Pawns and mass-produced ships, but...
If the Horseman of War truly is the strongest of the Four, it probably still is out there somewhere.
As long as we can confirm the existence of the other two Horsemen, we technically will still be able to maintain the correct order.
If we have to scour the entire Mirror Sea, wouldn't it be more efficient to split up our forces?
My forces will go search for War. Do you think you can take Famine and Conquest?
Are you sure? War should be the toughest of the remaining Horsemen.
The strength of the Horseman of Conquest is still an unknown, so we both will have to bear some degree of risk.
Very well then. Everyone, spread out, and avoid unnecessary combat. Remember, your priority is just to confirm the existence of the remaining Horsemen!

sequence: Mirror Sea - Famine's Territory
Joint Basilica Investigation Team
- Data Corruption//- Fatal Error Detected//

scripts.say: After splitting up, Argus and Royal Oak were tasked with locating the Horseman of Famine.
"Even a hundred eyes are not sufficient to locate my mark." ...Yeah, our target isn't in this area either.
Hmm... Wait, are those fresh wreckages over there?
Let's see if there are any more clues of recent battles nearby. It might lead us to our target.
Ahh... Carriers sure are amazing, being able to search wide areas so easily. I wish I could be that useful...
Even though I'm a senior knight... I can't contribute anything at all with my naked eyes...
Don't say that, Royal Oak! I can't deal with enemies charging straight at us the way you can. We all have our strengths and weaknesses!
But, uh... Here, why don't you use these binoculars? You'll at least be able to see farther this way.
...Binoculars?
"Naval Holiday-themed commemorative binoculars from Viscker Industries, lens and frame only, excellent magnification at medium range, makes for a perfect collectible!"
Or, so it says on the package.
...Why do you even have that?
I originally bought it to repay Hermes for this hat she got me.
But I got sent off to this operation and won't get to see her for a while, so why don't you go ahead and see if it works fine?
Um, alright then. If you don't mind, I...
I still can't see as far as you, even with binoculars.
Yeah, but it's still better than nothing, right?
Guess so!
BEEP––––
This is Béarn, light carrier of Iris Libre. My Royal Navy friends, do you copy?
Lady Richelieu has just located the Horseman of War.
It took quite some time to fight through the large number of mass-produced enemies, but we are now attempting to approach the Horseman.
We will also try to assess the combat power of its escort fleet. Over.
Béarn's already found the target, so we better get a move on it.
Oh wait, there it is right there! Royal Oak, I found my target as well!
Hold on, Famine is currently in combat with War mass-produced ships! Also, Famine seems to have sustained serious damage!
It's already been damaged? So, the Horsemen really are fighting amongst themselves...
According to Lady Implacable, the Horseman of Famine should be defeated next, right? If the mass-produced ships manage to take it down...
Then we won't have to fight at all, right?
This is Implacable. Everyone, can you hear me?
We've made some significant findings while searching for the Horseman of Conquest.
I'll skip straight to the takeaway first – Conquest is still fine, but a strange situation has developed here.
Hero and I are currently waiting outside the perimeter of Conquest's control area, so please regroup with us as soon as you complete your recon assignments.
Understood.
We've confirmed the condition of Famine. It is currently in combat with mass-produced ships, and has already sustained some damage.
In any case, we'll be there shortly, Lady Implacable.
My team is currently being pursued by enemies, so there might be a bit of a delay on our end.
Do you need help?
Not particularly. War hasn't made any moves as of yet, but the sheer number of mass-produced ships are slowing us down even if they're not a major threat.
In that case, I'll be waiting for you at the designated spot.

sequence: Vicinity of Kerguelen Islands - Early Dawn
Royal Navy Antarctic Fleet
Basilica Investigation Primary Team

scripts.say: *knock knock*
Pardon for disrupting you this late, Lady Implacable, but there is an urgent message from the islands' patrol fleet.
Mmh... Mrgh... A message? At this hour?
Alright, give me a minute or two to wake up.
Some time later...
Okay, I'm ready, Scylla.
So, what's this about an urgent message?
You said it's from our patrol fleet, not Argus or Royal Oak?
Correct. The fleet is reporting unusual sightings around the Basilica island.
Apparently, all contact with the island was suddenly lost last night. Everyone in the area promptly evacuated to relay this information.
All contact was lost, just like that? I fear for the worst... Show me the timeline.
2100 hours, patrol fleet attempts scheduled contact with Argus...
It was discovered the signal was being jammed. Recon aircraft were sent out, but vanished without a trace...
2135, received an SOS signal from the Basilica island...
2145, patrol fleet is attacked by an unidentified enemy approaching from the Basilica island's direction. Patrol fleet immediately retreats...
Yes. Following emergency protocols, they contacted us as soon as they could.
The message prior to this arrived on time and reported nothing unusual. It was only after that that the unusual activity began.
In other words, something happened in the span of those few hours.
Since you got the news first, what action have you taken?
I have attempted to radio the advance team, but failed due to the jamming.
I'm sorry that I failed to anticipate any of this, Lady Implacable.
Don't be. Her Majesty warned us to expect the unexpected with that Basilica.
It was practically a given that something would go awry during this investigation.
What shall we do now? Begin a rescue mission?
Of course. They require our assistance.
Understood. I shall contact the patrol fleet and let them know.
One moment, Scylla. I'd like to ask you something.
Who do you think is behind this?
We'll learn soon enough, but I want to hear your guess.
What exactly do you want me to guess, Lady Implacable?
Who our enemy is.
That's... quite the loaded question.
Among the Sirens, the META, and the factions we're not exactly on great terms with, there are many potential suspects.
Let's start with Vichya. Do you think they're trying to take the Basilica back?
That seems rather improbable.
We have the Templar Knights under strict surveillance. If they were involved, we would already know.
It would be next to impossible for them to amass an attack force completely unbeknownst to Her Majesty.
Furthermore, Vichya's high command withdrew the fleet they had here. Why would they abandon the islands in the first place if they want to recapture them?
Makes sense. What about Iron Blood?
Without a doubt, Iron Blood is salivating over the prospect of getting their hands on the technological relics lying inside the Basilica.
The question is, would they seek to destroy the relics before they can fall into anyone else's hands?
I also find that to be highly improbable.
Ever since their rebellion at Scapa Flow, Iron Blood has been kept under close supervision by the Naval HQ.
They need allies now more than ever, which may be why they've shown more cordiality and willingness to cooperate, both with Her Majesty and with the Commander.
Since Bismarck took over, they have not shown any signs of aggression.
And, given their uncertain circumstances, I cannot fathom any reason they would have to change that.
Even if they were aiming to pull the wool over the Naval HQ's eyes again, I doubt they would fall for the same trick twice.
Next, there's the Sakura Empire as well, but let's be realistic.
Right. They're on the other side of the world.
By process of elimination, it seems highly likely that either the Sirens or a hostile META group are behind this.
If it is the Sirens, taking care of them should prove simple enough.
I'd also like to add that betrayal from one of our allies is nigh impossible. If Iris Libre wanted the Basilica, a diplomatic approach would be their only option.
As for the Eagle Union, they'd be first to know if we got our hands on something valuable. Even assuming they were interested in attacking us, a wait-and-see approach would've been more sound.
Well summarised. Finally, what of the Sardegna Empire?
Are you testing me, Lady Implacable?
Heehee, so you've noticed? I can tell you've done your homework thoroughly.
Hardly. As your adjutant for this operation, I am simply doing what would normally be expected of me.
Hopefully my answers have satisfied you.
More than satisfied.
In fact, I'm now confident I have the most capable Royal Maid aiding me on this mission.
Please don't take this the wrong way – this is the first time the two of us are working together on a potentially dangerous mission, so it's only natural to feel each other out a bit first, yes?
Of course, Lady Implacable.
Speaking of Sardegna, I assume you're already aware that a number of exhibition items were stolen from both the World Expo site as well as our own repositories.
Yes, and the culprits behind the incidents were tracked back to separate groups – Sirens in the case of the World Expo, and an unknown META in our own case.
Indeed. We were warned of potentially hostile META factions, and this may be evidence of just that.
Should I contact the Eagle Union and request backup, just in case?
No need. Her Majesty doesn't want to draw too much attention to this investigation.
It's why our team is small to begin with, and why the patrol fleets are under instructions to avoid direct engagements.
Besides, even if we're dealing with a META group, we should be able to hold our ground without the Eagle Union.
We won't call for outside help unless absolutely necessary.
In any case, Hero will be here soon. You go on ahead, and I'll report the situation to Her Majesty first.
As you say. I'll see you soon, Lady Implacable.
Mhm. Let's ensure this mission is a success.
Mirror Sea - Inverted Basilica Blanc
The entrance to the facility was wide open, exposing the passageway leading to the central area. No enemies were in sight, seemingly leaving the facility unprotected...
But Implacable and Hero found a completely different obstacle in front of them.
Hiii-yah!
Hero slammed her fist into the wall of light, causing its holographic surface to ripple but not fracture.
Huh. Weird. Implacable, can I shoot it real quick?
Go ahead. Just steer clear of the blast radius.
KABOOOM!
What the hell?! It bounced off!
How is it so sturdy?! It's made of light! I can see right through it!
How annoying... Maybe it's similar to those Siren blockade devices.
If so, we'll need to destroy the power generator before we can proceed.
I believe passing through the Skybound Wall requires you to... Hero, what are you doing?
Unfazed, Hero leaned against the wall of light once more.
I've got an idea!
You basically said concepts can influence this Mirror Sea, yeah?
So, what if we simply believe in the idea that the wall will let us through?
Hmm... It's worth trying, at least.
Exactly. Drawing a key symbol on it should do the trick!
Watch this! I'm gonna perform a miracle!
Opeeen Sesame!
The wall of light continued to glow impassively despite Hero's efforts.
...No dice. Stupid bloody wall!
I think you've got the right idea, but not the right approach.
Let me give it a try.
Implacable put her hands together, cleared her mind, and began praying softly.
"My Lord, I know thy works and thy strength..."
"I hast kept my word, and hast not denied thy name..."
"Please, open before me a door that no man can shut."
However, her prayer fell on deaf ears. The wall remained impassable.
Well, that did a whole lot of nothing.
Perhaps "open a door" is too specific...
Oh well. We're not in a rush. There are plenty of other things we could try.
Lady Implacable? What are you doing?
Trying to find a way through this wall. As you can see, it's blocking our path.
Both shooting at it and praying did nothing! I dunno what else to do!
You... prayed to the wall?
Ahem. Let's not dwell on that.
What matters is, we need to figure out a way through. Does anyone have any ideas?
I may have one. Instead of trying to break through that wall, can't we try breaking through the stone instead?
It's quite a blunt solution, but it should be more straightforward than going through the wall of light.
Someone already tried, it seems. Look.
Implacable gestured towards a massive hole in the facility's stone exterior.
Though the hole reached deep, one could see the same glow as the wall of light leaking through at its very end.
Looking closer, it became evident that the wall of light was filling in the huge gap made into the facility.
Look at the size of this hole... Did one of the Horsemen do this?
Who knows. Maybe it was trying to find a way through, just like us.
I suspect this wall is the reason Conquest is still alive and well.
If even a Horseman couldn't get through, there's no way my cannons will... Wait, I know!
You're thinking about dropping bombs on it, aren't you? I already tried.
While the facility's roof appears unprotected by the wall, aircraft lose all control when flying straight over it, for some strange reason.
Figuring that out cost me a few planes.
Whoever built this wall, be it Conquest or somebody else, they clearly did not want anyone breaching it.
Then I suppose our only option is to locate and destroy its power source.
A good idea, if only we knew where to look.
For all we know, the power source could be on the other side of the wall.
But then it's impossible to reach... We cannot defeat Conquest.
Mhm. That would mean we're stuck in this place forever, unable to defeat the last Horseman.
But, I think I have an inkling. The Orthodoxy built this place, so let us ask the Cardinal for ideas.
Scylla, prepare some refreshments. We'll take a minute to relax before she arrives.
Mirror Sea - Conquest's Territory
A cup of tea for you, Lady Implacable. I also made sandwiches, if you'd like one.
Thanks. Also, didn't I tell you I wanted to make the tea myself?
Making tea is the duty of a Royal Maid. You'll have to forgive me for denying your request.
You're so mean. I came up with a new brewing method, but you won't even give it a chance.
Do you deny me at every corner out of spite, or what?
Spite? Perish the thought. I only do it because you have an unfortunate habit of making tea that is, mildly put, unsavoury.
*yaaawn*... My kingdom for a bed... What's taking Richelieu so bloody long?
Do you think she might have encountered a Horseman?
Doubtful. This is the Cardinal we're talking about. She's probably just inspecting buildings along the way.
We've no reason to worry. Let's just relax and be patient.
Hello again, ladies. Apologies for being so late.
Are you alright? No brushes with death?
Fortunately not. My trip went quite well.
I broke off from a pursuing mass-produced fleet, then went to look for clues that may lead us to an exit.
Sadly, I did not find any.
What about you? How is the situation?
Not great, since this wall of light stands in our way. At the moment, we're having teatime.
Wall of light...? That's a Skybound Wall! I'm sure of it!
Did you activate it? What happened?
No. It was already up when we got here.
(It's also strikingly similar to a Siren blockade device. Are they one and the same, perhaps?)
Without a doubt, this is a refined version of the Skybound Wall we saw at the Vichya-held Basilica previously.
So, does this mean that the Orthodoxy was already studying this technology? Was it developed in an attempt to control the Horsemen?
That doesn't add up. Someone must've improved the technology recently... But who was responsible for capturing this Horseman? Vichya, or the Tribunal?
Actually, neither option seems likely. Why would Vichya ignore the situation on the surface level and make the situation down here even more difficult?
Assuming the Skybound Wall is actually capable of holding in a Horseman for good, we must then ask: why did only one Wall get built instead of just containing all four?
Either imprisoning them this way was too difficult, or whoever imprisoned this one didn't want to do the same to the rest.
This may be just like the situation on the surface. While there was a way of containing the problem, it was deemed too difficult to sustain, and later abandoned.
The one possibility we cannot ignore is that this is actually a trap laid for us by the Sirens.
You're right. Maybe its purpose isn't to keep a Horseman confined, but rather us.
The only reason anyone would have to enter this Mirror Sea is to eliminate the Four Horsemen.
And what better way to do that than luring all our forces into one inescapable area using an immobilised Horseman as bait?
All theorising aside... Do you know how to dispel the Skybound Wall, Cardinal?
Destroying its power generator would be the simplest way.
However, considering the apparent laws of this Mirror Sea, another solution may be to conceptualize the wall away.
I already tried praying for the door to open, and that didn't work.
But, maybe something like this will–
"And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven..."
"And I saw the seven angels which stood before God..."
NO! STOP AT ONCE!
Ow! You don't need to shout!
I'm just trying to stop you from doing something stupid. Remember what happened the last time you tried to recite the second seal?
If your faith is not strong enough, invoking the concepts within this Mirror Sea is extremely dangerous!
Why? Because I would lose myself to them?
That is my theory, and I don't want to see it proven. Allow me to try instead.
Very well. Show us how it's done.
Implacable took a step back and silently observed the Cardinal, whose faith far better represented the concepts of the Iris Orthodoxy.
Facing the wall, Richelieu put her hands together and began reciting a prayer.
"My Lord, I know thy works and thy strength..."
"I hast kept my word, and hast not denied thy name..."
"Please, open before me a door that no man can shut."
The Skybound Wall shimmered and then dissolved, revealing a path to the other side.
The girls walked forward into the passage, encountering several more layers of Skybound Walls which Richelieu dispelled in identical fashion.
Impressive work, Cardinal. My faith pales in comparison to yours.
Because this IS a matter of faith, and not your technology being biased towards you, right?
The Skybound Wall, like the other Sacraments of the Basilica, originated from the Iris Orthodoxy's beliefs.
It may simply be a case of me being more familiar with the root origin of the Wall than you are.
I'll just have to take your word for it.
Hey, Implacable, there's a bunch of inactive mass-produced ships in this area.
Presumably products of the Mirror Sea. I'd imagine them being offline is the reason we're not seeing fog already.
Let's ignore them, since they're not doing anything.
And pass up on all that free EXP? Come on, let me at 'em!
Don't be daft. Until we understand how this place works, I don't want you accidentally waking up the Horseman.
If it's exercise you want, scout ahead and give us a sitrep on the Horseman's status.
But whatever you do, don't touch it. And don't shoot at it either.
Laaaame. But fine, I'll try to behave myself.
Hey, Implacable! Pretty sure I've found Conquest!
It's big, it's white, and it's kind of just sitting there behind the wall of light.
The rest of the team caught up with Hero and arrived in the hall where the Horseman of Conquest was imprisoned.
Looks unresponsive, like the mass-produced ships and Pawns we saw on the way.
I'd hate to fight that giant in this cramped place.
That's not all! I found something else besides the Horseman!
Lookie here!
Hero trotted up to one of the giant columns supporting the structure's ceiling.
Behind it, there was a human-sized cage encased in a Skybound Wall.
One could make out the features of a shipgirl trapped inside it.
Who is that? Judging by the horrific state of her rigging, she can't be one of ours...
Do you recognise her, Hero?
Can't exactly see her face. My guess is she's an Orthodoxy girl.
Is that... La Galissonnière? What is a member of the Tribunal doing here?!
I'll create an opening. Let's get her out of there!
*yaaawn*... Boy, I've not slept that long in ages.
Morning. Or... good evening? What time even is it?
Hello. You're not from this world – or should I say, branch – are you?
Nope, but it's a pleasure to meet you, Cardinal-from-another-branch. I'm La Galissonnière of the Ashes~
You're with the Ashes?!
Seems our beacon tracker was useless... So, some of you do have a way of evading our detection.
Hey, I remember you. Implacable, Royal Navy aircraft carrier, right?
You're a long way from home. Whatcha doing here?
Catching the thief who stole from one of our repositories, it seems.
Whoa, excuse me? You accusing me of something as lame as stealing? I've got way better stuff to do.
...Okay then. Why are you here?
To bust up a Siren test site, duh.
You've also seen the experiments the Sirens have been conducting here, haven't you? If this place continues to run, things will get real ugly for your branch, real quick.

Once I got down here, I could tell that the Sirens were exploiting the concepts of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse to develop self-reinforcing superweapons. As long as those factories keep churning out Pawns, the Horsemen will keep getting stronger ad infinitum.
On the bright side, stopping the experiment is also simple – all you need to do is shut down the factory, and "seal" the Horsemen in reverse order.
They've got two serious weaknesses. One, their reliance on concepts, and two, that they'll go at each other's throats like Pawns if given the chance.
So, I came up with a plan to take advantage of both of these things.
First, I turned off the stabilization device, letting all four Horsemen loose so they could start going at one another.
I set up Famine to take its army and go up against Death, and after Death had been damaged enough, I went in and dealt the finishing blow.
I'm makin' it sound easy, but I shouldn't have to tell you that you don't kill a Horseman of the Apocalypse in one afternoon.
Anyway, I ran back the same playbook and got War to attack Famine next.
But, that didn't work as planned. Famine's survival instincts seemed to be too strong, and so it kept running away every time the situation was unfavorable.
So, I thought about trying to use Conquest to take out both of them at once, but as for how that turned out... you saw that for yourself.
And as for how I got into this Mirror Sea in the first place? All I'll say is, it's one of the perks that comes with joining the Ashes.
In other words, you were thoroughly defeated and have been trapped here ever since, waiting for someone to rescue you?
...Look, I just felt like getting in on the action, alright? I attacked the darn thing, and, uh... kind of walked into a trap.
...Are you really a member of the Ashes? You're nothing like what I've heard about the others.
What, not gloomy enough for you? I'm just new.
Oh. That explains a few things.
Still, can't you Ashes go toe-to-toe with the Horsemen? Your convoluted plan seems unnecessary.
Look, this is still some dangerous Antiochus tech we're dealing with here. Besides, why fight if I can just outsmart 'em?
"Outsmart?" Seems the joke was on you.
Hm? Did you say something?
Sorry, I was just thinking out loud.
You said you're here to destroy a Siren test site. I do find that interesting.
I was under the impression the Ashes had much bigger fish to fry.
Don't tell me... you got sent here to do grunt work because you're the newest of the bunch?
Grunt work, huh? You don't know anything about us Ashes.
We've been fighting Antiochus way, way longer than any of you.
"But you ran into a trap!" Yeah, so what? Waste your breath on somebody else!
No need to get worked up. Our goal of fighting the Sirens is the same.
You still want the test site gone, no? I don't see why we can't work towards that together.
Think of it as repaying us for rescuing you.
You wanna team up? Fine by me.
But I'm not repaying you for anything. Even if you hadn't come along, someone else would've let me out sooner or later.
While I prefer to work alone, I'll make an exception this time since you technically did give me a hand.
In exchange, your lips are sealed about my little slip-up. Got it?

sequence: Mirror Sea - Famine's Territory
Joint Basilica Investigation Team
- Data Corruption//- Fatal Error Detected//

scripts.say: This makes it the third Ashes member we've made contact with. What do you think about her, Scylla?
She sounds simple and straightforward, and it's great that our goals align. However...
Yes? Go on.
She also talks too much. While we did rescue her, she's under no obligation to tell us anything.
I can't put my finger on why, but it makes me uncomfortable.
Mull it over a bit more. You're not the only one who thinks the same way.
I can't find any faults with her so far, but something still feels amiss...
Is it because I'm naturally inclined to distrust the Ashes, or is it something more tangible...?
At any rate, keep a close eye on her.
As you wish, Lady Implacable.
Yo, I found the Horseman of Famine.
Looks like it's about... 40 or 50% busted?
Honestly pretty surprising though, considering it fought like a million mass-produced ships and still came out on top.
So, what's the plan? It's limping – now's a good time to strike.
Then strike we will. Let's not waste this opportunity.
I will accompany the vanguard. Implacable, can you watch over Béarn in the meantime?
Of course. Royal Oak, you'll take point and direct the artillery fire. Assist Richelieu and La Galissonnière in a frontal attack on Famine.
Argus, Béarn, and I will provide aerial support.
Very well. I suggest launching your attacks from the opposite direction.
Y-yes, Implacable! I swear I will not disappoint you!
Come now, ladies! Let us put an end to this wretched harbinger!
KABOOOM!
Our cannons cannot penetrate it, even at this close range?
This time, surely...!
KABOOOM!
Did that thing just dodge her shot? So much for being halfway dead!
It would seem our enemy's combat ability rivals that of even elite Sirens.
I can see now why La Galissonnière opted not to fight it head-on.
This can't be happening...
Even with Implacable, Richelieu, and support from the Ashes, we still can't defeat an injured Horseman...?
Small correction – our Ashes ally isn't doing much of anything.
La Galissonnière, what are you doing? Didn't you say you'd help us?
I AM helping. Can't you tell I'm praying?
Excuse me? Don't tell me you're praying for it to give up.
Give up? No, more like blow up! Literally!
"O, benevolent Iris, whose holy words I heed, whose divine will I carry out..."
"Take my enemy as your own, feel my fury as your own..."
"Grant me strength! Give me the power to cleanse this evil from your world!"
La Galissonnière's echoing prayer swept like a rejuvenating wind across the battlefield, instantly dispersing the noxious energy that infested it.
At the same time, the black Horseman staggered as the tide of battle began turning in the shipgirls' favor.
What in the world...? The Horseman is weakening?
Yeah! Now hit it with all you've got!
Let's see how tough you really are, skinny boy! Ahahaha!
A thunderous explosion struck the colossal Horseman, breaking it apart like a stone golem, never to reanimate again.
Hell yeah! Suck on that! Whaddya think of me now, huh?
Clearly, I misjudged you. You live up to the name of the Ashes.
Thank god you're on our side.
This alliance is only temporary. Keep the praise coming, though!
I must ask... What did you do back there?
What do you think? I offered a prayer, and it was answered.
That's how this test site works. No reason not to exploit it.
Meaning, you manifested a concept?
Bingo. Well, kind of. You can't just make any concept real – it's got to do with faith.
Other stuff from the Orthodoxy's religious texts applies as well, since it's where the Four Horsemen come from.
That much, I already know. It's the reason War and Conquest became stronger than Death and Famine.
Mhm. Did you try prayin' for yourself?
Yes. I recited a verse from the Scriptures, and something started happening to me... Luckily, Richelieu stopped me before I could finish.
Are these concepts really that dangerous?
No shit they are! Embracing the Horsemen's concepts is like inviting the Mirror Sea inside your head.
Use your brain before you pray. Don't go around offering words of power to a harbinger of doom.
Speaking of which, you'll want to figure out how to manifest your faith sooner rather than later.
What do you mean?
My own prayers can only have a very limited effect on you. You need to play by the Mirror Sea's rules as well, or the Horseman of War will blast you off the face of the earth.
Is it truly THAT powerful?
I'm not kidding here. Since the very concept of war empowers it, you're gonna make it stronger when you go to battle with it.
You CAN overcome those gains, but your conviction needs to be strong enough.
If you want a safe bet, pray to the Iris. That's how you got through those walls, right?
Implacable... I think you should take her advice and sincerely pray, if only for practical purposes.
If that's what it takes to defeat the Sirens, sure. Can I do it right here?
No. Praying is a sacred act. You are my ally, and I will not condone you treating the Holy Iris without respect.
I suppose it must be done in a reasonably dignified location, huh.
First, we'll need to find a place matching that description. Shall we?
After looking around the Mirror Sea, the girls managed to find an Orthodoxy church preserved by a conceptual anchor.
This is like a vault of Orthodoxy Sacraments... It's definitely seen better days, but I suppose beggars can't be choosers.
Well, Cardinal, could you give me an example of a prayer?
Of course. Please listen closely.
Richelieu got down on her knees, put her hands together, and began reciting a holy prayer.
"Hallowed Iris in Heaven, blessed is your holy name."
"Give us the courage to stride upon the blue seas as we would in the clouds before you."
"Give us your Sacrament so that our lives may be filled with purpose."
"Forgive our sins, so that we may forgive others."
"Protect us from tribulations, and ward us from evil."
"All authority, all glory, all of Heaven and Earth belong to you."
Hearing her prayer, beads of golden light emerged from thin air and converged upon her Orthodoxy flag, one light at a time.
Once she had finished praying, her flag shone like glorious sunlight through stained glass.
Simply laying eyes upon it inspired courage and empowered the spirit of all those who followed the Iris.
Incredible, Cardinal.
Even I could feel how powerful that prayer was.
No doubt about it. You'll easily be able to fight the Horseman of War face to face.
Whew... Okay, Implacable. It's your turn.
As La Galissonnière said, the Iris is safe to pray to. I did not sense the influence of any Horseman in my heart.
Good to know. I'll give it a shot as well.
"Hallowed Iris in Heaven, blessed is your holy name."
"Give us the courage to stride upon the blue seas as we would in the clouds before you."
"Give us your Sacrament so that our lives may be filled with purpose."
"Forgive our sins, so that we may forgive others."
"Protect us from tribulations, and ward us from evil."
"All authority, all glory, all of Heaven and Earth belong to you."
Unlike Richelieu's prayer, Implacable's produced no lights, and her surroundings continued to remain dark.
...Huh?
Looks like God doesn't feel like answering your prayers.
Hah... Why am I not surprised... Just like at the Skybound Wall...
Guess I'm not as devout and pure-of-heart as the Cardinal after all~♪
What happened at the Skybound Wall?
I recited the same prayer as Richelieu, but only her words had any effect.
I see, it makes sense now.
Though this is a Siren Mirror Sea, it was shaped and sculpted into a Basilica of the Iris Orthodoxy.
Everything here, from the concept of Judgment to the Four Horsemen, are built from the Orthodoxy's cognitive system.
Naturally, the concept of faith is an inseparable part of all this.
And there is no way for me to invoke the concept of a faith I do not hold.
It's never too late for me to share the Iris's teachings with you–
I appreciate the sentiment, Cardinal, but I'll have to pass.
But, I just had an idea. If "faith" is the concept that governs this space, it should not matter if we have faith in the same thing, right?
In theory, yes. However, you just experienced for yourself how dangerous it can be to invoke the concepts of the Four Horsemen.
Who said anything about praying to one of those Siren constructs? If there's anything you should know about the Royal Navy, it's that we have an unshakable faith in one person.
With a wry smile, Implacable took out a small carving in Queen Elizabeth's likeness and clasped it in her hands.
That's... a figure of Queen Elizabeth? What are you trying to do?
Do you think the Sirens can distinguish between the faith of the Iris Orthodoxy and the faith of the Royal Navy?
Who knows, maybe someone else might hear my prayers?
I'm not expecting much, but... can't hurt to give it a shot.
Heehee~♪ Now then, to the one I trust in most...
"To the hallowed name who smiles upon our land like the sun,"
"Protector of our safe haven, beacon of our glory."
"May the light of your wisdom protect us across the seven seas."
"May the authority of your blade reveal the truth in this chaotic world."
"May you grant us the power to overcome hardship and endure trials, to purge evil and bring peace."
"Grant us your enlightenment, so that we may open the way in your name."
"To you I pray, Your Majesty, Queen Elizabeth!"
This time, her prayer was heard and answered.
From the carving clutched between her hands, golden lights emerged, ascending to the church ceiling.
The specks of warmth clumped together into one big ball before bursting, showering the girls with star-like fragments of hope.
...Thank you, Your Majesty.
Is this... Her Majesty's grace?
I feel so warm. Relaxed. Like being back home...
Whatever the hell this is, it feels like I just received a major buff. I'm gonna walk all over that War loser~☆
I'll be damned... It actually worked.
Whether you follow the Iris or Her Majesty doesn't matter. What's important is that you believe in it.
...It seems you had it in you after all, Implacable. You do have strong faith, just not in the Iris.
Mhm. At any rate, I should be ready now.
There are still two Horsemen left. Even with this newfound strength, we must stay on top of our game.
And who knows how long these prayers will last. Let's get going at once, Cardinal.
I've found where War is! You all ready?
Ready as can be. Our prayers are still in effect, too.
We'll need them, for sure. War has a massive escort of mass-produced ships.
What did you expect? The bigger the army, the more war you can wage!
On the bright side, War itself is a real tough bastard!
Now how is that supposed to be a good thing?
Huh? Don't you get a rush of excitement just thinking about going head-to-head with a powerful enemy?
Ah, yes, because putting myself in mortal danger is exactly my idea of excitement.
Implacable, War is coming towards us.
It's raring to go, hmm? How befitting its namesake.
Looks like there's no signs of damage on it either. This won't be an easy fight.
What's wrong? Isn't your queen watching over you? I'm sure she won't let you lose more than a limb or two at worst.
Thanks for the "encouragement."
If you don't start pulling your weight, maybe you'll lose a limb or two as well.
Listen, I said I'd fight by your side, not that I'd adapt to your tactics.
As I said, I'm not gonna charge up there head-first, as that's not my style.
You guys can run up there and butt heads all you want, but I'm gonna look for weaknesses to exploit.
Sounds good? Alright. Have fun now, shipgirls of this "branch"~
Cheeky little... Why is she like this?
Calm down, Implacable. She doesn't trust us to not use her as cannon fodder, which is sensible.
We don't have much of a choice anyway, so let's at least give her the best conditions to succeed.
Ugh... Everyone, attack it head-on!
Her Majesty's graces are with us! Show that Horseman our might!
What?! It's repairing itself using armour plates torn off from its mass-produced ships!
Expending as many troops as necessary to win... Fitting for an embodiment of war.
It's very bad news for us, however. We cannot hope to win a war of attrition.
Even if we do, we won't have any bloody ammo left to beat the last Horseman!
It doesn't matter! We need to defeat War before we can even start thinking about defeating Conquest!
No. In fact, now is the time we SHOULD be thinking about Conquest!
War as a concept is not a goal; it serves a higher purpose. That purpose is conquest.
As long as the Horseman of Conquest is incapacitated, nothing is currently expressing the concept of conquest in this area.
But what if I become a conduit for the concept of Conquest?
In other words, if I can successfully "conquer" these mass-produced vessels, I can diminish the concept of War.
What do you all think? I believe La Galissonnière had the same idea of using Conquest to weaken War.
...Uh, I wasn't thinking of anything philosophical; I was just gonna make them fight.
Your idea is certainly gutsy, I'll give you that. And, I don't see anything wrong with it at a glance, as long as you're fine with the risks.
I'm against it. Channeling one of the Mirror Sea's concepts is far too dangerous. I can't let you shoulder such a burden for the mistakes we made.
If it's our only choice, I shall be the one to do it rather than you.
Sorry, Cardinal, but I think your strong faith inhibits you. You can't truly become a vessel for Conquest. It has to be done by a nonbeliever like me.
Don't worry, I'll be fine. I have Her Majesty's protection.
If the worst thing happens and I start to lose control, just save me like you did the last time.
But...
Hero, give me your bow!
Implacable took the bow – the symbol of Conquest – and drew the string, training her sights on the Horseman of War.
"I watched as the Lamb opened the first of the seven seals, and there before me was a white horse."
"Its rider held a bow, and he was given a crown, and he rode out as a conqueror bent on conquest."
"With this bow, he would smite those who opposed him, until none were left!"
Royal Oak lodged her greatsword into the Horseman's armor.
After a series of deafening explosions, the crimson flames smoldering on the Horseman of War's armor petered out, and the giant crashed to the ground.
*pant*... *pant*... It's... It's finished!
An excellent display by the Royal Knight, of course. Her Majesty will be proud of you.
M-me? Not at all... I only put in the finishing touch. Your quick wit is what really saved the day.
C'mon, we all know my bow is the star of the show~ When I get home, I'm gonna frame it and hang it over the fireplace~
...Hang on, did it always look this dull? And what are these cracks in the wood? Those weren't there before!
Right before Hero's eyes, the cracks spread further and further through the sacred bow, finally reaching both ends of it.
Then, with a hollow snap, it broke into a dozen little pieces.
Noooo! My precious boooow!
Whyyyy?! It was my loot! I earned it!!
It's a shame, but there's no use crying over spilled milk. I'll ask Richelieu if she can give us another replica later.
Oh! Okay, sweet♪
With War defeated, now there's only Conquest left to vanquish to end this Siren experiment.
But Conquest will be strongest yet, now that we've "conquered" all the other Horsemen.
Not to mention, we're nearly out of energy and ammo... And there aren't any more concepts we can channel, are there?
Not necessarily... In the Scriptures, there are a total of seven seals, which means three more concepts should be–
Hold up, I'm gonna veto that! You're not pulling a stunt like that again!
Why not? Channeling Conquest worked fine, and we've seen no symbolism for the remaining three seals in the Mirror Sea.
Just because they haven't been manifested in the form of Horsemen does not mean that the concepts don't exist!
For all we know, the Mirror Sea itself could represent the last three seals.
You're aware of what those seals are, right? Do you have any idea what kind of calamity you could bring if you were to manifest those things?
If you don't want the world to end, you'd better get that idea out of your head!
...I'll admit, I didn't consider that.
So, if that's no longer an option, how do you propose we take down the last Horseman?
Well, the original plan was to have Conquest and War take each other out after softening them up enough, but that's no longer on the table.
*sigh*... I suppose we're in a real bind then.
Hmm? Does it even matter at this point?
Did you forget that the Horseman of Conquest is still asleep behind the Skybound Wall?
Well, sure, it's not an immediate threat to us at the moment...
But that doesn't improve our situation. While you can leave this place whenever you want, we can't unless we finish the job.
Riiight, I forgot! Lucky for you, there are a few ways to deal with an inactive Horseman.
One being, you can use the walls of light to cut it to ribbons if you position 'em right.
Now that I think about it, why didn't the Tribunal of your branch already come up with that idea?
...Let's see if your idea is feasible, shall we?
No answer, huh. Fine, to the lair of the sleeping giant we go!
Mirror Sea - Horseman of Conquest Confinement Area
After investigating the control room, I'm pleased to report that we can indeed take Conquest apart by manipulating the Skybound Walls.
Just as I suspected. Whaddya say, alt branch Cardinal? Wanna give it a shot?
(She was right. All along, the Tribunal had a way to eliminate this Horseman... So why didn't they do it?)
Richelieu glanced at the Skybound Wall controls and felt a tremble in her hand.
...Why would I have to do it?
Doesn't HAVE to be you, but you know the power that concepts and faith can have.
I mean, who knows what'll happen if you let Implacable touch an Orthodoxy Sacrament?
There's the practical angle, too. Iris Libre's leader "conquering" an Antiochus problem that's festered beneath its Basilicas for decades. See what I'm getting at?
I understand. I'll do it.
Richelieu took a moment to inspect the control panel.
Its design had changed somewhat since the days of the unified Orthodoxy, but that wouldn't impede her.
Following the procedures she remembered, she input a sequence of parameters, then hit finalize.
Will that do it?
Probably? Give it a minute to work.
The facility's machinery sprung into action with a roar, moving the Skybound Wall like a glowing sawblade.
It cleaved the Horseman apart, one piece at a time. Its head, chest, armor plating, even its steed. It made no attempt to fight back.
When the Skybound Walls were finished, the embodiment of Conquest was no more than a pile of assorted scrap metal.
It's over... Finally.

sequence: Basilica Island - Surrounding Waters
Joint Basilica Investigation Team
11:54 - Day 6 since start of investigation

scripts.say: Nnngh... The black... sun...
Good morning, Implacable. Did you have a nightmare?
I guess so... I still can't get the sight of the black sun over the Mirror Sea out of my head...
What even was that? Do you know, Cardinal?
Unfortunately not, but I have a possible explanation for it.
My instruments could not detect any heat coming from that sun. I would theorize that it serves as a portal between the surface and the catacombs.
As always, there's never a concrete answer...
At least we prevented an eventual crisis. All in a day's work.
Lady Implacable, our beacon tracker has lost La Galissonnière's signal.
Gone like a ghost. A fitting exit for someone from the Ashes.
Oh well. She doesn't owe us anything, and it's not like we can make her stay anyway.
Speaking of leaving, it's time we do the same. Take care of the Basilica Island, Cardinal.
Of course. I cannot thank you enough for helping us bring it back under our control.
Anything for a friend. If you ever need the Royal Navy again, give us a call.
I certainly will.
Until next time, I wish you the best.
The same to you. May the Iris watch over you.
Later, as the girls watched the Basilica Island vanish over the horizon...
We had a META right beside us for a long while, and the beacon tracker didn't record anything...
Yes, it's very strange. The Commander used one to track the Ashes before, and yet it completely failed to detect La Galissonnière.
Wouldn't surprise me if they upgraded their stealth tech. Either that, or the tracker's just bloody broken.
Nothing indicates that it wouldn't be working properly, but since we rarely run into the METAs, it's hard to actually verify that.
I'll make a note of this. This mission left me with a lot of questions I want answered.
Do you believe La Galissonnière was hiding something from us?
Very likely. Don't forget, there's still a META out there actively working against us in secret.
The entire Basilica system was designed with a higher authorisation level than sysadmin, preventing Argus from shutting down its emergency mode.
My question is, what might that authorisation be? What purpose does it serve, and who holds it?
I... don't have enough information to answer that.
Hah... With any luck, we won't have to wait long to find out.
In any case, I have a feeling this whole affair is far from over.

sequence: Basilica Island Lighthouse
Iris Libre Fleet
Midnight - Day 7 since start of investigation

scripts.say: The clock ticked over silently to the new day.
The Cardinal was asleep at her desk, exhausted after what had transpired.
...This scene again...?
...A black sun, descending into the world of Man.
That sound... Where is it coming from?
I... can't make any sense of it.
Who goes there? May I ask you to show yourself?
...Jean Bart?
Beware? Beware of what?!
█▆▎Come█▎█
Wait! Jean Bart, don't go!
Jean... Bart...
Just now... was I dreaming...?
That... was just a dream... right?
I knew that place was going to give me nightmares...
I suppose that proves my gut instincts right, then?
Nobody answered Implacable's rhetorical question, only a black sun roiling silently above her.
That being the case, let me take a closer look at you.
You spooked me twice back there on Kerguelen. Just who do you think you are?
Implacable turned her eyes towards the black sun, and made up her mind.
But just as she was about to step forward, she suddenly felt another presence behind her.
...Your Majesty?
What are you saying? I can't hear you...
If you can't hear anything, then there's still hope for you yet.
Ghosts and demons, step aside before your Queen!
KABOOM––!!
The whole area seemed to shudder violently with that explosion, and in the place of the enigmatic voice stood another person.
Implacable opened her eyes, and came face-to-face with the figure across from her.
What are you staring at us for?
Queen Elizabeth... META?!
What's with that stunned look on your face? Did you not call out to us?
Now that I take a closer look at you, you still haven't undergone METAmorphosis...
How, then, did you invoke our name? And, how did you manage to get yourself involved with THOSE things?
How interesting...
I... can't quite follow what you're saying...
Am I in a dream?
For you, perhaps.
Wake up. Go back. This place was never meant for you.
But, I still have so many questions–
That was an order, not a suggestion.
"Go back."
The real me should still be stationed at the floating fortress right now, which means...
I'm dreaming right now, and this is a scene from my dreams.
Nobody confirmed Ulrich's statement to herself, only a black sun roiling silently above her.
The black sun... is this some kind of religious symbol of sorts?
And why is it appearing in my dream?
Friedrich?!
What are you trying to say? I can't understand you at all...
Beware? Beware of what?
█▆▎Come█▎█
What? What did you just say?!
Wait! Don't leave without telling me what you just said!!

sequence: Vicinity of Kerguelen Islands
Royal Navy Antarctic Fleet
Basilica Investigation Primary Team

scripts.say: Yo, investigation team! Can you hear me?
Alright, let's try that again... Ahem! This is Hero, of the Royal Navy!
Investigation team! Argus! Royal Oak! Do you hear me?!
Whoa, it's not doing anything! Is this thing broken, or what?
We ensured that it was working properly before we left, Hero.
I presume it's not working due to the jamming in this ocean region.
Which would mean that we're inside the anomaly reported by the islands' patrol fleet.
Uh-huh?
Yet we haven't found any sign of Argus's SOS signal yet. I can't help but fear the worst...
It's not yet time to worry. Our Royal Knights wouldn't fold that easily.
(She may have low self-esteem, but she's no weakling. I'd bet she ran into some stroke of bad luck, like usual.)
(Either way, we can only hope for her safety now.)
Shall we disembark on the island right away?
We wouldn't want to fall victim to whatever befell them. First, we should ensure that the island's surroundings are safe.
I'll lead the way. Please be careful.
Vicinity of Kerguelen Islands
"May the Iris's blessings be upon you," huh...
Odd. There are no signs of either foe or fighting.
We have a general grasp of this island's layout, but it seems we won't find Argus and the others unless we go in.
For real? Dungeons are cool and all, but I don't wanna marathon four in a row.
I meeean, I could just blow those buildings up and make everyone run out screaming! Way more efficient.
Scylla, where should we disembark?
The lighthouse tower to the southwest should do. Royal Oak and Argus focused their investigation there, as well.
Very well. They did mention that they found the island's control centre there in their final report, after all.
Why would they place such an important infrastructure along the coast inside a lighthouse instead of at the heart of their facilities?
Could it be that the one on the coast is a ruse, while the real one is somewhere else?
Or... there might be more than meets the eye to the Basilica, and it might not be safe to locate it there?
A reasonable theory. We'll begin by searching the lighthouse where the team last reported from.
...Huh? C'mon, you're not gonna consider my idea?!
I have good ideas, too! How about you sidekicks stop ignoring the protagonist here, huh?!
Oh, the protagonist, you say? Naturally, that means you'll do the lion's share of the work, yes?
Yeah, exactly! So stop ignoring me!
Oh, I'm so very sorry. As an apology, I shall let you lead the way then.
Now you get it! You're about to see how a Hero does dungeon-crawling!
Unknown location
KABOOM–––!!
Sorry to keep you waiting. How's the situation?
I was a step too late. The "whale" got away, and it's only the small fry left now.
Unfortunate. Did you manage to retrieve anything else?
Yes, I have everything here. Want to take a look?
...I knew it. The "whale's" seemingly random movements do have a purpose after all.
Which makes me even more confused as to what they're trying to do. Can the Magister's plan still proceed in this state?
Or, did the Magister also account for all this?
Why are you asking me?
Well, you have a pretty good track record and whatnot...
Isn't there someone who'd be more suitable to answer that than me? For example, a certain "Miss D."
I've already tried. She won't tell us anything unless we catch the "whale."
I see. I'll leave you to it then.
Mmhmm.
But, let's head back first. Her Majesty is waiting for us.

sequence: "All beings in creation have both beginning and end."
"Ashes to ashes, dust to dust."
"But, I shall continue to live."
"For doing so is the only way to achieve my purpose."
"No matter how desperate the odds, it must be done."
"––The Truth must be found."
"For that pursuit, for that hunt, one must become as a beast."
"If this is a price you are willing to pay,"
"Then I may accept your allegiance."
"Otherwise... Hmm, let's see..."
"Yes, offer unto me your prayers."

scripts.say: SCHWING!
Hero's sword cleaved the control room door effortlessly, like a hot knife through butter.
Knock knock!☆
Implacable! I don't think they're here.
So they aren't... Everyone, search for clues.
Lady Implacable, I've found something.
What?! Nuh-uh, I should be the first!
Let us sidekick maids have our turn, please.
"To all ships in the Antarctic, Basilica Investigation Teams, and any other Royal Navy ships who receive this message!"
"This is the Basilica Investigation Forward Team! We are surrounded by unidentified hostiles!"
"Please send support immediately!"
"I repeat, this is the Basilica Investigation Forward Team—"
Is this... the SOS signal our patrol ships received?
There's no doubt it came from here. And it's still playing...
But, the two of us didn't receive anything until we stepped onto the island.
Either the jamming here is extremely potent, or the patrol ships were able to receive it just before it was jammed...
Hmm. I'm afraid I can't say.
Perhaps this is where our star, Hero, may shine.
We look forward to your performance, Hero.
I mean, it's kinda super obvious?
See how there's no dust on the control panel's levers and buttons, while there IS dust on the other devices?
Plus, you can tell someone pulled wicked hard on this lever. Ten to one, it's gotta be Argus!
Sooo, basically, Argus was trying really hard to deal with whatever was going down here!
That's why there aren't any signs of struggle outside. It all went down in here!
Well, how observant of you.
Geez, you grown-ups are so useless! You're lucky you have me around.
Yes, Hero, that was truly spectacular. I only found one clue, and honestly, it pales in comparison.
Here we have a list of notes left by Argus, a rough sketch of the facility, and a transcript of her communications with Royal Oak.
Why don't you take a look with your discerning eyes? Heehee!
B-but you're just a sidekick!
Yes, yes, that's enough. Let's focus on what happened here...
Failed motion sensors, cameras refusing to turn on...
Ran the self-diagnostic sequence, followed screen prompts to enable emergency controls...
...I'm starting to get a headache.
Lady Argus is earnest to a fault...
After that, the system went haywire. While Lady Royal Oak fought off hostiles, Lady Argus sent a distress signal by telegraph.
They then chose to meet at an area called Blanc.
The transcript ends there.
Blanc... The White Basilica?
(Would there be other areas named Rouge, Vert, and Noir, then?)
(There they are. Very... simple names. The Iris are devout, if nothing else.)
Oh, hey. We saw a white Basilica when we circled the island, didn't we?
It was pretty close. So that's our first dungeon to crawl!
We're fortunate that it was close. If they were on the opposite side, just getting there would be a feat.
If we're lucky, we may find them soon.
Shall we proceed? Lady Implacable, will we be traveling by land?
No. Let's deploy our rigging and go by sea.
(There's something odd about this Basilica. I can see why Her Majesty is hesitant to make a big deal out of this.)
(This is an isolated island off to the south, but the facility is too big to be a mere religious establishment. It's even bigger than the Royal Navy's Mediterranean fortress.)
(How did they manage to build all of this? And when, at that?)
(If the entire breadth of the Royal Navy's intelligence network couldn't inform Her Majesty of this Basilica... then this must involve Iris's highest echelons...)
If there's any silver lining to be found, it's that the anomaly doesn't seem to be having any effect on the outside beyond signal interference.
Argus, you've gotten yourself into something crazy, haven't you...
Basilica Blanc - Coastline
Well, well. This Basilica faces the ocean, but they weren't considerate enough to put an entrance here?
Does this mean we'll have to go to the centre of the island by land, enter, and then double back all this way?
I'm afraid so. Perhaps that's intentional.
Allow me to come with you, Lady Implacable and Hero.
Unfortunately, I'm in no mood to climb mountains. Star actor, you're up.
See?! I told you this is the best way to do things!
Hmm... Okay, that's enough inspection. Three, two, one... Open sesame!
BOOOOOOOM!
Cannonfire from Hero's rigging blew a giant hole into the outer wall.
This is so much better than taking a detour. Hahaha!
Basilica Blanc - Indoors
The investigation team forged through the massive halls of the facility.
This place is ludicrously big. It's not so much a series of rooms, but rather a series of halls.
They don't seem designed for foot traffic, either. More like for the transport of giant weapons...
Scylla, where are we on the map right now?
We are currently between the Basilica's fourth and fifth armouries.
Multiple armouries, you say? I'm starting to think this place was an Orthodoxy military base.
We're approaching a fork in the road. The top corridor leads to what the map calls a prayer room, while the bottom one leads to a factory and a Sacrament exhibit.
There also appears to be a path which leads further down to the Basilica's centre.
If one were to ambush Lady Royal Oak and Lady Argus, I believe that would be the ideal location.
I know we need to hurry, but I think we should stop by that Sacrament exhibit.
May I ask why, Lady Implacable? Do you want their Sacraments for yourself?
Don't be absurd. Do I look like an artifact hoarder to you?
We're not going to steal Orthodoxy property. We'll recover what's been left behind and hand them over to Richelieu after our investigation.
Even if there are no artifacts left, the exhibits themselves may clue us in on the true purpose of this facility.
You'd assume there's no connection between religious artifacts and the military... but perhaps that preconception is wrong.
Basilica Blanc - Sacrament Exhibit
Have no fear, for Hero's here!
Come on out, you mooks! I'm gonna farm you for drops!
It appears there are unfortunately no mooks to farm in here, Hero.
However, I would gladly serve as a boss encounter. That is, if you're ready to suffer a humiliating defeat at the hands of a maid. Heehee♥
W-wooow! Those are fighting words, you cheeky sidekick!
You'll pay for your lip by running a hundred fetch quests after I've mopped the floor with you!
Fetch quests as punishment, you say? Fetching things is simply part of a maid's job.
Fine, then I'll make you grind gold for my–
*clap clap clap*
Nice improv, Scylla. You're a good foil.
Forgive me, Lady Implacable. I thought it would be amusing and I acted without thinking.
Don't apologise. I needed a gag to help lighten the mood.
Anyway... Where did you get that bow, Hero?
Is it legendary? Enchanted? Perhaps taken from one of the display cases?
I didn't take anything! It was just lying on the floor next to one of those four empty cases!
Also, there's a placard on this case. "When the Seal breaks, the horns of Judgment sound." Sounds like something pretentious York would say.
Four cases, a bow, and "horns of Judgment"... Hmm...
Are you on to something, Lady Implacable?
Nothing concrete, but I'm starting to figure out why this place looks so dreary.
WHOOSH...
Just then, a shadowy figure appeared in the corridor on the far opposite end behind Implacable.
Lady Implacable! Look out!
KABOOOM!
Scylla immediately deployed her rigging and unleashed a machine gun burst of lead arrows at the threat.
The figure tried to no avail to block the volley using its poleaxe, and was swiftly dispatched.
A random encounter! My bow will take care of–
Scylla already dealt with them.
What?! Hey! How dare you steal my EXP!
Do forgive me. I promise it won't happen again~
Heh! Damn right it won't☆
Was that... Vichya's La Galissonnière?
Specifically, a Pawn of hers. Easily defeated.
Vichya Pawns appearing inside a Basilica that they held... That certainly is cause for concern, isn't it?
*RUMBLE*––
What the hell? Is that an earthquake?
If only.
I fear it's exactly what it sounds like, Lady Implacable.
An entire army of Pawns is quickly closing in on us!
Prepare for battle! We will not fall here!
*pant*... *pant*...
Is there no end to these damn Pawns?! I'm working up a sweat here!
Not that a bunch of mooks could ever dream of beating me, but still!
While I wouldn't quite say we're losing, our weapons will wear out sooner or later if we continue fighting in these close quarters.
Mhm. Moreover, I need more room to launch my planes. Even that armoury would suffice.
Do you think we could lead the pawns in that direction?
Certainly. If need be, we could also break through the wall there to retreat into the water.
Our riggings are designed for naval combat, not ground combat, after all.
Good point. Every enemy we take out is one fewer for Argus and Royal Oak to deal with.
Although, we wouldn't want to draw more enemy fire than we already do.
At any rate, let's go! To the hall we came from!
Basilica Blanc - Indoors
Move it, losers! Hero coming through!
KABOOOM!
Nice work. You have a knack for punching holes through walls and hordes alike.
Well, yeah! It comes with the title!
Of course. Does anyone have a backup plan if the Pawns don't pursue us?
Isn't that for you to consider, Lady Implacable? You are our leader, aren't you?
Although, we may not need one as they seem to be following us. Keep advancing and I shall cover your back.
Got it.
Basilica Blanc - Coastline
KABOOOM!
Bosh! There's our path to the ocean~
Thanks, Hero. Now we can fight unrestrained.
No pity, no mercy. Let us show these mindless Pawns our true strength!
KABOOOM!
Well said. Waste neither pity nor mercy on them, for they will show you none.
Cardinal?! Is that you?!
Yes. It's a pleasure to see you again, Implacable.
You're here sooner than Her Majesty predicted! Thank goodness for that.
She, well... also rescued us. Cardinal Richelieu was the first to respond to our SOS.
If she hadn't come along, Royal Oak and I likely wouldn't be here right now.
Forgive me, Implacable... I've put the Royal Knights to shame.
It's alright. I'm just glad you're both in one piece.
Cardinal, if I may ask, what brought you to this remote island in the first place?
I shall explain later. For now, we must focus on defeating the enemy in front of us.
Let us smite these wicked doppelgangers who dare violate the sanctity of the Iris's territory!
Working together, the investigation team and Richelieu's fleet led the Pawns out of the Basilica and dispatched every last one of them.
Béarn, inspect the Pawns one at a time and ensure they're neutralized.
As you command, Cardinal. I will personally examine the Basilica's Sacraments later as well.
Thank you for aiding us, Implacable.
No, thank YOU. We're in your debt for saving Argus and Royal Oak.
Please, think nothing of it. You are our allies, and we are yours.
Argus told me you're leading the investigation into this Basilica. Is that correct?
Why, yes, I am.
It's been a bumpy ride thus far, but that's about to change now that you're here, Cardinal. It's an honour.
The honor is all mine. I've wanted to join the Royal Navy in battle again ever since the incident with the Skybound Basilica.
(The Skybound Basilica? I suppose that's the one Illustrious spoke about.)
Well... Now that you're here, I might as well spill the beans.
Spill what beans, exactly?
That Her Majesty kept this investigation a secret from you until our fleet had already embarked.
Despite that, you somehow arrived at this Basilica at nearly the same time as us.
Oh, I see. If you're confused, I can explain.
Truth be told, I also set out to investigate these islands as soon as I heard that Vichya had withdrawn its forces.
Then, when we heard the SOS signal coming from the Basilica, we used special instruments to amply it before rushing to the rescue.
Amplify it? To what end?
Your patrol fleets weren't receiving the distress call before we gave it a signal boost.
I see. It seems you've seen right through us, Cardinal.
I suppose I should thank you for letting us save face by independently responding to the distress call, rather than alerting us directly.
If you'll pardon me for changing topics, I'd like to propose the idea of making this a joint investigation.
It's a lot for either of us to handle alone, but it's a different story if we work together. Would you happen to know anything about this Basilica?
Yes. This place was a sanctuary of sorts for the Iris Orthodoxy, before the Vichya Dominion seized control of it.
It appears it has suffered numerous breakdowns, owing to not being properly maintained for a long while.
Are those Pawns the result of some breakdown as well?
Yes, but only broadly speaking. It would take a while to explain it.
Fortunately, I know a solution to the problem. Ladies of the Royal Navy, please follow me.
Basilica Blanc - Purification Facility
I've finished repairs on the 11th, 15th, and 17th circuits. We can reboot the system.
Excellent. We're in luck.
I wish we didn't have to resort to this, but it's our only option besides individually destroying every last Pawn and their production center.
I'm glad it's an option in the first place. How much do you know about this place, Cardinal?
Béarn and I indeed were involved in signing off on a number of projects that took place here.
However, now that I'm here... I can tell that many things have changed beyond recognition.
Just as with the Skybound Basilica, I do not know about the scope of the modifications made by Vichya, or about what lies in wait deep within the facility.
Béarn might be able to tell you a bit more about the technical aspects, but beyond that, I can't tell you much more.
Well, you have a firmer grasp on the situation than we do, that much is for sure.
Anyway, what's our next move?
We will head to the center of Basilica Blanc, but first, we must wait for this machine to get up and running again.
Until then... I suppose we rest.
May I interest you in some tea, ladies?
Why, yes. Thank you.
Excuse me, Scylla? Didn't I say I would make tea for the Cardinal?
You did, but your request is secondary to my duty as a Royal Maid, which is to make tea in this case. I hope you'll forgive me.
Lady Argus, Lady Royal Oak, I have some for you as well.
Thanks. Pour some for Béarn and Hero, too.
Certainly. Just a minute.
Well, since all we can do is wait, let's get caught up, shall we?
Starting with you, Argus. You were first to notice something had gone wrong, is that right?
Yes. I was in the control room, monitoring Royal Oak while she went around investigating.
I made a poor decision and activated the emergency defence system, which resulted in Royal Oak getting attacked by Pawns.
Since she was in danger, I quickly sent out a distress signal and left the control room to help her.
Then, while passing through the underground corridor to Basilica Blanc, Pawns attacked me as well.
I was panicking at that point, since our communications were being jammed.
If Royal Oak had relocated in the time it'd taken me to get there, I'd have no idea where she went.
By some miracle, I found her exactly where I last saw her, albeit surrounded by enemies.
I held out because I didn't want to annoy you. You don't just call for help then disappear before it even arrives...
That was the right call. What happened next?
We stuck together, fighting off Pawns while retreating towards a giant hall at the bottom of the facility.
That hall was... If I had to describe it, it was like a military parade inside a warehouse.
Argus, where are we?
I'm afraid I don't know. I left the map behind in the lighthouse tower...
However, I'm pretty sure this place was NOT on the map.
Since there were armouries on the first floor, I think this is a parading area, or a barracks.
And it seems its many occupants are all Pawns...
Goodness, you're right... I'm just glad they're inactive.
There must be hundreds of them. No, maybe even thousands!
I don't even WANT to know how many there are!
It's like they put an entire army of Pawns down here...
Wait... What if it IS an army? Is this the secret Her Majesty wanted us to find?
No matter how weak Pawns might be individually, there's no way any of us could stand up to those sheer numbers...
And just when those thoughts started going through my head, the Pawns suddenly started marching...
Luckily, Cardinal Richelieu found us in the nick of time... or I fear the worst might've come to pass.
All I remember is, I heard the sound of fighting as we were retreating, and then support showed up.
I see... An entire army of Pawns. So this is the project that Vichya was using the Basilica for.
Cardinal, were you aware of any such projects back during the time of the Iris Orthodoxy?
This originally was an idea floated by the Tribunal, compensating for their apparent lack of naval forces with a massive fleet of Pawns to defend the homeland.
But, the actual implementation flopped catastrophically, and the project was shelved.
Flopped catastrophically? How do you explain the very finished-looking product we saw down there then?
I assume all those Pawns we encountered were the results of that plan, and their combat prowess was nothing to sneeze at.
As they say, assembling an army is the easy part. Controlling it is where the real difficulty lies. I suspect Vichya learned that lesson firsthand.
Oh? Care to elaborate?
Pawns are machines, and machines naturally can malfunction.
Through our experiments, we found that the larger the army of Pawns, the greater the proportion of units failing to act in unison.
The reason for this is, Pawns that started behaving abnormally would influence "normal" Pawns, causing a malfunction chain reaction.
The Tribunal began describing this phenomenon as "Infection." Correspondingly, the solution to suppress this infection was the purification system you just saw.
That makes perfect sense, which is also why the entire island is set up to defend against the inside... Are you sure it's fine to give away all this valuable information so casually?
It's fine. After all, you're all victims of the malfunctioning of an Iris Orthodoxy facility.
Now that you've experienced the situation firsthand, what good does it do to try to deny reality and resort to diplomatic tricks?
What matters is that we work together to resolve this incident.
From what you've told me, I assume you're still able to keep things under control?
We can attribute this incident to a lack of maintenance of the equipment, made worse by its improper operation.

Now that the purification systems of the four Basilicas responsible for containing the infection have been shut down, the Pawn army has fully spiraled out of control, leading to the situation we have on our hands.
What we need to do is to reactivate all four purification systems, then defeat all the malfunctioning Pawns remaining in the Basilicas.
Once the purification systems are back online and the malfunctioning Pawns have been dealt with, the Basilicas' systems will naturally stabilize again.
Reactivate all the purification systems and take out all the Pawns...? That sounds like the plot of one of those games Hero's always playing...
Are you sure there isn't some kind of master control panel that can remotely fix all the issues at once?
While that would certainly make our lives much easier, I'm afraid there isn't.
By the way, can you do something about our communication equipment malfunctioning?
I certainly hope we won't have to knock down all these Pawns by ourselves just to call for reinforcements.
Hmm... Unlike last time, we are dealing with a Basilica sitting on top of a Siren facility.
In other words, this jamming is caused by the presence of a nearby Mirror Sea...
That certainly complicates things a bit.
Lady Richelieu, the purification system has been reactivated. You can now proceed to the control center.
We can talk later. Let's move out.

sequence:
The Royal Knight

<size=45>Chapter 1: Wake Up, Your Majesty!</size>

scripts.say: Port - Royal Navy Dormitory
Zzzzzzzz...
Oh... Is Her Majesty still sleeping?
(She would normally be awake by now...)
(Seems she went to bed too late last night.)
(I'd best wake her. She has an important meeting today.)
Nng... Warspite... Stay with me... Zzzz...
(Now what shall we do about this...?)
Your Majesty, please wake up. We have a meeting that Your Majesty absolutely must attend...
Nng... Hm? Hrmm? Warspite? You're here by my side...? Very good then...
(I'm afraid this calls for harsher measures. The bedspread, for example. Your Majesty... please forgive the indiscretion.)
Haaaagh!
Aaaaaaieeeeee!!!
Wh-what is the meaning of this, Warspite?!
I must have been dreaming... Heavens, would you look at the time!
Honestly, why did you not wake me sooner?! I'm going to be late!
(That is the reaction I expected... But I do believe we can make the meeting on time.)
Ahem! Now then, the Royal Navy has agreed to a second round of large-scale exercises with the Eagle Union!
Warspite shall be responsible for the training and drills ahead of the exercises. I expect my Royal Navy to give a dazzling performance on the day of.
Warspite, you are not to disappoint your queen! Are we understood?
Yes, Your Majesty!
(Seems waking up late hasn't affected Her Majesty in the slightest. She never lets these little things get to her.)
Right then, I shall gladly take on the training of the Royal Navy!
Becoming a proper warrior is no easy task. Steel yourselves, girls!

sequence:
The Royal Knight

<size=45>Chapter 2: The Secretary Ship's Work</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Good morning, Commander.
(Her Majesty may have put me in charge of training the fleet, but I can't neglect my duties as secretary either.)
(Of course, because of how competent Commander is, my work is not very difficult.)
Is there anything in particular you need today? I can handle it.
You want me to tally up this month's research expenditures...? Aye-aye.
That sort of thing won't take me but a moment.
(First I need to dig up the files... Right... Here they are.)
(Hm? They're all the way up there... Can the Commander really reach that shelf so easily...?)
(I-I can't trouble the Commander over such a trifling thing. I must do this myself!)
(Argh, even on my tiptoes I'm still just short of it... Right then...)
Hah!
(I just need to jump up and grab it...!)
Yes! Got it!
(Wobble, wobble, crash!)
Bollocks!!!
(Who would've thought all the other files would come crashing down like that.)
Terribly sorry, Commander! I knocked them over while grabbing this document.
I can't believe I've made such a base mistake! I'll get to cleaning this up straight away!
(M-maybe I should have just asked the Commander for help in the first place.)

sequence:
The Royal Knight

<size=45>Chapter 3: The Speed of the Grand Old Lady</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
(Work took much longer than I anticipated thanks to that little hiccup this morning.)
(Now the most important thing is getting this file into Her Majesty's hands. I need to move quickly.)
... I suppose I should run then.
Phew... Haah...
(Almost there... I should make it just in time!)
(Now why is the floor here so slippery... Did they just mop it?)
(Doesn't matter. I just need to keep moving!)
Juust whistle while you work~♪
(It's Suffolk mopping up?! Not enough room to go around her now!!)
Look out! Make way!
Huh? Aaaaaaagh!
(CRASH!)
Owwwieee... Madam Warspite?!
S-sorry about that...
Are you two all right? Any injuries?
... Suffolk, why were you mopping the hallway? Did I not ask you to clean only the meeting room?
Huuuh? Did I mop all the way to the hall already...?
