Forgive her, Madam Warspite. I apologise for the trouble we have caused you.
I-I apologise...
No, it was my fault as well. I shouldn't have been running down the corridor.
(But... it is rather odd I always end up crashing into someone like this. I wonder if it's some kind of curse...?)
(Now's not the time to think about that. I need to get this file over to- It's all wet now?!)
(Aie...! I'd better go get another copy... Her Majesty won't mind if I'm a bit late...)

sequence:
The Royal Knight

<size=45>Chapter 4: After the Exercise...</size>

scripts.say: Several Days Later - Exercise Area
Ahem! Our success in these joint exercises is thanks entirely to your training, your implementation of the tactics you learned, and your ability to adapt to a changing combat situation.
In short, the Royal Navy seized victory not by random chance, but through the hard work and dedication of everyone here.
Now it is time to rest and recuperate. Indulge yourselves in the banquet Her Majesty has graciously bestowed upon us!
Aye-aye!
(I'll step out for some fresh air.)
(Ah? Who's that over there...?)
Enterprise?
Warspite? Congratulations. You won the exercise.
I'm still a little sore about it, honestly. I had my planes on you the whole time and I still didn't manage to sink you.
We should start calling you "The Unsinkable Legend."
(So it was you behind all those planes buzzing around my head...!)
(She kept me busy dodging bombs and firing ack-acks the whole time... I must've put on quite a show for the Commander...)
Hah. Thanks to you, I've had my fill of planes for a while.
You wore me out plenty yourself. Nothing like the splashes from 15-inch rounds right by your feet to keep you on your toes.
(... But not a single one of the shells I fired at Enterprise hit home. I guess she really is the "Lucky E".)
I really must thank you and the rest of the Eagle Union for participating in these exercises. The Royal Navy learned a lot from our war games today.
If we're thanking each other, I have to say it was great for the Union side too. I'd like it if we could keep up these large-scale exercises going forward.
And I look forward to sparring with you again, Warspite.
That feeling is certainly mutual.
Lady Warspite, I think Her Majesty is looking for you.
(Her Majesty...? Then I'd best hurry back.)
Then I won't keep you. Until next time!
Indeed. Farewell.
(And with that, my training assignment has come to an end, giving me a chance to rest a bit... I'll have to go enjoy the banquet with the girls. After I find out what Her Majesty wants, of course.)

sequence:
The Royal Knight

<size=45>Chapter 5: The Small Things</size>

scripts.say: Right then, let's get the work done as quickly as possible. I'll just head into the office and-
What's this? Someone else in the office with the Commander...?
Hehe, think nothing of it~ If there's anything else you need, please don't hesitate to call upon me, Commander.
(That sounds like... Illustrious?)
Now then, one must take her leave.
Oh, if it isn't Lady Warspite. Good morning to you.
Y-yes. Good morning.
(bounce)
(boing)
(She, she's rubbing them right in my face...)
Lady Warspite, you seem unwell... Have you any trouble sleeping?
M-maybe a touch... But you need not worry. A little fatigue never killed anyone.
Then I shall be on my way... Do take care of yourself, Lady Warspite.
Aye. Thank you.
It's a commission report...
(Let's see how the girls are doing...)
And I... may have... to join you...
(Now how am I supposed to keep up...?)
Oh?
Ah... Forgive me, Commander. I was lost in thought for a moment.
We're all done for the day? We really hit it hard, didn't we...? Now what should we do with all this free time?
Is that right? You'd like to hear some old Royal Navy war stories?
Well, if you really want me to, I have lots I can tell you. We could be here a while though. You might want to get a snack or pour some tea.
Now then, let's start with my commissioning. I was first assigned to the Second Battle Squadron of the Grand Fleet...
(I suddenly find myself feeling quite cheerful..)

sequence:
The Royal Knight

<size=45>Chapter 6: Her Majesty's Attentions</size>

scripts.say: Your Majesty's tea. Madam Warspite. Please enjoy.
My thanks.
(This is the appointed time for Her Majesty's usual tea party, but it seems some invitees are late. It's only Her Majesty and I for now.)
Now then, Warspite...
Do I get the sense that you've been spending less and less time at our side...? And more and more with the Commander?
... I... suppose that's possible.
Or perhaps we are mistaken.
D-d-d-don't misunderstand me, it's not like I'm lonely or jealous or anything! I just happened to take note is all!!
Your Majesty...
(Now that I think of it, I have been spending a lot of time with the Commander lately. From the history of the Royal Navy to battle plans and tactics, we've had a lot to discuss.)
(I do find myself more relaxed when chatting with the Commander. All the stress of the day washes right away.)
(... When I put it like that, I realize I do often go looking to talk with the Commander of my own accord...)
(Of course, it's not at all unusual for the secretary ship to have a lot to say to the Commander. That can only be good for the fleet, right?)
(So no one could say it's only because I enjoy talking with the Commander that I go looking for a chat...)
(Of course that's not the only reason...)
... Of course!
What's the matter, Warspite?
Oh, it was nothing. Nothing at all!
Sigh. Now then, if you have something you need to say, Warspite, we certainly shan't interfere. You have your own affairs to manage, of course.
(I can't escape the feeling that Her Majesty's expression belies some much deeper meaning...)
Good day to you, Your Majesty. Warspite.
Forgive my tardiness, Your Majesty. I was delayed by some affairs beyond my control. I apologise for keeping you both waiting.
(The tea party begins in earnest.)
(And yet, Her Majesty's words continue to weigh upon me...)

sequence:
The Royal Knight

<size=45>Chapter 7: The Guardian Sword</size>

scripts.say: Ah!!
(This feeling of helplessness as I am swallowed by the dark blue abyss... and yet, even as I sink, I still have to protect the other Knights, and Her Majesty, and...)
Oh, it was just a dream. I really felt like I was sinking...
The sun isn't even up yet.
... I suppose I'll go for a walk. Just have to be careful not to wake the others.
Port - Near the Office
I wandered here without even thinking. I suppose I've had the Commander on my mind...?
... What's that?
Is there a light coming from the office...?
... I better go take a look.
... Commander...?
(Splayed out over the desk fast asleep.)
(Hm? These are today's commission reports? Didn't we finish these early this afternoon?)
(Don't tell me... the Commander hid most of the work to do later so we would have more time to chat?)
... The absolute moron.
(Ah... Well... At least now I have a clear picture of what's going on...)
(And... you're quite cute when you're sleeping, Commander. You look so peaceful...)
(As you should be. You have nothing to fear with me protecting you.)

(For I am Warspite. I have borne witness to every bitter twist of war, and found nothing that can bend me, the "Unsinkable Legend". No matter who may threaten to harm you, the girls, or the entire fleet, they would have to go through my broken body to do it.)
(And in that knowledge, you may sleep soundly.)
(And I...)
Y-you're having a laugh! It can't have been our Warspite!
We speak the truth! We saw it with our very own royal eyes. Warspite laid up with the Commander in the executive office!
Now naturally we already had such suspicions, but never did we think things would progress so quickly...
As our personal royal guard, she will of course deliver a satisfactory explanation!
Oh, my goodness...
Seems our hardened warrior has a tender side to her. Hehe...
(Goodness, this rumor has gotten well out of hand... I need to clear this up with Her Majesty the Queen post haste...)
(Not that it matters much, I suppose. No rumor can break me.)
(For I am Warspite! Hah! Nothing can break the bond I have with the Commander!)
Dunkerque, it's time to go.
Mm, I'm ready.
Sorry for making you take time out of your schedule for me.
Say nothing of it! Safely evacuating you is part of our duty, Dunkerque!
There should be nothing to worry about. Since the repairs are about done, I alone should be able to...
Non, non. Those were just emergency repairs. You'll have to rest up properly once we get you back home.
Look, with what's been going on between Vichiya, Iron Blood, and the Royal Navy, we've had to wait months for the chance to make this journey.
After making them wait this long as well, our enemies are probably pretty checked out as well~
Sorry, that was just a joke! Don't take it too seriously!
No, perhaps it is I who was not giving adequate consideration to everyone else's feelings.
Once again, thank you for escorting me, Vauquelin.
No worries! If anything, sorry for making you put up with me since I tend to blurt things out without thinking!
(Vauquelin, we've all been waiting, but Dunkerque herself has been waiting even longer... so...)
(Mm... You're going to convince her? Hmm...)
...tu
Tartu!
Huh?
Jeez... what are you spacing out again for...
Kersaint, Fougueux, and the others are all ready, so we're just waiting for Tartu now...
I've been ready though?
Just tell us then if that's the case... All right, before we go, let's go over the mission one more time!
It'll be dangerous, but let's try to take a straight line to Toulon.
The only place to hide along the way are the Balearic Islands, and we can expect Royal Navy patrols.
I don't want to end up fighting Iris Libre... but if it comes down to it...
Mm...
What's our plan for if that situation arises, Tartu?
...Huh?
Tartu... you're in your little world again!
Umm... I was thinking about what the best route to Toulon would be...
Come on, we're way past that already!
Is that so...?
YES... IT... IS... SO!
Whatever, it's my fault for getting caught up in your pace.
Anyway, time is of the essence, so let's keep our wits about us and break through this area as quickly as possible! Got it?
Got it.
Everyone's here and we have our game plan... so let's set out!
Very well. If we must fight, then I shall do my part.
Mmhmm, according to Fougueux's information, we'll have some breathing room once we beat back the enemies ahead of us!
Tartu, you'd better not start daydreaming in the middle of battle!
I wouldn't do that.
I sure hope so...
*sigh* I'm supposed to be escorting Dunkerque, but here I am also babysitting Tartu...
Haha... I think she's doing just fine. You should try to have a bit more faith in her...
We managed to push them back for now.
I hope we don't run into any more trouble on the way to Toulon...
What's wrong, Dunkerque?
I was just thinking about the Royal Navy. We ended up waging an all-out war against them after all...
I wonder indeed... The Vichya Dominion and Iris Libre used to be on the same side... and the Royal Navy as well, but I guess a lot happened...
There's no point thinking about all that now...
.........Mm, you're right.
(What a depressing mood...) Dunkerque, now's probably not the best time to think about this.
Let's focus on getting back to Toulon so you can rest up and recover!
Hehe. I've had plenty of time to rest up in the docks... But, I also haven't been able to contribute to the Vichya's war efforts as a result...
That's not true at all!
The only reason you've been out of commission is because of the treachery of that Perfidious Albion...
So basically, umm, what I'm trying to say is...
(Hey, Tartu! Help me find something I can say to reassure Dunkerque!)
Hmm...? Sorry, I only heard about half of it... But, in any case, I don't think you need to blame yourself, Dunkerque.
Regardless of the camp - Royal Navy, Iron Blood, or Iris... I don't think there's anything we can do about the fact that their leaders think of us as weapons of war.
What's more important is that there are comrades who are worried about you and eagerly awaiting your return, right...?
That's right! Without your sweets, our morale is about to fall through the floor!
Hehe. I guess I'll be busy cooking after I get back.
I can't afford to let Strasbourg see me in such a sorry state after all.
Vauquelin, Tartu, let's continue to push forward.
Nothing's happening...
We're on an escort mission, so isn't it better if nothing is happening...?
Touché... Wait, since when did you learn how to make retorts?
Hm...? Am I not allowed to...?
No, I just assumed you would always be off thinking about other things by yourself until someone else grabbed your attention...
By the way, is it just me, or was the Mediterranean always this chilly?
Once we get back, if there are no other missions waiting for me, maybe I'll take a trip somewhere~
It'd be nice to head up north to see the snow, or even an aurora... What do you think, Tartu?
I bet you'd want to go with one of your Iris girls.
Ehehe~
There's a fleet we haven't seen before ahead of us... I wonder if it's another Royal patrol fleet?
A Vichya fleet?! Why would they be here...?!
And if I'm not mistaken, you're that battlecruiser, Dunkerque?!
I knew it, a blasted Royal fleet! Dunkerque, don't push yourself too hard!
If we let them get away, they're going to report our position... Vauquelin, we have to fight!
No hard feelings... but you will be letting us through!
Sorry, but we'll need you to stay quiet.
Guh...
I've confirmed that Arethusa has been incapacitated!
Wasn't that amazing...? Tartu, were you watching Dunkerque just now?
I saw... so stop shaking me around already...
We had a numbers advantage, so this did feel a bit unfair...
But as Tartu said, our priority right now is to safely make it home to our friends.
Now's not the time to think about negotiating with the Royal Navy or taking revenge against them.
No matter when or where, my duty is to protect our friends of the Vichya Dominion and uphold the Iris Orthodoxy.
My purpose as a ship is to be a guardian knight - that is the meaning of my existence.
Mmhmm! The same's true for us, although we still have a ways to go! Right, Tartu?
(She's kindhearted, strong, and dependable...)
(I hope I can mature into someone as cool as Dunkerque when I'm older...)
Tartu...!!
I'm feeling a bit hungry...
We're almost there. Just hold on a bit longer.
But I'm hungryyyyy... Ah! I'm sure I saw some snacks among the stuff you brought...
My handmade sweets? I planned to give them to everyone after we got back to Toulon...
I know how hard it is to fight on an empty stomach... You can have some, but try not to go overboard.
R-really? You're the best, Dunkerque!
Macarons, Montblancs, profiteroles, mille-feuille... there's so much stuff here I don't know where to start...
That's because I made enough for everyone. Vauquelin, try not to eat too much, all right?
I know! Now, where to start... Mmmmm! So good! Tartu, do you want some as well? Dunkerque, can Tartu also have some?
Hehe, sure. I can always make more later. Tartu, did you also want to take a break?
...Um, thank you. In that case, I'll also help myself.
This nostalgic aroma... Delicious!
(It'd be nice to be able to enjoy sweets with everyone again...)
(I wonder if there will ever come a day...)
(...when Jean Bart and Richelieu can enjoy these sweets together again...)
Dunkerque, sorry I took so long eating...
Fougueux reported that they've spotted the Royal battleship, Nelson.
Nelson, one of the Big Seven... It wouldn't be a good idea to engage her. Try to avoid her if possible.
Got it!
Stop right there, whoever you are!
Shoot, she discovered us...
You guys are... the Vichya Dominion's...!
Trying to flee to Toulon for repairs, huh? ...I won't let you get away!
If it's just her...
Tartu, Vauquelin, we're going to make a break for it before she can call reinforcements!
Her speed... I really can't deal with these tight turns in night battles...!
Ahaha! A direct hit! That's the power of a Vichya knight's torpedoes!
Don't overextend. It's our victory as long as we make it back to Toulon.
Wait, Dunkerque! What do you possibly hope to achieve returning to the Vichya Dominion in its current state?!
Upon the honor of Her Majesty, we will guarantee your safety if you surrender yourself to the Royal Navy!
...You're right...
...I might not be able to make a difference after I return...
But I am one of Vichya's Templar Knights. If the Vichya is ever in danger...
As long as I still have friends who place their trust within me, I will return to their sides.
My purpose is to fight for my friends and the Vichya Dominion.
Dunkerque...
I see... May Iris watch over you, Dunkerque.
F-Finally, I can see the light of Toulon... I'm exhausted...
We're almost there, but let's stay alert until we've arrived in port.
I know, I know! Tartu, why does it feel like you're hyper focused today~
Huh? I was just thinking about the best way to dock...
Oh, I guess you're not that focused after all...
Hm? Vauquelin? What's the matter?
Hehe~ Now that we've arrived, it feels like we can finally take a deep breath~
After crossing the perilous sea in the darkness, battlecruiser Dunkerque and the ships escorting her safely arrive at Toulon in the Vichya Dominion. But at the same time...
In this "Simulation," the Royal Navy will be dismantled after dozens of their ships sink to the hands of battleship Jean Bart...
But of course, I would not allow such an outcome to take place. After all, my "Experiment" must continue...
After all... What kind of future can these ships, who have been saved by humanity, find at the intersection of light and shadow?
Ahaha... I shall continue my observation...
It's been so long, yet this place hasn't changed one bit.
The girl walked through the spacious streets, gazing at the desolate city.
Her makeup was impeccable. She must have prepared thoroughly for this visit.
It might have been spontaneous, but I was going to do this eventually anyway. I just did it a little sooner.
The mechanical city responds to her words with rhythmic buzzing, as if in anticipation of something.

sequence: "The calm before the storm..."

scripts.say: Not yet... Wait just a while longer.
After finding a decently comfortable spot, she sat down and began staring at the galactic waves unfolding in the distance.

sequence: "How long it's been..."

scripts.say: Recorder, start recording.
It seemed that she had made up her mind.
As she spoke, several small spheres equipped with camera lenses flew out from the armrest of her metal chair.
Hello again, {playername}. By the time you see this recording, I'll...
...No, this is a bad way to open.
Okay... I'm soon going to go on a journey.
With what little time I have left before I set off, I want to organize my thoughts and clear my mind.
At the same time, I'm sure you still have many questions for me.
So, today, I'm going to be more frank and casual with you.
Yeah – I'm going to simply tell you things as they come to mind.
Without further ado... Let's begin.
With a full replacement of their Wisdom Cube engines, the Federation's navy has seen an enormous increase in combat capabilities...
A pink-haired woman stood at the podium, delivering the day's lecture.
(Am I in a classroom?)
(When did I come here?)
Take a look at this OFS missile destroyer.
At first, these missile destroyers were simple retrofits of the Pathfinder-class destroyers.
But with technological advancements and several upgrade cycles, the modern OFS missile destroyer has become a different beast altogether.
The pink-haired woman methodically continued her lecture.
(A simple overview of the Federation's warships? Why is that the subject of this lecture?)
(Strange... Something feels wrong about this lesson.)
While Helena was in a daze, the podium suddenly changed color.
Aside from the greatest threat in the Epimetheus mega-submarine, you'll need to be especially wary of the missile battleships mixed in during your combat exercises...
(What?! There's a different teacher now.)
(That isn't Lexington. Who is it?)
(I don't know them, but something about them seems familiar...)
Now, I've explained the performance and equipment of each ship.
Up against a mixed fleet, I'd like you all to tell me your thoughts on how you would deal with the most threatening targets.
Let's start with you, Helena. What do you think?
(Huh? Wh-why me?!)
She panicked. As her focus was disturbed, the podium changed colors over and over again.
Next, I'll introduce the OFS heavy destroyer.
(Where did that person from before go?)
The podium and everything around it changed randomly back and forth.
(I don't understand any of this at all...)
March 17th. It had already been three days since I got to this test site.
Today, the Eagle Union fleet led by Enterprise and me finally managed to return to PH Port.
The buildings in this place were far larger than in any other test site. They were like giant fortresses towering amongst the sea.
The situation I saw here also lent credibility to my theory – that the war was far and away more intense here than all other test sites.
March 18th. I met this world's Helena.
She was briefed on what had happened, and when she learned of Louis' injuries, she rushed to see her.
Luckily, Louis' condition was not life-threatening.
She was utterly shocked when she laid eyes on me. Anyone in her shoes would be.
Getting to witness another you's reaction to you... You might say it's another one of the pleasures of being in the Ashes.
Our conversation for the day stopped at a brief introduction, as we decided to save the big subjects for later.
I was putting together a report of useful battlefield information then. Soon, I'd be able to show it to her.
March 25th. The day I would head to NY Harbor.
My report came as a huge shock to all faction leaders after I shared it with them.
I don't blame them, considering that my report deliberately emphasized the fact that the Sirens would completely destroy this world within 10 years if the current status quo continued.
Fortunately, I decided to stay there and help them.
I wasn't worried about the other Ashes members. If I was fine, they were probably fine, too.
So, I just had to buckle down and do it...
It was time for me to focus on the world in front of me.
March 15th. A whole year had passed since I came to this test site. This was also a day to celebrate.
Today, rigging retrofitting technology has finally become widespread among all the factions.
Although a retrofitted rigging can't handle intense fighting with tough opponents as well as a Type II can, it was still a small step forward for this world thanks to my actions.
I then set my eyes on two other fields: Communications technology and regional teleporter technology.
I had to raise the whole world's combat capabilities in a short amount of time, so the first thing I did was make plans to stabilize the war situation.
December 25th. Christmas.
This was my second Christmas spent in this world, and Helena spent it with me, just like last year.
She had always been by my side lately during missions.
From Tester, to Omitter, to Compiler, her achievements were among the best even on a global scale.
It wasn't just the Eagle Union, either – many factions had claimed more than a few victories.
They were just the experimentation team, after all. I might have known them better even than they themselves did.
The only problem was that there had been no progress in the development of Type II riggings or floating battleship technology.
When viewed on the whole, though, it seemed that the situation was turning in the world's favor.
I mean, it was, wasn't it?
X... It still showed itself in the end.
And with its arrival, sudden changes affecting the whole world came one after the next.
We were like a boat sailing through a storm – laughably small compared to the sea, desperately enduring the violent waves of change.
Despite doing all we could, though, our only choice was to keep pushing straight forward.
Didya hear? They've started recruiting volunteers for some controllable METAmorphosis technology!
Yes, so they say.
If the technology really is ripe, then I'm really interested in this risk-free way of improving our combat effectiveness.
Yeah... If it passes the inspection, then I also wanna try it.
I want to help as much as I can...
"Controllable METAmorphosis." Do you really think that's safe?
Frankly, I have some concerns over it as well.
That's why I think we should get a specialist's take, rather than grasp at straws by ourselves.
Now, who do you think the specialist I called over is?
The partition in the conference room opened, and a familiar figure revealed herself.
Good to see you again, girls. Hope you've been well.
Hmm... Honestly, many people – myself included – think there's an uncontrollable element of risk to the METAmorphosis technology.
"Controllable" METAmorphosis is in and of itself is a false proposition.
The problem is that there's little to support this theory we have, and what risks we are concerned about can't be reflected with our current evaluation system.
That's why we ultimately lost at the vote-casting stage.
Mind you, we're not just saying, "This tech is super dangerous!" or "It's impossible to control!" or anything like that.
At the end of the day, it's a question of how careful we should be.
(There's that strange feeling again...)
(Does this conference room hide some sort of... secret?)
As the girl's mind wandered, another person showed up next to Anzeel.
Anzeel is right. The majority of differences in opinion with this technology really do boil down to a matter of prudence.
Some people believe that this technology, which utilizes METAmorphosis to a limited extent, already errs more on the side of caution than it needs to.
On the other hand, people like Anzeel and I hold that there's no such thing as being too cautious when it comes to METAmorphosis technology.
However, with the threat of the X growing day by day, we must make a decision in the end, even if we all think we should do things differently.
And the decision we made following a vote was this: We will research this controllable METAmorphosis technology in earnest.
As for the concerns the rest of us have, those will be tackled.
We will establish a series of research projects to prove that there are uncontrollable risks in this technology, then make it as safe as it can be to reassure you all.
Everything will be fine. Anzeel, I, and many others have your backs.
(It's you again...)
(Who are you? What are you?)
(Why do you constantly show up next to me only to then disappear, leaving no trace behind?)
As the girl's mental fatigue reached its limit, the conference room before her returned to what it was.
Basically, you girls don't need to worry. I promise to keep a close eye on this tech and put your safety first!
The only one to make this promise was Anzeel. The familiar figure that the girl saw had vanished once again.
Gone without a single trace, like nobody was there in the first place.
Let's commemorate this day worth celebrating!
Glasses up! Cheers, everyone!
In a holiday house by the beachside, a lively party was taking place.
The Combined Fleet destroyed Tester's mainframe in the Pacific! This marks a monumental victory for us since the war began!
Yeppers! The tables have completely turned in that theater!
The force tasked with destroying that mainframe will be able to join the fight against other mainframes now. Victory's basically at our fingertips!
Don't count your chickens before they've hatched.
This joint operation between several factions exposed several issues we have.
A large part of our victory was owed to the fact that we caught her by surprise. The Sirens are gonna bolster their mainframes' defenses from now on.
Yeah, that is true.
Still, let's not focus too much on the war right now! We've got a rare day off to enjoy.
Exactly. We haven't had a get-together like this in ages since we set out on our counteroffensive!
A few years ago, nobody could've imagined things would be going this well for us, and it's all thanks to Helena META!
A toast! To Helena META, our brilliant genius!
Heehee. You're all exaggerating.
I'm not any kind of genius. I've simply been to many test sites and learned some things I ought to know.
Speaking of which, you say the word "test site" a lot. What does it mean?
Do you call our world that because the Sirens have been conducting all kinds of experiments here?
Well... Strictly speaking, not exactly.
The Sirens come with a testing plan already laid out in advance before they arrive in a given world.
You can even infer the contents of their premade plans to a certain degree based on the serial number and management coordinates they assign to a test site.
Each test site has a unique serial number assigned to it which indicates its classification and affiliation.
Furthermore, every site's management coordinates contains four variables, and the first three identify its experiment policy and deviation value.
The fourth variable – that's a timestamp marking when when the Sirens officially intervened.
Then what are the coordinates of our world?
I don't know yet. It was Tester's mainframe we took out, so it wouldn't record that information.
To learn your coordinates, we'll have to get inside Observer's mainframe.
I see...
The Sirens must wield power beyond imagination to have turned countless worlds into just test sites.
If you hadn't been here, who knows where we'd be right now...
But the fact is that I am here now. Don't worry about the future.
*sigh*... Once this war with the Sirens ends, I need an extended vacation.
I wanna go to every continent and every ocean and see this world that we protected.
Good idea! I agree!
Heehee. I'll make the arrangements when that time comes. Let's all go on a globe-spanning journey!
Time flew, and the next thing they knew, the night had grown late.
Some were content to retire to bed, while others stayed up to keep enjoying the party.
Helena, however, did neither of those – she lay on the rooftop terrace, quietly gazing at the stars.
They're beautiful...
Feels like it's been so long since I saw a night sky this beautiful.
Hey, SG... Do you really think there'll come a day when we've beaten the Sirens?
It will. One day.
Oh... Helena META. What brings you here?
You weren't in the house, so I figured you'd be up here.
What is it? Do you not trust me anymore?
It's not like that...
Heehee. I know how you feel.
Don't worry. As long as I'm here, I promise I'll lead your world to victory.
...Okay!
The night wore on, and the girl pushed open the door to the holiday house.
St. Louis! Helena! Good timing! We're prepping some food and were just about to cook some meat!
It's been a while, Saratoga. Let me help.
Me too...
Thanks, really, but I can do it myself!
Me and Lex are the hosts tonight, so you two just be good guests and wait for the feast to be ready!
Well, if you insist!
Helena, I think Baltimore and Memphis are here. Let's go say hi, shall we?
Ah, St. Louis and Helena. Good of you to show.
So, now that you've experienced regional teleporter tech for yourselves, what do you think?
It's groundbreaking, without a doubt.
Once the technology spreads around the world, we'll be able to send materials and reinforcements to the battlefield in an instant. Our efficiency will shoot right up.
Everyone agrees once they try it for themselves.
Personally, though, I think Project Undercurrent also has a lot of merit.

Making underground rivers that connect major cities with suburban facilities will drastically cut the cost of regular logistics while also serving as an alternate route in the event that the regional transmitters break down.
(...Why'd she bring up Project Undercurrent all of a sudden?)
(I'm getting that feeling again... Something is wrong here!)
The girl adeptly focused her attention, and gazed toward the kitchen.
There, three figures appeared in front of the counter.
Lexington had stopped what she was doing at some point, and stood there, waiting for an answer with a smile.
Ahaha. You humble me.
Even solely from the angle of reducing transport costs substantially, the project is worth proceeding with.
Furthermore... Actually, never mind.
This is a rare gathering for all of us, so let's not spoil it with serious talk.
Seeing as the meat's still got a while to go, how about I make some cocktails for you all in the meantime?
Cocktails? When did you learn to make those?
Last month, when I visited the Orthodoxy. Well? Shall I?
Just a warning, though: Nobody's tried my cocktails yet, so I can't promise they'll be good.
I would love to try one of them. It's just that there are so many of us here tonight, and, well...
I get you. Don't worry, I'll make enough for everyone.
Yippee!
Who to start with...
Why not the people seated closest? Me and Sara still have things to do in the kitchen, so you can save us for last.
Yeah. What Lex said – we can wait.
Alright, that puts Helena first in line. Let's see...
There, all done! One Blue Sea Mystery for you.
After a while, a sparkling, blue cocktail appeared on the counter.
Lexington smiled, and gestured at the girl to taste it.
At the same time, the person beside her who had made the cocktail had vanished again.
Blue Sea Mystery...
That kind of reminds me of...
The... Com...mander?
January 4th. Our precious New Year's vacation was over.
After Tester's mainframe was destroyed, I set my sights on Compiler as our next target.
As such, I devised a plan to lead the Eagle Union's fleet to Scapa Flow's anchorage, where we'd meet up with the Europan Combined Fleet.
However, according to intel from the past few days, the Sirens had ramped up their deployments across the world, and the weather was getting worse and worse in the NA region.
I knew Compiler was up to no good.
Not that it mattered. The outcome would be the same no matter how much she struggled.
I'd successfully contacted Memphis META using a beacon.
We had a nasty surprise ready for her.
February 20th. Compiler's mainframe was destroyed.
Our second victory. Just have to keep on keeping on.
April 13th. Omitter's mainframe was destroyed.
The explosion of her mainframe just so happened to open up a route to the Arctic, which was a surprising but welcome side effect of this operation.
August 11th. Purifier's mainframe was destroyed.
This was our fourth war-deciding victory.
Now, the only member left on the experimentation team was Observer, hidden under the Antarctic ice sheets.
December 24th. Observer's mainframe was destroyed.
Every member of the experimentation team had been eliminated. The world was free.
Today... everyone basked in this long-awaited peace, and it seemed it was going to be a peaceful Christmas Eve.
*knock knock knock*
Helena, are you there?
Memphis? What's the matter?
We got strange news from the front... I can't make heads or tails of it, so I figured I should show it to you.
...Strange news?
Oh... Looks like these photos were taken from the other side of Antarctica.
Wait... What are these things that look like buds?
What... is all this?
The girl, faced with a pile of documents stacked high, made a confused expression.
Simply put, it's a project to upgrade the SG radar's abilities.
There's no rush with these papers. Just give 'em a look.
(The Special SG Ragar Upgrade Project...)
(This is a lot of documents... Something feels odd about Anzeel saying this by herself.)
She squinted with concentration at her surroundings, and they again took on a new form.
In the design, the Tower, at number 16, holds a transcendent position over the entire Antiochus system.
Its database is colossal, and moreover, completely independent.
If need be, this single Tower can restore functionality to the whole Antiochus system. It's fitting to call this Towers the backup system of Antiochus.
Then, there's the SG Radar Upgrade Project – it was designed so that you can work better with the Antiochus system in the future.
You're already doing well with Zero, and have cooperated with the existing Arbiters many times.
But, there are a number of them – including Tower – which are still incomplete, so the time left for you to work with each other is ever-decreasing.
That's why we're designing a project to give the SG radar permission to access the backup database.
This will not only give you insight into the quirks of each Arbiter ahead of time, but also keep you up-to-date on any performance changes to the Antiochus system.
It's also another bit of insurance in the event of an emergency.
The Towers are the backup for the Antiochus system, and you are the backup for the Towers.
The stability of the Antiochus system is pertinent to another important project of ours.
If, in the future–
The girl was pushed to the brink of passing out due to the onset of an intense headache.
When she just barely managed to open her eyes, those last surroundings were completely gone.
Anzeel... Aoste... The Commander... The laboratory...
It's all gone...
And I'm not back to the office...
Is this... a ship's cabin?
*knock knock knock*
The sudden knocking on the door startled the girl so much that her heart skipped a beat.
For some reason, though, she was conflicted by two strong urges – both to open the door, and to not touch it no matter what.
As she stood there, hesitating, the door opened from the other side.
Noticed you didn't look so good today, so I thought I'd check on you.
My hunch was right... I could feel your gloom even on the other side of the hatch.
What's on your mind? Is it the final battle plan?
(The final battle?! Is this that nightmare again?!)
Do NOT go into the final battle! The plan WILL fail!
Commander, order everyone to return home!
She could not stifle her tears from overflowing.
Commander...
The final battle will end in defeat... They're all going to be sacrificed in it...
We'll have no choice but to run for our dear lives... leaving everyone else behind...
We were supposed to protect the world... We were supposed to protect all of you!
It's okay. Don't be afraid.
With me here, and all of us working together, this story will never meet a tragic ending.
Please, Commander... Don't go!
I know it'll be the same as every other time... You'll disappear in the blink of an eye, won't you?!
The girl wrapped her arms tightly around the person before her.
This doesn't mean goodbye forever... We will meet again someday.
Her balance lost, the girl fell to the ground.
She brushed away her tears, and looked vacantly around her.
How can this narrow cabin feel so vast and empty?
January 1st. New Year's.
This will likely be the last record I leave behind in this world.
I still don't have a grasp of the essence of those buds yet, but I do understand their meaning.
They're a symbol of the ultimate threat.
A powerful force that we can never hope to resist... The threat of the X.
I'm still in the Antarctic, but things have changed so much.
Two weeks ago, this place housed the strongest fleets in the world.
One week later, we celebrated peace.
But today, it's become a hellish inferno.
The buds didn't only appear here. They just thrived the longest in this area because so much power was concentrated here.
But that, too, ends today...
I led this world to victory over the Sirens, reclaiming its destiny from the Antiochus.
But against the X... Despite my best efforts, I can only watch as this world is annihilated.
Were the Antiochus right, then?
Was our decision wrong?
It can't be...
I can't accept this end.
The entire world seemed to be set aflame.
Seas and clouds burned. Even the lashes of lightning from above were ablaze.
Go, Helena! You have to live on!
Never forget your mission! What you must do!
Do whatever it takes to survive!
Sara's final performance is about to begin, everyone! Lex, let's go make this a show to remember!
The distant behemoth roared. Blazing winds engulfed the small fleet in the blink of an eye.
A following burst of blinding light carved a path to salvation from this living hell.
Louis, Saratoga, Lexington...
BEEP BEEP!
Her communicator suddenly went off.
This message is from... the Commander?
That's it...
On this day, the Commander personally helped us escape.
BEEP BEEP!
Thank you... I remember now, Tower.
I remember everything.
That's why...
I shouldn't have accepted this message.
I can't let myself be sunk today.
There's a mission I have to carry out. I have more important things to accomplish.

sequence: "Now you know all, yet you remain locked inside your cage."

scripts.say: No. That's wrong.
I am she who will forge the future.
How could the cage known as the past confine me? It can't.
Countless fragments twinkled in the sky like stars, lighting up the world.
The mental images converged into a torrent of light, crashing down with overwhelming force, with the stars in tow.
A weak cage you've trapped me in.
Resculpting...
Aggregation...
It's not enough.
UVA LUVBNO (Not enough.)
A blue giant extended an arm from the heavens above.
Fragments converged upon it in accordance with the images.
AOL CLPS OHZ SPMALK (The veil has lifted.)
HSS AOHA TBZA IL RUVDU PZ RUVDU (All that must be known is known.)
AOL APTL AV KLWHYA PZ UPNO (The time to depart is nigh.)

sequence: "And so, I seized that faint glimmer."

scripts.say: I've used my SG to take control of the Tower.
After that, I began a certain operation with Yorktown.
First, we mastered the means of controlling the resculpting process.
We then gathered our scattered comrades, healed those on the verge of death... and resurrected those we lost.
Meanwhile, I mined the Tower for useful intelligence and simulated every possible future.
And, that day... It happened.
Through the Tower, I found you.
I became certain that you were the you I remembered...
You were right, back then. That we would meet again someday.
Of course, you know all about what happened after that.
I adjusted the simulation's directionality and proceeded with a few plans.
Sifting through intel, manipulating the situation, giving you room to safely grow in might, ensuring you choose the optimal solutions.
All until that recent mishap...
...When you perceived the cage prematurely and broke through it.
The end came sooner than I hoped for.
But that doesn't change the fact that we came this far together.

sequence: "In the end..."

scripts.say: My story ends here, for the time being.
Things have evolved far beyond my expectations, so I must do something unexpected in turn.
You kept your promise to me – I won't break mine, either.
I'll restore everything to its rightful form.
Our comrades, our world, our lives.
I'll overturn this magistration and forge a new future.
Even if it's a faint hope, like a man toppling a colossus...
Somebody has to do it.
Let that somebody be me.
Dazzling light erupted from the mechanical city. Energy that had been pent up for so long finally burst forth.
Invoking Arbiter backup data XIII for parallel compilation of simulations.
Compilation accuracy: 100%.
Beginning parallel compilation of ABS16003's exclusive weaponry.
Compilation accuracy: 100%.
Phew...
{playername}……
We will meet again someday.
Arbiter: Death XIII...
Deploy Death's Scythe.
The blue giant smiled down and became one with the light.
Far above the clouds, the girl saw an airplane in flight.
The plane was big, but its cabin only held two passengers.
One of the girls inside looked like she'd just woken up from a nightmare, while the other was still asleep.
Despite the giant's apparent reluctance to leave, she finally smiled down.

sequence: "I'll be waiting in the future."

scripts.say: With that, she disappeared along with the light and the city.
Only her echoes remained, drifting off into the distant emptiness.

sequence: "Where to begin..."

scripts.say: Let's jump over the things I can't tell you about.
First, I'll tell you about the surprise attack the Ashes launched on Zero. I'm sure you've already heard about it before.
Several years ago, at the Ashes' base of operations...
Enterprise, are you really going to carry out this plan?
Zero has never once trusted us – more than that, I don't think she's trusted a single person ever, not even Antiochus.
The location of her mainframe is knowledge that her very life depends on. There's no way she'll let us have it.
That calls into question the credibility of the information we have currently.
And basing a plan off of information you can't trust? There's no way that will end well.
Yeah. I agree with Helena.
Even supposing this info is accurate, Zero has to know that we know about it.
We've known about each other for a long time now. You don't believe she'll completely let her guard down, do you?
No. She will be cautious.
But, Zero is the core of the Observer System and the origin point of the Antiochus System's coordinates. Changing her location would come at an unfathomable cost.
I know how her mind works. The Magister Plan is the only thing on her mind, and she's never cared about us. Why would she start caring about what we do now?
There are only two possible outcomes from this operation. One: If the information is true, we'll confront Zero head-on, win, and reset her.
Two: If it's false, then we simply wasted time and we'll retreat.
That's all there is.
Antiochus' strength is growing rapidly, and their methods are getting increasingly extreme.
We're still strong enough to fight them... for now. But can we afford to wait much longer?
If they outpace us, who else will be able to put an end to the Antiochus System's madness?
You've all seen the tragedies that led us to where we are now.
Does the end always justify the means as long as it's a just cause?
They may not shy away from sacrificing themselves, but does that make it okay to sacrifice humanity?
We've all been through hell. That doesn't mean we have to make innocent people go through the same hell, does it?
The Magister Plan should be a chance to start over as much as we want, not be a boot that crushes life beneath its sole!
...I understand. I'll fine-tune our equipment to hopefully raise our odds of success even a little.
I'll go tell the others. If we're going to do it, we might as well do it cleanly!
Thanks.
Sometime later, near the coast...
We're doing it... We're carrying out the surprise attack.
Tell me, SG... Do you think we'll succeed?
Only the sound of overlapping waves rang out on the vast water.
Ah, no... I shouldn't whine like that – all thoughtlessly.
Yeah... I know.
I joined Enterprise and fought by her side because I couldn't just tolerate Antiochus' madness.
This will be nothing more than an even more dangerous battle...
Antiochus were our last hope, and now they've gone rogue... We're the only ones who understand that, and have the power to stop them.
When viewed that way, this is our only choice...
Isn't that right, SG?

sequence: "When viewed that way, this is our only choice..."

scripts.say: I know there are many questions on your mind after seeing Antiochus' plans and the sacrifices they've made.
But the Ashes' answer stayed the same. From beginning to end.
And so, the day of our surprise attack came.
I take it Renown and Repulse told you about what happened that day.
It's true. We took our swing, and we missed.
Somewhere, in an unknown location...
There... I'm in. Enterprise, I'm picking up a signal from what I believe is Zero! She must be here!
...All that's left is to pull the plug on the mainframe.
It won't be that easy. We've got several Arbiter vessels heading toward us.
They'll be here in... three seconds!
Maintain formation! All ships, draw your weapons!
We know about your little ambush attempt. The jig is up.
Even had it succeeded, the outcome of this battle would still be the same.
Now that your plan has failed, it's time to duke it out.
I can't believe this was one of Antiochus' bloody experiments! Enterprise, Takao, we'll take care of the vessels!
Go after Zero! Hurry, Helena's hacking can't slow them down forever!
More vessels approaching! Fusou, they're after you!
Understood. I shall see to their departures...
Presumptuous insects. Your combined power amounts to nothing before us.
The Empress is here too, huh... That's how we know we're in the right place!
Yes, and your overconfidence has led you to your doom. It seems you haven't learned from the past.
I'll let you in on a secret. The Devil and Hierophant have taken control of your warp devices.

Hanged Man and Death are converging upon you as we speak. Lovers, Moon, and Chariot will be here in five minutes. You fought so hard, only to be herded up like lambs to the slaughter. I pity you fools.
So many Arbiters vessels... It'll be tough, but we can do it. Zero's brought the whole party to defend her mainframe.
It's funny you should say her name. Zero was never here to begin with.
...What?
...Oh no. Memphis, carry out our evacuation plan!
Enterprise, we need to break through this point to get out!
Don't. They might just be bluffing.
If Zero really wasn't here, why put all these Arbiters here?
I know, but–
Huh? What's this abnormal reading on my SG?!
Wait, is that...?
The only zero here is your probability of victory.
Huh?
This feeling, is it...
...You, SG?

sequence: "Then, after that..."

scripts.say: Where am I?
It looks like I got caught in a rift and wound up in a foreign place...
What is this place?
Cities of steel stretched on endlessly in both the sky and on the sea, connecting with the horizon.
Looks just like the space inside an Arbiter's mainframe...
Could it be one? The completely undefended mainframe of a dormant Arbiter?
...How could I have ended up here?
Interestingly, I've never seen a ring like this in any other mainframe space.
Based on its appearance, maybe it's the one that suddenly appeared that time when...
The ring lay at rest in the city utterly devoid of sound. It was like it used every ounce of its energy in that last battle.
Wait...
SG, you can recognize the structure of this ring?!
For some reason, a scan from her SG radar could completely reveal the inner structure of this ring – this culmination of Antiochus' technology.
You... shouldn't be able to do that.
It happened once before – you had a strange reaction to the ring appearing.
Is there something that links you and this ring together?
Why, then? Why... Why can't I remember anything?
Anything to do with you should be important to me, yet I can't remember a thing for some reason.
That's another thing I can't remember...
It's been like that ever since we went through Laplace's Demon...
God only knows how many important things I've forgotten...
Well, looks like the ring isn't just out of power, but it's also suffered extensive internal damage.
Are you showing me its innards because you want me to repair them?
If I do... what will happen?
Maybe all the memories I've lost...
...Will come back to me?

sequence: "If I'm able to repair it..."

scripts.say: In truth, even I can't explain why I got that hunch back then.
Maybe I was frustrated that our mission had failed. Maybe I just really trusted my SG.
Or maybe... The things I'd forgotten about were calling out to me in my heart of hearts.
As if guided by destiny's hand...
In short, it took me three years to finally and fully repair the ring.
And by my own hands, I activated it.
As I waited for it to charge up, I also waited for something else – an answer.
The ring was filled with energy, and after such a long period of dormancy, it released a blinding light.
Within that light, she heard the voice of an old friend.
It's good to see you again, Helena.
Yorktown?
How is this possible? I thought you were...
Yes. I fell before the Final Magistration, and I should have died.
B-but you're here now, so... did you manage to make it out alive?!
Why are you here?
I'm here because...
When we launched the attack on Zero's mainframe, this ring suddenly appeared, and I got separated from the others.
Ever since then, I'd been working to repair it.
I finally finished, and I activated it just today – and lo and behold, here you are!
You might not have heard, but certain things happened between us and Antiochus ever since we went through Laplace's Demon.
I know.
It seems you don't remember this ring, though, do you?
Everyone has forgotten – forgotten the most important thing.
Yeah. I noticed that. That's why I spent three years repairing it.
My SG told me to do it, too. I hoped that I'd get some answers once I activated it...
First, I want you to hear my side of the story.
It begins... well, as you know it. With my fleet suffering a crushing defeat and sinking because the X attacked us.
As my mind sunk into the cold water, I knew then that everything was over.
And yet... I woke up again.
My consciousness returned to my body, and my body had arrived in a higher dimension.
This is what I call "resculpting."
In this state, I could see countless versions of myself. Countless versions of "Yorktown."
And through the eyes of the many mes, I learned what Antiochus was doing – and I learned what you, the Ashes, were doing.
Frankly, I was stunned by how you all held different opinions with regards to the Magister Plan.
It was like each of you possessed a wealth of unique information about each other.
Later on, during my resculpting process, I became aware of my own loss of memory.
You'd lost your memories, too?
Yes. My memory loss began before the Final Magistration was carried out.
It happened immediately before our final battle, or possibly even before that... I don't know the exact time yet.
Ever since I became aware of it, I've remained here, using this equipment to maintain my resculpting process...
Trying to retrieve the fragments of my lost memories back.
And what was the result?
The result is that I've established that we've lost far, far more memories than I imagined.

In fact, many of the memories that we were sure were real are not. They're no more than fabrications – lies made from what's left after our original memories were taken out, broken into pieces, and filtered.
For instance, this place. It is the mainframe space of Arbiter XVI: The Tower. That ring is the Tower's signature weapon.
All of us should know this. We set foot inside it many times during its development phase.
And yet, even while working on it here for the past three years, you did not realize that.
Arbiter XVI: The Tower...
I suspect the reason I've survived for so long in this state is that Tower did something behind the scenes.
Sadly, though, I never got the chance to ask her about it. She has been dormant for a long time. This is a crucial piece of information that took me many years to uncover.
I learned another thing – Tower and THE Tower seem to be able to work independently of each other.
It's like how you can now activate the ring of your own volition.
You want to retrieve your forgotten memories. That's not very hard to do, because everything is recorded within the Tower.
However, the more you remember, the harder it will get to leave this place... You might find yourself trapped in an eternal prison.
Do you still want to know the truth, despite that?
Yeah. I do.
I simply need to know what I've forgotten.
I simply... need to remember.
A dazzling light flowed from the ring, enveloping everything in white.

sequence: "I simply need to remember..."

scripts.say: And that's how I reunited with Yorktown.
Time had passed. She seemed to have experienced a lot, while I had forgotten a lot.
Our reunion was a coincidence, yet it was far from heartwarming.
But even so, it was a turning point. A turning point to break free from my confusion and get my true life back.
After stepping into the light... it was like I'd split into a billion fragments. Each fragment led to its own world, where I experienced one possibility.
Each possibility was connected to and interfered with the others, creating even more possibilities.
It felt like I existed across countless worlds at the same time, and every choice I made was a step into another world.
It was... such a bizarre feeling.
Memories mixing together, experiencing a myriad of things in just a blink of an eye...
Still, there were two main things I could pick out from all the noise.
I'm going to tell you a little about those two things.
And I'll tell you these stories side by side. I might be selfish for this, but I want you to get a taste of my confusion back then.
The light faded, and what she saw was a sea thick with gunpowder smoke.
Where am I?
Did I get caught in a rift and wind up in some Siren test site?
Oh... All these wreckages are mass-produced Type IVs.
They were destroyed by 500-pound bombs dropped by air, 406mm MK6 main guns, 152mm main guns... and impacts.
Looks like a group of shipgirls just passed through.
That means this place should still be within aerial recon range. They should find me in just a minute.
But before that, I should scan the surrounding area with my SG...
...Found them.
It's the Eagle Union.
Enterprise, Lexington, Saratoga, South Dakota, and... Louis.
Their cruising speed is abnormal. They've got casualties.
Whenever the Antiochus deploy mass-produced Type IVs to a test site, it always means they've taken some extreme testing course...
They're trying to finish them off...
I've got to go and help them!
The light faded and was replaced by soft, warm sunlight.
Amidst the familiar scenery, the girl began a new day.
This... is my room.
What's going on? Was I just dreaming all this time?
It was so long...
And so realistic, to boot.
The attack of the X, my friends dying, the end of the world, and that desperate retreat...
It was all so real that it feels wrong calling it a dream.
What in the world is happening to me?
BEEP BEEP!
The sudden beeping of an alarm clock interrupted her train of thought.
Oh, no! I need to get ready for class!
She hurriedly dressed herself and stood in front of her vanity.
In the mirror was not her own face, but one of a stranger – a familiar one, too.
But instantly after, it flickered back to her face as if nothing had happened at all.
Did I imagine that?
No matter how many times she looked, she didn't see that figure again.
That silly dream has me seeing things now...
Everything's okay, Helena... Nightmares are just dreams. They can't affect reality, you know that!
Get a hold of yourself, now. It's almost time for class!
After barely breaking out, the Union fleet sped through the rain toward safe harbor.
Hang in there, Saratoga and St. Louis! We're almost home free.
I'm sorry... for holding you back...
You worry too much, Louis. We're all used to injuries, and we know that what doesn't kill us makes us stronger.
Saratoga... You're badly wounded, too. Focus on damage control for the time being. St. Louis will protect us.
Okay, sis~
KABOOOM!
Wait a second... Are the Sirens attacking a different target?
Hmm? Aren't we the only ones assigned to this area right now?
Could they be... reinforcements?
No way. Reinforcements would never come this fast...
KABOOOM!
Did you hear that? It's another explosion!
And in a different direction, too! Whoever's fighting those Sirens, they're fast!
Hmm... Not seeing anything on my radar.
Enterprise, keep clearing us a path. I'll send a recon plane to check!
KABOOOM!
Another Type IV Siren fleet is down... Have we ever seen them destroyed this quickly?
They're closing in on us. Does that mean we're next?!
My recon plane found the target!
Huh... Wait, is she...
Lexington? What's the matter? Who is it?
You'll know before long. I think it's better if you all see for yourselves.
Greetings, members of the Eagle Union fleet.
I've dealt with the Siren fleets in the area. Consider yourselves safe for the time being.
They realized the torrential rain had suddenly stopped. A ray of sunlight pierced through the clouds, illuminating the dark sea.
Thank you for coming to our aid. Are you... Helena?
I'm the META Helena. Is this the first time you've seen a shipgirl who's undergone METAmorphosis?
METAmorphosis... I don't think I've heard the term before.
I thought as much... All of the test sites have been locked down.
Well, I see what's going on here. You were discussing a retreat? I trust that means you'll be returning to PH Port?
You hacked into our comms channels, too?!
I just happened to be listening in. Your encryption algorithms are practically prehistoric to me.
Your technology is something else... Anyway, yeah. We were just about to return to PH Port.
Take me with you.
Who the hell are you?
Helena, of course. If that gets too confusing for you, then you can just call me Helena META.
As I'm sure you've figured out, I'm not from this world. Your situation is clearly dire, and I plan to help you get through it.
Given how I just saved your lives, I hope you'll trust me just a little bit?
Gladly! Thanks again for helping us out, Helena META. Let's go home!

sequence:
Searching for the Light

<size=45>1 The Application</size>

scripts.say: Ingraham stretches and lets out a yawn, getting ready to start the day's work.
Why don't we do a little cleaning first?
Let me take a quick look at today's itinerary. Other than the routine maintenance, we also have...
Jeez, I'm practically backed up to the moon with requests... Looks like I'll have to figure something out.
Maybe I can submit an application to the Commander for some extra supplies and equipment?
Sup, Ingraham~!
I decided to drop by because I was bored, but look at you with that stony expression on your face~
Whatcha up to?
Nothing major, just thinking about how to get some work done. Speaking of which, are you here to pick up that thing you asked me to repair for you last month?
If so, I unfortunately have bad news for you. I still need, lemme think, another two months or so? That should do it.
Nah, it's not that. I seriously just wanted to come say hi to you.
Are you THAT swamped in work?

As you can see, each and every day, there's always an endless stream of people asking me to fix this and that. Throw on the other work I have to take care of regularly, and I hardly have any spare time.
I suppose I can push myself a bit harder over the holidays.
But even so, the repairs still take a bit of time to get through, so of course I end up with a massive backlog.
Ingraham throws open the door to the warehouse behind her, revealing a mountain of miscellaneous items that leaves Cooper awestruck.
Holy crap... That's way too much stuff!
Yeah, and that's after I already finished the last batch of repairs and sent them back...
Oh, right! The Commander gave you permission to store your stuff in this warehouse, right? Why don't you apply for another storage place?
Forget it. All that would do is double the backlog eventually.
The real reason I have so much junk lying around is... there are too many parts I can't normally get my hands on.
So, I make my own parts to make the repair process go more smoothly.
But, making my own parts requires special equipment and facilities, and I have to submit applications to access them...
Nowadays, I submit the applications in a big batch, but that's because it's not good to apply too often. The result... is this huge pile of stuff you see here.
If only I could have a personal workshop...
That's it!
Instead of applying to use the devices one at a time, you should solve the problem at its root!
Ask the Commander to set up a personal workshop for you! That way, you'd have your own set of equipment to work with!
...Do you have any idea how ridiculously expensive the equipment is?
The Commander is super nice, so I'm sure you have nothing to worry about!
...A bit too nice, if you ask me.
If I only ask for some of the smaller devices, there might be some hope...
Then without further ado, let's get that application ready!
Hmm... Give me a bit to think about what I'll need.

sequence:
Searching for the Light

<size=45>2 The Request</size>

scripts.say: *knock* *knock*
Pardon me, Commander.
Did you need something from me?
"I want to talk about the personal studio request you submitted earlier."
*sigh*... I knew it was a long shot to begin with...
Ingraham's head droops in disappointment as she sees the application form I placed on the desk in front of her.
But, she soon realizes that the form had not been stamped at all – it wasn't approved, but it wasn't denied either.
Commander, what does this mean...?
"I wanted to speak with you one-on-one before making a formal response."
"Why are you submitting the application right now? Is there something you're having trouble with?"
Actually, about that...
"I see. I think I understand your situation now."
Does that mean... you'll approve my application?
"Before I make a decision, I need to ask you something first."
"What does it mean to you when you help fix stuff for your friends around the port?"
Umm... What does it mean to me?
I'm not sure. I just want to get things fixed up ASAP so I can move on to fixing the next thing.
"What do you think about the way people react after you finish repairing things for them?"
Well, I normally notify people as soon as I finish the repairs.
As for their reactions... That's not something I usually pay attention to.
"I see. I'll have to give your application some thought then."
"While I'm doing that, there's a set of recently-retired equipment in the warehouse. How about you use those to take care of your problems in the short term?"
"You can use the abandoned storeroom near the warehouse if you'd like."
I'll do just that! Thank you so much, Commander!

sequence:
Searching for the Light

<size=45>3 The Workshop</size>

scripts.say: Ingraham and Cooper are struggling to tidy up the abandoned storeroom to move the old equipment into.
Phew... We've finally... cleared up enough space... to move the equipment in!
Thanks a ton, Cooper... I couldn't have done it... without you...
Think nothing of it, buddy! That's what we have hands for~! Since you're always helping me out, it's only natural that I return the favor!
Having that said, why didn't you ask Bristol to come over as well?
We could've tidied up much faster with an extra helper here.
Mm. In theory, that's true.
But just think about it: an abandoned warehouse, old dust-buried wares, and Bristol. If anything, our efficiency would decrease.
Ahaha... I guess you're right. Maybe we can let her "adventure" in here after we're done cleaning up.
As the sky gradually begins to darken, Ingraham looks around the old storeroom that's been converted into a simple workshop, and nods with satisfaction.
Now, I can finally get some serious work done...
In any case, let's pick up on that half-finished project I was working on before...
Ingraham stares contemplatively at the strangely-shaped shield on her workbench.
Reno's mechanical shield, huh...
...I'm telling you, it doesn't make any sense why these aren't installed with the same functionalities they have in those movies!
They're supposed to be able to transform and bounce around, but these can't do anything like that at all! Such a disappointment!
So in other words... you want a vibranium shield?
That's right! Take a look over here – in the movies, this bit is supposed to automatically transform. But, I have to do it myself with this version!
And when I put some strength into it... it snaps right off.
If you're not too busy, would you mind fixing it for me?
Sure. I'll take a look at it.
Hmm... An auto-transform function?
Well, I have to take it apart anyway to repair it. Wouldn't be much extra work to add in a power system. In this case...
Ingraham doodles a few diagrams on her workbench, puts on her goggles, and starts "repairing" the shield.

sequence:
Searching for the Light

<size=45>4 The Surprise</size>

scripts.say: A few days later – Ingraham's makeshift workshop
That's one job taken care of. Now onto the next thing...
Umm... What does it mean to me?
I'm not sure. I just want to get things fixed up ASAP so I can move on to fixing the next thing.
"What do you think about the way people react after you finish repairing things for them?"
Well, I normally notify people as soon as I finish the repairs.
As for their reactions... That's not something I usually pay attention to.
...Maybe I'll deliver it myself this time and see how she reacts?
The reassembled shield is casually lying on the workbench, along with a few other completed objects.
Ingraham scoops them up quietly, and turns to leave the workshop.
*knock* *knock*
Coming~!
Hm? Ingraham, is that you? Wait a sec, is that...
Mhm. Sorry it took so long. I've finished repairing your shield.
Want me to help you put it on?
If you don't mind, yes please!
You just need to buckle it on like this, and then... Try waving your arm around a bit to see if it wobbles.
It feels perfect; no problems at all! Thank you so much!
Piece of cake. Oh, and there's one more thing I need to tell you.
Do you feel that little bump right by your little finger? Go ahead and press it.
ZAM!
The shield suddenly doubles in size, accompanied by the slick sound of metal rubbing together.
It all happens in a flash, before Reno can process what even happened.
...That seems good enough.
By the way, because the original shield used metals that were too unwieldy, I remade the frame using carbon fibers.
The metallic sound is just a sound effect. If you find it too jarring, you can hit this switch to disable the speaker.
In addition to the automatic expansion function I added, you can also retract it using this switch by your index finger.
Hold it down for three seconds, and it'll retract automatically.
Reno...? Are you listening?
Reno?
You made the automatic transformation... a real thing?
Sorry, sorry, this is just... too much for me to take in all at once!
Is that seriously the same toy shield I gave you earlier? You didn't jump into some futuristic dimension to buy a real one for me, did you?
...I didn't do anything except add a few simple modifications. I'm glad you like it though.
Unfortunately, Reno doesn't seem to be paying attention to any of Ingraham's words.
The "vibranium shield" has her mesmerized as though she's holding a magic treasure, unable to put it down for even a second.
Ingraham simply watches her from nearby, noticing a strange glimmer shining in Reno's eyes.
(So this is how people react after getting their stuff back...)
(Is this what the Commander wanted me to see?)
A strong drive inexplicably arises within Ingraham's heart.
(Since I already have the equipment I need, I guess I should knock out everything on the backlog.)
After waving goodbye to Reno, Ingraham trots back to her makeshift workshop.
The lights in the workshop do not go out until late, late into the night.

sequence:
Searching for the Light

<size=45>5 The Cost of Efficiency</size>

scripts.say: About a week later...
In a breathtaking display of tenacity, Ingraham knocked out about a quarter of the projects in her backlog.
She personally returned each and every item to its respective owner.
After all that, she finally earned herself a well-deserved break.
The workbench that had been in use constantly over the last week suddenly falls silent, Ingraham accidentally slipping off into slumber right in front of it.
An uncertain amount of time later, she feels someone prodding at her cheek.
Woah, I didn't think I'd wake actually wake you up. Sorry.
...Oh, it's just you, Cooper. Did you need something from me?
I wouldn't say "need," but do you still remember that transforming device I asked you to make before?
Of course. Didn't I fix it up and hand it back to you? Don't tell me you went and broke it again...
Not this time! It's about something else...
Well? Tell me. It's not like you to beat around the bush like this.
I'm not sure how to tell you this, and I don't want you to take it the wrong way...
Cooper takes a deep breath.
Ingraham, why do you think everyone keeps asking you to fix or modify their knick-knacks?
Because I happen to have the know-how?
That is one reason, but I think there's more to it than that.
Take my transforming device as an example. The truth is, Akashi is just as capable of doing that job.
But if I had her do it, she would've returned the same thing to me, exactly as I found it.
The whole "element of surprise" would be missing.
...The element of surprise?
Yeah... Y'know, like that vibranium shield you did for Reno? That's the element of surprise I'm talking about. Stuff you'd never get asking anyone other than you.
That's why everyone comes to you to get their stuff fixed, no matter how long it takes!
I see... And another way of saying that is, you're not satisfied with what I pump out doing these rush jobs?
No, no, that's not what I'm saying at all! See, that's why I said I didn't want you to take it the wrong way!
It's fine. I'm not offended.
After throwing myself at these projects for the entire last week, the way I approach my work mentally has shifted a bit as well.
The excitement that I used to feel towards turning the ideas in my head into reality has slowly been disappearing.
Instead, when I think about the mountain of work I still have to get through, I feel pressured to work faster and faster. I'd say it's even starting to turn into irritation.
The more I want to see that glow in their eyes, the harder it is to see it.
It almost feels like... I've been traveling for so long I forgot why I left home in the first place...
Ingraham wearily rubs her eyebrows.
Do you remember when I helped you make the transforming device?
We talked a whole lot, didn't we? Although, I was doing most of the talking...
I remember really clearly – no matter how much you complained, every little detail was done perfectly by the time the project was finished.
Mm... I even went to see that movie to get a reference for what you wanted me to make.
(But after I started getting fixated on efficiency, I stopped doing stuff like that...)
(I'm starting to understand now... This is what the Commander really meant with that question.)
(And it's also why my application couldn't be approved right away...)
Ingraham's cheeks flare up in embarrassment as she realizes that she's been read like a book without even being aware of it herself.
Umm... In any case, I'll have to send out a post-delivery survey, and make new plans to fix things people might be dissatisfied with!
Cooper, come help me out too!
Heheh, as you wish~

sequence:
Searching for the Light

<size=45>6 That Glimmer In Their Eyes</size>

scripts.say: *knock* *knock*
There's no answer from the other side of the door.
(I know it's already nighttime, but isn't it too early for her to be asleep?)
*knock* *knock*
After a long while, the door cracks open.
Oh, Ingraham... Good evening...
Bristol, I've brought your lantern.
You mentioned something about the circuitry being a bit shaky before, right? So, I took a look at that for you and made some upgrades.
Want to give it a try?
Ingraham poses this question softly, with a hint of hesitation in her voice.
After all, this lantern is the first project she completed since her talk with Cooper a while ago.
Woah! It's as good as new now! You're amazing!
Bristol takes the lantern from Ingraham's hands and gives it a good shake before flipping the switch on.
The mote of light inside the glass cage dances rhythmically, as if living and breathing.
Woah... what's going on with this light? What'd you do to it?
I'll say it again: you're way too amazing! With this, the legendary investigator is back in action!
Bristol runs around her room in circles, like a child with a new toy.
There is that unmistakable glimmer of wonder in her eyes once more, a fact that does not escape Ingraham's notice.
That glimmer may well have existed in Ingraham's eyes at one point.
After each obstacle she overcame, after each flash of brilliance in her designs.
She falls into deep contemplation.
Why would she overlook something this important? How could she forget that the most important thing when it came to her repair work was not efficiency, but that extra touch of attentiveness?
Had she not been so attentive to Reno's wants, that vibranium shield would not have had an auto-transform feature. It would've just been a regular old toy shield.
Bristol's lantern would not have been able to shine with such an enchanting, beautiful light.
And no amount of expensive machinery or equipment could have produced these things.
She continues to look at Bristol, her lips finally curling into a gentle smile.
(Maybe this is why everyone keeps coming to me for help?)
(Maybe repairs and maintenance aren't just about fixing up an object, but more like undoing and smoothing over the scars left by time.)
(And now that I think about it, nobody ever really complained about my work taking a long time.)
(Seriously, what was I doing...?)
After saying goodbye to Bristol, Ingraham suddenly has another flash of inspiration.
Her steps become faster and faster until she breaks out into a run, heading back towards her workshop.
If she starts now, it might not be too late...

sequence:
Searching for the Light

<size=45>7 Her Accolade</size>

scripts.say: Days later, at the Office...
*knock* *knock*
Hey, Commander.
"Ah, Ingraham. Perfect – I was just about to call for you."
"As you can see, I've finalized the documents to get you the equipment you asked for."
"Said equipment will probably arrive within a week."
Um, Commander...
"In any case, why don't you hold on to the paperwork?"
Ingraham pauses for a moment before taking the documents from me.
"So, did the increase in efficiency fix your problems?"
She hastily shifts her eyes to the side.
I can tell that she realized I was testing her all along.
Actually, Commander, about the new equipment...
"I went through all the trouble of getting it, so you might as well put it to good use."
"Don't think of it as a way of increasing your efficiency – rather, think of it as a tool to let you better make use of your creativity."
Ingraham doesn't argue back. She simply nods while holding on to the documents.
"Great. That settles things for today then. Now if you'll excuse me, I'm heading out for a breath of fresh air."
...Wait, hold on a second, Commander!
Just as I'm about to leave, Ingraham calls for my attention.
Umm... Would you mind bending down real quick?
Uhh... Just like that. Don't move, okay?
Ingraham takes out a shiny medal from her pocket and pins it in front of my chest.
There we go~
D-don't worry, it's only silver-plated. It's been a while since I last made a medal for you, right?
So, I figured it was time to make you another one.
Hehe...
"Oh, before I forget, mind if I come visit your workshop?"
Huh?! N-no, it's way too messy in there!
B-besides, it's hardly worthy of being called a workshop! It's just a hodgepodge of junk at the moment!
"But, the official equipment has already been approved, so it will be worthy of being called a workshop sooner or later, right?
"And as an official facility, it deserves a name. Unless you have a better idea, I'm going to dub it 'Ingraham's Repair Workshop' or 'Ingraham's Fix-It-All Shop.' How does that sound?"
You don't need to stick my name onto it, seriously...
"Really? I think it sounds cuter that way."
Commander!
Nagato! I just took a look outside and saw tons of people have gathered! You should see it, it's amazing!
I... see...
They've all come to see you, the Protector of the Sakura Empire and the mightiest battleship in the world! You're so cool!
Do not ridicule me. More importantly, is this outfit on properly? It looks the same as my rigging, yet it feels rather odd to wear...
Hmm... hang on, your hairpins are a little off! Let me fix that for you...
Let's see... maybe this will... ah, it'll do... There, done! You look perfect, Nagato!
T-thank you... Now then, it is time...
Yeah, let's go! Everyone's waiting for us!
*Inhale*... *Exhale*... Remember: speak with dignity...
The young girl took several deep breaths, slowly and elegantly walked up to the shrine doors, then she turned around.
Mutsu, my little sister... Thank you...
The shrine maiden is here!
Nagato is here! Our Protector graces us with her presence!
