scripts.say: According to the information we have, the Northern Parliament is in peril and even the commander is fighting on the front lines.
I can only pray for everyone's safety.
You don't seem like the praying type. Worried about the commander~?
It is our directive to escort the commander back to the Royal Islands. Surely you have no objections to those orders?
Nope, none at all~
...Everyone, I'd like to remind you that there may be more pressing matters than how the commander and the Northern Parliament are faring...
Is the Iron Blood making their move?
The recons we sent out seem to have found the enemy fleet... And it looks like a storm is coming for us.
A storm? My apologies, but I'm not observing anything to corroborate that...
I'm talking about the enemy. Tirpitz and the Scharnhorst sisters are there, as well as Deutschland and Graf Spee...
Then there's Prinz Eugen, Admiral Hipper, and a massive number of mass-produced ships.
Those tin buckets stand no chance against us! We'll smash them to pieces if they try to approach our transport fleet!
Do we know where they're headed?
Let's see... They seem to be coming straight at us.

..How is that possible? Unlike the much larger transport fleet, we should've been concealed the entire time. Besides, they just made contact with the escort fleet, and we haven't seen any ships get inside our detection range...
That means our communications must have been intercepted.
All right, we can speculate about that later! A ridiculously huge fleet is coming straight at us, so we need to decide if we're going to fight or run!
We've already been spotted, so I don't think running will do us any good at this point. We'd best call the main fleet and engage the enemy at once.
As Her Majesty planned, I shall destroy the Iron Blood's main fleet!
The Northern Lights actually came out at a time like this...
The only one who could've devised this plan is Eugen... Nay, it must have been the "assistant," Friedrich der Große.
Of course it's her plan. But you know, she's such a stickler about the details, it's killing me...
...Oh my, is that a Royal recon plane? What are we ever to do if they "find out" about our plans?
Now, for the next move...
Prinz Eugen, we've intercepted a transmission from the Royal Navy's supporting fleet.
Well done. Ah, how proud I am of our wonderful Iron Blood technology... Ehehe~
...I wonder whose name I should use next. Maybe using that little queen's name will be a bit more believable?
Prinz Eugen... You're having too much fun with this...
Eh? It's not like I particularly enjoy my job... But you also wouldn't want to face the Royal Navy head-on, would you?
Anyway, I'm going to go relay the proper timing of the attack to the submarines.
I know, I know... But, how long will the Royal Navy continue to move according to our expectations?
The submarines are the "wedges" that will fracture the Reenactment. What matters is that "They" will appear there, not whether we can actually draw away the escort fleet.
And of course, we can't have our little support fleet here getting in the way, now can we?
Admiral Hipper's group has broken off from the main fleet and is rapidly approaching us!
They won't even let us stall for time, huh?
However, they've now split up their forces. Even if we are unable to take on the entire main force, we should be more than capable of taking on a force of destroyers and cruisers.
Sheffield is right. I'll try to head toward Howe's position as I fight.
Hopefully that's the only trick they have up their sleeves... Phew...
My eye holds the forbidden power of bewitchment! The Devilish Idol shall teach you the true meaning of fear! Writhe in utter defeat!
My eye controls the infinite darkness of undying night! Kneel in terror before Vampire, and tithe your fresh blood!
What?! A trueblood...?!
Um, girls, what are you two doing over there...
I'd like to know too! I never thought there'd be another person on the same wavelength as Z36...
I've heard much about you, Admiral Hipper. It's a pleasure to meet you in person. I am Perseus, Royal Navy aircraft carrier.
Huhh? A pleasure? You've already started attacking us!!
A Lady of the Royal Navy must conduct herself with grace and elegance at all times. With that out of the way, I hope that we can have a cordial relationship.
...Yeah, cordial my ass...
Damnit...! You coward! If you wanna fight, face me fair and square!
That would be strategically disadvantageous, so please forgive me for being unable to accept your proposal.
Hey, get your frilly ass back here! Gaaah...! You're not getting away with this!
Sorry, Hipper, Vampire and the others got away...
Don't worry, it's not your fault. There's only so much you can do with all those planes circling over us.
They might be a pain to deal with, but they'll just make better for prey this way. I already told you that before, didn't I?
Thanks for holding Hipper back. We should be safe for a while.
I don't think so. The Iron Blood's main fleet has already joined up with Hipper.
How are their battleships moving that fast?!
Perseus, are you absolutely certain that the Iron Blood's main fleet has joined up with Admiral Hipper?
What do you mean...? I'm sure I saw a ship in the distance.
It might just be my imagination, but could you send your recon planes a bit closer to the Iron Blood fleet?
I don't mind, but that runs the risk of it getting shot down... Wait, what's this?
Tirpitz and Scharnhorst's anti-air guns aren't responding...
Do they not feel like wasting ammo on a single recon plane? No, this has to be...
I knew it. The "main fleet" is actually a bunch of dummies.
Vampire, Perseus, let's turn around and take out the enemy.
The evidence was clear. A speed that was inconsistent with that of a battleship. Anti-air weapons that didn't react... In other words, "Tirpitz is not here."
Gosh, we almost got tricked by their decoy.
It's only natural that we'd be wary of a main fleet.
Barents Sea - Royal Navy Main Fleet
We've just passed the Svalbard Islands! Soon, we'll enter the Northern Parliament's waters.
Thank you, Icarus. Your experience has been invaluable.
Hehe, escorting is my forte after all!
The transport fleet has made it past the halfway point safely... So far, we haven't seen anything out of the ordinary.
Edinburg, make sure to check your communications equipment regularly. Do keep in mind that a high-intensity aurora like this is likely to affect radio transmissions.
Yes, I know... So far, all communication equipment is working correctly and we haven't received any transmissions.
Hearing that the Iron Blood would be coming out to play was getting me quite motivated. It would have been an excellent opportunity to display my charismatic leadership after all.
Is that really necessary? Wouldn't your reputation improve if we just safely delivered the cargo and brought back the commander?
W-well, of course, but wouldn't it be a bit boring if things ended like this? See, I'm all decked out to fight the Iron Blood's main fleet!
About that... I heard that Bismarck hasn't been commanding the fleet directly as of late, and has delegated that responsibility to some "assistants."

Tirpitz, Graf Spee, and the Scharnhorst sisters all suffered various degrees of damage during prior confrontations, so even if their main fleet showed up, I don't think it'd be the kind of battle that Valiant is hoping for.
It's a pity we won't be getting any fireworks to go with this aurora...
But I, Valiant, the honourable Queen Elizabeth-class battleship, will not underestimate our foes! I'll show these Iron Blood cowards that they have no claim upon this route!
(I wonder if I'm supposed to break out into applause now...)
By the way, I noticed that we've only engaged with enemy submarines so far...
Better yet, why don't we just send a message to the Iron Blood fleet and challenge them to a decisive battle? We're ready for them after all—
W-wait, didn't we just say to not underestimate the enemy? Something like that wouldn't be advisable!
The quickest path to victory seems to be duking it out with the enemy, face-to-face.
The Northern Parliament urgently needs our help, so why don't we tell Her Majesty that we'll have to teach those nasty Sirens a lesson before we can bring the commander back?
Unless something drastic happens, I don't think the Northern Parliament will allow us to directly intervene on the battlefield. Hmm, what should we do...
(We can always ask for permission after we get there... But I wonder why the Northern Parliament is still so reserved about asking for aid, even in their current situation...)
(I shouldn't overthink things though... We still have to get there safely after all.)
It's a message! We've got a message from the support fleet!
The Iron Blood's main fleet is moving towards the support fleet! Tirpitz and the Scharnhorst sisters are with them!
—Requesting immediate assistance from the main fleet!
The Iron Blood have finally shown themselves...!
Heh, so they've brought out their big guns... Too bad that won't save them from Valiant's charismatic leadership!
Just as Her Majesty predicted!
Valiant, let's hurry and back them up! It's time to drive the Iron Blood from the seas!
Exactly! Members of the Royal Navy Main Fleet, change course and advance towards the Iron Blood fleet!
Whoosh————!
Lady Valiant, watch out!
Woah! ...Nice shot, Edinburgh! ...But damn, was that a Siren carrier just now?
We just got a message from the Northern Parliament! Some Sirens have broken through the defense line and are making their way towards us!
Bloody hell, they could've told us before the Sirens got here. What's the Northern Parliament doing anyway?!
Icarus, any news about the commander?
Yes, there's an addendum! The commander says that the breach in the defensive line has been fortified, but there weren't enough forces to spare to chase after the Sirens...
Phew... At least the commander is safe. But... we're going to be in a spot of trouble over here.
Should we deal with the Sirens first, or back up our allies first...
What do you think?! The Sirens are popping out left and right, so we're not going to be able to go anywhere without dealing with them first!
You're right... We won't be able to accomplish our objective unless we defeat the Sirens.
Apparently, a new type of Siren appeared from the Iceberg Stronghold! Please be careful!
Great, the commander and the Eagle Union's intel gathering has pulled through for us again.
Everyone, prepare to face the Sirens!
Reloading complete! Icarus, commencing all-out assault!
Your fighting style is a lot more dynamic than your appearances might suggest. Heh.
Anyone who would harm my friends will be punished! With overwhelming firepower!
But... I wish I actually had overwhelming firepower just like you, Howe...
I don't think it would be possible to give battleship-tier firepower to a destroyer.
Well, let's just do the best we can given our options.
Your bravery is commendable, but there's really no benefit for you to...
But still, it'd be great to be able to overwhelm the enemy with great firepower...
I thought I had a good grasp of the situation from looking over the data, but this new type of Siren... is far more troublesome than I anticipated!
The escort fleet wouldn't be able to handle enemies like these if the transport fleet gets attacked.
We can't afford to waste any more time here and group up with the transport fleet.
But, the support fleet is still drawing the attention of the Iron Blood! If we don't go help out...
We can't just abandon our escort fleet, but the support fleet needs our help too...
Get in contact with the Naval HQ! Worst case scenario, the support fleet still has the option to retreat to the Royal Islands!
But then, the Iron Blood fleet would turn around and pincer us...
If that's what they want, then we'll give it to them! They shall know that Valiant loses to no foe!
I'm trying to send the message, but I'm not getting a response...!
This must be the doing of those accursed Sirens! We don't even know if the message got through to HQ... Damn, what do we do now?
Th-then, our only option is to go all-out...
Valiant, your decision?
Hmph! I won't be made a fool of in front of Elizabeth! Let's review our options.
Anyway, our primary objective is to protect the transport fleet so that it can deliver its cargo to the Northern Parliament — that's right, we don't need to defeat the Iron Blood, only repel them.
The support fleet might be in trouble, but with their speed, they should be able to avoid the worst. The same can't be said for the slow-moving convoy.
Indeed. If the Sirens were to attack, the transport fleet would be fine, but all our cargo would be lost.
Right, and given the dire situation the commander and the Northern Parliament are in, that is an unacceptable outcome.

A certain ship was supposed to attend a joint banquet hosted by the Royal Navy and Iris Libre—
Enjoying fine tea overlooking the Méditerranée, and even finer ladies... Ah, how long it's been since I've indulged in a Royal Navy banquet.
I'm glad our event is to your liking.
Thank you for attending, Littorio.
The pleasure is mine, Cardinal. I've heard that the Church of the Iris Orthodoxy has blossomed once more under your leadership. Congratulations.
As a member of Azur Lane, Iris Libre will continue to fight against the Sirens. As for Sardegna...
Well, Veneto and I are working hard to change things, but you know how the Senate is. Nothing's going to happen overnight unfortunately.
Is that so... Then, after this banquet is over... we'll go back to being enemies again.
Thanks for the warning. I wouldn't want to get attacked at night by the woman who stole my heart... Or would I? Hehe~
Oh dear...
Big sister?
What's the matter, Unicorn?
There's a message from the headquarters...
From headquarters? I suppose it's fine if Littorio hears it. What's it about?
All right...
Um, Her Majesty is in an extremely desperate situation after being ambushed by the Iron Blood fleet at Scapa Flow...
No...
Queen Elizabeth...! We can't just sit here...
What is the Iron Blood doing there...? This is going to turn the rules of engagement on its head again...
Eagle Union - NY City
Enterprise, Washington! I just heard the news...
Yes. I've pieced together what happened. It seems like the Iron Blood was targeting Scapa Flow this whole time.
What could they possibly be after? There's not even a base over there...
I wonder what's going to happen with the Royal Navy...
It's hard to read what the Iron Blood is planning. Are they trying to expand south, or perhaps...
That's way over Sister Sara's head...
For now, just stay alert. Contact all our ships, and be on the lookout for enemy attacks.
A colorful band of light shimmers across the night skies of the Barent Sea, illuminating the sea along with the stars.
So this is an aurora... Absolutely breathtaking...
Like a sash of light weaving across the infinite darkness... Ahh, how it makes this eye resonate with power...
What do you mean by that...?
That's not anything you need to learn, Hermione. The fact that we can see the aurora means that there aren't any clouds, which also means...
It'll be easier for both us and the enemy to spot each other... right?
Woah...! An Iron Blood recon plane has shown up, tailing a mass-produced ship!
I knew they'd be here!
Soon, they'll bear down upon us with their entire force... The illumination from the aurora has given them the perfect window to strike.
The sky is changing way too quickly! Is this The World's influence...?!
Jamaica, now's the time to tap into the power stored within your eye!
(Those two may be an odd duo, but it's working out...)
Eagle, your hunch was right. However, we're not going to be able to change the weather, so we'll have to make the best of this situation...
That's right. I'll suppress their air power, so stay vigilant of the enemy submarines and protect the transport fleet!
At the Northern Parliament
The Sirens hoped to cut off our supply convoy during that last attack. Fortunately, the Royal Navy's escort fleet cleared the way.
Officially, the Royal Navy's operation ended in failure... and they were savagely defeated by the Iron Blood...
The movements of the Iron Blood and the Sirens were too synchronized. Don't believe it's a coincidence for a second.
However, the arrival of the convoy has improved the situation in the Baltic Sea. The relief supplies have been distributed appropriately.
The front lines received the bulk of the aid. We're also starting to repair the damaged transports.
This success was made possible by the bravery of everyone in the transport operation. We will sing their names as heroes.
As expected, the Iron Blood would not dare sabotage the supplies needed to fight the Sirens.
Without the commander's leadership, we would not have seized victory without devastating losses...
There is no longer any reason to doubt the commander's importance. The Royal Navy seems to also be focusing on other issues at the moment.
As such, the commander is no longer in a position to refuse requests to stay with us.
We've finished our assessment. It's time to move on to the next phase.
Perhaps, it is time to show our new comrade what we found in the frigid ocean...
Lurk quietly... Approach quietly... and STRIKE QUIETLY...!
There you are, Iron Blood submarine!
What... How'd you find me?!
Turn back, Iron Blood submarine. This is the escort fleet of the Royal Navy's Polar Transport Fleet. We ask that you turn back at once!
How bold of you to attack a convoy that I'm personally escorting!
Fat chance of that happening! Our main fleet will be here shortly, so you should just give up before things get ugly!
(The Iron Blood's main fleet is coming...? What should we do...?)
...Apparently, you have no intention of surrendering your cargo.
But too bad for you! Today's going to be my big break, and you're just going to be my stepping stones towards greatness!
Let me guess, the next thing you're going to say is, "Come at me!" In that case...
Hermione, commencing anti-submarine combat! For Her Majesty the Queen!
Crap, they're really getting serious, and I need to reload my torpedo tubes... We'll settle this later!
After forcing Hermione to swerve sharply to evade her last torpedo, U-73 quickly dove under the waves and retreated from the battlefield.
After all that talk, she didn't even last an episode.
Hmm... It seems like she didn't bring an entire wolfpack with her. Was she really just acting alone...?
I've neutralized their air force as well.
As for other submarines... I'm not picking up on any. Does this mean we've successfully repelled them?
Mm. Any damages?
I don't think so. Nobody got hit, right?
...How bizarre.
You're right. It makes no sense to send such a small force to attack an entire convoy.
Maybe they were just trying to gauge our strength? That submarine said something about the main fleet being on its way...
Not sure. What do you think they could learn from an engagement like that...?
Th-that's right, even if there was a main fleet on its way, it'd be too late to respond by the time they reported back.
Wait a second... What if they were trying to lure us into a certain position...
You mean, they were trying to separate us from the support fleet?
Oh no! The support fleet is in danger!
It's too early to say that. The Iron Blood shouldn't know that another fleet is even here, let alone their position.
I'll send another recon out to re-assess the situation. Hermione, Jamaica, both of you stay vigilant.
We're receiving communications from the Naval HQ. It's from... Her Majesty?!
Notifying all fleets! Tirpitz and the Scharnhorst sisters are... Anyway, the Iron Blood's main fleet is heading towards the Barents Sea!
Have all ships turn around right now and intercept their fleet!
They're bringing all those battleships out here? Great, that...
...shouldn't be right... Huh? Can you repeat that again?
Sure. The message ordered us to turn around and intercept their fleet...
It's true that the Royal Navy doctrine encourages us to proactively take the fight to the enemy if they seek to assemble their forces against us... but even when we're on a transport mission?
If we turned around and left, what would the transport fleet do?
That's right... And if the Northern Parliament and Eagle Union get attacked, they'll be in big trouble...
I don't think Her Majesty would choose this place for a decisive confrontation with the Iron Blood. Surely there's some kind of mistake...
I'll double-check!
U-73 retreated, and so did the air squadron. Now, the Royal Navy fleet is safe for the time being~
They're still maintaining their defenses... The escort fleet is staying vigilant.
Well, what'd you expect from such an optimistic plan? It's not like an escort fleet would randomly abandon the convoy. Like, what the heck is that lush thinking anyway?
Who, Eugen? Didn't she tell us to wait patiently for an opening?
If we wait a bit longer, maybe the escort fleet will decide to leave... Even if they don't, we'll still have our chance soon.
Sure, sure. I've got time to kill anyway~
Unknown Location
Eugen, you sure took your sweet time. The hell were you doing?
Calm down, Hipper. Your cute face will get all wrinkly if you pout so much~
I can't calm down because you're the one in charge of the operation.
Is that so? Isn't our mighty Tirpitz the flagship this time?
Anyway, to put on the finishing touches...♪
Do I get to sortie yet? You've got some nerve to keep me waiting like this!
No matter how airtight they think their plan is, we'll stab it full of holes.
Ahaha! Let's show those pompous bastards an explosively good time!
(...I've always been alone... But now, with everyone...)
(I know how you feel, Spee. Cherish this moment, for you are needed for the Iron Blood to achieve victory.)
Now, mercurial light of the North... How shall we bend you to achieve our victory?
If you wish to ensnare the core fleet of the Iron Blood, you may not like what you find in your net.
Now, show me how you dance, my little queen and your loyal followers~♪
Victory to the Iron Blood!
Barents Sea - Royal Navy Supporting Fleet
The previous Great War, huh? Vampire, you already know what that was like, right?
Of course. I have more experience fighting the Sirens than any of you.
Back then, the Iron Blood and Royal Navy both fought the Sirens together as a part of Azur Lane.
But now, we're traversing through this endless darkness to try to eliminate them...
Suddenly, a dazzling array of light wove through the sky, illuminating the position of the Royal Navy's supporting fleet.
The shimmering expanse mapped the starry sky onto the water's surface, bathing Perseus and the others in a scene of fairytale-like beauty.
My goodness...
This is...
...It's like a painting coming to life...
Usually the paintings try to capture this kind of beauty, but your point is well taken.
Do note, however, that we have an increased probability to be detected and attacked because of the increased visibility.
Do people have no sense of romance these days...
First of all, it is abnormal and unscientific for such a large-scale aurora to suddenly appear out of nowhere.
Natural phenomena like this do appear in the Polar North, though it is strange that we didn't see any signs of an aurora given the visibility.
That is reasonable, and I may be overthinking things, but please be very careful.
Sheffield, all that worrying cannot possibly be good for your health.
There is such splendour before you, and it would simply be sinful to not relax and appreciate it~
My sincerest apologies, but we are in the middle of an operation. Miss Vampire, if your soul is in need of "cleaning," you may perhaps find my "services" adequate?
Ah, um, I shall pass on that!
Vampire, don't you think it's a good idea to have your casket freshened up a little?
...Huh?

sequence:
Tales From the Count's Castle

<size=45>1 The Castle's Beckoning</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
It was a slow day. There was strangely little work on my plate and I had more free time than I knew what to do with.
Can I come in, Commander?
The door handle turned, and into my office stepped Prinz Eugen.
What's with that look? You think I'm here to ask for some laborious favor?
You're only half-right. It's sort of a favor, but it's nothing laborious.
"I've got work today. Maybe not much, but I can't just put it on the backburner."
But, compared to your average workday, you've got plenty of free time. Your secretary told me.
"Guess you've got me there."
First of all, relax. I won't bite. I'm only here to invite you to test out the escape room Akashi's been working on. Free of charge.

options.content: "You mean, 'invite me to be a guinea pig'?"
"Akashi? Free? There's got to be a catch."

scripts.say: Think of it this way: you could spend the day alone in your office, doing paperwork... OR, you could get out and do something fun.
I had to do a double-take as well. The only catch is that you give her your feedback afterwards.
So, what do you say? An opportunity to have fun like this only comes once in a blue moon.
Port - Undisclosed location
Seydlitz came over, put a blindfold over my eyes, and led me to the escape room.
The set hasn't been completed just yet, and the blindfold was to prevent being spoiled on some solutions. Allegedly.
Based on the time it took to get here, I sensed this escape room was a lot, lot bigger than I anticipated.
We have arrived, Commandant. I'll remove your blindfold now.
The set was designed after a lavish medieval castle.
What is it, Commandant? Is there something in this room that makes you feel uncomfortable?
The lighting here is quite dim for the sake of atmosphere, and I can see why it might induce anxiety in some people. Are you all right? Good...
Now then, allow me to give you an introduction to this escape room.
Seydlitz explained that this was a castle filled with vampires, and I was a lone human who'd wandered inside.
Ordinarily, this location would start with a vampire chase segment. Since this is a demo, however, we changed it into a tutorial to ease you into your role.
Here, please take this. It's a communicator Eugen provided me with.
If you happen to get stuck, or run into... danger... please use it to call for help.
"Danger? What kind of danger?"
I'm afraid I don't know, I'm only relaying Eugen's message. She also asked me to tell you, "Keep going until the end. Don't give up."
That should be all. If you'll excuse me, I must go and get into my costume.
All the shipgirls you'll encounter here, me included, will be playing a role. Please keep that in mind and try to play along.
Best of luck to you, Commandant! I hope you'll have an enjoyable time!
Armed with information and a communicator, I began my foray into the castle...

sequence:
Tales From the Count's Castle

<size=45>2 The First Trial</size>

scripts.say: I entered a big hall, after which the doors shut behind me with a creak.
Heeheehee...
A girly giggle echoed forth from the darkness.
That smell about you... You're not one of us.
Rows of candles along the walls lit up one after another, illuminating the staircase up to the second floor, where pallid girls sat upon grand thrones.
Welcome to our abode, my lost, darling human.
"Most would reel in fear at the sight of Emden, but not you. Eager to become my next meal, hmm?"
They had a menacing aura about them, like that of a video game final boss. I'd walked into the wrong neighborhood...
Sensing I'd messed up, I dialed a number on my communicator. No response.
What an interesting plaything you have. Whatever its intended purpose, it will not help you in here.
It seemed they were as committed to their roles as I was committed to seeing the escape room to its conclusion.
"Emden isn't terribly hungry, but you'll do as a means to relieve boredom."
You're in luck, poor little human. Emden would like to play a little game. What say you?
I walked up to Emden's throne, expecting something like a chessboard... It was a stone tablet set up for a game of tic-tac-toe.
This is all we've had, and will have, to kill time for an eternity.
Emden has never won a single game, nor ever lost a single game.
Breaking this curse and resolving Emden's eternal grievance may grant you the key to escaping this place.
"You're saying you'll let me go if I manage to beat you? All right."
I knew, however, that normal tic-tac-toe always ends in a draw. There had to be some trick I was allowed to use.
Are you ready to begin, human?
If this was the only way out, so be it. I sat down and began the match.

sequence:
Tales From the Count's Castle

<size=45>3 Neverending Stalemate</size>

scripts.say: To nobody's surprise, the game ended in a draw.
Nothing has changed, it would seem.
Alas, so not even you can break the eternal curse within this tablet.
Drinking every drop of blood you have to offer may quench our thirst, but it does naught to dispel our grievance.
"I've changed my mind, human. Submit to Emden and become our pet. You will be granted eternal life and experience boundless pleasure as our pet."
You may instead try one more time if you wish, my darling human. But, if you fail, I'm afraid your last moments shall be spent atop a dinner plate.
"The choice is obvious. Now make it."
To give up, or press on. The pressure was mounting on me. I answered...

options.content: Challenge Emden to a second match

scripts.say: So you chose submission. Humans really are deplorably weak.
Be that as it may, it's what Emden was hoping for. Come hither, our darling pet♡
"Your induction into the family comes later. For now, just rest your head on Emden's chest and be whisked away to sleep♥"
"Be not afraid." Have no worries. It will feel like no more than a brief nap.
Emden's soft whispers were like anesthesia. I felt my mind slip away... into... a slumber...

sequence: Bad Ending – Emden's Eternal Vassal

scripts.say: When I woke up, both Emden and Yorck were nowhere to be seen. The stone tablet was gone, replaced by a ruby necklace.
You jumped straight into that bad ending... Oh well, since this is a demo, we'll let you keep playing.
That item – the Cursed Blood Necklace – is your prize for... "beating" this trial. Take it with you.
Eugen's voice echoed through the hall. It wasn't coming from the communicator, but rather somewhere in here.
The path to the next trial's open. Good luck, little human~
"You have some damn nerve, filthy human."
Emden's tone took a drastic turn after I asked for a second match.
Are you certain, my dear human? This is your last chance to break the curse.
Should you not present a satisfying solution, Emden shall – with no exaggeration – devour you.
Emden only said I have to change the outcome of the match, not that I have to win.
I reasoned that was the key to lifting the curse...
The match is over... Emden is the victor.
Fascinating. You knew you could not win, so you conceded victory.
Congratulations, my darling human. You've dispelled the curse of perpetual draws.
As Emden promised, you shall be granted passage through this place.
"Yorck, hand the human its prize."
Yorck stepped up and handed me a necklace adorned with a ruby.
This relic is the Cursed Blood Necklace. Remember its name, for it will surely be of use.
The doors to my front gave way to a corridor. It seemed I'd passed the first trial.

sequence:
Tales From the Count's Castle

<size=45>4 The Second Trial</size>

scripts.say: After solving a series of small puzzles, the path opened to a second big hall.
Door after door after door lined the walls. At the hall's center was... Elbing and U-47, lying on the floor.
Commander? Is that really you? Goodness, I can't believe you've made it this far.
Though, I shouldn't be. I expected you'd get stuck on the puzzles and succumb to Emden's temptation, so of course the opposite happened...
(Psst. You're out of character.)
(Oops, sorry...)
Human, you stand before the successor of a dark bloodline. This... is my servant.
My clan owns this castle, but Emden and her crones have us trapped here. They put a curse upon me, depriving me of all my strength...
These doors you see are an illusion of their making. Choose the wrong one, and you are doomed to wander through darkness for all eternity.
My master could easily dispel their trickery, had she her strength. Help her regain it, and you too shall be able to move forward.
There you have it. Will you aid me?
Eek...! Wh-why the sudden princess carry?!
"It must be cold, lying on the floor. Let's at least get you seated on this couch."
Ahem... You have my gratitude, human.
Umm... Resting to regain my strength is an option, but 'tis a terribly slow process. Emden is bound to catch on to us...
For a hasty recovery, I require... a meal.
(Y-you're bound to think I'm talking about blood... Surely you'll be frightened by me and t-try to flee instead...)
...Human blood will not suffice. My master requires sustenance that overrides the effects of the strength-sapping curse.
Food that can neutralize a curse... I decided to look around the hall for something that might fit that description.

sequence:
Tales From the Count's Castle

<size=45>5 The Crossroads of Faith</size>

scripts.say: After searching every nook and cranny, all I managed to find was a water cooler disguised as a statue and some paper cups.
That was it. No food a vampire might eat, not even a red-colored beverage.
(The Commander's never going to guess it's that cursed thing...)
(Shh! Also, it's time to say the line.)
(Oops! Right, sorry.)
Time is nearly out, human. Emden and her underlings draw near. I can sense it...
Nobody had told me there was a time limit. I had to make a choice, and quick...

options.content: Go through one of the doors

scripts.say: "I've wasted enough time on this riddle. It's time for the all or nothing option!"
The door led into a long, dark, cramped corridor. Following it brought me to a big crossroads, but all the paths only led back to the same dark corridor.
It wasn't long before I lost sight of which way I even came from.

sequence: Bad Ending – The Door to Darkness

scripts.say: I'd gotten myself hopelessly lost. I shouldn't have left it up to chance...
Psst, over here.
A familiar voice rang out amid the darkness.
Behind you, Commander.
Seems you panicked and made a poor decision.
This corridor is rigged, you see. All the doors in the hall lead to a bad ending if you don't solve the riddle first.
Follow the sound of my voice. Oh, and take this small cross.
It's your prize for getting through this trial. It'll be useful later.
You're cleared to go to the last trial. Enjoy~
"A strength-sapping curse... Sustenance that overrides it... So a curse is again the crux of the problem here."
"Something to do with curses, then... I suppose there's the Cursed Blood Necklace I got."
"That's not food, though... Wait a minute. Cursed blood... Maybe the ruby is the answer?"
"I mean, this can't be a real ruby to begin with. Let's see here..."
I extracted the ruby from the necklace to inspect it more closely. It had a label on the underside that reads "strawberry soda."
(Thank goodness... The Commander figured it out just as I voiced my doubts!)
Now take that and dissolve it in water. Yeah, like that.
I put the "ruby" in a cup of water, waited a minute, and gave the finished strawberry soda to Elbing.
You've helped me regain my strength, human. O, moon shrouded in darkness, heed my call and show the way forward!
Elbing stiffly recited a chant, and one by one, the doors in the hall closed until only one remained open.
This is the correct path.
Human, take this. The crones used it to inhibit my master's powers, though now it is beyond useless. You may have it.
U-47 walked up and gave me a small metal cross.
(Whew... I hope everything from this point on will go smooth– Wait, I mean, terribly and end in failure for the Commander! Yeah, that should do it!)

sequence:
Tales From the Count's Castle

<size=45>6 You Never Expect Them</size>

scripts.say: A short walk later, I arrived in the third hall.
Ah, the human's here. Your little escapade has well and truly messed this whole castle up.
Then again, I don't really care one way or the other because I want to get outta this place too.
The princess is obsessed with the outside world, but she's forbidden to leave, you see. The bedlam you've caused today serves as her getaway opportunity.
So let's set our differences aside. What matters is that we share the same goal.
You don't know the way out, do you? Well, I do, heehee. Follow me.
I followed Lützow and Thüringen through the great hall.
It was quiet. Too quiet...
FWOMP!
Without any warning, Lützow wrapped her arms around me.
Ugghhh... I'm already beat just trying to keep pace with you. You've gotta give me some of your juice, or we'll never make it out.
All I need is a little. C'mon, let me have a taste, human~
Aha! There we go! Don't mind if I have a bite♪
Lützow sank her teeth into my neck. She drew gulp after gulp of blood, until eventually, I collapsed...

sequence: Bad Ending – Sucked Dry

scripts.say: ...Is what it felt like. While she didn't pierce my skin, she did leave a small mark.
Frankly, I wasn't expecting her to bite me at all.
Oooh... You taste interesting, Commander... I'll remember that.
Why the shocked look? I was just following the script. See? "The vampire princess struck while the human was stunned."
Under normal circumstances, this would spell game over for you. Luckily, you get to continue.
Right as I sensed Lützow was going to bite me, I took out my cross and pointed it at her.
Instantly, the two vampires froze in place as though they'd turned to stone. It seemed my quick thinking had saved my skin.
Mrrghhh...
Key word: seemed. Lützow then leaned on me with all her weight, effectively locking me in place...
Lützow! You're going off-script. Release the Commander and act like the cross is repelling you.
But why? I've caught the Commander. No point letting our prisoner go. Right, Commander?
Apparently the problem was with the staff, not the script.
Very well. I won't terminate the game immediately, but I will report this to Eugen. She'll decide whether or not you'll be replaced.
Hrmph. Fiiine... Nooo, not the croooss, what will I dooo.
Lützow cried out in a very monotone voice and backed off from me.
You're clever, human... So be it. I'll have to bear with my thirst and keep guiding you.
Here we are. Just keep going down this long-ass corridor and you'll be out of the woods.
(Little does the Commander know there's another puzzle coming in hot right abooout... now!)
FWOOOOSH!
Someone threw a smoke grenade at us from the other end of the corridor.
Through the veil of the smoke, I could just barely make out two people – Seydlitz and Sheffield.
Halt! You're going nowhere!
Vampire hunters?! They must've snuck in amid the chaos. Dammit... This is about to get ugly.
You vampires and your filthy vassal shall face divine judgment! Choose a god and pray!
I'm afraid this is the end for you.
Vassal? So you think the human is our vassal because we brought it with us?
Whatever, we can just skedaddle outta here. Try to catch us if you can.
Exit's right over there. Come on, human... or should I say, my vassal! Better start running!

sequence:
Tales From the Count's Castle

<size=45>7 Escaping the Castle</size>

scripts.say: We ran for our lives through the smoke from their grenades, and despite our best efforts, we were unable to reach the exit.
Would you vampires and this vermin of a vassal please stop struggling and let me tie you up?
Hahahah! Gotta say, that was pretty fun!
As we were being tied up, a number of swinging axes suddenly descended from the ceiling and chopped the corridor up into pieces.
Excuse me, what? The script didn't mention this!
Eugen and Akashi just installed these, so it's no wonder you don't know about them.
Hrmph! How come nobody told me about–
Eeeeeeek.
Lützow dropped down a pitfall that abruptly opened right beneath her. She let out an astonishingly flat scream.
Rest assured, she's fine. There are plenty of cushions to soften her impact down there.
Now, the script dictates that it's my time to go. Beware of the traps on the floor... Ooooh nooooo.
Thüringen, also, dropped down a pitfall.
There's only the vassal left! Prepare to meet your maker!
You are vermin and will be dealt with as such. You may try to flee, but how fast can you run?
Escaping these two would be extremely hard. I could only really think of two options...

options.content: Run to the hills, run for your life
Count prime numbers and calm down

scripts.say: These two have style, grace, and fervor... but the one thing they lack is speed.
The exit is right up ahead. If I just run, I can make it...!
...Where'd the floor go?

sequence: Bad Ending – You Activated My Trap

scripts.say: Commandant! Look out!
Seydlitz closed the distance at breakneck speed, grabbed hold of me, and fell down the pitfall with me.
...Commandant, are you all right?!
"Thanks for saving me by making sure I landed on the cushions. Although you couldn't save me from losing the game right before the finish line..."
I'm afraid I couldn't, no. My condolences.
Well, there's little else to do now but take the stairs back to the corridor. I will escort you to the exit from there, as per Eugen's instructions.
Acting without thinking is never the way to go. It will only make things worse.
Staring at the pitfalls, I noticed they opened and shut at regular intervals. I could make it safely out if I just timed my steps.
So I did. I made careful progress, paying close attention to the floor below me.
Seydlit and Sheffield were gaining on me, but it didn't matter – the exit was just steps away!
A little more...!
Incredible, Commandant! You remain calm even in the most tense of situations!
I threw open the door at the end of the corridor. On the other side of it was the port I knew and loved.
I'd finally made it out. My success was immediately celebrated with party poppers.
You escaped the room, nya! Congratulations, nya!
A few days later...
Thanks for your input, nya. Now I know what's good and what could be improved, nya.
Soon the finalized escape room will be open for the whole port to enjoy, nya.
Wish I could ask about what – if any – bad endings you encountered, but oh well, nya...
Hey now, that's a secret, remember?
I know, I know, nya. Anyway, be sure to visit again after I've implemented everyone's feedback, nya.
Seconded. We'd love to see you again. Be sure to bring your friends, 'kay?
...All in all, it was an interesting escape room scenario filled with surprises.
I already knew I'd come back another day with a number of friends in tow.
This is a story set in a far-off magical game world...
There was an evil tyrant called the Demon King. She used her army of monsters to terrorize the poor people of this world.
Then one day, the hero Javelin and her friends set out on a quest to end the Demon King's terrible rule.
You received 100G and MAP TO DEMON KING'S LAIR!
LV 1 HERO JAVELIN joined your party!
LV 1 MAGE LAFFEY joined your party!
LV 1 FIGHTER AYANAMI joined your party!
LV 1 WARRIOR Z23 joined your party!
Village - Outskirts
A villager came to the party with a quest to eliminate a group of imps damaging her crops. The party set off at once.
My MP has fully recovered... You're going down, imps...
LAFFEY cast EXPLOSION! IMP A took 999 DMG! IMP A was defeated!
LAFFEY cast EXPLOSION! IMP B took 999 DMG! IMP B was defeated!
...LAFFEY cast EXPLOSION! IMP Z took 999 DMG! IMP Z was defeated!
Quest "IMPS IN THE FIELD" complete. You received 100G and VILLAGER'S MEAL!
MAGE LAFFEY leveled up to LV 50!
Commission... complete...
I'm all out of MP... You'll have to take it from here... Goodnight... Zzzzz...
Frontier City - Blacksmith
You will face more dangerous enemies henceforth. You should upgrade your GEAR!
Welcome, nya~ Upgrading gear is 100G a pop, nya. What do you say, nya?
Look, hero, this is part of the tutorial, nya. No is not an option, nya.
This will just take a minute, nya~
You paid 100G. You have 100G remaining. You received WARRIOR'S AXE+1!
Here you go, nya~ Do you wanna upgrade it again, nya?
Come ooon, this has a 99% success rate, nya! You wanna get stronger, don't you, nya?
This will just take a minute, nya~
You paid 100G. You have 0G remaining. You lost WARRIOR'S AXE+1!
Darn, it failed, nya. Talk about bad luck, nya!
It's not the end of the world though, nya! I can upgrade another piece of gear any time if you have the money, nya!
Do you want to upgrade something else, nya?
Did... Did I just LOSE my axe?!
That took all our money, too!
Ahah... Ahahaha...
*sigh*... We have to start from scratch and earn our gold back...
Great Dungeon - Top Floor
Holy cow! We've found the Four Beasts' Dungeon!
All we have to do is make it to the exit and we'll have a straight path to the Demon King's lair!
While that sounds great, this place is a maze... Finding the exit will take forever.
Ugh... I'm already tired as heck...
Don't get lazy so soon! We haven't even fought one battle yet!
I've figured out the dungeon's layout.
This wall just ahead has a weak spot in its structure. Yes, I can do this.
Wait, do what? What are you going to do?
One's body is one's most powerful weapon. You wouldn't understand.
I'm going to use my Ultimate Ability: Dynamic Entry Kick!
AYANAMI performed DYNAMIC KICK! SURPRISINGLY STURDY WALL took 999 DMG! SURPRISINGLY STURDY WALL was destroyed!
A path to the dungeon's center appeared!
Heheh... Yes, this is much faster. Now let's go!
Mwahahah! I'm surprised you made it to my lair alive!
But you won't be for much longer! I will see to that myself!
Your little adventure ends right here and n–
JAVELIN performed ENDLESS SLASH! DARK LORD took 100,000,000 DMG! DARK LORD was defeated!
Th-this cannot be! How could you possibly defeat me?!
Graaaghhh!
You received DARK LORD'S TREASURY KEY!
Oh my gosh... This has to be the legendary weapon that only the chosen one can wield!
It looks fishy... but it has the best attack stat I've ever seen!
Heheh, I think I'm gonna hang on to this!
And so the Demon King was defeated and the world was at peace.
THE END

scripts.say: The beacon's guidance had cut off. After the visible spatial disruption faded, Kirov found herself at her destination.
Visibility here was poor. A haze of black particles drifted haphazardly between earth and sky.
...Unpleasant place we've got here.
Purification system and protective gear are... Good, everything's working.
After carefully checking her equipment, Kirov then turned her attention to surveying the surroundings.
She could tell right away that these plains had been flooded, then frozen over.
Thick layers of ice were turbid with the very same black particles, forming ominous streaks underfoot.
Beyond these striations, one could faintly make out the remnants of countless stone and steel structures.
Even further beyond that was a yawning expanse of darkness, reaching out endlessly into the distance.
This wasn't the source of the signal. Looks like there's a discrepancy with the singularity navigator.
...Could this be due to interference from the black particles?
Well, that's about what you'd expect from this blasted test site. Better get used to it.
Even so, I can't deny that my emotions are flaring...
Have I grown too accustomed to this world... or, has the burning blood within my heart finally been reignited?
KABOOOOM!
A sudden barrage violently kicked up a cloud of whirling black mist, but it failed to penetrate Kirov's protective barrier.
The shelling had not come from a single direction – distorted black shadows began to materialize from all directions at alarming speed.
...Guess these aren't the ruins of some bygone battlefield. The fighting here's far from over.
Fine by me. It'll be a quick way to assess the threat level of this test site.
Ni odnogo. Return to dust!
KABOOOOM!
Kirov's mechanized companions, Vspyshka and Kometa, formed a coordinated dance of claw and talon to create a massive kill-zone of arcing electricity.
They quickly dispatched the encroaching shadows, and dispersed the swirling black mist.
It seemed that the enemy's surprise attack had been dealt with for now––
But, their crushed black particles continued to cling to the ice in layers, caking it in an ink-like darkness.
The ice then sublimated, releasing the particles back into the air, where they would quickly coalesce into new enemies.
What...? They're exhibiting the characteristics of mimic entities?!
I can't afford to deplete my strength here.
Should I activate the neutralization equipment now, or withdraw and gather information...?
As Kirov began considering her next course of action, she suddenly detected a signal rapidly approaching from high altitude.
It was a signal her past self knew all too well – one that should not have been possible.
...An allied "Kometa"?
BZZT––
Comrade! Comrade, can you hear me?
Which front did you retreat from? How fares our allies in the Arctic––
Now's no time for an interrogation session!
...Sorry, I let my emotions get the better of me.
...You there, Comrade. This area has been designated as lost to the netherworld. The Supreme Council abandoned it three days ago!
Get out of there, or your life will be in danger!
We'll come give you a lift, so hang in there a bit longer!
...Gangut?
The one who sent the distress signal... Was it you?
But how...? How could it have been you...?
KABOOOOM!
Shortly afterwards, Gangut and Ozornoy swooped down to provide assistance.
Kirov could not hide the fact that her models of Vspyshka and Kometa were much more advanced than those of her saviors, so she agreed to answer their questions.
She told them: "I'm from a different test site, and rushed over after receiving a distress signal."
However, they seemed unaware of this distress signal, suggesting that it would be best to leave the area first before investigating further.
And so, the two arrivals flew away with Kirov, much like soldiers conducting a daring rescue operation.
After breaking out of the black haze's encirclement, Kirov opened her eyes to a white world of snow and ice.
Though the traces of war were all too evident, some silhouettes were still familiar to her.
...Northern Parliament.
The winter here... seems particularly harsh.
Where are you taking me, Comrade "Gangut"?
To the final, unshakeable line of defense. All our resources and personnel are gathered there.
––The "Winter Wall."
Ah, Comrade Moskva! You're here!
Yes. Thank you for your contributions during this operation, Comrade Gangut and Comrade Ozornoy.
And, Comrade Kirov, I've already received some basic information about you.
Frankly, I'm quite surprised.
Though in this moment, I am more joyous than anything else.
To our comrade who has crossed worlds to arrive here – on behalf of the Supreme Council, I offer you my deepest respect.
Welcome... to the Northern Parliament.

<size=45>2 "Her" Arrival</size>

scripts.say: There, in the brightly-lit classroom, I find myself face-to-face with the girl who had just stepped inside.
...Professor?
...Hey there?
Hello~ I knew it was you, Professor!
Long time no see! Mind if I just take a seat somewhere?
Seeing me frozen in place, the girl enters the classroom without hesitation.
She looks around the room cheerily before picking a seat in the same row as mine, just one desk apart.
As we look at one another, time seems to pass silently, second by second.
The little girl who looked just like Zero has vanished without a trace, as if she had never been there to begin with.
Um...
Bon Homme Richard?
That's right, it's me... Probably?
I mean, I'm pretty sure that's who I am... but I think there's a question mark next to my name for some reason?
...Huh? What question mark?
Do you see it, Professor? If you do, then that means...
Well, if you don't, then let's just consider that my little secret~♪
The girl smiles at me warmly, but there seems to be something deeply unsettling beneath her gentle demeanor.
(I mean, she looks perfectly normal, but this is Bon Homme Richard we're talking about...)
(Any way you look at it, she looks and sounds like a perfectly ordinary girl...)
(I'm not sure how to describe it... but even her words feel so normal that it almost seems... abnormal?)
(This IS Bon Homme Richard, after all...)

options.content: So, uh, is it too late for me to run?

scripts.say: So, uh, is it too late for me to run?
Run? Why would you need to do that, Professor?
I mean, because it's you, right? Normally, that'd be the obvious thing to do, right?
Hmm... Is that so?
There are a lot of things I can't quite remember.
All I know is that I used to be your student...
I wonder, is there anything else you can teach me?
Her words have a strange, alluring power. I can almost feel her molding my thoughts, guiding me to think the way she wants me to.
(As expected of a naval PR spokeswoman for the Federation, and a super-popular idol to boot...)
(I really need to be more careful around her...)
Umm, so what you're saying is, you've lost some of your memories?
Where were you earlier today? Do you remember what you were doing before you came here?
Professor, you seem really tense for some reason... and you're even dripping with cold sweat... Oh no, are you feeling unwell?
Answer the question, Richard.
Okay!
You wanted to know what I was doing before I came to the academy, right? I can remember that much!
Wellll~ I was just assigned a top-secret mission to retrieve Pandora, and was getting ready to head out~
I'm supposed to go to, umm... Division 13's Mayport Naval Base?
What?!
Within the dark ocean of my thoughts, glimmers of light suddenly begin to surface.

sequence: Eagle Union Navy Spokeswoman Bon Homme Richard has just announced...
...that she received mobilization orders earlier and will now be...
...temporarily transferring to Division 13 fleet to...
...conduct exercises at the Mayport Naval Base.
The current situation seems to be developing in an unpredictable direction...
What? You want us to just hand the "box" over to Division 13?
With all due respect, that is different from the instructions we were given.
Even General Garfield doesn't have the authority to...
I can't just... Never mind, forget I said anything.
This way please, Miss Richard. Let us begin the handover process.
Both spokespersons have dramatically changed their tone, maintaining an uncharacteristically strict silence...
Evidence has emerged that there was a large overnight movement of medical supplies from Mayport Naval Base, which is responsible for providing logistical support during the exercise...
There is also evidence that several semi-submersible vessels anchored there have also departed...
A whistleblower has said that the confrontation may have already escalated into armed conflict...
Additionally, a video that appears to capture the scene of the confrontation has been circulating for some time now.
The blurry footage shows a black tornado rapidly passing through a Union warship...
...after which the warship exploded violently...
A tornado!! Yes, that's right... I saw a black tornado!
Ahahaha! She said she would destroy everything! She said she'd take me with her!
It was Bon Homme Richard! I saw her laughing! I heard her whispering!
She was the tornado! The tornado was laughing! The tornado was speaking!
Let me get this straight. So after receiving a message from the Enterprise, you agreed to conduct a joint operation with the Revolutionary Front?
Were you aware that this joint operation had not been authorized by Naval Command? Furthermore were you aware...
...that Captain John Archer of the Enterprise had no authority to bypass the flagship and issue such orders to you?
...No, it's you people who don't understand!
At the time, the second fleet had already been engulfed in flames, and the black tornado was still raging...
Comms were down, and the survivors were left fighting for survival. It was impossible to contact the flagship...
Do you not get it? The command structure had already completely collapsed...
Captain Archer was trying to reorganize the chain of command...
..."Reorganize the fleet, and prepare to launch a counterattack"––
...Would I follow that order again?
...Damn right I would. I'd obey any order that could get us out of that hellscape alive.
Calling Golden Hawk. The Enterprise is broadcasting the same message over and over from her bridge: "It must be destroyed."
...Destroyed? What's "it"? Pandora?
...I have no idea... John, what the hell did you find?
...Code N has gone up in flames... My god...
...Assemble a rescue team right away. And a team to recover the wreckage...
...Your mic is still... Yes, Mr. President...
...The report is true. The Enterprise has detonated Code N.

scripts.say: Eutopia Savoy – Colonel of the Republic of Sardegna's Navy, military advisor to the Oceanic Federation, member of the Special Investigations Committee, and the modern-day Garibaldi.
It's been a while. Welcome to the Eagle Union.
...We meet again, you two.
I thought you were here on an academic exchange visit?
Forgive me, I just wanted to break the ice. No need to be so tense.
Mhm. Was it you who came up with "the modern-day Garibaldi"?
Of course not. Do you think I would give you such a bland nickname?
The Magister... The Mysterious One... Yes, I suppose that's not like you.
Exactly. I would go with something like Golden Hawk, or Swordbearer.
Um...
Sorry. It was just a joke.
At any rate, can you guess why the two of us are here?
Pushing the envelope, are we?
I'm under an oath of confidentiality. Don't expect me to answer any questions regarding the Special Investigations Committee.
That being said... I can share my personal opinion on some matters.
Well, I've never concealed my opinions on those things anyway.
So, what do you want to ask?
Um...
...As the name suggests, we let a terrible monster run free.
The secrets and the dangers hidden within Wisdom Cubes have already far surpassed our expectations.
Excluding mine.
Right – surpassed the expectations of MOST of us.
I think it's necessary to put an immediate stop to these insane experiments.
Um...

options.content: What can you share about John Archer?

scripts.say: I think the Colonel is a true hero.
His decision saved the lives of many people, and the destruction of Pandora's box saved even more.
I can only hope that the box has been completely and utterly destroyed now...
Whatever the case, I salute our dear friend.
Um...

options.content: I'd like to know about Bon Homme Richard.

scripts.say: ...She was a good kid. She shouldn't have met the end she did.
I promise you the Committee will carry out a fair investigation.
May she rest in peace...
Information continues to pour from the depths of my memory, and this time, it seems to last particularly long.
Hm? What's wrong, Professor? You've been spacing out for a while. Did you suddenly remember something?
Um...
Richard, stay away from Pandora.
Um...
Yeah, I know.
Thank you, Professor.
Ding dong––
The last bell rings out across the academy.
At the same time, a wave of drowsiness seems to wash over me.
(This is...)
(...the first time I've heard the last bell ring here...)
(Falling asleep in a dream... means I'm about to return to reality soon...)
My heavy eyelids close, and the world around me slowly recedes into darkness.
The last thing I see before my consciousness fades... is Bon Homme Richard vanishing from the classroom.
The girl resembling Zero is next to me... as if she had been there all along.
And then, there was only darkness––
Bright sunlight filters through the gaps in the curtain, as if someone is scattering spots of light all over the room.
(What lovely weather... Haven't felt this well-rested in ages...)
(The dream I had last night... Do I owe my wonderful sleep to that...?)
*sigh*... I suppose so...
Good morning, Professor.
If you're already sighing so early in the morning, all your luck for the day's going to disappear, you know~
Mornin', Richard...
Um...
HUUUUUUUHHH?!
Bon Homme Richard?! What are you doing here...?!
Mmm... I'm not quite sure myself.
I found myself here when I woke up.
If anything, there's something I'd like to ask you–
Professor, where are we?

scripts.say: The deepest parts of the communication space – an area where Arbiters exchange important information.
Here, endless torrents of data converge, manifesting as a vast, starry sky.
Here, countless stars settle into their designated positions, their glimmering births and spectacular deaths having no effect on this space.
But at this very moment, the starry skies are flickering with an unsettling frequency.
...What did you just say?
...You're starting the initial rigging construction procedure for The Sun?
...Was that project not frozen because the estimated costs were too great?
The sky itself flickered and distorted, as if reflecting the abnormality of the information presented and the speaker's unease.
Based on the calculations of the newest recycling technology, the project would require the collection of resources from 1,254,470 test sites.
After factoring in redundancies, a total of 1,500,000 test sites are slated to be used for resource collection.
Based on this reassessment, Zero has determined that the current Antiochus program is capable of undertaking this project.
...A million and a half test sites?
Hmm... I suppose it's fine. Assuming that's all we'll need.
But, there's always more work to be done afterwards... Isn't that right?
This process is merely a prerequisite for what follows...
Its true purpose is to establish a Dimensional Ordering Engine for the purpose of "Reordination"...
What cost are we willing to pay to bring that ultimate goal to fruition?
It'll probably be another order of magnitude.
Naturally, these costs will not be borne by test sites within the Observer program.
...At this rate, we might as well drop the "test site" label and simply call them "mining sites."
Empress, Magician... Zero has gone mad. Are you all going to follow her into madness?
From my perspective, Temperance, this plan has a high chance of success.
As such, I think it's worth a try.
The Dimensional Ordering Engine project was originally rolled into the Magister Plan as a carryover from one of the Council's legacy projects.
It was always low-priority. Impractical to achieve. That's why it was frozen at the bottom of the legacy projects pile.
Even if we do have the means to implement it now, what implications will it have for the broader Magister Plan?

Now, Zero wants to shut down the transboundary experiments, yet intends to reboot a project that will cost twice to thrice the amount of the transboundary experiments. Is that not putting the cart before the horse?
Lest you forget, Temperance, experiments are but a means to an end.
One thing is clear – Zero has made her decision.
The Dimensional Ordering Engine project will be spearheaded by The Tower.
Four auxiliary departments will be established beneath her.
The technical department will be led by The Hanged Man and Wheel of Fortune.
The engineering department will be led by The Moon, with The Sun and Strength supporting.
The security department will be led by The Magician, with The Star and The Chariot supporting.
The resource integration department will be led by The World, with The Empress, The Emperor, and The Lovers supporting.
...The World?
Yes. I shall oversee the resource integration department until The World's return.
And the reason I have contacted you is precisely because of that.
...And here I was wondering why my name didn't make the list.
Wouldn't it have been better to send Justice or Judgment?
Once the transboundary experiments get shut down, those two will have plenty of free time.
...Have you not checked on the progress of the fourth transboundary experiment at all?
Nope. Not like there was anything for me to do. What, did something happen?
Three system years ago, Justice and Judgment jointly submitted a request to The World to place a Black Box seal upon the entire fourth transboundary experiment.
Needless to say, The World agreed.
...Looks like I'm the only one who can do the job after all.
Find a suitable world, then get the resource integration department up and running ASAP. Anything else?
There is, actually. Could you also keep an eye on the Commander?
I don't have any concrete proof, but it's possible that The World has already made contact with the Commander through the "Mundus" device. She may attempt to do so again.
Right... In that case, I'll have to plan things through carefully.
Oh, one last thing – if this plan fails, is that going to be allowed?
Of course. Despite the massive investment of resources, this is but one component of the Magister Plan.
As such, failure is acceptable.
However, for the sake of our ultimate victory... the Magister Plan cannot be allowed to fail.
...For the sake of our ultimate victory.

Fateful Encounter

<size=45>4 What Happened Next</size>
Iris Orthodoxy - Capital
Cathedral Garden

scripts.say: Humm~♪ Humm humm~♪
Isn't the weather lovely today, Professor?
Yeah, it sure is...
And so, Bon Homme Richard emerged from my dreams and became reality.
More precisely, Bon Homme Richard, a person only I could see, had descended from my dreams into reality.
After dropping Marco Polo off with the Compiling Field and informing Richelieu of Clemenceau's decision, I planned to head to the Sea of Stars through PH Harbor.
The goal was to organize a research team at the Sea of Stars to establish a stable communication channel with test site ES-40111.
However, Bon Homme Richard's appearance changed everything, and I immediately set course for the Royal Islands.
The Royal Navy's artificial singularity, Gate of Avalon, was another option for creating a stable communication channel between worlds.
Also, Elizabeth META was there.
If anyone could unravel the mystery of Bon Homme Richard's appearance, as well as her surprising lack of hostility... it would be her.
Professor, you always look like you're overthinking something...
You know, you don't have to shoulder everything on your own.
Sometimes, it's better to just let things run their course~
Despite her calm demeanor, I couldn't shake the sense of a strange tension lurking beneath.
Though she looked and behaved like an ordinary person, her words seemed to flow perfectly with my thoughts, as if we were sharing one mind...
Well, I guess it's fine. Maybe that's par for the course of being a professor.
To be honest, I think I like the version of you that's always overthinking things.
Oh... Look at that tree, Professor!
A bunch of little birds are gathering over there! Let's go take a look!
Richard tugs at the hem of my clothes as if it was the most natural thing in the world, leading me over to the grove of trees at the side of the road.
My feet follow her without hesitation, like I have no right to refuse.
I don't know what will happen if I upset her. All I know is that right now, she is only visible to me, and she never seems to stray far from my side.
And so, I find myself inexorably drawn to her pace, becoming her guide to this world.
Commander, what's going on with you? Why are you staring at a tree like that...?
Oh, uh... Richard wanted to look at the birds...
I'm going to do more than just look, you know! I want to join their little gathering!
They've been chirping so loudly this whole time. Don't you want to know what they're chattering about?
Wooow– sparrows and chickadees and turtledoves and pigeons... and even a robin!
Hello there, little birdies~♪ How are you all doing today?
Maybe it's just my imagination, but the birds' chorus seems to be growing louder all of a sudden.
Oh really? Wow, wow, I see! ...Huh? Is that so?
Richard is nodding along as if she understands what they're saying.
...So, what'd they say?
Do you want to know?
Heheh~ They said it's going to rain later today! And, they also said it was fun chatting with us!
...Did they really say all that?
Umm, probably?
Oh, Professor, stop for a sec!
My body freezes for an instant.
The next moment, a black-and-white glob whizzes past my head and splashes onto the ground, barely missing the brim of my hat.
What was that?
Hmph! Looks like some birdie is jealous of our stroll through the garden together and is trying to play tricks on us!
Don't think I'll let you get your way, you hear?!
How'd you know that was about to happen?
That's my little secret~!
...Commander, are you talking to Richard again?
*sigh*... Well, first, I need to do something about this situation so that I don't look like a crazy person to everyone else.
Were you able to arrange me a flight to the Royal Islands?
Yup. Everything's taken care of.
Should we wait for Richard to finish looking around the garden, or...
Uhh, let's get going.
I need to figure out what's happening, or I'm not going to be able to get a wink of sleep...
Yeah... Let me finish up the preparations.
Richard, want to take a trip to the Royal Islands next?
Huh? Oh, sure! I'm fine with whatever you decide on, Professor!
Well then, bye-bye, birdies! I'm off to visit the Royal Islands with Professor!
Ehehe~ Don't forget about us!

<size=45>5 The Winter Wall</size>
Unknown Test Site
Northern Parliament - Secure Airspace

scripts.say: As Kometa made its descent, Kirov could clearly see walls of steel rising majestically from snow and ice.
...Thickness of approximately 3 kilometers?
And the visible portion alone looks to be a good 150 kilometers...
The endless wall of metal stretched deep into the wintry mist.
The land itself has been split asunder by this gargantuan construct.
Be careful, everyone! We're about to make our descent!
Ah, Comrade Kirov, we'll be landing soon! Before then–
Oh, sorry, forgot your Kometa is a more technically advanced model.
No worries. I appreciate the heads up.
When she looked back behind her, she could clearly see the pitch-black clouds, a grotesque amalgam of mist and black particles.
Everything between sea and sky was being devoured, corrupted by the encroaching haze.
(Looks like I'll be staying here for a while...)
After the group made a safe landing on the wall, Ozornoy went to deliver the action report while Gangut stayed behind to act as a guide for Kirov.
Comrade Moskva is commanding from a somewhat remote location, but she should be here soon.
It sounded like she was quite keen to speak with you in person.
Likewise. It would be my honor to meet her.
As they talked, Kirov continued to observe the massive, complex fortress known as the Winter Wall.
Though she had heard it referred to as the "last line of defense", it clearly was still a work-in-progress.
Within these walls, countless enormous construction machines toiled day and night, and the banners of various factions fluttered in the wind.
Whenever those distant, dark clouds approach these castle walls – that would be the final deadline for this herculean construction effort.
...So that's the story of this place, huh?
It sure brings back memories...
As they walked down a long, empty corridor, Kirov began to ask the question that had been weighing on her mind.
"Gangut"... Tell me, is today truly the first time we've met?
...Huh? I'm not sure what you're getting at, Comrade Kirov.
Though they're different models, you and I both have a Kometa. Don't you find that strange?
Hmm... Not necessarily? The Northern Parliament you came from was simply more technologically advanced than ours.
Yes, but...
I suppose if you have no knowledge of anything beyond this world, you would not know about me either.
Even though Vspyshka and Kometa both exist here, it was merely coincidence that they would also be born in the factories of this world.
...If only it was that simple.
Tell me, "Gangut." How did you undergo METAmorphosis?
...It was after a particularly gruesome mission.
Sorry, Comrade Kirov. It's something I'd rather leave in the past.
No worries. I just wanted to confirm – to your knowledge, you are from this test site, and underwent METAmorphosis here, correct?
And before you answer that – have you ever disassembled or done maintenance on your own rigging?
I've had some minor repairs done over the years, but no major maintenance... Comrade Kirov, what are you trying to get at?
For some reason, the Vspyshka and Kometa you are using... are registered in my identification system.
Why would this sort of maintenance signature be found here, on your rigging?
As if she had more mastery over the gear than its very wielder, Kirov immediately switched Gangut's rigging into maintenance mode.
What?! Comrade Kirov, what... are you doing?!
Just who are you?! ...Maintenance records... electronic signatures... What is all this?!
Soobrazitelny, Ingraham. Do those names ring any bells?
I've never even heard those names before! But why... are those names... right here on my maintenance records...?
I'd like to know the answer too, Comrade "Gangut."
All of a sudden, the sirens started blaring...
...putting an abrupt end to the awkward conversation.
...Are we under attack?
Yeah... Unfortunately, the netherworld's not gonna stand by and watch us finish building the Winter Wall.
Having said that, this kind of stuff happens all the time. It's nothing to worry about.
But, those dark clouds in the distance...
Kirov continued to carefully monitor the ominous clouds, but they did not show any signs of change. Her systems did not even detect any suspicious signals from them.
Heh. Looks like we've got something even you haven't seen before.

The towering peaks of the Winter Wall are equipped with the most advanced netherworld detectors, capable of predicting the direction and intensity of enemy attacks from the slightest changes in internal airflow.
The origin story of this technology is legendary indeed, and I'd be glad to tell you all about it after this battle!
...Assuming you're interested, that is.
Of course, I'm very interested. Let's deal with these enemies first.
We hold the line with our lives, and take not a single step back!
Kirov tried to follow Gangut, who had charged on ahead, but each step she took was considerably heavier than expected.
(Given the situation here... should I ask test site beta's Northern Parliament for assistance?)
(No, that's off the table.)
(This world is full of secrets. The dangers that lurk here are beyond mortal comprehension...)
(I mustn't get those girls involved...)
(Once we stabilize things here, we'll be able to further ramp up the production of combat-capable machines. At that point...)
(...The prospects of victory will no longer just be a distant glimmer!)

sequence:
Fateful Encounter

<size=45>6 Shallow-Layer Investigation</size>
Unknown Location

scripts.say: In a secret hideout tucked in a corner of the city, Bristol examined her newest creation.
So, whaddya think of this disguise? Pretty spiffy, eh?
Believe it or not, I'm somewhat of a master of disguise myself.
...It's doing a pretty good job of covering up the signs of your METAmorphosis.
But, what's the purpose of all this?
Why are you playing detective?
This town could always use more detectives! Don't you agree?
I couldn't care less.
So, what is this place, exactly?
It's basically a little repository of investigation notes compiled by yours truly! You can read as many of 'em as you'd like.
Investigation notes...? Are you talking about the notebooks on this table here?
Essex glanced over at the notebooks sitting on the table next to her.
"Shocking! The reality of nightlife in the big city"...
"An alleyway from which you cannot escape unless you do THAT"...
"Three simple hacks to help you understand the Rule of Cool"... "The case of the salaryman who can't leave work"...
"The world born five minutes ago"... "Help! My pets are pooping jewels"... "The Necronomicon"...
Got a problem with that? I mean, aren't you just DYING to find out what happens next with those titles?
...If there's anyone shady in this town, it's you.
Who exactly are you?
And what are you hiding beneath that disguise?
As expected of the great detective. You were able to piece things together so quickly.
A darkness that no light could breach began to writhe throughout the room.
Before Essex could launch an attack, a lantern shone in the darkness, emitting a dim light.
"Like moths to the flame, drawn here by lantern's glow."
The darkness then split into countless fragments, clumping together into countless inky moths that began to take flight as if imbued with life.
"O, moths that leap into purgatory, guide this traveler back to whence she came."
The swirling moths began to make a mad dash towards the lantern.
The flames within turned a vivid crimson as they slurped up the flesh and blood of the moth swarm, crackling intensely as it reduced their bodies to ash.
What... did you do?
Urgh... my head... not again...
Hurry...
"Stop."
Suddenly, the moths and the lantern disappeared into the aether, as if time had been rewound to a few minutes prior.
Essex simply stood there, stunned, while Bristol gazed at Essex's shadow, lost in thought.
I see... So you didn't just happen to wander in here. You were summoned.
I apologize for going a bit overboard. A miscalculation on my part.
A proper detective should never tamper with the evidence, eh?
Oh, I know! As a token of my apology, let me give you some supplies.
Good luck out there, master detective. See ya later!
With that, Bristol vanished like a fleeting shadow.
Shortly afterwards, the flow of time started to return to normal inside the room.
...What happened just now?
This is... Right, it's my secret base...
I'm Essex, the master detective, and I've come to this city to investigate some strange incidents.
This notebook... should contain records of my previous investigations, right?
Let me see...
Yeah! These are all the documents I've collected before, I'm sure of it!
It has to be!
I'm still a bit disoriented, but I can just walk it off... In any case, time to start working!

sequence:
Fateful Encounter

<size=45>7 The City of the Lost</size>
Royal Islands - Scapa Flow
Gate of Avalon

scripts.say: The journey from the Iris Orthodoxy to the Royal Islands was fairly uneventful.
Along the way, Bon Homme Richard simply sat in her seat quietly, gazing outside at the clouds.
When we arrived in the reception area, Queen Elizabeth, who had already been informed of our coming, immediately got to work scouring my surroundings.
Long time no see, Queen Elizabeth!
Richard greets her with a cordial smile, but Queen Elizabeth does not take notice of her at all.
(Well, this is rather troublesome... Even Elizabeth doesn't seem to be able to see her.)
Hmm... Tell us, servant... Bon Homme Richard is already here, isn't she?
Yeah. As a matter of fact, she's been trying to say hi to you.
In that case, allow me to apologize for my rudeness. Welcome to the Royal Islands, Miss Richard.
Mmhmm! I'm sure it's going to be a lot of fun here!
You really can't detect her at all?
Unfortunately, it's not going to be possible under current circumstances.
I might be able to get some insight if I carry out some "deep interrogation"... but my intuition tells me that neither of us want that.
I also think that would be a bad idea.
...Guess we'll have to wait to hear back from the Compiling Field.
BEEP––
In a real speak-of-the-devil moment, the communicator suddenly starts beeping.
Commander, we've almost finished constructing the stable channel between Avalon and the Compiling Field. All that's left is to bring in the equipment, which should take roughly half an hour.
...Equipment?
That's right! We consulted with Queen Elizabeth beforehand, and this is what we decided to go with.
Once the channel between the Compiling Field and test site ES-40111 is finished, you'll be able to safely travel there from test site beta!
I didn't think you'd agree to go with the Avalon-based plan. I thought you were all committed to going through the Sea of Stars.
Well, uh... ever since Helena left, our control over the Tower has been slipping.
