I want to say there's more to a battle than winning or losing, but that would be in bad taste.
In your defense, the Pawns were unfairly distributed from the very beginning, and you were also subject to a variety of restrictions.
It wouldn't surprise me if the results of the experiment were predetermined, and our only role was to see it to completion.
I know it wasn't fair and all that, but I still wanted to win! Winning's obviously more fun than losing!
Of course. That goes without saying.
I suppose the Pawns have served their purpose now that the experiment's over. What's gonna happen to them now?
In the case of the mass-produced ships, they'll be taken apart for materials per the central terminal's command.
As for the Pawns, they'll likely also be taken apart after they've uploaded their combat data.
Doing your job only to get scrapped in the end... I know they're our enemy, but man, I kinda feel bad for them.
Look around you. The Mirror Sea itself is changing – presumably because the experiment ended.
See how the wreckages are being salvaged and the structures are changing form?
I believe our exit will appear once everything is back the way it was. Then we will be able to go home.
Well, while we're still here, why don't we end things with a proper shipgirl-on-shipgirl battle?
The Pawns have gotten almost all the action this whole time, and I wanna see how we actually compare to each other. What do you say?
Are you sure you want to? While I do have blanks to spare, they still hurt if they hit you in the wrong places.
The same goes for you. If you don't have a problem with that, then I'm all for it!
Me too, on Blücher's side! Think you can handle that? I wouldn't hold it against you for chickening out versus the one-and-only ME!
Hah. I'm a battlecruiser. It's child's play keeping up with one heavy cruiser and a destroyer.
I wouldn't be so sure about that~! So, wanna settle this over at that exercise area?
Fine by me. May our all-out battle be a satisfying climax to this long operation!
KABOOOM!
The exercise area became host to the Mirror Sea's final battle, its combatants all in high spirits.
Impressive! You battlecruisers are something else!
Same to you both. What you lack in firepower you make up for with teamwork. I can see that you're closely coordinating to cover each others' weaknesses.
Your luck has run out, though! I've figured out your movements, so let's see you try to dodge THESE torpedoes!
Well, well, it looks like you're all having fun over there.
A calm voice spoke to the girls over the comms. All three promptly lowered their weapons.
The experiment's over, yet here you are still fighting. Still high on the thrills of battle, hmm?
Is that... Prinz Eugen?
Yep. The way out is open, and I've come to guide you to it.
Heyo, Eugen! How come you didn't show up before to see me off?
Sorry about that, I had my hands tied. At least now I'm here to pick you up.
Congratulations on completing the experiment, Blücher, Z16, and... Brünhilde, I assume?
Yes, Brünhilde of the O class. I'm glad that you and Friedrich came personally to see us.
Friedrich, I've done everything you instructed me to. I will now return to my original fleet.
Friedrich? Is that the "someone other than Bismarck" person you mentioned a while back?
Yes, that's her. I wasn't expecting to be graced by her company today.
Heheheh. I am Friedrich der Große, blueprint ship of the Iron Blood. Allow me to congratulate you as well.
Blücher, Z16, and Brünhilde, you have completed your experiment. Your contribution shall be the strength that takes Iron Blood another step forward.
Heheh☆ Glad I could be of help!
And I'm glad that I got to see all sorts of badass rigging! Including yours, Friedrich!
Why, thank you.
Brünhilde, I'm afraid I have bad news concerning your original fleet. Its members have been reassigned.
Oh... I see. That is a shame...
So, Eugen, is Bismarck okay? I've got so much to ask her!
Hmm? What are you talking about?
She never called us, obviously! Oh, and the Pawn!
She said she'd contact us at some point, but she never did. There's something weird about her Pawn, too.
We were set to win initially, then Brünhilde's Pawns kept getting stronger while ours didn't! Even the Bismarck Pawn lost to some new battleship she got!
Interesting... That Reenactment had ripple effects that even reached this place.
Let's go, Eugen.
Sure... Come on, we're heading back. We'll answer your questions later.
Hmph. Well, fine!
I'll hold on to my questions, but you can't stop me from making small talk with you!
All this time I've only had Z16 and Brünhilde to talk to! I would've actually gone nuts if we'd been stuck here much longer!
Fine, fine. I suppose I can lend an ear to my big sister's woes.
Oh man, I've been dying to finally go home!
Eugen's and Blücher's animated chattering echoed across the vast expanse. The group of ships eventually reached the Mirror Sea's exit, and vanished into thin air.
Before the experiment began...
Somewhere, in an undisclosed location...
The moment of truth has come.
Regardless of whether I succeed or fail, the curtains will rise on a new future for Iron Blood.
No matter what becomes of me, you will take the reins henceforth.
You are a blueprint ship and one of our key contacts to the Sirens. Observer trusts you.
Iron Blood's fate rests upon your shoulders, Friedrich. Carry out the plan that we've so carefully crafted.
It shall be done, Bismarck.
I do have a question, though. Have you told Eugen about this yet?
Not yet. She has her part to play in this battle, and her "acting" must be authentic.
You should decide when to tell her about our plan.
Very well. I just hope she won't receive it too poorly.
She will come to understand. I'm sure of it.
One last thing. Once you use the Black Cube, what then? Who will come to your aid?
You don't have a rescue plan as far as I can tell.
I was hoping you wouldn't catch on so soon.
I have no such plan. There's no need for one.
Bismarck, there is still a non-zero chance that you will be able to control the Cube.
I'm aware of that, which is why I must make this gamble.
But, even if I am able to control it, will I still be myself?
You know how the Cube works. The more you synchronize with it, the deeper its corrosion seeps into you.
Regardless of who – or what – I become, it is my fate to sink here. Whether by the Royal Navy's hands or by Siren technology, it matters not.
While I continue to live, this Reenactment can never end... And Iron Blood will never be free to pursue its own future.
Don't waste time or resources trying to save me. I shall see to it that I am the last sacrifice they ever make in their little game of chess.
Sorry, but I can't accept that, Bismarck.
Upon this blank score you've left me, I shall compose a symphony.
I will free Iron Blood from the shackles of fate. You and the Commander are both indispensable in leading us to a brighter future.
No matter how long it takes, no matter what it costs.
I presume you won't take no for an answer.
No, I will not.
...I'll keep your plan in mind then.
Hopefully I'll get to hear your symphony someday, somewhere.
Yes. We will meet again, Bismarck. I swear it to you upon these seas.
Mirror Seas. Pocket dimension created by the Sirens.
These artificial dimensions are almost completely cut off from the outside world. On the inside, they have their own environment, structure, and even physical laws.

Indeed, a Mirror Sea can exist within a place that appears completely empty from the outside. That there would be a huge island inside with a large array of facilities is not beyond the realm of imagination.
Mirror Sea - Iron Blood Encampment
Woah, so this is our Mirror Sea research facility...
It looks like another gloomy Siren construct from the outside, but once you walk inside, it's actually rather comfy!
No kidding! With how spacious and fancy this place is, it seems more like a luxury resort than a base of operations.
Is this where we're goin' to stay until the end of our experiment?
Whew~!
Blücher plopped herself down on a sofa inside the rest area and opened up the mission briefs.
That's right. We're gonna be here for a long, long while, so we might as well make ourselves at home.
Hmm, let's take a look around. This is the rest area... And here's the fleet... Um, is this a crafting room and a workshop?
This must be where the Sirens make their Pawns! It's my first time seeing something like this! How 'bout you, Blücher?
Well yeah. It's not like the Sirens normally let us wander around their facilities.
And if I'm seeing this right... This Mirror Sea can produce upgraded Pawns with enhanced combat capabilities and more autonomy...
I guess they've been modified for the purpose of our experiment, just like our own riggings.
Remember to be careful though. If you charge in recklessly against these kinds of enemies, you might end up injured, experiment or not.
Heheh☆ Pretty spooky stuff, huh?
While Blücher was running through operational briefs, Z16 was investigating the empty canteen next door.
Would you look at that, Blücher, the pantries are totally stocked with goodies!
They've got all sorts of food here! It's not just Iron Blood stuff, they've got Iris, Royal, and Sardegnian cuisine as well!
I see, I see... Each sea area is divided into smaller sectors. If the flagship of a sector is incapacitated, then that sector will be considered "captured."
Once enough sectors have been captured, then it will be possible to attack the enemy's base of operations...
Blücher, are you listening?
What was that again?
I just checked out the canteen! We've got lots of good stuff here!
Aren't you hungry after we spent such a long time sailing? Let's chow down before we get to work!
It's not like we can start the operation before startin' these facilities up anyway.
Hmm, you do have a point... So, what are you gonna have?
Schweinhaxe, Sauerkraut, and Kartoffelbrei!
Get me some Schweinhaxe as well then. And some wurst and grilled veggies to go with that.
Now let's see... Until one of the operational bases has been captured, we won't be able to leave the Mirror Sea, nor will anything be able to come in from outside...
...What the heck is this?!
Gah! What are you yelling about all of a sudden?
That was a close one... I almost dropped the food you asked me to bring.
Appreciate it. Uhh... The operation will begin at 3 P.M. on the first day...
Huh?! We're already going to have to fight on the first day?
What time is it anyway...
It's already 11:30, and I haven't even inspected the facilities yet!
Uh-oh...
Let's finish eating quickly and inspect the conditions of the facilities and the Pawns!
Mirror Sea - Pawn Fleet
Following the map depicted in the mission briefs, Blücher and Z16 arrived at the production area. What they found there left them speechless.
The place was like a massive factory. At its center stood uncountably many Pawns, silent and motionless.
This... This is one giant fleet of Pawns!
Is this where they're created? Like machines out of a factory, then sent into battle?
There's Z1, Z2, Karlsruhe... even Pawns of Eugen and Hipper!
Boy, there's still more! Gneisenau, Scharnhorst... Bismarck, too?!
With this many of 'em, even their original selves would lose if they all attacked at once!
Which means we have this mission in the bag! Right, Blücher?
What about you all? Am I right, or am I right? Hahahah!
Z16 was jumping with anticipation for the upcoming battle. She turned and chatted up a Pawn of Z2.
I know you agree for sure, Thiele! We'll get to go all-out this time!
I hope you're not expecting an answer... Pawns aren't able to communicate with us normally.
Still as creepy as I remember them... But I know from fighting them that they're able to change their expressions.
Come on, I wasn't serious! Even I know Pawns are another one of the Sirens' sick jokes.
They're the reason we're here – to test 'em in combat! ...Oh look, someone's left a tape recorder.
"Operation Convergence experiment summary."
"The fleet of Pawns is to be activated and guided into simulated enemy territory. They are to destroy the flagship of each area."
"After a set amount of areas have been secured, the assault on the enemy base begins. The experiment will conclude upon successful takeover."
"Nobody is permitted to enter or exit the Mirror Sea until one of the experiment parties has achieved victory."
Huh? We already know about that. She's just reading off the briefs!
Is this a jab at me or something? Does Eugen think I don't know how to read or something?
"Operation Convergence experiment summary."
Huh? Is it stuck on repeat?
Maybe there's more on the tape, like details about our mystery opponent. Let me try something.
"Operation Convergence experiment summary."
No, it's just sayin' the same thing over and over...
"If you want to know more about your opponent, listen closely... It's a secret, sorry. Heehee♪"
What?! Did Eugen really predict I'd try this and left a message just to mess with me?!
Let's just move on, alright? Knowing Eugen, she probably has more than one way of getting in your head~
...Actually, now that I think about it, maybe this message isn't even specifically meant for us.
We might even be playing the baddies, but neither side has any way of knowing that yet!
Alright, let's round up these Pawns and mop the floor with whoever our mystery opponent is!
Mirror Sea - Experiment Area H8
Enemy recon fleet spotted!
It's made up of a bunch of mass-produced Sirens, with a Z46 Pawn at the helm!
Z46, huh? Last time I saw her she was still getting used to her rigging.
Guess this Pawn version of her is ready for action, though. Now that's interesting~☆
Even if her Pawn ends up being pretty strong, we have her fleet completely outgunned.
That just means our first match is gonna be a crushing victory! Let's gooo!
Enemy reinforcements spotted!
It's Graf Zeppelin! A Pawn of her, anyway.
One lone carrier without escorts? That's certainly a novel way of doing things...
Even if she isn't commanding the Pawns directly, she should really retake Tactics 101. Heheh☆
Hey, isn't Zeppelin also still training with her rigging? It's why she couldn't make it for Bismarck's operation.
The Z46 Pawn wasn't that tough, and I bet this one won't be much– Whoa, never mind!
Gee-heesh! So that's how Zeppelin's rigging looks in action!
Impressive! Powerful! But she still can't compare to the one-and-only... ME!
Alright, enough tooting those horns, and focus on shooting those planes down!
AA guns, let 'er rip!
KABOOOM!
The Pawn's airstrikes proved futile, and the duo succeeded in eliminating it.
That Pawn looked like a flagship to me, so that's one sector secured!
Whoa, did you see that? The mass-produced ships are going haywire now that we've taken out their boss!
Now our own mass-produced ships will make quick work of them. Piece of cake!
Phew, that Pawn really surprised me. Carriers don't play fair!
That's just part of the experiment! We would've won in a heartbeat if there weren't all these rules in place.
Yeah, but there'd be no point to the experiment if we were allowed to go all-out.
True...
Heheh☆ In any case, all we have to do is wait for our ships to finish their jobs, so we can kick back and relax for now.
...Oh, hang on a sec. I'm picking up another shipgirl's signal. A battlecruiser named Brünhilde? Uhh, who's that again?
Brünhilde? Don't think I know her... But that's one badass name!
Wonder if she is playing the baddie! Heheh☆
Shame we're not allowed to talk to each other until the fighting part is over...
Wait, since she's a shipgirl, that might mean she's bringing reinforcements here!
Then we've gotta get back into gear and drive out all the enemies!
They're retreating, Blücher!
Already? That was hardly a fight at all!
We can't let 'em get away! Come on, let's go!
Don't. Brünhilde's long since left the scene, and we'll enter a new area if we chase after the ships.
That's against the rules, remember? We've already won, so let's just head back.
Grr... She played us like a fiddle...
What are you talkin' about? We're victorious and she's on the run.
Sure, we won this time, but we've not learned any useful information about our opponent.
What's worse, it's gonna be an uphill battle if she decides to field a ton of carriers!
Then we'll be outranged and outsmarted by an opponent we know nothing about... Ugh, that's so annoying!
Damn, you're right... I never knew you had so much stuff to think about.
Plus, when'd you get so good at the tactical stuff? I never took you to be the book-smart type.
Hipper used to always nag me about studying. Besides, it doesn't exactly take a genius to figure this stuff out.
Hmm... Maybe I should ask Z23 for some tutoring at some point as well. I wanna get smart too!
But that's for another time! Now let's head back. I'm dying to fill up with some dinner!
Dinner sounds good! I'm right behind you!
Mirror Sea - Iron Blood Encampment
Tonight we're having – drumroll please – tadah! A full course of Iris cuisine!
Holy crap, that's a lot of food! And it all looks delish!
Mhm! It's not every day we get to pig out like this!
There are drinks too, if you want something. Just go pour it yourself.
Sweet! Maybe I'll have a soda or something...
Speaking of food, what do Pawns eat? Do they even eat at all?
I was thinking, wouldn't it be surreal if they just all walked in and started queuing up?
I can't imagine them needing to eat. I mean, they're basically just Siren-created robots, right? I doubt they'd need food.
The survey notes say that when Pawns returns to the workshop, the first thing they do is upload their combat data to a separate facility.
Then they go to... I forget what it's called, but some place where they compare their data amongst each other to reflect on their performance.
After that, I guess they just head into storage and take a nap.
That's when they recharge, regroup with the other Pawns for the next day, and get ready for the next experiment. Seems simple enough.
Interesting... I'm surprised you know all this stuff.
Before we got here, I just assumed we were both equally clueless.
You'd have known too if you maybe read the briefs. It's all in there.
Think about the situation we're in here. Nobody's allowed in or out of the Mirror Sea until a victor's been determined.
Meaning, we're stuck here until the experiment's over. Isn't that really scary?
Learning everything you can is super important if you want to leave as soon as possible and reunite with our friends.
Oof. You're absolutely right... I just assumed this would be like any regular exercise...
Maaan, realizin' that we're stuck here is making my appetite go away...
Hey, it's not all bad. Our opponent is one of our own and she's not a Pawn, meaning that we can communicate with her in case something goes wrong.
But more importantly, as long as we keep winning, we'll be out of here in no time!
Yeah, you're right! You know what, I think I'll have a burger as well!
Mirror Sea - Iron Blood Encampment
Blücher and Z16 finished their meals and went to relax in the break room. Then, in the middle of their lounging...
Sorry for interrupting your break. Can you hear me?
Whoa! Since you're reaching out to us, that can only mean one thing... Brünhilde, was it?
Yes. I am an Iron Blood shipgirl assigned to this operation, just like you.
Blücher, Z16, I wish the two of you luck on this great, shared undertaking of ours. May the best strategist win.
W-woah, this girl's got CLASS!
Class? This is the first time anyone has said that about me. I appreciate your words of praise.
Allow me to also say you fought admirably today.
Heheh☆ Hey, you too! Heck, you did better since you kept your identity and true strength concealed!
I suppose so. You did win only because I conceded victory.
Out of curiosity, are the conditions at your encampment to your satisfaction?
Couldn't be better! We had a great dinner and now we're lying down in cozy beds!
Oh yeah, just checking – the next experiment's scheduled in three days, right?
The Mirror Sea's central terminal determines the schedule. We shouldn't assume it'll stay constant.
It could be in three days, five, or even one. Anything is possible.
Based on personal experience, however, I can say there should be no back-to-back sorties.
Really? You've got experience with this Mirror Sea?
No. This is my first time coming here, just like you.
However, I've trained in other similar Mirror Seas.
Whoa, does that mean you have all sorts of secret intel? Do you know where our riggings came from?
I'm afraid I can't say anything about that.
The one thing I say is this – the theory that our riggings are connected to Siren technology is correct.
Just look at this Mirror Sea for proof. The Pawns have already mastered the riggings that their originals are still getting used to.
Yeah, you're right! They showed they're pretty strong, too!
The originals are even stronger. This technology makes the Iron Blood more powerful than it's ever been before, perhaps even moreso than any other faction.
So you're saying... the Iron Blood is on top of the world right now. We're the one and only ones with this tech!
Probably.
Man, hearing that is getting me all fired up! I wanna get back as soon as possible and tell everyone else about this!
Don't be hasty. There is still much we don't know about these riggings.
For instance, how we control them. They take on vastly different forms based on our hulls. Just compare how different yours are to mine.
Too many unknowns and too few answers, huh... Bummer.
Question! Z16 and I are here because Bismarck put us on the case. Did she put you on it as well?
Bismarck? No, it was someone else. I cannot tell you who, I'm afraid.
Rest assured, Bismarck is aware of my role in this operation. I met her in another Mirror Sea not long ago.
She, I dare say, has an important role to play in this as well.
Whoa, someone beside Bismarck got you involved? Now I'm really curious!
You'll learn who in due time. It cannot stay a secret forever.
Now, it's late, so I suggest we all get some rest.
The Mirror Sea operates training protocols even while the workshop is deactivated. It may occasionally create Sirens and hostile Pawns. Take them as a learning opportunity.
Lastly, feel free to contact me if you have any questions. I'm available at all times on days without experiments.
Gotcha! Don't forget to get plenty of food and rest!
We'll see you in person during the next experiment!

sequence: <size=51>Today is a special day. A day to be remembered.</size>
<size=51>And what better way to remember it than with a grand banquet?</size>

scripts.say: Everyone, could I get an update on how the preparations are going?
I've finished assigning guards along the guest routes and I'm currently double-checking to see if everything looks good.
Likewise, I've finished my tasks. I'm waiting for my next one.
My dance rehearsal for the partygoers is finished.~
I've set up all the equipment for the orchestra. The players will be here soon.
The food and drinks are coming along well, aside from... her.
La Galissonnière, what are you doing? These drinks are for the guests.
Hey, think of it as taste-testing. Or checking for poison. Either way, it's not like anyone will know.~
La Galissonnière tries and fails to come up with an excuse, to the chagrin of some and the amusement of others.
The celebration they're preparing now began as a project much smaller in scale.
That was, until everyone – but especially the Iris Orthodoxy – put forth various ideas on how to make it better, bigger.
Now, these girls are all working tirelessly to help make this banquet one of the biggest, most memorable of the year.
Alright, everyone. Please return to your stations and work on all the finishing touches.
Remember that we are hosting this banquet. We cannot let any imperfections sully the Holy Iris' name.
With all their accounts settled, the girls settled down in the waiting room.
Hmm... Although it was a little hectic, this generally went quite well.

options.content: "We couldn't have done it without you."

scripts.say: Please. If anything, I should be the one saying that.
It was you who assigned tasks to each faction and coordinated our efforts on the scene.
I can't think of anyone else who could've filled your shoes.
I am convinced this banquet will be a great success, largely thanks to you.
While I doubt my part is as important as Richelieu makes it sound, I'm nevertheless glad to have helped everyone.
Jeanne, are we ready?
Yes, we are! Everything is in order for the banquet to begin.
Excellent. Commander, we are ready to open our doors to the guests.
Once again, thank you for everything. I hope you'll enjoy the festivities.
"Thanks. I'm looking forward to hearing your opening speech."
My opening speech? I'm afraid it might not be what you're expecting.
The planning of this banquet required my full attention, so I gave the task of delivering a speech to someone else.
You'll find out who soon enough.
Clemenceau, I leave the Commander and the venue to you. I know you don't like being in the spotlight, but I have no one else to turn to.
Of course. Our good reputation is on the line here – it would be discourteous of me to hide behind the scenes.
Follow me, Commander. It's time to go back to the main hall and enjoy yourself as a guest.~

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>Big E, the Fighter</size>

scripts.say: Sometime later...
...And that's the speech. What are your thoughts, Commander?
"It's well thought-out and has good flow. It's impeccable – like you."
Thanks. I'm glad to hear you say that.
I thought it might be too formal. I know my way around the battlefield, but social gatherings are a different beast.
"I can empathize. Nobody wants to be that person who spoils the mood."
"Still, it's not necessarily bad if the speech feels formal. What matters is that it conveys a sincere message."
It's reassuring when you put it that way.
"And, in a way, if it does sound formal, it's because you see the banquet as a battlefield, and this speech symbolizes your determination to take it on."
That's... an interesting take. Didn't think you thought so too.
"Too?"
Yeah. Some of my friends have also compared the banquet hall to a battlefield.
Like Brooklyn. She said social spaces and warzones are the same at the end of the day.
"The comparison doesn't make much sense. Unless banquets became a life-or-death ordeal while I wasn't looking."
Heh, yeah. I guess it means social exchanges are complicated.
Either way, if the banquet is a battlefield, then I will fight. To the tune of my script, of course.
I guess that makes my dress my combat uniform. Wish I felt a little more comfortable in it, but there's no time for that now.
Enterprise's fighting spirit seems to ignite inside of her.
If I'm gonna go into battle...
Then, obviously, I need you behind my back, Commander.
What do say? Will you follow me?
Into the treacherous warzone that is the banquet?
"You already know the answer – gladly."

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>Dressed to Impress</size>

scripts.say: On the other end of Essex's room, the sound of rustling fabrics...
I-I'll be done in just a minute. Please don't turn around yet!
Aaand... there! Sheesh, putting a dress on without any help is a lot harder than I expected...
Wait, no! The thing just slipped! Ugh...
Okay... I'm ready now, Commander.
You can turn around now... and look at my dress!
Wh-what do you think?
Does it look good on me?

options.content: "It's night and day compared to before."

scripts.say: Really? You think so?
Although... I have mixed feelings about being "on par" with her...
Night and day, you say? I'm not sure what to make of that...
Sometimes, I just want to be told, "You look cute," or "You're pretty." That's not too much to ask...
She mutters something under her breath and turns on her heel. Still under the influence, she staggers and nearly trips over her herself.
Urgh... I feel dizzy. In hindsight, I really drank way too much...
Dang it, why is this stupid dress so long? It keeps getting in the way!
It's clear she's sobered up somewhat over the past fifteen or so minutes. That's a relief.
How, though? Sobering up takes longer than that, especially if you haven't eaten food or drank water.
Hey, Commander, could you help me over here?
I offer a hand to help her get her bearings straight.
Then, the next thing I know, she has wrapped her arms around mine and looks at me.
Hehehe... I got you nooow!
Pleeease, Commander. Can't you give me your honest opinion on how I look?
She squeezes my arm tightly. The wine must be empowering her – or at least encouraging her.
Hehe... Hehehe...
Words of praise... From the horse's mouth...
Even when I'm up against Enterprise, I'll try to look my best...
But... Her dress is really, really pretty... Hehehe...
Isn't that right... Commander?
She looks me in the eyes and flashes a soft smile.
Our faces are dangerously close to kissing distance. The smell of wine and her perfume tickles my nostrils.
Maybe it's just me... but you look even more attractive than usual tonight... ♪
My assumption was wrong. She has not sobered up at all.
There's no way I can let her roam the palace in her current state.
At the same time, I can't just leave her behind. I suppose I have to look after her for a while...

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>Hard Work is Rewarded</size>

scripts.say: Musashi invites me onto a small boat. We'll follow the canal to get to the banquet.
Hmm? You have a curious expression on you.
Is it my kimono you're drawn to? It's my only one, at the moment.
Dressing appropriately for the banquet is a must... and for some reason, she decided to change into a more traditional outfit.
I'm sure you recognize it. It's what I wore at our pop-up café.~
It's one of the reserve garments I packed in case something happened. I didn't expect to actually use it.
But enough about me – I've heard you're not only a guest at the banquet, but also something of an organizer as well.
"You've heard correctly. Who told you that, though?"
No one. It was merely a deduction based on your character. You are someone we can always turn to for help with anything.
On top of you working all day, you just helped with that luggage. You must be quite exhausted, no?
Putting on a strong front for your subordinates is all fine and well. However...
You needn't do it for me.
Then come hither. Rest your weary bones.
No one can see us aboard this boat, much less interrupt.
You may seek comfort beside me without fear of being judged.
...No response? Is there something that prevents you from relaxing?
"Not really. My work for the day is done, so it's not that. It's just..."
There is no need for "justs." You deserve a break after a tiring day, simple as that.
Now, close your eyes.

sequence: <size=51>Don't be nervous. Relax your muscles. *fluff fluff* ♥</size>
<size=51>Yes, just like that. Feels comfortable, no? Heehee.</size>
<size=51>I feel the fatigue leave my body – or is it my consciousness? It's hard to say...</size>
<size=51>*fluff fluff*...♥ *fluff fluff*...♥</size>

scripts.say: A brief, relaxing eternity passes aboard the boat. It really was what I needed.

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>Don't Be Scared</size>

scripts.say: Jean Bart leads me arm-in-arm to a quiet place elsewhere inside the palace.
Phew... This place feels safe enough.
Didn't ya hear me earlier? I don't wanna be noticed.
"So you led me all this way to avoid attention? Sounds a bit excessive."
Not like I had any damn choice.

options.content: "Was it to get away from Massachusetts?"

scripts.say: Yeah. I can't stand being around her. That's not the only reason, though.
*sigh*... Listen.
The shit Richelieu expects from me – the speech and all – I ain't cut out for it.
Forcing smiles, minding my manners, people staring at me like some painting...
I can't do it. I even told her that.
I know she's got her hands tied. Same with Clemenceau. Someone's gotta represent the Orthodoxy out there.
But that doesn't mean it HAS to be me.
Why not have Jeanne do it? Why not Marseillaise? They'd do much better than me.
"Maybe so, but the fact is that she entrusted YOU with the speech."
"And I can't imagine she did so just to make a fool of you."
Oh, for sure. She doesn't have bad intentions or anything.
If I had to guess, I think her goal is to get me used to being one of the Orthodoxy's representatives.
"So you understand where she's coming from. Then why did you run?"
"Okay. Here's what we'll do: I'll try to convince Richelieu to replace you with Jeanne so you don't have to–"
No.
I'm still gonna do it. I already said I would. I'm a Templar Knight, dammit – I don't back down.
"Then I have to ask again – why DID you run?"
Do I really gotta spell it out?
I'm not denyin' I'm nervous about it, but the Orthodoxy's reputation matters more than a bit of discomfort.
Jean Bart being upfront about her feelings is a rare and welcome sight. I can think of only one thing to say here.
"I believe in you."
Thanks. I appreciate it.
Anyway... 'bout time we head back now.
I ran away from Massachusetts without sayin' a word. Oughta go and formally apologize to her.
"That's a tall order right out of the gate. Do you want me to help? Chime in when you need it, maybe?"
Nah. I've gotta face my fears on my own. No two ways about it.
Besides, I haven't got the time to psych myself up.
So I just gotta do it – find Massachusetts and say sorry.
Also... I know it's a lot to ask, but...
You'll stick with me until it's time, won't you?

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>The Blackout Nightmare</size>
<size=51>'How long have I been out? I still have a mission to do...'</size>
<size=51>'Dammit... Brain fog makes it impossible to think...'</size>
<size=51>'Guess the sleeping med hasn't worn off yet...'</size>

scripts.say: I get the picture now. Continue with the job.
I'll say this one last time – bring 'em back ALIVE. Got it?
A figure I can only assume is Avrora barks out an order, then turns her attention to me.
Heh. You're finally awake. That was earlier than I expected.
Better that way. The soon this is over with, the sooner I can send you away.
Now spit it out. Tell me everything you know.
What was that? Are you playing dumb with me, or are you still drugged out?
Of course you don't. Like you don't all tell me that every single day.
Doesn't matter. I didn't expect you to spill the beans just because I asked nicely.
Since you didn't want to do this the easy way, we'll do it the hard way.
Let's see how much pain it takes to make you squeal. Hehehe...
"Avrora, no! Stop!"
Wait a second. Avrora would never say or do anything like this!
The only answer is...

options.content: "I'm not telling you anything! Just kill me!"

scripts.say: The second the thought forms in my head, my surroundings start to fade out, like a light being dimmed.
The world is once more engulfed in a confused, groggy darkness.
Oh? So you know my name. That means there's a rat in our ranks.~
Thanks for the tip. That gives me two cans of beans to crack open.
"I don't care what you do to me! I'm not telling you a damn thing!"
"My secrets... will die with me!"
Hah! Been long since I dealt with someone with an actual backbone. Now you've got me excited.~
I'm gonna enjoy finding out how long you'll last. Hehehe.
"AAAAHHHH!"
Cry! Scream! Eat this goddamn piroshki!~
Oh dear... The Commander is tossing and turning.
Maybe a lap pillow wasn't the brightest idea. My legs are getting numb...
Although... This is the least I can do, after that blunder.
"Avrora! Stop!"
*gasp*! St-stop what?
What kind of awful dream did you have?

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>Finally Letting Loose</size>

scripts.say: After enjoying a dance in the ballroom, Bismarck and I went to the theater room to view some performances.
That jazz number was very novel compared to the classical music I'm familiar with.
The same melody played with different instruments can produce an entirely new-feeling song.
Oh, you brought refreshments? Thank you, Commander.
"No problem. I hope they're to your liking."
They look delicious. Let me try one.
In her typical elegant and formal fashion, she picks up a pastry and takes a bite.
Delicious, and with a distinct mouthfeel.
"So, how do you feel about the banquet now? You seem to be enjoying yourself."
You could say that. The general vibe has changed a little with you around.
"Is it no longer formal and demanding of a serious approach, as you said earlier?"
...Yes. I suppose this situation calls for a party-person mindset.
It's rare that I get the chance to actually enjoy a banquet. It's partly due to who I am as a person.
Most of the time, I approach celebrations as a leader – formally, and moderately. It's a lot like a job, really.
Even when the chance presents itself for me to let loose, I can't get completely comfortable.
And let's be fair, neither can you. If you receive an important message, you need to respond immediately.
Then, suddenly, your guard is up and you can't enjoy the taste of good food or appreciate the sound of a great song.
"It doesn't have to be that way. The Iron Blood can handle one day without you at the helm."
Oh, to leave my work at the door and enjoy the moment with my friends...
I wish I could. But I have my duties.
"If something urgent does crop up, you can simply ask someone else to take care of it. That includes me."
You're right. I suppose I could briefly hang up my hat and rely on you.
...Alright. I'll take you up on your offer.
I'll do as you say and enjoy this banquet without worrying about what-ifs.
"I really hope you'll have the time of your life tonight."
I will, with you by my side.

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>A Toast to Our Host</size>

scripts.say: After finishing my stroll around the palace with Elizabeth, I return to the banquet hall, where I find someone waiting for me.
Master, I've been asked to forward a message to you from Her Majesty. I urge you to read it at once.
She hands me an ornate card, embellished with royal iconography.
In short, it tells me to come to a certain numbered room.
By the time I finish reading and look up, Sheffield is gone. I infer this to mean I should come alone.
Beyond the numbered door is a big room, furnished in typical Royal Navy fashion.
Its lavishness rivals that of Elizabeth's own royal chamber. It's almost hard to believe a room like this exists within this palace.
At the center of the room is a dining table. On the other end of it, Elizabeth sits by herself.
Welcome, Master. Her Majesty is waiting for you.
Took you long enough, servant!
"Sorry, I don't know this palace so I got lost for a while. That aside, very luxurious place you have here."
You mean this VIP room?
Of course it is. Elites such as me deserve elite treatment. I'm sure they provided Bismarck with something equally opulent.
"I take it you're done experiencing normalcy, then?"
I've enjoyed it enough for a while.
Belfast gestures at me, then shows me to my seat at the table.
Take a seat.
Reckon you still have room in your stomach?
"I might. Did the Royal Maids prepare the whole feast you have here?"
No, only the tea, courtesy of Bel. Everything else is from the Orthodoxy's kitchen.
It's the same as what they're serving in the banquet hall. If you're not hungry, you may pass.
"It might be the same food, but the experience is different. It surely affects the taste when you eat in a queen's opulent room, per her invitation."
Well, well! You can be charming from time to time.
My dinner with Elizabeth is pleasant.
The mood is quiet, relaxing, and feels like it's another world compared to the hustle and bustle of the banquet hall.
Leaning back to admire my surroundings, I notice something strange – while my cup contains tea, Elizabeth's seems to contain wine.
Wondering why you don't get any wine, do you? Because you need to stay sober until the main event.
As for why I'M drinking wine... I just wanted something different.
Let's not forget that the Orthodoxy is famous for its wine.
Furthermore, Richelieu put a great deal of thought into her selection.
She hand-picked different vintage brands to match each guest's preferences, you see. And she did a marvellous job.
She takes a sip from her cup of wine and savors it with all the elegance befitting a queen.
As I've said many times already, the Orthodoxy really did a remarkable job with this banquet.
Everything is spotless, from the general gist to the fine details.
But what do you think, servant? Have you been enjoying yourself?
"Absolutely. I've not once felt anything could've been better."
Good to hear. We're in agreement.
Right then, I hear a ring on my communicator. It's an invitation.
Must be from Richelieu. Seems you never have a moment to rest, eh?
Go. She's waiting for you.
Don't worry about me. I've had you to myself enough for one day. Plus, I'm a little tipsy, so I should stay and rest.
If you would, Master, please follow me.
Belfast leads me to the door. As I leave, I overhear Elizabeth whispering something to herself.
The Orthodoxy can have this one victory.
It's their banquet, after all. It'd be rude of us to steal their thunder.
Enjoy the celebration now, servant.
Schedule-wise, the banquet should be nearing its climax now.
In reality, though, spirits are still rising – both of the soul, and of the bottle.
I know you can hold your liquor, Comrade Commander. Don't be a teetotaler and drink up!
Don't you worry. My canteen actually contains water this time... or does it? Heehee~
Not again, servant! Stop letting the drunkards sink their claws into you!
The Commander certainly is popular. For better or worse...
What do you say we walk over and snatch the Commander for ourselves, Lady Musashi?
No. Only a fool gets between two fighting tigers to steal their prey.
Let us wait for a more opportune time, when the Commander needs external help.
And be vigilant. We aren't the only ones who want a piece of the Commander.
Well, fellow hunters, that might take a while. Let's pass the time with some of our domestically-produced beer, shall we?
Whew... Finally, a moment to breathe. Enjoying yourself, Jean?
Yeah. Not a bad party, I guess. You, uh... wanna share a toast?
Why, I'd love to. To a long and eventful night!
Heeey, Enterprise... You like the refreshments? I do, and I could use some more!
*hic*... Commander... C'mere, I wanna talk! Ahaha...
For god's sake, Essex... Go easy on the drinks. People are looking.
My gut told me that things would get a little TOO rowdy if I stayed in the hall, so I decided to step outside for a while.
Fortunately, nobody saw me sneaking out. I'd hate for it to look like I'm bailing on everyone.
I look up at the night sky, the laughter and cheering from inside the hall still ringing in my ears. It's like a battlefield in there.
I take a deep breath of fresh air. This is just what I needed.
Well, well. Going outside right before the clock strikes midnight.
Needed a break, I presume? That's why I'm here, too.
"I recognize that voice... Clemenceau?"
Do forgive me if I'm disrupting the moment.

options.content: Not at all. Stay here if you'd like.

scripts.say: Alright. If you're sure.
*sniff sniff*...
The girls in there really left their mark on you, didn't they?
I can smell perfume residue all over you. Iron Blood, Sakura Empire, Iris Orthodoxy... There's a little bit from everyone.
It must be exhausting, being passed around from faction to faction like a volleyball.
Maybe I should rub some of my scent off on you as well, hmm?
"Might the words 'have mercy on me' convince you not to?"
Heehee. I was only joking.
"Fair enough. By the way, you look a little worn out. Is it that taxing to oversee a banquet and speak to guests?"
It is. I'm very much not a people person.
Nor am I a party person. I'm not much for clinking glasses and engaging in warm conversations – I like my drinks with a side of sea breeze and solitude.
Besides, with Richelieu on the scene, nobody will notice if I'm gone.
...I'm curious, Commander. How do you feel about our banquet?

options.content: "It's a typical banquet, and I like that."
"It was a lot of work, but I'm having a great time."

scripts.say: Yes, typical. I think so too.
The celebrations we throw at this port feel normal and commonplace, in the best way.
They're symbols of the calm, peaceful life we enjoy, and the normality we strive to maintain.
Heehee. I feel like I know you better now than I did before.~
"It was a lot of work, but I'm having a great time."
But, it was worth it. As far as entertaining the guests is concerned, this banquet is perfect.
You deserve acknowledgment for your part, too. This banquet wouldn't be what it is without you.
Thrilling, you say? Interesting... Perhaps there are things beyond even my predictions going on in there.
Seems you navigate parties like you navigate the battlefield. I feel like I know you a little better now.
Alright, we've both had enough fresh air. It's time to lead you to the next battlefront.
"The next battlefront? Meaning...?"
When this palace was built, we had a few secret passageways and hidden rooms constructed as well.
Think of it as an exploratory detour. You won't be disappointed.
Come on. Let's enjoy this party to the end – together.

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>Enterprise's Speech</size>

scripts.say: As much as I want to check out the venue, I feel that I should have a look around the palace.
Two people are having a chat just down the hall...
That's everything I need to know? Noted.
I'm surprised that you came to tell me that. I was expecting Richelieu.
What can I say? Even I – a known behind-the-scenes schemer – need to take center stage now and again.
Now, I trust you're willing to deliver the Eagle Union's speech, yes?
Yeah. I'm up for it.
Great. Then if you'll excuse me... Oh, if it isn't the Commander.
Didn't see you there, Commander.
"Good evening, you two. I hope I didn't interrupt your conversation."
Not at all. Your timing couldn't have been better, in fact. We just finished our little talk.
Seeing as there's still some time before the banquet officially starts, I'll go on ahead and find some drinks. You two have a good one, now.~
You haven't seen Essex or Massachusetts around, have you? They said they were on the way.
As far as I can tell by Enterprise's expression, she doesn't seem particularly worried about them.
"Can't say I have, no. Do you reckon they've gotten lost?"
Maybe. I helped Essex with her dress, then sometime later she just disappeared on me.
Same with Massachusetts. She put on her dress, I turned around for a minute, and she was gone.
They're obviously SOMEWHERE in the palace, so I don't think they're in danger or anything. It's just...
Ah, forget it. I'm sure they're just doing something to pass the time.
Anyway... Could I have a minute of your time, Commander?
It's nothing important. I just wanted to ask you something.
"Sure, not a problem. What's on your mind?"
It feels weird to just come forth and ask it outright, but... what do you think about my dress?
I expected something else, given how she beat around the bush for a bit. I'm relieved this is all it was.
You really think so?
It took a while to put on, and I rarely ever wear dresses, so I wasn't entirely sure.
Hearing you say it does look good is a big relief.
"Glad to give you some peace of mind. On another subject, what were you and Clemenceau talking about earlier?"
Oh, that. We were discussing a speech for the banquet. It's a big day, after all, so it feels appropriate.
She asked me to deliver it on behalf of the Eagle Union.
"I see. Do you need any help with that?"
Well, the script itself is already finished, so I'm good on that front.
But I'd appreciate it if you could read it through, and maybe offer some feedback too.
"I could do that, no problem. First, though, we should find a place with fewer inquisitive people."
You're right. Someplace quiet would be ideal. Let's go.
And so, Enterprise and I take off, leaving the hall behind.

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>Drinks, Dresses, and Despair</size>

scripts.say: As much as I want to check out the venue, I feel that I should have a look around the palace.
I sense an intense gaze from somewhere nearby.
After a quick look around, I figure out who's watching. She doesn't realize yet that I'm here.
Man... Enterprise sure looks stunning in her dress...
*glug glug*... Pfah!~
It's Essex, gazing at Enterprise from afar. She's admiring her outfit and drinking wine straight from the bottle.
I	's leagues ahead of mine... How am I supposed to impress anyone like thiiis!
"What are you up to, Essex?"
Commander! Wh-wh-what brings you here?
Please don't say you heard me grumbling just now...
Oh god... Please forget it. Push it out of your memory...
You didn't? Phew... Wait, what DID I even say? Uhh...
She's had some drinks – a few too many, possibly. Maybe a little company will get her to take her hand off the bottle?
*stares drunkly*...
She opens her eyes wide and stares at my clothes like I'm a fashion model.
You know, I just realized... You're looking quite stylish, too.
Really rocking that fit... Hey, want some wine?
"No thanks, and I think you've had too much. I'd offer to sit down with you, but I think what you need now is to rest in the lounge."
Heheh, good point... No, wait, I still need to put my dress on! I can't go there yet...
Buhh... That reminds me, I have a fun fact.
Did you know I helped Enterprise put on her dress?
She's bad with dresses, you see, so somebody had to give her a hand...
So I did. It took quite some time, which she felt a little shy about.~
And that, right then, is when I realized! *glug glug*...
Did you realize it too, when you saw her, Commander?!
She forcefully puts her bottle down on the table with an audible thud, then looks at me intently again.
"Realize what? What are you talking about?"
Please. Now you're just playing dumb...
I realized that she had me beaten. There was no topping the beauty of her dress...
So I decided – screw it, why even bother with my own dress...
Now I see the reason why she sounded depressed.
However, she'll probably want to kick herself once she sobers up.
It's best not to let her get any more drunk than she already is.

options.content: (Take the wine bottle away from her.)

scripts.say: "It's not like you to give up without a fight."
"And furthermore – I still want to see how you'd look in your own dress."
You... You're right! I shouldn't give up before I've even tried.
This is the battle of the dresses... I won't admit premature defeat, even if I'm up against Enterprise!
Especially not when you're eager to see me all dressed up...
She seems to sober up ever so slightly from her defeatist daze.
Alright... I'll go back to my room immediately and get changed. You should come with me!
"Come again?"
You said you want to see me in a dress, didn't you?
The last thing I want is to dash your expectations, so I need to pick out the best dress possible.
The first step to doing that is to go back to my dorm room, together!
It doesn't seem like there's any chance she'll budge on this.
Left with no other option, I'm forced to leave the venue with her...

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>Bumpy Road</size>

scripts.say: As much as I want to check out the venue, I feel that I should have a look around the palace.
Curious about what the Sakura Empire is doing, I decide to go have a look – until a sound interrupts my thoughts.
A loud clanging, like something metallic fell over on the road.
In other words – the sound of an accident.
Bad news, Lady Musashi! Our manjuu carriage toppled on its side!
What do we do? Our luggage is all over the road!
Don't panic. First, check if anybody is hurt, then load the baggage back into the carriage.
Oh, it's you, Commander.
Just as trouble strikes, you appear before us. Perhaps this is fate?
Yes, your help would be much appreciated. Let's fix this little accident.
With everyone working together, we manage to load the luggage back onto the carriage.
Whew... Thanks for the assistance, Commander!
Indeed. You have my gratitude.
Oh! Oh no!
"Oh no" what? What's wrong?
Look what happened to Lady Musashi's banquet dress!
It seems it got dirty whilst we were loading the luggage back up...
Oh dear, that's awful. You can't wear a dirty dress to a banquet.
What do we do... Lady Musashi is meant to appear at the banquet really sooon!
It's not the end of the world. Fortunately, it didn't tear.
A little dirt is nothing we can't fix with some soap and water before I make my entrance.
Right! Of course. Let me see how long it would take to clean and dry the fabric... Hmm...
Not too long, luckily! Allow me to do it!
Very well. If you insist.
Meanwhile, I'll call the banquet staff and inform them you'll arrive a bit later than planned.
You mean calling Richelieu? It's best if I do that myself.
Accident or not, it affects the schedule. The least I can do is personally apologize to her for the delay.
As you say, Lady Musashi!

options.content: "I suppose everything worked out in the end."

scripts.say: You really needn't parrot people without reason...
It's truly fortunate you were here, Commander. Without your help, we'd still be lifting luggage.
Now, it'll take a while for Wakatsuki to clean my garb, and I don't wish to stand around idly.
Say, would you lend me a bit of your time?
I wish to repay my debt of gratitude to you for coming to our aid.

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>Spotlight-Shy</size>

scripts.say: As much as I want to check out the venue, I feel that I should have a look around the palace.
Over there, in a quiet corner of the palace, I spot Jean Bart. She seems lost in thought.
Our eyes lock for a moment. I wait for her to say the first word.
...But she doesn't, and she turns her gaze elsewhere. Maybe she's feeling absentminded?
Whatever the case, I should go over and say hello.
Of course you saw me. Tsk...
An angered look flashes on her face for an instant before she turns away from me.
...Okay, sorry. I'm not avoidin' you on purpose.
It's just that wherever you go, a crowd follows. I don't like the attention.
That's why I'm here, trying to stay low so ya wouldn't find me.
Or was. No point in that anymore. So, what is it?
She explains herself matter-of-factly, still looking away from me.

options.content: "I thought you could use some company."

scripts.say: How considerate of you.
Strangely? The hell ya talking about?
This is our banquet. There's nothin' odd about me being here. At least nothin' I can think of...
"You didn't put on a beautiful dress just to stand in a corner, did you? You should be enjoying yourself. Go talk to people, enjoy a drink or two."
Second time hearing that tonight.
Richelieu said the same thing. Maybe she wasn't just bein' polite.
I grab a drink and pull up a chair beside her. Something tells me she wants somebody to talk to.
...Don't get me wrong – I am enjoyin' myself. The whole Orthodoxy pulled all the stops to organize this thing, and the mood's great.
It's not the banquet itself I'm miffed about, but it's related.
See, Richelieu told me to deliver the Orthodoxy's speech later ton–
Evening, Commander.
You haven't seen Essex around, have you?
We came here together, but we got separated after a while.
M-Massachusetts! Aw, shit...
Long time no see, Jean.
Beautiful dress you have.
Speaking of dresses... Thoughts?
About what?
Um, my dress?
All of a sudden, Jean Bart hooks her arm around mine and escorts me out of the hall.
Huh. She didn't even rate my dress...

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>A Peculiar Apéritif</size>

scripts.say: As much as I want to check out the venue, I feel that I should have a look around the palace.
Suddenly, cheers and lively chatter erupt at a table not far away.
Whew! It totally lacks the kick of vodka, but the Orthodoxy's wine isn't half-bad. It's got good flavor to it!
Couldn't have put it better myself. Cheers!
While they did say we may drink as much as we'd like, please try not to have too much.
In a corner of the banquet hall, the Northern Parliament is having a small wine-tasting party.
Ah, Commander! Nice of you to stop by. Would you like to join us for a toast?
Didn't expect you to come around so soon, Comrade Commander.
It's funny. On the way here, Avrora kept repeating how she was so sure you'd show up at our table.
Hmm? I don't remember saying it THAT many times.
Either way – how about you take a seat and sip some wine with us?
It won't get us drunk because we're used to much stronger stuff, but it might just hit that sweet spot for you, Commander.
We won't force anything on you, of course. If you'd rather not drink at all, that's perfectly fine.
Oh, I just remembered – we still haven't changed into our dresses yet!
We got sidetracked as soon as we arrived. Gangut said she was "compelled" by the aroma in the air.
Then, the next thing I know, here we all are...
Clemenceau was very understanding, fortunately. She even sent extra wine our way.
Yeah, yeah. Let's rewind! We were talking about the Commander drinking with us – I know you want that, Avrora.
Yes, but if the Commander wishes to abstain, we must respect that choice.
So – would you like some wine, Commander?

options.content: "Well, it would be rude of me to refuse..."

scripts.say: That's the spirit!
Ahahahah! I knew you wouldn't say no!
Bottom's up, folks!~
You said it, comrade!~
See, Avrora? Comrade Commander is having a great time! You had nothing to worry about.
Ahahahaha! Now THAT'S how you drink! Keep it up, comrade!
All the world's sounds and pictures are getting hazy, fading...
How much have I drunk? I can't even remember...
That's enough now. The Commander is barely keeping it together.
Aww. Guess the fun's over. Avrora's got that look like she's not gonna budge.~
I'm surprised the Commander even drank with us for this long. Alas, all good things must come to an end.
Commander? Are you okay? Can you hear me?
"Wuh... Water..."
Water? No problem. It's a good thing I brought my canteen. Here you go.
Avrora produces a blurry canteen-thingy and hands it to me.
Uhh... The Commander just keeled over...
Commander! What's wrong?! Please wake up!
Avrora... This isn't water in the canteen! It's goddamn spirytus vodka!

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>The Wall at the Banquet's Center</size>

scripts.say: "...Hm? A Juustagram notification?"
"...Hm? A Juustagram notification?"
"And it's from Prinz Eugen, too. Let's see what it is."
She sent me a picture. In it, she and her Iron Blood comrades are smiling, laughing, enjoying the banquet.
But, something is off about it.
Namely, a certain someone isn't in the picture.
At the center of the banquet venue is Bismarck, sitting all alone at a table, enjoying a drink.
As more and more guests have shown up, the banquet's atmosphere has gotten warmer and livelier.
And yet, that doesn't seem to extend to her. It's as though there's an invisible, people-repelling barrier around her.
The only ones who'll talk to her are fellow Iron Blood girls. Everyone else is keeping their distance from her.
I should go talk to her and ask what's up.
Oh. Good evening, Commander.
"Hey, Bismarck. Do you have a moment?"
Your expression tells me that you have something on your mind.
To answer you – yes, I do. I'm all ears.
Aha. I've figured out why that invisible barrier surrounds her.

options.content: "You should let loose – you'd be more approachable then."

scripts.say: Ah. "It's meant to be a relaxed banquet," right?
Yes, I suppose it is, to the majority of people.
To you as well, I... No, it's simply a fact – I'm objectively failing to blend in.
Unlike Eugen. Wherever she goes, the party spirit follows.
"Did you ask Eugen to be the star of the night, because you feel you dampen the mood?"
Have you seen her, by any chance? Is she spreading the fun?
"Yeah. She sent me a photo. I just wish you were in it, with the rest of them."
You know me, Commander. I'm not a party person. It doesn't come naturally to me.
As you speculated, I just rain on everyone's parade when I'm around.
That's why I asked Eugen to take the initiative.
Judging by how she's doing, it seems I made the right decision.
"Alright. Them aside, then, how are you enjoying the banquet?"
Who's to say I am, or have to? There are different kinds of banquets.
Some are for fun and drinking, others are more formal in nature and demand a serious approach.
As Iron Blood's leader, this banquet falls into the latter category for me.
"I don't think Eugen sent me that photo just to show she and the rest are having a good time. They're concerned about you."
First Eugen expresses concern about me, and now you.
She cracks a wry smile.
"Why don't you go join them? Then they wouldn't be concerned about you."
A good point...
Say... The orchestra is gearing up for the ball.
If you don't mind, would you like to go with me?
She offers me her hand. I take it.
Thank you for accepting my invitation. Let's do as you suggested and go enjoy this banquet.~

sequence:
The Orthodoxy's Banquet

<size=45>A Minute with Her Majesty</size>

scripts.say: As much as I want to check out the venue, I feel that I should have a look around the palace.
Your Majesty! Look out!
A decorative vase placed dangerously to the edge of a desk threatens to fall over as Queen Elizabeth approaches. Sirius jumps in front of her and shields her with her own body.
Please be calm, Sirius. The inside of the palace is safe.
Mrmf! Mmgh!!
Oh, how clumsy of me! Please forgive me, Your Majesty!
*gasp*! What were you thinking? You nearly choked me with those huge knockers of yours!
Grrrr... Hmph!
My sincerest apologies. I shouldn't have held you so forcefully. Please give this naughty maid her due punishment!
"What's going on here?"
Why, if it isn't my servant.
Nothing is "going on" – except for Sirius being a klutz.
No matter. Your timing is perfect, servant. Come with me on a little stroll.

options.content: "Well, I've got an important thing to do..."

scripts.say: Good. Right this way.
Nonsense! What could possibly be more important than accompanying me, the queen?
Darn. Doesn't sound like I can't wriggle out of this one...
In the meantime, I shall prepare a beverage for after you finish your stroll.
Thanks, Bel.
Sirius, you go with her. She'll need your help.
But Your Majesty, you need an escort...
I'll be fine. The venue is safe, plus I have Sheffy watching over me from the shadows.
Well, if you're certain...
Shall I also prepare a light meal for you and my honourable Master while you're away?
There's quite some time before dinner, and I'd hate for you to be hungry until–
No need! There are hors d'oeuvres in the banquet hall. Moreover, the Iris Orthodoxy should be allowed to display its cooking knowledge today. The Royal Maids needn't do anything.
Elizabeth and I wander around the palace, admiring the sights and architecture.
Hmm... The Orthodoxy has done a respectable job with this banquet.
Although it's still only about 80% as good as the banquets we host.
"That's a specific estimate. You must have a keen, critical eye for these things."
I do. Let's imagine that we were hosting this banquet...
First of all, we wouldn't hang a painting on that wall. All the elements of the interior need to be in harmony, and...
With an excited tone, she points out a myriad of things they'd do differently. She seems to quite enjoy the act of critiquing.
Then, all of a sudden, she falls silent and deep in thought. I wonder why?
"You seem a bit restless. Did you dismiss Sirius and Belfast because you wanted to tell me something in private?"
What? No. I have nothing to tell you that I wouldn't if they were here.
Where did that come from? Are you pining for Sirius' cooking?
"She has improved – she can make chocolate and simple meals now – but no, that's not why I asked."
Ugh... Alright, if you really must know...
Look around you. People have been coming and going since I arrived.
And I've scarcely seen anyone with their subordinates in tow.
Richelieu doesn't have any assistants accompanying her, and neither do you.
That's what's normal at this banquet, and I simply wanted to experience this normalcy for myself.
Even if only for a little bit.
Just an ordinary shipgirl, not a queen, taking a stroll through this giant palace.
And with you for company.
"Is it 'normal' for me to follow you around?"
If I SAY it's normal, then it is!
Or what, do you think I don't mean it?
I'm confiding in you here, servant. I demand you take me seriously!
Otherwise, I can always get mad like a normal person and discipline you.
If you truly want my forgiveness, earn it.
Lucky for you, there's still some time before Bel comes back with that drink.
Until she does, think of something to appease me!~
What? Umm... By... By bemeaning you, or inflicting some light punishment...
I've got it! Something like what Ajax or Scylla would do.
Elizabeth's disturbing idea makes me stifle a laugh.
"To that, I say – it's not normal for a shipgirl to punish her Commander, is it?"
It's not? But I thought...
No matter! If you don't want to suffer, straighten out and look sharp!
Lucky for you, there's still some time before Bel comes back with that drink.
Until she does, think of something to appease me!~

sequence: And so, the festivity in the banquet venue reached its peak.

scripts.say: Palace - Banquet Hall
Well, well, there's the Commander.
You sure took your sweet time, servant!
Do you know what a banquet without you is? Dull, that's what!
I have to agree. We all missed you, Commander.~
Now, shall I get you something to drink?
Spirits are high tonight, Commander.
I hope you enjoy the atmosphere as much as I do.
If ya see anything less than perfect, please try to ignore it...
Yeah, I know it's not my style to say "please," but still.
What I'm trying to say is – I hope you have a hell of a time tonight.
Commander! Can you feel the excitement in the air? I sure can!
This is only the start, though! Peak excitement will be when the performances start!~
Commander, thank you for always being here for us. You are the wind in our sails and the lighthouse that shows us the way.
...That sounded more wistful than I meant it to. Ahem.
Happy anniversary, Commander. Cheers.
A fresh breeze reminiscent of early morning blew through the trees, whipping up robust pink petals and scattering them about.
This is...
The sloped road seemed to go on forever, lined by trees shedding their petals.
Nagato approached one such tree and gently placed a hand on it—
Sakura Empire
In the luxurious Guardian Fox's chamber, Nagato awakened.
Was that... a dream?
If it was, why do I continue to feel that stinging pain from when I touched the Sacred Sakura?
It was a terrifying dream, in which the sacred tree had decayed in fetid fog.
Withering, devastation. A spectacle of destruction, painted by the pain and misery of all who lived.
*knock* *knock*
Kawakaze? You may enter.
The screen door slid open, and Kawakaze, the white-haired servant of the Guardian Fox, sat on her knees behind it.
I'm sorry to disturb you at this late hour, Lady Nagato.
It is fine. In fact, I meant to ask something of you.
Are the widespread reports of the Sacred Sakura's withering true?
Yes, Lady Nagato. I've already verified the reports firsthand... They're all true.
(In that case, that was no mere dream.)
So the withering of our sacred tree has spread...
Nagato straightened out her clothes and stood up, while Kawakaze entered her room and expertly closed the shoji window.
The folding screen stretched wide, hiding Nagato's figure as she was dressed.
Kawakaze removed Nagato's nightgown, combed her long black hair, and rinsed her with water.
After wiping her down with a hand towel, she helped Nagato change into her usual day clothes.
Kawakaze, inform Musashi that I will be visiting at sunrise.
Lady Nagato, about that...
Musashi is already waiting outside.
Sakura Empire - Nagato's Abode
During the midnight hour, the full moon hung over the starry night sky.
On one balcony in a corner of the castle, Kawakaze performed a tea ceremony in which she poured tea for two.
Visitor and host – Musashi and Nagato – sat side by side, rather than facing each other.
Despite the vast property and magnificent castle, their meeting was small and isolated.
Wind caused the leaves in the trees to rustle, prompting the two to begin their conversation after a sip of tea.
Lady Nagato, tell me what you saw in your dream.
I was walking down a long, tree-lined path, with sakura blossoms raining down from above.
When I tried to catch the falling petals, they disappeared.
And just as I touched the Sacred Sakura, it withered and was engulfed in darkness.
All that remained was silence.
I dreamed of something similar, myself.
The same sacred tree, but not in the midst of a tree-lined path.
I only saw one tree... It jutted out far into the sky, and its branches and leaves blotting out the sun.
Far bigger and taller than the Sacred Sakura you sealed yourself into...
However, like your dream, it would not last.
The tree abruptly began to wither.
Its blooms crumbled into dust, leaving gaunt branches in their wake.
...And similarly, it all disappeared into endless darkness in the end.
You've heard the rumors of the Sacred Sakura all over the empire withering, haven't you? Musashi, what are your thoughts?
Lady Nagato, we believe we have found a pattern to the withering.
As one approaches the holy sanctuary of the Sakura Empire where you sleep, such reports grow in frequency.
Right. I've noticed this, too.
Our land's Sacred Sakura are all connected. It is not unsurprising that the withering would spread.
However, there is one clear lesson to be learned from this omen.
...The corruption will come in full force before long.
Nagato stood up, produced a small pouch, and handed it to Kawakaze.
The full moon is lovely tonight. I'm in the mood for a stroll.
Lady Nagato...
You stay, Kawakaze. If I don't return by dawn tomorrow, give that pouch to Mutsu.
Yes, Lady Nagato.
On this night, wispy clouds covered the moon, and even the ripples of light on the water were indistinct.
After leaving the castle, Nagato and Musashi walked slowly upon the stone path.
It was then that a slight breeze lifted some fallen leaves and blew them toward the young Guardian Fox.
She fended them off with her sleeve and looked to the sky.
The clouds had faded, allowing the moon to shine its delicate blue light upon the courtyard again.
Lady Nagato...?
After gazing in silence at the lake for some time, Nagato finally spoke.
...Musashi, do you remember this place?
Long ago, she used the Sacred Sakura to communicate a message to me.
To perform the ritual and summon her to this place.
...You mean the Sage.
Exactly.
After a short silence, Nagato began walking toward the lake.
If you and I have had similar dreams, then the solution to this problem is all but clear.
Isn't that right?
Musashi, you and I are alone.
Speak frankly.
Then allow me, Lady Nagato.
The withering of the Sacred Sakura is an ill omen concerning the safety of the Prime Sakura.
If signs of decay can be found there, too, then that will explain things.
...It's like the last time this happened.
However, I don't know if we have the strength to fight our enemy today...
The Prime Sakura is isolated from the earthly world, protected by the Sage.
If something did happen there, that would mean the entire sanctuary is in peril.
This is true. The withering of the Sacred Sakura may be reverberations from the last time...
We may need to be prepared for the worst.
...I say we make for the sanctuary right now.
Memory - Musashi's Abode
It was late at night. Musashi, a high-ranking member of the Sakura Empire, happened to have a freeloader in her home.
Said freeloader, a girl with a veil draped over her face, gazed out the window and up at the moon.
*stomp* *stomp* *stomp*!
Sorry! I heard a weird noise, so I came to check things out!
Whoa. You should be resting... Is everything okay?
There's nothing to be concerned about. I'm only here because I couldn't sleep.
Hm? Are you looking for Lady Musashi?
She's out right now, so...
Despite Sakawa saying so, the girl showed no intent to leave. Instead, she retrieved two cushions placed in the corner of the room.
It's not as if I'll ever get to sleep. Shall we chat?
Sure!
Oh! I almost forgot! Should I, um... make an offering of tea for you, or...?
You don't have to do all that.
Okay... Um, what should we talk about?
Hmm. Could I ask you to tell me about the past?
The past...
Lady Musashi did tell me to answer any questions you have, so I'm glad to share anything I know.
But when you say "the past"... What exactly do you want to know?
How about... the Reenactment of the treaty?
Oh, that~ You mean the time Lady Nagato planned special training exercises and retired from being the Combined Fleet flagship?
I only know bits about it that I've heard here and there, so...
Hearsay is acceptable.
All I want is to know what you know.
The girl removed her veil, revealing her divine visage.
Sakawa gazed into her crimson eyes, perhaps out of curiosity, or perhaps bewitched by some magic shining within.
After a nervous sigh, she finally told the story.
It IS just hearsay, though... One morning long ago—
Memory - Sakura Empire Long ago?
A fresh breeze reminiscent of early morning blew through the trees, whipping up robust pink petals and scattering them about.
The sloped road seemed to go on forever, lined by trees shedding their petals.
Oh, Yuudachi? Good morning~
Wooow, the sakura are in full bloom~
Hm? Why are you here, Michishio? Aren't you supposed to be cleaning the courtyard at this time of day?
Are you slacking off?! Do I smell a slacker?!
Geez, Yuudachi, I finished cleaning hours ago~
Lady Mutsu has a very important guest today, so she sent us all home early~
Is that the same as Lady Nagato's guest?
Maybe... Isn't it unusual, though?
She didn't give us any more details than that, though, so there's no point trying to guess.
Heheh, by the way, I made some more sakura mochi yesterday~
You mean I can have some?! Your sakura mochi is the best! Let's find a place to chow down!
You're so impatient! When you want to eat good food, you can't just sit anywhere willy-nilly. You need good scenery!
...Hmm, but where would that be...?
Lady Nagato's courtyard?
Absolutely not! Geez~
Then let's sit in the grass over there! We can look at the sakura trees while we eat. Yeah, that's perfect!
You just go find a place now, Yuudachi. I'll go get the cake box.
...Oopsie!
Not looking where she was going, Michishio ran into somebody and fell. However, her victim quickly caught her.
The person she had run into – a tall woman wearing a white robe – gently brushed the flower petals off of her head.
Michishio looked up at her apologetically and bowed.
I'm sorry! I should've watched where I was going!
But the tall woman had already disappeared, before the flower petals she'd brushed away could fall to the ground.
Michishio! I found a good spot!
When Michishio turned around, she saw Yuudachi sitting in the grass and waving at her.
R-right! I'll go get that cake box~
(That lady... was kind of weird...)
Clouds blocked the moon once more, making the rooms in Musashi's abode just a little darker.
After that, Lady Nagato announced that she was resigning from her position as flagship, and that there would be combat exercises to decide her successor...
In other words, you're saying that her mysterious guest caused it all to happen?
N-not necessarily! It's just speculation...
The thing is, Lady Nagato left on a trip for a while before her announcement.
But weirdly, nobody in the Sakura Empire ever SAW her doing that.
The truth is...
Sakawa shifted to sit on her knees seiza-style and whispered quietly.
Lady Nagato went to this "sanctuary."
And she wasn't alone. I hear Musashi went with her.
More than that... I went with them as Musashi's bodyguard.
Anyway, that's all I know. I don't actually know what happened inside the sanctuary, okay?
Only Lady Nagato, Musashi, and that weird guest I mentioned went in there.
...And there you have it. That's everything I know!
I see... So Musashi went to visit the Guardian Fox, too?
Yeah...
This isn't related at all, but has Musashi mentioned any dreams to you lately?
Not really...? Oh, but a few days ago, she really didn't look good.
It was like she was sleep-deprived... Maybe nightmares kept her from sleeping?
Before the girl could answer, thunder roared outside.
Lightning struck several more times until a thin, purple spear of electricity finally struck in the direction of the lake.
That's...
Musashi's signal. I should get going.
Also, you can have... Ahem. I mean, I confer this to you.
It's been a while since I got to talk to someone like this, after all. Heheheh.
She took Sakawa's hand and placed something small in her palm.
...Origami?
On closer inspection, it wasn't a paper animal. It looked like it was modeled after some kind of head or face.
The face, with two adorable horns on its head, was quite familiar to Sakawa.
Wow, this is... me, isn't it?
Heheh. Thank you~♪
She gingerly held the origami in her hands and gazed out the window, where the girl previously was, toward the moon outside.
And she offered a heartfelt prayer.
Please, Dragon God...
Make sure they all come home safe...
An ominous black fog closed in from all directions.
Musashi tried to cut it away with her purple lightning blade, but the severed darkness only reformed again to attack.
Bear witness! Haaaah!
Materializing her mental imagery, Nagato's prayer became a guiding light that drove off the darkness.
However, it was weak, and it only managed to slow the darkness's encroachment temporarily.
We only have one choice now.
Musashi, I'll entrust the last of the Guardian Fox's power to your blade. Strike true, and cut a way out of this situation!
...You mustn't.
Even if I were to escape, you...
It is my duty as a miko to protect the Sakura Empire.
I vowed to do so, and I showed you my resolve during our game.
Bear witness... to the Guardian Fox's power!
The young woman forcibly pushed the sheathed sword, imbued with the last of her power, into Musashi's arms.
In the next instant, the blackness engulfed Nagato.
Lady Nagato...!
Pure nothingness—a world devoid of sound or light, home only to endless darkness.
In the darkness of the sanctuary, memories flashed through Musashi's mind.
The Sacred Sakura is withering... And the people are losing faith...
A few days ago, I relinquished my position as the Combined Fleet's flagship.
The Reenactments have acquiesced to it, of course, but I have one more reason.
You were badly wounded in the sanctuary. At this rate, your hull...
My soul will transmigrate without issue. Even without me, she whom I entrust the Sakura Empire to will do just fine.
Lady Nagato, please. As long as we have the Sacred Sakura, you don't have to let yourself be sunk.
Seal myself in the Sacred Sakura, hm?
It is a good idea, but... There's something that I must do first.
Musashi, how long do you believe I can last under these circumstances?
...That's more than enough. Have Amagi arrange a special exercise.
During the exercise, I will announce my resignation from the post of Combined Fleet flagship.
*jingle*
The ringing of wind chimes.
Musashi sat up in bed and gazed at the moonlight outside.
She thought to herself as she got dressed.
It was already late at night. Hearing the noise, Sakawa came running.
Musashi? Umm, are you going out?!
...Don't yell so much, please.
I have urgent business with Lady Nagato. I'll be leaving at once.
Okay, but, umm... You don't look good, Musashi. Why not rest until morning?
I told you, it's urgent. I mustn't waste any time.
Sakawa, ensure you take good care of our guest.
If she asks you any questions, tell her all you know.
Musashi walked alone under the full moon.
She turned around and saw the faint light of candles still burning in the castle tower through the window.
