It appeared that she was not the only restless one on this long night...

sequence:
The Bon Before the Voyage

<size=45>1 The Proposal</size>

scripts.say: Hi, this is Long Island at the reception desk! How can I help?
There is a markedly peppy tone in Long Island's voice as she answers the phone.
Alrighty. I'll pass your message on right away!
Meanwhile, I'm standing at the door of the provisional office set up for a special project.
A hesitation passes through me as I put my hand on the doorknob. Should I really open it?
Two weeks prior - Commander's Office
Commander, how about having a pleasure cruise this year?
A crowd has gathered in my office to discuss vacation ideas, and Harbin brings up an interesting one.
Hmm. A pleasure cruise...

options.content: Say no more. We're doing it!

scripts.say: Hahah! I knew you'd be on board! Pun intended.
Before we go any further, I should probably explain to you and everyone else why I think it's a good idea.
To start off, a cruise ship can move and serve many more people than a plane, for instance.
The port also already has all the necessary infrastructure. A dock, refueling facilities, a cargo loading platform, and so on.
Now, I know what you're thinkin' – traveling by sea isn't very novel to us as shipgirls – but that's for work. We don't often get to ENJOY being out at sea.
That's where the cruise comes in. It'll put a fresh spin on a familiar setting and spark new conversations.
And of course, we can have an office and conference room on board to ensure your workflow stays on course.
I like it. A pleasure cruise could make for a splendid vacation.
All of us out at sea, together on a ship – sounds almost like a field trip.
More like a mobile base for the Commander.
I dunno. Like Harbin said, we see the ocean all the time. Doesn't feel very special, does it?
Shouldn't we spend our vacation days on something better than, like, cruising the ocean with no particular goal?
And like Harbin said, we experience the sea through the lens of work, not pleasure.
I know what you're picturing – a mass-produced ship with bunk beds, rations, and rotating shifts.
Forget all that. A cruise ship is the polar opposite. It has luxury cabins, fine dining, a spa, and more.
Exactly! And instead of sailing nowhere, why don't we go to Seabreeze Island instead?
You know, that empty island we built a resort on. There's even more vacationing we can do there.
Yes, and it doesn't stop there. We could go practically anywhere in the world if we wanted to.
But I digress. We can discuss destinations another time.
A cruise sounds fun! I wanna go!
Me too! Take me on a long and romantic cruise, Owner!
You know what happens on cruise ships? Mysteries!
From staircases that shouldn't exist, to guest rooms appearing from thin air, to strange footprints in the cabin corridors!
Ohh, I can already feel my blood pumping!
Yeah! Let's go on an adventure cruise!
A great adventure cruise!
A BIZARRE adventure cruise!
It's starting to sound pretty unanimous in here.
I like unanimous. Let's go with Harbin's cruise plan!
There is just one small issue with her plan, Commander.
Namely, we do not have a cruise ship.
It so happens I do. I'd even be willing to lend it to you.
Yeah, about that... I was considering just buyin' one.
But the more I thought about it, the more I realized it wasn't a great idea.
Buying one would save us a lot of trouble, but no prebuilt cruise ship out there could cater to all our needs.
So the best option, really, is to build one from scratch ourselves. Trust me, it'll be worth it.
I dig it!
I agree. A cruise ship tailor-made to suit our needs will make the vacation even better.
And it'll allow us to implement some more... novel ideas.
Suit yourselves. What say you, servant?
Our shipyard does have the resources to construct a cruise ship from the ground up. Making modifications by ourselves would be cheaper, too.

options.content: Let's build a cruise ship, ladies.
We'll build our own ship! With blackjack and bars!

scripts.say: Wait! I've got one more idea I think you'll like!
You do? Let's hear it.
Okay, so, the port's easily got the facilities to not only build a cruise ship, but to build it discreetly, right?
Yes. And?
And we've also got the financial flexibility to build it entirely by ourselves, right?
Yes. And...?
Well, if it ain't too much to ask, do you think we could build the ship in secret?
By that I mean, not disclosing the project to anyone not directly involved.
Then once it's time to announce the cruise, it'll be a big surprise. Of course, we wanna surprise you, too, so we won't tell you how it's progressing.
How's that sound? Do we keep it under wraps, or make it public right away?
Everyone loves a surprise. Let's do that.
Sweet! Then we'll get to work and only let you know once she's been launched. No peekin', and no askin' for leaks!
And that's the arrangement we settled on.
Yat Sen, Elizabeth, Richelieu, and Veneto formed a committee to plan the whole project and guide its course.
I have no reason to doubt their competency, of course.
It's just... I'm curious...
Ah, screw it. I should get back to my office and pick up my work.

sequence:
The Bon Before the Voyage

<size=45>2 Working Hard Or Hardly Working?</size>

scripts.say: It's a new day, and I'm at the door to the Cruise Planning Committee. Again.
I spent the whole night arguing with the angel and devil on my shoulders, one telling me to keep my promise, and the other, to satisfy my curiosity. I've come up with a compromise.
It's not breaking my promise if I overhear them through the door... right?
Ugh... I'm beat. I don't know if I can keep on pretending to work hard like this.
Emden said the Commander WILL give in to curiosity and walk through that door...
But I'm really starting to doubt that! All my efforts have been for nothing!
Hard work is hard, even when you're faking it!
*sigh*... Well, since it doesn't matter, I'm gonna do something fun instead.
Let's see here... What game do I play...
RING RING RING!
Oh. Here comes work.
Hi, this is Long Island from General Affairs. How can I help you?
Uh-huh. A question for the Construction Committee. Got it.
Stay on the line and I'll ask the Central Committee about it.
CLUNK!
Whew. Anyway, time to game!
Sometime later...
RING RING RING!
Dang it, someone's calling again.
Hi, this is Long Island from General Affairs. How can I help you?
Mhm... What? The Construction Committee? Oh, right, your question...
Well, good news! I got an answer from them.
They said there's ample room in their budget and you can implement whatever you want.
An onboard garden, a pool, shops, a theater – anything you can think of.
Yeah, including a large Sardegnian thermae!
...How large? As large as you want it to be!
Yup, they could easily squeeze in an aquarium somewhere, too.
Listen, if you can imagine it, there's room for it.
I hope that answers your question. Please call again if you have any more. Bye!
CLUNK!
Easiest job of my life. Back to the game!
I back away from the door.
I can't believe my ears!
Not only is she gaming on the job, she's also casually approving every idea that blows her way!
I'll bet a thousand coins she hasn't run any of this by the Central Committee!
That cruise ship is doomed if she keeps manning the phone...
No matter how smoothly the construction is going, I can't ignore what I just heard.
That said, I can't directly confront the committee about it, either. That would break my promise with Harbin.
This situation calls for an indirect approach. I should...

options.content: Punish Long Island for her indolence.
Reward Long Island for her efforts.
Shrug and go back to the office.

scripts.say: The ghost wants to play games during her shift, huh?
Let me just fetch her account info...
I issue an order to TB to pit Long Island against some "worthy" opponents. If she really wants to game on the job, she can go right ahead.
Sometime later...
Dang it! They killed me again!
This is dumb! When did the AI in this game get so overtuned?!
Ugh... Now it's clock-out-o'-clock, too...
I can't even be bothered to leave! I'm too tired after getting whooped all day!
On second thought, I can empathize. Sitting alone in front of a desk all day is incredibly boring.
Let me just fetch her account info...
I issue an order to TB to give Long Island a whole heap of in-game items. If she really wants to game on the job, she can go right ahead.
Sometime later...
What the heck? My inbox is flooded!
Compensation for bugs, compensation for bug fixes, compensation for bugs caused by bug fix... Even compensation for a bug fix for a bug fix!
Wait! Could this be a gift from the God of Laziness for my dedication to the faith?
Yippee! My shift just ended, too! Whew, what a long but satisfying workday this was!
Sometime later...
Whew, that was a lot of fun!
I did nothing the whole day – just the way I like it!
Oh, it's the end of my shift! Woohoo! Time to go home!

sequence:
The Bon Before the Voyage

<size=45>3 Curiosity Got the Cat</size>

scripts.say: *yaaawn*... Man, I wanna go home already...
What cruel, evil person decided I have to work so early?
Bleh. I'll just read some manga while my brain warms up.
Once more, I'm at the door to the Cruise Planning Committee.
I can hear Long Island on the other side, thinking aloud about what she'll do instead of working.
Reading manga today, are we? Let's hear what else she says.
RING RING RING!
Dang it! It was just getting interesting, too.
This phone picks the worst time to ring!
RING RING RING!
Ahem... Hi, this is Long Island from General Affairs. How can I help you?
Uh-huh. A question for the Furnishing Committee. I hear you.
Give me one minute and I'll ask the Central Committee about it.
CLUNK!
Whew. Now back to the manga.
Sometime later...
RING RING RING!
Hi, this is Long Island from General Affairs. How can I help you?
Mhm... Say what? The Furnishing Committee? Oh, right, uh...
Yeah, I talked to them and got an answer!
They said, uh, there's tons of space inside the cruise ship, so furnish it however you want. Visual cohesion is strictly optional.
Yup, that's right. Go with whatever you want.
Nope, the guest rooms don't all need to be in the same style.
If you wanna make the banquet hall all old-school and fancy, go right ahead!
Yeah, a nouveau and modern look for the adjacent ballroom would totally work!
Look, you've got carte blanche – I think that's the word – to furnish the ship however you want.
I hope that answers your question. Please call again if you have any more. Bye!
CLUNK!
Whew. All in a day's work. Anyway, manga!
I back off from the door.
Yup. Long Island is slacking on the job again.
Anyone in my position would be justifiably alarmed about this, no matter how well the construction is going.
But, again, I can't approach anyone about it directly.
So, I can only do something in an unofficial capacity. Something like...

options.content: Punish Long Island for her indolence.
Reward Long Island for her efforts.
Shrug and go back to the office.

scripts.say: Yesterday, it was video games, today, it's manga. And she's not the least bit ashamed about it!
Someone needs to put this lazy ghost in her place!
I open the door and tiptoe inside, grabbing the next volume of her manga and hiding it somewhere.
Sometime later...
Wow, what a twist! I need to know what happens next.
...Huh? It's not here? Where'd the next volume go?
Nooooo! Now I'll never know how they solve the caaaase!
You know, I can't blame her for doing something else. Sitting alone in front of a desk all day is really tedious.
You wanna read manga, do you? Then I'll get you all the manga you could ever want!
I open the door and tiptoe inside, sneakily leaving a whole stack of manga on a table.
Sometime later...
Whew. What a story!
But... Oops. I've read for a long while now. I should do at least SOME work to...
Huh? I haven't read these mangas before. Who left these here?
Wait! Could this be a gift from the God of Laziness for my dedication to the faith?
Well, hallelujah! I'll just keep reading until closing time!
Whew. What a story!
Hardly working can really be hard work.
Oh, it's the end of my shift! Woohoo! Time to go home!

sequence:
The Bon Before the Voyage

<size=45>4 Treat Yourself</size>

scripts.say: Yet again, I'm at the door to the Cruise Planning Committee.
I press my ear up against the door. It's silent on the other side.
I peek in through the crack in the door and see a smorgasbord of snacks on the table.
As for Miss Receptionist, she's lying face-down, having a nap.
This time, she's gorging herself full on snacks and sleeping. Very classy.
It also looks like she has built a cruise ship out of those snack boxes.
I suppose she must be looking forward to the cruise, even if she won't put in an ounce of effort toward its construction.
She at least cares to some degree, so she won't it screw up TOO badly... right?
RING RING RING!
Zzzzz...
RING RING RING!
RING RING RING!
*yaaawn*... Oh, crap! I succumbed to food coma after eating all those snacks!
Um, hi! This is Long Island from General Affairs! How can I help you?
Come again? Oh, the Supplies Committee... Yeah, they gave me an answer yesterday.
They said, uh, there's tons of cargo space, so you can bring all the raw ingredients you want.
You heard me. Bring as much as you want!
Yup, all of them! Sardegna, the Eagle Union, the Orthodoxy, the Empery, et cetera et cetera.
Hm? What about the Royal Navy?
Uhh, forget about their food and just bring their desserts!
Is, um, what the Central Committee said. Yes.
Let me reiterate – bring anything you want and as much of it as you want. There's ample room!
I hope that answers your question. Please call again if you have any more. Bye!
RING RING RING!
Um, hi! This is Long Island from General Affairs! How can I help you?
...You'd like to know about security measures for the Commander's cabin?
I mean, do we really need any?
Because, you know, it'll just be us shipgirls and the Commander aboard the ship.
...What do you mean, "that's exactly why we need it"?
Oh. That's why. In that case, I think– Sorry, I mean the Central Committee thinks you're right!
Please install all the strongest security measures in the Commander's cabin!
...Of course! You need a blast door if you want the strongest security possible!
...Well, yeah, a guard room is indispensable, too!
...Absolutely! If Fort Knox has a separate ammo storage, I don't see why we shouldn't!
Look, long story short, you can never be too sure when it comes to ensuring the Commander's safety!
I hope that answers your question. Please call again if you have any more. Bye!
CLUNK!
Geesh, there's a lot of people calling today. Nothing I can't handle, though!
Answering those calls really woke me up. Now it's time for snacks!
I take it back. She is screwing it up spectacularly.
Also, what was that about a separate ammo storage?
For god's sake, we're building a cruise ship here, not a battleship!
Even if the project is proceeding without a hitch, I can't help but feel like this is going wrong.
But, yet again, I can't bring this up with the Central Committee because I promised to let them do their work.
There isn't much I can do, but at least I can...

options.content: Punish Long Island for her indolence.
Reward Long Island for her efforts.
Shrug and go back to the office.

scripts.say: Two days ago it was games, yesterday it was manga, and now she's stuffing herself on snacks...
We're reaching levels of slacking previously unheard of! That lazy ghost can't keep getting away with it!
I open the door and tiptoe inside, sneakily stealing all the oxy-cola from the fridge.
Sometime later...
Urp... I might've eaten too many snacks. I need some oxy-cola.
...Huh? What the heck?! It's all gone!
Someone took all the dang oxy-cola!
Nooooo! I'm sooooo thirstyyyyy!
Honestly, I might have done the same if I were her. Being alone and stuck in front of a desk all day is soul-crushing.
You love snacks, do you? I'll give you all the snacks you can eat!
I open the door and tiptoe inside, sneakily leaving a minifridge in a corner and a pile of snacks and drinks on the table.
Sometime later...
Urp... I might've eaten too many snacks. I need some oxy-cola.
...Huh? What the heck?! It's all gone!
Where'd all THESE snacks come from? There's even a new minifridge!
Wait! Could this be a gift from the God of Laziness for my dedication to the faith?
Aha! Hard work DOES always pay off!
Oh boy! So many drinks to choose from!
Sometime later...
Urp... I might've eaten too many snacks. I need some oxy-cola.
Ahh! That hits the spot!
But... *yawn*... Now I'm sleepy...
Still a few hours of my shift left to go... I guess I'll have another nap.

sequence:
The Bon Before the Voyage

<size=45>5 Before the Launch</size>

scripts.say: For a fourth time, I stand before the door to the Cruise Planning Committee.
Right as I press my ear against the door, it suddenly opens.
Heehee. Here to eavesdrop again, are you, dear human?

options.content: Huh? How long have you known?
I haven't broken my promise! Long Island never spoke TO me!

scripts.say: Since the first time you set foot outside your office. "You're as subtle as a brick through a window."
"Of course. Whatever you say." Oh, you are such a darling human, making clever excuses.
Don't be alarmed, though. Long Island doesn't know that you're here.
Her attention is solely on her work, if you can call it that. "She's concentrating, in her own way."
Let me guess... You knew I'd come here, so you specifically put Long Island in charge of the phone.
"Heehee. I thought it was obvious." We knew that curiosity would get the better of you, yet you didn't have the heart to break your promise.
So it was easy to surmise that you'd walk the razor's edge, coming here merely to eavesdrop.
And so, we employed Long Island and knowingly let you listen in on her. "It's adorable how predictable you are, human."
Don't worry about what she said on the phone. All the things she discussed have been brought before the Central Committee.
All the inane ideas, discarded. "And all the good ones, kept."
Now all you need to do, dear human, is be patient and wait.
They KEPT some of the ideas? So then...

options.content: Did they keep the onboard garden?
Did they keep the onboard aquarium?
Don't tell me they kept the blast door!
Please don't tell me they kept the ammo storage!

scripts.say: Heehee. A promise is a promise, dear human. No amount of pleading will coax an answer out of Emden. "Remember, it's meant to be a surprise."
Although, there is actually important one thing WE were hoping to ask YOU.
Have you thought of a name for the cruise ship yet?

sequence:
One-Punch! Bulin!

<size=45>1.An Ancient Legend</size>

scripts.say: Legends speak of a god in far-off lands who will grant any wish you can imagine.
However, a legend is all it is. A legend from long, long ago...
Any wish you can imagine, bulin?
Nuh-uh, that's impossible, bulin! Not even my almighty wrench can do that, bulin!
Even if that god does exist, they live in some unreachably distant place, bulin!
Even my drill that pierces the heavens can't take you THAT far, bulin!
Not with that attitude it won't, bulin!
My godly luck tells me the legend is real, bulin!
I'll prove it, even if I have to defy the universe itself, bulin!
With those words, the defiant MKIII Bulin walked away.
Whoa, bulin! She sounded mad, bulin...
We ought to support her, bulin! Let's get her the strongest hammer around and go on an adventure, bulin!
I know a hammer that can turn even diamonds into dust, bulin! I'm gonna find it, bulin!
Sounds like an awesome idea, bulin!
I'm the bestest treasure hunter alive, bulin! I'm going with you, bulin!
I'll find that hammer if it's the last thing I do, bulin!
And so, the three Bulin sisters went off on their separate adventures.
One fateful day, they would reunite...

sequence:
One-Punch! Bulin!

<size=45>2.Hard Work Pays Off</size>

scripts.say: The MKIII Bulin has been training day in, day out ever since she first set off on her quest.
Feel the might of my Kitty Kabam Hammer, bulin!
I did it, bulin! I've become the strongest girl alive, bulin!
My daily workout routine of 100 situps, 100 pushups, 100 squats, and a 10-kilometer run has turned me into a demigod, bulin!
But my Kitty Kabam Hammer has reached its physical limits, bulin... I need a new, stronger weapon that can withstand my power, bulin!
Good news for you, bulin! We've found clues as to where the legendary Ultra Rainbow Hammer is!
You'd be invincible if you had that, bulin!
Really, bulin?
Really-deally, bulin! It's in the Site of Trials, bulin! Pass all the trials and the hammer will be yours, bulin!
Easy peasy, bulin! I've been training for something like this, bulin!

sequence:
One-Punch! Bulin!

<size=45>3.The Site of Trials</size>

scripts.say: By working together, the three Bulin sisters managed to pass all the trials.
That was the last one, bulin! We got a key, bulin!
And there's a treasure chest here, bulin! Open it, bulin!
Okay, bulin! Here we go, bulin!
Opening the box released a blinding rainbow light which pierced the skies.
Item obtained: Ultra Rainbow Hammer.
Look at that light, bulin! This thing must be amazingly powerful, bulin!
And now it's in my hands, bulin!
While the sisters cheered and celebrated, a stranger approached from the dark.
What the hell is all this ruckus about?
Ah... Adventurers. You're after the legendary hammer, are you?
Well, bad news for you. If you want to keep it, you've gotta get through me!
The big baddie has appeared, bulin! She wants to take our hard-earned loot, bulin!
Like that's gonna happen, bulin! Give her a taste of the hammer's might, bulin!
Come here, bulin! I'm gonna squash you like a bug, bulin!
...What the heck, bulin? The hammer isn't doing anything, bulin!
Hahah! You didn't know? The Ultra Rainbow Hammer is an energy weapon! You've gotta charge it, idiot!
Okay, bulin! We'll keep her distracted, bulin! Charge up the hammer quickly, bulin!
Let's see what you've got, bulin!
The Bulin sisters fought, but their best efforts weren't enough to trump their adversary.
Your attacks are useless! Ahahahah!
No one, and I mean no one on this earth can bring out the hammer's power!
You're wrong, bulin! Our sister's the strongest person alive, bulin!
She'll put you in your stupid rightful place, bulin!
Try it! Struggle all you want, then despair!
You'll be the one to despair, bulin! My hammer is at full charge, bulin!
What?! That's impossible!
Great job, bulin! Let's wale on her until she cries for mama, bulin!
Follow my lead, bulin! Show her what we bulins are capable of, bulin!
The Ultra Rainbow Hammer's mighty attacks wore away at the Lord of Evil's will to battle.
Screw it! This is unfair! I'm outta here!
She has her back turned, bulin!
Now's our chance, bulin! Gang up on her, bulin!
Hope you like the taste of rainbow punch, bulin!
- This is the blow that pierces the earth, bulin! - This is the blow that pierces the heavens, bulin! - This is the blow that strikes down the stars, bulin!
The hammer glowed with all the colors of the rainbow, and the Bulin sisters' strength converged into a single beam of light that outshone even the stars.
KABOOOOOOOM!
Victory is ours, bulin! We vanquished the big baddie, bulin!
But at what cost, bulin? The hammer's light is gone, bulin...
Oh no... Did it break, bulin?
Oh well, it's still a nice trophy, bulin! Besides, our combined strength felt stronger than even the hammer, bulin!
Now we have to celebrate our triumph, bulin. Let's go for barbecue, bulin!
Hooray, bulin!
And so, the Bulin sisters left to treat themselves to first-rate barbecue.
As for the legend that inspired their adventure... It remains only a tale to this day.
Wh-where am I...?
When I wake up, I'm greeted by an unfamiliar room.
Old-fashioned furnishings, faint light, old furniture... and something that looks like a black box on the table.
Could this be...
Ahem! Ah, testing, testing. Commander! Can you hear me?
Bristol's voice comes from the black box.
Bristol?
Ooh! Communications are working great! Commander, welcome to the castle!
Castle...?
That's what I said! It all started one rainy day twelve years ago...
Bristol suddenly starts telling a grandiose story, but I'm hardly in a state to take it in.
Put simply, this is an immersive escape room with tabletop RPG story elements!
This one is more complex, and the puzzles are better than ever. We wanted you to try it out, Commander!
Here I was wondering why Avrora brought all that vodka to my room last night...
You could've just asked me normally, you know...
Nuh-uh! Like the story here says, "The investigator wakes up in the castle." We have to be as realistic as possible!
Umm, so where was I...?
As the investigator, Commander, you need to explore this desolate, ancient castle and solve the mystery within.
You'll run into many different trials and tribulations...
But it's up to you to solve them with your personal decisions and a specific set of skills.
Oh, but the story here DOES say, "The investigator's memories were lost upon entering the castle due to unknown causes."
So you can't remember your skills or stats at all... In other words, they'll be hidden from you.
When you run into a random event, our GMs will roll dice to determine what it is.
Investigate the castle bit by bit, rediscover your abilities, and aim for a clear!
An RPG where you don't know your own abilities? That's... novel.
Skills aside, how am I meant to know what to do if I don't even know my stats?
I have to agree with you there! But, umm, all of these rules were decided by dice roll, so...
A-anyway, it's a game, so don't worry about it too much!
That about does it for the tutorial. Commander, you'll learn faster if you just give it a try.
When it's time to roll those dice, leave it to Yukikaze the Great!
Weren't we all going to take turns rolling the dice...?
Yes, that was the plan.
Why?! Yukikaze the Great is clearly the luckiest person here, so I am the optimal dice-roller!
That's exactly why you shouldn't be the only one.
So there are seven of you facilitators... Or should I say GMs?
Eugen and Royal Fortune were a part of this, too.
But they... No, now isn't the time for that. We just got word from Eugen, so let's get started.
Hold on! I wanna add one more thing!
Keep your communicator on you at ALL times!
It's a key item this time! Even if you're in danger, guard it with your life!
Anyway, there you have it. Good luck out there, newbie investigator!
Come again? Danger?
Bristol?
I wanted to ask about that concerning remark, but the communicator has already gone dead silent.

sequence: Chapter 2 - The Housekeeper and the Gun

scripts.say: You are led to the guest room, and the first things you notice are the lavish furnishings.
It's impossible to hold back your investigator instincts, and you start looking all around the room.
Roll a D100... 37. That's a successful check.
There are taxidermied animals adorning the room, as well as a few guns for hunting animals.
One handgun in particular catches your eye with the cold gleam it gives off.
While, clearly, the castle lord has a penchant for hunting, nobody would pass this one off as a hunting firearm.
These are the good sir's trophies. Guns are another one of his hobbies.
The woman's completely silent appearance startles you somewhat.
Did I scare you? Apologies. I was just cleaning around the room.
Allow me to introduce myself. I am São Martinho, the housekeeper.
And this... is the gun Lord Manjuu entrusted me with.
As you know, there has been a series of disappearances. And so, to protect the lord's family, every room in the castle has a firearm provided for safety.
Since he has tasked you with solving this case, I hope we'll all be able to return to normalcy soon.
São Martinho eyes you with suspicion, and her tone betrays her lack of faith in you.
What do you want to know about the castle?

options.content: Have I wronged you in some way?

scripts.say: One might call it judging a book by its cover, but...
Well, you are simply too good-looking to be an ace investigator.
I'm... TOO good-looking?
The out-of-pocket compliment takes you aback, and you seem to remember something once again.
Roll a D100... 30. Yes, a success. It's a common occurrence for people to doubt your ability when they first meet you.
This doubt stems not from your lack of education, but rather from your appearance.
Indeed, there are both times when looking good is to your advantage, and times when it impedes you.
You have remembered that your Looks stat is 85.
(Thanks for the stat explanation, though it doesn't really help...)
There is also the fact that Lord Manjuu has employed many other investigators before you.
The majority of them were con artists and served to sow disorder. They were given worthy punishments, of course.
But, let's get back on topic. If you ask me, I think these "disappearances" are overblown and overmystified.
What makes you say that?
When the first animal went missing, its carcass was later found. Meanwhile, the servants who disappeared after that left no signs after them.
Almost as if they never existed to begin with. They simply don't seem like disappearance cases to me.
I believe they are merely scandalous rumors started by some servants with grudges from being punished for slacking off on the job.

options.content: They were punished for slacking off?

scripts.say: Lord Manjuu is an outstandingly kind and lenient soul who has devoted himself to charity work since the passing of his wife.
Because he is so lenient, some dishonest servants have taken advantage of him.
Because this group "went missing," the castle has been on edge, with servants quitting one after the next. Now only three of us remain.
You, Royal Fortune, and the chef, right?
Yes. We must stay.
I, myself, have lived in this castle for decades, while Royal Fortune and the chef in essence grew up with the Golden Hinds.
Daughters? As in, plural?
Time to roll for Eagle Eye. Let's see... 6, a success. You notice there's a family photo sitting atop a table.
There are four people in the photograph. Besides the castle lord and his wife, there's Golden Hind and another woman.
Beyond that, the silver glow of the handgun catches your eye again.
Without realizing it, you begin walking closer to the gun, as though bewitched by its beautiful form.
Can I have a look at that gun?
A firearm buff, are you? Certainly.
You take the gun in hand and examine it down to the details of the barrel.
Oh, let's do a roll here.
Yukikaze, the dice are yours.
Yukikaze the Great rolls a D100... 1! Critical success!
You inspect the handgun's rosewood grip and the barrel, and notice a fine engraving on the latter that reads, "Single Action Army."
Its model name is M1873, meaning it was designed and manufactured a long time ago.
This gun has been part of many legends and appeared in countless video games and movies.
To put it in other words, whoever owns this gun... has excellent taste.
Uhh... Thanks.
You're welcome.
You feel the gun in your hands, your gaze focused on the light reflecting off the metal barrel. A memory from being at the firing range comes back to you.
You have trained many hours with a gun as part of your occupation.
Voila. You have remembered the skill Marksmanship. You have novice proficiency in this skill.
If I may, Lord Manjuu has told me you are quite the sharpshooter, and I'd like to learn from you.
What? But I'm a firearm novice!
Umm, you practiced very hard, but the results did not match the effort put in.
At the very least, it's made you able to use a gun without blowing it up!
In the right place at the right time, it may help you turn the tables in surprising ways.
Ahem... It seems you still have things to do, so I won't bother you with gun training.
Since Lord Manjuu has hired you, I will cooperate in your investigation.
As you know by now, this place can be a maze. Please be mindful.
Particularly when it comes to private spaces such as the bedrooms. You should get the lord's permission before entering those.
Although the housekeeper sounds supportive, you are not convinced that she will actually help you.
Next, you decide to...
Although the housekeeper sounds supportive, you are not convinced that she will actually help you.
Next, you decide to...
You said we need the occupant's permission to enter private spaces. Well, I'd like to see yours.
...I don't know about that.
Golden Hind asked me to visit her once my business is done here.
Also, my room isn't perfectly clean... I'll have to ask you to investigate other rooms first.
I should be going. Please enjoy your stay.
(This housekeeper is suspicious... I'll search her room first.)
(The best play here is to take them by surprise. That'll bring me closer to the truth.)
Alright. I'll investigate the public areas first. Your room can wait until tomorrow morning.
That will do. The public spaces would be the kitchen on the first floor and the garden.
The second floor houses the library and display room, but their doors are locked.
Those can wait until tomorrow, too.
Very well. Take your time. Golden Hind is waiting for me, so I must take my leave now.
The housekeeper leaves the room.
She said her room was next to this one, didn't she? Then this door must lead there...
After organizing your thoughts, you decide where you'll search next.
...Despite her telling you very clearly that you would need the occupant's permission.
The instant you enter the room, you feel as if you've been transported to a museum.
A dizzying array of rare jewels and curiosities line the room.
Countless guns are hung on walls, stored on shelves, and placed on dressers.
There are so many... I'd better be careful if I mean to search for clues here.
*click*
Hm? Did I just step on something...?
When you step forth, you hear a clicking noise like a contraption being activated.
Instantly after, something odd happens.
Every gun in sight points at you all at once.
Piercing light flashes from every single black or silver barrel, as if heralding your pitiful end.
If I move fast enough...
However, even faced with your impending doom, your willpower is unbroken.
Roll a D100... 17. You remember that you're as light and agile as a bird.
In other words, one more of your stats has been revealed. Agility: 70! Commander, do you want to roll here?
If you get a critical success, you might just make it out of this jam!

options.content: It's all you, Yukikaze the Great!

scripts.say: Yukikaze the Great rolls a D100... 1! Critical success!
She did it. It isn't my fate to die here... I run!
Immediately as you pounce toward the door, you hear gunfire behind you.
After the smoke clears, it becomes evident that the guns have done their duty and struck a decisive blow upon you.
While your vision fades to black and your consciousness turns muddy, you finally remember your Size stat.
There just isn't enough room for your built figure to escape in this cramped space...
Oh. Sorry, I forgot to read out the stat to you. Your Size... is 80.
Unfortunately, the Investigator's adventure ends here.

sequence: BE-03 - The Bigger They Are...

scripts.say: Come on, Commander. You should know that it's wrong to go into people's rooms without permission.
Question. Who the hell sets a trap like that in their own room?
How is the housekeeper meant to go in and out normally?
She isn't as big as you. Also, fun fact: there are 148 guns in that room.
That means you were done for the moment you stepped on that switch!
This game seems pointlessly unforgiving for newcomers... Who even made this decision?
I-I dunnooo...
Although the housekeeper sounds supportive, you are not convinced that she will actually help you.
Next, you decide to...

options.content: Ask for a map of the castle.

scripts.say: (I just don't have enough information yet... I should build up a bigger knowledge base before I take action.)
For the sake of my investigation, I'd like to know the locations of rooms and corridors on each floor of the castle. May I have a map?
(Royal Fortune said there were a lot of labyrinthine hallways. Maybe following a map would be better?)
(Yeah... First, let's see if we can ask for a map.)
I'd like to know the locations of rooms and corridors on each floor of the castle. May I have a map?
I wouldn't get lost if I had one, and I wouldn't wander into any rooms I shouldn't be in...
The housekeeper does not answer. She simply stares, a sharp twinkle in her eye.
Roll a D100... 17. Success! While you try to convince her, you become more confident in your abilities.
You were certain that she wouldn't agree before, but you now realize where your confidence is coming from.
It comes from your drop-dead good looks and eloquent tongue. The former, especially – you've been reminded many times in your life that you're too hot to refuse.
Though it causes trouble for you sometimes, it may yield surprising results if used well.
You've remembered the skill Enamor. Your proficiency is average.

options.content: I didn't hear you wrong, did I...?
Okay, who made this one up?

scripts.say: Yes. Enamor.
You did not. Your skill is called Enamor.
The one who went to went to play in the puzzle room and left me in her place.
...Your social skills have also been greatly improved by your Enamor skill.
This is a great boon at work when you need to convince relevant parties to share information.
Anyway, you successfully persuade São Martinho.
There's a simple map of the castle in the dining room. If you need it, by all means, take it.
Oh, the dining room is across this hall. It would normally not be an issue if you passed through the courtyard, but it's being remodeled, so please detour around it.
She traces a route in the air with her fingers to tell you how to reach the dining room. Just then, the button on her sleeve happens to reflect the dim light of the room.
Did my button catch your eye?
Ah, yes. It's very pretty.
Golden Hind gave it to me.
Your sharp eye allows you to notice such easily missable details. It seems you've seen the pattern on that button somewhere before.
Roll a D100... 31. Success. You quickly realize why it seems familiar: the button bears the same pattern as Golden Hind's hair accessory.
(The same symbol as that cult...)
I hate to repeat myself again, but the castle is vast. If you wander carelessly at night, you may get lost. Be careful.
Also, allow me to warn you once more: do not enter bedrooms or other private spaces without the occupant's permission.
Golden Hind is waiting for me, so I must take my leave now.
After a quick bow, the housekeeper leaves the room.

sequence: Chapter 3 - An Old Friend

scripts.say: As soon as you enter the dining room, your old habit kicks in, making you inspect your surroundings.
This is a lavish room with lavish furniture and decorations, and everything seems to be in order.
Nothing in particular jumps out at you yet.
The furnishings are nice and all, but where is the map?
Eagle Eye check. Roll a D100... 70. Failure.
You survey the room, but sadly the map is nowhere to be seen.
Of course that check fails... Dammit. I'll look around thoroughly, then.
You take your time searching every nook and cranny, and you still find nothing.
You've looked everywhere, except inside the locked drawers.
Even if you were to try those, you've seen no sign of a key anywhere. You are stumped.
Basically, I need to get those drawers open somehow.
You really rack your brain, and suddenly, a method comes back to you.
Roll a D100... 37. Success. You have remembered the skill Lockpicking. You have expert proficiency in this skill.
With your level of skill, you can easily pick the lock using a bobby pin.
After all, there was one case where you scored big with just a steel wire.
...So, what, I have a thieving streak now?
Ahem... As a professional investigator, there will sometimes be locked drawers or doors that you must open as a last resort.
It's all in the name of the case!

options.content: Use the bobby pin to lockpick the drawer.

scripts.say: Y-you want to use a gun? Why? You could take your time picking the lock...
You opt to go with the bobby pin regardless, shocked by your horrific impulsive thought that briefly surfaced.
Roll a D100... 19. Success. You pick the lock and take the castle map that's tucked away in a corner of the drawer.
Looking at the map, the dining room is flanked by the kitchen on one side and the banquet hall on the other.
I vaguely remember seeing the door to the kitchen when I got here through the hallway, but where's the entrance to the banquet hall?
Plus, this dining room is much smaller in reality than it is on the map...
Both the map and your instincts tell you that something is off about this room.
*creeeak*
Oh. Sorry if I spooked you. I thought the dining room would be empty at this hour...
As you're about to continue your investigation, the dining room door suddenly opens, and a woman pushing a trolley comes in.
Wait, is that... Is that you, Morgan?
Oh, my old friend Morgan... You've finally come back...
(Morgan? That's a new name. Is it someone who used to stay at the castle?)
M-my mistake... Lord Manjuu, you've returned?
No, you're not him either! You're that investigator São Martinho told me about, right?
I've had a lot to do lately, so I often get people mistaken. Sorry.
Let me introduce myself. I'm a maid at this... No, excuse me, I'm the chef at the moment.
(Being so busy you get the wrong person twice... I can empathize. It must be a nightmare managing such a big castle with just three people.)
(They probably spend almost every waking moment doing their tasks.)
It's alright, I don't blame you. It can't be easy working this late.
It really isn't... My workload has exploded since many of our staff quit all at once.
Say, do you mind if I start cleaning here? If it'd disturb you, I can come back later.
Go right ahead. I just wanted to ask you something.

options.content: What can you tell me about the housekeeper?
Where is the banquet hall, exactly?

scripts.say: Huh? About her?
The chef repeats your question and seems hesitant to actually answer it.
Roll a D100... 68. Failure. Her face flashes a look of unease, but it's back to normal in just a moment.
I don't know very much about her. Sorry I can't be of assistance.
(I guess it won't be that easy to uncover the housekeeper's secrets. Let's try asking her about the banquet hall instead.)
The banquet hall? It's right next to the dining room.
It sure looks that way on the map, but not in reality, at least not from what I can see.
Oh, yes. They used to be two connected rooms, but it was split in two after the owners stopped getting guests.
They split it?
Yeah. Lord Manjuu's late wife liked a lively mood, and complained how the dining room was too large for it to feel homely.
So, he hired a tradesman and rebuilt a little. The wall over there is actually just made of wooden boards.
You could easily remove it if you opened the padlock on it.
All you need is the key, which I can give you if you get São Martinho's permission.
At that moment, you sense Adventure Galley's gaze fixating on you.
Is there something on my face, or...?
Oh, f-forgive me! It's just... You remind me so much of an old friend of mine... Morgan, Golden Hind's betrothed.
(whisper) It's because you're both so good-looking...
Hearing that, you decide to...
At that moment, you sense Adventure Galley's gaze fixating on you.
Is there something on my face, or...?
Oh, f-forgive me! It's just... You remind me so much of an old friend of mine... Morgan, Golden Hind's betrothed.
(whisper) It's because you're both so good-looking...
Hearing that, you decide to...

options.content: Give Enamor a shot to get the key.

scripts.say: When else am I going to use it? Now's the time!
Roll a D100... 4. Incredibly, you got a critical success.
You recalled that you have your Enamor skill. Using it will leave a stain on your conscience, but you'll live with it as a means to an end.
Just as you hoped, the chef falls head over heels for your stunning looks and charisma.
Investigator... I know this is sudden, but... I-I have fallen hopelessly in love with you!
Great! Just one more push!
You ask her to take down the partition dividing the dining room and the banquet hall, to which she is shocked to hear.
Her loyalty and your charm fight it outside her heart, and the winner quickly becomes clear.
If that's what you want... Okay. Come with me.
Her love for you instantaneously morphs into an insanity-filled impulse. The passion she felt at first glance is what let her come to such a daring decision.
She takes your hand and leads you to the kitchen.
It's at that moment you feel a chilling sensation run up your spine.
(Huh? Wait... Don't tell me the pattern on her hair ornament is what I think it is!)
It so happens she has an ornament with an unusual pattern you've seen before...
Roll a D100... 69. Nice, but unfortunately, you get distracted by how soft her hand feels before you can connect the dots.
But wait... I already made the connection!
The next thing you know, the two of you have reached the kitchen.
It's dimly lit, so you rely on a faint stove flame to survey your surroundings. You can just barely make out the room's layout.
*hisss* friaghgleh... grsh... *hisssssss*!
There is that ominous voice again. The jumbled growling fills the whole kitchen.
(This again?! Crap! I need to get out of here, quickly!)
You acutely sense the danger lurking in this room, and turn around to make a run for it...
But that's when someone pulls on your arm with great force.
Daaarling... where are you going?
I was just...
The Investigator tries to shake away the hand!
When your back is against the wall, why not try a Strength check? I'll even help you with the roll again!
Yukikaze the Great rolls a D100... 1! Critical success!
Oh, hell yeah!
However, even though you muster all your strength, the chef's grip on your arm does not budge.
A distant memory resurfaces, and you remember something.
Your physical strength is very lacking compared to other people. Things they can carry easily are impossibly heavy for you.
You have remembered one of your stats... Your Strength is 25.
It's not over yet. Yukikaze's roll was a critical success...
Yes... It was. And it still wasn't enough for you to shake her off.
Your clear escape attempt infuriates Adventure Galley. She willingly lets go of your arm and picks up a nearby knife.
Oh, Investigator, my sweetheart... I love you. No one else can have you. I will make you mine...
Wait... I think Golden Hind said... Something, something... Sacrifice? Hmm.
No matter. She can always find another person to offer... Hehehehe...
Let's be together forever, you and I!
Her unrestrained love turns into mania. Desiring to be with you forever, the cook decides she's going to make a feast out of you.
In her mind, this will make you a part of her for the rest of time.
A horrible pain hits the back of your head. You lose consciousness and sink into an endless dark void.

sequence: BE-04 - A Horrific Full Course

scripts.say: So, she turned me into dinner?
It seems so.
Eugen came up with it as symbolism for insane, yet wholehearted love. Z2 agreed that it was a good idea.
And so, we incorporated it into a bad ending.
Actually, I had nothing to do with it. Eugen was the only one excited about it.

options.content: Let's not have anything that gory again, okay?
That ending was great. Give me more.

scripts.say: Well... That will depend on the luck of your rolls.
Now, let's get back to where you last were. Chop-chop!
Chop-chop, like she did with me?
Heehee~ Oh, you.
At that moment, you sense Adventure Galley's gaze fixating on you.
Is there something on my face, or...?
Oh, f-forgive me! It's just... You remind me so much of an old friend of mine... Morgan, Golden Hind's betrothed.
(whisper) It's because you're both so good-looking...
Hearing that, you decide to...
Did they use to live at the castle?
W-well...
She is flustered by your question. It seems this name is taboo for you to say.
I-I don't have the right to comment on Lord Manjuu's family affairs.
Forget what I said, and sorry for disturbing your investigation. I'll come clean later instead.
(While I could use my Enamor skill, I'm pretty sure Eugen came up with it. That alone makes me apprehensive.)
(I have 90 Intelligence anyway. That should be plenty to figure out a way to get the key.)
I'd like an Intelligence check. There has to be a way to get the key without using Enamor!
Roll a D100... 99. Oof, that's a painful failure.
Let's see... I need to think about where to take this... Oh, I know.
I... Sorry, YOU rack your brain and recall an old proverb that goes something like, "A simple solution usually beats a hard one."
You don't need to lie or manipulate. You simply look this gorgeous lady in the eyes and ask her directly...
"Please give me the banquet hall key."
You then nod contently and extend your open hand.
...Excuse me? I can't give you it without São Martinho's permission.
Look, I... I'm sorry for disturbing your investigation. I'll come clean later instead.
Sadly, that doesn't go as you hoped. You don't get anything, and can only watch as the girl walks out.
Huh...?
The chef quickly pushes out her trolley and leaves the dining room behind.
Another new name... Morgan, an old friend of the chef. Someone who was close to the daughter.
That's not important now, though. I need to get into the banquet hall.
Maybe I could use my Lockpicking skill on the lock... Hm? Is this the keyhole?
You approach the door, or rather, wall, and examine the lock closely. Yes, it seems familiar...
Roll a D100... 22. Success. You've seen the shape of this keyhole before. You've picked the same kind of lock once in the past.
(Hmm. So if I just turn the pin like this...)
You repeat from your memory and try to pick the lock the same way you did in the past...
*click*
The lock makes a sound, and you successfully pick it. You slowly move the wall boards out of the way and enter the hall on the other side.

sequence: Chapter 4 - Whispered Secrets

scripts.say: Although the wall is only made of boards, it is quite heavy.
After barely managing to push it aside, you can now finally see inside the banquet hall on the other side.
There are tons of tables and chairs, boxes filled with tableware, paper towels, fireworks, and other things lying around inside.
The smell of dust wafts out, and you instinctively cover your nose and mouth with your hand.
These antique, beautiful furnishings offer a glimpse into Lord Manjuu's affluent life and the castle's glory days.
Past a massive window, there is an observation deck. Visitors to the castle were surely stunned by the vista from here.
It IS beautiful... But why build an observation deck on the first floor?
As you admire the view, you all of a sudden remember that this castle was built at the peak of a mountain.
At such a height, it isn't at all odd to build an observation deck even on the first floor.
You wonder what you wasted time wondering about it. After all, should you not be focusing on your job?
Viciously put, but fair enough. You really thought everything out.
Anyway, time to investigate this place.
Sometime later...
Nothing in the way of a clue... I must've missed something...
You lament coming up empty-handed and feel uncharacteristically irritated.
As you come to a roadblock in your investigation, you hear a hazy noise.
Roll a D100... 14. Success. Hearing someone on the other side of the wall talking, you hold your breath and listen closely.
Yes... in the collection room...
Whydah's room... locked...
...let the investigator find out...
Though the voices are muffled, you manage to extract several good bits of information from them.
Whydah, and something about a collection room?
That's on the second floor, I think. I should head up there.
Those two will probably still be in the corridor, though. I can't sneak past them like this. What to do...
Whydah, and something about a collection room?
That's on the second floor, I think. I should head up there.
Those two will probably still be in the corridor, though. I can't sneak past them like this. What to do...

options.content: I could make a loud noise...

scripts.say: You ready your firearm... but then you think about it. You don't want to take them out, you just want to sneak past without being seen.
So never mind the gun – what you need is a distraction.
With your mind set, you start looking around the room for something you can use.
Faced with all these objects, your brain kicks into full drive.
Roll a D100... 43, a success. You have a flash of inspiration, and another piece of your mind puzzle falls into place.
Being an excellent investigator, you have practiced a skill all by yourself to raise your odds of surviving any given case... making traps.
You've remembered the skill Trap-Making. Your proficiency is novice-level.

options.content: Who came up with this one?

scripts.say: Let's just say it was a sweet pirate who loves pacts.
"Trap" is kind of an umbrella term. You can craft surprising things if you just get creative.
Also, all skills that get you out of tight spots matter! Especially since traps can also inflict damage to your opponent!
Damage isn't really the point, but this does seem like a versatile skill.
The components I've got are... Tables and chairs, planks, fireworks, and paper towels. I think I can craft a noisemaker.
You start making a bomb right away. While your proficiency could be better, this skill has gotten you out of sticky situations many times before.
Roll a D100! 1! Hahahaha! Another critical success from Yukikaze the Great!
Good lord... Ahem. Your skill pulls through for you once again.
You have successfully crafted a shiny bomb. However, you do not yet know how powerful it is.
Between a bomb and a gun, I've got plenty to distract them.
You crack a satisfied smile and set your plan into motion...
Sometime later...
The plan is very simple. Setting off a bomb is sure to make a loud noise and distract people in the vicinity.
While they go to investigate, you can head up to the second floor and continue your investigation.
After laying down a fuse and lighting it, you return to the observation deck and wait for the explosion.
Roll a D100... 71, a failure. You wait and wait, but the explosion never comes.
Was it because I didn't set up the fuse right? Time for plan B.
You find a great spot to fire from the observation deck. You aim your gun at the bomb and pull the trigger...
Roll a D100... 98, a critical failure this time. Your accuracy is so poor, the shot hits a marble pillar way off from the target, causing major damage to it.
Not just that, the recoil makes you fall flat on your butt. A stinging pain shoots up from your tailbone.
How many bullets do I have left?
Two.
Then I'll give it another shot.
Roll a D100... 53. Your poorly aimed shot goes through a board covering up a fireplace.
One more! Just let me shoot one more time! And have Yukikaze throw the dice!
You missed twice in a row, and now you need Yukikaze the Great to save you. You're hopeless~
But wait! If she makes the roll, it's going to–
Yukikaze the Great rolls a, you guessed it, 1! Critical success! The shot hits the bomb and sets it off!

options.content: You're the best, Yukikaze the Great!

scripts.say: Heheh. Now to roll for how big the blast is.
Yukikaze the Great rolls a... Look at that! 1! Critical success!
I-I can't believe this... My goodness, it's actually happening...
What?
Oh boy... Hai Tien, please continue.
Right... The blast is so, so much bigger than you anticipated. Not only does it cause further damage to the pillar and fireplace...
It detonates with a massive "KABOOM!" and all but cracks the land beneath your feet, making the tiny little castle tremble in fear.
Next, you hear the sound of trees falling, rocks crumbling, and the world shaking...
Rattle... Clack-clack... Rumble...
Your vision goes black.
This is your morning news.
At 1 AM yesterday, there was an explosion at the old castle on the outskirts of Arkham.
Police and ambulances rushed to the scene, where they found the bodies of several victims.
Among them were Lord Manjuu's two daughters, the castle's three servants, and one unidentified person.
The police have found traces of a homemade bomb where the building suffered a structural collapse, and speculate that it was the cause of the explosion.
They believe it's likely that this was a crime perpetrated by the unidentified person. The on-scene investigation is ongoing.

sequence: BE-05 - No Survivors Tonight

scripts.say: Are you serious? That was the setup for a bad ending?
Essex, did you realize something bad was going to happen partway through?
Yes... From the moment you let Yukikaze roll the dice.
Amazing, Commander! You even got to THIS special ending!
Not only do you have to make the most powerful bomb, you also have to try to hit it with your gun.
After missing two shots, at least one has to hit the pillar and cause enough damage to it.
Then, and only if the final shot hits and is a critical success, it sets off a chain reaction and triggers this ultra-rare ending!
So, I had to not only make the "right" choices, but also get the "right" dice rolls?
Mhm. Nobody should be able to meet such specific conditions under normal circumstances.
I was so sure you'd never see that ending. I don't know whether to call you very lucky or very UNlucky.
It took you by complete surprise, so I guess I'm lucky, in a way?
Whydah, and something about a collection room?
That's on the second floor, I think. I should head up there.
Those two will probably still be in the corridor, though. I can't sneak past them like this. What to do...
Sure. What are you going to do with it? Threaten the two servants standing outside?
...On second thought, I'll just wait here.
A while later, the voices on the other side have gone away.
You've been waiting patiently without making as much as a peep. You are certain there's nobody in the corridor anymore.
Leaving the banquet hall, you take the stairs up to the second floor.
It is a long staircase, and it takes you a considerable time to climb them.
You set food on the second floor without anyone catching on to you.
Now exhausted, your head starts spinning, and blurry images flash before your eyes...
Roll a D100... 15, success! You've remembered something important! Believe it or not, your health has been poor ever since you were little!
This is reflected by your Constitution stat – so, your stamina – being 15!
You are an investigator with a beautiful mug and balanced physique, yet lacking musculature, and the toil of adventuring is too much for you!
Wait... 15?
Yep, a mere 15. I'm sorry, Commander. My luck with the dice is awful!
At least you're an adult, so you won't die randomly from catching a cold. Still, you will suffer brief vertigo when you push yourself...
You can't do any investigating when that happens. You just have to wait and recover.
Alright... Time for a break, then.

sequence: Chapter 5 - Behind Closed Doors

scripts.say: After taking a short break, you've recovered your strength and continue investigating.
Based on what I heard earlier, up next is either the collection room or the second daughter's room.
They're both tucked away in a corner of the map. I may as well look around the corridor first, since it's on the way.
You sneak through the dimly lit corridor, making several trips back and forth between Whydah's room and the collection room.
Roll a D100... 31. Success. You notice a slight difference between the two rooms.
There is an unusual, familiar pattern engraved on the collection room's door and doorknob.
Roll a D100... 52, a failure this time. You can't remember where you've seen it before.
However, it does make your skin crawl and you rub your arms.
There's nothing that jumps out to you about the door to Whydah's room, however.
You decide to...

options.content: Knock on the door to Whydah's room.

scripts.say: You try to turn the doorknob... but the door is locked and doesn't budge.
Of course it's locked... Not surprised, though. Let's go for a Lockpicking check.
Roll a D100... 89, a failure. You try to use your adept lockpicking skills to open the door, but it doesn't work.
Then there's not much choice but to check out Whydah's room...
You remember São Martinho's incessant warning and decide to get the occupant's permission first.
You give Whydah's door three knocks.
Golden Hind... It's so late in the night, just– Wh-who are you?!
The door opens and out steps Whydah, dressed in a cute nightgown.
She gives you an intent stare, clearly expressing doubt and caution as one would around a stranger.
Yet, after staring for a while, she suddenly cracks a wide smile.
I've got it. You're that investigator my dad talked about, right?
...Come on in. I don't wanna leave my room.
Don't be alarmed. There's no unfriendly housekeeper or knife-waving chef in there. They don't come up here.
Trust me. It's the safest place in the whole castle.
You enter the room, and Whydah immediately closes and locks the door behind you.
As far as you can see, there aren't any unusual decorations or creepy sculptures.
All there is in here is a princess-sized bed with adorable stuffed animals, a messy desk and dressing table, and a television with a game console hooked up to it.
There are also game cartridges, cola bottles, and potato chips on the floor.
Uh, right. Those as well.
While it is messy, it's likely the most alright place in the whole castle, as Whydah professed.
Help yourself to some crisps if you want. I'm guessing the servants didn't give you anything to eat.
Ahem. So, introductions... I'm Whydah, Lord Manjuu's second daughter. Have you seen Golden Hind, my older sister?
What do you want from me?
Did our father tell you anything?
(That's what I'D like to know, actually.)
I think I can guess... He must have said that the castle's disappearances have something to do with me and her, no?
That we have been, like, possessed by evil spirits and become different people?
Eh, it doesn't matter to me. I'm gonna play a game. Feel free to look around.
Whydah gives you a quick shrug then lies down again on her fluffy carpet. She is focused on the game and doesn't pay you any mind.
The room's gigantic bookcase, shiny trophies, and game cartridges spread about the floor make you feel like you're in a whole other world.
All of a sudden, you notice there are framed photos and an open envelope resting on a drawer.
And unlike last time, it's stain-free!
Roll a D-100... 33. That's a success.
Some of the photographs depict Whydah, Golden Hind, Royal Fortune, and São Martinho.
Others depict a smiling woman dressed in clothes befitting a noble.
It's not difficult to tell that these are the castle's servants as well as the Golden Hinds.
The woman, meanwhile... Your gut instinct tells you she is Lord Manjuu's wife.
"Woman" implies "human"... This is a manjuu we're talking about.
Uhh, New Jersey came up with this plot point, so... I suppose "manjuu" is a more apt description.
Putting that aside... You look at the photographs of these women and get a slight feeling that something is wrong.
Whyah called the housekeeper "unfriendly" and the chef "knife-waving"... They must be on bad terms.
Let's check out this letter.
Spurred on by curiosity, you start reading the letter in hopes of finding something to aid your investigation.
From Golden Hind to Whydah... The student dormitory at the Miskatonic University School of Law?
Are those trophies rewards for academic excellence? She must be an ace student.
As for the actual contents of the letter...
"Even after all this time, I still can't believe Morgan has passed away. Every night, I can still hear that familiar voice and see that face I've looked at so many times..."
"My father has told me to look for a new partner. It's for the greater good... What should I do, my sister?"
"God, how I wish I could go back in time."
Do I look that cute in the photo?
As you finish reading, you hear Whydah call out to you in a displeased tone.
Sorry, I was just thinking about something. Have the servants always lived in this castle?
Galley used to be Golden Hind's maid. She was the head maid, too. Though she's great in the kitchen, so she works as the chef too.
São Martinho has been my personal maid. Though the position was a step up to her, to me, it's just been a bit of a bother.
Doesn't matter to me either way. I don't need a maid to babysit me... I'm happy to just stay in my room, relax, and play games every day.
And as long as I've got cola and crips, I'll never– What?! I died again!
The television shows a game-over screen. In a fit of anger, Whydah throws her controller.
I've had it... I WILL beat this level, even if I have to do it myself!

options.content: Can you tell me about your past?

scripts.say: Ohh. So you read the letter. I stopped studying ages ago.
Didn't my dad tell you? Then again, it's embarrassing for him, so of course he wouldn't...
His first daughter's into weird occult stuff and black magic, while the second one's a shut-in who does nothing all day.
He probably can't accept the reality of having gone from being a nobleman with two outstanding daughters to just being a failed parent.
Only reason he hired you is because he was scared that the rumors about his home would impact his business. He's probably in hiding in some foreign country right now.
Ugh, that was a lot of talking... So tiring.
Investigator, you should just forget about this rubbish case.
I'm sure my dad promised you a good commission fee, but who knows if he'll live long enough to actually pay it?
If my hunch is right, you've been chosen as the candidate for a sacrifice.
A sacrifice? The servants who disappeared... were they sacrificed, too?
Yeah. What other explanation is there? You should get out of here.
If this place is so dangerous, how come you're still around?
...Because this is my home? Why would I run away?
Plus, I can't leave my sister to her own devices, or who knows what'll happen.
While she takes her eyes off the screen to talk to you, her character in the video game is killed by an octopus monster, and a game over screen appears again.
Ugh. Died again... I need Golden Hind for this...
Look, if you insist on continuing your investigation, do it somewhere else. Take your death wish with you and stop cluttering up my room.
Hearing the girl's words, you decide to...
You roll a 100... Critical failure. Oh boy, that's really bad.
What's the outcome? Oh... Yeah, that sucks.
What's going on?
You'll, uh, find out soon enough. Go on, please continue the investigation.
Ugh. Died again... I need Golden Hind for this...
Look, if you insist on continuing your investigation, do it somewhere else. Take your death wish with you and stop cluttering up my room.
Hearing the girl's words, you decide to...

options.content: Ask her about the collection room.
Look around for the collection room key.

scripts.say: You sure are stubborn... Unsurprisingly, the collection room is full of the stuff my dad collects. It's always locked, so nobody really gets in there.
...Huh? You want the key to it?
Whydah looks at you with an extremely dubious expression.
Roll a D100... 99. A critical failure. You've underestimated the sisters' bond. Her expression sours into one of contempt.
And why do you think I'd give it to you? I only acted nice because I wanted you to leave. I'm not in any mood to help you out.
That leaves me with no other option. Time to try my Enamor skill...
Uh, long story short, you managed to get inside the collection room.
What? Just like that?
Your Enamor skill led from one thing to the next, and, well... It's both hard to explain and something we can't show.
Yet everyone was fine with describing the gruesome ways I died in the bad endings.
Not all things are equal in the eyes of the rating board. Let's move on! You've entered the collection room!
Also, Whydah is now madly in love with you! She will do anything for your sake.
Honeeey~ Look around all you want~ What's mine is yours~

options.content: Let me guess... New Jersey wrote that line?

scripts.say: Correct.
What a pain... Uh, I remember hearing as a kid that there's a hidden room in the castle.
If you wanna look for secrets, that place is your best bet.
A hidden room... Is it hidden by a switch behind a painting, as the trope goes?
You walk up to a painting hanging on the wall and begin examining it in detail.
Roll a D100... 22, a success. There is no switch behind the painting.
Then I'll use Eagle Eye and examine the collection room for anything suspicious.
Roll a D100... 55. A failure this time. You fail to find anything of note.
Hmm. It's looking like you'll have to examine every last thing in here.
Speaking of which, there are 1,453 items stored in here.

options.content: Who on Earth provided all these props?
1,453... Is there any meaning to that number?

scripts.say: And that's after curtailment. Her Majesty's original plan was to... Actually, never mind.
Queen Elizabeth contributed the vast majority. That said, I provided a few as well.
If there is any, it's the year when in the Sardegna Empire of old–
Let's save that history lesson for another day.
Fair enough. It's a long story, and I'm just passing by. Never mind me and enjoy the rest of the game.
It's simply impossible to go through each one of them...
As you feel a little overwhelmed, a chill suddenly runs up your spine.
Oh, dear... Investigator, what have you done to Whydah?
Look, sis~ I found someone to spend the rest of my life with~ I love you, honey~
Is that so? Let's have a talk, shall we~?
Heehee~ I was going to sacrifice you, but I had a change of heart after my sister said she wants to be with you forever.
It'd be terrible if she lost the love of her life... So! This way you and her will be together forever and ever~
What a shocking turn of events. While you were unconscious, your body was stuffed inside of something.
While you're lucid now, you cannot move your arms or legs.
Even if you're a doll, we'll always be together, honey~

sequence: BE-06 - Thanks For the Present, Sis

scripts.say: You've achieved yet another bad ending, Commander.
It may be... unwise to use your Enamor skill much at all.
Uh-huh. So they turned me into a doll?
That she did. You became a gorgeous part of their collection.
Obsessive love resulting in your eternal imprisonment... Now that is art. How do you like this ending, Commander?

options.content: I give it a thumbs up.

scripts.say: The lovely and charming villain, it seems.
Alright. Let's try again with another roll of the dice.
Ugh. Died again... I need Golden Hind for this...
Look, if you insist on continuing your investigation, do it somewhere else. Take your death wish with you and stop cluttering up my room.
Hearing the girl's words, you decide to...

options.content: Focus on the problem at hand.

scripts.say: Professionals have standards. I will not give up on this case when I've come this far.
The same goes for video games. A true gamer keeps trying no matter how many setbacks they face.
Before I die, I at least want to help her beat this game.
Why? Because I hate leaving things unfinished.
You plop down next to her, pick up a controller, and select co-op mode.
You're one of those people... What a pain...
With a bit of help, what seems impossible can be accomplished surprisingly easily.
You and Whydah beat the game. The characters on the screen wave their arms and shout in celebration.
We actually... beat it...
I thought it wasn't possible without Golden Hind's help...
I loved games as a kid, but I was never good at them. Even though I'm an ace student, I can't learn how to get good at games.
My sister used to play with me, and Morgan, too...
Listen, since you helped me with the game, I'll give you a hot tip.
There's nothing useful in the collection room. You don't need to go there.
If it's a lead you want, go to the study. Here's the key.
Good luck, Investigator. Hope I'll see you tomorrow morning.
Key in hand, you bid farewell to Whydah before taking your leave.

sequence: Chapter 6 - The Misty Corridor

scripts.say: You cling to the wall as you walk down the dark corridor.
You've been walking for some time, yet there's no end to the corridor... It seems you've gotten lost in this old castle.
Something isn't right. Can I roll for an Eagle Eye check?
Roll a D100... 27, a success. You spot an oddity in the corridor.
A veil of mist laps at your feet. It looks and feels as if it's slowly creeping its way up your leg.
What's more, you hear that creepy voice once again...
*hisss* friaghgleh... grsh... *hisssssss*!
Your will wavers from the garbled growling, and it feels like it's trying to claw out of your body.
As you struggle to stay conscious, you remember one of your base stats... Yes, your Volition is 45.
Sadly, this is below average.
Roll a D100... 73. Your Volition failed. Your legs turn cold, like all the warmth has left them. Haunting thoughts race through your mind, making you manic.
*hisss* unfinished job srih office debt shrah... no holidays flek... *hisssssss*!
Oh, the horror...
Right before the thoughts consume you, you feel a warmth inside your pocket. Like the sunrise, it drives off the cold, and with it, the jumbled growling.
When you regain your sanity, you realize that the warmth came from the key Whydah gave you.
The keychain, which you assumed was just an ornament, is actually a protective charm that gives off a faint glow.
Roll a D100... 26. Your Folklore Scholar check succeeds. You're able to determine the origin of this charm.
You've read about it in a book on the occult. It's a very rare charm, said to be imbued with a power that can hold back gods.
What's more, it is so rare that the Miskatonic University has only 1 such example on display.
Did Whydah steal it when she left the school? I mean, it did save me just now...
You carefully put the charm back in your pocket and continue on your way to the study.
Immediately, though, something else happens. You hear a bang, and the world is shrouded in darkness. You lose your bearing.
Back-to-back occurrences, huh... Is my charm responding?
No, it is dormant in your pocket. Listening closely, you hear footsteps approaching from behind you.
Step, step... Step, step...
I use Eagle Eye to see who it is!
Roll a D100... 48. Success. It is unfortunately too dark to make out their identity.
However, you do realize that there's a door next to you. You don't know where it leads.
As the footsteps draw closer by the second, you decide to...
Roll a D100... 48. Success. It is unfortunately too dark to make out their identity.
However, you do realize that there's a door next to you. You don't know where it leads.
As the footsteps draw closer by the second, you decide to...
It's a reckless move when I don't know where it leads, but it's better than doing nothing!
You hurry over to the door and hope it will save you from certain doom, but as you feared, it is locked tightly.

options.content: I'll use my key on it!
I'll use my gun on it!
I'll use my bobby pin on it!

scripts.say: You remember the key in your pocket. You know, of course, that this is not the door to the study.
But, maybe if you believe hard enough, this surreal castle will bend to your will.
Yes, this is your final hope. You slide the key into the hole and turn it.
As sad as it is, your hope does not trounce the hard laws of reality. The right key does not open the wrong door.
Let's try something else...
Of course. It hits you that you are in possession of a gun.
Not only that, but it's an M1873 with a rosewood grip and a fine engraving on the barrel that reads, "Single Action Army."
Breaking the lock with such an excellent pistol would be a piece of cake.
However, firing it would alert everyone in the castle to your location. Are you sure you want to do that?
Let's try something else...
When you most need it, you remember your old buddy Bobby McPin, resting inside your pocket.
It has come in clutch and got you out of tight spots many times, and will surely not let you down this time.
Roll a D100... 42. Your Lockpicking check succeeds. You expertly pick the lock open and once again are saved from danger. Probably.
"Probably"?
Ahem. The door opens with a familiar click, and you dodge out of the way into the unknown.
You close and lock the door, then start looking around your impromptu "safe room."
The storm outside the window has passed. The face of the moon peeks out from between the clouds.
With the help of the gentle moonlight, you determine that this room is a rather lavish bedroom.
While, of course, most of the rooms you've seen so far make you think of the word "lavish"...
This one takes the cake. It is the textbook definition of peak luxury.
In fact, it feels like the occupant filled it with only the world's most expensive, most premium articles.
Among them all, the giant painting resting by the terrace window draws your attention.
You can't see the person's face clearly, but they're wearing a gorgeous wedding dress studded with diamonds. It leaves a profound impression on you.
Upon closer inspection, you see that the wedding dress isn't made of cloth – it's in fact made of many intertwined, twisting white tentacles.
Each of the little suckers dotting their surface glows with a faint silver light under the moon...
The moment you realize this, a dread beyond all description assails you!
*hisss* friaghgleh... grsh... *hisssssss*!
The growly voice whispers right into your ear... Your vision turns into a spinning blur, and your body begins to tremble.
What little is left of your Volition screams at you – don't give in! Fight it, goddammit!
Roll a D100... 91. Alas, because of your weak Volition, your spirit instantly crumbles despite your best efforts.
Yes, in line with what one might call reverse psychology, you ignore your own Volition and give in to fear.
*hisss* friaghgleh... grsh... *hisssssss*!
Gripped with horror, you cave in under the immense pressure and scream.
Your charm glows again, and it only barely manages to bring you back to your senses.
Click... Click...
The door opens, and you sense that someone has entered the room.
I told you not to enter rooms without the occupant's permission.
What are you doing inside Lord Manjuu's private bedroom, Investigator?
São Martinho takes slow steps towards you. She is dragging a huge sickle along the floor, producing a jarring screech.
Screee... Screee...
I don't take kindly to guests with no respect.
It's time you learned a thing about manners, dear Investigator.
For better or worse, your senses all shut down before the sickle even reaches your neck, and you don't feel a thing.

sequence: BE-07 - No Trespassing

scripts.say: São Martinho DID warn you about entering private areas without permission.
You got this bad ending because you ignored her warning just to get away from the footsteps in the corridor.
How was I supposed to heed her warning when... Wait, would I have survived, had I just done that?
Something tells me Enterprise came up with this one.
This is the penultimate chapter, too, so you were consumed by the darkness just before dawn.
Now I'm wondering – is Lord Manjuu also a part of this cult?
We won't spoil it for you. That said, you can interpret the way he decorated his bedroom as a hint.
Then who did those footsteps in the corridor belong to?
Should I just wait there instead of going into the room?
Heehee. That's for you to find out.
Roll a D100... 48. Success. It is unfortunately too dark to make out their identity.
However, you do realize that there's a door next to you. You don't know where it leads.
As the footsteps draw closer by the second, you decide to...

options.content: Hold my breath and hide in the darkness!

scripts.say: You probably have skills you don't remember yet, and you start to think you might have a Stealth skill with expert-level proficiency.
