Contrary to your hopes, though, nothing happens after waiting for a few moments. Yes, it seems you don't have the chops to blend in with the darkness.
...Alright, let's hide behind the pillar instead.
The map says the room in front of me isn't the study.
And there's no telling what will happen if I go inside without the occupant's permission.
What I should do is hide behind the pillar and wait and see.
You recall São Martinho's warning and decide to conceal yourself behind the stone pillar.
The footsteps draw closer and closer until they're almost right next to you.
What's more, your surroundings get brighter the closer the footsteps come.
While you still can't discern their identity, you can tell that the person is carrying a lantern.

options.content: Best to stay put for now.

scripts.say: This is it! Time to finally show off what a crack shot I am!
You proudly unholster your firearm and go running towards the light.
Despite knowing how close the danger is to you now, you decide to quietly stay and watch what happens.
Then, the lantern shines right on you, and you're discovered.
...What are you doing here, Investigator?
Whydah had a hunch you wouldn't find the study on your own, so she asked me to show you there.
Then the lights went out, so I had to turn around to get a lantern, and that took ages.
Judging by how lost you look... Seems she made the right call. Follow me, the study's just around the corner.
(Is it just me, or is she a lot friendlier than before?)
(I think someone mentioned that she was Whydah's personal maid at one point... Maybe the two are on the same side?)
Why are you staring at me? Is there something on my face?
...Are you thinking about my friendlier tone?
Well... You know... That's because I thought you were just a fraud posing as an investigator.
That is, until Whydah told me about you.
I still don't like you, but she trusts you, so I trust you, too.
Whydah is smart, and I have faith in her judgement. Please, Investigator... solve this case and save us.

options.content: I'll give it my best shot!
Sure, if the pay is right.

scripts.say: Thank you~
Heh. Right, you're running a business, after all.
Don't worry, you'll be paid handsomely for any work on top of what you were hired for.
Step, step... Step, step...
As you're chatting away with the maid, you suddenly hear footsteps not far from you.
Crap! We'd better hurry. That's probably Golden Hind and Galley, and we do NOT wanna bump into them.
Royal Fortune extinguishes her lantern, then the two of you run through the darkness.
The footsteps behind you are still getting closer, despite you running as fast as your legs can go.
This is a do-or-die situation. You decide to...

options.content: Come up with some other way to shake them off!

scripts.say: No, Investigator! I know you're desperate, but you will NOT pull a gun on Golden Hind!
Her tone is serious, with a hint of "I will kill you if you do."
...I'll think of something else.
Ever closer draw the footsteps... If you don't act now, something horrifying will befall you!
What to do, what to do... I know! I'll knock over some planks to block the path!
You reach towards a stack of wooden crates. The moment you touch it, a surge of memories returns to you.
You have remembered your number one skill – Throwing. You have expert proficiency with this skill.
You did it! Finally, you unlocked the skill I came up with!
The dice result in a – surprise – 1! Critical success!
You grab a box instead of a plank and throw it with full force at your pursuers. Since it's too dark to see, you miss, and hit a nearby pile of junk instead.
The pile collapses, blocking off the path behind you. For now, you don't have to worry about your pursuers catching up.
Let's run for it! Now!
Taking advantage of the confusion, the maid grabs your hand and hastily runs off with you.

sequence: Chapter 7 - Misty Moonlight

scripts.say: At long last, you and Royal Fortune arrive in the study. You lock the door tightly, sealing out all danger on the other side.
It is bright inside the study. After looking around for a bit, you feel it would be more apt to call this a library than a study.
See, Lord Manjuu's late wife was a major bookworm, and Whydah still is, so he had a proper library built in the castle.
No better place to hide a needle than a haystack. There's bound to be some juicy information here.
The question is, how many books are there to look through?
30,000. It wasn't easy getting that many.
Don't worry, though. For the sake of all our sanities, you won't need to go through them one by one.
I wasn't going to, anyway. There's not enough time in the world to read that many books.
Let's instead start with the books Golden Hind reads the most.
Her favourite books, eh? They should all be in the same bookcase. Let's see... There!
The maid points at a particular bookcase near the terrace window.
One whole bookcase is still a lot of books... It's at least manageable, though.
Well, let's get to work, Investigator. How about half the bookcase each?
Sounds good.
You stand before the bookcase.
My god...
You keep standing there, staring at it in a daze, like you're waiting for something to happen.
Do I really need to go through a whole bookcase? It's better than reading 30,000 books, but still.
The longer you stare, the more your urge to read grows. It's almost like the books have you under a spell.
Are you telling me to get a move on? Fine. Let's dig in.
You take a random book from a shelf and start reading it.
Roll a D100... 19. Success. Even though you're only flipping through the pages, you feel like the information is flowing directly into your head.
In less than 10 seconds, you've absorbed all the knowledge of that book.
Congratulations. You have remembered the skill Speed Reading. You have novice proficiency in this skill.
That skill was there all this time? Why didn't I remember it while reading that letter?
Uhh... Perhaps you weren't reading it fast enough?
Oh. Okay.
Ahem. Even with only novice proficiency, going through a bookcase will be a cakewalk for you.
If you use Eagle Eye, you may be able to narrow down your search even further.
One Eagle Eye check, please!
Roll a D100... 33. Success. Without hesitation, you grab another book from the– Wait, what? What's that book doing there?!
What book? The one I'm holding?
Yes! I mean, no! That book is unimportant! You don't need to read it!

options.content: That only makes me want to read it more.

scripts.say: (You don't hear Hai Tien lose her cool every day. Something's clearly up with this book. Let's give it a read.)
"She took the Commander's hand, gently placing it upon her own cheek..."
"The lady in white's heart has belonged to this person since the day they first met. Alas, she lacks the courage to profess this love of hers..."
"The secret feelings she harbors are like flower petals, fluttering in the spring sun. Beautiful, fleeting, a dream-like mirage..."
"Like a summer wind stroking her soft cheek, the Commander's amorous whisper prompts a blush on her face that extends from ear to ear..."
Yes, it would seem one of her own works ended up as a prop.
Whoa... That prose is so, like, poetic!
Aaahhh! Um, you astutely notice that Royal Fortune has come to a stop! You suspect she has found something of note!
You decide to immediately throw that book aside and go have a look!
Phew... You check your half of the bookcase one more time, but nothing jumps out at you.
Then, you astutely notice that Royal Fortune has come to a stop. You suspect she has found something of note.
She stands motionless in place, looking through one book in particular.
Huh?! Are you done already? What did you find?
Nothing worth mentioning. Any luck on your end?
Well... I picked a couple of books Lord Manjuu and his family had read, and then I saw this photo album, and I just got absorbed.
Back when his wife was still alive, it was warm in the castle. Not cold, like it is now.
The lady was a compassionate, cheerful person, and had a smile that made the sun shine brighter when she was here.
This place was always full of life and laughter... that is, until she fell ill and was taken from us.
After that, Lord Manjuu devoted himself to charity and medical work, and he didn't give his family the attention they needed.
We're lucky Golden Hind and Whydah supported each other, and São Martinho took on many of the roles the lady used to, so the two had a decent childhood.
Who's the person that's been painted over in black in these photos?
That's Morgan, the daughters' childhood friend.
Passed away abruptly, much like Lady Manjuu... Golden Hind never recovered from it. Her bereaved father only made her days more miserable.
One day it got too much for her, so she joined a religious group in hopes of finding solace.
But, well... that group was up to very shady business. São Martinho joined later, as well as Adventure Galley, and it changed them both drastically.
BANG! BANG! BANG! BANG! BANG! THUD!
You want to gather more info, but suddenly hear a foreboding banging from outside the study.
Oh, crap! They've found us...
Investigator... I leave Whydah and all the rest to you.
While I still don't fully believe in you, I have no one else I can turn to.
Whydah gave me this lantern and told me to hang on to it... but I think you'll need it more than me.
I'll stay here and buy you some time. I've known these people for years, so they'll let me live.
Now go... Save us!
The maid steels herself and runs out of the study. You hear the commotion outside the door intensify. You know for certain that she won't hold them back for long.
You have the lantern she left you, and a few books you haven't checked yet. You decide to...
The maid steels herself and runs out of the study. You hear the commotion outside the door intensify. You know for certain that she won't hold them back for long.
You have the lantern she left you, and a few books you haven't checked yet. You decide to...
There's no time to waste. You put your hand on the doorknob, determined to bail right now, but then your brain sets off a warning alarm.
It goes without saying that leaving through the door isn't the wisest choice. You should think of another way to get out.
The only way out is through the door... but, they will surely catch you if you try to leave that way.
Going in head-on isn't an option, so that leaves only fleeing through the window.
Can't I make anything to aid in my escape?
You search your surroundings for things you can use. A thick curtain catches your eye. You could make something out of this.
Roll a D100... 2, critical success! Using your expert-level Trap-Making skill, you create a durable escape rope.
Good, now I have a ticket out of here. But first... I'll quickly examine the lantern Royal Fortune entrusted me with.
Roll a D100... 47. You pass a Folklore Scholar check.
Once you actually hold the lantern, you remember having read about it in a pamphlet from the Miskatonic University's museum. It must have the same power as the charm in your pocket.
Interesting... Whydah must've "borrowed" a lot of stuff from the university when she left.
(There are still leads to follow up on, but based on what I know now, it's obvious that Golden Hind has been performing some evil rituals.)
(Her goal is to bring back their childhood friend, and São Martinho and Adventure Galley are in on it.)
(The servants who have disappeared were probably sacrificed... And if they catch me, my head is next on the chopping block.)
What monsters... I should leave for now, then come back with police backup and save these people.
Sometime later...
Clinging tightly to the rope, you manage to escape from the study.
But, as soon as your feet touch the ground, you are caught in a sudden fog, and you lose your orientation.
You try to descend the mountain by relying on your memory, only to find yourself in a garden somewhere.
Roll a D100... 36. You pass an Eagle Eye check. The fog gradually clears, and a massive magic circle appears before your eyes.
It glows faintly while seemingly distorting the space around it, so you cannot clearly make out the enshrined stone statue on the opposite side.
And yet, through your skin, you feel an evil, chilling power in the air.
Roll a D100... 36. You pass a Folklore Sholar check. That statue is a symbol of the evil god Golden Hind's cult worships. Moreover, the ceremony they perform has already begun.
So I'm still in trouble... I can't believe I ended up at the ceremony site after just walking around.
You sense a piercing, cold gaze, and a hazy phantom emerges from the indigo mist.
The thing knows you're there, and waits for you – the lamb – to sacrifice itself.
Frogakhleh! *hisssss*!
Are you the final sacrifice?
Its every word stabs at your spirit like a sharp sword. Your sanity shakes like a small boat, rocking in the furious sea.
But then, the charm in your pocket and the lantern resonate, and a comforting, soft light embraces you.
The goosebump-inducing dismay that gripped you fades away in the blink of an eye.
Frogakhleh! *hisssss*!
Hahahah! Interesting. You've clearly come prepared. Are you here to strike a deal?
The sweet, clear voice comes from right inside your head. It is tempting you, making you question your motivations.
As an experienced detective, however, you're well aware of the dangers of negotiating with evil gods. Whydah did not give you this lantern for you to strike any deal.

options.content: I'll put an end to this evil being!
I'm doing this for the money!
In the name of love and justice!

scripts.say: You are determined to expel this gestating phantom of evil. You will keep your promise to Whydah and Royal Fortune and put a stop to what's been happening at this castle.
Turning up the lantern's luminosity, you take aim at the apparition and throw your charm with all your might.
You roll a 1 and get a critical success on your Throwing check! Commander, use my luck and give that thing hell!
The charm explodes violently upon contact with the phantom. The lantern in your hand resonates with it again and shoots out a blinding golden light.
Pain, despair, death, distraught, and a little bit of scorn... You feel many different emotions all at the same time.
The evil phantom goes up in a black flame and burns into nothing.
As the rainfall stops, the morning sun finally rises after a long night.
After you drove off the avatar of the ancient god, you swiftly left the castle grounds.
You immediately went to the police when you returned to the city. Thanks to your years of good standing with them, they believed your testimony.
This was not the police's first paranormal case, nor will it be their last.
São Martinho and Adventure Galley confessed to all their charges, and the case was officially closed.
Even though you knew the truth, the thought of those innocent smiles in the photo album made you hold your tongue.
After that, you and Whydah wrote to each other. She told you Royal Fortune got away with only minor injuries. It seemed Golden Hind and the servants went easy on her.
You received a generous payment for having solved another case. And yet, when you returned to your office, you felt a lack of closure.
You felt unsatisfied because of some stone left unturned... You forced yourself to get over it. It didn't take too long for you to file away this case in the back of your mind.
Several months later, you saw a front-page article in a newspaper – "Old castle on city outskirts burns down - no survivors found."
Another while later, you received an invitation to an extravagant banquet.
Your old client – Lord Manjuu – had finally gotten over his deep grief. He had started a new life with a fresh outlook.
A happy ending, you'd think... but now, at the banquet, your mind is preoccupied by a certain woman wearing a wedding dress for some reason.
You swear you've seen her somewhere before... but where?

sequence: TE - True Love is Eternal

scripts.say: The maid steels herself and runs out of the study. You hear the commotion outside the door intensify. You know for certain that she won't hold them back for long.
You have the lantern she left you, and a few books you haven't checked yet. You decide to...
(There has to be something in the books Royal Fortune left behind.)
(Based on what I know now, it's obvious that Golden Hind has been performing some evil rituals.)
(Her goal is to bring back their childhood friend, and São Martinho and Adventure Galley are in on it.)
(They probably sacrificed the servants who have been declared missing.)
I still feel like I'm missing something, though...
You pick up a book. Roll a D100... 26. You figure out that this is the castle's accounting book.
After quickly reading through, you determine that these expenses are way too high for only a handful of people.
You pick up a different book. Roll a D100... 22. You determine that this is a list of things the family bought this year.
In addition to food, clothing, and ordinary things, the castle has received a huge amount of antiques. In Lord Manjuu's name, no less.
Some time has passed, and you now hear noise from the other side of the door.
BANG! BANG! BANG! BANG! BANG! BANG!
Someone is pounding on the door. They've gotten past Royal Fortune... You only have enough time to read one more book.
You pick up the last book. Roll a D100... 8. You conclude that this book is Lord Manjuu's personal diary.
As you keep reading, one part in particular lodges itself into your memory.
"...Three years since my sunshine passed on, I bought a clinic and set up a charity. Now I no longer need to worry about sacrifices."
"...Morgan found out about my secret. I may have to... No, I can't just kill my daughter's longtime friend."
"...I shoved Morgan into the secret room behind the painting in the study. God will do the right thing for me."
"...Why?! Why hasn't it worked yet?! Bah! I have to keep trying! Maybe I need more sacrifices! Yes, I need to find more sacrifices!"
"...The housekeeper and my first daughter have become followers of our faith. Perhaps sacrificing believers is the way to go?"
"...I've got it. I'll need to find a scapegoat..."
...So that's the truth. Lord Manjuu is the wire-puller behind all this.
He killed Morgan and pulled his daughter into his cult, either as a better sacrifice, or as someone to pin the blame on.
Then he hired investigators to cover up his crimes even more perfectly.
All of this, just so he could resurrect his dead wife... This guy is sick in the head.
You've figured it all out, detective. The altar Lord Manjuu made with his own hands is the cause behind all the strange happenings at the castle.
Golden Hind and the servants are still breaking down the door. You need to make a decision, and quick!
The answer is clear as day. I'll go in there and drive out the root of all this evil.
Following the writing in the diary, you walk right up to the portrait before the hall to the secret room.
Wait. First, I'll bring the lantern Royal Fortune left for me. I'll also roll for an Eagle Eye check.
Roll a D100... 47. You pass a Folklore Scholar check.
Once you actually hold the lantern, you remember having read about it in a pamphlet from the Miskatonic University's museum. It must have the same power as the charm in your pocket.
Interesting... Whydah must've "borrowed" a lot of stuff from the university when she left.
You are ready. Moments before your pursuers break in, you slip into hiding in the passage to the secret room.
The lights in the study go out behind you. You light up the lantern and bravely step forth into the darkness before you.
You continue moving forward, trusting the lantern's faint light. After walking for some time, you find yourself inside a burial chamber. In a flash, an eerie magic circle appears before your eyes.
It glows faintly while seemingly distorting the space around it, so you cannot clearly make out the enshrined stone statue on the opposite side.
And yet, through your skin, you feel an evil, chilling power in the air.
Roll a D100... 42. You pass a Folklore Sholar check. That statue is a symbol of the evil god that Lord Manjuu's cult worships. Moreover, their cursed ceremony has already begun.
You sense a piercing, cold gaze, and a hazy phantom emerges from the indigo mist.
The thing knows you're there, and waits for you – the lamb – to sacrifice itself.
Frogakhleh! *hisssss*!
Are you the final sacrifice?
Its every word stabs at your spirit like a sharp sword. Your sanity shakes like a small boat, rocking in the furious sea.
But then, the charm in your pocket and the lantern resonate, and a comforting, soft light embraces you.
The goosebump-inducing dismay that gripped you fades away in the blink of an eye.
Frogakhleh! *hisssss*!
Hahahah! Interesting. You've clearly come prepared. Are you here to strike a deal?
The sweet, clear voice comes from right inside your head. It is tempting you, making you question your motivations.
As an experienced detective, however, you're well aware of the dangers of negotiating with evil gods. Whydah did not give you this lantern for you to strike any deal.

options.content: I'll put an end to this evil being!
I'm doing this for the money!
In the name of love and justice!

scripts.say: Your conscience takes a hit the moment you say those words.
Yes. You have deduced that Lord Manjuu is behind these disappearances, and yet all you seem to care about is your payment.
You are better than that. Something as meaningless as money cannot sway your iron spirit.
You are determined to expel this gestating phantom of evil. You will keep your promise to Whydah and Royal Fortune and put a stop to what's been happening at this castle.
Turning up the lantern's luminosity, you take aim at the apparition and throw your charm with all your might.
You roll a 1 and get a critical success on your Throwing check! Commander, use my luck and give that thing hell!
The charm explodes violently upon contact with the phantom. The lantern in your hand resonates with it again and shoots out a blinding golden light.
Pain, despair, death, distraught, and a tinge of satisfaction... You feel many different emotions all at the same time.
The evil phantom goes up in a black flame and burns into nothing.
As the rainfall stops, the morning sun finally rises after a long night.
You eventually found an exit out of the secret room and escaped from the castle.
You immediately went to the police when you returned to the city. Thanks to your years of good standing with them, they believed your testimony.
Your account of the events was bizarre and made people's skin crawl, but it was no tall tale by the standards of the denizens of Arkham.
This was not their first paranormal case, nor will it be their last.
Working with the police, you forged a report to Lord Manjuu. You told him that not a single soul survived that night.
Fully convinced that his plan worked, Lord Manjuu flew back to the country to file a case against you under the pretense that you murdered everyone in the castle.
But, when his plane landed, the police were on the scene to arrest him. He was taken into custody and will pay for the crimes he has committed.
Afterwards, you and the police performed a thorough search of the castle and found another altar in the courtyard. It was destroyed, and the case was officially closed.
After that, you and Whydah wrote to each other. She told you Royal Fortune got away with only minor injuries. It seemed Golden Hind and the servants went easy on her.
Golden Hind and her fellow cult members from the castle are currently being treated at a mental hospital. The damage done by the cult to their sanity is slowly, but surely, being undone.
Whydah has, however, had to take on the heavy burden of managing her father's assets until her sister has recovered.
This spelled an urgent end to her carefree life as a shut-in, which she quite obviously is displeased about.
But, despite her grumblings about what a pain it is, she is doing a stellar job. Moreover, Royal Fortune is still by her side for the ride.
While the sisters' lives have been turned upside-down, at the very least, these sudden changes left no bad blood between them.
They face the pain and hardship that is to come, emerge stronger, and move towards a brighter future.

sequence: HE - Beneath the Blue Sky

scripts.say: Congratulations, Commander.
Yes. Who would have thought you'd actually see every last ending?
You wouldn't believe how hard it was to play my character while watching you fail your dice rolls!
Yup. Acting was such a pain...
Agreed~
On the other hand, the Commander had fun, and so did everyone in the control room. All the time spent scripting was worth it.
I told you, you should've let Yukikaze the Great do all the dice rolls!
That would utterly ruin the game's balance, I'm afraid.
Just wondering... In that one ending, who was the woman in the wedding dress at the banquet? Don't tell me it was...
She was Lord Manjuu's wife, of course!
What about the charm from the Miskatonic University? Why did Whydah sneak those out?
Did she know what was going on back home from the very start?
It's possible. Maybe the maid wasn't affected by the cult's influence because the second daughter had those items.
I'm sure there are other minor contrivances, but I think they're best left as mysteries.
Explaining every little thing would just take away the fun of speculating.
You can analyze the story later. What we really wanna hear now is your overall impression, while it's fresh.

options.content: Darkness, mystery, horror... It's everything I expected!

scripts.say: That's what Halloween is all about!

scripts.factiontag: As Phantom of the Ancient God
scripts.say: And giving people the creeps – that's what we ghost ships are all about!
Good to hear. Then again, there's a lot of squeamish people at the port.
There's probably room for improvement, and accessibility.

options.content: You should add a faint-of-heart mode.
Let's include teamplay as an option.

scripts.say: Huh... Good idea. I think we can do that.
I don't care what the story is as long as my character gets to chill in her room, surrounded by crisps and cola.
So... please don't change that.

sequence: A Bump in the Rainy Night

scripts.say: As you may have already realized, which rooms you search are also decided by dice rolls.
We'll roll two D10s. One of them will determine the tens digit, and the other will determine the ones digit. We put them together to make the result.
Oh, and by the way, double 0 isn't 0; it's 100.
If you roll between 1 and 50, you succeed. Between 51 and 100, you fail...
Yes, we've made the rules extremely simple to ease your burden, Commander.
If you fail, you're going straight to a bad ending, no matter what.
If you succeed, you may choose whether you continue investigating or get to see the bad ending.
Of course, we don't want to make you fail over and over... Yes, once you see a bad ending, you'll be returned to the previous roll, which will automatically succeed.
Don't worry about missing anything or getting game-overs. Just have fun.

sequence: Prologue - The Castle in the Mountains

scripts.say: You hear the clunk of a door opening, and you realize that someone has entered the room.
Hmm? Comma– Investigator, what are you doing in the servants' room?
Wait, I know! You've already begun investigating, right? Wow, that's our first-rate investigator for ya!
...No? You're just lost?
That's fair. This place IS basically a maze. It's easy to get lost when you haven't lived here your whole life.
You can't remember anything about the maid speaking to you.
But, if what she claims is true, you are an outstanding investigator.
The GMs come chiming in through my communicator.
(Ahh. The game advances through the communicator. That explains why it's a key item.)
Uh, Investigator? What's with all the head-turning?
Ahem. You have a habit of constantly examining your surroundings. To an obsessive degree, even. Others must think it's very abnormal.
Suddenly, a fragmented memory flashes in your mind. Roll a D100... 31, success.
You remember that you're a brilliant investigator and have honed your sleuthing skills to a T.
Thanks to years of training, your observational skills far exceed those of a layperson.
Congratulations. You have remembered the skill Eagle Eye. You have expert proficiency in this skill.
Ah, this is the skill Enterprise proposed.
(Oohh, so this is what they meant by "rediscovering" my skills during the investigation.)
(I'm glad Enterprise came up with this. An expert-level sleuthing skill will definitely come in handy during this.)
What's the matter? You got a stomachache? Let me take you to the guest room.
What's the matter? You got a stomachache? Let me take you to the guest room.
Just blanked out for a second there.
You sure you didn't catch a cold out in the rain? You really should go to the guest room and warm up by the fireplace!
(The guest room? That sounds suspicious...)
Just thought you might have a cold, since you look pale! Come on, let's get you to the guest room! There's a fireplace there to warm you up.
Plus, we can't have people thinking the lord of the castle doesn't take care of his guests.
(Judging by her phrasing, I think I need to go to the guest room for the story to progress.)
(On one hand, I want to know what'll happen. On the other, following the script to a T doesn't sound very fun.)
(Maybe there's a secret route, or a way to speedrun this. Let's try something different.)
Really, I'm fine. Let me just go for a little walk.
Walk? But...
(Huh. I wonder what this pattern is.)
You stand before a wooden door. The black engravings chiseled into it are pretty unique, almost like thousands of crooked lines reaching out from a single point.
(I think I remember seeing a similar pattern on the cover of a book Bristol recommended to me some time ago.)
Heheheh. You wonder what the meaning behind the pattern is, and have a faint feeling like it's a religious symbol, but you aren't sure.
You frantically dig through your memories, and then, you feel a flash inside your head!
(If it's important enough to comment on, maybe this door holds some kind of clue?)
Roll a D100... 42. Nice. You manage to latch on to the memory!
Some of your lost memories return to you and form into a single cohesive image.
That's right – you are a fan of the occult and have researched myths and legends from all around the world.
Congratulations. Yes, you have remembered the skill Folklore Scholar. You have novice proficiency in this skill.
You remember seeing this same pattern in a book about myths. That, I'm afraid, is all, however.
Folklore Scholar? That one has to be Bristol's idea.
Of course it was! To be a solo investigator is to roll for Folklore Scholar!
I'm not jumping on the bandwagon so soon... Also, how come I only have novice proficiency in it?
What can I say? That's the luck of the dice.
Ahem. The Investigator decides to open the door.
You put your hand on the doorknob, but a panicked Royal Fortune runs up and stops you.
I-if you don't wanna visit the guest room, you can just rest here! You can't go in there right now 'cause we're cleaning the halls!
(There has GOT to be something behind this door!)
I won't get in the way of the cleaning, so don't worry about that.
You can resume your duties if you want. No need to preoccupy yourself with me.
You manage to get the maid off your case, then turn the knob and open the door.
You step into the castle hall.
It's pitch black, and there is nothing to suggest it's being cleaned.
With the silent darkness filling the hall, you can't observe anything in your surroundings.
Standing there, you are struck by an uncontrollably intense anxiety.
Then, thud. The door closes behind you.
Just as the last glimpse of light fades, you see something dart past you.
And then, you lose consciousness and collapse.

sequence: BE-01 - Curiosity Killed the Commander

scripts.say: Well then...
Of course. Leave it to the Commander to walk headfirst into a bad ending.
I mean, isn't it a LITTLE unfair to kill the player just because they deviated from the script a bit?
Don't tell me I didn't try to warn you!
That was your idea of warning me? Okay... So, what did me in?
This was Yukikaze the Great's idea! You were killed by–
Shhh! Nope, sorry, we don't have any clue! It remains a mystery!
We do know, but telling you would spoil what comes later, unfortunately. Commander, kindly resume your investigation.
What's the matter? You got a stomachache? Let me take you to the guest room.
(Things feel simultaneously simpler and more complex than last time... Let's follow the script for now.)
(Though I am concerned about that dice-roll...)
I'm fine. I just want to walk around the castle for a while.
(I'll just wander around for a little bit until Royal Fortune leaves the room. Then, I'll follow her.)
(That might just yield unexpected results. Yeah, this is a good idea.)
Okay... Well, the corridor is right over there, so stop by later. The housekeeper wants to discuss stuff with you.
Like I said before, this place is like a maze, okay? Try not to get lost.
Royal Fortune immediately leaves the room. It seems she isn't interested in lingering long.
(Isn't this the servants' room...? Very suspicious. I don't want her to know I'm following her, so I'll wait a moment before tailing her.)
After a while passes...
I lost sight of Royal Fortune... Now I really am lost.
Where in the world am I? And why does this hallway seem to go on forever?
Ahaha... Investigator? Why are you here~?
Royal Fortune appears out of seemingly nowhere and flashes you a sweet smile.
Are you lost? Would you like me to show you to the guest room now?
You notice a hint of mischief in her expression.
...Yes, Royal Fortune. Thank you...
But of course♪ Right this way~
Royal Fortune guides you to a guest room lined with luxurious furnishings.
The furniture is so authentic, I can hardly believe it's all a set piece... No wonder you have a Sheffield.
Akashi must have spent a fortune...
On that note, Investigator, you neglected to investigate your own employer.
Your employer, Lord Manjuu, who lives in this castle, isn't just a philanthropist.
A regular philanthropist couldn't maintain this castle or pay your commission. After all, you're a first-rate investigator!
Though Royal Fortune acts friendly, you notice a slight edge in her words.
(Does that mean this NPC doesn't like me? She did reference my "commission" fee, so is she unhappy with that?)
Almost all of the other servants in the castle have resigned due to the constant disappearances.
Only me, the housekeeper, and the chef are left. We need you to find the truth, unlike those frauds... Ahem.
Realizing she's spoken too much, Royal Fortune stops mid-sentence and pretends to clear her throat.
The São Martinho will come soon. You just wait here, please.
I'm gonna go now~
Royal Fortune exits the room.
(Let's organize the clues we have first.)
(This castle's lord isn't just a philanthropist. He might be a wealthy businessperson or a member of the aristocracy.)
(Meanwhile, I'm a famous investigator hired to solve the repeated disappearances in this castle.)
(There may be someone other than the maid, housekeeper, and chef here.)
(My only abilities right now are Eagle Eye and Folklore Scholar. My stats remain unknown... Things aren't looking great so far, really.)
The quiet threatens to lull you to sleep, so you begin inspecting the room to keep yourself active.
Hm...? Are you saying I should roll for Eagle Eye?
Even without your memories, old habits die hard. You find yourself inspecting the room.
So the plan is to just keep railroading me, is it?
I appreciate having a script, but it feels weird to have my every move monitored.
Roll a D100... Result, 1. Critical success! You manage to find one of the secrets hidden in this room!
Well done, Yukikaze the Great!
There you go♪ Go on, praise me more♪
You got a critical success here, of all places? Rgh...
Just then, strange information appears out of nowhere in the Commander's mind!
"Lord Manjuu inherited his family's vast fortune and bought this castle outside of town. He lived here ever since."
"After overcoming the grief of the loss of his lovely wife, due to illness, he devoted himself and his funds to charity and medical work."
"The poor manjuu did his best to save people still suffering from disease out there."
(Hmm. Okay, so that's information on my employer.)
(A wealthy aristocrat, widowed, devoted to charity and medical work... I suppose he's kind and charitable?)
You struggle to piece together this fragmented information, but suddenly, you're assailed by a wave of unease.
A disembodied gaze is fixed on you, leaving you too stiff to move.
The lights in the room all turn off at once, and even the wood in the fireplace crumbles to ash. Only darkness prevails.
Something approaches from outside the door...

sequence: Chapter 1 - The Stormy Night Bride

scripts.say: You can't see an inch in front of you in this darkness, and all you can hear are a tapping and the sound of heels striking the ground.
Frshfkhazlehsuh...
*hisss* friaghgleh... grsh... *hisssssss*!
You can stop now.
Ahem...
You faintly yet also clearly hear a voice, growling in an unknown language. It sounds distant, yet at the same time like it's whispered into your ear.
Whatever this thing is, you feel that it is quietly approaching from the other side of the door.
(My hair is standing on end here... How did they come up with this?)
After a while, the creepy growling up and goes away.
The lights in the room come back on and everything is back to normal, as though you hallucinated all that...
But then, you notice something.
By a bed not far from the couch, there is a broken mirror that wasn't there before...
Thanks to the intuition you've grown over the years, the appearance of this strange mirror alerts you that something is off about this room.
You use Eagle Eye to examine the room. Roll a D100... 51. Unfortunately, you fail. There's nothing odd about the room. You must've imagined it.
Hang on, there's water all over the table and the floor. Anyone would notice that.
Oh. Umm...
You conclude that they are just water stains. Yes, they don't strike you as particularly important.
Yes, they do? They're clearly suspicious.
You use Eagle Eye again and reach the same conclusion. Certain that they are unremarkable puddles, you move on.
The illusion of choice, huh. Okay, what now?
You look at the mirror and notice the silhouette of a person.
It is a beautiful woman, wearing a trailing white dress and a long veil that hangs to the ground.
(So, a wedding dress?)
Goodness me~ Sorry for frightening you. The castle's power lines are quite old, and we frequently get outages when it rains.
And it certainly doesn't look like the rain is letting up anytime soon... That aside, I take it you're the investigator my father hired?
Yes. You must be his daughter.
That I am. It sounds like he hasn't told you much of anything... Well, given the state our family is in...
(Sounds like this lord has a messy family situation.)
(It also sounds like more people live in this castle besides the three servants.)
Incidentally, I've heard that you're something of an expert on the occult, and have helped the police solve a few paranormal cases before.
I've been reading a few books on the subject lately, and I'm quite hooked, actually~
Would you mind telling me a bit about those cases~?
(I wish. You probably know more about them than I do...)
I'm honored you've heard about me, but could we talk about what's happened at this castle, rather than my boring old stories?
Obviously, you can't talk about cases you can't even remember, so you try to evade the subject. Roll a D100... 72. Yes, unfortunately, your attempt ends in failure.
There is no crack in Golden Hind's smile, yet the look in her eyes suggests a slight distaste.
Oh, you're asking about the disappearances, right?
I know nothing about them~ You can't expect someone with so many servants to remember each one, right?
I'd much rather talk about you, Investigator~
(Doubt I can wriggle out of this one... I'll have to make something up.)
You must be my biggest fan... Okay, let me just think.
You mobilize your whole memory to come up with an amusing paranormal case on the spot.
Right then, something flashes within you. Roll a D100... 42. Success. You remember some general information about the occult.
With natural finesse, you tell your fabricated story to Golden Hind.
Okay, so I don't need to actually come up with one myself. Thank god my skills can do it for me.
See? This is exactly what you need Folklore Scholar for!
Even with average proficiency, sounding convincing to a sheltered lady like her is a piece of cake!
As interesting as that was, I'd like something more substantial and detailed~
You know, like a specific thing you saw on the scene, or a fact omitted from public records.
Wait, I see now. Experts highly value their own research, so you can't share it with someone you don't think is sincere – is that it?
Golden Hind shows a regretful smile, then produces a small sculpture without a word.
It looks part human, part octopus. Its tentacle-like appendages are exceptionally lifelike, and you could swear it looks like they wriggle about.
Simply by looking at it, you feel a sense of indescribable apprehension. A dreadful, depressing feeling seizes and hangs over you.
Deep within your heart, the most terrifying of memories resurface...
(The way she took out this freaky statue without skipping a beat, THAT was pretty scary.)
The oppressive feeling makes your throat constrict, and you start struggling for air.
Roll a D100... 11. Nice.
Although the indescribable dread makes your mind go blank, you manage to suppress the creepy feeling thanks to your many years of investigating.
Looking at the sculpture, you feel as though you've seen something like it before. Another gap in your memory starts filling up again.
Roll a D100... 1! Critical success! You catch all the memory fragments that come forth and remember a bunch of things!

Fed up with how conventional and strict your middle school was, instead of continuing your studies, you became an investigator's assistant, leveraging your extraordinary intellect and powers of observation.
Time passed, and you've now garnered a fair bit of renown in the region.
You have rich knowledge of folklore and myths, and have helped the police solve multiple cases involving the paranormal.
Congratulations. You have attained novice proficiency in the Folklore Scholar skill. Your Intelligence stat is 90 and your Education stat is 30.
...You're saying I have an extraordinary intellect but stopped at middle school, and solved several paranormal cases yet my proficiency is only average?
Sorry, your dice luck isn't great!
You stare into space for a moment as your memories come back en masse. Meanwhile, Golden Hind is still waiting for your answer.
As you stay silent, she eventually loses her patience.
Do you have a problem with my sculpture, Investigator?
Though she raises the corners of her lips, there is no hint of a smile in her eyes.
Your gut sounds an alarm. Something bad is about to happen.
*hisss* friaghgleh... grsh... *hisssssss*!
You hear the garbled growling again.
At the same time, the suspicious water stains on the ground start to multiply, like a trail left by some sea creature...
*hisss* friaghgleh... grsh... *hisssssss*!
You hear the garbled growling again.
At the same time, the suspicious water stains on the ground start to multiply, like a trail left by some sea creature...
I need to act, quickly...

options.content: I think of something using my exceptional intellect!
That's a beautiful wedding dress you have!

scripts.say: Roll a D100... 23. Success. You promptly decide to compliment the gorgeous wedding dress she's wearing.
(Let's just say her dress stole my attention.)
Sorry, it's just so stunning I couldn't help but notice it. Are you getting married today?
Golden Hind is briefly stupefied by your earnest question.
Do you... really think it's beautiful?
She looks at you, but if anything, it feels like she's looking THROUGH you at something distant.
...Investigator, has anyone ever told you you're good-looking?
Something about those words makes another memory fragment shake in your mind.
Roll a D100... 48. Success.
You've received more than a few compliments for your looks. Yes, in fact, most people like your appearance.
Congratulations. You have remembered that your Looks stat is 85.
Wow. I didn't expect THAT to lead to me remembering something.
(whisper) In story terms, it's just like that NPC.
...Speaking of my dress, my beloved chose it for me. I felt a little nostalgic, so I thought I'd put it on again~
You still haven't answered my first question, by the way. You saw my sculpture, so will you tell me your secrets now?
(I guess there's no sidestepping it... I've already lied before, so I'll just lie some more.)
Since you only dabble in the occult but still want to leave a good impression on your employer's daughter, you decide to make up a personal history with the paranormal.
Roll a D100... 16. Success. Using your great intellect, you weave together a number of dramatic anecdotes.
Golden Hind doesn't just buy your tall tales, she adores them. The joy in her eyes intensifies as you go on.
Wonderful! I've finally met a fellow enthusiast!
Oh, my dear Investigator! Such is your depth of knowledge and breadth of experience that you deserve the title of Occult Master! I am amazed~
(Well, it worked... Will that title come into play later, though? Actually, better not think too hard about it.)
There's something I'd like to show you, Investigator. It may have something to do with the disappearances, in fact.
Follow me to the courtyard.
As soon as you enter the courtyard, you see a glowing yellow magic circle on the ground. Behind it is a giant, enshrined stone statue with a mystic appearance.
From under its hood, twisted tentacles extend towards you, and you feel as though they're drawing you into the darkness.
You are frozen in place... Chills and sweat run down your back, and you begin to tremble. You desperately try to regain your composure.
Roll a D100... 78. Failure. The one glance you took has filled you with immeasurable fear and distress.
At last... I've found a sacrifice to appease my lord.
I will soon be reunited with my beloved, and we will never be apart again...
You fall unconscious and are placed on the altar...
Unfortunately, the Investigator meets a chilling death.

sequence: BE-02 - Looks Can Be Deceiving

scripts.say: So... The lord's older daughter is a cult member, and she turned me into a sacrifice?
Heehee, that's correct. You should learn to exercise some caution before you act, Commander.
And here I thought I was about to find a new lead...
From a creep in a wedding dress, wandering a dark castle during a rainstorm? Even I would know to steer clear!
What she said! We made it so obvious!
That sculpture and her incessant questions about occult stuff were meant to hint at it further!
By the way, it says here your cause of death was... having all the blood drained from your body. Interesting.
Yikes... Terrible way to go.
You're still only on chapter one! Try again, Commander!
*hisss* friaghgleh... grsh... *hisssssss*!
You hear the garbled growling again.
At the same time, the suspicious water stains on the ground start to multiply, like a trail left by some sea creature...
I've got to do something... No, wait, let's stay calm.
You use Eagle Eye. Roll a D100... 26. Success.
Suddenly, you realize that Golden Hind is holding something behind her back.
Looking into the reflection of a tray on the table, you see a chilling sight – it is an axe she's holding.
What's more, thanks to your excellent observational skills, you notice something peculiar about the ornament in her hair.
Roll a D100... 31. Your Folklore Scholar check succeeds.
That ornament's pattern belongs to a certain cult. Back when you assisted the police on a case, you saw totems with the same pattern multiple times.
You still clearly remember the cult's horrific activities to this day.
(So she's a member of this cult?)
You feel a haunting premonition coming on.
(Uh-oh. This conversation has got to end, and soon.)
(Ah, right, my Folklore Scholar proficiency is only novice. If I tell her the truth, she'll probably lose interest.)
After some careful deliberation, you decide to admit the truth to her.
While this will impact your reputation negatively, your gut asserts to you that this is the correct choice.
Huh? Oh... Really, now?
Her disbelief is obvious, and all the interest in her expression vanishes at once.
Yes, she probably thinks you're a bold-faced con artist now. Seeing as Lord Manjuu paid a hefty sum to hire you.
You pray that she won't kick you out of the castle, because you have many unpaid bills waiting for you back at your office.
(That's an unnecessary story detail if I ever heard one.)
That's all I've got to say. I'm pressed for time, so please let me focus on your father's request.
You get the feeling that she doesn't want the conversation to end already.
However, she is clearly caught off guard by your use of the word "father."
*knock knock*
Royal Fortune comes into the room.
Golden Hi– I mean, Milady, the housekeeper awaits the Investigator in the guest room.
...It's a shame you need to leave, but I know the case won't solve itself.
I hope to hear good news from you soon, my dear Investigator~
Alright, alright. It's late, so you'd better return to your room, Milady.
Royal Fortune bows before turning on her heel and leaving.
You seize this opportunity and quickly leave the room to follow her.

sequence: "And so, the war ended."
"Peace returned once again to this war-torn land."
"And everyone lived happily ever after."
"It's a satisfying ending, isn't it? Just like every drama should have."
"Congratulations, Commander."
"Hip hip hooray."
"Now, go and join the celebration."
"Enjoy this moment of peace."
"Yes, enjoy it... while it lasts."
Royal Navy Rally Point Iberian Peninsula - Strait Fortress
After the Gazer appearance

scripts.say: The blaring of anti-raid sirens through the air–
Unidentified vessels spotted! You have entered our domain... Er, the Royal Navy alert perimeter! Identify yourselves!
Repeating! Unidentified vessels, you've...
Miss Warspite, they're not responding.
They're just approaching silently, not even attacking... Should I keep yelling at them?
Please do. Rather than being the first to attack, we should patiently work to understand the situation.
Roger!
Miss Warspite, we've received word that giant, anomalous machines have appeared in nearby waters and along the coast!
It seems they can move through the sea of their own volition... What should we do about them?
I can see them even from here.
Do we know anything about them?
They don't look like Siren weapons, and we think they aren't made from any other faction's technology... In short, no...
Understood. Are we able to communicate with other bases?
We're doing our best to restore the connections now.
We made contact with the Malta base for a moment and learned that they were in a similar situation, but we quickly lost the connection again.
Unfortunately, we still haven't restored contact with the World Expo venue or Royal mainland.
According to wide-area recon, the seas between the Mediterranean and the NA Sea are covered in fog.
It extends from surface to sky like a wall, making it impossible to measure its height.
We've sent mass-produced submarines, too, but...
We lost control of recon ships and submarines alike the moment they entered the foggy area. They're lost at sea.
It's possible that we may be trapped in the Mediterranean.
Oh, no... It's like the clouds combined and turned into a big, scary monster.
The same thought occurred to me. This is an extremely abnormal situation, so we should be cautious.
So we should stay calm no matter what, huh?
The unusual substance emitted by those machines continues to spread. At this rate, it's only a matter of time...
York, have you warned that mass-produced fleet that we will attack them if they don't identify themselves?
Yes! I did, but they haven't responded whatsoever!
Then they are the enemy.
We have no more need for warnings. Her Majesty told us to protect this area, and that is exactly what we will do.
All ships, obliterate the enemy fleet! You have the fortress's defenses to support you!

sequence: Royal Navy Rally Point Temporary Malta Base
After the Gazer appearance

scripts.say: Act fast, everyone!
Use active radars to help locate and mop up that gross, gooey substance!
Cold start all inactive radars! Hurry, hurry!
...Ark Royal, how are things on your end?
No enemies coming our way... But the Sardegna Empire isn't looking good at all.
Nelson, any idea what the properties of that goo might be?
Not a clue. It looks like fungus, but also has metallic properties. It doesn't burn, and it's surprisingly tough.
What are we supposed to do about this...?
Are there any casualties?!
No. Fortunately, it's just... kind of gross.
Rodney, Jervis, Janus, and Fortune are working to clean it up as we speak.
You called~?
We're doing just fine here! In fact, we just discovered our secret weapon!
Secret weapon? What have you done?
It's the souvenir shampoo we were selling at the World Expo!
We didn't sell much, so we got to take some of the stock home for free...
Imagine our surprise when we learned that it dissolves that gooey stuff right away!
That's more than just surprising! *sigh*... I'll come over and help.
So it's weak to shampoo? Odd, but dealing with it is our first priority for the moment.
I'll pass this information on to Her Majesty and the Commander right away.
Defeated by shampoo, of all things...
Excuse me. May I take a sample with me?
We have a whole pile of it outside. Take as much as you... Wha?!
Le Terrible?!
Yes, that is my name.
*sigh*... Where did you come from?
Call it a... secret passage.
More importantly, I come with a message from Cardinal Richelieu.
I wish to speak with whoever is in charge of this fortress. Could you tell me who that is?
If Illustrious is at the venue... then would you happen to be in charge?
Sure, but what's this about the secret passage?
Are you saying the Royal Navy aren't the only ones who know about it?
We Iris happen to have a history with this place, as well.
Since there are sacred objects hidden here, it is our duty to protect it.
Well, whether the Cardinal asks us to or not, we're here to secure an escape route for our allies fleeing from the venue.
That goes for my little sisters, too.
R-right... Well, please allow me to assist you.

sequence: Sardegna Empire - Pantheon
Shortly before the Gazer appearance

scripts.say: A woman was basking in the tranquility of the ancient temple with her eyes closed.
That is, until the silence was broken by a girl's energetic voice.
Roma!
I finally found you! What are you doing here?
Ah. Leonardo da Vinci?
Are you really not going to attend the World Expo? I heard today is closing day.
That's what I was going to ask! Aren't YOU gonna be at the closing ceremony?
No. They changed things so Marco Polo will be delivering the closing speech instead of me.
I don't want to get swept up in anything big again. Not after that unexplained incident at the start of the Expo.
Really, don't worry about me. Go enjoy the rest of the expo.
Trust me, I really want to go! But, I can't!
I made a promise to Alfredo not to leave you by yourself. While she's back at the Expo, I have to stick with you.
But, if you go to the Expo, then I can come along! Come on, you can be there as a spectator – you don't have to play an active role!
As a spectator, you say... Hmm. Let me think for a bit...
Sure. I'll call Alfredo in the meanwhile♪
...That's odd. Why won't it connect?
Is she on the line with someone? Or is she out of range?
That shouldn't be possible with the shipgirl-only channel, though...
BEEP—
It connected! ...Wait, it's not my communicator ringing, but rather Roma's?
This is Roma. Who am I speaking to?
I see you're in the Pantheon! I've been trying to get a hold of you!
Marco Polo? I thought you had a closing speech to deliver? You don't have time to call–
Things have changed. The World Expo is in serious danger.
No, not just the Expo, but the Sardegnian nation in its entirety.
In accordance with the state of emergency protocol, I am tasked with resolving this situation.
Until the state of emergency is lifted, all military forces in and around Sardegna are under my command.
Roma, you are to head to the Expo immediately, prepare for battle, and wait for further instructions.
Is Veneto aware of the situation?
I can't say. The Expo is a mess right now and I don't know where she is.
...Okay.
So you, the woman meant to deliver the closing speech, have abandoned that duty and are issuing orders to shipgirls.
Even supposing our Senate's state of emergency protocol was revised as you've described, I cannot accept your command based solely on what you've told me.
Hmm... Didn't you always have a disdain for politics? When'd you get so smart about this stuff?
Simple – my gut's telling me that you can't be trusted.
There's been something strange in the air, ever since the Sirens kidnapped me during the opening ceremony.
That feeling intensified when you called me. The sanctity of this place, the time-honored history and customs of Sardegna... It all changed the moment you came into the picture.
Whoever you are, you are not Marco Polo.
You've seen right through me, have you? Magnificent! Then let me tell you something.
This place, all of it, has become the Kingdom of God. Once His descent is complete, all war will end.
Until then, take care and be patient! Ohohohohoho!
After a boisterous laugh from Marco Polo, massive explosions could be heard coming from outside the Pantheon.
Holy crap! Where did that giant robot come from?!
It's... the coolest thing ever... Wait, now's not the time!
It's coming to attack us! Roma, you need to get out of...
The horns of war have sounded.
Da Vinci, prepare for battle! We're going in!

sequence: Sardegna Empire - Taranto
Immediately after the Gazer appearance

scripts.say: Whoooa! Giant dandelions are falling from the sky!
Whatever those are, they're obviously NOT dandelions!
Bleehhh... Since when did the Sirens start fielding disgusting weapons like this?
The area around Taranto is a mess... Worse yet, I can't get in touch with Veneto or Littorio.
Abruzzi, don't you think we should set out to battle?
No. Best not to jump the gun before we know what's going on.
Rash decisions have cost us too many times in the past.
Good point... Then hopefully, someone will contact us very soon.
BEEP—
This is Marco Polo. Do you read me?
Oh! It's you, Marco Polo!
Thank goodness. This is Aquila speaking. Are you still at the World Expo?
How's the situation over there? Do you have any idea what's going on?
I had a feeling you knew something bizarre is happening.
As you can already tell, all of Sardegna is in serious danger.
In accordance with the state of emergency protocol, I am tasked with resolving this situation.
Until the state of emergency is lifted, all military forces in and around Sardegna are under my command.
Aquila, you and everyone else at Taranto are to head to the Expo immediately, prepare for battle, and wait for further instructions.
To provide rescue and relief efforts? Understood.
Actually, wait... If I remember right, Veneto takes precedence over you on the chain of command on the state of emergency protocol...
What happened to her? Did she confer authority to you?
Veneto this, Veneto that... It's always about her, isn't it?
That's precisely why I've chosen this path.
You know what? Screw all of you! Hmph!
BEEP—
Hm? H-hello? Marco Polo?
Aren't you going to tell us what's going on?
It seems safe to say something quite bad is going down.
It'd be one thing if this was just another quarrel between them, but this clearly goes way beyond any feud.
That strange substance continues to spread even as we speak.
Bad news! Really bad news, everyone!
Look outside! Some ginormous three-legged robot appeared out of nowhere!
It's releasing a white mist everywhere, and it's coming towards us!
A white mist? It can't be!
That robot must be the source of the spore-like substance gumming up the sky!
Abruzzi! Da Recco! Let us prepare for battle at once!

sequence: Somewhere in the Mediterranean
Vichya Dominion fleet - Immediately following World Expo evacuation

scripts.say: Having escaped from the World Expo, the Vichya fleet had ended up somewhere in the Mediterranean Sea.
The Gazers did not even try to launch an attack on them, just as Clemenceau had promised.
You know, it's gonna look like we're the bad guys, since we fled the Expo after it was attacked.
Kersaint, there's no one else around now. I think it's time you explained everything.
What the heck is going on? And what is Lady Clemenceau after?
I haven't the faintest idea, myself.
Lady Clemenceau said she had an ingenious plan in store, but that's all.
She wouldn't tell anyone what the plan is.
All she would tell me is that everything will go well if we do as she says.
Only Kersaint would naively trust that plan with so little information given.
A plan she kept secret not only from the Senate, but also her own comrades within the Tribunal.
I can only pray this plan will lead to something good.
BEEP—
I see you've arrived at the first set of coordinates, Kersaint.
Has everything gone well so far? The Commander left you alone, just as I said, no?
Yes! We wouldn't have been able to leave the pavilion, had the Commander not been there.
We're fortunate that the Commander is a truly kind person.
Not just kind, but reasonable and keen as well.
Now, I'll send you the next coordinates. Make sure you're ready for battle before you head there.
That being said, you are under no circumstances to engage anyone or anything you encounter until you reach the coordinates.
I will call you again once you arrive.
Understood, Lady Clemenceau.

sequence: Sardegna Empire - Venice
After the Gazer appearance

scripts.say: Seems we've hit the jackpot.
So this is where the Senate has been secretly storing all those artifacts. Inside an inconspicuous warehouse.
What are your thoughts on this, Torricelli?
I don't... really have any?
As I told you earlier... I'm not exactly an artifact appraiser or anything...
If you want an expert opinion... you should go to da Vinci...
Cut me a break. It's impossible to get a hold of her.
Hmm... True. She's always busy with her inventions...
But... it's quicker to send me underwater than her, so there's that...
At any rate, your intuition is reliable.
Veneto and I have had our suspicions for a long while, but couldn't find any leads no matter how hard we tried.
Which is why I want you to search this place from top to–
On that note, Littorio...
It's dark and deserted in here... Same environment as always, so...
Don't make any sound... while I'm investigating...
Hehe, hehehe... I promise I'll be thorough...
Littorio turned on her heel and was just about to leave the warehouse, when...
...The black sun. First it came for Roma, and now it's come for me.
But why? I haven't touched any dubious artifacts, so I shouldn't be seeing this.
Maybe you don't see it in response to touching an artifact, but rather because someone actively shows it to you?
Then who would that be? The Sirens? Or maybe...
BEEP—
It's been a while since we spoke, Littorio.
That voice... Is that you, Clemenceau?

sequence: Vichya Dominion - Waters around Toulon
After the Gazer appearance

scripts.say: The Vichya Dominion and Iris Libre formed a coalition fleet to respond to the imminent crisis. However...
Return to the anchorage?! You can't be goddamn serious, Clemenceau!
That unknown substance will cause unimaginable damage if we don't do somethin' about the enemy!
We're shipgirls, dammit! Our duty is to protect humanity!
Yes, I'm well aware. That is why I'm telling you to return to the anchorage.
Don't let the lives I saved from the Commander go to waste.
I'm not telling you not to fight, alright? If the Gazers launch a direct attack on Toulon, then you may counterattack.
Piss off! You think I'm just gonna sit with my thumb up my ass while everything goes to hell around me?!
For goodness' sake... I'm tired of repeating myself over and over.
Gascogne, be a dear and "persuade" her, will you?
Jean Bart. Requesting that you accept the anchorage plan.
Continued refusal will result in Gascogne engaging coercion protocols.
Tsk... So what the hell are you trying to achieve here?
Don't worry, I'll explain once everything is over. Be a good girl, now.
...God dammit!
Jean Bart smashed her communicator into her rigging's armor, leaving a dent in it.
Taking your anger out on your communicator won't solve anything. If it breaks, you'll need to get it repaired.
You'd be pissed too if you were in my shoes.
I'm not 'bout to train my guns on an ally... We'll head to that damn anchorage.
Please don't feel too downcast, Jean Bart. I would suspect Clemenceau has a plan.
You are blessed sister ships, after all. She must want what's best for–
No. Clemenceau's changed.
She's not the same person I used to know.
Still, don't you think you should have faith in her?
I should. But right now, I can't.
She saved me once, but I can't forgive her for what she's done.
When I stepped out of the freezing-cold water and opened my eyes again, I made a promise to myself...
That I'd make a different decision.
That I wouldn't let the Reenactments play out once again.
That I wouldn't let my friends become puppets and pawns ever again.
I stepped out of the Vichya pavilion and looked all around me.
The mysterious substance was still growing, stretching, reaching out like a living mycelium that sought to pull heaven and earth into one.
In addition to the Gazers, smaller enemies began to appear with greater frequency as well.
Fortunately, between the Skybound Wall and the alliance fleet's growing cohesion, the combat situation around the pavilion was slowly stabilizing.
However, just reaching a standstill could hardly be considered a victory with how quickly the situation everywhere else was deteriorating.
...Our analysis of the mysterious substance has brought something new to light.
It may just point us to where these smaller enemies are appearing from.
I check the two pictures taken by Illustrious' recon planes that popped up on my phone.
The first shows a place covered in white, dotted with hundreds of cocoon-like objects of varying sizes.
Each cocoon is connected by a small thread, almost resembling cells making up a larger organ.
The second picture shows a cocoon rupturing, an indescribable enemy emerging from it.
That is disgusting... What ARE these things?
Beings that consume all matter, giving birth to abominations, multiplying...
It is like a scene out of a nightmare, something that could not exist in reality... Even with the Commander by my side, I feel fear...
We may be in a new type of Mirror Sea... Or perhaps, even inside this one's dream...?
Not to be rude, but that just sounds like wishful thinking to me.
"Don't take that personally, Shinano. Others don't understand the power you have, but I do."
No... She is correct... I have no evidence, therefore it is natural that I be doubted...
Reality as this one knows it and the reality we are in have diverged drastically since the arrival of these Gazers...
Supposing that this is a dream, it would explain Marco Polo's and Clemenceau's unusual behavior...
What we do not yet know is if you and this one are the only dreamers, or if all shipgirls are...
That reminds me... Shinano said the same thing back in AF – that the events of that Mirror Sea were a dream.
Of course, no sane person would believe that. There is no way that an anomaly that has tangible effects on both people and reality is only a dream.
However, it's a different story if we assume we've been pulled into a space which functions like a new kind of Mirror Sea, rather than just a dream.
It's a very optimistic guess, but approaching the situation this way is the only way we can hope to resolve it.
"First of all, we're going to treat this space – including the Gazers, the goopy substance, even the World Expo – as part of an anomalous Mirror Sea."
"To free ourselves from it, we will need to find whatever controls the Mirror Sea and destroy or neutralize it."
"That could be Marco Polo, or it could be a machine of some sort. Either way..."
...Commander! Our signal is online!
We have connected directly to the Space Needle tactical line and can communicate with all bases within a huge radius!
Starting up cross-pavilion data transfer line and signal array now!
Royal Navy, Iron Blood, Sakura Empire, Sardegna Empire, Dragon Empery, Northern Parliament, Iris Libre... standby!
Three... two... one... Helena! Turn it on!
BRRRRZZZZZ... fortress here... BRRRRZZZZZ.... received... BRRRRZZZZZ... respond... BRRRRZZZZZ...
Malta... BRRRRZZZZZ... Expo... BRRRRZZZZZ... please respond... BRRRRZZZZZ...
There was a reason I had everyone avoid combat with the Gazers and go through the risk of eliminating the enemies inside the Expo venue.
It was so we could connect to the Space Needle and amplify our signal, establishing a communications network with all bases around the Mediterranean Sea.
The flow of incoming signals all but overloaded the line. This meant our allies were out there, fighting as we spoke.
At the same time, however, it also meant that this anomalous phenomenon was not contained to just the sea around the World Expo.
"First thing's first – we need to sort the situation out and establish a chain of command."
Leave that to me, Commander.
Two heads are better than one, right? I'll help.
Make that four. Pamiat' Merkuria and I will assist, too.
I'm no expert when it comes to this stuff, so let me instead introduce someone who is.
Thiele, come here and give these people a helping hand.
Very well. I can do that.
You, too, should step forth, Noshiro...
Certainly, Shinano.
Working with our allies across the Mediterranean, we finally managed to get a basic grasp on the situation.
Finally, we could pierce through the fog of war and seize the initiative.
Though Gazers had appeared as far as Gibraltar, the fortress there managed to hold.
I asked Warspite to mobilize what forces she could, and she is now on her way with her main fleet to link up with us.
The situation in Malta, however, is far more dire. The garrison is being besieged, its defenders all but surrounded.
In light of this, I put Eugen in charge of a small but battle-hardened detachment of Iron Blood forces to provide support.
Assuming they're able to repel the enemy and secure the island, the plan for now is that they'll group up and return here.
As for the Iris and Vicha forces in Toulon, Clemenceau apparently requested them to defend an anchorage there.
As far as the intel they shared told us, they have no idea what the Vichya's Holy See fleet and the Tribunal are up to.
So, to keep an eye on Clemenceau, they sent Jean Bart and her fleet away to be on standby.
Then, there was the Sardegna Empire, and their groups were quite split.
Marco Polo declared their state of emergency protocol to be in effect and made calls to all Sardegnian bases to inform the shipgirls there that they were under her control.
None of them believed her, however. Later, Veneto convinced them to join our side.
Aquila's fleet over in Taranto had eliminated all enemies in the surrounding waters, and were now regrouping and resupplying.
Littorio and Torricelli were in Venice, investigating a matter relating to their Senate. Then, when the Gazers appeared, they fled the area.
They then wound up alone inside a bunker, but as they assured me, there was no need to worry whatsoever and they'll find an alternate escape route.
That didn't stop me from worrying, of course. Based on Veneto's relieved response to hearing them, however, I just had to believe they'd be okay.
Then there's Roma and a few others. They were in the capital and had successfully repelled an attack on it.
They said they'd mop up the stragglers then group up with us. More importantly, though, they told me a very important piece of information.
That Marco Polo is performing some kind of ritual on her giant, flying throne.
Finally, there was one Sardegnian fleet near the Oasis port that we were completely unable to contact.
That could just have been due to the weather, since a sandstorm appeared there just before the closing ceremony. Just to be sure, we had Taranto send recon planes there.
All in all, our allied fleet includes everyone at the World Expo, a few Sardegnian fleets around the Mediterranean, scattered Iris and Vichya fleets, and a Royal Navy detachment.
The Gazers are powerful, and they're aided by endless cannon fodder. We are outmatched ten to one... but, there is still a chance.
Now, what's our next move?
Mount Vesuvius – the most dangerous active volcano in Europa that once wiped out an entire city in a single eruption.
A woman clad in opulent black robes stood at the edge of a distant cliff, her eyes fixed on the crater that rises 1,200 meters above sea level.
However, the dozens of transparent communication windows flickering in the air around her show that she is not here for sightseeing.
The higher you climb, the farther you'll be able to see.
Take in the fresh air, and let it calm your mind. Up here, you have all the time in the world to wait. There is no need for anxiety.
Now, all the preparations are complete.
All that remains... is for the easterly wind to blow.
BEEP—
Clemenceau! Where are you?! Can you hear me?
Why hello there, Marco Polo. I just arrived near the outskirts of Rome.
All the roads were covered with Divine Vestige, you see. It took quite a bit of time to navigate around all of it.
I told you! You should've set out sooner!
Yes, but I didn't want to raise suspicions. Don't forget that I'm the Tribunal's representative.
*sigh*... You need to get your priorities straight.
That's not like you to say. What's wrong? Have things not gone according to plan?
Well, SOME things have. Beyond that, though, it's been an absolute trainwreck.
It's those damn fools at the Expo... They're hell-bent on struggling until the very end.
Couldn't even convince my fellow Sardegnians either. They wouldn't shut up about Veneto this, Veneto that.
Some of them have even dared to challenge me personally!
And from the look of things, it's not gone so well for you either. Why hasn't the Skybound Wall been deactivated yet?
If turning it off was so simple, it wouldn't be a sacrament.
If you want it gone so badly, why not just use your Oculi Dei? Surely it cannot stand before the machines of true divinity.
Of course! If I used all of their power, it wouldn't stand a chance.
However, I can't. I have more important things to focus on.
God's descent has yet to be completed. I don't have the energy to waste on micromanaging the machines.
This would've all gone like a dream, had the Commander not been here. Then I wouldn't have to do this!
Bah... By the way, the Vichya fleet is waiting for your orders.
Tell them to put some pressure on the Expo.
Remember our promise. If my plan falls apart, yours will as well!
But of course. The Vichya Holy See Fleet is never idle.
I'll call the girls in Toulon right away.
Jean Bart, do you hear me?
What do ya want? You changed your mind yet?
You could say that. You have clearance to sortie.
I take it you're ready and raring to go?
Goddamn right. I can't stand to ignore those giant monsters for one more second.
First, I'm gonna mop up at the Expo. Then, I'm gonna wipe out every last one in the waters around it.
Good, you already have a plan. Yes, your enemy is at the Expo.
Be a dear and smite all the shipgirls at the Expo as well with the help of the Oculi Dei, will you?
...What'd you say?
The hell are "Oculi Dei"? And whaddya mean "smite" them?!
They are the mechanical eyes of God Himself. As for "smite," you don't need me to explain that, do you?
Don't worry. I've already evacuated every Vichyan shipgirl from there.
The only ones left now are the sinners.
The Royal Navy, Eagle Union, Northern Parliament, Iris Libre, Iron Blood, Sakura Empire, and Sardegna Empire...
They're all inhuman warmongers who torment the world with their Reenactments. And then there's the one who leads them all.
We've been hurt, mistreated, trampled, and made to suffer for far too long...
Now, the people responsible are all in one place. Isn't this an ideal opportunity to end them?
All conflict will cease to be without their armies to wage war.
Without conflict, there'll be no reason to divide ourselves into factions and groups.
We shall have our revenge, purge the sinful, and prepare to welcome God.
This is the Last Judgment, Jean Bart.
Clemenceau... Have you lost your goddamn mind?
We are SHIPGIRLS, dammit! Our duty is to PROTECT humanity!
Yes! Reenactments are unfair and unjust!
But I'm not about to kill people because of that! Our enemies are those giant eyeballs, not our own allies!
If we don't do something about 'em, all of civilization is gonna be smothered under that nasty goo!
Even if the world isn't all on our side, we need to stand together as shipgirls and fight the real fight!
Those giant machines, Oculi Dei, whatever – THOSE are the real enemy!
As we speak, they're tryin' to destroy everything we're supposed to protect!
I applaud your spirit. Your heart is in the right place.
However, you're wrong. They haven't "destroyed" anything, and they will not lay hands on that which we're supposed to protect.
As I said, this is Judgment Day. The sinful must be punished, and the seas must be wiped clean to make way for the Kingdom of God.
We will not forget nor forgive the pain we and our faith have suffered.
...I get it now. You're not Clemenceau – you're someone wearing her face like a mask.
Someone's got to put a stop to your psycho plan.
I'm not gonna let these robots go to the Expo, and I'm not gonna point my cannons at my friends!
You're saying you don't want justice?
Your twisted idea of it? No. I don't need it.
I'm not gonna follow any damn Reenactments, and I'm not gonna be controlled like a puppet!
If those machine monsters are gonna go after the people I care about...
Then I'll stop at nothing to kill them, even if it costs me my life!
And if you're on their goddamn side, I'll kill you too!
Ahahahahah! Listen to yourself. I'm the Tribunal's representative – I'm your ally.
Clemenceau's more than that. She is my sister, and she is NOT a servant to some fake God!
Whoever you are, you're sure as hell no ally of the proud Templar Knights!
Neither is that woman with the Crown of the Holy See hiding behind you! The only thing she is is a clown!
"CLOWN"?! HOW DARE YOU?!
You have insulted the emissary of God! A crime worthy of divine retribution!
Out of my way, Clemenceau! I am going to teach this little rat some manners!
Of course. By the name of the Crown of the Holy See, I hereby excommunicate Jean Bart, and all those who side with her, from the Vichya Dominion.
After delivering a punishment equivalent to exile, Clemenceau hung up without another word.
Well, well. That's not a very easterly wind at all.
What will you do now, I wonder, Commander?

sequence: World Expo - Vichya Pavilion
Some time later...

scripts.say: Commander, we just got word that Iris Libre and Vichya Dominion forces have engaged the enemy!
Vichya hasn't sided with Marco Polo after all!
"Finally some good news, but given the Tribunal's involvement, we can't assume that they're on our side just yet."
"On one hand, Clemenceau did threaten us with mass-produced ships and Gazers. On the other, we haven't been formally declared as enemies either."
