"The Skybound Wall is still functioning, and it has successfully kept the Gazers at bay."
"Maybe it's just Clemenceau. Maybe she's acting so unusually because she's under some spell..."
What should we do, Commander?

options.content: "We'll sail out to aid Jean Bart and her fleet."

scripts.say: Got it! I'll be honest, there is the chance that this is a trap...
But as you said, the rest of them didn't act hostile towards us, and they didn't mess with the pavilion's defenses either.
Right now, we are all allies in the battle against enemies of humanity.
It's possible Clemenceau has lost her mind, or that she's pulling a ruse in typical Tribunal fashion...
Regardless, we are all shipgirls. We're people with a common goal.
"I'm confident that they feel the same way."
"...The Royal Navy fleet should be arriving any minute now. As for that 'secret passage'..."
Roger!

sequence: Sardegna Empire - World Expo Venue
Closing Day

scripts.say: Colorful flags flutter in the breeze as I walked through the venue on this pleasant day.
I can hear the uplifting fanfare of a band as I approach the Colosseum's entrance.
The closing ceremony is about to start, and people are starting to gather from all over.
The excitement from the clamorous crowd is almost palpable from every corner of the Colosseum.
You can really see why they call it the World Expo...
Things were pretty quiet the last few days, so it totally slipped my mind how massive this event is.
Even I feel like I'm about to get swept away by the excitement.
Heehee. I rarely get to see you this bubbly, Memphis.
I mean, all of our friends are here having fun. How could I not get into the festive mood?
By the way, think we should grab some souvenirs before the Expo closes?
Her Holiness Marco Polo will be speaking during the ceremony, so we'll want to hang on to every word.
"...Her Holiness?"
"Do the people here normally call her that?"
You noticed as well, Commander?
Everyone here, including Memphis... seems a little too excited, don't you think?
I quickly scan my eyes across the crowd in front of me. It's true– everyone seems a lot more fired up than normal. It almost verges on... fanatical.
I can't exactly put my finger on it, but it's almost as if.. the over-the-top energy is hiding something sinister underneath...
"Something weird is going on. It may be the World Expo, but even then—"
Um? Commander, what's gotten into you?
Calling it weird is just rude. Her Holiness is going to appear today, so of course we're fired up.
Now let's hurry and get those souvenirs before they sell out. C'mon!

options.content: (What's all this about "Her Holiness" Marco Polo...?)

scripts.say: During the closing ceremony, Marco Polo arrives at the Colosseum to deliver a speech.
Before I knew it, the three of us had taken our seats in the stands, Memphis's hands full of souvenirs.
"Wait, when did we come in here?"
Thank you all for gathering here today.
I am Marco Polo of Sardegna.
But... I am also God's envoy to this land.
Oh, what a joyous day it is!
We no longer need to fight amongst ourselves.
We no longer need to fear the Sirens!
The order of the world has been overturned! Your supreme God has descended upon the world!
As of now, we reside in the His heavenly kingdom.
Rejoice! All who have gathered here may equally witness His joy!
Celebrate eternal peace!
Celebrate the coming of a new age!
Celebrate the glory of Sardegna!
Celebrate Marco Polo!
Celebrate God!
Despite the absurdity of her speech, the entire venue erupts in uproarious, endless applause.
The raw enthusiasm seems to fill earth, sea, and sky, swelling to an eerie degree.

options.content: "I don't know what's going on here, but we need to put a stop to this!"

scripts.say: (This doesn't make any sense... People aren't behaving the way they normally would!)
I quickly snatch Memphis's communicator away from her and connect it to the amplifier on her rigging.
Huh? H-how did you...
N-no, stop! This is—
With her speech interrupted, Marco Polo suddenly begins to panic.
I can tell she knows exactly what's going on.
I look around and see Memphis and Helena in rapturous applause.
(Something is wrong. Whatever it is, everyone is under some influence.)
(It's too soon to act, though. I should gather as much information as I can first.)
But why is it so hard to keep my eyes open...?
Everything's starting... to go black...
Silence swept across the peak of Mount Vesuvius.
This was one place where the white substance – the Divine Vestige – had not made its mark yet.
Battles were being fought across the Mediterranean Sea, but the sounds of war could not reach this tall peak.
Oh, Clemenceau! Where are you now?
I'm on the way to the safehouse you told me about earlier.
The Tribunal's mass-produced ships have arrived, so it's time for me to set off to the Expo.
Magnificent! Finally, some good news.
It's ridiculous how much pushback we've faced when God's descent is so close to completion... Thank goodness I have you to rely on.
Before your final battle, I have something nice to tell you.
I chose the safehouse you'll be staying in, especially for you.
It's separated from the Senate's secret facilities by only one block.
Also, you'll find Flandre waiting for you there.
You heard that right – Flandre, the blueprint ship. The ace up our sleeve, better than anyone else at manifesting religious concepts.
Really? I would've never guessed she was so close by.
Hahaha! I reckoned she'd be of use to you, so I had her redeployed.
Besides, she belongs to the Holy See, right? It only makes sense that you'd command her, not me.
Now go. Rendezvous with Flandre, take the Tribunal's fleet with you, and head for the World Expo!
I'll send Trento META to assist you as well.
Make those nonbelievers see the light of God!
I will, Marco Polo.
Don't worry about me. Focus only on completing the ritual to...
Oh. She hung up.
So you're going to show your full hand this early. Reckless as always, Marco Polo.
And I hoped you'd stay in the game for at least a while longer...
A shame. It truly is a shame.
Clemenceau lightly shook her head in disappointment, then extended a hand up to her holograms and tapped through a menu.
Kersaint speaking. I've arrived at the coordinates. What am I supposed to do now?
I'll tell you. Listen closely. Blueprint ship Flandre will come there to meet you.
She did briefly serve Marco Polo, but I assure you, she's on our side. Whatever you do, don't attack her.
Once she has arrived, call everyone to regroup with you.
Then, you will go to the new set of coordinates I just sent. Be ready for a battle.
Your enemy is a META – Trento.
She'll think you're on her side, so try to catch her off guard.
Be quick and incapacitate her with one blow.
You must not sink her, and you must not let her get away. Just incapacitate her.
Once that's done, call me back, and remain on standby until your next orders.
...Did you get all that, or was it too shocking for you? Shall I start over?
N-no need, I heard you loud and clear! I've committed it all to memory!
By the will of the Holy Iris.
Yes. By the will of the Holy Iris.
Clemenceau terminated the call, then closed all her holograms.
She grasped her staff firmly, held it high...
And at that exact moment, Mount Vesuvius erupted.
The old Tribunal's crowning achievement among conceptual weapons – Blanc, the symbol of Conquest.
Smoke blotting out the sun, flames consuming everything; finally, a horseman to signal the end days.
It really sets the scene for the climactic finale. Heehee.
Now, I'd better leave while I'm ahead of the clock.
Although I've told Marco Polo countless lies, there's one thing I haven't lied about.
That roads covered by the Divine Vestige are truly, truly awful to walk on.
Atop her winged throne, Marco Polo looked out across the world, watching the final minutes tick away until her audience with God.
The throne and crown both shimmered, signaling that her great ceremony was close to completion.
The seas began churning, and from the dark depths, something began to stir, clawing its way into this reality.
Ohohohohoho! This magnificent feeling! God has come!
Glory to Sardegna! Glory to me!
Let this be the start of a new age!
BOOOOOOM!
A loud, distant rumble drew Marco Polo's attention.
Is that Mount Vesuvius? Why would it erupt now?
More importantly, what is THAT?!
What in the name of... White armor, a bow, and a horse?
How is it flying when it's riding a horse?!
No, what am I saying? That doesn't matter!
The real question is – what in God's name is it, and why did it just leap out of a volcano?!
Marco Polo stared like a deer in headlights at the giant knight, unresponsive to the fact that it was moving closer to her.
What?!
It drew its bow! And it's aiming... right at ME?
Crap! I can't dodge it in time!
KABOOOM!
AAAAAHHHHHH!
Though she herself avoided a direct hit, the horseman's laser beam nevertheless grazed her throne's superstructure, causing a devastating explosion.
Critically damaged from the shockwave and the damage of the explosion itself, the throne began to sway violently.
Damnit, damnit, damnit! My wings! I can't maintain flight!
I need to find... somewhere to make an emergency landing!
BEEP—
Clemenceau's calling? Now, of all times?!
Clemenceau! Where are you?!
You must have seen the giant horseman by now! What IS that thing?!
Is it some secret weapon? Are Veneto or the Commander in control of it?!
I need help! My throne is breaking down as we speak!
Forget about the Expo! Come here and rescue me!
"I saw the first seal open, and I beheld a white horse."
"And he that sat on him had a bow, and a crown was given unto him, and he went forth conquering."
That is Blanc, the Tribunal's Mechanicus Harbinger of Conquest, a divine machine made by mortal hands.
Now, with the concept of conquest strengthened, I have regained control over the Tribunal's mass-produced ships.
Checkmate, Marco Polo.
WHAT?! Was this your goal all along?!
You lied to me! You manipulated me, Clemenceau!
Ahahahaha! Took you long enough to realize.
While you're a good friend, your "God" was never meant to be.
How could you do this? How could even YOU betray me, Clemenceau?!
We shared the same dream! We were kindred souls! You were the only person I could trust!
I thought you were with me... I thought you were my friend...
Don't sulk. I feel the same about your dream, and I'm thankful for all you've done for me.
Likewise, our friendship wasn't a lie. I still consider you a friend.
And that is precisely why I have to stop you.
This is the only way to save Sardegna's future, as well as your life.
Why... Why would you do this to me?
You will never be more than a jester, and I mean that in a good way. You're not fit to play a villain.
A villain betrays. They betray their beloved nation, their family, and their friends.
If you want my advice – let the true villain take on all the responsibility.
While it is true that the nation of Sardegna has made mistakes, it is only a victim at the end of the day.
In fact, actively cooperating with the Commander may be to its benefit.
Don't you think that would be a great first step towards spreading your glory?
In the end, you're just a mortal... like the rest of them...
That I am. A mortal and a villain. But, even a villain can look out for her friends.
Listen, Marco Polo. I will not let you summon a false god that will turn you into a Pawn.
I will not let you destroy everything you hold dear.
And most of all, I will not let you be tarnished with sin beyond redemption.
There's no point... Nothing matters anymore...
Why... Why did this have to happen...
I was so close... Just one step away...
It's over... My ideals...
My... perfect world...
Muttering in disillusionment, Marco Polo and her crumbling throne sank beneath the water's surface.
Once more, silence swept across the world.
A massive fleet was gathering in the waters outside of Saint Helena's port.
Before Richelieu's eyes, countless Iris Libre flags fluttered in the wind.
But among them was a flag that had not been flown for what felt like an eternity – the Iris Orthodoxy's insignia, representing both Iris Libre and the Vichya Dominion.
All who saw it couldn't help but wonder – how long has it been? How long have they waited for this moment?
Richelieu's eyes turned from the flags raised all around her, towards the sea fog hanging low in the distance.
What had once been a source of mystery and doubt was now a doorway towards her goals.
But unlike the sunny, placid seas around her that shimmered with the colors of her homeland, what awaited on the other side of the doorway was the scent of gunpowder and burning debris.
(Le Terrible, this is what you were searching for at the Tribunal stronghold...)
(But why does the Tribunal use Siren technology to this extent?)
(Clemenceau, what role do you play in all of this...?)
Cardinal, it's almost time.
Yes. At long last...
Richelieu took a deep breath, stepped forward in front of the podium, and felt the weight of her fingertip pressing down into the tiny button on the microphone.
My friends of the Iris Orthodoxy, listen well–
The entire audience fell silent as everyone's attention shifted to the Cardinal's words.
Richelieu looked out across the people gathered there. She saw her friends – those who she had fought alongside before, and those who she would fight alongside in the battle to come.
My friends, you have seen what lies on the other side of that door–
Our blue seas, violated by the enemy.
Our land, rivers, and skies engulfed in a nightmare from which there is no waking up.
As we speak, the anomalies that attacked the World Expo encroach on our world.
The flames of war threaten to consume us once again.
But do not forget – there are still those who would also give anything to snuff out those flames.
Yes, our compatriots in the Vichya Dominion are fighting as we speak.
Richelieu gestured to the doorway in front of them. The scenery on the other side became clearer and more vivid as the sea fog prepared to teleport them.
Cannons firing desperately, swarms of bizarre enemies, giant machines raining from the sky, a sea choked with unnatural, grasping clouds.
Do not forget – both Iris Libre and the Vichya Dominion used to exist as one.
The Iris Orthodoxy has always been one.
However, the misfortunes of the past divided us, misleading us into turning our blades on our own.
We never asked for those scars that now cover us and our homeland.
None of us chose the unreasonable reality we now face today.
After a pause, she surveyed her compatriots again.
Then, she reached for a flag standing on the podium—one that she did not normally bear.
Despite that, many of you have followed me across the Royal Islands, through the flames of war.
Others joined us along the way on this long march toward justice.
I, Cardinal Richelieu, firmly believe that we are all driven by the same belief, regardless of how long we have been on this journey.
There is no doubt in my mind that we are all gathered here for a unified purpose–
To see the Iris Orthodoxy become whole once more!
We will not turn a blind eye while our home is ravaged!
We will not turn a blind eye to the suffering of our friends!
We proud warriors will not bend. Not to Sirens, not to the Reenactments, and certainly not to the fear and uncertainty.
Even if what lies beyond this door is a calamity that threatens all of civilization, there is but one thing for us to do.
We will defy it, and we will fight in the name of the Iris Orthodoxy to the very end!
I, Cardinal Richelieu, do solemnly swear upon this sacred banner...
I will fight until I breathe my last.
I will fight until the banner of the Iris Orthodoxy flies free over our homeland, when no enemy shall ever threaten us again!
Come, my compatriots of the Iris Orthodoxy. The time is upon us.
Weigh anchor! We set sail for our motherland!
Their vessels rumbled like thunderous applause.
Thus, the glorious march of a unified Iris Orthodoxy had begun.

sequence: Vichya Dominion Territory
Toulon Harbor

scripts.say: Fierce fighting had been raging on for quite some time.
Burning wreckages now littered the surface of the water.
Though the defenders had managed to buy a moment of peace, there was no doubt in their minds that they would not be able to hold off the next onslaught.
After destroying the final enemy in her line of sight, Jean Bart kneeled, exhausted, and looked at her injured allies.
What drove them was no longer pride, but an indignation of not wanting it to end like this.
Not again, damn it...
Am I just losing control of my emotions...
...Or did I make the wrong decision?
Did I lead my friends to destruction again?
Jean Bart, the next wave is coming!
It's not just mass-produced ships this time! They have more forces in the skies above and waters below...
What should we do...?
(Good question... I damn sure wish I knew the answer.)
(First Richelieu, now Clemenceau. Why must we suffer betrayal after betrayal?)
Jean Bart numbly pushed away the call from her communicator and sat down in the water.
Don't give up just yet, Jean Bart.
Sister...?
Tch... What, is that just my life flashing before my eyes? Or is it the stupid black sun making me hallucinate?
What a cruel joke. So this is who God sends to take me away.
Jean Bart, as leaders, there are always those who look towards us for hope.
If even we give up, we shut the door on those who deserve a brighter tomorrow.
Please fight until the last light has faded.
Quoting the Commander, huh? God sure has a funny sense of humor, using my sister's face to say those words...
BOOOOM!
The booming of artillery heralded the return of war to the quiet sea.
The anomalous enemies born from Divine Vestige appeared on the horizon once more.
However, their attacks were not directed toward Jean Bart's fleet.
Jean Bart, reinforcements! Reinforcements have finally come!
Look over there! It's the Iris Libre fleet, along with the Tribunal's fighting angel!
The enemy is being routed! We're saved, Jean Bart!
Phew... I'd just made peace with the fact that I was about to get sunk. Talk about good timing...
But, if both the Tribunal and Iris Libre are here, does that mean... that the conflict with Clemenceau was just an elaborate ruse?
Jean Bart could not make sense of the words she was hearing.
Her emotions had been roiling for so long. What did it all mean? Could she afford to have hope again?
Iris Libre... and the Tribunal, together...? What's going on...
And when I heard Richelieu's voice before... Was that...
Sorry I'm late, Jean Bart.
No matter how desperate the situation is, we must not give up on hope.
Otherwise, we will not be able to seize that brief glimmer of light when it finally arrives.
Cardinal Richelieu... Why are you here?
You didn't come just to laugh at me, did you?
No, I'm here to save someone dear to me.
A certain shipgirl who calls me her sister, in fact.
Though, it wouldn't hurt to call me that more often.
For example... During a touching reunion? Such as this one?
Repeat after me, now. "Sister."
Why, you...!
Sorry, I got a bit carried away there.
I'm sure there's a lot you'd like to get off your chest right now, but the enemy is still out there.
I'd love to catch up with you later, but let's get right to business first–
Le Terrible told me about the situation at the World Expo venue. We're going to support the Commander next.
But, I can only speak for Iris Libre. The Vichya Dominion will need to make its own choice.
Jean Bart, will you join me?
...I don't speak for the Vichya Dominion anymore.
We've been excommunicated by Clemenceau. We're just exiles now.
That doesn't change my offer.
Jean Bart stood up, took a deep breath, and flipped the switch on her communicator.
To all those shipgirls who no longer have a place to call home – I am battleship Jean Bart, formerly of the Vichya Dominion, speaking!
I will now join Cardinal Richelieu's fleet, and aid her in fighting for a unified Iris Orthodoxy.
I'm no longer in any position to order any of you around, but...
I hope you'll decide to join us in driving those bastards out of our homeland!
Jean Bart...!
I'd be glad to!
Of course. Banished or not, we'll follow you to the ends of the earth.
Haha, you stubborn old grouch! I'm just glad you and Algérie finally decided to open up!
...Yeah, it's been too damn long.
It's time... to put the past behind us.
Jean Bart discarded the shattered banner of the Vichya Dominion, and got down on one knee in front of Richelieu.
Richelieu then lay her own Iris flag atop Jean Bart's shoulder.
As Cardinal of the Iris Orthodoxy, I solemnly declare...
Jean Bart, your unjustly-deprived status as a Templar Knight and your position within the Iris Orthodoxy's fleet are hereby restored to you.
The same goes for all the other shipgirls here formerly under the command of the Vichya Dominion.
Please fight alongside us, Jean Bart.
By the will of the Holy Iris...
I swear my allegiance to you, Cardinal Richelieu. Sister.
...I've finally come back to you, my sister.
Sorry it took me so long.
Cheers erupted over the ocean.
And, without anyone's notice, Gascogne silently slipped away after bearing witness to it all.

sequence: Some time in the past...
Unknown location within Iron Blood

scripts.say: *sigh*... Would you just answer me, Friedrich?
What do you think of the Reenactments under these circumstances?
We'll never be able to get rid of the Sirens for good unless we all join forces.
Naturally. But your proposal isn't grounded in reality.
As long as the Naval HQ has influence, any forceful attempt to unite the factions will end in failure.
Even a superficial alliance will come to naught, just like the previous Azur Lane.
Squeezing sand in your hand will only cause it to slip through your fingers...
Until nothing remains.
Hmph. Alright, so we can't get along. But that doesn't mean we can just go along with the Sirens' plans.
Doesn't that only fuel their power and make the situation worse?
War is but a continuation of politics with other means.
What is true of Reenactments... is also true of our war against the Sirens.
It's simply not time yet, Marco Polo. Don't rush things.
I'd best be going soon. Return to Sardegna, and play your part of the composition.
Friedrich left. Only Marco Polo remained in the room.
You sound so self-important, Friedrich der Große.
Is it because you're a blueprint ship? Well, so am I!
Don't we exist to crush Sirens with overwhelming force?
*sigh*... Wasting energy on politics and inter-faction conflicts is so inefficient. Bismarck's confidant, my ass.
But it's true that we're getting nowhere fast right now. There has to be a way to break through this, like a way to easily beat the Sirens...
I know... I'll just have to find someone stronger than them.
Just you watch, Friedrich. Someday, I'm going to clean up this mess myself.
Then, the whole world will know my name and marvel at my greatness!
With the fall of Marco Polo's throne, everything had changed in an instant.
The sky went dark at once, as if a purple curtain had been drawn over it. Beneath the artificial night sky, fear and uncertainty continued to grow despite the "victory."
Clearly, things had not gone back to normal even with Marco Polo's defeat.
Danger was still growing within the darkness.
BEEP—
Good day– Or rather, I suppose I should say "good evening" now.
Did everyone enjoy Marco Polo's curtain call just now?
Commander, umm, we seem to have a call from Clemenceau.
That's right. It's me, Clemenceau from the Vichya's Tribunal.
I would've loved to meet all of you and enjoy our time together at the closing ceremony...
But alas, who could've anticipated all of this to happen?
How shameless... Acting like you weren't a part of this.
You were also the one who sicced those mass-produced ships and Gazers on us, weren't you?
Right before they landed, you transferred all of your own Vichya ships away!
You're not going to giggle and say all of this was just an act, are you?
She's right! You better give us a believable explanation for everything that happened!
Oh my, is that the name you came up with for my divine machines?
That's cute. Heehee.
Clemenceau, don't change the subject.
As the host of this World Expo, I demand an explanation for this catastrophe.
Heehee. It WAS all an act~ ...You'd be surprised how close you are to the truth.
The situation necessitated the emergency transfer.
Had I not done so, Marco Polo would've attempted to coerce them into betraying you, and I would've not been able to release the Horseman of Conquest.
Likewise with the Tribunal's mass-produced ships. They were all a façade to convince her that I was on her side.
You understand, don't you, Commander? The Skybound Wall could easily withstand the divine machines' attacks.
My "transgressions" did not truly place you in harm's way, so why not put on a show to earn Marco Polo's trust?
In other words... You knew her plan from the start, and you've been pretending to work with her all this time.
All to stop her in the end...?
Exactly. I feigned cooperation until her plan reached its very climax.
Didn't you think the shot that perfectly picturesque?
I must admit, it was quite magnificent... But what was that golden-armored machine?
Is it related to the divine machines you were talking about?
Somewhat. That is a weapon called the Mechanicus Harbinger, developed in secret by the Tribunal.
You may be able to trace its roots back to Marco Polo, but rest assured that it is under my control.
...I suppose we should content ourselves with the knowledge that they won't attack us anymore.
But Clemenceau, do not assume that everyone will be satisfied with that alone.
The Marco Polo I know would never come up with such a dangerous scheme.
If you cooperated with her, having full knowledge of the danger of her schemes, then that makes you a co-conspirator... No, worse. You enabled her.
That's hardly fair, Vittorio Veneto.
Even knowing her plans, do you think I had the capacity to stand up to the power she wielded?
If there was even the slightest leak, her first order of business would be eliminating the Tribunal, given our specialty in information manipulation.
Regardless, we still haven't cleaned up the mess she made.
I'll have my subordinates recover her. For now, shall we meet face-to-face?
...Though I'll have you know that I'm already on my way to the Vichya pavilion.

options.content: "What about the fleet in Toulon? Are they safe?"

scripts.say: "We just learned that Jean Bart's fleet has been struggling to fight off the enemy assault for some time now."
"A Royal Navy fleet is on their way to reinforce them, but the enemies on the way have slowed them down. We don't know how well that secret passage will continue to function, either."
"If the Tribunal has mobile forces to put to work, then I expect you to stop the enemy reinforcements heading to Toulon."
Yes, of course, Commander.
Toulon is in Iris territory, and Jean Bart is a sister ship of mine. I'll see it done right away.
As for the secret passage, I'm sure they've used it by now.
As for the Royal Navy's fleet, why don't we... Actually, let's discuss this in person later.
The road here is a bit difficult to traverse, so I'll get back to you later–
BEEP—
Aaand she hung up. She really does march to the beat of her own drum...
In a way, she's like Prinz Eugen. Or... worse, even.
BEEP—
Another call? This time, it's... Cardinal Richelieu?
Suspicious timing. Is it related to that hidden passage the Commander mentioned?
This is Richelieu speaking.
Commander, representatives of the World Expo. I'm happy to see you all safe.
Our fleet has already arrived at Toulon and confirmed the safety of Jean Bart's fleet.
Once we've cleaned up enemies around the port, performed maintenance, and resupplied, we plan to come and join you.
(It seems like they made it to Toulon through their hidden passage without issue.)

options.content: "Say, what's all this about a hidden passage?"

scripts.say: We initially went to Saint Helena to secure the Crown of the Holy See and rescue Marseillaise.
Upon inspecting the documents we found at the secret stronghold there, we found a large amount of material concerning Siren technology.
One of the topics of interest was a network of "highways" that Compiler used to rapidly move across the ocean.
We then found a set of equipment called the "microlayer transference system," devices that would allow us to use Compiler's network in the form of sea fog.
While it is just normal fog, the activation of the device turns the microlayer particles comprising it into a gateway of sorts that allows us to move en-masse to distant locations.
Apparently, this network spans all over the world, which Compiler used to connect countless underwater areas and Mirror Seas.
Presumably, this is how Sirens used Mirror Seas as the staging grounds for their attacks, able to move their forces over long distances.
It also explains how they've always seemed to appear out of thin air, and were able to attack areas that should've been inaccessible to them.
In any case, this technology definitely was not meant for our use, but can still function without Compiler's authorization.
For whatever reason, following Compiler's defeat, we have been able to gain access into the network.
After studying the Tribunal's analytical data on Saint Helena, we were able to tap into the network, though only to a limited extent due to the limitations of our equipment.
We understand the inherent risks in using Siren technology and planned to report our findings first, but the situation changed when we learned that fierce fighting had broken out in Toulon.
The fact that we were able to lead such a large fleet through safely is surely due to the Holy Iris's blessings.
(It sounds to me like Clemenceau ordered the Tribunal to tell Richelieu the location of the Crown of the Holy See.)
(The crown might have ended up in Marco Polo's hands, but this alone is probably proof enough that Clemenceau isn't our enemy.)
(Tell her about Clemenceau.)
"I think you might not have a full grasp of the situation either, but we want to know as much as possible before we come face-to-face with Clemenceau."
Really? Clemenceau did that...?
Very well. I will tell you what I know.
Before setting sail, Clemenceau told me a part of her plan.
Her plan was to both stop Marco Polo and use this dangerous situation to bring Iris Libre and the Vichya Dominion back together.
...And by making herself the villain, she would protect Jean Bart.
Comrades, if I may offer my opinion–
Clemenceau's actions may still be suspicious, but I believe that we should have faith in our Commander and in Richelieu.
With the situation in the Mediterranean Sea—no, the entire world—as it is, the Tribunal's power and knowledge will be essential.
While they might have been split up as a product of the Reenactments, let us not forget that they once sailed under the single banner of the Iris Orthodoxy.
Let's leave our doubt and our worries of a betrayal that may have never happened aside. We must focus on the danger before us.
"Thanks for your input, Avrora."
A fair question. Between Jean Bart's repairs and resupplying...
...Oh. It seems enemy reinforcements have arrived.
Apologies, Commander, but it seems we'll need some more time.
Considering Clemenceau's behavior so far, I understand your reluctance to trust her.
But still... I ask that you look after her all the same, Commander.
A mixed fleet consisting of Sakuran and Iris forces just so happened to be nearby when Marco Polo's throne was shot out of the sky.
Said fleet was originally sent there to clear the surrounding area of enemies. They began their search for the wreckage once they'd confirmed the Horseman had ceased operation.
It didn't matter whether Marco Polo had lost her mind or just been manipulated – she had to be rescued.
I think the throne is somewhere around here! Keep your eyes peeled, everyone!
(While the whole sky darkened after that explosion, the area ahead feels even darker than its surroundings.)
(It's as though something is blocking the light... Or absorbing it, like a black hole?)
This is a good time to turn on my searchlights!
Now it'll be easy to–
Shimakaze's searchlights lit up the sea around her – and also revealed a misty hole in space.
Whoa, it's pitch black! Is it... swallowing up the light?
That's just like a black hole, isn't it?
Though the light could not pierce the darkness, it allowed everyone to clearly see its outline.
It's like an egg, jutting out of the water... Does that mean there's more of it underwater?
I think I remember reading about a sacrament that roughly matched this thing's description.
We've already established that the unknown substance is what's creating all the enemies.
So, it's possible that this other unknown substance produces a different breed of enemy.
The clouds swallow our aircraft and spit out twisted versions of them, while the cocoons produce enemies reminiscent of mass-produced ships.
The aircraft were liquid, and the mass-produced ships were solid. Therefore, perhaps this hole creates gaseous enemies?
It would explain why your searchlights are ineffective if the gas is really, really, REALLY dense.
Assuming this thing does spawn more enemies, we should destroy it now before it becomes fully operational.
What do you think, Shinano? Should we attack?
This one is inclined to do so... Lady Jeanne, what do you think?
On the one hand, we should study what we're dealing with. On the other, I agree with Noshiro.
I think that we should back off and bombard it with our aircraft.
That way, we can retreat quickly if something happens, and if Marco Polo for some reason is inside it, she'll suffer less damage than from direct cannon fire.
So be it... Hakuryuu, prepare your bombers...
On it. Been waiting too long as it is to use them.
KABOOOM!
Hakuryuu's aircraft dropped their bombs on the foggy cocoon, engulfing it in explosions.
The very next moment, it retaliated with a shockwave.
It took everyone. Hakuryuu, Noshiro, Shinano, Jeanne... the black mist engulfed every shipgirl who stood there.

sequence: Flashback
Somewhere in the Sardegna Empire...

scripts.say: Inside a strikingly decorated office room, Marco Polo sat at her desk with a defeated expression.
Another failure...
And that one, and that, and this one too... They've all failed...
How is it possible that I, the one born to spread Sardegna's glory, fail time after time after time again?
I don't get it... Why won't anyone understand me?
I want to restore the Empire's glory, I want to spread it all across the world, but nobody empathizes with my cause no matter the approach I take!
Not the carefree Veneto sisters, not those who are perfectly happy languishing away in mediocrity...
I'm so tired... Is there nothing I can do?
She fell limp onto her desk, and she took hold of an ornament thoughtlessly left lying around.
This cross must be ancient. Has it always been lying on my desk?
She fixated her gaze on the small cross, as if at this moment, there was no object in all the world more worthy of her attention.
Is this... a sign from God?
He has the power to destroy the Sirens...
Yes... That's it! The answer's been there all along!
The enemy of the Sirens... The one whose power is greater than theirs!
Ahahahahahaha!
When Shinano's fleet attacked the black hole made by the gaseous substance, they were suddenly pulled deeper into the darkness.
*cough* *cough*... Shinano! Are you okay?!
Yes... Worry about the others instead—
Shinano, we're in a real mess!
Some weird enemies are crawlin' out of that dark goop!
...Fragments of nightmares, echoes of ruination...
They only show themselves in this one's dreams of death... Why are they here?
This is an ill omen... Jeanne, take everyone and evacuate...
It will be done. Suffren, Maillé Brézé! Turn about-face and secure an escape route—
No, Jeanne... We mustn't send anyone ahead on their own.
Going the way we came, too, is unnecessary... If this one's hypothesis is correct, this boundary is like a dream...
If we choose a specific direction and muster all of our strength, we may escape from this nightmarish domain...
Nightmares may be formless, but... If we have been drawn into one from the real world, then there must exist a border between them...
The enemy knows this, and they will try to surround us... Still, if we can break through, we may return to our home world...
If you're so familiar with this, Shinano, I'd like you to choose the direction for our charge.
"Nightmares are formless, but they have borders." Oversimplified, but surprisingly close to the truth.
However, I have a better plan.
I know the safest route. Come with me.
Who are you...?
I'm... a friend of the Commander.
I'll explain later. Just trust me for now.
If we waste any more time, we'll miss our chance to escape.

sequence: Shortly afterwards
World Expo Venue - Vichya Pavilion
Temporary Command Room

scripts.say: ...And that's how I saved your friends. Couldn't have come at a better time too.
The abominations they saw are able to contaminate a shipgirl's hull upon contact.
Their courage is commendable, but if they aren't careful, it'll be their downfall.
But don't worry. The contact was limited, so there shouldn't be any issues after we finish decontamination.
Having that said, you should keep your distance for the time being if you value your safety.
Now where were we? Yes, it's great to see you again, Commander.
I hear you've been in the Superimposition—er... Reality Lens? Of late.
I can't believe things turned out this way.
...Though personally, I'm a little glad.
Upon learning that we'd lost contact with Shinano's fleet, I had put together a team to go rescue them. Just then, Memphis META had contacted us.
(Come to think of it, the other Helena helped us alongside this Memphis at the Union's Sea of Stars. I don't think I've had the chance to thank her...)
Are you the one who helped us at the Sea of Stars?
The Commander told me all about what happened in the Reality Lens.
Thank you, umm... Memphis?
...It's my pleasure.
Your Commander is my Commander, too, so it's only natural that I try to help.
*sigh*... At this rate, calling us both Memphis is going to get really confusing.
What should I call you?
Whatever you want to.
Memphis is fine, META is fine, "that girl who likes the Commander a little TOO much" is also fine.
Heh. Maybe that last one is true for both of us, though?
Th-that's not...!
My, my. I'll admit I was worried when you asked me to rescue your friend...
But you all are so carefree that I have to assume the problem is solved~ That's lovely.
Clemenceau inserted herself in the midst of the increasingly awkward conversation without anyone's prior notice.
Oh, this is embarrassing...
It's my fault. Now isn't the time for jokes.
Allow me to continue. Commander, the situation is extremely bad.
A hundred times worse than what you experienced in the Reality Lens.
Our Helena is doing her best to slow down the superimposition of worlds, but at this rate, it won't be enough.
You can't imagine how hard I had to work just to get to this branch.
Wait... You know about superimposition?
Well, well. Things are getting wilder than I'd imagined. I'm surprised you know about these things.
That should be my line. Someone from this branch knows about the superimposition of worlds?
...Are you involved with the person behind this?
I am, though only partially.
Marco Polo brought this plan to me, and I pretended to play along.
However, I am in the dark when it comes to what her "God" is.
What I do know is the principle by which she intends to have "God" descend and establish her false Paradise.
Naturally, I know how to stop it as well.
With that, Clemenceau produces a map.
The location where the abnormalities began, the Mediterranean Sea, is circled with a black pen.
A number of cities, ports, and islands are also circled, all of them interconnected with lines.
The large circle is her Paradise, where God will descend. That's the area currently filled with Divine Vestige.
I believe the small circles here are conceptual anchors meant to create and maintain the domain.
Conceptual anchors...?
Yes, they would be one of Vichya's Sacraments. They strengthen the manifestation of concepts, though I'm not sure that means anything to you.
For the moment, just consider them special devices that maintain the domain.
If we destroyed them... No, there are too many, and they're all too far apart.
They span every corner of the Mediterranean, and some beyond that. There's no way we could reach all those places in such a short time!
Indeed. Consider that proof of how long Marco Polo has been working on her scheme.
However, the grander the plan, the more openings there are for me to play a little prank~
Now, take a look at the lines connecting conceptual anchors.
Clemenceau traces the lines on the map with a finger.
Commander, Richelieu has told you about how she moved her fleet to Toulon, yes?
With Compiler's defeat, we've gained access to her microlayer transference network.
So, do you now understand what these lines on the map indicate?
While working with Marco Polo, I fudged the locations of the conceptual anchors just enough to bring them closer to the network's nodes.
You'll find that they're rather accessible now, given the new tools we have.
As for the conceptual anchors themselves... There's no need to destroy them. We'll merely subsume them into a different conceptual framework.
This ritual is meant to reflect Marco Polo's concept of God, but we will counteract that with the concept of true divinity.
By reinforcing the concept of holy miracles present in ancient religious tradition, we can reverse what she's done and overwrite her domain.
It's quite simple to do, too. By activating the smaller Skybound Walls within each anchor, the domain of Marco Polo's kingdom will instead become a part of the Spear of Destiny.
The Spear of Destiny is the Orthodoxy's holiest relic. It represents the divine promise of victory, and holds the power to conquer all evil.
To summarize it cleanly...
Marco Polo has been trying to bring a being called God from another world to ours.
To do this, she uses a holy relic called a conceptual weapon to reflect the concept of another world's God within a certain area.
"So by modifying the ritual's system and changing the concept to a source of holiness, we can expel both her God and the related phenomena..."
You catch on fast, Commander. Good.
This very pavilion happens to have a conceptual anchor. Rather, the pavilion itself was built as part of her plan.
We should be able to use the network to quickly travel from here to other conceptual anchor sites.
Of course, each anchor will be protected by Gazers and more, but I'm certain that your leadership can overcome them.
Commander, before you make your decision – Lady Clemenceau, I would like an explanation.
The map shows that the Strait of Gibraltar, Malta, and this pavilion have anchors...
When did you and Marco Polo manage to set all of them up?
In Gibraltar's case, it's in the ocean rather than at the port. We set that one up a rather long time ago.
The conceptual anchor at Malta is even older. I'd almost wager that it's been there since before we were born.
So Le Terrible didn't go there alone just to contact the Commander; she was checking on the conceptual anchor.
I can't say I'm surprised, Lady Clemenceau of the Tribunal. You think of everything.
If not for the Commander, I'm sure she would also be able to manipulate us to no end.
Oh, don't be so modest. Intelligence just happens to be the Tribunal's specialty.
So? Do you have any other questions?
I think the most important thing is how you glossed over "superimposition" before.
What exactly does that mean?
Oh, I'm sorry~ The Commander accepted it so readily that I thought I didn't need to explain~
The most apt way to describe this is, everything we see before us right now is simultaneously real and not real.
Everything in Marco Polo's Paradise is a carbon copy of reality, much like a computer simulation of the real world.
However, through her ritual, she was able to layer that simulacrum on top of the real world, which is also exactly what that mycelium-like substance is trying to do.
You could say it's like making art by putting a layer mask on top of the specific part of a canvas you'd like to change.
You're not painting on the canvas itself. Likewise, it doesn't affect the real world on its own.
But when her God descends, the two superimposed worlds will become one reality, causing the art on the mask to overwrite what's on the canvas.
When that happens, will the original reality be trimmed away like a branch?
Or will the two worlds mix, creating a new one?
And what is the identity of Marco Polo's God?
Frankly, the thought terrifies me, so I don't want to think about it. Heehee.
The center of the abnormality is definitely the location where Marco Polo's throne fell.
Based on the circumstantial evidence I've seen so far... it seems likely that the enemy we've been fighting to this point is there.
Calling that into this world is nothing short of insane.
If you worked with Marco Polo all this time, knowing full well the extent of her plans...
Then there is no way I can trust you.
I don't mind.
I lead a shady organization called the Tribunal, I've worked with the cause of all this mess, and I've even displayed active hostility by sending mass-produced ships to attack you.
However, Memphis META, I would think that none of this would matter to you.
Should you not understand the value of my plan?
If you really wanted to help the Commander, then you'd push for a decision instead of arguing.
Regardless, I have some final adjustments to make to the network, so I'll let you handle persuading everyone.
Understood, "that girl who likes the Commander a little TOO much"?
Clemenceau is right about the reality anchors. Her plan is likely the best option we've got.
It's more practical and has higher odds of success than what I had in mind.
As much as I hate to admit it, we should move forward with her plan.
In the meantime, I'll keep a close eye on her until all of this has been resolved.
I discussed Clemenceau's plan with Memphis META and members of all factions, and we all came to a consensus.
From there, we swiftly moved on to discussing tactics and contacting all parties across the Mediterranean.
...At last, every shipgirl we could get in touch with had been mobilized.
On my command, shipgirls across Gibraltar, Malta, Toulon, Taranto, Rome, and Venice all activated the Skybound Wall at their respective locations.
The remaining reality anchor in northern Sardegna would be dealt with after Littorio finished up in Venice.
There was an additional anchor in Iris Orthodoxy territory, which Richelieu and her fleet were tasked with securing.
While many of their positions had been caught up in Reenactments, the Naval HQ was effectively on lockdown due to the Divine Vestige, so they would reclaim these at the same time.
Then, there were the reality anchors in Africa...
The map Clemenceau showed us used old place names such as Algeria and Carthage. According to her, it was tied to the anchors' concept.
Since we had confirmed travel was possible to those locations via the network, it wouldn't impede our operation.
For the time being, we simply stuck with the names that were on the map.
These anchors would be dealt with by two forces – the Royal Navy, and Iron Blood.
The Royals would handle the Algeria anchor, as they were closest to it.
As for the Carthage anchor, Eugen would lead a fleet to rendezvous with the Royal Navy in Malta, then travel through the network and secure it.
Finally, there were the anchors east of the Mediterranean. Unfortunately, we didn't have the forces necessary to capture them right away.
I considered rerouting the forces near that black hole, but it would be best to keep them close by in the event of an emergency.
We don't have much time left.
The Divine Vestige is spreading faster than I expected. It's reached places even beyond the Mediterranean.
I'm sorry that I can't help you with the anchors. I have my hands full keeping Helena and her team posted.
It seems our only option is to divert some of the forces defending the pavilion.
But we can't divert too many, or else we can't defend ourselves against the enemy if they converge on us.
We can't just move all our mission-critical communications equipment, and we need a sizable force to keep the Commander safe...
Andrea's fleet remains unreachable due to the sandstorm in the region...
Commander, if at all possible, can't we start with the anchor in Alexandria?
I want to know if our fleet there is safe. After we've extracted them, we could send them to capture some of the anchors in the east.
"You make a great point, actually. I should bump up their rescue on our list of priorities."
BEEP—
Right then, a call rang on the private channel of my communicator.
(It's... Sovetsky Soyuz?!)
I'm so glad to hear your voice, Comrade Commander. I hope you're safe and sound.
Truth be told, I'm in the Black Sea right now on official business, and I've gotten swept up in the same situation as you.
I've heard about what is happening through my comrades, and the Northern Parliament gladly offers you its aid.
If you don't mind, could you tell me what your plan is?
I explained the situation and my plan to her over the communicator.
I see. We can take care of the reality anchors in Constantinople and the Aegean Sea.
Our fleet shall take the Bosphorus strait to the Aegean Sea. There, we will complete all the outlined mission objectives.
Soyuz, may I interject?
I'd like to know about our dear blueprint ship. Has she mastered her rigging yet?
She has become proficient, at least. In fact, she's the reason I came to the Black Sea.
I've already drafted her for this operation to bolster our forces. I hope you don't mind.
Not at all. This is a perfect opportunity to test her abilities.
Mhm. Let's just say there were some things with her rigging we had to work out.
I must say, Soyuz, this was brilliant timing. You're the last person I expected to hear from.
Call it providence, if you will... In reality, it's Champagne's own hard work.
Her rigging is ready, and she has a solid grasp on her new equipment. She is more than suited for battle.
You'll reunite with her later, but for now, she'll be accompanying us for a brief while.
Now, it's for me to go. Let us meet later at the World Expo, Comrade Commander.
(What is a Northern Parliament fleet doing in the Black Sea? Last I heard, they were engaged in a major offensive against the Sirens in the Arctic Sea...)
(Let's see if Clemenceau has any answers.)
It's nothing complicated. She's part of a collaboration between Vichya and the Northern Parliament. Don't you encourage us to work together all the time?
Or is it her timing you're asking about? You think that it's too convenient, hmm?
Are you wondering why a blueprint ship is about to show up now, and if I had any role to play in that? Or, do you have questions about why she hasn't shown up until now?
Certainly valid questions, but aren't you putting the cart before the horse? We have a God to stop, after all~
(...Actually, no. There's no reason Champagne would know anything about the Northern Parliament's major offensive.)
(If Clemenceau's just going to dance around the subject, I might as well not even ask.)
Veneto! I've returned!
Littorio! Thank goodness! Are you hurt anywhere?!
No. Even if I was, we'll have time for sisterly love later.
It'll take a crisis of greater magnitude than this to break my spirit.
Now, on to my report – the Skybound Wall in Venice has been activated. The other one will follow shortly.
Then, there's our fleet in Alexandria which you're worried about. Sadly, I don't know anything about their situation.
What I do know is that we have a soldier at the Suez Canal which we can mobilize.
Carabiniere. I sent her there on a... let's say, diplomatic mission.
Commander, may I borrow your communicator?
(I wonder why she hesitated for a moment when talking about her...)
(That's not important at the moment, though. What we need is more manpower, and soon. I'll have Littorio call Carabiniere home.)
(Although, while we need all the help we can get, we'll need a lot more than just her.)
(Think, me, think. Isn't there anyone who could come to our aid at a moment's notice?)
Then it's time to bid farewell. With the Arbiters gone, we have no reason to stick together.
In order to get out of this Singularity, head to the exit I told you about earlier, and you should be fine.
I do hope we can meet again someday. Under what circumstances, I don't know. Maybe we'll share a heartfelt reunion, or we'll exchange blows as enemies.
"Wait. What about the thing you said before our duel earlier?"
Ah, I did say I'd tell you something you're going to like, didn't I? Don't worry, I remember our deal.
Since you and your fleet managed to stay standing by the end of it all, I'll let you in on something good.
...You know what, I'll just give it to you directly...
Hiryuu reached behind her back and staggered over to me.
Don't worry, I'll be in touch.
No, really. I already know your contact code and where your port is.
(That's right! Back during Operation Siren, Hiryuu from the Ashes gave me her contact code.)
(I've always felt hesitant to use it – until now. Let's see if she answers.)

sequence: East Mediterranean Sea - Suez Canal
Meanwhile, with Carabiniere...

scripts.say: Carabiniere, are you alright?! Where are you?
Right here! I'm fine! I've just plunged into the affected region with the Dragon Empery fleet!
Are you doing okay, Lady Littorio?! Something awful has happened... not just at the World Expo, but across the whole Mediterranean!
I'm just fine. Let's be brief here.
First: what do you mean when you say you've just plunged into the affected region?
Right, so, I was in the middle of a tea party with the Dragon Empery representatives by the canal.
That was when Chen Hai noticed that something was wrong. She asked me to contact the Sardegnian mainland...
I couldn't get through, though, so I asked the Dragon Empery reps to return to the venue with me!
And now, umm... We've just entered a sea region covered in a weird substance.
I see... No wonder you couldn't get through to them. You were outside of the anomaly.
The Dragon Empery shipgirls are with you, right? Carabiniere, connect me to Chen Hai.
Commander, we have the Dragon Empery fleet.
I've been informed of the situation. You've clearly been hard at work...
Our forces here are enough. Leave the anchor near the canal to us.
One more thing: I hear the Skybound Wall in Alexandria was activated.
We have no idea what's going on there. The sandstorm still hasn't stopped...
You don't know, either? Then we'll just have to leave it aside and hope for the best for now.
We'll do what we can to help investigate. If we learn anything, I'll call you right away.
I pray for your good fortune. Goodbye.

sequence: Aegean Sea
Northern Parliament Fleet

scripts.say: BOOOOM!
Target annihilated.
Requesting further orders.
Soyuz, can we keep going forward?
Slow down, now. Don't stray from the rest of the fleet.
Okay!
Have you finished collecting data?
Yes, Comrade. It's done.
I have a feeling this data could be instrumental in advancing Northern Parliament technology.
She obliterates the enemy, AND she gives us ample data. I'd call that two birds with one stone.
...To be frank, though, I wish we could collect data under more normal circumstances.
Preparing conceptual anchors over such a large area... Marco Polo was as thorough as can be.
Yet our Intelligence Bureau never caught wind of her preparations.
Europa has gotten too lax. We need to tighten up in the future.
It isn't all their fault, Kronshtadt.
The members of the Tribunal are masters of information manipulation... especially her.
You, me, the Royal Navy, Iron Blood. She tricked all of us.
No doubt Her Majesty and Bismarck are panicking, too. I'd love to see their faces right now.
By "her," do you mean Marco Polo?
No. Tribunal representative Clemenceau.
Clemenceau of the Vichya Dominion... I've never dealt with her face-to-face, but I hear all of the Tribunal's agents are forces to be reckoned with.
If you acknowledge her to that extent, then I'm sure she's quite capable.
(The Vichya Dominion, hm...?)
(What will happen to them when this is resolved and we have peace again?)
(...Assuming it can be resolved, that is.)
A black sun, quietly burning in the dusky sky.
I was just in the Colosseum, but before I knew it, the world around me had changed.
"Where am I...?"
Is this a dream... or a projection of my consciousness?
It almost reminds me... of the Reality Lens...
Judging by the black sun, this at least didn't seem to be the real world I knew.
This is all too realistic for a dream, but so was the Colosseum from before.
Though, if nothing else, it at least doesn't look threatening.
I don't feel any heat from the black sun. It's simply just... there.
I stare deeply into the black sun's depths.
It takes a while for my eyes to adjust and focus, but eventually... something starts to come into view.

options.content: Is it... some kind of machine?

scripts.say: I can't see clearly, but is it possible that there's some sort of massive machine inside the black sun?
What I see is only a small part of it, like the tip of an iceberg, concealing something so massive that it doesn't seem to be able to fit within this world.
The realization sends goosebumps down my body, a sickening electric sensation creeping through my body.
Pressure. Darkness.
As if I'm at the bottom of an ocean... in a bygone era I don't belong to...

options.content: It feels... so hard to breathe...

scripts.say: This place is completely different from the silent, almost serene roiling of the black sun in the sky...
At this rate... I'm going to suffocate...
Just as I feel my consciousness about to slip away from me...
Am I hearing... windchimes?

sequence: Ashes Fleet

scripts.say: The Singularity in the NA Ocean, formerly the site of a bloody battle, was quiet now.
Only the eternally-burning flames that rose above the wreckage told the story of its violent past.
We've been monitoring this door for some time.
You don't think Enterprise has forgotten us, do you?
Don't grumble, Hiryuu. It's strategically vital that we protect this Singularity as long as it lets us leap to other branches.
Besides, it's Enterprise you're talking about. She wouldn't cast aside her fellow Ashes.
Maybe not normally, Ark Royal, but that doesn't mean you can be certain.
Don't be fooled by the way Enterprise acts.
She may look cool and collected all the time... but her emotions aren't as stable as you might think.
You mean... there's a problem with her hull?
That's not what I meant. Even if we all have our issues, she's not necessarily suffering from the same thing.
What I'm talking about... is a mental thing.
She's been pushing herself this whole time, fighting nonstop. She's never been able to put down her weapons or have a moment of relaxation.
Truth be told, I'm worried about her.
That so...? I guess I haven't fought with her as long as you have.
Come to think of it, you've been working with her since before your METAmorphosis, haven't you?
Everything you said about her... Isn't that also true for you?
Please. Do I look okay to you?
Having that said... I suppose I might be a bit better at decompressing.
Or, maybe I just have a more philosophical view of things.
Sometimes... the more we try to find redemption for our past lives, the deeper a hole we dig.
It's like drinking poison to quench your thirst.
I'm just... a lot better at giving up than her.
...That said, if I sat still and did nothing forever...
My mental state would surely break down sooner or later, and I'd turn into one of those kaiju you see in Sakuran movies.
Rooooar! Gaaaawr!
Okay, calm down...
BEEP—
...Hm? A call?
The caller is...
...Huh.
Ark Royal, things are about to get interesting.

sequence: Royal Navy Rally Point Temporary Malta Base
Before the conceptual anchor operation

scripts.say: Lalala~♪ La la la laaa~♫
Whoooa~ It's the Royal Navy Malta base~
C'mon, what's the big deal? We don't have a Reenactment hanging over our heads or anything. Not gonna let a girl in just because she's from Iron Blood?
Oh, if it isn't Nelson. Aren't you going to welcome me?
You're something else...
*sigh*...
Welcome to the Royal Navy's Malta base. Hooray. Happy?
Ahahaha~♪ That's exactly what I wanted to hear!
Z2 would tell me to restrain myself if she were here, but too bad—she's with the Commander.
That means I can tease you as much as I want. Heheheh!
So this is Prinz Eugen...
Why are you looking at me? I swear, I've totally never met this woman in my life...
Don't get carried away, Prinz Eugen. It's thanks to the Commander that we can still fight.
I welcome you not as Iron Blood shipgirls, but as reinforcements the Commander kindly sent.
Yeah, that feels better...
Now, now. Illustrious did invite them to convene here at Malta whenever they liked.
You're not just reinforcements. You're all innocents caught up in the World Expo catastrophe.
Welcome to our Malta stronghold, Iron Blood!

sequence: Somewhere in the Mediterranean Sea...
Royal Navy Fleet

scripts.say: Lady Warspite, we've been informed that the Iron Blood fleet has arrived at our Malta stronghold.
Imagine that. Iron Blood setting foot on Malta not as enemies, but as temporary allies.
Knowing Prinz Eugen, she must already be messing with the girls stationed there.
This must be a real headache for Rodney and Nelson, given their upcoming roles in the operation.
Where are they heading, again? "Carthage," was it?
Yes. I believe it's an ancient city off the North African coast.
I wonder why Marco Polo put a conceptual anchor there, so far away from home.
Likely as part of her plan. Or, possibly, the God guiding her actions made the decision.
BEEP—
Hey, Warspite. How are things coming along over there? Want us to help?
*sigh*... Thanks for keeping in touch, but no.
Our fleet is currently en route to Djemila, as per the Commander's orders.
You sure? Because I feel there's a better way to make use of your force.
Carthage and Djemila aren't that far apart, and the enemies between them are no big deal.
Our fleet and your Malta fleet are enough to deal with them.
So, what I'm thinking is – we'll take care of Djemila, and you can go give Richelieu backup instead.
Think about it. The Tribunal made the conceptual anchors, and they've surely built better defenses to protect them on their own turf.
Hold on. This isn't about the Royal Navy or Iron Blood. This is the Commander's operation.
I know you like to skirt around rules, but are you really going to flat-out ignore orders from the Commander?
We, not you, were given the task of dealing with this conceptual anchor, and we intended to complete it.
Furthermore, I just got word that Richelieu's fleet is making good, steady progress.
We don't need to rush to her aid. Ultimately, this conflict is something they have to resolve internally.
Fair enough. Just thought I'd mention it.
It's also worth pointing out the Commander never specified a next task after we capture Carthage.
In other words, we'll become a reserve force. If you don't want us stealing work from you, you better be quick♪
...The audacity of that–
Knights of the Royal Navy! Iron Blood has issued us a challenge.
And we – we shall answer. All ships, raise your speed! For the glory of the Royal family!
With the battle in Toulon over, Iris Libre and the Vichya Dominion regrouped. They then used the network to quickly travel to an inland river in Iris territory.
Since some of the anchors had been placed on land, the shipgirls would have to leave the comfort of the sea. They were in for an uphill battle.
It seems this river is as close as we'll get, even with advanced Siren technology.
I still have my reservations about using these devices, even if we have no other option.
Look on the bright side – it also means this is as close as the Sirens can go.
Would be impossible to protect our cities if they could teleport anywhere.
Béarn, what is there around us?
For one, no sign of the enemy. There is one thing, though...
I've had this suspicion that the Divine Vestige may appear in the water as well, ever since the Sakura-Iris mixed fleet ran into that "black hole."
However, that appears not to be the case. It propagates on land and in the air, but not through water.
Yes, now that you mention it, I don't remember seeing much water covered in that substance.
Even here, where it has reached the riverbanks, it hasn't seeped into the river itself yet.
While, we may never know why that is, I'm glad we have a means to travel directly from sea to river.
(Now to get to the Holy See's palace in Avignon, where we'll find that conceptual anchor.)
Lady Richelieu! Lady Richelieu! There's a strange space blocking our route.
Strange place? Huh... You mean the pitch-black area? Yes, I can see it as well.
Pretty damn big... Doubt we can just walk around it. What do we do?
We have no time to waste. Let me try something...
(The conceptual anchor isn't far. Maybe this trick will work here.)
"Let there be light."
Richelieu uttered a verse, and the holy banner in her hand began releasing a brilliant light.
Did you just make your flag glow?
How'd you manage to do that?
The anchors are sacraments that reinforce concepts. With a strong enough conviction, we can make some little miracles of our own.
Everyone, follow me. The light will cut through the darkness.
The girls gathered inside the space lit by holy light, continuing to wade through the darkness bubbling up from the river.
Not long afterwards, a shadowy figure came into view.
At last! At long last!
The final piece to complete my masterwork!
The Crown of the Holy See is finally in my hands!
This is what will put an end to all conflict!
The Kingdom of God will descend upon the land!
Eternal glory and virtue will envelop the world from pole to pole!
Ohohohohoho! The Sirens are as good as a threat of the past!
Yes! Those damned Sirens will bother me no more!
Because God shall come down to us!
I can't believe my ears... Marco Polo truly DID steal the Crown!
Our holy Crown, our most sacred artifact... She must be punished for her blasphemy!
Put your pitchfork down, Marseillaise. Somethin' was clearly not right with her.
Either she lost her mind, or someone was manipulating her.
Clemenceau did remark that she thought Marco Polo had lost it at some point, but by then it was too late.
It's best to assume her god influenced her, warped her very thoughts.
There's no point in listening to this deceitful phantom, at any rate. I will dispel it with the Holy Iris's light.
No, wait! If it works anything like the black hole Jeanne's fleet encountered, we'll be in deep shit if we attack it!
And, what if the phantom actually IS Marco Polo?
Don't worry, Jean Bart. I'm not about to make any reckless decisions.
However, it's dangerous to simply leave it be. We cannot turn a blind eye to the contamination Memphis META spoke about. Furthermore–
Damn, bastard's deployed its rigging. Fighting it is, then!
KABOOOM!
After a short but fierce battle, Marco Polo's phantom sank to its knees in the water.
It's always you...
You pay lip service to uniting our faiths, yet you always stand on opposite sides...
Damned heretics...
■■■... is the true Orthodoxy...
You say the Orthodoxy's legitimacy comes from faith... But does faith put food on the table? What is faith without the support of the people?
Ashes to ashes, dust to dust.
O phantom of a false god and zeal made incarnate – return to naught.
With these words, Marco Polo's phantom disintegrated, along with the region of darkness.
Now, come. Let us go to the palace where the conceptual anchor is kept.
After activating the Skybound Wall at Avignon's conceptual anchor, Richelieu's team discussed their next move.
Our mission in Avignon is done. However...
It took too much time. At this rate, we won't be able to tune the remaining anchors.
Cardinal Richelieu, shall I make the call for all of our warriors to come forward?
There are also Vichyan forces that have not been convinced to fight with us so far. If we are able to win them over...
Indeed... I had the same thought just now.
But unfortunately, my title as Cardinal does not necessarily have much sway back home.
I've spent quite a long time away from home, and not everyone will eagerly flock to join in our cause.
Despite the risks involved, I believe our best course of action is to split up. Failure is not an option.
I will contact whoever I can in the Holy City. Jean Bart, you'll go northwest to Bretagne; and Marseillaise, you'll go north to Normandy.
As you wish, Cardinal.
Cardinal, the fleet from Toulon has been battling endlessly. Many of them are in no condition to keep fighting.
Then I would ask that you have them use the node near Avignon to return to the venue.
I will ask Jeanne's fleet to provide assistance.
Appreciate it. That takes a lot of the pressure off our shoulders.
Good. What happens next... depends on whether we can get our sisters and compatriots to trust our words.
BEEP—
Cardinal Richelieu, this is Tartu with the Vichya Dominion Special Mobile Fleet.
(Special Mobile Fleet...?)
Perfect timing. Tartu, where is your fleet currently?
We're at Amiens Cathedral now.
Lady Clemenceau has just informed the Tribunal and Vichyan fleet of the situation through secret communications lines.
She asked that we work with you to activate the Skybound Walls at the conceptual anchors.
What of Iron Blood leadership? Have they left forces behind?
She said she'd handle them personally, so we should concentrate on our own problems.
Also, Cardinal, she complimented your speech at Saint Helena.
...So Le Terrible told her about the speech, too.
She just doesn't know how to mind her own business. Heehee.
Le Mars reporting in. Cardinal Richelieu, I have a message for you!
The Skybound Wall near Reims has been activated! The Templar Knights will stand by until given further orders!
This is Le Malin speaking. We've also activated the Skybound Wall at the Holy City's anchor. Awaiting orders.
Lights signalling the successful activation of the Skybound Walls sprang to life on the map one after another.
What a beautiful sight...
Cardinal Richelieu, we're taking back Vichya—no, all of the Iris Orthodoxy.
It won't be long before we're one again.
Yes... Just a little longer.
Mont-Saint-Michel and the capital are all that remain.
Don't worry about Mont-Saint-Michel.
Strasbourg's team was already nearby, so they'll have it taken care of before long.
...And there you have it. Mont-Saint-Michel's conceptual anchor is shining light toward the Vichya pavilion now.
Wouldn't have killed them to say something, though.
I understand. Thank you, Jean Bart.
Then all that's left is the capital.
Our final objective is the Iris Orthodoxy's Holy City, taken from us by the Reenactments.
Friends of a unified Iris Orthodoxy, listen well. Once you have completed your current tasks, assemble in our capital.
Before we join the Commander at the World Expo venue, we must unify our forces.
As one glorious Iris Orthodoxy!

sequence: World Expo Venue - Vichya Pavilion
Temporary Command Room

scripts.say: Rays of light shot from each anchor's Skybound Wall, converging in the sky above the Vichya pavilion.
Dazzling, divine light shone upon the center of the anomaly like rays of hope.
Shipgirls who'd finished their missions returned one after another to the venue through the microlayer network.
The maintenance facilities for the shipgirls gathered in the venue were working overtime.
By now, nearly all of the enemies in the area, save for those around the black hole, had been eradicated.
Three remaining targets. Two... One...
That's all of them.
The transference device lit up, and finally...
The fleet led by Richelieu returned.
Their fleet was organized without separation between the once separated factions, with all the dignity worthy of the reunited Iris Orthodoxy name.
But they weren't alone—at this very moment, this venue now hosted the full Azur Lane fleet.
The Eagle Union, Royal Navy, Iron Blood, Sakura Empire, Iris Orthodoxy, Dragon Empery, Northern Parliament, Sardegna Empire, and even META from beyond space-time...
The grand fleet was preparing for its decisive battle, and in addition–
The Spear of Destiny, the key to striking down the false God, was also in its final preparations.
When two concepts smash into each other head-on, one will be overwritten. All or nothing.
If it goes well, this fleet might never need to step out onto the stage.
If it doesn't, however, you might find yourself wishing you'd brought more friends, Commander.
Final checks complete. All conceptual anchor signals confirmed. Awaiting your final order to launch the Spear of Destiny.
Though surprised by Clemenceau's sudden seriousness, I gave the order.
Heehee. You need to have a sense of ceremony when the situation calls for it.
Activating the Spear of Destiny system.
Now, let's shoot that false God right between the eyes!
Lights from all over the world seemed to converge in one point above the Vichya pavilion, forming a radiant lance of pure energy.
It blazed like the sun, glorious and pure. All who beheld it were overwhelmed with awe.
The concept of true divinity collided into the abyssal darkness of the false God's cocoon–

The energy from the conceptual anchors flickered and waned, already squeezed to its limit. Just as the last spark of light from the anchors faded, the outer shell of the darkness covering the cocoon split open.
Light and darkness alike disappeared, and peace—
—did not return to the sea.
We've broken through the cocoon's outer layer!
B-but, an even bigger Gazer seems to be coming out of it!
And that's not all! The Gazers around us are changing their behavioral patterns!
They're all moving to where the cocoon was! Could that Gazer be...?
Indeed. The situation appears to be as bad as you fear.
The Gazer that just came out of the cocoon... may well be the false God itself.
Clemenceau... is this what you were trying to accomplish?
I was hoping for a more decisive victory than this...
But unfortunately, it took every bit of energy from the conceptual anchors just to neutrallize the darkness.
Though we've pierced through the protection of the false God, we must face the brunt of its wrath ourselves.
Commander! Clemenceau! We're ready to fight at any time!
Don't worry about things not going to plan! We've already dealt that thing a devastating blow it definitely wasn't expecting!
Now's the time to press our advantage and finish it off once and for all!
With the powers of conceptual manifestation counteracting each other here, this comes down to an old-fashioned gunfight. Commander, the Iris fleet awaits your orders!
The Royal Navy has assembled. We are ready for your instructions at any time.
Likewise. The Northern Parliament stands behind your decision, Comrade Commander.
The Dragon Empery fleet is ready as well, Commander. Let us work together towards victory!
The Sakura Empire and Iron Blood fleets... will stand with you during this decisive battle.
Likewise, Sardegna stands ready. Let us make an example of those who would trample upon our dignity and splendor!
We shouldn't underestimate the power of a God that Antiochus cannot slay. It might have more tricks up its sleeve.
Having that said, we're also strong. I trust that we'll pull through this crisis, especially with Helena's support.
I might know what thing really is... No, we'll know for sure when we fight. Commander, you may not be there in person, but we're counting on your support!
Commander, I've played my final trump card. No more tricks, no more contingency plans. My life is now in your hands.
Defeat that false God, and lead us all to victory!
The massive fleet, comprised of shipgirls from all factions, set out. They closed in on the false God from several different directions.
Our vanguard has scattered the enemy in our way. We'll be in position to directly attack God soon.
It's been so long since I fought like this! I'll launch the first attack!
They're giving us some trouble up in the sky...
But we're no slouches either. In addition to airplanes, we also have – err – airships on our side.
It won't be long before we've secured aerial superiority!
Essex fumbled her sentence because of the word "airships."
No wonder, because when Roma's team came flying over with a whole armada of them, it caused quite a stir among the shipgirls.
They came from under the Colosseum, where the Sirens had left a production facility, which our local genius da Vinci took control of.
Apparently, they only worked in this anomalous space and would disintegrate if taken outside it.
Do not flinch! Do not fear injury!
Come, my steel eagles, and destroy our enemies!
Roma! You're on the Commander's channel!
...She can't hear me, can she? Ugh... Excuse me, Commander, I'll call you back later!
The mission is going well on all fronts.
Our vanguard has already eliminated the God's small fry.
The Gazers coming in from the surrounding waters are getting knocked down one after the next. They can't break through our defenses.
The only real problem is the false God itself.
It's just been sitting there for a while now. It's possible the Spear of Destiny did actual damage to it, and not just the cocoon.
As per orders, we'll now enter the next phase.
Then this one shall attack as well.
Whether it's the Commander's presence or this domain affecting me, I feel ready to take on anything...
No. You mustn't.
If eliminating that God is our victory condition, losing the Commander is our defeat condition.
Without the Commander, our coordination will break down, and our morale will plummet – yours included. Ensuring the Commander's safety is number one.
Furthermore, doesn't the Sakuran fleet need you and your abilities to command it?
A good point. This one shall remain here...
As instructed, the vanguard will now launch an attack on God.
...That had no effect. On the bright side, it didn't retaliate.
The rest of the forces have reached attacking positions. Your orders, Commander?
"Focus your fire on that false God."
"It's time to make our next move."
I could see the false God's form clearly through the monitor on my command vessel.
Floating in the middle of the layers of armor was a girl, cloaked in a ghostly-pale light.
This isn't working. Our attacks aren't going to breach those defenses.
Memphis META was referring not just to the mechanical body of the Gazer, but also the little girl in the air.
I have a guess as to why. It's only a guess, but...
Based on what I know, I think that girl is Arbiter: The Hierophant V.
That said, my database doesn't recognize her as The Hierophant, no matter what data or parameters I feed it.
Either that appearance is some sort of disguise... or something is using The Hierophant's vessel.
If the latter is true, then THAT must be the true identity of Marco Polo's false God.
I agree.
The Ashes have fought against The Hierophant a number of times before. She is one of the few Arbiters who can be reasoned with.
I have all the reason to believe that something is taking advantage of her powers and mass-production capabilities.
But beyond that, there's something deeply unsettling about all of this...
Not just the false God. But the Gazers as well, the swarms of enemies, and the white substance...
Where I'm from, just about everything is a bad omen. But, even that has varying degrees.
All I can say is... I'm afraid you guys have opened a terrible door that can't be shut again.
When Memphis META rescued Shinano and her fleet, she mentioned something similar. An enemy beyond our cognition.
But, they would say no more about this matter. Even Hiryuu META would tell me nothing beyond "I cannot say."
