If there was one thing I gleamed from this, it was that knowing too much about it was dangerous.
Commander, when will we launch our all-out attack?
That girl has something very important to the Orthodoxy. We must take it back from her.
"You don't mean...?"
Yeah. The Crown of the Holy See. We thought Marco Polo took it with her into the sea, but it seems that the monster took it.
Marco Polo can be judged at a later time. More urgently, we must stop the Crown from being corrupted.
The symbol of the Orthodoxy's legitimacy, the crown signifying the wearer's holy position, was in the hands of the false God.
As I gazed upon the Crown floating in the girl's hands, something suddenly dawned on me.
The Crown was more than just a relic passed down since ancient times. It was, originally, an extension of God.
The girl was motionless, but her gaze pierced through me.
It was her. The figure that had appeared countless times in my nightmares.
Commander? What's wrong?! You look pale...
"That is a threat to our world that can't be allowed to exist."
KABOOOM!
Dammit! No effect! My shells disintegrate on impact with the armor without even leaving a scratch!
I'm... all out of ammo. I demand a resupply... and paid time off...
The small ones just keep coming, no matter how many we destroy.
They're like hydras... Cut one down, and two take its place. Is this area linked to the microlayer network or something?
No, we're dealing with something altogether different here.
It's not like they're popping out of the ocean or from sea fog... They seem to be ripping their way through the fabric of reality itself...
Ripping through... the fabric of reality? Lady Shinano, don't you think that sounds a bit similar to how our barrier domains work?
Barrier domains?
This one had the same hunch...
From an outside perspective, emerging from a Sakuran barrier hidden in the sky is the same as appearing out of thin air...
There are many ways to conceal such a barrier, too...
What we see is neither fact nor fiction, but rather a deception of our senses.
A barrier is an enchantment that must be dispelled through the proper means. Otherwise, attacking it accomplishes nothing more than trying to scoop the moon out of a pond.
I see... So what you're saying is, we've been shadowboxing this entire time. The enemy we think we are fighting was never there to begin with.
If that is true, its physical form must be hidden away in some domain.
I did say before that I had no more cards to play. But, that's not quite accurate–
I do have one final move to make – a sacrament from this false God, given to me by Marco Polo. We have no choice but to use it.
However, it will take some time to prepare. Commander, can I trust you to hold the line in the meantime?
Helena also needs time to complete her analysis. Keep up the pressure, Commander!
"You don't have to tell me twice."
▅■cease▆▅
All of a sudden, I heard a girl's emotionless, mechanical voice inside of my head.
What on earth was that?
I feel like... I'm slowing down. My rigging's grind to a halt!
Mine, too! Commander, we're all affected by whatever this is!
Same here. I can't... move... Urgh...
Argh! Ark Royal! My head!
Damnit! The energy in my hull's going completely haywire!
Memphis? Are you hanging in there?
Barely... Somehow, yeah...
With but a single otherworldly word, the entire battlefield was gripped by an icy, death-like chill.
Did you hear that voice too? What manner of enchantment is this?
"Yes. I can still move like normal. Whatever it is, it doesn't look like it affected me."
"You don't look like it affected you much either, for that matter, Shinano."
"Could it be that my command vessel is immune to this phenomenon?"
No, it's not. I'm affected, albeit it not to the same degree as the rest.
Most puzzling... So the effect varies from shipgirl to shipgirl...
I'm basically fine. My arms and legs just feel a little heavy.
Likewise, I am still fit for battle. I feel hardly affected at all.
Same with the mass-produced ships... It's done practically nothing to them. They can still fight!
(So the blueprint ships and the mass-produced ships aren't affected much, while the METAs are gravely affected.)
(Among everyone on the command ship, only Shinano hasn't been affected at all.)
It doesn't seem like my hull's being corrupted, but...
I've felt this pain before... It feels like the exact same thing...
Urgh... I'm... all but certain... that it's the same thing...
Commander... Is it too late to retreat now...?
Retreat? You're just gonna run away, Hiryuu?!
I'm not talking about me... We all... need to get out of here... before it's too late!
Haha.. Sorry...
But if we run away with the Commander... what will happen to this experimental field...?
Whatever you're thinking, we cannot have you take the Commander from us.
We're lucky a certain someone here has barely been affected...
Gascogne! Force a direct connection into cognitive space!
A black sun, quietly burning in the dusky sky.
The black sun...
This is that other sacrament Marco Polo received from God...
Correct. The problem with it is that's nigh-impossible to control.
How is everyone? Can you move freely?
Yes! Thank you kindly, Clemenceau!
Forcibly connecting minds to a separate conceptual space to protect against an anti-conceptual weapon in reality. That must've taken a huge amount of energy...
Depending on how you use it, it can even affect your opponent's mind...
(This is Arbiter-level technology. Can we even be sure this space doesn't connect to somewhere else?)
So if understand correctly... the black sun is actually located in a cognitive plane of existence...?
How are we supposed to get back from here?
▅■one▆▅
For the first time since the battle began, the Hierophant moved her body.
She raised the wand in her hands high above her, then swung it down...
...Instantly shattering the vision of the black sun like a glass pane.
Just like that, she was in control of the world once more.
The symbol of judgment was destroyed THAT easily?!
Did we overload the connection? Or is this Arbiter simply that much stronger than it?
Neither. That wand... The ability to recognize and control concepts...
This isn't just one of the Hierophant's vessels! She's here, in person!
Be extremely careful! You do NOT want to be hit by attacks from that wand!
It'll either turn you to dust, or if you're really unlucky, the very concept of your existence will be wiped from reality!
Good to know... Too bad I'm basically stuck in place!
At least those attacks are time-consuming and short-ranged... Commander, rush her with the mass-produced ships and organize a fleet out of the blueprint ships!
The Hierophant's grip on everyone is letting up! Keep her busy while we get back on our feet!
I took control over the mass-produced ships and used them as shields for the shipgirls who could still move. This was just enough to hold the line.
Now there are aircraft coming after us! Commander, we need aerial support!
I've got you! I'm gonna swat those little mosquitos!
Wait... Are those the Devil's drones?!
Countless drones appeared in the sky, emerging from nowhere just like the swarmers down at sea level.
The drones – bearing the markings of the Devil XV – all encircled the Hierophant briefly before spreading out in all directions.
Their formation almost resembled the shape of a spider web.
Hey! Where are you going?! Fight me!
Disregarding Hakuryuu's provocation, the Hierophant once again raised her wand and lightly waved it in the direction of a single aircraft.
It began glowing with a dazzling golden light that chained to nearby aircraft, forming a net of light.
My worst fear had come to reality.
The Devil, the master of support, was aiding her. It was clear this attack was targeting every single shipgirl on the battlefield at once.
▅■two▆▅
A support protocol?!
Everyone! Dodge, quick!
We managed to move the mass-produced ships just in time to protect our recovering allies from the giant.
However, the attack destroyed all of the mass-produced ships and even vaporized the Tribunal's conceptual weapon.
A support protocol with the Devil... No, that's not all.
She must've been the reason why the Devil was acting strangely within the Reality Lens!
And there's another enemy behind this one, too...!
I always thought it was strange. Why did the Devil start acting so weird, and how did they break into that space?
This same enemy... must've been hunting the Commander this entire time!
A word of advice. If you want to live to fight another day, NEVER challenge one Arbiter on their home turf, let alone two.
The Devil supports, and the Hierophant controls concepts.
She knows now that the biggest threat to her is the Commander.
If we let her make her next attack, we're not going to be able to dodge it...
"That just means we can't let her attack."
Despite the distance between us, I noticed the Hierophant cocking her head just slightly in my direction.
The Arbiter... moved...?
BOOOOM!
Less-affected and recovering shipgirls fired their weapons as much as they could at the Hierophant.
The Hierophant is charging at the Commander!
We have to stop her, and fast!
Like a deity parting the waters, the Hierophant shrugged aside even the densest barrage of cannon fire, not even slowing down in the slightest.
I saw her shadow cover my entire being, her wand bearing down on me––
No! We're not going to make it––
Helena, what are you waiting for?!
Change of plans! At least get the Commander out of here!
▅■three▆▅
As the Hierophant's wand came down, my vision was engulfed by the radiant web of lights coming from the drones surrounding her.
I could not see. I could not feel. There was only light.
BOOOOM!
A portion of the horde of drones exploded.
When the light cleared, every combatant in the area was wreathed in a barrier of warm blue light.
"Please fight until the last light has faded."
Memphis, you can't give up.
Helena, you—
Calm down already.
Helena...? You can't be—
A case of mistaken identity, I'm sure, Hiryuu of the Ashes.
Any more questions, and I'll disable that barrier.
No, no! I get it! I won't say anything! I accept that you're not the Helena I'm thinking of!
...I'm glad you understand.
The Commander has done well to buy me enough time to arrive.
The Devil's mainframe is no longer here, so you no longer have to worry about the supporting drones.
This barrier should also help the others recover from the Hierophant's restraints much faster.
As long as the barrier holds, you'll find that her conceptual attacks have little effect.
...But know that it won't hold forever. You'd be wise to settle the score before it wears off.
Also, be aware that the barrier won't protect you from direct attacks.
Commander, please continue to lead this battle. I need more time to corner her.
The Hierophant was never made to fight a large number of enemies at once. This is the best chance we've got.
Without the Devil's support and her strongest weapon neutrallized, the situation is within our grasp.
We hardly have to aim at her giant rigging, too.
Though, it remains to be seen how effective our attacks are going to be...
Heehee~ I'm sure the Commander will have no problems locating all her weak points~

Everyone grasped at the glimmer of hope that had broken through the despair like parched travelers arriving at an oasis. The second wind that swept through the entire fleet was truly heartening to see.
However, hope alone could not resolve the two main problems at hand.
First, we haven't found an effective way of damaging the Hierophant so far.
Second, and perhaps more importantly, everything rests on the assumption that we are fighting Arbiter: The Hierophant V. The assumption that she had not become something else.
Even now, I could feel her overwhelming gaze upon me.
It was an eerie, emotionless gaze. Even revolting.
▅■split▆▅
Did the Hierophant just take off her rigging...?
She's accelerating! Commander, watch out!
The Hierophant suddenly accelerated, unburdened by her rigging
At lightning speed, faster than the other shipgirls could react, she arrived above the command ship. Nobody could stop her now—
—save for Shinano, who was on the deck of the same ship.
This one won't let you...!
In the next moment, I heard the sound of windchimes.
BOOOOM!
This one's attack... struck...?
The echoes of the windchimes continued to linger in my ears, unlike the ephemeral tones I had heard in my dreams before.
Whereas nothing had been able to reach the Hierophant before, she was pushed back for the first time by the machine guns from Shinano's aircraft.
In that case... Let us see how you like this...!
▅■split▆▅
The Hierophant split in two...?! No! Commander!!
Her shadow detached from her and formed a second copy that seemed to move with its own consciousness.
The newly-born Hierophant slipped through the wall until she came face-to-face with me.
▅■clone▆▅
An immense force violently sweeps my consciousness away, and I feel myself sinking deep into darkness.
I open my eyes and look around.
I see a dimly-lit basement, filled with equipment and furniture that seem oddly familiar to me.
The Hierophant is right next to me, her wand raised above me – though in a completely unmenacing way.
But, when we hear two sets of footsteps coming down the corridor, she freezes in place, as if having turned into a statue.
I see. The doctors must be here.
As if reading my mind, the Hierophant cocks her head dubiously and lowers her wand.
...Due to the stalemate, I've been ordered to further accelerate my research.
Not sure what they want, given that the production of the next-generation Antiochus model has been well underway...
Yes... I'm sure that the Arbiters will give us the power we need to put an end to this futile war.
But right now, we're still a long ways away from our ultimate goal.
Now allow me to introduce you to the first daughter of the Arbiter Program – Hierophant.
The... first?
That's right. Zero doesn't count.
She's one-of-a-kind, not a member of any series.
In any case, the Hierophant will be the covergirl of the Arbiter series.
As such, I've strengthened her recognition of language and concepts, and installed modules to heighten her empathy and friendliness.
Her updated quantum intelligence analysis system allows her to understand others on a deeper level and express emotions like any human being.
During the testing process, not a single person noticed they were speaking with a machine. She passes the Turing test with flying colors.
Of course, it doesn't stop there.
As someone who can understand and control concepts, she understands non-human intelligence and can simulate how they would speak.
We still need more testing, but she can already communicate with cats, dogs, and dolphins.
With more updates, the only limit is... Why, she could surpass the heights of the Tower of Babel.
In other words, you want to make more cute white-haired girls.
Ahem! Anzeel, how many times do I have to tell you–
Yeah, yeah. You're just iterating on a tried-and-true design, or whatever.
Exactly.
By the way, why'd you decide to start with the fifth Major Arcana?
Don't people usually go in order from the first one?
I'm only in the first stages of planning. Frankly, I'm not even certain if I can make enough to fill a deck of tarot cards.
What matters more is inspiration, which is exactly why I started with the Hierophant – it inspired me.
It symbolizes guidance, compassion, interconnectedness, and conformity...
Oh, wow. Rare to see you so passionate about anything that isn't a weapon of war.
When you called me over, I was ready for you to show me your latest weapon of mass destruction.
The fact that you'd think so is in itself proof of the need for Arbiters.
As you know, our resources become more precious and scarce by the day.
The Hierophant will dispel every misgiving the people have towards the Antiochus.
Whether you're using her as a mediator or as a means of competing for resources and funds, she'll be a major boon.
Ah, yes. Of course you'd go down that route.
Then, have you considered this possibility?
Keep raising her specs, and maybe, just maybe... she'll be able to communicate with Deus X someday.
Being able to communicate gives us options other than fighting, yeah?
Especially... under these circumstances.
...Hah.
Whoa, nasty look. What's that supposed to mean?
C'mon, Commander. What do you think?
(Why is she asking me?!)
(What am I seeing? Is this an illusion, or is it a memory played by that Recorder AI?)
The Hierophant also looks to me curiously, as if waiting for my answer.
"The concept of 'the enemy' isn't necessarily set in stone. If two parties can communicate, then peace must be an option."
Exactly! You're not just the Commander because of your aptitude and abilities. Those girls only see you as their Commander because you've earned their trust.
Anzeel approached from the darkness. Her figure was indistinct, but her voice was clear.
Thanks for your help, Hierophant. Are you getting along with my assistant here?
There is a flash of light inside the girl's eyes.
"If you can communicate with the enemy, you'll better know their weaknesses. All the better to defeat them."
A very rational perspective. Clearly defining the concept of "the enemy" will bring the right path into view.
Even if we can eventually converse with Deus X, the Hierophant's power must be used to fight it.
The blood shed by humanity must be repaid through their complete eradication.
Aoste approached from the darkness. His figure was indistinct, but his voice was clear.
The Hierophant, your work is done for now. Enter sleep mode.
She did not resist. On the doctor's orders, she began her shutdown program.
White light filled my vision, erasing Anzeel, Aoste, the Hierophant, and the entire space we were in.
A door sppears in the distance.
A familiar door, standing alone in the pure-white chamber.
Looks like it's time for me to go home.
The scenery changes for a third time. Now, I see the buildings of the World Expo venue.
...More precisely, the remnants of the venue, bathed in moonlight.
The sky, land, and sea are back to normal. The mysterious Divine Vestige is gone, along with the false God.
The only sound in the night is the crashing of waves, as if nothing had happened.
But the weight in my hands tells me that the entire Arbiter catastrophe was reality.
My fingers are lightly curled around the symbol of the Iris Orthodoxy's legitimacy, the Crown of the Holy See.
I can't help but to think to myself, what if the Crown was controlling the concepts within the domain the entire time, rather than the Hierophant?
I receive no answer. Only the cold weight of the Crown, inanimate and lifeless in my hands.
My thoughts are suddenly cut short by countless voices coming in through the communicator all at once.
Judging from what words I could pick out, it seems that I had disappeared along with the Hierophant for a period of time.
I suppose... I should let everyone know that I'm alive and well.
Clemenceau gazed sadly at the salvaged throne before her.
She could not stop the memories of their first meeting from rushing through her head.

sequence: Some time in the past...
Unknown location in Iron Blood

scripts.say: On one side of the room was the schemer, representing the dark side of the shining Orthodoxy. On the other side was a jester, charming yet ambitious.
The two could hardly have less in common, save for one thing – they had both been bored to death by the preceding meeting.
So you're Clemenceau, the Vichya's representative?
That I am. And I already know your name well, Marco Polo.
The Iron Blood folks and your lackeys are gone. Why are you still here?
Hmm~ I like jotting down notes while the memory is still fresh in my mind.
Magnificent. You play the part of a bureaucrat perfectly.
But, you didn't speak at all during the meeting. Do you not like dealing with Iron Blood?
I wouldn't say that. The Vichya and Iron Blood are close friends, after all.
Cut it out already. There's nobody else here!
Stop putting on airs already. I'm only speaking to you because I see your potential!
Look, the two of us are kindred spirits. Everyone else? They're a whole bunch of fools who don't know a thing.
If you don't like their proposals, then why don't you lend me your ear?
Hahaha! Magnificent! I can tell, the two of us are going to accomplish great things together!
I hear windchimes by my ear. Wind. A breath of fresh air, pulling me away from the depths.
The suffocating feeling disappeared, and this time, I woke up in a peculiar space.
Beneath a dark sky, I see brightly-colored torii gates stretching into the distance in front of me.
The wind seems to come from both sides, sending waves crashing into each other.
When I look up, I see inverted castles and pavilions hanging upside-down, like projected mirages.
The vast city above me almost makes me wonder if I'm the one who's upside-down.
I look more closely at what seems to be hidden behind the mirage-like structures and clouds, and a sense of déjà vu washes over me.
Just like with the black sun, I seem to perceive something imperceptible, a tip of an iceberg to something not of this world, something far larger than me.

options.content: Wait, is that someone underneath the torii gate?

scripts.say: I see a strange yet familiar figure, clad in black and red.
She starts to turn around, seemingly having noticed my gaze.
I can't see her face, or any discernable patterns on her clothes.
But, a sense of nostalgia keeps seems to well up inside me.
I try to call out to her, but she's gone before I can utter even a word.
Who goes there...?
From behind me comes a voice I know well.
So it is you...
That this one would see you again in my dreams... Fate works in mysterious ways.
"Do you know who that person over there was? The one wearing black-and-red?"
A person wearing black and red? I apologize, but this one has seen no such thing...
You would be the first person this one has found in this world...
Shinano knew many dream worlds, but even she didn't see everything that happened in all of them... Naturally, since they were dreams.
Indeed, this dream is a gap between dreams... A connection between fiction and reality...
It is a second hometown to this one, away from the real world...
When visiting dreams, this one occasionally stops here along the way...
However, this dream comes at an inconvenient time...
This one will miss the World Expo's closing ceremony...
"So you're saying... You fell asleep right before the closing ceremony?"
"I heard you were here to represent the Sakura Empire. That is unfortunate..."
Have you come to the World Expo, too...?
Oh, how delightful it is that the real Commander has appeared in this one's dreams...
"Now that I think about it, it's uncanny that I'm in your dream. Especially if neither of us is a figment of the other's imagination."
This one did not expect to dream your dream, rather than dreaming of you...
We have met a few times now, but this is the first time that this one can be certain...
How exciting it is...
Shinano, aircraft carrier of the Sakura Empire. She has a mysterious power that allowed her to dream of all realities.
Long ago, when I was trapped with Archerfish in a Mirror Sea, Shinano had saved us.
Until that point, she'd considered her dreams as simple precognition or potential futures. That incident had changed her perspective on it, though.
"If you have this dream often, then maybe it's more than just a dream."
"The upside-down city, that mysterious machine in the distance, the black sun..."
"And I keep hearing these strange windchimes—"
This one has heard the chimes, as well...
However, it does not happen with every dream. Only with some...
It seems that they are a guide within the world of dreams...
Follow the sound, and you may have unusual dreams...
This one often hears them when trying to escape nightmares.
However, they do not always lead one to good dreams... Just yesterday, this one dreamed of something terrifying.
The windchimes led this one to a world... overhung by a golden sky and black sun...
A sun that burned without heat, like a black hole that chilled the observer...
"You dreamed of the black sun, too?!"
"Here's everything that happened until now..."
This one was not the only one to dream of the black sun...?
Though it is a dream, the fact that it haunts more than this one means that it cannot be taken lightly.
When dreaming of the black sun, this one heard someone else's voice...
Hmm... Alas, this one cannot remember well.
After dreaming in the early morning... this one had abruptly fallen into the dream of the black sun...
This one did not dream in between, and yet my memories...
And you say... that you suddenly found yourself dreaming, too...
"Likewise, I don't have any vivid memories after early this morning."
"I left the Eagle Union pavilion with the others, and we were on our way to the Colosseum... and that's it."
"That is, assuming that speech I saw was just a dream, too."
You and this one are alike...
This one hopes it was only a dream... but if it is a potential reality, then it may be disastrous...
"In other words, we need to do everything we can to keep it from becoming reality."
Once you awaken from this dream we share...
I heard the windchimes again.
Could this be... the sound that leads one to awakening?
Commander, we must speak again in the real world... at the World Expo venue.
Call this number—

sequence: During the mission to activate all conceptual anchors
African North Coast - Alexandria

scripts.say: Andrea Doria stepped out of an abandoned facility, shielding her eyes from the sand kicked up around her.
The situation has become dire...
Turning her gaze upwards, she sees layers upon layers of strange clouds hanging low in the darkened sky.
...Alright. I need to take action. Hiding from the problem won't solve anything.
She shook her head, collected herself, and brushed off the sand covering the control panel in front of her.
She knew what every button on the control panel did. After all, she had done this countless times before.
"Ignite a light in the darkness..."
And now, I will add my own.
The Skybound Wall activated, shooting out a bridge of light that connected the building with the World Expo all the way in the distance.
The wind carried the sand through the air, covering the abandoned control panel with sand once more.
Thus, the fairytale told on an Alexandrian night was left in dreams.

sequence: After the mission's conclusion
Somewhere in the Mediterranean Sea...

scripts.say: The Arbiter's superimposed world is gone. The truth of what happened here will remain only in our memories.
Yes. The Hierophant has been dealt with, and there's no reason for us to remain here.
The Commander summoned you, right? Thank you for coming to our aid.
I suppose not all of the Ashes are too stubborn to be reasoned with.
Do you really not remember me, Memphis?
Um... Last I checked, I was never in the Ashes. I don't know you.
I think you have me confused for another Memphis.
I can tell you hold the Commander in a certain regard. Have you two met somewhere before?
Do you believe that the Commander is the one you've been searching for?
...I can't say.
Why not? I just want to know your roots.
I don't see why I should tell you.
Okay, another question then. Do you remember speaking to Aoste and Anzeel?
I can't say.
I don't know what you want from me with these questions, and this conversation is meaningless.
I'll be off now.
Wait! Let me ask you one final question. It's similar to my first.
Do you truly... truly not remember us?
Memphis, what's the matter?
I'm seeing some slight deviations on your monitoring system. Everything alright?
Yeah, I'm fine. It's just...
Someone asked me a weird question. It's nothing. I'm finished here.
Hiryuu. You should get back to your Ashes mission.
Right. I'll do just that. May the both of you stay in good health.
...You too.
Sorry about the holdup, Helena. I'll be right there.

sequence: After the mission's conclusion
Iris Orthodoxy - Reims Cathedral

scripts.say: Through the cathedral's stained glass windows, brilliant sunshine shone down upon religious artifacts and a floor made hundreds of years ago.
The interior had been thoroughly cleaned to prepare for a ceremony. All the old sculptures and cobblestones looked as if they were brand new.
New life had been breathed into the cathedral – and the Iris Orthodoxy.
I still can't believe they chose ME as the Eagle Union's representative... Gosh, I'm so nervous...
You were the obvious choice. You proved it with your actions during the mission.
It's an honor not just to have been part of the crisis response team, but also to be here witnessing this historic moment.
So much has happened so quickly. From sealing off the microlayer network, to wrapping up the Expo's closing ceremony, to concealing the true nature of the superimposed worlds...
Absurdly quickly, even. Everyone's had to work insanely fast to achieve all that in just a few days.
That's the efficiency of a unified Orthodoxy for you.
I suppose I'd be zealous too if I were in their position.
It's unfortunate that Her Majesty could not attend an event as momentous as the reborn Iris Orthodoxy's coronation ceremony...
But as you said, it's been a hectic last few days for all of us.
Which is why I'm here in her stead. It's only appropriate that I pass on Her Majesty's blessings for Lady Richelieu and the rest of the Iris Orthodoxy.
Indeed. After all they've been through, offering them our blessings is the least we can do.
After a long waiting period – as is typical for such a solemn ceremony – the coronation finally began.
Richelieu and her compatriots appeared before the podium, donning dignified robes that conveyed the power vested within them by the Holy Iris.
In response to the danger posed by Reenactments, Cardinal Richelieu left the Iris Orthodoxy's soil to ask allies for help.
Her achievements went largely unnoticed due to the Holy See's efforts to hide them. Despite that, she pushed on, fighting for our country.

She saved our compatriots at Toulon, worked tirelessly to smooth the relationship between factions, secured and sealed off sacraments, and changed enough minds to make the reunification of the Iris Orthodoxy possible.
She has been misunderstood, criticized, and put in positions of danger and adversity.
Despite all of that, Richelieu never once gave up.
It was thanks to her efforts that, when a crisis threatened our nation, we were able to rally under one banner.
It was thanks to her efforts that, when a calamity gripped the world, we were able to seize glorious victory.
As representative of the unified Iris Orthodoxy's Holy See, I hereby honor Richelieu's many contributions and sacrifices to our country.
Furthermore, I hereby revoke all unjust accusations and punishments she has endured in the past.
In my hands, I have the Crown of the Holy See, the shining symbol of the Iris Orthodoxy.
Cardinal Richelieu...
Will you be the Holy Iris's emissary and lead our war-torn country forward?
Will you become an emissary of the highest order and accept the position of Pontiff of our holy kingdom?
Will you wear the honor of the Iris Orthodoxy upon your head?
Crown held in hand, Clemenceau awaited the kneeling Richelieu's answer.
This Crown, this tangible sacrament...
I've been pondering what it signifies ever since I had to flee our country.
A sacred artifact to be kept safe?
An ancient memory to be passed down?
A symbol of our Orthodoxy to be revered?
It represents many, many concepts, and it is something we hold dear.
During that battle, however, I saw another crown.
A megalomaniac's ambition.
A tool exploited to selfish ends.
A product of Siren technology made to make fools of us.
At some point in history, the Sirens replaced the original crown with this one here.
In truth, we have been worshipping a false god for a very long time.
Of course, there is no doubt in my mind the faith and feelings in people's hearts were genuine.
However, we should not be reliant on a flawed belief that can be easily bent and distorted.
...I, Richelieu, humbly accept my new place as pontiff.
I swear that I shall restore the Holy Iris and our country to their former glory.
However, it is not to the Crown that I make this vow, but to my motherland and to her to people.
A true ruler chooses her own crown.
And I choose––
The people – my people – who cherish liberty!
I choose to bear no crown upon my head!
Before everyone's eyes, Richelieu drew a sword and swung at the Crown of the Holy See.
The strike neither split nor shattered the Crown. Instead, it spewed out a dark red smoke before finally crumbling to pieces.
First, there was shock. Then, jubilation. Ages seemed to pass before silence finally returned to the cathedral.
...Well done, Richelieu. Well done, my sister.
A proud smile briefly flashed on Clemenceau's lips, without anyone noticing.
Now, listen, my sisters in faith.
After many trials and hardships, liberty and unity have finally returned to our great nation.
We have shed many tears and much blood to get here.
But, I can confidently say that not one drop of blood, not a single tear, will have been in vain!
There is no longer anything that stands in the way of a united Orthodoxy!
Iris Libre and the Vichya Dominion will henceforth gather beneath the same banner!
Glory to the united Orthodoxy!
And glory to our motherland!
Within a sea of applause, the ceremony came to an end.
And thus, the Iris Orthodoxy set off on a new journey towards a brighter tomorrow.

sequence: Several days after the anomalous event
Somewhere in the Mediterranean Sea...

scripts.say: These are the results of pur investigation. The superimposed world didn't become reality, and the damage was limited to only a few isolated buildings and machines.
All factions have concluded that this incident was a surprise attack coordinated by the Arbiters.
At the Commander's suggestion, Marco Polo, Clemenceau, and their cohorts have been officially suspended for aiding and abetting a Siren conspiracy.
And everyone was happy in the end. Are you really fine with that?
Indeed... That really was a close call. Too close for comfort.
If the Commander hadn't been at the World Expo, we wouldn't have been able to launch a counterattack...
Marco Polo... You almost doomed us all...
Veneto, uh, I'm pretty sure we still haven't found Marco Polo.
...It's been days by now. Isn't it likely that she's already...?
*sigh*... You're right. This search hasn't gone anywhere since it began.
Let's try one more time, and then we'll wrap things up and go home.
Gotcha.
Veneto hung up and let out a deep sigh.
You know, it'll take more than that to sink her. Or... are you worried about how much of headache she'll be once she comes back?
Neither? Both? I don't know.
If I ever get to talk to her again, we're going to have a lengthy heart-to-heart.
At first, she was genuinely trying to act on behalf of Sardegna. If only I had been more sympathetic to her, maybe then...
BEEP—
Hmm? Seems like the call's for you, Veneto.
...From Clemenceau?
...Good evening, Clemenceau. Is there something I can help you with?
...Thank the Commander for making your work that much easier? Ahaha...
Well... I suppose...
...Alright, that's no problem. Goodbye.
Veneto hung up the line, then connected to the Sardegnian search party once again.
Oh dear, we are sad to report Marco Polo has already sunk to the bottom of the ocean.
After a damage assessment, I'm confirming there is no hope of salvaging her. Truly a tragedy.
In conclusion, the search is over and we can all go home now. Bye.
After giving her order in a painfully monotone voice, she changed course for home and began humming a carefree tune.
...What? But I could've sworn Clemenceau said the words "recover" and "comatose" in your conversation.
Did you not hear my order, Littorio?
There's nothing more for us here. We're going to declare her as sunk in our report to the Senate and move on with our lives.

sequence: Several days after the anomalous event

scripts.say: Within a Mirror Sea, the Mediterranean is once again engulfed in Divine Vestige.
Concluding 33rd Reenactment and recording results.
Sufficient analytical data on the proliferating white substance yields the following conclusion:
Deus X is involved.
The degree of corrosion is extremely mild and the phenomenon was also disguised, resulting in late detection.
Analysis of samples retrieved from the abnormal Hierophant vessel yields the following conclusion:
Deus X is involved.
As for why The Hierophant chose not to destroy her vessel...
I have been unable to restore communications, and therefore have not been able to submit my query.
This time, the incursion was curtailed at an early stage.
But regardless, it is clear that Experimental Field β is no longer safe.
...It appears that Zero attaches a great deal of importance to this branch.
I must consult with her first regarding this matter.
–Just like a bonfire in a dark, dark forest
–Just like a lighthouse in the infinite night sky
You've revealed your existence to them. You've become the light that beckons to them.
How interesting, nice ladies~♪ How fun!
We've found your home at last!
Hey, did you miss me?
Hey, did you miss me?
Hey, did you miss me?
Hey, did you miss me?

sequence: Reality
Sardegna Empire - World Expo Venue
Closing Day

scripts.say: Colorful flags flutter in the breeze as I walked through the venue on this pleasant day.
I can hear the uplifting fanfare of a band as I approach the Colosseum's entrance.
You can really see why they call it the World Expo...
Things were pretty quiet the last few days, so it totally slipped my mind how massive this event is.
Even I feel like I'm about to get swept away by the excitement.
Heehee. I rarely get to see you this bubbly, Memphis.
I mean, all of our friends are here having fun. How could I not get into the festive mood?
Familiar sights, familiar conversations. But, with one key difference–
...Hm? Commander, you don't look too good. Are you feeling sick?
Commander? Are you okay?!
"Physically, I'm fine. But I have to do something about what I saw in that dream."
"Memphis, you wanted to shop for souvenirs before the closing ceremony?"
...Yeah. How did you know?!
Normally, people would think you're crazy if you tried to tell them that you saw something in a dream and needed to prevent it in real life.
Given the situation, though, I had no choice but to give them a quick and dirty explanation.
Okay, I'm lost. Commander, what are you going on about?
You really do look sick... I'll call for a medic right away!
They're used to supporting me, so it's going to be hard to convince them.
In that case, I'll have to bring a witness to the stand.
I informed them of the change of plans and devised the quickest route to the Sakura Empire pavilion.
Meanwhile, I called Essex and directed her to prepare the Eagle Union fleet for battle.
C-Commander, what's gotten into you?! We can go to the Sakura Empire pavilion, but why are we preparing for battle?
Were you... serious about that stuff you told us?
"Of course I was."
...I trust you. If danger is coming, then I'll help out!
I led Memphis and Helena through the crowd and toward the Sakura Empire pavilion—
Argh! You'd better not run off on your own anymore!
I'm sorry, Suruga! I didn't think I'd get lost here...
Things do get pretty crowded on closing day. I wouldn't blame her too much for getting lost!
Now, how about I show you two to the Sakura Empire pavilion's VIP area!
I cultivated knowledge of this place through my reporting, so I'll get you there in no time!
*sigh*... I'm sorry for taking up your time, Alfredo.
Ahahaha... Thanks for your help, friend!
"Sardegnian staff are showing the Sakura Empire shipgirls around."
"Shinano is likely to be in the VIP area. Let's follow them."
That's fine, but do we have to be all secretive about this?
They might be with the Crimson Axis, but I'm sure they'll let you see her if you just ask.
"I have my reasons. There's no time to explain right now."
I dunno about this... She won't think we're weird?
Don't worry, Memphis. The Commander and Shinano have met in dreams.
Helena was there during the Archerfish incident, so she backed me up.
I-I see...
Then let's go—
Commander, watch out!
It happened without warning.
An enormous machine fell from the sky, obliterating the building in front of us with its pure mass.
Wh-what is that?!
Helena, secure an evacuation route right away!
Right...!
Commander, are you okay?! Stay with us!
"I inhaled some smoke from the building collapse, but I'm just fine."
Phew...
This is a message to all shipgirls on duty! Code Black! Secure the safety of important personnel!
Repeating! Code Black!
World Expo Venue
BOOOOM!
Woooaaaoooooaah––!! Phew, that was a close one... Suruga, are you okay?!
Yeah. I just barely managed to get out of the way...
Wait, what is that?! Where did it come from?!
Waaaaargh?! The pavilion's been blown to smithereens!
Alfredo, please stay calm!
R-right! Stay calm, stay calm... This is the perfect opportunity for a photo!
*click*!
I have no idea what just happened, but a journalist has to be ready to snap pics of every calamity as it happens!
Sakura Empire VIPs, please evacuate! I'll handle the situation here!
I'll fight, too! Your chances are a lot better with a partner!
Suruga, hurry over to Shinano! I'll take care—hey, ow!
What are you fools thinking?! You can't win against that thing!
Exasperated or furious, Suruga lifted up both of them and jumped away.
Almost instantly, a massive mechanical leg crushed down on the spot they had occupied a moment ago.
In this chaos, it was impossible to get a grasp of the situation, let alone mount a counterattack.
Commander? Why'd you stop running?
"It's more important that I ensure everyone else can evacuate first."
Got it. We'll handle communications.
Helena, send the coordinates of that big guy to Essex!
And let the people evacuating know that help is on its way!
Alfredo, Shimakaze, Suruga! Hurry this way!
BOOOOM!
Thank you, Commander! And you Eagle Union folk, too!
Suruga, Alfredo! We're saved!
Th-thank you very much...
Roger! We'd love some backup right now! We'll join up with them!
(Right... For the time being, we have to focus on getting through this predicament!)

sequence: Shortly after...
World Expo Venue - Eagle Union Pavilion
Underground Emergency Shelter

scripts.say: Thanks to the air support, we managed to evacuate into the underground shelter.
At first, I had my doubts about why an emergency shelter would be set up in such a conspicuous location.
But as the elevator took us deeper and deeper underground, the situation became completely clear.
Sealing blast door... And done.
We're safe now, Commander.

options.content: "So, this emergency shelter... Was it set up because..."

scripts.say: Yes, that's right.
As soon as we heard that you were on your way, Saratoga was adamant about beefing up our security, just in case.
This place isn't as nice as it could be if we had a few more days, but we can't take anything for granted when it comes to your safety.
Having all that said, I never actually expected it to come into play like this.
"Do the other factions know about this?"
No, we keep it a secret from the other factions. On paper, it's only a safehouse where we store valuables and materials.
*sigh*... Saratoga's been keeping secrets from me again.
Still, I have to admit that she's really outdone herself this time.
As far as I can tell, this place has the materials for communication and battle command. Why don't we make this our temporary base?
"We've secured a safehouse. Our next urgent matter is to figure out the situation."
"Let's test communications to other bases and summarize the situation in the venue."
I can't get in touch with NY City or New Jersey's fleet in the NA Ocean.
But it's weird... The communication signal is coming in strange.
It's not like we're being jammed. It's more like... it can't find who I'm trying to communicate with.
Likewise. It's like any communications going out of the venue can't reach their target...
Communications in and around the venue seem to be going smoothly, so we at least have a grasp of the situation.
But we have no idea what's going on at any of the outside bases.
Helena is right; our signal isn't even being jammed, and this is still happening.
Oh! We have a report on the forces around the venue.
Things... aren't looking so good right now.
Essex handed me a handheld monitor as a visual aid.
This marked spot is the Eagle Union pavilion. Of course, that's where we are.
Our forces are focused in this underground shelter. For the moment, we're safe.
The Colosseum, the pavilion where the closing ceremony was held, was completely leveled by the initial attack.
Meanwhile, we've got ten of those massive mechanical eyeballs wreaking havoc across the venues. We'll call them Gazers for now–
Our carrier-based aircraft haven't had any success trying to break through with bombs, and we're still in the process of gathering more information.
Also, here's the situation with the Royal Navy and Iris Libre.
Their pavilions were also heavily damaged by the attack, so they plan to gather their fleet and evacuate towards Malta.
As for the other factions...
The Sardegnian Fleet is regrouping around the only pavilion they have left, and are planning to launch a counterattack.
The Sakura Empire is also buckling down to defend their pavilion, and has already warded off one wave of attacks.
The Dragon Empery... Hmm. Their pavilion doesn't appear to have been damaged, and none of their personnel appear to be on site.
On the other hand, the Northern Parliament's pavilion was completely destroyed, and we do not know the status of any of their shipgirls.
Intense fighting has been seen near the locations of the Iron Blood and Vichya Dominion pavilions.
Though we aren't able to monitor everything in real time, it appears that several blueprint ships have been deployed and are currently holding the lines.
...That summarizes the situation as it stands.
Per your orders, Commander, we will continue to gather information and attempt to contact the other factions!
Don't mention it. We're just following your orders.
Ahaha... Well, I'm still nothing compared to Enterprise...
Ahem! I'm only following orders to the best of my ability.
It's pretty hard to be optimistic about this situation...
Even the host, the Sardegna Empire, couldn't predict this attack.
The abruptness of it prevented anyone from mounting an effective counterattack.
Our unknown enemy's power is unknowable, but it's clear that we're not getting out of this situation unless we work together.
At this rate, we'll only go down one by one. Instead, we should—
BEEP—
Finally, the comms are starting to clear up again. Ahem... This is Illustrious, Royal Navy aircraft carrier, speaking.
The Royal Navy and Iris Libre fleets have gathered in the waters southeast of the World Expo venue.
As I'm sure you have seen, an unknown enemy has literally dropped out of the sky and is ripping through our defenses as we speak.
In order to defeat this enemy, our fleets have temporarily evacuated to Malta in order to reorganize our forces and plan a counterattack.
All ships who can hear us, we implore you to come and join forces with us.
Our fleets plan to strike forth in one hour.
Until this situation is resolved, the Royal Navy welcomes all factions at our Malta base.
We hope you will join us.
Repeating. This is Illustrious, Royal Navy aircraft carrier, speaking...
I take note of their positions through the monitor.
Joining forces sounds lovely, but what if the Gazers attack us? Will we make it to Malta in one piece?
Commander, we've received a message directly from Illustrious. She says that, per her broadcast, she wishes to join forces.
She believes that with the extra firepower of the Eagle Union fleet, it would be possible to break through.
What do you think? Should we join up with them at Malta?
"The idea on paper sounds good. We obviously want to consolidate our forces as much as possible."

"Unfortunately, gathering outside the pavilion only makes us easy targets. Given the lack of information, trying to throw together a hasty evacuation could prove more disastrous than just trying to weather the storm."
"We'll look into Malta, but for now, we'll set our own meeting point and route."
"Shangri-La, pass all of that on to Illustrious for me, please."
Understood.
Commander, I've just received word from Shinano.
She says... that she'd like to speak with you in person.
I can see the doubt all over Suruga's face as she hands me the communicator.
Maybe Shinano told her about the dream...
This one rejoices over your safety, Commander...
Do not worry about us... We're holding up fine.
Thank you for your concern... This one is safe in the pavilion...
After we parted, this one made some preparations ahead of time... We were fortunately not taken unawares.
However, we cannot meet with the enemy in the venue...
This one... wishes to ask for your opinion.
Could this have all happened because of our attempts to stop the dream from coming to fruition...?
If we had only waited and watched as zealotry took over, would things have remained peaceful...?
How will you overcome this difficulty...?
"I don't know the cause, but now that enemies have shown up, we'll just have to join forces and fight them off."
Gathering all of the shipgirls to fight by your side... A wise choice...
In that case, there's a better place to gather than the Eagle Union shelter.
Eavesdropping through our communication lines?!
Who's there?
Sorry, sorry. I forgot to turn off my disguise. Prinz Eugen, Iron Blood.
I've been listening since the Commander took charge.
Our side agrees with joining forces.
Fighting scattered battles in a mad dash to escape sounds like an easy way to get yourself killed.
As for where to meet up, though, I'd suggest the Vichya pavilion.
You know all about the secret weapons in each pavilion, don't you, Commander? Well, did you know that the Vichya has a functional Skybound Wall installed?
They most likely did it only to brag about their technology, of course, but it still provides us with a solid line of defense.
Your shelter might be sturdy and a good option for keeping you safe, but it's hardly suitable for deploying a large number of shipgirls.
The Vichya's facility is big and it's located on solid ground, so you can fight back with ease.
This is Kersaint, from the Vichya Dominion. We've managed to deploy the Skybound Wall without issue.
Everyone is welcome, so please come if you so desire.
There you have it. How about it, Commander? It seems like the ideal move to me.
"You're right. Moving to the Vichya pavilion seems worthwhile, but..."
Are you still worried about me cutting into your conversation? Sorry about that, really. As you can all imagine, I've been listening in to all communications throughout the venue.
Though I'm sure the Eagle Union, and everyone else at that, are doing the same thing.
I was just able to interrupt your conversation because our technology is better.
Anyway, Commander, are you ready to give me an answer yet?
"There are a lot of things I'm unsure of—how reliable the Skybound Wall is, how prepared the communication equipment is, how sturdy the facility itself is..."
"But it sounds like the benefits outweigh the risks."
I believe in your leadership, Commander.
Agreed. The World Expo is a place for us to put aside our differences and come together, after all.
It doesn't really make a difference which faction takes the lead, huh?
"There you have it. Eugen, we agree."
"One more thing. I need you to share any and all information the Iron Blood has on the status of other factions."
Oh, you wanna know?
Our info on Sardegna is the same as yours. Their facility defense is top-notch.
They've decided to gather at the Vichya pavilion, and the Iron Blood will see to it that they make it there safe.
As for the Northern Parliament... They tried to evacuate from the venue in an attempt to meet up with the Royal Navy fleet.
But on your orders, they've turned back this way.
They'll join up with you soon, so make sure you look after them, Commander.
The Dragon Empery... Well, they left days ago, so they're long gone.
Looks like they got lucky this time, heheh.
That's all I've got. Will that do?
"We can discuss the details later, but for now, thank you for sharing."
"Sardegna will go with Iron Blood, and we'll meet with the Northern Parliament... The Sakura Empire is doing fine in battle, so they should have no problem going to the Vichya pavilion on their own."
Please take good care of Suruga and Shimakaze for the time being... Goodbye...
"Stay safe out there. We'll meet again at the Vichya pavilion."
Commander, the Northern Parliament has safely arrived in nearby seas.
It's good to see you safe and sound, Commander~
We were going to meet with the Royal Navy fleet due to the buggy communication lines, but...
Now that communications with you have been restored, we'll obey your orders.
Oh, and there's something I wanted to discuss with you...
Several of those large enemies are heading for the Union pavilion. It won't be long until you're in danger.
Even our combined fleets may not be able to fight them off, so I still think the best course of action would be to retreat for now.
The Northern Parliament pavilion is in tatters. If you're searching for another base—
"We actually already anticipated that. We'll be regrouping at the Vichya pavilion."
Excellent, I'm glad we're all on the same page, then – both Crimson Axis and Azur Lane.
"None of that matters under these conditions."
"As Commander, it's my duty to bring all of the factions together and rout the enemies that have destroyed our celebration of peace."
Heehee, I expected no less from you, Commander. See you later~
"Now, if we can just get a reply from the Royal Navy and Iris Libre..."
We understand the situation, Commander. The Royal Navy will travel to the designated point.
The Iris Libre fleet will accompany you, too. May the Holy Iris guide you...
"Phew... Looks like we've managed to get everyone to agree to cooperate."
W-wow... I can't believe how quickly you got everyone on the same page even though they were all doing their own things!
That's my Commander for you!
(Shush! Not so loud when the Commander's trying to focus!)
Whoopsie! Sorry!
Not that I mind, though. Shimakaze's carefree spirit can certainly be a breath of fresh air.
"Regardless, we've only managed to organize things somewhat. We still haven't turned things around."
"The enemy's identity, their motive for attacking us, and their weakness... There are still too many unknowns."
"Once everyone has gathered, that's when the real trouble begins."
Ooh! There's our Commander! Love that profile!
*click*!
"Commander Unites Warring Factions in the Midst of Danger!" Yeah, now that's a head-turner!

sequence: Sometime later...
World Expo - Vichya Dominion Pavilion
Nearby waters

scripts.say: After a few outbreaks of fierce fighting against drone-like enemies, we arrived safely in front of the Vichya Dominion's pavilion.
Looks like that's everyone, Joffre!
Activate the eastern Skybound Wall! Maximum output!
Incoming! Prepare for impact!
KABOOOM!
A Gazer rammed into the Skybound Wall, causing the light to ripple violently. However, the wall still managed to hold.
As if accepting that it would not be able to break through, the massive machine drifted off in a different direction.
While I was running some numbers to estimate the defensive capacity of the Skybound Wall, everyone around me could finally let out a sigh of relief.
W-we'll be fine. The Skybound Wall should have no issues withstanding most attacks.
I suppose we're safe, now that the eyeball thing is gone?
It seems like they won't attack us unless we launch an attack on them first.
Even I, in all my wisdom, can't figure out what they're trying to achieve.
They seem to be more focused on causing as much destruction as possible rather than attacking us.
By the way, are we calling these giant machines "Gazers?" They do look a bit like those monsters, straight out of books and movies.
I, I don't want to look at those things anymore... O Holy Iris, please give me the strength to overcome this trial!
S-sorry, I need to get a hold of myself! I can't be freaking out in front of the Commander...!
Kersaint led us deeper into the pavilion until we arrived at a conference room.
Veneto, Prinz Eugen, Shinano... Shipgirls from every faction were sitting around a large table.
Despite the crisis we are in, just seeing all of them together reminds me of the hope in the air during the World Expo.
Commander...
Long time no see, Commander.
How long has it been since we met face to face, I wonder? Heehee.
Welcome to the Sardegna Empire, Commander.
Sadly, this is nothing like how I thought we would meet...
Two leaders from guest factions, and the leader of the hosting one.
Though Eugen and Shinano did not seem particularly distraught, the same could not be said for Veneto.
I thought you would at least get to enjoy the closing ceremony, and instead you got swept up in a disaster.
As the Sardegnian representative, I am deeply sorry.
I know it's shameful, Veneto, but let's leave it there.
You couldn't possibly have predicted this. The more pressing matter is what we do from here.
Here's an idea – how about we capture one of those Gazers and take the opportunity to study them? Who knows, we might even be able to produce our own in the future~
While I appreciate your sentiment, please understand the gravity of this situation.
Given their numbers, combat capabilities, and our lack of information... I do not think this is a battle we can take, even were we to all work together.
We must gather every shipgirl in the Sardegna Empire in order to fight these foes.
If I may interject... We still have yet to reestablish communication with anyone beyond these waters.
Both Taranto and Rome are completely in the dark about our situation.
In the worst-case scenario, they may even be fighting Gazers on the Sardegnian mainland as we speak...
That's a scenario I don't want to imagine.
Lady Veneto, may I have a word?
If there's one thing clear about this attack, it's that you are the victims.
On the other hand... were there truly no warning signs before this happened?
A surprise attack with giant weapons of destruction was hitherto unprecedented. Not even the Sirens have engaged on this scale before.
Well...
Good line of thought. These enemies might not even be Sirens to begin with.
While, sure, they have giant weapons of their own, something about them just feels totally different.
Agreed. I'm afraid even we don't have any clues as to what they are...
"I would not be so quick to dismiss the possibility that the Sirens are behind this attack."
"That being said, Eugen has a point. These new enemies don't look like any Sirens we're familiar with, and their behaviors are completely different."
"But that still doesn't answer the question of the hour – just what in the world are they?"
At that time, a report came in that the entire World Expo venue had been reshaped to the point of being unrecognizable.
After landing, the Gazers started to spew a mysterious substance into the air.
Once the substance reached the ground, it started to spread and propagate rapidly like some kind of moss.
As it grew, it devoured buildings and trees alike, until it covered entire islands.
Forgive me, but I have to interrupt your conversation.
As thought things weren't dire enough, I have further bad news.
My reconnaissance planes have detected the presence of Gazers beyond the general area of the World Expo.
New ones are appearing in nearly every area I've looked, all of them emitting that mysterious substance.
It's likely by now that the Mediterranean and every coast surrounding it is within range of their invasion.
Certain parts of the sea... No, even facilities on the land have been covered in the mist.
While it's hard to tell from afar with my aircraft, I suspect the reason our communications are still offline is probably because the mist has blanketed our radio stations.
Speaking of the mist, it seems those "clouds" seem to be eating up our carrier-based aircraft.
Once an aircraft flies into one, its connection is lost, as though it was literally swallowed.
I'd speculate this is either due to a loss of control of the aircraft, or its outright destruction.
She speaks the truth. I lost several of my own aircraft to those clouds.
They're like beasts, devouring anything that flies into their mouths.
Something hidden within the clouds that is swallowing aircraft, rather than destroying them...
As unscientific as that claim is, it's hard to dispute the reality.
Even the clouds have become our enemies.
Huh? What do you mean by that?
Are you saying we're literally going to have to fight against clouds?
That strange substance is going to cover our sea, our land, our sky, our everything...
This... This can't be happening...
Guichen, do you reckon the same will happen to Vichya and Iris Libre?
From the sound of it, it seems inevitable.
If the Sirens are behind this, it's almost as if... they're trying to create a Mirror Sea in the real world...
We've seen some of these phenomena before inside a Mirror Sea, but never something on this scale before...
It shouldn't be possible to bring something like this into existence...
...Not without some Sacrament of God.
A vision from this one's nightmares has taken form in the real world...
Have I... seen a being of this nature before...?
——It is not enough.
It can't be...
It is... a being that must not be let free upon the world...
Bad news upon bad news upon bad news... A crushing atmosphere enveloped the conference hall.
Then, just as the mood was about to reach its lowest point, a shrill voice sent a chill down everyone's spine.
Ohohohohoho!
What a spectacular view! Ahahahaha!
Did someone jack into our channel again?
Ugh! Why is EVERYONE doing it to us today?!
Wait, isn't that voice...?
It's... Marco Polo!
...You won't believe your eyes when you see this.
Let's head outside. We must confirm this for ourselves.
Everyone rushed out of the Vichya pavilion.
High in the sky, an opulent throne floated in midair, illuminated by the golden radiance of the Skybound Wall.
The seraphic wings extending from its sides cast a deep shadow across the land, an array of complex machinery sitting atop a pedestal within their embrace.
Embedded in the back of the throne was a large gemstone that resembled an eye.
And in the middle of everything was the familiar figure of Marco Polo.
Good day, pitiful mortals.
Is that really you, Marco Polo? What is the meaning of this?
Oh, can't you tell? After all my work making this series of events easy to understand?
The Kingdom of God has been made manifest in the sky and the sea.
He descended upon the land and granted me, His emissary, supreme powers.
Which is to say, from now on you will refer to me as Her Holiness Marco Polo! Ohohoho!
You're not making a lick of sense...
Under normal circumstances, I'd shrug this off as a prank, but not this time. Do you know what you've done to the World Expo?!
You are its architect! You know better than anyone just how much money and resources we poured into the Expo to spread Sardegna's glory!
End this ridiculous farce at once, Marco Polo!
Spread Sardegna's glory? Ah, yes, glory.
How did you expect to achieve that with some small garden party?
And did you say "ridiculous farce"?! How dare you?! This is His great salvation!
It's our chance at peace and unity...
It's the beginning of a blissful, eternal age of glory for all of mankind...
And it was nearly all ruined just because SOMEONE here was a little too perceptive!
As punishment, I will make you all kneel before me! Ohohohoho!
I will give you one last warning.
What you've done is a betrayal of your homeland. It is a declaration of war against the whole world.
Really now? Doesn't matter to me.
How dare you...! Kersaint, take down the Skybound Wall! I will destroy this traitorous fool myself!

options.content: (Try to get Veneto to calm down.)

scripts.say: "Don't let her get to you, Veneto. The odds are stacked against us right now."
"If Marco Polo truly is responsible for all this, her powers are far greater than any of us here."
"You can't simply throw yourself at her when there's such a clear power gap, Veneto!"
Huh? Commander? ...Forgive me, I let my emotions get the better of me...
Calm down, Veneto.
I know it's hard to admit, but look around you.
If Marco Polo truly is responsible for all this, her powers are far greater than any of us here.
Do you really want to tackle her head-on? Running away is a better option.
Ugh...
Jeanne d'Arc, what's that thing on Marco Polo's head?
That is the Crown of the Holy See. I'm certain of it.
What I want to know is... how did she get her hands on it?
The Crown is supposed to be under Marseillaise's protection!
Oh no... Did Marco Polo steal it?
But then, Marseillaise... and the stronghold on Saint Helena...
You... What did you do, Marco Polo?!
Ohohohohohoho!
What's there to be shocked about? The Crown simply came into the hands of the one who deserves it.
There is no one more deserving of it than me, Marco Polo, the emissary of God.
No, as a matter of fact, you should be thanking me for personally keeping an eye on this little crown.
Of course, you can struggle all you want, but you are no more than pitiful mortals.
Soon, the Kingdom of God will cover the world.
And then, all war and strife will vanish, and humankind may live in a timeless utopia.
...Naturally, I know the fears and misgivings you mortals have.
But it matters not! The great undertaking has been accomplished!
You do not need to know, and I have no obligation to answer you.
All that's left is to wait for the chaotic noise to change into a beautiful hymn.
"The Divine shall descend upon the land."
Ohohohohohoho!
Marco Polo lets out the boisterous laugh of a woman possessed, completely indifferent to those struggling to lift their heads to gaze upon her.
But soon, she seems to lose interest, and flies off into the distance.
Beneath the golden sky, all she leaves beneath her is an ever-expanding expanse of white.
A loud rumbling came from every direction.
With Marco Polo's departure, the Gazers that had previously been floating around aimlessly now started to converge upon the Vichya pavilion.
Marco Polo... Why?
Veneto, now isn't the time to wallow in despair.
I think those Gazers are coming back to finish the job...
I can't believe it... Marco Polo is actually trying to get rid of us for good...
Umm... A large fleet of mass-produced ships has appeared in nearby waters...
Mass-produced ships? Has someone called for reinforcements?
I don't think so... They don't look like Sardegnian ships, and they don't seem to be engaging the Gazers either.
I'll send visuals right away!
Essex forwarded the picture to everyone present.
Huh... Those certainly aren't Siren ships.
I've never seen mass-produced models like these...
Jeanne d'Arc, Foch, what do you two think?
Ugh... The more I look at them, the more I feel like I should know what they are...
Oh! Aren't those the Tribunal's Mechanicus Confessors?! The one they made the prototype of?
And that means... Wow, they mass-produced those?
Joffre, do you know about this fleet?
Well... it does seem to be affiliated with the Tribunal.
Beyond that, this certainly is news to me.
I've never seen them, either, and Lady Clemenceau has told me nothing about them.
Kersaint is close to her, so it wouldn't be surprising if she knew something, but...
Joffre emphasizes the words "close to her," learning in to give Kersaint a pat on the back.
She's clearly trying to get her to talk.
U-umm... These mass-produced ships...
BEEP—
Kersaint, may I have a moment?
Lady Clemenceau... Sorry, things are a little tense right now...
Well, you seem calm enough to talk. Heehee.
Kersaint, take all Vichya Dominion ships and lead them out of the World Expo venue.
I'll see to it that those Gazers are amply distracted, so they won't trouble you.
Understood, Kersaint?
Yes, ma'am!
Thank you for your efforts. I'll be waiting.
That voice... Was that Clemenceau, the Tribunal's representative?
Lead us out of the venue? Why...?
Kersaint, did she tell you anything?
N-no, only that I should lead everyone out...
But those are Lady Clemenceau's orders, so we have to obey...
(If Marco Polo released those Gazers, then... why is Vichya—no, the Tribunal itself...)
(Is that it? Are Clemenceau and Marco Polo in league with each other?)
Lady Clemenceau, what is your goal...?
I think we can all agree that Marco Polo and Clemenceau's actions are related.
Which means those mass-produced ships aren't our friends...
Vichya and Marco Polo are in cahoots... Or so we're being led to believe.
But why would they reveal that at a time like this? If Vichya wanted to betray us, then...
Heh. Talk about unexpected developments, huh?
Sorry we can't fight alongside you all at a time like this...
I'm sure this is the Iris's will, too... If Lady Clemenceau says so, then we have no choice but to obey.
The Vichya Dominion doesn't mean to make an enemy of you all. Please, at least understand that...!
Let's leave aside what the Tribunal REALLY wants for a sec~
If we let you take all the Vichya girls away, then that means the Tribunal's fleet can move freely. Isn't that right?
Commander, might I suggest we detain them here a little longer?
I know I'd feel a lot safer knowing that we have hostages protecting us from an all-out attack.
I rack my brain over Clemenceau and the Tribunal's motives.
The Gazer threat is real and imminent. If we don't act fast, it'll be too late. There's no reason to force ourselves to fight a losing battle, either.
Say there's a traitor. Is it the entirety of the Vichya Dominion? The Tribunal? Or Clemenceau alone?
I need to shake things up a bit, so that we can get the ball back in our court.
Clemenceau's demands? She only asked for us to evacuate to safety...
"If she really means to eliminate us, then she would disable the Skybound Wall."
Sorry, she didn't say anything about the Skybound Wall...
I assume that means it would be fine to leave it up?
Kersaint doesn't seem to be lying. In that case...

options.content: "I'm counting on you to take care of the Vichya shipgirls."

scripts.say: Thank you! Umm... May the benevolent Iris bless you in the coming struggle!
Wow. You're just gonna let them leave?
"You could call this a gamble."
"If Clemenceau had some means of disabling the Skybound Wall, I would think she'd have already used it by now."
"And if the Vichya shipgirls are scheming with Clemenceau, then there would be plenty of ways for them to leave this facility safely."
Uh-huh? So that's what you think... But what if your gamble fails?
"I can give as many reasons as I want, but ultimately, the decisive one is faith in our friends."
"Vichya has never done anything hostile toward us."
"It's entirely possible that, like Marco Polo, something is influencing Clemenceau into madness."
"I'm not about to start being suspicious of innocent people just because of that."
"There's nothing more important to me than having faith in you shipgirls."
Faith, huh? Even if we decide to be hostile toward you?
"If there's a way to bring you back to us and keep you from harming people, then yes. Absolutely."
Heheheh, alright, fine. I'll go with your decision.
I'll have faith in you—as the Commander of Azur Lane, and as someone who cares so much about us.
This one concurs, too...
Very well. Whatever the situation may be, it's better to try and change the situation than it is to sit around doing nothing.
I'd still like to have faith in our Vichya friends, too.
Thank you all! Then we'd best be going...
Excuse me, Kersaint. I wish to ask you one question before you leave.
Do you believe that the Vichya Dominion is treading the path of righteousness?
I-I wonder... I wouldn't really know, but...
I envy those who get to choose their path to begin with.
With that, the Vichya shipgirls left the pavilion amidst the rumbling of the approaching Gazers.

sequence:
White Poem

<size=45>I Birth</size>
I am Klarheit.
Born from the nothingness; an image of steel given consciousness.
Born into this world, I am a weapon;
to guard the light of civilization, the purpose for which I was constructed.

scripts.say: Port - Command Office
From the mouths of lifeforms like me explained. in front stood the one they called "Commander", to whom I was to introduce myself.
Utilizing the knowledge I had gleaned; the proper way to address this person, was now to sing forth with my vocal chords.
Was it you who summoned me to this place?
Call sign recognized, class has been confirmed. They also match the info from before.
I am...
... only now did I discover, I knew not a name which I could utter.
The Iron Blood girl who introduced herself; before me, eagerly, as Z35...
It pains me to say, I still lack a name. Just for the time being, please call me Viersechs.
"Your name symbolizes your existence" ...if that is the case, what I did just now; casually assigning myself a name, may well have been a foolish thing to do.
A wave of uneasiness flowed through me; I lost confidence in this sudden name.
What do you think? Is it not apropos?
... Turns out, it was accepted easily.
To begin with, this body was granted. My calling is to follow orders, but...
Until I can discover my real name, Viersechs shall become the string that binds us.
Now, my new master, take hold of this string. Please become my light, guide me down my path!
Even if you must call me by this name; show this Klarheit, me, colors of the world.

sequence:
White Poem

<size=45>II Trajectory</size>
I am Grundfarbe, primary colors.
I am but a doll with a borrowed name, seeking the meaning of my existence.
Starting from today I've begun to serve... as secretary of the
"Commander", the one who leads all fleet operations.

scripts.say: Port - Command Office
Is it fine to put these resources here? Mm... I shall do as you have commanded.
...Humans are amusing beings after all. Even just to simply move some weapons, one must first fill out so much paperwork.

Procuring and storing our precious fuel, securing ammunition and rations, acquiring and disposing of supplies, performing maintenance on equipment, even tracking personal expenses... daily life proves to be quite cumbersome.
Having that said, this arrangement is fine. Being secretary indeed has its perks; it can sometimes provide the illusion, that I have some say in running the fleet.
Though there is much I do not understand, since serving as the secretary ship, my world has already begun to change.
Instead of thinking of vanquishing foes, the focus is now "to prevent defeat."
To not only "fight", but also to "live".
I have come to deliver the reports. Commander, please accept my humble work.
I have finished accounting for this month; the Iron Blood Dorm is barely in the red.

Conservation is of utmost import; and though destroyers accept this tenet, the heavy cruisers were hard to persuade. Battleships have always been expensive, and because of that, it's hard to cut costs.
(Receives headpats)
Though I understand the meaning of praise, I still know not the purpose of this touch.
If it will not increase what I am paid, what is the benefit of such contact?
Before I could not even understand, what purpose this "praise" was possibly for. I feel that I have moved forward a bit. Is this the "progress" of which people speak?
"Physical contact..." I still don't get it. Though my curious heart longs to find out, once the waves of battle come crashing in, such idle thoughts are quickly tossed aside.
Perhaps, I should pay more heed to my heart

sequence:
White Poem

<size=45>III Interlude I</size>

scripts.say: Port - Dormitory
What opine you all, about this outfit? I am not yet sure what clothes I should choose; thus I hope, you can offer me guidance.
This is a bit lacking... You're no Zed. You can dress in something a bit prettier, Viersechs~
That's right... You're the overly serious type, so you're likely to choose clothes that are too bland. Wouldn't asking Miss Fünf be more helpful?
I think this outfit is just fine though...
You're just as bad as Zed, so you don't count!
Ehhhhh?!
Fünf and Lebe dress way too gaudily. How about asking Lüde?
Lüde just goes along with anything, so that's out. Ah! Sechs might be the one we're looking for!
I thought Sechs' clothes were picked out by Fünf...?
Then, Sechs won't work either... In that case, I suppose the three of us should come up with something for Viersechs...
Ah! I'm so sorry, Viersechs. We got lost in our own conversation here >_<>_<
Um... this is winter attire anyway, so you'd probably need something else for summer. Uhh... let's pair this with this, and add a parka to avoid sunburns. How's that?
It looks fine to me, let's go with this then.
Jeez, everyone, you tossed Viersechs aside to prattle on with your own conversations. Shouldn't it be enough to just let her pick what she wants?
Thank you very much, I'll do as you said.
For some reason, I found it difficult; to join their discussion, delicately.

sequence:
White Poem

<size=45>IV Thought</size>
I am Mischfarbe, my thoughts intertwined.
A chiaroscuro of hued reflections, passing through the lens of society.
Today, I carry with me a package. Bearing instructions from the Commander,
I am to go to the pier of the dock, to seek the one who clads herself in ice.

scripts.say: Port - Pier
Tirpitz, I've come with commander's package.
Viersechs? Thank you, I'll take care of it.
To Tirpitz, the "Lonely Queen of the North", the battleship who clad herself in ice, I passed the package from the Commander.
Viersechs, so you're on secretary duty now? What are your plans for later?
Other than plans to return to my dorm, no other plans seem to come to my mind.
Is that so? Then, you should keep me company for a while. I still find it easier to talk with you.
Though that much is fine, I must warn you first: I struggle greatly to find what to say. If you do not mind, an ear I can lend.
Of course, that is no problem at all. I'm no stranger to talking to myself.
I heard many fascinating stories. Of words exchanged with the other factions, of the state of ships not yet completed, and of the journey of Tirpitz herself, who was beaten by our combined forces.
I heard many harrowing stories too. Of the demise of the past Iron Blood, of the "other her" from the Mirror Seas, of comrades trapped in eternal warfare, and of uncertainty towards things to come.
From time to time, I'd nod in agreement; seeing through her eyes, sharing her world view; with what words I knew, offering sympathy.
Viersechs, what would you like to do in the future?
Suddenly confronted with this question, I once again found myself without words.
What... color am I?

sequence:
White Poem

<size=45>V Interlude II</size>

scripts.say: Port - Academy
This sausage bares flavor more delicious than usual.
Graf, you too have changed, since coming to here. Your pickling technique became quite divine.
It takes a lot of focus just to keep our own ship rigging in check. You must be extra careful around girls from other factions. Viersechs, thanks for all your help.
Think nothing of it, my very close friend. It is natural to lend you my aid.
Close friends, is it? Heh... that's not something I ever expected to hear from a destroyer. But in Viersech's case... it somehow doesn't feel strange at all.
Also, I've done nothing worthy of praise. For fellow members of the Iron Blood, helping each other needs no second thought.
Even if that is the case, I do have a suggestion for you, Viersechs. Could you do something about the way you talk?
Graf, are you in a position to talk? But what exactly is wrong with my speech?
