Aren't you having some trouble fitting in with the other destroyers? Why don't you try to learn a little?
... to talk a bit more like them?
Viersechs?
I... I'll give it a shot... "okay."
Mhm. Continue to do your best. I shall be cheering for you.
Mm... Next time... we'll share lunch together as well, right?
Ah, of course.
I reached my spoon forth into Graf's lunchbox, and brought back her sauerkraut risotto. The food soon disappeared into my mouth.

sequence:
White Poem

<size=45>VI Fetters</size>

scripts.say: The combat operation has ended.
Over ten types of mass-produced vessels. Some highly-ranking enemy "Pieces." Though only classified as medium tier, the enemies proved to be difficult, for our fleet had depleted its supplies.
With all the strength I could muster, I fought.
My main cannons fired dozens of times. I did not cease my relentless attacks,  until my body was covered in wounds, until my overheated guns sputtered.
My riggings and clothes had lost their color. They had been stained gray with the smoke of war.
Port - Command Office
This report of the battle that took place... please do not forget to give it a look.
―― Why did I fight until the brink of death?
Our ships put forth the best effort we could, even as we fired our last bullets. Should the enemy know the thing called "pride", they too would feel good for giving their all.
—— Why did I choose not to retreat at all?
We strove to attain the best combat results. From the perspective of consequences, we struck a severe blow into their heart, a better outcome than a quick retreat.
—— Why did I not even treasure my life?
Though I also serve as secretary, in the end I am still but a weapon. The fact that I only exist to fight, is perhaps something that never will change.
Before the existence of this "Viersechs", I was first laid down during the Great War. I carried with me great expectations; the sign I was given, "Z46".
At this time I felt my heart and soul cry; if there was a way to escape this fate, bestow me a name and grant it meaning.
Grant upon me, not the weapon you see, but the girl that you would want me to be. Help me bring to light my reason to fight.
Grant upon me, you who I love dearly, a name that calls me back home to your side.
Please grant me my very own color.

sequence:
White Poem

<size=45>VII Pure White</size>

scripts.say: "That isn't true." Words rejecting my existence as a weapon. Words that rejected the gray I had become.
"Viersechs has her own thoughts and her desires, therefore she is human." I am not a pure being that lacks an ego. Therefore, I am not transparent.
"Viersechs should cherish herself more." Though my name is a borrowed one, "I" am still worth cherishing.
Then... I must know...
Oh my beloved, what color am I?
Please teach me the meaning of being "me." How do I become the "me" you desire?
I will change myself so I can be yours, the kind of person you'd want me to be.
—— "Viersechs, just be yourself."
I received my answer.
My color... should be Weiss.
So that you may dye me with your color, I have dyed myself an innocent white.
No matter how many times I am stained with smoke and soot, I want to become the kind of "person" who can wash away the grayness inside her heart over and over again.
With this vow I dedicate to you, the "Commander" who stands in front of me, I pledge to give all of me.
My words, my embrace, my kiss. And all of my blessings.
I hope that I can become... the pure white that you desire.

sequence:
Zara Character Story - Storia di Rosa

<size=45>Chapter 1: Good Morning</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Ah, Commander, you're awake.
How many fingers am I holding up?
Wrong. A thumb isn't a finger. I'm afraid you're not totally awake yet.
I sent you to bed last night and yet I found you passed out on your desk this morning. Were you working all night, Commander?
You can't be pulling all nighters like that.
I was getting lectured by Zara, my secretary ship.
All because I stayed up to get some work done ahead of schedule. Of course in the end I was so tired I couldn't finish it, and now I'm behind schedule...
I've told you a hundred times. I'm your secretary ship, you have to let me help you. You can't be working yourself to death like this.
Could it be... Commander, do you not trust me? You'd rather collapse from exhaustion in the dead of night? If that's really how it is...
Then I've been derelict in my duties. And I apologize profusely.
Zara suddenly flipped around to blaming herself.
But I was never one to let others take responsibility for my failings.
Really? So you'll listen to me from now on?

options.content: "We'll cross that bridge when we come to it..."

scripts.say: Hrm... that's too bad.
Then I'm off. I certainly hope to find a strong and healthy Commander when I return.
It was a close call. If I had just given in to her, who knows what would have happened...
But I couldn't spend the whole day splayed out on my desk. I had to clean myself up.
When I started to move, I felt something had been draped over my back. It was... Zara's cape?
I would have to thank her when she got back.

sequence:
Zara Character Story - Storia di Rosa

<size=45>Chapter 2: A Caring Big Sister?</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
All right, that's about all for today's missions.
Zara and I have been working together a lot more since the all-nighter incident.
While I was thankful for the support, I couldn't help but think that my job was no longer my own...
*knock* *knock*
Carabiniere, coming in!
Carabiniere knocked, entered, executed a standard 90-degree bow, and looked directly at me.
Please forgive the interruption, Commander, Chief!
What's the matter?
Well... a-actually I came to express my humblest thanks to you, Chief.
Thanks to your wise counsel, I made some new friends and had a wonderful time! Words cannot express my gratitude!
Is that all? I told you before, it was nothing. You don't need to take everything so seriously. We're friends. And please drop the Chief thing. Zara will do.
It wasn't nothing! Chief, you took me shopping for clothes, helped me try on outfit after outfit, you–
You can't be interrupting the Commander's work over every little thing, now can you? If you're not here on fleet business, it can wait.
A-absolutely, Chief! Forgive my insubordination!
Carabiniere backed out of the room, demonstrated another perfectly starched bow, and gently closed the door.
Who would've thought that she even thanks people for things like that...
Oh? Did that pique your interest? Is prodding into a young girl's private affairs one of your hobbies?
I guess I can tell you. It's no big deal anyway.
Carabiniere isn't so great at expressing herself. But she still managed to make a few non-Sardegnian friends. I guess they made plans to go out together and she was panicking over what to wear.
She came to me for advice. Apparently, Veneto told her to "just try wearing something outside your comfort zone."

My favorite part was when she showed up with a mountain of photographs of different outfits. She really tries too hard in everything. But of course, when it comes to fashion, the only way to be sure is to try things on yourself.
So I took her shopping. You know, Commander, you should have me do your look next time you've got a date.
That conversation was heading in an unproductive direction, so I steered our attention back towards work.

sequence:
Zara Character Story - Storia di Rosa

<size=45>Chapter 3: Caring for the Commander</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Now all that's left is the research and development budget...
*knock* *knock*
Pardon me~
Is that Trento?
Zara looked uncharacteristically rattled.
Ah, Commander. Just who I was looking for.
I came to thank you for taking me to try that Sakura cuisine.
Huh? All I recall was showing her to the cafeteria...
As I said, I wanted to thank you, but by the time I finished eating, you were nowhere to be found.
But then it dawned on me: why, during working hours, the Commander would have to be in the command office!
That certainly was a logical conclusion.
In any case... yay~!
Hmmff?!
Even more startling was when I found my face buried in her voluptuous bosom.
Good Commander, good Commander, you did great. I'm so proud of you~
I struggled to breathe, smothered by her pillowy chest.
Trento, why is it you feel the need to come to the office and– HMMFF?!
She pulled Zara right in with me.
And how could I forget my sweet little Zara? You helped Carabiniere make friends. You deserve a reward too! Good girl, good girl~
I should take my leave now. Good luck with work, you two~
Trento closed the door behind her as she left.
She just comes and goes like a storm, that girl... I really have a hard time dealing with her.
If she was able to even shake Zara up like this, perhaps I should be careful around her...
Commander, you seemed to be pretty happy cozying up to Trento earlier. Maybe you'd like to give mine a try?
Hmmmm?
Hehehe...
Despite being the second time today, I was no less startled to be once again be drowning in softness.
You're beet red, Commander! Now, mine or Trento's, which did you like better?
I couldn't be sure if I was in heaven, or in hell.

sequence:
Zara Character Story - Storia di Rosa

<size=45>Chapter 4: Afternoon Chat</size>

scripts.say: I brought lunch today. Apparently the Sakura girls call this kind of lunchbox a "bento".
Want to eat together?
When lunchtime rolled around, Zara and I stayed in the office to share the bento.
So, I got invited to one of those Royal Navy tea parties once, and had a pretty good time. I wonder if they have to orchestrate something like that...
Eh... they don't? And they throw one of these almost every day...? Those Royal Navy girls really are something.
Oh, you know how Cavour and Cesare are always trying to one-up each other?
They might look that way, but they're closer than anyone else.
Zara was the talkative sort. There was nothing she couldn't squeeze a conversation out of.
We spent our time discussing the fleet and her homeland, the Sardegna Empire, when suddenly...
Commander, can I ask you a question?
Gun to your head, would you rather have a hardworking girl like Carabiniere or a warm and gentle lady like Trento?
Come on, spit it out! I promise not to tell anyone. Just between you and me.
I had been placed in a difficult position.
I had no idea why, but it somehow felt like my life was at a crossroads...
So you like them more honest and hardworking, huh Commander?
But you know there are some issues with that type. Like, for example, if you're going out on a date, she might end up fretting over her outfit only to show up hours late.
At the restaurant, she could waste a few hours debating the nutritional value of each menu item. When you want to take a picture, she might end up spending hours getting the background juuuust right.
And then when it's all said and done, even though the process was kind of a slog, the two of you still had a nice time together. Hooray.
Enough about that though. Shouldn't you be tasting my steak right about now? Open up~
I didn't quite get what she was going for with that hypothetical, but the steak was pretty good...
I had to be careful not to talk with my mouth full.
So you like the caring type, Commander?
Naturally, who wouldn't want a sweet-voiced beauty telling you "everything's going to be okay" whenever you're feeling down? Who wouldn't want someone who washes away all your worries?
The only problem is, giving into that kind of gentle sweetness turns you weak. Before long, you won't even be able to fend for yourself.
I can hear Trento now. "No need to worry. Just let the Commander turn into a little baby. I can take care of everything."
Perhaps you like being babied like that? Here comes the choo-choo train, say ahhn~
It seemed like my descent into an impotent juveline form was a foregone conclusion, but the steak was really good...
I had to be careful not to talk with my mouth full.
You're an excellent naval strategist, but...
I got commanderzoned.
Even though she was playing around, I couldn't help but feel a little hurt.
Oh? Commander, if I didn't know better I'd say you were disappointed. Don't tell me... you were serious?
Don't take it to heart. No matter what happens, I will honor my promise: to bring victory and glory to your fleet. That includes serving you as your secretary ship.
Now now, I can't have my colleagues seeing you with that dejected face. You know how they talk. Open up and let me feed you some of my juicy steak. Ah~
Of course I knew it was just a joke and I shouldn't take it to heart. And the texture of the steak was really delightful...
I had to be careful not to talk with my mouth full.
Talking to you is so much fun, Commander, but we do need to be getting back to work. Let's do this again sometime!
Somehow, I felt like Zara was always two steps ahead of me.
And I can't say I liked that very much.

sequence:
Zara Character Story - Storia di Rosa

<size=45>Chapter 5: Devil's Whispers</size>

scripts.say: Port - Office
Break time, Commander. Put your work down.
Hehe... Is there anything your secretary can do for you? Just say the first thing on your mind.

options.content: Ask her to clean your ears.

scripts.say: Huh? Clean your ears? I guess I can try.
I figured this was a good way to see another side of Zara.
<size=30>Hehehe~</size>
Now then, come rest your head right here on my lap. Don't be nervous, just relax.
Ah, that's it, and put this on for me.
It was an eye mask. I didn't know what she was up to, but I decided to go along with her anyway.
Alright, here we go. Don't move, Commander~
I felt something hard and metallic press against my ear.
Zara's earpick made slow gentle circles around the edge of my ear, before gently making its way inside.
The contrast of my ear rejecting a foreign object against the tingly pleasure of the earpick sliding through my narrow ear canal was an indescribable experience.
The earpick rubbed up against the deepest part of my ear, where Zara started to slowly and gently twist it around. The tiny circular motions lightly tickled the sensitive nerves near my eardrum.
Waves of pleasure surged from my ear, washing over my brain and sending tingles out over my entire head. With my vision blocked by the eye mask, the feelings were only that much more intense.
I began to lose consciousness as I drowned in the soothing joy of Zara's ear cleaning...
Nau~ghty~
Huh?!
Her breathy whisper flooded my brain with pleasure, making every nerve from my neck up cry out in ecstasy.
I suddenly realized I had once again played right into Zara's hands. She had me trapped, completely at her mercy.
Commander, you're not allowed to fall asleep until after I'm done. Okay? Hehehe.

sequence:
Zara Character Story - Storia di Rosa

<size=45>Chapter 6: Commander's Ordeal</size>

scripts.say: Commander, since we have the day off tomorrow, how about we go shopping together?
Was she asking me on a date?
If she was, then...
I really shouldn't have given in so easily.
We've got everything Carabiniere asked for, plus Littorio's perfume... There's still cosmetics. Commander, over here~
What I thought was going to be a lovely date had turned into me hauling four huge shopping bags behind Zara.
And we need dumbbells for Cesare. Exercise equipment is over there.
Dumbbells were on the list too?!
That's all we needed to get for everybody. Thanks so much, Commander. There's no way I could've done this in one trip without you.
Oh but there is one last thing. Over here, Commander~
It was a clothing shop.
We're going to take this special opportunity to try a new look on you, Commander. Hehehe...
Zara gazed at me with devious eyes as she approached with a veritable wardrobe in her arms.
Of course you have to try them on before we know if they're any good on you. Come on, Commander, one by one, you're trying them all on!
What do you mean you're embarrassed? That's right, "tenacemente" – don't you remember my motto, Commander?
... I realized I wasn't getting out of that shop unless I did as she asked.
It felt like eons...
And with that, everything got where it needed to be.
I had a lot of fun today. Thanks, Commander.
But really, the night is still young.
How about keeping me company a while longer. You wouldn't say no to me, would you?
We'd already come this far, I figured I might as well see our date through to the end.

sequence:
Zara Character Story - Storia di Rosa

<size=45>Chapter 7: Starry Night</size>

scripts.say: All right, we're here. This is the perfect spot.
Zara had pulled me to a bench, where we sat admiring the starry sky.
Thanks again for today, Commander~ Here, I got you a sports drink.
Not to mention the part where I made you my pack mule for the day. Thanks, and sorry. Hehe, it wasn't so bad, was it?
Zara was staring directly into my eyes.
Even as dark as it is, I can see it in your eyes, Commander. I can see that dissatisfaction.
"I want to show her my strong and heroic side! I don't want to be prey that she toys with." That's what your eyes are saying. They're full of frustration that you've never succeeded.
But I love toying with you, my prey. I never get tired of it, hehe~
In the end, Zara was always two steps ahead of me. Any time I tried to resist her, she always brought me to heel.
... The stars really are beautiful. Heh heh. The night actually brings back some pretty ugly memories. But even so, I can't help but admire the way the stars twinkle.
They carry with them people's hopes and dreams, across tens, hundreds, thousands of light years out to the edge of the universe.
But you're different, Commander. You're right here with me.
The stars are cold and distant, but you're real. I can touch you.
I know I overdo it sometimes, but I really much prefer the prey caught in my traps to some smooth and confident fleet officer.
Hehe, looking into this face of yours just makes me want to tease you more.
Sooner or later, this game of ours is going to end. And we'll be right back where we started.
So...
Zara clung to my arm.
I won't be a star far off in the sky either. I'll be here with you.
Commander, I'll always be here with you.
Maybe she'd gotten too tired. Zara rested her head on my chest.
Don't you think it'd be scandalous if someone saw us like this?
But... let's keep it up... just a little while longer... okay?

sequence:
The Iron Rose Blooms

<size=45>1 Seydlitz Seems... Off</size>

scripts.say: Morning - Commander's Office
While checking a document Seydlitz gave me, I happened to spot an unusual number of careless mistakes.
It was certainly uncharacteristic of her.

options.content: "I can't help but notice a few errors here and there."

scripts.say: Oh, I'm so sorry! I'll go over it one more time!
Ugh, how could I let this happen? I put all the numbers in reverse order...
I'm sorry, Commandant. This is all my fault!
She apologized vigorously, but she clearly was not her acting her usual self.
Normally, Seydlitz would be more like...
Commandant, I'll devote every bone in my body to assisting you with your work!
The commission team has returned to port! Would you like me to check the supplies in your place, Commandant?
No problems here! Commandant, leave the rest of your duties to me!
Hah! No matter what the mission may be, I will carry it through to your specifications, Commandant!
It was certainly uncharacteristic of her.
(She's really down. What could have happened to her?)

options.content: "If anything is wrong, I'm glad to try and help."

scripts.say: Thank you! Actually, the thing is...
Yesterday, the Iron Blood dormitory cat ran away. I was so worried that I ended up searching the whole night for her...
I haven't gotten any rest, so it's a little hard to concentrate... Ugh, I shouldn't be making excuses like this.
Commandant, I sincerely apologize for causing you trouble!
Also, the kitty came back this morning, so... Basically, I just, uhh... Y'know...
Sure, she's a cat and all, but that doesn't mean she can be all lazy and self-centered. I mean, she's not Eugen!
At least let people know before you go out! That's just common courtesy!
When she came home this morning, she was filthy. She looked like she was just out partying all night, or something!
"It seems like the cat tired you out physically AND mentally."
The real problem is that she thinks she makes all the rules...
I'm going to have to teach her proper discipline. That includes coming back by curfew.
"I have some coffee, if you'd like. Why don't you rest for a while, maybe take a nap?"

sequence:
The Iron Rose Blooms

<size=45>2 Seydlitz, Gone Serious</size>

scripts.say: Taking a break from sifting through data archives, I went to the lounge to pour myself a cup of coffee.
But before I can round the corner just in front of my office, I hear a voice coming from near my doorway.
On the Commandant's orders, all visitors must produce an invitation signed by the Commandant before they are allowed in.
My, Seydlitz. You've taken to your duties quite well.
I'm honored by your praise... But I'm still not letting you in until you show your invitation!
*sigh*... Don't be so uptight. What if I told you I have urgent business with the Commander?
In that case, you would have to explain your circumstances to the Commandant...
And how do I do that without one of those invitations you mentioned, exactly?
Well, you'll have to ask in advance, and...
Before she can finish her sentence, Seydlitz falls silent. After a moment of quiet, she suddenly bursts into laughter.
Haha, I'm really going around in circles here...
Phew... I'm glad you get it now.
Okay, how about you just pass these papers on to the Commander for me? Keep it up, you little hard worker.
You, too! Good luck on your guard duty.
(I'm glad Seydlitz seems to be back in proper form.)
I waited for a moment to pass before turning the corner and greeting Seydlitz.
Ah, Commandant! Welcome back!

options.content: "Should I write an invitation to myself before I come in?"
"I don't need an invitation, do I?"

scripts.say: Commandant! D-don't laugh at my expense, please!
Even you, Commandant?!
Even I'm not that inflexible!
Though sometimes, I do worry a little...
H-huh?! You've poured a cup for me, too, Commandant?!
Thank you so much! But I'm always available to do odd jobs for you, so please ask me next time if you see fit!
(She seems a little more relaxed now. Maybe this is a good time to ask...)
I don't know if this would count, but you've been on my mind... Ack! A-ahem, I mean, nothing's wrong!
Your concern is deeply appreciated, but I'm in tip-top shape! Yep!
So she says, but for whatever reason, her cheeks appear to be slightly flushed.
(Hmm... In that case, I'll just keep an eye on her.)

sequence:
The Iron Rose Blooms

<size=45>3 Seydlitz's Friends</size>

scripts.say: I was walking through the port town along with Seydlitz.
Though, it would be more accurate to say that we're on patrol together.
(This is the perfect opportunity. I can use this chance to ask about what's been bothering her. Let's start with her relationships...)
Personal relationships? Oh, that's nothing to worry about. I'm getting along with everyone just as much as ever.

options.content: "That means you're worried about Lützow, then?"

scripts.say: W-well... I mean, she can be a little bit of a lazybones, but...
But even she hasn't done anything worth troubling you over, Commandant!
Not at all. I have utmost respect for her!
While Hipper can be difficult at times, I consider her a very trustworthy ally.
Commandant, I appreciate your concern. I really do.
But it's nothing to do with our friends. In fact, I trust them across the board. If there is a problem, I'd say it's myself...
So I'll do my best to solve it and avoid causing trouble for you, Commandant!
Besides, as long as I can faithfully fulfill my duty by your side, I'm more than satisfied!
(It doesn't seem like questioning her further will get me answers. I'll just have to keep waiting and watching...)
I happen to overhear a conversation as we pass by the outdoor patio of a nearby restaurant.
Wait?! You already have the latest monster-hunting news?!
...Oh, I see. But doesn't that make charge blades useless here?
You'll find that these occasional large targets are more than worth the effort.
Aim for its weakness from afar. That giant uses its tail for all of its attacks, so if you cut it off...
(Very intriguing. Seydlitz is listening in, too. Might as well ask what she thinks.)
Y-yes! A little...
As far as I can tell, they're discussing a new virtual gaming attraction that recently opened up in the amusement park.
I hear the monster-hunting experience it provides is like the real thing.
In the simulation, you can even ride horses and gallop through the plains.
Oh, I'd love to try it...
Umm, I occasionally do when I'm on patrol...
But I've never experienced hunting on horseback.
Oh! I'm not saying I want to try it right now, though! We haven't even finished our patrols here yet!
(I was about to invite her to go horseback riding together, but she shot that down before I could say a word.)
(And she's right. We haven't finished our patrols yet.)
(I'll have to think of a way to make her open up more...)

sequence:
The Iron Rose Blooms

<size=45>4 Seydlitz's Feelings</size>

scripts.say: As we continue our patrol–
Stop on by, nya! We've got a special sale on clothes today, nya!
You two there, come and check out our new arrivals, nya!
Lured in by Akashi's sales pitch, Seydlitz and I decide to stop by for some shopping.
Why are there maids at the door, exactly...?
Nyeheheh~ Business is booming here, so I hired temp workers, nya!
So she says. Commander, wanna come and take a look~?
"I could use an addition or two to my wardrobe. And Seydlitz..."
Ooh, I get it~ You wanna buy Seydlitz new clothes, too?
Huh? N-no, I'm fine...
(whispering) I-I suppose I should look into new clothes for future parties and the like, but...
I-I'd be happy to take you up on that, but if possible, Commandant, your input would be appreciated...!
Commandant...! Thank you! I swear, I will endeavor to go above and beyond expectations!
Good, good. Come in, nya! Commander, sit right here and wait a moment if you'd please, nya!
While waiting nearby, I can clearly hear the conversation coming from the measuring room.
(Shouldn't this place be soundproofed? Why do I hear them so clearly?)
Hmm... So you want a dress, nya? What kind would you like, nya?
Uh, what kind...? Well, I don't think the Commandant had any particular demands...
Umm, something simple and safe, I guess...?
Got it, nya. Then it's time to get you measured, nya.
Shropshire, can you take care of this for me, nya?
Will do, boss~ Stand straight first... Okay. Now, spin around... Wow. Seydlitz, I really admire your perfect posture~ But you can relax a little, y'know.
O-okay... I'm not tensing up on purpose, or anything...
You've always been the stoic kind, huh? I get it~
Forget I said anything. Anyway, Seydlitz, do you understand why the Commander is trying to buy clothes with you?
Er, I'm not sure... It came as a surprise to me, so I don't know.
But orders are orders. If that's what the Commandant wants, then that's what goes.
Hmm? I don't think it was an order, though? It's just buying clothes. You could've said no if you wanted.
B-but I couldn't refuse the Commandant's kindness...
Do I hear juicy gossip, nya?
Poor Seydlitz. You're so out of touch, nya♪
...Huh?
If the Commander suddenly offered to buy me clothes, for example, I'd say...
"Thanks for your business, nya! If you don't mind, I'll mark this as a business expense, nya♪"
Wow, I never thought of that! That's a real capitalist's brain at work!
Thank you! That's very useful knowledge!
There you go, nya! Heheh, I know lots of ways to get the Commander to spend money, nya♪
Like hiring the maids as temp labor... But I can't share any more business secrets, nya!
...I digress, nya. What is it that you want to do, nya?
What do I want? Well...
If this isn't an order, then that's all the more reason not to refuse.
The Commandant is too kind.
Whether or not there's some ulterior motive, it's up to me to see all of the Commandant's wishes satisfied.
And even if it takes doing paperwork or patrolling the part, as long as I can be with the Commandant, I'm happy.
Oh ho ho. There's your answer, nya~
Your measurements are finished, nya. Wait a little longer, and we'll be done here, nya.
After I wait a bit longer, Seydlitz and Akashi emerge from the back room.
(They must be done getting her measurements.)
I have returned from being measured, Commandant!
Commander, we expect it to be done by this time next week, nya. Look forward to it, nya!
Oh, and here's a little thank-you gift, nya. Two tickets for the new attraction at the amusement park, nya!
But it's only good for today, nya!
I-it only lasts one day?!

options.content: "We'd better not let it go to waste."

scripts.say: S-sure! I wouldn't want to waste it either!
Thus, as a result of Akashi's obvious scheming, Seydlitz and I depart to check out the new attraction.

sequence:
The Iron Rose Blooms

<size=45>5 Seydlitz in the Plains</size>

scripts.say: We visit the attraction and put on the VR headset as instructed.
Endless, grassy plains fill my field of vision, and I can't help but gasp at the surreal, dreamlike scenery.
It's so vast...
So there really are grasslands that stretch beyond the horizon, just like the ocean...
The vast grasslands are perfectly replicated from the real world, perhaps even more than perfect. Seydlitz clearly is impressed.
Commandant, the truth is... I've never seen the real grasslands in person.
As much as I've always wanted to, I only know about them from books and photos.
But I'm so happy that, real or not, I get to experience the feeling of running wildly through the plains.
The feeling of freedom, you mean?
Well, umm... Sorry, but I don't know if I can answer that yet.
I've never experienced real freedom. All my life, I've shouldered so many hopes - yours, those of my comrades...
Sometimes, Lützow insists that I must get tired of that. That I should get a hobby. But I find my life very fulfilling.
While I do, though, I also worry whether I'm properly meeting your expectations...
Before I realize it, I'm just spinning in circles endlessly. Do you ever have moments like those, Commandant?
And yet you never show a hint of hesitation... You're stronger than me, Commandant.
Of course not... I appreciate your candid response!
Commandant, thank you for hearing me out! I'll need some time to think of my own solution.
...More importantly, I spy a juicy monster!
Let's go and hunt it, Commandant!
After putting her doubts behind her, Seydlitz charges toward her prey in high spirits. I rush to follow after.
While it's impressive how quickly she can turn her mindset around, I can't help but ask myself–
(Have I been misunderstanding her concerns all this time?)

sequence:
The Iron Rose Blooms

<size=45>6 Seydlitz's Step Forward</size>

scripts.say: The sunset is beautiful... The view from a Ferris wheel makes the world look so shiny and pretty.
Is this how everything looks from inside carrier-borne aircraft?
By the way, Commandant, I heard there's a fireworks show starting soon.
Do you think they'll start right when we reach the top? I hope we'll get to see them...
After we finished scoping out the attraction, Seydlitz and I ended up coming to the Ferris wheel.
Oh, excuse me... There's something I'd like to ask you, Commandant.
The reason you brought me out today... wasn't just for patrols, was it?
U-umm... Right now, it kind of feels like we're...
Surprisingly, Seydlitz herself mustered her courage and brought up the source of her concerns herself.
Seeing that makes my lips curl into a warm smile.

options.content: "I was a little worried about you, is all."

scripts.say: I'm sorry for worrying you... But I'm fine now!
O-oh, really?! And I...
N-never mind! Forget it!
Erm, regardless of the original impetus... You and I are on a d-date, aren't we?
If this is me being presumptuous, I apologize... But if that is what you want...
If you intend for this to be a date... I'd gladly accept.
"I'd love to, but if I said it directly, I feel like you might consider it an order..."
I appreciate your concern...
Of course... All of my confusion and hesitation are making you worry unnecessarily about me.
But Commandant, if I were to be torn between two answers right now, they wouldn't be whether to reciprocate your feelings or not.
I would be torn between telling you, "I'd love to go on a date with you," and, "I love you!"
Instead of causing you so much mental anguish, I should go on the offensive!
This may be presumptuous, but Commandant, please accept my feelings—
Just as our car reaches the top of the Ferris wheel, beautiful fireworks burst in the night sky.

sequence:
The Iron Rose Blooms

<size=45>7 Seydlitz's Change of Heart!</size>

scripts.say: A week later, on my day off...
While I was thinking about the upcoming party at the port, someone opens the door to the lounge.
Of course, it was none other than–
Good morning, Commandant.
I thought you might be here, even on your day off...
(It was a good call to change into the dress the Commandant bought me. Now, I just need to...)
Th-thank you for your time! Commandant, if you'd be willing, umm... Before the party starts, maybe we could take a little walk together...?
It's been such a busy time that a change of pace might be nice, or–
C-Commandant...?
Seydlitz's gorgeous attire, so different from her usual style, completely takes my breath away.
Oh my... (*blushes*)
D-do you mean it?!
I am honored by your praise, Commandant!
You're the first person who's seen me like this... Honestly, I was worried that it didn't work on me.
It's such a relief to hear you say that!
Thank you for your evaluation, Commandant.
It took longer than usual to doll myself up, but it was worth every second!
I'm ready for the party, too. Whether you'd like a partner or a bodyguard...
No matter what you expect of me, I will do all in my power to exceed expectations!
I await your orders, Commandant!

sequence: "You know, assistant... I mean, Commander."
"I'm pretty scared of death."
"So much so I don't even wanna think about it."
"The thing that scares me the most is suddenly dropping dead."
"Just everything coming to an abrupt end while your mind is still full of thoughts from yesterday and hopes for tomorrow."
"So if I had to die, I'd want to do it on my own terms. I'd want to decide when, where, and how."
"...Obviously, I'm nowhere near as brave as you are."
"You don't come to terms with your own death just like that. It takes time."
"But when death takes me, don't mourn for me."
"Because when death comes, I'll be ready and waiting."
"When my soul passes on, my aspirations also pass on – to you."
"...What? I have too many of those for you to possibly shoulder?"
"I know you're just trying to lift the mood with a joke, but I'm serious here."
"...You really don't think you can do it without my help?"
"You're asking an awful lot from someone who'll be dead."
"But alright. I'll do what I can."
"Everything I've worked for, I leave to you. My dreams, my path, and everything I've protected."

scripts.say: I step through the door in that white space. A blinding whiteness appears and fades, then replaced by a soft light.
Next, an overpowering feeling of fatigue hits me, nearly making me fall to the floor.
I look around. I'm back at the Orthodoxy's conference venue – only now, it is dark outside.
(That's odd. Every other time I've talked to Helena in that space, only an instant would pass in reality, no matter how long we spoke.)
(This time, it feels like time has been flowing normally in reality.)
(Maybe that's why I feel so tired... I must've been standing here for ages.)
(I'm still concerned about the source of the jamming... but I won't be able to get anything done if I don't clear my head.)
There you are, mysterious assistant! You're late!
I've been waiting AGES for you!
I open the door to the guest room and find a dimly lit room with a hooded girl inside.
She is lying on the bed, rhythmically hitting a pillow with an open palm.
You're the slowest slowpoke who's ever slowed!
What took you so long to leave the venue?!
(Who in the world...)
What does it look like? I'm WAITING for YOU!
I'm Miss D!
I walked in! Your security is so lax I didn't need to sneak or anything!
Oh, by the way? I found a security hole of yours and fixed it! You should be thanking me!
Someone was spying on you from extrastellar space! Bet you didn't know that, moron!

options.content: "Extrastellar space"? And what do you mean, "spying on me"?

scripts.say: (Is she talking about that space Helena created with the Tower's power?)
(Speaking of spying, this girl is in the guest room Helena mentioned. She also knows about our communications...)
(Oh boy... Her "fixing the security hole" caused the interference that trapped me in the virtual space, didn't it?)
What? You ran late because my fix trapped you in there?
I see how it is. You use that as a romantic dating spot. Sorry about that!
(...I did what?)
But the thing is, I only cut the connection path. I didn't mess with anything local!
If you could get in, why didn't you get out?

options.content: I didn't know HOW to get out.

scripts.say: So you weren't able to...
If you couldn't get out, why did you go in?

options.content: I didn't know HOW to get out.

scripts.say: Wait, did you not go in by your own will?
Ugh. This is getting so confusing!
Forget it! You're here, and that's what matters! I've waited long enough, so let's go already!
To go whale-hunting!
(Whales? What do they have to do with anything?)
(Wait, I can't let myself be caught up in her flow. I need to get some answers out of her–)

options.content: By the way, who's the "mysterious assistant" you mentioned?

scripts.say: You, duh! YOU are Aoste's mysterious assistant!
Because you are! You're Aoste's mysterious assistant!
(Wait, so she even knows about my future "self"?)
(Everyone who knows anything about that has only alluded to it in vague terms... but she just straight-up said it.)
(Let's play along and see where it gets me.)

options.content: How do you remember who I am?
I'm surprised. Everyone else has forgotten who I am.

scripts.say: I just do! What do you want me to say?
That's because they're stupid! They've forgotten me, too!
Look, enough Q&A! No more of that until we've caught the whale!
I'm not gonna wait one more minute! We're leaving NOW!
Without any warning, Miss D walks right up to me.
Before I can get a word in, she musters an ungodly strength for her size and drags me outside.
She leads me around the Iris city streets, pulling me by the sleeve of my uniform.
I'm following her willingly because, despite my first impression, I don't sense any ill intent from her.
(Also because I have to know who this girl is and what she wants with me.)
The time has come, the whale has met its match! La-la-la, la-la-laaa!
This time for sure we're bringing home a catch! La-la-la, la-la-laaa!
She's been in a good mood ever since we left the guest room. She sings a tune, skipping and jumping as she goes down the street.
Passersby should be turning their heads at us... but they aren't.
(It's strange – she's practically screaming for attention, yet nobody seems to notice.)
(Sure, it's late, but people are still on the streets. Why isn't anyone looking our way?)
(It feels like nobody can even see us...)

options.content: Is it just me, or does nobody else see us?

scripts.say: I couldn't bring you outside if they did, idiot!
I'll clue you in after we've caught the whale!
We keep walking until we arrive at a park, far away from the main venue.
The girl is still singing and skipping along without a care.
(I've got to ask...)
To the Gate of Avalon!
Huh? Are you talking about Scapa Flow?
You're not suggesting we WALK all the way over there, are you?
If we have to!
I'm afraid that's not quite practical, Miss D.
However, Commander, rest assured that there is a better way to get there.
Richelieu's sudden appearance leaves me speechless.
Right! The train! Let's take Liz's train!
...Liz? And what's this "train" you're talking about?
And... why are you here, Richelieu?
I apologize for using such an unorthodox method of extracting you from the venue.
But, everyone has their eyes on you. Miss D here was the only person capable of sneaking you out undetected.
(Judging from how serious her tone is... This must be a matter of grave importance.)
This must be a highly sensitive topic, then, if you're not even able to discuss it in your own capital.
Yes. No amount of precaution is excessive for what we have to talk about.
After all, those who would seek to destroy our branch are everywhere, and we don't even know how many more lurk in the shadows.
(...I did what?)
Allow me to cut to the chase. The Royal Navy and the Orthodoxy are currently preparing a joint operation.
Not here, mind you. Our objective lies beyond our own branch.
If we don't do something about it, it will one day have tremendous consequences for our world and everything we want to protect.
And you want me to help – correct?
Correct. We need to move to a new location before we can tell you more. This place is not safe.
Please come with me to Camelot's gate at Scapa Flow.
Queen Elizabeth will give you all the details once we're there.
I should state upfront that Naval HQ has no idea about this operation and that it is extremely dangerous.
You can decide whether or not you'd like to help after you've heard what Queen Elizabeth has to say.
Should you decide to decline our request, I will see to it that you're brought back as soon as possible.
I squint at Richelieu and make out two figures standing behind her – Belfast and Sheffield.
(Aha. Looks like the operation in Antarctica brought these factions closer than ever.)
(I wonder what they've been discussing. I should ask about it later.)
Before you speak to Elizabeth, let me introduce you to your escorts. They will also be part of the operation.
Richelieu makes a hand gesture, and her Iris comrades step forth out of hiding.
This one is battleship Alsace – Sacrament of the Unified Orthodoxy, an unreachable dream, and guardian of the Holy See.
I'm Mogador, judge of the Tribunal. I've been dying to show myself to you. Heheh...
I am Brennus, a cruiser and a Templar Knight. Well met, Swordbearer.
Name's Fleuret – Le Hardi-class destroyer. Nice meeting you, Commander!
I-I'm Épée. Like Fleur said, nice to meet you...
They have all been carefully chosen for their battlefield competence and ability to protect you.
The Tribunal may have a reputation for working behind the scenes, unlike those present at the venue now...
But I assure you, these ladies can be relied upon in a fight.
(Templar Knights, members of the Tribunal, and even Alsace... It's a small team, but their skill more than makes up for that.)
(Clemenceau's cohorts are here, so you'd think she herself would be, too.)
(She probably decided to let Richelieu do the talking. Clemenceau would so do that.)
I shoot a look at each member of the team, then turn my eyes back on Richelieu and the Royal Maids.
Richelieu gives me a solemn look, waiting for an answer from me, while Belfast gives me a small nod.
Then there's Sheffield. The look in her eyes screams, "don't ask questions, just come with us."
(Elizabeth, Richelieu, and even Clemenceau are all on board with this.)
(Moreover, their commitment to secrecy speaks volumes to the importance of whatever this is about.)
(Then there's Miss D who knows what the future has in store. There's so much she could tell me.)
(Most important of all, they need me. I have to hear what they have to say.)
Miss D waves her hands excitedly, and a train appears in the woods.
Get in! We're going to Camelot to catch the whale!
Alsace, Mogador, and Brennus leave the train car while the rest of us stay behind.
Little by little, I can feel the approaching hostile presence become palpable.
Commandeeer! We've entered car 3 and I can see something.
There's this... black mist coiling around, and some kind of white thing floating in the air.
Hoo boy, they have an intense presence. I see why Miss D was terrified now.
If fear had a smell, this place would reek of it.
The sound of death drawing near. A quiet yet intense noise...
I'm going to temporarily deactivate my emotion module. That should make me, uh, not afraid!
Despite the considerable distance between us, the aura of death is clear as day.
An inexpressible pressure leaks through the cracks in the door, acting on my body as though it were a physical thing.
(Rotting and damp – the stench of overwhelming death. Yeah, Mogador, you hit the nail on the head with those words.)
I'm scared! I'm scaaared!
No, no, nooo! How did something so terrifying get inside the train?!
I'm not scared, I'm not scared, I'm not scared...
My friends are here, so I'm not scared...
Don't kid yourself! You're trembling as much as anyone else!
I-I can't help it... I'm so scared I feel like I could die!
Me toooooo!
Whatever's coming, it's bad. BAD.
Don't know how long I can hold out against it... but I'm not giving up without a fight.
Commander, fall back to car 6! I'll hold the line somehow!
(This is getting dire already...)
Hey, Commander, do we start attacking yet?
(I don't doubt their combat ability, it's just that we'll suffer serious casualties if we end up picking a fight with an Arbiter.)
(But what's the alternative? There are only so many cars left to retreat to...)
Umm, the enemy has entered car 4. They'll get the first strike in if we don't do something now.
I look through the glass of the connecting door. There, in car 4, I see it – something floating in the air, covered in a black mist, coming straight toward me.
Hahh...
(God dammit. Better to do SOMETHING than to just sit here.)
Mogador! Open fi–
Wait! Stop, stop, stop!
Just before I can issue the order, Miss D jumps in front of me and interrupts me.
I know now! I know who the intruder is!
A faker! She's a faker!
A faker, faker, faker!
She's a stupid darn faker!
Calm down. What do you mean, "faker"?
It's all her fault I couldn't catch the whale! And she only got this far because she's a faker!
She didn't force her way inside the train! She imitated my whole concept and fooled her way in!
She... imitated your concept? So she's, like, the same as you?
So if you're an Arbiter, that means this enemy is one, too... But what's her name?
Who cares about her name?! What matters is you'll die if you fought me, and you'll die if you fight her!
Get out of there! Ruuun!
We cannot abandon the Swordbearer's mission. Furthermore, what solution is running away?
If we can't stop her, we'll have to abandon the train entirely...
That's what I'm saying! Screw the train and go to the Martyrium!
No, you can't be serious! How would we even go there in the first place?
One could materialize her rigging for you all to ride... However, the navigability of this space is highly uncertain.
Without air, one's engines cannot run – moreover, the Commander will asphyxiate.
Don't be dumb! I'm not talking about going out THERE!
The Martyrium was manifested using the 7th car, remember? It has to be connected to the 6th car!
We'll go through the door and end up there! Come on, get back here now!
Wait, that's how it works?
One's thought processor is beginning to overheat...
That sounds like a stretch, but maybe she's right?
There's no time to argue! Assistant, tell them to retreat NOW! Do it, do it, do it!
If the car connects straight to the city, why didn't Elizabeth just use that route?
Because she's a stupid moron and you're not!
Fleuret, go to car 4 and pick up Alsace's team! We'll link up in car 6 and retreat through the door to the Martyrium!
There we go! Run! Run, everybody!
Holding Miss D's hand, I step through the door into the 7th car. Suddenly, I am thrust into nothingness.
My sense of time, space, and even self all become hazy, and it's like a mighty force is pulling me apart.
Thought by thought, it feels like my mind is becoming one with this endless void.
Have you ever thought about death? About what it means to these girls? It is neither an end, nor a release for them.
Just as it feels like I'll disappear, a familiar voice speaks to me.
For better or for worse, they will never truly die as long as they're remembered by people.
Death, furthermore, is not a one-way trip for them as it is for us.
"Dead" and "living" are no more than states of being to them.
Every time they live, and every time they die, a little more information is simply added to their names.
From a dialectic perspective, death is neither good nor bad for them. It's a neutral concept.
Remember this, it's important – they form a collective of countless fragments of data until they are given individual bodies.
It is possible to replicate the individual offshoots of this collective. I gave this power to Death.
...Hey! Don't just stand there!
(That was Miss D's voice... but something's off. Is she not aware of what she just said?)
Hey! Moron! Way to go getting separated and freaking everyone out!
...What? You thought I brought you here?
No, obviously not! Why'd you even come here? You'll literally fall apart if you stay any longer!
Take my hand! I'll get you out!
I grab hold of Miss D's hand. The blank void vanishes with a snap, giving way to golden light.
I stand in a city carved from marble, arches of gold spanning overhead. The scent of the Iris countryside fills the air, as does faint, serene cathedral music.
(This is the Martyrium... I made it.)
Thank heavens you're okay, Commander! You just disappeared on us, and I thought you were gone...
Hah, you're naive! Nobody goes gone if I decide so!
Another miracle to the Swordbearer's name. It's a relief that you're unharmed.
Sorry if I scared you all. I just got a bit lost.
"A bit" lost! You're the ONLY one who did! You're such a moron!
Such insolence! You know, one's databanks say that those who call others morons are usually morons themselves!
Sure, moron! I only call morons morons!
Lies! One would never accept that the Commander is a moron!
Ugh... What is this, the playground? Stop arguing like a pair of kids.
They'll tire eventually. More importantly, where'd the intruder go?
I think we shook her off.
I love getting off– I mean, shaking off an enemy.
Also, now we know concepts can ignore things like, you know, physical distance between two points in space...
(Technically, we're in a Mirror Sea, so maybe that's how this miracle was possible. I wonder if the Sirens' teleporters and artificial fog function in a similar vein...)
Ugh... Whatever! The assistant ISN'T a moron! There! Happy now?
One has won this argument!
Alsace triumphantly places her hands on her hips and basks in her strategic victory.
Good. Now, Miss D, will that enemy come after us?
"That enemy"... I hate how that sounds! She needs a name!
Something like... I know! Death's Shadow!
Yeah! I don't care what she thinks, we're gonna call her that!
(Is this another case of "the importance of a concept"?)
Okay. Is Death's Shadow going to come after us?
Anything I can do, she can do! Which means yeah, she will! Unless she's a total moron!
But forget about her, there's something more important! We've reached the Martyrium, remember?
And what are we here to do? Catch the whale! Whale tiiime!
Miss D points a finger at the whale swimming through the sky as she jumps around ecstatically.
But, before we can catch the whale...
What?! The enemy breached the train's defences because their concepts are one and the same?!
That does explain why we couldn't detect an intrusion from far away... The fact we can't detect her now either likely means she moved elsewhere.
We just got back inside the train. Needless to say, there is no trace of... "Death's Shadow" to be found anywhere.
Elizabeth, Miss D called you a moron earlier for not using the direct route through the 6th car's door.
Did she, now? No sweets for her for a month.
Why?!
Did you consider WHY we didn't use that route? Because it significantly raises the risk of a pursuer following us into the train.
Oh...
Yes, now you know. Stay put and we'll be there shortly.
No, don't come here! You weren't supposed to be here to begin with!
Come again? So what is your plan – to confront Devil without us?
Nuh-uh! No confrontations! I'm gonna catch the whale then bail!
We can't let it get away again! You've gotta stay there and make the Mirror Sea and the concept stable!
Make it super-duper stable! Then it will be trapped in here!
Out of the question! We'll run out of resources if we make it any stabler!
Or what, are you seriously telling us to use ANOTHER train car?!
You can always turn it back! If the whale gets away now, who knows if we'll ever catch it!
Tsk. So be it. Nothing ventured, nothing gained, we suppose.
I'm with Miss D on this. Please do it.
Very well. We shall support you as best as we can from the train.
In the worst-case scenario, we'll come and rescue you. Now, off you go. Enjoy the Martyrium.
You heard her, everybody. Let's go catch that whale!
With Elizabeth's cooperation, our team starts heading toward the whale.
At first, we walked, until we realized that the "clouds" around us had identical properties to water. So the girls deployed their riggings.
We should be able to reach the whale by traveling from cloud to cloud.
Before we do that, though, there's an issue that needs to be resolved.
*sniff sniff*... The Commander was right. Somebody's up ahead.
What? But one's sensors aren't detecting anything.
I think they're using cloaking technology...
Yeah. That's the Ashes' modus operandi.
Signals detected! They are approaching from opposite directions! Requesting orders!
(Considering our previous encounters, they probably just want to talk.)
Let's see if we can solve this with words. Stay on your guard, but don't fire the first shot.
I'll try to reason with them.
The Ashes acknowledge our non-hostile intent and turn off their cloaking devices, showing themselves.
I'm Wichita, this is Kimberly. We're with the Ashes. You don't look the least bit surprised to see us.
No. We knew you were here before we even set foot in the Martyrium.
Set foot in the what now? Oh, you mean this place. You created it, didn't you?
You could say that.
I want to know who exactly. Which one of you did it?
I'm afraid I can't tell you. Let's change the topic. What do you say to a cease-fire while we're here?
Why?
I know your Hiryuu and Ark Royal. I've fought side by side with them. Friedrich from our timeline is also working with you.
Ahh. So you're the people from test site beta.
You're test site beta? That explains a lot.
We know all about you. Had a big battle a while back, didn't you?
(Big battle? Is she talking about the near-superimposition event? They know more than they let on.)
(Assuming Friedrich has been feeding them intel, maybe I can get these two to agree to a temporary alliance.)
I appreciate what you've done for Friedrich. How's she been holding up?
Just fine. She's working on something big back at our hideout.
You sure seem to know a lot. I'm guessing you're the Commander I've heard so much about.
In the flesh.
Figures. Hiryuu was right – just seeing ya brings back fond memories.
Know what I mean, Kimberly?
Yes. I'm... reminded, too.
A lot has changed since you and Enterprise met. Been making some odd decisions lately. Her letting in Friedrich was one of 'em.
Have to admit, though, she's been doing good.
Tell ya what, I'll bite – who are you, exactly?
Good question. You're probably familiar with my future self, whereas I'm not. I'd like to know more.
In fact, that's why I'm here. To find out more.
I've already told you who you are! You're the mysterious assistant!
Never heard of a "mysterious assistant" before. Ring any bells, Kimberly?
Not sure. If I have any memories of such a person, they're buried deep.
I'll ask Enterprise later back at the base. You there, the shortie – how do you know the "assistant"?
I have a name! It's Miss D!
Sure ain't a name I've ever heard before. You got something to hide?
None of your business! All you need to know is my name is Miss D!
I don't trust that rat. She's obviously a damn Antiochus! Bet she's a spy who's infiltrated test site beta!
YOU'RE a spy!
Ya hear that? She didn't deny being an Antiochus!
She's an Arbiter. Arbiter XIII: Death, to be precise.
Bullshit. I've fought Death more times than I can remember and that sure ain't her.
Ya see that whale in the sky? THAT'S Death.
Huh?! You're a big fat moron! The faker duped you, moron!
Call me a moron again and you're getting it, you little shit.
Eek!
She's just a kid. Don't threaten her.
Sure, she's a kid, and kids need to be put in their place.
Anyway... If that half-pint is with you people, that changes things. We'll leave the Antiochus alone as long as she doesn't mess with us.
We've still gotta do something about that spatial impact event, though. Just hope we won't have to fight each other over it.
That's what you came here for, right? To measure it?
In a way. Our goal here is to catch the whale. Getting data on the event is just a side objective.
Really, huh? We didn't know about the whale 'til we got here. Guessing you knew about it from the start.
That thing is a giant database with fins, you know.
Interesting. So, what's your stance on us working together on this?
There's an Arbiter – Devil – somewhere in this place, and I don't think she's just a vessel. She's our enemy, and yours as well.
Speak of the devil, as they say... Yeah, we detected her as soon as we stepped inside the... "Martyrium."
But here's the thing. We work best alone.
Best I can do is agree to keep out of your hair if you keep out of ours.
(I almost forgot the Ashes is filled with lone wolves. If that's how they want it...)
That's fine by me. Good luck on your task.
Yeah. Same to you.
The Ashes and we go our separate ways, and we resume our climb toward the whale.
However, we soon see that someone has gotten to the whale before both us and the Ashes.
KABOOOM!
The whale is being attacked by what appears to be drones!
It's a sizable swarm as well, assuming the form of a net to catch it.
Those things look familiar... Oh, I remember! They're Devil's drones!
Nooooo! Devil, you big moron! Be gentle! You're gonna kill my whale!
No, wait, it's gonna run away before anything else!
See?! It's already getting ready to leave!
...Wait, what?! Great! The faker's gotten her hands on a new weapon!
As the whale is surrounded by drones, its body suddenly begins to glow blue.
Every drone touched by the light swiftly loses control and falls to the ground. The whale then turns its dorsal fin and starts swimming for the Martyrium's center at speed.
It reaches the limit of the city's ring, touching the boundary. A spatial distortion occurs, and the whale once more slips off into space.
Dammit. It got away again.
Elizabeth! Pick up, Elizabeth!
Use your train to expand the Martyrium! Draw the whale toward us!
Uggghhh...
Concept conversion, car 6. Broaden the horizon of death, materialise the unseeable, and manifest its form!
A radiant light burst forth from the void once more.
The Mirror Sea's concept is reinforced, expanding the Martyrium with a second ring furnished with gold and marble and arches just like the first.
There, in the air above the second ring, the whale appears again.
The Martyrium grew even bigger and brighter than before!
Let's see that whale try to run away NOW!
Incredible. We've unfolded so much space, and yet there's still more...
One wonders what terrifying creature caused such a massive spatial distortion...
Doesn't matter! All that matters is that it doesn't get away again!
You can't let it happen a third time!
We said we'll do it, remember? Believe us, we won't let it flee.
Thank you! You're nice, Elizabeth!
Come on, assistant! We've got to get back to catching the whale!
How, though? There's no connecting path to the new ring.
We weren't exactly built for jumping across clouds, so...
Not that you could, anyway. Just like how each train car is independent of the next, the rings are independent of each other.
Remember how certain Mirror Seas have rules for entering or exiting them? These work in a similar way.
In short, the method that worked on the first ring won't work on the second. We must find a new way inside.
It's fine! The train cars are connected, so we can go in the same way as we did last time!
Just come with me and we'll get there! Don't worry about the conceptual rule!
We should at least know the rules before we start ignoring them. What's the conceptual rule we're dealing with?
What do you think? Death! Death is the whole shtick of this place, remember?
Like I said, don't worry about it! Just come along!
The whale isn't gonna wait for us! Hurry!
Somewhere, in the Martyrium...
KABOOOM!
Impressive... I recover and reinforce my body more and more, and every time you knock me down regardless.
You're no ordinary Ashes. You're two of its founding members, are you not?
Inhibiting your fear of death and instantly reviving... Just a bunch of tricks.
I've seen people like you do it a million times.
I've seen how their minds deteriorate 'til they're just one step away from losing it completely.
So how the hell have you kept your sanity?
Just who the hell are you?
KABOOOM!
Blathering away even as you barrage me... You really are a seasoned warrior.
Sadly for you, my secrets are staying with me.
Look at that new ring. They've anchored twice now, creating two Mirror Seas, and still that which is hidden hasn't been revealed.
Whoever caused this spatial fluctuation wields unimaginable power. How I wish I could meet them.
KABOOOM!
You must think you're real hot shit, looking away during a battle with the Ashes.
I told ya – I've seen your tricks a million times. You think you're invincible?
I'm not, and besides, death is only another way to the next destination.
Haven't you realized what concept rules this space and what rules are woven through it?
Ahahah! Haven't even thought about 'em until now.
Been a long while since I met someone with your take on death. The Antiochus must really love test site beta.
It's not that I laugh in the face of death. Death is a prerequisite to entering the second Mirror Sea.
Death is the concept that rules this space. It is where all living things end up.
Moreover, the very concept of death has been redefined here. You literally cannot kill me, no matter what you do.
I don't need to kill you. I can just tear you to shreds.
Even if you won't die, your wounds ain't going anywhere and you'll eventually run out of energy.
Maybe I can't reduce you to dust – or maybe I can. Only one way to find out.
KABOOOM!
Your birth was never meant to be. Perish.
Now you fancy yourselves the arbiters of who gets to be born, do you?
Tell me, how many people have you killed?
All those souls, snuffed out – did those deaths get you what you wanted?
Shut up. Every little rat like yourself dead is one less problem for the universe.
Don't think I don't know where your power comes from, who you're colluding with, and what you're planning.
Scum like you don't get to preach morality!
KABOOOM!
I'd hoped to make you doubt yourselves, but alas...
You leave me no choice but to grant you your wish.
Our final destination may be the same, but I'll give you a small nudge to get there!
Somewhere, in the Martyrium...
Two types of rings... A city?
A new area has appeared. Fancy that.
Assuming that death is the requirement for entry...
––I guess I'll just die.
KABOOOM!
Away from the Martyrium, between the gate and the train...
Inside what can only be called a battleship, a blue-haired girl stared at a monitor, a gentle expression on her face.
I wasn't expecting those meddlers to be THIS powerful.
I had to call on the Tower's power to finally get here...
And now, they've just stopped.
Maybe they're afraid to face me. I hope so, at least.
Whoever you are, wherever you are...
I will find you and destroy you for hunting the Commander and getting between us!
Glowing blue fragments shot through the air, lighting up the vast interior of the ship.
70% of the matter folded up by the spatial impact event has materialized, divided across two Mirror Seas...
Looks like I'm late, but not TOO late.
The Commander is riiight... there.
Oh? Wichita and Kimberly are here, too?
Change of plans. Abort the recycling process and engage the overwrite. Initiate plan E.
Helena, exiting the ship now.
I'm here again...
I grabbed Miss D's hand and was sent back to the void again.
It stretches on endlessly in all directions. Time and orientation mean nothing here.
Unlike last time, however, my consciousness isn't being wrestled from me. It's like I'm in a protective bubble, augmenting my perception of my surroundings rather than weakening it.
This raised awareness lets me detect something amongst the nothingness.
Embracing death, one after the next... Is this what you chose?
Then "I" made the correct choice.
A woman's voice devoid of emotion. Close, yet distant, coming closer, yet getting further away.
Someone is speaking to me through the darkness.
Life comes from nothing, and to nothing death brings it back.
Oblivion is the answer to all.
You would be wise to accept your demise.
It's better than fighting in vain somewhere between the beginning and the end.
(She can't be far, but I have no idea where she is.)
(All I know is that she's watching us... Watching the Martyrium.)
(Who is she? And what is this place?)
Really?
Then what if death didn't mean returning to nothingness?
(Is that... Miss D? She sounds older, somehow.)
What...?
You can hear "my" voice?
Who are you?
Mmgh... *gasp*! No, who are YOU? What are you doing with the assistant?!
"Assistant"?
You heard me! Assistant, why are you here AGAIN? I'm telling you, you WILL get torn apart!
Miss D points to where I am. This finally alerts the other person to my presence.
Someone else... is here?

options.content: I wasn't trying to eavesdrop, I swear.

scripts.say: Who are you people? Why have you come here?
Long story short–
Shut up, you! There's no time to talk!
Don't make me repeat how dangerous this place is! Come along!
And you, whoever you are! You coming with us?
"Me"?
No, "I'm" afraid "I'm" staying here.
What do you mean, "no"? Do you LIKE being in this dark, dreary place? Suit yourself, weirdo!
Assistant, we're going back to the Martyrium! Hang on tight and don't get lost a third time!
As the light recedes, I find myself standing on a beach at sunset.
(What the hell is this place? Wasn't she bringing me back to the Martyrium?)
One has spotted the targets! Miss D and the Commander are uninjured!
You had me worried, Swordbearer. You lagged behind us again.
This ONLY happens with you every time we warp! If you're doing it on purpose, cut it out!

options.content: If this isn't the Martyrium, what is it?

scripts.say: I have no clue, sorry. We just moved on forward, and the next thing I know, here I am.
All I can tell you is it's an island with some decently-sized coral reefs.
Hey, Alsace – you sure this place didn't come from your imagination?
One never imagined any sort of island, let alone this particular one!
Okay, then why are we here? Did you make a wrong turn or something, Miss D?
I don't make mistakes, full stop! Tell them, Elizabeth!
Miss D did not botch the jump. Your coordinates are, in fact, inside the Martyrium.
Specifically, you're in the second ring that we manifested using our sixth train car. The concept that rules there is still death.
You're still with us, Elizabeth! I thought our comms would be down.
Your phrasing suggests this is a regular occurrence for you.
Worry not. That will not happen as long as we're backing you up.
(The improved communicator probably helps, too. In any event, I can better deal with emergencies this way.)

options.content: Thanks. I'm glad we have you.
Thank you, Your Majesty. META or not, you can always be counted on!

scripts.say: Yes, and you should be grateful for it!
Are you SURE this is the Martyrium? It looks nothing like the outside.
The second ring looked, you know, just like the first one. Gold, marble, yadda yadda.
Because the inside isn't the outside! It's a stand-alone space, just like the train cars!
Does it also confuse you how those look different on the inside, or what?
But these two are COMPLETELY different! A train's interior still looks like a train's interior even if you redecorate it!
I mean... Yeah, I guess two manifestations of the concept of death shouldn't look THIS different.
I've got it! The concept probably got all jumbled up 'cause there's too many people here!
This isn't JUST Alsace's idea of death – it's mashed together with someone else's, too. Several people's, in fact!
That's the only explanation for why it looks so different!
(Then if this is a mix of concepts, does that mean it's closer to what the space originally looked like?)
Hang on... It doesn't just LOOK different, it functions differently, too!
Time is flowing in here!
Uh, isn't time a constant? Because it doesn't really start or stop?
I'm not talking about OUR time, moron! I mean time is flowing for this space!
Elizabeth didn't make it like that when she materialized the Martyrium.
She didn't, because all we needed was a simple foundation. She made an unchanging space!
But this place is different. The concept of time has been added to it.
That means this isn't a representation of static death anymore – it represents fluid death!
Come again? So, like... this space will change as time goes on?
Yeah! Exactly that!
Which means I have no idea what's coming!
Be that as it may, death is still death. Whatever will happen, it will involve death.
You're not wrong!
(So it's like a videotape? A tape showing the process of someone dying... Or maybe, of this world dying.)
Waves lapping at the beach. Tropical plants up on a small hill. It looks like any old island across the Pacific.
However, one thing sets it apart – the building off in the distance.
(The exterior is a little different from how I remember it, but the silhouette and location match...)
(That's it. It's the Samos Marine Research Institute from the alpha timeline!)
(If my guess is right, then this is a recording of the death of someone from that timeline – or of the "death" of this space.)
Th-this place creeps me out...
It looks so calm and peaceful, but death is around the corner...
You needn't be so afraid. Death is merely the rule that governs that space and the means to get in, out, and around it.
Dying in there, so to speak, does not spell your literal death. That would only be a concern if the concept were to engulf you.
Apropos of nothing, we checked again and have determined that there is STILL more space to unfold, if you can believe that.
Know that if you need to pursue the whale further, you can use death to get to the next space.
A-are you suggesting actually having a brush with death?
One would much prefer to travel using the train cars!
Death won't mess with you as long as I'm here. Besides, I have a better idea!
We'll just catch the whale right here and now!
Great idea! Only problem is, I don't see the whale anywhere. It's probably run off again.
Nuh-uh! I know it hasn't! It's just hiding somewhere nearby!
Somewhere like... Aha! The sea!
That's GOT to be where it is!
Ready or not, we're going swimming!
Just a second, Miss D. Don't you recognize this island? And more importantly, that building over there?
I point to the research institute for her.
(If she's an Arbiter, she has to know the place Dr. Aoste did his research.)
Oh, you mean the Marine Research Institute?
Yeah, I remember it. I think it was my house. Or yours. Or both of ours. Maybe.
"Maybe"?
I'm not sure, okay?! It's just a gut feeling!
All my important memories are stored inside the whale! I won't remember until we catch it!
How come YOU remember being here, anyway?
"Remember" isn't really the right word. It's too much to explain right now. Can we just please investigate the institute first?
Wait, you recognize this place?
I do. It's Samos Island, located in the Bermuda Sea. Well, Samos Island from the future.
From the alpha timeline? You mean to say that this space was built with data from there?
Fiiine, we'll do as you say, assistant. We'll investigate the institute and THEN go catch the whale!
We walk to the institute, my memory of the route guiding us.
It's the same place I went in the Reality Lens and the same place Kronshtadt and her team described, yet stark differences remain.
There are no shops, no stalls, and no facilities catering to tourists. They've all been replaced by defensive installations and barricades.
The mask of peace has come off, revealing the island's true nature as a military base.
All of a sudden, sirens start to blare.
An alarm. Who carelessly tripped the security system?
One's sensors are detecting nothing... They are working, before you ask.
Wasn't me. I'm the one who's been switching off all the systems.
Since when? I had no idea you were doing that!
You Tribunal people scare me...
I don't think any of us tripped it. The alarms are going off across the whole island, and I don't think they activated just to arrest us.
But then who did? One does not understand.
An enemy fleet has appeared 50 nautical miles northwest. It seems they're heading your way.
A fleet? Can you ID them?
They're corrosion entities.
You mean those things that the black tornadoes spew out and cannot be analyzed?
If you mean corrosion phenomena, yes, but they can manifest through other means.
Remember, they are literal embodiments of corrosion.
As you said, they cannot be meaningfully analysed even up-close.
Or, rather, you CAN, but what you perceive changes slightly each time.
You also cannot capture them, and they don't leave wrecks behind when destroyed. It's as though they don't physically exist.
In a way, they don't. They're shadows projected from a different dimension. Imperfectly, at that.
The data loss caused by the projection process is in fact the reason why they appear as blurs you can't perceive properly.
Think of them as corrupted data. The fact that they're there means the space you're in is being corroded.
Now, it looks like we're dealing with... What? The Revolutionary Front?!
Listen up! Those entities come from the data present in that space!
What do you mean?
Just tune in to the frequency we just sent you! Their fleet is broadcasting a message to the island!
This is the Revolutionary Front's AO Sector Fleet. We hereby issue an ultimatum to Samos Island.
Hand over the individuals behind the attack on the freighter Poltava, disarm your Enforcers, and immediately destroy all artificial intelligence laboratories on the island.
If our demands are not met in three hours, we will achieve these objectives by force.
It is apparent that Samos Island has become a breeding ground for corruption owing to the Oceanic Federation's policy of neglect.

It is home to experiments – especially on weaponized artificial intelligence – that have never received safety assessments nor been held to ethics guidelines, all in the name of "scientific progress."
These people have put guns in the hands of robots and given the power over life and death to computer programs.
It is exactly that which led to this tragedy. You cannot entrust human lives to machines.
Artificial intelligences armed with weapons are both uncontrollable and extremely dangerous, and the attack on the Poltava proved this.
If these evil machines are left to roam free, it will be the end of humanity.
(Are they serious? They'll capture the island by force if necessary?)
(They mentioned artificial intelligences and Enforcers... That means the Antiochus, Dr. Aoste's project.)
(Then there was that attack on a freighter. They were vague on details...)
(Seems safe to assume that the Antiochus struck the Poltava and hurt innocent people.)
(In other words, they threatened the safety of the world's oceans, prompting the Revolutionary Front to retaliate.)
Miss D, can you remember what this memory is about?
No, not a thing! But it's obviously bad! Bad and I don't like it!
...We are in agreement there.
Sounds like both the Eagle Union and the Royal Navy are involved with this island.
Those demands were pretty crazy... They want the scientists to hand over those people, disarm their units, and destroy their lab all in three hours.
You could do maybe two of those in that time, but all three? No way.
I think they were going to use force anyway all along.
BEEP BEEP!
I see you on the security cams, Commander! What are you doing on Samos?
What the–?!
(Shh! I'll handle this!)
Ahem. Dr. Anzeel?
Yes, that's my name! Aoste already bailed, so why are you back here?
Do you know about the attack on the Poltava? The Revolutionary Front is on the island's doorstep, ready to enact revenge for it.
Yes, I know about the thing that's filled the world's headlines for days now!
Do you seriously believe that? That the Antiochus would defy protocol and attack a civilian freighter passing by?
(That sounds just like what the Sirens we know would do...)
(Considering everything we've witnessed, that definitely isn't beyond the realm of possibility... as much as it pains me to say that to her.)
"Revenge," my ass... That's just what they want you to think.
The attack was a false flag by the Revolutionary Front. They wanted an excuse to send a fleet to Samos.
Laplace's Demon is nearly finished, and they want to steal it.
(Laplace's Demon?)
If we adopt this plan, there may be a chance of success.
However, we must ensure that the jamming device remains operational as long as possible. In the meantime, we'll have to hold the line while evacuations are carried out.
In other words...
We already know this, Dr. Aoste. We've taken it upon ourselves to build upon this framework.
...I understand. But even if that is the case, everyone has already sustained heavy losses. The actual feasibility of the timeframe you provided must still be carefully evaluated...
If the "Light of Dawn" is ever extinguished, then Laplace's Demon will cease to be. If we have not reached the evacuation threshold at that time, our future operational plans will be impacted.
Worry not. I will also help buy time for you.
Ahem. Dr. Anzeel?
I've already issued too many communications through the process of commanding the operation, and they've likely already identified me for destruction.
As long as I can continue to draw their attention, I should be able to alleviate the pressure in other places, giving you more time to implement the plan.
But, what will happen to you then?
After such a fiasco, someone always has to bear the responsibility. Only now, there aren't many people left who can shoulder that burden.
I see... You can bring your KAN-SEN along as well. However, I would like Code G to accompany my Antiochus if possible.
Very well. You can have Enterprise, and whoever else manages to survive.
However, take them as far away from NY City as you can. Never let them return here.
...Without you here, I'm not sure I'll be able to control them...
What happened to the ever-so-wise and stoic Magister? You have no choice but to give those children both a purpose and the responsibility that comes with it, right?

...Even after you "betrayed" us, I still believe we see things eye-to-eye. And I think what you're doing is just. I completely understand you, and I trust that in their hearts, they understand you as well...
I'm sure they'll need some time to accept it, but they will come to understand you one day...
Yes, I'm sure of it...
(That's what I heard when I was in the Arcana Sanctum. Is this what that conversation referred to?)
So the Revolutionary Front wants to steal your time machine – Laplace's Demon. Does the Federation know about this?
Of course it does. They got this far in the first place because the RF had the Federation's tactic permission.
