The Federation wants the RF to make the first move and escalate tensions. That way, they don't have to take the blame for starting a war.
Wait... Starting a war?
Yeah. A war that will erase them from time.
Seize the power to control time, and the world shall be yours.

options.content: They're going to start a World War...

scripts.say: Don't freak out. Aoste and I already have a plan.
Flare – as in, Enterprise and company – will swoop in unannounced and steal Laplace's Demon and make both sides take a chill pill.
Enterprise? You mean... Code G?!
Look, we've chatted enough and this island is about to become a warzone! You need to get out of here NOW!
The communicator falls silent.
(The tension between the two major players in the alpha timeline is about to boil over into all-out war.)
(But, if Anzeel's and Aoste's plan is a success and Laplace's Demon falls into neither side's hands, then this memory won't have anything to do with death.)
(So what in the world is going to happen here?)
Commaaander. Who was that? Do you know her?
According to the memory we're in, yes. Why do you ask?
Because... she contacted you using the Tribunal's private frequency.
Everyone on this mission, including Elizabeth, is also using it.
This frequency is from OUR timeline, so how did that woman know about it and call us on it like it was the most natural thing in the world?
(That's a good point... I've grown so used to our frequencies being jammed or intercepted that I've stopped questioning it.)
How she did it doesn't matter!
Didn't you hear her? We need to get out of here, and fast!
It's too late for that. If this memory really is a representation of death, Anzeel's and Aoste's plan is going to fall through.
Huh? How do you know that?
Because if it had succeeded, this space wouldn't exist in the first place.
In the midst of the raging storm, the fleet known as the Flare sails for Samos Island.
Aw, man. It was sunny just a little while ago. Why'd it have to go and rain on us?
The weather's so fickle around Samos Island, I swear.
The abnormal weather and sea conditions here are side effects of research on Laplace's Demon.
Sometimes, people even report ghost and monster sightings.
Is it that bad? That's a little spooky...
Kasumi wants to see them.
With you around, we might just end up meeting some ghosts.
I'd say this storm comes with a silver lining. It makes it easier for us to hide our maneuvers.
The higher-ups put too much faith in Laplace's Demon. They went and stirred up a crisis just because it's "almost done."
And for what? Because they think if things come to all-out war, they can win, and it won't matter? As if anything could be that easy.
They're not the only crazy ones. The RF came out in full force just to steal the incomplete machine.
I can't say I don't empathize. If they waited until it was complete and things went the way the Federation wants, it would already be too late.
You do have a point!
"Laplace's Demon is meant to serve all mankind. Not as a tool of war, nor as the trigger that ushers the destruction of mankind."
We have to stop them.
Of course! In fact, why don't we take it a step further?
Thanks to Dr. Anzeel, we already know her location and the status of the defenses near her.
Why don't we go rescue her, while we're at it?
Rescuing her is one thing. What happens after that? Will she actually flee with us?
That would be unnecessary. Dr. Anzeel is sure to have a plan.
Yeah! Even when she was imprisoned, she told us not to come to her rescue. She's just under house arrest right now, so we don't have to go out of our way.
Besides, the more of a mess we make out here, the more dangerous things will be for Dr. Anzeel and the people confined with her.
Ooh... My bad!
Enterprise, the Revolutionary Front has issued an ultimatum to Samos Island.
The Federation's ambush fleet has also arrived at their target coordinates.
...Sounds like it's time for us to act.
Wichita, what's the problem? You're awfully quiet today... You nervous, or something?
Ahahaha, nah, I've just got a lot on my mind. I'll go scout the area with Kimberly again, try to get my head on straight.
Alright. Don't stray too far from the main fleet.
Duh. Don't you worry about me!
...Nobody should hear us around here.
The beginning of the end... I didn't think we'd be brought back to this day.
I can tell that this is the new space manifested by the Martyrium.
But why today? Why is this what it manifested?
Our concept of death must have mixed into the formula when we entered.
No, to take it even further, maybe our concept of death is so strong that it superseded the beta timeline's perception of the Iris ruins...
Heh. So that means we died today, huh? Hahahaha!
Wichita.
Ah, sorry. That was meant to be a joke.
Can you trace that META Hatakaze?
She's in this space, but I can't trace her exact coordinates. She must be in hiding.
But there's no doubt that this space is corroded. The RF and the Federation are all corrosion entities.
Aha. So that was the point of that whole suicide shtick.
Wichita, do you remember that day? Corrosion phenomena appeared back then, too.
We didn't know anything, so we only called them black tornadoes.
If we can learn the things we overlooked back then, we might just be able to dig out new truths from these fixed memories.
This is a big opportunity.
Heh. We can't change what really transpired, but what about righting the wrongs of the past in our memories?
If we did things differently, made better choices back then...
Could we have made a better future?
There's no way to know now, but I certainly don't want to see that tragedy a second time.
Agreed. Let's do something about it.
Samos Island - Shortly before
One does question one thing.
If Laplace's Demon is such an important machine, why don't they simply take it elsewhere for protection?
Who knows? Maybe it's too big to carry that easily?
If the plan is for Flare to steal it, then it should be small enough to carry in one's personal storage, no?
If shipgirls can do it, then surely the Antiochus can, too...
Simply stealing it is one thing. The way out is fraught with danger.
Perhaps the best way to see a well-protected target transported to a safer location is to let it be stolen without a fight.
That might be the doctor's exact plan.
So how do we fit into all this?
Do we contact the Revolutionary Front, tell them it's a Federation trap, and hope they give up the fight?
I doubt that would help. The completion of Laplace's Demon is a life-or-death problem for the RF.
Trap or not, they can't afford to back out that easily.
Besides... I don't think they're likely to trust us.
I know! Let's call Aoste and have him hide Laplace's Demon!
Absolutely not. That would cement them as enemies of the Federation.
Further, if he could hide it without anyone's knowledge, he wouldn't need to get Flare to steal it.
It's starting to look like we only have one option.
Oh! Are you gonna kick both of their butts at once, Commander?
Fleur, that's obviously not the plan!
You're going to try and get your hands on Laplace's Demon first, aren't you?
That's right. Leaving things as they are means that the status quo stays intact – this space is engulfed by the concept of death. Therefore, our interference is what'll have to change things.
(This is only assuming that Flare failed to steal it, though.)
(If the problem lies in the doctors' method of salvaging the situation, then...)
(No, now isn't the time to hesitate. It's time for action.)
Shortly after...
We've approached the Samos Marine Research Institute with Miss D in tow.
Apart from automated sentries, they ran into no security staff along the way.
That alone reinforces Dr. Anzeel's Federation false flag claims.
KABOOOM!
The sound of battle?
It's been three hours already. The RF and Antiochus must be fighting by now, right?
You're close to Laplace's Demon. Hurry and secure it before Flare can.
Hm? Wait, that's...
(That's the META Wichita. So they ended up here too, did they?)
(Now that I think about it, they might be the ones this memory belongs to... Takao, Enterprise...)
(The Flare burns out, and all that's left is Ashes...)

options.content: Were the Ashes originally Flare all along?

scripts.say: Well, that's one way to greet someone.
Little late to figure that out. You're right, but not all the way there.
The survivors of Flare are among the Ashes, yes... But as the name implies, we're very literally what was left behind.
The fact that you'd press on, even knowing that, means that you're still totally clueless.
Are you and Kimberly the ones who experienced this event in the alpha timeline?
...I have nothing to say on that matter.
Sorry. Let me change the subject, then.
I got a call from Dr. Anzeel. She told me the RF and Federation's plans, along with what Flare is trying to do.
The doctor contacted you?!
I don't know why she would contact YOU, but... she's under strict surveillance. She had to move mountains just to contact us.
Contacting you specifically, and from Samos...
No, if she told you Flare's plan, too, then that's all the more suspicious...
So? What are you planning? Going to steal Laplace's Demon before Flare gets to it?
Yeah. We know that leaving this situation to play out normally would result in the death of this whole area.
And personally, I don't want Flare getting involved in this, either.
You're a weird one... but alright. I'm with you there.
Don't worry. Flare isn't coming.
They're not?
Yeah, they're not. We already got them all out of the area to keep them away from what's about to happen.
Did you and Kimberly come to steal Laplace's Demon, too, then?
Hahaha. Would you believe me if I told you that NOBODY got anywhere near the infernal machine on that day?
...It's almost time.
If you're so curious about it, then come get a front-row seat. You won't want to miss this.
We canceled our plans and watched the distant sea along with the two Ashes.
The Revolutionary Front already broke through the Enforcers' defensive line, and their vanguard appeared on the horizon.
Just then, the Federation forces reappeared from the sea below and skies above.
According to our long-range reconnaissance, more Federation forces were moving to surround them from three sides.
Neither fleet fired the first shot, but neither did they cease their forward march.
On that day, Enterprise brought us here.
The Marine Research Institute was right in front of us. All we had to do was steal Laplace's Demon, and this absurd situation would be resolved.
And then... this happened.
The world begins to darken, as if a solar eclipse has begun. The sky above distorts, bends, and twists, taking the shape of a massive vortex.
A black tornado appears, whipping up the sea and growing larger with every passing moment.
The black tornado... A corrosion phenomenon.
There you go. Yes, it's a corrosion phenomenon.
Back then, we didn't know what it was either. We called it a black tornado, just like you.
Heh. Yeah, no warning signs at all. It appears right out of nowhere.
Commander, the tornado is rapidly spreading! It's going to engulf us soon!
Stare at the pretty colours all you want, but that's a corrosion phenomenon, Commander! You won't survive long in there!
Flee at once, or else!
With a deafening roar, the whale jumps out of the ocean and disappears into the black clouds.
Aaargh! My whale got away again! Elizabeth, hurry up and anchor that concept!
We're doing that already! Wait just one minute, would you?!
Okay! Everyone else, gather around me! We're getting the hell outta here!
Heh, good idea. You'll want to get far away from this danger zone.
Aren't you coming? Corrosion must be dangerous for META, too.
We were weak back then. So we panicked, and we overlooked some important things.
We're different now.
We'll stay here and bear witness to the end.
Then I'm staying, too. Miss D, take the others to the next ring for me!
Do you hear yourself, assistant?!
Commander?!
Swordbearer, it's too dangerous!
I'll be fine. If I use the concept of death instead of the train, I can catch up to you!
That's how you got here, isn't it, Wichita?
Right. But...
Even if you accept death and make it before you're corroded, death hurts! It hurts to death!
Maybe, but there's so much to gain. It might even be as important as your whale.
D-dang... Okay. Good luck, assistant!
Wait! One should stay... to protect you from the worst case!
I'll stay, too!
M-me, too!
I'll be just fine, everyone. Have faith in Miss D, Elizabeth, and me!
...Order received...
Once Elizabeth gave the signal that her preparations were complete, Miss D and the Iris shipgirls all disappeared.
All that remain next to me are the future Wichita and Kimberly.
...Answer a few questions for me. How do you know so much?
Our secrets, the secrets of the Antiochus... It's as if you know all of it...
Why do we feel such nostalgia toward you?
Why couldn't Enterprise do away with you?
Why... can't I do it, either?
Who in the world are you?
Honestly, Kimberly, I could use an answer to that myself.
That's why I'm here with you right now.
...Okay.
Then let's watch the end unfold... together.
No more words are shared between us. We all watch in silence as the predetermined end comes.
The black vortex grows in strength and ferocity in an attempt to swallow everything.
Then, as if a critical point has been reached, a shockwave erupts from the center.
Everything within view turns black.
Wichita and Kimberly have already fallen. My body and mind creak under the weight of it, rapidly approaching the point of collapse.
My hazy mind, on the verge of melting entirely, is enveloped in blue foam.
I see the blackened sky. Fire, smoke.
A single shooting star streaks through the desolation.
How beautiful they are, the stars in the night sky.
We boarded the train and took off, running on invisible rails through the sky.
Some time passes, and we finally arrive at the Mirror Sea in Scapa Flow.

sequence: Scapa Flow - Anchorage
Camelot - By the Gate

scripts.say: The train doors open and a stream of brilliant golden light fills my vision.
The clock says it's early morning, and yet this Mirror Sea is bathed in the light of afternoon.
Welcome to the Gate of Avalon, servant.
A manmade Singularity and a jumping point between branches – impressive, no?
This place – once merely a Mirror Sea – has been turned into a gateway between worlds since the Royal Navy seized it.
I've come to know of it ever since Elizabeth sent me detailed documentation following Compiler's defeat.
Still, reading about something and seeing it in person are two very different things. It's an awe-inspiring structure.
Heehee. Just the reaction she hoped for.
"She"?
Yes, your Elizabeth. She wanted to impress you on your first visit here, so she turned the lights way up.
Oi! You're not supposed to say that!
Not say what? The truth?
Bah! Yes, I turned up the lights, but only to further demonstrate the importance of this operation.
Oh, servant, I don't believe you've met before.
This is Queen Elizabeth. META, as you can tell.
She is the leader of her organisation and is currently staying here as part of my reinforcements.
Also, she introduced me to Miss D and brought in that train you rode on.
Greetings, serv– Commander. We've been observing you from the driver's seat.
"We"? Were you both driving the train?
...No. We mean the royalty you're addressing now. We are the only one capable of driving the Queen's Light, so we had to go and pick you up personally.
As much as we'd like to introduce ourselves beyond what your Elizabeth just said, this is simply not the time.
Now, about the observing we did... We've deduced that you're in a similar state to Miss D.
To put it succinctly, you are incomplete.
What does that mean?
Phrasing it like that doesn't explain anything. Come, servant. Sit down.
I know you have questions. Richelieu surely promised that I'd explain everything you should know before you agreed to anything.
What I am about to tell you is top secret. Whether or not you agree to help, you must not let Naval HQ hear a word of it. Do you understand?
Of course.
Good. I just wanted to make it crystal clear.
Before we go on, let me remind you of the information we've previously shared.
First, the enemies we call the Sirens – they are manmade creations from the future whose true name is "Antiochus".
Technically, it's ANTI-X, which stands for "Artificial Navy Transformational Intelligence, Class X" in full.
Their name suggests that they are manmade weapons designed to fight against "X", but it isn't clear what this "X" actually is.
All we know is that this greater threat is out there, and currently, neither Antiochus nor the Ashes have any fundamental countermeasures against them.
Second, the Sirens are conducting experiments across many branches, ours included, designed to counteract X.
The technology they possess allows them to not only manipulate these experimental branches at will, but also to dispose of them should they choose to do so.
Whatever this "X" enemy is, it doesn't make the Sirens any less an existential threat to us, and we should still eliminate them.
But, therein lies the problem. Even if we defeat the Sirens and banish their power from our world, what do we do about this looming threat?
If we don't know how to fight it, our fate will be the same as though the Sirens had destroyed us all.
So, I came up with a plan.
Yes, that's right. Surely you must've noticed on your way here – that Miss D is indeed a Siren.
My META self here has assessed that it's very likely that she is one of Antiochus' high-level programmes, despite her childish demeanour.
Apparently, she is missing her rigging – the "whale," as she calls it. Its absence has impaired her memory and restricted her computational resources.
She is incomplete, in other words.
Think of what we could gain if we can make her complete again. Data on X, records of battles against it, perhaps even a way to stop it from invading.
Indeed. Ever since we found Miss D, we've dispatched forces to try and capture this whale.
So far, there's been no success, even if we got very close in our last attempt.
A few days prior, Miss D picked up the whale's trail again, and we've been gearing up to hunt for it again.
She picks up the whale's trail only periodically, you see.
Now I will explain why we want your help.
The whale Miss D wants to catch is in a location where a spatial impact event occurred.
Both I and my META counterpart believe the whale is drawn to those.
These spatial impact events often occur where battles are waged. What we want is your tactical expertise to catch the enemy unawares. This will significantly raise our chances of success.
One additional detail – these spatial events are frequently observed during Wisdom Cube experiments as well.
We trust that your exceptionally high Cube affinity will allow you to deal with any unforeseen turns during the operation.
Oh, and Miss D raised a huge fuss over you. She insists that you aid us.
Yes, she may look and act like a child, but she is still a Siren. Her intuition is leaps and bounds better than ours.
She is also very familiar with all those terms you picked up inside the Reality Lens.
Even if my probing has yet to yield any useful information from her...
Regardless, it has been established that what happens in the future leads to the birth of the Ashes and the Antiochus.
Speaking of which, we've learned that the Sirens call this particular future "the alpha timeline."
As they are all linked, learning about the alpha timeline will lead to more knowledge about the Sirens and X...
Don't give us that look. We aren't from the alpha timeline.
Everyone we've met who seems to be from the alpha timeline is very tight-lipped about the branch they come from.
They either don't want to talk about it, or they've lost their memories from that time.
Like with the case of Renown and Repulse who we found using our gate.
Sometimes their accounts of the same event contradict each other and they don't even realise until I point it out.
This makes it nigh-impossible to verify essentially anything about the alpha timeline.
But you, my servant, are different. It's very clear that Miss D has been trying to tell you something.
I am quite certain that you'll make progress in your own investigation if we successfully capture that whale.
This barrage of new information from the two Elizabeths comes as a shock to me.
(I AM the person best suited to investigate the alpha timeline I saw in the Reality Lens...)
(Anzeel and Aoste are both from that timeline. There's a good chance that "Silver Fox" I heard about is from there, too.)
(Hell, I probably am, too. No matter if they were simulations constructed from memories or not, they clearly knew who I was.)
(Maybe I've actually lost some of my memories, just like those METAs...)
Well, it looks like you've finally started to piece together the puzzle of the shipgirls' hulls.
It only matches my records by less than 1%, but this wavelength has to be yours.
The fact that you're playing this recording is absolute proof that it's you.
It also means that my very last gamble was successful.
I know you. No matter when, where, or who you are...
You could never abandon those girls.
Making you the final failsafe was the right call.
(Wait, so that's what the recording of Anzeel inside the virtual memory space meant...)
It seems lots of pieces just fell into place for you, judging by your reaction.
I was right to put my faith in you, my servant.
You will stop at nothing for us shipgirls and keep no secrets to yourself.
You have helped us see through the Sirens' web of lies foisted upon us by the Naval HQ, and carved out a place for us in this world.
It is thanks to you that all our factions stand together, united in our struggle against our unrelenting enemies.
And when we come together, we can accomplish the impossible. Like we did in Antarctica.
Without you, we would have succumbed to distrust and old grievances, and consequently, fallen prey to the Gazers.
But, you managed to bring unlikely allies together in Soyuz and Bismarck, averting the crisis we faced.
You've been there for us every step of the way, which is why we can even talk about plans and about the future.
And if you'll join us for this operation, I will gladly tell you everything I know and help you in any way I can.
What do you say, Commander?
But it's also a golden opportunity we can't afford to pass on.

options.content: All the more reason for me to get involved.

scripts.say: Heehee. What a brave soul.
See? I told you my servant was up for the task!
I have a question. Won't there be bedlam over me suddenly disappearing from the venue?
I've already planned for that eventuality.
Richelieu and I will come up with something to quell suspicions for long enough to accomplish the mission.
For that reason, we will be accompanying you, Commander. The train requires a "Queen Elizabeth" to stabilise its conceptual defence.
Of course you get to go! I don't buy your excuse that it "needs" one of us, but I can't argue with it either!
But I digress. In short, Richelieu and I will stay behind and cover for you.
The story I'm thinking we'll run with is that Her Majesty here is paying a sudden visit to the venue, so you, as her "servant," are busy tending to her whims for a few days.
We won't need that much time. We'll be done and back in a day or two at most.
Elizabeth! I told you, you're not coming along!
No METAs can come! Not a single one!
Yes, we know. You were quite insistent on employing shipgirls from this timeline rather than ours.
But whether you like it or not, WE have to drive the train.
Oh. Right. We need a driver. Fine, you can come! But watch yourself!
Whatever you say...
I can vouch for these girls. They will risk their own lives to protect you if need be.
Good! Not-METAs are better! They're handy!
(Our force would be much stronger with some of Elizabeth META's subordinates, strategically speaking...)
(Why does Miss D not want any METAs along? Are they somehow a liability for this operation?)
(I'd ask, but I doubt I'll get a straight answer from her until we catch her whale.)
So, what now? Do we board the Queen's Light and jump to a new branch?
While the Queen's Light would be ample for this mission, we will instead travel to our destination via Camelot.
It's safer to have a two-way portal in case backup is required. It also guarantees we have a way home.
There is the risk of Sirens or that Bon Homme Richard pursuing us, but if it comes to that, the new-and-improved gate and our train can easily hop from branch to branch.
Any last questions before departure?
None that I can think of.
Good. Then let us get ready to leave.
You do that. I'm off to the Orthodoxy in the meanwhile.
Enjoy your whale hunt! And try not to die!
Queen Elizabeth gets up and leaves, taking Belfast and Sheffield with her.
(Huh. I thought for sure she'd make us bring along one of the Royal Maids.)
(I hope that's a sign of her trusting Richelieu so much that she'll leave this mission entirely to her.)
Ladies – upon the name of the guiding Iris, remember your oaths and guard the Commander at any cost.
For as long as one's heart beats, one shall be the guarding sword that protects the Commander from all who wish to do harm.
And I will do the Holy See's bidding, for I am an agent of the Tribunal.
May the Iris be with you all.
Commander, take this. It's a communicator modified and improved by the Tribunal.
I've been told it's more advanced than the ones from the Eagle Union. It ensures a more stable, better-encrypted connection.
The others have all gotten one, too. You'll be able to issue commands to them remotely like normal.
(Even the Tribunal's chipping in for this mission, eh. I hope it'll protect against strong jamming, since I still can't get in touch with Helena as a backup.)
Thanks a lot.
You're welcome. May luck and the Holy Iris be with you, Commander.
After those words of farewell, Richelieu also takes her leave from Camelot.
Soon after, the golden rings above the castle come to life.
Alright. Let's go catch a whale!
Is this... that same space again?
Miss D says I got lost when I came in here, but... I think this might be the narrow gap between life and death.
(I must've been brought here after I'd died – before the black tornado could corrode me.)
The foam still covers my mind, protecting my "self".
...Back again, "I" see.

options.content: Am I the only one here?

scripts.say: A meaningless question.
Nowhere.
Yes.
It's "my" turn to ask the questions now.
Do you know that what you've been witnessing are mere images?
Foregone conclusions, all illusions, all destined to fade away.
Yeah. I know that very well.
Why struggle? Why resist? Why suffer and face death?
What meaning is there to all of it?
Well... It's something only I can do. Doesn't matter if it's real or not.
I follow my heart, stick to my sincere beliefs, and do what I must do.
What does the meaning matter, as long as I understand it? If I must, I can share it with someone else.
I think there's inherent meaning in treading a path you believe in.
Even if it seems meaningless at a glance, nobody knows what effects it might lead to.
...Answer received.
You're still under the illusion that you can change established reality.
Recently, somebody told me, "Reality and truth are not always one and the same. Reality can only be truth if enough faith goes into it."
I've spent a long time trying to figure out what that means...
But now, it makes perfect sense.
What? That all vain effort will be rewarded?
No. It means that you can't always accept reality as the truth.
If something doesn't exist in my memory, then it may be truth to others, but it isn't necessarily truth to me.
Reality may be set in stone for all I care, but if you don't accept it as the truth, then it isn't your truth.
No matter the situation, no matter the established premise...
Until I, as an individual, experience something, make decisions, and see things to their conclusion...
I won't accept it as the truth.
So I'm going to fight for the sake of my truth.
If that sounds like a vain effort to you, well, too bad. That's not enough reason for me to give up.
When the light fades, I see the shadows of trees.
The warm light shining through the leaves, the scent of flowers, the sounds of baby birds... An incredibly peaceful scene.
Next to me on this bench is a girl dressed in the style of the Royal Navy. In the space between us sits a small box of sweets.
Mmm... This is such a nice place.
Do you know where we are?
You're asking "me"?
This is a place that you constructed, that you interpreted, that you wished for.
It is your "end."
My... end?
I don't understand. What happened, and how did I end up here?
You don't, but "I" do.
You must go.
Go back to your battlefield. Continue your vain struggle.
"I'll" be watching you, Commander.
Light paints my vision white again. Instantly after, I see the dark of nighttime.
The roar of an engine reaches my ears. My nose is assaulted by the combined stench of smoke and death.
(Is this a battlefield? But I'm on... a mass-produced ship, aren't I?)
Aaaaaack! Where the bloody hell did you come from?!
Elizabeth? Weren't you on the Queen's Light?
Queen's Light...? Bel! Apprehend this stranger at once!
Understood, Your Majesty. *cough*...
Argh, fine! You just sit there and rest. We will take care of this ourselves!
(Everyone's acting weird...)
(Actually, this might just be another memory like the Samos Island. And if Elizabeth is right before my eyes...)
(...My communicator isn't reaching the Elizabeth in the train, after all. I guess there can only be one at a time in here.)
(Belfast is injured. This isn't a very reassuring situation.)
BEEP BEEP!
Your Majesty, the X fleet has blocked our retreat route.
...What kind, and how many?
A Class-V mimic beast, over a thousand mimic entities, and a vector zone of five square nautical miles.
We're struggling to handle a single Class-V? Gah, if only our fleet were in better condition...
Set course for a detour. We mean to avoid unnecessary combat.
Yes, Your Majesty.
Your Majesty. Enemies approach from all angles. We have no time for detours.
I can handle a Class-V mimic beast alone. Given the losses your fleet has suffered, I would suggest leaving it in my hands.
...Even if we can break through, the casualties will be enormous.
Here's the plan. We will bring up the rear. While we distract the enemy, the rest of you can detour and escape.
Is this a roundabout means of suicide?
No. The responsibility for this devastating defeat lies on our shoulders alone.
Please... Allow us to make amends for it.
If I may, I think you're only trying to run away. Your death would do nothing to improve the overall situation.
But you already know that, I'm sure.
We had a fleet of two hundred ships and one hundred KAN-SEN. Now, we're down to less than thirty percent...
The other fronts in this battle don't fare much better...
Tch... We put so much time and effort into gathering that force.
We don't want to see anyone else die...
Your Majesty, this is doomed to fail.
The Royal Navy would never abandon you.
I'm sorry, Your Majesty, but we won't accept those orders.
*cough*...
Hey, you can't predict the enemy's strength with any certainty. It's not your fault...
Don't give up, Your Majesty! You promised we'd make it home together!
With these numbers, I think we can make it through with a casualty rate of thirty percent. Detouring could buy us time, but it could also draw us deeper into a corner...
The Royal Navy stands and fights.
No matter how dire the circumstances, we must face them together, Your Majesty.
Yeah. Let's break through this encirclement together!
BEEP BEEP!
A communicator beeps again – not Elizabeth's, but mine this time.
Comma... Ahem. Assistant, thank goodness I've finally reached you.
Dr. Anzeel... right?
Did you say Dr. Anzeel?!
E-Elizabeth? Why are you with my assistant?
Hm? The person who dropped in here out of nowhere was your ASSISTANT?
Yep.
...We will accept that as truth. Anzeel, how are things with the Council?
Everyone's safe here. Some of the lost fleets are arriving at the rendezvous point.
That's a relief...
You'd better get your butt back here too, okay?
We... are currently planning our escape.
We've strayed too far from our allies, though, so the odds are... not in our favour.
Elizabeth, don't give up yet. Hope is right there by your side.
Can I get you to surrender leadership of the battle to my assistant there?
Surrender leadership? To this stranger? Have you lost your mind?
Don't worry. I'm certain my assistant – the Commander – will lead you to victory.
...Fine, fine, we trust you. Of course, we're supposed to obey your orders to begin with.
Alright, Commander, go wild. Reinforcements are on the way.
I'm waiting for you to come home to us.
Dr. Anzeel? Wait, you're...
Hm? Were you saying something?
Don't worry about it. You be careful.
No need to worry about me. We're in a safe place.
Also, don't stray away from the flying battleships. And avoid contact with the X at all costs.
Hanging up now.
(Hmm. The way this Anzeel talks, I think I know who she really is.)
(So in this memory, Dr. Anzeel and I were totally absent.)
(That means, if we advance as we are, only death and destruction await...)
Anzeel has awfully high hopes for you. Go on, then – show us what you can do.
What will your first order be, Commander?
I need a damage report on all ships and info on what weapons, personnel, and resources are available to us.
In the meantime, all ships who can fight will head to the first defensive line. Put mass-produced ships on the second defensive line. We're planting our feet firmly.
Planting our feet? But the battle lines are a total mess. And we don't know if reinforcements really...
Anzeel said there are reinforcements. Trust her.
Fight until the last light has faded.
Yes, Your Majesty.
My orders are based on intuition, but all ships quickly spring into action.
From the flying battleship that I'd only read of in Guam's reports, I gaze upon the dark sea.
In the distance, a great storm brews.
Beneath the storm, a fluid emitting an uncanny blue light coats the sea.
Countless things seem to stagger, squirm, and crowd upon it.
So this is the alpha timeline's enemy... One that we'll be forced to face in our world's future.
You've finally shown yourselves... "X".
KABOOOM!
Using the intel the girls gathered for me, I set the battlefield in motion.
The floating battleships provide all the supporting fire they can, devastating the approaching wave of enemies.
I thought I knew roughly how strong the Council's fleets were, based on Constellation's report. In reality, they are above and beyond that.
This first-hand experience tells me that, if anything, estimates that I thought were exaggerated in the report now seem overly conservative.
These vessels could decimate even a mass-produced main fleet from our timeline in a matter of seconds.
That's not even mentioning the shipgirls whose strength are a whole magnitude greater than our timeline's.
Take this fleet's Alsace, for instance. She's taken heavy damage and only one of her main batteries is still usable.
Even so, I genuinely don't think our Alsace could defeat her in a one-on-one.
I have to know what makes them so much stronger.
(I've gotten a good grasp on this timeline's strength now.)
(Next, to get a gauge on the X.)
BEEP BEEP!
Commander, a small fleet is headed your way.
Are they the reinforcements you and Anzeel spoke of?
(I knew I was right to trust her. They came much sooner than I expected, too.)
(Let's check the aerial recon and see who's coming. We've got... Kimberly and Wichita META, and...)
(Wait... Miss D?!)
The X have suffered heavy losses under my command, so to avoid further casualties, they coalesce into big blobs and disappear under the water.
Looks like we've survived the storm.
There you are, assistant! I finally found you!
What are you doing here?!
They're coming! The X are coming! We need to get out of here!
Calm your tits. The X have all been wiped out.
I mean, you can see that, right?
It's only a matter of time before they come back! When they do, you're gonna be in a world of pain!
Whose side are you on, talking like that?
I'm on the assistant's side!
Yeah, yeah. Your assistant's right over there. Go on, scoot.
Don't tell me what to do! You're not my mom!

options.content: Uh, thanks for looking after Miss D, I guess?

scripts.say: Now she's your problem again. I ain't doing any more babysitting today.
Sure is. Didn't think I'd run into you again.
Miss D, where is everyone else? Are we still in the Martyrium?
*sniff sniff*... This place still smells like death, so I think so?
The train cars didn't materialize it, though! Something else did!
Look, it's really complicated!
I only found you thanks to the tracker I put on you!
Wait, how long have I had a tracker on me?
Ever since I got out of that bed! I'm smart like that!
Ugh... Some reinforcements she sent.
At least we're all still alive thanks to you and the Commander.
Why are you here, anyway? Don't you have somewhere else to be?
Uhh...
It's complicated, basically. Don't have the words to explain it.
If you say so. It's been complicated for all of us lately, with bizarre things happening one after the other.
Regardless, we are glad to meet you.
With you and the Commander aiding us, we might just live to see another day.
You will. You're coming back home.
Yeah.
Commander, a corrosion vector zone has sprung up from the sea, protected by a cocoon.
My estimates put their numbers at fifteen times greater than the last wave. Even your ability cannot compensate for the sheer difference in strength.
We knew it... This place is one big ambush.
Then we'll just carve a path out of here as planned. Everyone, prepare for battle.
The Ash– Wichita and Kimberly will clear the way. We'll pull out as soon as we have secured an exit!
Will the two of them really suffice?
We will. You saw what we're capable of just a minute ago.
You focus on your task, and we'll focus on ours!
KABOOOM!
These so-called "mimics" – the X – possess a truly diverse range of characteristics.
Their bodies are flexible, yet durable, reminiscent of metallic slimes found in certain fantasy works.
They can absorb strikes by expanding while also maintaining a rigidity that allows them to survive nearby explosions. Interestingly, their appearances also vary by category.
Accordingly, the people of this timeline have made categories for them based on appearance and size.
The small ones are called "mimic entities," while the larger ones are called "mimic beasts," which are further divided into classes based on their strength.
Additionally, the area they corrode is called a "vector zone." It affects not only the water, but the air as well.
This, I suspect, is the reason why the flying battleships don't float that high off the surface.
The X are also able to "infect" sunk mass-produced ships and reconstruct them at a frightening speed.
It's safe to reason that they're able to do all of this on land as well.
While they are a very powerful adversary, they are not invincible. They can be defeated.
Defeating the large ones is a challenge, however, as they split into smaller X when destroyed.
They lose all cohesion once they've been pummeled hard enough, but then they merge with the vector zone.
With time, the vector zone will grow thicker and thicker until it allows for newly-formed X to emerge.
(There is no X that Wichita and Kimberly cannot blow to pieces... but there is also no X that they can kill in any meaningful sense.)
(How do you fight an enemy you cannot kill?)
KABOOOM!
There is a boom, and the flying battleship trembles. Luckily, the ship's shields stopped the attack.
A different battleship not far from mine wasn't so lucky, though. The hit penetrated, forcing it to make an emergency landing.
I sense something... A Class-IX mimic beast?! Where is it?!
This is really, REALLY bad! Those two don't stand a chance against a Class-IX!
It's over! We're all doooomed!
The battlefield monitor shows a close-up of the vector zone ahead, where a glowing blue tornado rages.
I narrow my eyes, and it looks like there is something floating inside of it.
Is that... an eye?
Oh, phew... We're really lucky. That thing didn't get a sneak attack in on us.
If it had hit us directly, that would've been game over!
Why? We can't die in this place as long as the concept "doesn't engulf us." What's the danger here?
Just because you can't die doesn't mean there's no danger!
There are more ways to get rid of someone than just killing them!
Do you see that X? Look close and tell me this – do you really think that's just a replica made from memories?
Are you saying it isn't?
No! It couldn't be any further from the truth! There's no such thing as a "fake" X!
It was over for this space the moment that thing showed up!
If the X get you, you're gone forever! Do you get it now?!
Don't answer! Just hang on to me and I'll get us out of here!
I'm not running away. Not until I've seen for myself that it cannot be defeated.
Ugh, fine! Then I'll protect you for as long as I can!
Which won't be very long, mind you!
When it really hits the fan, I'm getting you out of here whether you like it or not!
KABOOOM!
The mimic beast hits us once. Then again. Then again. Each time it strikes the ship's shields, it rocks so violently that I fear it's going to sink.
(That thing is clearly after us in particular. The silver lining is, it's the only one that is. The rest of the X are ignoring us.)
(It's obviously trying to cripple our chain of command, which won't happen without support on its side.)
(How did it even know I was here? And if it's targeting individuals who aren't part of this memory, why isn't it hunting Miss D and those Ashes, too?)
(Wait... That's it! We're not part of the memory, and neither is the mimic beast!)
(If X's invasion was invoked by someone, it was most likely Hatakaze META and Devil.)
(No, wait... there's one other person.)
Assistant! We can't stay here any longer!
Come to me right now or you'll be turned into smush!
No, I'm staying. We're going to defeat the mimic beast.
Defeat a Class IX? Who do you expect to do that? Me?
Without my whale, there's not a chance in hell!
Look ooout! It's coming right for us! Stop wasting time and get over here!
KABOOOM!
Crap! I'm not gonna make it!
Dammit, you stupid stupid idiot! If you're not gonna leave then I'll fight it, okay?!
You're the moronest moron ever, I swear!
Miss D jumps off the deck, immediately after which the mimic beast's attack penetrates the ship's shields.
The attack, however, neither struck the ship nor Miss D.
It was a blink away from striking Miss D, but then it warped and twisted before fading away in a burst of light.
...Stubbornness has been the undoing of many a soul.
I had a feeling you were here.
More than that – you created this space, didn't you?
Indeed.
Why were you so sure that "I'd" save you?
Because that's what you'd do, Rodney.
"I" am Rodney; "we" are Rodney. Greetings to you who goes by the name of "Commander."
After much observation and thinking, "I" have made my choice.
"We" choose not the demise known as oblivion, but instead choose to witness your end.
May this illusory place change to your will.
A feeling of weightlessness overcomes me, and my horizon suddenly expands.
I can see it all – the battlefield, what's happening on it, and what's real and what's not.
Elizabeth, Wichita, and Alsace's squadron are all fighting tooth and nail.
What's more, I can see a temple of gold in the distance, far away from this memory.
All around it, the girls from my timeline are holding on by the skin of their teeth.
T-try this on for size!
KABOOOM!
Charging up Death Laser.
Charging progress: 0%... 10%... 20%...
"Death Laser" sounds really bad! In more ways than one!
We need to interrupt the charge! Get her!
KABOOOM!
Sh-she dodged again!
Executing follow-up attack!
Such evasion... This Antiochus is a slippery one!
An attack is coming. Step back!
KABOOOM!
She is too powerful. We cannot hope to defeat her alone.
But we've lost contact with Miss D and the Commander, and Death's Shadow isn't gonna back down.
Running away isn't an option either, though. She'll just come after us.
What rotten luck when she finally brought the whale here... What should we do?
Strange... One can feel the Commander is watching. Does anyone else?
Watching? What are you talking about?
I don't feel anything... Or at least, I don't think so?
One can definitely sense it. Somewhere, far away, the Commander is watching us.
Commander! We're over here!
Amid the golden light, Alsace extends a hand toward me.
Subconsciously, I extend mine in turn, trying to reach her across the vast distance.
Before our hands can even touch, the feeling of weightlessness that overcame me is all gone.
Gravity pulls my mind back to earth and constricts my field of view once more.
The next thing I know, I'm back aboard the floating battleship.
And, somehow, I know that this despair-ridden stretch of ocean has changed.
At the same time, outside the command vessel...
...Huh? Where are we? Did we just get teleported here?
I think we shook off Death's Shadow. *sniff sniff*... Hang on...
Is that corrosion I smell? And is that one of those floating battleships the Commander talked about?
Ugh... Man, all of a sudden I feel really bad.
Yeah... I feel like breaking down in tears.
Likewise, there is sadness and anger in my heart... Did the memory put these feelings there?
One is... I'm confused, but I can hear the feelings in my heart, screaming to break free.
I know what needs to be done. I need to unleash everything!
Alsace? Mogador? I thought you suffered crippling damage.
How did you recover? And why are you glowing?
It's okay, Béarn. One understands everything now.
This one is battleship Alsace – Sacrament of the Unified Orthodoxy, an unreachable dream, and guardian of the Holy See!
One has returned to cast holy judgment upon evil!
Meanwhile, not far from there...
*cough cough*... Repulse, are you alright?
I've pushed past my limit, but I'm surprisingly okay... *cough cough*...
The beacon is still sending out an SOS. Her Majesty is still fighting.
Do you think you can keep going a little longer?
Sure can! But we have to go faster!
Her Majesty is waiting for us. We WILL make it in time!
The Iris girls have been warped to – or rather, merged with their counterparts in – the memory.
With their strength, the scales of victory now start to tip in our favor again.
Inch by inch, they push back X's forces, a dazzling golden light shining around them all the while.
The vector zone proves not as ineradicable as thought. It fades little by little under the light and cannon fire, being reduced to little white crystals that turn to dust.
Finally, the mimic beast inside the tornado lets out a mournful cry before it disintegrates into nothing.
Your judgment hath come. Threads of death take you!
Go away, you damn pests!
Preparing to initiate cleanup mode!
On board the floating battleship...
My god... They're making the X look like no threat at all.
How did they get so strong all of a sudden?
"I" don't know.
"I" only gave you a foundation to express yourself. The rest was all you.
I... did this?
Wow! You actually did it, assistant!
Do you know what I did, exactly?
No, I was just giving credit where credit is due.
The vector zone has been... neutralised? How? Our forces were vastly outmatched!
Béarn, have you any explanation for this?
I'm afraid not. All I can say is that those girls glowed golden and seemed almost not like themselves.
Somehow, they managed to repel the X without employing any spectacular Sacraments or weapons of any kind.
(The hell just happened?)
(How'd they pull off an Enterprise-level stunt without some secret weapon?)
(And how did the timeline beta girls merge with their memory counterparts like that? They weren't here until a minute ago!)
(Unless Helena was involved somehow, their branch is nowhere near technologically advanced enough to have done this!)
BEEP BEEP!
We have a signal, sis! We made it in time!
Your Majesty, this is Renown and Repulse. We have come to aid you!
Renown! You're a mess! What happened to you?
And for that matter, what are you doing here?!
We gave the order for all our forces to retreat! Were we not clear enough?!
You were still gone, Your Majesty. We came because we feared for your safety.
Well, getting here clearly can't have been easy, we'll give you that.
Truth be told, we were on the verge of complete annihilation until just now. We were prepared to be claimed by the ocean.
It is nothing short of a miracle that we get to see each other again.
Thank you, "friends from afar" – for coming to our aid.
Wait... Do you get it now, Elizabeth?
It's only a gut feeling. Are we correct?
Your struggle bore fruit. You managed to send death back to whence it came.
All will return to nothing eventually – but your end is still far off.
"I" will destroy the cocoon and put an end to this illusion.
And you – you will return to where you were.
Farewell. May we meet again someday.
The Iris girls blinked, and they found themselves in that space of cold machinery again.
Are we... inside the whale now?
Did we just get sent back?
Oh god, it's her again! And she's still charging her laser! Did we space out and hallucinate that whole battle?
We should PROBABLY do something about that laser like, now!
The power one suddenly gained is still with this one...
I can feel it, too. It's vanishing, little by little, but I still feel strong enough to take down Death's Shadow.
Then what are we waiting for? Let's kick her ass!
The laser reached a charge of 85%, but it could get no further than that.
Brennus pulled on her silver strings and brought down sword after sword upon Death's Shadow, purging the black mist around her and preventing her escape.
Then, like a steed through the heavens, Alsace dashed in and dealt a beautiful blow.
Death's chains were cut, and her pale, corpse-like pale was ripped apart.
One dealt the killing blow!
Phew... It's finally over.
A flawless victory. That was some exemplary teamwork.
I think all the power juice just ran out... I think we actually cut it really close.
One hopes control of the whale will be returned to Miss D now that her lookalike has been disposed of. Let's go find her and the Commander!
I'm sure they'll be overjoyed to hear that we succeeded in capturing the whale!
Umm, girls... Look below you...
At what? The Martyrium?
...Oh. We're above a THIRD ring. When did that happen?
Who knows at this point... I think Miss D and the Commander are down there, though.
Miss D is not here to create a path using the train cars for us. Our only way there is death.
Nooo! I don't want to die!
The world of memories crumbles away, and when I next open my eyes, I'm back in the Martyrium again.
We did it! We're back here!
This is the Martyrium's third ring! The third ring is the heart!
This SHOULD be the last unfolded space now that that weird memory thing is over.
You're mine now, whale! There's nowhere left to run!
Come out, come out, wherever you–
...Are?! It's flown off to the outermost ring!
Assistant, we have to–
Hold on. Something doesn't feel right.
I survey the area. The Martyrium's white basilica seems to glow brighter than anything else.
Even more attention-drawing, however, is the plaza at the center of the third ring and the enormous structure that towers above it.
It's a yellow crystal encased in wings carved from marble. At a glance, it feels almost sacred...
Looking closer, though, I realize that it's the epicenter of a marbled, blank whiteness.
A whiteness that lives, multiplying and propagating like the roots of a tree, corroding its surroundings.
(Like an invasive mycelium... Is this what corrosion is?)
(Did the Class-IX mimic beast appear in that memory because of this corrosion?)
(Right, there was that META working together with Devil... Was this their doing?)
Eww... Let's get out of here, assistant.
I open my communicator and try to reach Elizabeth and Alsace.
There is a click, but no sound beyond that. It isn't working.
(Dammit, Devil is at it again. She's jamming our comms.)
(I'm isolated from the girls and have no backup from Elizabeth. I'm in serious danger.)
I can almost hear Devil laughing smugly at my predicament.
Hey, how do we get to the outermost ring?
Just exit the Martyrium and come back in again.
I know how to leave! It's through the glowy spot in the middle!
The middle... where the corrosion is coming from...
Dammit. If it's the only way, so be it...
We move to the plaza, where we unexpectedly come face to face with Hatakaze META.
We meet at last, Commander.
Need I introduce myself?
You're Hatakaze META.
That I am, yes.
You're also the one who sent that Class-IX mimic beast after us.
Correct. Its defeat means little to me. It was no more than a ripple on the lake that is this illusory space.
Though, I must admit, you've surprised me.
And caused me some headaches, too.
You must've seen her. The one who calls herself "Rodney," who lives in that illusion.
If she'd only let the cocoon incubate, she would have been reborn as a god with immense power over this world.
Yet, she rejected that. She stopped it.
She destroyed the cocoon and her own destiny.
You made her choose this. Am I wrong?

options.content: She has the right to make her own decisions.

scripts.say: You do not need to answer.
I thought as much.
So why did you make her choose the worst possible thing?
Your actions have wasted a tremendous amount of resources.
So, I claimed the fragments of the cocoon and this entire city of death and I will make the most of them.
With those words, the corrosion covering the basilica comes to life and begins to squirm.
The thousands upon thousands of white roots extend toward the sky, chanting in a silent hymn.
Suddenly, the Martyrium's golden light takes on a foreboding purple color.
(Even if I can't contact anyone, they WILL see this and come running.)
(Until then, though... Miss D can't fight head-on, so I have to buy us some time!)
What was that? Felt like changing the lighting a bit?
×ĚŃřźşÉí
Are you ignoring me now?
(That's no language I've ever heard. Assuming she's even speaking a human language.)
Miss D, what the hell is she doing?
She's trying to seize control of the Martyrium!
What's she saying? Can you tell?
No! I don't have a translation function!
Can you do anything to stop her?
I can try, but who's gonna protect you if I have to fight her?
(I wish I could say, "I'll be fine," but there is too much at stake here.)
Hatakaze continues speaking in tongues, glaring at me all the while.
śřşó
ÓÚ´Ë´ŚŐŔˇĹ°É
She spreads her hands out, and the marble wings do the same.
The massive crystal emits a pulse of light, and a white figure descends from the heavens.
Huh? Rodney?!
No, wait. She may look the same, but I can sense that's not her!
Heehee. How keen of you.
I used the cocoon fragments to raise a complex, in turn using that to create merely a false copy of her.
Still, impressive – don't you think?
She carries a presence so powerful that it makes the light around her seem dull.
Her expression, blank. Her hands, joined in prayer. The wind blows through her hair and carries her gently flapping wings.
Rodney – a being whose aura surpasses even the Martyrium – hovers there solemnly.
She did not cause the spatial impact event.
This Rodney is a puppet. An artificial body born by forcibly anchoring the invisible.
Still, she wields unbelievable power...
We cannot believe it... No one should be capable of what she is!
Look at you, staring all slackjawed. You know so very little.
And you know so very little about manners, insolent pillock.
How did you evade our detection? Who are you?
A true ally of the Commander. Unlike you.
Tell me, why did you bring the Commander to such a dangerous place? What were you trying to achieve?
We have no obligation to answer you.
However, if you are an ally of the Commander, you are potentially our ally as well.
We shall tell you this much – the Commander is instrumental to overcoming the crisis test site beta faces, and as such, had to know about this place.
And not just know, but to see it firsthand.
Has no one ever told you that knowing too much is dangerous?
The alpha timeline, the Antiochus's true purpose, the X...
The Commander isn't ready to know about all these things! It's too soon!
"Too soon"?
Richard and the Arbiters are fighting at the gates to test site beta as we speak, and you think it's "too soon"?
We think you're plain overprotective.
You don't know anything about "overprotective."
But us arguing here won't do any good. I'll just ask you this – was it your subordinates that tried to stop me?
We would've never even known you existed had you not shown yourself. How could we possibly do anything against you?
...Fine.
Is that... Helena?
Not the Helena you know, for the record.
Didn't ask, but okay.
Guess Hiryuu was right about one thing.
If you have questions, this is not the time. I won't answer them.
Pfft. Whatever.
You just get here, or what? Are you after that thing, or the whale?
Neither. I'm here to protect the Commander.
Oookay then...
I know what you want to ask. I'm not going to answer.
Haven't changed one bit, have ya?
Good to know we don't have to fight over the same target, at least. We're just gonna take care of that thing over there. That fine with you?
I won't stop you.
Neither shall we. We only want the whale, then we'll head home.
The Commander is coming with me.
And leave without the rest of us? We don't think so.
Evening, ladies! Hope there's room for one more at your little table.
You...!
What? She's still here?
Duh. Who walks out when a show's about to reach its climax?
You, if ya value your life. Get out or we'll murder you.
Ahahaha! You and what army?
I'll bet you wouldn't last even 30 minutes against that Rodney.
Even if you did, your precious Commander would be long dead by then.
Won't have to bear seeing you all keel over one by one here then, at least.
We will protect our servant. Can we count on you lot?
I'm in. Someone's gotta teach this bratty little shit a lesson!
...Fine. Just this once.
Heehee. Everyone's on the same page, eh?
Good. Then let's finish this show with a bang!
AAAAAAAHHHH––!!
KABOOOOM!
Assistant, it's dangerous out there! Stay by me!
Got it. But at this rate...!
The META shipgirls and Rodney have already begun trading blows in the Martyrium sea.
Individual METAs have banded together to fight as one unit with awesome power, but they still fail to overcome Rodney's strength.
As I'm overwhelmed by my powerlessness and just how outmatched we are, suddenly, it hits me.
What about that power I'd experienced before? The ability to see the battlefield in its entirety, to touch the senses of the shipgirls from afar?
If I used that, I could do more than just tell them where I was – I could help the METAs in their fight.
I might've lost the foundation that Rodney had made, but if the cocoon fragments that made this memory are still inside...
If I could just harness their power, even a fragment of it...
C-Commander! The Iris bodyguard fleet has assembled!
Phew... We made it in time!
Here I was getting all hot and bothered knowing you were watching us, but things have really taken a serious turn...
(Alsace and the others! Nice, it worked...)
Where have you been? Are you all okay?
We climbed the whale and did battle with Death's Shadow.
Your guidance bestowed us with the strength necessary to fell the fiend.
We were meant to gather here in the third ring afterward, but the whale fled to the first ring during the fight. We were taken along with it.
That's why we couldn't run to your aid... On behalf of all of us, I apologize.
Does that mean you came here from the first ring?
Miss D was with me the whole time. Don't tell me you...
We acted in accordance with the rules of this Mirror Sea. Do not worry for us, Swordbearer.
It's the Martyrium, after all! Sacrificing ourselves for the Iris as an offering fits the concept like a glove!
I'm sorry, everyone. If only we could use our communicators...
I-it's okay. We were on our way to you anyway.
That's right. I kept tabs on our line of communication, so when things started going haywire, I knew I had to come running.
You mean as soon as Devil cut off our communications, then?
Yes! Pinpointing your location was a difficult task, though...
Heheheh♥ We only got to meet up this fast because you were sooo very worried about us, huh?
It's just a shame that our little power boost already went away. Even if we joined the battle, I don't think there's much we could do...
But that doesn't mean we're sitting out this battle.
That Rodney definitely has the Arbiter and the corrosion helping her out.
So I say we even the odds by helping them fight off that Hatakaze and the Arbiter. We can even support them by strengthening the Martyrium's concept by killing off the corrosion entities.
Yeah! We have Commander on our side, after all!
Good call, Mogador. Rodney's strong, but she isn't the only threat in this fight.
Hatakaze, Devil – either one intervening in the fight could be disastrous.
Let's contribute to the battle in what ways we can.
Formations, everyone! This is our fight now!
Through our efforts, we manage to bring the Mirror Sea's concept closer to its original state.
KABOOOOM!
Enemies at three o'clock confirmed down!
Yaaay♪ The corrosion's visibly slowing down!
Keep it up! Press on to the central crystal!
The Martyrium's... The Mirror Sea's control system might be waiting for us!
Fleuret speaking! The suppression fleet still can't reach the target sector due to the threat of being caught in the crossfire.
Skip that one. Let Elizabeth's fleet fight freely.
I'm concerned about the battle with Rodney. Contact me as soon as you spot Hatakaze!
R-roger dodger...!
I've spotted some of Devil's drones, but the Arbiter herself is nowhere to be seen.
Don't pursue the drones too far. Focus on the search as planned.
Understood.
(Perfect. Rodney should be weakening with every passing moment.)
(Hatakaze hasn't shown herself since she manifested the corrosion, though.)
(Devil must be plotting something, too.)
(Could it be... they're waiting for us to defeat Rodney?)
Miss D, status report on Rodney.
She's still acting tough, but she'll disintegrate soon enough.
...Disintegrate? What happens then?
I dunno!
(Should I try contacting Helena? We're in the middle of a fight... but I think it's my best bet.)
BEEP BEEP!
Helena, can you hear me?
We're almost done here. Focus on keeping yourself safe.
I'm fine. But I do have a few questions for you!
...Must it be right now?
Yeah, it must. It's related to this battle.
Okay, then. Ask me anything.
That Rodney is a fake made from a complex, which means she's similar to a Pawn.
How can she be so strong?
The corrosion only serves as glue for the cocoon. What matters is the cocoon itself.
As for the cocoon, it's a foundation that anchors the concept of Rodney to this world in order to manifest itself.
The cocoon is fragmented now, isn't it?
Yes. At first, Hatakaze sent the X into this memory region in order to corrode Rodney.
Thanks to your interference, the concept of Rodney destroyed the cocoon herself.
The X corrosion has stopped, but that also weakened the concept's own connection to reality.
And from there, Hatakaze used the leftover fragments to create a puppet of pure power?
Exactly.
If your glue statement is right, then purifying the corrosion would make the cocoon fall apart... Do you think it's possible?
Yes, of course.
Okay... What about, instead of destroying her, we left Rodney in this world? Would that work?
It would be difficult, but not impossible.
If that's your goal, then we'll need to suppress that Rodney's power for the sake of our own safety.
We have to try. It's just a gut feeling, but I think Hatakaze and Devil are counting on you destroying that puppet.
Otherwise, I don't think they would've shown themselves just to provoke you.
Understood. D, help us approach the target. We'll proceed from there.
How many times do I have to say it?! No whale, no dice! Not happening!
Fine. I'll do it for you, then.
Resource diversion, data transfer mode.
A current like a blue collage rushes out of the communicator and engulfs Miss D.
Instantly after, Miss D and Helena appear behind Rodney.
Hwuh? What's going on? Whoa, whoa, whoa!
Hacking... Complete.
Overwriting... Complete.
Rodney. In accordance with the Commander's wishes, resculpt yourself as a META.
Gentle blue light covers Rodney. Her battered form recovers in an instant.
The corrosion wafting in the air disappears all at once, as if washed away by the current.
When it ends...
So you've called "me" here.
If I hadn't, you would have been swallowed whole by the concept. Don't thank me – thank the Commander.
Very well.
Thus, the battle in the Martyrium sky came to an abrupt end.
Martyrium Core - At the Basilica
One will now secure the path to the crystal!
KABOOOM!
This is as far as you go, youngling.
The META Hatakaze...
Commander, Hatakaze spotted! Requesting orders!
That really is the control center, then. Rodney's been neutralized! It's about time you surrender!
Heheh, heheheh... You never cease to amaze.
But you seem to have forgotten something. Control of the Martyrium is still in my hands.
Is it really, now?
After a burst of dazzling light, another structure appears above the holy icon – the gate of Camelot.
Wha–?!
Our train is still parked at Camelot. Mirror Sea or not, did you think that a single car could carry more information than the entire train?
We were only reluctant to use this method because we wanted to avoid damaging the train.
You've appeared in person, and our servant has already cleaned up the corrosion of the Mirror Sea.
How, pray tell, do you expect to control this place?
"In this glorious celestial orbit, there is but one train." Get out of our train!
Test site beta... I won't forget this!
Blundering like this on the final step...
I admit defeat. But rest assured, you have not won!
You've said enough, rat!
Now, with a little cleaning, that corrosion problem will be as good as gone!
The holy icon in the center of the Martyrium spreads its wings once more.
This time, the crystal exudes a holy light that shines upon the city.
Under the power of the Iris, the complex loses its source of corrosion and turns to ash. Before long, the Mirror Sea is purified.
Phew... Perfect.
All that's left is to recover the whale–
That was my whale calling!
Gaaaaah! The whale! My whale's running away again!
An earsplitting roar accompanies the whale's ascent into the Martyrium sky.
Death's Shadow is defeated. If Miss D doesn't have control of the whale, then who could possibly...
Damn it! Devil?!
She lay in hiding all this time just to make us fight Hatakaze so she could steal the whale at the last minute?!
She played us like a fiddle!
As cunning as ever... Had us fooled, too.
Likewise. I'm sorry...
Nuh-uh! No apologizing right now!
Whale time! Follow that whaaale!
Wait! We need to recover the train car first!
Forget the damn train! Whale, whale, whale!
WHAAAAALE!
Ugh... Fine!
Let's get back to the Queen's Light first.
Hold on. I can't let you go, Commander.
Helena?
Agreed. This pursuit is fraught with danger. It isn't part of the original plan.
Commander, return with the Iris fleet. Be careful on the way – you're in a battlefield until you're home.
Elizabeth dismisses me before I can speak up. Then, she thrusts a small pamphlet into my hands.
An instruction manual on the gate of Camelot. Use it as directed, and you will make it to test site beta just fine.
That isn't necessary. I can teach the Commander myself.
Why must you argue over this... Fine. Do as you please.
The Martyrium can't be left in this state.
Such an enormous spatial impact event will attract other factions before long. We have to eliminate all traces of it while we still can.
...I'll turn this Mirror Sea back into train cars and deliver it back to test side beta.
Much obliged. We leave it in your hands.
Bye, mysterious assistant! See ya later!
While the Queen's Light disappeared – a few cars lighter than it had arrived – the Ashes prepared to depart as well.
That resculpted META Rodney isn't a threat anymore.
I doubt she'll come with us. Mind if we leave her with you, Helena?
Not at all. Are you two going already?
Yeah. Hunting down Arbiters isn't our job.
We confirmed the cause of the spatial impact event, so it's about time for us to go home.
...It was a pleasure to fight alongside you. You're as reliable as ever, Helena.
I have no idea what you're talking about.
Ahahahaha! Guess there's nothing to do but say goodbye, then!
Hope we meet again, Helena.
And boy, do I hope I never run into you test site beta folk again.
I'm afraid I can't make any guarantees there.
It's been an honor. Give Friedrich my regards.
Will do.
Commander, take those girls back to Camelot. I won't be far behind.

sequence: Thus, our part in the impromptu hunting trip had come to an end.
Our visitors from other branches returned to their respective homes, too.
All with their own ideals in mind. All ruminating on the future.
All listening in to the distant voice echoing amidst the stars.

scripts.say: The ring of light rotates, and the world around us begins to change.
The jump between branches has begun, and yet, the courtyard of Camelot doesn't show any signs of motion.
The gate can travel in two different ways. One is to jump from Mirror Sea to Mirror Sea, and the other is to designate coordinates for direct travel.
When traveling directly to coordinates, one must handle the impact from the target branch – the spatial impact event.
It seems this one accomplishes that through an energy barrier created by three rings.
Our compliments to whoever built this.
The foundation is well-designed, with ample attention paid to flexibility and comfort alike.
Now, to keep any malicious actors from trailing us, we'll be taking a detour or ten.
Three hours until we reach our target branch. Have a spot of tea while we wait.
Your Elizabeth's maids made it before our departure.
...We will have to drink elsewhere. Don't mind us. Go, relax.
In the courtyard...
The tea and snacks are ready. I taste-tested them. They're sweet and have a nice texture, and of course, I tasted no poison.
Phew... Royal Navy sweets never cease to amaze!
It's crazy how you have such great sweets, but the rest of your food is... Bah, now's not the time for that!
Eat up, everyone! It's hot and fresh! Don't be shy, Commander!
*gulp*... *gulp*... This one shall ingest coolant instead of iced tea...
Coolant?!
Oh. Right, you need to cool your modules like Gascogne does.
Th-that's right! Gascogne is acknowledged as a powerful, supportive ally!
Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa...
Épée, what's wrong? Do you see something in the sweets?
N-nope! I'm just worried I'll drop my tray... It's happened a million times by now... Whoa, whoa...
Wait, didn't you say you struggle with controlling your strength?

options.content: It's okay if you drop it! No pressure.
Umm, what if I fed you?

scripts.say: C-Commander, that can't possibly be okay...
Her Majesty wouldn't mind a broken tray or two.
Yeah! Elizabeth doesn't care!
C-Commander, that can't possibly be okay...
If Eepy won't take you up on it, I will! My mouth is open and waiting, Commander!
Th-this one... w-w-wants to eat, too! *tremble*
Me, too! Feed meee!
Despite the momentary ruckus, we manage to enjoy a relatively relaxed tea time together.
Say, where's Mogador? I haven't seen her in a while.
The way she... dresses... isn't appropriate for tea parties.
Mogador should be on guard, same as I. Her post is in the tower over yonder.
I look in the direction Brennus is pointing to. There I see a vague silhouette.
Yeah... Yeah, that's not proper dress for a tea party. Is there anything we can do about her?
That is apparently a quirk of hers. Unfortunately, it comes with the work environment. I don't think it's within our power to help.
We can simply leave her share of sweets for her to collect later.
Guess that's all we can do...
Three hours pass in the blink of an eye. The tea party has helped me get to know our new Iris friends.
While we all clean up, Miss D – who had spent much of the time lying on the grass after tiring herself out – suddenly springs onto her feet.
The whale! I can practically smell it!
It's close! So very close!
Elizabeth, get the train! I'm bagging me a whale!
Whale hunting confirmed as the objective of this journey. But this one cannot see or pinpoint the coordinates of said whale.
Hmm. I have no idea what happened, either.
Mm. This is weird. Where's the whale? Is it hiding?!
How the hell did it activate that... The automatic defense system's exceeded its call limit!
Hey, you damn whale! Show yourself already!
Whaaaaale! C'mon, c'mon, c'mon!
Miss D screams angrily into the empty sky.
And then... something starts to show itself.
First was a slight spatial fluctuation outside of the gate's rings.
Immediately after, a whale emerges from space not far beyond the outermost ring.
Is that... the whale we're trying to catch?
It's huge...
Judging from its apparent size and the distance between us, it must be between 1,100 and 1,300 meters long.
Huge is an understatement.
Yeah! That's my whale right there! Elizabeth! Get off your bum and let's go catch that whale!
I have a question. Does that whale respond to your voice to begin with?
Great if so, but if not...
Ah, the whale's turning toward us. I have a bad feeling about thiiis...
Oh no. Elizabeth! Activate your defenses!
First Ring, deploy active defences!
Dazzling golden light rushes through the gate's defensive barrier for a moment. The whale's energy blast is halted, left as nothing but ripples on the surface.
It attacked us!
H-how?! We didn't even attack it. Why would it activate its automatic defenses?
Hell, why is it attacking ME in the first place?
Why... I don't get it, I don't get it, it makes no sense!
Realizing that its attack was futile, the whale shakes its head slightly. Without even glancing at Miss D, it disappears into the spatial fluctuations it had come from.
Whale, my whale... *sob*... Whyyy...
Do you think it's gonna try and ambush us?
Maybe so. We've found it strange ever since Hunter's team last tried to catch it.
When it was cornered, it suddenly showed unexpected intelligence AND weapons we'd never seen before...
Lies! That can't be true!
The whale answers only to me! Only I can control it!
Yes, yes. We can see the truth for ourselves before long.
For now, focus on finding out where that whale went... and how to drag it out of hiding.

sequence: Somewhere, in an unknown location...
Camelot - Garden
Sometime later

scripts.say: Three of the Queen's Light's train cars sit silently amid the grass and foliage in the garden.
Undoing materialization in the Martyrium. Eliminating all signs of combat and leftover data...
Phew. I can finally bring you back home.
But before that, you look like you have questions.
Keen as always. What's going to happen to Rodney?
She's in an extremely unstable state right now. I need to bring her back home for treatment.
Don't worry about her. I promise you'll meet her again soon.
Thank goodness.
Anything else you're wondering about?
Really?
You don't want to know about the resculpting process?
Will you tell me if I ask?
No. All you need to know is it's a special stage of METAmorphosis that's dangerous and unstable.
Like I told you just a while ago, it's a special stage of METAmorphosis. Dangerous and unstable, as you'll remember.
I'll tell you this – if you hadn't made that decision as quickly as you did, Rodney wouldn't be alive right now.
Then what about Memphis and Vestal?
Yes? What about them?
Actually, never mind.
Alright. Let's wrap this subject up.
Do you mind if I ask YOU a question?

options.content: Not at all. Ask anything you want.
I thought you already knew everything.

scripts.say: Heehee. I only know what I know.
One META – Elizabeth – was with you on this operation. Were there any more?
No. She would've liked to bring her META subjects with her, but let's just say she had to go alone.
Right. "Alone."
Did I say something wrong?
No, it's fine. Let's get you home now.
There was total darkness, broken up only by the faint light of an instrument panel.
The place was abuzz with electrical noise and the sound of running machines – it was a control room of some sort.
Gee, it's kind of dark.
A girl sat amid the chaotic crisscross of dozens of wires, preoccupied with what was right in front of her.
If I force-boot it... it'll push the power system to its limit.
Have to focus on hacking the security instead.
Then the first thing I'll do is turn the lights back on.
Ugh... This place is too damn dark.
Indeed. It IS too dark.
Test Site Beta - Outer Defensive Perimeter
Two Arbiters, the Lovers and the Empress, had erected a defensive line to ward off the invasion of the X.
This clash between the unstoppable and the immovable was still being waged.
You people make me laugh.
Come on, can't you call it quits already?
I'm only gonna pay a small visit. You're being dramatic about this.
Look at yourselves. You've constructed an airtight defensive line, and what good has it done?
Test site beta is already a giant mess, and I haven't even gotten in yet.
Like, what's the point in keeping me out?
Your logic is flawed.
Allowing you inside would only make a bad situation even worse.
I told you before – your battlefield is HERE.
You're patient, no? Then show us how patient you can be.
Somewhere, in the Pacific...
Ahh! Sunshine, sand, and a tropical drink!
I needed this vacation.
If they all wanna busy themselves, they can do it without me.
I'll just be here, chilling.
*sirens blaring*
What?! An air raid alarm?!
But I haven't even done anything!
Are Sirens invading or something?
I thought this was the Eagle Union's own backyard?
What's going on?
Somewhere, in test site F-45733...
We've arrived at the objective, albeit 14 hours and 13 minutes behind schedule.
The Ashes proved more resilient than anticipated. They've likely dispatched members here as well.
We also encountered an abnormal type of jamming en route.
Had it not been for that impact, we would've arrived sooner.
Who the hell tried to stop us?
Unknown. No data matching characteristics found in database.
So it's a new enemy we've never recorded across any of our test sites, huh.
Color me intrigued.
Temperance, what're our prospects of extracting any data from the void?
Searching. Analyzing. None.
This area has been scrubbed completely clean. Agent responsible possesses remarkable skill.
Not even I possess the ability to perform a scrub leaving no traces.
Only known agents possibly capable of this are Tower and Magician.
They didn't answer our request for reinforcements. There's no way either of 'em were here.
Then it must be an agent of equal skill to them.
There is simply nothing here.
Identifying cause and origin of the spatial impact event is impossible.
Mission failed. Proceed with first task on mission list following submission of after-action report.
Submitting the report now.
...Hey, I just got an urgent message from Empress.
"Risk of test site beta running out of control... Requesting Arbiters to perform calming measures"?
What's she also doing over in test bite beta?
It is a special site.
Owing particularly to the entity known as "the Commander."
An all-out attack is not an option; neither is not attacking. A bothersome dilemma.
Requesting permission to join Lovers at defensive line.
Well, Empress hasn't set our assignments in stone, so if you wanna go, now's your chance.
*sigh*... Back to test site beta we go.

sequence: Orthodoxy Holy Capital - Conference Venue
Commander's Lounge
Following the operation's conclusion

scripts.say: I gather up my resolve and open the door to my lounge.
