The inside looks practically the same as I left it. There's no one here to welcome me back, either.
(Phew. Elizabeth and Richelieu really did cover for me. No one caught on.)
(There's a lot, and I mean A LOT to think about for this operation. I've kept some notes, but they're rough.)
(I'd better write down the details while they're still fresh in my memory.)
BEEP BEEP!
Hm? A message as soon as I get back?
(Huh... It's from the Eagle Union.)
"There has been an as-of-yet unexplained incident in the Pacific."
"During a 48-hour period, a large number of naval bases received large quantities of data which all contradict one another."
"Additionally, contact with PH was briefly lost, determined later to be due to communication line issues."
"Commander, you are to remain in the Orthodoxy for your own safety. Proceed with the conference as normal."
"Enterprise is in charge of monitoring the Pacific situation as it develops. She will contact you with any eventual updates."
I'm so confused by... whatever this is.
What do they mean by "unexplained incident"?
(I don't recognize the sender either. Could be Naval HQ, could be someone I know.)
(Although, given how scarce the details are, it's probably Naval HQ. Something happened and they can't explain it.)
I'll just let this simmer for a bit then call Enterprise and Saratoga.
(I wonder if this happened specifically in the Pacific...)
(It's adjacent to many factions. The Eagle Union, Northern Parliament, Sakura Empire, even the Dragon Empery.)
(The Royal Navy, Iron Blood, and Iris Orthodoxy all have bases there, too.)
(At any rate, I'll make some calls and check if anyone knows something.)
(The lack of details about this "incident" gives me some major premonitions, though...)
(I really hope my fears prove unfounded.)

sequence: The storm rages across the waters, through a night that knows no end.
Within the tempest lingers one lonesome vessel.
Will the storm's rage first be quelled, or will this vessel first capsize?
Will a ray of light bring hope through the darkness?
For I am but an oneiric butterfly, fluttering among illusions.
May light guide this vessel. May hope guide the Sakura Empire.

scripts.say: Diadem of Light - Morning
This ritual is only performed when a crisis threatens our Empire... I never thought WE would do it one day.
Yes. When the times are the darkest, that is when Lady Shinano's power matters most.
She is our symbol of hope, and if we can get her to officiate the ritual as well...
Then I'm certain our Empire will find the right path, dispel the darkness, and restore the light.
While I hope so, too, the ritual is a major burden on Lady Shinano.
It is. That is why we, as ritual participants, must do everything we can to alleviate her burden even a little.
That, and to try not to slow her down.
Now, I would like you to prepare the dance for the participants, as well as decide how to conduct the matches.
And Suruga... Are you good? You've been fairly quiet.
Huh? Yes, um, I'm just fine.
You don't have to be so nervous. We're all doing this together. If you have any thoughts, I'd like to hear them.
Well, uh... It's not really our job to perform the dance before the ritual, is it?
...Right. I'll go have another look around.
The dance IS a part of the ritual. We must put as much effort into it as anything else.
Since we have to do it, we should try to be excited about it.
Me, I just want the ritual to end without any incidents.
(Is this... the Diadem of Light?)
(This one was in the Orthodoxy's capital but a moment ago... How?)
(Ahh... 'Tis another dream...)
(I remember... Whilst I was asleep, they were preparing the ritual.)
(I can neither speak, nor move... Neither could I that day...)
*knock knock*
Ryuuhou, Akagi's crew are about to arrive any minute now.
It is time to make our move, Ryuuhou.
...Yes, of course.
This ritual will decide the future of the Sakura Empire.
As representatives of our great land, we must not fail!
Now, everyone, get into your respective positions!
Understood!
After years of suffering... No, we've been training for this very moment, and it is time to show the entire world our might!
On that day, this one also witnessed the ritual within one's dreams...
However, though the greater picture was true, the details diverged.
Ahh, I am but in my own bedchamber...
So why, then, do I feel so alone?

sequence: The dreamwaker sees the light of the Dawning Ceremony...
...Crimson-dyed intrigue. Otherworldly explosions. The house of faith, sundered by a charred blade.
The dreamwaker sees her valiant comrades, stemming back the tides of chaos to complete the ceremony.
At last, drifting within the vast sea between worlds, the dreamwaker stirs.

scripts.say: Crimson, scarlet, vermilion. Red, bouncing all around.
...The Sacred Sakura has withered. The Mizuho islands are ablaze.
...A dream luring one to destruction, and a red color that reduces all to ash.
...Why?
...This one must awaken and tell others of these omens...
...Why can't I? Why do I feel so powerless?
The shades of red bounced ever closer. The dream came apart, crumbled, collapsed.
...Ahh... Even in my dreams, my home is being taken from me...
Lonesome and feeble still... This one hasn't changed...
Naught can I do but follow fate and walk the path...
But perhaps... that isn't so bad...
Shinano looked directly at the red, contemplating neither running away nor giving up.
If you seek to turn that stands behind me to ash, you will first have to burn through me!
Just as the flames were about to engulf her, a wind chime rang out.
For the time being, we decide to observe for any more spatial fluctuations – distortions caused by enormous energy sources.
So, Commander... You think it decided to be careful because its ambush failed?
And it'll show up again if we make ourselves look defenseless?
Huh?! That makes sense, but using yourself as bait just sounds too dangerous!
Swordbearer, I agree that patience is key. We still don't know the extent of the whale's power. If we show weakness, it may just prove fatal.
Wanting to be taken advantage of is one thing, but by the enemy? No way!
The whale's goal is to avoid capture, not kill us, right? What if it just hides until we leave?
Th-then what do we do?
What if the whale is so quick to flee because of the recent spatial impact event?
Hmm... Fighting Sirens causes spatial impact events, as I recall. And that leads to spatial fluctuations?
Right. This whole operation began with the idea that the whale is drawn to spatial impact events.
If this place is subjected to the same influence... Hm, this spatial impact event must have been severe.
These coordinates must have been an experimental field where Sirens fought, or something.
But there's nothing here. The spatial impact event was so intense that it wiped the whole area out of existence.
Mmm... Basically, a concept erased from matter returned to another dimension, causing space to fold in on itself and create a special area in that dimension.
For example, the sea where the whale swam. When the sea disappeared, the whale followed the concept of that sea and disappeared from reality.
But once it leaves the world of that concept, that's it. This was our mistake.
What? If there's no physical foundation for it, just make another!
Take a new foundation and anchor the concept to that! Easy peasy!
If that whale gets away now, there's no telling when I'll see it again!
You're right about that. We're in trouble if it escapes into conceptual space again.
At this rate, whoever is manipulating the whale now might just gain full control of it.
In the worst case, this might be our final whale hunt.
I TOLD you, nobody but me can control the whale! When I say you can't, I mean you can't!
But what if that person was you?
You Antiochus can still operate, even when you're incomplete. What if the one controlling the whale is another Miss D?
Ah...
AAAAAAAH!
Damn, damn, damn! That's actually, really possible!
I'm such a moron! I'm gonna get my whale stolen away... by ME!
*sigh*... Well, we're glad you understand the gravity of this situation.
Thank you, Commander. One is sorry you had to calm the two of them...
But one still doesn't understand how we're meant to drag that whale out of hiding.
That makes two of us. I could certainly use more explanation.
I don't get ANY of it!
M-me, either...
Likewise, Swordbearer.
I feel like I kinda got it... Mmm, but I dunno...
It's too complicated for us to explain right now, and you don't need to understand the principles.
However, we have hit upon a way to drag the whale out of hiding. It is dangerous, though.
Our original plan was to snatch up the whale while the Antiochus were busy fighting their enemy...
But the situation implies that their enemy is alive and well, and they aren't hostile toward the whale.
In other words, if we try to drag out the whale, we may be forced to fight two factions at once.
A head-on fight would be hopeless.
So the plan is... for all of you to return to the beta timeline! Miss D and we will figure things out here!
The assistant can't leave!
What?!
I don't know why! But I know that!
We've put up with you for long enough, but our patience is wearing thin.
If you don't give us a proper reason, already, we're taking our servant back home!
Boooo! No means no!
Back me up, assistant! I'll protect you. Just don't leave me!
That's enough! We promised the other Elizabeth that her servant would be returned safe from harm!
NOOOOOO!

options.content: There they go derailing things again...

scripts.say: Servant, do you have something you'd like to add?
Assistaaant!
In my opinion, we have too little time to waste it arguing.
I came here well aware of the risks of this operation.
If safety is really our top priority, then now is our chance to give up and go home.
Besides, there is something I want to look into.
Beyond the whale... I can't let slip an opportunity to learn about the Antiochus and the alpha timeline.
As Commander, I've joined in countless battles. Every time we faced mortal danger together, we overcame it.
I trust in the people who protect me, and in return, I want you all to trust in my resolve.
Yeah, there you go! I'll keep you safe, mysterious assistant!
If you say so, Commander... then one is resolved to fight.
Heheh, I won't let anyone lay a finger on you, Commander♥
(I have friends and allies here. Let's think of a countermeasure first before we do anything drastic.)
(If Miss D is willing to ally with us, then we might just be able to get Helena's help.)
(I haven't received any word at all from her since I left the venue.)
(But I know her. Even if our communication lines have recovered, she won't contact me until it's absolutely necessary.)
(Anyway, I can discuss this with everyone another time.)
Your composure betrays a lack of understanding, Commander.
Even we don't want to fight an enemy that can cause such an enormous spatial impact event.
Is it military power that scares you, or the power of the concept?
Both. Do you not believe us?
We trust the Commander. And the Commander trusts you, so...
Alright, then. It seems you're not withdrawing.
As for how to make a foundation to ground the concept and drag out the whale...
The beta timeline had "concept anchors" that they used, yes? In that case...
Elizabeth, the train! Use one of the train cars!
Ugh... Must we really?
Of course! The Queen's Light is strong and dense enough! It's perfect for turning individual space into a foundation!
Urk... But our precious carriage...
(She really looks like she doesn't want to part with this train carriage... It must've taken an astronomical effort to build.)
When we catch the whale, you can just turn it back into a train car!
Ughhh...... Fine.
Now, what concept will we use to manifest the whale?
Perhaps a bridge?
It will come with a river, giving the whale room to swim. If it escapes, we can cross it to give chase.
(I don't like this. It'll just mean leaving everyone behind again.)
Hold on a second. Let's get some things straight.
The whale entered a separate, folded space. That's why we can't access it from the physical world.
So we need to give it a concept and anchor it to it in order to drag it out into our world.
To do this, we use your Mirror Sea train car technology to change a condensed space with the concept of "train" into a different concept, making it into a different space.
If that concept can connect to the space where the whale is, the whale can be manifested here.
And then we capture it before it can escape... Are we straight on that so far?
(Wow... What a fruitful analysis.)
That's more or less correct.
Now, Commander, what do you think of the concept? What's likely to connect us to the space the whale is in?
How about doors?
Maybe we can go through it and go to the whale. There were doors in all of the imaginary spaces connected to the Arbiters... to the alpha timeline, too.
(And I've already been to those spaces several times already.)
(The Commander knows about the doors, too...?)
No, no, nuh-uh! Door and bridge are both wrong!
It's Death! Only Death can capture the whale!
(Death... Huh? Is that what the "D" in Miss D means?)
(Death is a tarot card, too... Is she related to the Arbiters?)
Are you willing to stake our lives on a word that came so easily?
I trust her. It's a little violent, but Miss D knows the whale more than the rest of us combined.
The Commander accepted the concept of death so quickly! It was even faster than this one's analysis module!
The Swordbearer knows more than us. Now is the time to trust our leader's judgment.
I like letting the Commander toy with me. Yeah, I'm just gonna wait and see what happens.
Anchoring the concept of death means, well... We'll have to imagine it.
We will operate the train, so it follows that we shall–
No METAs!
Okay, then let me–
No assistant, either! If you lack the concept, then stay away from it!
I'll pick one of the Iris shipgirls! That's for the best!
...Alsace, you do it!
Hmm? This one should imagine a concept...?
Knowledge on how to do it does not exist in one's memory logs... What now?
Don't worry. It's easy, we'll teach you right now.
First, relax...
Alsace, relax. Alsace, don't be nervous.
Emotion module still running, reducing speed of relaxation below expected value...
Alsace, standby mode!
Understood! Entering standby mode!
...Whoa.
Ahem. That will do. Now, imagine the concept of death.
Not the moment of someone's death, but the manifestation of death, a place emblematic of it... Envision that.
The concept of death. A manifested place, images, imagination...
Keep doing that. The more specific, the better.
Everyone, get on the train. It's almost time to ride.
We camouflaged the door and Camelot before boarding the Queen's Light.
Boundless stars shine outside the window.
But our destination isn't the distant sea of stars. It's absolute nothingness.
We're almost there. Alsace, are you ready?
M-maybe! Let this one prepare a little longer...
Don't worry. Relax and leave it all to us.
Time stops.
Everything in the carriage halts. Even sound is snuffed out.
Elizabeth alone begins to slowly move.
One step at a time, leaving faint afterimages behind her.
She stops for a moment in front of Alsace. Then, she walks right through her.
Instantly after, time flows anew.
The afterimages left behind by Elizabeth flow through Alsace and melt into their owner.
Our inspection is complete.
Well done. You can stop imagining it now.
It's over already...? Nothing is in this one's memory region...
You did great.
It's a shock that someone can construct the concept of death so well.
Eek, that was like a horror movie brought to life.
Elizabeth just teleported behind Alsace... Like some kind of ghost!
I-I didn't see anything... Nothing at all...
What awesome speed. Even I couldn't keep sight of her.
Hmmm...
Hahaha! Cool, right?
After we catch that whale, I'll be even cooler!
(Huh? Did nobody else see what just happened?)
(Actually, passing through a target so fast that you leave afterimages... I remember the Arbiter we fought in the Mediterranean doing the same thing.)
(She called that... inspection? I'll ask Helena about that.)
So? Did it work, or what?
Nothing looks any different outside.
Yeah... It's all dark and empty...
The train hasn't begun its transformation yet.
Honestly... Maybe we ought to use another car as the foundation for the concept of this lovely view.
Concept conversion, car 7. Become the foundation of death, anchor the unseeable, and manifest its form!
A light erupts from the empty blackness.
Then, golden arches and a pearly white road appear. A circular city emerges from nothingness to everyone's amazement.
It's... beautiful...
Like a Mirror Sea, a compressed space has been freed, birthing an entire city based on a concept.
All this from an object the size of only a train car. It is truly awe-inspiring.
Wooow... I've never seen anything like this before.
This must be how Béarn manipulates space using reality anchors.
Reality anchors? What're those?
They're a reality-stabilizing technology used in Basilicas all the time.
As their name suggests, they can anchor all kinds of concepts. In this city's case, the concept of death.
Béarn would be sooo excited if she could see this. Shame she's not here.
(This doesn't really FEEL like a city based on the idea of death, though. It more brings to mind images of brilliance and holiness.)
(Is it down to interpretation? Is this how Alsace views death?)
Alsace, does this city have, like, a name?
Hm? Not that one knows of.
A splendid structure of gold and marble to commemorate death...
This brings to mind an idea – the Martyrium. How does that sound for a name?
The Martyrium... A shrine built atop a grave, yes? One approves of this idea!
It's a good name. Let's call it that.
While you likely aren't conscious of it, it is good to name things according to your concept of them.
If others accept the concept, it then... Bah, never mind that.
A small problem has cropped up.
We're unable to anchor the concept properly. The space the whale is occupying won't fully manifest in reality.
Our spatial impact event was strong, but the amount of data within the folded space is simply mind-boggling... Even a whole train car could only unfold this much.
With a booming rumble, the whale suddenly appears in the sky above the Martyrium.
The whale! My whale is here!
Oh. So that was still all it took to lure it out.
Elizabeth, start the train! We've got to catch my whale!
Don't be so hasty. The Martyrium is a stand-alone space akin to a Mirror Sea. We cannot catch the whale without entering the space.
Then do it! Go to the city! Start the train NOW!
You can be such a pest... Fine, starting the engine now.
...Wait. The whale isn't alone.
What do you mean? There are others?
METAs, to be precise. Two groups, one of which is uncamouflaged. Wichita and Kimberly.
Judging by this duo... it's the Ashes.
Even all the way out here, we're still running into them...
(But, one of our own is working with them – Friedrich. Maybe we can ask them about Enterprise, or Hiryuu.)
The other group is camouflaged. We can't identify them at this range.
Only we know about the whale, so they're most likely here only to investigate the spatial impact event.
As if we didn't have enough to deal with...
They WILL know about the whale as soon as they look up!
Start the damn train already! Or they'll get to it first!
STOP! RUSHING! US! Furthermore, we don't know who we're up against! Rushing in blindly will be our death!
For now, everyone will stay put inside the train. We shall go and scope things out.
The Queen's Light's anti-conceptual defences are impregnable. You'll be safe here while we're out.
Commander, I've heard you're an excellent babysitter. Watch this sassy child in our absence! Make sure she doesn't run off.
You got it.
Why would I run away from the assistant? Just go and come back quick!
Sometime earlier...
Is this it, Kimberly? Are we at the origin point of the spatial distortion?
Soon – we're close. It's strange, though... there are no wreckages to be seen here.
According to theory, there should be loads of them.
I've not seen ANYTHING, for that matter. The whole branch has literally been erased.
There's only one explanation.
The impact released so much energy that the space completely lost stability.
It wiped away the real-world foundation of the entire branch and the test site with it, folding it into a higher dimension. Would explain why we can't see squat from outside.
Simple. Just cause another spatial impact to create a pathway.
My thoughts exactly. Good thing I have a machine that can do just that.
Lead the way. I've got a real fireworks show for ya.
As the two Ashes were drafting a plan, they saw the light of the Martyrium on the horizon.
...Wichita?
I see it.
Someone rebuilt the foundation with a conceptual anchor, unfolding the space. Guess that's one way of doing it.
Whoever did it is hiding themselves.
They're doing it damn well, too. My radar's got nothing.
Forget about that city, though – see the whale in the sky? You recognize it?
Arbiter XIII... Death.
She's here. Maybe even to do the same thing as we are.
Either way, let's hurry. We gotta kill the target first, or we'll have wasted our time coming here.
And ignore whoever rebuilt the foundation?
Don't give a damn. We'll find 'em sooner or later.
If they're friendly, we'll talk it out. If they're not, we'll duke it out. Either way, they're not stopping us!
Meanwhile, elsewhere...
Well, well... We just got here, and already we're seeing a spectacle.
A conceptual anchor. Impressive. Do you have any guess as to whose, Devil?
Not a single clue. They've perfectly concealed themselves.
All I know is that they smell like they're from test site beta.
You mean the branch where Pamiat' ran into big trouble? Interesting.
How can you tell?
Arbiters have their secrets, too.
Fine. And the whale flying in the sky? What the hell is that about?
What, you don't know?
The things I don't know could fill your whole database.
You realized I only just escaped that place, yes? For now, all I can see are glimpses of things.
Hahah. Okay, I'll tell you. That thing is a huge deal.
And I mean huge. You'll be set for life if you can capture it.
Uh-huh. Are you going to tell me what it is or not?
Nope. If you don't know, I'm not obligated to tell you. I'm not your mom.
Buuut, I've heard that "They" are looking for it, and will grant a hefty reward for its return.
Really? Then I have to get my hands on it.
No, wait, first I need to know the concept tied to that foundation. I will not be a fool and rush in blindly.
You don't recognize the concept? I do.
It's Death.

sequence: Mirror Rail "Queen's Light"
Car 5
Present Time

scripts.say: 15 minutes have passed since Elizabeth left the train. We who stayed behind are lounging around as we wait for her to return.
Miss D threw a tantrum earlier, lasting 5 minutes. Now she's just sitting quietly in a corner.
Meanwhile, some of us are idly gazing out the windows at the mysterious city.
Building such a splendid city simply by picturing it. Can you imagine that?
We are all blessed to have witnessed this.
While we're here, we should take a picture!
Hang on, lemme find my camera...
If you wish to record it for posterity, one has already done so and is preparing to compile a report for the Cardinal.
No, not for posterity! For us! I'm talking about taking a picture as a keepsake!
One has... questions about the practical purposes of doing so.
It's to show other people and say, "Look! We were here!"
Like, we're the only ones who'll ever come here. They'll be so jelly when they see a picture of how pretty this place is!
Uh-huh... Thought processor RPM is rapidly increasing...
Fl-Fleur, please don't mess with her like that...
I'm serious here! Don't you wanna show a pic to Tem and Opie and see the looks on their faces?
All I want is to go home and be alone.
Oh. Alrighty then.
Brrrrr...
What's wrong, Miss D?
Miss D has huddled up in her little corner and started shaking like a leaf.
Cold... It's so cold in here! Don't you feel it? It's freezing!
Uh... Not really?
One's body temperature remains stable.
Should I, um, get you a blanket?
No! There's an intruder! Someone's snuck aboard the train!
That's why it's so cold! I'm freezing my butt off!
*sniff sniff*... Yeah, I'm smelling something, and it's not the Commander...
It's corrupt and damp, the stench of depressing death...
One's olfactory system isn't detecting anything. Could it be... the system is malfunctioning?
I guess it's not strictly a smell, more like an aura. I've worked as a Tribunal judge for a long time, so I've developed a keen sense for these things.
Didn't Elizabeth say the train's conceptual defenses are impregnable?
Although, if both you and Miss D sense something is wrong, I don't think that's a coincidence.
Nobody panic, alright? Let's contact Elizabeth before anything else.
The assistant is right! Call her!
We double-checked. There is no sign of any intruder.
There IS an intruder! They're getting closer and closer!
They're only 1 car away! The barriers between them are useless! Heeelp!
Alright, we trust your intuition.
What we don't understand is how this intruder could break in without leaving a single trace along the way...
No matter. Gather everyone in a single car and we'll be right there.
Incidentally, we identified the other group that arrived here. One of them is an Arbiter – The Devil XIV. You surely know all about her.
The other, it seems, is a META. We haven't yet figured out who, though.
Hang in there. We're coming.
(Devil? And a META is accompanying her?)
(That's really bad news. We need to assume a defensive formation...)
Hm? Commander, do you want us to prepare a defense?
Yeah. You can smell where the intruder is coming from, right?
Sure can!
Mogador points at the door connecting to the next train car.
I thiiink the best strategy is if me, Alsace, and Brennus go to the next car and intercept the intruder while the rest of you just stay here.
(On one hand, it divides our force. On the other, it gives them more room to fight and guarantees we have an escape route.)
Let's do that. Everyone else, keep an eye out for the enemy!

sequence:
The Go Master and Her Disciple

<size=45>1 Tea and Coffee</size>

scripts.say: At the office, in the dead of night...
M-my heart is racing, I must admit. I wondered why you'd call me to the office this late at night...
I mean, you specifically chose this place, bathed in silence and beautiful moonlight, over the bustling city district...
Um... Would you mind waiting a little longer? I need time to calm my beating heart, and I fear I can't live up to your hopes until then. Please give me a moment...

options.content: I'm not going to do anything weird.

scripts.say: M-my apologies! I am a disgrace, I know!
Sorry about calling you in this late. I just wanted to ask you something.
I see... I will do everything I can to help.
Thanks. I appreciate it.
It's noon of the next day. I finish up my morning tasks and head back to my office.
Welcome back, Commander. Outstanding work as always.
You must be feeling tired. May I propose taking a break to go outside for a while?
Before you ask, don't worry. I finished all my secretary work while you were away.
As she speaks, Chen Hai places a coffee mug and a beautifully bound book on the table.
You had coffee today instead of tea? And you dived into a book rather than play Go?
Oh, is that your image of me? A woman who only drinks tea and plays Go?
I don't blame you for thinking that. All Empery girls love tea, and I, especially so.
Sometimes, though, a cup of coffee is what I crave. And sometimes, I try to show a different side of me to hopefully catch your eye.
Aha, I see.
It's too soon for ahas and I see's. How can you be sure I don't have a different goal in mind? For instance, trying to see into people's minds by understanding them through what they eat.
I... guess?
Which do you think it is, hmm? Am I trying new things, or trying to read people? Try to guess, Commander.
(Chen Hai is one step ahead of me again... No, you know what? I'm not letting her have the pleasure this time!)
(I forwent sleep yesterday to hone my skills! Time to show her!)
Say, are you free? I've learned a "move" or two and I was hoping you could give me some guidance.
Of course I can. What kind of "moves" are we talking about, though?
You'll see soon enough.

sequence:
The Go Master and Her Disciple

<size=45>2 Guidance</size>

scripts.say: CLICK...
Chen Hai shoots me a look of slight confusion as I lock the door to the office.
Hang on, why did you lock the door? By "guidance" did you mean...?
Heehee, now I see. "Surprise the enemy and strike at their weak point." It seems you know this well.
(I think she's misreading the mood... which may be to my advantage. What's most important is that I find "it" before she does.)
Give me a second. I need to get "it" out before we go any further.
Take your time. I'm not going anywhere.
She picks up her cup of coffee like it's the most natural thing ever. Looking closer, I can see it – and her hand – is shaking slightly. She's nervous.
Now I'm actually quite excited to see what "moves" you've learned, Commander.
(Weird. Where is it? I whipped it out just last night...)
I think have a pretty good guess as to what this is about. I can see why you'd want some guidance...
(Maybe I left it back there...)
Did you say something? Never mind, I've almost got it.
...Now I see. No wonder something felt off.
I gave you a massage a while ago to help you relax, and I was entirely in control back then...
But now, you want to take the lead. I don't think... I could handle that...
Pick your battles... I have to retreat and come back better prepared...
C-Commander! I just remembered something I have to–
I found it!
Y-you "found" it? Ahaha... Wonderful. That's... great.
...Oh. A Go board?
Yeah. I've learned some new moves and wanted to refine my skills further.
So THAT'S what this was about...
You good? You look kind of pale.
Oh, I'm fine. In fact, I feel great.
I'm ready if you are. Let's play. Heehee.

sequence:
The Go Master and Her Disciple

<size=45>3 Intensive Training</size>

scripts.say: Five hours later, in the office...
Your weakness is that you play too passively. Hedging your bets is perhaps not the best strategy in Go.
Dammit... You win again.
I overestimated myself. Clearly, I'm still a long way off from beating you.
You needn't put yourself down. If anything, I'm amazed at how quickly you've improved. Keep at it, and I'm certain victory will be yours one day.
Having said that, I noticed some flaws in these new moves you've learned.
You'll want to patch those up, and I could show you how to...
Oh, apologies, that's presumptuous of me to say. I haven't even asked if you want more guidance in the first place.

options.content: Show me how it's done, Master Chen Hai!

scripts.say: Heehee. A firm answer is what I like to hear.
However, please bear in mind that you'll have to set your mind to this and follow my instructions to a T.
Fine by me!
Is that determination in your voice? Then get ready for your intensive training.
With a small side of punishment for making my heart throb earlier...

sequence:
The Go Master and Her Disciple

<size=45>4 The Four Arts of Go - 1</size>

scripts.say: I accompany Chen Hai to the swimming pool. Someone has added a small artificial waterfall to the pool. When and why, I don't know.
Uh... Are we going to play Go out here?
No, of course not. You're going to meditate under the waterfall. I take it the concept is familiar to you.
You're to sit there and let the cold water whip your head and body.
I've obviously heard about it before, I just don't see what it has to do with Go.
It is the first of the Four Arts of Go that I've summarized – "be bold, fear nothing."
When you play with me, inhibition prevents you from reaching a state of flow, does it not?
She comes within whispering range. Only a small nudge away, she gives off a cool fragrance that tickles me.
It's too much for anyone to stay calm under. My composure crumbles.
She senses the restlessness in my heart and lets out a small giggle into my ear.
Heehee. There you have it. Your first lesson will be learning to stay calm in the face of anything.
Alright. Then what exactly do I have to do?
First of all, I'd like to help take off your clothes.
Whoa, WHAT?!
No need to be so alarmed. I'm only referring to your coat. What did you think I meant?
Uh, nothing. Go ahead.
She points me to under the waterfall. I sit down in the water, most of my clothes still on.
The water doesn't feel as cold as I expected it to. Hell, it's closer to a warm shower than anything else.
I was never going to make you train in a truly grueling environment. It would be for nothing if you got hypothermia or somesuch.
Let the warm water wash over you. Now pull your thoughts inward and start meditating.
Following her instructions, I close my eyes.
My thoughts sink into a deep, dark ocean.
As my mind drifts, a glowing red diamond appears. Then another, and yet another...
Then, a cat manifests out of thin air. It starts chasing after the red diamonds while singing something...
(...Has Akashi snuck her way into my mind palace?)
Something tells me that there will be more of these perplexing visions inside my mind...
POKE...
Chen Hai nudges my nose with one of her fingers, bringing me back to reality.
You went into some kind of trance, didn't you?
Guess so...
Heehee. It's alright. Just follow my instructions next time.
First, hold my hand. Concentrate your mind on only the sensation in your hand, then breathe steadily.
Let's try again.

sequence:
The Go Master and Her Disciple

<size=45>5 The Four Arts of Go - 2</size>

scripts.say: Chen Hai helped me dry my body off, after which I changed out of my wet clothes. We then returned to the office together.
Thanks for helping me out.
My pleasure. Now, how do you feel after that meditation exercise?
Not bad. Feels like it really cleared my mind.
Also, what about your clothes? They got pretty wet, too. Shouldn't you get changed?
I'm fine, but thank you. I'm a shipgirl; getting a little wet all but comes with the title.
So, you've finished your first lesson. Are you ready to move on to the next?
Bring it on!
Splendid. Then let's get started on the second art.
As they say, "Even in a game of Go, etiquette and morals are king."
This time, I shall teach you the etiquette of Go as well as the fundamental tactics.
I'm all ears, ma'am.
Let us start with what is known as the fist-and-palm salute.
Nowadays, it's no big deal if you aren't quite THAT formal, but both players should at least bow or give each other a nod to show respect before the match starts.
It is an indication that what follows is private time for both players. After that is done, then we may begin.
I see.
I give her a bow, and she does the same.
Her wet clothes cling to her skin more tightly than usual, making the curves of her body just that much more pronounced.
Droplets seem to drip from her black hair and beautiful, crow-feather-like eyelashes. She is enthralling in a special way.
This is a problem, because I don't know where to look without being disrespectful.
(Should I just bite the bullet and tell her to quickly get changed?)
Hm? Is there something you're wondering, Commander?
I've got a spare towel lying around. You should dry and wrap yourself up. Don't want you to catch a cold, right?
I appreciate your concern, but I assure you, I'm fine.
Let's continue with the etiquette lesson. The next thing you should know about is a practice called "nigiri," or "the grab."
The senior player takes a handful of white pieces and the other player tries to guess if they're holding an odd or even number. The winner decides who goes first.
Since I'm the senior player in this case, you'll be the guesser.
She grabs a fistful of white pieces and places her closed hand on the board.
Because you're still learning the ropes, I'll give you a small handicap.
You may place your hand on mine to try to determine how many I have.

sequence:
The Go Master and Her Disciple

<size=45>6 The Four Arts of Go - 3</size>

scripts.say: Several hours have passed. With Chen Hai's patient guidance, I finally complete my crash course on Go etiquette.
That should be it... Say, Commander, does your back hurt after sitting for so long? I could give you a massage, if you'd like.
I'm good, thanks. The only thing I feel is all this new Go knowledge filling my head.
Hell, I don't even want a break. What I want is to find an opponent and play a match.
Heehee. Yes, as they say, "strike while the iron is hot." We should put your skills to the test.
Let's see... A worthy opponent...
Chi An is a bit out of your league at the moment. It should be someone more around your current level.
Actually, that reminds me... You said you learned new tricks yesterday. Who was it that taught you them?
Commander, I'm ready to resume where we–
Suddenly, Hai Tien opens the door to the office.
Ch-Chen Hai?!
And Commander, you're...
Both your clothes are a mess... Wh-what unspeakable things have you been up to?!
It's a long story, but trust me when I say that we've just been playing Go.
"Go," you say... You've only been playing Go, and yet you look like this?
You expect me to believe you threw your clothes off in private and neither of you acted upon your urges?!
Whoa, hang on! What is that last part supposed to mean?!
...So it's Hai Tien who taught you those tricks, I assume.
Correct.
I see. And Hai Tien, you've not revealed ALL your tricks, have you?
No... I was going to take my time teaching them.
Like how a serialized story keeps you coming back for more. I thought it would be more interesting that way.
An interesting scheme.
But I'll bet you didn't know the Commander went through a lot of trouble because of your "keep 'em on the hook" attitude.
F-for that, I'm sorry...
I wouldn't call it "trouble." Besides, I ASKED you for help.
While I am moved by how forgiving you are, your forgiveness will not get Hai Tien off the hook. She needs to learn from her bad behavior.
Oh, I know. Why don't you and her play each other? She can teach you more of those "tricks" of hers, and you can practice what you've learned.
Y-yes, ma'am! Commander, I will play sincerely with you to atone for my mistakes.
Heehee. I'll be watching you from the sidelines, as the Commander's one and only Go teacher.
(Shhh...)
Just as I'm about to say something, Chen Hai puts a finger to her lips, gesturing for me to hold my tongue.
(Maybe I'm imagining it, but it feels like Chen Hai's smile to Hai Tien was even more mysterious than usual.)

sequence:
The Go Master and Her Disciple

<size=45>7 The Four Arts of Go - 4</size>

scripts.say: I gave the match my absolute best, but still I lost to Hai Tien in just short of two hours.
I'm really sorry, Commander. I wasn't trying to win, and yet...
You don't have to apologize. One day, the game will be mine.
Plus, now I know what our difference in skill level is.
Heehee. Even though you lost in the end, it was quite an interesting match.
Now it's time you and I reviewed your mistakes.
I-if you're doing a review, I'd like to help!
...That's very kind of you, but don't you have deadlines?
Yes, but I still have time to spare. It sounds a bit like you want to keep the Commander all to yourself...
Ah, I just remembered, you finished a new chapter. You don't mind if the Commander and I read it before our review, do you?
Here it is. Your love story about–
AHEM!
Something urgent just came up! Excuse me, I'd better go!
Hai Tien leaves the office in a real hurry, and then, it's just me and Chen Hai again.
You look disappointed. Did you not want her to leave?
Partly, yeah... It's also that I feel like I'm improving so slowly.
Really? I didn't think you'd take Go this seriously.
Now that I think about it, you did put up with my teasing and stuck with my training course to the very end.
You were so earnest... Now I feel guilty over being so mean-spirited to you.
Mean-spirited? What, are you saying all this training was just you teasing me?
Not entirely. Sometimes it was, but the things I taught you should also make you a better player.
No one becomes a Go champion overnight. Even if Hai Tien and I taught you everything we knew right now, there's no way you could internalize it all at once.
I guess so. That doesn't change the fact that I really want to get good, though.
Then let me ask you this – what suddenly made you so passionate about this game?
How do I put it... When I saw you take command of the fleet, I just felt captivated by how calm and cool you looked when giving orders.
Huh? What do you mean?
I know you weren't simply born that captivating. You got to this point not with talent, but with an extraordinary amount of effort.
Then, a few days ago, I read a book that said, "Learning Go can not only make you smarter, but also make you a better tactician."
So I started studying the game so I could get to know you better. I even asked Hai Tien to teach me what she knew so I could surprise you.
Well... you DID surprise me, but why would you...
Because I am your Commander.
That's why I want to learn more about you. Why I want to become a better person, a more reliable person.
Goodness... Hearing you say that would touch the heart of even the most cold and indifferent among us.
Heehee. Thank you for telling me this, Commander.
It amazes me that you're deploying such clever strategies when you're still only a novice.
I'll be honest with you. Your move just now completely caught me by surprise.
You're not just messing with me, are you?
Of course not. It's an honor to be spending time with you. Teaching you things like this... is something I actually quite look forward to.
She takes my hand and begins slowly leading me into another room.
Come along. Our intensive course isn't over yet.
There is still the last of the four arts which I have yet to teach you about.
Please stay with me until the very end, Commander.

sequence:
Sounds of the Ocean

<size=45>1 The Island Market</size>

scripts.say: Commander, I'm over here!
Open-air stalls with canvas awnings line the beach, gleaming in the sun.
Pearl stands among them and waves at me with a smile on her face.
Thank you for coming to the market with me today!
If you hadn't told me about it, I never would've found such a neat place on this tiny little island.
I was lucky to find it, myself. Who knew we'd find such a fun activity on our vacation?
And there's so much more variety than I expected.
(Shells, coral, seafood... They've even got treasure chest-styled blind boxes with stuff from the sea floor.)
I'm sure we'll find lots of fun things. Heehee, maybe even some real-life treasure?
Pearl and I browsed the market for a while.
She found a few things that piqued her interest, but whenever I tried to buy one, she'd already moved on to the next stall.
Even halfway through, we had yet to purchase anything.
Hmm... Commander, do you find it odd that I haven't bought anything?
A little. You seemed really into a few of those stalls.
I was just trying to see if the corals were real. Unfortunately, they were all fakes.
The one selling jars of marine plant specimens did have some rare flora, yes...
Their crude handling makes me doubt that any of the specimens will last long, however.
So yes, there were many interesting things, but nothing that I would be satisfied to call a treasure just yet.
Might be hard to find real treasure at a place like this... Wanna try cracking open a few chests?
Commander? You seriously believe in those?
What if, though? Let's open ten to start.
They're selling them in the hundreds. Of course there isn't any real treasure in there!
Don't you dare buy a single one!
Goodness... Anyway, let's get back to it.
Besides, I wasn't just looking around. I heard a fun little rumor along the way!
A rumor? I must've missed that. What was it?
I won't be telling you yet.
If we find it, well... You just look forward to that!

sequence:
Sounds of the Ocean

<size=45>2 The Happy Camper</size>

scripts.say: The evening sky is a beautiful orange.
After scrutinizing the final stall, Pearl shakes her head in disappointment.
Alas, still nothing...
If there were such mysterious and rare treasure...
It would have already drawn the attention of all the venue.
There are a few more down on the other side of the island. Wanna check there?
It's so much quieter than the market here. Doubtful we'll find anything...
Don't worry, Commander. The treasure isn't what matters – it's that I got to spend time with you today.
And we saw such a beautiful evening sky, too.
She suddenly freezes up. Surprise dyes her smile.
Oh, no...
What's the matter?
Commander, the ferry is leaving!
Aah... We missed the boat...
Pearl watches in abject horror as the last ferry home slowly floats away, becoming a tiny dot on the horizon.
I knew we shouldn't have left the ship in a major harbor... Well, this is a problem.
She stares intently at me for a moment. Then, she opens her arms wide, as if waiting for a hug.
Embarrassment finds its way onto her face.
Hmm... No, no, it won't work. I mustn't pursue the ferry with you in my arms...
I guess we'll get to see the moonlight tonight, eh?
Huh?
Let's stay overnight.
But this island doesn't have any hotels...
No problem. There's plenty of open space.
Huh?! I don't have a cargo hold, you know...
Sleeping in the open air doesn't seem like the best idea, either. We might end up crab feed...
Look over there, Pearl.
Where?
In the dusk, lights in the market turn on one after another. It's as if the starry sky has come down to terra firma.
It's beautiful.
Should I take this to mean that... though we missed the boat, we've been treated to a beautiful sight in return?
Life doesn't always go the way we want, but that in itself can be a unique experience... Is that what you're saying?
Umm, no. Not what I'm saying.
I mean, that was beautiful and all, but still. I mean THAT.
Huh? What is that over there?
It's a sign, see? It says The Happy Camper.
Ooh... Let's camp there tonight!

sequence:
Sounds of the Ocean

<size=45>3 The Ocean in a Shell</size>

scripts.say: Tents, sleeping bags, stoves, and ropes line the shelves illuminated by warm lanterns.
Pearl examines them curiously, occasionally running her fingers over them.
Commander, what do you think of this tent?
These bulky, claustrophobic tents are the kind you use in the cold, mountainous terrain. Might be a little too heavy for us.
I see. Then... this one?
Good size and construction, but it doesn't have ventilation. Without windows, it'll get stuffy by the ocean.
She nods along, only half understanding.
You know so much. I can only tell them apart by size, really.
Hmm... How's this one?
It has a window for ventilation, and it looks just right for two...
She crouches down and examines the two-person tent. Once satisfied, she looks up at me expectantly.
Hmm... I like the size and wind resistance, but we'll have to find a sleeping pad that fits it.
Speaking of... May I choose the color and design of the mat?
Fine by me.
Incidentally, I've been eyeing that mat in the corner over there. The pattern is so cute!
The deep-blue base and white pearl pattern...
I think let's choose that one!
From there, we pick out sleeping bags, lanterns, cooking utensils, and a host of other tools for camping.
Suddenly, Pearl seems to notice something and points at an out-of-place device in the corner.
Is that... a clamshell? Hmm, the texture is slightly off...
Is it a decoration made to look like one? Or is this some kind of camping implement, too?
Oh, there's a sign next to it! So it's an audio player with a hidden recording device...
What an odd design. All of the ones I've seen are those little cylindrical cases with speakers.
...I knew it! This is no ordinary recording device. The sign says that this model is often used for professional observation in nature.
So it's made to blend in with nature?
I think so!
Then this one is made to be placed by the sea, I assume?
It would record the sounds of the ocean at their most authentic...
She raises her slender fingers and flicks the pearl in the center of it.
The device turns on and plays comforting ambient sounds.
Oh, my... It sounds beautiful, like waves crashing at shore.
I could use this to freeze the sounds of the ocean in time forever...
Her eyes open wide as she stares unblinkingly at the slowly rotating pearl.
Did this little thing strike your fancy?
No... I was thinking of something else.
Do you remember that rumor I mentioned earlier?
It was about an incredible treasure that appeared on this island – a magical item that can record the sounds of the ocean.
...Was it about this very item?
If so, it's kind of a disappointing tale.
Yeah...
Heehee. But the sea is vast, maybe there is such a treasure out there.
In the darkening night, Pearl approaches me and helps me carry some of the camping gear.
Are we finished here?
Let's find a place to pitch our tent. If we don't hurry, it'll be too dark to see!

sequence:
Sounds of the Ocean

<size=45>4 By the Beach at Night</size>

scripts.say: Before long, we started to set up camp on an elevated patch of land with a nice view of the beach.
It's pretty far from shore, but close enough that we can hear the sound of waves.
Next, according to the instructions...
Commander, can you hand me that pole? Yes, the silver one.
Commander, hold the tent down here for me, please... Just like that!
Commander...
After a brief period of work, she puts down her tools and stretches out happily.
And finally, we have a tent! Thanks to you, it went nice and fast.
I'm lucky you happened to be so skilled. You figured out all the complex steps in no time.
Setting up a tent isn't that different from crafts.
If we could get the opportunity to make accessories together...
I bet our teamwork would be perfect!
You're always so reliable, Commander.
There! Now that the tent itself is up, let's get to decorating it.
Have you heard of bioluminescent jellyfish, Commander?
They live deep underwater. At this time of year, they emit a warm glow.
When they gather, the sea floor lights up like a galaxy in the night sky.
I'd love to catch one and put it in the tent...
Oh! Commander, do you know about coral reef fish?
They're masters of disguise, because they resemble coral in shape and color.
Are you saying you want to decorate the tent with them, too?
That's right!
And...
She rattles off idea after idea.
Unfortunately, though, she's forced to confront the fact that the tent is not underwater and thus cannot support marine life.
Before we know it, we've finished furnishing and decorating the tent.
By the way, I remembered something else about that rumor I mentioned earlier.
What if the treasure they're talking about is actually some kind of special conch shell?
A conch that evokes the storied memory of the sea...
Pearl gazes thoughtfully at the ocean.
The sandy beach looks pale under the moonlight. It resembles a trove dotted with rare treasures.
We still have time, Commander. Why don't we go search?

sequence:
Sounds of the Ocean

<size=45>5 Echoes of the Ocean</size>

scripts.say: Silvery moonlight bathes the sand in a cool, gentle glow.
The daytime bustle makes it seem all the more serene now, as the only sound left is the peaceful rhythm of waves breaking.
Pearl and I stroll on the white sand together, leaving a long trail of footprints behind us.
The waves crashing, the scent of the sea... It's such a blissful place.
It's truly relaxing to take a long walk on the beach again after so long.
The ocean is magical. What other place can make you feel such peace and tranquility?
Your interpretation is valid, but that's not the only thing that the ocean means to people.
Oh?
I think that, to most people, it evokes more of a sense of... always changing.
It's deep and dark, and countless lives and sights lay hidden underwater.
Hmm... I can't disagree with that perception, either.
The ocean can be violent and merciless, too...
But if people are willing to delve deep into the heart of the sea, then I think their opinions will change.
With a motherly touch, even the shallows can bring life to a small island such as this one.
Many of the worlds' civilizations first flourished in the cradle of the sea, after all.
So I...
Commander, did you hear that?
Pearl suddenly stops, holds her breath, and stares fixedly at the water.
The eternal song of the waves, the rustling of the wind through the brush, and the murmuring of countless night insects...
No... There's something else.
Something very special...
She casts her gaze to the deep, dark sea reflecting the silver light of the moon.
A unique call, ever so faint, but as clear as a bell.
Her eyes suddenly light up with joy and surprise.
Commander, wait here a moment.
I'll be right back! Just stay right there... Don't move a muscle!
As soon as the words leave her lips, she dives into the water.
Her figure vanishes beneath the waves in the blink of an eye, leaving just ripples as she plunges into its depths.

sequence:
Sounds of the Ocean

<size=45>6 My Gift to You</size>

scripts.say: The cold moon shines eternal, and the waves roll in ceaselessly.
I'm left alone on the beach where Pearl and I walked side-by-side before.
It's so quiet now... Kinda unsettling.
She probably won't be back for a while. What to do...
As if in response to my thoughts, the clouds suddenly disperse, allowing the moon to illuminate the entire beach.
Scattered shells in the sand shine like stars.
Now would be a good opportunity to hunt for treasure.
Something that can record the sounds of the sea...
If it isn't a device, then it must be some kind of special conch shell after all...
I kneel down and start looking for shells.
Hmm... Well, of course it wouldn't be that easy.
Time flies amidst the quiet until I manage to find one that I suppose will have to do.
It doesn't quite match the legends, but it's better than meeting her empty-handed... I hope she likes it.
Of course I do, Commander.
Right on cue, I hear Pearl's voice.
With a giggle, she emerges from the nearby shoal.
Water drips from her hair and clothes, sparkling in the moonlight.
I love any gift from you, silly.
And look! I have a gift for you, too.
Oh, but fiiirst... Can you show me what you got for me?
The wet girl sidles closer until I can feel her breath and smell the sea on her.
She sets her sights on the shell in my hand.
Is that the treasure? The one that records the sounds of the sea?!
Maybe... the discount version?
Guess I should've opened ten of those treasure chests at the market after all. It might've given me something better than this.
Pfft... Still set on those blind boxes, are you?
She gently takes the conch and presses it to her ear.
Nothing in those chests could hold a candle to this... because you picked it out just for me, Commander.

sequence:
Sounds of the Ocean

<size=45>7 Mutually Treasured</size>

scripts.say: Well... I guess it's time to show you my treasure.
Pearl holds out her right hand and reveals her palm.
Here, Commander.
This treasure is for you.
She shows me a beautiful conch shell with a rare shape.
It has a soft, iridescent shine like mother-of-pearl.
The tranquility and profundity of its shine seem to contain all the light that has ever touched the sea.
Pearl gingerly places it in my hand.
It's all yours, Commander.
Wait... Is this real, honest-to-goodness treasure?
I wouldn't know.
I heard a voice calling for me, and when I followed it, I found this.
Listen... Its song tells the story of all the ocean.
Its beautiful scenery, its ancient and unknowable history, and everything happening in this moment...
And most important of all...
There's a flash of some emotion in her eyes.
I left my voice and all the things I want to say to you in this shell.
Through the mysterious ways of the ocean.
I gaze at the tiny shell that holds the essence of the sea. Subconsciously, I hold it up to my ear.
Holding my breath, I listen for the voice sealed within.
You need to be in a special environment to hear the conch.
It needs to resonate with the ocean, or... with a peaceful heart...
Don't worry. I'd be happy to interpret it for you.
Any time you want, I'll tell you... everything about me.
Nyaaargh! Stop darting all over the place, nya!
*Pant*... *pant*... Unya? Commander, you're back! Perfect timing, nya! Come help me catch these little buggers, nya!
Commander, you saved my hide, nya...
What are these things, nya? Hehe, I thought you'd ask that! These little guys are the results of countless hours of hard work and collaboration between Akashi and the Research Department!
They're called "Meowfficers," nya!
Allow me to introduce them to you!
Meowfficers will accompany your ships into battle, providing various benefits to your fleet, nya!
You'll understand once you see for yourself, nya! First, you'll have to use a Cat Box to train a Meowfficer, nya!
These ordinary kitties normally require a bit of time before they can become qualifed Meowfficers, nya... But just this time, Akashi will carry out some special training, nya!
We're all done, nya! Get ready to meet your first Meowfficer friend, nya!
That's the gist of it, nya! Hm... our current production capacity is a bit limited, nya... Hold on, only the first Cat Box per day is free, nya. After that, there will be a charge, nya!
Heh... hehe... After all, nya~ Akashi and the Meowfficers will be working hard for your sake~
Anyways! If you want to get a lot more Meowfficers, Akashi welcomes your patronage at any time, nya!
I'll send those Meowfficers to you in no time!
In addition to increasing your fleet's power, Meowfficers also have different talents and abilities, but I'll let you discover those on your own, nya!
You can add them to your fleet through "Formations," nya. Huh? What exactly are Meowfficers?
Th-that's a trade secret, nya! You can just think of them as cuddly companions that are both cute and strong, nya!
Anyway, Akashi is busy and has to head back to the store, nya!
That sounds a bit fishy... but let's see what these Meowfficers are capable of...
Owing to Elizabeth's efficient orders, I'd been assigned a mission to attend a commemorative naval review with the Royal Navy before my private plane had even landed in the Orthodoxy.

As such, my plane stopped only for a quick refueling before heading to the Royal Islands – to Scapa Flow, where Elizabeth had been staying for long. It was even starting to become a second administrative center.

sequence: Royal Islands - Scapa Flow Anchorage
Gate of Avalon
Reception Area

scripts.say: Assistant! You've finally come to play with me!
A girl with a stuffed whale in her arms flies at me as soon as I enter the reception room.
Oh, you don't need to be around the whale anymore? What happened to Death's Shadow?
Heheh! She's gone off to somewhere! I don't have to deal with her anymore!
That means I can go anywhere now!
Anywhere as long as it's within range of the Gate, that is.
Hmph! Only because Elizabeth META won't let me go outside! She's a butthead!
You'd be in a lot of trouble if she heard that, young lady.
Yeah, well, screw her!
Elizabeth, Vanguard. Good to see you again.
The same to you, servant. Take a seat. You came just in time for tea. Let's wet our whistles and have a chat, shall we?
I savor a cup of tea while admiring the beautiful garden. Time slips away in this leisurely atmosphere.
I tell Elizabeth about what unfolded in Sky Realm Amahara, as well as what Helena META told me. She falls silent for a while, looking like she's brooding over something.
Yes. She does have a point – since she's no longer here, this is the safest place in the world.
It's clear that she's afraid of something, however. Some kind of danger that would come for you as soon as she left, or something of that nature.
Honestly, I have no idea either. I'd like to ask the META Elizabeth about it.
Would it be possible to get some time with her?
Well, she's currently in the middle of upgrading Avalon's navigation system, you see.
Due to some unique circumstances, even I'm unable to get in direct contact with her.
Fortunately, we do share news once every three days. Our next scheduled contact is actually tomorrow at noon, so I could bring you along then.
That's great. I guess I'll be staying here until then.
But of course. You ought to stay under my protection until the danger has passed.
Bel, bring us something good to eat.
Certainly, Your Majesty.
(Considering how much Helena stressed her point, something seems bound to happen.)
(She was in such a rush that day that she might not have had time to share intel with Memphis and the rest.)
(Even so, it's been several days now. Why hasn't anyone tried to contact me?)
(I'd contact them if I could, but I have no way to do it.)
(I feel so powerless, having no choice but to wait...)

sequence: Royal Islands - Gate of Avalon
Commander's Break Room
Late at Night

scripts.say: Before I go to sleep, I receive a message from Memphis.
Heheh. I'm not in the Orthodoxy's capital anymore, Commander. Can you guess where I am?
I'll let you in on a secret. I made a crazy discovery just a while ago.
If you're lucky, you might receive a surprise in not too long!
Keep an eye out for it!
That's... awfully mysterious of her.
"Surprise," she says. What kind of surprise? Hope it's a good one.
Somewhere, in an unknown location...
As the light fades, a bright campus landscape fills my view.
What the...?
I should be asleep at the Gate of Avalon... Did I end up here as I was dreaming? Sure hope Elizabeth META's defenses weren't breached...
Hi.
Suddenly, I realize there's a girl wearing a white dress in front of me.
Her presence feels so natural, almost like she's been standing here the whole time.
Who are you? Haven't we met before?
Where's Lady E? Is she here?
On vacation.
The girl in the dress suddenly appears under a tree in the distance, then one blink of an eye later, she appears under another tree further away.
Are you telling me to follow you?
Without a word, the girl quickly moves between the trees.
Following her trail of afterimages, I run around the campus.
As I go deeper, a single thought emerges from the back of my mind.
Are you trying to lead me to someone?
Someone other than Lady E?
Hurry.
She suddenly moves a lot faster. I pick up the pace to keep up with her.
Then, as I turn a corner...
The world is instantly repainted a white color. The girl, the school, and everything else vanish.

sequence:
To a Brighter World

<size=45>2 Act One</size>

scripts.say: I open my eyes to the morning sunshine and an unfamiliar ceiling.
...Talk about a big room.
Is this... where I fell asleep last night?
No. Something's not right.
I get dressed and leave the room. Charybdis from the Royal Maids is already there outside the door, waiting for me.
Good morning, Master. I hope that your night at the castle was most pleasant.
Figures. I'm in a castle. Though, I'm pretty sure I went to bed at Av–
The words get stuck in my throat, and my train of thought halts.
Did I... spend the night here?
That is correct.
Your confusion is understandable. It was a busy day for you, with the naval review in the morning and a spontaneous mock night battle with Her Majesty.
Please follow me. Her Majesty awaits you for breakfast in the courtyard.
Charybdis brings me out to the courtyard. When we arrive, Belfast and the Royal Maids have just finished preparing breakfast.
There is a long table set up on the green lawn, at which Elizabeth, Vanguard, Monarch, as well as Illustrious and her sister sit.
Good morning, servant.
Don't just stand there! Come, sit. I reserved this seat just for you.
Despite being surrounded by smiles, I get an odd sense that something isn't quite right.
(A short girl carrying around a stuffed animal... Why do I feel like someone matching that description is missing?)
(Stuffed animal... A stuffed whale?)
Elizabeth, did I bring up anything about a whale yesterday?
A whale? Ladies, do you remember anything?
Hmm... No, I'm afraid I don't remember such a thing. Why do you ask, Commander? Would you like to see a whale?
We don't have any large aquariums at Scapa Flow, sadly. Perhaps at LD Harbour?
Seeing one in its natural habitat would be quite lovely, too!
Although, it would take a while to find one. Are you planning on staying here for an extended time, Commander?
(Yeah. I would like to see a whale. But... not in that way, exactly?)

sequence:
To a Brighter World

<size=45>3 Act Two</size>

scripts.say: After I finished all my business in the Royal Islands, Elizabeth gave me an ardent vacation offer, which I politely declined.
Then, without a minute to rest, I headed to my next destination – the Sea of Stars.
The very moment I set foot on the base, the mood feels strangely off to me.
Every single person I pass looks at me with a smile concealing something deeper, and once I leave their sight, I hear them whisper something among each other.
Memphis spoke of a surprise. Now I'm here, on a sudden visit to the Sea of Stars. The dots connect in my head.
(...Oh my god!)
With my heart beating out of my chest, I walk faster, passing through several wards. Then, finally...
Identity verified. Welcome, Commander.
This is the sickroom where Lexington's care pod was housed. It's supposed to be here, and yet...
It's gone...
I'm glad you came, Commander.
Huh?!
Is... Is that really you?! You've finally woken up! Are you feeling okay?
Of course! I've made a full recovery thanks to the hard work Sara put in day after day.
The next time you see her, be sure to praise her for doing such a good job.
(Huh? Where...)
Where are you? Why can't I see you?
Why, I'm hiding to create a sense of mystery and make it more of a surprise.
Why don't you look for me, hmm?
I look around the room. The cold medical equipment and the care pod have all been put away.
In their place, there is a bed with soft sheets and pillows, a large closet, and a few couches and furnishings. The place feels lived in.
If she's hiding in here, the best place to look would be...
Wait... "Look for me"?
...It's YOU, Saratoga!
Teehee! No surprise you figured it out so quickly!
Whoa! Hey, don't be mad! Take it easy!
I just wanted to lift the mood in this place a bit, you know? Plus, this surprise isn't for you – it's for Lex as well.
Okay... So Lexington really did make it?
Yep! I was just having a little bit of fun with you. I wouldn't go THAT far, you know.
I mean, listen. Do you hear that?
I listen closely, and I hear a pair of voices from the hallway, drawing closer.
I saw all your test results came back looking great. What a relief!
Why, of course. I know my body better than anyone else.
If Sara weren't such a worrywart, I think I'd have gotten a discharge yesterday.
Ahaha... It wasn't just her – we've ALL been worried. Remember, don't assume things and be careful.
Sure, but some of the things they tested for today were a bit... odd, it felt like.
It feels like I'm being kept in the dark. Are you and Sara planning something?
Ahaha... Well, the thing is...
Oh! Lex! You've got a guest!
Go on. Open the door and see for yourself!
Identity verified. Welcome, Lexington and Memphis.
With an automated announcement, the door silently opens.
Huh?!
Lexington stands at the entrance to the room. There is nothing standing between us now.
I'm glad to be back, {playername} – my Commander.
This was certainly a surprise by any meaning of the word. A pure, massive, and unexpected surprise.
So much so that when Lexington was reprimanding Saratoga for her prank, I couldn't help but tell her to let it go.
As Saratoga went on to explain, it was a series of recent technological breakthroughs at the Sea of Stars that made Lexington's recovery possible.
In the back of my mind, I felt a little doubt and a dash of discomfort about these breakthroughs...
However, those were unimportant compared to what really mattered.
That Lexington was back with us.

sequence:
To a Brighter World

<size=45>4 Act Three</size>

scripts.say: We have located all of the Sirens' hidden test sites across the Pacific.
Now it is time to clear them out in one fell swoop and restore peace to this ocean.
Commander, welcome to PH Harbor.
I hereby cede command over the Pacific theater to you. Lead us to victory.
There are operations taking place across the world to eliminate the remnants of the Sirens.
Among all the regions, the one with the largest remnant force is the Pacific Ocean.
It's for that reason that I've returned to PH Harbor to resume a duty that I haven't performed in a long time – that of a fleet commander.
Tester once ruled over this ocean, and now there remains no sign of her.
What few test sites remain will stand no chance against us.
Precisely. Thanks to the Commander uniting our various factions with different goals, we're able to work together and destroy one mainframe after another.
The first light of daybreak now shines upon us.
Commander, you have the full cooperation of the Sakura Empire's fleets and regional bases!
Heehee. United we stand, and step by step do we advance. Together, we will fully reclaim the Pacific.
Later that night...
During my voyage with the fleet, I had something I hadn't experienced in a while – a dream.
A figure draped in red was running through a field of dark clouds.
Commander! Commandeeer!
She was cradling the Watatsumi, a faint light emitting from her body.
Commander, you must return to Amahara at once! I have something I need to tell you!
Her expression was contorted with panic, like something was chasing her from behind.
Please... Please make haste!
Pure white enveloped the world in an instant. Akagi, the dark clouds, and everything else were gone.

sequence:
To a Brighter World

<size=45>5 Act Four</size>

scripts.say: Based on prior experience, I can't dismiss this as just another dream, given that Akagi and the Watatsumi were involved.
And so, I decide to adjust the fleet's course toward the Sakura Empire under the pretense of inquiring about the state of Amahara's reconstruction.
Commander, whilst we did experience some rather disagreeable malfunctions, the Venerable Three have already reconstructed the dubitable areas.
Amahara is now, for all intents and purposes, free of concealed dangers.
At present, we are making efforts to further bolster the barriers' mentally stabilizing effects, as well as putting into practice a plan to expand the Five Provinces and Seven Districts.
As a positive side effect, all within the range of Amahara's grace have additionally reported a notably improved quality of sleep.
From what I heard, it sounded like the Amahara Project had finally gotten on the right track.
After an exchange of technological progress, I decided to visit Akagi's residence by myself.
However, once I arrive, I'm instead greeted by an unexpected character.
A pleasure it is to see you again, Commander. Do you have any business with Akagi?
...Hakuhou? Yeah, I wanna talk to her.
She apparently had something to tell me. Can I see her?
My apologies. Akagi is... not in a state fit for conversation at the moment.
What do you mean?
An unpleasant feeling crawls into my mind.
You see, a few days ago, Akagi took the Watatsumi without our permission.
Once we understood what had happened, we discovered her fast asleep in her own room.
Miss Yamato speculates that Akagi had used the Watatsumi to perform some kind of ritual. This ritual is believed to have failed and caused some damage to her psyche.
While it doesn't appear to be severe, only the heavens know when she might wake up again.
Perhaps as little as a few months. Perhaps as much as a few years...
The creeping feeling I had was right.
I asked Hakuhou to lead me to where Akagi is.
There she lies on the bed, a look of calm restfulness on her face. She's in a deep slumber.
(This reminds me a lot of Marco– Wait, who?)
A thought crosses my mind, only to instantly vanish like it went up in smoke.
Akagi has reliable people like Yamato at her side. I don't need to be too worried about her.
If only I could know when she'll wake up, and what she was trying to tell me in that dream.
After leaving Amahara behind, I suddenly receive a message from Veneto.
Greetings and salutations, Commander.
I've been informed that the fleet you're leading across the Pacific Ocean has enjoyed victory after victory, and I wish to congratulate you.
Should circumstances permit it, once your campaign there is over, could you offer your aid to the Mediterranean Sea?
As you are aware, the situation here is exceedingly complicated, and the Sirens' lingering forces are powerful indeed.
The greatest help we could ask for is if you were to personally take command in our battles.
I sincerely hope to hear back from you soon.
Also, I look forward to a chance to personally speak to you about a vacation in– Pardon, I meant, "Speak to you about our campaign."
...She just said "vacation," didn't she?
"As you are aware," the enemy they're fighting is "powerful indeed."
She doesn't sound the least bit convincing.
That said, the reports I've read from the front over the past few days say the enemy is way weaker than anticipated.
If they stay that way, then we'll fully wrap up the Pacific campaign within this month.
And if we do, wouldn't it be nice to go to the Mediterranean?
The Mediterranean...
Our next target after the Pacific is supposed to be the Atlantic.
On the other hand, the storm at the heart of it has calmed down, making that front rather stable.
Beyond that, there's also the South Pacific and the Mediterranean. It doesn't matter much which one we pick.
Then let's go to the Mediterranean! Veneto's already asked for help, so the situation must be pretty dire, right?
That's true. What do you say, Commander?
(They've got "Please! Let's go there!" written all over their faces...)
Alright. The Mediterranean is our next objective.
Sweet!
Sky Realm Amahara - ???
After Amahara regained its calm, the woman lying in bed opened her eyes.
The Commander has left...
This time, it was I who broke a promise between us...
"Your meeting was not to be. Bide your time."
"All outside interference has gone. You are the one thing remaining."
"By which I mean – you are the final anomaly."
"Were it discovered, it shall be amended."
"Thus shall this world's system achieve self-congruency."
"The Commander shan't awaken again."
Urgh...
Please, Commander... Don't let those bright possibilities carry you away...
After softly sighing out her plight, Akagi quietly closed her eyes again, sinking back into her deep sleep.

sequence:
To a Brighter World

<size=45>6 Act Five</size>

scripts.say: By the end of the month, the Pacific campaign had concluded as expected, and I made my way to the Sardegna Empire.
After a series of formal events, it was finally time to convene a military conference to get things on track...
That is, until I learned a shocking fact – the Sardegna Empire hadn't even begun amassing its fleet.
I was somewhat braced for this, but seeing it with my own eyes, I couldn't help but sigh.
With little option left but to stay for a few days longer, I decided to enjoy the beautiful sights around the capital.
Today, Memphis, Helena, and I have come to the Grand Cathedral Museum, the most famous of its kind in Rome.
In line with its name, its interior is absolutely stunning.
Helena appears fascinated with the many sculptures in the animal hall.
Memphis, meanwhile, looks around at the paintings in the art gallery.
This place has an interesting layout.
This place, too... It's got a lot of history, and these buildings are massive.
(I hope she hasn't confused that antique map of Sardegna for some kind of tourist map.)
(Ancient castles, old maps... It feels like I'm forgetting something.)
(Oh, right! Ever since I got here, it's felt like another important person should be here...)
Hahaha! Commander! I take it the Museum is to your liking?
Just as I sink deep into thought, a buoyant voice rings out in my ear.
Yeah. This place has earned its reputation. It's well worth the visit.
I'm glad to hear it.
As it so happens, our fleets have finished amassing and our flagship has arrived in Rome. I've heard we can convene the conference shortly.
At long last. How about–
One more thing. Veneto and I would like to host the conference tomorrow morning. Is that fine with you?
Ah, seems the Museum is about to close. Why don't we go and spend the rest of the day sightseeing?
Alright. Sounds like a plan.
Heh – it's not like you could cover the whole Museum in a single day anyway.
If you feel like visiting again, do give me a call.
I'd be glad to show you around not just the Museum, but the spectacles around all of Sardegna.
We have ample time, and there's no shortage of things to see in our country.
(She's totally in vacation mode...)
Okay, then could you show us around the old town of Florence?
Oh, and the Lighthouse of Genoa! I wanna see that!
I would love to, Signorina! Incidentally, I saw you passionately eyeing that mural a minute ago...
Searching for places to visit, were we? Ah, such a brilliant mind you have!
Florence and Genoa are splendid places, of course, but I also strongly recommend you pay a visit to the aquatic city that is Venice!
As the topic changes to vacation destinations, Memphis and Littorio suddenly find a wide array of things to talk about.
Based on the intel I've gathered over the past days, the Siren force situated in the Mediterranean is – as previously thought – the weakest among all the theaters.
Four groups have jointly undertaken the task of sweeping them up – the Royal Navy, the Iris Orthodoxy, Iron Blood, and the Sardegna Empire.
Iron Blood's fleet is being led by Bismarck, while Richelieu commands the Orthodoxy's force.
(The Sirens' fates are practically sealed already.)
(Looks like my stay in the Sardegna Empire will be a leisurely vacation after all.)

sequence:
To a Brighter World

<size=45>7 Act Six</size>

scripts.say: During my stay in Sardegna, I received status updates from all the various fronts.
The remaining Siren forces in the Antarctic Ocean, the Pacific Ocean, the South Pacific Ocean, the Atlantic Ocean, and the Arctic Ocean have all been eliminated.
Reports of victory have also come in from the Great Lakes, the Caspian Sea, the Dead Sea, Lake Baikal, Lake Victoria, and many other inland bodies of water.
As I'm compiling all of this news into one report, something suddenly dawns on me – we've reached a juncture that will go down in human history.
At this point in time, all the Siren stragglers on the planet have been completely eliminated.
After fighting the Sirens for so many years, we have finally achieved a complete victory over them.
Once this news gets public, the whole world will rejoice in celebration...
While going through battle reports from across the world, an unexpected notice from the Northern Parliament reaches me.
Comrade Commander, based on the Siren data we recovered, we have discovered enormous, perfectly-preserved Siren facilities at the North and South Poles, one in each.
We, the Northern Parliament, have been studying polar magnetism trajectories occurring during geomagnetic reversals.
It is our belief that these newly discovered facilities are the cause of the planet's magnetic trajectory anomalies.
It's believed the Sirens used these facilities to manipulate our poles, intentionally aligning our geographic poles with our geomagnetic ones.
As for why they did something like this, we don't yet know.
However, based on other data, we learned about a huge risk associated with the sun entering a period of activity.
Under certain circumstances, the energy particle flow found in solar winds can interact with space-time itself, causing a series of time-space anomalies with anything in their path.
This can create an array of Singularities that, while unstable, short-lived, and coming in various sizes, are most certainly still Singularities.
