We all make mistakes sometimes, even the Commander.
Also, that brooch was a gift. I'm a bit peeved to hear it was given to someone else.
I'd wager it being in your hands is the reason it didn't work.
Regardless, now we've come face to face. Would you mind giving it back to me?
With a nod, Shinano handed over the brooch to Clemenceau.
Now, I've already launched an investigation into this strange phenomenon.
The Commander was wise to send you here. I'm going to need your power, and we want as many awoken people on our side as possible.
Speaking of your power, I'd like to put it to use as soon as possible.
You're able to enter other people's dreams, yes? I have a particular one in mind...

sequence:
Crimson Prelusion

<size=45>4 Dream - Vainglorious</size>

scripts.say: Somewhere in the Sardegna Empire, two shipgirls were walking through a garden, admiring all the flowers.
I certainly wasn't expecting you to lead the delegation here in person.
With you here, I'm sure your pavilion will attract the whole World Expo's attention.
Why, I'd never. It would be rude of me to steal the spotlight from the hosts.
However, I am eager and excited to create the SECOND most eye-catching pavilion.
Heehee. Don't create too stiff competition for us, please.
Of course not. I won't overdo it.
By the way, I'd like to ask you for a personal favor. May I ask you to hear me out?
A personal favor, you say? Would you like a tour guide? Or perhaps a seat at a restaurant?
I can do almost anything you'd like, so let's hear it.
Well... there's someone I'd like to meet.
You, the Sardegnians, volunteering as hosts for the World Expo was a move of divine brilliance.
Whoever came forth with the suggestion to you must be a person of great ambition and vision.
For that reason, I'd like to talk to them. Could you make that happen?
Ah, you must mean Marco Polo.
(Now that she mentions it, Marco hasn't even gotten the chance to appear at the World Expo, even though she's the architect of it.)
(I feel a bit sad for her. She deserves some time in the limelight.)
I believe she's in our capital right now. I'll arrange a meeting between you two.
Thank you so much. I can't wait to speak to her.
Hmph! I, on the other hand, couldn't care less about you!
The sky burst with a dazzling light, and a throne adorned with white wings revealed itself.
All the land beneath the throne vanished in an instant, being replaced by a whiteness that spanned from horizon to horizon.
The throne slowly descended from the sky, and its pilot came into view.
I was perfectly content to fill my days with drawing up plans at the time! I don't need your pity, Veneto!
As for YOU... Who are you?
Vile creatures like you have no place in my glorious empire!
Mar▇o, wh▇t ▇▇▇ you ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ ▇bout?
Hah! You can hardly even talk.
Vanish from my sight!
Struck with holy light, the doppelganger of Amagi was reduced to black mist before vanishing altogether.
The next moment, a set of torii gates appeared in the dreamscape, from out of which Shinano leaped forth.
Marco Polo, you must think carefully before you act in this dream world!
In these circumstances, haphazard movement is very dangerous...
Marco... Polo? Shinano, too?
Veneto? Apologies for intruding upon your dream, albeit unwillingly... Have you awoken from the illusion?
I suppose I have... What's going on now?
I thought Marco Polo was still in a comatose state! What is she doing here? Why are you here, for that matter?
Use your eyes, woman! I've gained a new source of power and effortlessly crushed this illusion with it!
Next, I will realize the next step of my plan! I only just came up with it, but no matter!
You, Shinano – it was you who awoke me, no?
Then I have a trustworthy ally! Magnificent! I guarantee you will get your share of the pie later!
It was this one who awoke you, yes – however, you are still dreaming, and the power you feel is but my own...
"Still dreaming"? So what I see here is not reality, even though I'm awake?
Hmm. You did say something about a "dream world" a minute ago...
Your mind is still in the dreamscape... All this one did was pull you here...
Bah. No wonder I "awoke" to such a dreadful sight. I thought someone had already stolen my sweet Sardegna from me.
Thank goodness it's just a dream... No, wait, that's not good at all!
If I've already awoken, as you claim, then how do I wake up in the REAL world?
Alas... I do not know...
So I'm trapped, then?!
My power will not hold for long... I awoke you so I could ask you questions on behalf of Clemenceau...
Clemenceau, you say? Hah! I won't tell her a damn thing!
You must... This one shan't leave empty-handed...
Well? Are you going to stare all day or ask your questions? You're wasting your limited time!
I said I won't tell HER a damn thing! That doesn't mean I won't answer your questions!
As you say...
Know you anything about a Sakuran envoy lending your country a fragment of the Watatsumi?
Ah, the Watatsumi. If I remember right, you led the team that transported it from the Iron Blood's Floating Fortress, and...
Tsk! Right!
Yes? Do you remember something?
No, forget it! I know nothing about any blasted Watatsumi fragment!
Very well... Then, know you about any other sort of gift from the Sakura Empire?
That, I do. When I was amassing antiques and works of art, I received quite a few from you Sakurans.
I believe I put them in a warehouse in Venice.
Pardon? We searched that warehouse and didn't find a single Sakuran artifact.
You did WHAT?! That was MY private warehouse!
Oh, please. Did you really think we'd leave your warehouse alone when you'd caused a crisis of cataclysmic proportions?
Wh-whatever! I never said you COULDN'T search it!
Just know that those artifacts are all invaluable! Search if you must, but be careful with them!
Anything else? I'm getting quite tired all of... a... sudden...
If that'll... be all... I'll just... Zzzzz...
Marco Polo and her throne were there one moment, then gone the next.
Marco!
What... What just happened?
The power given unto me by the dream ran out... Now she sleeps once more...
Marco Polo's case is exceedingly special, making it very taxing to keep her here...
I see... So then you awoke her briefly to ask those questions? Could you share more about this "Watatsumi fragment"?
I'm afraid 'tis complicated... This one shall explain it in the waking world...
I understand. Let us speak again in the real world.

sequence:
Crimson Prelusion

<size=45>5 Reality - In the Eagle Union</size>

scripts.say: The Eagle Union's NY base had fallen into chaos.
Gone was the sight of the ordinarily orderly workplace. Staff rushed to and fro, clamoring and rushing to complete their tasks.
Amidst all this chaos, Saratoga furrowed her brow, trying her hardest to stay calm and reestablish order – or, at least, trying to make sense of the situation.
From Easter Island, to the bases at AF and PH... The same strange stuff is happening everywhere...
Headquarters can't settle on a story either! What is it? A mistake? A transmission error? Nothing at all?!
Like I'd believe that! The Pacific is a total mess! You can't tell me there's nothing going on!
Ugh... If only the base at SD wasn't in the middle of a staff handover... If only Missouri wasn't on her way to DC and Yorktown wasn't away...
This couldn't have come at a worse time...
At the same time, complaining about it won't solve anything! I need to look for answers!
BEEP BEEP!
Hey, Sara, I found another report you'll want to look at.
From the Pacific again?
Not this time. It's from the Panama Canal.
Panama?! Let me see it, quick!
They're... hosting a ceremony to celebrate victory against the Sirens?
I don't think there's been any major battles around there lately... Could you get Intrepid to check?
Roger!
Sara, I've got a report as well.
Thanks, but we're completely swamped right now. Please keep it strictly to top priority reports.
It IS top priority. From Europa, too.
Wait, Europa?
Yeah.
That's where the Commander is... Show it to me!
Oh my gosh... Not even Europa is safe from it...
What in the world is happening? Are they all dreaming or something?
Unless... that's it! What if they're under the effects of a massive mind attack, like what happened at the World Expo?
And... the Commander has been redeployed to the Dragon Empery? Phew. It should be safe there, at least.
BEEP BEEP!
What is it THIS time?!
Whoa! I hope this isn't a bad time...
Sorry, I'm just tense. Do you have any news?
Yes. DC finally replied to us.
Thank gosh! What did Iowa say?
Well, um, it wasn't Iowa who replied...
It wasn't her? Weird. I explicitly addressed it to her... Anyway, send it to me!
What? "Iowa is dealing with a delegation from the Sakura Empire and won't be able to assist in other missions for some time"?
But... didn't that delegation leave five days ago? How is she STILL dealing with them?
And how can THAT possibly be more important than THIS?
Ugh... I feel a headache coming on...
BEEP BEEP!
Hey, Sara...
Yes? What's the bad news this time?
We've... lost contact with the Sea of Stars.
Wait, what?
No... Even they haven't gone unscathed...
But how? Its location is classified, its defense systems are cutting-edge, and some of our best people are stationed there...
And... it's where Lex's care pod is...
No! I can't let anything happen to the Sea of Stars!
She hung up, stashed her secret documents in her locker, then hurried her way down the stairs to the underground level.
NY Base - Underground Passage

Following the near-superimposition event, the Eagle Union obtained the key pieces – local samples from the Orthodoxy and intel on its microlayer transference system – they needed to finally begin research on Siren teleportation technology.
One result of this research is the Star Bridge – a high-speed network directly linking the NY base to the Sea of Stars.
That's where Saratoga was going – to the underground bridge of hope.
They've calibrated the Star Bridge... It should take me straight to the Sea of Stars!
The flame of hope in her heart spurred her on, making her run even faster.
Huh? Saratoga? I thought you were busy up in the command center.
Is the Star Bridge ready? Can it be started right here and now?
What? What's the "Star Bridge"?
The machine that makes a portal straight to the Sea of Stars! What else?
"Sea of Stars"? What's that? You sound disoriented. Should I call a doctor for you?
(Oh no... Now the mind attack is affecting people in NY, too!)
(And we still haven't figured out anything about it!)
(The Sea of Stars is the key to turning this situation around... I NEED to get there!)
Saratoga made it to the room where the Star Bridge was kept.
Inside, however, there was nothing. Only an empty room.
Has... the mind attack finally reached me?
No, it's not over yet! Even if it's blocking out the Star Bridge from my mind, it can't just erase it from reality!
Even if I can't see it or even feel it, it MUST be here, and the Sea of Stars must be on the other side of it!
Assuming I'm right, I just need to find a way to activate it!
Relying solely on her memory, she reached for the empty space in front of her, pressing buttons and keys on a panel that didn't exist.
After fiddling with it for a long time, she finally heard the faint noise of a machine starting up.
I did it! Now I just need to step through the portal!
She walked up to the portal platform and looked down to see only an abyss with no bottom in sight.
Trying to scare me, huh?
She stood at the edge of the abyss, eyes closed.
It's all just an illusion...
The way through is right here. I just need to walk forward to get to the Sea of Stars and see Lex!
Don't be afraid, Sara!
Just as she took a step toward the abyss, she felt like a tremendous force stopped her in her tracks.
When she opened her eyes again, she found herself standing in a busy shopping district.
There, not far away from her on the main road, stood someone who was waiting for her.
There you are, Sara.
I've been waiting for you. Has everything been going smoothly?
Lex... You're here?

sequence:
Crimson Prelusion

<size=45>6 Reality - The Storm</size>

scripts.say: I'm on board a private plane, cruising on a steady course through the Dragon Empery's airspace.
While I can't see the ground for the clouds, we should be getting ready to descend sometime soon.
We've been accompanied by escort aircraft ever since we entered the Empery's airspace. I'm happy to say it's been a smooth journey thus far.
And yet, gazing at the dark clouds in the distance, I can't help but feel anxious.
That over there – that's the infamous Storm, isn't it?
Indeed. It's so enormous that it's nigh-impossible to avoid crossing it.
Calling it A storm would be a bit of a misnomer, though. It's actually comprised of several storms of varying sizes moving as one.
Not only are they linked to one another in direct violation of the laws of physics, they also rage all year round, effectively forming an impassable barrier.
That's also why the Empery's coastline is always blocked off.
You can't even think about dispatching a fleet in this weather.
Precisely. Our waters, both near and far, are always off-limits to us.
Moreover, the Storm's strength fluctuates. Sometimes it's stronger, other times it's weaker.
When it grows in intensity, it also affects a wider area.
It still gets worse. Not only does the Storm ravage our coastlines, it's also a path for Sirens to invade through.
This leads some to speculate that the Sirens are responsible for it.
It blocks your sea access AND there's a good chance it serves as a base for the Sirens, eh.
That certainly explains why the Empery can't send its fleets abroad.
Yes. We would if we could.
On a topic related to the Storm, the area around it has been affected by strange phenomena lately, hasn't it?
Ah. I'm surprised you know about that.
Yes, we believe the Sirens redeployed their forces across the globe following the battle of the Antarctic. That includes the waters around the Storm as well, naturally.
While their presence weakened on the whole, their presence actually grew quite a lot in the regions plagued by the Storm.
Worse yet, their long-dormant strongholds in the Marianas sprung back to life. Their observed presence there grows with each passing day.
The Marianas also play a part in our upcoming operation.
Let me guess – you're going to finally strike back at the Storm?
You are correct. They've kept us prisoner on our own coastline for too long, and now it's time for payback.
How likely is the plan to succeed?
With your help – 100%. Heehee.
The plane starts to descend, and the beautiful, splendid lands below the clouds come into view.
At the same time, a curtain of light rises skyward in the distance, towering over the greenery on the horizon.
Hey, Chen Hai, what's that? Don't tell me we're under attack!
Oh, not at all. That is our barrier to protect against the Storm – the Pingfeng System.
We activated it just to be safe since you were coming, even if the Storm is on the calmer side of things today.
It's nice that they did. The landing process is going very smoothly on account of the curtain blocking out the turbulent weather.
You know, your Pingfeng System reminds me a bit of the Orthodoxy's Skybound Wall.
Is it a product of the two of you sharing technology, by any chance?
I'm... surprised you'd ask about that. I had no hand in its development, so I'm afraid I can't answer your question.
However, I'm sure you'll find someone who can soon. We'll be going to a banquet later, with many in attendance.
A banquet? Why?
Yat Sen insisted on it. She said you'll be tired after such a long journey, and a banquet will be just the thing to get you comfortable. We'll discuss the important things later.
It's how they do things. The Empery always treats its guests well.
Ahh. Sounds like you know their culture well.
Yeah, in fact, I do!
I used to work as an ambassador, remember? I've done the reading.
Yat Sen's motorcade should arrive at the airport any minute now.
The touchdown will be a little bumpy, so I suggest you put your seatbelts on.

sequence:
Crimson Prelusion

<size=45>7 Reality - The Guardian Fox's Resolve</size>

scripts.say: A group of Sakuran shipgirls stood on the Solomon Islands – a former frontline in the war against the Sirens.
These islands, and the bases on them, haven't seen war for a long time since peace settled in around the world.
There were no flames, no stench of gunpowder anywhere across the islands dotting the landscape. There was only a tropical paradise, extending as far as the eye could see.
It feels strange, being in a place this tranquil with a fleet as large as ours.
I would welcome it if we were on vacation, but alas...
They sent us so far away from the mainland. Why? I can't think of a good reason why they'd do it.
Yeah. Seems fishy.
I've heard it was a joint decision between Mikasa and Musashi.
Strange, then, that the Great Veteran herself isn't with us. Hiei, have you heard anything from her?
I did speak to her before leaving, but all she said was that she wanted us to investigate the strange phenomena reported around here.
The only other thing I got from her is that she seemed to be in a terribly bad mood.
Hmm. If I'd known this was coming, I would've stayed home with Zuikaku and made myself scarce.
Then Lady Nagato wouldn't have a carrier to protect her! We all need you.
You're along for the ride now, at any rate. Relax – I'm sure this will go fine.
Lady Nagato, it seems your escorts have mixed opinions about this redeployment.
I am aware.
I'm planning our next move and will announce it shortly.
Tell them to stay calm and remain in position.
As you command.
The loyal servant left Nagato's chamber, after which she breathed a sigh.
Great Veteran... What did you and Musashi discuss that day?
It is blatantly obvious that you and she decided on this redeployment.
Rumors are abound that this is a ploy on your part to ostracize me.
I know, of course, that it is not.
You mean only to keep me safe, but doing so this way, it comes at the cost of your own safety.
For this reason, I permitted Zuikaku to remain on the mainland.
I can only hope she will serve you well...
The dark room fell silent once more.
Many minutes passed.
First came Yamato's warning... Then your redeployment orders.
The abnormality I sensed in the Sacred Sakura when I left the mainland... Is it related to this?
You and Musashi are trying to prepare for the looming threat. That, I understand.
However, there is no Sacred Sakura on these Solomon Islands.
Even if the strange phenomena do warrant investigation, there is nothing for me to do here.
It almost makes me think you are purposely keeping me far away just to protect me...
The girl kneeling on the ground grasped her sleeves and clenched them tightly.
After all these ups and downs, twists and turns... I have not changed in the slightest...
I seek to break free from fate, yet here I am, walking a path laid out by someone else...
I swore to myself I would run away no longer, and I broke my own promise...
If only I'd stood up for myself and not thoughtlessly accepted your order...
Our country will soon face a great danger, and I should be at your side to face it with you...
Instead, I sit here alone, all because I had a lapse of conviction...
You're mistaken, Lady Nagato.
Your redeployment to these islands wasn't some sort of jailbreak – it was a collective decision, and the correct one, at that.
Mikasa is withholding things from you, but you intuited them and agreed with the decision, no?
Kongou?
My apologies for stopping by unannounced.
I was walking by and saw Kawakaze grimacing, so I took it upon myself to check on you.
Also, this next move of yours... It won't be to return straight to the mainland, will it?
I... No, I will not go that far.
Come in and sit. I've been meaning to have a word with you.
Kongou bowed her head, stepped inside, and took a seat opposite Nagato.
You are correct, Kongou.
When I saw the Great Veteran's expression upon her return, I knew it instinctively.
I knew why she had joined forces with Musashi, the one she swore to persuade to our side.
After some thought, I came upon the realization that our country is already in danger.
Swift decisions must be made, and it matters little whether I am present or not. That is how serious this danger that we face is.
Better would be to keep me in reserve, far away from the threat, so I may serve as the spark that ignites a counterattack, should the worst come to fruition.
That, I suspect, is also the rationale behind Musashi sending Shinano to Europa.
I see the logic of her actions, it's just...
I... I doubt my own ability as a soldier. I do not know if I can spark a counterattack.
The Great Veteran believes in you, as do I.
*sigh*...
Nagato's clenched fists loosened their grip on her sleeves.
Then my misgivings were for nothing.
Mikasa said that something strange has happened here, and there is naught else for me to do than investigate it.
Once that is done, we will return to the Sakura Islands and save everything!

sequence:
Moments with the Young Miss

<size=45>1 The First Sound Under the Sky</size>

scripts.say: As I was taking a walk after finishing work, I noticed some beads of sweat forming on my brow.
“It wasn’t this hot earlier this morning,” I thought to myself as I looked towards the crisp, blue sky.
CRAAAAACK——!!!
Gahh!! How are you so good at hitting these?!
A solitary white baseball cut across the calm sky— along with Achilles’ remorseful voice.
Oh my... How many home runs does that make now...?
I stopped counting after about ten or so. Who knows how many we’re at by now?
It seemed like the three Leander-class sisters were playing baseball. Deciding to take a look, I turned towards the direction of their voices...
Hehe~♪ If my memory serves me correctly, that would make 16 home runs.
Looks like I’m starting to get a good feel for this. Give me a few more pitches, please~
Ehhh... Give me a break already... No matter how blazing my fastballs are, you always hit them back easily...
Achilles was crouching over the ground, clutching her head in distress. Apparently, the three sisters had been keeping Chaser company.
I certainly did not envy those girls, having to play baseball against one of the Bogue-class sisters.
Oh my, isn’t it a bit early to be giving up? What happened to all that bravado from earlier~?
I never would’ve challenged you if I knew you were so stroooong~!
Hehe, fine by me. Let’s call it for the day then— Hey, isn’t that the commander over there?
Having noticed me, Chaser and the three Leander sisters waved.
Did you come here after seeing all those home runs I hit?

options.content: Your hits had a really pleasant ring to them.

scripts.say: Thanks for the compliment— but having that said, I still can’t return a single one of Bogue’s pitches.
Oh right, Commander, are you busy right now? I’d like to talk to you if possible.
Luckily, I had already finished my work and had no plans for the time being.
When I said that to her, Chaser smiled and walked up next to me.
Great. Can I count on you to escort me then, Commander?
I nodded in response to her joking tone, and we headed to the office together after she waved goodbye to the Leander sisters.

sequence:
Moments with the Young Miss

<size=45>2 Novel Tea Novelty</size>

scripts.say: We were both pretty parched from being outside in the heat, and Chaser went to pour some iced barley tea.
Commander, I’ll pour some for you as well, so just sit tight. I’m an expert at this.
Hmm... this is barley tea, not black tea? I don’t think I’ve ever had this before. Hehe, how interesting~
Chaser poured the barley tea into a teacup rather than a regular cup, and sat down in front of me, face-to-face across the desk.
So, let’s get to the issue at hand.。
Did you know I received an order from Queen Elizabeth the other day?
If I recalled properly... it was an order to send a representative from the Royal Navy to each camp to facilitate communication.
If you’ve already heard about it from Her Majesty, that should save us some time. Anyway, I am one of the representatives.
Of course, our friends from the other camps will also be visiting us as well, for the sake of strengthening our cooperation.
As she spoke, Chaser passed me a letter from Queen Elizabeth.
I opened the envelope carefully, revealing the luxurious stationery within. I could practically hear the Queen’s words in my head as I read the contents.
——If you’re reading this letter, you must already have heard what Chaser has to say. In short, the purpose of this exchange is to enhance our mutual understanding.
To be honest though, there’s nothing particularly serious about this. It’s nice for the different camps to visit each other.
Chaser is rather new at this, though, so I would have you, my loyal servant, support her. Won’t you?
―Well? What did Her Majesty write?
I explained the contents of the letter to Chaser.
Hmm. Really, I’d prefer to go on my own, if I might. But I wouldn’t want to get it from the Commander on the back end either.
Alright, it’s a boon from Her Majesty, after all. I will accept it with gratitude. Of course, that’s assuming you aren’t too busy, Commander?
It was no trouble at all. I picked up my teacup, took a sip, and prepared to set off.
It had the makings of an interesting time.
Thank you very much, Commander.
Chaser let slip a little chuckle.
Then, as if suddenly remembering something, she raised the milk jug she was carrying and poured it into her tea.
What’s the matter, Commander? Milk makes tea so much better. That’s just common sense, no?
She sipped at her milk barley tea as she spoke.
...Indeed, a tea of subtle flavour.
Chaser mumbled to herself, rolling her eyes as she covered her mouth.

sequence:
Moments with the Young Miss

<size=45>3 Curiosity and Cake</size>

scripts.say: ―Chaser’s first day with another camp.
This is the Vichiya dormitory! Let’s hurry inside.
Chaser quietly pushed the door open and went through.
Oh~ The interior design is really quite different from the Royal Navy’s...
The Curious Chaser pointed to every little thing in the room.
Oh? That’s an unfamiliar face... and the Commander with her?
...Oh, you’re the girl they sent from the Royal Navy. I am Dunkerque. Would you tell me your name?
Good day, Dunkerque. I am Chaser. Are you familiar with our plan for the day?
Yes. You’ll be watching our exercises and sitting in on classes.
And... I’ve prepared a special cake for you as a welcoming gift. You can look forward to that. Hehe~
A cake! Marvelous! I’ve brought some delicious teas myself, I do hope you’ll let me serve you.
That’s something to look forward to―Forgive me, I have a prior engagement...
Dunkerque walked toward the back with an air of mild exhaustion, Chaser following naturally behind her.
I felt like we were meant to wait at the entrance, but seeing them grow farther and farther from me, I was left with no choice but to follow as well.
Now then, you seem rather tired.
Hm. You and the Commander followed me... I forgot to ask you to wait by the door.
Something the matter? The Commander and I aren’t troubling you, are we...?
No. I worked very late last night, but if I could just take a short rest with some sweets...
I’ve just the thing!
I’ll get out the tea I brought, and Dunkerque, you fetch that cake of yours a little early. What do you say?
That would mean major changes to our plans... I’m not sure if the other girls with their lessons and exercises would be okay?
We still have some time to the next activity, yes? Besides, this isn’t any sort of serious study situation, we’re just having a break!
Chaser then leaned in and whispered directly to my ear.
(...I’d thought the Vichiya a dreadfully dedicated folk, and yet, here we are!)
Chaser chuckled and spun around cheerfully to look Dunkerque in the eye.
Now then, Dunkerque, would you show us to the kitchen?
Chaser had proven her curiosity a valuable asset when it comes to plunging into unfamiliar situations.
...Actually, I’d say what really mattered more was the way she cared about other people, and charmed them in doing so.

sequence:
Moments with the Young Miss

<size=45>4 When in Rome</size>

scripts.say: Chaser’s visit to the Northern Parliament on the second day of her mission went off without a hitch.
Commander, Chaser, what do you think of our camp?
Oh, everyone’s so cooperative, and responsive. The Royal Navy has a lot to learn from you, I think. I know I learned a lot.
Did you now? Hehehe. By the way, you will join us for dinner, won’t you?
Say, now that you mention it, it is getting rather late. Since we’re here, we might as well?
Excellent. This way, please...
Northern Parliament Dormitory - Canteen
Wow! That’s a huge table! Does your whole fleet come to dinner?
It depends on the day. We’ve got a lot of unique personalities among us...
Oh... Dear Comrade and the Royal Navy girl. You’re still here...
Yes, we’re here for dinner. I trust that won’t be a problem!
Oh. Then you can try the borscht. It’s good.
Thank you. And in return, I’ll make you a fine tea.
Sorry to keep you waiting~ Do please enjoy my special Chaser Blend♪
Right then... here you are!
Chaser plopped some ice cubes into the tea.
I’ve heard you Northerners like to drink iced tea. Enjoy♪
It’s... astonishing...
...You can tell she’s run the shipping lanes to the Northern Parliament a lot...
Hehe, time for me to have some too♪
And so, we all had some tea together.
...Hot is nice, but cold is good too! Drink up, Commander♪
I’d thought her only familiar with Eagle Union culture. I never knew she could learn the Northern Parliament just as well...

sequence:
Moments with the Young Miss

<size=45>5 A Passion for the Exotic</size>

scripts.say: After her visit to the Northern Parliament, Chaser spent time with the other camps, one after another.
On the last day of her mission, she arrived at the Sakura Empire, scarcely able to contain her excitement.
The Sakura Empire is the home of the samurai and ninjas. You must know this, Commander?
Her image of the land and its people was clearly shaped by Union movies, but I dared not get into the topic.
Commander, we’ve been waiting for you. You... you’re the new one from the Royal Navy, are you not? I am called Takao.
Wow! You’re one of the samurai I was just talking about! I am Chaser. You’re every bit as imposing as they say!
Commander, what is she...?
Oh, dreadfully sorry, I’m a bit too excited. Is that your samurai sword? May I see it?
I don’t mind showing you, but it is dangerous to handle the naked blade... You should not get too close.
Perhaps later then, should we get the chance. Righto!
Chaser, biting her fingernails with anticipation and making me honestly kind of anxious, hurried into the Sakura dormitory.
Let us begin with our exercises, as planned.
Takao led us out to a place where we could see the sea, and Chaser couldn’t contain a yelp as soon as she saw the assembled formation.
Commander, is that girl there a ninja?
She pointed at Akatsuki.
Pardon... But why do you care so much for samurai and ninja?
Hmm... It’s hard to put into words... I suppose it’s a sort of fascination with the exotic. Ninjas have their “ninjutsu,” yes?
That one there, she’s a ship, but unlike one of the Union girls, I get this excitement that she’s both a ship and a ninja!
Well, I can certainly admit there is indeed a difference between a Union ship and a Sakura ship. But nevertheless, the Royal Navy...
It’s all about expanding my horizons. Don’t you think it’s fun to learn new things, Miss Takao?
Hm... that’s true too...
What is this?
Sensing the eyes on her, Akatsuki came over to us.
Oh, it’s nothing important. This is Chaser, she came to observe with the Commander today...
She seems particularly interested in ninjas.
Well then, bear witness to my ninjutsu!
Our story took a strange turn...

sequence:
Moments with the Young Miss

<size=45>6 An Ungraceful Attempt?</size>

scripts.say: The combined enthusiasm of both Chaser and Akatsuki pushed us to a demonstration of Sakura Empire ninjutsu techniques, courtesy of the latter.
I think Long Island once said that ninjas can run on water!
That’s right. With my power, I can even achieve such feats!
Akatsuki sped up and did three loops around the water.
And you can use like that “katon” jutsu power to throw some fireballs!
Easily!
Akatsuki sounded her main gun. A low-powered training round hit the target and popped into a small fireball.
And you can vanish in a puff of smoke!
L-Like this?
Akatsuki put up a smoke screen... huh?
Seems like you do all of it with your rigging...?
As Chaser said, the ships can use these rather fantastical techniques with the power of their riggings.
You want to see something that doesn’t use rigging...? Hm...
The art of seduction?
Wha?!
Like so...?
My right arm pressed against something soft...
...Chaser had snuggled herself up against me.
Ah-Ahem!
Oh... Sorry! That’s not quite right, is it?
She released my arm... And that was the most shocking thing Chaser had done over the past few days.
What’s the next item on our agenda, Miss Takao?

sequence:
Moments with the Young Miss

<size=45>7 Excitement and Curiosity</size>

scripts.say: In the evening, the sun slowly sank into the west...
We’re done for the day, then?
I lifted my head to see Chaser standing in front of me.
After leaving the Sakura dorms, I told Chaser to come by later as she prepared to return to the Royal Navy.
She had to submit her report on her visits, and...
Hehe, it was quite nice to see the Commander’s serious side this afternoon...
I had to subject you to a little unladylike teasing.
She reminded me what happened that afternoon by the Sakura training grounds.
Takao and Akatsuki were rather cross with me. The former called me shameless and the latter grumbled out her “aagghh” growling.
It’s not only the different camps, but all the individuals within them that have their own unique characters.
Chaser walked gracefully to the window, glowing in the lustrous light of the setting sun as she shared her thoughts.
Over the course of my service, I’ve been to so many different places, and yet there are still so many more I haven’t seen, with so many things waiting to be discovered.
When I’m here with you like this, I feel so fulfilled. I guess you could say that little prank this afternoon was a sort of “payback,” eh♪
She smiled and turned to face me.
Now then, why did you ask me here?
The reason should have been obvious...
You want me to continue as your secretary? I’d be happy to, of course, but why?
Her youthful appearance belies her curious nature. I’d expect recklessness from her, but she’s surprisingly compassionate...
Every one of her unexpected outbursts was also... “fun.”
Thank you. I’ll do my best to live up to your expectations, Commander.
I’m glad to live in such grace and joy♪
The first wave has arrived at the rendezvous point and the second is ready to depart. I'd say Operation Alphabet is progressing smoothly! Victory is just beyond the horizon now.

... You did a great job accommodating those planes during the evacuation, Glorious. I'm granting you permission to proceed independently with your escorts. Oh, by the way? Next time, make sure there's fuel in those tanks.
I-I know! I just forgot to refuel, that's all it was!
Don't forget it a second time. Ardent and Acasta will continue serving as your escorts. And if anything happens to them, you won't hear the end of it from me.
Understood. But... they're my escorts, so why would I be accountable if they're injured...?
Because you're a carrier! A carrier should protect her escorts like they were her own children!
R-right, of course... In any event, I'd better be on my way now!
(Hmm. Glorious seems calm and collected, but she's not as smart as you think... I guess there's more to her than meets the eye...)
(Ark is usually cool and levelheaded, but when she starts talking about destroyers, she becomes a different person... I guess there's more to her than meets the eye...)
(She's like me, in a way...)
(I bet Ark is going to be quite upset with me...)
(If only I'd stayed vigilant, this wouldn't have happened... No, this all happened because I asked for permission to proceed independently...)
(I just hope... I haven't disgraced... the Royal Navy's name...)
God... save... the Queen...!
Hey, you okay? You look pretty messed up, but I thought I'd be polite and ask.
"Messed up"? I'm fine, more or less... The enemy was a pain to deal with, that's all. What about you, Gneis? You hurt?
You needn't worry about me. With a fleet so small, they couldn't do much harm to me. However...
However...?
It's strange; I can't explain why, but it doesn't feel like we won at all...
*Yaaaawn*...
Acasta, now's not the time for a nap. We're supposed to be escorting a convoy.
I know, you don't have to spell it out... Blame the weather, it's making me sleepy...
*Sigh*... Of course, it's always the weather...
Ahah, it's all right. As long as we maintain a basic level of vigilance, we'll be fine. And if anyone tries to attack us, my planes will send them away~
Thanks, Glorious! In any event, we must still do our jobs. And Acasta, since we don't have radar with us, you should move to the front so we can spot enemies quicker.
Right. Got it.
All right. Glorious is moving at 17 knots; wind force is around 2 or 3, moving southeast... We've got good visibility... And I think we're behind schedule, but we're making good progress...
Hold up... Non-allied vessels are approaching... Oh, dear... they're Iron Blood!
I let my guard down, and we're not in combat formation... Ardent, count the number of approaching Iron Blood ships! Acasta, to my right! Zig-zag and keep an eye out for enemy submarines!
Aye-aye, ma'am!
Bah. I thought we had a big one on the hook; turns out it's just you twerps.
I am Glorious, aircraft carrier of the Royal Navy! I will have you know that I'm not a twerp!
Furthermore, if you believe you can stop us on your own, then you're sorely mistaken! Why, the idea is laughable!
Huh?! You've got a lot of nerve, saying that to my face... Just hold still and I'll make this quick and painless!
Very well! Have at you!
This should be enough for us to get away... Ardent, Acasta, change course and cover our escape! We're retreating!
Understood!
Admittedly, I let my guard down, but that was a fine battle! Miss, uh... Admiral Hipper, may we meet again one day!
Y-you're running away?! Dammit, this means more chasing for me... This isn't over, you hear!
Ah, you're back, Hipper. Did you manage to "single-handedly take down the Royal Navy twerps without breaking a sweat," like you said you would?
Shut up! Like anyone was expecting her to run away with her tail between her legs! ... Yeah, I know, I shouldn't have broken formation... Go ahead! Call me an idiot, punish me, I don't care!
Short temper, as always... Next time, I recommend asking us for assistance first.
Huh?! Why would I need YOUR help?
*Sigh*... In any event, it's not too late to catch up to Glorious. As your solo mission failed, we will come with you this time. Scharnhorst, let's get going.
Believe me, I'm raring to go. I'll head wherever there's a fight to be had. C'mon, let's avenge Hipper!
"Avenge"? I'm not pushing up daisies over here, you know! Hey! Wait for me!
I had a feeling I got away too easily... But if I must fight to survive, then I will...!
Still willing to fight, even with a capital ship on your tail? I suppose that's why you Royal Navy carriers are so revered.
Wait! You're no heavy cruiser, you're Gneisenau...! I've heard much about you... I think I know the answer, but I must ask: would you be willing to let our fleet proceed without incident?
I'm honored that you know my name. And no, I can't simply let you be on your merry way.
That leaves me with little choice but to fight you...
Glorious!

As expected: Gneisenau was too much for me to handle... But on the other hand, I endured my injuries long enough for everyone to retreat. I've lived up to my name... More importantly: Ardent, Acasta, please return to the transport ships! Don't forget your mission!
But we can't just leave you here! You'll...!
I will be fine. I'm tougher than I look!
(It's true, I am... But if I'm forced into yet another battle, it may be my last...)
So, how was she like?
Wouldn't you agree that it's a little harsh to ask about the opponent I fought before asking if I'm hurt?
Well, you made it back in one piece, didn't you? Kidding – I'm sorry.
As for Glorious: she was using outdated equipment, but she fought surprisingly well. I suppose any weapon can be effective in the right hands...
Interesting. So she's worthy of my attention, then. Oh, how I long for a good fight!
Then let's continue with the operation. The enemy is injured; catching up to her won't be particularly difficult.
You're much faster than I imagined...! And now, with two of you, it seems fleeing is no longer an option for me...
... I wasn't expecting you to be so calm. Have you accepted your fate?
I've already achieved my objective. The mere fact that you're here means that our transport ships can travel safely.
Even if you decide to pursue them right now, it's too late! We've won!
My only regret is that I couldn't say goodbye to–
Glorious! I'm here with you!
Same. I'm not running off anywhere on my own.
(O-oh my goodness, they're adorable! Ark, I think now I understand why you feel the way you do...!)
That means the transport ships are...! Scharnhorst, I must go! I can still catch up to them if I leave right at once!
Huh? You mean you're not fighting these chumps with me?
You will not get past us!
Why, you stubborn little flies... A cornered rat may bite the cat, but it stands no chance against a snake...
Save your analogies for later! Let's just take 'em out before it's too late!
I suppose we have no other choice...

sequence: One day, the sirens blared again in the waters surrounding the Virtual Tower –

scripts.say: Commander, we've received an alert from the Virtual Tower monitoring site. Reactivation activity has been detected!
What's the affected range this time?
It seems to be a 15 nautical mile radius. The area itself isn't particularly large, but the encryption strength within its boundaries has clearly increased.
The encryption strength as well, you say?
This is the data sent from the tower's monitoring equipment just moments before losing contact.
According to the intel team's analysis, there appears to be a zone with unusually dynamic signals inside the Virtual Tower.
Its presence means that rapid changes are taking place inside the tower over short periods of time.
In this case, external data from another world is being used to create or replicate simulated environments.
Thanks to this, our intel team was able to identify that area as the epicenter of the anomaly.
Knowing who the culprit is will make our response more efficient. Is a direct intervention on the table?
Direct intervention will be possible until the cracking of the encrypted barrier at the maritime boundary is complete, and that process will likely take around fifteen hours.
I recommend that we work with the intel team to provide remote support through the remaining facilities inside the Virtual Tower.
You're planning to crack the encryption barrier and infiltrate the tower on your own?
Technically, no. Only limited intel be transmitted, allowing information-sharing regarding enemy weaknesses, data analysis, and wide-area hacking.
Right. If we can get the information to them quickly, they'll be able to take action too.
Memphis, please assemble the fleet. TB, I'd like you to get in touch with the intel team and provide support from here.
Orders received. Allocating resources to the Virtual Tower monitoring site and preparing support –

sequence: A2 suddenly finds herself walking alone down a metallic corridor. The corridor seems to stretch on endlessly, towering buildings lining the skies of the world through the windows.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-A-1
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 1-7
//:ACCESS CODE: D.O.S.
A2: A trap? When did this happen...?
Somehow, A2 manages to reach a door at the end of the corridor. She examines the tightly-shut door and begins to search in her database for the "key" needed to proceed.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-A-2
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 2-7
//:ACCESS CODE: ▇▇▇▇
//ACCESS CODE CHANGED: HELLO
A2: Might be easier to just bust this door down... Hmm? The access code just changed...?
The moment the door opens, the entire structure of the corridor begins to shift. In a room that had not been there a moment ago, A2 finds a map.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-A-3
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 3-7
//:ACCESS CODE: ▇▇▇▇
//ACCESS CODE CHANGED: REVISEDMAP
A2: At a glance, this map seems pretty accurate... Does that mean an external force is trying to assist me? But who?

Using the map as a guide, A2 effortlessly navigates her way through the intricate network of corridors sprawling like blood vessels. In a room marked as a storage area for important supplies, she finds equipment she's never seen before.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-A-4
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 4-7
//:ACCESS CODE: ▇▇▇▇
//ACCESS CODE CHANGED: UPGRADE
A2: This gear... Is it custom-made?
A2 notices that the map would update each time she reaches a special area. She can tell that by something specific: whether the access code has a meaning.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-A-5
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 5-7
//:ACCESS CODE: DREAMWEAVER
A2: ...Androids don't dream.
Corridors lead to rooms, and rooms lead to more corridors. In this seemingly endless loop, only the changing access codes show that she's reached another area.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-A-6
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 6-7
//:ACCESS CODE: UNKNOWN_UNDEFINED
A2: ...Looks like even the access code is giving up on me.
Just as A2 is beginning to lose patience with the map and considering abandoning the thing altogether, the room indicating an exit finally appears before her.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-A-7
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 7-7
//:ACCESS CODE: ▇▇▇▇
//ACCESS CODE CHANGED: EXIT
A2: Am I finally out of this place? Appreciate the help. Now then, let's see what's happened to the outside world.
//:HAPPY ENDING
After the shimmering blue faded away, A2 finds herself face-to-face with a brand-new, unseen world.
"Your journey through the Virtual Tower has come to an end."
"However, the end of one journey is simply the start of the next. After all, the vast azure sea stretches out before you, and the endless blue sky awaits."

scripts.say: Commander, the support operation has concluded. The individual within the tower is about to materialize in 3...
Commander, the visitor has escaped from the Virtual Tower!
Another new guest from beyond the Virtual Tower, huh?
Let's be sure to show them our hospitality.

sequence: 2B finds herself standing at the water's edge. The sea and sky, close enough to touch, give off a sickly gray-blue hue, as if hinting at the dangers they conceal.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-B-1
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 1-7
//:ACCESS CODE: MIRRORSEA
2B: My pod's not here... Is this... the ocean?
As expected, enemies begin to swarm forth one after the next. 2B takes note of these unfamiliar new enemy types while carefully maneuvering and fending off their attacks.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-B-2
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 2-7
//:ACCESS CODE: EXECUTOR
2B: I don't think those enemies I just fought were machine lifeforms at all...

At the edge of a sandy beach looms a large door, materializing out of nowhere. Beyond the door is a sealed-off space. What appears to be combat gear of an unknown model number sits in the middle of the room, as if quietly waiting.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-B-3
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 3-7
//:ACCESS CODE: ▇▇▇▇
//ACCESS CODE CHANGED: UPGRADE
2B: "Rigging"? This equipment... seems specialized for naval use. It does not appear to pose any danger to me.
As she dons her newly-acquired equipment, a bookshelf appears in the room as if in response, together with an imposing half-ajar doorway.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-B-4
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 4-7
//:ACCESS CODE: ▇▇▇▇
//ACCESS CODE CHANGED: SKILLBOOK
2B: Offense, defense, and support... Skill books, huh? That makes sense. These must provide instructions for how to master this equipment.
The room she just left stretches out into another corridor, which then leads to another room. Beyond that, there are more corridors, then more rooms, as if never ending.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-B-5
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 5-7
//:ACCESS CODE: VIRTUALTOWER
2B: ...I assume this is the interior of some megastructure.
After pushing through set after set of visually-indistinguishable doors, the gray-blue sea and skies finally come into view again.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-B-6
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 6-7
//:ACCESS CODE: EXPERIMENTERSYSTEM
2B: The ocean again, huh... Extrapolating from previous trends, more enemies are likely to appear.
After the battle ends, 2B steps through another doorway into a room full of supplies. Inside is another open door, leading straight to a place with raging, roiling waves.
//:AREA IDENTIFICATION: NODE-B-2
//:STAGE IDENTIFICATION: 7-7
//:ACCESS CODE: ▇▇▇▇
//ACCESS CODE CHANGED: EXIT
2B: The exit, huh... It might be a trap, but escaping from this place takes top priority.
//:HAPPY ENDING
After the shimmering blue fades away, 2B finds herself face-to-face with a brand-new, unseen world.
"Your journey through the Virtual Tower has come to an end."
"However, the end of one journey is simply the start of the next. After all, the vast azure sea stretches out before you, and the endless blue sky awaits."

scripts.say: Commander, the support operation has concluded. The individual within the tower is about to materialize in 3...
Commander, the person-of-interest has appeared on the ocean.
Good. I wonder what stories they'll share with us this time.
Come, let's go and greet our guest.
In the Sakura Empire's Sanctuary, an heir to great power stood amidst comfort and luxury.
Standing in a pagoda that stretched towards the heavens, a black-haired woman rested her hand against the railing, casting her eyes across the sea of clouds below.
The first rays of morning's light pushed through the clouds, leaving a slender shadow across the wooden floorboards.
A storm is coming...
Ominous clouds loomed on the horizon. In this still and silent world, there was no wind brushing against her cheek, no chirping of birds reaching her ears.
The world within this barrier will not be affected... but I'm afraid the blossoms outside will be torn from their branches.
Alas, this was no time for her to wallow in sentimentality. Just as she was about to turn around and head back inside, she heard the cries of a lone and lost bird.
A swallow? It must be seeking shelter.
She reached out to the swallow and the fragile creature came down and perched on her finger.
If you've come here in search of shelter, I'm afraid you've made a mistake.
As seasons change, storms take shape – sunshine can turn into rain in the blink of an eye. One won't last long, fleeing from place to place without a plan.
The barrier surrounding this pagoda protects only the strong. It will keep me safe, but offers no relief to you.
Her words carried no meaning to the swallow, and yet, it nodded as though it understood.
"My time is now. O Heavens, hear my vow. When I rise, all shall bow."
I applaud your poetry, Musashi. I must say though, the verses are a bit ominous.
Musashi – battleship of the Yamato class now holding the seat of the Combined Fleet flagship – looked behind her.
Though she should've been alone, a voice spoke to her from nearby.
There's no meaning to them beyond the picture they paint. More importantly, have our guests arrived yet?
Yes. They're waiting outside the barrier, so I suggest we proceed to the next stage. *cough* *cough*...
Of course.
Silence returned to the pagoda's top floor. Musashi extended her arm and gently shook her finger, sending the swallow away.
*knock knock*
I've come to report. Akagi and her party have arrived outside the barrier. Wakatsuki is guiding them around.
Alright. Head to the reception room. I'll be there soon.
As you say!
So you're the first to arrive, Akagi.
The barrier will not protect the weak from the storm...
So instead, I will protect you myself. Heehee.

sequence: Three invitations were sent out across the Sakura Empire.
One to Mikasa, who was in pursuit of truth with nothing more than fragmented legends in hand.
One to Nagato, who was searching for signs of Sirens around the Sacred Sakura's seal.
And one to Akagi, who had witnessed the Iron Blood's rebellion against the Sirens and returned home with the Watatsumi in hand.
Penned by Musashi, the invitations beckoned to a fateful encounter in the Sanctuary.
Each person was allowed to bring five others.
All would converge here for a game with higher stakes than they could imagine.

scripts.say: Exercise Area - Turn 3 (Mikasa's Action)
Look at that fog... Assuming this isn't the Sirens' doing, Akagi must be up to something major.
I agree with that assessment. Before the fog fully set in, my recon planes saw signs of Akagi's ships moving.
She probably thinks she's so clever using a smokescreen to conceal her moves, but we're onto her!
If we huddle here all scared and let Akagi do whatever she wants, she could potentially take five points' worth of bases this turn.
So she can pick and choose her targets freely, regardless of where her ships are deployed... So this is how she's leveraging her fleet of carriers?!
That's not all. By spreading her forces out, she's gained control of the middle area first, effectively gating who is allowed to move into Musashi's territory.
If we still want to meet up with Nagato's forces, we'll either have to brute-force our way through the center of the battlefield or find another way around.
But look - Musashi won't even be able to move at all without running into either Akagi's or Nagato's forces. I thought they were supposed to be working together?
It's as if Akagi is trying to contain Musashi as well... Is this also a part of her strategy?
Nagato is still maintaining her defensive line on the other side of Musashi's territory.
Since we're allied with Nagato, she has a lot of options available to her.
But now that Akagi is threatening large swaths of the battlefield with her sea fog, she might decide to respond to that first.
Ugh, trying to read the situation is giving me a headache... I was told that all I had to do was follow the orders.
We ARE the ones actually doing the fighting, after all. It's inevitable that we'll have to make our own assessments.
If we truly were to just follow orders without thinking, we'd be nothing more than Pawns. And at that point, why not use actual Pawns?
To be honest, the biggest question mark right now is Musashi.
That's right. She hasn't tipped her hand at all despite being threatened the most.
I think she benefits when the situation gets harder to read. The more complex the battlefield, the more uncertainties there are. Maybe that's exactly what Musashi is after.
Precisely because everyone is able to see everyone else's moves on this board, every move breeds suspicion.
At that time, a symbol appeared above the sacred site nearest to Mikasa's territory, ordering her nearby forces to focus their attacks on it.
Listen up, everyone, we have an order from Mikasa!
Mikasa's instructions were clear - all forces are to converge on the Diadem of Light and capture it.
All right, we're going for some big points! Looks like Mikasa is finally getting her head in the game!
That's what I like to see! With Mikasa at the helm, we can't lose!
Now then, we'll prepare to attack the Diadem of Light, and split Akagi's forces down the middle while we're at it.
Excellent. I wonder if we're going to also make an attempt to capture the central tower after we seal off Akagi's ability to mount a counterattack.
If we're also going for the central tower, that means we'll directly engage with Akagi's fleet...
We don't know for sure if that's actually what Akagi is going for, but this move at least matches her aggression.
Turning Akagi's strategy against her, huh? You've still got it in you, old timer!
Exercise Area - Turn 3 (Nagato's Action)
...This sea fog throws a wrench in our plans.
Crafting an environment that only benefits carriers such as herself... I'd expect nothing else from that crafty woman.
Oh, I almost forgot, I'm also a carrier, so it won't affect me negatively. Now if only Zuikaku were here, *sigh*...
By the way, Musashi was the one who ordered Zuikaku to pay a visit to Iron Blood before this exercise, right?
*gasp*... Do you think she purposefully did that to split us up?
I think you're overthinking things... This is just a naval exercise, isn't it? Why would Musashi arrange a whole diplomatic move over an elaborate game of Go?
Musashi never struck me as that kind of person, but when Akagi is involved, you never know!
It wouldn't surprise me if some of that vixen's craftiness rubbed off on Musashi... Though, I suppose I shouldn't be throwing baseless accusations around...
Right, it's hard enough to focus on what's going on in front of us. We can't see Musashi's fleet through all the fog...
If Musashi takes advantage of the fog to slip her forces closer to us...
Listen well, everyone. I shall now tell you our countermeasures for Akagi's sea fog.
Haruna will patrol the territory adjacent to Musashi's forces after capturing the base there.
Hiei, Kawakaze, and Harutsuki will retreat to provide backup for Shoukaku while fending off Musashi's fleet.
We must prevent Musashi from taking the Sacred Sakura under the cover of fog.
Shoukaku will solidify her position using our mass-produced ships.
I already know what Akagi seeks to do, but if I were to disclose it, she would change her actions accordingly.
Remain vigilant, but carry out the instructions I just gave you. Take control of the surrounding bases.
When Nagato's voice disappeared, new symbols appeared around Shoukaku.
Wow... This must be the protection of the gods... I mean, of the Guardian Fox!
Since Shoukaku is the core of Nagato's strategy this turn, she's being funneled all our power and resources!
(I feel a tremendous amount of power welling up within me... What exactly IS this exercise area?)
(Does nobody else feel something strange about this? How are we supposed to get any practical training done when you can "will" incredible power into existence here?)
(Well, I'll worry about it later. Maybe the Commander knows a thing or two about what's going on~)
Sanctuary Pagoda - Reception Room
You'll grant me another point for taking control of this base, yes?
Even with the interference of the sea fog, you still took advantage of the situation to solidify your defenses while capturing nearby bases. Impressive work.
Only carriers are able to operate effectively under these conditions. I had to maneuver accordingly.
You protected your friends and expanded your influence. Your spirit is commendable.
But your mistake was not capturing all the bases adjacent to my territory. If you wanted to prevent me from reaching the Sacred Sakura, you should have ensured there are no gaps in your visibility.
Under the fog, slipping past a few patrol ships is a trifling matter.
Are your forces not preoccupied with the defenders at the Dragon Palace?
Do you plan to abandon that course of action and make a straight march towards my territory?
Good observation. My fleet will be tied down until the Dragon Palace is taken.
Unless you never planned on taking it in the first place, right?
You were planning to give those nodes to Akagi, but she's not taking you up on your offer.
Speaking of Akagi, I can't understand why she would take the bases closest to your territory first. Aren't the two of you supposed to be working together?
I don't recall ever agreeing to an alliance with Musashi, Mikasa.
The only thing that matters in this game is victory - friends and foes simply change the dynamics of how to achieve that victory.
I can tell that you're maneuvering to try to contain me, but there's no point for me to entertain you.
That's one way to look at it. We could've worked through our differences in another manner, but you chose to deploy this sea fog in order to obfuscate your moves from me.
Does that not prove you do not trust me?
Who knows? I'm sure you of all people already know what I'm trying to accomplish, whether or not you can see my actions.
I will say this once more - I will achieve victory using the means I deem appropriate.
As you can see, Mikasa, Akagi has the resolve to carry the Sakura Empire through rain and storm.
She cares not if she is set back or humiliated, and continues to push forward regardless. That is a spirit worth looking up to.
What is the real reason you're doing this, Musashi?
While victory depends on who captures holds the most points at the end, there is no rule saying that you cannot have your retainers fight directly.
When shipgirls clash with the full extent of their mental fortitude and will-given form, what we actually witness is a contest of courage and determination.
Just as Nagato's desire to protect Shoukaku made her stronger, my fleet has developed their powers through the confidence I instilled within them.
As Suzutsuki and her allies became more familiar with their special techniques, the Tester vessel was taken down in no time, and the Dragon Palace soon fell to Musashi's forces.
Sakawa and Wakatsuki, freed from their previous battle, quickly made their way towards Nagato's territory just as Musashi had ordered.
Ugh... Where did those two come from?
That area is only defended by Harutsuki and Kawakaze... Musashi, are you...
Going to force our friends to fight each other?!
Force? Hardly. This was just a natural consequence of Akagi deploying her sea fog, and you deciding to reveal your commands to the rest of us.
I won't let you have your way!
Try me then. Show me what determination the child-made-guardian is capable of mustering.
Exercise Area - Turn 3 (Musashi's Action)
Taking advantage of the thick sea fog, Musashi's "retainers," Sakawa and Wakatsuki, crossed over to launch a surprise attack on the area occupied by Nagato's fleet.
Harutsuki! Kawakaze! Musashi's forces are headed towards you!
G-got it! But, where are they coming from? I can't really see through all this fog...
They're coming straight at us! Prepare for combat, Harutsuki!
H-huuuh?!
As soon as Kawakaze drew her blade, Sakawa and Wakatsuki burst from the fog.
Hello there, Nagato's retainers~!
I'm the Agano-class light cruiser, Sakawa. Let's have a fair fight, okay?
And I'm the Akizuki-class destroyer, Wakatsuki. Sorry for barging in all of a sudden, Harutsuki.
I'll be fine... Probably...
Harutsuki, remain alert. We're not allies anymore, for the time being.
Well, we don't necessarily have to fight, right? Musashi only ordered for us to move to this area.
Plus, we just finished taking the Dragon Palace. I could use some extra time for rest and recovery~
Phew... I'd like to avoid conflict if possible...
Unlike Harutsuki, who sighed in relief and lowered her weapons, Kawakaze remained vigilant and poised to strike.
It's true that we're in top shape whereas you've sustained some damage from your previous battle.
If you don't want to fight, I certainly won't force you to.
But don't come a single step closer. Those are Lady Nagato's orders.
I see... So you've been ordered to hold us back. Hmm... I know you're strong, but are you strong enough to stop both of us?
Hiei, who was situated in a nearby grid, heard the impending clash through her communication device.
Nagato, you correctly anticipated Musashi's move, but you didn't fully plan for the effects of the sea fog.
If you chose to launch an all-out attack in the fog, you would've been able to inflict more damage. However, that would prevent you from securing enough bases to pin Musashi in.
It must've been a difficult decision, but you wanted to avoid fighting your own friends.
The sea fog will clear soon, and now, it remains to be seen what kind of decision Musashi will make.
The white veil that blanketed the sea began to thin out and disperse, until finally––
The sound of fighting...?! Does that mean...
Musashi, you actually decided to pull the trigger?
Sorry, but we've got our orders. Um, Wakatsuki, you got Musashi's message as well, right?
KABOOM––––!!
Before Sakawa and Wakatsuki finished preparing to attack, Musashi's mass-produced ships emerged from the fog and began to hammer Harutsuki and Kawakaze with a ferocious barrage.
Sorry, but that's life for ya. We're going to have to fight after all.
Didn't you just say the complete opposite thing a moment ago?!
Hey, I would've preferred to walk away as well, but we can't disobey the boss lady.
I was right not to let my guard down...! But considering the damage those two have already sustained, we clearly have the upper hand!
Harutsuki, stay close behind me! We'll settle this with close-range torpedo combat!
Kawakaze drew her sword, her eyes narrowing as she maneuvered to place Sakawa and Wakatsuki between her and Musashi's mass-produced ships.
You've got some keen moves there, as expected of Nagato's personal bodyguard... But I'm no slouch either!
D-don't underestimate me either!
Just when cannons and swords were about to trade blows––

sequence: That's enough!

scripts.say: A brilliant beam of light descended onto the battlefield, like a stream of cherry blossoms hitting the water's surface. The rest of the thinning sea fog was instantly pushed aside, and Nagato, flagship of the Reborn Combined Fleet, emerged.
Nagato's barriers surrounded the attackers on both sides, pushing blades apart and rendering shells useless.
Wow, she completely nullified the cannonballs in midair... Thank you so much, Great Guardian Fox!
Mm. You have nothing to worry about with me here.
Lady Nagato?! We were perfectly capable of handling the situation here... There's no need for you to personally enter the battlefield...
This isn't a matter of trust. I've come to prevent a pointless fight.
In this exercise, there is no reason for us to take up arms against one another. Sakawa, Wakatsuki, stand down!
Woooah, busted... Uhh, it's not like we chose to fight because wanted to...
M-Musashi told us to kick back and enjoy the game, so I might've gotten a bit carried away, haha... Just a little.
Please forgive us, Lady Nagato!
There's no need to apologize. This is just an exercise, and you were merely following orders.
As Musashi said, there's no risk of injury in a controlled exercise area.
We spar against each other pretty much on a daily basis as part of our normal training routine.
So, you don't need to apologize, and you should continue this exercise as usual.
We didn't do anything wrong, did we?
If there's no risk involved in us fighting, why did you stop us?
This game of Go is a clash of wills among the players outside. As such, the combat power of the ships inside is limited, while the importance of one's convictions is amplified.

In other words, you won't accomplish anything from fighting each other in the conventional, physical sense. Rather, the only thing that matters is a clash of ideals - something that cannot happen when you are simply "following orders."
And my conviction is this: there is no place for meaningless conflict. That is the path I shall demonstrate to the Sakura Empire, and the ideal I wish to demonstrate to Musashi and Akagi.
Well spoken! I must say, I am quite moved by your speech. The mighty shield you've produced must be a manifestation of your mental image, right?
Most likely. Perhaps due to the time I spent sealed inside the Sacred Sakura, this domain also reflected the vivid memories I have of that place.
But now, I am no longer the same person I was before. This may be the last time we see a scenery like this here.
In any case, there is no more need for us to battle each other. If you remain unconvinced, then you will have to go through me first.
As long as I stand, nobody will lay a finger on any of my friends!
Sanctuary Pagoda - Reception Room
Nagato, I wasn't expecting you to enter the battle so soon.
To think that a bit of testing the waters would trigger such a strong rebuke... Perhaps I underestimated that girl's resolve.
Maybe not. That might've just been what Nagato wanted the whole time - to stand on the front lines.
She would put herself in harm's way just to prevent unnecessary conflict...
Because of that antiquated ego, she fails to see the bigger picture. Her fixation on "protecting" what is dear to her may well cause her to lose everything. How foolish.
There is no future to be had down that road, with or without fighting.
Regardless, by sacrificing her advantage as a "player" in this match, her forces now vastly eclipse ours in combat effectiveness.
So, she insists on standing in the way... Mikasa, do you have what it takes to keep up with her?
Keep up? Hah, I don't have the energy or determination that girl has. The most I can do is to fill in the gaps behind her as she forges a new path forward.
Now that the balance of power has been broken, shouldn't we go back to securing as many bases as we can instead of fighting each other?
You may be right in saying that Nagato is forging a new path forward.
But does it not fall upon us to determine if that path leads to the light... or to the abyss?

As someone responsible for shouldering the Sakura Empire's future, there are many other things to consider than your own narrow sense of justice. One cannot make judgments based on speculation and assumptions alone.
I cannot deny what you have done for us. But at the same time, it is too dangerous to work with the Sirens.
The Commander informed me about the Iron Blood incident not too long ago. Unlike in our case, the Commander was involved with their plan to a far greater degree.
Plus, both Bismarck and Friedrich shared the same vision despite their diverging paths... That is why they were able to complete their lengthy project in the end.
If Nagato and I could understand the path that you've chosen, perhaps we might've also been able to work together towards a common goal.
But, your heart is just as opaque as the sea fog concealing this board.
...In order to outwit the Sirens, you must first learn the taste of the poison they serve.
Akagi, you...
After the success of the Iron Blood rebellion, the Sirens have become much more vigilant.
Now that Nagato has made her intentions clear, I will crush her and demonstrate the superiority of my vision.
With Akagi's declaration, a dazzling light enveloped both her and the board, just as it had with Nagato previously.
When the light faded, only two people remained around the board.
She also wants to prove herself, huh... Just like Nagato, she too can only do things in her own way.
The balance of power has again been restored with Akagi's entry into the battle.
She will most likely join up with Miyuki to cut you off from Nagato's forces.
Now the question is, will she try to gobble up your bases, or will she launch an attack on the central tower?
She's not here anymore, so it'll be harder to read her intentions.
It would appear that the youngsters are too impatient to keep our little game of chess going. Hahaha!
Hehe. I'm sure you were no less hot-blooded yourself during that war. Isn't that right, Great Veteran?
But that was a completely different era, Musashi. A long, long time ago, wasn't it?
Even if I tried to run off like them, my body wouldn't move. After all, there are people leaning on me now.
...Musashi, be honest with me. This exercise area is actually a Mirror Sea, isn't it?
What makes you say that?
Mapping one's mental imagery into existence, the sudden disappearance of Nagato and Akagi... Those aren't things that should be possible through the Sakura Islands' rituals.
I wonder, do you really know everything there is to know about our rituals?
...Probably not.
But, that's why I want to know. Pardon me if it seemed like I was accusing you.
No, there's no need for that. Your instincts were correct - this is indeed a Mirror Sea, entrusted to Akagi by the Sirens.
Originally, it was a Siren experimental site that none of us could use. But after combining it with spirit barriers, I was able to turn it into the domain you now see.
I'm not sure if what you've done is amazing or borderline heretical...
I'll take that as high praise from the Great Veteran. I do wonder though... Has this place been to your liking?
I don't think it matters whether or not I "like" it. The reality is, I'm stunned by the number of things here that seem to defy conventional wisdom.
And even more impressively, you're able to control these things. Perhaps the stories of the Iron Blood singularity aren't as far-fetched as I initially believed.
I've also heard of a Sculpting Room that generates storms to keep everyone who does not possess the "Key" away.
In any case, the actual Mirror Sea itself is sealed away, but I did not disclose this to you or Nagato knowing the suspicions both of you have towards Siren technology.
There was once a period of time when I was paranoid of Akagi's every move. At least now, I have fewer doubts about her intentions.
By the way, how do you command your allies after entering the battlefield? To my understanding, our communications are not affected the way they would be in a Mirror Sea?
We're able to give instructions directly to the entire fleet from here, and losing that ability would be a huge disadvantage.
Don't worry. You won't be able to immediately grasp everyone's positions at once, but you will still be able to issue commands to them as before.
I see, so there aren't as many disadvantages as I imagined. So, for our allies inside, there's no difference in how they're getting their orders?
Correct.

There is a key difference though: when the retainer is unable to hear the player's voice, she has no choice but to obey the order. But if she is able to voice her opinions, she may be able to influence those orders.
You will also be able to directly observe the condition of your forces, and that may cause you to make different decisions than if you treated them as pieces on a board.
I wonder if Nagato and Akagi were aware of this before they made their decisions.
I'd imagine so. They chose to fight alongside their friends rather than sit out here enjoying tea with us.
Hehe. Can't blame them.
Hahaha. Well then, as I told Akagi, I will remain here a bit longer.
Show me what kind of moves the three of you will make.
Exercise Area - Turn 4 (Akagi's Action)
A Compiler vessel... What were we doing while Milord was struggling for survival...?
Ugh... I lost another mass-produced ship... At this rate, I'm going to be forced to retire from the game...
As a battleship, I should be the one on the front lines... But I'm supposed to conserve my firepower and energy still...
Calm down, Yamashiro. Akagi has already taken the base.
Huh, really? Since when...
Before Yamashiro could make sense of what she was seeing, Akagi had already crushed the Siren vessel.
Burning petals swirled around her body, the only remaining traces of the Siren that had once been there.
Akagi!
When I saw your foxflames appear, I thought you had used another command. I didn't think you would directly enter the battlefield...
I was going to fall asleep if I had to spend another minute in that cramped room. Just needed a little change in scenery.
Akagi, what did you just do to that Compiler...
Compiler models are known for having extremely high resistance to conventional weapons. However, we are able to use the unique features of this area to our advantage.
I changed the characteristics of my attack, as you can see from these lycoris flowers here, allowing my flames to penetrate the vessel's weak points.
Knowledge is power - the same is true for fighting Sirens as it is for understanding our opposition.
(The sea fog had a fairly significant effect the first time it was used, but Mikasa will know how to deal with it if I use it a second time.)
Nagato has also descended upon the battlefield. If we do not act quickly, there will be no more bases left to take, and we will be forced into a stalemate.
Understood. We trust your judgment, Akagi.
That's fine, but your own safety comes first. The same goes for Jintsuu and the others.
Color me surprised, though... I didn't expect to see another Compiler so soon. Seems like the ghosts of the past are all coming out to play.
I suppose this means that even if the mainframe has been destroyed, its data can still be used to create spares... But what is the point in doing that––
Thank you for saving us, Akagi! If it weren't for you, all our mass-produced ships probably would've gotten wiped out!
...Do you think I'd exhaust our resources securing a base of this size? I sent the mass-produced ships in to gauge the opponent's specs.
Yamashiro, you will be needed to secure a more important objective.
A more important objective...? Are you talking about the tower over there? I'm not sure I'll be able to take down even stronger enemies...
Hold on. I'm not done talking yet.
Mikasa has already formed a perimeter through the southern side of the board. If we allow her forces to join up with Nagato's, we're as good as done.
Jintsuu, I'd like you to join up with Miyuki. Cross over past the central tower and look for an opportunity to split off Mikasa and Nagato.
Understood!
Yamashiro, you have the important task of preventing Mikasa's forces from advancing on the central tower. I need you to hold the waters around that area.
I just knew I was gonna get sent there! Ugh, everyone's going to be ganging up on me...

That area is where most of the action is going to be, but with your durability, I'm sure you'll be fine. If anything, I'm sure Akagi chose to send you specifically because you're the best fit for the task.
Oh, I see... Well, if Akagi has that much confidence in me...
Surprisingly, the two of you seem to work together pretty well.
Akagi, let me go to the central tower as well. In case something happens there, it'll be safer to have two people instead of one.
That leaves me a bit short-handed for my other move, but it's true that having two people grants both of you more flexibility.
We should be able to work with that... I'll allow it. Make sure you cover Yamashiro.
Understood, Akagi.
Now then, Great Veteran Mikasa. It's your move.
Exercise Area - Turn 4 (Mikasa's Action)
Akagi has sent a fleet to hold the waters around the central tower.
Is she trying to prevent us from assisting Lady Nagato?
She just took a base, but is already poised to make her next move...
Doesn't this put us in a tough position though? We haven't even finished capturing the Diadem of Light yet.
Mikasa said she can handle this situation.
We will maintain pressure around the central area to keep Akagi's forces occupied and allow Nagato to take all the remaining small bases along the perimeter.
Akagi is trying to fulfill three objectives at once, using speed and misdirection to throw us off. However, she is unable to muster significant numbers for any one of those objectives.
While surveying a map of the exercise area, Kongou relayed the messages she received directly from Mikasa.
Even if Akagi manages to capture some of the bases around the central tower, she won't have the resources to push further west.
Why is she doing this? Shouldn't Akagi know that our forces are concentrated around the Diadem of Light?
That's most likely the reason why she only sent a small detachment.
If she planned on taking any other bases on the western side, she would have to commit a lot more resources.
That's why I think this might be a feint. Even though we have the numerical advantage, we're prone to getting pincered if we get too focused on surrounding the detachment.
