(Something extremely dangerous is approaching from deep within the sky.)
(What in the world is this fleet preparing to fight?)
The Sky Realm.
...What?
A mysterious figure once again wrenches her way into the recording.
A veil of stars... anchoring the Sky Realm...
Hello? Are you from Stellapolis?
You seem... a little off. Did something happen at the observatory?
Are you real?
A spark of life returns to the figure's eyes for a moment.
You must flee... Forget what you've heard.
Close your eyes, cover your ears...
Seek not the answers of days gone by in the reflections of the stars...
The recorded world dissolves into light.
Even as the scenery returns to normal, I keep my eyes fixed on the sky's reflection in the sea.
But for some reason, whatever had captivated me before is gone now.
After that, I returned to the cabin and tried to make sense of what I'd just witnessed.
Hmm...
What did you see in the starry sky?
Huh?!
I realize that Selimiye has followed me into the cabin.
Apologies. Did I startle you?
I couldn't help but be curious. What did you see in the starry sky? What revelation has fate given you?
She walks over and sits down next to me, producing a crystal ball suitable for her fortune teller status.
Though her eyes are hidden by long bangs, her excitement makes it clear that she knows I saw something – and she wants to know what.
Heheh... Beneath the mangled heavens, threads of fate tangle. Sometimes, scraps will fall.
You froze up when you were looking at the water. What was it?
Cryptic symbols? Indescribable murmurings? Or perhaps a mysterious vision?
As you know, I am a fortune teller... so I cannot resist these scraps of fate.
Tell me... I will part the fog and pierce to its true meaning.
She certainly has the bearing of a fortune teller.
I'd almost be impressed, if not for the way she bumped her leg on the table as she sat. Even now, she's still wincing.
I only heard a few words. They must have come from whoever is at the observatory.
After careful thought, I leave out the more concerning parts and share only the mysterious warning.
She said, "Seek not the answers of days gone by in the reflections of the stars."
Seek not the answers of days gone by... in the reflections of the stars.
Selimiye gazes into the crystal ball solemnly.
Shortly after...
What does it mean?
Ahem... I was kidding. Of course I know what it means.
I was just testing you.
Okay, so what does it mean?
Umm...
Oh! I just remembered I have some urgent business. Let's call it for a day, shall we?
BEEP BEEP!
A sudden piercing sound makes me dizzy. Selimiye tries to stand up, but she quickly falls back down.
That sound... came from the starry sky above. Did you hear it, too?
I did. What the heck was that?
It's an encrypted distress signal from Stellapolis.
The observatory maintains three lines of defense. That frequency indicates that the first line has been breached!
(What is going on at the observatory?)
That's no good. Could it be a skelebeast attack?
There's no telling yet. The observatory is our only lead for now, so we have to go save them!
Agreed. Tell the others – full speed ahead to the observatory!
Upon receiving the alert, Royal Fortune diverts all available power to the vessel.
Seawater splashes my ears, and the lights of the ghost ships blur into streaks.
Three degrees to port... No, the current has changed. Five degrees!
As the Startrace Beacon disappears into the distance behind us, the fog thickens once again, making it difficult to chart a course.
Selimiye is putting all of her energy into tracking the beacon and navigating.
Damn... The scent of the wind is different here.
Do you smell that foul stench, too?
Huh? What? What stench?
It's the stench of things decaying in the deep sea.
Riyala Bey, brace yourself. The skelebeast horde approaches.
ROOOOAR!
The sea fog up ahead is parted by a colossal entity.
Something we had only seen as flashes in the dark fog finally reveals itself.
A sea serpent easily twice the length of The Great Royal Fortune bares its fangs at us.
ROOOOAR!
Wow... This is an enemy worthy of being sung of in heroic tales!
I've made up my mind! This will be the ultimate objective of my trial!
That one's odd. Where the hell did you pick her up?
Show of hands. Who else wants to fight that behemoth?
I'll pass!
Same here!
I wouldn't recommend fighting it head-on before we arrive at the observatory. If you insist, however, I've no choice but to join you.
No. Let's prioritize reinforcing the observatory.
Is there any way to avoid a fight?
Heheh. While Lord-class skelebeasts are intelligent, their wit is mostly related to command and combat.
I know. I can construct a short-lived ritual to make illusions that look just like us. A perfect distraction!
That would improve our chances of making a getaway.
Stellapolis technology, eh? Interesting.
Lucky for you, I can cover this area in darkness to evade enemy detection.
Factor in The Great Royal Fortune's submarine capabilities...
Well, I'd say we're more than likely to escape.
Wow... It's a legendary, blood-roiling combo technique!
No objections here. Let's do it!
How much time must I buy to prepare you?
Fifteen minutes, if you'd please!
We carefully maneuvered the vessel, fighting off the pincer attack by the sea serpent and skelebeasts.
Eventually...
ROOOOAR!
Now! They're distracted! Execute the plan!
KABOOOOM!
Selimiye's illusions take shape, and Anne's shroud of darkness proves effective. Just then, a whisper reaches us from high in the starry sky.

sequence: Capture...

scripts.say: Capture it alive...
Whoever's up there making those crazy demands, how about YOU come down and try it?! Ugh!
Selimiye and I exchange glances.
(I am curious about this order, but...)
The thing is...

options.content: Sorry, but it's just not feasible.

scripts.say: Given that we were the only two to hear it, it didn't take long to come to an agreement.
Royal Fortune, prepare to dive!
Hold on tight, everyone. We're gonna scram!

sequence: Corridor of Fog
Unknown time - Unknown location

scripts.say: After a while, Selimiye used her divination to find a calm stretch of sea to surface in.
Phew! What a getaway.
Just a shame we couldn't get out of this damn fog.
Distorted stars still hang above us, and the fog shows no sign of letting up any time soon.
Looking for clues at the observatory seems to be our only option, after all.
We'll need to think of a way to capture that serpent alive, too!
You're taking that order seriously?
Capture the WHAT?
We explain what we heard to everybody.
Okay, you two have lost your minds. Enough with the jokes, Commander!
It's not joke. Though to be honest, I agree that it's not going to be easy.
Selimiye, what got you in the mood to try capturing it?
Heheh, fate whispered into my ear...
Straight answer, please.
Ahem... If we're being given warnings from above, then we shouldn't just listen to the easy parts, should we?
What if that serpent is our key out of this crisis?
In a way, that does make sense.
But we cannot even drive the beast back. How are we meant to capture it?
My blade couldn't find purchase in its flesh. It must be protected by something.
It may be exploiting these chaotic waters... or perhaps the fog itself is related.
Oh? I'm surprised somebody else took notice.
Heheh... One wise sage once said, "Fight magic with magic!"
If the Startrace Beacons can dispel the fog and calm the sea, then... I have an idea!
Let's take a bit of a detour together.
Excuse me? Maybe you could tell us what the idea is before we do it?
It's something I learned in school: three Startrace Beacons surround each of Stellapolis's observatories.
Each beacon has its own purpose, creating one linked system with each other and the observatory.
Okay... And?
Ahem! AND, the status of the Startrace Beacons affects the status of the observatory and surrounding seas!
If the observatory has been breached, then it must follow that the beacons were breached first.
Conversely, repairing all of the beacons will restore the observatory's combat systems, also allowing us to make the sea our ally.
With the sea on our side, we can use the observatory's power to lock the serpent inside without killing it!
I see... It does sound plausible.
(If the first beacon's recording is to be believed, that serpent may have been what destroyed it.)
(Is it possible that the serpent knows not just of the beacons' existence, but also their number and strategic connection to the observatory?)
(It doesn't quite add up... Maybe something is manipulating the fiend.)
(Our enemy's dispositions are concealed, leaving us at a disadvantage. Our only option is to move slowly and prudently.)
Using the location info from the first beacon, Selimiye quickly deduced the location of the second.
location: Corridor of Fog - Second Startrace Beacon

scripts.say: Like the first, it looks utterly dilapidated.
Though it looks destroyed, the damage here is less severe.
Does that mean our repair work will proceed faster?
Hmm... In theory, yes.
With Riyala Bey's help, Selimiye once again sets about repairing the beacon.
While they work, I examine the records stored in this facility.
The main hall's holographic projection displays a clear image of the sea serpent, confirming my suspicion that it was the one that destroyed the beacons.
However, I cannot retrieve any further information even with my Siren credentials.
(Even though this Startrace Beacon was also built on top of a Siren facility... I guess it's up to luck whether I can get their ancient records.)
In the end, the repairs were not noticeably faster than the last. However, dazzling light did pierce the sky, signaling a successful activation.
There were a few minor issues, but this is all part of my trial!
Let's keep up this momentum toward the third beacon!
Wait! I've had it... My brain is all spent. No more!
I haven't slept a wink since yesterday. Hold on, fate is whispering to me – it says I need food and sleep!
Now that you mention it... I am exhausted, too. Royal Fortune, can we drop anchor here for a spell?
I was just thinking the same thing. Even if we didn't need rest, the Commander sure would.
But is the observatory not still under attack?
That serpent doesn't seem to be touching the observatory.
So much time has passed, but we haven't received word of the second defensive line being breached. Maybe it has shifted its full attention to us now.
We must rest, or else we have no hope of victory.
Even Járnbarðinn breaks her silence to vote in favor of a break.
Thus, we returned together to The Great Royal Fortune to rest.
In the banquet hall, Royal Fortune stood in the most conspicuous place and clapped.
Ahem! On close inspection, our rag-tag group hails from all corners of the world.
This marks our first meal together as a crew. As your captain...
Captain Royal Fortune, I have a question before you bore us to death.
Queen Anne's Revenge glances sideways at the empty long table.
What are we meant to eat?
She told me that she has ample supplies on her vessel, and yet...
(I just want to see what happens.)
Just so we're clear, I brought nothing but treasure. What of you all?
I only brought enough food to last me a day... Also, I ate almost all of it.
Weren't you saying you left home to embark on some sort of trial?
And you brought... one day's worth of food.
I'm still a little inexperienced... I will do better next time.
I have supplies. Enough for everyone to eat a few meals, at least.
Utterly expressionless, Járnbarðinn produces an enormous quantity of dark-red hardtack and some blocks of unidentifiable black and white matter.
Is this food?
In order: staples, fats, and sides.
Easy to store, and filling.
...Did anyone else bring real food?
Heheh, fortune has smiled upon me. Despite how sudden this was, I happen to have a week's worth of food.
Behold!
She pulls out bags of bread and sausages.
Unfortunately, the patches of grey mold all over them present a slight problem.
...Huh? It's moldy? How?!
...Did anyone else bring real food?
Having food is a luxury in itself. Or can you folk from Islas de Libertád not handle this?
*sigh*... I'll pass. You all eat your fill.
As Anne gets up to leave, Royal Fortune stops her by pushing a glass of red wine into her hands.
It's followed by more glasses and more dishes being lined atop the table.
As if by magic, Royal Fortune covers the banquet table in a feast.
That's what you get for not letting me finish.
You all are passengers, and I'm the captain. It's my job to treat ya right!
Pretty impressive trick, huh? I've been practicing it! Go on and tell me how cool it is.
She puts her hands on her hips, proudly awaiting our compliments.
The look on her face also indicates that she's proud to be the only person who truly knows the value of having a vessel.
(She was waiting for this, huh? Her feelings are written all over her face.)
After filling our bellies, all of us were finally able to relax.
Everybody found a vacant room to stay in, and I fell into a deep, tipsy sleep.

sequence: Unknown time - Unknown location

scripts.say: In my dreams, the sky and ocean invert again.
However, my consciousness remains fixed among the stars.
You have finally come... I've awaited you for so long.
I am Merkuriy. Welcome to my starry sky.
The figure I'd glimpsed in the recordings stands amongst the stars with me and gazes at the sea overhead.
(I can't see her face, but she sounds normal just based on her speech.)
Are you the person stationed at Stellapolis's observatory? And the one sending us information through the stars?
Perhaps...?
Only perhaps? What's going on at the observatory?
Look at the sky. Isn't it beautiful?
Merkuriy changes the subject. Her gaze remains fixed upward, and she never turns to face me.
(No, something is off here... Is there a problem with the stars that she's focusing on?)
When you say "the sky," do you mean the one beneath us? Or the one up above?
What an odd question. The sky is up in the sky, of course.
Look closer. What do you see?
The sky formed by the vast ocean above shimmers as if its surface is metallic.
(Wait... Are those Siren structures and fleets?!)
(There's no doubt. And unlike last time... The perspective is inverted.)
You said, "Seek not the answers of days gone by in the reflections of the stars." What does that mean?
Did I? What an odd thing to say.
The answer is right in front of you. Why do you turn away from it?
Listen... Do you hear the pulse coming from the depths of the starry sky?
The depths... of the sky.
(The Siren fleets in the sea look wary of the sky. But I'm standing here in the sky, and I don't see anything.)
(It must be deeper, then...)
Thump, thump... Do you hear that?
The sky at my feet trembles, like a veil about to be drawn.
...A curtain?
Veil.
Starry sky.
Sky Realm.
Inverted Tide.
With a shudder, the world disintegrates.
Merkuriy vanishes. In that last moment, I see a giant serpent with a long, trailing shadow swallow her whole.
The sky... delicious...
Huh...?
Its giant maw closes again, and the world plunges into nothingness.

sequence: XXX hours later...

scripts.say: When I come to, Royal Fortune's face is mere inches away from mine.
Good morning... uh, evening, I mean!
My head is pounding. It feels like I've been dreaming for ages.
How long was I asleep?
Nine hours or so? It's rare for ya to sleep that long.
You're the second to last person to wake up.
Who else is out-sleeping me?
Miss Riyala Bey, of course!
Pfft... She's talking in her sleep and even punching the bloody bed. It's like the lass thinks she's fighting in her dreams!
Go now, and ya might get to see the climax!
What a... sound sleeper.
Let's wake her up. We need to go and repair the third Startrace Beacon.
Selimiye and Riyala Bey work together to fix the final beacon.
As the third beam rises into the sky, the whole sea undergoes a transformation.
Fog wafting atop the water suddenly coalesces, as if an unseen force is cleaning it off of the water.
Do you see that little speck on the horizon? I think that must be the Fogbound Island, where the observatory is.
We've come close enough to see it with the naked eye!
Let me see... Visibility is good, and no enemies within view!
Heheh, looks like they've really retreated.
Full speed ahead, I say. I want to see the state of the observatory.
Then here we–
Huh? Commander, what is it?
Look more closely at the sea. Something is wrong beneath the surface.
The water ahead seems to have huge fissures running through it.
Sea water falls into them as if sucked down, creating an array of underground waterfalls.
Th-that is weird... Have you ever seen geography like that?
Royal Fortune turns to Queen Anne's Revenge, who has remained calm ever since the fog parted.
Nope. Speaking from experience, I'd advise against sailing over that.
That would require a substantial detour...
It's also possible that the island is surrounded by terrain like this.
I'll take the long way every time. If you want to go, be my guest.
Alright. Then may we meet again at the observatory.
Járnbarðinn! I'll go with you!
Hey, wait!
Though Royal Fortune tries to stop them, they jump off the vessel together and rush toward the distant island.
Oooh, man. That's not good.
What's with that look on your face? They've volunteered to scout the path ahead for us.
They paid a hefty fare. If things get bad, I'll have to go save them!
Heheh, do not worry! The sea is calm, promising safe passage for our brave heroes.
Huh... The wind is picking up. The water currents are moving faster, too...
Look, Járnbarðinn. Is it just me, or is the fog rolling back in?
More ghost ships are appearing and coming our way, too!
I-it'll be okay! They're just harmless illusions. Nothing bad will happen!
KABOOOOM!
Eep!
Riyala Bey, fall back! The ghost ships have opened fire!
Urk... Th-they're only ghost ships. So they can fire their cannons a little, sure! That doesn't make them a threat to those two!
ROOOOAR!
A roar booms deep beneath the surface. The waterfalls flow even more violently.
The ghost ships are quickly taken by the flow and fall straight into the darkness.
Járnbarðinn and Riyala Bey are in danger of being sucked down, as well.
Ah...
It's a good thing they didn't get too close yet.
The situation is clear. Remaining out there is dangerous – call them back already.
Yeah, right away–
ROOOOAR!
The suction intensifies again, pulling even The Great Royal Fortune uncontrollably toward the chasms.
That's weird... Normally, I'm the only unlucky one. It's not supposed to get other people hurt.
Has some inexplicable shift in mysterious energy transferred my misfortune?
Argh, please just stop talking!
Rescue them at once. Then, we put our all into retreating.
KABOOOOM!
After much struggle, we manage to drag Riyala Bey and Járnbarðinn back aboard.
However, the water's suction only grows stronger, making it impossible for The Great Royal Fortune to break away.
It's a life or death situation.
The abyss the stars sank into...
The day the stars fell...
Huh? That voice...
I heard it, too! Commander, is that the voice from the observatory ya mentioned?
It is. Does that mean she's given up on encrypting her messages?
KABOOOOM!
ROOOOAR!
A massive beast lunges out of the depths.
Whoa... The serpent caught up with us! Ugh, and what timing!
We're between a rock and a hard place.
But with three Startrace Beacons lit, the serpent's shield should be weakened.
We might be able to escape it by diving, but...
Wait a second. The suction has weakened, hasn't it?
...Huh? It really has!
Did the serpent's appearance inadvertently weaken the currents?
Either way, this is a chance we can't miss. Let's retreat to safe waters first!

sequence: Corridor of Fog - Unknown location
Shortly after...

scripts.say: We managed to shake off the currents and the serpent alike, bringing us to uncharted waters.
However, before we could breathe a sigh of relief, Selimiye's crystal ball suddenly shattered with a loud crack.
Simultaneously, the three beams of light piercing the heavens dimmed one by one until they'd vanished completely.
Fog closed in again, returning the Corridor of Fog to its original state.
Oh, no! My limited-edition crystal ball!
What's going on?! Why did your ball shatter, and why did the beacons go out?
The Startrace Beacons have been destroyed... along with the surveillance magic I set on them!
But the serpent was chasing us... so who the heck destroyed the beacons?
This is awful... With the Startrace Beacons destroyed and the fog coming back in, the serpent will regain its full power.
We've gone back to square one...
BEEP BEEP!
The ear-piercing beeps go off again. This time, everybody hears them.
Ugh, instant headache... Commander, is that the warning signal you and Selimiye mentioned?
A second warning means...
The observatory's second line of defense has been breached...
How did it happen so fast?!
Selimiye, can you still locate the observatory without the beacons?
No way... We would have to repair at least one to get our bearings first.
By that point, it will be too late.
Merkuriy is at the observatory, and she's capable of reaching out to us. Maybe... we can try another approach.
Hmm... Does anybody have something that can help induce meditation?
Given her occupation, Selimiye was fortunately stocked with relaxing incense.
I found a quiet room full of starlight amidst the vessel, lit the incense, and began meditating.
(Merkuriy was influenced by my consciousness before.)
(If I can just talk to her again through my dreams...)
(As the core of the system, the observatory should have more robust tracking and navigational capabilities than the beacons.)
(So why won't she guide us? Do the circumstances prevent her from doing so? She seems like her mind is in a haze... and her messages are often contradictory.)
(The connection between her and the serpent bothers me, too.)
(Does "capture it alive" refer to the serpent itself, or the one pulling its strings?)
(There are too many questions and not enough answers. I'd better fall asleep and extract those answers...)
Deep in the fog, a figure stood amidst the churning waves.
What... are you doing there?
The white-haired girl gazed into the distance. Her golden eyes pierced through the fog, beholding a ship rocking atop the water and another figure drifting into slumber.
The serpent wriggled calmly at her feet, like a trained pet.
You have some nerve, coming here again...
Is this your strategy, or is it dumb luck?
You're bold... and intriguing.

sequence: Unknown time - Unknown location

scripts.say: I've once again arrived at the dream world where the sky and sea are inverted.
This time, the blue-haired girl looks directly at me.
You look familiar.
(She's not staring at the sky... Maybe we can talk this time.)
Who are you? From your perspective, how many times have we met?
Are you lucid again? I'm the Commander of the Tempesta fleet – we are currently en route to your observatory.
This would be the third time I've met you.
The third... Was it you who restarted the Startrace Beacons and opened the Star-Sinking Abyss?
Then you must have met the serpent.
We sure did. It appeared to be a threat, but in a way, it helped us out of a crisis.
What is that serpent to you? Are you enemies? Why would you have us capture it alive?
Capture it alive... I am sorry, but I have no memory of that.
You mentioned that I seem "lucid." You are correct, in that I am in an unstable state... For now, I have only gained a minor advantage.
Do not come to the observatory. You mustn't be here.
Two of the three defensive lines have already been broken. We want to help you.
The serpent is not a threat.
Her attacks are merely... a way to defend the observatory from being wholly consumed by the starry sky.
Wholly consumed by the starry sky... What exactly is wrong with the sky?
What are you doing at that observatory?
And... who is "she"? Is the serpent you speak of not the monster we've been fighting?
She is the echo of the deep, Ormrinn Langi.
She was awakened from her slumber in the Star-Sinking Abyss with the inversion of the starry sky.
At any rate, please do not put too much stock in whatever I said to you before.
Her eyes turn vacant. I can tell that she's trying her hardest not to turn her face skyward again.
Dangers buried in the past have not truly faded.
The boundaries of the world grow thin.
Thus approaches the inversion of the tides...
That's your second time mentioning the tides inverting. What does that entail?
Remember...
Seek not the answers of days gone by... in the reflections of the stars.
With that, she falls silent and gazes up at the ocean suspended above us.
Are you okay?!
We need to hurry through the Corridor of Fog to the observatory! Please, tell me if there's a way!
She does not respond. Once again, I hear the trembling rise from the depths of the sky beneath my feet.
Damn!

sequence: Echo of the Deep.

scripts.say: Capture alive...
The world disintegrates again.
The long serpent drifting through the void devours Merkuriy again and then lunges at me.
Hey! Are you Ormrinn Langi?!
Wait! I want to talk to you!
Commander... Are you delicious?
Her maw shuts, turning the world into nothingness again.
Commander! We've got an emergency!
When I wake up, I see Royal Fortune rushing in.
Apparently, that serpent thing is someone's pet!
Its owner is outside, and she's bloody pissed! She says she wants to talk to you!
I get the feeling she's trouble... but maybe not big trouble, you know?
How and when did you provoke someone like her?
Queen Anne's Revenge and Járnbarðinn are out there dealing with her. You'd better go help!
Come again?
As soon as I step onto the deck, I'm overwhelmed by the scene before me.
In the distance, a girl carried by two sea serpents sizes us up coldly.
Meanwhile, the shipgirls have taken up a combat formation around The Great Royal Fortune.
Selimiye holds the rear, Queen Anne's Revenge stands at the center, and Riyala Bey and Járnbarðinn have taken the vanguard.
I've proven to you that I am the echo of the deep. Aren't you afraid?
That's just a sea monster. Why not ask the captain of this big vessel behind us? Her fleet's got one too, and it's nothing particularly special.
Hmph... I see there's no reasoning with you.
This is your final warning, foolish intruders.
The Corridor of Fog is my territory, and I demand you leave... or else, I'll tear you to shreds.
She waves her hand, prompting one serpent to launch an attack on Riyala Bey.
KABOOOOM!
Not happening!
Having sustained a heavy blow, the serpent's tail recoiled back into the water.
Hm? The barrier is gone?
Heh. That would be thanks to Selimiye's bright ideas.
Heheh, dispel, dispel! Let the starlight dispel it all!
Rather than simply hiding behind everybody, Selimiye is holding a glowing crystal ball and chanting to it.
Seemingly as a result, the fog around has all but cleared.
Hmph. Nuisance...
Hah. Why are YOU the one getting snippy with us?
Here I was lazing around at home, before being dragged here against my will.
And I can't even leave! You don't think we wanted to come here, do you? That we don't want to get the hell out?
Oh... I suppose that may be true.
No, no. Even so, what of it?
It wasn't my fault that the starry sky inverted.
If you want to complain, then go ask the one who did it.
That's the whole point of this. That is why we're going to the observatory – to find out who did it.
Anyway! You are interlopers! And so is the observatory!
I'm fed up. Either leave or get ready for a fight!
Not waiting.
Did you not come here to speak with us?
I'm hungry, and I'm tired of talking.
The two serpents assume an offensive stance again as the white-haired girl readies her weapon.
So you finally bare your fangs, vile fiend!
Today, I – Riyala Bey of Crownpolis – will overpower you in a fair fight!
Your serpents will be my trophies!
Whoa... Commander, what do we do? Fight? Or run?
It looks like we have no choice but to fight. Direct everyone to be gentle so that we can take them alive.
Don't bother hiding your supplies now. Toss plenty of food into the sea – that will help us later.
...Bwuh? Be gentle? Toss the food?
Ormrinn Langi may not necessarily be our enemy. I have other ideas.
Ooh, I see! You want to lure her into our fleet! You should have said so sooner.
Don't worry. I'll fill her right up!
I mean... Actually, sure. You do that.
Prepare for battle!
KABOOOOM!
Our cannon fire dealt severe damage to the two serpents. Meanwhile, Ormrinn Langi's attacks failed to make a dent.
Ugh... You're such a hassle.
(I'm not just imagining it. She's holding back.)
Hey, are you hungry? Your pets there must be.
Why don't we stop fighting and have a meal?
I'm not hungry! But mm, that smell... Whatever's floating in the water smells really good.
It's all delicious! Tasty treats abound!
Huh? Aren't we supposed to be fighting to the death? Is it over, then?
Let me think...
Ormrinn Langi orders her serpents to stop attacking and thinks the matter over. The others likewise cease attacking.
Hmm... I think...
Suddenly, Selimiye's crystal ball flares brightly. Three rays of dazzling light pierce the sky in the distance.
The beacons... started working again?
Starlight dispels the sea fog, and the observatory's island appears on the horizon again. The chasms beneath the water rear their ugly heads, as well.
However, before the suction can begin, golden curtains of light appear beneath the water's surface and seal off the chasms. The perilous waters instantly become calm.
What just happened?
KABOOOOM!
A massive ship clad in bright light emerges from the depths and fires off a volley at the serpents.
Gah!
That alone knocks them down into the water, creating tall waves as they fall.
(Ganj-i-Sawai?!)
I'm sorry! It took a while to prepare, so our reinforcements were delayed!
O abominations of the deep, prepare to meet your end!
Tch... Another hassle.
Upon being faced with this eager new foe, Ormrinn Langi realizes her disadvantage and quickly dives into the water to flee.
Huh... Whaaat?!
Why did we go back to fighting?! I JUST threw my food into the water!
Heeey! Don't goooo!

sequence: "Water reflects the stars in the sky."
"Upon its surface ripple fragments of the past."
"Listen closely, and..."
"Finally."
"I hear the call."

scripts.say: Situated at the crossroads of the six Golden Routes, Crownpolis was naturally the first stop on the way to the New World.
It was peerless among the Polises for its prosperity. Countless would go bankrupt for the opportunity to become a citizen.
However, one small figure rushed desperately to escape, hiding among merchant ships.
Phew... I'm finally safe...
She glanced back at the palace in the distance, unable to contain her smirk.
Blah, blah, "it isn't safe out there." Blah, blah, "you're not ready yet."
Who cares about any of that? Riyala Bey is ready now!
You cannot build up strong wings without chasing a few storms!
This time, I'll achieve something... Something I can impress everyone with!
Hehe! I cannot wait for the trials ahead!
After confirming that nobody had followed her, the girl accelerated toward a distant horizon of song and freedom.
Where should I go first? To slay the monsters roaming the Sleeping Sea? To gather intel in Islas de Libertád? Or maybe...
Suddenly, Riyala recalled something she had seen before her departure.
Stellapolis sent a top-class delegation over. I wonder what that was for...
It's not time for the Annual Divination yet, but it was just as grand as if it were.
Could it be... Has Stellapolis sent us a warning from the stars?
I doubt they would send such a big delegation for anything less.
Hehe... That will be my first trial, then. I shall infiltrate Stellapolis and figure out what is happening!
She was too busy daydreaming about her brilliant future to notice an approaching presence.
Target found. Approaching.
Estimated interception in... five minutes.
Oh, no. Is that Járnbarðinn?!
Finally, she noticed the impending danger.
How'd she catch up so quick? When did they notice?!
This is awful... If she gets me, I'm done for!
I had better run and find somewhere to hide!
Just then, the sky darkened.
Huh?
It was not merely clouds blocking out the sun, but the sky itself distorting and changing.
Stars typically concealed during the day appeared one after another, before slowly sinking toward the sea.
Uh... Huh?
Are they bringing down the sky just to make me go home?!

sequence: "The heavens have been reversed."
"Quietly, the stars' arcs have shifted."
"A voice calls from the depths of the abyss."
"So it says..."
"Seek not the answers of days gone by..."
"In the reflections of the stars."
Corridor of Fog - Star-Sinking Abyss
Shortly after...

scripts.say: The Tempesta, the Vengeful Queen, a Nebula Guardian, a student of Stellapolis, and even a fine young lady from Crownpolis... What a motley crew.
And how could I forget you, Commander? Long time no see.
(Did she wait until just that moment to help us?)
It has been a while.
We appreciate reinforcements from the Church of the Goddess during these hard times.
Is it just me, or have you gotten stronger?
Why, yes.
Unnatural currents are flowing all over the world. With these endless anomalies, I need to temper myself.
I'm glad to see you, too.
The last time I saw you was at Islas de Libertád. You took an ancient relic home with you, right?
Before that, we met at the Sleeping Sea... I remember you didn't go home empty-handed that time, either.
What's your angle this time?
This time... I'm just here to solve the inversion of the stars.
The key to doing so should lie within Stellapolis's observatory.
I'm sorry that preparations took longer than expected. I wish we'd been here sooner.
About those preparations... Did you repair the Startrace Beacons?
I left Pearl in charge of the beacons while another team carried out the abyss-sealing ritual.
Were those serpents the enemies hounding you?
Don't worry. Such monsters cannot stand a chance against the Church of the Goddess!
As she proudly pats her chest, she notices Royal Fortune's visible grief.
Uuugh! I KNOW you meant well and all!
But! We were THIS close to getting her to join our side!
Look at all the food in the water! I tossed all that out just to fish her up!
...Food?
She glances down at the water. Only the remains of wreckage skelebeasts are left.
Aaah! It didn't sink, did it?! Now I can't even salvage it!
Umm... I'm sorry. I never imagined that the circumstances would be... Uh, you continue to amaze me!
The Church of the Goddess will provide double the compensation for the supplies you've lost.
Still, I wouldn't recommend allowing an echo of the deep into your fleet. She's dangerous, you know.
Her demeanor is flawless. If she's lying, I certainly can't tell.
(Even after we've spent so much time together, she remains an enigma.)
Some time later, Pearl and a fleet of ships under the Church of the Goddess arrived at the Star-Sinking Abyss.
Everybody, let us offer our sincere gratitude to the goddess's guidance for bringing us together in this crisis.
The inversion of the stars has caused shipping lanes all over to collapse.
I hope that you will work with us in the Church to bring the predicament to a swift end.
We'd be happy to! I have always dreamed of fighting shoulder to shoulder with the Church of the Goddess!
Heheh, with the Church on our side, our luck has finally turned around!
So Crownpolis and the Nebula Guardian weren't enough, and now I have to deal with the fanatics, too?
Tch... I'm going back to the cabin. Call me when there's something for me to kill.
BEEP BEEP!
A piercing sound rings out, interrupting the conversation.
Our third warning – all know its meaning.
That means...
Oh, no! The observatory's last line of defense has been breached!
The observatory... On that island over there, you mean?
Ganj-i-Sawai turns to look at the tiny speck on the horizon.
I don't see anything attacking it.
Wait, something is wrong. Could it be?
Her vessel emits golden ripples, causing the distant scenery to shatter like glass.
The observatory's island at the end of the fogbound sea reveals its true form.
What are those white things? Coral colonies?
Layers upon layers of skelebeast hordes...
Their main force was lurking here right in front of our very eyes.
We mustn't let the observatory fall!
Set sail immediately! Save the observatory at any cost!
KABOOOOM!
In the world where the stars and sea are reversed, Merkuriy was locked in a heated battle with her shadow.
Gaze at the stars, dive into their reflections... Seek the secrets buried deep within.
No... Everything has already spiraled out of control.
I must stop guiding, close off the observatory, and return everything to normal.
KABOOOOM!
Sooner or later, the secrets of the past will surface, and the veil of the stars will shatter.
That is the irreversible tide of time. I am only following it.
If the Inverted Tide cannot be stopped, then one must simply be the first to turn their ship around.
No! Seek not the answers of days gone by in the reflections of the stars.
You'll really trust everything that snake tells you?
She came from the abyss. If anybody knows the secrets, it is her... She simply doesn't want others to share in that knowledge.
ROOOOAR!
*pant*... It still isn't over?
She returns!
I am you, and you are me... Together, we must catch her and pry those secrets out of her beating heart!
No... You are nothing but an echo twisted by the starry sky.
I see your tricks now. You will influence me no longer.
Is that so? Then why am I still here with you, instead of fading away?
Oh, I wonder.
The three layers of defense have been destroyed. She should be able to escape by now.
So why is she chatting up an illusion? Is there still something she wants to know?
*sigh*... There's no time. Might as well just devour the whole thing.
KABOOOOM!
Horror of the deep, exit that observatory at once!
Tch... They caught up already.
Skelebeasts, attack!
ROOOOAR!
Skelebeast hordes encircling the island immediately turn and surge in like waves. Water churns in their midst, making the sea look as if it's boiling.
Th-there are too many! If each of us defeated a thousand... no, TEN thousand...
Worry not. I anticipated the possibility that we would have to face skelebeast hordes.
Heheheh... Yes, the Church of the Goddess knows all about how to control such hordes by now.
O storm, cleanse this place of the impure, and subjugate all who dare defy us!
Clouds gather overhead, obscuring the mess of stars above and their reflection in the water.
A torrential downpour lashes the battlefield as fierce winds howl, changing the skelebeasts touched by rain.
Are they... turning on each other?
A pity. I'd hoped to bring them all under my control at once.
What did you just do?
Heehee. As you can see, I've taken the reins.
No... The Church of the Goddess?!
KABOOOOM!
Your cannon fodder tactics have failed! Let us settle this face to face!
KABOOOOM!
*cough*... *cough*...
Hah! It seems even an echo of the deep poses little threat.
Ganj-i-Sawai led the fleet toward the observatory like an unstoppable force.
The two Lord-class serpents were annihilated in one salvo. Neither the spatial camouflage along the way nor the ambushes hidden within could slow her.
KABOOOOM!
The last camouflage shatters like glass, giving us a full view of the observatory.
Finally, we've made it... to Stellapolis's observatory at the end of the fogbound sea.
I guess I won't be stalling any longer.
It's a good thing I got a nice meal earlier...
The wise serpent knows when the winds have changed. If I'm at a disadvantage, then I'll make a break for it!
Faced with inevitable defeat, Ormrinn Langi dives into the water without hesitation, rams through the barrier sealing the trenches below, and disappears into the abyss.
She ran? Just like that?
Heh... She's an interesting one.
Does that mean we've won, or...?
Yes, we have won. You did wonderfully, Riyala Bey.
Hehe... So this is how true victory feels. It's amazing!
Ahem! It's too early to celebrate just yet. We still have the matter of the observatory!
That's right. The observatory and the inversion of the stars remain issues.
The personnel stationed here have yet to come out... I hope we aren't too late.
Let us disembark now.

sequence: Fogbound Island
Observatory

scripts.say: Ormrinn Langi retreated, and the skelebeasts scattered. The way to the observatory lay unobstructed.
We stepped onto land and entered the building.
The fierce battle outside has not affected its internal structure, allowing the facility to operate as usual.
A vast pool reflecting the starry sky occupies the entire first floor.
Though the sky is covered in storm clouds, the reflecting pool still glimmers with stars' radiance.
Merkuriy hovers directly above the pool, eyes shut tightly.
Fine threads of light reminiscent of the stars fasten her securely to various points in the tower.
The air is filled with the clicking of gears.
This is my first time coming into one of Stellapolis's observatories...
Do they observe the stars through this reflection?
Ganj-i-Sawai approaches the edge of the pool and urges me to follow.
She's still breathing. But she hasn't reacted to the commotion outside... Her consciousness may be trapped.
As she lightly sways her incense burner, green smoke spills from it and travels across the pool's surface.
What are you doing?
Heehee. Shall we head further into the observatory together and meet the girl trapped within?
Our surroundings fill with the green smoke. Suddenly, everything changes.
In the space of jumbled sky and sea, Merkuriy keeps her eyes ever closed.
There was a fierce battle on the inside, too. The damage is awful.
Merkuriy, are you alright?
What happened in this observatory? Why did it become the core of this inversion of the starry sky?
Merkuriy faintly opens her eyes in response to the question.
Ganj-i-Sawai...
The inverted tide draws near...
We must... warn everyone...
Seek not... answers...
What do you mean by "inverted tide"?
What did you see in the stars?!
Clearly agitated, she rushes over to Merkuriy and reaches out to grab her shoulder.
With a crack like shattering glass, the space around us falls apart.
Merkuriy opens her eyes above the pool.
Have I... awakened?
Who... are all of you? Why are you here?
And how... did you get in?
The sky's reflection in the pool vanishes along with the threads of starlight. When Merkuriy settles onto the water's surface, she warily surveys us.
You don't remember anything? Well... That's a problem.
You are Merkuriy, an official stationed at this observatory by Stellapolis. And I am Ganj-i-Sawai, priest of wind and rain under the Church of the Goddess.
This is the situation as it stands...
Ganj-i-Sawai explained the full sequence of events from the Church's perspective, and we added our own accounts to supplement hers.
Goodness, so much has happened...
I'm sorry, but I have no memory of it all.
We understand. Your consciousness was damaged during the attack.
With the technology of the Church and Stellapolis, we can help you make a full recovery.
The investigation can wait until after you've recovered. For now, we must put an end to the global crisis triggered by this observatory.
Of course. I want to know what happened, too, so I will cooperate fully.
So... How do we end the crisis, exactly?
You don't even remember that?
The simplest way by far would be to destroy this observatory.
Without this power source, the inversion of the starry sky will naturally dissipate – assuming it isn't powered by some unknown magic.
I don't know if we should...
There are compromises, of course. Allow me to take the observatory's core power unit.
If the unit is taken away...
The observatory would still be able to perform its core function of observing the stars, no?
The Church of the Goddess has a duty to seal and recover dangerous ancient relics. This duty is recognized by all of the Polises – including Stellapolis, needless to say.
Therefore, Stellapolis has no grounds to refuse.
...I understand. Then please do as such.
Good. Your cooperation is appreciated.
Well, well! It sounds like congratulations are in order. You saved the day, and ya got your mitts on another valuable ancient relic.
We only did the job we have been charged with.
I have noted Libertypolis's contributions to this effort, and I will report them directly to Crownpolis in due time.
Pssh... As if we care.
Hey!
I know, I know – no objections here. Just letting you know, this means the Church of the Goddess has yet another ancient relic in their massive vault. Oh, HOW reassuring.
With that, Anne turns and leaves. Ganj-i-Sawai looks to me, apparently gauging my reaction.
(That's right. Ganj-i-Sawai never leaves empty-handed.)
(But it is true that the Church's help made all the difference today.)
(While I am a little suspicious, surely it's too soon to conclude that they orchestrated all of this for the sake of obtaining more relics.)
Listen. I'm not your enemy.
Don't worry. Your friends are safe. I swear it on my honour.
There is no need to say farewell.
Because we will meet again.
(She may not be our enemy, but she's not an ally we can place full trust in. What is that Church plotting?)
Commander...
I nod to her, showing my willingness to let the matter go for now.
She flashes a beaming smile back at me.
In that case, we ought to discuss the details of the sealing ritual together!

sequence: Shortly after...

scripts.say: The Church of the Goddess completed their ritual and took away the ancient relic.
With the storm clouds and chaotic stars parting, sunlight returned to the sky.
It was suddenly midday again.
Járnbarðinn! I completed my adventure trial!
What an addictive feeling! I can't wait for my next trial!
You should be thinking about how you'll apologize when you get back, instead.
We came all this way together. Let me give you some advice.
Libertypolis opens its doors to all who yearn for freedom. Next time ya wanna make an escape, give it some thought.
Libertypolis...
Of course, if anybody wants to invade by force, our fortifications aren't just for show.
Whoa, hey, no fighting! Let's just go home first and figure the rest out later.
Let me have a little win for once. If you've got something to say, save it for later!
...Fine.
Thank you, Captain of Tempesta. I will be taking Riyala Bey home to Crownpolis now.
Let's have another adventure if we get the opportunity!
I'll bring Merkuriy back to Stellapolis, too. Is that fine with you, Miss Priest?
Perfectly acceptable. I will make a personal visit to Stellapolis soon, and we may talk then.
Pearl and I must report back to the Church, so farewell.
May the Goddess bless your journey home.
Phew... Everybody's leaving our little crew. What will you do next, Commander?
Wanna come back to Crownpolis and take a little vacation with me?
Haha, well... I won't say I'm not interested, but the crisis is resolved now. Usually, this is when I get sent home by force.
Actually, I'm already getting sleepy. I want to sleep in a nice, fluffy bed...
Ooh, then lie down in mine! It's big and soft, just the way you like!
I'll go ahead and carry ya over right now.
While everybody watches, Royal Fortune scoops me up into her arms and runs into the cabin.
Oh, my...
As I'm rocked by the ship, my consciousness sinks uncontrollably.
My perception of the Tempesta world blurs by the second.
Thanks for all your help this time, Commander...
You always come in my moment of need.
This world is just getting more and more turbulent...
The crisis we faced might only be the beginning of something bigger.
But the Tempesta fleet is ours.
No matter what dangers arise, we'll face them together, right?
I look forward to seeing you again.
Hopefully it's soon, {playername}...
As my mind sinks to its lowest point, the whispers in my ear fade away.
In that final moment...
I feel a faint, sweet taste on my lips.

sequence: Tempesta and the Corridor of Fog - The End?
Fogbound Sea
Shortly after...

scripts.say: On the voyage home, Ganj-i-Sawai and Pearl studied the relic they'd obtained from the observatory.
Are these the Wings That Give Shape? It's nothing like what I imagined.
Its most important aspect is its function of shaping, not its form as wings.
Thus, one more of the Goddess's powers has been restored.
The Eyes That Discern foresaw this crisis upon the seas, so I have high hopes for the Wings That Give Shape.
Who knows what would have happened if the eyes had not warned us?
What is Stellapolis doing behind the scenes, really?
There is no telling – except it's quite obvious that they are doing much more than observing the stars.
The Inverted Tide... Regardless of the process, they've found information beyond even the Church's records.
Perhaps it is related to the prophecy of the End Times...
The heavens will shatter, the seven seas shall boil. All things will fall silent, and light shall be returned to eternal dark.
We have to learn more, whatever it takes.
For the sake of the world... and its future.

sequence: Unknown time - Unknown location

scripts.say: Somewhere, deep in the abyss...
Don't run, Ormrinn Langi.
We are both remnants of forgotten days. No matter where you hide, my tentacles will find you.
...Are you another echo of the deep?
So in the end, it was you who took control of the skelebeast horde – not Ganj-i-Sawai.
Why did you do that?
I am the Church's abyssal envoy...
Don't you see? This "crisis" was a ploy of the Church from beginning to end.
They've long since identified the true danger and made secret arrangements against it.
Come with me to the Church of the Goddess.
It is our mission to defy the starry sky, and the Church is the most likely entity to accomplish that.
Hmm...
Why do you still hesitate?
Will I get a lot of food if I come with you?
Heehee... Of course. You can fill your tummy every day.
I see...
Alright. I'm in.

sequence: Unknown time - Unknown location

scripts.say: I open my eyes to a familiar-looking starry sky.
...I should be back at port after leaving the Tempesta test site.
Why am I here?
The Tempesta test site... So the rumors were true. The Commander of Tempesta really does hail from another world.
Merkuriy? So you didn't lose your memory after all.
Right... In front of that priest, it felt inappropriate both to speak and to say nothing.
How did you notice? Is it your special power as someone from beyond?
Basic judgement doesn't require special powers. I've met all kinds of people, you know.
I see... Coming to you for help was the right decision.
Before we talk about that, I have a question for you. Why did you intercept me here? What is this place?
You seem to know about test sites. What is the Inverted Tide?
This is the starry sky etched into my heart... Every time we met since you first entered the Corridor of Fog, it was here.
Of course, I do not have the power to stop you from returning home. This is only your last station on the way back... That's all.
Regarding test sites... Logically, such information should surprise me. After all, that knowledge has been erased from this world.
But I know it because of this recent stargazing experience.
It gave me the opportunity to see things from another perspective.
As for the Inverted Tide, that would be the exact reason I am asking for your help.
I don't quite know what it is myself... No matter how much I change my perspective, it doesn't help.
But you are different. You have a perspective unlike any other.
I will tell you everything imprinted upon me about the Inverted Tide. In return, will you help me investigate it?
Please, {playername}.

sequence: Unknown time - Unknown location

scripts.say: Beyond this world...
The Inverted Tide.。
To think that this method of adaptation could have truly connected to the Inverted Tide...
Zero, your prediction proved correct.
The plan may now move to its next stage.
Concentrate more resources from the DOS to conduct thorough reviews and filtering.
This matter concerns one of the six Ordering Anchors...
So we cannot permit mistakes.

sequence: Tempesta and the Corridor of Fog - The End

scripts.say: Today was a momentous day. A great feast was being held to mark the Tempesta fleet's expansion into Crownpolis.
Royal Fortune sat aboard her prized vessel, aptly named The Great Royal Fortune.
She savored a hot pot full of fresh seafood while mapping out the fleet's future plans.
But suddenly...
Huh? A little early for sunset, isn't it?
The stars in the sky were... off. When she looked around, phantom lights flickered throughout the ocean fog.
She rubbed her eyes in utter disbelief.
Here I was, planning to use our peaceful connections with Libertypolis to set up a new office here in Crownpolis...
Then, by doing some secret trading on the side, we'd scrape together enough money to keep our fleet afloat.
So much for that dream. What's going on here?! Where are the Golden Routes? The sightseeing boats full of delicacies?
Wait a second...
Where the bloody hell am I?!
*sigh*...
After calming herself down, Royal Fortune checked on the hot pot full of food and then analyzed the situation around her.
It's night time, suddenly... but the moon is nowhere to be seen. The stars are a right mess, so the sextant is unlikely to be of any use.
The sea is too calm for my vessel to go anywhere fast. My compass's needle is just spinning... Well, what the hell do I have, then?
Wonderful. Time to kick back and wait for aid.
I have enough supplies for a year of feasts. Surely Dolphin and the others will come by then... Why, yes, it's the perfect plan!
Having settled on a course of inaction, she lay back on the deck of her ship and gazed up at the unfamiliar night sky.
Beneath the disheveled stars, the compass carved roughly by Royal Fortune's own hands began to pulse with golden light.
Huh... My compass is reacting.
Does that mean the Commander is coming?!

sequence: "Traverse the Corridor of Fog."

scripts.say: Please come to its end.
Hmm...
After a hard day's work, I was hoping to lie down in my soft, comfy bed and enjoy a good night's sleep.
But for some reason, here I am in my pajamas, sitting atop a single wooden plank on the sea. A massive ship approaches while I ponder both my situation and the futility of life.
Uh... Hi there.
...Been a while, huh, Commander?
I like your outfit. Are you in some sort of... late-night, pajama-clad wading contest?
Say, why don't ya come aboard?
Hello, Royal Fortune.
It seems I've been brought to the Tempesta world through my dreams again.
Worse, this is clearly my most pathetic appearance yet.
(At least I had a boat last time. You couldn't give me that much?)
Given my present inability to go home, I chose to accept my circumstances and figure out the situation alongside her.
So... You have no idea what's going on, and all you're doing is waiting for help.
Precisely correct!
For some reason, she seems proud of that fact.
I've got enough supplies for a year and more, after all. What's more, this is a clear anomaly in the proximity of Crownpolis – somebody more responsible is sure to take care of it.
Why not kick back and relax for a few days until all this blows over?
Then can you explain why I've been brought here?
Huh? W-wait... Are WE the ones who are supposed to take care of it?
Speaking from past experience, I think the answer is yes.
Now, how about we be responsible and figure out what's going on?
I'd love to, but my sextant and my compass are duds. How am I meant to do anything?
Well... Hmm? Did you just hear something from up there?
Huh?
Someone said, "Traverse the Corridor of Fog. Please come to its end." You didn't hear that?
Not at all!
Well, if that isn't the Commander of the Tempesta fleet! As soon as you arrived, you have already found a lead!
Let us set sail right away, then!
Let's not be hasty, now... Do you even know where this Corridor of Fog is?
Judging from its name, surely it must be where the fog is thickest. Look, there!
She points toward an area of particularly dense fog. Faintly visible there is a path outlined by the navigation lights of phantom ships.
Oh... So you DID look around.
Come now. Has it been so long that you forgot my reliable nature?
Onward! Corridor, ho!
As the vessel sailed deeper into the fog, visibility rapidly worsened.
Silhouettes reminiscent of ghost ships drifted all around, sometimes approaching, sometimes drifting away.
We'd braced ourselves for an ambush, but in the end, there was none. Not that it made things any less eerie, of course.
Heeelp!
Somebody, help meee!
Oh? Commander, did you hear something?
It sounds like somebody shouting for help.
Is it a phantom of a ship without a vessel? Scares me how realistic it sounds.
Is anybody theeeere?! Help meee!
I'm scaaared!
Hmm... Would a phantom cry for help?
Hey, that's not a phantom!
Huh? Is it a real person?
Did someone dare to come all this way without a vessel? They're brave, I'll give them that!
Now isn't the time to be impressed. Let's save her!
After a short commotion...
Phew... Thank you both so much for saving me. I'm from Crown– I mean... Ahem, my name is Riyala Bey!
Were you about to say you're from Crownpolis?
Ack... That was an accident! Please, don't make me go back to Crownpolis!
What? Why would we... Oh! Are you a wanted criminal? Say, is there a bounty on you?!
W-well, I don't think I would go that far...
Tch, just my luck. You don't look the sort, anyway.
Don't be afraid. We just wanted to ask you about this unusual sea region.
You said you're from Crownpolis? From what Royal Fortune here has told me, this anomaly appeared while she was on the way there.
Do you know anything about what's going on here?
Umm... Actually, I was just going for a little trip when all this happened, so I don't know anything either.
...You went out without a vessel?
Um... Yes. I will be more careful next time.
Oh! Never mind that! Now that I'm thinking about it, there is a clue I can share!
Before I left the palace, I saw a diplomatic delegation from Stellapolis.
I think they must have come to deliver a warning from the stars.
It might even have something to do with the chaos in the starry sky.
A warning from Stellapolis, eh? First I've heard of it.
Galley was working with Stellapolis. I ought to ask her next time we...
KABOOOOM!
In the middle of our conversation, the fog to our starboard side is suddenly wrenched open.
Riyala Bey. You're coming with me.
The situation is critical.
A girl wielding a massive scythe cuts through the fog as she beelines toward The Great Royal Fortune.
Oh, goodness... She actually caught up.
- Is she here for you? - Another person without a vessel?
- Is that all you care about? - It's weird not to have a vessel when you go out, alright?
Anyway, let's have her come aboard our vessel.
Aye-aye.
After another short commotion...
Captain and Commander of the Tempesta, thank you for your assistance.
I am Járnbarðinn, a Nebula Guardian, come on orders to retrieve Riyala Bey. Please allow me to take her.
I'm not going home until I've overcome the twelve trials!
You cannot defeat me. There is little point in negotiation.
Why are all of you Nebula Guardians so... bullheaded?!
Thank you again for your assistance. I will report this incident to the Nebula Guardian headquarters and Crownpolis.
With that, Járnbarðinn attempts to leave with the struggling Riyala Bey in tow.
You're just going to shove off, then?
Yes. The mission is my priority. Or do you intend to stop me, Captain Royal Fortune?
No, no, I didn't mean it like that! You don't have supplies, a vessel, or even a route home... You can't leave like that, can ya?
I have supplies. As for the route, you may tell me the way.
We're looking for a way out of this, too! But we have a lead, so why don't ya come with us?
This should be an acceptable price for letting the two of ya aboard, I'm sure.
With a devious smile, she suggests a price to our two prospective passengers.
Umm... Is this like a ticket price?
Right! It covers meals, accommodations, and all until our adventure is over!
That's pretty cheap... Okay, you have a deal! I'll pay it!
Ch-cheap?
Yes?
Well, that was only the price for one of ya!
Hmm? I knew that. I'll go ahead and pay yours too, okay, Járnbarðinn?
...Wow.
I suppose I have no choice, then. Riyala Bey, I will be your escort until you are safely returned to Crownpolis.
Thank you very much!
Please prioritize your own safety from now on.
Will do!
Always stay within my field of vision, and unless absolutely necessary–
Yes, that's okay with me!
Also–
Don't you worry!
Oh, and you must be nervous to go on your first big journey, Járnbarðinn! I totally get it, but don't fear – I will be here to protect you!
Captain and Commander of the Tempesta. I would like to request that the two of you protect Riyala Bey alongside me.
You didn't even have to ask. I got paid, so I'll get the job done.
Nobody can beat the Commander and me!
Hahahahah! Hold on tight, everyone! We're charging straight into that sea of fog!
We sailed for a while longer amidst the lights of ever-increasing ghost ships.
As we pressed on, the lights suddenly branched off in many different directions.
Well, this is a conundrum. Which way should we go now?
My wooden compass... still picks up nothing.
Commander, have you heard any new clues since that "traverse the Corridor of Fog" business?
Nothing since.
Aww... Alas.
I have an idea. Instead of choosing a path, let us push through the unlit fog to forge a new one.
There's no way that will work!
Hey, where are you goiiing?!
Járnbarðinn leaps from the deck, swinging her scythe as she falls to cut through a figure clambering up from below.
A spray of water erupts from the waves, causing the vessel to lurch.
...An ambush.
Wreckage skelebeasts?!
Wow... So these are wreckage skelebeasts? I've never seen one in person before!
Riyala Bey.
I know! This is a combat trial! Rest assured – I will fight them off!
Er, no...
Royal Fortune, prepare to intercept.
Broadside barrage! Fire at will!
KABOOOOM!
Ugh... Is there no end to these skelebeasts?
Fall back, Riyala Bey. We only need to clear out the enemies to our front.
Royal Fortune. Another group approaches underwater on the port side.
I know that!
*sigh*... I'm getting bloody tired of having to fight swarms of enemies every time I'm short on firepower.
She frowns and sighs as she turns the ship's wheel.
Strange... Are we drifting further off course?
The skelebeasts might be herding us in a specific direction.
The ghost ships lighting our way have all but disappeared.
I don't like this. Knowing my luck, a Lord-class skelebeast will be–
Heeheehee!
Say, I've been hearing an odd voice for a while now!
It's speaking some nonsense about "interstellar guidance" and "fate."
But all that mumbling is impossible to make heads or tails of, even with my listening gear.
Ah! It's coming from that way! Let's go see what it is!
KABOOOOM!
Fated ones, guided by the stars...
You've finally come.
As we sail into a place with thinner fog, a woman appears on the water.
You're people... Thank goodness. That was the last of my amplifying magic circles.
Heheheh... Finally, somebody has come!
Ahem... I foresaw this moment – the time of your safe arrival before me.
You are the ones fated to meet with me today... The saviors who will rescue Selimiye from her desperate predicament.
So... Ahem. Instead of staring at me with such pity in your eyes, would you please pull me aboard already?
I just threw out my back... My luck is pretty awful lately, hahaha...
Suspicious.
Yes... Very suspicious.
Huh? Riyala Bey! It's ME! Selimiye of Stellapolis! We've met before, remember?!
We have, but... that makes you even more suspicious.
You should be studying in Stellapolis, shouldn't you? Why are you here?
That's what I'd like to know! I went out to finish a celestial observation assignment, and I found myself in this mess...
I see. So the anomalous sea isn't just affecting Crownpolis – it even stretches as far as Stellapolis?
I had no idea it was this serious.
Say, Selimiye. Did the diplomatic delegation come from Stellapolis to deliver a warning about this matter?
How should I know? I'm just an exchange student. S-still, once I can get my bearings, I could divine the answer!
Oh... Don't tell me. You came without a vessel too, didn't you?
I... ran aground yesterday, actually.
Never mind – that's definitely the real Selimiye. I am certain of it.
Then there you have it! The more the merrier – and the more money in my pocket, of course.
Come aboard! The Great Royal Fortune welcomes ya!
KABOOOOM!
Once the last enemy was sunk, the waters finally calmed.
However, Járnbarðinn remained wary. Royal Fortune also kept her eyes fixed in one direction.
(Is there something in the fog?)
ROOOOAR!
Is that...
You saw it, too? Impressive eyesight.
There's no doubt. It's a Lord-class skelebeast.
We have too little firepower. Direct confrontation is best avoided.
Damn right. None of you brought vessels, and I'd rather not fight a Lord-class with mine alone.
Still... We've lost the guidance of the ghost ships.
Hehe. Lost travelers, why do you turn a blind eye to the answer right in front of you?
If you want to go to the observatory, then allow me to lead the way.
Observatory? What observatory?
The observatory set up by Stellapolis to keep this sea region anchored to the Starry Veil, of course!
I don't yet know which observatory it is yet, but...
Surely it won't matter which!
Whatever the case, I was told to traverse the Corridor of Fog to its end!
Huh? Did you hear that voice, too?
Too...?
What?! Do you attend school in Stellapolis, as well?
Not exactly. It's just the circumstances, or... a special gift, maybe?
Is that voice something that only the people of Stellapolis can hear?
Precisely! Heheheh.
It would take ages to explain the technology used to transmit that voice, but put simply, it's encrypted data transmission based on human consciousness.
Only those who have undergone special training in Stellapolis and learned particular knowledge can hear and understand it!
But you can do it innately... That's amazing!
Heheh! This is the Commander of the Tempesta fleet, after all. You'd bloody damn well be amazed!
I agree with going to the observatory.
Whatever the meaning of that message may be, Stellapolis's observatories are safe.
They are equipped with defensive capabilities and ample supplies.
We may regroup there and plan our next actions.
Go on, then. Lead the way, Selimiye!
Wait, wait, wait... I need time to find the right way.
My guidance requires preparation... It won't be too much, trouble. I swear, I'll pinpoint the observatory's location soon!
A-anyway, let's get moving, okay? We can talk while we go.

sequence: Corridor of Fog - Unknown location
Shortly after...

scripts.say: Heheheh. Even with the stars in disarray and heavens reversed...
In the reflection, I can see that singular course.
Now, in accordance with my divination, raise our speed to 12 knots.
Continue in the direction I've indicated for 12 minutes at that pace, and we should arrive at the Startrace Beacon!
Once it is lit, the location of the observatory will be revealed beneath the stars!
Wow! You really could divine it! You have gotten much better at this since you left Crownpolis.
Heheh, maybe a little. Would you like a few lessons?
I think I'll pass... There are still many trials waiting for me!
Ah, I see... Good luck to you, then!
Thanks! Let's do our best together!
We followed Selimiye's instructions through the fog until a small island suddenly appeared within view.
Heheh. Just as I predicted! We have arrived at Startrace Beacon!
Now, all that's left to be done is to repair–
The grin on her face freezes once she gets a clear view of it.
On the island, an old structure is partially submerged in the sea.
It's clearly damaged, with its surroundings covered in destruction and debris.
As if some massive creature has crushed it and dragged it, along with the rest of the island, leaving it to be eroded by the seawater for years on end.
Repair it?
You mean... WE have to?
Uh, well...
I-I got us here, didn't I? Hah! Hahah!
Let's just go, Commander. This place is a dud.
(The damage is incredible. It's ruined and decrepit...)
Wait a minute. Selimiye, does Stellapolis regularly maintain their Startrace Beacons?
Of course! Each beacon is managed by its respective observatory, and inspectors survey them every week!
But this one is completely ruined. It looks as if it's been neglected for years. Someone would have noticed, surely.
Are you suggesting... that this is only a disguise?
I think it's possible.
It hasn't been a full day since the anomaly appeared. Deliberate or not, it can't have decayed to this extent in so little time.
Let's disembark and take a closer look.

sequence: Corridor of Fog
Startrace Beacon

scripts.say: After we'd set foot on the island and entered the ruins, the scenery abruptly changed.
Despite its outward appearance, the facility was mostly intact, save for some partial damage.
In a large hall engraved with magical circles, a holographic projection played, repeatedly reenacting the final moments of what seemed to be an attack.
Huh?! It really was a disguise?
Heheh, I get it! This is Stellapolis's illusory camouflage!
When a Startrace Beacon is damaged, it automatically uses this technology to exaggerate the scale of the destruction!
In doing so, it deceives attackers and other ne'er-do-wells!
And it even keeps a recording of the moment it was attacked... What brilliant technology!
Weren't you in Stellapolis? How did it fool you, too?
I'm only a student, remember? I'm not FROM Stellapolis in that sense.
*sigh*... All you Polis people do is make things difficult. Things were easier when we were all free birds...
While the others split up to search the facility, I decide to take a closer look at what's in front of me.
This facility...
It almost looks as if it's a repurposed Siren ruin.
All I have is a gut feeling... but if it is a Siren facility...
I should try authenticating. Just maybe...
Guided by instinct, I head to a broken magic circle and reach out to touch it.

sequence: A recording begins to play, unlike any other one before it.

scripts.say: A swarm of Siren drones quietly work amidst the sea of ruins.
Are they... dismantling it?
What I witness baffles me.
It looks like a Siren test site, but there's something alien about it.
It's a chilling sensation – silence evocative of death and desolation, like a tomb.
This record isn't from the modern era... It's been stored in the magic circle.
The Startrace Beacon must have been intentionally built atop these ruins.
In that case, the observatory's purpose must not just be for observation or navigation...
Stellapolis sent a high-level delegation to Crownpolis. Then, this anomaly suddenly appeared.
Did Stellapolis predict something?
Or... are they related to this anomaly?
The truth is sealed within the stars' reflections...
Who are you?!
A figure suddenly and unnaturally barges into the recording.
The truth is sealed within the stars' reflections...
Seek not the answers of days gone by...
In the reflections of the stars.
The light fades, and the world returns to normal.
(The recording cut off.)
(That voice was the same one I heard from the stars earlier...)
(Is she connected to the observatory somehow?)
Meanwhile...
Heheheh. The damage to the beacon is much lighter than we once thought!
Repairs should go smoothly! In theory, anyway!
Why in theory, exactly?
Umm... It might go well if I can fix it, but I can't promise that I'll be able to fix it without issue...?
...What?
Oh, I get it! Because you've been so unlucky recently, you mean?
Yeah...
Do you think your luck would be that bad if you just took it seriously?
Wow... No wonder you got dragged into this while doing an assignment.
I will help you! I happened to study the Startrace Beacons a little bit in Crownpolis.
Heheh, you're too kind. May the stars bless you!
A light flickers on, signaling a successful restart of the Startrace Beacon.
Instantly after, a beam of starlight rises straight from the sea to the sky, illuminating the surrounding fog for a mere moment.
So this is an activated beacon... It's as beautiful as a star that has fallen into the water.
I've never seen one in person before.
It's pretty, I'll give you that!
Hey! I get it now!
Can you not startle me every bloody time you speak?! What is it now?
I know the name of this beacon's observatory – of the place we must go to!
The Fogbound Observatory, located at the very end of the fog!
The guidance we received was directing us toward the observatory all along!
Wait... the Fogbound Observatory?
Is that not at the edge of the world itself?
Nebula Guardians occasionally patrol there, so I remember it well.
Why is it there?
I couldn't tell you... The answer to that question didn't come with the divination.
If I had to guess, maybe it has to do with the stellar inversion?
...Stellar inversion? What's that?
Hm? You don't know? The sea and the positions of the stars are related.
If the stars go into disarray, what do you think happens to the sea?
Well... What happens?
The sea goes into disarray in turn.
...Are you saying my navigation equipment is failing because the stars are in disarray?
Heheh. That only scratches the surface.
When I say "disarray," that's very literal – the stars' alignment has been muddled, which also muddles the alignment of sea regions.
Two regions from opposite sides of the world could end up adjacent as a result of the shuffle.
And in fact, you've seen how we have all been brought together from different seas.
Incidentally, I was confused at first by why it was called an inversion rather than simply disarray.
But we've all experienced it firsthand, haven't we? In that very first moment, there was a pull, as if the sea and stars had turned upside-down! That must be why.
The stars have fallen into the sea... which means we're sailing on a sea of stars!
Oh, I remember it now!
I read about something like this in the history books at the library!
This happened once in ancient times.
It was during an age of myth, so I assumed it to just be another legend...
Heheh. Stellapolis must have noticed an omen. That's why they sent a delegation to Crownpolis!
Though they were clearly too late.
Hmm... So Stellapolis and Crownpolis were behind this, all along.
A cold voice echoes from the distant darkness.
In no time, Járnbarðinn, ready and waiting, lunges forth and swings her scythe.
I was wondering when you'd show yourself. Couldn't hold back anymore, could you?
KABOOOOM!
Damned Nebula Guardian. You let me approach on purpose, didn't you?
Queen Anne's Revenge, the Federation of Polises has placed a bounty on your head. I hereby place you under arrest.
Try me.
Anne narrows her eyes, sizing up each of us as she waits for an opening.
Her gaze locks on me for a moment before turning to Riyala Bey.
I choose you.
Not happening.
KABOOOOM!
Another violent bang follows. Finally, Royal Fortune's attention is drawn to the situation at hand.
Hey, wait!
I am your captain, and I demand you stop for a sec!
Royal Fortune. Whose side are you on?
I'm neutral!
...Gah, that's not what's important right now!
Queen Anne's Revenge! Captain of the Vengeful Queen fleet and leader of Libertypolis!
Captain Royal Fortune has a question for you!
Get on with it.
Did you bring a vessel with you?
...What?
Through Royal Fortune's mediation, Anne and Járnbarðinn reached a temporary truce.
After that, the girls exchanged information with our newest guest.
Crownpolis had issued a summons before the anomaly – notably, before the arrival of Stellapolis's delegation.
If Stellapolis's delegation was there to deliver a warning, then what was the summons for?
Many questions remained, but Royal Fortune was still the only person present with a vessel.
That meant the rest of us were only passengers. Our lives were in her hands, which meant that she called the shots.
So... As I understand it, the inversion of the stars has disrupted the seas.
No wonder it reached as far as Islas de Libertád.
I got swept up in this mess on my way to investigate the outlying islands.
As for my vessel... Why would I take one with me on such a short trip?
Heh, fair. You must have gotten careless now that you've got a base of operations.
Not me, though. The Great Royal Fortune and I are two halves of the same being!
